Narayanan said Mr. Singh was able to rise above the mundane and produce a treatise that he regarded as thought leadership in the field of tax administration. “How does thought leadership come into tax administration, that is the gulf that Mr. Singh has managed to bridge,” he said.
“There is a thread that runs through the book about India, a nation intent on regaining its past glory so as to take its appointed place in the committee of nations,” Mr. Narayanan observed, adding, “What makes this book special is that it demonstrates how an elite, technical education can translate into refining public service leadership, including in fields such as revenue generation, also how tax administration should be simply refined in a way that it becomes more citizen centric.”
Amitabh Kant, former G20 Sherpa of India and former CEO of NITI Aayog, said each chapter in the book captured not just the places where the author was posted but also the various phases in the evolution of tax administration and institutions. “You see how technology reforms and data systems slowly transform an old-styled tax system into a modern, data-driven, and citizen friendly organisation,” he added.
Shankar Jiwal, former Tamil Nadu Director-General of Police, A.K. Viswanathan, former Commissioner of the Greater Chennai Police, Shreesh Chandra, founder-director, OakBridge Publishing, and Mr. Singh, and his wife Sadhana Singh also spoke.

title: ‘Heritage Treasure Hunt’ for Poorna Chethana School students and parents to be held on December 21
summary: Join the Mysuru Heritage Treasure Hunt on December 21 for Poorna Chethana School students and parents, celebrating culture and teamwork.
content:
The Poorna Chethana School has organised ‘Mysuru Heritage Treasure Hunt’ for students and their parents on December 21. The event will also feature a heritage flash mob, through which students will showcase Mysuru’s culture and traditions.
The programme aims to instil cultural awareness among children while strengthening the parent-child bond. Designed for children below 16 years, the event will begin at 7 a.m. at Sri Kote Anjaneya Swamy Temple. The competition will conclude at the same venue.
Each participating team will be provided with a special treasure kit containing 10 clues. A press release explained that teams will have to visit historical and heritage locations in Mysuru city and solve the clues.
The winning teams will receive cash prizes of ₹10,000, ₹7,500, and ₹5,000, along with trophies. All participating teams will be awarded certificates. For registration, participants can send a WhatsApp message to 7204836513, the release added.

title: UDF returns to power in Kannur Corporation
summary: UDF wins a decisive majority in Kannur Corporation, defeating LDF and celebrating a significant electoral victory.
content:
Delivering a major setback to the Left Democratic Front (LDF), the United Democratic Front (UDF) secured a clear majority in the Kannur Corporation by winning 36 of the 56 wards.
In the Kannur Corporation, where 1,35,780 of the total 1,93,079 voters cast their vote, the LDF finished a distant second with 14 seats, while the National Democratic Alliance (NDA) won four seats. Besides retaining the Pallikunnu ward, the NDA also won Kokkenpara, Thulicheri and Temple wards. The Congress lost the Thulicheri and Temple wards to the BJP.
Compared to the previous election, the UDF improved its tally from 34 to 36 seats, while the LDF’s strength fell from 19 to 15 seats. The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) increased its representation by three seats. The Social Democratic Party of India (SDPI) also secured one seat from the Arakkal ward.
Several prominent LDF leaders suffered defeats. P.K. Ragesh lost from Panikkara, former State Sports Council president O.K. Vineesh was defeated in Thalikkavu, and former standing committee chairperson K.P. Sabira lost from Arakkal.
Meanwhile, three rebel candidates who contested against the UDF in Payyambalam (K.N. Bindu), Varam (K.V. Riyas) and Adikadalayi (V. Muhammadali) wards were defeated, further consolidating the UDF’s position in the Corporation.
Following the victory, UDF workers celebrated across key parts of the city, bursting firecrackers and holding victory marches. UDF convener P.T. Mathew, DCC president Martin George, IUML district president Abdul Kareem Cheleri, and former Mayor Muslih Madathil led a victory procession in an open vehicle along with the elected candidates, greeting the public. Party workers participated in large numbers, carrying flags and banners.

title: Cong-backed candidates win 45 GPs in Sangareddy constituency, felicitated
summary: Cong-backed candidates win 45 GPs in Sangareddy constituency, felicitated
content:
SANGAREDDY
District Congress Committee (DCC) president and Telangana Government Industrial Infrastructure Corporation (TGIIC) chairperson T. Nirmala Jagga Reddy on Saturday felicitated newly elected Sarpanches, ward members and Upa-Sarpanches who secured victories in the Sangareddy Assembly constituency at a programme held at a constituency-level meeting in Sangareddy.
Telangana Pradesh Congress Committee (TPCC) working president T. Jagga Reddy also felicitated Congress candidates who were defeated in the elections, acknowledging their efforts and commitment in strengthening the party at the grassroots level. It said that Congress-backed candidates had won in 45 Gram Panchayats in the constituency.
Addressing the gathering, Mr. Jagga Reddy said the victories were achieved through unity, strength and dedication, despite his absence from the campaign.
Clarifying the party’s stand, Mr. Jagga Reddy said there would be no entry into the Congress for candidates who contested and won as rebels. However, he said independent candidates who emerged victorious could join the party after a decision by the Block Congress and Mandal Congress leadership.
On the occasion, he announced that Masku Alavani Narasimha Reddy, who was defeated in the Kondapur sarpanch election, would be appointed as chairman of the Sadashivapet Market Committee.

title: Maghi Sambhrama highlights traditional winter flavours
summary: Experience Mysuru's Maghi Sambhrama, celebrating traditional winter flavors and culinary delights, showcasing unique crops and dishes.
content:
The two-day Maghi Sambhrama, inaugurated in the city on December 13, brought to the fore traditional winter flavours and culinary delights to the people of Mysuru.
Conducted by Sahaja Samrudha and Sahaja Seeds at Nanjaraja Bahadur Choultry, the event has evoked a warm response from the public. The mela is showcasing winter crops such as groundnuts,avarekai,halasande,togari, roots and tubers,desimaize, and pigeon pea, apart from a variety of millets.
Different varieties ofavarekai—chinugalu, dabbe, kempu, mani,andhittala— relished by older generations but relatively unknown to the youth, were on display and for sale. The bulk of it has been cultivated in places around H.D. Kote, Periyapatna, Tumakuru, Dharwad, and Bengaluru Rural.
Dr. Shivaprasad Huded, Vice-Principal of JSS Ayurveda Medical College, inaugurated the Maghi Sambhrama and underlined the importance of consuming pulses and legumes during winter.
“It is essential to increase the intake of foods prepared from traditionally grown crops such asavarekai(field beans),halasande(cowpea), and pigeon pea pods. Their use benefits farmers who follow the multi-cropping system by enhancing their income, while consumers derive health benefits,” he added.
“The aroma and taste ofavarekaiand pigeon pea, available during the Maghi season, are truly special. These are protein-rich foods available at an affordable cost. Maghi Sambhrama has introduced traditional foods and cooking practices to urban residents. It should also be organised in other centres where the culinary culture associated withavarekaiis fast-disappearing,’’ said Dr. Huded.
Kalappa, an organic farmer from Hitnehebbagilu village of Periyapatna taluk, rued that cultivation of traditional crops such as groundnut, tree pigeon pea, and sweet potato, which require minimal care in cultivation, was becoming rare.
‘’Farmers, attracted to commercial crops like tobacco and hybrid maize, have forgottenavarekai,halasande, and tubers, and are becoming dependent on store-bought groceries. At least for their personal consumption, farmers should grow pulses and tubers,’’ he noted.
Maghi Sambhrama is not just an exhibition and sale of pulses and legumes. Visitors can also relish dishes such asavarekai uppittu, avarekai dosa, muddewith shelledavarekai sambar, avarekai bath,and evenavarekai jamun,in addition tojowar rottiof north Karnataka,’’ said Krishnaprasad of Sahaja Samrudha.
A salient feature of the Maghi Sambhrama is the availability of rare and indigenous varieties of rice, such asuduru sali, brought by the Devadhanya Farmers Producer Company. A display of bottle gourds in various shapes and sizes, apart from an exhibition of  ‘gourd art’ which entailed making artistic or decorative objects using gourd, are other attractions of the event, which will conclude on December 14.

title: Focus on coal price rationalisation, quality improvement and workers' welfare: Union Coal Minister G. Kishan Reddy tells SCCL
summary: Focus on coal price rationalisation, quality improvement and workers' welfare: Union Coal Minister G. Kishan Reddy tells SCCL
content:
Hyderabad
Union Minister of Coal and Mines G. Kishan Reddy called upon the Singareni Collieries Company Limited (SCCL) to immediately focus on reducing coal prices, improving coal quality, securing new mining blocks and strengthening workers’ welfare, to ensure the organisation’s long-term sustainability.
The Minister chaired a high-level review meeting on Singareni at Singareni Bhavan in Hyderabad on Saturday. Emphasising the need for timely reforms, Mr Kishan Reddy said that the Centre was in the process of introducing reforms in the coal sector and made it clear that public sector undertakings can survive only if they function with complete commitment and efficiency.
He said that new labour laws have been implemented with a focus on workers’ welfare and stressed the need for their strict and effective implementation. “There should be no compromise whatsoever when it comes to the welfare of Singareni workers,” the Minister asserted.
Since coal production remains the core business of Singareni, the Minister directed the company to enhance coal quality standards by setting up coal washeries, including the adoption of new dry washery technologies.
Earlier, Singareni Chairman and Managing Director Shri N. Balaram made a detailed PowerPoint presentation, explaining the company’s financial position and future strategies. The meeting was attended by Coal Ministry Secretary Vikram Dev Dutt, Telangana Energy Secretary Naveen Mittal, B. Veera Reddy, Director (Technical), ED (Coal Movement) B. Venkanna, among others.

title: Amaravati farmers’ issues will be addressed on priority, says Union Minister Pemmasani Chandra Sekhar
summary: Union Minister Pemmasani Chandra Sekhar prioritizes resolving Amaravati farmers' issues, with most land acquisition cases nearing resolution.
content:
Union Minister of State for Rural Development Pemmasani Chandra Sekhar has asserted that the government is committed to resolving the Amaravati farmers’ issues on priority basis through the three-member committee, with justice, transparency and farmers’ confidence as its guiding principles.
Addressing a review meeting at the APCRDA headquarters in Amaravati on Saturday, Mr. Chandra Sekhar said farmers’ problems were being classified into general and major issues, and examined in depth. He said nearly all of the 47 land acquisition cases under review had reached the resolution stage, and the remaining would be settled in a week.
As part of Amaravati’s capital requirements, acquisition of around 2,500 acres of land would be taken up in phases. He said that of the 69,421 land pooling plots, registrations for 61,793 plots had been completed, and issues related to the remaining would be resolved soon.
Mr. Chandra Sekhar said a proposal had been finalised for road alignment at Mandadam village after considering farmers’ views and suggestions from local MLA Tenali Sravan Kumar. He added that legal hurdles related to the lanka lands had been cleared to enable registrations, while a special committee was constituted to study soil and water levels in about 180 acres of Jareebu lands.
Municipal Administration and Urban Development Minister P. Narayana said social infrastructure development in Amaravati was a top priority, with DPRs for 26 villages under preparation. He said ₹22.6 crore had been sanctioned for 18 community halls, and assured clarity on road-hit lands, compensation and TDR bonds in three months.
Mr. Sravan Kumar said the government was in continuous dialogue with farmers and conducting regular reviews to address concerns related to land acquisition, village abadi lands and infrastructure development.

title: Revanth briefs Rahul on Telangana’s political situation
summary: Revanth briefs Rahul on Telangana’s political situation
content:
HYDERABAD
Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy and Telangana Pradesh Congress Committee (TPCC) president B. Mahesh Kumar Goud received Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha, Rahul Gandhi, at the Rajiv Gandhi International Airport (RGIA) and travelled with him to Hotel Falaknuma Palace on Saturday.
During the journey, Mr. Revanth Reddy and Mr. Goud briefed Mr. Gandhi on the latest political situation in the State. The duo informed him about the Congress party’s victory in the recent Jubilee Hills Assembly byelection and the strong performance of party-backed candidates in the first phase of the ongoing Gram Panchayat elections.
Mr. Gandhi has reportedly expressed satisfaction with the performance of the State government and the party. Mr. Gandhi was here to meet football legend Lionel Messi, who is visiting India as part of the GOAT India tour.

title: Family trio holds the key as voters deliver hung verdict in Pala municipality
summary: A family trio's unexpected victories in Pala municipality create a hung council, influencing the political landscape amid fierce competition.
content:
As the UDF and LDF locked horns in a high-stakes battle for control of the Pala municipality, a little-known family collective has stolen the spotlight, pulling off a stunning three-seat sweep.
The surprise winners are Binu Pulikkakkandam, a CPI(M) renegade, his daughter Diya Binu, and his brother Biju Pulikkakkandam. While Mr. Pulikkakkandam, a businessman-turned-politician, emerged victorious from Ward 14, Ms. Binu, an economics graduate from Madras Christian College who is preparing to pursue an MBA degree, has won from Ward 15.
His brother, who has worked closely with Union Minister Suresh Gopi for years, clinched Ward 13. The trio contested and won from three adjoining wards in the Thekkekkara region of the municipality, located across the Meenachil river.
With the UDF securing 10 seats and the LDF 11 in the 21-member council, the three Independent victories have assumed critical importance, as 14 seats are needed for a clear majority. “Both sides have approached us, but no decision has been taken yet. We will arrive at a decision after due consultations with our voters,” Mr. Pulikkakkandam said.
With a hung verdict and neither front in a position to form the ruling combine on its own, Ms. Binu has emerged as a strong contender for the chairperson’s post, with support from either the UDF or the LDF.
This is not the first time Mr. Pulikkakkandam has pulled off such a political coup. In 2010, he had led a mini independent collective in the same region, contesting alongside Independents Ranjini Pradeep and Latha Mohan, and made surprising inroads.
Over the past one-and-a-half decades, he has worn multiple political hats, serving as an Independent, a BJP councillor, and a CPI(M) councillor. A constant thread running through his political journey has been his fierce opposition to Jose K. Mani, chairman of the Kerala Congress (M).
Mr. Pulikkakkandam was expelled from the CPI(M) last year following months of friction over seat-sharing, after the KC(M), the dominant partner of the LDF in Pala, rejected the CPI(M)’s proposal to project him as municipal chairperson.
Adding to the narrative of young faces making an impact, attention has also turned to 24-year-old Riya Cheeramkuzhy, also known as Riyo Bino, who has won from Kaveekunnu on the Congress ticket.
An off-road driver with a deep passion for adventure sports, Ms. Bino inherited her love for jeep racing from her father, Bino Jose. Trained in driving from a young age, she obtained her driving licence at 18 and a heavy vehicle licence at 22, going on to make a name for herself in jeep racing circuits.
Interestingly, her father’s younger brother had earlier served as an LDF councillor in the Pala municipality.

title: At least 60 students at State-run schools fall ill after taking meals
summary: At least 60 students at State-run schools fall ill after taking meals
content:
At least 60 students, in two separate incidents, fell ill after consuming their meals at State-run schools in the city on Friday.
The incident at Mandal Parishad Primary School, Chandra Naik Thanda in Madhapur, affected about 40 students. The students were rushed to the Area Hospital at Kondapur and the nearby private hospital for immediate attention.
It was reported that the students showed the symptoms a little after consuming their mid-day meal. It was also stated that the food at the school was supplied by the centralised kitchen of  Akshaya Patra Foundation. The lunch included dal, potato curry, sambar andpayasam.
In another case, about 20 students at Telangana Minorities Residential Educational Institutions Society at Bagh Lingampally fell ill after consuming their breakfast. The students complained of stomach pain, and showed vomiting and diarrhoea symptoms. They were admitted to King Koti Government Hospital and Niloufer Hospital.
The students in both the incidents were declared stable and were being monitored.

title: State Sugarcane Cultivators Association warns against fake donation drive
summary: The State Sugarcane Cultivators Association warns the public about fake donation drives using its name for unauthorized fundraising.
content:
The State Sugarcane Cultivators Association has said that donations are being collected in its name on the pretext of celebrating national events and other such programmes by certain groups.
In a release, the Association’s general secretary, Atahalli Devaraj, said that it has come to his notice that funds are being collected from officials in government offices, private organisations, and institutions, apart from politicians and others.
Mr. Devaraj said that the Association does not collect donations from anyone and if the need arises, the amount is pooled from fellow members. He cautioned the public against entertaining such requests.

title: Kerala local body polls: UDF reclaims Thrissur Corporation after a decade
summary: UDF's decisive win in Thrissur Corporation marks a decade-long comeback, leaving LDF with a significant urban setback.
content:
The United Democratic Front (UDF) has staged a decisive comeback in the Thrissur Corporation after 10 years, winning an absolute majority and delivering a clear verdict against the much-touted “Suresh Gopi effect.”
The Congress-led front emerged victorious in 33 divisions, comfortably crossing the halfway mark in the 56-member council. The Left Democratic Front (LDF) secured 11 seats, while the National Democratic Alliance (NDA) won eight, with four Independent candidates also making it to the Corporation.
After being confined to the Opposition benches for two consecutive terms, the UDF went all out this time to overcome that fatigue — and its determination has not gone in vain. The UDF, however, narrowly lost the Kottapuram division, where the contest ended in a tie after both the UDF and the NDA candidates polled an equal number of votes, forcing the decision to be settled by a toss.
Laly James, UDF candidate from Lalur division of the Thrissur Corporation, celebrating her victory with daughter, Maria, on Saturday.  
                                                            | Photo Credit: 
                                K.K. NAJEEB
The outcome marks a sharp turnaround from the 2020 elections, when the UDF fell just short of power in dramatic fashion. That election had produced a rare deadlock with the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) winning six seats and the remaining 49 split evenly between the LDF and the UDF at 24 each. The stalemate elevated Independent councillor M.K. Varghese to the role of kingmaker, a position that eventually saw him become the Mayor.
This time, however, the UDF’s commanding lead has rendered the Independents politically inconsequential, underscoring a clear and unambiguous mandate for change in the city.
Equally notable is the absence of any visible “Suresh Gopi wave.” The BJP had entered the civic polls with high hopes, banking on Union Minister Suresh Gopi’s sweeping victory in the 2024 Lok Sabha election and his strong performance across the Thrissur Corporation divisions. Party leaders had openly spoken of “capturing Thrissur” by replicating the parliamentary success at the local body level.
That projection, however, fell short. While the NDA marginally improved its tally — from six seats in 2020 to eight this time — it failed to achieve the breakthrough it had promised, unlike its gains in Thiruvananthapuram. Still, the NDA did manage to establish a notable presence in the core areas of the city, signalling pockets of growing influence.
For the UDF, the verdict represents a decisive correction of what it once described as the “slip between the cup and the lip.” With voters consolidating firmly behind the Congress-led alliance, the Corporation appears set for a clear change of guard. However, the defeat of sitting councillor and Kerala Pradesh Congress Committeesecretary John Daniel in the Patturaikkal division, at the hands of NDA candidate A. V. Krishnamohan, came as a setback for the UDF.
“The people had been waiting to give a fitting reply to 10 years of corruption, mismanagement and poor governance under the LDF. Issues such as the stray dog menace and what people perceived as a tax onslaught pushed citizens to the brink. This verdict is a clear response to that,” said Rajan Pallan, former Opposition leader in the Corporation.
Reacting to the setback, Communist Party of India (Marxist) [CPI(M)] district secretary K. V. Abdul Khader acknowledged the need for introspection. “This defeat calls for a serious and in-depth review. However, the reversal has largely occurred in the city. The LDF has retained its dominance in the municipalities, grama panchayats, block panchayats and the district panchayat. Organisational weakness in urban areas was a factor, and the BJP’s advances in the city’s core areas need close examination,” he said.

title: LDF fails to get majority in Kozhikode Corporation, BJP makes big gains
summary: LDF loses majority in Kozhikode Corporation as BJP and UDF gain seats in local body polls.
content:
With three seats short of a simple majority, Kozhikode Corporation remains the only major consolation for the Left Democratic Front (LDF) that has faced a setback in the local body polls in the State, the results of which were announced on Saturday.
The LDF won 35 of the 76 seats, while the United Democratic Front (UDF) bagged 28 seats and the National Democratic Alliance (NDA) 13 seats. The UDF has staged a comeback in the civic body, increasing its tally from 17 to 28. However, the BJP has made big gains in the Corporation, winning 13 seats, as against seven in 2015 and 2020.
S. Jayasree, LDF candidate in the Kottooli division of the Kozhikode Corporation, arrives at the counting centre at Nadakkavu after she was declared the winner.
                                                            | Photo Credit: 
                                K. Ragesh
S.K. Aboobakker of the UDF defeated LDF’s ‘mayoral candidate’ C.P. Musafar Ahamed in the Meenchanda Division of the Corporation by 271 votes.
Sreeja C. Nair, NDA candidate in Mavoor Road ward of the Kozhikode Corporation, celebrating her victory with party workers in Kozhikode on Saturday. 
                                                            | Photo Credit: 
                                K. Ragesh
Incidentally, the UDF’s mayoral candidate, KPCC general secretary P.M. Niyas, also tasted defeat. He was defeated by Hareesh Pottangadi of the NDA by 320 votes.

title: Excise officials seize 2 kg ganja, MDMA and illicit liquor in multiple raids across Hyderabad, six arrested
summary: Excise officials in Hyderabad arrest six individuals, seizing 2 kg ganja, MDMA, and illicit liquor in multiple raids.
content:
Telangana Excise and Prohibition Department officials arrested six individuals in multiple raids across Hyderabad and adjoining areas on Saturday and seized two kg ganja, small quantities of MDMA, illicit liquor, multiple vehicles and mobile phones from them.
In the first case, the State Task Force (STF) City team seized 1.1 kg ganja from one Panduga Bhanu. Investigators later identified the involvement of another individual, Bobbala Narendra Reddy, and registered a case against him as well. A motorcycle used in the offence was also seized, and the accused along with the contraband were handed over to the Bhongir excise station.
In a separate raid in Kukatpally Housing Board (KPHB) Colony, the STF-D team conducted inspections and apprehended Reniguntla Ajay, 23, while he was allegedly selling ganja. The team seized 100 grams of ganja and 0.40 grams of MDMA from him. The accused, along with the drugs, his two-wheeler and mobile phone were handed over to the KPHB excise station.
Another raid was carried out in Musheerabad, leading to the seizure of 480 grams of ganja from a man identified as Abdul Samad. His mobile phone and motorcycle were also confiscated, and he was produced before the Musheerabad excise station along with the seized contraband.
In the fourth case near the Hanuman Temple in Bagh Lingampally area of Chikkadpally, an STF team seized 230 grams of ganja and arrested Avadhoota Harshavardhan. The accused and the banned substance were handed over to the Chikkadpally excise station for further action.
Meanwhile, officials seized 20 bottles of illicit liquor during inspections at the Indian Family Dhaba and Restaurant in Annaram village on the Hyderabad–Narsapur highway. Two accused, identified as G. Hemanth Kumar and G. Keshav Kumar, both residents of Gummadidala mandal in Sangareddy district, were booked. According to AES Srinivas Rao, the accused, a two-wheeler and the seized liquor bottles were handed over to the Patancheru excise station for further investigation.

title: LDF retains Varkala municipality
summary: The CPI(M)-led LDF retained its grip on the Varkala municipality, vastly improving its performance from 12 seats in 2020 to 16 this time, indicate data released by the State Election Commission (SEC) following the counting of votes on Saturday.
content:
The CPI(M)-led LDF retained its grip on the Varkala municipality, vastly improving its performance from 12 seats in 2020 to 16 this time, indicate data released by the State Election Commission (SEC) following the counting of votes on Saturday.
The BJP-led NDA’s tally fell from 11 last time to 10 in 2025, while that of the Congress-led UDF dipped from 7 seats to 6. Independents won two seats.
Following the ward delimitation in local bodies in Kerala, the number of wards in the coastal municipality had increased from 33 to 34.
The newly-formed Janardhanapuram ward was won by the LDF’s Anushree.
The three-cornered fight in Varkala municipality had garnered a lot of attention this time on account of the sharp rise of the BJP in the 2020 elections, the infighting within the UDF and the presence of rebels.
LDF wrested the Karunilakode, Chaluvila, Kallamkonam and Sivagiri wards from the BJP, and Kallazhi, Cherumkunnam, Maithanam wards from the Congress.
UDF wrested Kanwasramam ward from the BJP, and  Raghunathapuram and Panayil from the LDF. BJP took Teachers Colony, Municipal Office from the LDF and Jawahar Park from the UDF.
LDF won the following wards: Vilakkulam, Idapparambu, Janathamukku, Karunilakode, Kallazhi, Chaluvila, Kallamkonam, Cherukunnam, Sivagiri, Puthenchantha, Vallakadavu, Maithanam, Janardhanapuram, Mundayil, Papanasam and Kurakkanni.
NDA won Ayanikkuzhivila, Kannamba, Teachers Colony, Thachankonam, Perumkulam, Municipal Office, Hospital, Temple, Jawahar Park and Pinnamoodu.
UDF won Pullanikode, Kanwasramam, Raghunathapuram, Panayil, Kottumoola and Panayil.
Nadayara and Ramanthali fell to independent candidates.
In the 2020 elections, the LDF, with 12 seats, had managed to retain power in the 33-ward municipality with the aid of three independents. The UDF was pushed to third spot with seven seats, yielding the status of main Opposition party to the BJP. The latter had increased its score from three wards in 2015 to 11 in 2020.

title: UDF makes major gains in civic bodies in Palakkad
summary: Front improves its standing across municipalities, the district panchayat, block panchayats and grama panchayats
content:
The United Democratic Front (UDF) has made gains in the civic body elections in Palakkad district, improving its standing across municipalities, the district panchayat, block panchayats and grama panchayats compared to 2020.
Although the Left Democratic Front (LDF) retained control of the Palakkad district panchayat, its victory lacked the sheen it enjoyed in 2020. The LDF won 19 of the 31 seats, while the UDF secured 12. UDF had only three seats in 2020.
The National Democratic Alliance (NDA), which had hoped to win a seat or two in the district panchayat, faced a disappointing outcome.
In the 13 block panchayats, the LDF won nine while the UDF secured three, with one block remaining without a clear majority. This marks a shift from 2020, when the LDF had won 11 blocks and the UDF only two.
The LDF suffered notable losses in the district’s municipalities. Of the seven municipalities, it managed to win only two: Shoranur and Ottapalam. The UDF claimed victory in Chittur-Thathamangalam, Cherpulassery, Mannarkkad, and Pattambi, while the NDA retained control of the Palakkad municipality.
In 2020, LDF had won five municipalities and UDF and NDA one each. This time, UDF wrested Pattambi, Cherpulassery and Chittur-Thattamanagalam from LDF.
Although the BJP fell short of a majority by two seats in Palakkad, it retained control of the municipality as the party secured the largest number of councillors.
The NDA secured a total of 52 municipal seats in the district, including 25 in Palakkad municipality. It emerged as the main opposition in Ottappalam and Shoranur municipalities, winning 12 seats in each. However, its performance in the other municipalities was dismal, capturing just one seat each in Cherpulassery, Mannarkkad and Pattambi, and failing to win any in Chittur-Thathamangalam.
In the district’s 88 panchayats, the LDF claimed 46 panchayat councils, the UDF 31 and the NDA two. Nine panchayats, Ayiloor, Chalavara, Eruthempathy, Kottayi, Mathur, Parali, Thenkara, Vadakkenchery and Vilayur, remained hung, with no party securing a majority.
In 2020, the LDF had won 63 panchayats and the UDF 23.

title: Students cautioned against cyber fraud, crimes against women
summary: Chittoor police warn students about cyber fraud, women's safety, drug abuse, and road safety in an awareness program.
content:
The Chittoor police on Saturday organised an awareness meet on cybercrimes, crimes against women, drug abuse and road safety as part of sensitising students of various educational institutions at Sri Vidya Educational Institutions campus here.
Urban Inspector (Law and Order) M. Maheswara and Circle Inspector (Crime) P. Umamaheswara Rao addressed the students and faculty, highlighting emerging social and cyber threats and the importance of responsible behaviour among youth.
The Inspector urged students to stay away from narcotic substances, warning that drug abuse could destroy careers, families and futures. He underlined the need to adopt a healthy lifestyle and maintain clear personal goals to contribute positively to society. Referring to the rise in cyber offences, he advised students to use social media cautiously and avoid clicking on unknown links or responding to suspicious messages.
He also briefed students on women’s safety initiatives, particularly the ‘Shakti’ mobile application, which enables women to seek immediate police assistance during emergencies, and urged women students to download the app. He further highlighted road safety norms, stressing on wearing helmets and seat belts.
Mr. Umamaheswara Rao briefed the gathering about cyber frauds, especially the emerging ‘digital arrest’ scam. He explained that fraudsters impersonate cyber police officials and threaten victims through phone or video calls, falsely claiming legal action to extort money. The police never conduct arrests digitally and urged students not to panic if they receive such calls, the Inspector clarified.
“Victims of cyber fraud should immediately report incidents to the national cybercrime helpline 1930 and avoid sharing personal or banking details on social media platforms,” he said.

title: Use technology with wisdom to achieve goals, UPSSSC chairman tells students
summary: UPSSSC Chairman urges students to wisely leverage technology for personal success and contribute to achieving India's "Viksit Bharat-2047" goals.
content:
Youngsters should play a significant role in achieving “Viksit Bharat-2047” goals set by the Union government, said Uttar Pradesh Subordinate Services Selection Commission Chairman S.N. Sabat. He advised them to use technology with wisdom to achieve their personal goals while contributing to the development of the nation.
He attended as the chief guest fifth convocation of Centurion University of Technology and Management, along with ICICI Prudential-AMC Chief Investment Officer Sankar Naren, in Vizianagaram on Saturday (December 13, 2025). Speaking on the occasion, Mr. Sabat said that youngsters who do courses in accordance with the needs of the industries achieve successs, but those who also do courses in artificial intelligence and other technological advancements get more opportunities.
Mr. Sankar Naren said that courses related to finance and others would ensure a bright future owing to the Indian economy’s progress in the last few decades.
University Chancellor G.S.N. Raju and Vice Chancellor Prasant Kumar Mohanty felicitated and presented honorary doctorates to both the guests on the occasion. Founder of the University Mukti Kanta Mishra and University Vice President D.N. Rao said that the university introduced new courses like aerospace, drone technology, forensic science and others to ensure students get wider learning experience.
University Registrar P. Pallavi gave a presentation on the achievements of the students in various branches. Earlier, the University heads and guests presented gold medals and cash awards to 14 meritorious students. As many as 409 students were presented degree certificates in the programme.
Bapuji Rural Enlightenment and Development Society Chief Executive Officer A. Ramakrishna Raju congratulated the University management for offering new courses such as genetics, agronomy, soil science and plant breeds which have been helping students with rural background to get decent jobs in top seed companies, agriculture research organisations and others.

title: More than 300 farmers ended life after NDA came to power in Andhra Pradesh, alleges YSRCP
summary: YSRCP alleges over 300 farmer suicides in Andhra Pradesh since NDA's rule, citing agricultural decline and unmet welfare needs.
content:
YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) general secretary M.V.S. Nagi Reddy has alleged that more than 300 farmers have ended their life after the NDA government came to power in the State as the agriculture sector has plunged into a crisis.
The coalition government failed to improve the lot of farmers, and, as a consequence, at least two farmers were committing suicide every week, Mr. Nagi Reddy said while addressing the media at the party office in Tadepalli on Saturday. Demanding that remedial action be taken forthwith, he said farmers were in distress because of unremunerative prices.
He said the YSRCP government had paid ₹5 lakh each to the families of 474 farmers who ended their life in 2014-19.  Mr. Nagi Reddy said the NDA government should pay an ex gratia of more than ₹7 lakh on humanitarian grounds. He demanded that the farmers’ welfare schemes introduced by the YSRCP be restored. He said that the prices of chilli, tobacco, banana, maize, cotton, onion, tomato, sugarcane and mango declined steeply, causing huge losses to the farmers.

title: Aland voter fraud case exposed loopholes in NVSP; EC introduces reforms
summary: Aland voter fraud case reveals NVSP loopholes; ECI implements reforms to enhance voter security and prevent future misuse.
content:
The modus operandi in the attempt to delete names of genuine voters from the rolls without their knowledge in the Aland voter fraud case has used the loopholes in ECI’s National Voters’ Service Portal (NVSP).
The chargesheet in the case filed by the Special Investigation Team (SIT) in Bengaluru on Friday, naming former BJP MLA Subhash Guttedar as the prime accused in the case, lists six loopholes on NVSP misused by the accused, sources said.
Any mobile number and the OTP sent to that number could be used to create an account on NVSP, and for subsequent logins, only password was needed, no OTP was needed to be sent again.
Misusing this, Akram Pasha, who ran a call-centre-like firm in Kalaburagi, was allegedly hired by the then incumbent MLA Subhash Guttedar to target and delete names of voters who were likely to vote for his rival. He bought mobile numbers and OTPs sent to these numbers from West Bengal-based Bapi Adya, who ran a website called ‘otp bazar’. This had a tie-up with a USA-based website called ‘sms activate’. The website would randomly provide a mobile number, using which transactions could be made and would provide the OTP sent to that number for a price.
It is suspected that this website may have helped others with digital impersonation and identity theft, and in cyber crimes, earlier. The servers used to host the otp bazar website have been seized and the website will be taken down, sources said.
SIT has pointed to other loopholes in NVSP misused by the accused. There was neither a fixed session time on NSVP. Any number of applications could be made from a single account, any mobile number could be used for the applicant, and no alert was sent to the voter whose name sought to be deleted.
ECI introduced an e-verification system and double authentication on NVSP in September 2025 to prevent such misuse, and limited the number of applications that can be made from an account to six, sources said. This was following the report inThe Hinduand a press conference by Rahul Gandhi, the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha.
However, ECI has not yet shared the key data sought by investigators in Karnataka and delinked the reform measures on NVSP to Rahul Gandhi's press conference and said that it had been planned earlier itself.
With these new safety measures in place as well, whether these measures have plugged all six loopholes is not clear, sources in the SIT said.

title: Karnataka orders immediate solar connectivity for government hospitals; scales up ‘Saura Swasthya’ programme
summary: Karnataka mandates immediate solar connectivity for government hospitals, enhancing the 'Saura Swasthya' program for sustainable healthcare.
content:
The Karnataka Power Transmission Corporation Ltd. (KPTCL) has directed all electricity supply companies (Escoms) to immediately provide connectivity to solar rooftop systems installed in government hospitals, after it was found that several facilities had been denied integration due to long-pending dues.
In a communication to the Managing Directors of Bescom, Hescom, Mescom, Gescom, and Chamundeshwari Electricity Supply Corporation (CESC), the KPTCL noted that hospitals, given their essential and uninterrupted public service role, cannot be deprived of solar power on account of financial arrears. The government has taken a serious view of the delays, the letter said, and instructed all field officers to facilitate immediate connection and ensure compliance without further lapse.
The directive comes as the Health Department accelerated efforts to bring down electricity expenditure through large-scale solar adoption. Karnataka has emerged as the first State in the country to install solar power units in 3,600 government health centres within a year, achieving 80% to 85% savings in electricity bills, according to officials.
The installations are supported through CSR funds under the Saura Swasthya scheme, implemented in partnership with the SELCO Foundation. The initiative aims to ensure uninterrupted power supply across rural health institutions, benefiting more than three crore people.
Since its launch in November 2024, solar units have been installed in around 3,000 centres, with over 1,150 facilities fully solarised. Work is under way in nearly 1,300 sub-centres, and the department expects to reach 3,700 installations by the year-end.
By 2026, Karnataka plans to solarise 5,000 health facilities, including 2,877 sub-centres, 1,971 Primary Health Centres (PHCs), 28 Urban PHCs, 12 Community Health Centres and 112 taluk hospitals. The sub-centres are equipped with 0.25 kW to 1 kW rooftop units, PHCs with 4kW to 5 kW systems, and taluk hospitals with capacities of up to 10 kW.
The ₹120-crore project has already generated power savings of more than three megawatts and reduced electricity bills by up to 70% in covered facilities. Monthly savings are expected to touch ₹50 lakh, amounting to over ₹100 crore over a decade, by reducing reliance on grid power and diesel generators.
Minister for Health Dinesh Gundu Rao toldThe Hinduthat the project would help strengthen healthcare delivery in rural pockets. “Saura Swasthya will not only ensure uninterrupted healthcare services but also lead to immense savings in electricity bills, which can be utilised to improve hospital infrastructure and patient care,” he said.
Beyond installation, the SELCO Foundation is working on a long-term system sustainability through strengthened operation and maintenance (O&M). Remote Monitoring Systems enable real-time tracking, while a dedicated Saura e-Mitra mobile app allows health staff to raise service requests.
Of the 626 complaints logged so far, 314 have been resolved, and more than 2,000 personnel have been trained in maintenance.
The State has also set up India’s first Solar O&M Learning Centre for health institutions in Raichur, aimed at building local technical capacity. “The initiative is lowering electricity costs, reducing CO2 emissions, and strengthening uninterrupted healthcare delivery for last-mile communities,” said SELCO Foundation director Huda Jaffer.

title: Child malnutrition sees sharp decline in Mysuru district
summary: Mysuru district achieves remarkable decline in child malnutrition, with severe cases dropping significantly due to targeted health interventions.
content:
Mysuru district has recorded a significant reduction in child malnutrition levels, with the proportion of severely acute malnourished (SAM) children dropping from 7.2% to 0.21% and moderately acute malnourished (MAM) children declining from 15.6% to 1.05%, according to data from the National Family Health Survey-5 report. Officials said the improvement reflects sustained interventions by the Department of Women and Child Development.
Basavaraj, deputy director of the department, said that according to data from November 2025, 90 children in the zero to six months age group were identified as SAM, while 137 were categorised as MAM. These children are undergoing regular health check-ups, and parents are being educated on the importance of breastfeeding. Community awareness programmes are also promoting the use of locally available leafy vegetables and the importance of maintaining hygiene, officials said.
The department is also supplying nutritious food to pregnant and lactating women. Officials noted that children in the zero to six months group show improved recovery from malnutrition when complementary feeding is introduced along with breastfeeding, according to a press release.
In the six months to six years group, 129 children were identified as severely malnourished and 947 as moderately malnourished. To address this, SAM children are being given milk under the Ksheera Bhagya scheme and five eggs per week under the Srushti scheme, along with additional nutritional supplements.
With the support of the Central Food Technological Research Institute (CFTRI), Mysuru, blood tests are being conducted for SAM and MAM children, followed by the supply of specialised nutritious food for a period of six months. The food supplements include energy- and protein-richburfis, high-protein and iron-rich biscuits, mango bars, spirulinachikki, and glucose-based beverages, distributed on a weekly basis, officials said.
Monthly health check-ups are being conducted with the cooperation of the Health Department, and children identified as severely malnourished are being admitted to Nutrition Rehabilitation Centres (NRCs), the release added.
“Coordinated efforts of the Health Department, CFTRI, and parents have played a key role in improving the nutritional status of children in the district and ensuring their gradual recovery from malnutrition,” officials noted.

title: National Puppetry Festival in Mysuru to be held from December 16 to 21
summary: Join the National Puppetry Festival in Mysuru from December 16 to 21, celebrating India's rich puppetry heritage through performances and workshops.
content:
The Indian Institute of Educational Theatre (IIET), Mysuru, will hold the National Puppetry Festival at the Hardwicke School campus, J.L.B. Road., Mysuru, from December 16 to 21.
Organised in collaboration with Astikya Foundation, this national festival aims to celebrate, revive, and promote the diverse heritage of Indian puppetry through performances, workshops, and scholarly engagement.
The festival will open with the inauguration of a puppet workshop on December 16 at 11 a.m. Led by G.K. Jayaram, author and founder–managing director of Institute of Leadership and Institutional Development, Bengaluru, and puppet designer Shashidhar Adapa, the workshop will run until December 20. At 4 p.m., it will end with a valedictory session, which will be graced by Monnanda Appaiah, managing director, Wienerberger India.
The inauguration of the National Puppetry Festival will be held on December 19 at 6 p.m., with K.M. Gayatri, director, Department of Kannada and Culture, Bengaluru, as guest of honour. Senior theatre director and actor Indira Nair will be the chief guest, and the session will be presided over by renowned theatre exponent Rameshwari Varma.
A major highlight of this year’s festival is the strong national artistic collaboration. Leading puppetry and storytelling teams are participating. The list includes Burdwan The Puppeteers, West Bengal, Talking Turtles Storytellers, Hyderabad, Rangaputhali Puppeteers, Bengaluru, Sanchari Theatre, Bengaluru, Gagan and team, Bengaluru, and Pyooppatree, Kerala, a press release read.
Adding another dimension to the festival, IIET has expanded its outreach through collaborations with various educational institutions across Mysuru. This initiative introduces children to the creative world of puppetry and thus includes active participation from Hardwick School, Arivu Vidya Samsthe (Lingambudhi Palya), Pramati Hillview Academy, Phoenix International Academy, Vidyavardhaka Sangha School, Morarji Desai Residential School (Doddahundi), Vanitha Sadana, Hari Vidyalaya (Bogadi), and Bachpan Play School.
The festival will conclude with a valedictory ceremony on December 21 at 6 p.m., presided over by Guru, philanthropist and industrialist, N. Ranga Rao and Sons, Mysuru, as guest of honour.
IIET invites artists, students, educators, and the general public to join this cultural celebration. For more details, contact +91 98456 05012 or send an email to indiantheatrefoundation@gmail.com.

title: 12-day Christmas celebration begins at historic SIMMS Memorial Baptist Church
summary: The historic SIMMS Memorial Baptist Church in Vizianagaram kicks off 12 days of festive Christmas celebrations and charitable activities.
content: The historic SIMMS Memorial Baptist Church of Vizianagaram wore a festive look on Saturday (December 13, 2025) with the beginning of 12-day Christmas celebrations as well as Messiah March in which hundreds of Christian families took part. After offering prayers at the Church, they participated in the holy march which covered G.T. Road, Railway Station, RTC complex, Balaji junction, Fort area, and culminated at the church premises. South India Baptists Association-Vizianagaram district founder and the church secretary R.S. John said that the special prayers in the place of worship would continue till December 25. He said that the Church would take up charitable activities for the next 12 days as part of the festival.

title: TSCPCR member inspects Shamirpet gurukul, flags serious issues
summary: TSCPCR member inspects Shamirpet gurukul, flags serious issues
content:
Member of Telangana State Commission for Protection of Child Rights, Sarita Gogula, visited Mahatma Jyotiba Phule BC Welfare Gurukul School, Shamirpet, on Saturday, and raised serious concerns about its conditions.
The school has a strength of about 1,200 students but lacks adequate toilet and bathroom facilities, even as the existing ones lack doors.
Ms. Sarita’s visit comes at a time when students from the facility recently staged a protest at a police station over the lack of basic facilities.
In her inspection and interaction, students reported that the mid-day meal scheme was not being implemented properly. They alleged that some teachers are rude in their behaviour, and pointed to negligence by school in-charge.
Students also flagged health concerns and said several of them are suffering from skin rashes and other ailments, reportedly linked to water quality issues at the place.
Ms. Sarita instructed officials to address the concerns within a week, including medical examination of students, and improving basic facilities. Noting that the school is currently operating in a rented building, she said the management should undertake repairs urgently.

title: Minister felicitates national award-winning artisans in Srikalahasti
summary: Minister S. Savitha honors national award-winning artisans in Srikalahasti and distributes toolkits to empower local craftsmanship.
content:
Handlooms and Textiles Minister S. Savitha felicitated five artisans, who recently received national awards from the President of India, at Srikalahasti in Tirupati district on Saturday. Along with A.P. Government’s Handloom and Handicrafts Advisor Suchitra Ella and MLA Bojjala Sudheer Reddy, she also distributed toolkits to 100 artisans from Madhavamala and Srikalahasti.
The recipients include Gorsa Santosh (National Award 2024 for Etikoppaka toys), D. Sivamma (Shilp Guru Award 2023 for leather puppet craft), P. Vijaya Lakshmi (National Handicraft Award 2023 for Kalamkari hand painting), Khande Anjanappa and Khande Harinath (both got Special Mention Award 2024 for leather puppetry craft)
During the year 2025-26, Andhra Pradesh Handicrafts Development Corporation Limited (APHDC) had received grant-in-aid for implementation of improved Toolkit Distribution Programme to artisans in wood carving craft at Madhavamala (50 artisans) and Srikalahasti (50 artisans) under National Handicrafts Development Programme (NHDP) – Skill Development in Handicrafts sector.
APHDC Vice-Chairman and Managing Director Vishwa M. said, “This initiative aims at promoting and preserving the State’s rich handicraft traditions. The local artisans, who possess the identity cards issued by the Development Commissioner – Handicrafts, were selected for the distribution of improved toolkits worth ₹10,000 per artisan under this project.”
The APHDC also provides regular marketing support through 19 Lepakshi Emporiums, conducts training and technical development programmes in various clusters, and creates marketing platforms by organising Gandhi Shilp Bazaars with the financial support of the DC (H). The toolkits include hand-operated tools, electronic machines, and other accessories.

title: Five arrested with ₹70 lakh worth hash oil and ganja in Hyderabad
summary: Five arrested in Hyderabad with ₹70 lakh worth of hash oil and ganja in a major interstate drug supply bust.
content:
The Hyderabad Narcotics Enforcement Wing (H-NEW), along with Langar Houz police, arrested five persons on Saturday (December 13) in connection with an interstate drug supply racket and seized hash oil and ganja valued at ₹70 lakh.
Those arrested were identified as Paul Khila, 33, a labourer from Malkangiri district in Odisha, Krushna Jalla, 31, a mason from Koraput district in Odisha, and Vykunta Rao alias Balu, 33, a peddler residing in Madhapur and originally from Srikakulam district.
Two delivery agents, Balaji, 42, a Rapido driver from Malkajgiri, and Chaitanya, 17, a student from Srikakulam district, were also taken into custody, said an officer from the H-NEW.
“The arrests were made during a joint operation conducted on credible information. We seized five kg hash oil, five kg ganja, a scooter, mobile phones, cash and packing material, including a weighing machine and containers,” the officer added.
Investigators said Vykunta Rao had been procuring hash oil and marijuana from suppliers in Odisha at low cost and selling them in small quantities across Hyderabad and Cyberabad through delivery agents. He is said to have used virtual phone numbers to avoid identification. Police said further investigation is underway to trace other links in the network.

title: Kidwai to set up 50-bed hospice for terminally ill cancer patients
summary: Kidwai Memorial Institute plans a 50-bed hospice for terminally ill cancer patients, enhancing compassionate end-of-life care in Karnataka.
content:
In a move aimed at improving end-of-life care for terminally ill cancer patients, the State-run Kidwai Memorial Institute of Oncology is preparing to establish a dedicated 50-bed pain relief and palliative care centre (hospice).
It seeks to ensure that patients in the advanced stages of cancer are able to spend their final days with dignity.
The proposed hospice, to function under the Department of Palliative Medicine at this recognised Centre of Excellence in Oncology, will be built at an estimated cost of ₹2 crore. A three-storey building will be constructed on a 6,000 to 8,000 sq. ft. site within the institute’s campus, with a private organisation funding and executing the project under its corporate social responsibility (CSR) initiative.
The construction is expected to begin within a month, with the facility likely to be ready by the end of 2026.
The hospice will focus on reducing pain, suffering, anxiety and emotional distress experienced by patients in the terminal stages of cancer, while also offering psychological and emotional support to their families.
“End-of-life care is as important as treatment at the beginning of life, and patients deserve compassion and respect in their final phase,” said Naveen T., Institute Director (additional charge).
The three-storey structure will have patient care wards on the ground and first floors, while the upper floor will provide space for attendants, family members and support staff. Medical manpower, medicines and day-to-day operations will be managed by Kidwai, while the building, equipment and infrastructure will be provided through CSR support by Garuda Foundation.
Hospice care is a specialised form of medical support for patients who no longer have curative treatment options. Unlike conventional treatment, hospice care focuses on managing symptoms rather than the disease itself.
M.K. Yaduraj, Head of the Department of Palliative Medicine at the institute, said pain is controlled using appropriate medications such as morphine and oxygen is provided for breathlessness. “Equal attention is given to emotional, psychological and spiritual needs. It is a family-centred model of care, where caregivers are also supported during an extremely difficult time,” the doctor said.
Kidwai sees around 3,000 outpatients and admits around 750 inpatients daily. Every year, about 24,000 new cancer patients are treated, with over three lakh patients coming for follow-up care. Nearly 20% of them require palliative or hospice services.
Dr. Naveen said the new centre would be the first hospice in a State government hospital in Karnataka to provide comprehensive pain relief and end-of-life care.
Kidwai Institute has also drawn up a phased plan to expand home-based palliative care for terminally ill cancer patients who are unable to travel to the hospital due to advanced illness or immobility.
Under Phase I, services will be extended to patients living within a 10-km radius of the institute. A dedicated team comprising a doctor, nursing staff, a social worker and a volunteer will visit patients at home to provide symptom management, wound care, counselling and caregiver guidance, said M.K. Yaduraj, Head of the Department of Palliative Medicine at the institute.
“Patients will be identified during outpatient visits and followed up through a structured telemedicine programme, including scheduled video consultations. Home visits will be undertaken when patients show worsening symptoms or require in-person clinical assessment,” Dr. Yaduraj said.
“The programme will subsequently be expanded to cover a 20-km followed by 30-km radius around the institute,” he added.

title: Assam’s Demow Model is focus of ICMR project for ‘zero snakebite deaths’
summary: ICMR's ₹13.5 crore project aims to implement the Demow Model for zero snakebite deaths through community engagement and integrated strategies.
content:
Thec from eastern Assam’s Sivasagar has been chosen as one of the successful systems of snakebite prevention and management to be scientifically studied and potentially scaled up across the country, under a project sanctioned by the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR).
The ICMR sanctioned the four-year research project worth ₹13.5 crore to “tackle the devastating public health challenge of snakebite envenoming” in India. The project, called the Zero Snakebite Death Initiative: Community Empowerment and Engagement for Mitigation of Snakebite Envenoming, aims to develop a unified, replicable, and highly effective national model for prevention and management.
The research, spearheaded by Jaideep Menon of Kerala’s Amrita Institute, will span seven States — Assam, Himachal Pradesh, Jharkhand, Kerala, Maharashtra, Odisha, and West Bengal.
The project will analyse and integrate proven regional strategies, topped by the Demow Model, which focuses on robust community engagement and referral networks, and involves community awareness, volunteers, and participation.
For Assam, the study will focus on the Demow and Gelekey blocks of Sivasagar district. Surajit Giri from the Demow Hospital has been appointed as the investigator for the State on this project.
The other models are for protective equipment distribution (Maharashtra), anti-snake venom injection during transport (Himachal Pradesh), and using digital tools for better coordination and real-time surveillance (Kerala).
“The research will be conducted under the banner of SARPA (Snakebite Awareness, Response, Prevention, and Action). This integrated approach seeks to bridge the critical gap between affected communities and formal health systems, ensuring victims receive life-saving treatment within the crucial golden hour,” an ICMR spokesperson said.
The research and community study are scheduled to begin in January 2026. ICMR has already allocated resources, including a research scientist and four technical staff members for each participating State, to ensure rigorous implementation and data collection.
This collaborative effort seeks to produce high-quality implementation evidence to significantly reduce snakebite mortality and morbidity, addressing India’s disproportionately high burden of snakebite envenoming, estimated at approximately 58,000 deaths annually.

title: Azhar visits hospital after 24 students fall ill from school food
summary: Azhar visits hospital after 24 students fall ill from school food
content:
Minister for Minorities Welfare Mohammed Azharuddin and other officials on Saturday met students of the Telangana Minorities Residential Educational Institution Society (TGMREIS) at hospital, and interacted with doctors.
According to sources, the students were from TGMREIS’ Musheerabad Girls School, which has a total over 400 students. As many as 24 students had fallen ill after consuming food in the school.
According to sources, staff of the school, including principal and warden were suspended. They said that there was an inordinate delay in informing the head office.
The head office is closely monitoring the situation, sources said.  Efforts will be undertaken so as to ensure that such incidents do not happen again, said sources.

title: MIEL threatens to pull out of 850MW Ratle power project in J&K if ‘threats, political interferences’ not stopped
summary: MIEL threatens to withdraw from the Ratle power project in J&K due to threats and political interference jeopardizing safety and operations.
content:
Megha Engineering and Infrastructures Ltd. (MEIL), which is constructing the 850 MW Ratle Hydroelectric Project in Jammu and Kashmir’s Kishtwar district, on Saturday (December 13, 2025) said it may pull out of the project if the administration failed to stop threats and interference from locals and politicians.
“There is a lot of pressure on our workers. The way locals and politicians act is undemocratic and should not happen. If the outsiders don’t allow us to work, we may have to leave the project. It will cause a lot of losses as we have paid bank guarantees, invested in machines and material. But we cannot meet the impossible demands like hiring additional staff,” Harpal Singh, chief operating officer of the dam project from Hyderabad based MEIL, said.
Mr. Singh warned that the prevailing situation had the potential to compromise the safety and quality of the project. “We seek support from all. We have a secular character. We can’t work as an extension of or join any political party. Unless we have a good work atmosphere, the safety and quality of the project could be compromised,” he said.
The Ratle project is a run of the river scheme located on the Chenab at Drabshalla village in Kishtwar. The project was approved in 2021 at a total cost of ₹5,281.94 crore, with the scheduled commissioning date set for May 2026.
The trouble for the company began on December 4, when the head of its human resources team was allegedly attacked and beaten while on the way to the residential quarters. “The incident spread fear among the workers,” Mr. Singh said.
The company alleged that it was under pressure from local politicians to hire more local workers for the project. “I want to underline to locals, the district and State administration, and the Union Ministry of Power that the company has no vacancy,” Mr. Singh said.
The project currently employs 1,434 workers. “From Kishtwar, we have 900 workers. From nearby Doda and Ramban, we have 220 and 24 workers respectively. Around 215 workers are from outside as the project requires specialised labour too,” Mr. Singh said.
The officer said the project had been marred by blackmail from politicians, attacks, and false court cases. “Many have been recruited because of local interference. We are making a 133 metre high dam and underground electricity generation of 850 MW. It is a key project,” he added.
In September this year, the company had planned to retrench 300 workers. “We stopped at 200 workers retrenched only. We even assured locals that we would hire in case of any vacancy,” Mr. Singh said.

title: Local body polls: LDF to analyse reasons for poll debacle
summary: LDF leaders plan introspection after local body poll defeat, citing UDF-BJP alliances and communal influences as key factors.
content:
Smarting from the defeat in the local body elections, the Left Democratic Front (LDF) leaders have vowed to do an introspection and devise measures to win back popular support.
Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan, who conceded that the LDF could not make expected gains in the polls, said the reasons for the debacle would be analysed. The National Democratic Alliance (NDA)’s upper hand in Thiruvananthapuram and the influence of communalism in the electioneering were worrying the secularists in the State. People should be made aware of the devious designs of the communal elements. The poll outcome underscored the need for collective efforts against communal elements, said Mr. Vijayan in a statement.
The LDF government would remain steadfastly committed to implementing development and welfare schemes in the State and to widening and securing the vote base of the LDF, he said.
The Communist Party of India (Marxist) [CPI(M)] State secretariat, which termed the poll results an unexpected setback, said it would evaluate the poll results. The United Democratic Front (UDF) managed to win the local body elections by forging tacit and open alliances with communal elements. The UDF and the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) helped each other defeat the LDF. The support of communal elements that stood committed to a theocratic State helped the UDF. The discussions over the UDF's unholy alliance with the communal elements also benefited the BJP, the statement said.
The party discounted the claims that the BJP made huge poll gains in the State. While the BJP became the single largest party in Thiruvananthapuram Corporation, the LDF wrested back the Pandalam municipality from the BJP. The BJP lost the majority in the Palakkad municipality, where it was in power. The LDF won back the Kulanada, Cherukole and Mutholi grama panchayats which were ruled by the BJP, it said.
The CPI(M) would do an introspection whether the deficiencies in the functioning of the local bodies where the Left front was in power culminated in the LDF defeat. Introspection would be done at the organisational level too, the statement said.
CPI(M) State secretary M.V. Govindan said the party had a political history of rising from electoral debacles. Although the front suffered a major setback in the 2010 local body polls, it came back from behind. That time, the party lost power in the Assembly by just two seats. It was the effective work undertaken among the masses that helped the organisation that time, he said. Mr. Govindan claimed that the political base of the LDF remained intact. Barring the gain it made in the Thiruvananthapuram Corporation, the BJP failed to make a big impact, he said.
Communist Party of India (CPI) State secretary Binoy Viswam said the party accepted the people’s verdict with humility. Each constituent of the front would evaluate the poll results. The LDF should uphold the Left values in its functioning. The CPI and the CPI(M) were bound to hold the Left values high. The approach of the two parties on the PM SHRI scheme was the same. Yet, a controversy broke out over the project, hinting at the objection of the CPI to the State government signing an agreement with the Centre, Mr. Viswam said.
The Left parties shall correct themselves and learn lessons from the defeat, he suggested.

title: UDF sweeps Wayanad district in local body polls
summary: UDF secures a sweeping victory in Wayanad's local body polls, dominating district panchayat and block panchayat elections.
content:
The United Democratic Front (UDF) recorded a dream run in Wayanad district in the local body polls.
The front tasted victory in the district panchayat and four block panchayats, besides two of the three municipalities in the district. Of the 23 grama panchayats, 16 favoured the UDF, while six stood with the Left Democratic Front (LDF), and it was a tie in the Pulpally panchayat. The Kalpetta municipality was the only saving grace for the LDF in the district.
The UDF registered a clear victory in the district panchayat. Of the 17 divisions, the front won 15, leaving two to the LDF.
The Sulthan Bathery municipality, which was under LDF governance, favoured the UDF this time. The LDF won only 14 seats as against the UDF’s 19, while the National Democratic Alliance (NDA) bagged one seat. Two seats were won by Independents.
In the Mananthavady municipality, the UDF retained power, winning 21 seats, while the LDF won 14 and Independents won two seats. Meanwhile, the UDF lost the Kalpetta municipality as the LDF capitalised on the unrest within the front. The LDF won 15 seats, while the UDF was confined to eight seats. The NDA opened its account in the municipality with two seats, while five seats were won by Independents.
The UDF got a clear majority in all the block panchayats. It has eight seats in the Sulthan Bathery block, while the LDF has five, and an Independent candidate won the remaining seat. The UDF has 10 seats in the Mananthavady block while the LDF has four. In the Kalpetta block, the UDF has 14 seats, while the LDF was confined to two seats. In the Panamaram block, the UDF won 13 seats, while the LDF could get only one seat. An Independent candidate won the remaining seat.

title: LDF’s experiment with Independents fails to make impact in Koduvally
summary: LDF’s strategy of fielding Independents in Koduvally backfires, securing only three seats in recent local body polls.
content:
The Left Democratic Front’s (LDF) political experiment of fielding Independent candidates in the Koduvally municipality seems to have made not much of an impact. When the results of the local body polls were declared on Saturday, a majority of those candidates lost to their rivals.
Of the 37 candidates fielded by the LDF, 31 were Independents, who contested under the ‘glass’ symbol of the National Secular Conference floated by Kunnamangalam MLA P.T.A. Raheem. The Communist Party of India (Marxist) contested in six wards.
When the results were declared, the United Democratic Front (UDF) won 21 seats, the LDF three and others won 13 seats. Among the others, eight are supported by the LDF and the rest by the UDF. Those who lost included Karat Faisal, incumbent councillor, who had hit headlines when he was questioned in connection with the diplomatic baggage gold smuggling case.
In 2020, he had won from the Chundappuram ward though the LDF disowned him. The LDF candidate, O.P. Rasheed, had polled zero votes then. This time, the LDF declared him its own candidate.

title: Air Chief Marshal AP Singh surprises cadets with Kiran flypast at Air Force Academy
summary: Air Chief Marshal AP Singh surprises cadets with Kiran flypast at Air Force Academy
content:
While many in attendance were wondering about the absence of Chief of Air Staff, Air Chief Marshal Amarpreet Singh at the Combined Graduation Parade (CGP) at the Air Force Academy, Dundigal, the Chief of the Air Staff delivered an unexpected moment that drew attention across the parade ground.
The Air Chief took everyone by surprise when he flew past above the parade ground in a Kiran aircraft, making a dramatic aerial appearance during the ceremony. The flypast came as the parade was underway, momentarily shifting focus skyward before the event continued as scheduled.
The 61-year-old officer is no stranger to cockpit duties even after assuming the top post. Just a month ago, he flew a Rafale fighter jet as part of a two-aircraft formation in which President Droupadi Murmu flew a sortie.

title: Kerala local body polls: Idukki gives UDF a resounding victory
summary: UDF secures a decisive victory in Idukki's local body elections, reclaiming power from LDF in multiple municipalities and panchayats.
content:
Idukki district, for long a Congress bastion before voting the Left Democratic Front (LDF) to power in the 2020 local body elections, has once again favoured the Congress. This time, the party-led United Democratic Front (UDF) has swept to power with a healthy margin in the Thodupuzha and Kattappana municipalities, Idukki district panchayat, and majority of the block and grama panchayats. According to UDF district chairperson Joy Vettikkuzhi, the front’s victory this time was on the lines of its performance in 2010, when it won all 14 district panchayat seats.
This time, the UDF has won in 20 seats in the Kattappana municipality, and the LDF in 12 seats. In the Thodupuzha municipality, the UDF bagged 19 seats and the LDF, 3. The National Democratic Alliance (NDA), led by the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), demonstrated its growing influence by securing nine seats in Thodupuzha.
The UDF got 14 out of the 17 seats in the district panchayat, while the LDF secured the remaining three. In the Idukki block panchayat, the UDF won seven out of eight seats.
“Out of the 52 grama panchayats, the UDF won in 36. This victory shows that the people of Idukki trust us. It also proves that the Kerala Congress (M) does not have much influence here. The UDF has come to power in eight grama panchayats in the Idukki Assembly constituency, the segment of Water Resources Minister Roshy Augustine,” said Mr. Vettikkuzhi.
Apart from the Thodupuzha municipality, the NDA performed poorly in the district. The party could not win any seat in the Kattappana municipality, Idukki district panchayat, and block panchayats, with only a few of its candidates winning in grama panchayats. The NDA had actively campaigned in Edamalakkudy, the first tribal panchayat in the State. But the BJP, which had won five seats in the grama panchayat in 2020, lost two this time and the LDF gained control of the panchayat.
The Kerala Congress (M), which helped the LDF come to power in many grama panchayats and the district panchayat in 2020, could not repeat the performance this time around.
Three political parties based in Tamil Nadu, the All India Anna Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (AIADMK), the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK), and the Viduthalai Chiruthaigal Katchi (VCK), had fielded candidates here banking on the votes of Tamil-origin plantation workers, but they could not win a single seat.
In the 2020 election, the LDF had won in 28 of the 52 panchayats, the UDF in 22, and the BJP in one. The UDF had won in the Kattappana and Thodupuzha municipalities. Initially, the LDF had come to power in Thodupuzha with the support of a Congress rebel, but in 2024, the UDF returned to power after moving a no-confidence motion. The LDF had won the district panchayat.

title: Union MoS Pankaj Chaudhary set to be announced U.P. BJP president
summary: Union MoS Pankaj Chaudhary to be announced as U.P. BJP president, strengthening OBC representation ahead of 2027 Assembly polls.
content:
Union Minister of State for Finance and seven-time Lok Sabha MP from Maharajganj Pankaj Chaudhary is set to be announced as the Uttar Pradesh unit president of the Bharatiya Janata Party.
Mr. Chaudhary filed his nomination papers at the BJP party office in Lucknow on Saturday (December 12, 2025) in the presence of U.P. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath and other senior leaders. He is expected to be declared as the State president on Sunday (December 14) as he was the only person to submit the nomination for the post.
Mr. Chaudhary filed his papers, and his name was proposed by 10 senior party leaders, including Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath and both Deputy CMs Keshav Prasad Maurya and Brajesh Pathak.
“Participated in the nomination filing ceremony of Shri Pankaj Chaudharyjifor the post of Uttar Pradesh BJP president at the State BJP office in Lucknow,” wrote CM Mr. Adityanath onX.
केंद्रीय मंत्री श्री@mppchaudharyने भाजपा उत्तर प्रदेश के अध्यक्ष पद के लिए नामांकन दाखिल किया।pic.twitter.com/1qIEVGCW0D
Mr. Chaudhary, a seven-time MP, graduated from Gorakhpur University and started his political career at the local level when he served as a councillor of the Gorakhpur Municipal Corporation in 1989. In 1991, he was elected as the Lok Sabha MP for the first time from Maharajganj Lok Sabha seat on a BJP ticket.
He won the seat again in 1996, 1998, 2004,2014, 2019 and 2024 representing the party. He was appointed as Union Minister of State for Finance in the second PM Modi Cabinet.
Mr. Chaudhary belongs to the Kurmi caste, coming under Other Backward Classes (OBC) category. Among the numerically significant OBC voters constituting over 35% electorate in the State, Kurmis are the second largest group after Yadavs. Kurmis are roughly 4.7% of U.P. population according to the 1931 caste census, the last time caste centred count was done in the State.
Through Mr. Chaudhary, the BJP is eyeing to consolidate the Kurmi and larger OBC vote bank for the 2027 Assembly polls. The seven-time MP’s elevation comes at a time when the Opposition Samajwadi Party (SP) has given important roles like national general secretary to its Kurmi leaders — Ramprasad Chaudhary and Lalji Verma. Mr. Chaudhary’s appointment holds significance as the BJP’s ally Apna Dal (S), led by Union Minister Anupriya Patel, is also a contender for the Kurmi vote bank.
The appointment of Mr. Chaudhary comes after extensive deliberations in Lucknow and Delhi with B.L. Santosh, BJP national general secretary (organisation) and Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) joint general secretary Arun Kumar holding discussion with senior party leaders in U.P. and New Delhi.

title: Drill to test fog preparedness and low visibility management conducted at Mysuru Airport
summary: Mysuru Airport conducts a comprehensive drill to enhance fog preparedness and low visibility management for passenger safety and comfort.
content:
Mysuru Airport authorities reviewed the fog preparedness and low visibility management through a comprehensive dry run exercise and review meeting here on December 13.
The exercise entailed the participation of all internal and external stakeholders and aimed to strengthen operational readiness, enhance inter-agency coordination, and ensure maximum passenger comfort during fog-related delays, cancellations, or diversions, according to P.V. Usha Kumari, director, Mysuru Airport.
She said the meeting focused on reviewing critical areas essential for seamless airport operations during low-visibility conditions, including timely dissemination of meteorological information from India Meteorological Department, advance coordination among all stakeholder agencies, ensuring serviceability and backup of airside, city-side, and terminal lighting systems, and readiness of all ground handling equipment.
In addition, care was taken to ensure timely display of delay/diversion information, adherence to Directorate General of Civil Aviation‑mandated passenger rights, deployment of additional manpower during disruptions, assistance for Passengers with Reduced Mobility (PRMs), elderly passengers, pregnant women, and those travelling with children, apart from coordination with hotels and taxi operators to prevent overcharging.
