It also called for reinstating accelerated depreciation benefits to further incentivise fresh capital expenditure and technology upgrades, particularly for MSMEs and manufacturing industries, provided the measure is structured to stimulate modernisation without triggering Minimum Alternate Tax (MAT) obligations.
Besides, CII urged strengthening the National Investment and Infrastructure Fund (NIIF) by forming a Sovereign Investment Strategy Council (SIFC) to align investments with national priorities.
The Union Budget for the 2026-27 fiscal year is expected to be presented on February 1, 2026.
According to CII, reinforcing fiscal stability through an economic-cycle-based public debt framework, in place of inflexible annual deficit rules, would enhance resilience by allowing counter-cyclical flexibility during global shocks and avoiding repeated breaches of yearly targets.
Such a framework would strengthen credibility by aligning fiscal policy with medium-term debt sustainability, it said.
“The forthcoming Union Budget 2026-27 has to serve the dual role of stabiliser and growth enabler, and promoting investments will be one of the most critical components in this regard,” CII Director General Chandrajit Banerjee said.
Towards this objective, CII has proposed a comprehensive investment strategy anchored in fiscal prudence, capital efficiency, and investor confidence.
The recommendations emphasise strengthening public capital expenditure as the backbone of infrastructure-led growth, while simultaneously unlocking private and foreign investment through targeted incentives, institutional reforms, and enhanced global engagement.
Bolstering public investment remains essential, CII said, noting that public capital expenditure has been a key driver of India’s post-pandemic recovery, catalysing infrastructure expansion and crowding in private capital.
To strengthen project selection and execution, CII proposed institutionalising a Capital Expenditure Efficiency Framework (CEEF) to prioritise high-impact projects, track physical and financial progress, and evaluate outcomes based on productivity and regional spillovers.
Second, facilitating private investment will be the next major priority.
While public investment lays the foundation, private and foreign capital will be the true accelerators of India’s transformation.
“The Government of India has provided a big demand push via income tax relief in last year’s Union Budget and recently via GST 2.0. Investments, especially private sector investment, will be the next big driver for economic growth that needs to be focused on in the next fiscal to continue the growth momentum,” Mr. Banerjee added.
In this context, incremental tax credits or compliance relaxations for firms achieving significant new investment, production, or tax contribution milestones would encourage reinvestment of profits into productive assets and the scaling up of capacity in high-growth sectors such as clean energy, electronics, semiconductors, and logistics, CII said.
It suggested creating an NRI Investment Promotion Fund, structured as a government-private holding company with up to 49 per cent government stake, to channel NRI, FPI, and institutional investments into sectors such as infrastructure and artificial intelligence.
The fund could raise capital through long-term convertible bonds benchmarked to FCNR rates, offering secure returns with equity upside, including special India Global Diaspora Bonds, the industry body said.
CII also called for simplifying external commercial borrowing processes and providing higher borrowing limits, longer tenures, and partial risk cover for infrastructure and manufacturing projects to improve access to global capital while maintaining external sustainability.
A single-window clearance mechanism for large FDI proposals, backed by dedicated facilitation cells at the Centre and in States, with deemed approval within 60 to 90 days, would deliver predictability, reduce administrative delays, and accelerate large investments, it said.
To deepen global investor engagement, CII recommended establishing an India Global Economic Forum as a government-led platform bringing together multinational corporations, sovereign wealth funds, pension funds, private equity firms, and other institutional investors for structured dialogue with senior government leadership on emerging investment opportunities across sectors.
“An investment-driven growth strategy, anchored in fiscal credibility and institutional reforms, will define India’s next development phase,” Mr. Banerjee added.

title: It is natural meet High Command when in Delhi: Satish Jarkiholi
summary: Satish Jarkiholi says it's natural for Congress leaders to meet the high command in Delhi, but has no updates on key meetings.
content:
Minister for Public Works Satish Jarkiholi has said that it is natural for the Congress leaders to meet the high command when in Delhi, but he had no information on possibility of the Chief Minister and Deputy Chief Minister meeting those in the party high command.
Speaking to presspersons in Belagavi on Sunday, he said that he had information that both Chief Minister Siddaramaiah and Deputy Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar had gone to participate in the campaign against ‘vote theft’ in New Delhi. “But I have no clear information on them meeting the party high command”, he said.
On MLA Iqbal Hussain’s statement on the Chief Minister’s post, Mr. Jarkiholi said that it would be apt to pose questions to the leader concerned who had made the statement. “The high command’s decision is final on the issue of leadership. You should ask them. Chief Minister Siddaramaiah and Deputy Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar will consult and take a decision on the issue,” he said.

title: New Uttar Pradesh BJP chief has internal and external challenges before next Assembly battle
summary: New Uttar Pradesh BJP chief Pankaj Chaudhary faces internal and external challenges ahead of the crucial 2027 Assembly elections.
content:
TheBharatiya Janata Party’s (BJP)newly elected head of the Uttar Pradesh (U.P.) unit, Union Minister Pankaj Chaudhary, may have come to the job after a long process of consultation, but was likely signalled by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in July 2023 itself, a choice seemingly aimed at combating the organisational challenges faced by U.P. BJP, with Assembly elections due in 2027.
It was on July 7, 2023 that the Prime Minister, in Gorakhpur for a felicitation ceremony related to the historic Gita Press publishers, made an unannounced visit to Mr. Chaudhary’s residence in the Harivansh Gali there, a street not totally accessible by car, due to which Mr. Modi, along with State Governor Anandiben Patel and Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath walked a short distance to the house itself.
The impromptu visit made news, and tea leaves were read of the greater prominence coming Mr. Chaudhary’s way, and when in 2024, he was made Minister of State after the Lok Sabha elections, the impromptu visit was said to have fructified, then forgotten.
Not so in the Prime Minister’s mind, it seems, as after extensive floating of names between Mr. Adityanath, Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) joint general secretary Arun Kumar, and BJP president J.P. Nadda, Mr. Modi has selected Mr. Chaudhary for the crucial role.
Mr. Chaudhary thus finds himself at the helm of affairs of a party unit that has several challenges in its path, and his affable persona, Other Backward Class (OBC) identity, Poorvanchali location, and general acceptability to both party workers and the Chief Minister are expected to address all that.
Since the Assembly election of 2022, the sundering within the BJP between the party organisation and the government that runs the State has been obvious. During the 2022 poll, the fact that Mr. Adityanath, considered independent of the BJP’s organisational structure because of the influence of his own outfit, the Hindu Yuva Vahini, and the historic appeal of the Gorakhnath Peeth, was treading his own line. That he had differences with his deputy, Keshav Prasad Maurya, the quintessential organisation man, who had come up through the ranks of the State unit, was obvious.
Then U.P. election in-charge, Union Minister Dharmendra Pradhan, had his hands full calming the tempers of district-level party workers, who were reluctant to help elect the party to power when their voices weren’t heard at the top levels of the State government. That is an issue which persists, and Mr. Chaudhary’s first order of business would have to be to establish coordination between the State government and the party organisation, in terms of programmes, and in fostering some bonhomie.
TheLok Sabha election of 2024saw the BJP lose its dominant position in the previous two Lok Sabha elections (of 2014 and 2019), and slide down to 33 seats from the 62 seats it had won in 2019. This was largely attributed to OBC and Scheduled Caste (SC) voters drifting to theSamajwadi Party (SP)and the Congress, with the decline of the Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP), especially in eastern Uttar Pradesh. Mr. Chaudhary, a Kurmi, and a seven-term MP from Maharajganj in northeastern U.P., is expected to shore up support in this critical area.
As the BJP goes into the U.P. Assembly election of 2027 to attempt an unprecedented hat-trick of wins, the Prime Minister and the party appear to have staked their hopes on Mr. Chaudhary.

title: Two CRPF jawans injured in IEDs blast in Saranda forest
summary: Two CRPF jawans injured in IED blasts in Saranda forest, suspected to be planted by Maoists during a search operation.
content:
Two CRPF jawans of a CoBRA battalion suffered serious injuries in separate improvised explosive device blasts inside Saranda forest in Jharkhand's West Singhbhum district during a search operation on Sunday (December 14, 2025), a police officer said.
The IEDs were suspected to have been planted by Maoists.
West Singhbhum Superintendent of Police Amit Renu toldPTIthat the two CoBRA battalion jawans were part of a team engaged in the search operation against Maoists in the Saranda forest when the IEDs exploded.
"Both jawans have been airlifted to a private hospital in Ranchi for better treatment after receiving basic treatment at the CRPF barrack," the SP said.
The two injured men have been identified as head constable Alok Das and sepoy Narayan Das.
The SP said, "It is an act of desperation by the Maoists. We will intensify the search operations in the Saranda forest."

title: Three Karnataka men arrested for murder in Sathya Sai district
summary: Three men arrested in Karnataka for the murder of a 44-year-old man over a land dispute and personal grudge.
content:
The Sri Sathya Sai district police arrested three persons for the murder of a 44-year-old Karnataka native, on Sunday. According to the police, the three had allegedly killed the deceased following a long-standing land dispute and personal grudge stemming from an earlier humiliation.
Speaking to the media here, Superintendent of Police (SP) S. Satish Kumar said the accused were nabbed following an investigation, and special teams were formed to solve the case registered at Amadagur police station.
The body of the victim, identified as C. Muthappa, a resident of Devaravanka village in Chikkaballapur district of Karnataka, was found on September 4 in a tomato field at Amadagur mandal in Sri Sathya Sai district, close to the Karnataka border. His wife allegedly complained that he was found lying in a pool of blood with fatal head and neck injuries.
The accused, identified as Suresha (54),  R. Somasekhara (36), and A. Ananda (42), all residents of Billur village of Bagepalle taluka in Chikaballapur district, were arrested near Mohammadabad in OD Cheruvu mandal early on Sunday. Police said they would be produced before a court.
According to the SP, Suresha had land-related disputes with the victim, while Somasekhara had a grudge after being allegedly humiliated by the victim in the past. The deceased had reportedly slapped Somasekhara with a chappal in public, after the latter had reportedly misbehaved with his daughter.
Acting on these motives, the accused allegedly planned the murder for nearly six months and attacked Muthappa with iron rods on the night of September 3 when he was returning home after attending an errand at a village in Amadagur mandal on the A.P. border, the SP informed.

title: MP Priyanka Jarkiholi to take 15 meritorious girl students with her to watch Parliament session
summary: MP Priyanka Jarkiholi takes 15 outstanding girl students to New Delhi to observe a Parliament session, inspiring future leaders.
content:
Thanks to the initiative taken by MP of Chikkodi Priyanka Jarkiholi, fifteen meritorious girl students from various colleges in Chikkodi Educational District will fly with her to New Delhi to watch the Parliament session.
These students have excelled in the SSLC and II year PUC examinations in the academic year 2024-25 and will now fly with Ms. Jarkiholi to New Delhi from Sambra Airport on Monday at 8.45 a.m.
Ms. Jarkiholi is bearing the entire cost. The meritorious students are Komala Havaldar, Daneshwari Chougala, Sneha Pujeri, Srushti Padolkar, Amruta Terani, Vishalakshi Shelar, Roopa Hadaginal, Nirmita Savadatti, Revati Madar, Srushti Akkiwater, Sanjana Patil, Aishwarya Patil, Kaveri Mallapure, and two others.
Speaking on the initiative Ms. Jarkiholi has said that similar to the opportunity given to the selected school students to watch the legislature proceedings, she wanted to provide the opportunity to the students to watch the parliamentary proceedings. “So I am taking the girl students with me to New Delhi,” she said.

title: Over 800 booked for drunk driving in Cyberabad and Hyderabad weekend drives
summary: Over 800 motorists were booked for drunk driving in Hyderabad and Cyberabad during recent weekend enforcement drives.
content:
A total of 867 motorists were booked for driving under the influence of alcohol during special enforcement drives in Hyderabad and Cyberabad over the past weekend.
In Cyberabad, the traffic police booked 407 offenders. A majority of offenders, 158, were in the age group of 21-30 years while 147 fell in the 31-40 years bracket. Interestingly, six offenders aged above 61 years.
During the previous week from December 8 to December 13, 385 drunk driving cases were disposed of in courts, with 16 offenders receiving a combination of fine and jail term, 21 being awarded fine along with social service, and 348 being fined.
Meanwhile, the traffic cops in Hyderabad conducted a two-day special drive on December 12 and 13, during which 460 drivers were caught driving under the influence of alcohol. The officials warned that if an intoxicated driver causes a fatal accident, the individual will be booked under Section 105 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, which deals with culpable homicide not amounting to murder and carries a maximum punishment of up to 10 years of imprisonment along with a fine.

title: Vijayawada MP sends 45 SHG women to NIRD-Hyderabad for skill trainning
summary: Vijayawada MP sends 45 SHG women for skill training at NIRD-Hyderabad, promoting sustainable self-employment and entrepreneurship.
content:
Vijayawada MP Kesineni Shivanath (Chinni) is working with a clear vision to ensure that every woman in the district becomes a successful entrepreneur, said Kondapalli Municipality chairman Chennuboyina Chittibabu and TDP State executive secretary Jampala Seetharamaiah here on Sunday (December 14, 2025).
A bus carrying 45 women members of Self-Help Groups (SHGs) was flagged off to the National Institute of Rural Development (NIRD), Hyderabad, for a five-day skill development training programme to be held from December 15 to 19, here on Sunday. The programme, jointly organised by the Kesineni Foundation and NIRD, aims to promote sustainable self-employment opportunities for women. Participants will receive hands-on training in natural farming, vermicompost production, and honey processing.
Addressing the gathering, the leaders said that MP Kesineni Shivanath, through the Kesineni Foundation, has been consistently working to empower women from both rural and urban mandals of NTR district. The initiative seeks to transform SHG members into independent entrepreneurs and improve their livelihoods.
The selected women belong to various mandals across Tiruvuru, Mylavaram, Nandigama and Jaggayyapeta constituencies. Mr. Chennuboyina Chittibabu noted that this was the third batch sent to NIRD, following two earlier training programmes. Jampala Seetharamaiah said the Foundation is also supporting women in product manufacturing and marketing, including training at FDDI, Gachibowli, in Hyderabad of Telangana.
NTR District Rural Federation president Kandula Kalpana lauded the initiative, calling it a landmark effort in women empowerment.

title: Fire breaks out in shopping complex in Gudivada town
summary: Fire engulfs shopping complex in Gudivada; no casualties reported as authorities investigate the cause.
content: Fire broke out in a shopping complex near Nehru Chowk at Gudivada town in Krishna district, in the early hours of Sunday (December 14, 2025). However, no casualties were reported, said the Krishna district Fire Department authorities. The fire broke out in a shop and spread to other shops and reasons for the cause is not known immediately. Fire tenders from nearby stations rushed to the spot and put off the flames, the Fire Department personnel said.

title: Kerala Congress (M) alleges misinformation campaign over ’poor electoral performance’
summary: The party had rather fared well at the just-concluded local body polls, retaining 10 of 11 sitting seats in Pala municipality, it says
content:
A day after the declaration of the local body election results, the Kerala Congress (M) [KC(M)]on Sunday alleged that a deliberate misinformation campaign was being carried out against the party.
In a statement, KC(M) district president Lopes Mathew refuted allegations that the party had performed poorly in the local body elections. He cited the Pala Assembly constituency as an example and pointed out that across grama panchayats and municipal wards the United Democratic Front [UDF] secured 91 seats, while the Left Democratic Front [LDF] won 87 seats. In the Pala municipality, the KC(M) retained 10 of the 11 seats it had won in the previous election, losing just by a narrow margin, he said
The party at the same time also held on to key district panchayat divisions in the constituency, besides reclaiming the Kidangoor division, which covers panchayats such as Kozhuvanal, Mutholi and parts of Karoor. As a result, the party succeeded in winning seats in almost all segments of the Pala constituency across district panchayat, municipality and local bodies.
At the same time, the KC(M) district president acknowledged that the party’s overall seat tally declined from 208 in the previous local body polls to 152 this time.
Mr. Mathew also noted that while the LDF had improved its seat count compared to the last election and managed to reclaim seven panchayats from the UDF in Kottayam district, the BJP’s electoral gains effectively worked to the advantage of the UDF.

title: Labour courts in limbo as new labour codes yet to be brought into force
summary: Labour courts face confusion and stalled proceedings as new codes are introduced without clear repeal of older laws.
content:
Labour courts across the State are facing uncertainty following the recent notification bringing the Industrial Relations Code, 2020 – one of the new labour codes – into force from November 21 this year.
Labour lawyers and activists say the absence of clear directions on the repeal of older labour laws has left adjudicatory bodies unsure of their authority, and this has resulted in stalled proceedings and mounting concerns among workers, trade unions, and employers.
According to advocate V. Prakash, the confusion is due to the lack of a specific notification clarifying the status of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, the Trade Unions Act, 1926, and the Industrial Employment (Standing Orders) Act, 1946. While the new code has been notified, the government has not expressly stated when these earlier enactments stand repealed, he adds.
This has led labour courts to adjourn cases on the assumption that they no longer have jurisdiction, even as new forums under the code are yet to be fully constituted.
For enforcing a law, the government needs to notify rules under the law to operationalise the legislation. It is said that the government intends to enforce the rules for operationalisation of the four codes from April 1.
Industrial tribunals in the State also are reportedly unable to function effectively, as the way they are constituted currently does not align with the requirements under the new legislation. As a result, hundreds of pending disputes relating to wages, dismissals, and service conditions remain undecided. New disputes, including those involving individual workers who are bound by limitation periods, are also left without a clear legal pathway, activists say.
R. Geetha of the Unorganised Workers’ Federation says access to justice is a fundamental right, and the current impasse denies workers and employers a functioning forum to resolve disputes. Many have expressed concern that prolonged delays could heighten tension at workplaces, and weaken confidence in the labour justice system.
Acknowledging the confusion over the functioning of labour courts since November 21, a court officer in the labour court for State cases in Chennai says existing labour courts should continue to function until alternative mechanisms are established.

title: Technology unlocking new opportunities, continuity of policies key to Kerala’s transformation: CM
summary: Kerala's CM highlights technology's role in transformation, emphasizing policy continuity and innovation as keys to attracting investment.
content:
Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan has said that Kerala is moving to a new era where technology is unlocking new opportunities in key emerging sectors. The State has also been empowering every citizen in the process of modernisation, he said.
Addressing the ‘Kerala future form: A dialogue with the Chief Minister’ on Sunday, the concluding day of Huddle Global 2025, a start-up festival organised by Kerala Startup Mission (KSUM) at Kovalam, he also emphasised the need for a continuance of policies and initiatives in sustaining the momentum of the ongoing transformation.
“This is Kerala’s moment. A moment to show India and the world that Kerala is not just participating in the future. We are helping to shape a Kerala where universities become innovation powerhouses, where global partnerships fuel local breakthroughs, where every young person feels that this is the best place to dream big, build boldly and scale new heights,” he said.
Recalling a series of milestone policy interventions and initiatives taken by the government in the past few years, the Chief Minister said Kerala is now a large metro city that is fully connected through optical fibre and providing high quality talent, and which together provides the most ideal destination for investment and innovation.
He also said the State is committed to sustaining the socio-economic progress by addressing the complexities in the labour market.
Speaking on the occasion, General Education and Labour Minister V. Sivankutty said Kerala has made major strides in skill education over the years.
Pledging that collaborations entered into for strengthening skill education will be pursued pro-actively, the Minister added steps are under way to set up a Skill India International Centre in the State capital.
Saeed Al Falasi, Executive Director, Dubai Centre of AI, Dubai Future Foundation, said bringing about a change in the mindset is vitally important in embracing technology-driven social and economic progress. Dubai is a good example of how a change in mindset facilitated a big leap, he said.
S.D. Shibulal, co-founder, Infosys, and vice-chairman of the State government’s High Power IT Committee, said building AI-ready Kerala, choosing a set of domains like Spacetech for specialised development, and keeping the State clean and pollution-free are there critical areas the State needs to focus on in its transition.
Special Secretary (Electronics and IT) Seeram Sambasiva Rao, KSUM chief executive officer Anoop Ambika, and actor-entrepreneur Nivin Pauly also spoke on the occasion. Letters of Intent (LoIs) were exchanged between entities on the occasion to formalise collaborations that would impart scale and speed to the State’s start-up ecosystem.

title: Umayalpuram K. Sivaraman performs after 80 years at the venue where he made his debut
summary: Mridangam maestro Umayalpuram K. Sivaraman is privileged to celebrate both 80 years of his illustrious musical career and his 90th birthday at the very same venue — the Kalahastheeswarar Temple on Madathu Theru in Kumbakonam.
content:
It is not uncommon for a musician to perform at the venue where they made their debut. Rarer still is the opportunity to do so eight decades after that first performance. Mridangam maestro Umayalpuram K. Sivaraman is privileged to celebrate both 80 years of his illustrious musical career and his 90thbirthday at the very same venue — the Kalahastheeswarar Temple on Madathu Theru in Kumbakonam.
“My first performance took place at the Kalahastheeswarar Temple because my first teacher, Arupathi Natesa Iyer, lived in theagraharamadjacent to the temple. I played for the vocalist Srinivasa Iyengar. Vedaranyam Krishnamurthy Iyer accompanied him on the violin, and my teacher played the kanjira,” recalled Mr. Sivaraman.
The temple also figures in Kumbakonam-based writer Na. Pitchamurthy’s short storyKanjamadam. “Although the temple is not named, the ambience and surroundings clearly suggest that it is the Kalahastheeswarar Temple,” says Rani Thilak, who compiled the bookKumbakonam Kathaikal.
The Kalahastheeswarar Temple on Madathu Theru in Kumbakonam.
                                                            | Photo Credit: 
                                R. Vengadesh
Mr. Sivaraman recalled, with nostalgia, the temples and streets of Kumbakonam, the musicians who lived there, and the hotels renowned for their filter coffee and tiffin. It was from the Kumbeshwarar Temple that his grandmother procured his first kanjira, as he displayed a keen interest in percussion instruments from a very young age. He had a habit of keepingtalamon the medicine boxes that arrived at the home of his father P. Kasiviswanatha Iyer, a physician, on Kamatchi Jossier Street.
“My father was searching for a teacher to train me. One day, a patient visited him, and when my father learnt that he was Natesa Iyer, he requested him to teach me. After performing at the temple on August 16 this year, I visited the house where Natesa Iyer once lived and paid mynamaskarams,” said Mr. Sivaraman, who later trained under Thanjavur Vaidhyanatha Iyer, Palghat Mani Iyer, and Sakottai Rengu Iyengar.
When a mridangam maestro meets a Marxist leader
Umayalpuram Sivaraman: ‘I have not even touched the tip of the iceberg’
Watch: Umayalpuram explains how to play for the stalwarts of Carnatic music
Describing his return to the Kalahastheeswarar Temple on his 90thbirthday as a “divine calling”, Mr. Sivaraman recounted an unusual coincidence.
“Mr. Swaminathan, a native of Kumbakonam, wrote to me requesting that I perform at the temple, but he did not write the correct address. However, the postman noticed my name with the title ‘Padma Shri’ and delivered it to The Music Academy, from where it eventually reached me. That is why I call it a divine calling,” he said. Mr. Sivaraman recalled that he had accompanied many eminent musicians who had moved to Kumbakonam during the evacuations of World War II.
“I also had the opportunity to meet and pay my respects to Umayalpuram Swaminatha Iyer on Dabir Street. He was a disciple of Umayalpuram Krishna Bhagavatar and Sundara Bhagavatar, who were direct disciples of Saint Tyagaraja,” he said.
Mr. Sivaraman’s joy was boundless when the headmaster of the Kumbakonam Town High School, where he studied, presented him with a laminated copy of his SSLC certificate on the day he performed at the Kalahastheeswarar Temple. “I came to Chennai in 1955 on the advice of Palghat Mani Iyer, who felt it would be better for my career as a mridangam player,” he added.

title: ISRO lines up 7 launches, including uncrewed Gaganyaan mission by March 2026
summary: ISRO plans seven launches by March 2026, including India's first uncrewed Gaganyaan mission featuring the robot 'Vyommitra'.
content:
ISRO has lined up seven launch missions by March next year, including one to demonstrate home-built electric propulsion systems for satellite and quantum key distribution technologies, and the first uncrewed mission of the Gaganyaan project.
The first of the seven launches is expected to take place next week.
India's heaviest rocket, LVM3, will place in orbit the Bluebird-6 communication satellite for U.S.-based AST Spacemobile through a commercial agreement with ISRO's New Space India Limited (NSIL), Union minister Jitendra Singh recently told Parliament.
The human-rated LVM3 will soar into the sky early next year, carrying the first uncrewed mission of India's human spaceflight Gaganyaan with a robot 'Vyommitra' onboard the crew module.
One more uncrewed mission is planned later next year before ISRO sends Indian astronauts into low earth orbit in 2027.
"First uncrewed mission of Gaganyaan to demonstrate end-to-end mission, including aerodynamics characterization of human rated launch vehicle, mission operations of Orbital Module, re-entry and recovery of Crew Module," Mr. Singh said.
Next year will also see the launch of India's first industry-built Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle (PSLV) that will put in orbit Oceansat satellite. The PSLV will have two more passengers — Indo-Mauritius Joint Satellite and LEAP-2 satellite of Dhruva Space.
To increase commercial launches of satellites, NSIL had given a contract to a HAL-L&T consortium to manufacture five PSLV rockets, under a technology transfer agreement signed in September 2025.
An ISRO-built PSLV will put in orbit an earth observation satellite (EOS-N1) for a strategic user and 18 smaller satellites of Indian and international customers.
The GSLV-Mk II rocket is expected to launch the EOS-5 satellite or GISAT-1A, which will be a replacement for GISAT-1 which failed to reach the intended orbit in 2021.
The PSLV63 mission of ISRO will put in orbit the TDS-01 satellite to demonstrate technologies such as the high thrust electric propulsion system, the quantum key distribution, and indigenous travelling wave tube amplifier.
The High Thrust Electric Propulsion System (HTEP) will enable ISRO to launch all electric satellites in future. This technology will make satellites lighter and reduce the dependence of chemical fuels.
"The technologies and components, once proved in TDS-01, will be employed in navigation and communication missions in the near-future," Mr. Singh said.
A four-tonne communication satellite carries more than two tonnes of liquid fuel, which is used to fire thrusters to steer the satellite in space. But in case of electric propulsion, fuel requirement reduces to just 200 kg, an official said.
As fuel mass is reduced, the electric propulsion system-based satellite will not weigh more than two tonnes but will still have the power of a 4-tonne satellite.
The indigenous TWT (Travelling Wave Tube) Amplifier will enable self-reliance in critical technologies of satellite transponders.
The Small Satellite Launch Vehicle (SSLV) will also launch a dedicated satellite before March 2026.

title: Carol singing competition ushers in Christmas season
summary: The Carmel Catholic Association's annual Carol Singing Competition in Mysuru celebrates Christmas with music, unity, and community spirit.
content:
The Carmel Catholic Association (CCA), Mysuru, organised its 33rd annual Carol Singing Competition at the Teresian College auditorium here on Sunday.
The day-long event, which was organised to foster the spirit of Christmas through music and harmony, featured competitions in 12 categories, with participation ranging from pre-primary students to college teams and religious congregations. Several teams presented carols in English, Kannada, and other regional languages.
Winners in various categories received trophies and cash prizes, while the institution securing the highest cumulative points was awarded the Champions Trophy. Each participating choir comprised 5 to 50 members, performing carols conveying messages of peace, joy, and unity, according to CCA.
The association has expressed optimism that the event would bring the community together in celebration of the Christmas spirit through music, joy, and togetherness.
Rev. Dr. Thomas Antony Vazhapilly, Bishop Emeritus of the Mysore Diocese, inaugurated the competition. Rev. Fr. Augustine Payampalli CMI, provincial of St. Paul’s Province, Mysore, and patron of CCA, was the guest of honour. Prof. Joseph Mathew, President of CCA presided over the function. Other dignitaries were present on the occasion.

title: CPI(M) MP objects to Rijiju’s ‘NDA family’ post featuring nominated Rajya Sabha members
summary: CPI(M) MP V. Sivadasan criticizes Kiren Rijiju's 'NDA family' post for misrepresenting nominated Rajya Sabha members as party affiliates.
content:
CPI(M) Rajya Sabha member V. Sivadasan has written to Union Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju expressing “serious concern” over a recent social media post in which the Minister shared a photograph and video of Rajya Sabha MPs heading to the Prime Minister’s residence, captioned “NDA family”.
In his letter, Mr. Sivadasan pointed out that the post included nominated members Sudha Murty and P.T. Usha, who were appointed under Article 80(1)(a) of the Constitution. “They do not belong to the National Democratic Alliance or to any political party. Describing them as part of the ‘NDA family’ is factually incorrect and politically misleading,” he wrote.
The CPI(M) leader said such representation was not a “minor semantic issue” but amounted to “political appropriation” of constitutionally nominated, non-party MPs, undermining the non-partisan character of their nomination. “When this mischaracterisation is made by the Union Minister for Parliamentary Affairs, it assumes greater seriousness and carries institutional implications,” he added, terming it an “insult” to the President who nominated the members.
NDA MPs from North-East and some of very distinguished MPs riding a bus to Prime Minister's residence. We are extremely grateful to hon'ble PM@narendramodiji for hosting dinner at 7, Lok Kalyan Marg for the NDA MPs.A family atmosphere throughout.pic.twitter.com/c5DKapFRV0
Mr. Sivadasan urged that public communication by senior constitutional functionaries must respect parliamentary conventions and factual accuracy. “Blurring the line between nominated Members and party-affiliated MPs sets an unhealthy precedent and erodes parliamentary propriety,” he said, calling for withdrawal of the post and a public apology.

title: State Govt Employees’ Association president Shadakshari asked to vacate quarters in Shivamogga
summary: Karnataka State Govt Employees' Association president Shadakshari is asked to vacate government quarters in Shivamogga after his transfer.
content:
The Public Works Department has asked C.S. Shadakshari, president of Karnataka State Government Employees’ Association, to vacate the government quarters in Shivamogga, as he was transferred to Bengaluru years ago.
The Executive Engineer of PWD (Special Division) in Shivamogga, on November 29, wrote to Mr. Shadakshari to vacate the government residential quarters (ON-4) in Basavanagudi, Shivamogga. When he was allotted the quarters, Mr. Shadakshari was the Accounts Superintendent at the office of the Joint Director of the Audit and Accounts Department in Shivamogga. He was transferred from Shivamogga to Kolar in November 2023 and later to Bengaluru.
The PWD officer, in his letter, stated that Mr. Shadakshari was asked to vacate through a letter on October 10, 2024. In response, Mr. Shadakshari wrote to the PWD and requested that his family continue to stay in the quarters until the end of the academic year. However, he did not vacate even after the academic year ended.
The PWD has brought the issue to the notice of Shivamogga Deputy Commissioner Gurudatta Hegade as well. The Executive Engineer of the PWD sent the letter, as the Chief Engineer (Communications and Buildings) of the PWD wrote to Shivamogga DC on November 18, 2025, and requested him to ensure Mr. Shadakshari vacates the quarters. The officer stated as Mr. Shadakshari had not vacated the quarters as per the rules, the quarters could not be allotted to any other official working in the city.
WhenThe Hinducontacted Mr. Shadakshari for his comments, he denied receiving any such letter. However, he added that he would follow the rules and vacate the quarters.

title: Kannada must get priority in Karnataka, says Mysuru MP
summary: Mysuru MP Yaduveer emphasizes prioritizing Kannada while promoting multilingualism for personal and professional success in Karnataka.
content:
Yaduveer Krishnadatta Chamaraja Wadiyar, MP for Mysuru, on Sunday, said that Kannada should always get priority in the State and underscored the need to protect and promote the language. At the same time, he emphasised the importance of learning other languages to remain competitive and achieve success in life.
Speaking after inaugurating the Karnataka Rajyotsava celebrations at the Central Institute of Indian Languages (CIIL) here, the MP said that knowledge of multiple languages gives individuals an advantage, as language skills can be effectively used for personal and professional accomplishments. “While learning other languages is also necessary, Kannada must always remain the priority in our State,” he said.
He noted that the Mysuru-based CIIL has the potential to emerge as a model institution in promoting all Indian languages while safeguarding linguistic diversity.
Referring to development and infrastructure, Mr. Wadiyar said the time had come to realise the aspirations of Kannadigas by effectively utilising the infrastructure being created. How best this infrastructure is leveraged for economic growth should remain the focus, he said, adding that one must introspect on whether facilities created by the governments are being meaningfully used.
He emphasised the need to safeguard Karnataka’s culture and heritage. “If the goal of Viksit Bharat is to be achieved, Viksit Karnataka is equally important,” he said.
Expressing concern, the MP said Karnataka was gradually losing its prominence as other States had taken the lead in technological advancements. He cited examples such as Hyderabad, Warangal, and other cities where new-age projects like Quantum City and Aero City are being developed. While Karnataka had led the IT revolution and achieved significant progress, he said, recent setbacks must be addressed by establishing a strong and robust system to regain lost ground.
In his speech, Mr. Wadiyar highlighted the need to adequately recognise the contributions of historian and writer Aluru Venkata Rao to the Karnataka Ekikarana (unification) movement. He said Rao’s role must be represented on par with other leaders, adding that the credit for Ekikarana must be rightfully attributed to him.
CIIL Director Shailendra Mohan, Vice-Chancellor N.K. Lokanath, Centre of Excellence for Studies in Classical Kannada Project Director Talwar, and others were present.

title: If it can’t be done in two years, how in two months?: Krishna Byre Gowda takes on Bengaluru metro officials again
summary: Krishna Byre Gowda criticizes Bengaluru metro officials for delays, questioning the feasibility of rapid project completion amid ongoing hardships.
content:
Revenue Minister Krishna Byre Gowda once again came down heavily on officials of the Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Limited (BMRCL) and contractors over the slow pace of work on the Blue Line (airport corridor), saying prolonged delays have been causing avoidable hardship to the public.
Mr. Gowda on Sunday conducted an early-morning inspection of the Phase 2B stretch from Nagawara to Bagalur Cross, covering junctions including Veerannapalya, Hebbal, Esteem Mall Junction, Allalasandra, Jakkur Airdrome, Byatarayanapura and Kodigehalli. The inspection began around 7 a.m. and Bangalore North Corporation Commissioner Pommala Sunil Kumar, metro engineers, and officials from BWSSB, Bescom, and the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) were present.
Noting the pace of construction, the Minister questioned officials over pillars that have remained incomplete for nearly two years at several locations. “If it takes two years to build a single pillar, how can you suddenly claim the work will be completed in two months? Can you do magic?” he said, pulling up the metro contractor and engineers on the spot.
He also criticised officials for blocking work at some locations while proceeding elsewhere, asking why the public should suffer owing to poor planning and coordination.
He also raised concerns over footpaths and service roads being filled with construction debris, which has made movement difficult for pedestrians and motorists alike.
He directed the authorities to immediately clear encroachments and dispose of metro waste to restore public access and further instructed removal of the debris in front of him during the inspection.
The Minister also flagged unnecessary road blockages caused by metro works, stating that these had resulted in daily traffic congestion across several parts of north Bengaluru, instructing officials to clear avoidable barricades, reopen roads wherever possible, and ensure smoother vehicular movement.
The inspection follows a review conducted by the Minister on December 3, in the Byatarayanapura Assembly constituency which he represents, where he had criticised the prolonged delay in the Blue Line project. The airport corridor, originally scheduled for completion in 2025, was later revised to 2026 and has now been pushed to 2027.
Mr. Gowda had then warned that the sluggish progress of the project was causing severe inconvenience to commuters and called upon BMRCL officials to address bottlenecks without further delay.

title: Youth electrocuted while erecting tent during gram panchayat election campaign in Nirmal district
summary: A youth was electrocuted and another injured while setting up a campaign tent in Nirmal district's Sirpalle village.
content:
A youth was electrocuted and another suffered injuries when they accidentally came in contact with a live wire while erecting a tent as part of gram panchayat election campaign in Sirpalle village of Kubeer mandal in Nirmal district on Sunday morning.
Elections for Sirpalle gram panchayat are scheduled to take place in the third phase on December 17, sources said.
The deceased was identified as Naveen, 25, a resident of Sirpalle.
Another person from the same village suffered an electric shock in the incident. He was rushed to a hospital in Nirmal.
The Kubeer Police registered a case and took up investigation.

title: Govt. borrowings not translating into welfare benefits, says Buggana Rajendranath Reddy
summary: YSRCP leader Buggana Rajendranath Reddy criticizes government borrowings failing to yield welfare benefits amid declining revenue.
content:
The YSRCP has accused the NDA government of resorting to double standards on borrowings and financial discipline.
The TDP-led NDA dispensation was adopting the financing structures it had vehemently criticised while in the Opposition, senior YSRCP leader and former Finance Minister Buggana Rajendranath Reddy said while addressing the media in Hyderabad on Sunday.
Mr. Rajendranath Reddy said the government’s borrowings were not translating into welfare benefits, while declining revenue receipts point to Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu’s failure in wealth creation.
People and media houses who had questioned the YSRCP government’s financing mechanisms were now silent, he pointed out.
The TDP had objected to the previous government issuing Non-Convertible Debentures (NCD) backed by liquor sale revenues, which were used to fund welfare schemes. “The present government is borrowing through the same structure,” he said.
“The government should clarify whether its earlier allegations are meant to mislead the public or whether it is now consciously adopting a structure it once branded as fraudulent,” he said.
He further alleged that the future borrowings of the State Mineral Development Corporation had been pledged and access to the State exchequer extended to private entities, and called it unconstitutional.
Mr. Rajendranath Reddy said the government had raised over ₹2.66 lakh crore so far, yet key welfare schemes had either been stalled or failed to take off. Promised initiatives under the Super Six had not been implemented, including unemployment allowance and Aadabidda Nidhi, he alleged.
Despite increased liquor sales, he said the revenue growth was not reflected in State’s finances, indicating large-scale corruption.
He asserted that the YSRCP government delivered welfare schemes as per schedule even during the COVID-19 period, while the present dispensation relied on propaganda.

title: Minister inaugurates trade fair in Vizianagaram
summary: Minister inaugurates a trade fair in Vizianagaram, highlighting the city's revival as North Andhra's commercial hub.
content:
:
Minister for MSME Kondapalli Srinivas on Sunday said that Vizianagaram would regain its past glory as the largest commercial centre in North Andhra region with the rapid developmental activities taken up by the State government, while inaugurating the three-day mega trade fair in Vizianagaram on Sunday (December 14, 2025).
Speaking at the event, the Minister congratulated Vizianagaram Business Enterprises Association president and convener of the trade fair Arisetti Mukhesh and the trade fair co-convener Darisipudi Ramesh for organising the event as consumers would get to know about drop in prices of goods due to the reduction of GST. Mr. Mukhesh also praised the door-delivery method being implemented by all shops and establishments in the backdrop of tough competition from online e-portals.

title: Will ensure necessary approvals from UGC for Ambedkar Open University in A.P., says TDP MP
summary: TDP MP pledges to secure UGC approvals for establishing Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Open University in Eluru, Andhra Pradesh.
content:
TDP MP and party’s Parliamentary Chairperson in the Lok Sabha Lavu Sri Krishna Devarayalu on Sunday (December 14, 2025) said that he will ensure all the necessary approvals from the University Grants Commission (UGC) for the proposed establishment of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Open University at Eluru in Andhra Pradesh.
In a statement, the Officer on Special Duty (OSD) of the University Velaga Joshi said he, along with academician K. Subba Reddy, met Mr. Devarayulu in New Delhi where the latter gave them assurance that he would write to the UGC and personally pursue the matter to expedite the process.
Mr. Joshi said that he discussed the requirements and formalities related to the establishment of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Open University and submitted a comprehensive report outlining all relevant details to the MP.
After the bifurcation of the State, Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Open University continued to function as a common institution for both States for a period of 10 years. With the completion of this 10-year period, the need arose to establish a separate Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Open University, exclusively for Andhra Pradesh. In this context, the State government took the initiative and decided to set up the university in Eluru and issued necessary government orders. However, due to certain technical issues, the immediate establishment of the university could not take place. This necessitated specific amendments and approvals from the UGC.
Accordingly, a detailed report with comprehensive information has been submitted to the UGC by the Andhra Pradesh State Council of Higher Education. The issuance of a formal notification by the UGC is now awaited.
Every year, nearly 40,000 students in the State pursue various courses through distance education under Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Open University. However, due to the lack of operational activities in recent times, the admissions process has come to a standstill. As a result, thousands of students have been deprived of the opportunity to continue their studies through distance learning.
In this backdrop, Mr. Joshi and Mr. Subba Reddy requested the TDP MP to take immediate steps to secure UGC approvals and to facilitate the establishment of the University at Eluru on a war footing.

title: Autonomy for classical Kannada study centre not too far: MP
summary: MP Yaduveer Wadiyar expresses optimism for the Centre of Excellence for Studies in Classical Kannada to gain autonomy soon.
content:
Yaduveer Krishnadatta Chamaraja Wadiyar, MP for Mysuru, on Sunday, expressed confidence that the Centre of Excellence for Studies in Classical Kannada (CESCK) would soon be accorded autonomous status, while reaffirming his commitment to the development of the centre.
Speaking at the Karnataka Rajyotsava celebrations held at the Central Institute of Indian Languages (CIIL) in Mysuru, Mr. Wadiyar said the process for granting autonomy had already begun. “I think the process has started, and I am with you on this. Only the final decision remains. Land for housing the centre has been identified and development can take place,” he said.
The MP had recently urged the Ministry of Education to accord autonomous status to CESCK, stating that autonomy was crucial for the centre’s growth and long-term development. He pointed out that although Kannada was declared a classical language 17 years ago, the study centre is yet to receive autonomous status.
At present, CESCK functions under CIIL. Mr. Wadiyar, in a memorandum, noted that the centre’s potential remains constrained in the absence of autonomy and adequate infrastructure.
A dedicated building is a key prerequisite for autonomy. In this regard, the University of Mysore Syndicate has identified four acres and two guntas of land near the Pump House, opposite Basavapeetha, for establishing a permanent campus. The State government had issued an order in 2020 approving the allotment of the land.
Mr. Wadiyar had urged the Ministry of Education and the Department of Higher Education to expedite the release of the required funds and extend full support for the construction of the new facility and the upgradation of CESCK’s infrastructure.

title: Rowdy-sheeter stabbed to death in suspected revenge killing in Pahadishareef
summary: Rowdy-sheeter Shaik Amair stabbed to death in Pahadishareef in a suspected revenge killing linked to a previous murder.
content:
A rowdy-sheeter with a criminal past was stabbed to death at Pahadishareef late on Saturday night in what the police believe could be a revenge attack linked to an earlier murder.
The victim, Shaik Amair, 32, a resident of Chintalmet in Rajendranagar, was allegedly attacked by a group led by Ahmed, a relative of Mubarak Sigar, who was murdered two years ago. Amair had been named as an accused in that case.
According to the police, Amair arrived at a hotel in Chandrayangutta on Saturday night to discuss certain issues. Soon after, a group of men took him into a nearby lane, where he was stabbed multiple times. He died on the spot due to his injuries, the Pahadishareef police said.
Police records show that Amair was arrested and remanded for the murder of Mubarak Sigar, reported in January 2024. He was later released on bail.

title: Labour codes will benefit management, not employees, say speakers at seminar
summary: Speakers at a seminar claim new labour codes favor management over employees, lacking minimum wage guarantees and hindering union formation.
content:
The labour codes introduced by the Central government in place of the 29 labour laws will benefit only the management and not employees, said speakers at a seminar on ‘Labour Codes’ organised by Save Public Sector Committee, here on Saturday.
LIC Employees Union Zonal Secretary (Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and Karnataka) G. Tirupathaiah highlighted that the new codes did not offer any guarantee of minimum wages and would make formation of unions a difficult task in the future.
B.R. Ambedkar Mission secretary and lawyer A. Sampath Kumar said that any issue would be settled only under the purview of the Constitution, and hence deviating from the existing laws and withdrawing the powers of unions would not be accepted. He called the Constitution as the guiding light for amicable settlement of all issues.
Save Public Sector Committee convener A. Raghunatha Reddy, employee leaders Avadhanam Srinivas, K. Jagadish and others took part.

title: MP for Mysuru’s growth in harmony with heritage; cautions against repeating Bengaluru’s mistakes
summary: Mysuru MP Yaduveer Wadiyar emphasizes planned growth, urging preservation of heritage to avoid Bengaluru's urbanization pitfalls.
content:
Yaduveer Krishnadatta Chamaraja Wadiyar, MP for Mysuru, expressed support for the planned and organic growth of the city in harmony with its ethos of heritage and culture.
He was participating in a public interaction on ‘’Greater Mysuru or Greater Vision: What does the City Truly Need’’ organised by V.R. Trust on Sunday.
He said any city’s growth was inevitable, but warned that unplanned expansion in the case of Mysuru would irreversibly damage its heritage and liveability index.
Development of any city cannot be stopped, but its growth has to be organic and policy-driven and guided by a clear framework of how the city should develop, said Mr. Yaduveer.
He pointed out that Mysuru had already expanded well beyond the existing limits of the Mysuru City Corporation, with areas such as Bogadi, Kadakola and Koorgalli functioning as part of the city despite being outside the limits of the MCC. The question is not whether Mysuru should grow but what kind of city one would like Mysuru to be in the years ahead, Yaduveer  added.
The MP drew the attention to the situation in Bengaluru and said that the unbridled urbanization and development there surpassed any planning. and solutions were conceived as an afterthought.
“We should not allow Mysuru to repeat the mistakes of Bengaluru’’, he said, stressing the need to provide facilities to citizens without compromising the city’s character.
Pointing out that Mysuru’s economic growth rate was relatively modest, the MP said planning should be realistic and aligned to the city’s strengths.
The MP pointed out that the opinions on Greater Mysuru were sharply divided, and one section was supportive of it mainly due to expectations of a steep hike in property rates. “We are not against Greater Mysuru or development. We are against growth that compromises heritage and culture of the city,” he said.
Mr.Yaduveer called for preserving the core heritage zone of Mysuru and said that it should be non-negotiable. ‘’City’s heritage buildings gave Mysuru a unique identity and must be conserved. Beyond a five-km radius, a clear strategy on industries and services — including IT that could work in tandem with Bengaluru, tourism infrastructure such as hotels, and the promotion of medical tourism etc, could be conceived’’, Mr.Yaduveer added
The MP reiterated opposition to the proposed flyover from Metropole Circle, warning that it would lead to the felling of hundreds of trees around Kukkarahalli Lake and mar the heritage ambience
He urged citizens to learn from Bengaluru and ascertain whether construction of flyovers in that city had helped reduce traffic congestion at all. “We do not need development for the sake of development,” he said.
Chamaraja MLA K. Harish Gowda said the concept of expanding MCC limits was meant to plan for future growth, but flagged serious concerns over finances and manpower. He raised questions about funding, recruitment of additional staff, and called for an analysis of the MCC’s revenue against its expenditure before taking any call on Greater Mysuru.
Former Chief Secretary A. Ravindra; Prof. N.K.Lokanath, Vice-Chancellor of the University of Mysore; Dr. Sushrutha Gowda of CR Trust, and others were present.

title: NEP-2020 key to achieve ‘Viksit Bharat’ and ‘Swarna Andhra’, says ABRSM member
summary: NEP-2020 is crucial for realizing ‘Viksit Bharat’ and ‘Swarna Andhra’ by enhancing employment and eradicating poverty, says ABRSM.
content:
The New National Education Policy (NEP)–2020 is playing a vital role in achieving the vision of ‘Viksit Bharat’ and ‘Swarna Andhra’ by creating employment opportunities and helping eliminate poverty, said Akhil Bhartiya Rashtriya Shaikshik Mahasangh (ABRSM) national secretary Guntha Lakshman.
He was speaking as the keynote speaker at the State Faculty Training (Prant Abhyas Varg) organised by ABRSM Andhra Pradesh at K.L. University in Vijayawada. Mr. Lakshman said that within five years of implementation, NEP has already begun delivering positive results and would yield even stronger outcomes in the coming years.
He stressed that India’s education system should evolve in line with the country’s culture, values, ethics and humanism, while integrating ancient Indian knowledge systems to help India emerge as a global knowledge leader. He noted that ABRSM has been conducting regular workshops to familiarise teachers with NEP reforms and added that the organisation represents nearly 15 lakh teachers nationwide.
The two-day workshop featured deliberations by CBI former Joint Director V.V. Lakshmi Narayana, APSCHE chairman K. Madhu Murthy, KL University Pro-Chancellor Rajashekhar Rao, Seetakanth of Ramakrishna Mission and senior RSS leaders.
During the programme, faculty members submitted a memorandum seeking resolution of issues including recruitment, promotions, salary payments and infrastructure. Prof. Madhu Murthy assured that the concerns would be taken up with the government.

title: Ambedkar Students’ Association seeks Parliament intervention over alleged roster violations at Central University of Karnataka
summary: Ambedkar Students’ Association urges Karnataka MPs to intervene in alleged roster violations affecting reservations at Central University of Karnataka.
content:
The Ambedkar Students’ Association (ASA) of the Central University of Karnataka (CUK) has written to all Members of Parliament from Karnataka, seeking their intervention over alleged large-scale violations of reservation norms and manipulation of the post-based roster in faculty and non-teaching recruitments at the university.
In a representation dated December 13, the students’ body alleged that the existing administration, under Vice-Chancellor Battu Satyanarayana, had altered the 200-point post-based reservation roster in violation of the government norms, thereby reducing opportunities for candidates from Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and Other Backward Classes.
The association said the CUK, the only central university in the State and located in the educationally backward district of Kalaburagi, was established to serve as an academic hub for marginalised regions. It alleged that the objective had, however, been undermined by “partisan administrative decisions” and deliberate roster manipulation to accommodate favoured candidates, seriously compromising social justice and institutional integrity.
According to the representation, more than 80 teaching posts across the ranks of professor, associate professor and assistant professor have already been filled using what it termed a “manipulated roster”. In addition, over 50 more posts have reportedly been notified on the basis of the same altered roster, the association claimed.
The students’ body contended that the alleged violations amounted to a denial of constitutionally guaranteed reservation rights under Articles 14, 16(4), 16(4A) and 335 of the Constitution, particularly affecting SC, ST and OBC communities.
Seeking immediate corrective action, the ASA has urged MPs to raise the matter in Parliament and press for a judicial inquiry or a Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) probe into the alleged irregularities. It has also demanded that all ongoing and proposed recruitment processes at the university be put on hold until a thorough investigation into the roster violations is completed.
A detailed note, along with 13 annexures, containing documentary evidence has been enclosed with the representation for examination and further action.

title: 10,700 cases settled at Lok Adalat in undivided West Godavari District
summary: Over 10,700 cases were settled during the National Lok Adalat in West Godavari, providing swift justice to litigants.
content:
As many as 10,798 cases were amicably settled during the National Lok Adalat held across the undivided West Godavari district on December 13, 2025, according to District Principal Judge and chairperson of the District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) Y.S. Sridevi.
The National Lok Adalat was organised under the directions of the National Legal Services Authority (NALSA), New Delhi, the Andhra Pradesh State Legal Services Authority, Amaravati, and the Administrative Judge for the undivided West Godavari district Justice D. Ramesh. The programme was conducted under the supervision of the District Legal Services Authority, Eluru.
A total of 34 Lok Adalat benches were constituted across the district to ensure smooth and effective disposal of cases. These included nine benches in Eluru, four each in Bhimavaram, Kovvur, and Narasapuram, three in Tanuku, four in Tadepalligudem, two in Jangareddygudem, and one bench each in Palakollu, Nidadavole, Chintalapudi, and Bhimadole.
Of the total cases settled, 10,351 were criminal cases, 153 motor accident claims (MACT) cases, and 294 civil cases. In addition, 238 pre-litigation cases were also resolved through mutual settlement, significantly reducing the burden on courts and providing speedy justice to litigants.
Giving a mandal-wise breakup, Ms. Sridevi said that 1,988 cases were settled in Eluru, 974 in Bhimavaram, 1,248 in Chintalapudi, 971 in Jangareddygudem, 1,092 in Kovvur, 434 in Narasapuram, 458 in Palakollu, 1,433 in Tadepalligudem, 1,082 in Tanuku, 919 in Nidadavole, and 153 in Bhimadole.
The District Legal Services Authority expressed gratitude to all those who contributed to the success of the National Lok Adalat, including judicial officers, advocates, police personnel, revenue staff, insurance officials, bank officials, chit fund representatives, labour department officials, municipal staff, BSNL officials, district panchayat staff, transport, excise and railway officials, advocate clerks, agriculture department officials, media representatives, and personnel from various other departments.
Ms. Y.S. Sridevi, Chairperson-cum-District Principal Judge, and K. Ratna Prasad, Secretary-cum-Senior Civil Judge of the District Legal Services Authority, appreciated the coordinated efforts of all stakeholders in ensuring the effective resolution of disputes through the Lok Adalat mechanism.

title: Maharashtra Cong chief Sapkal cites political links in Satara drug case, slams CM for 'silence'
summary: Maharashtra Congress chief Sapkal criticises CM Fadnavis for silence on Satara drug case and demands accountability for alleged political links.
content:
Maharashtra Congress president Harshwardhan Sapkal on Sunday (December 14, 2025) accused the Devendra Fadnavis Government of shielding those involved in drug manufacturing.
In a post on X, Mr. Sapkal stepped up his attack on the Mahayuti Government over the Satara drug case alleging it has failed to curb the drug menace and questioned whether the state was being pushed towards becoming drug-ridden.
Mumbai police had unearthed a mephedrone manufacturing unit in Satara district and seized contraband worth ₹115 crore. It had arrested three persons, all workers from West Bengal.
Mr. Sapkal sought to know how labourers from West Bengal were accommodated in a remote area and under whose assistance.
He also questioned the alleged role of one Omkar Dighe in the case.
Mr. Sapkal claimed Mr. Dighe had sought to use the premises, where drugs were manufactured, for work related to Shiv Sena corporator Prakash Shinde. Mr. Dighe was detained at the site but was later released due to political pressure, the Congress leader further alleged.
Since when had Dighe been residing in Savli village, and who facilitated his stay there, Mr. Sapkal sought to know.
He also demanded details about nearly 40 other labourers who were allegedly working at the site and whether anyone helped them flee.
Referring to the arrest of Vishal More with 2 kg of mephedrone, Mr. Sapkal said the former is the Pune student wing chief of the Ajit Pawar faction (of NCP).
Mr. Sapkal sought clarification on More’s alleged links with Dighe and Prakash Shinde.
Mr. Sapkal further questioned the movement of Prakash Shinde from Tejas Hotel following the arrest and asked whether police conducted a panchnama of the hotel.
Calling the incident serious, Mr. Sapkal criticised Chief Minister Fadnavis, who also holds the home portfolio, for remaining silent and demanded an immediate clarification from the government.
The Congress has accused the Maharashtra Government to trying to suppress the case.

title: Four months to go for the academic year to end, govt. yet to procure sanitary pads under the Shuchi scheme
summary: Despite the academic year ending soon, Karnataka's government delays supplying sanitary pads under the Shuchi scheme, impacting students' needs.
content:
There are only four months left for the completion of the academic year 2025-26. But the State government is yet to supply Shuchi kits (sanitary napkin kits) to adolescent girls aged 10 to 18 in government and aided schools, colleges and hostels under the menstrual hygiene programme, Shuchi. Tenders to procure these sanitary napkins are still under way.
The scheme, that was discontinued in 2020 during the pandemic, was resumed in January 2024, following a High Court order. Sanitary napkins were procured in 2024-25 without tenders after availing an exemption under Section 4G of the Karnataka Transparency in Public Procurements (KTPP) Act, 1999.
However, this year, the government has called tenders for procurement leading to a delay.
Responding to a question raised by Congress MLC Madhu G. Madegowda in the ongoing Legislature session, Minister for Health and Family Welfare Dinesh Gundu Rao said that the Cabinet had approved the distribution of sanitary pads under the Shuchi programme for the year 2025-26, and a tender had been called by Karnataka State Medical Supplies Corporation Limited (KSMSCL) for the procurement process.
Under the Shuchi scheme, the State government distributes 12 Shuchi Kits, each with 10 sanitary napkins, per year per student. The State government has identified 19,64,507 beneficiaries for the year 2025-26, and the scheme is expected to cost ₹71.83 crore this year.
Meanwhile, the Department provided sanitary pads for schools and colleges in July and August, 2025, from the pending stock of the procurement from the previous academic year, which is now over in most institutions, forcing students to buy sanitary napkins out of their own pockets.
“This year I only got sanitary pads twice in college. When I inquired recently, the college staff told me that the pads were out of stock. So, I am buying pads from my own money. The government should earnestly implement the schemes they announce,” said Ranjitha, a  student from Bengaluru.
All India Democratic Students’ Organisation (AIDSO) has criticised the inordinate delay in providing sanitary napkins to students. “This negligence highlights the contradictory attitude of the governments. On the one hand, the Union government champions slogans likeBeti Bachao, Beti Padhao, but fails to deliver essential support. On the other hand, the State government offers guarantee schemes, while simultaneously withdrawing basic necessities. We strongly condemn this anti-student attitude of the government,” said Apoorva C.M., Vice President, AIDSO, Karnataka.
With the State government not supplying sanitary pads to schools and colleges, many institutions have turned to non-governmental organisations (NGOs) to fill the gaps.
A headmaster of a government school in Laggere, Bengaluru, said that their school had over 150 adolescent girls, and the Shuchi kits provided by the Department of Health and Family Welfare in July were over. “A local donor purchased enough sanitary pads for all the girls in our school for a month. We have approached another NGO for pads next month,” he said.

title: Top officials shifted after Bilaspur accident report
summary: Top railway officials were transferred following a report revealing the loco pilot's unfitness linked to the Bilaspur train accident.
content:
The Ministry of Railways has transferred the Principal Chief Electrical Engineer of South East Central Railway (SECR), Rajiv Kumar Barnwal, and the Divisional Railway Manager, Bilaspur, Rajmal Khoiwal, in the aftermath of theBilaspur train accident.
The transfers came hours after the report of the Commissioner of Railway Safety (CRS) Brijesh Kumar Mishra, who investigated the circumstances that led to the tragic accident, was published inThe Hinduon December 11, 2025.
The accident took place on November 4, 2025 when a Mainline Electrical Multiple Unit (MEMU) train crossed the signal in danger and collided with a stationary goods train, leaving 12 people dead and 19 others injured near Bilaspur in Chhattisgarh.
In his report submitted to the Railway Board, Mr. Mishra said the loco pilot of the commuter train, who also died in the collision, had failed in the mandatory ‘aptitude’ test and was therefore not fit to operate the service.
The CRS also recommended that only loco pilots who had passed the aptitude test should be deployed to operate MEMU services.
He said the aptitude test assessed intelligence, memory, reaction time and personality traits, and warned that engaging loco pilots who had failed the test would compromise operational safety.
“Deploying loco pilots on MEMU services who have failed to perform against the above parameters will certainly hamper timely decision-making and reaction time during train operations. Loco Pilots should be deputed on MEMU services only after passing the aptitude test,” Mr. Mishra said in his report.
In SECR, of the 142 loco pilots required to operate MEMU services, only 102 had cleared the mandatory aptitude test, leaving a shortfall of 40. The CRS recommended that the Railway Board arrange additional manpower to address the deficit.
He flagged concerns over Signal Passed At Danger (SPAD) incidents. As many as 33 SPAD cases were reported in 2024-25, while six such incidents were recorded in the first two months of 2025-26. He recommended that assistant loco pilots be instructed to apply emergency brakes if a loco pilot crossed a signal at ‘red’ or exceeded prescribed speeds after passing a ‘yellow’ signal, to help contain SPAD occurrences.
Referring to the Indian Railway Medical Manual, Mr. Mishra said only a “zero” blood alcohol level was acceptable. However, during the inquiry, the Principal Chief Medical Director of the SECR stated that blood alcohol levels of up to 10 mg/dl were being treated as negative, citing metabolic factors that could cause such readings. In view of this, the CRS recommended that Indian Railways review the acceptable blood alcohol limits.
He further recommended that in the event of the death of any crew member involved in an accident, the railways should ensure that blood alcohol content is included in the post-mortem report to ascertain intoxication levels. These instructions, he said, should be incorporated into the Accident Manual and the Indian Railway Medical Manual to prevent lapses by Safety and Medical Department officials.
Mr. Mishra concluded the Bilaspur train accident occurred due to an “error in train working”.

title: Late-night waste dumping under scanner as BSWML deploys marshals on night patrol
summary: BSWML intensifies night patrols to combat late-night waste dumping, imposing fines to tackle littering in Bengaluru.
content:
In an effort to eliminate black spots, Bengaluru Solid Waste Management Limited (BSWML) has intensified its crackdown on littering by regularly deploying marshals for night patrols across the city. As part of a strategic plan, marshals are now intercepting offenders and imposing spot fines during nighttime, according to a BSWML source.
Karee Gowda, Chief Executive Officer, BSWML, toldThe Hinduthat marshals are being deployed regularly between 8 p.m. and 11 p.m. “We are collecting nearly ₹3 lakh to ₹5 lakh in fines every day as we strictly enforce the law by cracking down on littering,” he said.
Another BSWML source explained that in areas where the black spot problem persists, marshals extend their duty by an additional hour to catch more offenders.
“Many individuals who work late step out at midnight to dump garbage, which is why black spots continue to exist in some regions. In such areas, strict deployment of marshals is required, and we are ensuring that,” the official said.
However, residents in several areas blame BSWML for failing to collect waste on time. Earlier,The Hindureported on the irregular movement of waste collection vehicles in the Ejipura area. The problem still persists in Ejipura, with black spots visible in almost every cross. A similar situation exists in Suddaguntepalya and Tavarekere in south Bengaluru, areas with a large student population.
Dheeman Garg, a resident of 22nd Cross, Ejipura, lamented that garbage piles up near his house every week owing to the irregular timing of waste collection vehicles.
“There is no fixed timing here. Sometimes they come around 11.30 a.m. and at other times around 7.30 a.m. I leave home around 9 a.m. and return in the evening; when am I supposed to dispose of my garbage?” Mr. Garg said. “This is not just a problem on 22nd Cross, but across Ejipura. Every lane in this area greets people with garbage, and black spots extend for over 50 metres,” he added. He contended that irregular waste collection inevitably forces people to dispose of garbage in public spaces.
When asked about this, Mr. Gowda reaffirmed that immediate action would be taken against irregular garbage collection and urged residents to share details whenever such issues arise.
Apart from this, BSWML is also acting on complaints against habitual littering. Recently, a video showing a Ward 29 resident, identified as Sandeep, dumping three large bags of garbage from his car went viral, drawing the attention of BSWML. The agency traced him and imposed a fine of ₹5,000. Marshals are also tracing offenders by identifying houses through bills and other documents found in garbage piles.

title: Joined Congress due to YSR, not Harish Rao: Jagga Reddy
summary: Joined Congress due to YSR, not Harish Rao: Jagga Reddy
content:
Hyderabad
Senior Congress leader Jagga Reddy strongly refuted K. Kavitha’s claim that he had joined the party “due to personal anger against former minister Harish Rao”, and called the statement “false and misleading”. He said that he joined the Congress after being invited by former CM Y.S. Rajasekhara Reddy.
Addressing the media on Sunday, Mr. Jagga Reddy clarified that his decision to quit the TRS had no connection whatsoever with Mr. Harish Rao. “Harish Rao’s politics and my politics are entirely different. I neither left the party out of anger nor in opposition to him,” he asserted.
Taking a swipe at Ms. Kavitha, Mr. Jagga Reddy said that she rose in politics as KCR’s daughter, while he had built his political career independently. “Why am I being dragged unnecessarily into your internal disputes?” he asked.
Explaining the real reason behind his entry into the Congress, Mr. Jagga Reddy credited YSR, who was impressed by his political standing, and invited him to join the party promising major development initiatives, including an IIT and a four-lane highway for the region.
He said that political rivalry between him and Mr. Harish Rao had continued in the district, alleging that the latter attempted to politically corner him after the successful meeting of Rahul Gandhi in Sangareddy.
Stating that he believed in “direct politics”, Mr. Jagga Reddy said he was disturbed by certain recent developments but would reveal all details at an appropriate time. “I will speak in May. Once I take a decision, I never turn back,” he declared, adding that he was not interested in positions like campaign committee chairman.

title: Cantonment Railway Colony: With biodiversity heritage site tag withdrawn, activists feel 368 trees could be axed
summary: Activists warn that 368 trees at Bengaluru's Cantonment Railway Colony may be endangered after the biodiversity heritage site tag was revoked.
content:
With the State government withdrawing its earlier order to bestow biodiversity heritage site tag to the 8.61-acre Cantonment Railway Colony in Bengaluru, environmental activists fear that 368 trees in the colony could face the axe.
Activists said earth movers were brought on Sunday to expedite the construction work in the colony which is home to 50 different species of trees, some of which are more than 70 years old.
Mahesh Basapur of Parisarakkagi Naavu said that on Sunday morning when the activists visited the colony, they spotted earth movers and other equipment which he said was to commence construction activity.
He said that the work is being expedited by a private realty firm with plans to construct a business park on the premises.
“It is very unfortunate the state government has withdrawn its own notification on September 10 which declared the colony a Biodiversity Heritage Site. We have questioned the government why it has reversed its own decision within three months. However, we have not received any reply from them,“Mr. Basapur said.
He added that no tree has been felled in the colony and that those who were present on the site promised the activists that there were no such plans to cut down trees.
“They promised us that no trees will be felled but we are scared that they might do something in the night and we are appealing to the government to protect this lung space,” he added.
On December 6, a notification was issued that an earlier notification issued on September 10 was being withdrawn.
“The Government Notification No.: APG 187 ENV 2025, dated: 10.09.2025, declaring an 8.61 acre green area with 371 trees adjacent to the Railway Cantonment Station, Bengauru as a Biodiversity Heritage Site under the powers conferred under Section 37 of the Biological Diversity Act, 2002, is hereby withdrawn with immediate effect,” stated the December 6 notification.
On September 10, Environment Minister Eshwar Khandre announced that the Cantonment Railway Colony area, containing 371 trees from 50 different species, has been declared a biodiversity heritage site.
“The area also carries historic significance, as Mahatma Gandhi had interacted with freedom fighters here in 1920. The trees play a vital role in reducing carbon dioxide levels, curbing air and noise pollution, and preserving the city’s green cover,” he said then.
