Deputy Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary, standing behind Mr. Kumar, could be seen trying to stop the Chief Minister even as Health Minister Mangal Pandey and Principal Secretary to the Chief Minister Deepak Kumar could be seen laughing.
Sharing the 11-second clip, the RJD said, “What has happened to Nitishji? His mental state has now reached a completely pitiable condition, or has Nitish babu become 100% sanghi now?”
RJD spokesperson Ejaz Ahmed said, “The removal of the hijab from a Muslim woman’s face clearly reveals the NDA government’s attitude towards the Muslim community. Nitish Kumar is now engaged in the politics of appeasing the BJP and RSS. The Indian Constitution guarantees people of all religions the freedom to follow their religious traditions and customs.”
Earlier in August, Mr. Kumar had triggered a storm when he had refused to wear a skull cap at an event in a madrasa.
This is not the first time the Chief Minister had behaved strangely in public. A few months ago, he placed a flowerpot on the head of an IAS officer at a function. In January, he suddenly started clapping after paying floral tributes to Mahatma Gandhi on his 77th death anniversary. In March, he was seen laughing and talking to his Principal Secretary as the national anthem played out at a function. Last year in Darbhanga, Mr. Kumar attempted to touch the feet of Prime Minister Narendra Modi following which Opposition leaders called him a “helpless CM”.

title: Regularisation of Sada Bainamas faces hurdles as officials insist on affidavits
summary: Hurdles in sada bainama regularisation persist as officials demand affidavits, causing significant delays and complicating land transactions.
content:
The State government’s ambitious scheme for regularisation of sada bainamas, land transactions on plain paper, appears to have hit a major road block.
As against more than 9.2 lakh applications received for regularisation of the lands, a bare minimum of them are supposed to have been regularised till date almost a year after the passage of the Telangana Bhu Bharati (Record of Rights) Act, 2024 by the State Legislature. Insistence on the affidavits from the persons who sold the lands through sada bainamas by the officials concerned is said to be one of the major impediments in the regularisation process. Mismatch of the names of those who sold the lands decades ago and the names in the enjoyment column at present leading to software related problems is said to be another reason behind the delays in the process.
Unlike the BRS government, the Congress government made specific mention of sada bainamas in the Act incorporating Section 6 containing the provision for regularisation and rules were framed accordingly. However, Revenue officials at the ground level are said to be insisting on affidavits from the earlier owners who transferred the lands through sada bainamas in spite of such a provision not being part of the Record of Rights Act.
The clause of obtaining the affidavit has been included in the rules framed for regularisation of sada bainamas. Moreover, absence of written guidelines to the officials concerned entrusted with the regularisation of transactions on plain paper is resulting in different interpretations of the provisions resulting in inordinate delays as well as giving scope for alleged discretion in conducting the exercise.
Land Laws expert M. Sunil Kumar who was roped in by the government to give recommendations relating to Bhu Bharati Act, said officials can instead focus on conducting local enquiries and take up regularisation of the lands. He toldThe Hinduabout the process adopted in neighbouring Andhra Pradesh where the government has undertaken a resurvey of the lands and extended the last date for application of regularisation of sada bainamas till December 31, 2027.
In sharp contrast, there is no scope for receiving new applications in Telangana where the cut-off date for regularisation has been fixed as June 2, 2014 coinciding with the State Formation Day. There is no scope for receiving new applications even though sada bainamas regularisation was one of the major issues raised during the recent revenue sadassus.
He suggested that the government frame the rules afresh demarcating the roles of officials at different levels and addressing the minor irritants that are impeding regularisation of sada bainamas so that the process can be taken up effectively giving relief to land owners who had been deprived of the benefits of owning the lands.

title: Independent holds key to power in Shoranur municipality
summary: Although the LDF emerged as the single largest bloc by winning 17 seats in Shoranur, it still falls one seat short of a majority
content:
The position of a United Democratic Front-backed Independent could prove decisive in shaping the leadership of the Shoranur municipality for the next five years.
Although the Left Democratic Front (LDF) emerged as the single largest bloc by winning 17 seats in Shoranur, it still falls one seat short of a majority.
P. Nirmala, the UDF-backed Independent who narrowly defeated LDF’s T.P. Rajani by 20 votes in the Manjakkad ward, is set to be the decisive factor. The LDF has already begun efforts to win her support.
With 17 seats, the LDF emerged as the frontrunner, while the National Democratic Alliance (NDA) secured second place with 12 seats. The UDF managed only five seats, in addition to Ms. Nirmala’s seat.
The LDF is concerned that if the UDF and NDA extend their support to Ms. Nirmala, it could be relegated to the opposition in Shoranur. Negotiations along these lines are already underway.
Ms. Nirmala said that she intended to contest for the chairperson’s post. She could secure the position if backed by the UDF and NDA in their bid to keep the LDF out of power.
The CPI(M) leadership is making a determined effort to thwart the UDF-NDA initiative by attempting to bring Ms. Nirmala back into the LDF fold. She had previously served as the CPI(M)’s standing council chairperson in Shoranur municipality during the LDF’s rule from 2015 to 2020.
CPI(M) district committee member M.R. Murali said that Ms. Nirmala would be free to collaborate with the party. He said that no alternative options were considered.

title: Tezpur University stakeholders observe fast, demand V-C’s ouster
summary: Tezpur University stakeholders hold a hunger strike, demanding the ouster of Vice Chancellor Shambhu Nath Singh amid ongoing turmoil.
content:
Teachers, non-teaching staff, and students of north-central Assam’s Tezpur University observed a nine-hour hunger strike on Monday (December 15, 2025), demanding swift action from the Union Ministry of Education against“absconding” Vice Chancellor Shambhu Nath Singh.
TheCentral University has been in turmoil since September 22, when Mr. Singh allegedly disrespected Assamese cultural iconZubeen Garg, who died while swimming off an island in Singaporeon September 19. The incident opened the floodgates of accusations of corruption and mismanagement against him, apart from his absence from the campus for 388 days between April 2023 and September 2025.
“The stakeholders of the University observed a fast to demand an immediate response from the Ministry of Education, which has been ignoring our growing frustration over its continued silence despite the sustained agitation and repeated appeals for the ouster of the Vice-Chancellor,” a statement from the apex body of the agitating University associations said.
The stakeholders questioned the Ministry’s commitment to resolving the crisis in the university. “The responsibility of restoring academic and administrative normalcy lies with the Ministry,” they said, demanding a fair and unbiased high-level inquiry against Mr. Singh.

title: YSRCP’s signature campaign on PPP model of medical colleges a sham, alleges TDP leader
summary: TDP's Neelayapalem Vijay Kumar criticizes YSRCP's signature campaign against the PPP model for medical colleges as a sham.
content:
TDP spokesperson Neelayapalem Vijay Kumar challenged YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) president Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy to prove his claim of collecting one crore signatures against the PPP model of development of medical colleges. He alleged that YSRCP’s signature campaign a sham, and sought credibility on the signatures collected by the party leaders.
Addressing media persons at the TDP central office near Mangalagiri on Monday, Mr. Vijay Kumar said the YSRCP was opposing the PPP model in spite of a clear recommendation from the Central government and the Parliamentary Standing Committee. He alleged that Mr. Jagan Mohan Reddy did not want medical colleges to be established in the State.
He recalled that though the YSRCP government had announced 17 medical colleges, it failed to complete a majority of them, which pushed the projects into a limbo and caused a a lot of suffering to the students.

title: Four boys picked up for throwing stones at Vande Bharat
summary: Four boys arrested for damaging Vande Bharat Express windows with stones, prompting increased safety measures by the Railway Protection Force.
content:
The Railway Protection Force (RPF) of Vriddhachalam in Tiruchi Division has apprehended four boys in connection with the stone throwing on the Chennai Egmore-Tirunelveli Vande Bharat Express on Sunday evening which caused damage to the glass windows of six coaches.  The incident was reported between Vriddhachalam and Talanallur railway stations.
Preliminary inquiry had revealed that a group of boys which was walking alongside the track had thrown stones at the train causing damage to the glass windows of coaches C5, C6, C7, E2 and C18.  There were no injuries to any passenger as ascertained by the inspection of the coaches and interaction with passengers by the railway officials at Tiruchi railway junction.
The RPF pursued the culprits in nearby villages and apprehended four boys who were later sent to a juvenile home, said a press release from the Chief Public Relations Officer, Southern Railway M. Senthamil Selvan on Monday.  Stone pelting on trains is a criminal offence under Sections 153 and 154 of the Railway Act, 1989.
In addition to stepping up vigil, the RPF was organising awareness drives at locations of such incidents as well as in the nearby areas, including schools and villages, to discourage miscreants from indulging in acts that endanger the safety of train operations, the release added.

title: Seeking development, NK activists threaten fast-unto-death from Jan. 1
summary: North Karnataka activists threaten a fast-unto-death from January 1 if their development demands are unmet by December 31.
content:
Members of Uttara Karnataka Agitation Committee have threatened to start a fast-unto-death if their demands for comprehensive development of North Karnataka are not met by January 1.
They have submitted a list of demands to the State government.
Nagesh Golashetty, Nagaraj Kallukutigar and others of the committee told reporters in Belagavi on Tuesday that they are setting a deadline of December 31, for the State government to fulfil their demands.
Their main demands include focused development of north-east and north-west Karnataka, declaration of Belagavi as the second capital, transfer of secretary-level officers to Suvarna Soudha and setting up of a Secretariat for Kittur Karnataka development.
Mr. Golashetty complained that a majority of the 97 legislators from North Karnataka have not participated in the discussion related to the development of the region.

title: BJP names Piyush Goyal in-charge of T.N. polls, Panda for Assam
summary: BJP appoints Piyush Goyal for Tamil Nadu polls and Baijayant Panda for Assam, enhancing campaign leadership ahead of elections.
content:
The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) on Monday (December 15, 2025) madeUnion Minister Piyush Goyal the poll in-charge of Tamil Naduand put Lok Sabha MP Baijayant Panda in charge of its campaign in Assam.
An earlier notification had said that Mr. Panda would handle Tamil Nadu, but he has been replaced by Mr. Goyal and given charge of Assam, where he had been the in-charge during the 2021 polls. Mr. Goyal has experience in handling Tamil Nadu having facilitated the BJP-AIADMK alliance before the 2019 elections.
Union Ministers Arjun Ram Meghwal and Muralidhar Mohol have been appointed as co-in-charge with Mr. Goyal. Sunil Kumar Sharma, Leader of Opposition in the Jammu & Kashmir Assembly, and Darshana Ben Jardosh, former Union Minister, are co-in-charge of Assam.

title: BBP imports eight black-capped capuchin monkeys from South Africa
summary: BBP imports eight black-capped capuchin monkeys from South Africa, ensuring compliance with all regulatory requirements and health checks.
content:
The Bannerghatta Biological Park (BBP) has imported eight black-capped capuchin monkeys (Sapajus apella) from the Induna Primate and Parrot Park in South Africa under an animal exchange programme.
The eight capuchin monkeys, which includes four male and four females, arrived at the Kempegowda International Airport (KIA) on Sunday.
The capuchins have been kept in a designated quarantine facility and will undergo post-import health checks before being moved to the zoo premises.
The BBP said that the import was carried out in strict compliance with all statutory and regulatory requirements.
Prior approvals were obtained from the Central Zoo Authority, New Delhi, along with No Objection Certificates (NOCs) from the State Chief Wildlife Warden, Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying and Wildlife Crime Control Bureau.
It added that import permits were also obtained from the Directorate of Foreign Trade as per the guidelines prescribed by the Department of Animal Husbandry.
BBP said that all animals were inspected and quarantined in South Africa in accordance with the guidelines prescribed by the Department of Animal Husbandry and NoC’s were obtained from the Animal Quarantine Services before importation.

title: HC grants Rahul Mamkoothatil interim protection from arrest till Thursday
summary: Kerala High Court extends Rahul Mamkootathil's interim arrest protection as government challenges his anticipatory bail in a rape case.
content:
The Kerala High Court on Monday extended till Thursday the interim protection from arrest to expelled Congress leader Rahul Mamkootathil, MLA, who had been charged with rape and forced abortion.
A case in this regard had been registered by Nemom Police, Thiruvananthapuram. A Bench of Justice K. Babu posted the matter for hearing on Thursday.
Mr. Mamkootathil had approached the High Court with an anticipatory bail plea, earlier this month. In the bail plea, he claimed that there was admittedly a consensual relationship with the woman who levelled the rape and forced abortion allegations. He approached the court with the anticipatory bail plea after the Principal Sessions Judge, Thiruvananthapuram, dismissed his bail petition.
He had contended that his political opponents wanted to cash in on the situation, in view of the local body polls (that concluded on December 11). The allegation of miscarriage and forced abortion is false, he said in his plea.
Meanwhile, the State government on Monday approached the High Court, challenging the anticipatory bail that the Principal Sessions Judge, Thiruvananthapuram, had granted him in a second rape case he had been charged with. A Bench of Justice Viju Abraham then granted time to Mr. Mamkootathil to file objections against the government’s plea and posted the matter for hearing after after the court’s impending vacation.
As per the alleged victim, a woman studying outside Kerala, Mr. Mamkootathil contacted her through messaging app Telegram, gave her false assurance of marriage and took her to an isolated home stay-like building when she was assaulted and raped, causing her grievous injuries. The court had granted him bail, citing absence of prima facie materials linking him to the alleged offence.
The government approached the High Court, contending that the trial court failed to appreciate the gravity of the allegations and the materials collected during the probe, which it said established his role in the non-bailable offence.

title: Rails users pitch for increasing frequency of trains to Kashi from T.N.
summary: Rail users urge increased train frequency between Varanasi and Tamil Nadu to accommodate rising spiritual tourism and pilgrim traffic.
content:
Train travellers here have urged the Railways to approve a proposal to increase the frequency of train services between Varanasi and the central/southern parts of Tamil Nadu, in view of the rising spiritual tourist traffic to Kashi.
The Varanasi Railway Division has proposed an increase in the frequency of train services between Varanasi and Tamil Nadu, sources in the division toldThe Hindu.
A senior official in Varanasi Division confirmed that a proposal had been forwarded to the Railway headquarters for increasing the frequency of the Banaras-Rameswaram-Banaras (22535/22536) Weekly Express.
“Given the high demand on the section, we have proposed to the headquarters an increase in frequency of the train. We have the capacity at Varanasi to handle the additional frequency. We are hopeful that the proposal will be approved soon,” said a senior official in Varanasi Division, indicating that the train could initially be made a bi-weekly service.
A commercial survey has been done indicating the passenger traffic potential.  Depending on theen routecapacity and acceptance by other divisions, the frequency of the train could be increased gradually, the officer said and added that discussions had been held on the need to increase train services to South India from Varanasi.
Rail users here have long been demanding an increase in frequency of services between  Tamil Nadu and Kashi. “There is heavy demand and a need for more trains to Varanasi from Tamil Nadu. The Rameswaram-Banaras Weekly Express and the Kanniyakumari-Banaras Kasi Tamil Sangamam Weekly Express trains are highly insufficient,” says A. Giri, secretary, Thanjavur District Railway Users’ Association.
Since the trains connects holy places of Hindu religion and pass through major pilgrim centres in Tamil Nadu, they have good patronage. Despite good occupancy, these trains continue to be operated as weekly services. There are not many convenient trains from Chennai too for people from the south and central Tamil Nadu, he said.
“Normally, pilgrims of Southern states start the holy Kashi Yatra from Rameswaram and reach Varanasi. After performing rituals and visiting temples in and around Kasi, they return to Rameswaram to complete the yatra. Likewise, pilgrims from North India visit Rameswaram,” Mr. Giri said.
Further, a large number of pilgrims visit the navagraha temples in Tamil Nadu. The Masi Maham festival every year and Mahamaham, celebrated once every 12 years, in Kumbakonam also attract large number of religious pilgrims from north India, he said justifying the demand for increasing train services.
Besides, both the trains run on the same days on Tiruchi-Varanasi/Varanasi-Tiruchi section and not convenient for passengers to schedule their journey for travelling up by one and return by the other.
The association had sent representations to the Prime Minister and Railway Minister about two years ago demanding that the Banaras-Rameswaram-Banaras Express be made a tri-weekly service.
With the Prime Minister Narendra Modi scheduled to attend the valediction of the fourth edition of Kashi Tamil Sangamam in Rameswaram soon, rail users hope the Railways would firm up its plans to increase the frequency of services on the section soon and announce it during the visit.

title: Kerala local body polls: Model Code of Conduct withdrawn
summary: MCC to remain in places where special elections are scheduled following death of candidates
content:
The Model Code of Conduct (MCC) has been withdrawn with effect from Monday (December 15) in Kerala.
The MCC will, however, remain effective in the whole of the Moothedam grama panchayat in Malappuram and the Pambakuda grama panchayat in Ernakulam district and within the Vizhinjam ward of Thiruvananthapuram Corporation where special elections are to be held following the death of candidates, the State Election Commission (SEC) said.
The MCC had come into force in the State following the November 10 announcement of the 2025 local body elections. But elections were later postponed in three wards including Vizhinjam following the deaths of candidates. The panchayat wards are Payimbadam in Moothedam panchayat and Onakkoor in Pambakkuda panchayat.
State Election Commissioner A. Shajahan said on Monday that the SEC was able to conduct the 2025 local body elections in a “transparent, impartial and peaceful” manner in the State.
He pointed out that a mammoth exercise that began with the delimitation of local body wards, and progressed to the multiple revisions of the electoral rolls  had culminated in the two-phased elections held on December 9 and 11 and the counting of votes on December 13. Mr. Shajahan attributed the success of these exercises to the cooperation extended by the voters, political parties, election officials, various government agencies and departments, district administrations and local self government institutions.

title: Nitin Nabin takes charge as BJP working president
summary: Nitin Nabin assumes BJP working president role, facing upcoming Assembly elections in multiple states amid generational leadership changes.
content:
BJP’s new national working president Nitin Nabintook charge on Monday (December 15, 2025) at the party’s headquarters in New Delhi in the presence of senior leaders, including Union Home Minister Amit Shah, party president and Minister J.P. Nadda, and Ministers Piyush Goyal and Dharmendra Pradhan among others.
Before leaving Bihar, Mr. Nabin visited the Mahavir temple in Patna and offered homage at the statue of his father, the late BJP leader Nabin Kishore Prasad Sinha at a park in the city.
“I have always worked on the ideas of my father, who considered the party as his mother and prioritised the nation over everything. I think that is the reason the party has blessed me with this opportunity to continue working with BJP workers,” he said. He expressed confidence over the BJP’s prospects in the coming Assembly polls in West Bengal, Assam, Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Puducherry.
Mr. Nabin’s elevation as possibly the youngest ever BJP president at 45 years of age took many by surprise even as it has ended more than 18 months of suspense over who would replace Mr. Nadda at the helm of affairs in the party. The generational shift effected by this move comes after nearly a decade of such changes being made in the BJP at the block, mandal and district levels, to reduce the average age of the office-bearers of the party to below 50. Even before the formal election of Mr. Nadda, this push was made before 2020, as a result of which nearly all the 700 district presidents of the party had been chosen from party men and women among below 50 years of age.
Mr. Nabin’s immediate challenges, after his formal election as BJP’s national president, would be to face the Assembly elections due in West Bengal, Assam, Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Puducherry. But a more delicate balancing act would be the putting together of his new team, whether he continues this trend of a generational change in his choice of office-bearers at the national level or opts for more senior colleagues.

title: Need seen for extensive use of AI to improve quality of education
summary: Karnataka's education leaders emphasize the vital role of AI in enhancing academic quality at a responsible AI conference.
content:
There is a need for extensive use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) to improve academic standards, vice-chairman of Karnataka State Higher Education Council (KSHEC) S.R. Niranjana has said.
He was inaugurating an International Conference on “Responsible Artificial Intelligence” organised at Karnatak University in Dharwad on Monday.
The Department of Computer Science of Karnatak University has organised the international conference in association with Cardiff Metropolitan University, Canara Engineering College, KLE Technological University, Mangalore University, University of Wales, Presidency University and P.M. USHA.
Prof. Niranjana said that the education system has developed from gurukul system to artificial intelligence (AI) and now, there is a need for giving priority to skill-based education.
“In order to excel at the global level, students should not only have thorough knowledge of their domain but also have an understanding of other fields,” he said.
Prof. Niranjana said that post-Independence, food, communication and poverty have become a challenge and these have been addressed through the adaptation of technology and through revolutions in various sectors.
Only through social and economic development India can reach the target of Viksit Bharat, he said.
Vice-Chancellor of Mangalore University P.L. Dharma said that Artificial Intelligence, which is a fruit of human intelligence, has spread its tentacles to every field. Now, it is time for the universities to build academic relationship with other universities and make efforts for further improvement in academics, he added.
Vice-Chancellor of Davangere University B.D. Kumbar warned students against the excessive use of AI as it will adversely affect the human thinking capacity.
Director of Indian Institute of Information Technology, Dharwad, Mahadev Prasanna said that AI has now taken the shape of an industry. This has resulted in its extensive use in various fields.
Presiding over the inaugural ceremony, Vice-Chancellor of Karnatak University A.M. Khan emphasised the need for proper use of AI for building a health society.
Aghnesh Anupam of Cardiff Metropolitan University, Karnatak University Registrar (Evaluation) N.Y. Mattihal, Head of Computer Science Department Sridevi, Vijaykumar Gurani and others were present.

title: Lokesh to launch India’s first AAD Educity at Bhogapuram
summary: Nara Lokesh to launch India's first AAD Educity in Bhogapuram, creating a hub for aviation, aerospace, and defense education.
content:
IT and Human Resources Development (HRD) Minister Nara Lokesh will launch the GMR MANSAS Educity Project coming up at Bhogapuram on Tuesday (December 16, 2025). This initiatve is part of the State government’s plan to establish the country’s first Aviation, Aerospace, Defence (AAD) educational city.
According to an official release, the aviation, aerospace and defence sectors in India are developing at a rapid pace. Passenger footfall is projected to reach 700 million across the 200 airports in the country. Similarly, the aerospace and defence market, valued at ₹28.7 billion in 2024 is expected to touch $57 billiion by 2034.
The release highlighted the shortage of pilots and aircraft maintenance engineers, including shortage of advance courses in arospace design, sustainable aviation, and AI/cyber security. Presently, only 8,000 aerospace engineers graduate annually just 0.5% of the total engineering graduades in the country.
The AAD Education City in Bhogapuram will be India’s first integrated education and innovation hub for the sector. Officials said that renowned universities will be set up within the City along with International branch campuses of these renowned universities.

title: IFFK 2025: Fazil Razak’s Moham is an antidote to films celebrating toxicity
summary: Explore Fazil Razak's "Moham," a poignant film addressing toxic relationships and mental health at IFFK 2025.
content:
In the grainy, nostalgia-laden opening sequence of Fazil Razak’s sophomore filmMoham(Desire), a young girl looks longingly at a motorcycle. Minutes later, when the scene cuts to a present day image of a grown up woman gazing similarly at a scooter parked in front of a house and later slowly walking away with it, one wonders where the filmmaker is intending to take us. The feeling remains the same, in a good way, as the film’s themes slowly unravel.
Only well into the meaty centre ofMoham, being screened in the Malayalam Cinema Today category at the 30th International Film Festival of Kerala, does it reveal its true colours and intentions. Portraying the oppressive and corrosive nature of toxic relationships and the toll that the violence takes on women who are at the receiving end of it, as well as the men, appears to be one of the filmmaker’s concerns.
He has clearly drawn inspiration from the frequent reports of spurned lovers taking the path of violence. Razak’s viewpoint towards the issue is uncommon and even unfashionable in an era in which films likeArjun ReddyandAnimalare celebrated. At the centre of the story is Amala, a woman facing mental health issues and Shanu, a violent troublemaker, who is itching for revenge against the woman who broke up with him due to his overbearing nature. Catalysing the unlikely coming together of the two characters from disparate backgrounds is a stolen motorcycle.
As Amala walks around on the streets in lazy abandon when her mother is away on work, one wonders whether she would be safe enough considering her mental state. The meeting with Shanu compounds these fears, as he begins to use her to execute his nefarious schemes. But Razak mines some effective humour out of these seemingly dark and sombre situations, pulling off a careful balancing act which keeps the film ticking and engaging all through its close to two-hour runtime.
Later, the unlikely duo’s encounters appear to be mere distractions, as Razak’s aims are broader. The placement and timing of a flashback sequence, which throws more light on Amala’s past, is perhaps one of the reasons for the way the film works as it does. It comes out of nowhere, suddenly making us feel the enormity of her and her mother’s struggles. As an aside, the sequence also tells us why Amala eats only chapatis.
Razak’s debut filmThadavu, which premiered at the 2023 edition of the IFFK, and which went on to win Best Debut Director awards at the IFFK as well as the Kerala State Film Awards, was noted for its complex character sketches and life situations not very commonly seen even in Malayalam independent cinema. Beena R. Chandran, who won the State Film Award last year for the Best Actor (Female) forThadavu, appears to have walked intoMohamfromThadavu, for both are struggling women, at whom life throws one punishing challenge after another. Yet, both these characters seem to have an unending reserve of strength and positivity.
Fazil Razak’s Moham is an antidote to films celebrating toxicity.

title: State intensifying energy conservation initiatives across all sectors, says AP-Genco MD
summary: AP-Genco MD S. Nagalakshmi launches National Energy Conservation Week-2025, promoting sustainability and energy efficiency across Andhra Pradesh.
content:
AP-Genco Managing Director and State Energy Conservation Mission (SECM) CEO S. Nagalakshmi launched the National Energy Conservation Week-2025 celebrations by flagging off an awareness rally from the District Collector’s camp office to IGMC Stadium, here on Monday.
On the occasion, Ms. Nagalakshmi stated that energy conservation, energy efficiency and clean energy generation were cost-effective tools that help in securing a sustainable future, and called upon the citizens, especially students, to become active stakeholders in the State’s clean energy transition. She highlighted that every unit of energy saved contributed directly to climate action, economic savings, and energy security.
She said that Andhra Pradesh was intensifying energy conservation and energy efficiency initiatives across all sectors, including industry, buildings, institutions, and households. During an interaction with students, she stressed the importance of LED lighting, BLDC fans, star-rated appliances, and the growing adoption of rooftop solar systems and electric vehicles.
AP-Transco Joint MD G. Surya Sai Praveen Chand, CPDCL CMD P. Pulla Reddy, NREDCAP Vice-Chairman and MD M. Kamalakar Babu and senior officials of power utilities took part in the event.

title: Model autism complexes to come up in all 14 districts: Minister
summary: Facilities to be set up under the STARS (Strengthening Teaching-Learning and Results for States) scheme
content:
Model autism complexes, with modern facilities, will be set up in all 14 districts under the STARS (Strengthening Teaching-Learning and Results for States) scheme, Minister for General Education V. Sivankutty has said.
At a press conference here on Monday, the Minister said ₹2.75 crore had been set aside for each autism complex.
Subject minimum will be implemented this year in Classes V to IX. It would also implemented in the SSLC examinations in 2027.
The government had sanctioned 12-day Christmas vacations this year, instead of nine.
Distribution of Braille textbooks for Plus Two higher secondary students had been completed, the Minister said.

title: 2026 elections: UDF hints at keeping Sabarimala row at top of Opposition’s anti-govt. rhetoric
summary: UDF MPs have chosen to raise the theft in the Parliament
content:
The Congress-led United Democratic Front (UDF) on Monday signalled that it would keep the Sabarimala gold theft case at the top of the Opposition’s anti-government rhetoric into the 2026 Assembly polls, and perhaps beyond.
On the eve of the second phase of the local body polls, senior Congress leader Ramesh Chennithala had sought to highlight the scandal by seeking time to “reveal incriminating disclosures” to the High Court-appointed Special Investigation Team (SIT) probing the case. However, the SIT deferred his deposition to a later date.
On Monday, Mr. Chennithala stated that he had, on Sunday, given evidence to the SITpointing to a “global conspiracy” involving international gangs which trade in revered objects looted from religious places of worship for sale to wealthy collectors.
Mr. Chennithala’s interaction with the media came on a day when UDF MPs chose to raise the theft in the Parliament, prompting CPI(M) State secretary, M.V. Govindan, to accuse the Opposition of echoing the ideologies of Hindutva forces.
Mr. Chennithala told reporters that a non-resident Keralite businessman had approached him, stating he was willing to provide further information to the SIT about the crime. He said the industrialist was hesitant to approach the SIT independently and had sought his intervention.
Mr. Chennithala said the informant had expressed a willingness to give an official in-camera deposition. He said the businessperson claimed to have direct knowledge that the theft of gold artefacts from Sabarimala was the result of an entrenched conspiracy between Travancore Devaswom Board (TDB) officials, including political appointees and international rackets which trade in such valuable objects, including antiques.
Mr. Chennithala said that the CPI(M) was continuing to provide political protection to the two former Dewaswom Ministers, whose alleged involvement in the gold theft was evident. He reiterated that the SIT was yet to retrieve the stolen artefacts. He said the CPI(M) was fearful of taking action against the arrested former TDB president and ex-MLA, A Padmakumar, lest the suspect spill the beans on other leaders.
Mr. Chennithala ’s statement putting the CPI(M) firmly on the dock over the Sabarimala scandal came even as the CPI(M) State secretariat on Monday dismissed the contention that the scandal had cast a shadow over the just-concluded local body polls, with the LDF’s achievements in governance eclipsed by the religious and emotional overtones of the gold theft at Sabarimala.
On December 11, Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan, who spoke to reporters immediately after casting his vote, had said that the controversy over the gold theft at Sabarimala would not affect the elections because his government had taken a firm stand regarding the issue and had initiated appropriate action against those involved in the incident. However, on Monday, following the poor show by LDF in the local body polls, the State secretary of CPI, Binoy Viswam, told reporters that the Sabarimala scandal did indeed seem to have overshadowed the ruling front’s attempts to highlight its development and welfare initiatives.

title: MLAs from Malnad, coastal regions raise areca issue in Assembly, seek relief for growers
summary: Legislators from Malnad and coastal regions urge state support for areca growers impacted by crop diseases during Assembly session.
content:
The legislators representing the Malnad and coastal regions, cutting across party lines, have raised issues concerning the areca growers in the region multiple times during the Legislature Session being held in Belagavi. They have appealed to the State government to support the growers, who have been facing huge losses due to the diseases, particularly the leaf spot and yellow-leaf disease affecting the areca, a major commercial crop in the region.
Former Minister and Tirthahalli MLA Araga Jnanendra, Gurve Suresh Shetty, MLA for Kaup; Kiran Kumar Kodgi (of BJP), MLA for  Kundapur; T.D. Raje Gowda, MLA for Sringeri; Bheemanna T. Nayak, MLA for Sirsi; Ashok Kumar Rai, MLA for Puttur; and Basavaraju V. Shivaganga (of Congress), MLA for Channagiri, raised questions on the issue.
Areca is a prominent commercial crop of Karnataka, and annually 10.19 lakh tonnes of areca are grown. Due to the variations in the rain pattern and increase in the moisture content, the plantations in the Malnad region were affected by the leaf-spot disease.
S.S. Mallikarjun, Minister for Horticulture, in his written reply to the calling attention notice submitted by Mr. Jnanendra, stated that 25210.04 hectares in Chikkamagaluru district, 32,124.8 hectares in Shivamogga district, and 8,730 hectares in Uttara Kannada district had been affected by the leaf spot disease. More than 2 lakh growers had been affected.
The disease, a fungal infection, has brought down yield significantly in many farms. In some farms the yield has come down by 60%.
Nagaraj Adivappar, professor and head of the Areca Research Centre at Keladi Shivappa Nayaka University of Agricultural and Horticultural Science in Shivamogga, toldThe Hinduthat the disease causes spots on the leaves. “As the spots grow in size, the photosynthesis process is affected. Gradually, the yield comes down, causing loss to the grower,” the scientist said.
The effective remedy is nutrient management of the plants. “If the plants are healthy and strong, the impact of the disease is less. The measures to prevent the spread of the disease, by removing the affected leaves and having a proper drainage system to ensure that water does not stagnate in the farm, are essential. Besides that chemical treatment using fungicides is necessary,” he stated.
The State Government, in its budget for the year 2025-26, had earmarked ₹62 crore for the management of the disease.
However, now, the Horticulture Department has sent a proposal to the Centre under the Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture for the disease management, the Horticulture Minister said in his reply.
As per the recommendation of experts, the Minister said, a proposal for ₹577.76 crore had been sent to the Centre under the MIDH. The guidelines of the schemes suggest that the disease management would require ₹5,000 per hectare. The financial assistance, under the scheme, would be 30%, which would be 1,500 per hectare. And, each farmer would get the benefit for a maximum of two hecatres, he added.

title: State Election Commission issues guidelines for December 21 oath-taking of elected members
summary: The State Election Commission (SEC) has issued the guidelines for the oath-taking of newly-elected members and councillors of local bodies, with the ceremonies being scheduled for December 21.
content:
The State Election Commission (SEC) has issued the guidelines for the oath-taking of newly-elected members and councillors of local bodies, with the ceremonies being scheduled for December 21.
The most senior among the elected representatives must take the oath or affirmation first before an official nominated by the government.  In the case of Corporations and District Panchayats, the District Collectors are the nominated officers. The Returning Officers concerned are the nominated officers in the grama and block panchayats and specially-assigned Returning Officers in the case of Municipalities.
Thereafter, the most senior member will administer the oath or affirmation to the rest of the members.
In the three-tier panchayats and the municipal councils, the ceremonies will be held at 10 a.m. on December 21. The Corporations will host them at 11.30 a.m. on the same day.
After the ceremony, the firest meeting of the elected members will be chaired by the most senior member. The Secretary of the local body will read out the instructions regarding the election of the president and vice president - or Mayor, Deputy Mayor, Chairperson, Vice Chairperson as the case maybe - at this meeting.
All candidates who contested in the 2025 local body elections have been directed to submit their election expenditure to the SEC before January 12. The details are to be filed online by logging in on the election expenditure module on the SEC website www.sec.kerala.gov.in. Election rules require candidates to file their expenditures within 30 days of the announcement of the results, SEC said. Failure to do so can lead to disqualification from contesting the elections or continuing as an elected member for a period of five years. Submitting misleading information or expenditure in excess of the permitted amount also can lead to disqualification, the Commission said.

title: S.P. Balasubrahmanyam’s statue unveiled at Ravindra Bharathi in Hyderabad
summary: IT and Industries Minister D. Sridhar Babu unveiled the statue of legendary playback singer S.P. Balasubrahmanyam (SPB) at Ravindra Bharathi in Hyderabad on Monday.
content:
IT and Industries Minister D. Sridhar Babu, along with former Vice-President M. Venkaiah Naidu and former Haryana Governor Bandaru Dattatreya, unveiled the statue of legendary playback singer S.P. Balasubrahmanyam (SPB) at Ravindra Bharathi here on Monday.
Speaking at the ceremony, Mr. Sridhar Babu said that SPB, who rendered more than 40,000 songs in 14 Indian languages, demonstrating the universal appeal of music, had left an indelible mark on the history of Indian film music.
The Minister described him as an artiste who transcended linguistic and cultural boundaries, noting that SPB was not only an unparalleled playback singer but also a versatile actor, music composer and dubbing artiste. He observed that SPB’s singing was marked by natural expression and emotional depth, often giving the impression that the actors on screen were singing themselves.
Mr. Sridhar Babu added that SPB consistently encouraged young talent and embraced new musical trends while remaining rooted in discipline and humility. The statue, he said, symbolises a lasting tribute to Balasubrahmanyam’s artistic excellence and the values he embodied.
Reiterating the State government’s commitment to promoting art and culture, the Minister said efforts to honour and support artists would continue. The programme was attended by BJP State unit president N. Ramchander Rao and Balasubrahmanyam’s son S.P. Charan.

title: Two more convicted in Vizag espionage case
summary: Two more individuals are convicted in the Vizag espionage case, bringing total convictions to ten in the Pakistan-linked investigation.
content:
Two more accused were sentenced to imprisonment by the National Investigation Agency (NIA) special court in the Pakistan-linked Visakhapatnam Navy spying case, on Monday. So far, a total of 10 accused have been convicted by the court. The trial continues against the remaining five accused arrested by the NIA.
The two accused convicted are Somnath Sanjay Ikade of Ahmednagar district in Maharashtra, and Sonu Kumar of Hathras district in Uttar Pradesh. They were arrested in December 2019 from Karwar in Karnataka and Visakhapatnam respectively, according to the official NIA release. 
 
Each of the accused has been sentenced to Simple Imprisonment (SI) of 5 years, 11 months and 15 days under Section 18 of UA(P) Act and section 3 of the Official Secrets Act. The Special Court at Visakhapatnam has also imposed a fine of ₹5,000 each on the duo, who will have to undergo one year additional SI in case of default in payment of the fine.
 
 The case, which NIA took over from the Counter Intelligence Police Station of the AP police in December 2019, relates to spying at vital installations and Indian Navy establishments by foreign spies/agents. In June 2020, the NIA had chargesheeted 14 accused persons, followed by a supplementary chargesheet against one more accused person in March 2021.
 
 Investigations are ongoing as part of NIA’s efforts to expose the full conspiracy behind the espionage that was intended to disrupt India’s unity, integrity, security and sovereignty, the release said.

title: Drone tech contributing to national security, agriculture, smart city needs, says expert
summary: Expert highlights drone technology's impact on national security, agriculture, and smart cities during a national workshop in Nellore.
content:
Drone technology and the ongoing research is contributing significantly to national security, agricultural modernisation, and smart city development, said Dr. K. Krishna Naik, Department of ECE, Indian Institute Of Information Technology, Design and Manufacturing (IIITDM) Kurnool, while delivering a lecture at national-level workshop on ‘Drone technology’ here on Monday (December 15, 2025).
Addressing the students, Dr. Naik said that crop health analysis, water resource mapping, traffic monitoring, and border surveillance can be carried out at lower cost and in less time using drones. He emphasised that the students acquiring skills in drone hardware design, embedded systems, and communication protocols would find excellent opportunities in the industry.
He also stressed on the necessity of awareness regarding safety norms, DGCA (Directorate General of Civil Aviation) guidelines, flight permissions, and no-fly zones. “By aligning academic research with industry needs, students can explore not only job opportunities but also venture into start-up,” he added.
The week-long workshop is being organised under the aegis of the Department of Computer Science, Vikrama Simhapuri University (VSU) at its Kakatur campus. University Vice Chancellor Prof. Allam Srinivasa Rao said that in the present era of rapid technological advancement, the importance of drone technology is expanding day by day.
Keeping in view the upcoming Drone City at Kurnool, the Vice Chancellor directed the faculty of the Department of Computer Science to initiate M.Sc. programmes in ‘Drones and IoT’, with the objective of creating a skilled workforce capable of effectively utilising the emerging opportunities in this domain.

title: Former legislator publicly criticises CPI(M) leadership
summary: Former CPI(M) legislator K.C. Rajagopalan  on Monday launched a scathing attack on the party’s local leadership in Pathanamthitta following the party’s defeat in the Mezhuveli grama panchayat and the erosion of its majority in Ward 8.
content:
Former CPI(M) legislator K.C. Rajagopalan  on Monday launched a scathing attack on the party’s local leadership in Pathanamthitta following the party’s defeat in the Mezhuveli grama panchayat and the erosion of its majority in Ward 8.
Mr. Rajagopalan said he would submit a formal complaint to the party leadership against the Kozhencherry area secretary, alleging organisational lapses and a leadership style that, according to him, prioritised pleasing higher committees over maintaining grassroots connections.
He said he had expected to win Ward 8 of the local body with a comfortable margin, but alleged that multiple factors, including external interference, worked against him. Referring to the district conference held on December 30, 2024, Mr. Rajagopalan said he was removed from the district committee and claimed that celebrations were organised by party workers close to the area secretary on that occasion as well as after the LDF lost power in Mezhuveli.
“The party itself pulled the rug from under my feet,” he alleged, adding that there were interventions even from higher levels of the leadership. Mr. Rajagopalan said he suspected the role of the area secretary in the developments and questioned his competence.
He further alleged that the prevailing organisational culture within the party was one of appeasing leaders rather than engaging with people at the grassroots. He said he would raise all these issues in a written complaint, naming the area secretary, and submit it to the party leadership.

title: Govt. to introduce mobile app to save ryots’ waiting time in queues
summary: The government is launching a mobile app to streamline urea booking for farmers, reducing wait times and enhancing accessibility.
content:
HYDERABAD
The State government (Agriculture department) is planning to make available a mobile app to the farming community for simplifying urea distribution/sale form this Rabi season and it would be introduced on an experimental basis from December 20.
Through the app, farmers could book urea, the most sought after soil nutrient supplement from home from the dealer of their choice instead of waiting for long hours in serpentine quest for getting urea bags, which led to chaotic scenes across the State for most part of the Kharif season.
Minister for Agriculture Tummala Nageswara Rao made this announcement during a meeting on the Rabi plan for agriculture and horticulture departments here on Monday. He also instructed the authorities to educate the farming community on the adverse effects of excessive urea and other fertilizers use on human health and also the ill impact of stubble and other agricultural waste burning.
He stated that the mobile app was being introduced to save the valuable time of the farming community from wasting in queues at the fertilizer shops. The farmers could book urea based on his landholding through the mobile app not only with the nearest dealer but any other dealer of his choice within the district. They could also know the stock position.
After booking the fertilizer, the farmer concerned would get a booking ID on his mobile phone and based on that ID he/she could take the stock from the dealer with whom it is booked. A complaint redressal cell would also be made operational to resolve problems, if any, in urea booking through the mobile app, the Minister stated.
The app would have features to book urea only to farmers who raise crops that season to prevent its misuse since Telangana was among the top States in the country in urea use. The app would have separate login options for farmers/citizens, departmental officials and dealers.
After booking the urea on app based on the pattadar passbook number and the extent in which crops are raised in a particular season, the farmers would be issued a required quantity of urea bags in 1 to 4 phases in 15 days span. The farmers not having passbooks (tenants and others) could book urea with the help of their Aadhaar numbers.

title: Juvvaladinne to be developed as tourist destination, says Minister
summary: Minister announces plans to develop Juvvaladinne as a tourist destination while honoring Potti Sriramulu's legacy.
content:
Minister of Municipal Administration and Urban Development Ponguru Narayana said that Juvvaladinne village of Bogole mandal in SPSR Nellore district would be developed as a tourist destination, after offering tributes to Potti Sriramulu on his 73rd death anniversary at the memorial building, here on Monday.
More detailed discussions will be held with Chief Minister Nara Chandrababu Naidu after examining the location at field level, the Minister added. Speaking on the occasion, he said, “To mark the 58 days of his hunger strike, 6.8 acres have been allocated for the installation of a 58-foot statue within the CRDA limits in Amaravati and the work will be completed very soon.”
He said that Potti Sriramulu had laid the first step towards the formation of the States based on the language. Along with the Minister, Kavali MLA (Kavya) D.V. Krishna Reddy also paid homage to the statue of Potti Sriramulu in Juvvaladinne, which is close to Padamatipalli, the birthplace of freedom fighter known as ‘Amarajeevi’.
Meanwhile, State Social Welfare Minister Dola Sree Bala Veeranjaneya Swamy paid floral tributes to a statue of of Potti Sriramulu opposite the local CVN reading room in Ongole. “The Telugu State was born as a result of his sacrifice. He went on a hunger strike for 58 days demanding a separate State for all the people who spoke Telugu language,” he said on the occasion.
Prakasam District Collector P. Raja Babu, Santhanuthalapadu MLA B.N. Vijay Kumar, Giddaluru MLA Muthumula Ashok Reddy and other leaders also laid floral garlands on the statue and offered tributes.

title: LSG dept. to make temporary contract appointments
summary: LSG department in Kerala announces temporary contract appointments for various engineering and finance positions in urban local bodies.
content:
As part of measures to strengthen the activities of the urban local bodies of Kerala, the Local Self-Governments department has decided to make temporary contract appointments for one year in various posts.
The new temporary posts are Environmental Engineer (30 vacancies), Mechanical Engineer (30 vacancies), Electrical Engineer (22 vacancies), Hydrologist (22 vacancies), Public Health Engineer (22 vacancies), Accountant (Special Cadre- 22 vacancies), Finance Officer (Special Cadre-22 vacancies). The temporary appointments for one year will be in urban local bodies across the State. Details are available on the official website of the Local Self-Governments department lsgd.kerala.gov.in.

title: TTD to introduce QR codes, kiosks in its temples
summary: TTD plans to enhance digital convenience in temples with QR codes and kiosks for hassle-free offerings and payments.
content:
In a significant move to enhance digital convenience for pilgrims, the Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams (TTD) is contemplating installing kiosk machines and QR codes to facilitate UPI payments in all its 60 temples spread across various States in the country.
A decision to this effect was taken at a high-level review meeting chaired by TTD Executive Officer Anil Kumar Singhal on Monday at the TTD Administrative Building in Tirupati.
Directing officials to ensure seamless implementation, he said the initiative would enable devotees to make offerings and payments in a hassle-free manner, in line with modern digital practices. He also instructed them to collect structured feedback from devotees on TTD services at Tiruchanoor and the Tirupati Govindaraja Swamy temples.
Mr. Singhal asked the Chief Engineer to prepare two to three standardised templates for the proposed construction of 5,000 temples in backward regions so as to speed up execution and maintain uniformity. Stressing financial discipline, he directed that payments to contractors should not be delayed.
Reviewing the progress on the proposed temples at Belgavi in Karnataka and the allotment of land for the construction of the temple of Lord Venkateswara by the Bihar government in Patna, he directed the senior officials to also conduct field-level inspections of the Bandra temple in Mumbai.
On publications, he ordered the constitution of an expert committee to review the distribution of previously printed spiritual books and directed reprinting of high-demand titles based on readers’ preferences.

title: NIA charges four LeT-TRF terrorists, two locals in Pahalgam terror attack; conspiracy traced to Pakistan​​
summary: NIA charges seven in Pahalgam terror attack, linking conspiracy to Pakistan and identifying key terrorists involved.
content:
The National Investigation Agency (NIA) on Monday (December 15, 2025)charged seven personsin thePahalgam terror attack casein a Jammu court, including Pakistani handler and terrorist Sajid Jatt of the Pakistan-based Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) and The Resistance Front (TRF) terrorist organisations, and traced the conspiracy to Pakistan.
“Through a meticulous scientific probe spanning the past almost eight months, it had traced the conspiracy in the case to Pakistan, which has been unabatedly sponsoring terrorism against India,” an NIA spokesperson said.
The NIA invoked a penal Section of the law against the accused for “waging war against India”.
The 1,597-page charge sheet submitted to a special court named three Pakistani terrorists killed by Indian security forces during the action in Operation Mahadev at Dachigam, Srinagar, in July 2025. They were identified as Faisal Jatt alias Suleman Shah, Habeeb Tahir alias Jibran, and Hamza Afghani, besides Jatt.
Jatt is a Pakistani national from Kasur district in Pakistan’s Punjab. Officials said his original name is Habibullah Malik and he had many aliases, including Saifullah, Noomi, Numan, Langda, Ali Sajid, Usman Habib, and Shani.
The chargesheet details the conspiracy by Pakistan and the roles of the accused. “With supporting evidence in the case, [the NIA] has charged the banned LeT/TRF as a legal entity for its role in planning, facilitating, and executing the Pahalgam attack,” the NIA said.
The attack left 25 tourists and one local civilian dead.
The LeT and TRF, and the four accused terrorists, have been charged under relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023; the Arms Act, 1959; and the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967.
The NIA also chargesheeted two locals for allegedly harbouring terrorists. They were identified as Parvaiz Ahmad and Bashir Ahmad Jothad, who were arrested by the NIA on June 22, 2025.
“During interrogation, the two men had disclosed the identities of the three armed terrorists involved in the attack, and had also confirmed that they were Pakistani nationals affiliated to the proscribed LeT terror outfit,” the NIA said.

title: Medico killed, father injured in hit-and-run accident in Hayathnagar
summary: A hit-and-run in Hayathnagar kills a medical student and injures her father; police are investigating the incident.
content:
A 19-year-old medical student was killed and her father was injured in a hit-and-run road accident in Hayathnagar on Monday.
According to the police, Yamsani Pandu, 50, and his daughter Yamsani Aishwarya, 19, a second-year MBBS student studying in Mahbubnagar, were crossing the road near RTC Colony at around 7 a.m. Aishwarya was to board a bus to travel to her college when a car, bearing registration number TS 07 KG 9006, came at high speed from the LB Nagar side and hit them.
The car, allegedly driven rashly and negligently, did not stop after the collision and the driver fled the scene.
“Aishwarya suffered a severe head injury and died on the spot, while Pandu sustained a fracture to his left leg. He is undergoing treatment at a private hospital,” said an officer from the Hayathnagar Police.
Based on a complaint lodged by Mr. Pandu’s elder brother, Soma Venkatesham, the police have registered a case against the unknown driver. Efforts are on to identify the vehicle user and trace the driver involved in the accident.

title: Kooria calls for introspection in global history of law
summary: Historian Mahmood Kooria of the University of Edinburgh has urged scholars to rethink some of the most taken-for-granted assumptions that shape modern engagements with the premodern global history of law.
content:
Historian Mahmood Kooria of the University of Edinburgh has urged scholars to rethink some of the most taken-for-granted assumptions that shape modern engagements with the premodern global history of law.
Delivering the Prof. Scaria Zachariah Memorial Lecture at the Mahatma Gandhi University here on Monday, Dr. Kooria drew on examples from the Indian Ocean world and beyond to outline certain key perspectives that are essential for understanding law before modernity, especially when viewed against modern or modernist notions of legality.
According him,  ritual formed a central component of law in premodern societies, particularly within religious legal traditions such as Buddhism, Hinduism, Islam, Christianity, and Judaism, where law governed everyday life from worship to crime. He also  sought to challenge the idea of the State’s monopoly over law, noting that in many premodern contexts legal authority was dispersed among jurists, families, and communities. Law was often created and administered by jurists rather than rulers, making legal pluralism a useful, though limited, framework for understanding premodern legal orders.
He, at the same time, rejected the tendency to equate modernity with the rule of law, arguing that premodern societies possessed strong notions of justice and legal order. He also urged historians to treat legal texts as valuable sources for social history rather than dismissing them as purely doctrinal, since they offer insights into everyday conflicts and social relations. Dr. Kooria also stressed the importance of studying paratexts such as marginal notes, interlinear translations, and manuscript features, drawing on social codicology and new philology to better understand how law was transmitted, interpreted, and lived.
The session included memorial talk by Aju K. Narayanan and was chaired by Dineshan V.

title: ‘Koti Santhakala Sekarana’ material dispatched to YSRCP headquarters
summary: YSRCP launches signature campaign against medical college privatization, dispatching materials from Tirupati to mobilize public support.
content:
The YSRCP leaders flagged off a vehicle carrying the signature-campaign (Koti Santhakala Sekarana) material against the government’s alleged move to privatise medical colleges, at the undivided Chittoor district party office in Tirupati on Monday (December 15, 2025).
The campaign was taken up by the YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) across the State to mobilise public opinion against the alleged privatisation of government medical colleges in the State ‘in the garb of PPP mode’.
The party’s Regional Coordinator Peddireddy Ramachandra Reddy flagged off the vehicle in the presence of combined Chittoor district president Bhumana Karunakar Reddy, city Mayor B.R. Sireesha Yadav, former Minister R.K. Roja and youth wing’s State vice-president Bhumana Abhinay Reddy.

title: Court extends NIA custody of Delhi blast accused Soyab, Naseer Bilal, by four more days
summary: Delhi Court extends NIA custody of Delhi blast suspects Soyab and Naseer by four days amid tight security and media restrictions.
content:
A Delhi Court on Monday (December 15, 2025) extended the NIA custody ofDelhi bomb blast accused Soyab and Dr. NaseerBilal Malla for four more days.
The two were produced before the Principal and Sessions Judge Anju Bajaj Chandna, who allowed the probe agency to question Soyab and Naseer in its custody for four more days. Soyab, a Faridabad resident, and Dr. Naseer Bilal Malla, a resident of Jammu and Kashmir’s Baramulla district, were brought to the Court amid tight security on expiry of their previous custodies granted by the Court.
Media persons were barred from covering the proceedings. As per the probe by the NIA, the two had provided logistical support to Umar-un-Nabi before the Delhi terror bomb blast. They destroyed the evidence related tothe terrorist attack,the agency stated earlier on December 9, 2025.
Umar-un-Nabi allegedly drove the explosive-laden carthat detonated outside theRed Fort on November 10,killing 15 people and injuring several others.

title: Charging crisis sparks trouble for e-auto drivers in Kozhikode city
summary: E-rickshaw drivers in Kozhikode face operational challenges due to insufficient charging points, despite governmental promises for improved infrastructure.
content:
Hundreds of electric autorickshaw drivers in Kozhikode are facing operational difficulties owing to a shortage of public charging points. The issue remains largely unaddressed even as private and taxi vehicles are shifting from petrol and diesel to electric power, in line with the proposals of the Central and State governments to combat air pollution and reduce dependence on imported fuel.
Several lamppost-mounted charging points installed earlier by the Kerala State Electricity Board (KSEB) are non-functional. According to autorickshaw drivers’ union functionaries, fewer than 10 such charging points are presently usable in Kozhikode city, a number they say is far below actual requirements.
“There are close to 2,500 electric autorickshaws operating across Kozhikode city alone and the lack of accessible charging facilities affects daily operations and undermines the government’s stated goal of promoting pollution-free public transport,” says T.V. Noushad, an autorickshaw driver and functionary of the Kozhikode District Auto-Taxi Light Motor Workers’ Union. He points out that the memorandums submitted to the Electricity Minister and the Public Works Minister six months ago have received no response.
According to Mr. Noushad, the drivers’ unions approached the ministers directly following a recommendation from the KSEB citing technical issues they faced in opening new charging points. The project will become a reality only with the approval of the KSEB, which requires final clearance from the State government, he claims.
Drivers affiliated with various trade unions point out that the KSEB could easily utilise free spaces under flyovers to install new charging points. They say these locations provide secure spots for charging equipment and allow drivers to park without obstructing traffic or pedestrians.
K.B. Rjeevan, an autorickshaw driver from Pavangad, says many drivers opt for electric vehicles now believing assurances from the local authorities and the State government that adequate charging infrastructure will come up within a couple of years. Now, many are in a situation to cut short their trips, lacking the promised arrangements for several years.
The fear of running out of power on the road has also prompted a section of private vehicle owners to campaign for more accessible public charging points in the private or cooperative sector. Mahesh Chathoth, a tourism entrepreneur from Mavoor, says fully-equipped charging stations should be encouraged in private or cooperative sectors with government assistance to address the crisis. Though a few such charging stations are there in the State, the limited numbers show the need for better interventions, he adds.
Meanwhile, KSEB sources confirm that proposals for opening charging stations in 128 locations in Kerala have already been submitted under the Centre’s PM Electric Drive Revolution in Innovative Vehicle Enhancement Scheme. Such modern stations will also be equipped to cater to heavy trucks, they add.

title: Congress keen on one Assembly seat per district and share in power
summary: Congress aims for one Assembly seat per district in Tamil Nadu, seeking power share in the DMK alliance ahead of elections.
content:
The Tamil Nadu Congress Committee (TNCC) and All India Congress Committee (AICC) are reportedly on the same page regarding the need to push for a share in power and to seek not less than 38 seats (one seat per revenue district) as a part of the DMK alliance in the upcoming State Assembly election.
The strategy was discussed at a meeting in New Delhi in which AICC senior leaders, Congress Tamil Nadu MPs, AICC in charge for Tamil Nadu, Girish Chodankar, AICC secretaries, Suraj Hegde, Nivedith Alva, TNCC president K. Selvaperunthagai and State Congress Legislative Party leader, S. Rajeshkumar participated. The leaders also discussed scheduling of the visits of Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, Mallikarjun Kharge to Tamil Nadu and the campaign strategy.
Confirming this a senior leader, who attended the meeting, toldThe Hindu,“The feeling is that when Telugu Desam Party can let allies be a part of the government despite having a majority, why can’t the DMK do the same and include Congress as a part of the government?”
Despite the fact that the Congress seat sharing committee had already met the Chief Minister M.K. Stalin and other DMK leaders, doubts were cast over DMK-Congress alliance because of All India Professionals’ Congress chairman, Praveen Chakravarty’s meeting with Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam founder, Vijay.
Asked if this was discussed, a senior TNCC leader said, “The meeting (with Vijay) was not discussed. It doesn’t matter now. The DMK-Congress alliance is strong.”
Tamil Nadu Congress SC department head M.P. Ranjan Kumar on Sunday along with Chinnadurai, Devendiran, Ayyasamy, who are survivors of Dalit atrocities in Nanguneri, Thoothukudi and Manamadurai, met Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge.
“They apprised our Congress president of what they experienced and Kharge ji explained how he dealt with such instances and told them that only education will uplift them. He also assured them of all the help from the Congress party,” Mr Kumar said.

title: Winter comes calling early in Munnar, temperature drops to 3°C
summary: Munnar experiences an early winter with temperatures plunging to 3°C, attracting tourists ahead of the holiday season.
content:
The Munnar hill station in Idukki is witnessing an early arrival of winter, with the mercury dropping sharply. This year’s lowest temperature, 3°C, was recorded at the Chenduvarai tea estate under the Kanan Devan Hills Plantations (KDHP) on Monday morning. Frost was also recorded in the area.
The United Planters Association of South India (UPASI), a tea research foundation in Munnar, recorded the temperature of 3°C on Monday. The temperature in Letchmi Estate was 4°C and in Sevenmalai, 5°C.
The India Meteorological Department (IMD)-installed automatic weather station at Kundala near Munnar recorded its lowest temperature of 6°C. According to climate experts, Munnar is witnessing an early winter after 2018.
Climatologist Gopakumar Cholayil said that the temperature might move to subzero in the Christmas week. “Presently, the conditions are favourable for a chilly weather. Alerts for depression or heavy rain have not been issued so far. Hilly regions, including Munnar, will witness more temperature drops in the coming days,” said Mr. Cholayil.
Tourism stakeholders expect a surge of tourists to the hill station to enjoy the chilly weather in the coming days. “The IndiGo flight cancellations had initially affected the Christmas and New Year bookings to Munnar. Now the situation has changed, and we are receiving bookings and enquiries,” said a tourism stakeholder.
“Tourists, especially north Indians, are arriving in Munnar to enjoy the chill in December and January. We hope the early arrival of winter will attract more tourists,” he said.
The normal winter season starts in Munnar in November. Extreme cold is experienced in the first week of January usually with the valleys and hills covered with frost. But this year, the hill station is experiencing extreme cold from the second week of December itself.

title: ‘Suicide bid survivor’ wins sarpanch election
summary: A suicide bid survivor wins sarpanch election in Khammam, overcoming adversity to secure victory by 134 votes.
content:
A BRS functionary, who allegedly attempted suicide in September this year after recording a selfie video alleging harassment by some local Congress leaders, emerged winner as sarpanch in the gram panchayat elections in Khammam district.
The BRS-backed candidate B. Ravi of Suddavagu Thanda in Thirumalayapalem mandal emerged victorious, defeating his nearest opponent by a margin of 134 votes in the second phase of gram panchayat elections, the results of which were declared on Sunday night.
According to BRS sources, the ‘suicide bid survivor’ succeeded in his electoral debut with a positive outlook and self-confidence.
Roshini - Suicide Prevention Helpline numbers: 8142020033/44 and 040 66202000/2001.

title: Discussions on KC(M)’s return to UDF gather momentum once again
summary: Close on the heels of the Left Democratic Front’s stinging setback in the recent local body elections, speculation is ripe over the possibility of the Kerala Congress (M) returning to the United Democratic Front to strengthen the coalition ahead of the Assembly polls.
content:
Close on the heels of the Left Democratic Front’s stinging setback in the recent local body elections, speculation is ripe over the possibility of the Kerala Congress (M) returning to the United Democratic Front to strengthen the coalition ahead of the Assembly polls.
According to sources, the Congress has sent feelers to the KC(M), signalling that the party’s position within the LDF may be precarious, particularly after Central Travancore delivered a poor verdict for the Left in the local body polls.
A quick review of the Assembly constituencies in the region shows the LDF could maintain its lead in only three seats in Kottayam and one in Idukki. With Pala and Kanjirappally, long regarded as KC(M) strongholds, remaining the last pockets of the LDF in Kottayam, the UDF sees an opportunity to consolidate its gains by wooing the party led by Jose K Mani to its fold.
Within the UDF, however, opinions remain divided. The Indian Union Muslim League supports KC(M)’s inclusion, while the Kerala Congress led by P.J. Joseph has escalated its objection . “The KC(M) has lost its relevance. Our breakthrough in the local body elections does not depend on them. They have remained silent on LDF corruption issues, including the Sabarimala gold case,” remarked Mr. Joseph.
Inrestingly, Pala legislator Mani C. Kappen has softened his stance,  even expressing no objection to handing over the Pala seat to the KC(M) if the UDF decides. Leader of the Opposition V.D. Satheesan, in Kottayam on Monday, emphasised the coalition’s readiness but remained noncommittal on the KC(M): “The UDF will contest the Assembly polls with a strong base. We have neither pursued nor invited any party yet. Decisions will be taken at the right time,” he said.
KC(M) chairman Jose K. Mani has so far refused to alter alliances, stating that “winning and losing elections are part of politics. There is no question of changing alliances even after this defeat.” Yet, some within the party privately feel that remaining with the LDF may not be strategically advantageous in the upcoming elections.

title: Explain why you sat on files to prosecute two IAS officers, Madras High Court directs Public Secretary
summary: Madras High Court demands explanation from Public Secretary for delaying prosecution of IAS officers in ₹98.25 crore corruption case.
content:
The Madras High Court on Monday called for an explanation from the Public Secretary for having sat on the files, seeking sanction to prosecute two IAS officers in the ₹98.25 crore corporation contract irregularities case against former AIADMK Minister S.P. Velumani, from January 5, 2024 to August 30, 2025.
Justice N. Anand Venkatesh passed the orders after impleading the Public Secretarysuo motuas one of the respondents to a contempt of court petition filed by anti-corruption organisation Arappor Iyakkam against the investigating officers for having delayed the prosecution by a considerable number of years.
The judge impleaded the Vigilance Commissioner as well as the Director of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption as respondents and directed them to respond, by January 6, as to why they did not follow up the issue with the Public department and reminded the latter to send the files to the Centre for obtaining sanction.
Justice Venkatesh agreed with the petitioner’s counsel V. Suresh that the anti-corruption organisation had to knock on the doors of the court at every stage of the case, beginning from the lodging of the complaint, and obtain a direction to the police even to perform their statutory duties.
The court took note that the irregularities in the award of contracts had allegedly taken place in Chennai and Coimbatore municipal corporations when Mr. Velumani had served as the Municipal Administration Minister between 2014 and 2018. Thereafter, a First Information Report was registered against him and others in 2021.
Though nearly four years had lapsed since then, the trial against the accused had not commenced till now despite multiple petitions filed by Jayaram Venkatesan of Arappor Iyakkam for speeding up the process. Justice Venkatesh was now seized of a second contempt of court petition filed by the organisation.
While perusing the case papers, the judge found that the Vigilance Commissioner (in the rank of Additional Chief Secretary) had forwarded a recommendation to the Public Secretary on January 5, 2024 for obtaining sanction to prosecute the IAS officers K.S. Kandasamy and K. Vijaya Karthikeyan in connection with the case.
The recommendation was, however, kept in cold storage in the office of the Public department from January 5, 2024 and was forwarded to the Centre only on August 30, 2025. Expressing dismay over such a lethargic attitude when it comes to prosecuting IAS officers, the judge wanted to know if the delay was deliberate.
“The Prevention of Corruption Act cannot be confined to lower level staff such as Tahsildars, VAOs, RTOs and so on. If the system does not work with equal alacrity against Ministers, IAS officers and judges too, the people will lose faith in the system,” Justice Venkatesh told the DVAC officials present in the court hall.

title: Private hospital penalised for collecting excess money from NTR Vaidya Seva beneficiary
summary: Private hospital penalised for overcharging NTR Vaidya Seva beneficiary; ordered to refund excess fees and face strict regulations.
content:
A private hospital in Narasaraopet was penalised for illegally collecting money from a beneficiary under the Dr. NTR Vaidya Seva scheme. The Palnadu district administration imposed a penalty three times the excess amount and directed the hospital to refund the collected sum to the patient.
The action was taken during a District Disciplinary Committee meeting held at the Palnadu Collectorate on Monday under the chairmanship of Collector Kritika Shukla. The case pertained to a 2023 complaint, in which the hospital allegedly collected ₹23,000 as co-payment from a patient, in addition to the amount paid by the government under the scheme.
During the meeting, Dr. NTR Vaidya Seva District Coordinator Dr. G. Chandrasekhar placed details of complaints received under the scheme before the Collector and committee members. Taking a serious view on the violation, the Collector ordered that the penalty amount be deposited with the government and the illegally collected amount be returned to the patient.
Warning that any repetition of such violations would not be tolerated, the Collector directed all empanelled hospitals to strictly provide cashless treatment to Dr. NTR Vaidya Seva beneficiaries without collecting money or issuing bills. She also instructed hospital managements to take immediate corrective measures.

title: Phase II GP elections: Results declared for all 3,911 Sarpanch, 29,917 ward member posts
summary: Results of Telangana's Phase II GP elections reveal a diverse leadership with 3,911 Sarpanch and 29,917 ward member posts filled.
content:
The second phase of Gram Panchayat elections in Telangana concluded with results declared for every contesting post across the State, according to a report issued by the State Election Commission.
