Replying to member Jagadev Guttedar during Question Hour in the Council, the Home Minister said that as the process for providing internal reservation has been completed, the recruitment process has gained momentum.
And, with regard to the notification issued before the process of internal reservation was initiated, he said that recruitment of 947 police sub-inspectors was completed. Now, the selected candidates are undergoing training. This apart, 167 Home Guards have also been appointed, he said.
Replying to question from member Sharavana T.A., the Home Minister categorically stated that those policemen who are found guilty of conniving with criminals and indulging in crimes will be dismissed from service.
He mentioned that 88 police personnel and officers have been thus suspended, criminal cases have been registered against them and in some cases, they have been arrested also.
Considering the matter seriously, the senior officials in the department have been directed to monitor the functioning of police personnel and officers under them, he said and added that regular sensitization programmes are also being conducted.
Replying to member Keshav Prasad S., the Home Minister said that 6,768 cases have been registered under NDPS Act 1985 during 2023, 4,168 during 2024 and 5,930 during 2025, while drugs in all worth ₹484.21 crore have been seized since 2023.
Since 2023, nearly 300 foreign students involved in drug peddling have been deported.

title: Private bus operators told to follow safety norms
summary: Vizianagaram's Deputy Transport Commissioner urges private bus operators to comply with safety norms amid rising accident concerns.
content:
In the backdrop of accidents taking place in several parts of the State, Vizianagaram Deputy Transport Commissioner D. Mani Kumar on Thursday has urged private bus managements to strictly adhere to safety norms.
Speaking toThe Hindu, he said that the department has been conducting inspections periodically on the 27 private buses which operate from Vizianagaram to various other destinations.
He said: “A few buses were found violating safety norms, with sleeper berths set up at the emergency exits, while many buses lacked fire extinguishers and alarms. For those violating the norms, we have imposed fines and cautioned them that the department would seize their vehicles if the seating arrangement were not done in accordance to safety norms. "
Mr. Mani Kumar further added that inspections would also extend to college and school buses. Presently, random fitness tests are being conducted to ensure the safety of students.

title: Kishan Reddy accuses govt. of power sector mismanagement
summary: Kishan Reddy accuses govt. of power sector mismanagement
content:
Union Minister of Coal and Mines G. Kishan Reddy accused the Telangana Government of planning to raise fresh loans under the pretext of forming a new power distribution company without a clear roadmap to clear pending dues.
“Telangana’s power distribution companies have poor ratings. The government is trying to transfer ₹26,000 crore of GENCO - power generation company dues and another ₹9,000 crore loan to the new entity. Meanwhile, ₹47,000 crore remains unpaid to Singareni Collieries,” he said at a press conference in New Delhi on Thursday.
He warned that Singareni Collieries’ inability to contribute to the District Mineral Foundation (DMF) has affected welfare mesaures like providing clean drinking water, employment, and agriculture in mining-affected areas.
Mr. Kishan Reddy criticised the government for failing to support power utilities despite promises of attracting global investments at the recent Rising Telangana summit. The budget allocation is only ₹21,000 crore, most of it for free schemes. He noted that future power demand is projected at one lakh MW, but there is no infrastructure for generation and distribution.
The Minister also slammed the government for neglecting the renewable energy goals of generating 20,000 MW by 2030 and 40,000 MW by 2035. He questioned plans to set up private-sector plants, saying costs would burden consumers. Instead, he suggested a Power Purchase Agreement with NTPC, which has completed 1,600 MW plants at a cost of ₹11,000 crore and is ready to add 2,400 MW.
Highlighting Centre’s efforts, he said that under ‘Saubhagya Yojana’, 5.15 lakh households in Telangana received electricity connections, and under ‘UJALA’, 3.14 lakh LED tubelights and 28 lakh bulbs were supplied. A 100 MW NTPC floating plant is operational, and a 176 MW solar plant will be completed soon.

title: EV maker Olectra Greentech faces ₹2.58 cr penalty from TGIIC for delay in project completion
summary: EV maker Olectra Greentech faces ₹2.58 cr penalty from TGIIC for delay in project completion
content:
The Telangana Industrial Infrastructure Corporation (TGIIC) has imposed more than ₹2.57 crore penalty on electric vehicle maker Olectra Greentech for delay in completion of the greenfield EV manufacturing facility in Hyderabad.
A demand notice from TGIIC imposing a penalty of ₹2,57,87,484, including GST, for the period from November 12, 2023 to November 11, 2025, has been received. The penalty is due to the delay in the full completion of the ongoing construction of the facility at the Industrial Park, Seetharampur, Hyderabad, Olectra Greentech said in a filing on Thursday.
TGIIC has directed the company to remit the penalty amount within 7 days of receipt of the order. Olectra Greentech said as per the sale agreement dated November 11, 2021 with TGIIC, the company acquired 150 acres of land at the Industrial Park. In response to the company’s request for an extension of the timelines, for setting up of the facility and for issuance of the required no objection certificate (NOC) to obtain credit facilities against the property, TGIIC invoked the penalty clause set out in the sale agreement and levied the penalty for the delay in completing the construction.
The company, however, has already partially commenced commercial operations at the new facility within the timelines stipulated in the sale agreement, the Megha Group company said. Apart from the penalty amount, there is no material impact neither financially nor operationally for the company, it said.
Olectra is focussed on the electric bus and the e-truck segments. It has a technology tie-up with Chinese EV major BYD.
Senior executives had told investors last month that the greenfield plant has partially started operating and achieved a capacity of 2,500 vehicles per shift. The plant can reach a capacity of 5,000 if operated in two shifts, they said, adding that the market last year was 4,200 vehicles and expected to be about 6,000 vehicles. The company has the highest market share and positioned well, with the capacity available, to meet the market demand. The second phase of expansion will happen as the market grows.

title: Organ donation saves five lives in Kerala
summary: Divakar S. Rajesh's organ donation saves five lives in Kerala, highlighting the impact of generosity in times of loss.
content:
Divakar S. Rajesh, 53, who died at a private hospital here following cerebral haemorrhage, will now live through five others, who received organs from him.
Divakar, a tax consultant and a resident of Jawahar Nagar, Kowdiar, was admitted to a private hospital in the city on December 14 after he fainted. Following the confirmation of brainstem death on December 17, the family came forward to donate his organs.
The organ donation processes were arranged and coordinated by Kerala State Organ and Tissue Transplantation Organisation (K-SOTTO). One kidney and liver was received by a private hospital in the city and the other kidney was received by a private hospital at Kozhikode. Both corneas were transplanted in patients undergoing treatment at the Regional Institute of Ophthalmology.
Mr. Divakar is survived by his wife Aswathy Bose, an advocate and a daughter, a Plus Two student. The funeral rites will take place on Friday.
Health Minister Veena George conveyed her condolences and thanked the family for coming forward to donate organs which have given a new lease of life to five others.

title: Don’t overexploit Karnataka, Minister tells Centre
summary: Describing Karnataka as a goose that lays the golden eggs, Revenue Minister Krishna Byre Gowda on Thursday asked the Centre not to kill it by overexploiting it.
content:
Describing Karnataka as a goose that lays the golden eggs, Revenue Minister Krishna Byre Gowda on Thursday asked the Centre not to kill it by overexploiting it.
He made the remark in the Legislative Assembly when Leader of the Opposition R. Ashok expressed concern that the State was on the borderline of breaching the norms prescribing that revenue deficit should be below 3%, as presently the State’s revenue deficit stood around 2.95%.
Mr. Byre Gowda who piloted the Karnataka Appropriation (No. 3) Bill 2025, said the State’s stand was to ensure that its loans and revenue deficits were below 3% as prescribed by the Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act.
Launching a counter-attack on the BJP, the Minister said, “Around 20 States have never followed the FRBM Management Act as they have indulged in indiscriminate borrowings unlike Karnataka. But it’s ironical that Karnataka is being punished for its financial discipline and those States that did not stick to FRBM Act are being incentivsed by the Finance Commissions that has given more funds to them.”
He  told the Centre that it could get more funds in terms of taxes only if the golden goose was not overexploited.
The quantum of supplementary estimates of the State amounted to just 1.45% of the total budget size, he explained.
The Supplementary Estimates (Second Instalment) for 2025-26, aggregating to ₹ 6,279.87 crore, got the clearance from the House.
Mr. Byre Gowda said a sizeable part of this money would go to farmers. The need for seeking ₹ 1,015 crore had arisen due to the decision taken to provide an additional ₹8,500 per hectare as compensation towards crop losses in the kharif season, above that prescribed by SDRF, he said.
Similarly, ₹300 crore was needed to pay an incentive of ₹50 per tonne for sugarcane farmers as they demanded an increase in FRP, he added.

title: PESCE students win Smart India Hackathon
summary: PESCE students win Smart India Hackathon 2025 with an innovative project improving artificial limb comfort and precision.
content:
A team of students of P.E.S. College of Engineering (PESCE), Mandya, emerged as the overall winners in the hardware edition of Smart India Hackathon (SIH) 2025. The Smart India Hackathon is organised under the aegis of the Ministry of Education, Government of India, in collaboration with AICTE and the Ministry of Education’s Innovation Cell. The finale of SIH 2025 was held at Galgotias University this month.
The winning students include Ananya R. from Civil Engineering; Karan Dhandale from Electrical and Electronics Engineering; Swarna Diksha S. from Mechanical Engineering; R.M. Monith Surya from Robotics and Artificial Intelligence; Abhishek J.S. from Computer Science and Engineering and Nandan T. Nayak from Civil Engineering.
Out of 1.2 lakh teams from across the country who participated in the hackathon, 1,300 teams qualified for the final round. In the Healthcare and Prosthetics category, around 500 teams had registered, but only five teams reached the finals. Among them, the PESCE team secured the winning position, excelling in innovation, technical precision, and social relevance. The winning project focuses on a low-cost innovative technology to improve the comfort and precision fit of artificial limbs.
K. S. Vijayanand, president of People’s Education Trust (PET), Mandya, N.L. Muralikrishna, principal, Vinay S., vice-principal, and faculty members of PESCE congratulated the students.
Pavana K.N., coordinator of PES NEXT Innovation and Incubation Centre, and Shalvian John D’Souza, incubation manager (Infinity), provided technical guidance to students.

title: Orphans, differently abled children participate in semi-Christmas fete
summary: Orphans, differently abled children participate in semi-Christmas fete
content:
Over 100 orphaned and differently abled children from Jeevodaya Home participated in semi-Christmas celebrations at a luxury hotel in the city on Thursday.
The programme was facilitated by Dundra Kumara Swamy, chairman of Blissberg – Future of Hope (a social service organisation), and national president of BC Dal, where a special lunch was organised for the under-privileged children.
Dr. Nirmala Gudapati founder and chairperson of Sheep NGO, Jeevodaya Home for children, and representative of Aavasa Hotel, Sagar Raut, were present on the occasion.

title: Five babies rescued from trafficking gang, 10 arrested in A.P.
summary: Five babies rescued from a trafficking gang in A.P.; ten suspects arrested for selling infants to childless couples.
content:
The Task Force police, in association with the West and North Zone police, busted a child trafficking racket and arrested ten people in connection with the case. The police rescued five children from the gang and seized ₹3.3 lakh cash from the accused.
The police conducted simultaneous raids at different places under Bhavanipuram, Nunna and Kothapet police station limits and rescued the babies kept in the houses of the mediators, Police Commissioner S.V. Rajasekhar Babu told the media, here, on Thursday.
The gang allegedly trafficked the children from Delhi and Mumbai by paying ₹1 lakh and above for each. They had plans to sell away babies for ₹5 lakh each.
The accused have been identified Balagam Sarojini, Garikamukku Vijayalakshmi, Vadapalli Blessy, Shaik Baba Vali, Amadala Mani, Shaik Farheena, Shanka Yohan and P. Srinivas Rao and B. Kiran Kumar, all hailing from Vijayawada and Guntur districts, and Muktipeta Nandini of Hyderabad.
Sarojini, Vijayalakshmi, Mani and Farheena were arrested earlier in similar cases in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana and were on bail.
Explaining about the modus operandi of the gang, Mr. Rajasekhar Babu said the accused would identify childless couples and sell the trafficked children to them.
“We are trying to nab Kiran Sharma, Suri, Kavitha and Satish, who allegedly supplied babies to the gang,” Assistant Commissioners of Police K. Latha Kumari and N. V. Durga Rao said, who monitored the operations, said.

title: Sri City firm exports huge liquid nitrogen storage tank to Egypt
summary: Sri City's VRV Asia Pacific exports a massive liquid nitrogen storage tank to Egypt, showcasing India's cryogenic engineering excellence.
content:
Sri City-based VRV Asia Pacific, a subsidiary of Chart Industries, achieved a landmark international milestone by exporting a massive liquid nitrogen storage tank to Air Liquide in Egypt.
The 531-kilolitre vessel, weighing 168 tonnes and stretching 39 metres, was made under the ‘Make in India’ initiative. Its transportation represented the pinnacle of cryogenic engineering and required complex multi-axle logistics to reach Chennai port.
Sri City managing director Ravindra Sannareddy called the export a ‘crowning success’ that further cemented VRV’s reputation for world-class cryogenic engineering.
As Sri City’s founding tenant, VRV has successfully transitioned from a local manufacturer to a vital global supplier for high-stakes sectors like aerospace and healthcare.
The company has a history of constantly supporting Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) and also providing life-saving oxygen infrastructure during the Covid-19 pandemic.

title: BJP has made inroads into rural Telangana: Ramchander Rao
summary: BJP has made inroads into rural Telangana: Ramchander Rao
content:
BJP-supported candidates have won nearly 1,000 Sarpanch posts, 1,200 Deputy Sarpanch positions, and over 10,000 ward member seats across Telangana, despite threats and pressure from local leaders, indicating the party’s growing strength in rural areas, claimed Telangana BJP president N. Ramchander Rao on Thursday.
Speaking at a felicitation programme for newly-elected local body members in Bhuvanagiri, the former MLC said that these victories are a strong rebuttal to critics, who once labelled BJP an “urban-centric party.” He noted that BJP-affiliated candidates secured key positions across districts, while the number of BRS-supported Sarpanches dropped from 8,000 to 2,000, reflecting its waning influence.
“This victory reflects the hard work of our workers and leaders, and the trust people have placed in the Modi government’s commitment to rural development,” Mr. Rao said. He added that these wins strengthen the party at the grassroots level and lay a solid foundation to expand BJP to every household in Telangana. Welfare and development schemes of the Centre, including free rice distribution, grain procurement, and PM Kisan Samman Nidhi, have played a major role, he observed.
Mr. Rao asserted that a “double-engine government” is essential for Telangana’s progress. “BJP’s rise in villages is unstoppable, and the party will come to power in the State in the next election,” he said.
In a separate press conference at the State BJP office, Legislature Party leader A. Maheshwar Reddy highlighted Nirmal district’s strong support for BJP that won 80 Sarpanch posts out of 128. In Mudhole, BJP secured 98 out of 178 panchayats, while Khanapur added 36 Sarpanches. Overall, Nirmal district delivered 213 Sarpanches, 213 Deputy Sarpanches, and over 1,300 ward members, he said.
“These results reflect growing public anger against the Congress government, which has failed to fulfill its six guarantees and 420 promises, plunging the state into corruption and misrule. Despite triangular contests and local pressures, voters decisively supported BJP, signaling a major shift in rural Telangana,” Mr. Reddy added.

title: Centre has cut ₹5,900 crore  from Kerala’s borrowing limit, says Balagopal
summary: Centre reduces Kerala's borrowing limit by ₹5,900 crore, impacting state finances ahead of Assembly elections, says Finance Minister Balagopal.
content:
Finance Minister K.N. Balagopal said on Thursday that the Centre had slashed the borrowing limit of the State by ₹5,900 crore in the current quarter.
He said the Centre issued a letter on Wednesday stating that ₹5,900 crore had been reduced from the borrowing limit in the current quarter. “This is the last year of the Left front government and the last quarter ahead of the Assembly election. The reduction on the borrowing limit will impact the State considerably,” he said.
Mr. Balagopal said the State government was able to sail through with its plans, despite the ceiling on borrowing limit imposed by the Centre over the past four-and-a-half years. The annual expenditure in 2024-25 was about ₹1.75 lakh crore. “We expect it to touch 2 lakh crore this fiscal,” he said.
He said that the Viksit Bharat – Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin), or VB-G RAM G Bill, replacing the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA), would adversely affect the State. Last year, about 13.7 lakh families had participated in the scheme and the total enrolment was about 22 lakh, he said.
Mr. Balagopal said the Bill would have far-reaching consequences as it would result in the loss of jobs for lakhs of people not only in Kerala, but across the country. With the Centre abdicating its responsibility, the financial burden related to the scheme would fall on the State government, he said. He added that the benefits of the GST rationalisation needed to be passed on to consumers, and the Centre must compensate the States for the annual revenue loss.
On the Left Democratic Front’s electoral setback, Mr. Balagopal said the  front would ‘reach out to the public and make required amendments’ ahead of the forthcoming Assembly elections.

title: Collapsing roads and retaining walls of newly developed NH stretches in Kerala cause concern among residents
summary: Concerns rise in Kerala as collapsing roads and retaining walls on NH 66 threaten public safety and expose engineering flaws.
content:
When R. Resmi, a veterinary doctor, set out on the afternoon of December 5, she had no idea that her routine drive would turn into a terrifying race for survival. While navigating the familiar service road beneath the under-construction National Highway 66 (NH 66) stretch at Mylakkadu, near Kottiyam in Kollam, she experienced a sharp, unexpected jolt.
Her car lurched violently, and before she could react, the right side of the vehicle shot upwards. Her immediate thought was an earthquake.
Then, panic erupted. The driver of an autorickshaw ahead of her began screaming, hysterically urging her to run. She abandoned her car and sprinted for her life. Looking back, she witnessed a scene of absolute chaos.
The Reinforced Soil (RS) wall of the embankment was disintegrating, spewing soil and rubble onto the road. An elderly woman who had emerged from the car behind Resmi was paralysed by fear as the road surface split open faster than she could move. She was saved by the quick action of residents.
There was also a school bus trapped among the vehicles. As the road yawned open, the bus driver and a staff member frantically evacuated the children. They were immediately joined by local residents, and together, they were seen running for safety carrying the small children.
“The wall was on the right, and there was a paddy field on the left,” recounts Resmi.
“We had no choice but to sprint across the cracking, unstable surface. As we ran, the road bulged ominously, electric poles began to buckle and tilt, and water started gushing through the fresh fissures. It was a very scary situation,” she says.
Vehicles seen trapped on the service road following the collapse of the Reinforced Soil wall along the under-construction National Highway 66 at Mylakkadu, near Kottiyam in Kollam, on December 5. 
                                                            | Photo Credit: 
                                C. Sureshkumar
There was no time to fully process the disaster as the cause became clear—the massive Reinforced Soil (RS) wall had failed. Four vehicles, including a school bus, were trapped, though none were injured in the incident.
“The collapse started with a small hole in the RS wall next to the service road, which then quickly grew into a huge crater. The culvert over the stream collapsed, and soon, the surrounding land, extending up to the paddy field, cracked open with a thud. This was followed by a major pipe burst that flooded the service road. Thankfully, the power supply stopped right away. If the elevated wall had completely collapsed, it would have toppled onto the service road, turning into a major tragedy,” recounts Sreejith S., a resident.
The collapse of the national highway at Kooriyad in Malappuram earlier serves as a stark precedent to the Mylakkadu incident.
Engineering assessments confirm that the fundamental flaw in both the cases is identical. In both Kooriyad and Mylakkadu, the collapses were triggered because the underlying foundation was structurally inadequate to bear the imposed load.
Construction of an underpass in progress on National Highway 544 at Amballur in Thrissur. The Mylakkadu accident has stoked fears among the residents of the area over the stability of the mud-filled structure being built for the underpass.  
  
                                                            | Photo Credit: 
                                K.K .NAJEEB
“It is a fundamental engineering principle that an earth embankment built on a weak foundation will collapse when the applied weight exceeds its capacity. Elevated earth embankments mandate rigorous soil testing, strengthening measures, and foundation improvement to safely enhance load-bearing capacity. However, these essential steps were neglected—neither was the necessary inspection conducted nor the soil strengthened,” criticises Kottiyam Ajithkumar, a member of the Desheeya Patha Samara Samiti, a collective formed in protest against the unscientific construction. The base supporting the massive earth embankment at Mylakkadu is marshy land, and the authorities conveniently ignored the area’s sensitive terrain and high groundwater saturation. Failure is inevitable when the load surpasses the weak foundation’s bearing limit, he says.
Senior geotechnical engineering consultant Jayakrishnan Menon confirms that the wall was designed without addressing the low soil strength conditions of the site. “Kerala’s coastal regions feature soft marine and alluvial deposits, unlike other States where large embankments are common. The Mylakkadu fill imposed a load far exceeding the weak subsoil’s shear strength,” he says. He emphasises that inadequate geotechnical investigation led to a poor understanding of the soil profile. In order to rectify the current flaw, the failed section should be removed, and soil conditions scientifically re-established before reconstruction.
He adds that solutions like stone columns are potential alternatives, but can be employed only after detailed testing. “Insufficient soil reports pose long-term risks, as failures can occur years after construction. Precise and truthful soil data is critical for safety in Kerala’s geologically sensitive areas,” he observes.
As per the company in charge of construction, the ₹1,385-crore project involves upgrading a 31.25 km stretch of NH 66 from an existing two-lane road to a six-lane dual carriageway highway. This extensive development plan encompasses the construction of a bypass for Kollam city, six flyovers, a rail overbridge, 10 underpasses, seven new major/minor bridges, and 42 culverts. Achieving this target requires massive earthwork, specifically involving more than 2.5 million cubic metres of earthwork and the construction of over 1,00,000 square metres of reinforced earth wall.
“The construction of the RS wall without considering the topography, climate, or the specific characteristics of the soil in each location is unscientific, and it should be stopped immediately. With the collapse of elevated roads built using RS walls in several places, it has been unequivocally proven that such structures are impractical for Kerala’s roads. Pillar-supported elevated highways should be constructed instead of relying on RS walls,” suggests N.K. Premachandran, Kollam MP.
Following the collapse, the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) has launched a massive, Statewide geotechnical investigation. As per the preliminary assessments, the failure was due to a deep-seated shear or bearing capacity failure, which means the foundation soil was critically weak and unable to support the imposed load of the wall and earth fill.
The NHAI has temporarily suspended the project’s concessionaire and its promoters, M/s Shivalaya, and the Independent Engineer, M/s Feedback -Satra JV, from bidding on future projects. It has also issued show-cause notices to both parties regarding potential debarment—up to three years for the concessionaire and two years for the Independent Engineer—besides the imposition of penalties.
To guarantee structural integrity, the NHAI has mobilised 18 geotechnical agencies to conduct rigorous soil sampling and testing at 378 RS wall locations across 18 NH 66 project sites in Kerala, covering sites already built, in progress, and yet to start.
The Kottiyam Merchants’ Association is planning to launch large-scale protests in the wake of the extensive damage to utility lines and the service road following the collapse. “With more than 35 educational institutions and seven hospitals in the vicinity, Kottiyam is a high-traffic zone where over 4,000 students commute daily. The current construction poses a direct threat to commuters. The hazardous wall between Mylakkad and Parakkulam should be replaced with a stable, pillar-supported structure," demands S. Palani, general secretary of the association.
Palani points out that the project has been marred by systemic violations from the outset, specifically wall heights that exceed legal safety limits. “We had warned the authorities of the impending disaster in the area. Besides petitioning the State and Union governments, we met the officials of Shivalaya Construction Ltd. and explained that the soil conditions could not support the wall. Our repeated warnings were met with total inaction, and the recent collapse is the direct result of that negligence. Public safety cannot be compromised, and accountability has to be fixed,” he adds.
The Kottiyam accident has stoked fears among the residents of Amballur in Thrissur district over the stability of the mud-filled structure being built for an underpass on National Highway 544. The underpass is being constructed across an extensive wetland area where soil has been filled and raised along a north-south axis for nearly 1.2 km. Residents allege that the natural east-west water flow has been obstructed, with no proper outlets provided to drain rainwater from the highway or run-off from the eastern side. As a result, there is severe water-logging around the underpass and the overbridge area even after a short spell of rain, they complain.
“No proper and scientific studies were carried out before starting the Amballur underpass work,” says T. Sreenath, an activist of the Kerala Sasthra Sahithya Parishad (KSSP).
A special meeting of the grama sabha had warned the authorities of the risk of flash floods if the project was implemented without adequate drainage plan. “Amballur is a flood-prone area. If heavy rain occurs, the situation will worsen as there are no channels to let water out,” he cautions.
According to residents, the existing drainage system along the highway is unscientific and unable to handle intense rainfall. The elevated, mound-like structure formed by dumping large quantities of soil has further aggravated the problem, they say.
Water that once flowed through canals such as the Keli thodu to the Kurumali river  now has no clear outlet, as parts of these channels have been converted into roads. Over 60 houses, besides commercial establishments, hotels and a cinema theatre near the Amballur junction, stand in the affected zone.
A study group led by the Nenmanikkara unit of the KSSP found that both the water flowing from the eastern side through the underpass and the water carried by the concrete canal on the western side of the highway is unable to drain westwards due to the absence of proper channels. The condition increases the risk of widespread inundation in the area.
Highlighting the similarity with the Kottiyam incident, K.K. Aneesh Kumar of the KSSP says the soil-filled structure is likely to become heavily waterlogged, compromising its stability. He demands a comprehensive geotechnical study and safety audit of the Amballur underpass as well as the other underpasses along NH 544 on the lines of the safety assessments carried out on NH 66.
Calling for urgent intervention, local residents say alternative designs—such as pillar-supported underpasses without extensive soil filling—should be considered, especially in high-value (so that the area under the underpass can be utilised) and flood-prone areas, to allow natural water flow and reduce environmental and safety risks.
The collapsing roads and retaining walls along the newly developed national highway stretches have become shortcuts to accidents in Kerala.
(With inputs from Mini Muringatheri in Thrissur)

title: Bombay film crew reunites at Bekal Fort for 30th anniversary celebration
summary: Bombay film crew reunites at Bekal Fort to celebrate the movie's 30th anniversary and promote Kerala's cinema tourism.
content:
It is not solely the exceptional performances, compelling narratives, and striking cinematography that elevate a film to brilliance. Often, a perfect location, carefully chosen by the crew, plays a crucial role in transforming it into something truly memorable. This view is echoed by the crew of the iconic movieBombay,shot by Mani Ratnam and starring Arvind Swami and Manisha Koirala, as they come together at Bekal Fort in Kasaragod on December 20 on the occasion of the 30th anniversary of the 1995-released film.
For instance, it’s hard for movie buffs to forget the sight of the lead character in the movie leaping across cliffs beside a turbulent sea beneath a brooding sky at Bekal Fort. If the song ‘Uyire’ from the movie still echoes in one’s memory, credit belongs not only to composer A.R. Rahman and his soundtrack — a score of conscience that stirred a nation, but also to its stunning setting that elevated the emotional impact of the movie.
The crew, including Manisha Koirala, Mani Ratnam and cinematographer Rajiv Menon, gets ready for an anniversary bash on Bekal Beach and the fort on Saturday at the invitation of Kerala Tourism as part of promoting cinema tourism in Kerala, a project that envisages promoting the tourist places which have become popular due to their appearance in films. According to officials, what made Bombay indelible wasn’t just the subject it showcased, but the breathtaking locations that enhanced the appeal of the movie. Through this initiative, Kerala Tourism also plans to  draw the attention of filmmakers in India and abroad to the picturesque locations in Kerala, along with popularising such destinations among the tourists visiting the State, said the officer.
Despite the film's huge popularity in India and abroad, only about 5% of international tourists who visit Kerala reach the stunning locations in northern Kerala. While around 2,500 foreigners visited the fort in 2019, the recent peak in footfall, it dropped by 40% in 2023. As part of the cine tourism promotion programme, the crew will take a stroll through the beach on Saturday, and a visit to Bekal Fort is also scheduled on the same day, said Shijin P, managing director (MD) of the Bekal Resorts Development Corporation (BRDC).

title: Govt. yet to refund educational expenses of 461 children of farmers who ended their lives due to drought in Karnataka
summary: Karnataka government delays educational refunds for 461 children of farmers who died due to drought, causing distress and outrage.
content:
Karnataka government has not paid the educational expenses of as many as 461 children of farmers who ended their lives due to drought in the State over the last five years.
From the academic year of 2020-21 to 2024-25, a total of 797 students, the children of farmers who ended their lives due to drought across the State, have applied for their educational expenses. Of these, only 336 students have been paid a total of ₹45.94 lakh.
Responding to a question raised by Member of Legislative Council (MLC) from Janata Dal (Secular) Govindaraju in this regard, at the ongoing legislature session, Minister for School Education and Literacy Madhu Bangarappa said that the educational expenses of the remaining 461 students were pending due to non-submission of proposals from the respective districts.
The government has been bearing the entire educational expenses, including hostel charges, of children of farmers who ended their lives due to drought in the State since 2016-17. Between 2017-18 and 2024-25, the DSEL received 1,589 applications of which 1,128 applicants have got their refund.
Following applications made by the students, the district level DSEL officials have to submit a proposal to the State government with documents, including certified copies of names of the parents in the Students Achievement Tracking System (SATS) and death certificate of the farmer parent who ended his/her life. In the case of these 461 students, such proposals have not been submitted from the districts.
The School Development and Monitoring Committee (SDMC) Association has condemned the lackadaisical attitude of the DSEL officials and demanded that the educational expenses of all 461 students be immediately refunded. “Children who have lost their parents are already in distress. The negligence of the DSEL officials at the district level is inhumane. The government should take immediate action to refund these expenses to all eligible students and take action against officials who caused this delay,” said Umesh G. Gangavadi, State president, SDMC Association.
(Those who are in distress and having suicidal tendencies can seek help from Arogya Sahayavani Ph:104)

title: IUML makes historic gains across Kerala in local body polls
summary: IUML achieves historic success in Kerala local body polls, securing 3,203 seats and expanding influence beyond Malappuram district.
content:
The strong performance of the Indian Union Muslim League (IUML) in the recent civic body elections has propelled the party to the third place in the State in terms of civic body representation.
By securing 3,203 seats across Corporations, municipalities and the three tiers of panchayats, the IUML now ranks just behind the Congress and the Communist Party of India (Marxist) [CPI(M)] in the State. The party significantly improved on its tally of 2,338 seats it won in 2020 by winning 865 more seats in the latest elections.
However, a notable aspect of the IUML’s performance is that it secured more seats outside Malappuram district than within it. While the party won 1,456 seats in Malappuram, it captured a larger tally of 1,747 seats in the rest of Kerala.
“We have demonstrated that the IUML is not a party confined to Malappuram district. We secured seats in every district, from Thiruvananthapuram to Kasaragod. That is a creditable achievement this time,” said IUML State secretary Abdurahman Randathani.
In Pathanamthitta district, the IUML ended its dry spell by securing seven local body seats for the first time. Across the southern districts of Kerala, the party now has 285 councillors in panchayats, municipalities, and Corporations. Several non-Muslim candidates, including Christian, have been elected on the IUML symbol.
The party improved its performance across all districts. In Kasaragod, its tally rose from 196 to 263 seats; in Kannur, from 223 to 262; in Wayanad, from 106 to 178; in Kozhikode, from 384 to 497; in Malappuram, from 1,103 to 1,456; in Palakkad, from 171 to 262; in Thrissur, from 42 to 85; in Ernakulam, from 41 to 88; in Idukki, from 20 to 35; in Alappuzha, from 13 to 18; in Kottayam, from 17 to 20; in Pathanamthitta, from zero to seven; in Kollam, from 16 to 19; and in Thiruvananthapuram, from six to 13 seats.
“Our victory reflects the wider acceptance of the IUML’s political stance in the State. We have never been communal. We have consistently taken the lead in demonstrating how a political party should respond with positivity and humanitarian concern whenever crises have struck Kerala. The COVID-19 pandemic and the Wayanad landslide disaster are examples,” said Mr. Randathani, explaining the party’s success across the State.
The party won 2,248 seats in grama panchayats, nearly 13% of the total in the State, along with 300 block panchayat seats, 51 district panchayat seats, 568 municipal seats and 36 Corporation seats.
IUML State president Syed Sadikali Shihab Thangal said he was delighted that the party had brought many educated women into the forefront of civic governance in the State. According to him, the IUML’s contribution to the empowerment of Muslim women in society surpassed that of any other organisation.
The party sees its State-wide performance – especially in Malappuram, where it won 11 of 12 municipalities, 14 of 15 block panchayats, the entire district panchayat council, and over 80 grama panchayats in alliance with the Congress – as a strong foundation for the upcoming Assembly elections.

title: Sanjay Saraogi assumes charge as Bihar BJP State President, expresses gratitude to party workers
summary: Sanjay Saraogi takes charge as Bihar BJP President, emphasizing party unity, ideology, and commitment to worker participation.
content:
The newly appointed Bihar State president of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), Sanjay Saraogi, on Thursday (December 18, 2025) formally assumed charge at the party office.
Addressing party workers and leaders during a felicitation ceremony, he said the organisation was supreme in the BJP and its ideology was the soul of the party. He said that party workers were the backbone of the organisation.
Mr. Saraogi told party workers that his education began in theshakhasof the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) and that his journey from “I” to “We” began with the Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad.
Acknowledging senior leaders and former State presidents, Mr. Saraogi said veteran leaders had shaped him like skilled artisans and entrusted him with this important responsibility.
He expressed gratitude to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Union Home Minister Amit Shah, BJP national president J.P. Nadda, and National Working President Nitin Nabin, stating that he would live up to the confidence reposed in him.
Mr. Saraogi arrived in Patna from his Assembly constituency of Darbhanga, where he received a warm welcome at several locations. After reaching the State office, he was accorded a grand reception.
Members of the Mahila Morcha welcomed him with the ceremonial sound of conch shells. Addressing the felicitation ceremony, he said, “This is not a post, but a responsibility. I assure you that I will work day and night to fulfil this responsibility and leave no stone unturned in strengthening the party’s ideology.”
He expressed hope that he would continue to receive the support of senior leaders in Bihar and guidance from the national leadership. He assured party workers that no worker would be neglected and that every worker would be given due respect.
Mr. Saraogi further said efforts would be made to ensure coordination between the organisation and the government, with the goal of building a developed Bihar.
Addressing the gathering, Deputy Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary congratulated the new State president and said that in the BJP, responsibilities keep changing and everyone moves forward by fulfilling their duties with excellence.
He expressed confidence that as there are no elections in the next three years, the new president would further strengthen the organisation. Mr. Choudhary also said that nine former State presidents would guide him.
Deputy Chief Minister Vijay Kumar Sinha said the central leadership was entrusting major responsibilities to party workers and that it was the duty of everyone to fulfil these responsibilities effectively.
He expressed confidence that under the new leadership, the honour, respect and self-esteem of party workers would increase, and the goal of a developed Bihar would be achieved.
The function was attended by Assembly Speaker Prem Kumar, Legislative Council Chairman Awadhesh Narayan Singh, and several Ministers, MLAs and MLCs of the party.
Before reaching the BJP’s party office, Mr. Saraogi paid floral tribute to the statue of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar near the Patna High Court. He then proceeded in an open vehicle as part of a procession accompanied by party workers on motorcycles. The procession also included elephants and horses. He later paid homage by garlanding the statue of Loknayak Jayaprakash Narayan.
Outgoing State president Dilip Kumar Jaiswal, while expressing gratitude for the support he received from party workers and senior leaders during his 17-month-long tenure, said the return of the National Democratic Alliance government in Bihar with a massive mandate was the result of a collective effort. He said the taking over by the new State president was a day of celebration, joy and pride for the BJP.

title: Understanding Vachanas can help in personality development, says V-C
summary: V-C D.V. Paramashivamurthy emphasizes Vachana literature's role in personality development at a special lecture in Hosapete.
content:
Hampi Kannada University Vice-Chancellor D.V. Paramashivamurthy on Thursday said that understanding the life values and messages embedded in Vachana literature can serve as an effective path towards personality development.
He was speaking after inaugurating a special lecture programme organised jointly by the Department of Kannada and Culture, the Karnataka Sahitya Academy, the Chakora Sahitya Vichara Vedike and Sri Shankar Anand Singh Government First Grade College on the college premises in Hosapete, Vijayanagara district.
Prof. Paramashivamurthy said that among various literary forms, Vachana literature occupies a unique and significant place. However, in the age of technology and artificial intelligence, the number of readers engaging with Vachanas has been steadily declining.
He stressed the need for people, especially students, to read Vachanas to understand their deeper meaning rather than treating them as mere ritualistic texts.
Explaining the essence of Vachana literature, he said that correctly interpreting their philosophical message can lead to self-motivated transformation.
He highlighted the global contribution of Kannada Vachana composers and described their literary output as a remarkable gift to world literature. He also explained to students the concise meaning of Basavanna’s well-known Vachana beginning with “Kalabeda Kolabeda…” emphasising the concepts of inner and outer purity.
Speaking on the occasion, Karnataka Sahitya Academy member-secretary Mallikarjun B. Manpade said that the Chakora Vachana Sahitya Vedike programme is being organised in PU and degree colleges across the State to create awareness and interest in literature among students.
He urged students to go beyond textbooks and read Vachana literature, novels, short stories and poetry. He said that the Karnataka Sahitya Academy is publishing 100 literary books and called upon youth to move away from excessive mobile phone usage and take to reading Vachana literature.
College principal G. Narayan Hebasur said that the Vachanas written by Basavanna, Allama Prabhu, Sarvajna, Akkamahadevi and others carry timeless relevance.
Noting that Vachana recitations and studies are being encouraged not only in India but also abroad, he said that studying Vachana literature can help students develop patience, knowledge and an appreciation of literary excellence.
Eminent thinker and retired professor Mrutyunjaya Rumale delivered a lecture on the role of Vachana literature in shaping a strong personality.
Head of the Kannada Department C. Devanna, Kannada professor Naganna Kilari, Chakora Sahitya Vichara Vedike coordinator Venkatesh Badiger, Umeshwar Mudenur, other faculty members and students were present.

title: Internal reservation Bill passed in Karnataka Assembly amid debate on Alemari and EWS quota
summary: Amid demand to increase the reservation for Scheduled Castes (SCs) to accommodate the interests of 59 Alemari (nomadic) communities, the Karnataka Legislative Assembly on Thursday unanimously passed The Karnataka Scheduled Castes (Sub-Classification) Bill, 2025, that provides legislation cover to internal reservation in 17 % reservation for 101 Scheduled Castes.
content:
Amid demand to increase the reservation for Scheduled Castes (SCs) to accommodate the interests of 59 Alemari (nomadic) communities, the Karnataka Legislative Assembly on Thursday unanimously passed The Karnataka Scheduled Castes (Sub-Classification) Bill, 2025, that provides legislation cover to internal reservation in 17 % reservation for 101 Scheduled Castes.
The government was under pressure from the Dalit Left groups to legislate the internal reservation matrix.
Social Welfare Minister H.C. Mahadevappa, who moved the Bill, said, “Internal reservation was a promise made during the 2023 Assembly elections and we have kept it.”
The Bill seeks to provide legislative cover to the GO that apportioned 17% reservation. Of this, 6% reservation has been provided to 16 castes in Category A (Dalit Left), 6% to 19 castes in Category B (Dalit Right) and 5% to 63 castes, including 59 Alemari castes in Category C (Lambani, Korama, Koracha and Bhovi).
The Minister justified three categories introduced, after modifying the five categories recommended by the one-man commission headed by H.N. Nagamohan Das.
He said, “The 1% recommended to Adi Karnataka, Adi Andhra and Adi Dravida was modified and allowed to choose either between Category A or Category B because they were getting benefits from the two categories.”
On the 1% reservation for Alemari community being merged with Category C, he said, “With 1% benefit we felt the 59 communities may not get justice. Now, they will be given first post (in recruitment) in Category C to provide justice to them.” Those who still feel slighted can approach the Scheduled Castes Commission, he said.
During the discussion on the Bill, Deputy Leader of Opposition Arvind Bellad said that Alemari communities could not compete with other castes and inequality would continue. The Chief Minister’s Economic Adviser Basavaraj Rayaraddi suggested that the State could explore possibility of increasing the total reservation for SCs to 18% to include 1% reservation to Alemari communities.
Earlier, when Mr. Bellad pointed out that Chief Minister Siddaramaiah had once said that 17% reservation for SCs had not received legal sanction, Mr. Siddaramaiah took exception to it.
“I have not said anything like that anywhere. In fact, we were the first to seek 17% for SCs and 7% for STs as per their population. I am someone who would seek 75% reservation. The Centre has brought 10% reservation to EWS. Where is the provision for it in the Constitution?” the Chief Minister asked.
A little later, Leader of the Opposition R. Ashok brought Assembly records where the Chief Minister had suggested that the then Bill had to be inserted in IX schedule without which it would exceed the 50% cap on reservation imposed by Supreme Court. This led to another round of exchanges.
Meanwhile, expelled BJP member Basannagouda Patil Yatnal, took objection to Chief Minister’s statement on EWS. “The Supreme Court has also upheld it,” he said, adding reservation was needed for other communities where there were poor people.
The Chief Minister, who initially disagreed with Mr. Yatnal, later admitted that the Constitution was amended in 2019 to provide for EWS reservation.

title: Hyderabad’s IT belt sees one-third fall in traffic as year-end festive break sets in
summary: Hyderabad’s IT belt sees one-third fall in traffic as year-end festive break sets in
content:
As Christmas and New Year draw closer, theusually choked roads of Hyderabad’s IT corridorare beginning to ease, offering commuters a brief but tangible respite from the daily grind.
Daily traffic count and classification reports from the Cyberabad traffic police indicate that vehicle volumes on the key arterial stretches across the commissionerate have declined sharply by mid-December, with officials expecting the numbers to taper further in the coming days as offices thin out.
On the Radisson Hotel stretch between Le Meridien and the Gachibowli flyover, total vehicle movement reduced from 1,86,886 on December 1 to 1,26,033 by December 15, marking a decline of over one-third in less than two weeks. Car traffic alone dropped by nearly 30%, falling from 85,329 to 59,466, while two-wheeler movement eased from 60,032 to 40,274. Bus traffic recorded one of the steepest declines on this stretch, almost halving from 1,881 to 1,010 during the same period.
A comparable trend was recorded on the Hitec City Road–Yashoda Hospital stretch, where the total number of vehicles captured by traffic cameras declined from 1,91,123 on December 1 to 1,39,881 on December 15, a reduction of over 27%. Cars, two-wheelers and autorickshaws all registered notable drops, with volumes falling from 73,544 to 54,957, 87,545 to 62,216, and 23,468 to 17,811 respectively, translating into declines ranging between 24 and 29%.
Hitec City road buckles under tech traffic boom, clogs with 1.5 lakh vehicles per day
Elevated gridlock: Traffic crawls through Gachibowli’s newest flyover
The busy Cable Bridge–Ikea corridor also reflected the seasonal slowdown. Traffic volumes fell from 2,18,225 on December 1 to 1,58,466 by December 15, a reduction of nearly 60,000 vehicles or 27%. While car numbers declined from 1,02,708 to 76,516 and two-wheelers from 85,820 to 60,861, bus movement on this stretch saw one of the sharpest changes, dropping by 46% from 1,406 to just 764. Autorickshaw traffic also eased from 23,466 to 17,208.
On the Shaikpet–Raidurgam stretch, total vehicle movement reduced from 2,22,396 to 1,52,686 over the same 15-day period. Each vehicle category recorded a broadly similar decline of around 30%, with cars falling from 90,372 to 60,922, two-wheelers from 92,966 to 64,854, buses from 2,659 to 1,722, and autorickshaws from 30,545 to 21,733.
“The traffic is decreasing by 10-15% per day and will reduce further as fewer employees are travelling during the festive season,” said T. Sai Manohar, Deputy Commissioner of Police (Traffic), Madhapur.
The trend is also visible in cumulative monthly data. Between November 1 and 15, around 17 lakh vehicles were recorded on the Hitec City–Yashoda Hospital stretch, which dipped marginally to 16.8 lakh during December 1 to 15. On the Shaikpet–Gachibowli route, traffic volumes eased from 13.9 lakh to 13.7 lakh during the same comparative periods.
For daily commuters, the numbers are translating into precious minutes saved. Aditya Sharma, who works with a financial services firm in Gachibowli, said most teams have shifted to work-from-home arrangements or are on leave for the festive season. “There are barely any employees in offices or on the roads these days. I am now reaching my office in 20 minutes, which would otherwise take 40 minutes during peak hours,” he said.
Prithvi Kumar, an IT employee commuting from Gachibowli to Ramanthapur, echoed the sentiment. “I am saving at least 15 to 20 minutes every day. On some days, I start at 6 p.m. and reach home by 6.45 p.m., which is nearly half the time it usually takes on a regular weekday,” he said, adding that while some choke points, including Malkam Cheruvu, Mehdipatnam signal and the Masab Tank junction, continue to see congestion, overall travel has become noticeably smoother.

title: RRII unveils sustainable paint made from natural rubber
summary: In a major  breakthrough, the Rubber Research Institute of India (RRII), under the Rubber Board, has discovered that high-quality, eco-friendly paint can be produced from natural rubber latex.
content:
In a major  breakthrough, the Rubber Research Institute of India (RRII), under the Rubber Board, has discovered that high-quality, eco-friendly paint can be produced from natural rubber latex.
According to RRII authority, the newly developed formula, using natural latex, sea shells, natural clay and plant extracts will surpass the performance standards of conventional emulsion paints. The innovation is the result of nearly 18 months of systematic research and trials.  The paint is health-friendly, VOC (Volatile Organic Compound) free, and water-based, posing no known health hazards.
``Since natural plant extracts can also be incorporated for coloration, all commonly used interior shades can be produced without relying on synthetic chemicals. The fact that natural latex forms the principal raw material adds further significance to the development, especially from a sustainability and farmer-centric standpoint,” noted Shera Mathew, officer in charge of RRII, in a statement.
For rubber growers, the prospect of manufacturing paint from natural rubber latex offers renewed optimism, as it opens up a promising new avenue for value addition and enhanced income generation, it added
The natural paint has been developed for Kerala Paint Industries Pvt. Ltd, which will be marketed under the brand name Kerala Paints – Bhadram. The official launch and technology transfer ceremony will be inaugurated by Devaswoms Minister V. N. Vasavan on December 23.

title: Digitisation of SIR enumeration forms nearing completion in Kozhikode
summary: Kozhikode completes 99% digitisation of SIR forms for the 2026 voters’ list update, enhancing electoral transparency and efficiency.
content:
With the support of Booth-Level Officers (BLOs), election authorities have completed the digitisation of 99% of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) enumeration forms as part of the ongoing voters’ list update for 2026 in Kozhikode district.
Of the 26,58,847 forms distributed across the district, 26,58,722 have already been digitised. According to Revenue department officials, BLOs played a crucial role in achieving the targets set earlier.
Meanwhile, 1,95,605 forms, accounting for 7.36% of the total, were not returned even after the deadline for submission of the filled enumeration forms ended on Thursday (December 18). Officials said forms received by the deadline would be included in the draft electoral roll, scheduled for publication on December 23.
Election authorities have also finalised the ASD (Absent, Shifted, Dead) list, which includes voters who could not be located despite repeated visits by BLOs, those who had passed away, individuals without permanent residence, and cases of duplicate registrations. The ASD list has been shared with all BLOs and booth-level agents to ensure transparency. Voters and political representatives can verify the details through the BLOs concerned.
At the same time, officials said 3.87% of the returned forms — a total of 1,03,029 — could not be matched with the 2002 electoral roll and would undergo further verification. The voters concerned would be contacted as part of the verification process, they added.

title: PT teacher gets five-year jail for misbehaving with student on school bus
summary: A PT teacher in Hyderabad sentenced to five years for misbehaving with a Class 8 student on a school bus.
content:
A physical training teacher from St. Ann’s School has been sentenced to five years of rigorous imprisonment by the Fast Track Special Court in Medchal on Thursday (December 18, 2025) after being found guilty of misbehaving with a Class 8 student on a school bus. The court also slapped a fine of ₹3,000 on the accused.
The accused was identified as 35-year-old Dappulapudi Suresh. The case dates back to August 30, 2016, when students from St. Ann’s School had travelled to Gachibowli for a sports meet, accompanied by their PT teacher, Suresh. While travelling in the school bus, he misbehaved with one of the students.
Following a complaint, the Petbasheerabad police booked a case against him under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act. The verdict came after Special Public Prosecutor G. Prabhakar Reddy presented arguments with supporting evidence.

title: Protest by supporters of defeated candidate: Police step up investigation into stone-pelting incident
summary: Protest by supporters of defeated candidate: Police step up investigation into stone-pelting incident
content:
The Velgatur police have stepped up investigation into the stone-pelting incident in which four police officers were injured soon after completion of vote counting during the final phase of Gram Panchayat polls in Paidipally village of Jagtial district on Wednesday night.
Chaos prevailed in Paidipally on Wednesday night when the supporters of a defeated candidate staged a sit-in in front of the polling station demanding recounting of votes soon after the vote counting process.
According to the police, the protesters prevented the transportation of ballot boxes by obstructing the polling staff from discharging their official duties.
Despite attempts to persuade them, they allegedly tried to damage polling materials forcing the police to resort to mild lathi-charge to control the situation.
In the melee, the protesters allegedly pelted stones at police personnel resulting in injuries to four police officers and damage to two police vehicles. As tension mounted, police resorted to firing in the air to disperse the protesters and bring the situation under control.
Additional police personnel rushed to the village to defuse tension. All the ballot boxes and the polling personnel were safely evacuated from the location under tight police security.
Based on the complaints lodged by the Returning Officer and local police officers, the Velgatur police registered two separate cases against the culprits concerned for violation of the Model Code of Conduct.
Strict legal action will be taken against those responsible for the incident, said Jagtial DSP Raghu Chander.

title: Hyderabad to host Asian Thalassemia Conclave on January 10 and 11
summary: Hyderabad will host the Asian Thalassemia Conclave on January 10-11, 2026, focusing on prevention strategies for thalassemia.
content:
Hyderabad will host the Asian Thalassemia Conclave (ATC) on January 10 and 11, 2026, bringing together doctors, policymakers, researchers, non-governmental organisations and patient groups from India and across Asia to discuss a coordinated response to thalassemia, one of the country’s most serious yet preventable genetic blood disorders.
The two-day conclave is being organised by the Thalassemia and Sickle Cell Society (TSCS), Hyderabad. India continues to carry one of the highest global burdens of thalassemia, with thousands of children born every year with transfusion-dependent forms of the disorder, despite the fact that it is largely preventable through early screening and informed reproductive choices.
During the conclave, discussions will focus on prevention-first strategies aimed at reducing new thalassemia births. Key themes will include premarital and antenatal screening, strengthening and standardising genetic counselling services and integrating thalassemia screening into existing maternal and child health programmes.

title: Bombay High Court refuses bail to Daman Crime Branch constables accused of abduction, extortion
summary: Bombay High Court denies bail to Daman constables accused of abduction and extortion, citing serious allegations and questionable investigation.
content:
The Bombay High Court has rejected the bail plea of three Crime Branch constables from Daman who have been accused of abducting a group of friends from Surat, and extorting ₹7 lakh from them.
Dismissing the bail application filed by Ramdevsinh Jadeja, Vishal Mir and Chintan Arvindbhai Desai, Justice Neela Gokhale observed that the allegations were “grave and serious”, holding that the magistrate had rightly taken cognisance of their non-bailable offences. The order was pronounced on December 16.
The case stems from a first information report (FIR) registered at the Coastal Police Station in Kadaiya, Daman, this year, under Sections 140(2), 308(7) and 3(5) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023. The FIR says that on August 25, complainant Aajessh Patel and his friends were intercepted while travelling to Daman, taken to police headquarters, slapped, and threatened with false cases, unless they paid ₹25 lakh. The amount was later negotiated to ₹10 lakh, and ₹7 lakh was allegedly handed over near a Hyundai showroom before their release.
Appearing for the applicants, senior advocate Manoj Mohite argued, “The offences under which the Applicants and the Co-accused are charged are all bailable offences and hence, as of right, the applicants deserve to be enlarged on bail.” He contended that Section 140(2) was “appropriately dropped” during investigation and added, “If an officer detains someone for investigation, that does not constitute abduction, even if the person detained is later found innocent.”
Mr. Mohite further submitted, “It is the complainant and his friends who offered money to the Police and no demand was made by the Police personnel. They were not detained as they were allowed to move freely in the Headquarters.”
Opposing the plea, advocate Shreyas Uday Lalit, for the complainant, said: “The entire facts narrated in the FIR clearly establish illegal abduction without sufficient and justifiable cause, releasing them only on receiving the ransom as demanded. The ingredients of Section 140(2) of the BNS are adequately made out.”
He pointed out that the Daman magistrate had already taken cognisance of offences under Sections 140(2) and 308(2), both non-bailable. “The bail Court is not bound by an errant investigation,” he said. Mr. Lalit also submitted that the act attracts Section 7 of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988.
Rejecting the plea, Justice Gokhale cited Supreme Court rulings to underline that a magistrate is not bound by the investigating officer’s opinion, “The Magistrate can ignore the conclusion arrived at by the investigating officer and independently apply his mind to the facts emerging from the investigation, and take cognizance of the case.”
The magistrate’s order dated October 20, which remains unchallenged, amounted to taking cognizance of Section 140(2), punishable with death or life imprisonment and fine, and Section 308(2) for extortion.
The judge flagged contradictions in the investigation, “Strangely, on the same date, the same officer conveyed to the Magistrate that further investigation established offences under Section 140(2), yet filed the charge sheet under bailable sections. The entire conduct of the investigating agency is thus, questionable.”
The court also described the UT’s claim of “sterling investigation” as “a mere attempt to eye-wash the narrative before this Court.”
On the gravity of the offence, Justice Gokhale observed, “Crimes by police officials themselves, therefore, undermine the integrity of the entire justice system, erodes public confidence and compromises the fairness of legal proceedings. Law enforcement personnel are held to higher ethical and legal standard than ordinary citizens because their job requires public accountability and adherence to the law that they enforce.”
The court recorded that the accused had attempted to derail the probe by feigning illness and destroying electronic evidence, “They would immediately start to inflict injuries on themselves discreetly, vomited so that they can be immediately taken for medical examination, turn to the places where CCTV cameras are placed and start shouting.”
It noted that mobile phone data was deleted and recoveries included Apple AirPods and documents from the Crime Branch office.
Concluding that prima facie offences taken cognizance by the magistrate are made out, and considering the risk of tampering and intimidation, the court said, “The conduct of the applicants and the co-accused does not inspire confidence in this Court that they are not likely to tamper with evidence, and intimidate witnesses if enlarged on bail.”
The order added, “This is not a fit case to enlarge the applicants on bail. The bail application is thus, rejected.”

title: IFFK 2025 | ‘A Sad and Beautiful World’ movie review: a romantic drama infused with life, energy and resilience
summary: Discover the beauty and resilience in Cyril Aris's debut film, "A Sad and Beautiful World," a poignant romantic drama set in conflict.
content:
Nino and Yasmina occupy almost every frame in Lebanese filmmaker Cyril Aris’s debut featureA Sad and Beautiful World,just as expected in a romantic drama. It begins right from the opening sequence of their birth, a few minutes apart, in a hospital in Beirut. But by the end of the film, one gets a sense of what it is to be living in a region constantly mired in conflicts, where your life carefully built over decades can fall apart any moment.
Conflicts frame every major juncture in their life. The moment they open their eyes, the hospital in which they are admitted gets bombed, in a scene which immediately brings to mind the state of hospitals in present-day Gaza. Their childhood friendship is cut short by another spate of violent attacks from Israel. Decades later, they recognise each other amid a more local conflict between their family and friends.
But these violent events, which make a deep impression in our minds, appear on the screen only for a few fleeting moments. The rest of the time, we are immersed in the world of Nino and Yasmina, just like how they are immersed in each other’s worlds. It is what could have become a straightforward love story with all the usual conflicts that can happen in one. Yet, in Aris’s telling, it takes some exquisite turns in craft and narrative, which one would not normally expect from a debutant filmmaker.
Just like the house in Joachim Trier’sSentimental Value,another of the popular draws this year just likeA Sad and Beautiful World, Nino’s restaurant in the film turns into a space that almost feels like a character, making us feel the beauty and weight of their decades of laughter and pain witnessed by the walls. For that matter, there is more laughter than one would expect from a film of this nature.
Nino falls back on his innate humour and exuberance to get over even the most insurmountable crisis, while Yasmina appears to know her way around the world in a more practical sense. It is therefore natural that Nino hangs on to the restaurant which his family had opened decades ago with a sense of nostalgia, while Yasmina, a corporate consultant, is ready to move to safer shores. Yet, for all their contrasting nature, at no point would anyone imagine these two ending up with anyone else.
Hasan Akil and Mounia Akl  play the couple so convincingly that it feels like an extension of their own real-life personalities. Mounia is familiar to the audience at the International Film Festival of Kerala (IFFK) as the director of the superb ecological dramaCosta Brava, Lebanon,which was screened here in 2022. Then there are remarkable characters like Nino’s chief chef who is particular that he will not let customers customise the dishes he made, not even letting them add a pinch of salt. Some of the most beautiful moments in the film belong to Nino’s and Yasmina’s childhood, with the young actors deserving a special mention.
Aris infuses what could have been just another romantic drama with so much life and energy that it is no wonder thatA Sad and Beautiful Worldis one of the crowd favourites this year at the IFFK. The film is Lebanon’s official entry for the Best International Feature Film at the 98th Academy Awards.

title: RBI Governor asks CM to notify BUDS Act
summary: CM, RBI governor
content:
Hyderabad
Reserve Bank of India Governor Sanjay Malhotra has asked the Telangana Government to notify the BUDS (Banning of Unregulated Deposit Schemes) Act in the State.
The RBI Governor made the request to Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy on Thursday. Mr. Malhotra, who was here in connection with the RBI board meeting, called on the CM in the evening.
He explained about the initiatives taken by the apex bank on Unified Lending Interface (ULI) and also briefed him on the Government Private Deposit Claim campaign underway.
The CM informed Mr. Malhotra about the reforms ushered in different fields by the Congress Government in the State. He briefed the RBI Governor about the reforms in the energy sector and the decision to create a new power distribution company to cater to the needs of the categories supported by the Government.
Mr. Malhotra appreciated the fiscal policies of the Telangana Government and wanted it to bring in more reforms and progressive policies.

title: Water board MD responds after septage dumping video goes viral
summary: Water board MD responds after septage dumping video goes viral
content:
The Hyderabad Metropolitan Water Supply & Sewerage Board (HMWS&SB) has admitted that the twin reservoirs supplying drinking water to several parts of the city occasionally face the issue of pollution through sewage flow from the surrounding areas.
Through a video statement on Thursday, the Managing Director of the Board K. Ashok Reddy said over the years a few habitations have sprung in the areas surrounding the reservoirs from which sewage occasionally enters the water bodies. However, Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy has sanctioned ₹85 crore for construction of sewage treatment plants on either side of each reservoir which are expected to solve the problem. The STPs, four in number, will be ready within the next six months, after which the sewage entering the lakes may be fully treated.
The clarification came on the heels of a viral video clip which showed a tanker caught in the act of dumping septic waste into Osmansagar reservoir. The person who shot the video is seen accosting the tanker driver and questioning him about this infringement.
Responding to this, Mr. Ashok Reddy sought to clarify that an attempt was made to dump the septic waste into Gandipet reservoir through the tanker with the registered number TG11 T1833. A criminal case has been registered against the persons who resorted to this act, including driver of the tanker Ramavat Shiva Naik and the resident of Himayatnagar, Niranjan, at whose behest the dumping was attempted.
Moinabad police informed that cases were registered against both the accused under Section 279 of BNS that deals with fouling water of public spring or reservoir, and Section 43 of Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974.
Three kinds of serious violations were noted in the incident, first the illegal use of the the HMWS&SB’s  and GHMC’s logos on the tanker, unauthorised use of the vehicle for carrying sewage, and environmental pollution by way of mixing the septic waste in the protected reservoir.
Mr. Ashok Reddy informed that the tankers authorised to carry septic waste function through an app monitored by the Administrative Staff College of India. The tankers can be booked to carry the waste to any of the 45 STPs functioning in the city, where it can be treated.
Assuring that the water from the reservoirs is not polluted, he said the raw water is purified at Asif Nagar and Miralam treatment facilities before being pumped for the drinking water requirements. In future, it is planned to bring water from Godavari river and store in the reservoir, which rules out pollution, he said.

title: Kerala women’s panel unhappy over court verdicts in rape cases
summary: Kerala Women's Commission expresses dissatisfaction with recent court verdicts in rape cases, highlighting concerns over minimum sentencing.
content:
Kerala Women’s Commission Chairperson P. Sathidevi has expressed her displeasure over recent court verdicts in custodial rape and gang rape cases.
Addressing the media here on Thursday (December 18), she said that though ensuring maximum sentence in such cases was the norm, the judicial verdicts in some recent cases had gone against this. Ms. Sathidevi pointed out that it was a cause for concern that the accused in gang rape cases were getting only the minimum sentence.
Meanwhile, an official release quoting her said the Commission was not satisfied with the court verdict in the actor assault case. The Cyber police should take action against those who bully the survivor on social media, as per sections of the IT Act, Ms. Sathidevi said.

title: Army towers association files contempt plea as owner refuses to vacate
summary: CATAOA files contempt plea against a stubborn apartment owner refusing to vacate despite court-ordered demolition and safety concerns.
content:
In an unexpected turn of events, the Chander Kunj Army Towers Apartment Owners Association (CATAOA) has filed a contempt of court petition in the Kerala High Court against an apartment owner for refusing to vacate his flat, even after all the other 207 owners moved out of their apartments earmarked for demolition and reconstruction as per the court order.
CATAOA moved the petition before the same bench where apartment owner Ciby George, a resident of apartment number 101 in Tower C, had filed a contempt petition against the district collector for alleged non-compliance with the court’s verdict regarding the evacuation, demolition, and reconstruction of the twin towers. In August, the court had disposed of a writ appeal filed by the association and a few owners against the February 3 verdict of a Single Bench of the Kerala High Court — which had ordered demolition and reconstruction on grounds of serious structural problems — along with several related review petitions.
The committee chaired by the Collector is required to pay affected residents six months’ advance rent of ₹35,000 per month to owners in C Tower, ₹30,000 to owners in B Tower, and ₹30,000 as relocation charges, using funds transferred by the Army Welfare Housing Organisation into an escrow account held by the collector. Mr. George, a retired army colonel, continues to stay in his apartment, claiming he has not yet received the advance rent and relocation charges.
However, CATAOA office-bearers said they moved the petition after confirming that Mr. George had been paid three months’ rent from the escrow account, while the remaining three months were presumably deducted because he continued to stay in his own apartment during that period. “Our primary concern is his personal safety. A large chunk of concrete recently collapsed from the ceiling of the Tower C lobby. The association cannot be held responsible for his safety simply because he refuses to vacate. His reluctance is also disrupting the entire project schedule, as the twin towers were to be handed over to the tahsildar after all residents had evacuated. Moreover, utilities and infrastructure now have to be maintained solely for him, funded through collective maintenance charges,” said CATAOA office‑bearers.
While Mr. George admitted receiving ₹1.05 lakh in his account, he said there was no clarity on whether it was meant as advance rent or compensation, which he had demanded. He rejected the allegation that his continued stay had disrupted the project timeline, arguing that no steps had yet been taken to even finalise a demolition contractor. “I will move out the moment I am paid the advance rent and relocation charges,” he said.

title: Police dog ‘Sonu’ helps solve murder in Kadapa
summary: Police dog Sonu aids in solving a Kadapa murder case, leading to the swift arrest of the accused.
content:
Police dog ‘Sonu’ played a pivotal role in finding the accused in a murder that took place in Kadapa city on December 11 evening.
According the police, Vallepu Venkaiah alias Venkat was found dead at NGO plots in Swaraj Nagar on December 11, and based on the complaint by his mother Vallepu Subbamma, a case was registered at RIMS Police Station.
When the dog squad was pressed into service, Sonu reached the crime scene and went on the trail of the accused, significantly contributing to the rapid arrest of the accused.
On coming to know of Sonu moving around his residence, the accused, identified as Arun Kumar, and a juvenile reportedly involved in the case surrendered before the police through the Village Revenue Officer on December 17.
Arun was produced before a court, which remanded him in judicial custody. The minor was sent to a juvenile home. Material objects and electronic evidence like mobile phones, photographs have been forwarded for forensic examination.
Childhood friends Arun and Venkat turned into enemies after Arun failed to repay some money that Venkat had arranged for him by mortgaging his motorcycle. After Venkat hurled abuses at Arun’s family members, the latter nursed a grudge. He got him drunk and then hit him on his head with cement blocks, according to the police.
Sonu was recently inducted into the district police dog squad at Mangalagiri headquarters, on completion of the dual training on detecting explosives as well as criminals. Sub-Divisional Police Officer (Kadapa) A. Venkateswarlu called Sonu “a proven asset” and gave him a pat on its back, telling him: “Well done Sonu”.

title: BRS exudes confidence in political resurgence after GP poll triumph
