summary: BRS exudes confidence in political resurgence after GP poll triumph
content:
HYDERABAD
Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) working president K.T. Rama Rao said that the revival of the party had begun with BRS-backed candidates winning in the Gram Panchayat elections in the erstwhile Nalgonda district, the very region where the party earlier faced a setback. He added that the party is poised for sweeping victories in all the upcoming elections.
Addressing a felicitation meeting for newly-elected Sarpanches in Bhuvanagiri on Thursday, Mr. Rao asserted that people are now realising the reality of Congress ‘misrule’ and extending decisive support to BRS.
“Despite Congress intimidation and misuse of power, people delivered a clear verdict in the Panchayat elections. BRS secured 161 Sarpanch seats across Yadadri Bhuvanagiri district. This mandate has infused renewed confidence among party cadre across Telangana and marked the beginning of BRS’s return to its former glory,“ KTR said.
Responding to Assembly Speaker’s decision on MLAs’ defections, KTR said the Congress government has normalised defections as a survival tool, destroying democratic values.
Taking a swipe at Chief Minister Revanth Reddy, the former minister said that the CM had made tall claims and failed to deliver them.
Meanwhile, BRS senior leader and Siddipet MLA T. Harish Rao said the Sarpanch election results clearly indicate Mr. Revanth Reddy’s declining popularity. He also claimed that people are revolting against the State government as it has failed to deliver on its six guarantees.
Harish Rao
Speaking at a felicitation ceremony for BRS-backed Sarpanches in the Medak constituency, Mr. Rao said that the ruling party in any State normally secures 80 to 90 percent of Sarpanch seats. However, despite the Chief Minister personally campaigning and allegedly violating the election code, the Congress was restricted to less than 50 percent, while BRS-backed candidates secured over 40 percent of the seats. He added that the Chief Minister’s fear of BRS’s growing momentum would prevent him from conducting ZPTC and MPTC elections anytime soon.
Mr. Harish Rao further highlighted that the promise of 42% BC reservation remains unfulfilled, Rythu Bandhu has been stalled, and farm loan waivers have reached less than half of the intended beneficiaries.

title: SDPI credits K.S. Shan’s legacy for election success in Alappuzha
summary: The success of the Social Democratic Party of India (SDPI) candidates in the recently held local body elections in Alappuzha district is a reflection of the public’s solidarity with K.S. Shan, SDPI State president C.P.A. Latheef has said.
content:
The success of the Social Democratic Party of India (SDPI) candidates in the recently held local body elections in Alappuzha district is a reflection of the public’s solidarity with K.S. Shan, SDPI State president C.P.A. Latheef has said.
He was speaking at the K.S. Shan memorial meeting in Alappuzha on Thursday. Shan, who was the party’s State Secretary, was attacked by assailants at Kuppezham Junction at Mannancherry in Alappuzha around 7.30 p.m. on December 18, 2021, and succumbed to his injuries around 11.30 p.m.
Mr. Latheef said that Shan continues to live on in the hearts of the people. “Despite all opponents uniting against the SDPI in the local body polls, the party was able to strengthen its foundation. Political parties, including the Indian Union Muslim League, even allied with the BJP in an attempt to defeat SDPI candidates. Secular Kerala must reflect on the message such efforts convey,” he added.

title: Curb wildlife attacks on people: Catholic Bishops Council
summary: The Kerala CSI Bishops’ Council, which held a two-days long meeting in Kottayam, has urged both the Central and State governments to take proactive measures to curb the ongoing wildlife attacks that pose a serious threat to human lives.
content:
The Kerala CSI Bishops’ Council, which held a two-days long meeting in Kottayam, has urged both the Central and State governments to take proactive measures to curb the ongoing wildlife attacks that pose a serious threat to human lives. The council also called on the State government to ensure equal rights for all school managements in the recruitment of differently abled persons.
Deputy Moderator Bishop V.S. Francis was elected president of the Kerala CSI Bishops’ Council, while Bishop Dr. Malayil Sabu Koshi Cheriyan was appointed Secretary. Bishop Kurian Peter of the Kochi Diocese was elected Regional Chairman of the Youth Fellowship, and Bishop Jose George of the Kollam-Kottarakkara Diocese was named Chairman of the Sunday School Fellowship.
The council also emphasized the urgent need for the implementation of the Justice J.B. Koshy Commission report.

title: Forest Department wins in Supreme Court, gets back 102 acres of land
summary: Forest Department wins in Supreme Court, gets back 102 acres of land
content:
The Telangana Forest Department scored a major victory in Supreme Court on Thursday, when over 102 acres of land in Sahebnagar Kalan of Ranga Reddy district was declared a part of the reserve forest, Gurramguda reserve forest block, and not private land.
The victory is especially important because the department faced defeat at lower courts as well as the Telangana High Court, officials informed. A few people claiming to be the legal heirs of Salar Jung III, Mir Yousuf Ali Khan, tried to usurp the land, they said.
The apex court supported the State government’s stand over the land, and overruled the previous orders to the contrary, a statement from the District Forest Officer Rohith Gopidi said. The land is thus a continuing stretch of the forest block.
The judgment by Justices Pankaj Mithal and S.V.N. Bhatti also noticed that lung spaces were shrinking in all cities, and the twin cities of Hyderabad and Secunderabad were no exception. It directed the Telangana Chief Secretary to ensure completion of the pending proposals and declare the land as reserve forest within eight weeks and to file compliance report.

title: Dedicated multi-level parking app to be launched to address traffic congestion
summary: A new multi-level parking app in Hyderabad aims to reduce traffic congestion by helping motorists find nearby parking spaces.
content:
A dedicated multi-level parking app would soon be launched to help motorists locate nearby parking spaces to address growing traffic congestion commercial zones across Hyderabad. The development was shared by the GHMC Commissioner R.V. Karnan during a convergence meeting, held at the Telangana Integrated Command and Control Centre in Banjara Hills on Thursday (December 18, 2025).
With parking emerging as a major contributor to congestion, particularly in busy commercial and hospital zones, the meeting decided to expand multi-level parking facilities across the city.  “This app will allow vehicle owners to easily locate nearby parking spaces,” the official said.
The meeting was chaired by Hyderabad Police Commissioner V.C. Sajjanar and attended by top officials from the Greater Hyderabad Municipal Corporation, the traffic police wings of Hyderabad, Rachakonda and Cyberabad, Hyderabad Disaster Response and Asset Monitoring and Protection Agency (HYDRAA), the Water Board and the electricity department. The discussions focused on practical, inter-departmental solutions to long-pending urban mobility and infrastructure problems.
Several infrastructure changes were also discussed to improve traffic flow and pedestrian safety. These included relocating bus stops that currently choke narrow roads to stretches with wider carriageways, shifting Sulabh complexes located on road medians or carriageways, and constructing foot overbridges at locations where frequent pedestrian crossings slow down traffic and increase accident risks. The installation of central railings in accident-prone areas such as Puranapul, Bahadurpura, M.J. Market, Masab Tank and Begumpet was proposed to prevent haphazard road crossings.
HYDRAA Commissioner A.V. Ranganath said inspections of waterlogged areas during the rainy season would be intensified to identify permanent solutions, while steps were being taken to remove encroachments on footpaths. Joint Commissioner of Police (Traffic) D. Joel Davis outlined several on-ground challenges, including poorly placed bus stops, road-blocking public toilets, lack of pedestrian infrastructure and indiscriminate parking of auto-rickshaws, particularly near Osmania Hospital. He called for immediate allocation of designated auto parking spaces to ease congestion.
Cyberabad Joint Commissioner of Police Gajarao Bhupal suggested that to avoid delays after road digging, both excavation and restoration work should be entrusted to the same contractor. Water Works Managing Director Ashok Reddy said efforts were underway to further strengthen the city’s sewerage and drainage systems and stressed that lasting solutions would be possible only through close coordination among all departments.
The meeting was attended by additional and zonal commissioners, traffic deputy commissioners of police and senior officials from HMDA, GHMC, the cantonment board, the Hyderabad Metropolitan Water Supply and Sewerage Board and other departments.

title: MLC seeks use of temple funds for development of villages near M.M. Hills
summary: MLC K. Shivakumar advocates using Sri Male Mahadeshwara temple funds to enhance infrastructure in nearby Chamarajanagar villages.
content:
MLC K. Shivakumar has said that the revenue generated by the Sri Male Mahadeshwara temple should be utilised to develop basic infrastructure in the villages surrounding Male Mahadeshwara Hills in Chamarajanagar district.
The MLC said that the temple earns crores of rupees annually and suggested that amendments be made to set aside a portion of the income for the development of local villages.
Mr. Shivakumar, who was speaking during the Winter Session of the Legislative Assembly at Suvarna Vidhana Soudha in Belagavi, said several villages in the region have been deprived of basic amenities and added that the absence of proper roads has caused severe hardship to residents. Women are forced to walk difficult forest paths daily to fetch drinking water, he pointed out.
Due to poor road connectivity, pregnant women are often carried in cloth slings to hospitals during delivery. Even the sick elderly people are also compelled to walk several kilometres to access medical care. Such conditions amount to a violation of human rights, he observed.
The people who have lived on the hill for generations are the true devotees of Lord Mahadeshwara and also serve as protectors of the forest. While the temple development can continue, a portion of its resources should be utilised for benefitting the local population, he added.
Welcoming the government’s recent move to hold a Cabinet meeting atop the hill and announce several development projects, he described it as a positive step.

title: Congress Working Committee to meet on December 27
summary: The Congress Working Committee will meet on December 27 to discuss the repeal of MGNREGA and upcoming election strategies.
content:
The Congress Working Committee, the party’s highest decision-making body, will meet on December 27 to deliberate on thegovernment’s move to replacetheMahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act(MGNREGA) with new legislation, sources said on Thursday (December 18, 2025).
The MGNREGA was a flagship scheme introduced by the United Progressive Alliance (UPA) government in its first term in 2005.
This would be the first meeting of the CWC following the debacle the party faced in theBihar Assembly election. It also assumes significance as the party’s strategy for the next round of Assembly elections in the first half of 2026 — in Assam, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, Kerala, and West Bengal — could be framed.
The Opposition party is also looking to up the ante over the repeal of the MGNREGA, and to construct a campaign around the issue.
An open letter to the Indian government in support of the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act
CM Mamata slams Centre over G RAM G bill, says Bengal’s job scheme will be renamed after Gandhi
Watch: Change for the worse: On MGNREGA to VB-G RAM G
‘VB-G RAM G’ Bill will weaken MGNREGA: Priyanka Gandhi
This is not merely a case of renaming MGNREGA but the “systematic murder of the world’s largest employment scheme”, Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge said, speaking about the Viksit Bharat Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB-G RAM G) Bill.
The Union Government was taking away the right to work from people, and “there will be a nationwide movement against it”, Mr. Kharge said.

title: BJP to rope in national leaders for ‘Atal Modi Suparipalana Yatra’
summary: BJP's 'Atal Modi Suparipalana Yatra' will feature national leaders and conclude in Amaravati on December 25, honoring A.B. Vajpayee.
content:
BJP’s flagship programme, ‘Atal Modi Suparipalana Yatra’, which is currently under way across Andhra Pradesh, will soon witness the participation of senior national leaders.
Though it is a pan-India programme, the Andhra Pradesh unit, led by its president P.V.N. Madhav, has converted it into a ‘Bus Yatra’ to highlight the achievements of former Prime Minister A.B. Vajpayee across the State on his birth centenary year by unveiling his bronze statue in every district headquarters.
The yatra started in Dharmavaram, where Madhya Pradesh Chief Minister Mohan Yadav unveiled the statue. Later, it was the turn of Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami to unveil the statues in Madanapalle and Tirupati on the fourth day.
Union Minister Bhupathiraju Srinivasa Varma, State Ministers N. Lokesh, P. Keshav, A. Ramanarayana Reddy, Satya Kumar Yadav, G. Ravikumar, K. Parthasarathy, N.Md. Farooq, B.C. Janardhan Reddy and A. Satya Prasad took part in the statue-unveiling events during the first phase that concluded December 16.
In the second phase, the party plans to rope in former Vice-President M. Venkaiah Naidu (Vizianagaram), Chhattisgarh Chief Minister Vishnu Deo Sai (Rajamahendravaram and Kakinada), Union Minister Bandi Sanjay (Visakhapatnam), B. Srinivasa Varma (Bhimavaram), BJP national secretary K. Annamalai (Eluru), and Agriculture Minister K. Atchannaidu (Srikakulam).
The concluding session of the second phase will be a grand event in Amaravati on December 25, which also marks the birth anniversary of Mr. Vajpayee.
“We are expecting the arrival of Home Minister Amit Shah or Minister for Road Transport Nitin Gadkari or Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis for the event, who will share the dais with Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu and Deputy Chief Minister K. Pawan Kalyan,” said yatra convener N. Ramesh Naidu.
“This yatra will pay fitting tribute to the tall leader, known for his value-based politics and good governance,” Mr. Ramesh Naidu said.

title: Munambam land: HC asks officials to allow only collection of land tax
summary: Kerala High Court limits authorities to only collect land tax from residents of disputed Munambam land, amid ongoing legal disputes.
content:
The Kerala High Court has restrained the authorities concerned from permitting anything other than the acceptance of land tax from persons living in disputed land at Munambam, which the Waqf Board claimed was Waqf property.
On being informed that the authorities permitted mutation and also accepted register of rights, beyond what was permitted in the court’s previous order, the court orally observed that the court had permitted only payment of tax and nothing beyond that. The court was hearing a batch of petitions, including by the Munambam Bhoo Samrakshana Samiti, and people who lived on the said land. The matter has been posted for hearing on January 14.
The High Court had in November, through an interim order, directed the Revenue department to temporarily accept land tax from the over 600 families in the disputed land at Munambam. This followed a plea by the Samiti and others who submitted that the village officer concerned was not accepting tax, citing Waqf Board claims over the property. They thus sought a directive to the District Collector and the tahsildar to accept land tax and to effect mutation, transfer, issue encumbrance certificate, and also changes in Tandaper register in relation to the property situated in Kuzhuppilly village. The court had then permitted the officials concerned to accept tax from the petitioners and similarly placed persons provisionally, subject to the result of the proceedings regarding the land pending before the Supreme Court.

title: ELCOT inks MoU with Perplexity AI to train college students in Tamil Nadu
summary: ELCOT partners with Perplexity AI to offer free AI training for Tamil Nadu college students, amid political laptop distribution debates.
content:
The Electronics Corporation of Tamil Nadu Limited (ELCOT) inked a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Perplexity AI to provide training to college students in Tamil Nadu in Perplexity Pro AI for six months free of cost,Tamil NaduDeputy Chief Minister Udhayanidhi Stalin said on Thursday (December 18, 2025).
In a statement, the Deputy Chief Minister rejected the criticism of AIADMK general secretary Edappadi K. Palaniswami over the distribution of laptops to students in the middle of the academic year. Mr. Udhayanidhi Stalin said the announcement for distribution of laptops was made in the Budget session.
Once students returned after the vacation for Christmas and New Year, laptops would be distributed to them in all districts in phases, the Deputy Chief Minister said. By February, 10 lakh laptops would be distributed to students.
The Deputy Chief Minister contended that the AIADMK leader was against the distribution of laptops to students and further charged, "Mr. Palaniswami has been consistently expressing the intention of the fascist BJP that the students of Tamil Nadu should not get education and develop."
Charging that Mr. Palaniswami was attempting to prevent the distribution of laptops, Mr. Udhayanidhi Stalin said his government would certainly distribute the laptops and that neither Mr. Palaniswami nor "his Delhi owners" could prevent the distribution.
The government was intending to distribute laptops to students with software that could be used by engineers, Mr. Udhayanidhi Stalin said, and added that ELCOT had signed an MoU with Microsoft in this regard.
During an event in Chennai, the Deputy Chief Minister inaugurated an exhibition organised by the Tamil Nadu Corporation for Development of Women involving women self-help groups at Nungambakkam in Chennai.

title: Govt. did not spend a rupee on Messi event: Revanth Reddy
summary: Govt. did not spend a rupee on Messi event: Revanth Reddy
content:
Hyderabad
Clarifying his presence at football legend Messi’s match in Hyderabad recently, Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy said that he attended it only as a guest and categorically stated that no government funds were spent.
Mr. Reddy explained that CSR funds released by Singareni Collieries Company Limited for promotional activities were used for the event strictly, as per a decision taken by the Singareni Board.
In an informal chat with reporters on Thursday, the Chief Minister said that he wanted his grandson to become a sportsperson and therefore took him to the stadium, while taking a dig at the BRS leadership that he does not take children to pubs.
On the Formula E race case, the Chief Minister said the government would proceed strictly in accordance with established rules and procedures. He said permission is required to question senior officer Arvind Kumar and that the State has already written twice to the Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT).
“Once approval is received, the investigation will move forward. At present, only permissions related to KTR have come,” he said. Turning to irregularities in the employment of contract and outsourcing employees, he said that several fake Aadhaar documents were found and inquiry was ordered into all such cases.

title: Assault case: bail plea of P.T. Kunju Muhammed posted on Saturday
summary: Filmmaker P.T. Kunju Muhammed's bail plea in a sexual assault case postponed to Saturday amid conflicting claims from both parties.
content:
The Principal Sessions Court, Thiruvananthapuram, on Thursday posted an anticipatory bail plea filed by filmmaker and former Left-backed Independent MLA P.T. Kunju Muhammed in a sexual assault case for Saturday (December 20, 2025).
In the hearing held here on Thursday, the counsel who appeared for Mr. Muhammed argued that the case was fabricated and alleged that the woman had trespassed into his room. His charges were strongly refuted by the prosecution while opposing his bail plea.
After a detailed hearing, the case was posted for Saturday. The police case was that on November 6, Mr. Muhammed invited the woman to his suite room on the pretext of discussing the movie selection process and outraged her modesty, forcing the survivor to flee. On November 26, the woman petitioned the Chief Minister’s Office, who forwarded the complaint to State Police Chief Ravada Chandrasekhar for further investigation.
On December 2, the Cantonment police charged Mr. Muhammed with offences of outraging the modesty of a woman, illegal detention, intimidation, and trespass under the various sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.

title: Employee unions stage protest in Ballari against 100% FDI in insurance
summary: Employees in Ballari protest against 100% FDI in insurance, fearing it will jeopardize the domestic sector and policyholder interests.
content:
Nearly 200 employees from the banking and insurance sectors staged a joint demonstration in Ballari on Thursday opposing the Union government’s move to allow 100% Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) in the insurance sector.
The protest was staged in front of the LIC Branch-2 office following a joint call given by nine national trade unions.
Employees affiliated to the All India Insurance Employees Association (AIIEA), All India Bank Employees Association (AIBEA), Bank Employees Federation of India (BEFI), National Confederation of Bank Employees (NCBE), All India Bank Officers Confederation (AIBOC), LIC Class-I Officers Federation and pensioners of the All India Insurance Pensioners Association (AIIPA) participated in the agitation.
Addressing a gathering, D.V. Suryanarayana, who led the protest and coordinated the programme in Ballari, said that the proposed hike in FDI limit from 74% to 100% will seriously undermine the domestic insurance sector.
He said that the move will effectively hand over control of India’s long-term household savings to foreign capital which is against the interests of policyholders and the broader economy.
Quoting the joint appeal issued by the trade unions, Mr. Suryanarayana said that the Insurance Laws (Amendment) Bill 2025, if passed, will allow foreign investors greater control over Indian insurance companies without bringing any tangible benefit to the common public.
“The existing FDI limit of 74% is more than sufficient for capital infusion. Increasing it to 100% will neither deepen insurance penetration nor strengthen public sector insurers like LIC,” he said.
He cautioned that higher foreign control will push insurers to focus on high net-worth clients and profit-driven products, sidelining social security objectives and insurance coverage for the poor, rural population and marginalised sections.
He also expressed concern that foreign partners can exit joint ventures at will, destabilising the sector.
As a symbolic mark of protest, the agitating employees switched on their mobile phone lights expressing strong resentment against what they termed a “retrograde policy decision” of the Centre.

title: India issued 200 medical visas since launch of new Afghan visa in April: Health Ministry
summary: India has issued over 200 medical visas to support Afghanistan's healthcare, reaffirming commitment to humanitarian needs and infrastructure projects.
content:
Since the launch of the new Afghan visa module in April 2025, more than 500 visas, including over 200 medical visas, have been issued in the last four months, noted a senior Health Ministry official on Thursday (December 18, 2025) adding that India has now approved and implemented several key healthcare infrastructure projects in Afghanistan.
These include the construction of five maternity and health clinics in the provinces of Paktia, Khost and Paktika, a 30-bed hospital in Kabul, and the construction or upgradation of major facilities such as an Oncology Centre, Trauma Centre, Diagnostic Centre and Thalassemia Centre in Kabul. Additional proposals for health sector support are currently under active consideration.
On Thursday, India reaffirmed its continued commitment to supporting Afghanistan’s health sector and humanitarian needs during a meeting held between Union Minister for Health and Family Welfare J.P. Nadda and Afghanistan’s Minister of Public Health Mawlawi Noor Jalal Jalali.
During the meeting, both sides reviewed ongoing health cooperation and discussed avenues to further strengthen collaboration in healthcare infrastructure, medical supplies and capacity building.
The Union Minister underlined that guided by India’s long-standing people-centric approach, Prime Minister Narendra Modi has always emphasised that India’s engagement with Afghanistan should remain focused on welfare, capacity building and access to critical healthcare services.
Mr. Nadda added that India’s assistance to Afghanistan remains guided by humanitarian considerations and the long-standing bonds between the peoples of the two countries.
“India has supplied 327 tonnes of medicines and vaccines to Afghanistan over the past four years. Cancer medicines and one CT scan machine, as requested by the Afghan Ministry of Public Health, are ready for dispatch and will be delivered by the end of this month. Proposals from the Afghan side for a radiotherapy machine and additional medical supplies are also being processed,” the Health Minister said.
The meeting also discussed capacity-building initiatives. India is working on modalities to send a team of senior Indian doctors to Afghanistan to organise a medical camp and provide training to Afghan doctors. The success of the Jaipur Foot Camp organised in Kabul in June 2025, where 75 prosthetic limbs were fitted, was highlighted, with plans to organise more such camps in the coming year.
“At the meeting, India has reiterated its commitment to providing free treatment in India to Afghan patients suffering from emergency and serious ailments, and to facilitating medical visas,” said a Health Ministry official.

title: CM pats Nellore Collector for ‘Champion Farmers’ initiative
summary: CM lauds Nellore Collector's 'Champion Farmers' initiative for agricultural reforms, aiming to boost farmer income and sustainable practices.
content:
Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu on Thursday (December 18) lauded SPSR Nellore District Collector Himanshu Shukla’s concept of ‘Champion Farmers’, calling it an innovative initiative and a good experiment. He congratulated Mr. Himanshu Shukla for designing this programme to directly benefit the farmers by comprehensively connecting all the departments.
On the second day of the Collectors’ Conference held under the chairmanship of the Chief Minister at the Secretariat in Amaravati, Mr. Himanshu Shukla presented the details of the ‘Champion Farmers’ programme, explaining water reserves, crop patterns and the measures taken to increase farmers’ income.
“Champion Farmers programme has been launched with an aim of bringing comprehensive reforms in the agricultural sector of the district. Although the area under cultivation has decreased in the past few years, the situation has changed from 2024. This year, there is 75 TMC of water storage at 100-meter level in Somasila Reservoir.”
“Under these circumstances, the main objective of the ‘Champion Farmers’ programme is to redirect the farmers towards alternative crops. This programme also addresses issues such as shortage of agricultural labourers, lack of farm mechanisation, excessive use of fertilizers and pesticides, lack of market linkages and lack of investment in food processing and value addition,” he said.
One ‘Champion Farmer’ has been identified in each village across 727 panchayats of the district, and he will act as a role model and ambassador for that village, the Collector said, adding that these Champion Farmers will be trained to use the latest agricultural techniques and continuously guided by the local Village Agricultural Assistants (VAAs) for the next couple of years.
The Chief Minister lauded Mr. Himanshu Shukla for designing the programme to efficiently utilise the human resources. He said, “The self-help groups should be formed through ‘Champion Farmers’ or they should be transformed into MSMEs (Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises). There is a need to extend these policies to horticultural crops as well, not just seasonal crops.”
“The purpose of programmes like ‘Rythanna Mee Kosam’ is also to provide ultimate benefit to the farmers,” he said, advising the Collectors of all districts to raise awareness about the government policies for the benefit of the farmers through Rythu Seva Kendra (RSKs) and Swarna Andhra Vision Action Plan Units.
“All measures should be taken to make agricultural mechanisation clusters easily accessible to the farmers as well as to reduce the agricultural costs and maximise their incomes,” the CM suggested.

title: Jagan’s flawed understanding of PPP model exposed, says Lanka Dinakar
summary: NDA leaders criticize YSRCP's contradictory stance on PPP model, highlighting Jagan's flawed understanding and hindrance to healthcare progress.
content:
Several NDA leaders have criticised the YSRCP for opposing the Public Private Partnership (PPP) model of developing medical colleges.
Addressing the media in Amaravati on Wednesday, Lanka Dinakar, Chairman of the 20-Point Programme, alleged that YSRCP president and former Chief Minister Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy was creating unnecessary apprehensions on the issue.
Mr. Dinakar said the YSRCP president’s remarks reflected his flawed understanding of the PPP framework, which had been used extensively during his term in extending public health services such as Aarogyasri and emergency ambulance network.
Mr. Dinakar pointed out that medical services delivered through PPP were earlier projected as government initiatives by the YSRCP.
The BJP leader said the coalition government was focused on completing the construction of the stalled medical colleges and expanding healthcare access. He said the YSRCP allegations and protests were hindering progress.
Mr. Dinakar further observed that lack of clarity on the PPP  model among the YSRCP MPs was evident during their recent interaction with the Union Finance Minister.
Sharing a similar view, TDP official spokesperson and Swachh Andhra Corporation Chairman K. Pattabhiram said the YSRCP was adopting contradictory stance on the PPP model.
Speaking in Mangalagiri, Mr. Pattabhiram noted that the YSRCP MPs had endorsed private participation in medical education at the national level, including the recommendations of the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Health and Family Welfare. “This contrast between the party’s stance in Delhi and its protests in Andhra Pradesh has created confusion among the people,” he said.

title: Action plan ready to revive polluted rivers, says Minister
summary: Karnataka Minister Eshwar Khandre announces an action plan to revive polluted rivers, addressing wastewater issues affecting communities.
content:
Minister for Forests and Ecology Eshwar Khandre said in Belagavi on Thursday that domestic wastewater generated from residential areas of municipalities and villages in the river basin is directly or indirectly entering 12 rivers in the State causing death of marine life and affecting the lives of residents of 30 urban and rural areas.
Responding to a question by member Darshan Puttannaiah in the Aassembly, he said that a time-bound action plan has been prepared to revive such rivers.
The Karnataka State Pollution Control Board is trying to effectively implement the Water Pollution (Control and Prevention) Act 1974 and is issuing establishment permits and operating consent letters under Sections 25 and 26 of the 1974 Act.
These include ensuring that wastewater generated by industries is treated and reused. It is the duty of the industries to adopt wastewater treatment plants to treat wastewater and treat and purify it to the prescribed quality standards and reuse it.
Though several urban local bodies have set up solid waste management units and sewage treatment plants, there is still a need to purify 203 million litres of water per day. As many as 19 ULBs are working on setting up sewage treatment plants.
The Karnataka State Pollution Control Board has also suggested adopting Wetland Treatment System for treating sewage entering rivers through drains. The board has filed criminal complaints against officials in 11 towns and issued notices to officers in 12 others.

title: Tiger captured near Gundlupet easing villagers’ fears
summary: A four-year-old tiger captured near Gundlupet brings relief to anxious villagers, ensuring safety after recent livestock attacks.
content:
A four-year-old male tiger was captured by a Forest Department team in the early hours of Thursday from a barren land at Bommalapura village, near the Bandipur Tiger Reserve. The big cat is healthy and has been safely shifted to Bandipur, where it is being closely monitored by a team of veterinarians.
The capture has brought immense relief to villagers and farmers living around the Gundlupet buffer zone of the tiger reserve, who had been living in fear following sightings of the tiger and incidents of livestock attacks.
Tiger sighting was reported in Bommalapura, K.K. Hundi, Shivapura, Kodasoge, Hullepura, Devapura and surrounding villages, triggering panic among the local population.
Acting on the complaints, the Forest Department installed camera traps in the area, through which the animal was identified as Bandipur-26 (GPS). After several attempts over the past few days, forest officials captured the tiger on Thursday.
The operation was led by Deputy Conservator of Forests S. Prabhakaran under the guidance of the Principal Chief Conservator of Forests (Wildlife), Bengaluru, and the Additional Principal Chief Conservator of Forests (Wildlife), Bengaluru. The Gundlupet taluk administration and the Police Department extended support during the operation.
According to a note issued by the Assistant Conservator of Forests (ACF), Gundlupet, the tiger was shifted safely to Bandipur under veterinary supervision, and the authorities are awaiting further instructions regarding its future management.
Meanwhile, villagers have been advised to clear overgrown shrubs and weeds in their uncultivated fields, as such vegetation could serve as hiding places for wild animals. The Forest Department has written to the authorities concerned, urging them to act on its request to remove thick bushes and shrubs in vulnerable areas.

title: Public satisfaction is true measure of officials' performance, says Naidu
summary: Naidu emphasizes public satisfaction as the key measure of officials' performance and plans surprise inspections to assess government delivery.
content:
The two-day Collectors’ Conference ended on Thursday with an assertion by Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu that public satisfaction was the only true measure of the officers' performance and announcement of surprise inspections by him beginning in January.
“Numbers do matter but I will not entirely believe them. I will soon make field visits to see for myself to what extent the  government’s promises are being delivered,” he said, reiterating that the NDA was under the obligation to fulfil the people’s wishes.
Mr. Chandrababu Naidu said the government would fix a Welfare Calendar in April 2026 and wanted the ​Central funds to be fully utilised in order to garner additional sums for implementation of the Centrally Sponsored Schemes. He ordered that the presentations given by the Collectors of six districts on best practices related to various departments adopted by them to be followed across the State to achieve better results.
He told the Collectors to duly focus on resolving the ‘22-A land disputes’, noting that they were an impediment to development in many areas, and to register cases under the Preventive Detention Act against individuals committing frauds thereof.
The CM went on to instruct the Collectors and SPs not to tolerate political interference in land disputes, when Deputy CM K. Pawan Kalyan pointed it out by citing some specific instances in Visakhapatnam district. He exhorted the Collectors to eliminate corruption in the Registration Department. Boats should be immediately purchased for strengthening coastal security.
Speed of Delivering Governance should be the new norm, he said, adding that the Collectors should strive to realise the potential of the respective districts in various fields.
In a social media post, the Chief Minister said he reviewed the progress achieved in the last 18 months and reflected on key areas to strengthen governance. “Accountability to the people is central to our responsibility, and service to them is our foremost duty. Collectors are the brand ambassadors of the government. I encourage them to lead by example and continue working with commitment to improve the lives of citizens,” he stated.

title: Kerala stands for pro-worker development policy: Minister
summary: Kerala's Minister emphasizes a pro-worker development policy, opposing Union government actions at the upcoming Labour Conclave 2025.
content:
Kerala favours a development policy that has a pro-worker perspective, Minister for Labour V. Sivankutty has said.
‘Labour Conclave 2025’ that will be inaugurated by Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan in the State capital on Friday is part of the State’s strong responses to the anti-worker policies of the Union government, a statement by the Minister ahead of the conclave on Thursday said.
The conclave, the Minister said, sought to create a resistance against Union government policies that took away States’ powers and rights. The move to implement the four Labour Codes that replace 29 laws was intended to undermine rights and protections that workers had managed to secure after many struggles. The Labour Codes paved the way for corporate greed and modern slavery though the Union government claimed these would help to increase investment and create job opportunities. Safety guidelines for industrial establishments had been simplified and wage provisions watered down to increase the uncertainty in the labour sector.
Besides building up resistance against the Labour Codes, the conclave sought to come up with strategies to counter Union government laws and announce a policy to protect the State’s labour culture.
Instead of seeing workers merely as resources, they should been as protectors of the States, the Minister said in the statement.

title: Shivakumar to inquire into ‘diversion’ of Bhima waters by Maharashtra
summary: Shivakumar will investigate Maharashtra's alleged over-utilization of Bhima waters, addressing concerns raised in the Legislative Council.
content:
Deputy Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar, who holds the Water Resources portfolio, told the Legislative Council here on Thursday that he will inquire into the issue of reported over utilisation of Bhima waters by the neighbouring State of Maharashtra.
Replying to a question raised by member Talawar Sabanna under Rule 330 in the Council, Mr. Shivakumar said that what has been pointed out by the member is an issue of serious nature and that he will inquire into it and get a report on the said utilisation of more than allocated share of waters by Maharashtra.
Earlier, raising the issue, Mr. Sabanna said that while the allocated share of water in the Bhima under the Bachawat Commission is 95 tmcft for Maharashtra and 15 tmcft for Karnataka, the neighbouring State is utilizing close to 200 tmcft by diverting water to the Sina river through a tunnel.
Consequently, the farmers of Vijayapura, Yadgir and Kalaburagi districts are facing water scarcity, he said and urged the Minister to send a team to look into the issue.

title: Karnataka Govt. exploring annual contracts to ensure price stability of eggs
summary: The State government was exploring several options like annual contracts to see that the price of eggs supplied to students remained stable throughout the year, Minister for School Education and Literacy  Madhu Bangarappa said here on Thursday.
content:
The State government was exploring several options like annual contracts to see that the price of eggs supplied to students remained stable throughout the year, Minister for School Education and Literacy  Madhu Bangarappa said here on Thursday.
He was responding to a question by Harish Poonja in the Legislative Assembly, who said that government school teachers in charge of midday meals were forced to contribute some money whenever the prices of eggs rose.
“We are aware of the problems faced by teachers. As of now, the government is paying for procurement of eggs two days a week. The Azim Premji Foundation is paying for eggs bought on four other days of the week. We are releasing fixed amounts of money to schools for egg purchase. But then, we cannot increase our rates only for two days. We are trying to find a solution to the problem,’’ he said.
Speaker U.T. Khadar intervened by saying that the government had to find a long-term solution to the problem, as the price of eggs kept fluctuating. The Minister said the government was considering entering into annual contracts to ensure price stability.
V. Sunil Kumar wanted to know if the government was sure that consuming eggs was safe for children, in the wake of news reports that eggs could contain carcinogenic materials.
Health Minister Dinesh Gundu Rao said studies had shown that eating eggs was safe and nutritious, and that the news reports had referred only to one brand of eggs that allegedly contained some carcinogenic elements.

title: ICG Ship Anmol Apprehends Two Bangladeshi Fishing Boats in India’s EEZ
summary: ICG Ship Anmol apprehends two Bangladeshi fishing boats in India’s EEZ, highlighting efforts against illegal fishing activities.
content:
Indian Coast Guard (ICG) Ship Anmol, while undertaking routine surveillance operations in the Northern Bay of Bengal on Tuesday (16 December, 2025), apprehended two Bangladeshi fishing boats along with 35 crew members for engaging in illegal fishing activities inside India’s Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ).
ICG on Thursday (December 18, 2025) informed that the apprehension was carried out for violation of the Maritime Zones of India (MZI) (Regulation of Fishing by Foreign Vessels) Act, 1981. The presence of active fishing gear and approximately 500 kilograms of fish catch on board the boats clearly indicated that fishing operations were being conducted within Indian waters.
Following the interception, the apprehended fishing boats and their crew were taken into custody by the Indian Coast Guard and subsequently handed over to the Marine Police at Frazerganj on 17 December 2025 for further legal proceedings in accordance with applicable laws, it said.
This operation underscores the Indian Coast Guard’s steadfast commitment to safeguarding India’s maritime interests, preventing illegal fishing and ensuring the safety and security of Indian fishermen operating in the region. The ICG has maintained heightened vigilance in the Bay of Bengal to deter unlawful activities that threaten marine resources and maritime security.
Over the last three months, the Indian Coast Guard has apprehended eight Bangladeshi fishing boats along with 170 crew members for similar violations, reflecting sustained enforcement efforts against illegal fishing in India’s maritime zones.
The Indian Coast Guard continues to maintain a robust operational presence across India’s maritime areas, enforcing maritime law, protecting marine resources and promoting responsible and lawful use of the seas.

title: Man charred to death as parked car catches fire in Palakkad
summary: A man was killed in Palakkad when his parked car caught fire, prompting a police investigation into the incident.
content:
A man was charred to death after a parked car caught fire here on Thursday, the police said. According to the police, the incident occurred around 4 p.m. when local people noticed a car engulfed in flames on the roadside along the Dhoni-Mundur stretch near Arimani Estate.
When people rushed to the spot, they noticed a man seated in the driver’s seat of the vehicle, the police said, adding that the fire was so intense that attempts to douse it failed. Fire and Rescue Services personnel later extinguished the blaze.
The police said a preliminary investigation based on the vehicle registration number revealed that the car belonged to a person from Velikkad near Mundur. They said they were unable to contact the owner immediately, but were in touch with his relatives.
The vehicle had been filled with petrol from a nearby fuel station around 3 p.m. A detailed probe has been launched to ascertain the identity of the deceased and the cause of the fire.
The Hemambika Nagar police will register a case after completing the preliminary inquiry, they added.

title: NCST to probe suspected murder of tribal boy on KISS campus
summary: NCST investigates alleged murder of a tribal boy at KISS, with multiple departments ordered to report on the incident.
content:
The National Commission for Scheduled Tribes (NCST) on Thursday announced that it would investigate the alleged murder of a minor tribal student by three of his hostel mates at the Kalinga Institute of Social Sciences (KISS), which claims to provide education to nearly 30,000 tribal students on its Bhubaneswar campus.
The NCST has issued notices directing the Home, School and Mass Education, and Scheduled Tribes and Scheduled Castes Development, Minorities and Backward Classes Welfare Departments to furnish information on the incident. In addition, the Director General of Police, the Commissionerate of Police for Bhubaneswar-Cuttack, and the District Collector of Khordha have been asked to submit details on developments in the case.
“The Commission has decided to investigate/inquire into the matter in pursuance of the powers conferred upon it under Article 338A of the Constitution of India. You are hereby requested to submit the facts and information on the action taken on the said allegations to the Commission within three days of receipt of this notice,” the NCST said in a letter to six offices.
It may be noted that the Odisha police on Wednesday arrested eight employees of KISS for allegedly suppressing information related to the suspected killing of a Class IX student by fellow hostellers.
KISS, founded by former Biju Janata Dal MP Achyuta Samanta, is widely described as the world’s largest residential educational institution for tribal children. Three students allegedly involved in the death were also detained and produced before the Juvenile Justice Board as children in conflict with the law.
Commissioner of Police S. Debadatta Singh had said that after a detailed investigation and questioning of hostel inmates, there were sufficient grounds to believe that it was a case of murder.
“The deceased had a quarrel with the accused students, who were reportedly known for bullying as a group. Over a trivial issue, the victim was brutally assaulted and later strangulated,” Mr. Singh said.
The preliminary investigation found that KISS authorities had allegedly threatened witnesses not to reveal anything about the incident and attempted to destroy evidence. The Odisha State Commission for Protection of Child Rights took a strong stance, demanding action against doctors who allegedly issued a false medical report to convince the victim’s parents that he had died of cardiac arrest.

title: Numaish stall allotments face allegations of broker control, inflated prices
summary: Allegations of broker manipulation and inflated prices mar stall allotments at Hyderabad's Numaish, raising transparency concerns.
content:
For generations of Hyderabadis, the arrival of the All India Industrial Exhibition, or the Numaish, has been a much-awaited annual ritual. As preparations are underway for the 2026 edition, a major  row has surfaced in the allotment of stalls with allegations that stalls meant to be allotted through a formal application process are being sold at double or even triple the official rates through a network of brokers.
WhenThe Hindureporter visited the exhibition grounds to enquire whether a stall could still be set up for the Numaish, scheduled to begin on January 1, several individuals present at the venue said the legitimate application process had ended on November 15. “Agar aapku abhi stall hona toh black me lena padta (If you want a stall now, then you will have to purchase it in black),” said one person seated near the central circle of the grounds.
Preparations underway at the Nampally Exhibition Grounds ahead of the upcoming Numaish 2026, with workers setting up temporary structures and infrastructure in Hyderabad on Wednesday. 
                                                            | Photo Credit: 
                                SIDDHANT THAKUR
Another individual directed the reporter to the Ajanta Gate area, suggesting that brokers stationed there could arrange a stall at a higher price. “Wo Ajanta Gate ke pass jaake malum karo, dukaan miljati aapku (Go near Ajanta gate and ask, one of the brokers there will help you get a stall), “ he said, adding that the situation was similar to buying cinema tickets in black.
According to allegations, while stall allotment is officially governed by a documented application process, the reality on the ground is different. Multiple brokers allegedly secured several stalls at the officially prescribed rates and are then selling or reselling them to vendors at highly inflated prices.
Preparations underway at the Nampally Exhibition Grounds ahead of the upcoming Numaish 2026, with workers setting up temporary structures and infrastructure in Hyderabad on Wednesday. 
                                                            | Photo Credit: 
                                SIDDHANT THAKUR
As per the application form for the 2026 Numaish, the rent for a regular stall measuring 10x12 is ₹1 lakh. A two side opening small stall measuring 8x8 is priced at ₹1.15 lakh. Periphery stalls are priced at ₹1.55 lakh from Gate 1 to Gate 2, ₹3.05 lakh from Gate 2 to Gate 3, and ₹2.05 lakh from Gate 3 to Sarojini Naidu Vanita College. The form also states that stalls in prime locations would attract an additional premium, to be decided by the exhibition society.
However, Mr. Abrar, who has brought the issue to light, alleged that a stall officially priced at ₹1 lakh is being sold for ₹2 lakh, while a ₹1.15 lakh stall is fetching ₹4.3 lakh. Periphery stalls priced at ₹3.05 lakh are allegedly being sold for ₹8 lakh, and those priced at ₹2.05 lakh for around ₹4 lakh.
Mohammed Sardar, who ran a stall named ‘AR Rajasthan’ selling bedsheets and other items at the exhibition this year, said he paid ₹9.5 lakh for a periphery stall officially priced at ₹2.05 lakh. “I was the third purchaser of that stall. Initially, a broker bought it for ₹2.05 lakh, then it was sold to someone for ₹7 lakh. I eventually had to purchase it for ₹9.5 lakh,” he said.
A group of affected individuals have written to Chief Minister, the IT Minister and the Director General of Police, alleging opaque and discriminatory practices in stall allotments. “Certain individuals involved in the allotment process had been allotted multiple shops, in some cases up to 50 stalls, which appeared to be benami in nature and intended to serve vested interests. Shops were being diverted through fake or proxy allotments, resulting in gross discrimination among genuine applicants,” said their representation.
Meanwhile, Exhibition Society secretary Rajeshwar has denied the allegations saying that the process is transparent and only those who do not get stalls make such allegations. “The allotment is not done in any closed or separate place. Applicants are called, officials are present, and the process happens before everyone,” he said.

title: DSU functionaries’ swearing-in ceremony disrupted at Calicut varsity
summary: Calicut University’s DSU swearing-in ceremony disrupted as Vice-Chancellor objects to non-official oath format, leading to his walkout.
content:
The swearing-in ceremony of the newly elected functionaries of the departmental students’ union (DSU) on the University of Calicut campus (CU) was disrupted on Thursday (December 18) after Vice-Chancellor (V-C) P. Raveendran objected to the “violation” of the official format of the oath.
According to sources, the newly elected functionaries wanted to pay tributes to “the martyrs who lost their lives in the struggle to build a new world order” while assuming office. However, Mr. Raveendran pointed out that this would violate the official format, according to which the functionaries can either take a solemn oath or swear in the name of God. When they refused to oblige, Mr. Raveendran walked out of the event. Denoj Sebastian, Registrar, also left the venue. Sources close to the V-C’s office claimed that the official oath in the proper format had earlier been given to the new functionaries.

title: Jagan Mohan Reddy ‘misleading’ people on PPP model of developing medical colleges, says Health Minister Satya Kumar
summary: Health Minister Satya Kumar accuses Jagan Mohan Reddy of misleading the public on PPP medical college development and challenges him to prove allegations.
content:
Andhra Pradesh Health Minister Satya Kumar Yadav on Thursday accused former Chief Minister and YSR Congress Party president Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy of deliberately obstructing development and misleading the public through “irresponsible protests and false propaganda.”
At a press conference, Mr. Satya Kumar condemned the “threats” allegedly made to companies involved in the construction of medical colleges, and challenged Mr. Jagan Mohan Reddy to seek a CBI inquiry, or legal action, if he had proof of any wrongdoing.
The Minister defended the Public Private Partnership (PPP) model of developing the medical colleges, stating that it was an NDA policy and it was also used during the previous YSR and YSRCP regimes for services such as ‘108’, Aarogyasri, and Cath Labs.
Mr. Satya Kumar said ₹6,000 crore had been spent under NTR Vaidya Seva in 18 months, and reiterated the NDA’s goal of providing medical coverage up to ₹25 lakh for 1. 4 crore families.
He alleged corruption in scholarship schemes and hospital constructions during the previous YSRCP government’s term, and dismissed claims on the misuse of funds, and asserted that the PPP model hospitals would increase medical seats and healthcare access for the poor.
Mr. Satya Kumar further claimed that the allegations made by Mr. Jagan Mohan Reddy were politically motivated, and warned that such behaviour could further weaken his own party. He said the YSRCP government had never sent the AYUSH proposals to the Centre.
He also denied the allegation that ₹300 crore was spent on the yoga day event held in Visakhapatnam, and said it was a Centrally-funded programme.

title: Karnataka to write to Centre on revising rules for BPL categorisation
summary: The State government is considering revising the rules to include families in the Below Poverty Line (BPL)  category, Food Minister K.H. Muniyappa said here on Thursday.
content:
The State government is considering revising the rules to include families in the Below Poverty Line (BPL)  category, Food Minister K.H. Muniyappa said here on Thursday.
Responding to questions by Rajesh Nayak Bantwal in the Legislative Assembly, he said that around 73% of the population of Karnataka had been declared BPL and was now getting the due benefits.
“The Union government, however, believes that going by the strength of our economy, only around 45% to 50% of the population should be considered BPL. It has introduced new guidelines for identifying BPL families. The Union government has, therefore, removed over 7.76 lakh families from the list of BPL families. BPL ration cards, called priority cards, have been turned into Above Poverty Line (APL) cards, now called non-priority cards. We have got several complaints from citizens and people’s representatives against this move. We are of the opinion that the Central norms need to be changed. We are asking officials to study the rules and find out ways to relax them or revise them,’’ he said.
As per rules, any family that earns over ₹ 1.2 lakh per year, or the gross turnover is ₹ 25 lakh per year, holding land of 7.5 acres or more, owning light motor vehicle or other vehicles, government or non-government employees who are taxpayers, were not considered BPL families.
“But we find that even manual labourers who earn ₹500 per day, cross the limit fixed by the Centre. Some legislators have complained that some families who have taken loans for business or house construction are forced to pay taxes and that those who operate taxis or commercial vehicles have been barred from getting BPL cards,” he said, adding that officials had been asked to review such cases and issue fresh BPL cards in 15 days.
He said he would write to the Union government to revise the guidelines.

title: Former ISRO Chairman expresses concern over competence and capability of start-ups to innovate in aerospace
summary: Former ISRO Chairman S. Somanath raises concerns about start-ups' innovation capabilities in aerospace and the slow AI integration.
content:
Former Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) Chairman S. Somanath on Thursday expressed concern over the competence and capability to innovate among start-ups and companies working in the domain of aerostructures.
Speaking at the International Conference on Advances in Computational and Experimental Approaches in Aerostructures, Mr. Somanath said, “I think it is a point of concern to me because I have been going around the country and looking at start-ups and companies who have been designing aerospace structures. Concerning hardwares, especially in the domain of aerospace structures, I am not seeing that type of competence or that type of capability to innovate or do things differently than in the past.”
He added that classical approaches still continue and integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in practice is not happening.
“Possibly some of you might differ with me, but the classical approaches still continue though you talk about data driven models. The AI integration of this is being talked about in practice but not happening. Of course, it is happening in the domain of companies who are coming out with solutions because multi-physics problem-solving software is coming in our midst and using it to find solutions has become a routine,” he added.
Mr. Somanath also said that he has also not been able to see much progress around digital twins in the aerostructures sector.
“They also talk about digital twins, but I am not able to see digital twins in these domains (aerostructures) on a scale that should have actually happened. Why is it not happening? I think this is a question that we need to ask. It may be happening in academics and on a small-scale level, but on a larger scale it is still not visible in institutions where they are actually practicing it. So, I think the conferences should debate, discuss what are the limitations and why collaboration is not happening among people with those types of skills in building at least some models,” Mr. Somanath said.

title: ‘Sahamithra’ project to transform Kozhikode into a disabled-friendly district
summary: Kozhikode's 'Sahamithra' project aims to create a disabled-friendly district through a comprehensive Barrier-Free Mega Building Audit.
content:
As part of its mission to make Kozhikode a completely disabled-friendly district, the district administration will launch a Barrier-Free Mega Building Audit in the last week of December.
The initiative is a component of the ‘Sahamithra’ project, which coordinates multiple departments to ensure accessibility for persons with disabilities. The administration is implementing the project in collaboration with the Composite Regional Centre (CRC), Chevayur, Calicut University’s NSS wing, and the ‘Campuses of Kozhikode’ units, according to a press release.
Around 10,000 National Service Scheme (NSS) volunteers from 70 colleges will assist with the auditing activities, which is a major step towards building inclusive infrastructure. During the initial phase, the volunteers will access nearly 7,000 public buildings under various local self-government institutions.
Officials released the official poster of the project at a meeting of NSS programme officers held at Malabar Christian College here on Thursday (December 18). Calicut University NSS programme co-ordinator V. Vijayakumar and district co-ordinator Faseel Ahmed addressed the gathering.

title: Jagan complains to Governor against PPP model for medical colleges
summary: YSRCP's Jagan Mohan Reddy petitions Governor against PPP model for medical colleges, threatening legal action if not withdrawn.
content:
A delegation of YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) led by its president Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy lodged a complaint with Governor S. Abdul Nazeer against the PPP model of construction of medical colleges, maintaining that its intention was to privatise the colleges and that it would be detrimental to medical education in the State.
Addressing media persons later, Mr. Jagan Mohan Reddy said he submitted a report to the Governor on the one crore signature campaign organised by the YSRCP against the government’s attempts to '’privatise the medical colleges under the garb of PPP’’ and that the matter would be challenged in the courts, to which the papers containing 1,04,11,136 signatures would be submitted if required to convey the gravity of the situation.
He said the YSRCP would not keep quiet if the government does not give up its plan to privatise the colleges, and that completion of the construction of the colleges which came to a pause in 2024, would require ₹5,000 crore and the government appeared to be reluctant to spend it from its ₹2 lakh crore budget.
The government owed an explanation for this, he said, while appealing for a rethink on the decision. Mr. Jagan Mohan Reddy pointed out that during the YSRCP regime, a medical college was sanctioned for every district to make free super - specialty services accessible to the people through the teaching hospitals.
Completing the 17 medical colleges would bring additional seats within the reach of the students. He insisted that under the PPP model, lands, buildings and employees would be under the government control, but management of the colleges would be entrusted to private entities to whom the profits would go.
Addressing a meeting of YSRCP leaders earlier in the day after flagging off vehicles (at his residence in Tadepalli) carrying papers containing the one crore-plus signatures to the Lok Bhavan in Vijayawada, Mr. Jagan Mohan Reddy vowed to cancel the PPP model when the YSRCP returns to power, calling it a big scam.
He recalled that former CM N. Janardhan Reddy had to step down for giving permission to private medical colleges and hoped that Mr. Naidu would understand the rationale behind keeping schools and hospitals with the governments since independence, which was to ensure that the services were affordable and reached all those in need.

title: PHFI opens admissions for MPH programme on Hyderabad, Bhubaneswar campuses
summary: PHFI opens admissions for its two-year MPH programme at Hyderabad and Bhubaneswar campuses, with applications due by December 25.
content:
The Public Health Foundation of India’s (PHFI) Institute of Public Health Sciences, has announced the opening of admissions for its Master of Public Health (MPH) programme for the 2025–27 academic session.
The MPH programme is a full-time course with a duration of two years and will be offered at the Hyderabad and Bhubaneswar campuses. It is open to graduates from all disciplines who have secured at least 50% marks, with no upper age limit.
The application window will remain open until December 25. The admission test is scheduled to be held on December 28. Further details on eligibility criteria, curriculum and the application process are available on the institution’s official website.

title: Assembly passes resolutions demanding Centre act to alleviate backwardness plaguing NK
summary: In a bid to bring pressure on the Centre to fund long-pending projects in North Karnataka region, the Congress government moved five resolutions, which were adopted by the Legislative Assembly on Thursday.
content:
The Hindu Bureau
In a bid to bring pressure on the Centre to fund long-pending projects in North Karnataka region, the Congress government moved five resolutions, which were adopted by the Legislative Assembly on Thursday.
Pointing out the long-pending demand of people in Raichur seeking establishment of All-India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS), the resolution, citing earlier communications by the Chief Minister, urged the Centre to establish AIIMS in Raichur immediately.
In another resolution, Karnataka has urged the Centre to shift at least 25 of the 73 Centrally-administered and important research institutions now located in regions around Bengaluru and Mysuru to North Karnataka and Kalyana Karnataka regions in phases to ensure balanced development.
The resolutions were moved by the Law and Parliamentary Affairs Minister H.K. Patil.
Another resolution adopted urged the Centre to release ₹5,000 crore as matching grant to Kalyana Karnataka region on the lines of the Vidharba development model, as it is one of backward regions in the State.
The State government, which recently came under pressure from sugarcane growers over the price for cane, also moved a resolution urging the Centre to allocate ethanol production as per the ethanol producing capacity in the State and protect the interests of farmers. The allocation should be on the lines of those given to Gujarat, Haryana and Bihar, it said.
In the irrigation sector, two resolutions on Upper Krishna Project and Mahadayi project were adopted.  They urged the Centre to declare to Upper Krishna Project -3 as a national project and release funds besides notifying the Krishna Water Dispute Tribunal -II award in the gazette that will allow utilisation of 173 tmcft of water allocated by the tribunal.
The legislature also adopted a resolution urging the Centre to provide forest and environmental clearance to Kalasa-Banduri canal project to utilise 3.9 tmcft of water for drinking water purpose as per the Mahadayi tribunal award. Though there is no court stay, the legally bound project is being obstructed, and the Centre has not given permission, the resolution said.
Taking exception to the choice of words as “discrimination by the Centre,” Leader of the Opposition R. Ashok said, “We are not opposed to any of the resolutions. But have you shifted any departments to Suvarna Soudha, which is now empty? What have you done before urging Centre to shift its institutions?”
Reservation under Schedule IX
The Karnataka Legislative Assembly unanimously resolved to urge the Centre to include reservation in Karnataka provided to Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and backward classes that has exceeded 50% under Schedule IX of the Constitution.
The provisions of The Karnataka Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and Other Backward Classes (Reservation of Appointment), Act, 1990, and The Karnataka Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Reservation of Seats in Educational Institutions and Appointments of Posts and Services under the State) Act, 2022, rules and regulations that have been formed should be inserted in Schedule IX, said the resolution. Law and Parliamentary Affairs Minister H.K. Patil said, “It is imperative to protect social justice.”
While the Supreme Court has capped the reservation at 50% in its landmark judgement in Indira Sawhney case, total reservation has gone up to 56% in Karnataka.  While 32% has been provided for backward classes, 17 % and 7 % have been provided to Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes respectively.

title: Of 202 Indian recruits in Russian Army, 26 killed, seven missing, MEA tells Rajya Sabha
summary: India reports 202 recruits in the Russian Army, with 26 fatalities and ongoing efforts for the safe return of others.
content:
As many as 202 Indians are “believed to have been recruited into the Russian armed forces” since 2022, and 26 of them are reported to have lost their lives, the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) informed the Rajya Sabha on Thursday (December 18, 2025), adding that at least two Indians have been cremated in Russia.
Parliament Winter Session:Follow LIVE updates on December 18, 2025
“Concerted efforts by the Government have resulted in early discharge of 119 of them; 26 are reported to have lost their lives and seven are reported missing by the Russian side. Efforts are ongoing for early discharge of 50 individuals,” Minister of State Kirti Vardhan Singh said in a written reply.
Also Read |Families of Indians stuck in Russian warzone say they last heard from them 50-days ago
The Union government remains continuously engaged with the Russian government, to ensure the safety, well-being, and early discharge of all Indian nationals in the Russian armed forces, the Minister said. He added that the matter is being discussed at various levels, including during interactions between leaders, Ministers, and officials of the two sides.
Mr. Singh was responding to a question by Trinamool Congress MP Saket Gokhale and Congress MP Randeep Singh Surjewala on the number of Indian nationals identified as illegally working or forced to work in the Russian Army, along with the count of fatalities and missing people since 2022.
Also Read |44 Indians serving in Russian military; India once again urges Moscow to release them
On December 17,The Hindureportedthat the bodies of two Indians killed in the Russia-Ukraine warzone over the past three months had been brought to Delhi.
The deceased were identified as Rajasthan resident Ajay Godara, 22, and Rakesh Kumar, 30, from Uttarakhand. Both Godara and Kumar had gone to Russia in the past year on student visas, but were allegedly enlisted in the Russian Army after being misled by agents who promised them work as cleaners and helpers. Indians continue to be enlisted in the Russian Army despite an assurance by Moscow in 2024 that it longer admits Indians.
Also Read |Release Indians from Russian army, stop practice of recruiting Indians, MEA tells Moscow
“The Ministry has provided assistance in repatriation of mortal remains of 10 deceased Indian nationals to India, and local cremation of two deceased Indian nationals. DNA samples of family members of 18 Indians, who were reported dead or missing, have been shared with the Russian authorities in an effort to help establish the identity of some of the deceased Indian nationals,” the Minister said in his reply.
The MEA, along with the Indian Mission and Posts in Russia, has assisted those Indians discharged from the Russian Army to return to India, “including through facilitation of travel documents and providing air tickets, wherever required,” Mr. Singh said.
The Indian Mission in Russia has also assisted with the task of the evacuation of mortal remains. Once the mortal remains are shifted to a safe zone, the identification process involves the matching of DNA samples with the next of kin, the Minister said. “When the identity is conclusively established, the Indian Embassy assists in completion of requisite documentation for local cremation or transportation of mortal remains to India, in close coordination with the family,” he said in his reply.

title: Court fines parents ₹25,000 for letting minor ride two-wheeler
summary: Mysuru court fines parents ₹25,000 for allowing their minor to ride a two-wheeler, emphasizing strict traffic regulations.
content:
A city court has fined the parent of a minor for allowing the boy to ride a two-wheeler in Mysuru.
During routine patrol on Thursday, PSI K.S. Ganesh noticed a minor riding a two-wheeler within the limits of the Krishnaraja Traffic Police Station.
The parent was summoned to the police station and served a notice. The 2nd JMFC Court imposed a fine of ₹25,000 on the parent for permitting a minor to operate a motor vehicle.
A release issued by the office of the Commissioner of Police, Mysuru, warned that action will be taken against parents if they allow their minor children to operate their motor vehicles.

title: Population Management Policy will be introduced in A.P. by Ugadi, says CM
summary: Andhra Pradesh CM Naidu announces a Population Management Policy by Ugadi and emphasizes job creation and law enforcement improvements.
content:
Reiterating that the Andhra Pradesh government is committed to providing 20 lakh jobs as promised during the TDP’s Yuva Galam programme in the run-up to the 2024 elections, Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu has said that 4.50 lakh jobs have been given so far.
The government is striving to realise the Swarnandhra-2047 Vision by focusing on its 10 principles (Padi Sutralu), he said and announced that a Population Management Policy would be introduced by Ugadi.Besides, the details of the people receiving government services and welfare schemes would be registered on Family Cards soon.
Addressing the Collectors’ Conference on its second day at the Secretariat on Thursday, Mr. Naidu said the future depends on skills and that degrees would be offered in skill development, alongside traditional courses.
He instructed the Collectors to achieve zero maternal and infant mortality rates, and zero suicides, for which farmers, students, and families should be counselled.
He said Rayalaseema would be developed as a horticulture hub for international markets and asserted that Andhra Pradesh would be positioned as a logistics hub along the East Coast.
The Chief Minister ordered that top priority be given to resolving disputes arising from placing lands under Section 22-A of the Registration Act. “Political interference in land disputes will not be tolerated,” he said.
He instructed the Collectors to ensure that the groundwater levels were at three metres by the end of the monsoon season and not drop below eight metres before the start of the next rainy season.
He clarified that power tariffs were not being hiked and instructed the Collectors to make aquaculture farmers promptly pay their electricity bills.
Referring to Law & Order (L&O), Mr Naidu advocated for zero tolerance towards crime and the expulsion of habitual offenders from the State. He said a Cabinet Sub - Committee would be formed to help curb the menace of malicious propaganda and fake accounts used on social media for character assassination.
D​irector General of Police Harish Kumar Gupta reported a 5.50% decline in the crime rate in the State. However, the crime rates were rising in Annamayya, Konaseema, Nellore, Guntur, and Tirupati districts.
Deputy Chief Minister K. Pawan Kalyan stressed the importance of maintaining law and order to achieve 15% growth rate. He directed the Collectors and Superintendents of Police to be proactive in controlling crimes.

title: Mass spectrometry & sophisticated bioinformatics propels innovation
summary: Mass spectrometry & sophisticated bioinformatics propels innovation
content:
The advent of high-resolution mass spectrometry and sophisticated bioinformatics have enabled unprecedented depth in the analysis of cellular processes and disease pathways accelerating biomarker discovery, enhanced understanding of complex biological systems, and propelled innovations in personalized medicine, agriculture, and environmental science.
This was the major observation at the 17th Annual Conference of Proteomics Society (India) themed “Proteomics and Metabolomics: Innovation, Applications, and Impact”, hosted by the CSIR-Centre for Cellular and Molecular Biology (CCMB) here on Thursday.
The program was curated to encompass a broad array of topics, including disease mechanisms, immunity, and their pharmaceutical, clinical, and agricultural applications with scientists, research scholars, and industry leaders discussing the the progress in the field.
“The conference catalyzes exchange of innovative ideas, knowledge, and resources, thereby advancing the frontiers of proteomics and metabolomics. The rapid evolution of these disciplines continues to expand their impact, fostering new collaborations and driving scientific breakthroughs, said senior principal scientist and lead organiser Swasti Raychaudhuri, in a press release.

title: Committee will be set up to study plight of project displaced people, says Shivakumar
summary: Shivakumar announces a committee to address the concerns of project-displaced individuals affected by irrigation projects in Karnataka.
content:
Deputy Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar, who holds the Water Resources portfolio, told the Legislative Council in Belagavi on Thursday that a committee comprising leaders from the Opposition benches will be constituted to study the plight of people displaced by various irrigation projects, including UKP (Upper Krishna Project), and make recommendations to the State government.
He was responding to the issue raised by Hanumanth Nirani and P.H. Pujar under Rule 330 in the Legislative Council on rehabilitation for UKP-displaced people.
Mr. Shivakumar said that he is committed to ensuring development of irrigation and at the same time, concerned about the people who part with their land for such projects. The State government is committed to extending all the required assistance to the project-displaced people, he said.
A committee will be formed to study the plight of these people and recommend remedial measures, he said. Senior members from the Opposition benches will be nominated to the committee to give constructive suggestions towards resolution of issues faced by displaced people, he said.
Earlier, raising the issue, Hanumanth Nirani and P.H. Pujar pointed out that only 50% of targeted land has been irrigated under the UKP and no official has visited the 146 rehabilitation centres set up for the project-displaced people.
Their plight is pitiable and the State government should take up the issue on humanitarian basis and provide proper rehabilitation and livelihood to them, they demanded.

title: Watch: India worst doping offender for third straight year, says WADA report
summary: India ranked first globally in doping violations for the third consecutive year, according to the World Anti-Doping Agency’s annual report published on December 16. The report said 260 out of 7,113 samples collected in 2024 tested positive, raising concerns as India prepares to host the 2030 Commonwealth Games.

title: Tragedy averted as Air India Express flight makes emergency landing in Kochi after tyre burst
summary: Air India Express flight safely makes emergency landing in Kochi after tyre burst, averting potential tragedy for 160 on board.
content:
