title: Congress dares Kerala government to arrest creators and broadcasters accused of politically parodying Ayyappa devotional song
summary: Congress dares Kerala government to arrest creators and broadcasters accused of politically parodying Ayyappa devotional song
content:
The Congress on Friday (December 19, 2025) challenged the government to arrest the creators and broadcasters of the controversial political parody of a popular Ayyappa devotional song, which lampooned the ruling Left Democratic Front (LDF) for the alleged culpability of its Travancore Devaswom Board (TDB) political appointees in the Sabarimala gold theft case.
The catchy song had gone viral on social and conventional media, arguably catalysing the United Democratic Front’s (UDF) strong showing in the local body elections.
The Congress cast the police case registered against the creators of the song as an infringement on artistic freedom and political dissent, and as a clear violation of the constitutional protections for freedom of speech and expression.
The police had booked the lyricist, composer, and singers on grave charges of outraging religious faith and fostering enmity between different sets of people. The song’s creators had claimed they had staged the parody song to promote their fledgling studio on social media.
They claimed their intent was merely to pull the leg and not to insult any religion. The studio manager said the establishment created ingenious parody songs for opposing political campaigns, along with devotional songs across the religious spectrum.
All India Congress Committee (AICC) general secretary Pawan Khera pushed back rather dramatically by rendering the first two lines of the ditty at the party’s State headquarters at Indira Bhavan in Thiruvananthapuram. He dared the police to arrest him. Kerala Pradesh Congress Committee (KPCC) president Sunny Joseph, MLA, urged Congress workers to form choirs to intone the song at town and village centres across Kerala.
AICC general secretary K.C. Venugopal said the government’s quixotic bid to proscribe the song and erase the ditty from public memory indicated the LDF’s panic and lack of grace in defeat.
Meanwhile, Leader of the Opposition V.D. Satheesan strongly opposed the government’s move to remove the parody song from social media accounts, chiefly those operated by Meta. In a letter to the Meta, Mr. Satheesan underscored that to date, no court has prohibited the parody song or ordered its removal from social media platforms. Moreover, the satirical content woven into the song did not violate the Meta’s community standards.
Mr. Satheesan told the Meta that the Supreme Court  has consistently held that the State has no right to curtail freedom of speech and expression unless there is a clear and legally established violation of the law.
Meanwhile, the Communist Party of India (Marxist) [CPI(M)] sought to distance itself from the accusation that the government had stifled artistic freedom and political dissidence.
The CPI(M) noted that the police had taken cognisance of a complaint filed by the Pathanamthitta-based Thiruvabharana Patha Samrakshana Samathi, an organisation closely associated with the tradition of the Sabarimala Ayyappa temple.
The party’s Pathanamthitta district secretary Raju Abraham said neither the CPI(M) nor the government was a party in the case.

title: Don’t turn Marina beach into Marina bazaar, Madras High Court tells Chennai Corporation
summary: Madras High Court inspects Marina beach to ensure vendor regulation and blue flag certification, avoiding a chaotic marketplace.
content:
Two judges of the Madras High Court on Friday (December 19, 2025) decided to inspect the Marina beach in Chennai on Monday (December 22, 2025) in order to take stock of the Greater Chennai Corporation’s (GCC) proposal to regulate vendors and obtain theinternationally-recognised blue flag certification.
Justices R. Suresh Kumar and A.D. Jagadish Chandira told Advocate General P.S. Raman that they would be inspecting the beach at 9 a.m. on Monday and ordered the officials of the State government, GCC, Collectorate, and Greater Chennai Police Commissionerate to assist them in the inspection.
The judges said, all revenue records related to the beach, the maps of the proposed area abutting the service road where the vendors would be allowed to put up shops in a row, and the facilities that the visitors to the beach would be provided under the blue flag project should be placed before them.
The Bench decided to pass further orders on the issue on January 7 after completing its inspection on December 22. The decision to conduct a personal inspection was taken during the hearing of a writ petition filed by S. Devi of Chepauk, who had sought a direction to the GCC to grant a vending licence for her at the beach.
During the course of hearing of the writ petition, Justice Kumar recalled that a Division Bench comprising Justices Vineet Kothari (since retired) and himself had passed several directions related to the upkeep of the Marina beach and regulation of the vendors a few years ago, but nothing concrete had happened so far.
The senior judge said, in 2020, the GCC had decided to procure about 900 uniformly-sized push carts for the vendors on the Marina beach and allot them through a transparent process. However, subsequently, the project was dropped and the vendors continued their haphazard business on the beach, the judge rued.
However, now, when the Environment Secretary as well as the GCC Commissioner have apprised the court of the plan to regulate the vendors and the blue flag project, the judges said, it must be ensured that visitors, especially children, to the beach get to enjoy its beauty without it being choked by vendors.
“Don’t convert the Marina beach into a Marina bazaar. If you allow thousands of vendors on the beach, where will there be space for the visitors who want to enjoy the sea breeze? If you allow too many vendors, there might be problems in getting the blue flag certification too,” Justice Kumar told the A-G.

title: Nitish hijab row: AYUSH doctor will join duty in Bihar on Dec. 20, says official
summary: AYUSH doctor Nusrat Parveen will join duty in Bihar despite controversy over her veil removal by Chief Minister Nitish Kumar.
content:
Amid rumours that a doctor has declined a government job in Bihar after her ‘naqab’ (veil) was removed by Chief Minister Nitish Kumar during a programme in Patna, an official concerned on Friday (December 19, 2025) claimed that she will join duty.
Dr. Mahfoozur Rahman, principal of the Government Tibbi College and Hospital in Patna, toldPTIthat AYUSH doctor Nusrat Parveen’s family has confirmed that she will join duty on Saturday (December 20).
"I spoke to Parveen's husband, relatives and her classmates. They told me that she would join duty on December 20. She has to first join the Government Tibbi College and Hospital, and later she will be shifted to her place of posting. Her family members and classmates have assured me that she would join duty," Dr. Rahman said.
The incident, a video clip of which has been circulated widely and sparked a major political row, took place on Monday (December 15) at the chief minister’s secretariat in Patna when Ayush doctors had gathered to receive their letters of appointment. When the woman came up for her letter, CM Kumar saw her 'naqab', said “what is this” and then removed the veil.
Following this, there were rumours that Mr. Parveen declined the job.
The incident has drawn criticism from far and wide, including several West Asian countries, and Kumar, also the JD(U) president, has been facing accusations of disrespecting Muslims traditions allegedly in line with the 'RSS agenda'.
Bihar Minister Dilip Jaiswal on Friday (December 19) said, "A controversy is being created unnecessarily over the issue. The NDA government under the leadership of Nitish Kumar ji has taken several steps for the empowerment of women in the state."  	Meanwhile, the CM has reportedly received a threat from a Pakistan-based man over the naqab controversy. The Cyber police station in Patna has registered a case.
DGP Vinay Kumar on Thursday (December 180 told reporters that the case has been handed over to Patna Inspector General of Police.

title: Air purifiers to be installed in 10,000 classrooms in first phase: Delhi Education Minister
summary: Delhi plans to install air purifiers in 10,000 classrooms to combat pollution and ensure cleaner air for students.
content:
DelhiEducation Minister Ashish Sood on Friday (December 19, 2025) announced thatair purifiers will be installed in 10,000 classroomsto ensure clean air for the students.
ALSO WATCHWatch: Delhi govt planning overhaul of PUC certificate issuing system: Environment Minister
Addressing a press conference, Sood said that the government is committed towards tackling the problem of pollution through long-term administrative reforms and policy measures.
Also Read |Consider suspending toll booths at Delhi borders; no coercive action against BS-IV car owners: Supreme Court
"We are not those who flaunt IIT degrees and do campaigns like Odd-Even or Gaadi On, Gaadi Off campaign. We are tackling the issue of pollution through long-term administrative measures," he said, taking a dig at the previous Aam Aadmi Party government.
The Odd-Even scheme,first introduced by the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) under the leadership of then-Chief Minister Arvind Kejriwal, was implemented twice in 2016, from January 1 to 15 and again from April 15 to 30.
The scheme aimed to curb vehicular pollution by restricting the movement of private vehicles based on the last digit of their registration numbers.
According to Mr. Sood, there are 38,000 classrooms, and air purifiers will be installed in them in a phased manner.
"We want our children to study smart and also breathe smart air. In the first phase, air purifiers will be installed in 10,000 classrooms. Tenders have been floated today itself," he added.
Official data shows there are 1,047 government and government-aided schools.
The Minister, who also holds the urban development portfolio, said the Public Works Department, using the environment cess, will also procure mechanical road sweepers for each of the assembly constituencies.
"Money is also being provided to MCD for procuring mechanical road sweepers. The Aam Aadmi Party government did nothing for MCD. Salaries were not released for sanitation workers. They were at the helm of MCD for two years. But what did they do?" he asked.
Mr. Sood also said Delhi is surrounded by states, and the weather conditions there determine the weather.
"We are committed towards the issue of eradicating pollution. I want to assure people of Delhi that we are taking all possible steps which will show their results on the ground very soon," he added.

title: Iltija Mufti seeks to book Nitish Kumar over removing veil of a female doctor
summary: Iltija Mufti files complaint against Nitish Kumar for removing a female doctor's veil, sparking widespread condemnation in Kashmir.
content:
Peoples Democratic Party leader Iltija Mufti on Friday (December 19, 2025) moved a complaint before the J&K Police in Srinagar and sought registration of an FIR against  Bihar Chief Minister Nitish Kumar over therecent attempt to remove the veil from the face of a female doctorduring an official function.
Meanwhile, addressing the congregation at the historic Jama Masjid in Srinagar, chief cleric Mirwaiz Umar condemned the act of the Bihar Chief Minister pulling off the veil of a woman doctor, and described it as a grave violation of personal dignity and moral boundaries.
Earlier on Tuesday (December 16), several political parties in Jammu and Kashmir condemned Bihar Chief Minister Nitish Kumar. Former J&K Chief Minister and PDP President Mehbooba Mufti said it was time for Mr. Kumar to step down. “Having personally known and admired Nitish ji, I was shocked to see him pull down a young Muslim woman’s naqaab (veil),” Ms. Mufti said. She said does one attribute it to old age or the normalisation of humiliating Muslims publicly. “The fact that people around him watched this horrific incident unfold as some form of an entertainment is even more unsettling. Nitish Sahab perhaps it’s time you step down?” Ms. Mufti said.
Also Read |Kashmir parties slam Bihar CM Nitish Kumar over removing veil of a female doctor
Awami Ittehad Party spokesperson Inam Un Nabi said such an act “strips the office of Chief Minister of any moral credibility left.” “Mr. Kumar’s behaviour was not just inappropriate, it was disgraceful, arrogant and shockingly shameless. He has humiliated a young doctor and disgraced his own chair,” Mr. Nabi said.

title: Several Noida schools receive hoax bomb threat emails: Police
summary: Noida schools received hoax bomb threat emails, prompting thorough inspections by police and security teams, confirmed authorities.
content:
Several schools in Noida received emails containing bomb threats on Friday (December 19, 2025), which later turned out to be a hoax, police said.
Additional Commissioner of Police (Gautam Buddh Nagar), Rajeev Narain Mishra, told reporters that some schools in Noida received emails threatening bomb attacks on their premises.
"Upon receiving information, senior police officers, along with local police teams, bomb disposal squads, dog squads, and anti-sabotage units, carried out thorough inspections of the schools," Mr. Mishra said.
“Security teams also conducted searches in the surrounding areas, including nearby Metro stations, markets, and other crowded places as a precautionary measure,” the officer said.
"Preliminary investigations suggest that the emails were hoax. Full vigilance is being maintained and necessary legal action is underway," the ACP said.

title: Possible Middle Palaeolithic site found at Mallankinaru in Virudhunagar
summary: A Madras University student discovers possible Middle Palaeolithic stone tools at Mallankinaru, Virudhunagar, sparking archaeological interest.
content:
A field survey conducted by a postgraduate archaeology student from the University of Madras has unearthed stone tools that could date back to the Middle Palaeolithic period, according to preliminary observations by experts from the varsity.
N. Thilagarajan, a student of the Department of Ancient History and Archaeology, discovered the stone tools during an exploration at Mallankinaru in Virudhunagar district. The tools, made of quartz, include multidirectional and radial cores, as well as flake tools such as notches and scrapers. They were found in a stratigraphic layer of a quarried section near a waterbody in Mallankinaru.
Based on a preliminary analysis of the type and shape of the stone tools, they could belong to the Middle Palaeolithic period, said Jinu Koshy, excavation in-charge of the Department at the University of Madras. He added that the sediments in the locality were formed due to fluvial activity, as the site is part of the lower Gundar basin.
J. Soundararajan, Associate Professor and Head of the Department of Ancient History and Archaeology, University of Madras, said no Middle Palaeolithic period stone tools had previously been found in the village. He said further exploration and excavation of the site could lead to the discovery of more artefacts, and detailed scientific analysis would help determine the exact period of the site.

title: Puncha season under threat as fertilizer shortage grips Kerala’s Kuttanad
summary: Kerala's Kuttanad faces a fertilizer crisis, threatening puncha season crops and risking farmers' livelihoods due to severe shortages.
content:
A severe shortage of fertilizers, particularly urea, potash and phosphate, has triggered a crisis in Kuttanad and other parts of Alappuzha district in Kerala, where puncha crop season is under way. The season accounts for the largest acreage of paddy cultivation in the district. Besides paddy, these fertilizers are essential for other crops as well.
“Paddy crops require urea application between 18 and 22 days after planting. In many fields, it is already time for this application. However, farmers are finding it difficult to procure adequate quantities of fertilizers. It is high time the government addressed the issue, as there are serious concerns that productivity will be affected. Farmers are staring at huge losses,”said Siji Chacko, secretary, Aikya Kuttanad Padasekhara Ekopana Samithi.
“The severe shortage has forced many padasekhara samithis and farmers to skip cultivation during the puncha season. This could severely affect agricultural productivity and push farmers into a deep crisis,” he said
Urea costs ₹300 for a 45-kg sack, while the price of potash has increased to ₹1,800 from ₹1,500 per bag. According to sources, the Union government was to supply Kerala around 43,000 tonnes of urea between October and December, but the State has received only about 20,000 tonnes so far. The State government and farmers believe that the Centre’s push to promote nano fertilizers has contributed to the shortage.
Raising the issue of the acute shortage of urea and potash in Kerala in the Lok Sabha recently, Kodikunnil Suresh, MP, said that the scarcity was seriously affecting agriculture in the State. He pointed out that the shortage had disrupted all major crops, including paddy, coconut, arecanut, rubber, cocoa, cardamom and pineapple.
“In the pineapple sector alone, the annual requirement is 22,500 tonnes of urea and 15,000 tonnes of potash. The prevailing shortage is forcing farmers to shift to costlier alternative and complex fertilizers, leading to a sharp rise in production costs and causing nutrient imbalance in agriculture,” he said.
Terming the plight of the farmers as grave, Mr. Suresh criticised the Centre for failing to ensure timely supply despite repeated requests from the State government. In view of the serious situation threatening farmers’ livelihoods, he urged the Union government to act with urgency and ensure the immediate supply of the required quantities of urea and potash to Kerala.

title: CPI(M) condemns delay in announcing Sahitya Akademi Awards
summary: CPI(M) criticizes the delay in Sahitya Akademi Awards, accusing the BJP government of interfering with cultural autonomy and expression.
content:
The delay in announcing the Sahitya Akademi Awards has drawn strong criticism from CPI(M) State Secretary P. Shanmugam and party MP Su. Venkatasan, who accused the BJP-led Union government under Prime Minister Narendra Modi of attempting to bring the Akademi under its control.
The awards were scheduled to be announced on December 18, but it was postponed after the Union Ministry of Culture sent a note to the Akademi reminding it of a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) signed with the four autonomous institutions under the Ministry — the National School of Drama, the Sangeet Natak Akademi, the Lalit Kala Akademi, and the Sahitya Akademi. The note stated that any restructuring of awards should be undertaken in consultation with the Ministry.
Condemning the Ministry’s intervention, Mr. Shanmugam alleged that, henceforth, awards would be given only to those who “play second fiddle to the BJP government and supporters of Sanatana ideology.”
“Quality in literature and history means nothing to them. Their politics is to destroy everything,” Mr. Shanmugam said in a social media post.
Mr. Venkatasan said that the National Executive Council of the Sahitya Akademi had met earlier this month and approved the recommendations made by the respective language juries for selecting the Sahitya Akademi Award recipients for 2025.
“It is unacceptable that the autonomous Sahitya Akademi remains silent and claims an inability to announce its decision. This silence and helplessness amount to a betrayal of our rich literary tradition and the Akademi’s illustrious history. I urge the Akademi’s Executive Council to boldly make its decisions public,” said Mr. Venkatasan, who is himself one of the award recipients.
He further alleged that the Modi government was openly forcing the country’s eminent cultural institutions to “kneel at its feet.”
“All those who love literature and writing must come together and resist this attack on our freedom of expression,” he said.

title: ED attaches assets of Yuvraj Singh, Sonu Sood, others in illegal betting app case
summary: ED attaches assets of Yuvraj Singh, Sonu Sood, and others in ₹1,000 crore illegal betting money laundering case.
content:
The Directorate of Enforcement (ED) on Friday (December 19, 2025) provisionally attached movable and immovable assets valued at ₹7.93 crore belonging toformer Indian cricketers Yuvraj Singhand Robin Uthappa, and five actors including Urvashi Rautela, Sonu Sood, in “illegal” offshore betting platform linked money laundering case.
The properties of actor Neha Sharma, mother of model Urvashi Rautela and Bengali actor Ankush Hazra, and Mimi Chakraborty have also been attached after the federal probe agency issued a provisional order the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA
The ED probe is based on multiple First Information Reports registered by the police in different States against the operators of 1xBet platform. “The investigation has revealed that 1xBet and its surrogate brand 1xBat, 1xbat Sporting lines were engaged in promoting and facilitating illegal online betting and gambling operations across India,” said the agency.
Ms. Chakraborty is also a former Member of Parliament. According to the ED, the celebrities knowingly entered into endorsement agreements with foreign entities for the promotion of 1xBet through its surrogates. These endorsements were made in return for payments routed through foreign entities to conceal the illicit origin of the funds, which are linked to Proceeds of Crime (POC) generated from illegal betting activities.
1xBet allegedly operated in India without authorisation and used surrogate branding and advertisements to target Indian users via social media, online videos, and print media. Payments for endorsements were structured through layered transactions using foreign intermediaries to disguise the illegal source of funds.
Earlier on October 6, the agency had attached assets amounting to ₹11.14 crore of former cricketers Shikhar Dhawan and Suresh Raina.
“The ED cautions that illegal betting and gambling platforms cause serious economic harm and are widely used for money laundering and other unlawful activities. The public is advised to avoid such platforms and report any suspicious transactions or advertisements to law enforcement agencies, or the ED,” the agency said, also cautioning celebrities and social media influencers against endorsing or promoting illegal betting or gambling platforms, directly or indirectly.

title: Mega job fair to be held in the Nilgiris on December 20
summary: Join the mega job fair in Udhagamandalam on December 20, 2025, with opportunities from over 100 companies.
content:
A mega job fair organised by the Nilgiris District Administration, the District Employment and Career Guidance Centre and the Tamil Nadu State Rural Livelihoods Mission will be held from December 20, 2025 (Saturday) at the Government Arts College in Udhagamandalam.
In a press release, the district administration stated that over 100 leading private sector companies from various districts, including Coimbatore, Erode, Tiruppur and the Nilgiris will be participating in the job fair where up to 10,000 people can potentially be hired for various vacancies.
“Candidates with all educational qualifications from class V to XII, graduates, diploma holders, ITI, computer operators and drivers can participate in this camp without any fee. All interested job seekers in Nilgiris district are requested to participate in this employment camp and benefit from it. Job seekers who are interested in participating in the camp should register in advance on the websitewww.tnprivatejobs.tn.gov.in,” a press release from the district administration stated.
Private sector companies from the Nilgiris district were also invited to participate in the job fair and recruit employees for their organisations. The companies too can register their company details on the above-mentioned website, it was stated. For more information, interested persons were asked to contact the Udhagamandalam District Employment and Career Guidance Centre in person or by phone at 0423-2444004, 9489026936.

title: ED seizes assets worth ₹3.78 crore in Ponzi scam
summary: ED seizes ₹3.78 crore in assets linked to a Ponzi scheme promising unrealistic returns and defrauding investors in Kerala.
content:
The Directorate of Enforcement (ED), Kochi Zonal Office, has provisionally attached movable and immovable properties worth ₹3.78 crore belonging to individuals accused of operating a Ponzi scheme.
The attached assets represent the proceeds of crime generated by Muhammed Faisal, Abu Sufiyan, and their associates, who allegedly cheated unsuspecting investors by promising exorbitant returns through a scheme named My Club Traders. The properties include agricultural land, residential premises, commercial plots with office buildings, and bank accounts held in the names of Faisal, his associates, and related companies.
According to an ED statement, the investigation was initiated based on multiple FIRs registered by the Kerala Police under various sections of the Indian Penal Code (IPC), 1860, relating to cheating and fraud. These cases involved the collection of large deposits from the public under the guise of investment opportunities.
The probe revealed that the accused promised unrealistic returns, such as 1% of the invested amount as daily profits on working days. The scheme functioned as a pyramid-style money circulation plan, falsely presented as legitimate trading in cryptocurrencies and other ventures. Investors were also promised a 10% binary commission for introducing new participants, enabling the collection of substantial sums.
“However, the scheme depended on funds from new investors to pay earlier ones, leading to its eventual collapse and failure to return investments or profits. Throughout its operation, money was collected in cash to avoid detection, laundered through shell companies such as M/s Princess Gold and Diamonds LLP and M/s Toll Deal Ventures LLP, and used to acquire assets. These individuals and their associates generated and laundered proceeds of crime by deceiving investors with false promises and extracting large sums from them,” the ED statement said.
On June 4, 2025, the ED held searches at five locations under the provisions of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA). During the raids, incriminating documents and materials, including diaries recording cash collections, investor details, financial transactions, and digital devices, were seized. Further investigation is under way, the ED added.

title: Workshop on ‘Shantarasa’s Literary World’ on December 20
summary: Join the ‘Shantarasa’s Literary World’ workshop on December 20 at Gulbarga University for insightful discussions on literature.
content:
The Kannada Studies Institute of Gulbarga University, in association with Dr. Besagarahalli Ramanna Pratishtana, Bengaluru, will organise a literary workshop titled ‘Shantarasa’s Literary World’ on the university campus on Saturday.
The workshop will be held at the Harihara Auditorium of Gulbarga University at 10 a.m. Short story writer Amaresh Nugadoni from Hosapet will inaugurate the programme. The inaugural session will be presided over by H.R. Sujatha, president of the Dr. Besagarahalli Ramanna Pratishtana.
Director of the Kannada Studies Institute, Gulbarga University H.T. Potte and theatre personality H.S. Basavaprabhu from Kalaburagi will participate as chief guests.
As part of the workshop, the first technical session will be held from 11.30 a.m. to 1.30 p.m., during which researcher K. Ravindranath from Hosapet will speak on research and book editing, while critic Shreeshail Nagaral will deliver a lecture on prose literature.
The second session, scheduled from 2 p.m. to 5 p.m., will have a critic Shailaja Bagewadi speaking on the portrayal of women in literature, writer Mahantesh Navalakal on the world of poetry, and translator Suryakant Sujata on translation literature.
Poet and translator Chidanand Sali will take part in the valedictory session at 5 p.m.

title: Bombay HC grants bail to former Maharashtra minister Manikrao Kokate in cheating case; suspends sentence
summary: Bombay HC grants bail to former minister Manikrao Kokate in cheating case, suspending his two-year jail sentence amid ongoing appeals.
content:
The Bombay High Court on Friday (December 19, 2025) granted bail to NCP leader and former Maharashtra minister Manikrao Kokate in a cheating and forgery case linked to a government housing scheme, and suspended his two-year jail term.
The court, however, refused to stay the conviction noting that prima facie evidence pointed to Kokate's involvement. The NCP leader was accused of securing a flat in a government scheme for the economically weaker section (EWS) by submitting false affidavits about his income.
"Permitting a person convicted of criminal offence (to hold a cabinet position) solely on account of suspended sentence would cause grave and irreparable prejudice to public service," said the court.
In his order, Justice R.N. Laddha noted that Kokate was on bail throughout the trial before the magistrate's court and also during the pendency of the appeal before the session's court.
As the jail term was only two years, it was inclined to grant bail, the high court said. "The application for suspension of sentence is allowed....The applicant has to deposit a sum of Rs one lakh as surety," the HC said as it admitted for hearing Kokate's revision petition against the sessions court's order which upheld his conviction.
Kokate's counsel Ravi Kadam argued that he was admitted to Lilavati hospital in Bandra where he underwent an angiography, and was scheduled to have an SOS angioplasty on Friday afternoon.
Public prosecutor Mankunwar Deshmukh opposed Kokate's bail plea.
Kokate's conviction was upheld by the Nashik district and sessions court on Tuesday (December 16). On Thursday (December 18) night he resigned from the Maharashtra cabinet where he held the sports and youth affairs portfolio. A team of Nashik police reached  Bandra late Thursday (December 18) night to execute the arrest warrant.
The case against Kokate dates back to 1989-1992, involving a housing scheme for EWS with an annual income limit of ₹30,000. He was accused of securing a flat for him in the scheme by submitting false income affidavits.
Citing bank loans for grapes and rabi crops, as well as records from the Kopargaon Sahakari Sakhar Karkhana (sugar factory), the magistrate's court noted that he was a  prosperous farmer whose income far exceeded the eligibility threshold.
Former Maharashtra minister and NCP leader Manikrao Kokate underwent coronary angiography on Friday (December 19) at Mumbai’s Lilavati Hospital, doctors treating him said.
Kokate resigned from the Devendra Fadnavis government on Thursday (December 18).
“He has four severe blockages and we have advised him bypass surgery (process to reroute blood flow around blocked arteries). He underwent coronary angiography (X ray test to view blockages or narrowing in the heart’s arteries) today,” Dr. Jalil Parkar and Dr. Suresh Vijan said.
“If Kokate does not want to undergo bypass surgery, angioplasty (procedure to widen narrowed or blocked blood vessels) can be done and treatment will continue. Kokate had two stents placed 15 years ago and these are in good condition,” they added.

title: KSRTC to operate 1,000 additional buses to clear Christmas rush
summary: KSRTC is adding 1,000 extra buses for Christmas travel to meet increased demand across Karnataka and neighboring regions.
content:
The Karnataka State Road Transport Corporation (KSRTC) has announced the operation of 1,000 additional buses during the Christmas festival to cater to the increased travel demand across the State and neighbouring regions.
The special services will run in addition to the existing schedules on December 19, 20, and 24, ahead of Christmas celebrations on December 25.
According to KSRTC, return special services from various intra-State and inter-State destinations to Bengaluru will be operated on December 26 and 28 to facilitate the smooth return of passengers after the festival.
A release by KSRTC stated that exclusive special buses will be operated from Bengaluru’s Kempegowda Bus Station to major religious, tourist, and commercial centres, including Dharmasthala, Kukke Subramanya, Shivamogga, Hassan, Mangaluru, Kundapura, Sringeri, Horanadu, Davangere, Hubballi, Dharwad, Belagavi, Vijayapura, Gokarna, Sirsi, Karwar, Raichur, Kalaburagi, Ballari, Koppala, Yadgir, Bidar, Tirupati, Vijayawada and Hyderabad, among others.
Similarly, special services from Mysuru Road Bus Station will operate exclusively towards Mysuru, Hunsur, Piriyapatna, Virajpet, Kushalanagar and Madikeri.
“KSRTC has enabled advanced computerised reservations for all special buses, and the passengers are advised to carefully note their boarding points mentioned on the tickets. Tickets can be booked online through the KSRTC website as well as at reservation counters across Karnataka and other States,” a release stated.
To encourage group travel, KSRTC is offering a 5% fare discount for four or more passengers booking on a single ticket, and a 10% discount on return journey tickets if onward and return tickets are booked together.
“In addition, KSRTC will operate special buses from all taluk and district bus stands based on traffic requirements to ensure hassle-free travel during the festive season,” release added.

title: Multi-crore online fraud: Crime Branch squad in search of 20 more suspects
summary: Crime Branch intensifies search for 20 suspects in a multi-crore cryptocurrency fraud targeting job seekers in Kozhikode.
content:
The Crime Branch has zeroed in on 20 persons suspected to be involved in a multi-crore cryptocurrency fraud operated across the State. The suspects are believed to be a part of a large racket, the details of which emerged following the arrest of a popular vlogger, Muhammad Diligent Blesslee, who was at large in connection with one of the cases registered at Kakkur police station in Kozhikode district.
The investigation is being led by Deputy Superintendent of Police V.V. Benny and has been intensified with the support of more than 30 police officers from various stations. Police sources said 12 members of the suspected racket have already been arrested from different parts of the State with solid digital evidence.
Police officers from Kakkur station said the fraud was carried out by offering fake online job opportunities with reputed companies, mainly for promotional video shoot assignments. The racket allegedly collected large sums of money from them under the pretext of selling various company shares under their control. Social media platforms and instant messaging applications were used to lure the investors.
Police sources said the first suspected case against the racket was registered at the Kakkur police station after one of the complainants lost ₹5.15 lakh. The defrauded money was reportedly routed through multiple mule accounts and later transferred as cryptocurrency to accounts held by unknown individuals abroad. The total amount involved in the scam was estimated to be around ₹145 crore.
The details of many of the suspects in the racket were gathered following the interrogation of Mr. Blesslee who reportedly played key roles in the gang’s operations. It was after a six-month long probe that the police nabbed the suspect from Thiruvananthapuram airport on December 16. They had also issued a lookout notice against him after confirming his alleged role in the multi-crore investment fraud.
The preliminary investigations revealed that the majority of the cheated victims were job seekers from Thamarassery, Kodenchery and Koduvally regions in Kozhikode district. A senior police officer associated with the probe said some of the suspects left the country a few months ago noticing the criminal proceedings initiated against them. Repatriation measures would be initiated soon against them in pace with the ongoing investigation, he said.

title: ED seizes crores in cash, gold, and silver in ‘Donkey Route’ case
summary: ED uncovers illegal immigration syndicate, seizing ₹4.68 crore cash, gold, and silver in 'Donkey Route' money laundering case.
content:
The Enforcement Directorate (ED) has seized ₹4.68 crore in cash, gold bars worth ₹8.07 crore, and silver bars valued at about ₹6.42 crore during searches at 13 locations across Punjab, Haryana, and Delhi in connection with a money laundering investigation in the “Donkey Route” case linked to illegal immigration into the United States.
According to the agency, besides cash, gold bars and silver bars weighing 5.9 kg and 313 kg were impounded, along with gold coins worth ₹2.7 lakh and several digital devices and documents. Over 50 original passports of third parties were also impounded from various premises.
On December 15, the ED provisionally attached movable and immovable properties worth ₹5.41 crore, including agricultural land, residential and commercial premises, and bank accounts.
The money-laundering probe stems from multiple First Information Reports registered by the police in Punjab and Haryana concerning the deportation of 330 Indian nationals to India in February 2025 by the U.S. government, as they had entered the country illegally.
The ED found that various agents and their associates deceived people by promising legal entry into the U.S. and charged hefty sums. The syndicate involved a large network of travel agents, middlemen, “donkers” (human trafficking agents), overseas associates, hawala operators, and providers of lodging and other logistical arrangements.
The accused reportedly sent people via dangerous routes through various South American countries, eventually making them enter the U.S. illegally through the Mexico border. Midway, the victims were subjected to torture, forced to pay additional sums, and coerced into committing illegal acts.

title: People with nothing to hide need not be bothered about surveillance, SC says
summary: Supreme Court affirms that those with nothing to hide need not fear surveillance, while emphasizing citizens' right to privacy.
content:
The Supreme Court on Friday (December 19, 2025) reasoned that people with nothing to hide need not be bothered about or afraid of surveillance, even as the State of Telangana batted for citizens’ right to privacy, emphasising that even the President of India cannot direct anyone to be put under illegal snooping.
The State reminded the court of its own nine-judge Bench judgment upholding privacy as part of the fundamental right to life under the Constitution.
The top court, the sentinel on thequi viveof fundamental rights, which includes the right to privacy, justified that citizens lived in an “open world”, indicating that those with clear hearts and minds need not be scared of snooping.
The State defended that the question involved was not about an “open or closed world”, but the basic right to be protected against illegal surveillance by the state machinery.
The debate in the court room between the Bench, headed by Justice B.V. Nagarathna, and Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, appearing for Telangana along with senior advocate Siddharth Luthra, occurred during a hearing in the Telangana phone-tapping case.
“The question is can it [illegal surveillance] be done? The question here is not whether a person is ‘bothered’ or whether he has something to hide,” Mr. Mehta submitted.
The State had sought an extension of the police custody of former Telangana Special Intelligence Bureau (SIB) chief T. Prabhakar Rao, who is an accused in the snooping phone-tapping case during the previous BRS government in the State.
“Now we live in an open world. Nobody is in a closed world. Nobody should be really bothered about surveillance. Why should anyone be bothered about surveillance unless they have something to hide?” Justice Nagarathna questioned.
Mr. Mehta asked whether the court was saying if “every government will have a free hand in putting people under surveillance”. He said illegal snooping by the government the Supreme Court was simply not permitted. It was plainly against the law.
“The Supreme Court knows the difference between an ‘open’ world and being under illegal surveillance. My personal communications with my wife… I have a right not to be under surveillance,” Mr. Mehta pointed out.
The top law officer referred to the court’s judgment in the Puttaswamy case, which had upheld privacy as integral to human dignity, liberty and autonomy, encompassing personal intimacies, family life, and sexual orientation.
Though acknowledging at one point that “ideally” surveillance should not be done, Justice Nagarathna’s oral remarks continued to focus on the logic that a person above board personally and professionally had nothing to conceal or feel guilty to fear from the state targeting them through snooping.
“Why should anyone be scared of surveillance? If you have nothing to hide, why should you be afraid?” Justice Nagarathna queried.
The prosecution case against Mr. Rao concerned an alleged conspiracy to “misuse” the resources of SIB for political purposes by putting citizens from different walks of life under surveillance. Those named as accused in the case had allegedly developed profiles of several persons without authorisation. They were accused of monitoring their subjects secretly and illegally, using the information gleaned from snooping in a partisan manner to favour a political party. The accused were also suspected of a conspiracy to destroy records and evidence of their crimes, according to police.
“This was an illegal surveillance without any authority of law under the guise that they were being monitored in connection with left-wing extremism. The information obtained through these illegal means included personal and medical records… This was profiling. It has to stop here. Thereafter they tried to destroy the data and evidence,” Mr. Mehta argued.
The court extended the police custody of Mr. Rao, who had surrendered, till December 25. The Bench directed that he should be released from custody thereafter since the case was pending in the Supreme Court.
The Bench ordered that no coercive steps should be taken against Mr. Rao till the next date of hearing in the top court, January 16, and he should cooperate with the probe when summoned.
Mr. Rao had surrendered before the investigating officer at the Jubilee Hills police station on December 12 on the directions of the top court. He had moved the top court challenging an order of the Telangana High Court which dismissed his plea seeking anticipatory bail.

title: Bhatti meets Odisha’s CM over thermal power generation
summary: Bhatti meets Odisha’s CM over thermal power generation
content:
HYDERABAD
The Telangana Government would explore the possibilities of setting up a pit head thermal power plant at the Naini coal block, operated by Singareni Collieries Company Ltd (SCCL), Deputy Chief Minister and Energy Minister Mallu Bhatti Vikramarka said.
He said this during a meeting with Odisha’s Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi here on Friday. Mr. Vikramarka said that a delegation of the Energy Department officials would visit the Naini area soon and prepare proposals so that the Telangana Government could take a decision.
Principal Secretary (Energy) Navin Mittal, Chairman and Managing Director of SCCL D. Krishna Bhaskar, and a few directors of Singareni were present during the meeting.

title: Anantapur police bags ABCD Award for dismantling Cambodia-based cyber fraud
summary: Anantapur police win ABCD Award for successfully dismantling a Cambodia-based cyber fraud operation, showcasing exceptional crime detection efforts.
content:
The Anantapur district police have won the prestigious State-level Award for Best Crime Detection (ABCD) for cracking a major international cybercrime racket. Director-General of Police Harish Kumar Gupta presented the award to Superintendent of Police P. Jagadeesh at the Police Headquarters in Mangalagiri on Friday (December 19), in the presence of Anantapur Range DIG Shemushi.
The award was conferred on Anantapur police in recognition of an outstanding investigation led by the SP with coordinated efforts by the Rayadurgam urban police station, Rayadurgam rural police station and the District Cybercrime Wing.
The team cracked a sophisticated fraud run from Cambodia, with Delhi as the domestic hub, where fake mobile applications were used to siphon off money and route it through multiple fake bank accounts before conversion into cryptocurrency.
The case came into light after a complaint was filed on June 18, 2025 by Narasimhappa, a software engineer from Veparalla village in Rayadurgam mandal. A case under Section 318(4) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and Section 66(D) of the IT Act was registered by the area police.
Subsequently, the police nabbed five accused on August 1, and seized ₹41.20 lakh in cash, eight mobile phones, a car, 20 ATM cards, 15 SIM cards, five bank passbooks, 10 cheque books and two routers. Investigations revealed that the fraudulent money was channelled through 13 fake accounts across India.

title: Gujarat SIR: Over 73 lakh voters deleted from draft electoral roll
summary: Over 73 lakh voters removed from Gujarat's draft electoral roll amid unprecedented public participation in the Special Intensive Revision.
content:
The Election Commission of India (ECI) on Friday (December 19, 2025) published the draft electoral roll for Gujarat as part of the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, underscoring what it described as an unprecedented level of public participation and transparency in the exercise.
Enumeration forms have been submitted by 4,34,70,109 electors out of a total electorate of 5,08,43,436.
The names of 73.73 lakh voters in Gujarat omitted due to various reasons in draft electoral rolls published by ECI after SIR, said an official toPTI.
The Commission said the verification phase of the state-wide campaign, which began on October 27, has been successfully completed across all 33 districts and 182 Assembly constituencies.
(With PTI inputs)

title: Koil Alwar Thirumanjanam in Tirumala on December 23
summary: Join the Koil Alwar Thirumanjanam ritual in Tirumala on December 23, from 6 a.m. to 10 a.m.
content: As a prelude to the annual Vaikunta Ekadasi festival, the customary Koil Alwar Thirumanjanam will be organised at the temple of Lord Venkateswara here on December 23. The purificatory ritual will be performed from 6 a.m. to 10 a.m., during which period ‘Astadala Pada Padmaradhana Seva’ will remain cancelled. VIP break darshan on December 23 have been cancelled, except for protocol dignitaries, while letters of recommendation will not be accepted on December 22.

title: Swaralaya Samanwayam: Palakkad gears up for 11-day cultural spectacle
summary: Join Palakkad's 11-day cultural festival, Swaralaya Samanwayam 2025, featuring diverse music, dance performances, and renowned artists.
content:
Starting Sunday, the Rapadi open air auditorium in Palakkad town will host an 11-day cultural extravaganza featuring dance and music performances by artistes from across the country.
The programme, titledSwaralaya Samanwayam 2025, is being organised by Swaralaya Palakkad in collaboration with the South Zone Cultural Centre, the State and Central Departments of Culture and Tourism, the Kerala Sangeetha Nataka Academy, and Soorya Thiruvananthapuram.
The programme will feature a variety of performances, including classical Carnatic and Hindustani concerts, dance and music shows of different genres, youth-oriented music bands,  fusion music and dance.
Minister for Excise M.B. Rajesh will inaugurate the festivities on Sunday evening. Fifty singers of Swaralaya will sing a welcome song written by Murali S. Kumar.
Grammy award winner L. Shenkar will lead a double violin and vocal music concert on the inaugural day. He will be accompanied by Anirudha S. Bhatt on mrudangam and Manjunath Sathyasheel on rhythm pad.
Achievers from various fields of life, including Dr. Shenkar, Sidheeque Ahmed, P. Krishnadas, K.S. Mani and Raju Subramanian, will be felicitated at the inaugural function.
Minister for Power K. Krishnankutty will inaugurate the Christmas celebrations on Thursday. Kerala Sangeetha Nataka Academy chairman Mattannur Sankarankutty will be the chief guest.
Minister for Cultural Affairs Saji Cherian will inaugurate the valedictory function on December 31.
Apart from Dr. Shenkar, the artistes who will present programmes on different days include playback singer Anitha Shaiq; classical singers Kalapni Konkali, Nityashree Mahadevan, Ustad Rafique Khan and Pandit Shailesh Bhagavat; Bharatanatyam dancers Aswathy and Srikant, Rama Vaidyanathan, Krishna P. Unni, Kirthi Ramgopal and Gopika Raj Pillai; Kuchipudi dancer Sreelakshmi Govardhan; Mohiniyattom dancers Sunanda Nair and Gyatri Govind; Odissi dancer Sharmila Mukherjee; and classical singers Trivandrum Krishnakumar and Binni Krishnakumar.

title: Six dead as water tank collapses at solar panel manufacturing factory in Nagpur
summary: Six people died when a water tank collapsed at a solar panel factory in Nagpur's MIDC Butibori area.
content:
Six persons died after a water tank collapsed at an industrial unit on the outskirts of Nagpur city on Friday (December 19, 2025), a police official said.
“The incident occurred around 9:30 a.m. at Avaada Electro Private Limited, a solar panel manufacturing factory located in the MIDC Butibori area,” the official said.
While three persons had died at the time of the incident after getting trapped under the debris, three others who were rushed to hospital have also succumbed to injuries, he informed.

title: School timings changed in view of cold wave conditions in Adilabad district
summary: School timings changed in view of cold wave conditions in Adilabad district
content:
Adilabad
With severe cold wave conditions sweeping across Adilabad district, the district administration has rescheduled the timings of all primary, upper primary and high schools in the district.
All schools, including government, local bodies, KGBV, Telangana Model Schools, and private schools will function from 9.40 a.m. to 4.30 p.m. instead of 9 a.m. to 4.15 p.m. with immediate effect, said a press release.
Collector Rajarshi Shah has issued orders to this effect on Thursday.
It may be mentioned that the India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a cold wave alert in Adilabad and eight other districts for Friday.
Meanwhile, Arli in Bheempur mandal recorded the lowest temperature of 7.7 degree Celsius in Adilabad district on Thursday.

title: Huge NDA rally demands district HQ status for Rajampeta
summary: Thousands rally in Rajampeta demanding its recognition as Annamayya district headquarters for better accessibility and administration.
content:
Leaders and activists of the TDP, the JSP and the BJP on Friday (December 19) organised a huge rally here, demanding that Rajampeta be declard as Annamayya district headquarters. Representatives of voluntary organisations, traders, lawyers and students also took part in the protest.
The rally with participants from across the Rajampeta and Railway Kodur Assembly constituencies began at the Old Bus Stand junction and culminated at the Sub-Collector’s office. The protestors raised slogans in support of “Rajampeta as District Headquarters”, highlighting administrative convenience and accessibility to the public.
The protestors contended that Rajamepta meets the requirements to function as an administrative center. They observed that the present district headquarters Rayachoti was geographically a distant entity to the people of Rajampeta division.
TDP in-charge (Rajampeta) Chamarthi Jaganmohan Raju, JSP parliamentary in-charge Vellaturu Srinivasa Raju, BJP leaders led by Potugunta Ramesh Naidu and a number of Congress activists took part in the rally.
Speaking on this ocassion, the protesters urged the government to consider the essential factors of location, infrastructure and population of Rajampeta to bestow it the status of district headquarters.
Later, the Coalition leaders submitted a memorandum to Sub-Collector H.S. Bhavana. They said the protests would continue, coupled with a bandh call on December 23, covering the Rajampeta and Railway Kodur constituencies.

title: BRS flays Congress claims on GP poll results
summary: BRS flays Congress claims on GP poll results
content:
HYDERABAD
The Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) has observed that a large-scale dissatisfaction and opposition in building up among people against the Congress Government and the results of the Gram Panchayat election results, despite the Chief Minister’s whirlwind visits to districts, are a clear indication.
Addressing a press conference here on Friday, party leaders Singireddy Niranjan Reddy, Methuku Anand and others claimed that the BRS supported candidates were elected as Sarpanches in a majority of villages in several districts and in some others, the party supported candidates had secured 50% Sarpanch posts on a par with the ruling party.
They pointed out that when the BRS was in power, the Congress-backed candidates could hardly win 10% of Sarpanch posts. When in power, the BRS had never gone to town about the results despite the party’s supporters winning a majority of the Sarpanch posts across the State, but Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy held a press conference and made tall claims about the GP poll results, whereas the ground reality was different.

title: Survivor in actor rape case appeals to online attackers to let her live
summary: Survivor of actor rape case urges online attackers to stop targeting her after convict reveals her identity in a video.
content:
The survivor in the 2017 Kerala actor rape case has lashed out at Martin Antony, the second accused and now a convict in the case, for posting a video on social media revealing her name. His video, which went viral, had led to comments in social media platforms targeting the survivor.
"The mistake I made was that when an attack was committed against me, I immediately complained to the police and went ahead demanding legal action. I should have remained silent accepting everything  that happened that day as my fate. Later, when that video surfaces some day, I should have committed suicide without knowing what to say to those who accused me of not reporting this to the police," she wrote in a post on her social media page on Friday.
The Thrissur Cyber Police had on Thursday registered a case against Martin on the charge of posting a video revealing the name of the survivor. The video is believed to have been made when he was out on bail.
"The second accused, who was sentenced to 20 years in prison, made a video.  He could have as well said in that video that he was the one who took the nude video. I can only say to those who make such perverse statements and to those who spread them that may neither them nor anyone in their family ever have to face such a situation," she wrote.
She ended the post with the statement, "Not a victim, not a survivor, just a simple human being! Let me live."

title: CM seeks Central aid for Dugarajapatnam shipbuilding and repair cluster
summary: CM Naidu requests Central aid for Dugarajapatnam shipbuilding cluster and additional funds for fishing harbours during ministerial meetings.
content:
Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu sought Central assistance for the development of the Dugarajapatnam shipbuilding and repair cluster and the construction of fishing harbours in tune with Prime Minister’s chip-to-ship vision and in compliance with the provisions of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 during an interaction with Union Minister for Ports, Shipping, and Waterways, Sarbananda Sonowal in New Delhi on Friday.
He said an agreement has been reached for providing 3,488 acres of land for the project and the techno-economic feasibility report (TEFR) has been prepared. Besides, the Chief Minister requested the allocation of additional funds for four fishing harbours (Juvvaladinne, Nizampatnam, Machilipatnam and Uppada) undertaken in Phase-1 at a cost of nearly ₹1,362 crore, of which a sum of ₹591 crore is expected from the Centre.
Mr. Chandrababu Naidu later called on Union Minister for Power, and Housing & Urban Affairs Manohar Lal Khattar and asked him to approve the Visakhapatnam and Vijayawada metro rail projects while stating the revised DPRs have already been submitted.
The Chief Minister also met Union Minister for Petroleum & Natural Gas, Hardeep Singh Puri, whom he invited for the foundation stone laying for the BPCL refinery project in Nellore district and sought his cooperation in attracting investments from natural gas and LNG companies. He sought expansion of gas pipelines and City Gas Distribution (CGD) networks across the State.

title: Give up junk food and consume millet-based foods, says Chamarajanagar Zilla Panchayat CEO
summary: Chamarajanagar Zilla Panchayat CEO urges public to replace junk food with millet-based dishes for better health.
content:
Chamarajanagar Zilla Panchayat CEO Mona Roat has appealed to the public to stop consuming junk food and instead eat food prepared from millets to improve their health.
She inaugurated a ‘Cooking Competition of Forgotten Recipes’ as part of a district-level millet fair organised in Chamarajanagar on December 18 by symbolically pouring ragi from a bamboo basket into a clay pot. The millet fair was organised jointly by the Chamarajanagar district administration, Chamarajanagar Zilla Panchayat, and Agriculture Department in Chamarajanagar in the run-up to the International Millet Trade Fair 2026, scheduled to be held in Bengaluru from January 16 to 18.
Ms. Roat noted with regret that that the consumption of fast food and junk food had increased in recent times while food items prepared from millets were gradually disappearing from dining tables.
Pointing out that there were fewer nutrients in the food that people in general consume today, she noted that junk food, however palatable, has adverse effects on health. “Instead of offering such food to children, it is better to give them home-cooked dishes made from millets,” she said.
Further, she cautioned that the consumption of certain packaged food products can be harmful to health. “Our elders lived long and healthy lives by eating meals and snacks prepared from millets. Mothers should ensure that children are given home-cooked food,” she said, emphasising the need to cultivate millets and pass them on as a legacy to the next generation.
Meanwhile, Sushma, joint director, Department of Agriculture, recalled that participants from Chamarajanagar district had won prizes in earlier State-level competitions. She hoped that participants from the district would take part in the International Millet Trade Fair 2026 and win prizes again.
Judges for the cooking competition included Dr. Dhanyashree and Dr. Manjunath from Chamarajanagar Institute of Medical Sciences (CIMS), besides Dr. Deepa from Krish Vigyan Kendra (KVK), Haradanahalli.
Ms. Roat, Ms. Sushma, and the judges sampled and appreciated the variety of dishes prepared from different types of millets during the event.

title: Forex reserves jump $1.68 bn to $688.94 billion
summary: India's forex reserves rose by $1.68 billion to $688.94 billion for the week ending December 12, 2025.
content:
India's forex reserves jumped by $1.689 billion to $688.949 billion during the week ended December 12, the Reserve Bank of India said on Friday (December 19, 2025). In the previous reporting week, the overall reserves increased by $1.033 billion to $687.26 billion.
For the week ended December 12, foreign currency assets, a major component of the reserves, increased by $906 million to $557.787 billion, according to the data.
Expressed in dollar terms, the foreign currency assets include the effects of appreciation or depreciation of non-U.S. units, such as the euro, pound, and yen, held in the foreign exchange reserves.
“Value of the gold reserves increased by $758 million to $107.741 billion during the week,” the RBI said. The Special Drawing Rights (SDRs) surged by $14 million to $18.745 billion, the apex bank added.
India's reserve position with the IMF rose $11 million to  $4.686 billion in the reporting week, according to the apex bank's data.

title: Enforcement measures strengthened in Kollam ahead of Christmas and New Year
summary: Kollam strengthens enforcement measures for Christmas and New Year to prevent price hikes, hoarding, and ensure public safety.
content:
The district administration has intensified joint inspections in view of the upcoming Christmas and New Year celebrations. Specific instructions to strengthen enforcement measures were issued by Distric Collector N. Devidas at a meeting of the department heads held at the Kollam Collectoratethe other day.
While joint squads of the Excise and Police departments will conduct inspections to prevent the sale and consumption of illicit liquor, drugs, and other intoxicants, striking force units and special squads from range and sub-offices are operating 24/7 to ensure public safety. Public can report such cases to the 24-hour excise control room at the following numbers: 0474 2745648, 9447178054, or 9496002862.
Border patrol teams will conduct rigorous checks at border checkpoints. Joint raids and vehicle inspections will be strengthened by the Police, Excise, and Forest departments. Directives have also been issued to tighten surveillance at railway stations, parcel offices, homestays, resorts, houseboats, and the premises of schools and colleges.
To prevent price hikes and hoarding during the festive season, squads comprising officials from the Civil Supplies, Legal Metrology, Food Safety and Health along with tahsildars will conduct inspections. They have been asked to ensure that there are no malpractices such as tampering with weighing and measuring equipment, hoarding, black marketing or food adulteration in commercial establishments and shops. Additionally, the Health, Local Self-Government, and Food Safety departments have been directed to take necessary action regarding public health, food safety, and waste management.
The regional transport office (RTO) has been directed to take strict action against those who violate traffic rules, including drunk driving and speeding.
The Forest department will implement measures to prevent the production of illicit liquor in forest areas and the smuggling of intoxicants through forest borders. To enhance safety on beaches during the festive days, more lifeguards will be deployed and the services of civil defence volunteers will be used. Necessary security arrangements will also be made at other tourist centres to ensure a festive season free from law and order issues and health concerns.

title: Unidentified animal kills cattle in Chittoor villages
summary: Residents of Chittoor villages live in fear as an unidentified animal attacks and kills cattle at night, raising safety concerns.
content:
Fear gripped several forest-fringe villages of Tavanampalle and Irala mandals of Chittoor district after a series of nighttime attacks on cattle by an unidentified wild animal. Over the past fortnight, a few cattle were found mauled to death, leading to some villagers believing that it could be the handiwork of a leopard or two.
Residents observe that the animal strikes late at night after people fall asleep and disappears without leaving a trace. The impact now is such that the residents have stopped going out after dark and started securing their livestock and dogs within the house premises.
Some of the villages facing the threat are BC Colony, Tavanampalle, Aragonda, Gurukuvaripalle, Sarakallu, Echaneri, Cherlopalle, Boyapalle, Vengampalle, Putramaddi, Kullampalle, Mittur, Guravanampalle, Thottlopalle, Kaminayanapalle and Chengampalle in these two mandals. Incidentally, the forested hills in this region are known for frequent leopard movements and crop raiding by wild elephants.
A team of forest officials from Chittoor visited the affected villages and installed camera traps to identify the animal. Despite search, neither the team nor the villagers could find any clues such as pugmarks, which further escalated tension among the public.
A shepherd in the locality said that a few days ago, his dog, which guarded his sheep as they grazed, was killed in a mysterious manner. Since then, he stopped taking the sheep close to the forest zone.
A forest official said proposals would be sent for providing compensation to the villagers who lost their cattle in the attack.

title: Discipline is the key to competitive exam success: Regional Commissioner
summary: Regional Commissioner Nitesh Patel emphasizes discipline and focused study as essential for success in competitive exams during a training camp inauguration.
content:
Nitesh Patel, Regional Commissioner of Mysuru division, advised aspirants preparing for competitive examinations to cultivate learning discipline and engage in continuous, focused study to achieve success.
He was speaking after inaugurating a 50-day training camp for banking and Union government recruitment examinations, organised by the Competitive Examination Training Centre of Karnataka State Open University (KSOU) here on December 19. On the occasion, he also released a study book titledMuktabhandaraand interacted with candidates.
Mr. Patel said success in competitive examinations becomes meaningful only when it leads to securing a job. While lakhs of candidates apply for recruitment notifications, only a few are finally selected. Many aspirants refrain from appearing for examinations owing to fear, while others apply casually without serious preparation. Only those who prepare sincerely emerge successful and secure a government job, he said.
He advised aspirants to appear confidently for all recruitment examinations conducted by Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) and Karnataka Public Service Commission (KPSC). Writing more examinations helps build experience and confidence, he added, recalling that he himself had appeared for several smaller examinations while preparing for UPSC.
Referring specifically to banking examinations, Mr. Patel stressed the importance of regularly taking mock tests, which help aspirants manage time effectively and identify mistakes.
He also advised students to prepare concise notes, highlight key points, and revise them regularly as the examination approaches. Mental preparedness, hard work, and the ability to effectively express one’s knowledge are crucial to reach the pinnacle of success, he added.
KSOU Vice-Chancellor Sharanappa V. Halse, who also spoke on the occasion, described learning as a continuous journey that cannot be completed in a single day. He urged students to constantly assess the knowledge they acquire after joining the university and move forward with clear goals.

title: Parents are essential for effective care of neurodiverse kids: Expert
summary: Parents play a crucial role in supporting effective care for neurodiverse children, emphasizes expert Thomas Kishore at a national workshop.
content:
Stressing that families are the cornerstone for effective care of neurodiverse children, Thomas Kishore, noted researcher and clinical psychologist at NIMHANS in Bengaluru, inaugurated a two-day Rehabilitation Council of India’s Continuing Rehabilitation Education (RCI–CRE) national workshop at the All India Institute of Speech and Hearing (AIISH) here on December 18.
Speaking after inaugurating the workshop ‘Emerging Trends in Multidisciplinary Evidence-Based Intervention of Neurodiverse Population’ on the Naimisham campus, Prof. Kishore highlighted the growing evidence supporting parent-mediated interventions as a sustainable and impactful approach in managing Neurodevelopmental Disorders (NDDs) such as Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) and Intellectual and Developmental Disabilities (IDD).
He emphasised that intervention strategies must be family-centric, focusing equally on child training and parental well-being. Early identification of parental distress, he said, is critical, as parents and extended family members inevitably become the primary support system for children with NDDs.
Explaining the concept of neurodiversity, Prof. Kishore said variations in thinking, learning and behaviour should be recognised as natural human differences rather than deficits. He observed that parent-mediated interventions have proven effective even in resource-constrained settings and often lead to positive transformations within families, including enhanced sensitivity, resilience and a more optimistic outlook on life. Sustained success, he added, depends on long-term, trust-based partnerships between families and professionals to reorganise supports and strengthen coping mechanisms.
M. Pushpavathi, director, AIISH, who presided over the workshop, underscored the importance of early identification of neurodiverse populations and the adoption of evidence-based, multidisciplinary practices to achieve meaningful outcomes. She called upon professionals and students to enhance inter-professional collaboration in clinical and academic settings.
Program coordinator Jayashree C. Shanbal, head of department of Speech-Language Psychology, AIISH, said the workshop aims to bridge the gap between research and clinical practice by equipping participants with technology-enabled assessment and intervention tools. The workshop is providing rich clinical exposure and fostering collaborative approaches to promote social-emotional development and active engagement among individuals with ASD.

title: SC refuses to stay CBI probe in FIRs against suspended Punjab DIG Bhullar in bribery case
summary: Supreme Court declines to halt CBI investigation into suspended Punjab DIG Bhullar's bribery case, leaving high court proceedings intact.
content:
The Supreme Court on Friday (December 19, 2025) refused to entertain a plea of suspended Punjab Police DIG Harcharan Singh Bhullar seeking stay of the CBI investigation in two FIRs lodged against him in a disproportionate assets case.
A bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and justices Joymalya Bagchi and Vipul M. Pancholi said the Punjab and Haryana High Court was seized of a similar plea of Mr. Bhullar. The officer has challenged the December 4 order of the high court which had denied interim relief of stay on the CBI proceedings and adjourned his plea for hearing in January.
When Mr. Bhullar's counsel sought direction for deciding on interim relief, CJI Kant said, "It's better, we don't open our mouths. Don't invite harsh observations from us." 	Senior advocate Vikram Chaudhary, appearing for Mr. Bhullar, submitted that the high court erred in adjourning the matter by a month without considering the prayer for interim relief.
He submitted that it was a case where the CBI has wrongly assumed jurisdiction in violation of the Delhi Special Police Establishment (DSPE) Act, as the State's consent for CBI has already been withdrawn.
"CBI has surreptitiously entered Punjab and circumvented section 6 of the DSPE Act," he submitted, adding that the high court has not assigned any reason for not giving interim relief, except saying that it was hearing the matter.
Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, appearing for the CBI, said that regular bail has been denied to Mr. Bhullar.
The Bench said it was not inclined to interfere with the proceedings before the high court and was inclined to dismiss the petition. Sensing the mood of the court, advocate Chaudhary said he wants to withdraw the petition and avail the remedy before the high court.
The top court disposed of the matter.
On October 16, the CBI arrested Bhullar, along with another person, in connection with a corruption case involving bribery of Rs 8 lakh.
It had claimed to have recovered around ₹5 crore cash, 1.50 kg of jewellery, documents of immovable properties, keys of two luxury vehicles, 22 luxury watches, locker keys, 40 litres of imported liquor, firearms, including a double-barrel gun, a pistol, a revolver, and an airgun, along with ammunition during a raid at DIG Bhullar's residence.
He was held from his Mohali office following a complaint lodged by a scrap dealer from Mandi Gobindgarh in Fatehgarh Sahib who accused the senior police officer of demanding recurring monthly payment for "settling" a 2023 FIR against him.
He was appointed the DIG (Ropar Range) in November 2024. The Ropar Range comprises Mohali, Rupnagar and Fatehgarh Sahib districts. He is the son of former Punjab Director General of Police M.S. Bhullar.
DIG Bhullar had earlier served in many positions. He remained DIG (Patiala Range), joint director, vigilance bureau, and senior superintendent of police in Jagraon, Mohali and Sangrur, Fatehgarh Sahib, Khanna, Hoshiarpur and Gurdaspur.
He had also headed a special investigation team, probing a 2021 drug case against Shiromani Akali Dal leader Bikram Singh Majithia.
The officer was actively involved in the Punjab government's anti-drug drive Yudh Nashian Virudh.

title: Nara Lokesh inaugurates ₹6.3 crore academic buildings at Rajahmundry Arts College

Minister for Education and IT Nara Lokesh inaugurating Vandemataram memorial park at the Government Arts College in Rajamahendravaram City on Friday.
