He interacted with international students in the C.V.Raman International Studies and Research Centre and inquired about their experiences. Collegiate Education Commissioner Bharat Gupta, Government Arts College (Autonomous) Principal K. Ramachandra Rao and faculty were present.

title: Sri Lanka Deputy Minister meets Stalin, thanks him for Cyclone Ditwah relief
summary: Sri Lanka's Deputy Minister thanks Tamil Nadu's CM Stalin for cyclone relief efforts during a recent meeting in Chennai.
content:
Sundaralingam Pradeep, Deputy Minister of Plantation and Community Infrastructure, Government of Sri Lanka, met Tamil Nadu Chief Minister M.K. Stalin on Friday (December 19, 2025) and thanked him for providing assistance to those affected by Cyclone Ditwah in the island country.
Mr. Stalin had, on December 6, 2025, flagged off 950 tonnes of relief materials aboard two Indian Navy vessels from the Chennai and Thoothukudi ports to support people affected by the cyclone. Chief Secretary N. Muruganandam, Ganesanathan Geethiswaran, Deputy High Commissioner of Sri Lanka, and senior officials were among those present at the meeting.
Separately, office-bearers of various associations of persons with disabilities called on Mr. Stalin and thanked him for providing representation to persons with disabilities through nominations in local bodies.

title: Drug peddler arrested in Ameerpet, 5 grams of MDMA seized
summary: Drug peddler arrested in Ameerpet with 5 grams of MDMA; police investigate his connections and ongoing drug network.
content:
A drug peddler was arrested by the Elite Action Group for Drug Law Enforcement (EAGLE) Force, Telangana, along with the S.R. Nagar police. The officials seized 5 grams of MDMA along with a mobile phone from the accused.
The accused was identified as Asif Goulani, 31, a cafeteria manager at Priston Hospital on D K Road. He is a resident of Attapur in Hyderabad and a native of Bhavnagar district in Gujarat. The arrest was made on December 18 near the Guru Govind Singh MCH Multi Purpose Sports Complex on D.K. Road in Ameerpet, following a tip-off.
Preliminary investigation revealed that the accused had been involved in drug peddling for several years. A native of Gujarat, he had moved with his family to Telangana during his childhood and discontinued his education due to financial difficulties, taking up work in bakeries. During this period, he developed alcohol addiction and later began consuming narcotic substances.
In March 2024, he moved to Mumbai to work at a restaurant run by a friend, where he began procuring MDMA from local suppliers in the Nala Sopara area. After returning to Hyderabad in June 2024, he planned to make quick money through drug peddling.
Police said he was arrested in October 2024 by Petbasheerabad police in a Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act case and was released from jail in May this year. After his release, he resumed work at the hospital cafeteria but continued his involvement in the drug trade. About two weeks ago, he procured 10 grams of MDMA from a childhood friend in Gujarat through a courier service, consumed half of it himself and attempted to sell the remaining quantity.
On December 18, while trying to sell the remaining MDMA to a customer, he was apprehended by the EAGLE Force team and S R Nagar police. Further investigation is underway to trace his suppliers and possible links to a wider network.

title: SPDCL installs over 100 pole-mounted transformers in Hyderabad, makes them safer
summary: SPDCL installs over 100 pole-mounted transformers in Hyderabad, enhancing safety and efficiency while planning 300 more installations.
content:
HYDERABAD
The Southern Power Distribution Company of Telangana Ltd (TGSPDCL) has installed over 100 pole-mounted distribution transformers in the Greater Hyderabad limits so far in locations where the existing equipment, installed in the conventional method, are  posing a risk to the public or obstructing roads.
Traditionally, installing a transformer on a plinth requires a minimum space of 30 to 35 square feet. The construction of concrete plinths and the curing process take about a week. Moreover, equipment such as the HG (horn gap) fuse set, distribution box and AB (air break) switch need to be installed separately on another pole, leading to poor cleanliness around the DTR plinth.
According to Chairman and Managing Director of the TGSPDCL Md. Musharrf Faruqui, the PMDT system would enable installation of the transformer at a height of 6 to 9 feet on an 11-metre-tall spun pole with a diameter of just 377 millimetres. All associated equipment including the HG fuse set, distribution box and AB switch are specially designed to be mounted on the same pole.
Under the new method, a transformer can be installed within a single day. Using a bucket ladder, only one staff member can safely and conveniently carry out maintenance activities. Future underground (UG) cables could also be connected to these pole-mounted transformers with ease, Mr. Musharraf said.
At present, transformers with capacities of 63 kVA, 100 kVA and 160 kVA are being installed on 11-metre poles under the PMDT system. While these poles are suitable for transportation along major roads, some difficulty is being faced while transporting them through narrow lanes. To overcome this issue, TGSPDCL is taking steps to install transformers on shorter, 9.5-metre poles as well, he explained.
Additionally, the feasibility of installing higher-capacity transformers under this system is also being examined, the CMD stated and added that the PMDT installation works are underway at another 304 locations across Greater Hyderabad now. The new method would significantly reduce space requirements and ensure that the surroundings of the transformer are safer and more orderly.

title: National Herald case: Police foils Congress workers’ attempt to lay siege to BJP office in Mysuru
summary: Police thwart Congress workers' protest at BJP office in Mysuru over alleged misuse of central agencies in National Herald case.
content:
A large number of Congress workers were taken into custody and later released when they tried to lay siege to the BJP’s office in Mysuru on December 19 in protest against the BJP’s alleged misuse of central agencies to foist a false case against party leaders Sonia Gandhi and Rahul Gandhi in the National Herald case.
The Congress activists, led by the party’s district unit president B.J. Vijaykumar and city unit president R. Murthy, gathered near Ramaswamy Circle in large numbers before marching towards the BJP’s office, shouting slogans against the saffron party.
Mr. Murthy pointed out that a Delhi court had rightly dismissed the complaint filed by the Enforcement Directorate (ED).
However, the police set up barricades on the way to the BJP office as a precautionary measure and stopped the Congress workers en route. But when some Congress activists tried to push through the barricades and run towards the office, the police managed to restrain them before taking them away in a vehicle.
The detained Congress workers were taken to CAR parade ground in the city and later released.
Tension prevailed for some time around the BJP office during the protest. BJP workers too had assembled in front of their office and raised slogans condemning the Congress.
Meanwhile, Mr. Vijaykumar alleged that the ruling BJP at the Centre was trying to harass Congress leaders Sonia Gandhi and Rahul Gandhi by misusing central agencies like the ED to book politically motivated cases against them.
Mr. Murthy said the BJP-led Union government was using investigative agencies to “pursue its politics of vendetta”, which poses a serious threat to the nation’s democracy and sovereignty. He said the Congress party was always ready to fight against such unethical policies of the BJP government.

title: Over 97 lakh voters deleted from Tamil Nadu draft electoral roll after SIR
summary: Over 97 lakh voters removed from Tamil Nadu's electoral roll after the Special Intensive Revision, impacting Chennai significantly.
content:
TheElection Commission of India has published the integrated draft electoral rollforTamil Naduwith 97.37 lakh voters deleted in the draft roll after the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise, according to Chief Election Officer (CEO) Archana Patnaik.
Press release.(1/2)pic.twitter.com/WBbuY1kOLX
The total number of voters as of October 27, 2025 was 6,41,14,587. According to the draft roll published on Friday (December 19, 2025), the total number of electors in the State is 5,43,76,756. The total number of voters removed after the exercise stands at 97,37,831.
The total number of deceased voters identified is 26,94,672.  As many as 66,44,881 voters have either shifted or were absent during the exercise. A total of 3,39,278 voters have been found enrolled in multiple places.
The Greater Chennai Corporation (GCC) released the draft electoral roll for 16 constituencies in the Chennai district, listing a total of 25,79,676 voters. This includes 12,47,690 male voters, 13,31,243 female voters, and 743 transperson voters. A total of 14,25,018 voter names have been deleted due to reasons such as death, relocation, duplication, and absence.

title: District task force clears procurement of toor dal under MSP in Kalaburagi
summary: Kalaburagi's Task Force approves toor dal procurement under MSP for 2025–26 season, benefiting local farmers and ensuring fair pricing.
content:
Deputy Commissioner says that registration and procurement at purchase centres will be carried out using Point of Sale machines, and Aadhaar-based biometric authentication will be mandatory.
                                                            | Photo Credit: 
                                FILE PHOTO
The district-level Task Force Committee has approved the procurement of toor dal from farmers under the Minimum Support Price (MSP) scheme for the 2025–26 season, following orders issued by the State government.
The decision was taken at a meeting chaired by Deputy Commissioner Fouzia Taranum on Thursday. Under the scheme, toor dal will be procured at ₹8,000 per quintal, with a ceiling of four quintals per acre, based on the cultivated area reflected in the FRUITS software.
Addressing the meeting, the Deputy Commissioner said that if market prices remain higher than the MSP, the National Agricultural Cooperative Marketing Federation of India would procure toor dal through the e-auction portal of the Agricultural Produce Market Committees (APMCs) and in the open market at rates higher than MSP for buffer stock purposes.
For Kalaburagi district, the Karnataka State Pulses Development Board and the Karnataka State Cooperative Marketing Federation have been designated as State procurement agencies. Toor dal will be procured through 141 Primary Agricultural Credit Cooperative Societies (PACCS) and Farmer Producer Organisations (FPOs) across the district.
The Deputy Commissioner said that registration and procurement at purchase centres would be carried out using Point of Sale machines, and Aadhaar-based biometric authentication would be mandatory. She appealed to farmers to cooperate with the procurement agencies to ensure smooth implementation of the scheme.
The registration of farmers under the MSP scheme will be open till March 6, while procurement of toor dal from registered farmers will continue till March 16. The payment for the procured produce will be made directly to farmers’ bank accounts through the Direct Benefit Transfer portal.
Ms. Taranum urged farmers to approach their nearest PACCS, FPOs or toor dal procurement centres at APMCs to register within the stipulated time and avail the benefits of the MSP scheme.
For further information related to registration and procurement, farmers can contact the Karnataka State Cooperative Marketing Federation, Kalaburagi, at 9449864446 or the Karnataka State Pulses Development Board, Kalaburagi, at 9964474444.
Joint Director of Agriculture Samad Patel, Deputy Registrar of Cooperative Societies Kishor Patil, Assistant Director of the APMC Department Santosh, and officials from procurement agencies and the Pulses Development Board were present at the meeting.

title: Public cautioned against cyber fraud disguised as festive gifts
summary: Superintendent of Police warns public to stay vigilant against cyber fraud disguised as festive gift offers this holiday season.
content:
Superintendent of Police Vikrant Patil on Friday (December 19) issued an advisory cautioning the public against cyber frauds being carried out in the guise of Christmas and New Year gift offers.
Speaking to the media here, he urged the public to remain vigilant and not fall prey to deceptive online links promising gift cards, prizes or festive rewards. Cybercriminals were actively exploiting the festive shopping season by circulating fake links through social media platforms and emails. Clicking on such links could lead to theft of personal and financial information.
Mr. Patil warned people against sharing sensitive details such as Aadhaar, PAN, voter ID, bank account information or mobile numbers on unknown or suspicious links, saying that such actions could result in manipulation or withdrawals from banks. The SP stressed that merely clicking on malicious links could compromise personal data.
The SP urged the public to ignore and delete any suspicious messages or links and to verify the authenticity of online offers before responding. He further appealed to victims of cyber fraud to immediately report incidents to the nearest police station or cybercrime numbers, such as the National Cyber Crime Helpline (1930) or online at cybercrime.gov.in.

title: Kerala HC asks Chief Secretary to form panel to check if sand removal from Thottappally can be done without eco damage
summary: Kerala HC orders a committee to assess ecological impacts of sand removal from Thottappally, balancing flood control and environmental safety.
content:
The Kerala High Court has directed the Chief Secretary to set up a high-level committee to check whether the removal of sand and soil from the Thottappally spillway in Alapuzha can be carried out without harming the ecology of the region.
A Division Bench comprising Chief Justice Nitin Jamdar and Justice Syam Kumar V.M. observed on Thursday that any decision on the matter ought to be taken on the basis of environmental assessment. Flood-control measures should be balanced by including an ecological impact monitoring mechanism that ensures compliance with environmental safeguards, the court said.
Stating that the ecological impact of the activity cannot be ignored, especially since the area falls within the jurisdictional ambit of the Kerala Coastal Zone Management Authority, the court directed the Chief Secretary to constitute a committee headed by the District Collector, Alappuzha, with experts and officials from the departments of Irrigation and Water Resources, Forest and Wildlife, Kerala Coastal Zone Management Authority, the Purakkad and Thakazhy grama panchayats and representative of a Non-Governmental Organisation (NGO) having local presence and expertise.
The committee should be competent enough to suggest, determine and monitor all aspects of sand or soil mining and removal from the Thottappally Spillway after due assessment of its ecological and environmental impact. Removal of soil/sand from the Thottappally Spillway/sand bar should hence be carried out only after obtaining relevant inputs from the said committee constituted within two months, the court added.
The direction was issued on the basis of petitions filed by Green Roots Nature Conservation Forum, Thottappally, and by M.R. Omanakuttan, also from Thottappally. They had challenged the legality of an order and the ecological impact of flood containment measures that the Alappuzha District Collector, as the Chairman of the District Disaster Management Authority, had issued. They included the removal of sand from the Thottappally Spillway as well as the soil accumulated in the Thanneermukkam Bund and the cutting and removal of casuarina trees which ‘blocked’ the flow of water from the spillway.
They contended that the sand removal measures were not a disaster prevention measure, as made out to be. Their real objective, allegedly, is to permit continuous and unregulated extraction of mineral-rich sand from the area, unmindful of its ecological impact. The direct result during the past few years is the devastation of nearly 15 acres of ecologically sensitive area near the spillway, which is also a ‘turtle nesting ground’ coming under Regulation Zone Notification, 2011. Species of Olive Ridley and Hawksbill turtle, which are included in Schedule I of the Wildlife Protection Act, use the said area as nesting grounds. Among others, this would have a detrimental impact on such protected nesting grounds.

title: TPCC announces statewide protests against BJP’s move on MGNREGA
summary: TPCC announces statewide protests against BJP’s move on MGNREGA

title: Man dies in road accident in Belagavi
summary: A 30-year-old man dies in a road accident involving a car carrying a personal secretary to the Deputy Chief Minister.
content:
A 30-year-old man died in a road accident, involving a car in which Rajendra Prasad, personal secretary to Deputy Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar, was travelling, on Thursday night.
The deceased has been identified as Manjunath Byranahatti, a resident of Saundatti. Byranahatti was an employee of Harsha Sugar Factory, owned by Minister for Women and Child Development Laxmi Hebbalkar’s family.
He had left his home for work. At the Saundatti Cross, he was hit by the car and died on the spot with serious head injuries.

title: Two arrested for duping senior citizen of ₹59 lakh in Hyderabad ‘digital arrest’ scam
summary: Two men arrested in Hyderabad for duping a senior citizen of ₹59 lakh in a 'digital arrest' scam.
content:
The Cyber crime wing of the Hyderabad police arrested two key accused in connection with a ‘digital arrest’ scam case in which a retired senior citizen was cheated of ₹59.03 lakh.
The accused were identified as Surampudi Chandrasekhar, 31, and Emandi Venkat Naveen, 25, both residents of Kakinada in Andhra Pradesh. Police said that they acted as account suppliers in an organised interstate cyber fraud network.
The case came to light on December 4 when the victim received WhatsApp calls from unknown persons impersonating police and government officials. The callers falsely accused him of involvement in serious offences including human trafficking, overseas job fraud and money laundering. To intimidate him further, forged arrest warrants were sent via WhatsApp. Under sustained threats of immediate arrest, the victim transferred ₹59.03 lakh through RTGS from his Union Bank of India account between December 4 and December 6.
Investigation revealed that the fraudsters operated a well-coordinated ‘digital arrest’ scam by posing as law enforcement officers and creating fear through continuous video and voice calls. In such cases, the gang forced the victims to move money into multiple bank accounts and, in some instances, used malicious APK files to gain access to internet banking and SMS services. The cheated amounts were routed through shell firm accounts, converted into cryptocurrency, mainly USDT, and later withdrawn through Binance peer-to-peer transactions into personal accounts.
The arrested accused, part of an interstate cyber fraud racket, procured and shared bank accounts to facilitate the movement of cheated funds. Police said at least 15 current accounts had been arranged by them for the prime accused. They also allegedly received proceeds in cryptocurrency, which were later converted into Indian currency.
The accused were found to be linked to 65 cyber fraud cases across the country, including in Karnataka, Maharashtra, Delhi, Tamil Nadu, Uttar Pradesh and Gujarat. In Telangana alone, they are connected to five cases registered in Hyderabad, Cyberabad and Sangareddy. The total amount involved in the cases nationwide is estimated to be around ₹8 crore.
During the arrests, police seized five mobile phones, four cheque books, ten debit cards and three PAN cards. Other accused involved in the case are absconding. The arrested men have been remanded to judicial custody, and further investigation is underway.

title: Gap of over 13% in vote share with LDF powered UDF’s landslide win in Kochi Corpn.
summary: UDF secures a decisive victory in Kochi Corporation with a 13.20% vote share lead over LDF in local polls.
content:
A sizeable vote share difference of 13.20% turbocharged the United Democratic Front’s (UDF) landslide victory, enabling it to wrest the power back from its immediate rival Left Democratic Front (LDF), in Kochi Corporation in the just concluded local body polls.
While the UDF amassed 41.45% of the total polled votes, the LDF could only muster 28.25% of the votes, while the Bharatiya Janata Party-led National Democratic Front ended up a distant third with only 14.45% of the votes. The UDF polled a total of 1.13 lakh votes compared to 77,234 votes and 39,408 votes garnered by the LDF and the NDA, respectively.
The UDF recorded the biggest vote share in Pachalam (74.89%), followed by Panampilly Nagar (63.35%), Perumanoor (63.16%), Thoppumpady (62.45%), Vaduthala West (61.20%), and Mundamveli (60.51%). Besides, in another 18 divisions, it polled in excess of 50% of the total votes polled. This included Fort Kochi (58.99%), Kathrikadavu (56.41%), Stadium (55.90%), Puthiyaroad (55.45%), Vyttila Janatha (54.94%), Dhevankulangara (54.84%), Elamkulam (54.65%), Ayyappankkavu (54.62%), Vennala (54.47%), Kaloor South (54%), Vaduthala East (53.73%), Palluruthy (53.51%), Chalikkavattom (52.64%), Island South (51.92%), Kadavanthra (51.70%), Chakkaraparambu (51.40%), Kaloor North (50.94%), and Thammanam (50.64%). It polled the least in Amaravathy (10.41%), Cheralayi (14.34%) - both seats won by the BJP -and Kadebagham (17.55%).
The LDF was reduced to a single-digit vote share in Cheralayi (5.47%), Island North (7.72%), and Panayappilly (8.34%). Kadebagham (64.80%) division gave it the biggest vote share, while it registered a vote share in excess of 50% in Thazhuppu (54.73%), Nazreth (54.64%), Palluruthy-Kacherippady (53.56%), Palluruthy East (51.72%), and Chakkamadom (51.56%).
While the NDA didn’t field candidates in four - Earaveli, Mattancherry, Chalikkavattom, and Manasserry – out of the 76 divisions in the Corporation, its vote share was restricted to a single digit in 30 divisions, though overall it managed to increase the number of seats from the previous five to six in this election.
The BJP’s biggest vote share of 56.83% was registered in Cheralayi against Independent candidate Shyamala S. Prabhu, who won the division for the party for six consecutive times between 1988 and 2020 before she quit the party ahead of this election. This was followed by Amaravathy (52.75%) and Island North (50.68%).

title: Parliament Winter Session: 8 out of 10 Bills tabled pass both Houses, two sent to Standing Committee
summary: Parliament's Winter Session saw 8 of 10 bills passed, including SHANTI and reforms to employment and insurance sectors.
content:
The 15-sitting winter session of the Parliament held between December 1 and 19 this year, saw the introduction of ten new Bills in the Lok Sabha, passage of eight by both Houses and two sent for further scrutiny by a Standing Committee.
ALSO WATCHWatch: Explained: What are Supplementary Demands for Grants?
Of the eight Bills passed, three were ‘Money Bills’ (i.e. don’t require passage by Rajya Sabha) -The Health Security se National Security Cess Bill, 2025,The Central Excise (Amendment) Bill, 2025andThe Manipur Goods and Services Tax (Second Amendment) Bill, 2025. While the first two dealt with levying cess and excise on tobacco manufacturing plants, the last one revised the GST slabs into two – 5% and 18%, according to the Council’s decision.
Six ‘Financial Bills’ were introduced of which three have passed by both Houses -The Sustainable Harnessing and Advancement of Nuclear Energy for Transforming India (SHANTI) Bill, 2025, theSabka Bima Sabki Raksha (Amendment of Insurance Laws) Bill, 2025 andViksit Bharat Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB-G RAM G) Bill, 2025. While the first one opens up the nuclear power sector to private players (domestic and foreign), the second one allows upto 100% Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) in the insurance sector.
TheVB- G Ram G Bill replacesthe 20-year-old Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA). Amid vehement protests from the Opposition, which staged a twelve-hour dharna in the House, the Lok Sabha passed this Bill via voice vote, and the Rajya Sabha followed suit within hours. The Bill drops the Mahatma’s name from the Bill, adds ‘Ram’ in its name and revamps the employment scheme from a demand-driven to an allocation scheme. It also cuts the Centre’s contribution to 60% and adds a 40% burden on state’s finances.
Opposition had pleaded with the government to send the Bills for further scrutiny by a Parliamentary Standing Committee, but to no avail.
Financial Bills are categorised as such when it impacts the Consolidated fund of India (CFI) but not through taxes. The above bills all have penalties which would be credited to the CFI. Such Bills can be amended, debated and have to be passed by Rajya Sabha.
The only ‘Ordinary’ Bill which was passed both Houses is the Repealing and Amending Bill, 2025 which repeals 71 laws and amends four. Of the laws repealed, only six were passed prior to 2015. Others were introduced and passed by the current Modi government only.
Two Bills which have been sent for further scrutiny are - The Viksit Bharat Shiksha Adhishthan Bill, 2025 and the Securities Markets Code, 2025. Vehemently critiqued by the Opposition, the first seeks to centralise Higher Education in India under one single board and the second seeks to consolidate financial laws dealing with the securities market into a single framework.
Opposition has condemned the Centre’s spree of renaming laws to Hindi, accusing it of ‘Hindi imposition’. TMC MP Saugata Roy also pointed out that terms like ‘Viksit Bharat’, ‘Sabka Bima Sabka Raksha’ echo BJP’s own campaign terms.
The short session also saw adiscussion on ‘Vande Mataram’, in which 65 members participated and lasted 11 hours and 32 minutes in Lok Sabha, informed the Speaker. The debate saw theCentre accuse late Prime Minister Pandit Jawaharlal Nehruof ‘distorting’ the national song as he allowed only the first two stanzas be recognised as India’s official national song. In response, Congress accused the Centre of staging the debate as a distraction to avoid discussing issues like pollution, inflation, dropping rupee value in Parliament.
ALSO WATCHWatch: Amit Shah targets opposition on SIR in Lok Sabha
Another debate was held on electoral reforms, in which 63 hours participated in and lasted for 13 hours, informed the Speaker. A fiery debate was witnessed between Leader of Opposition (LoP) Rahul Gandhi and Home Minister Amit Shah over the ongoing Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls in 12 states. While Mr. Gandhi demanded the Centre reply to his accusations on ‘vote chori’ in Haryana polls, voter deletion in Bihar and protecting the Election Commissioner from prosecution, Mr. Shah affirmed faith in the process reiterating the Election Commission’s clarification on the above accusations.
Overall, the Lok Sabha held 15 sittings spanning 92 hours and 25 minutes and clocked productivity of 111%.

title: TP murder case convict granted parole again
summary: T.K. Rajeesh, convicted in the T.P. Chandrasekharan murder case, is granted a controversial 20-day parole amidst renewed scrutiny.
content:
T.K. Rajeesh, the fourth accused and a life convict in the T.P. Chandrasekharan murder case, was granted parole again, triggering a renewed row. He was allowed a 20-day parole and is required to return to prison by January 10. This is the second parole granted to him within a span of three months.
The parole was granted with strict conditions, including a ban on entering Kannur and Kozhikode districts. Rajeesh was earlier granted a 30-day parole from August 1. After returning to prison, he underwent Ayurvedic treatment for one-and-a half months and returned to jail on December 7.
The latest parole comes at a time when allegations have surfaced regarding irregularities in granting parole to convicts in the case.
Rajeesh, a native of Kannur, has provided an address in Ernakulam district in jail records. Hence, one of the parole conditions is that he should not leave Ernakulam district during the parole period.

title: Tripura CM flags concern over law and order in Bangladesh
summary: Tripura CM Manik Saha expresses concern over Bangladesh's law and order, ensuring preparedness for potential border contingencies.
content:
Tripura Chief Minister Dr. Manik Saha on Friday (December 19, 2025) spoke on the developing situation in Bangladesh, expressing concern over violent incidents and what he described as a sharp deterioration in law and order since deposed Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina left the neighbouring country.
He said the State government was prepared to deal with any situation emerging out of developments in Bangladesh, given that Tripura shares its border with the country on three sides.
“We have all been aware of the security situation in Bangladesh from the time former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina left the country. Convicts involved in various serious crimes were released from prisons,” Dr. Saha said during an interaction with journalists here.
He, however, noted that the situation in Bangladesh was an international issue and said the State government was communicating its concerns to the Centre.
The Chief Minister, who also holds the Home portfolio, said security had been tightened along the border. He added that the central government was aware of the situation.

title: Karnataka govt.’s decision to revoke Cantonment Railway Colony’s biodiversity tag draws criticism
summary: Karnataka's decision to revoke the Cantonment Railway Colony's biodiversity tag faces backlash from environmentalists and community leaders.
content:
An environmental organisation, Parisarakkagi Naavu, has criticised the State Forest, Ecology and Environment Department for withdrawing its earlier order to bestow biodiversity heritage site tag to the 8.61-acre Cantonment Railway Colony in Bengaluru.
Former MLA and environmentalist A.T. Ramaswamy, who is also the president of the organisation, on Friday, said that the reason given by Environment Minister Eshwar Khandre for withdrawing its earlier notification issued on September 10 reflects the inefficiency and irresponsibility of the department.
Mr. Khandre had said that the State government is withdrawing the September 10 order due to legal restrictions under the Railway Act.
“The Environment Minister said that the Railway Land Authority has promised to relocate and replant these trees. This statement by the Minister shows that the protection of 371 huge trees is not his priority, but rather to allow the trees to be cut down and to construct buildings there,” he said.
The organisation welcomed the High Court’s order against the cutting of 371 trees in the Cantonment Railway Colony without permission.
“The Railway Land Authority should either give a vacant land (without trees) under its jurisdiction to a private company to build a building or demolish the old quarters and build multi-storey buildings there or allow multi-storey buildings to be built on top of railway stations like those built in foreign countries,” he added.

title: Congress dominates Sarpanch polls in Vikarabad: Rammohan Reddy
summary: Congress dominates Sarpanch polls in Vikarabad: Rammohan Reddy
content:
Hyderabad
The Congress party registered a decisive victory in the Gram Panchayat Sarpanch elections across the Pargi Assembly constituency in Vikarabad district, by securing a clear majority of posts in both the first and third phases of polling, according to Pargi MLA T. Rammohan Reddy.
Mr. Reddy said that out of the total of 206 Gram Panchayats in the constituency, Congress-backed candidates won 137 Sarpanch posts, accounting for 67%, while the Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) secured 57 posts (28%). BJP won only four posts, while eight positions went to other candidates. As many as 20 Gram Panchayats unanimously elected candidates supported by the Congress.
Congress emerged strong in Gandeed (62%), Mohammadabad (77%), Chowdapur (83%), Kulkacharla (69%), Doma (63%) and Pudur (75%) mandals. BRS performed comparatively better only in Pargi mandal, where it secured 60% of posts, while Congress managed 43%.
Across Vikarabad district’s four constituencies, Pargi, Kodangal, Tandur and Vikarabad, the Congress-backed candidates maintained a dominant position, said Mr. Reddy.
In Kodangal, represented by Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy, Congress won 132 out of 181 Gram Panchayats (72%), while BRS secured 29. In Tandur, Congress won 110 out of 155 posts (71%), with BRS claiming 42.
In Vikarabad constituency, the contest was relatively tougher with Congress winning 72 out of 143 posts (49%), while BRS secured 30 and other candidates won a significant 38 posts.
Overall, Congress won 451 out of 685 Sarpanch posts (65%), while BRS secured 158 posts (22%). Other candidates won 64 posts and BJP managed only 12, Mr. Rammohan Reddy said. The results indicate a strong rural endorsement for the ruling party in Vikarabad district, he said.

title: Pawan Kalyan holds one-to-one meetings with party MLAs
summary: Pawan Kalyan meets with nine MLAs to discuss constituency development and welfare scheme implementation in Vijayawada.
content:
Jana Sena Party (JSP) president and Deputy Chief Minister K. Pawan Kalyan held separate meetings with nine MLAs at his camp office, near Mangalagiri, on Friday, and discussed issues related to development of the respective constituencies and implementation of welfare schemes. He also took stock of the political situation in the constituencies.
The MLAs with whom Mr. Pawan Kalyan had deliberations were Mandali Buddha Prasad, D. Varaprasad, Lokam Naga Madhavi, Giddi Satyanarayana, Pantham Nanaji, Ch. Vamsi Krishna, Nimmaka Jayakrishna, Panchakarla Ramesh Babu, and Sundarapu Vijay Kumar.

title: Nara Lokesh inaugurates three academic buildings in Adikavi Nannaya University
summary: Nara Lokesh inaugurates three new academic buildings at Adikavi Nannaya University, enhancing educational infrastructure in Rajamahendravaram.
content:
Minister for Education and Information Technology Nara Lokesh on Friday (December 19, 2025) inaugurated three academic buildings at Adikavi Nannaya University on the outskirts of Rajamahendravaram city. The buildings, named after the rivers Manjeera, Gouthami, and Indravathi, were constructed at a cost of ₹33.80 crore.
Adikavi Nannaya University Vice-Chancellor Prof. S. Prasanna Sree announced that the examination building, named after Manjeera river, was built at ₹8.25 crore and College of Engineering building, named of river Gouthami, was built at ₹20.05 crore. The School of Commerce and Management, which was named after Indravathi river was built with ₹5.50 crore. Prof. Prasanna Sree briefed the Education Minister on the building infrastructure facilities of the campus.
Rajanagaram MLA B. Balarama Krishna, Rajamahendravaram Urban Development Authority Chairman B. Venkataramana Chowdary, Collegiate Education Commissioner Narayana Bharat Gupta, Registrar K. V. Swamy and other officials were present.

title: Congress, CPI(M) protest removal of Gandhi’s name from MGNREGA
summary: Congress and CPI(M) protest in Tirupati against the removal of Gandhi's name from MGNREGA, criticising the government's actions.
content:
Leaders and activists of the Congress and CPI(M) on Friday (December 19) staged separate demonstrations in Tirupati, condemning the Union government’s decision to remove the name of Mahatma Gandhi from the MGNREGA scheme.
“The scheme brought by the Congress was meant to provide work and income to the rural poor. The BJP-led NDA government has belittled the well-intended scheme,” said Congress Tirupati City president Goudaperu Chittibabu.
Mahatma Gandhi remained synonymous with local self-government, but with this act, the incumbent government killed the spirit of self-governance, the protesters said.
Meanwhile, the CPI(M) district committee members staged a separate demonstration not only against the removal of Gandhi’s name, but also against the change of the scheme’s framework, which, the party alleged, burdened the States.

title: IN-SPACe invites proposals to establish space labs across academic institutions
summary: IN-SPACe invites proposals to establish innovative space labs at academic institutions across India to enhance space technology education.
content:
The Indian National Space Promotion and Authorisation Centre (IN-SPACe) has rolled out a Request for Proposal (RfP) to establish Antariksh Prayogshala (Space Labs) at select academic institutions across India, as part of its ongoing efforts to strengthen the country’s space technology ecosystem and build future-ready talent.
IN-SPACe said that Antariksh Prayogshala is a first-of-its-kind initiative aimed at creating state-of-the-art space laboratories within Indian academic institutions.
These labs will provide hands-on training and exposure to students pursuing space tech courses in academic institutes spread across the country. This initiative is intended to enable meaningful industry–academia collaboration and support India’s long-term vision of becoming a leading global space economy.
Under the scheme, up to seven academic institutions will be selected in a phased manner from different zones across the country.
“To ensure balanced regional representation one lab is proposed in each zone. These labs will also be available to NGEs for utilization in that zone. IN-SPACe will provide financial support of up to 75 percent of the total project cost, with a cap of ₹5 crore per institution, to be released on a milestone-linked basis,” IN-SPACe said.
It added that the selection process will be carried out in two stages. Institutions will first be screened based on eligibility criteria outlined in the RfP.
Shortlisted applicants will then be evaluated and ranked by an Empowered Committee (EC), following which final selections will be made on a zone-wise basis.
“Antariksh Prayogshala is designed to translate academic knowledge into deployable capability. By creating shared spaces for students, researchers, and industry, these labs will enable applied research, early-stage innovation, and skill development aligned with real industry needs. This is a practical step towards building depth, scale, and sustainability in India’s space ecosystem,” Vinod Kumar, director, Promotion Directorate, IN-SPACe, said.

title: Drone, aerial activity ban imposed in parts of Cyberabad during Vice President’s visit
summary: Drone, aerial activity ban imposed in parts of Cyberabad during Vice President’s visit
content:
The Cyberabad police have imposed a temporary ban on the operation of drones and other aerial devices in parts of the commissionerate in view of the visit Vice President C. P. Radhakrishnan to Hyderabad later this week.
According to a notification issued by Cyberabad Police Commissioner Avinash Mohanty, the Vice President will be in Hyderabad from December 20 to December 21 to attend the World Meditation Day celebrations and other official programmes.
The restriction will be in force in the jurisdictional limits of RGIA, Shamshabad and Nandigama police stations in the Cyberabad commissionerate on December 20 and 21.

title: Alert bank staff, cyber crime police foil ‘digital arrest’ scam, save retired teacher from losing ₹18 lakh
summary: Cyber crime police thwarted a ‘digital arrest’ scam, saving a retired teacher from losing ₹18 lakh in Nalgonda.
content:
The Telangana Cyber Security Bureau (TGCSB) has foiled a ‘digital arrest’ fraud attempt and saved a retried school teacher in Nalgonda district from losing ₹18 lakh.
The intervention was carried out by the District Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (D4C) of the TGCSB after fraudsters attempted to coerce the elderly victim into transferring his retirement savings. The victim, P Devender Reddy, a resident of Nalgonda, who retired a year ago, had deposited his retirement benefits in his bank account.
Police said the victim had been under sustained psychological pressure for nearly three days from cyber criminals posing as  Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) officials. The callers falsely claimed that his Aadhaar number had been linked to a criminal case involving the circulation of obscene photos and videos on social media. They threatened him with ‘digital arrest’ and demanded an immediate transfer of ₹18 lakh to close the alleged case.
On December 19, around noon, the victim and his wife went to the State Bank of India’s Prakasham Bazar branch in Nalgonda to transfer the money. Bank officials noticed his anxious behaviour and urgency, which raised suspicion. The branch manager promptly alerted the Deputy Superintendent of Police of the D4C, Nalgonda.
The DSP and the cyber crime team rushed to the bank and temporarily halted the transaction. After conducting a detailed enquiry, the team confirmed that it was a ‘digital arrest’ scam. The victim and his family were counselled and informed that no police or government agency conducts digital arrests or demands money over phone calls.
Owing to the timely intervention and effective coordination between the D4C team and bank officials, the fraudulent transaction was stopped and the entire amount of ₹18 lakh, the victim’s retirement benefits, was successfully saved.
Cyber Crime Police have initiated further technical analysis to trace the fraudsters involved. Investigators are examining digital footprints, call records and associated bank accounts to identify the culprits and prevent similar incidents.
Police have once again urged the public, particularly senior citizens and recently retired individuals, to remain vigilant. They reiterated that no law enforcement or government agency conducts digital arrests or asks for money transfers under any circumstances. Citizens have been advised to immediately report such incidents by calling the national cyber crime helpline 1930 or by lodging a complaint on the cybercrime portal.

title: Polavaram displaced families look to tide over livelihood crisis
summary: Displaced families from Polavaram face livelihood challenges, struggling for survival as government support remains insufficient amid project-related disruptions.
content:
A mighty Peepal tree stands guard as the sacred Godavari River curves along the hillside to reach Penikilapadu, a village once inhabited by the Koya tribe, in Mantooru Panchayat of Devipatnam Mandal in the Alluri Sitarama Raju district. The tribal community, which eked out a living through fishing, had to abandon the village in July 2020 to make way for the Polavaram Project, labelled India’s largest multi-purpose irrigation project.
The Polavaram Project is being built across the Godavari River in the erstwhile West Godavari district. Declared a national project, it aims to divert 80 TMC of Godavari water to Krishna River, irrigate 4.36 lakh hectares, supply drinking water to 28 lakh people, and generate 960 MW of hydropower.
At least 56 Project Displaced Families (PDFs) were relocated to the Kondamodalu Polavaram Project Resettlement and Rehabilitation (R&R) colony at Pedda Bhimpalli village in Devipatnam Mandal. With this, the total number of PDFs in the colony rose to 310, belonging to three tribes—Koya, Konda Kammara and Konda Reddi, a Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Group in Andhra Pradesh. The Kondamodalu R&R colony lies 40–50 km away from their ancestral villages.
“It was around the end of July 2020 when the river swelled with record-high flood inflows, forcing us to flee. The floods washed away nine dhones—traditional boats—belonging to our village and buried part of the settlement near the Polavaram spillway,” recalled Mr. Ramana Dora.
In July 2020, the flood level at Bhadrachalam, upstream of the Polavaram project, touched 71.30 ft—the highest since the great flood of 1986, when it reached 75.6 ft.
The dhone used for fishing, crossing the river, and even during medical emergencies.
                                                            | Photo Credit: 
                                T. Appala Naidu
In the Polavaram submergence area, the Konda Reddi, Konda Kammara and Koya tribes shared a deep bond with dhone. Crafted from the Booriga tree (local name) and measuring approximately 10 to 15 feet, the dhone was used for fishing, crossing the river, and even during medical emergencies. Owing to the nature of the wood, thedhonecould float even when overturned and could carry eight to nine people.
The PDFs said that they are struggling to earn a livelihood in their rehabilitated areas. Farming or fishing in their abandoned villages for temporary sustenance has become nearly impossible due to the inaccessibility from the R&R colonies.
“In our ancestral villages, everything came from nature—the river and the forest. In the R&R colony, nothing comes without cash. How can we earn money when we have no skills to find work outside the forest?” lamented 36‑year‑old Kareem Ramana Dora, a bachelor enrolled as a Para Legal Volunteer. “Our family’s seven acres of land in our native village are yet to be submerged. But tending to the fields or resuming fishing is impossible, as we cannot afford to cross the river regularly,” he added.
In Kachuluru village, located two kilometres upstream from Penikilapadu, at least 80 families fled during the 2020 floods and settled in the Indukuru‑2 R&R colony. The tribes of Kachuluru had displayed remarkable courage by rescuing 26 tourists after the private tourist vesselRoyal Vasishta Punnamicapsized near their village on September 15, 2019, killing 51 people.
“Our family’s 20 acres of land, with nearly 300 palm trees, fell within the Polavaram submergence area. Most villagers are now jobless in the R&R colony, particularly the men,” said Konutula Chittibabu.
Recalling that his only fishing boat, the dhone, was washed away by the river, he said, “I sold mylanchi, which once plied across the river between Polavaram and Kondamodalu, at a throwaway price of ₹80,000. If I hadn’t sold it, where would I have anchored it in the R&R colony?” Mr. Chittibabu asked.
A father of three, Mr. Chittibabu is now trying his luck in agriculture on the land allotted under the Land-to-Land (LTL) component near the Indukuru-2 colony.
As of October 2025, of the total 38,060 PDFs across 172 habitations in the submerged areas of the erstwhile East and West Godavari districts, 14,371 PDFs have been relocated to 26 R&R colonies, according to the Polavaram Project Authority under the Ministry of Jal Shakti.
A total of 89,996 acres of land has been acquired for constructing 121 R&R colonies and allotment under the LTL component. The acquisition of 1,00,100 acres requires ₹12,832 crore, but nearly half of the funds are yet to be released by the Centre.
Polavaram Irrigation Project Administrator V. Abhishek said the State government has roped in the Andhra Pradesh Industrial Infrastructure Corporation (APIIC) to identify suitable land for setting up industries near R&R colonies.
“We have adopted consent-based rehabilitation for economic viability. Families are being asked to choose LTL land, and ₹700 crore has already been spent on land acquisition since November,” he said. Construction of 49 more R&R colonies is underway following re-tendering. Land is also being identified for rehabilitating 17,114 PDFs from 49 habitations in the Chintoor agency area, which faces submergence risks post-2020 floods.
Despite these efforts, many families are still struggling to make a livelihood. Konuthula Papayamma, a mother of five from Thallooru village, said: “We were allotted 2.5 acres under the LTL component, but it has no irrigation access and is unsuitable for cultivation. Using compensation money, we prepared the land, but in four years, we could grow cashew on only half an acre.”
“Only four families among the 310 PDFs in Kondamodalu R&R colony accepted land under the LTL component. Every family here is still searching for a guaranteed livelihood,” she said. Accompanied by her husband Babu Rao, she works wherever labour is available in nearby Gokavaram town.
Alluri Sitarama Raju District Collector A.S. Dinesh Kumar said that a mapping exercise is underway to assess skill-training requirements among PDFs. “MSME parks are being encouraged near R&R colonies. Each colony will eventually have a Skill Training Centre.”
Polavaram-displaced women returning from a day’s work in the nearby towns, near Konda Modalu R&R Colony in Pedda Bhimpalli village, Devipatnam Mandal, Alluri Sitarama Raju district.
                                                            | Photo Credit: 
                                T. Appala Naidu
Sangam Sreelatha, 26, a mother of three, said families now accept any unskilled work in nearby towns like Rajamahendravaram, Gokavaram and Kakinada. “My husband works in construction, while women find seasonal work in tobacco and maize fields. The wages are meagre—₹350 per day—excluding ₹100 for transportation. Monsoon is the hardest time,” she said.
In R&R colonies under ITDA limits, women travel long distances by autorickshaws to find work, while many men remain unemployed. “During winter, we leave home by 5 a.m. and return in the evening after working in maize fields and tobacco nurseries, travelling nearly 50 km one way,” said Nesika Subbayamma of Indukuru-2 colony.
Quality concerns continue to haunt Polavaram project, despite foreign experts’ recommendations
Women earn a maximum of ₹500 per day in agriculture and shift to construction work during the off-season. “Over the years, men have remained unemployed and take care of children,” she added.
Families have also been forced to alter their traditional diets due to worsening poverty. “I haven’t seen Vonjalu fish since 2020. In our village, it was abundant. Here, we can’t even afford farmed fish. Our food habits have changed to those of the plains,” said Mr. Ramana Dora. Women once fished alongside men in the Godavari.
The PDFs remain hopeful that they can resume fishing, as they are entitled to fishing rights in the Polavaram reservoir only once the project is commissioned.
According to the Second Schedule of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013, “In cases of irrigation or hydel projects, the affected families may be allowed fishing rights in the reservoirs, in such manner as may be prescribed by the appropriate government.”
“If entitlements are honoured in letter and spirit, we hope to regain our fishing rights in the reservoir. We wish to live the life we once lived by the river — perhaps after the project is commissioned. Until then, our lives hang between uncertainty and the sacred river Godavari,” he added.
Meanwhile, during a high‑level review in Amaravati on October 3, 2025, Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu set a new deadline to commission the Polavaram project by the Godavari Pushkarams in 2027. As of October, 79% of earthwork, 84.78% of concrete work, and 86.26% of steel work had been completed.

title: BJP gains in city, fails to make a mark in rural Kozhikode
summary: BJP excels in urban Kozhikode elections but struggles in rural areas, winning only 17 of 1,343 panchayat wards.
content:
The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) made significant inroads into the urban landscape of Kozhikode in the recently held local body elections, but it failed to leave much of a mark in rural areas.
Securing 13 of the 76 seats in the Kozhikode Corporation is a huge leap for the party, which was restricted to seven seats in the council over the past decade. Almost doubling the number of seats this time, the party not only made its presence felt in some pockets of the city but also ensured that it would have more voice in the council that is barely hanging in the balance.
While the CPI(M)-led Left Democratic Front (LDF) secured only 35 of the 76 seats, and the Congress-led United Democratic Front (UDF) won 28 seats, no front enjoys a simple majority in the Corporation council. Neither front can remain in power without the support of the other or the BJP, which may lead to major power struggles within the council for the foreseeable future.
The BJP found support in some new pockets, including the newly formed Mavoor Road division, and some of its victories are politically relevant. Two-time councillor Navya Haridas continued her dream run in the Karaparamba division. The party won the Chalappuram division, considered a Congress stronghold, Pottammal, which was represented by Mayor Beena Philip and had been a stronghold of the LDF for over four decades, and the Paroppady division, where the party’s Hareesh Pottangadi defeated P.M. Niyas of the Congress, who was projected as the UDF’s mayoral candidate. On the other hand, the party lost ground in some sitting divisions, such as Meenchanda, Athanikkal, and East Hill.
Despite the noticeable gain in the city, the BJP’s footprint across municipalities and grama panchayats in the district remains minimal. It had won nine wards across seven municipalities in the district in the 2020 local body polls and has not been able to improve the tally in 2025. As for grama panchayats, the BJP could win only 17 of the 1,343 wards in 70 grama panchayats in the district.

title: Traditional medicine doesn’t get recognition it deserves; has to win confidence via science: PM Modi
summary: PM Modi emphasizes the need for scientific validation to enhance the global recognition of traditional medicine at the WHO summit.
content:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday (December 19, 2025) said traditional medicine does not get the recognition it deserves and has to win the confidence of the masses through science to expand its reach.
Addressing the WHO Global Summit on Traditional Medicine, PM Modi said strengthening research, use of digital technologies and developing a trusted regulatory framework will further bolster traditional medicine.
“The one whose body maintains this balance is healthy. Today, restoring balance is not just a global cause, but a global urgency. We will have to take steps at an even faster pace to address it,” PM Modi said.
The Prime Minister said the question related to safety and evidence always crops up when it comes to traditional medicine.
“India is continuously working in this direction. Here, in this summit, you all have seen the example of Ashwagandha. For centuries, it has been used in our traditional medical systems. During COVID-19, its global demand increased rapidly, and its use began in many countries,” PM Modi said.
“India is promoting Ashwagandha through its research and evidence-based validation,” the Prime Minister said.
PM Modi launched several landmark Ayush initiatives including My Ayush Integrated Services Portal (MAISP). He also unveiled the Ayush Mark, which is envisioned as a global benchmark for the quality of Ayush products and services.
PM Modi released the WHO technical report on training in Yoga and the Book ‘From Roots to Global Reach: 11 Years of Transformation in Ayush’.
He also released a commemorative postal stamp on Ashwagandha, symbolising the global resonance of India’s traditional medicinal heritage.

title: Statewide vigilance checks flag irregularities at cotton procurement centres and ginning mills
summary: Statewide vigilance checks flag irregularities at cotton procurement centres and ginning mills
content:
The Vigilance and Enforcement Department has concluded a three-day Statewide programme of surprise inspections at cotton procurement centres and ginning mills, aimed at ensuring transparency in procurement and safeguarding farmers’ welfare.
The inspections were carried out from December 16-18 in coordination with the Cotton Corporation of India, Legal Metrology Department and Agriculture Marketing Department. Officials said that the exercise was intended to ensure that farmers receive MSP and irregularities in cotton procurement process can be curbed.
More than 65 ginning mills and procurement centres were inspected across major cotton-growing districts, including Adilabad, Khammam, Nalgonda, Warangal, Vikarabad, Ranga Reddy, Sangareddy, Nagarkurnool and Narayanpet. During the inspections, teams verified weighbridge certifications, moisture meters, CCTV surveillance systems with data backup ranging from 15 to 120 days, fire safety licences and the implementation of the Kapas Kisan mobile application.
Several violations were detected, leading to cases being registered under the Legal Metrology Act. Action was initiated against cotton mills in Yadadri Bhongir district at Mothkur and in Nalgonda district at Chinthapally for using substandard or unsealed weighbridges. In Sangareddy district, cases were booked against mills for failing to maintain standard 20 kilogram test weights, while a fine of ₹85,000 was imposed on a mill in Rangareddy district for weighbridge variations.
Officials also observed a significant lack of scientific instruments at several mills for measuring staple length and micronaire values in real time. Cotton samples were drawn from heaps at mills in areas such as Warangal and the erstwhile Mahabubnagar region and sent to specialised laboratories for technical verification of ginning percentage and quality. While CCTV cameras were found to be installed at most locations, several mills lacked adequate data backup facilities.
Detailed inspection reports, along with recommendations for upgrading technical equipment at mills, are being submitted to the government for further action. The public has been urged to report any irregularities or misuse of government funds or resources to the V&E Department through the toll-free number 14432.

title: A.P. government urged to clear pending bills of pensioners
summary: Andhra Pradesh pensioners urge government to clear pending bills amid financial struggles affecting senior citizens' livelihoods.
content:
Andhra Pradesh Government Pensioners Welfare Association’s State president P. Ramachandra Rao and Vizianagaram district president Ramachandra Panda on Friday (December 19, 2025) urged the government to clear bills related to provident fund, gratuity, earned cash leaves, and surrender leaves as many senior citizens were facing financial troubles.
In a press release, Mr. Ramachandra said that the pensioners were unable to meet financial expenditure with regard to marriages of children, medical bills, and others. He said that many could not build houses even after 30 years of service in the government in the absence of enhancement of salaries for the last few years.
A.P. Government Employees State Secretary L.V. Yugandhar promised the pensioners that the State body would take up the issue and request the government authorities to clear bills of pensioners as well as staff of other departments. The association leaders Balivada Bala Bhaskar, Pakki Bhusana Rao, Nuka Raju, Sonthi Kameswara Rao and others were present.

title: ‘Your Money, Your Right’ campaign launched in Chamarajanagar
summary: Chamarajanagar's 'Your Money, Your Right' campaign aims to refund ₹30.51 crore in unclaimed deposits to rightful owners.
content:
Chamarajanagar Zilla Panchayat Chief Executive Officer Mona Roat launched the ‘Your Money, Your Right’ campaign on December 19 to refund the unclaimed funds lying in bank deposit accounts to the rightful owners.
Ms. Roat said the district administration will extend full cooperation in settling government accounts related to deposits that did not have any heirs.
Addressing the gathering at the Chamarajanagar Zilla Panchayat office, Meenakshi Ganju, general manager of Reserve Bank of India, Bengaluru, instructed bank officials to make sincere efforts to trace depositors and repay the amounts to original depositors or their nominees as applicable.
She also emphasised the need to bring deposits transferred to the Depositor Education and Awareness Fund (DEAF) back into the financial mainstream and thereby promote economic activity.
In Chamarajanagar, a total of 1,21,881 DEAF accounts remain pending, involving ₹30.51 crore in unclaimed deposits. So far, 208 accounts, amounting to ₹6.11 crore, have been settled by identifying the rightful owners.
Representatives of various banks were also present on the occasion.

title: CPI faces turmoil in Idukki, senior leader quits active politics
summary: CPI turmoil in Idukki escalates as senior leader K.K. Sivaraman quits, criticizing party leadership and electoral performance.
content:
The Communist Party of India (CPI) in Idukki is facing intense turmoil following the setback suffered by the Left Democratic Front (LDF) in the recent local body elections in the district. Former CPI district secretary K.K. Sivaraman announced his retirement from active politics on Friday after levelling serious allegations against the party’s district leadership.
Talking to mediapersons in Thodupuzha on Friday, Mr. Sivaraman said he would henceforth remain just a party worker. “I will not hold any party posts in future. I have ended my 45-year political career,” Mr. Sivaraman said. “The CPI district leadership is moving in the wrong direction, and the party’s condition in this district is pathetic. Vested interests are ruling the district leadership, and there is no space for self-criticism within the party,” said Mr. Sivaraman.
He further alleged that a ‘mafia’ is operating in the district with the cooperation of certain party leaders. “During the tenure of previous State secretaries, the party was active and disciplined. Now, there is no progress. I cannot cooperate with the current stance of the district leadership,” he added.
The public fallout comes amid conflicting reports regarding the party’s electoral performance. According to party sources, the CPI won only 44 of the 200-odd seats it contested in the district. “In the district panchayat, the party lost all five seats it contested. Furthermore, the party failed to win a single seat in nearly 25 panchayats,” said the source.
“The district leadership has systematically sidelined senior leaders such as Mr. Sivaraman, G.N. Gurunathan, and Mathew Varghese to protect the interests of the land mafia. There were also allegations of a ‘paid seat system’ used during seat-sharing negotiations, which led to the party’s downfall,” said the source.
However, CPI district secretary K. Salimkumar refuted these claims, asserting that the party contested 192 seats and won 87. In a press release, the CPI district council dismissed Mr. Sivaraman’s allegations as “anti-party.”
“The allegation that leaders are associated with land and quarry mafias is driven by vested interests. The CPI has always opposed mafia activities in the district,” the statement read. The council attributed the local losses to a broader State-level trend against the LDF rather than issues within the party.

title: AIDSO condemns HECI Bill, calls it attack on institutional autonomy
summary: AIDSO condemns the HECI Bill, asserting it undermines institutional autonomy and promotes centralization in higher education governance.
content:
The All India Democratic Students’ Organisation (AIDSO) has strongly opposed the Higher Education Commission of India (HECI) Bill, recently approved by the Union Cabinet and renamed as the Viksit Bharat Education Supervision Bill, alleging that it seeks to centralise control over higher education and undermine the autonomy of educational institutions.
In a press statement issued on Friday, AIDSO’s Ballari district secretary Kambali Manjunath said the proposed legislation would dissolve existing statutory bodies such as the University Grants Commission (UGC), All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE), and National Council for Teacher Education (NCTE), and merge them into a single regulatory authority functioning directly under the Central government.
According to the statement, the Bill envisages a structure in which the majority of members of the proposed HECI would be appointed by the Union government, giving it sweeping powers over academic regulation, accreditation and professional standards, while financial matters would be handled separately by the administrative Ministry.
This, the AIDSO alleged, would erode institutional autonomy and threaten the democratic functioning of higher education institutions. The student body also criticised what it described as sustained cuts in education Budgets, ideological interference in curricula, and an assault on secular, scientific, and democratic values in the education system. It alleged that the government was retreating from its responsibility of ensuring equitable, accessible and affordable education, while simultaneously seeking greater administrative control over academic institutions.
Recalling that the HECI Bill had faced widespread opposition from students, teachers, and other stakeholders when it was first introduced in 2018, the AIDSO said the reintroduction of the Bill had once again triggered strong resistance from student organisations, teachers’ unions, and educationists across the country.
The statement also linked the Bill to the implementation of the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020, which the AIDSO described as promoting centralisation, communalisation, commercialisation, and privatisation of education. Since the introduction of the NEP, the organisation claimed to have been building sustained movements against what it termed anti-student and anti-education policies.
Calling the present situation critical, the AIDSO urged students, teachers, and education activists to unite against what it described as authoritarian and “fascist” tendencies in education governance, and appealed to democratic, progressive and left-oriented student organisations to come together in defence of a secular, scientific, and universal education system.

title: Government urged to create new panchayat to boost development in three Viziangaram villages
summary: Government urged to establish a new panchayat for three Viziangaram villages to enhance development and civic amenities.
content:
Andhra Pradesh Backward Classes Association’s Vizianagaram district president Golagana Ramesh Yadav on Friday (December 19, 2025) requested the government to create a new panchayat for three villages Nallalapeta, Bethanapalli, and Vudukulapeta, located on the outskirts of Vizianagaram. The creation of a new panchayat will ensure that they get funds and witness developmental activities in future, he added.
In a press note, he said that the three villages which were currently under the jurisdiction of Pedatadivada panchayat of Denkada mandal of Nellimaarla constituency had been facing trouble in the absence of proper roads, drainage system and civic amenities. Mr. Ramesh Yadav said that the association has submitted a memorandum to Collector S. Ramsundar Reddy. He said the move will benefit nearly 15,000 people living in those villages.

title: Praja Vani is solely for resolution of public grievances, says Bhatti
summary: Praja Vani is solely for resolution of public grievances, says Bhatti
content:
HYDERABAD
Deputy Chief Minister Mallu Bhatti Vikramarka said that Praja Vani has been launched by the Congress Government, reaffirming that its governance is meant solely for people.
The one-of-a-kind programme for receiving applications every Tuesday and Friday to hear and resolve people’s grievances and successfully resolving them was a major achievement of the Government. The programme ensured resolution of 74% issues represented by the people in the past two years.
The Deputy Chief Minister was participating in the celebrations organised to mark completion of two years of Praja Vani here on Friday. He said that achieving resolution of issues represented through Praja Vani would not have been possible without the committed efforts of officials and staff who focussed on addressing the petitions received.
In addition to receiving applications, the efficiency of Praja Vani was enhanced with setting up of a special software at the State and district levels with the support of the Centre for Good Governance for speedy resolution of issues.
He recalled how the previous government, which was in power for 10 years, did not open the gates of Praja Bhavan for people to represent their issues. The goal of the present government was to ensure that institutions and systems served the public.

title: Kerala SIR: Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan urges EC to avoid undue haste and include all eligible citizens on voter roll
summary: Kerala CM Pinarayi Vijayan urges the Election Commission to ensure all eligible citizens are included in the voter roll amid concerns.
content:
Expressing concern over reports that 25 lakh people in Kerala could be excluded from the draft electoral roll following the Special Intensive Revision (SIR),  Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan on Friday (December 19, 2025) asked the Election Commission of India (EC) to “re-examine the SIR process in the State and avoid undue haste.”
Rather than excluding voters from the roll on technical grounds, including all eligible citizens by absorbing the values of democracy should be the basis of the electoral roll revision, Mr. Vijayan said in a strongly-worded statement.
“There is a concern that large-scale exclusion from the voter roll is happening under the ‘others’ category in addition to deceased, permanently shifted, duplicated registration and untraceable categories of voters. Even the EC is not clear as to who the ‘Others’ are. There is no doubt that the list under preparation is filled with inaccuracies. The right to vote is not something that should be revoked on technical grounds. It is a right that should be ensured to adult citizens in a democratic society. Its denial is tantamount to destroying the foundations of democracy,” Mr. Vijayan said.
Mr. Vijayan blamed the “undue haste” shown by the EC to undertake the revision during the local body election season in Kerala for the current situation.  Voter roll revision is an exercise that calls for long-term planning and consultations, he pointed out. He demanded the EC to ensure that all eligible voters entered in the rolls after the summary revision in September 2025 find a place in the SIR rolls.
The Chief Minister’s comments have come a day after the enumeration phase of the SIR ended in Kerala. As per the data released by Chief Electoral Officer (Kerala) Rathan U. Kelkar, the number of ‘Uncollectable forms’ (absent, shifted, dead and untraceable voters) stood at 24.81 lakh as on Thursday. This includes 6.49 lakh deceased voters, 6.89 lakh untraceable voters, 8.21 lakh shifted voters, 1.34 lakh duplicated names and 1.86 lakh in the ‘others’ category.
Mr. Vijayan observed that a situation has emerged where people who were below 18 years of age during the previous SIR in 2002 are being asked to prove their relationships. Available data show that, on an average, the number of ineligible people come to nearly 2 lakh  per district, he said. He further criticised the EC for implementing the exercise without ensuring adequate transparency.
The Chief Minister said that the State government would adopt all necessary measures to ensure that all eligible citizens find a place in the list. The government moved the Supreme Court as part of this commitment. Taking a serious view of the concerns raised by the State government, the Court too has instructed that they should be addressed, he said.

title: Hyderabad man loses ₹3.41 lakh in sextortion scam
summary: Hyderabad man loses ₹3.41 lakh in sextortion scam
content:
A resident of Gowliguda in Hyderabad was cheated of ₹3.41 lakh in a sextortion scam, police said on Friday.  The scam unfolded on October 5 at around 1:30 p.m. but it came to light only on December 19.
On October 5, the victim received a call from an unknown woman who identified herself as Jyothi Gupta and attempted to seduce him during the conversation. Shortly afterwards, he received a video call from another person who introduced himself as Vikram Goswami and appeared to be wearing a uniform. The caller threatened to circulate an alleged video of the victim on social media and ruin his reputation.
Out of fear and panic, the victim was coerced into making multiple payments on different occasions through Google Pay to an account held by one Manjeet Singh. The accused assured him that the matter would be closed and that the money would be refunded. However, the threats continued and the victim later discovered that his bank accounts were hacked, resulting in further financial losses.
Police said that the accused escalated the intimidation by falsely claiming that the woman involved in the call had died and demanded additional money to prevent legal consequences. Overwhelmed by fear, social stigma and a sense of helplessness, the victim ended up losing a total of ₹3,41,950.
Following a complaint, a case has been booked by the cyber crime wing of the Hyderabad police and further investigation is underway.
The police issued an advisory cautioning that such video call blackmail cases are a common form of online fraud and urged the public not to accept video calls from unknown numbers or engage with callers making threats. They stressed that no law enforcement agency ever demands money over phone or video calls to close cases or prevent circulation of videos.
Citizens have been advised to immediately disconnect and block threatening calls, avoid sharing OTPs, bank details or screen access, and preserve all evidence such as call logs, screenshots and payment details. Victims of cyber fraud have been urged to report incidents immediately by calling the national cyber crime helpline 1930 or by lodging a complaint on the cybercrime portal to enable timely action.

title: Ready to face inquiry on land-grab allegations: Revenue Minister
summary: Denying allegations of land-grab by his family, Revenue Minister Krishna Byre Gowda has volunteered to face any inquiry.
content:
Denying allegations of land-grab by his family, Revenue Minister Krishna Byre Gowda has volunteered to face any inquiry.
Making a statement in the Legislative Assembly here on Friday, Mr. Byre Gowda appealed to the Speaker to order a probe by a suitable agency after consulting Leader of the Opposition and the Chief Minister.
Leader of the Opposition in the Legislative Council Chalavadi Narayanaswamy had alleged that the Revenue Minister grabbed government land at Garudanapalya in Kolar district.
The Minister said that the land originally belonged to Mysore rulers. His grandfather, Chowde Gowda, had got the land for a lease of 10 years from the trust in the name of Srikantadatta Narasimharaja Wadiyar Trust in 1953. However, even as the lease was in effect, the original owners sold the land to Habeebulla Khan in 1959. Chowde Gowda questioned the sale of land and finally it was resolved through a compromise.
“Since 1953, our family has been in possession of 256 acres of land at Garudanapalya, a village that belonged to one family. The land consists of two tanks, which are intact. Not even an inch of tank is encroached upon. When I traced the land records, at one stage a portion of 20 acres of land had been mentioned as a tank, which is against the nature of the land and the survey records. And, we got the entire land through an absolute sale deed, and there was no question of encroaching on government land,” he stated, adding his grandfather got the land before he was even born.
Further, he opined that the allegations against him may be due to his strict stance with regard to his department.
“People who were affected by my action might be behind the allegations. However, let there be an inquiry by whichever agency, and I will accept the outcome,” he said.
The Minister also invited the Speaker and the Leader of the Opposition to visit the land and verify.
Leader of the Opposition R. Ashok suggested a suitable inquiry into the allegation so that the matter could be clarified.

title: Traffic advisory issued for President’s visit through Cyberabad on December 20
summary: Traffic advisory issued for President’s visit through Cyberabad on December 20
content:
The Cyberabad Traffic Police have issued a traffic advisory in view of the movement of President Droupadi Murmu on Saturday, alerting commuters of possible congestion along several major routes in the city.
According to the advisory, the President will be travelling from Rashtrapati Nilayam to Brahma Kumaris centre in Gachibowli, and traffic congestion is expected within Cyberabad limits between 3 p.m. and 7 p.m.
Key junctions likely to be affected include Gachibowli, IIIT and ITC Kohinoor junctions. Traffic movement is expected to be impacted along Road No. 45, Cable Bridge, IKEA flyover, Deloitte stretch, Gachibowli Junction, Indira Nagar, IIIT Junction, Pullela Gopichand Academy area and the road leading to Brahma Kumaris centre.
Motorists have been advised to avoid these routes as far as possible during the specified hours and to use alternative roads to reach their destinations. The traffic police have urged people to plan their travel in advance and cooperate with the authorities to ensure smooth vehicular movement during the President’s visit.

title: ED seizes assets linked to YouTuber Anurag Dwivedi in ‘illegal’ betting case
summary: ED seizes assets worth ₹7 crore from YouTuber Anurag Dwivedi linked to an illegal betting investigation in Delhi and Uttar Pradesh.
content:
The Enforcement Directorate (ED) has seized luxury vehicles worth over ₹4 crore and frozen movable assets valued at about ₹3 crore during searches at 10 premises in Delhi and Uttar Pradesh linked to YouTuber and social media influencer Anurag Dwivedi in a case of alleged illegal betting and gambling, the agency said on Friday (December 19, 2025).
The searches were carried out in Uttar Pradesh’s Lucknow and Unnao. “During the searches, four high-end cars, incriminating documents, digital devices, and about ₹20 lakh in cash were seized. Papers detailing real estate investments made by Mr. Dwivedi in Dubai through ‘hawala’ channels were also recovered. Further, movable assets in the form of insurance policies, fixed deposits, and bank account balances amounting to about ₹3 crore have been frozen,” said an official.
The ED initiated its probe under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) based on a case registered by the West Bengal Police against certain individuals for allegedly running illegal online betting operations. “Investigations revealed that an online betting panel was being operated from Siliguri by accused persons, namely Sonu Kumar Thakur and Vishal Bhardwaj, using mule bank accounts, Telegram channels, and other digital platforms for conducting online betting and gambling activities,” the agency said.
According to the ED, its investigation also revealed that “Anurag Dwivedi, a social media influencer and YouTuber, played an active and significant role in promoting illegal online betting platforms”.
“He has been found to have received proceeds of crime (PoC) from illegal betting apps through various ‘hawala’ channels and mule accounts.
