He created and circulated promotional videos for illegal betting apps, thereby influencing the public at large to bet on those platforms. Large sums were received in the bank accounts of his companies and those of his family members without corresponding legitimate commercial justification,” it said.
The agency alleged that Mr. Dwivedi had acquired immovable properties outside India, particularly in Dubai, using the PoC generated through the promotion and facilitation of illegal betting websites.
“It was also gathered that, after the generation of such proceeds, Mr. Dwivedi has left India and is currently residing in Dubai. He has been issued multiple summons so far; however, he has failed to appear before the ED. The agency has so far frozen or attached movable assets worth ₹23.7 crore,” the ED said, adding that it had earlier arrested three persons in the case and filed a prosecution complaint before a Kolkata special court on August 1.

title: North Karnataka braces for cold wave, with Bidar logging the lowest minimum
summary: North Karnataka faces a cold wave with Bidar's lowest temperature at 5.5°C; yellow alert issued for several districts.
content:
North-interior Karnataka is bracing for a spell of severe cold wave, with the Karnataka State Natural Disaster Monitoring Centre (KSNDMC) warning that minimum temperatures are likely to remain 4 degress Celsius to 6 degrees Celsius below normal across large parts of the region between December 19 and 23.
According to the latest district-wise weather data released by the KSNDMC, Bidar recorded the lowest minimum temperature in the State at 5.5°C during the 24-hour period from 8.30 a.m. on December 18 to 8.30 a.m. on December 19. Other districts in the region also reported sharp drops in night temperatures, with Kalaburagi recording 7.5°C, Vijayapura 6.9°C, Belagavi 6.4°C, and Dharwad 6.7°C, indicating intensifying cold conditions across North Karnataka.
The KSNDMC has issued a yellow alert for Bidar, Kalaburagi, Raichur, and Yadgir districts, warning of cold wave conditions and advising heightened preparedness during the period. The alert indicates a moderate risk of cold-related impacts, particularly during night and early morning hours.
In an extreme weather index forecast issued on Thursday evening, the KSNDMC said severe cold wave conditions are likely at isolated places over north-interior Karnataka on December 19, 20 and 21, while both north and south-interior Karnataka may experience minimum temperatures significantly below normal levels till December 23.
Some parts of the Malnad region are also expected to witness similar cold wave conditions during the same period, while Coastal Karnataka may see a dip in temperature by 2°C to 3°C below normal between December 20 and 22.
Despite relatively high daytime temperatures, with maximum temperature crossing 34°C in districts such as Kalaburagi and Vijayapura, the sharp fall in night temperatures has resulted in a wide diurnal variation, aggravating cold stress, especially during early morning and late night hours.
The KSNDMC has advised the public to take precautionary measures, particularly the elderly, children and those exposed to cold winds. People have been urged to minimise outdoor movement during night and early morning hours, wear adequate winter clothing and remain alert to symptoms of hypothermia and frostbite.
The advisory also cautioned farmers and livestock owners to take protective measures, including light irrigation to safeguard crops from cold injury and ensuring proper shelter and nutrition for cattle and poultry during night-time.
The KSNDMC noted that forecast accuracy may reduce with an increase in lead time, but warned that prevailing conditions indicate an extended cold spell over large parts of the State in the coming days.

title: Bride attempts suicide after marriage called off following threats by ‘blade mafia’
summary: Bride attempts suicide after marriage cancellation due to threats from moneylending group, prompting police investigation into intimidation.
content:
A woman attempted suicide in Kallambalam on Thursday after the bridegroom withdrew from their marriage following a threat from the ‘blade mafia.’
The Kallambalam police have registered a case against eight people involved in illegal moneylending and for alleged intimidation.
According to the police, the woman’s wedding with the Kollam native expatriate was scheduled for January 1, and preparations, including invitations, had already been completed.
The bride’s mother had borrowed nearly ₹1 lakh from the group for an exorbitant interest rate in 2018 following her husband’s death. Though she had reportedly repaid large sums towards the principal amount and interest over time, the moneylenders allegedly began demanding immediate repayment ahead of the wedding.
The group, including women, visited the groom’s house and publicly humiliated the bride’s family by accusing them of being heavily indebted. They allegedly threatened the groom and warned him of dire consequences if the marriage went ahead. This prompted the groom’s family to withdraw from the marriage. Deeply distressed by the turn of events, the woman attempted to commit suicide by consuming an excessive quantity of tablets. She is being treated at a private hospital in Varkala.
(Suicide prevention helpline: DISHA: 1056, 0471-2552056).

title: Satyagraha Soudha: ₹2 crore grant for development works
summary: Mysuru's Shivapura Satyagraha Soudha receives ₹2 crore grant for conservation and development works to honor India's freedom struggle.
content:
Deputy Commissioner Kumar on December 19 inspected the historic Shivapura Satyagraha Soudha at Maddur taluk in connection with the preparation of a comprehensive development plan for the monument.
The Shivapura Satyagraha Soudha, associated with India’s freedom struggle, has been sanctioned a grant of ₹2 crore by the government for its conservation and overall development. During the inspection, the Deputy Commissioner directed the officials concerned to take up the proposed works in accordance with prescribed guidelines and ensure timely execution.
These works include repairing toilets in the annex building, drilling a borewell, installing name boards and stone plaques, constructing an arch gate, painting the Satyagraha Soudha, levelling low-lying areas on the premises, and laying interlock pavers.
Other proposed works include constructing a compound wall around the purified drinking water unit, installing iron gates, required stands, and seven portraits depicting freedom fighters, apart from deploying security guards on the premises.
The development plan also proposes to construct an annex building to showcase information on the Shivapura freedom struggle, freedom movements across the State and the country, and screen documentaries on Mahatma Gandhi. Reviving the musical fountain on the premises has also been proposed.
The Deputy Commissioner instructed officials to take up the works on a priority basis while maintaining quality standards and completing them within the stipulated time-frame.

title: Vizianagaram revives educational legacy with new institutions in 2025
summary: Vizianagaram is revitalizing its educational legacy in 2025 with new institutions and initiatives, attracting students and job opportunities.
content:
Vizianagaram, which was a major educational hub 150 years ago, seems to be regaining its lost glory with the establishment of several major educational institutions in and around the Fort City in 2025.
When Vizianagaram was a princely state prior to India’s independence, hundreds of students from different regions thronged the Fort City to pursue higher education. Several colleges, including Maharaja Degree and PG College, M.R. Music College, and M.R. Sanskrit College, offered educational facilities on par with institutions in Varanasi, Chennai, New Delhi, and other places.
Maharaja Alak Narayana Society of Arts and Science (MANSAS) trust, established in the year-1958 by the last king of the princely State P.V.G. Raju, entered into an agreement with the GMR group and State government on December 16, 2025, for the establishment of GMR-MANSAS Aviation, Aerospace and Defence Education City.
The trust allocated around 120 acres of land in Annavaram village near Bhogapuram international city which is expected to begin its operations in June, 2026. Vizianagaram MLA Pusapati Aditi Vijaya Lakshmi Gajapathi Raju said that the Trust had allocated land at free of cost to ensure the construction of the AAD Educity in Vizianagaram.
Many other educational institutions have also taken several initiatives in the year-2025, enhancing the image of Vizianagaram which was the most sought after destination for higher education.
Centurion University of Technology and Management (CUTM), which has campuses in Bhubaneswar, Parlakhemundi, Rayagada, and other parts of Odisha, placed special focus on its Vizianagaram campus in 2025 by constructing new blocks and launching 112 skill-oriented courses, along with 30 manufacturing units to meet practical training needs.
“Quality education in Vizianagaram is more affordable compared to educational institutions in metro cities. This is one of the main reasons students choose Vizianagaram to pursue their higher education. Job opportunities will also increase with the establishment of the Google data centre, along with campuses of Infosys, Cognizant, and other companies in nearby Visakhapatnam,” said D. N. Rao, Vice President of CUTM.
JNTU engineering college, which was upgraded as the University recently, got more powers in the year-2025. Now, its jurisdiction has been expanded to all engineering and pharmacy colleges located in the North Andhra region. The government medical college management constructed many new blocks this year. The public representatives of Vizianagaram district requested the government to establish a dental college also in the Fort city.

title: Bengaluru: South city commissioner urges organisations to study urban conditions and design gaps as residents flag civic issues
summary: Bengaluru's commissioner calls for studies on urban conditions to address civic issues raised by residents and improve city planning.
content:
Highlighting the need for evidence-based urban planning to address growing civic challenges, Bengaluru South Corporation Commissioner K.N. Ramesh said private organisations could be encouraged to take in-depth studies of the city’s current urban conditions and design gaps. He said college students could be encouraged to study urban planning and design and submit practical suggestions.
The commissioner was speaking at a meeting with office bearers of apartment associations and resident welfare associations from the Jayanagar zone, held to discuss civic grievances faced by the residents.
Residents raised concerns regarding unauthorised construction, maintenance of public toilets, e-khata-related problems, and garbage management issues, among other issues.
While discussing solid waste management, the commissioner said several non-governmental organisations had already studied waste-related issues within the city limits and offered recommendations. He said that close coordination between the corporation and citizens would lead to effective implementation and that garbage kiosks should function in partnership with the private sector to ensure efficient management without creating any black spots.

title: Ernakulam incident exposes brutal face of police, says K.C. Venugopal
summary: K.C. Venugopal criticizes Kerala Police's brutality, blaming Chief Minister for transforming them into a "haven for criminals."
content:
All India Congress Committee (AICC) general secretary K.C. Venugopal, MP, on Friday said that Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan bore full responsibility for turning the Kerala Police into a “haven for criminals.”
He said the brutal face of the police had once again been exposed through the incident in Ernakulam where a police officer slapped a pregnant woman. “The situation is such that women cannot approach police stations without fear to lodge complaints. The visuals of the assault reflect the police’s attitude towards women. The Kerala Police were not like this earlier. It is the government’s administrative policies that have pushed the police to such a state. Used by the Communist Party of India (Marxist) [CPI(M)] to protect criminals, the police force has now turned into a haven for criminals,” he said, terming the situation shameful.
Mr. Venugopal said the public was often unaware of the brutal assaults inflicted on those taken into custody, as such incidents came to light only after years of legal battles. “What Youth Congress activist Sujith faced earlier in Thrissur was a similar form of torture. The Kerala Police, once known for upholding the rule of law, have been turned into an instrument of assault. A series of custodial torture cases have come to light in recent times,” the Congress leader said.

title: African swine fever resurfaces in Thrissur, authorities step up containment measures
summary: African swine fever resurfaces in Thrissur, prompting authorities to implement strict containment measures and biosecurity protocols.
content:
Thrissur district is once again on alert following the confirmation of African swine fever (ASF), a highly contagious viral disease affecting pigs, with the latest case reported from Kadangode panchayat. The new detection takes the number of affected panchayat in the district to three within the last three months, raising serious concern among farmers and authorities.
As part of intensified containment measures, the pig farm where the disease was detected has been declared an infected zone within a one-kilometre radius, while a 10-kilometre area around it has been notified as a surveillance zone. Restrictions have been imposed on the sale and distribution of pork from these areas. District Collector Arjun Pandian has directed officials to strictly regulate the functioning of shops and to prevent the transport of pigs to other districts.
To curb further spread, suspected infected pigs are being culled, with 396 pigs already destroyed so far. A special task force under the Animal Husbandry department has begun operations across the district to monitor farms and enforce biosecurity protocols.
Chief Veterinary Officer Isaac Sam clarified that the African swine fever affects only pigs and wild boars and poses no threat to humans or other animals. “There is no risk of transmission to people. However, strict control measures are essential to prevent further spread among pig population,” he said.
Health and animal husbandry officials have issued detailed advisories to pig farmers. They have been instructed to avoid introducing new pigs into farms during outbreaks and to quarantine newly purchased pigs for at least three weeks to ensure they are disease-free. The movement of breeding boars into and out of farms has also been temporarily banned. Farmers have been warned against feeding pigs with slaughter waste and dumping leftover feed in open areas that could attract wild boars. Proper disposal and scientific treatment of waste have been strongly emphasised.
The disease was first reported from pig farms in areas of Thirumittakode panchayat along the Palakkad district border before spreading to the Mandanparambu area of Kadangode panchayat. Last year, the ASF had severely affected Kadangode panchayat, particularly in Pathiyaram, Malayakam and Mandanparambu regions, forcing authorities to cull around 1,500 pigs.
Describing the severity of the disease, T.P. Sethumadhavan, former Director of Kerala Veterinary and Animal Sciences University, said, “It is a devastating pig disease marked by high fever, internal haemorrhage and very high mortality. Measures must be taken to strictly control the movement of vehicles, feed, waste and animals across farms. Organised slaughter practices and scientific waste management are crucial. All biosecurity measures must be followed without compromise.”
He added that the ASF is caused by a viral agent and stressed the need for farmers and farm workers to strictly adhere to scientific protocols. “The disease spreads among domestic pigs and wild boars but is not zoonotic in nature. Newly elected local bodies, in coordination with the Animal Husbandry department, must implement well-planned awareness programmes to effectively control the infection,” he said.
With containment efforts under way, the authorities have urged pig farmers to remain vigilant and cooperate fully to prevent further losses and safeguard the district’s livestock sector.

title: Two serial offenders arrested in Mangalhat, gold chain worth ₹2.48 lakh recovered
summary: Two serial offenders arrested in Mangalhat; police recover gold chain worth ₹2.48 lakh linked to multiple theft cases.
content:
Two individuals were arrested by the Mangalhat police on Friday (December 19) in connection with a chain-snatching case. Officials seized gold chain weighing two tolas and worth ₹2.48 lakh from their possession.
The accused were identified as Upadi Bolenath, also known as U. Bholanath, 42, a shoeshiner and Mohammed Khadeer, also known as Khader, 26, an auto driver, both residents of Hyderabad.
Police said a check of records revealed that both men are habitual offenders with a long criminal history. Bolenath has been involved in as many as 70 cases, while Khadeer has been linked to 66 cases registered across various police stations.
During interrogation, the duo confessed to their involvement in 11 additional cases, including five cases within the Hyderabad commissionerate, five in the Cyberabad commissionerate and one under the Rachakonda commissionerate. Bolenath also confessed to one more case registered at Attapur.
The arrests were made by a team from Mangalhat police station after collecting technical evidence. The accused are being produced before the court for judicial remand. Further investigation is underway.

title: Music and theatre should be used to promote equality and fraternity, says senior journalist
summary: Senior journalist G.P. Basavaraju advocates using music and theatre to promote equality and fraternity at the Niranthara festival.
content:
Senior journalist G.P. Basavaraju has emphasised the need to use music and theatre to promote values of equality, freedom, and fraternity enshrined in the Constitution.
Addressing the gathering at the Niranthara theatre festival in Kalamandira on December 18 evening, Mr. Basavaraju observed that in present times, when divisive voices are increasing, efforts to unite the nation, society, and people are decreasing.
In this context, he appreciated the work of Niranthara Foundation, which organises “socially-oriented” theatre festivals with the spirit that “everyone is one” and strives to build a society without any distinctions in religion, faith, or caste.
He also said it was wrong to view music and theatre merely as forms of entertainment. “Music and theatre are powerful art forms that stimulate thought and reflection,” he said, while pointing out that Niranthara Foundation practises values of equality, freedom, and fraternity as enshrined in the Constitution through their actions rather than mere words.
Sudarshan M.D., Assistant Director of the Kannada and Culture department, also addressed the gathering, saying that people are closely observing the theatre activities taking place across the State.
A musical concert featuring performances by Ravi Shankar Mishra on the flute, Junain Khan on the sitar, and Rishi Prasad on the tabla were also held that evening.
The five-day Niranthara theatre festival was inaugurated by senior theatre artiste Rameshwari Varma on December 17 in the presence of noted litterateur S.G. Siddaramaiah.

title: Kerala Leader of Opposition Satheesan condemns police excesses under Pinarayi Vijayan’s tenure
summary: Kerala's Leader of Opposition Satheesan criticizes police brutality and government inaction under Pinarayi Vijayan's leadership.
content:
The Kerala Police, once comparable to the Scotland Yard, have thoroughly degenerated during Pinarayi Vijayan’s tenure, which has been marked by a string of very disturbing stories of police excesses, Leader of the Opposition V.D. Satheesan said here on Friday.
Talking to mediapersons, he said that the brutal manner in which a police officer had assaulted a pregnant woman who had come in distress to the police station with young children in tow because her husband was taken away by the police, was way too cruel and unprecedented. The incident which took place right in front of her family shows the true face of police under the Pinarayi Vijayan regime, he said.
Even more serious was the fact that the Chief Minister, who heads the Home department, did nothing to investigate the incident, even though he received a complaint in 2024 , Mr. Satheesan said.
He asked whether the Chief Minister did not have the facility to get information about the incident which took place in a police station or whether he chose to ignore the complaint. The Chief Minister should apologise to the people  for the abominable manner in which his police force was treating the public and ensure that those responsible for the incident are punished, he said.
It should be probed whether the Chief Minister’s office or any senior Police officials had intervened to protect the officer accused of violence. Had the victims not shown the tenacity to pursue the matter in court, this case of police brutality would never have come out in the open.
Under the Chief Minister, the police seemed to view the public as prime enemies, he added.
It was disgraceful that a police officer in the rank of DIG was taking bribes from criminals in exchange for arranging their parole. Under the Chief Minister’s police regime, criminals with money and muscle power can remain in the comfort of their own homes rather than the jail .
He pointed out that the promise given by the Chief Minister on the floor of the Assembly that action would be taken in the incident wherein a Youth Congress leader was assaulted by the police, remains as a mere promise
Referring to the parody song on the Sabarimala gold theft which had resulted in the police filing a case against the song writer and others associated with it, Mr. Satheesan said that it was becoming very clear that the State was being ruled  by an extreme right-wing Government, which was so intolerant that it could not even allow a parody song because it seemed to make fun of the ruling dispensation.
He pointed out that Communist Party of India [CPI(M)]’s M. Swaraj had been recorded spewing nonsense about Lord Ayyappa and that had not offended the sensibilities of CPI(M).
He said that the government, so drunk on power, had become unhinged following the defeat in the local  body polls that it could not tolerate anyone even singing a parody song that seemed to lampoon them.
Mr. Satheesan also welcomed the High Court’s ruling, cancelling the preliminary licence granted for the setting up of a brewery at Elappully, Palakkad, that it vindicated the objections raised by the Opposition.

title: Over 2 lakh voters in Ernakulam ‘unmapped’ as SIR enumeration ends
summary: Over 2 lakh voters in Ernakulam remain ‘unmapped’ as electoral roll revision concludes, with details unlinked from 2002 records.
content:
With the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls entering its final phase, over 2 lakh voters in Ernakulam district have been left ‘unmapped’ as they have not been linked to the voters’ list from 2002, the base document for the ongoing exercise.
As of Thursday (December 18), the last date to complete the enumeration process as part of SIR in the State, 2,15,957 voters in the district were categorised as ‘unmapped’. Though they have submitted their enumeration forms back, their details could not be successfully linked to the electoral data from 2002, official sources said.
The officials arrived at the number as the booth-level officers (BLOs) completed the digitisation of enumeration forms in the district on Wednesday (December 17), a day before the deadline to complete enumeration works.
A draft electoral roll on the basis of SIR enumeration is scheduled to be published on December 23.
Officials involved in SIR in the district said they aim to reduce to the maximum extent the number of voters who will have to be called for a hearing after publishing the draft rolls. Those called for a hearing will have to produce either of the identity proofs as instructed by the Election Commission of India (ECI) to be enrolled in the fresh electoral rolls.
“Among the forms digitised, there are voters who could not trace details of their own or their relatives from the 2002 list. They or their relatives would have been excluded from the 2002 list for one reason or another, mostly since they failed to fill in the required details during the SIR held then. Such voters have been categorised as unmapped,” an election official said. The officials have repeatedly allayed fears over eligible voters getting excluded from the list following SIR.
In a bid to fix the gap, Electoral Registration Officers (EROs) on Thursday convened a meeting of the representatives of political parties at the Assembly constituency level. “If one can find the required details from 2002, in which political parties may help, we can still add those details in the enumeration forms, which have already been digitised,” an official source said.
New electors are, meanwhile, being encouraged to fill up the Form 6 along with a declaration and submit it to the booth-level officers or fill the form and declaration online using the ECINet App/website https://voters.eci.gov.in/ to get their names included in the final electoral rolls to be published in February 2026.

title: Need for road-rail satellite station, says Vijayawada MP
summary: Vijayawada MP Kesineni Sivanath urges the Railway Minister to develop a road-rail satellite station for improved transport efficiency.
content:
TDP MP from Vijayawada Kesineni Sivanath submitted a representation to Union Minister for Railways Ashwini Vaishnaw on December 18, stressing the need to prepare an integrated plan for transport management and a road-rail satellite terminal that would divert the rail as well as road traffic to reduce the pressure on Vijayawada station.
Mr. Sivanath noted that there were open lands, which could be easily acquired for the stated purpose, while pointing out that the area was going to be connected to the major roadways/airways, and to the upcoming new Amaravati line. Therefore, it was essential to develop a railway station as a halt / satellite station to Vijayawada station, he observed.
Mr. Sivanath said, keeping it in view, Mr. Vaishnaw should call for a feasibility report, along with DPR, to direct joint inspection with the departments concerned so that the facility would make transportation and logistics a lot more convenient.

title: SGOU to launch public digital library
summary: Sreenarayanaguru Open University is launching a global digital library for accessible academic resources, enhancing learning for all.
content:
As part of expanding its academic services, Sreenarayanaguru Open University is setting up a state-of-the-art public digital library that can be accessed from anywhere in the world.
This knowledge repository is being designed to provide 24-hour access to students, researchers, and the public.
Implemented on a Software as a Service (SaaS) model, the project will provide digital access to journals, theses, lecture notes, and study material for competitive examinations. In addition, the works of Sree Narayana Guru and other historical documents will be made available to everyone, including researchers and students.
The primary objective of the university is to ensure access to knowledge resources for all, including students from economically backward backgrounds. This digital library, expected to be completed within a year, will help enhance the university’s global presence in the academic field. The university has invited Expressions of Interest (EoI) to select the agency for developing the digital library. After evaluating the proposals, a contract will be signed with the agency that submits the most suitable proposal.

title: Bengaluru: East city commissioner inspects PGs; holds meeting to improve traffic congestion
summary: Bengaluru East Commissioner inspects PG accommodations and meets officials to address traffic congestion and enhance pedestrian safety.
content:
Bengaluru East Corporation Commissioner D.S. Ramesh conducted inspections of paying guest (PG) accommodations under the Mahadevapura Zone on Friday. During the inspection, he directed officials to strictly verify whether PGs were functioning in compliance with the prescribed standard operating procedures, instructing them to take action as per the rules in cases where violations or lapses were found.
Mr. Ramesh and Additional Commissioner (Development) Lokhande Snehal Sudhakar held a joint meeting with officials from the Engineering Department, BMTC, and the city traffic police on easing traffic congestion. The meeting focused on examining various measures to improve traffic flow and pedestrian safety in the East zone.
Officials were asked to review the proposed relocation of 21 bus shelters situated near major junctions to help reduce congestion.
The meeting discussed a proposal to construct 17 new skywalks at high-traffic roads and junctions, including T.C. Palya, Outer Ring Road, Old Madras Road, areas near Phoenix Mall, Carmelaram, and Doddakannalli, to improve pedestrian safety.
Officers were instructed to examine the feasibility of implementing a bus bay system on major roads such as Kasturi Nagar, Devasandra, ITPL Main Road and Bellandur–Kasavanahalli Road.

title: BJP Mahila Morcha stages protest condemning Minister Laxmi Hebbalkar
summary: BJP mahila morcha protests in Belagavi, condemning Minister Laxmi Hebbalkar for delaying Gruha Laxmi incentives for poor women.
content:
Members of the BJP Mahila Morcha staged a protest in Belagavi on Friday, condemning Minister for Women and Child Development Laxmi Hebbalkar fo0r the alleged delay in release of Gruha Laxmi monthly incentive.
They sat in dharna at the Rani Chennamma circle and raised slogans against the Minister. The protesters said that the Minister was negligent about the problems faced by poor women, especially in rural areas.
They alleged that Ms. Hebbalkar had been negligent and irresponsible and was trying to pass on the blame to officers.
Geeta Sutar, Deepa Kudchi, Uma Jadhav, and others took part in the protest.

title: P. Pushpangadan, plant scientist and ethnobiologist, passes away aged 81
summary: Renowned plant scientist P. Pushpangadan, 81, passes away, remembered for his groundbreaking contributions to ethnobiology and plant research.
content:
Palpu Pushpangadan, acclaimed plant scientist and ethnobiologist, passed away here on Friday. He was 81.
A former Director of the National Botanical Research Institute (NBRI), Lucknow, Dr. Pushpangadan is best remembered for the equitable benefit-sharing model between the Kani tribal community and the Jawaharlal Nehru Tropical Botanic Garden and Research Institute (JNTBGRI), Palode, of which he was director from 1990 to 1999. The model was linked to  ‘anti-fatigue’ herbal formulation Jeevani developed from the herb Trichopus zeylanicus, known locally as Arogyapacha.
Dr. Pushpangadan’s research areas spanned cytogenetics and plant breeding, molecular taxonomy, conservation biology, ethnobiology and ethnopharmacology.
Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan, in a condolence message, said the benefit-sharing model had garnered global attention. Dr. Pushpangadan was noted for his contributions to biology, specifically ethnopharmacology, the Chief Minister said.
Dr. Pushpangadan was born in Prakkulam in Kollam district in 1944. Prior to his tenure at JNTBGRI  he worked at the Regional Research Laboratory, Jammu, and the Ministry of Environment and Forests, as chief co-ordinator of an all-India programme on ethnobiology.
According to the JNTBGRI website, it was Dr.  Pushpangadan who reorganised the institute into the garden system and the research and development system. For a short period, he also held the charge of director, Rajiv Gandhi Centre for Biotechnology, Thiruvananthapuram.
He has also served as director and Additional Secretary, Science, Technology and Environment Department, Kerala government, and director (in-charge), Central Institute for Medicinal and Aromatic Plants. Dr. Pushpangadan left the JNTBGRI in 1999 to head NBRI, Lucknow. From 2004 onwards, he was director general of the Kerala-based Amity Institute for Herbal and Biotech Products Development in Thiruvananthapuram.
P.G. Latha, a former Director of the JNTBGRI, remembers Dr. Pushpangadan as an able administrator who promoted youngsters. “Practically all the research divisions at the institute were developed to international standards when he was at the helm,” Dr. Latha, who first met him in 1990, recalled on Friday.
A recipient of many accolades and awards, Dr. Pushpangadan received the Padma Shri in 2010. He was a Fellow of the National Academy of Sciences, the Ethnobotany Society of India, and the National Society of Ethnopharmacology among others.
Dr. Pushpangadan is survived by his wife Sreedevi Pushpangadan, a gynaecologist, and Vipin Mohan Dan, senior scientist at the JNTBGRI.

title: Doctors should practice sympathy and kindness, says NMCMARB chairman
summary: NMCMARB chairman emphasizes the importance of sympathy and kindness in medicine, despite advancements in technology and artificial intelligence.
content:
National Medical Council’s Medical Assessment and Rating Board (NMCMARB) chairman M.K. Ramesh on Friday said that modern-day doctors were using several high-end technology tools in disease detection and treatment, and artificial intelligence was making our jobs easier and faster but doctors have to stick to age-old ethical principles of sympathy and kindness.
These are always trending, and they will never go out of fashion, Mr. Ramesh said, while speaking at the 13th convocation of the  B.L.D.E. Deemed University in Vijayapura on Friday.
Health care services in the country have reached a new level, as state-of-the-art technology was being used to deliver quality services to patients, he said.
There was an increase in the number of people using technological tools. Patients can be treated remotely through telemedicine through internet, and digital platforms have helped patients reach doctors easily, the NMCMARB chariman said.
“The use of artificial intelligence has helped in identifying the characteristics of diseases. Robotic technology has become a boon for performing surgeries in a simple, easy, low-cost and minimally invasive manner,” Mr. Ramesh said.
Genomics and precision medicine technology, nanotechnology, regenerative medicine and stem cell therapy, healthcare data analysis, medical devices and wearable technology have facilitated the rapid detection, treatment and recovery from diseases in the field of medicine. Therefore, young doctors should make good use of these technologies and help those in need of treatment,” he said.
Mr. Ramesh said that doctors should engage in research and enhance their professional skills.
He further said students pursuing higher education should realise that their study never ends. Young doctors who are entering the profession should treat patients with compassion. “At the same time, self-study and research in the field of medicine should always continue,” he said.
Vice-Chancellor Arun Cham. Inamdara presented the annual report. He spoke about the researches that were being conducted in the university, recognitions received, new agreements signed, and achievements of doctors, and about future projects.
Chancellor B.M. Patil conferred the degrees on the graduates. A total of 502 degrees were conferred, including 11 PhD., three MCh (Urology), two DM (Cardiology), 239 Medical Post graduate degrees, three fellowships, 156 MBBS, 10 Postgraduate Allied Health degrees, 19 Postgraduate Science and Technology degrees, 13 Bachelor of Physiotherapy, and 46 Allied Science degrees.
As many as 28 gold medals and three cash prizes were awarded to meritorious graduates. In the Medical Postgraduate category, Narla Surekha and Shankar Narayanan R. received two gold medals each; in the graduate medical department, Yash Arya received five gold medals and one cash prize; Nishtha C. Raja received three gold medals and one cash prize; Saloni Verma received two gold medals and one cash prize; and Sirisha M.S. received two gold medals.
Pro-Chancellor Y.M. Jayaraj was present on the occasion. BLDE president and Minister for Large and Medium Scale Industries M.B. Patil, Registrar R.V. Kulkarni, Controller of Examinations Shashidhar Devarmani, deans, faculty members, directors, and others were present.

title: Govinda Rao panel report on regional imbalances will be implemented, says CM
summary: Stating that the government was committed to removing regional imbalances through development, Chief Minister Siddaramaiah on Friday declared that it would implement the report of M. Govinda Rao High Power Committee for Reddressal of Regional Imbalances which is expected to be submitted in January, 2026.
content:
He offers to lead a delegation of elected representatives of North Karnataka to PM to seek clearances for pending projects
Stating that the government was committed to removing regional imbalances through development, Chief Minister Siddaramaiah on Friday declared that it would implement the report of M. Govinda Rao High Power Committee for Reddressal of Regional Imbalances which is expected to be submitted in January, 2026.
“Whatever may be the requirement of funds, we will implement the committee’s recommendations fully,” the Chief Minister told the Legislative Assembly while replying to a debate on issues related to development of North Karnataka.
Again accusing the Centre of coming in the way of development of North Karnataka by not giving clearances to prominent projects of the region, the Chief Minister also offered to lead a delegation of elected representatives from North Karnataka to Prime Minister Narendra Modi to seek justice in this regard.
The government would take measures to focus on taluks that would be identified by the Govinda Rao committee as backward, the Chief Minister said.
He pointed out that earlier measures had been taken to provide funds to the tune of ₹31,000 crore over the period of eight years to 114 taluks that had been identified as most backward, more backward and backward taluks in the State.
However, the Goinda Rao committee had been formed later to know if regional imbalances still prevailed and the measures to be taken to tackle them, he noted.
The disparities in terms of development were clearly visible with about 10 districts of the total 31 in Karnataka, particularly those from the northern region, having a per capita income of less than ₹2 lakh as against the State’s average per capita income of ₹3,39,813, he noted.
He termed the guarantee schemes too as tools for removing regional imbalances. As much as 43.63% per cent of the funds meant for guarantee schemes had been spent in North Karnataka region, he pointed out.
Of the total population of 6.95 crore in the State, North Karnataka accounted for 2.96 crore (42%). Geographically, the northern region accounted for 14 districts of the total 31 districts in the State and 97 Assembly constituencies of the total 224 in the State, he explained.
Citing lack of dairy development in North Karnataka as one of the reasons for its backwardness, particularly in rural areas, he pointed out that as against the State’s milk production of over one crore litres a day, the northern milk unions accounted for just 10 lakh litres a day.
Accusing the Centre of indulging in non-cooperation with the State, he alleged that the Centre had failed to keep its promise of providing assistance of ₹5,300 crore to Upper Bhadra Project as listed in its Budget a few years ago.
Similarly, it had put a stumbling block in the path of development of North Karnataka by not notifying the award of Krishna Water Disputes Tribunal-2 and by not providing clearances to the Mahadayi drinking water project, he alleged.
The Centre was yet to provide the State’s share of ₹13,000 crore towards Jal Jeevan Mission and ₹3,000 crore towards peripheral ring road in Bengaluru, he said, and reiterated that Karnataka had suffered a loss of ₹ 1.5 lakh crore in the last five years in terms of devolution of funds, grants and its share of Central taxes though it contributed a tax amount of ₹4.5 lakh crore a year.
He agreed to bring out a White Paper on the status of promises made for the development of North Karnataka.

title: Ernakulam collector sends Sabari rail land acquisition proposal to State
summary: District collector sent the proposal to Transport department seeking the administrative nod day after receiving requisition details from Railways
content:
In what could be a significant step relating to the Angamaly-Sabari rail project, the Ernakulam district administration has sent to the State government a proposal for acquiring the required land for the much-delayed infrastructure plan.
The district collector sent the proposal to the Transport department seeking administrative sanction on Thursday, a day after receiving the requisition details from the Railways. The requisition and the proposal comprise the survey numbers of the land to be acquired for the project, official sources said.
It is still not clear if there is any difference in the alignment of the project from the existing one. “It will be known only after receiving the alignment sketch,” an official source said.
The land acquisition procedures, including reopening the offices for the purpose, can be started once the district administration receives the administrative sanction, a top official said. The Transport department has already received detailed land acquisition proposals from Kottayam and Idukki, the other two districts covering the project, it is learnt.
The latest developments come amid the persisting uncertainty over the project caused by alleged procedural confusions and lack of clarity on funding.
While the State government has been demanding that the Railways defreeze the project so that it can expedite the land acquisition procedures the Railways has repeatedly requested the former to start land acquisition proceedings so that the project can be defrozen by the Ministry of Railways.
The Railways has also reportedly requested the State to give ‘clear acceptance’ to share 50% of the cost instead of ‘conditional acceptance.’
A decision was yet to be made on the State’s demand that the debt incurred by the Kerala Infrastructure Investment Fund Board by financing the project be fully exempted from the State’s borrowing limit.
The Central Action Council, a federation of forums comprising land owners whose properties have been stuck in the project since years, has, meanwhile, placed a request to Union Minister of State George Kurien to press for an allocation of ₹800 crore for the project in the upcoming Union Budget for 2026-27.

title: Short film festival inaugurated; Komatireddy reaffirms support to film industry
summary: Short film festival inaugurated; Komatireddy reaffirms support to film industry
content:
Roads & Buildings and Cinematography Minister Komatireddy Venkat Reddy said short films provide creative freedom to young film-makers, enabling them to experiment, think innovatively and present their stories in their own style.
The Minister, who inaugurated the Hyderabad International Short Film Festival (HISFF) 2025 along with Tourism and Culture Minister Jupally Krishna Rao, pointed out that many leading filmmakers began their careers with short films.
He said Hyderabad has today emerged as a major hub for cinema, attracting filmmakers from across India, and described HISFF 2025 as a positive beginning for Hyderabad and Telangana. He said short films continue to be a strong platform for discovering new talent.
Reiterating the State government’s commitment to the film industry, he said the Telangana government, under the leadership of Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy, is extending full support to cinema. The government’s objective, he added, is to make Telangana the best State in the country for film-makers by ensuring easy permissions and improved infrastructure.
He also appreciated the participation of filmmakers from the north-eastern States, noting that stories from eight States are being showcased at the festival. “Hyderabad represents mini-India, and such festivals help bring the country closer,” he said.
Film Development Corporation (FDC) Chairman Dil Raju, FDC Managing Director CH Priyanka, festival organiser Uma Maheshwar Rao, along with film-makers and delegates from various parts of the country, were present.

title: Over 2 lakh voters deleted as part of SIR in Cuddalore district
summary: Cuddalore district's draft electoral roll reveals 2.46 lakh voter deletions due to various reasons after Special Intensive Revision.
content:
The draft electoral roll of Cuddalore district released on Friday after the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) has indicated that the names of around 2.46 lakh voters have been deleted on grounds of death, shifting/absent, duplication and non-submission of enumeration form for various reasons.
Releasing the draft electoral rolls, District Election Officer and Collector Sibi Adhithya Senthil Kumar said a total of 19,46,759 lakh voters (9,60,645 men, 9,85,832 women and 282 others) found place in the draft roll.
As many as 1,46,612 electors have been identified as shifted/absent during enumeration, 88,972 identified as dead and 10,844 electors found to have made entry in the rolls at multiple places.
The maximum number of voters deleted are in Bhuvanagiri (35,015), Cuddalore (33,534) and Vriddhachalam (31,824). The least number of deletions happened in Thittagudi (Reserved) 21,975, Panruti (22,741) and Kurunjipadi (24,941).
The deletions were made after field-level verification and cross-checking with Booth Level Agents of political parties.
Genuine electors will be added in the electoral rolls during the next phase of claims and objections period of SIR, which commenced on December 19 and would go on till January 18. The final rolls would be published on February 17, the Collector said.
A total of 11,60,607 voters were enrolled in Kallakurichi district’s voters’ list as of October 27 this year, before the SIR exercise started. Of them, 10,76,278 names have featured in the draft voters’ list and 84,329 electors have been dropped on grounds of being absent, shifted, dead and duplicate, District Election Officer and Collector M.S. Prasanth said.
In Villupuram district, a total of 15,44,625 voters (7,64,377 men, 7,80,042 women and 206 others) found their names in the draft rolls.

title: Thiruvambady Ekadasi Sangeethotsavam begins
summary: Thiruvambady Ekadasi Sangeethotsavam, featuring Carnatic music, kicks off its 29th edition, concluding on December 29.
content:
The 29th edition of the Thiruvambady Vaikunda Ekadasi Sangeethotsavam, held in connection with Thiruvambady Vaikunda Ekadasi, has begun. The festival was inaugurated by Carnatic music maestro Cheppad A. E. Vamanan Namboothiri on Thursday, who also presented the inaugural concert.
The music festival will conclude on December 29 with Pancharatna Keerthanalapanam. Thiruvambady Vaikunda Ekadasi will be observed on December 30.

title: Marottichal Riju murder case: three accused sentenced to life imprisonment
summary: Three accused in the Marottichal Riju murder case receive life imprisonment and fines from the Thrissur court.
content:
The Thrissur First Additional District Court on Friday sentenced the three accused in the Marottichal Riju murder case to life imprisonment along with a fine.
The verdict was pronounced by Justice K. Kamanees. The court awarded life imprisonment and imposed a fine of ₹3,10,000 on the second, sixth and seventh accused — Sherry alias Kunjumon, Prakasan and Anoop. The sentence relates to the attack on brothers Riju and Biju at Ragam Junction in Marottichal, in which Riju was killed and Biju sustained serious injuries. The case was registered by the Ollur police.
The incident dates back to 2010 and stemmed from a dispute linked to a private bus service operating on the Kallur–Marottichal route. The rivalry intensified after a police case was registered over vandalising of a bus owned by Biju, Riju’s brother. This enmity ultimately culminated in the fatal attack.
According to the prosecution, the assault was carried out by an unlawful assembly led by the first accused, Keetayi Baiju. Though the first accused died before the commencement of the trial, proceedings continued against the remaining accused under Sections 147, 148 and 149 of the Indian Penal Code for unlawful assembly and rioting. During the course of the trial, the fourth accused also died.
The court noted that the third accused had absconded during the trial, following which his bail was cancelled and an arrest warrant issued. The fifth accused is currently undergoing treatment in hospital and is in a critical condition.
The judgment brings closure to a long-pending case that had shaken the Marottichal region more than a decade ago.

title: Hate Speech Bill passed in Council after over six hours of debate, amid BJP protest
summary: After over six hours of debate, an adjournment and protest by the BJP in the Well of the House, The Karnataka Hate Speech and Hate Crimes (Prevention) Bill, 2025, was passed by the Karnataka Legislative Council on Friday.
content:
After over six hours of debate, an adjournment and protest by the BJP in the Well of the House, The Karnataka Hate Speech and Hate Crimes (Prevention) Bill, 2025, was passed by the Karnataka Legislative Council on Friday.
The debate on the Bill, which was earlier adopted by the Legislative Assembly, began at 10.40 a.m. on Friday with Home Minister G. Parameshwara explaining the objective of the Bill.
Dr. Parameshwara quoted the Supreme Court observation in Vishal Tiwari vs Union of India and others, which said, “Hate speech cannot be tolerated as it leads to loss of dignity and self-worth of the targeted group members, contributes to disharmony amongst groups, and erodes tolerance and open-mindedness.” The Minister also placed some data on increasing cases of hate speech  before the House emphasising the need for a new law.
The subsequent debate saw 23 members presenting their views. While the ruling party members made suggestions and welcomed the Bill, BJP members opposed it, with some demanding that it should be taken back. A few others demanded that it should be sent to the House committee for scrutiny.
The debate which started on a calm note with K.S. Naveen placing his objections, took on an aggressive pitch when C.T. Ravi made religious reference and took the name of Mahatma Gandhi and Basavanna in his argument to oppose the Bill. The tone angered the ruling party members, resulting in cacophony and adjournment for five minutes.
When the session resumed, several members joined Mr. Ravi in terming the Bill “draconian, and against the Constitution” and expressed apprehension about the State becoming “police raj.” On the other hand ruling party members defended the need for the Bill.
Trouble again started while Dr. Parameshwara was replying to the debate. At one point, Opposition members took exception to Minister Priyank Kharge’s comment on Union Home Minister Amit Shah and demanded that it be expunged from records. They also demanded Mr. Kharge’s apology and rushed to the Well raising slogans.
Amid the ruckus, the House passed the Bill, even as a few Opposition members tore copies of the Bill and threw it in the air.

title: Murder convict gets 20-year imprisonment
summary: A 35-year-old man sentenced to 20 years in prison for murdering his wife in Nellore after a violent altercation.
content:
The 8thAdditional District Judge’s court in Nellore sentenced a 35-year-old man to twenty years in jail for murdering his wife. The incident took place in Jangalagunta of Sullurpeta mandal in the then SPSR Nellore district (currently the mandal is in Tirupati district) on February 28, 2017.
The convict, Puli Muniswamy, an alcoholic, used to physically and mentally torment his wife Puli Mounica. On the fateful day, Munuswamy picked up a quarrel with his wife in an inebriated state and, in a fit of rage, doused her with kerosene and set her ablaze. She succumbed to her injuries in a hospital on March 4.
The trial continued for eight years, and the court pronounced its verdict on Friday, sentencing the man to 20-years imprisonment, besides a fine of ₹2,000.

title: Chief Secretary calls for foolproof arrangements for Godavari Pushkarams in 2027
summary: Andhra Pradesh Chief Secretary directs detailed planning for Godavari Pushkarams 2027, emphasizing advanced technology for crowd management.
content:
Andhra Pradesh Chief Secretary K. Vijayanand has directed the Secretaries to prepare department and district-wise action plans from now itself for the smooth conduct of the Godavari Pushkarams scheduledfrom June 26 to July 7, 2027, by drawing from the experiences of the Maha Kumbh Melaheld in Allahabad.
Addressing a meeting of the Committee of Secretaries constituted by the government for successfully organising the mega event, on Friday, Mr. Vijayanand said the government had also formed a Group of Ministers and appointed Health Commissioner G. Veerapandian as the special officer.
He directed the Collectors to prepare and submit detailed DPRs on aspects such as identifying bathing ghats, drinking water, sanitation, transportation, medical camps, security, crowd management, traffic management and coordination of emergency services.
Mr. Vijayanand stressed the need for foolproof arrangements in Alluri Sitharama Raju, Eluru, East Godavari, Kakinada, West Godavari and Konaseema districts (with due focus on Rajahmundry city) through which the Godavari river flows, and the use of advanced technologies for handling the massive crowds.
Mr. Veerapandian mentioned that 4.86 crore devotees had taken the holy dip in the Godavari during the 2015 Pushkarams and the number could be between nine crore and 10 crore people in 2027.
Endowments Commissioner Ramachandra Mohan, RTGS CEO Prakhar Jain, Water Resources Department Chief Engineer Seshu Babu and other officials were present.
Principal Secretaries S. Suresh Kumar and Shashibhushan Kumar, RTC MD Dwaraka Tirumala Rao, Additional DGP (L&O) N. Madhusudan Reddy, APTDC MD K. Amrapali and Director of I&PR K.S. Viswanathan, and Collectors of the aforementioned districts took part virtually.

title: Congress MP Vamsi Krishna urges NRIs in Netherlands to invest in Telangana
summary: Congress MP Vamsi Krishna urges NRIs in Netherlands to invest in Telangana
content:
HYDERABAD
Congress MP from Peddapalli, Gaddam Vamsi Krishna, has invited the Netherlands-based Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) to invest in Telangana as the State offers best of the pro-industry policies and incentives.
He was speaking at a two-day conference organised by the Foundation for Critical Choices for India (FCCI) in New Delhi on Friday. The event drew a significant turnout from the Netherlands diaspora, coinciding with FCCI’s 45th anniversary and the 75th year of India-Netherlands friendship.
During the session themed, Indian Diaspora: Dedicated to the Progress of India, Mr. Vamsi positioned Telangana as a burgeoning hub for industrial and sectoral investments. “The future belongs to India in the field of investments,” he asserted, noting India’s emergence as a preferred destination globally.
He cited the Viksit Bharat–2047 roadmap as a model for the world and highlighted the Telangana Rising Summit’s success in attracting investors, while emphasising the inseparable bond between India and the Netherlands. Mr. Vamsi acknowledged the contributions of FCCI members in fostering an industrial revolution in the Netherlands, describing their efforts as unforgettable and integral to repaying the nation’s debt.
The MP also engaged in a panel discussion, detailing the investment policies of the Telangana government and reinforcing the State’s appeal to global investors. The conference, aimed at encouraging people of Indian origin to partner in India’s development, particularly highlighted Telangana’s role in building a Viksit Bharat.

title: PWD Minister reviews arrangements for Chief Minister’s proposed visit to Kallakurichi
summary: PWD Minister E.V. Velu reviews preparations for Chief Minister M.K. Stalin's visit to Kallakurichi, focusing on upcoming projects and welfare schemes.
content:
Minister for Public Works E.V. Velu reviewed the arrangements being made to host Chief Minister M.K. Stalin, who is slated to visit the district in the last week of this month.
The Minister accompanied by Collector M.S. Prasanth on Thursday inspected the arrangements at the venue near Veeracholapuram on the Salem-Chennai national highway where the integrated Collectorate complex for Kallakurichi district built at a cost of ₹139.41 crore will be inaugurated by the Chief Minister, along with the unveiling of new projects.
Mr. Velu also held discussions with officials of various line departments, whose schemes were proposed to be introduced. The Minister previewed the arrangements and the beneficiary list of the welfare schemes slated for distribution on the day by the Chief Minister.
According to the administration, the foundation for new projects will also be laid by the Chief Minister.

title: Farmers celebrated Ellu Amavasya in Yadgir
summary: Farmers in Yadgir celebrated Ellu Amavasya with rituals and a communal feast, honoring Mother Earth for good harvests.
content:
Ellu Amavasya celebrated as a form of thanksgiving to Mother Earth, in Yadgir district on Friday.
                                                            | Photo Credit: 
                                SPECIAL ARRANGEMENT
The annual festival of the farming community, Ellu Amavasya, was celebrated with religious fervour in Yadgir district on Friday.
Farming families accompanied by friends performed rituals that signify worshipping Mother Earth and made offerings of jowar-mixed food items.
“It is the prime duty of every farmer to honour Mother Earth by making offerings to the fields with a prayer for a good yield in the rabi season,” Chandrashekhargouda Bilwar, a farmer from Hadnur village, said.
Traditionally, it is a form of thanksgiving to Mother Earth during which farmers offer a special puja on their farmland before they have a feast together.
“We are indebted to Mother Earth. Through the puja and offerings, we thank Mother Earth. For centuries, it has been the practice. It will continue for centuries to come,” said Bheem Reddy, who also belongs to a farmer’s family.
The feast usually consists of a variety of dishes, including jowar and bajra rotis, groundnut chutney, spicy dishes of rice and millets and sweets.
For the farming families, the day begins early, as they have to prepare the special feast before heading to their farmland. “We begin preparing food early in the morning. The usual practice is to share it with others after the puja,” another farmer, Rudragouda Patil, said.

title: HYDRAA reclaims 20 acres of government land in city
summary: HYDRAA reclaims 20 acres of government land in Hyderabad, tackling illegal encroachments and protecting vital water bodies.
content:
The Hyderabad Disaster Response & Asset Protection Agency (HYDRAA), on Friday, reclaimed 20 acres of government land in two operations respectively in Hyderabad and Medchal-Malkajgiri districts.
In the first instance, the agency secured about seven acres of government land which included a water body, at Mohammed Nagar-Lalita Bagh area in Kandikal village of Bandlaguda Jagir. The 9.11 acres of original piece of land surrounded by thickly populated residential area, has been in legal wrangles for some time now. Two acres were encroached and houses were constructed on the land.
Attempts are being made to encroach the remaining seven acres too, by filling up a water body, the existence of which HYDRAA confirmed from the Survey of India maps. A statement from HYDRAA informed that the illegal occupant had been fined ₹1 crore for filing a false case, despite which he is continuing his claim on the land.
HYDRAA has also reclaimed another piece of land in Nizampet, upon a request from the Revenue department officials, a statement from the agency informed. Acting on the directions of HYDRAA chief A.V. Ranganath, HYDRAA officials conducted field inspection, and concluded that four acres of land had already been occupied where permanent residential structures came up. Without touching those houses, the agency removed temporary structures from the remaining 13 acres of land, and provided fencing and sign boards.

title: 101 mobiles, 84 SIM cards seized in prisons across Karnataka in last 20 days
summary: Karnataka prisons seized 101 mobiles and 84 SIM cards in 20 days, addressing smuggling issues and enhancing security measures.
content:
In over 20 days, the Karnataka Prisons and Correctional Services department seized 101 mobile phones in different prisons across the State, according to an official statement.
The officials said that 23 chargers, 84 SIM cards, 16 earphones, ₹64,880 in cash, and 18 sharp objects were seized.
In a big haul at Parappana Agrahara Central Prison, officials seized 30 mobile phones during a late-night operation on Thursday, Director General of Police Alok Kumar said.
He praised the team led by Chief Superintendent of Central Prison Anshu Kumar and Jailer Shivakumar for the operation and announced a ₹30,000 reward.
In a post on X, Mr. Kumar said similar seizures were made in other prisons across the State, including Kalaburagi, where 10 mobile phones were recovered, Mangaluru (six), Ballari (four), and Shivamogga (three), in a span of two days. The searches led to the recovery of eight SIM cards, he mentioned.
The seizures follow Mr. Kumar’s inspection of the Bengaluru Central Prison earlier this week, his first since assuming office. He said he was committed to addressing long-standing issues at the prison.
Mr. Kumar revealed that a 15-day deadline has been given to officers to plug gaps in the system. He warned that stringent action would be taken if any violations are detected after this period.  He said that there was a need to get to the root of the problem and understand the network through which mobile phones are being smuggled into prisons.

title: Vajpayee will continue to inspire generations, says Venkaiah Naidu
summary: Venkaiah Naidu honors Atal Bihari Vajpayee's legacy, highlighting his inspiring leadership and significant contributions to India's growth.
content:
Former Vice President M. Venkaiah Naidu on Friday (December 19, 2025) said that former Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee would continue to inspire generations because of his work during his two tenures between 1996 and 2004. Along with BJP State president P.V.N. Madhav, Mr. Naidu attended the inauguration of Vajpayee statue as the chief guest and later addressed a public meeting in the Fort City.
Speaking on the occasion, he said that telecom sector, national highways, defence and other sectors witnessed rapid growth during the administration of Vajpayee, who was respected by everyone cutting across party lines. Minister for Health and Family Welfare Satya Kumar Yadav said that Prime Minister Narendra Modi has been developing the nation on the lines of Vajpayee’s administration.
Minister for MSME Kondapalli Srinivas, TDP MLA Aditi Vijaya Lakshmi Gajapathhi Raju, Etcherla BJP MLA N. Eswara Rao recalled the bond between TDP and BJP since Vajpayee regime. Earlier, BJP Vizianagaram district president Rajesh Varma, party general secretary Pativada Rajesh, BJP State executive committee member Kotagiri Narayana Rao, senior leaders Bobbili Srinu, Katta Babu and others organised a massive rally, highlighting the achievements of NDA governments both in Centre and State.

title: MGNREGS diluted to help corporates loot national wealth: CPI(M)
summary: CPI(M) criticises MGNREGS dilution, alleging it benefits corporates at the expense of poor workers and national wealth.
content:
The CPI(M) on Friday (December 19) expressed anguish at the “dilution” of the MGNREGA and lambasted the Centre for covertly trying to help corporate entities “loot the national wealth”.
At a demonstration near Bapuji market here, the party leaders led by secretariat member Kankanala Anjaneyulu and district Secretary Sk. Mabu recalled that the then UPA government introduced the scheme in 2005 with the pressure exerted by the Left parties.
“It is not just renaming the scheme as ‘Viksit Bharat Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission’ to give a go-by to Mahatma’s name, the structural changes in the policy will also hit the poor workers hard,” the leaders said, maintaining that Prime Minister Narendra Modi had “expressed displeasure” over the scheme way back in 2014, immediately after taking charge as the Prime Minister.
The scheme not only helped create social assets like waterbodies and check dams in rural areas, but also helped create wealth by improving the purchasing power of rural folk, said the district committee member V. Balakotaiah.

title: KIIFB masala bonds: Kerala HC reserves judgment on ED appeal against interim stay by single judge
summary: Kerala HC reserves judgment on ED's appeal against KIIFB's interim stay concerning masala bonds for infrastructure funding.
content:
A Division Bench of the Kerala High Court on Friday reserved its judgment on an appeal filed by the Directorate of Enforcement (ED) against a three-month interim stay issued by a single judge earlier this month on a notice issued by the ED to the Kerala Infrastructure Investment Fund Board (KIIFB) on the utilisation of funds raised through masala bonds.
The single judge had issued the interim stay on further proceedings on the matter, in a plea filed by KIIFB challenging the ED notice, in connection with the use of funds generated through masala bonds for infrastructure development in the State. The ED had initiated proceedings against KIIFB and issued notice under the Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA).
On Friday, after hearing the ED’s appeal, a Division Bench of Justice Sushrut Arvind Dharmadhikari and Justice P.V. Balakrishnan reserved the case for judgment. The Additional Solicitor General of India, who appeared online for the ED, submitted that the agency has issued merely a preliminary notice under the FEMA Adjudication Rules, calling upon KIIFB to explain why an inquiry should not be initiated on the masala bonds issue. The ED contended that the adjudicating authority must be allowed to conduct an inquiry to examine whether generating funds through masala bonds violated the external commercial borrowings policy.
Opposing the appeal and appearing for KIIFB, the Advocate General contended that the proceedings on the issue were initiated without proper application of mind. KIIFB said it had obtained RBI approval and regularly reported about the funds’ utilisation. There was no complaint about funds misuse from the RBI. Moreover, the continuing adjudication proceedings would affect infra projects in Kerala, and affect investor confidence.
Having heard the contentions, the court observed that the proceedings have not yet found any violation and asked KIIFB whether there would be any problem if a reply is filed (to the ED notice).

title: A.P. women’s commission chief warns of action against those harassing women, girls
summary: A.P. Women’s Commission warns of strict action against harassment of women and girls, urging awareness and legal safeguards.
content:
Andhra Pradesh Women’s Commission Chairperson Rayapati Sailaja on Friday (December 19) warned that strict legal action would be taken against those found harassing women and girls.
During her visit to Ongole, she inspected the nursing hostel at RIMS campus, Sakhi One Stop Centre, Domestic Violence Prevention Centre and Bala Sadan.
She directed the officials to spread awareness on the legal safeguards meant for women at workplace, both public and private enterprises. She also called upon the staff to explain to schoolgirls on ‘good touch and bad touch’.
Ms. Sailaja said every office or institution is equipped with an ‘Internal Complaints Cell’ where women employees or students can walk in to complain against harassment.
At Bala Sadan, she participated in the pre-Christmas event along with the children. District Women Welfare Officer Suvarna, Nursing School Principal Sumitra Devi and Deputy Superintendent (DISHA police station) Ramana Murthy took part.

summary: The Election Commission of India published draft electoral rolls for Tamil Nadu and Gujarat after the Special Intensive Revision, removing over 97 lakh voters in Tamil Nadu and 73.73 lakh in Gujarat. Officials said the deletions were due to deaths, relocation, duplication and absence.

title: IFFK 2025: Japanese film Two Seasons, Two Strangers wins Suvarna Chakoram
summary: IFFK 2025 celebrates winners, including Japanese film "Two Seasons, Two Strangers" and notable awards for Indian and international filmmakers.
content:
Japanese filmmaker Sho Miyake'sTwo seasons, Two Strangers, an introspective drama on a scriptwiter's emotional upheavals, won the Golden Crow Pheasant (Suvarna Chakoram) award for the best film at the 30th International Film Festival of Kerala (IFFK), which concluded here on Friday. The award carries a cash prize of ₹20 lakh, memento, and certificate.
Argentine filmmakers Carina Piazza and Lucía Bracelis won the Silver Crow Pheasant (Rajatha Chakoram) award for best director for the filmBefore the Body.
Shadowboxdirected by Tanushree Das and Saumyananda Sahi won the  Silver Crow Pheasant (Rajatha Chakoram) award for the best debut director as well as the Federation of Film Societies of India’s (FFSI) K.R. Mohanan Award for the best debut director from India.
The Network for Promotion of Asian Cinema (NETPAC) Award for the best Asian film in competition went toCinema Jazirehdirected by Gozde Kural.
Thanthapperudirected by Unnikrishnan Avala won the jury prize in the international competition, the audience poll award, and the NETPAC Award for the best Malayalam film. The last award was shared withKhidki Gaavdirected by Sanju Surendran.Khidki Gaavalso won the International Federation of Film Critics (FIPRESCI) Award for the best film in the international competition.
The FIPRESCI award for the best Malayalam film of a debut director went to Fazil Razak forMoham. Tillotama Shome won a special jury mention for her  performance inShadowbox. The special jury mention for technical excellence went toBlack Rabbit,  directed by Shahram Mokri.
Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan presented the awards at the closing ceremony of the festival.  Mr.Vijayan also presented the IFFK's Lifetime achievement award his year to African filmmaker  Abderrahmane Sissako.
Iranian filmmaker Mohammad Rasoulof, jury chairperson who is facing a prison sentence in Iran for his creative endeavours, was also felicitated at the function. Filmmaker Syed Akhtar Mirza was honoured to mark his completion of 50 years in cinema.
"No place in India that has such a tremendous history of cinema as Kerala. When this State honours me, it means a lot to me," he said.

title: Intermediate Board releases revised timetable for public exams
summary: Andhra Pradesh Board of Intermediate Education releases revised timetable for 2026 Intermediate Public Examinations.
content:
The Andhra Pradesh Board of Intermediate Education (BIE) on Friday released the revised timetable for the Intermediate Public Examinations (IPE) for first and second-year students, scheduled to begin in February 2026, aligning the schedule with the list of general holidays.
As per the updated timetable, first-year Intermediate examinations will be held from February 23 to March 24, 2026, while the second-year examinations will take place from February 24 to March 23, 2026.
BIE Secretary P. Ranjit Basha announced that the Ethics and Human Values examination will be conducted on January 21, 2026, from 10 a.m. to 1 p.m., and the Environmental Education examination on January 23, 2026, during the same hours.
The practical examinations are scheduled from February 1 to 10, 2026, for general courses, and from January 27 to February 1, 2026, for vocational courses. They will be conducted in two sessions every day—from 9 a.m. to 12 noon and from 2 p.m. to 5 p.m.—including Sundays.
In addition, the Samagra Shiksha Vocational Trade Examination (NSQF Level-4 – Theory) will be held on February 13, 2026, from 10 a.m. to 12 noon, the Secretary added.
A detailed subject-wise timetable is available on the official website bie.ap.gov.in.

title: Kudumbashree food fest showcases Malabar culinary heritage
summary: Experience Malabar's culinary heritage at the Kudumbashree food fest in Kozhikode, featuring traditional dishes and local entrepreneurs.
content:
The ongoing food festival and trade fair, organised by the Kudumbashree District Mission near Lions Park at Kozhikode South Beach, is celebrating the rich culinary heritage of Malabar. The seaside venue welcomes visitors with stalls selling traditional dishes, snacks, combo meals, cakes, desserts, and a wide array of ethnic delicacies prepared by various Kudumbashree units across the district.
“Kudumbashree offers a vital marketing platform for grassroots entrepreneurs like us who lack access to mainstream retail spaces,” said Thesleena, a home baker who is retailing at the event.
Aimed at empowering small-scale sellers financially, the festival promotes micro-enterprise products through its dedicated stalls. A particular highlight of the fest is the range of cakes and desserts prepared by the Kudumbashree Cafe training group.
In addition to food stalls, trade hubs have been set up at the fest for selling organic and natural products such as forest honey, red sanders, ginger coffee, true indigo, and palm candy.
​“The unique flavours have drawn visitors not only from across the district but from neighbouring districts as well. Despite the slow start, we are hoping to host more customers in the coming days,” said Neethu A., district programme manager, Kudumbashree.
​By focussing on microfinance and livelihood development, the Kudumbashree Mission aims to stimulate the local economic growth of women entrepreneurs. It provides small-scale units with a marketing space to showcase their skills, helping them secure financial independence and achieve a sustainable livelihood.
”Kudumbashree offers products with no added preservatives, ensuring purity and natural quality,” said Kavitha P.C., district mission coordinator.
​The festival is open from 11 a.m. to 10 p.m. until Sunday (December 21).

title: SSUS nod for KCA’s cricket stadium on Kalady campus
summary: SSUS approves land for KCA to develop a first-class cricket stadium and multi-sport facilities at Kalady campus.
content:
Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit (SSUS) will provide around six acres on its main campus at Kalady to the Kerala Cricket Association (KCA) for setting up a first-class cricket ground along with allied infrastructure and facilities.
A Syndicate meeting held on Friday (December 19) discussed the revised master plan for the project ahead of signing a memorandum of understanding with the KCA. K.S. Arun Kumar, Syndicate member, said the cricketing body would have the right to use the six-acre land for developing the stadium and allied infrastructure. He added that the total cost of the project was expected to be around ₹55 crore. The KCA leadership was not available for comment.
The agreement is for a period of 33 years. According to the draft agreement, the KCA will develop/construct multi-sports facilities, including a football ground with an athletic track (400-m synthetic track). It will construct and hand over a sports hostel to the university. The KCA will have to meet the cost and expenses incurred towards developing cricket facilities, which include a first-class cricket ground, turf pitches, an office room, players’ and official pavilions, sight screens, camera towers, and indoor and outdoor practice facilities.
Mr. Kumar said the facility would accommodate around 100 students. A seven-member managing committee will be in control of the affairs of the cricket facilities and scheduled premises. It will include four members representing the university, nominated by the Vice-Chancellor and three members nominated by the KCA.

title: Tamil Nadu SIR draft electoral roll: How to check your name in voter list
summary: Check the newly released Tamil Nadu draft electoral roll and find out how to verify your voter registration status.
content:
The Election Commission of India (ECI) haspublished the draft electoral roll of voters in Tamil Naduon Friday (December 19, 2025), after carrying out the much-debatedSpecial Intensive Revision (SIR)exercise. This assumes significance as the State is just months away from Assembly elections due next year.
Earlier on October 27, theECI announcedthe conduct of second phase of the the Special Intensive Revision of electoral in 12 States and Union Territories, including poll-bound Tamil Nadu, West Bengal, Kerala and Puducherry, covering nearly 51 crore voters. The first phase was conducted in Bihar.
In Tamil Nadu, the enumeration phase which was initially scheduled for a period of 30 days from November 4 to December 4 was extended twice —by a week till December 11and again by three daystill December 14.
SIR will lead to fresh voter list in Tamil Nadu, ECI tells Madras High Court
Unrealistic targets, missed meals, no toilets: Booth Level Officers across T.N. say SIR work causes immense stress
Addressing journalists at Chennai on December 19, Archana Patnaik, the Chief Electoral Officer of Tamil Nadu, said the names of more than 97.37 lakh voters have been deleted on grounds such as death, shifting, absenteeism, duplication and non-submission of SIR enumeration forms.
After these deletions, Tamil Nadu’s draft electoral rolls contain the names of 5,43,76,756 voters including 2,66,63,233 men, 2,77,06,332 women and 7,191 persons of third gender. It is 97,37,831 voters fewer than a total of 6,41,14,587 voters as on October 27, 2025, said Ms. Patnaik.
The draft electoral roll that has been prepared after the SIR process will be available both online and offline, according to the ECI. Eligible voters in Tamil Nadu can check if their names are present in the draft electoral roll through any of the following ways.
If your name is missing from the published draft electoral roll, Form 6 will have to be filled and submitted. Supporting documents for proof of age as well as residence and a recent passport-size photograph will also have to be submitted along with Form 6. The submission can be made either online (via ECI’s website atvoters.eci.gov.inor ECINET app) or directly to the respective BLO.
Special camps also will be conducted for this purpose, the dates of which are to be announced later.
All the above forms can be downloaded online at —elections.tn.gov.in/Download_Forms.aspxorvoters.eci.gov.in— and the guidelines to fill each type of form are also available in these websites.
