title: Soil tests in Kuttanad paddy fields show aluminium levels 39 to 165 times above safe limits
summary: Soil tests in Kuttanad reveal alarming aluminium levels, urging immediate government action to protect agriculture and farmers' livelihoods.
content:
Soil tests in Kuttanad, the rice bowl of Kerala, have revealed dangerously high aluminium concentrations in paddy fields, posing a serious threat to crop health and productivity.
Analyses of soil samples collected from paddy fields in different parts of Kuttanad and upper Kuttanad by the Kerala Centre for Pest Management (KCPM), and tested at the Rice Research Station, Vyttila, under the Kerala Agricultural University, showed aluminium levels ranging from 77.51 parts per million (ppm) to 334.10 ppm. This is about 39 to 165 times higher than the permissible level of two ppm or two mg per kg of soil for rice cultivation.
Smitha B., project director, KCPM, said the problem was linked to increasing soil acidity. “We collected samples from 12 paddy fields, and all of them showed very high aluminium concentrations. Aluminium becomes more soluble and toxic as soil pH drops below five, with its availability increasing tenfold for every unit decline in pH. Excessive aluminium damages the plant root system and severely interferes with the absorption of essential nutrients such as phosphorus, calcium, potassium, and magnesium. In highly acidic soils, iron, along with aluminium, is also present in quantities harmful to plants,” she said.
Officials said corrective measures must focus on reducing soil acidity. “When soil acidity decreases, and the pH rises above 5.5, the solubility of aluminium and iron declines, reducing their harmful effects. Effective control of soil acidity is possible only through the application of liming materials and proper leaching. The most effective materials for controlling excess aluminium are dolomite and calcium silicate,” said an official.
Meanwhile, Kodikunnil Suresh, MP, said the alarmingly high aluminium contamination pointed to a “grave environmental imbalance”. From an agricultural perspective, Mr. Suresh said the decline in soil productivity and the resulting significant reduction in paddy yields directly threaten the livelihoods of thousands of small and marginal farmers.
“The government should intervene urgently to scientifically assess the extent of aluminium contamination in the Kuttanad region, identify the sources of pollution, and implement immediate soil and water remediation measures,” he said.

title: Umesh Moghe to launch ‘Gen Z Grooves’ workshop series on Dec. 22
summary: Umesh Moghe's 'Gen Z Grooves' workshop series launches on December 22, training young percussionists in Kozhikode.
content:
Noted tabla artiste Umesh Moghe will launch ‘Gen Z Grooves,’ a State-level workshop series for training young percussionists at Pookkad Kalalayam near Koyilandy in Kozhikode district on Monday (December 22). The project, designed by emerging percussionist Arjun Kaliprasad, will give an opportunity to over 30 students in Kozhikode district on the launch day.
Celebrated percussionists from various States will lead the upcoming district-level workshops in Kerala, which will culminate in Thiruvananthapuram in December 2026. Students who attend the master classes as part of the intensive workshops will be given the opportunity to connect with leading artistes in the field and explore openings for various scholarships.
According to the organisers, eminent tabla artistes and trainers will also be invited and honoured during the district-level workshops as part of popularising the art among youngsters. On Monday, veteran tabla artiste and trainer Sivadas Chemanchery will be honoured, they said.

title: Jagan’s birthday cutout featuring KCR, KTR sparks political discussion
summary: A birthday cutout of Jagan featuring KCR and KTR ignites political discussions and speculations in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.
content:
A cutout erected to mark the birthday of YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) president and former Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy has become a talking point across Andhra Pradesh and Telangana, after photographs of senior Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) leaders were featured alongside him.
The cutout, installed near Tadepalli, close to Jagan’s residence, prominently displays the message “Happy Birthday Jagannanna”. However, what drew immediate public and political attention was the inclusion of images of former Telangana Chief Minister K. Chandrashekar Rao (KCR) and BRS working president K. Taraka Rama Rao (KTR).
According to sources, the cutout was erected by Ravinder Yadav, a resident of Serilingampally in Hyderabad, Telangana. Soon after it was put up, photographs and videos of the display began circulating widely on social media platforms, going viral and sparking discussion among political observers and party supporters.
The presence of KCR and KTR on a Jagan’s birthday cutout has led to speculations about the cordial relations between the YSRCP and the BRS. Many political commentators allegedly view the gesture as symbolic, suggesting mutual respect and a continuing political rapport between the leaderships of the two regional parties.
Meanwhile, leaders across party lines extended birthday greetings to the YSRCP chief.
Andhra Pradesh Governor S. Abdul Nazeer conveyed his greetings, wishing him good health, happiness and a long life. Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu extended birthday wishes to Mr. Jagan, praying for his long and healthy life. Deputy Chief Minister and Jana Sena Party (JSP) chief K. Pawan Kalyan extended his wishes, praying for the former Chief Minister’s good health and happiness. HRD Minister Nara Lokesh also extended birthday greetings to Mr. Jagan, wishing him good health and a long life.
APCC president and Jagan’s sister, Y.S. Sharmila, extended her warm birthday greetings, expressing her sincere wish that god bless him with good health and longevity. Former Rajya Sabha MP V. Vijayasai Reddy conveyed his warm birthday wishes, praying for Mr. Jagan’s strength, good health, happiness and continued success in serving the people.
BRS leader K.T. Rama Rao also extended his heartfelt greetings, wishing Mr. Jagan strength and success in public life. Senior Congress leader Bhatti Vikramarka Mallu wished the former Chief Minister good health, happiness and a long life.

title: TGCSB warns public against Chrome attacks and WhatsApp ‘Ghost Pairing’ scams
summary: TGCSB warns against rising Chrome attacks and WhatsApp Ghost Pairing scams, urging citizens to enhance their online security.
content:
The Telangana Cyber Security Bureau (TGCSB) has issued an advisory warning citizens about a rise in Chrome-based cyber attacks and WhatsApp takeover frauds, commonly known as Ghost Pairing attacks.
The advisory said that Chrome attacks occur when users visit malicious websites or click harmful links that exploit browser vulnerabilities to steal sensitive data, including saved banking credentials. The bureau also cautioned against WhatsApp Ghost Pairing scams, in which victims are deceived into sharing a WhatsApp code through fake messages or links, allowing attackers to secretly link their own devices and monitor chats without disrupting normal app activity.
The bureau advised users who suspect a compromise to immediately check the ‘Linked Devices’ section on WhatsApp and remove any unfamiliar devices, enable two-step verification, and stop using the affected browser or application. Citizens were urged to document evidence by saving screenshots, transaction details and call logs, update Google Chrome to the latest version, and change passwords for email, banking and social media accounts. Banks and payment apps should be informed if any financial loss is detected.
The TGCSB further cautioned the public against sharing OTPs, PINs, CVVs or WhatsApp codes, clicking on urgent or unfamiliar links, or logging into unknown websites or pop-up windows.

title: Railways to prepare reservation charts 10 hours in advance
summary: Indian Railways will prepare reservation charts 10 hours before departure to inform remote passengers and reduce anxiety.
content:
The Indian Railways has decided to prepare the reservation charts 10 hours before the scheduled departure of the train from the  charting station.
“This helps in informing the passengers from remote locations and long distances about their reservation status and relieve them of anxiety,” South Central Railway (SCR) Chief Public Relations Officer A. Sridhar said in a release.
For trains that depart between 5 a.m. and 2 p.m, the reservation charts would be prepared by 8 p.m. the previous day. For trains that depart between 2 p.m. and 11.59 p.m. and between 12 a.m. and 5 a.m., the reservation charts would be prepared preferably at least 10 hours in advance, Mr. Sridhar said.

title: Nirmala stresses on AI, regulatory predictability for Viksit Bharat
summary: Nirmala Sitharaman outlines AI integration and regulatory predictability for India's economic future at a high-level brainstorming session in Hampi.
content:
Union Minister for Finance and Corporate Affairs Nirmala Sitharaman on Saturday set a strategic roadmap for India’s economic future, emphasising the integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and the establishment of regulatory predictability to achieve the vision of a Viksit Bharat.
She, along with Union Minister of State for Corporate Affairs Harsh Malhotra, was chairing a high-level Chintan Shivir (brainstorming session) of the Ministry of Finance and the Ministry of Corporate Affairs that commenced at the UNESCO World Heritage Site of Hampi in Vijayanagara district.
The session brought together the top brass of India’s financial policy-makers, including all Secretaries of the two Ministries, the Chairmen of the Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) and the Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC), and the Chief Economic Adviser to the Central government.
The primary deliberations centered on the theme of “AI, Ease of Doing Business, and Financing for Viksit Bharat”, where officials engaged in intensive discussions on strengthening institutional capacity and policy-making through technology-enabled systems.
The Union Finance Minister underscored the importance of process reforms to improve the ease of doing business, highlighting that the simplification of procedures and coordinated inter-departmental functioning are essential for a robust economy.
The sessions also covered critical areas such as ensuring efficient fund flows, establishing a future-ready tax administration and identifying financing pathways for sustained growth, all while leveraging digital tools to enhance transparency, efficiency and accountability in governance.
Reflecting on the choice of venue, Ms. Sitharaman spoke on the profound historical significance of the Vijayanagara region.
She noted that the erstwhile empire represents the peak of Indian imperial power from barely 500 years ago, with its cultural and administrative imprint still visible across large parts of the subcontinent.
She, however, balanced this historical pride with a call for pragmatism, drawing the attention of senior officials to the stark contrasts within the Vijayanagara district.
The Union Finance Minister pointed out that while the region is home to magnificent world-heritage monuments, it also encompasses drought-prone areas struggling with low agricultural productivity and persistent human-animal conflict.
She emphasised that the vision for a developed India must remain grounded in these present-day development realities to ensure that economic policies effectively address the challenges faced by such regions.

title: 90-day campaign to settle pending cases through mediation to begin from January 2
summary: Mysuru courts launch a 90-day mediation campaign on January 2, 2026, to expedite resolution of pending cases.
content:
All the taluk courts and the district court in Mysuru will take up a 90-day campaign to settle pending cases through mediation from January 2, 2026, as per the directions issued by National Legal Services Authority, New Delhi, and Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, Bengaluru.
A press statement issued here by the Mysuru District Legal Services Authority described the national campaign as a “golden opportunity” for the public to obtain speedy relief in cases pending before the courts.
Through this campaign, appropriate guidance will be provided to both parties to arrive at a mutual settlement in compoundable criminal cases, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal cases, bank recovery cases, labour disputes, claims relating to wages of industrial workers, land acquisition cases, cheque dishonour cases, compoundable civil cases, and matrimonial/family court cases (excluding divorce cases), the statement read.
As the cases will be resolved with the consent of both parties, relationships will be preserved and disputes will be amicably resolved. Compromise will be effected only if the solution suggested by the mediator is acceptable to both sides. “This campaign offers a special opportunity for quick resolution at minimal cost,” the statement added.
For more information, Mysuru District Legal Services Authority can be contacted through the toll-free number 15100 for Mysuru city cases while the respective taluk legal services committees can be contacted directly for taluk-level cases, stated the press release.

title: Minister urges parents to strive for polio-free India
summary: Minister Dola Bala Veeranjaneya Swamy urges parents to ensure polio drops for children to help achieve a polio-free India.
content:
Minister for Social Welfare Dola Bala Veeranjaneya Swamy on Sunday (December 21, 2025) urged parents to have their children aged 0-5 years administered polio drops, thereby contributing to making India polio-free.
Speaking after administering polio drops to an infant at a camp organised at Thoorpunaidupalem village in Tangutur mandal of Prakasam district on Sunday, he called it the primary responsibility of every parent to ensure that the disease is completely eradicated.
Mr. Swamy called upon the medical and health officials to visit every doorstep to ensure that every child is covered, in order to achieve 100% coverage.

title: Chairman of Supreme Court’s Road Safety Advisory Committee inspects Bengaluru-Mysuru highway
summary: Chairman Abhay Manohar Sapre inspects Bengaluru-Mysuru highway, recommending enhanced road safety measures and AI camera updates to reduce accidents.
content:
Abhay Manohar Sapre, retired Supreme Court judge and chairperson of the apex court’s Road Safety Advisory Committee, inspected the road safety measures on the National Highway 275, which also connects Bengaluru and Mysuru.
Mr. Sapre, who carried out the inspection along with senior officials including Mandya Deputy Commissioner Kumar on December 20, also held discussions with the officials on the additional measures required to prevent serious road accidents on NH 275.
During the review, the retired judge appreciated that road accidents on the national highway had reduced in 2025 compared to previous years after the installation of AI-enabled cameras.
However, he instructed the officials to take necessary steps to carry out regular technical updates of the AI cameras and other devices to ensure their smooth functioning.
Other safety improvements were also recommended at places where road accidents were reported frequently.  Mr. Sapre also recommended the installation of digital speed control systems to regulate over-speeding of vehicles.
He suggested installing adequate signboards that are prominently and clearly visible at accident-prone locations, in addition to undertaking measures to ensure strict adherence to lane discipline and prevention of over-speeding.
Other officials present during the inspection included A.M. Yogeesh, transport commissioner, Bengaluru, Mallikarjun Baladandi, Superintendent of the Mandya district police, Thimmaiah, Additional Superintendent of the Mandya district police, and M.S. Obale, project director of National Highways Authority of India, Ramanagara.

title: More facilities at Kottayam medical college hospital soon set to open
summary: Several key facilities at the Kottayam Medical College Hospital, including the surgical block, paramedical hostel, cath lab, biogas plant, renovated outpatient department and a lactation unit, are ready for inauguration, Medical College Superintendent  T. K. Jayakumar has said.
content:
Several key facilities at the Kottayam Medical College Hospital, including the surgical block, paramedical hostel, cath lab, biogas plant, renovated outpatient department and a lactation unit, are ready for inauguration, Medical College Superintendent  T. K. Jayakumar has said.
The superintendent informed this at a meeting convened by Ports Minister V. N. Vasavan on Saturday to review the progress of various construction works under way at the hospital. The meeting, held at the Medical College Conference Hall, was attended online by Health and Women and Child Development Minister Veena George, Additional Chief Secretary (Health) Rajan Khobragade and Director of Medical Education K. V. Vishwanathan.
Construction of the cardiology block and the surgical block, both included under the KIIFB project, has been completed. In addition to the existing seven operation theatres, seven more have now been made fully functional.
Addressing the meeting, Health Minister Veena George directed officials to examine the possibility of imposing penalties on the contractor for failing to complete the construction of the super-speciality block within the stipulated timeframe.
The Executive Engineer of the Public Works Department (Buildings) informed the meeting that construction of the building for the infectious diseases treatment department has reached 60% completion and is expected to be completed by February.
The Health Minister also instructed that steps be expedited to demolish the EFG block, which has remained unused for a long period.
Mr. Vasavan directed that a special meeting be convened involving the Electricity Minister and KIIFB representatives to discuss the construction of a 110 kV substation to ensure uninterrupted power supply to the hospital.

title: Enthusiasm and fervour marks Jagan’s birthday celebration’s in A.P., Europe
summary: YSRCP celebrates Jagan's birthday with fervor in A.P. and Europe, honoring his transformative governance and commitment to welfare.
content:
The birthday of YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) president and former Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy was celebrated with enthusiasm and fervour by party leaders, cadres and supporters, both in India and across Europe.
Members of the YSRCP Europe unit, along with supporters from the Netherlands, Germany, Belgium and Switzerland, gathered to celebrate Mr. Jagan’s birthday at Eindhoven in Netherlands. The celebrations turned emotional as speakers recalled Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy’s political journey and praised his people-centric governance, transparency and unwavering commitment to the welfare of the poor and marginalised sections of society.
Addressing the gathering, YSRCP national spokesperson Karthik Yellapragada described Mr. Jagan as an inspirational leader whose politics was rooted in compassion, credibility and social justice. He said Mr. Jagan’s leadership continues to motivate party cadres and supporters across the globe to uphold the ideals of welfare-oriented governance and public service.
Europe core team leaders Sarathi Reddy Vanga, Krishna Teja Reddy Gaddam and Srinivas Reddy Sanikommu highlighted Mr. Jagan’s governance model in Andhra Pradesh, particularly his focus on welfare schemes, transparency in administration and empowerment of the underprivileged. They said his model became a benchmark and source of pride for YSRCP supporters living abroad. The venue echoed with chants of “Jai Jagan”. The members also discussed plans to strengthen the party’s presence across Europe.
Meanwhile, grand celebrations were held at the YSRCP central office in Tadepalli. Speaking on the occasion, YSRCP State coordinator Sajjala Ramakrishna Reddy said Mr. Jagan delivered transformative, people-centric governance that changed the lives of ordinary families, and that public affection for him remains undiminished despite the party’s recent electoral setback.
Mr. Sajjala Ramakrishna Reddy paid floral tributes to the statue of late Chief Minister Y.S. Rajasekhara Reddy and inaugurated the celebrations, which included cake cutting, distribution of saris to the poor and the launch of a blood donation camp. He said Mr. Jagan governed with the welfare of every family as his core objective, implementing promises without discrimination.
He said that the people of Andhra Pradesh had now realised what they lost after witnessing the coalition government’s one-and-a-half-year rule, and recalled that development which would normally take five decades was achieved in just five years under Mr. Jagan’s leadership.
MLC Murugudu Hanumantha Rao said Mr. Jagan enjoys unparalleled public acceptance for redefining governance by making eligibility the sole criterion for welfare delivery. Several senior party leaders and functionaries attended the programme. The celebrations concluded on a note of unity and renewed commitment to the party’s people-first agenda.

title: Maharashtra MP says Belagavi DC illegally restrained him from entering district
summary: Maharashtra MP Dhairyasheel Mane files complaint against Belagavi DC for prohibiting his entry amid local political tensions.
content:
Maharashtra MP Dhairyasheel S. Mane has filed a privilege complaint against Belagavi Deputy Commissioner Mohammad Roshan for issuing prohibitory orders against him from entering Belagavi district.
Mr. Mane met Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla in New Delhi on Saturday and submitted a letter saying that his privilege as a Lok Sabha member has been violated and sought action against Mr. Roshan.
Mr Mane is a Member of Parliament from Hatkanagala in Maharashtra and a member of the Maharashtra government-appointed committee on inter-State border affairs.
Mr. Roshan restrained Mr. Mane from entering Belagavi on November 1 this year and stopped him from participating in a Black Day event organised by Maharashtra Ekikaran Samiti (MES).
The MES, a Belagavi-based political party, that is fighting for the merger of Marathi-speaking areas in Karnataka with Maharashtra, has been organising Black Day events in Belagavi on Rajyotsava Day (November 1) every year. This time, the MES invited Mr. Mane to speak at the Black Day event.
The prohibitory order against Mr. Mane was to avert any law and order problem following his speech as the district administration had inputs that Mr. Mane was likely to make a provocative speech. Successive Deputy Commissioners have taken similar action against Maharashtra politicians during Black Day events in the past.
Mr. Mane has said that he was going to Belagavi to express solidarity with the MES members who have launched a movement to get Belagavi and 865 other Marathi-speaking villages included in Maharashtra.
“MES members are deeply upset that it was on November 1, 1956 these Marathi-speaking areas were merged with Karnataka and not Maharashtra. They have been protesting against this since the linguistic reorganisation of States and I stand in support of the agitation and against the injustice suffered by the Marathi-speaking people,” he said.
“On November 1, this year, the MES members were planning to hold a peaceful protest by showing black flags. They invited me as an MP and a member of the border dispute committee,” he said.
“However, when I was travelling from Maharashtra to Karnataka, Mr. Roshan, who is also the District Magistrate of Belagavi, issued a notice against me. The police stopped me from entering the district. This notice was illegal, unfair and unjustified. I have a right to travel anywhere in India. I am a people’s representative and have no criminal record. Notices against my travel, therefore, are unjustified. My privilege has been violated. Hence, I seek action against the officer,” Mr. Mane said.
However, Kannada organisations have strongly condemned the complaint against the Deputy Commissioner.
“The complaint by Mr. Mane against Mr Roshan is unreasonable and illogical,” said chairman of the central committee of Kannada organisations Ashok Chandaragi. The committee has sent a letter to Mr. Birla’s office.
“By submitting this letter to the Lok Sabha Speaker, Mr. Mane has not only hidden a truth but also proved true to the old Kannada adage that the guilty try to shout the loudest that they are not. Citizens from any part of the country, including MPs from Maharashtra, are free to travel all over the country. Ministers and MPs from Maharashtra also visit Belagavi hundreds of times. There have been no orders against such movements,” he said.
“But there was a clear reason why the Belagavi district administration restrained Mr. Mane. The timing of his visit and his history of making provocative speech made it to prohibit his entry. Mr. Mane and his supporters should understand this,” he said.
“There are many examples of Maharashtra leaders coming to Belagavi on that particular day and making provocative speech, thereby jeopardising law and order. Similarly, there was every possibility of Mr. Mane coming here and inciting the Marathi populace. He has hidden this fact from the Speaker,” he said.
By complaining against the pre-emptive action of the Belagavi Deputy Commissioner, Mr. Mane has not only tried to behave in an unprofessional manner but has also treated the [Lok Sabha] Speaker’s office with lesser importance than it deserves, the letter said.
“Kannada organisations of the border areas not only fully support the action of the Belagavi Deputy Commissioner but also stand firmly behind the officer,” said Mr. Chandaragi, who is also a member of the Karnataka State Border Development Authority.
Copy of the letter has been given to Belagavi MP Jagadish Shettar.

title: Dog park inaugurated in the Nilgiris
summary: The Nilgiris inaugurates its first dedicated dog park, featuring play areas and an agility course for pets.
content:
The Nilgiris MP, A. Raja, inaugurated the State’s first dedicated dog park, established at the tree arboretum in Udhagamandalam, on Sunday.
The Nilgiris district administration said the park has been constructed at ₹42.30 lakh and has playing areas for both large and small dogs. An agility course for dogs has also been installed as part of the dog park.
Pet owners from across the district and tourists have been urged to register ownership of their animals through the portal www.umcpetregistration.in. Each pet owner will have to provide basic details such as their name, address, email address, phone numbers, photo of their pet as well as their own, address proof and vaccination card of the pet before gaining entry into the dog park.
Mr. Raja also laid the foundation for the setting up of a skate park at ₹1.85 crore near Butfire in Udhagamandalam. The skate park will be set up over two acre with an 110-metre long ramp for skaters, a press release from the district administration said.
The Nilgiris MP also laid the foundation to instal high voltage underground cables worth ₹6.02 crore for the Municipality’s water supply station at the Parsons Valley Dam. Mr. Raja said that as overground power cables often became disconnected during monsoon season, that water supply to Udhagamandalam town would occasionally be cut off during spells of intense rain in the past. The new underground cables, once installed, will ensure water supply to all residents even during inclement weather, said the MP.

title: Polio immunisation drive held across three districts
summary: Polio immunisation drive successfully held in Nandyal, Kurnool, and Anantapur, targeting over 2.35 lakh children under five.
content:
Pulse Polio Immunisation drive was held across Nandyal, Kurnool, and Anantapur districts on Sunday (December 21, 2025).
Minister for Roads and Buildings B.C. Janardhan Reddy administered polio drops to children at the camp held at Priyadarshini school at Banaganapalle mandal in Nandyal district. He said that every child below the age of five years should be administered the drops and called upon the people to make the immunisation drive a success. “Two polio drops will secure the future of a child,” he said, adding that the government has made polio drops available at all government hospitals and offices.
In Nandyal town, Collector Rajakumari Ganiya inaugurated the polio drops immunisation camp at the municipal school in Nunepalle and administered polio drops to the children. She said that they have set a target of administering drops to 2.35 lakh children in the district this year and the drops was administered at bus stations, railway stations, and markets for the convenience of travelling women. She said that medical teams will make door-to-door visits from Monday (December 22).
Ms. Rajakumari said that the government is providing nutritious food to children through anganwadi centres. She urged parents to send children below five years of age to anganwadi centres and those aged six to government schools.
In Anantapur, MP Ambica Lakshminarayana and Collector O. Anand took part in the camp at the local municipal school. Mr. Lakshminarayana said that those who could not administer the drops to their children, can get the drops administered to them on Monday and Tuesday (December 23).
Mr. Anand said that 2,84,774 children between the age group of 0-5 are there in the district and the polio immunisation drive was being held in 1,785 polling booths in the district along with 51 PHCs and other medical facilities in urban and rural areas. A total of 5,247 staff are participating in the activity and for those in transit, they have formed 58 teams at bus stations and railway stations and also 68 mobile teams.
In Kurnool, Collector Dr. A. Siri participated in the immunisation drive at the municipal corporation high school in A Camp and administered drops to the children.

title: Over 800 booked for drunk-driving in Cyberabad, Hyderabad during weekend drive
summary: Over 800 individuals were booked for drunk-driving in Cyberabad, Hyderabad during a weekend enforcement drive.
content:
Over 800 individuals were booked for driving under the influence of alcohol during a weekend-special enforcement drive carried out between December 19 and 20
In Cyberabad, 409 motorists were booked, with two-wheeler riders accounting for the bulk of the violations with 290 cases, followed by 95 four-wheelers and 23 three-wheelers. One heavy vehicle driver was also found driving under the influence.
Data released by the police shows that alcohol consumption levels among those caught were significant. As many as 352 offenders recorded blood alcohol concentration levels between 35 mg/100 ml and 200 mg/100 ml, while 37 drivers were found with levels ranging from 201 mg/100 ml to 300 mg/100 ml.  This apart, 20 motorists had alarmingly high BAC levels between 301 mg/100 ml and 550 mg/100 ml. All those apprehended will be produced before the court.
The Cyberabad Traffic Police reiterated that drunken driving remains a serious offence with severe legal consequences. Officials warned that if a person driving in an inebriated condition causes a fatal accident, the accused will be booked under Section 105 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, which deals with culpable homicide not amounting to murder and carries a maximum punishment of up to 10 years of imprisonment along with a fine.
During the previous week, between December 15 and 20, a total of 756 drunk-driving cases were disposed of in the court. Of these, two offenders were sentenced to a combination of fine and social service, while 754 were penalised with fines alone.
Meanwhile, the Hyderabad traffic police booked 403 motorists. Here too, two-wheeler riders formed the majority of offenders with 320 cases, followed by 59 four-wheelers and 23 three-wheelers. One heavy vehicle driver was also found driving under the influence of alcohol
Officials said there would be zero tolerance towards drunken driving and said such special drives would continue. Commuters were urged to cooperate with traffic personnel to ensure safer roads.

title: Loans, lost documents, and loss of houses: Residents face crisis after Kogilu Layout demolition
summary: Residents in Kogilu Layout face homelessness and financial crisis after government demolishes over 150 houses, leaving 500 people vulnerable.
content:
While some women said they had not drunk water throughout the day because there were no toilets left after their houses were demolished, others spoke about the difficulty of breastfeeding their children without even a place to sit.
Men in the area, meanwhile, said they were worried about loans they had taken to meet daily needs, now left with debts but no shelter. For families in Kogilu Layout, multiple problems unfolded at the same time after the families, living in informal settlements, turned homeless.
On December 20, government agencies demolished over 150 houses in Fakeer Colony and parts of Waseem Layout in Kogilu Layout, Yelahanka, leaving around 500 people homeless. With no alternative accommodation provided, many families stayed in a nearby government Urdu school, where they remained through the weekend. However, residents said they were now worried that they would be asked to vacate the school when it reopens on Monday morning, once again leaving them homeless.
The uncertainty has also worsened the financial stress many families were already under. Several men said they had taken loans at high interest rates to manage daily expenses, medical needs, or temporary housing over the years. With the demolition, they said they were left with debts and no shelter. “I took a loan of ₹3 lakh just last month. I sold my two-wheeler to repay part of it. Now, there is no house, and the loan is still there,” Mohammed Zaishan, 53, said, adding that much of what families earn through daily-wage work, domestic labour, or seeking alms goes towards loan repayments.
Several women toldThe Hinduthat they were menstruating but had no access to sanitary products, clean clothes or any space, as all their belongings were destroyed. “Everything was inside the house. We don’t even have spare clothes. All of us have been avoiding drinking water for long hours because there were no toilets left after the demolition. If we drink water, where do we go?” Soukanya M., a native of Bagepalli who works as a daily-wage labourer in Bengaluru, said, while feeding her three-month-old baby.
Families said schoolchildren had lost books and certificates during the demolition drive. Bhanupriya, an LLB student, said all her study material, including her examination identity card, was buried under the debris. “My exam is on Monday, and I don’t even have my ID card. We are trying to reach out to anyone who could help appear for the exam, she said. They also pointed out to children who were left exposed to the cold, asking, “Does the government have no humanity? It is peak winter, we have no roof, our children are falling sick, and we don’t even have blankets.”
Displaced residents also protested outside the office of MLA for Byatarayanapura Krishna Byre Gowda, demanding alternative accommodation and relief. The residents, however, said Mr. Gowda did not address their concerns and asked them to return again on Monday. They argued that their address was listed on electricity meters, Aadhaar and ration cards, and questioned how the government could now label them as illegal occupants.

title: Fisherman killed in deep-sea fishing accident
summary: A 58-year-old fisherman died after a pulley fell on him during deep-sea fishing off Vadakara coast.
content:
Kozhikode: A 58-year-old fisherman was killed after a broken pulley fell on his head during deep-sea fishing off the Vadakara coast early on Sunday (December 21). The victim was identified as Vamanan, a resident of Puthiyanirathu near Elathur. The accident occurred around 2 a.m. on a fishing boat named Jinaraj.
The police said the overhead pulley fell when the fisherman attempted to release a net that had become entangled with it. He was declared dead at a private hospital in Vadakara, police added.

title: Centre rejects mining push charge behind Aravalli definition
summary: Centre denies mining changes in Aravalli, asserting Supreme Court's definition enhances protection and freezes new leases for sustainable management.
content:
The Centre on Sunday (December 21, 2025) rejected reports that the definition of the Aravalli hills had been changed to allow large-scale mining, and cited a Supreme Court-ordered freeze on new mining leases in the region.
It said aSupreme Court-approved frameworkprovides for stronger protection of the mountain system and places a freeze on new mining leases until a comprehensive management plan is finalised.
Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav told reporters in the Sundarban Tiger Reserve that the Supreme Court-approved definition will bring more than 90% of the Aravalli region under “protected area.”
In an explanation issued amid controversy over the “100-metre” criterion, the government said the definition of Aravalli hills and range has been standardised across states on the directions of the Supreme Court to remove ambiguity and prevent misuse, particularly practices that allowed mining to continue dangerously close to hill bases.
Sources in the Environment Ministry said the Supreme Court, while hearing long-pending cases on illegal mining in the Aravallis, had constituted a committee in May 2024 to recommend a “uniform definition”, as different states were following inconsistent criteria while granting mining permissions.
The committee, chaired by the Environment Ministry secretary and comprising representatives from Rajasthan, Haryana, Gujarat, and Delhi along with technical bodies, found that only Rajasthan had a formally established definition, which it has been following since 2006.
That definition treats landforms rising 100 metres or more above local relief as hills and prohibits mining within the lowest bounding contour enclosing such hills, irrespective of the height or slope of landforms inside the contour.
Also Read |Citizens’ report highlights illegal waste dumping and burning in Aravalis
The sources said all four states agreed to adopt this long-standing Rajasthan definition, along with additional safeguards to make it objective and transparent.
These include treating hills located within 500 metres of each other as a single range, mandatory mapping of hills and ranges on Survey of India maps before any mining decision and clear identification of core and inviolate areas where mining is prohibited.
In a backgrounder, the government rejected claims that mining had been permitted in areas below 100 metres and said the restriction applies to entire hill systems and their enclosed landforms and not merely to the hill peak or slope.
It said it is “incorrect to conclude” that all landforms below 100 metres are open for mining.
The dismal state of India’s environment
‘Road to hell is paved with good intentions’: Congress slams govt over new Aravalli definition
Biting the dust in the Aravalis
The government said the apex court has accepted the committee’s recommendation to prohibit mining in core and inviolate areas, including protected areas, eco-sensitive zones, tiger reserves, wetlands and areas close to such sites, while allowing limited exemptions only for critical, strategic and deep-seated minerals in national interest.
According to the Supreme Court’s directions, no new mining leases will be granted in the Aravalli region until a Management Plan for Sustainable Mining is prepared for the entire landscape by the Indian Council of Forestry Research and Education.
Existing mines may continue operations only if they strictly comply with sustainable mining norms laid down by the committee.
The government said district-level analysis across Rajasthan, Haryana and Gujarat shows that legally approved mining currently covers only a very small fraction of the Aravalli region, amounting to about 0.19 per cent of the total geographical area of 37 Aravalli districts.
Delhi, which has five Aravalli districts, does not permit any mining.
The government said the primary threat to the Aravallis remains illegal and unregulated mining, and the committee has recommended stronger monitoring, enforcement and use of technology such as drones and surveillance to address this issue.

title: Tipra Motha to go solo in district council polls if Tiprasa Accord not implemented: Pradyot
summary: Pradyot Debbarma announces Tipra Motha Party will contest district council polls solo if Tiprasa Accord remains unimplemented.
content:
Tipra Motha Party (TMP) supremoPradyot Kishore Manikya Debbarmaon Sunday (December 21, 2025) saidhis party would contest the elections to the Tripura Tribal Areas Autonomous District Council (TTAADC) aloneif the Tiprasa accord is not implemented.
TMP, a BJP ally, signed an agreement with the Centre and the State government in March 2024 for the overall development of the indigenous people.
In the 2021 TTADC elections, the BJP had to concede defeat at the hands of the TMP, then a newly formed regional party.
"What is there to say when Chief Minister Manik Saha himself has announced that the BJP will win all 28 seats of the tribal council. If the Tiprasa Accord is not implemented, we will fight the election alone because I cannot fool my people," Mr. Debbarma told reporters.
Claiming that the Centre was willing to implement the accord, the TMP chief said certain leaders in the State appeared to be opposed to its implementation.
Mr. Debbarma also made it clear that the party would not compromise on the issue of thescript for Kokborok, the mother tongue of most tribal communities in Tripura.
Referring to the fallout of attempts to impose Urdu in the then East Pakistan, he said the choice of script for Kokborok was an internal matter and no one could dictate it to the Tiprasa people.
"The Centre and the State government must respect the sentiments of the indigenous people regarding the selection of the Kokborok script. We will not change our stand. This is our internal issue," he said.
OnBangladesh's turmoil situation, Mr. Debbarma said the Centre and the State government must adopt a clear policy for the Northeast because fundamentalists are active across the border.
"Minorities, especially indigenous tribes, are being oppressed in Bangladesh. Radical forces are threatening to provide shelter to anti-Indian forces in Bangladesh. A nationalist party can't remain a silent spectator in the volatile situation", he said.

title: Police counsel repeat offenders, warn of strict action
summary: Police counsel known offenders in Puttaparthi, warning strict action against repeat offences to enhance community safety and accountability.
content:
Superintendent of Police S. Satish Kumar on Sunday (December 21, 2025) ordered district-wide counselling for known offenders and rowdy-sheeters, warning of strict action in the event of repeat offences.
Police officials across all subdivisions in Sri Sathya Sai district summoned habitual offenders and rowdy-sheeters and counselled them to change their behaviour and desist from criminal activities. The initiative is part of a focused strategy to prevent sexual harassment, rape, kidnapping, murder, and other serious offences involving women and minor girls, the police said.
Speaking to the media here, the SP said that special attention was being given to prevent incidents of stalking and harassment of girls travelling to schools and colleges, as well as indecent behaviour towards women in public places. He warned that such acts would not be tolerated and would invite stringent legal action, including opening of rowdy sheets and continuous surveillance of offenders’ movements.
Stressing the need for behavioural changes, Mr. Satish Kumar said that counselling is intended to provide offenders with an opportunity to correct themselves and reintegrate as responsible citizens. He cautioned that those who failed to reform would face uncompromising enforcement of the law. He reiterated that offenders must abandon criminal conduct and maintain good behaviour.

title: HYDRAA Commissioner’s PSO critical after alleged suicide attempt
summary: A personal security officer attached to HYDRAA chief allegedly attempted suicide at his Hayathnagar residence on Sunday, with police suspecting financial distress due to losses in online betting and gaming apps as the possible trigger.
content:
A personal security officer attached to the Hyderabad Disaster Response and Asset Protection Agency (HYDRAA) Commissioner allegedly attempted to end his life using his service pistol at his residence in Hayathnagar on Sunday morning. Police suspect financial distress linked to losses in online betting and gaming apps as a possible reason.
The victim, identified as Mutyalapayti Krishna Chaitanya, 32, an Armed Reserve Constable of the City Security Wing, belonging to the 2020 batch and working as personal security officer to HYDRAA Commissioner A.V. Ranganath, sustained a gunshot injury to the head at his house in Sai Surya Nagar, Munaganoor, around 6.30 a.m.
He was shifted to Kamineni Hospital in L.B. Nagar. Doctors said he was brought in a “comatose condition”. A CT scan revealed extensive fractures to the skull and brain. Hospital authorities said he underwent emergency surgery and is currently under intensive neurocritical care. His condition remains serious.
Police said preliminary inquiry indicates that Chaitanya was under financial stress due to debts allegedly incurred after suffering losses on betting and gaming applications. A case has been booked by Hayathnagar police and further investigation is under way to establish the exact circumstances leading to the incident.
(Roshni suicide prevention helpline numbers: 8142020033/44 and 040 66202000/2001.)

title: Vijayanagara legacy offers lessons for inclusive growth: Nirmala Sitharaman
summary: Nirmala Sitharaman highlights Vijayanagara's inclusive governance lessons for India's development goals during her visit to Hampi.
content:
Union Finance and Corporate Affairs Minister Nirmala Sitharaman on Sunday said that the ideals of prosperity and inclusive governance reflected in the Vijayanagara Empire remain relevant to India’s goal of becoming a developed nation by 2047.
Ms. Sitharaman, who visited the UNESCO World Heritage site at Hampi in Vijayanagara district along with a team of 120 officers from the Union Ministry of Finance, said that the visit enabled officials to understand the historical, administrative and economic significance of the erstwhile empire.
“The message of Vijayanagara, ‘Prosperity for all’, aligns with the principles guiding the current public policy. As preparations are under way for the forthcoming Union Budget, the visit offers perspective on building a prosperous and inclusive India,” she said.
Earlier, Ms. Sitharaman planted saplings of tamarind, custard apple and other species on the Hampi Development Authority premises near Kamalapur. She also participated in the National Pulse Polio Programme at the Community Health Centre in Kamalapur by administering polio drops to children.
Stressing the need to sustain India’s polio-free status, Ms. Sitharaman said that continued institutional support is essential for doctors, paramedical staff, nurses and caregivers engaged in immunisation efforts.
Referring to her visit to Kasapur village in Kudligi taluk in October this year, where facilities for agricultural processing were inaugurated using funds from her MP Local Area Development Scheme, she said that rural livelihoods require sustained policy and institutional support.
She added that the plantation drive undertaken by the visiting officers reflected a commitment to environmental conservation.
Union Minister of State for Corporate Affairs and Road Transport and Highways Harsh Malhotra, Ballari MP E. Tukaram, MLAs H.R. Gaviappa and N.T. Srinivas, Finance Ministry Secretary Nagaraju Maddirala, Central Board of Direct Taxes Chairman Ravi Agrawal, Economic Affairs Secretary Anuradha Thakur and senior officials were present.

title: JAC calls for Rajampeta bandh on December 23
summary: Rajampeta JAC announces a bandh on December 23 to demand district status for Rajampeta as headquarters.
content:
Rajampeta Joint Action Committee (JAC) has called for a dawn-to-dusk bandh on Tuesday (December 23, 2025) across Rajampeta Assembly constituency in Annamayya district, stepping up its agitation for district status with Rajampeta as the headquarters.
Rajampeta Telugu Desam Party in-charge Jaganmohan Raju, Jana Sena leader Vellaturu Srinivasa Raju, and BJP leader Lokesh jointly announced the bandh at the protest camp here on Sunday (December 21). The leaders appealed to educational institutions, government offices, commercial establishments, voluntary organisations, and the public to extend support to the bandh.
As part of mobilisation efforts, banners and posters were displayed across the town, highlighting the demand for a separate district. Representations were already submitted to Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu, Deputy Chief Minister Pawan Kalyan, and Education Minister Nara Lokesh, urging the government to consider Rajampeta as district headquarters.
The organisers said that Rajampeta serves as a central hub for surrounding constituencies such as Railway Kodur and Rayachoti, and that district formation would ease administrative access for people from several mandals and villages.

title: Violations at entry, exit points endanger traffic flow on Kozhikode bypass road
summary: Traffic rule violations at entry and exit points on Kozhikode bypass endanger safety, disrupting flow and increasing collision risks.
content:
Rampant violations of traffic rules at the demarcated entry and exit points along the six-lane Kozhikode bypass road have emerged as a major safety hazard for motorists. Despite the installation of CCTV cameras and cautionary signboards, many drivers continue to flout regulations by making sudden entries onto the bypass or accessing service roads through unauthorised points.
Road safety bollards erected to mark permitted entry and exit points remain partially damaged at several stretches, further encouraging unsafe practices. While light motor vehicle drivers and motorcycle riders are frequently involved in such violations, heavy vehicles have also been found breaking highway discipline in attempts to shorten their journey by a few kilometres.
Inter-district taxi operators, who regularly ferry passengers to Kozhikode international airport, point out that unauthorised and unexpected entries and exits from restricted areas disrupt the smooth flow of traffic on the six-lane highway. In many instances, motorists enter the bypass through service road exit points without checking the speed of oncoming vehicles, increasing the risk of collisions.
Ambulance drivers have also raised concerns over frequent violations of one-way traffic regulations on service roads, particularly by drivers attempting to access the bypass quickly through exit points. They allege that delays in conducting flash inspections have allowed such violations to go unchecked. Although camera surveillance covers the entire 28-km-long bypass, proper monitoring of the footage to identify and penalise violators is yet to be effectively implemented, they claim.
“From Thondayad to Malaparamba, the one-way traffic regulation on the service road is hardly enforced. As a result, there is a chaotic situation at the Thondayad junction now,” says Rathnakumar Paravath, a building contractor from the area. He points out that the free left movement of vehicles from Malaparamba towards the Medical College side is frequently disrupted due to violations of one-way rules.
Reckless entry of vehicles from the Chevayur side onto the bypass near the Malaparamba junction has also begun affecting the free movement of traffic on the main carriageway. The police are forced to camp at the spot regularly to prevent rash entries.
A retired Public Works department engineer recalls that experts had earlier raised strong objections to the provision of numerous entry and exit points along the bypass, citing the risk of interruptions to fast-moving vehicles. “There should be stronger measures to monitor stray vehicle movements at such high-risk points to prevent major tragedies,” he adds.
Meanwhile, police sources say that enforcement actions based on CCTV visuals will be intensified in the wake of growing public concern. They also claim that local drivers form the majority of violators and often refuse to cooperate with the newly introduced regulations following the opening of the six-lane road.

title: Congress targeting BJP through Karnataka-style hate law: Ramchander Rao
summary: Congress targeting BJP through Karnataka-style hate law: Ramchander Rao
content:
Telangana BJP president N. Ramchander Rao strongly opposed the inclination of the Congress Government led by Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy to bring a “hate speech Bill on a par with the Karnataka government”.
He alleged that the Telangana government is trying to bring such a Bill only to “harass BJP workers and target the party”.
Mr. Rao accused the Congress leaders of indulging in hatred campaign by making ‘anti-sanatan’ remarks. “Is it not a hate speech when Mr. Revanth Reddy had commented on Hindu gods and said that Congress is Muslims and Muslims is Congress,” during the Jubilee Hills byelections, he questioned.
Talking to the media on Sunday, he said that BJP would oppose any such move by the Congress government.
He also said that BRS president and ex-CM K. Chandrasekhar Rao, after a long time, coming out and getting involved in politics would not make any difference. It was like ‘OTP’, he quipped and said that the BRS has no credibility among people, as they have realised that “BRS leaders have involved in deep-neck corruption during its regime”.
Earlier on Saturday, Mr. Rao said that, attracted by the good governance of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, cine artistes are joining BJP with a desire to serve the nation. Addressing a gathering at the party office, after welcoming actress Aamani, along with makeup artist and Nandi Award winner Shobhalatha, into the party by draping them with the BJP scarf in the presence of Union Minister G. Kishan Reddy, he said that a “double-engine government” is essential for Telangana’s all-round development.
He highlighted that the party had won around 1,000 sarpanch posts, over 1,200 upa-sarpanch positions, and more than 10,000 ward member seats. Despite threats, these representatives remain committed to the BJP, which he said is a testament to the people’s faith in the party.  “The results have proved critics wrong who claimed the BJP was confined to urban areas,” he added. General secretary N. Gautam Rao, vice president Jayashree, SC Morcha national secretary S. Kumar, chief spokesperson N.V. Subhash, and other leaders, were present.

title: Flower show inaugurated at Mysuru Palace
summary: Discover the vibrant Palace Flower Show 2025 at Mysuru Palace, featuring 25,000 flowers and cultural events until December 31.
content:
The Palace Flower Show 2025 was inaugurated at Mysuru Palace on December 21 evening.
The flower show features more than 25,000 ornamental flower pots with large varieties of flowers including roses, chrysanthemums, carnations, gerberas, orchids, anthuriums, and lilies. These will be on display from 10 a.m. to 9 p.m. till December 31.
One of the highlights of this year’s exhibition is the Preamble of the Indian Constitution, designed in the form of a book and decorated with flowers. A floral replica of the Sringeri Sharada Peetham is also another major attraction of the flower show.
Meanwhile, cultural programmes are also scheduled to be held on the palace premises from December 21 to 25 between 5 p.m. and 9.30 p.m. The palace will be illuminated from 7 p.m. to 9 p.m. every evening.
On the concluding day, December 31, a police band performance will take place from 11 p.m. to midnight, to usher in the New Year, followed by an eco-friendly fireworks display.
Tanveer Sait, former Minister and MLA, T.S. Srivatsa, MLA, D. Thimmaiah, MLC, G. Lakshmikanth Reddy, Mysuru Deputy Commissioner, Yukesh Kumar, Mysuru Zilla Panchayat Chief Executive Officer, and Subramanya, Deputy Director of Mysuru Palace Board, were present at the inauguration of the 10-day flower show.

title: Human-wildlife conflict: Bhupender Yadav chairs meetings to review measures, discuss project updates
summary: Union Minister Bhupender Yadav leads high-level meetings on human-wildlife conflict and conservation strategies for tigers and elephants in India.
content:
The National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA) on Sunday (December 21, 2025) appraised the expansion of Project Cheetah and reviewed measures to address human-wildlife conflict at high-level meetings chaired by Union Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav at the Sundarbans Tiger Reserve.
The 28th meeting of the NTCA and the 22nd Steering Committee meeting of Project Elephant brought together officials, scientists and field experts from tiger-and elephant-range States to review progress and future strategies, the Environment Ministry said in a statement.
Chairing the NTCA meeting, Mr. Yadav underscored the importance of science-based management, landscape-level planning, community participation and inter-State coordination in India's globally recognised tiger conservation model.
The meeting focused on challenges faced by tiger reserves. Measures to address human-tiger conflict, including a three-pronged strategy and the project 'Management of Tigers Outside Tiger Reserves', were highlighted, the statement said.
Issues such as staff shortages, financial constraints, habitat degradation and invasive species management were also reviewed, with directions issued for follow-ups.
The NTCA ratified decisions of its technical committee, including approval of tiger conservation plans, extension and expansion of Project Cheetah, tiger translocation, prey augmentation, landscape management planning, carnivore health management training programmes and inputs on proposals placed before the Standing Committee of the National Board for Wildlife (NBW).
Updates were presented on compliance with directions by the NBW, including expansion of Project Cheetah to Gandhisagar Wildlife Sanctuary and Banni grassland in Gujarat, and the progress of the initiatives supported by the National Compensatory Afforestation Fund Management and Planning Authority (CAMPA).
Preparations for the proposed Global Big Cat Summit were also reviewed.
The Minister reviewed ongoing NTCA activities, including progress under the sixth cycle of the All India Tiger Estimation, commencement of ground surveys from November 2025, landscape-level training programmes and international cooperation under Project Cheetah, including visits by delegations from South Africa, Namibia and Botswana.
The Project Elephant Steering Committee confirmed the action taken on decisions of its previous meeting and reviewed regional action plans for elephant conservation in southern and northeastern India, identifying priority areas for coordinated inter-State action.
The committee examined updates on the 'All-India Synchronised Elephant Estimation', progress under the Model Elephant Conservation Plan for the Nilgiri Elephant Reserve and ongoing work on DNA profiling of captive elephants, with emphasis on strengthening scientific management and welfare standards.
A comprehensive review of human-elephant conflict was undertaken, including findings from studies on conflict drivers and mitigation measures, and the status of compensation mechanisms adopted by States.
The committee also discussed evaluation of elephant population estimation methods, conservation strategies for the Ripu-Chirang Elephant Reserve and future action plans, including management effectiveness evaluation of elephant reserves with CAMPA support and a proposed study on elephant corridors and conflict hotspots in the Bandhavgarh region.
On the occasion, Mr. Yadav released six publications, including reports and journals on Project Cheetah, the sixth cycle of the All India Tiger Estimation, India's tiger conservation framework, biodiversity in tiger reserves and best practices in captive elephant management.

title: Bagalkot teacher-couple, among others, arrested
summary: Bagalkot teacher couple arrested for assaulting a mentally challenged boy, sparking calls for legal action and school closure.
content:
The police have arrested four people, including a teacher couple facing the charge of assaulting inmates of the Divya Jyoti Mentally Challenged Residential School in Navanagar of Bagalkot district.
Officers arrested teachers Akshay Inglekar and his wife Anandi Hindulkar for mercilessly assaulting 16-year-old Deepak Rathod, a mentally challenged boy, in the school in Bagalkot town.
His father complained that Askhay attacked the boy with a belt and a plastic pipe, while his wife Anandi threw chilli powder in the boy’s eyes.
The police have also taken into custody fellow teachers Vitthal and Vishal. A First Information Report (FIR) also names Ravikant Budihal, among others, who have been arrested.
It lists offences under the Juvenile Justice Act and Prevention of Atrocities against Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes Act and BNS and other laws.
The incident is three months old. But the boy’s parents learnt of the offence after a video surfaced on social media. The boy’s father Ashok Rathod has filed the complaint.
A team led by Deputy Superintendent of Police Gajanan Sutar inspected the place and seized material used for the attack.
The police also helped officials of the Women and Child Welfare Department shift the victim to safety. Officers said that 11 of the 32 children have been sent to other schools or are back with their parents. The rest will be rehabilitated soon, they said.
Minister Laxmi Hebbalkar said that she has instructed officials to close down the school and rehabilitate the children by sending them to other public facilities, with the permission of their parents.
She said that an inspection by District Disabled Welfare Officer and the Joint Director of the Women and Child Welfare Department has found that the residential school has not obtained due permissions.
“Strict legal action will be taken against it,” she added.

title: Judges must uphold values with discipline, legal knowledge, says SC judge
summary: Supreme Court Judge Prashant Kumar Mishra emphasizes the judiciary's role in upholding constitutional values and delivering quality justice.
content:
Supreme Court judge Prashant Kumar Mishra observed that the judiciary should act as a bridge between law and justice, and that judges must uphold values and responsibilities with discipline and sound legal knowledge. Judges must strive for excellence in a competitive environment and to continuously enhance their knowledge, he added.
Delivering the keynote address at ‘Upholding the Constitutional Vision – The Role of the District Judiciary’ seminar held at the A.P. Judicial Academy in Mangalagiri on Sunday, Justice Mishra said India had one of the largest judicial systems in the world and that the Indian Constitution embodied the best features compared to many other Constitutions. He emphasised that every aspect of the justice system must function in accordance with the principles laid down by the Constitution.
He also advised judges to remain calm and composed even in complex situations and stressed on the importance of the district judiciary. He noted that the Constitution accorded a significant place to the district judiciary and the judiciary should recognise delivering quality justice as its primary duty.
Access to justice for the common citizen depends largely on the performance of the judiciary, he stated, while calling upon the judiciary to ensure that the court proceedings were understandable even to ordinary people in order to enhance public trust and confidence in the justice system.
Further, Justice Mishra said the conduct of a judge was of utmost importance and clarified that the Constitution was not merely a legal document, and the legislature, judiciary, and executive must function within the constitutional framework. Delivering judgements was not merely about resolving disputes, but giving justice in a meaningful form, he said, adding that the Constitution encompasses matters relevant to everyday life and urged everyone to implement them fully.
A.P. High Court (HC) Chief Justice and Patron-in-Chief of the Judicial Academy, Justice Dheeraj Singh Thakur, said the district judiciary holds a vital place in the justice system and cautioned against negligence in judicial functioning, adding that it would make delivery of justice properly under Articles 14 and 15 of the Constitution impossible.
HC judge and Chairman of the Board of Governors of the Judicial Academy, Justice Ravinath Tilhari, Academy Director Chintalapudi Purushottam Kumar, Principal District Judges and judicial officers from across the State took part.
