University of Mysore registrar M.K. Savitha inaugurated the seminar on December 22. Senior academicians N.B. Ramachandra and S. Basavarajappa were present on the occasion.
The inaugural session featured a lecture on ‘Entrepreneurship – Concepts and Innovation’ by Amulya, a professor at the B.N. Bahadur Institute of Management Studies (BIMS), University of Mysore. She elaborated on entrepreneurship concepts, innovation and invention, and highlighted their relevance from an anthropological perspective.
The second session was delivered by Prof. Ramachandra, Department of Studies in Genetics and Genomics, University of Mysore, on ‘Family History Study as a Road Map for Understanding Genetics and Genomics‘.
The third session was handled by Prof. Basavarajappa, chairman, Department of Studies in Anthropology, University of Mysore, who spoke on ‘Research Methods and Their Applications in Field Research’.

title: Another tiger captured near Gundlupet
summary: Forest authorities capture another tiger in Gundlupet, ensuring safety for local residents after recent wildlife concerns.
content:
Authorities of the Forest Department on Sunday captured another tiger in the Gundlupet sub-division of the Bandipur Tiger Reserve.
The tiger, which appeared to be weak, was found in a banana plantation at Survey No. 197 in Mukti Colony, near Gongalli village, in the Maddur range of the reserve. The animal was safely captured around 5 p.m. after being tranquillised.
The male tiger, estimated to be around five to six years old, looked sick at the time of capture. It has been shifted to the Maddur range office, where it is being kept under close observation by veterinary staff. Further instructions on its management are awaited from the higher authorities.
The operation was led by Bandipur Tiger Reserve Director S. Prabhakaran. Gundlupet Assistant Conservator of Forests (ACF) Suresh K. and other forest officials were present during the operation.
A few days ago, forest officials captured a four-year-old male tiger from a barren land at Bommalapura village, near the Bandipur Tiger Reserve, also in the Gundlupet sub-division. That operation brought immense relief to villagers and farmers living in and around the Gundlupet buffer zone, who had been living in fear following repeated tiger sightings and incidents of livestock attacks.
Tiger sightings had been reported in Bommalapura, K.K. Hundi, Shivapura, Kodasoge, Hullepura, Devapura and surrounding villages, triggering panic among local residents. Forest authorities had advised villagers to clear overgrown shrubs and weeds in uncultivated fields, as such vegetation could serve as hiding places for wild animals. The authorities concerned were also requested to remove thick bushes and shrubs in vulnerable areas.

title: Chief Minister M.K. Stalin to inaugurate Chennai Sangamam on January 14
summary: Chennai Sangamam, a vibrant festival of Tamil art, kicks off on January 14 with diverse performances and exhibitions.
content:
Chief Minister M.K. Stalin will inaugurate Chennai Sangamam-Namma Ooru Thiruvizha, a festival showcasing over 50 art forms of Tamil Nadu, on January 14. The inauguration will feature performances by 250 artistes at the Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium.
Organised during the Pongal festival, the event is a brainchild of DMK Parliamentary party leader Kanimozhi. The festival will bring together folk and classical artistes from across the State, who will perform at parks, stadiums, beaches, and other public spaces in Chennai from January 15 to 18.
A food festival will also be held as part of the three-day celebrations. Poompuhar, the State-run handicrafts corporation, will organise an exhibition during the event, an official release said on Monday.

title: Cong govt. creating hope among youth by efforts to attract investments, says Sridhar Babu
summary: Congress government aims to inspire youth through industrial investments, countering BRS's reliance on hype, says Minister Sridhar Babu.
content:
The State government strongly condemned the comments made by Bharat Rashtra Samithi president and Opposition leader K. Chandrasekhar Rao over the memorandums of understanding (MoUs) signed by companies willing to invest in Telangana.
Industries and IT Minister D. Sridhar Babu said the Congress government was trying to create a ‘hope’ among the youth with its efforts to boost industrial investments as they will result in employment opportunities. The BRS on its part depended on ‘hype’ not hope during its more than nine-year tenure in the government.
He advised the BRS president not to demoralise investors, including major firms, and hinder the progress of the State. The BRS government too signed several MoUs with assurance of subsidies and concessions and it was a fact that all the companies with whom the agreements were signed did not make investments.
“Governments will change, but industrial development is a continuous process. Companies look for congenial atmosphere to invest and we are trying our best to instil confidence among the industry to invest here,” he said. He recalled how the government could secure investments in the form of Global Capability Centres (GCCs) in the last two years which helped Telangana secure a sobriquet as ‘GCC capital’ of the country reflecting the confidence expressed by the companies in investing in the State.
He recalled that the Congress government secured assurances of ₹3.4 lakh crore investments in the last two years as several companies started ground work for their units with a direct employment potential of 1.4 lakh and two lakh indirect jobs. He recalled that the foundation stone for Hyderabad to emerge as drug, pharmaceuticals and vaccine capital of the country were laid by successive Congress governments. “We (Congress governments) hold the patent for boosting Hyderabad as vaccine capital with two thirds of vaccines being manufactured out of here,” he said.
Mr. Sridhar Babu said the Congress government adopted a low profile unlike the BRS government which lived in hype. “You (the BRS) will remain at your place if you continue to depend on hype,” he said. He faulted Mr. Chandrasekhar Rao for casting aspersions on the development of green pharma ecosystem in the upcoming Bharat Future City as real estate venture.

title: AIISH’s ‘Hearing Horizons’ brings together hearing care professionals
summary: AIISH’s ‘Hearing Horizons 2025’ conference unites hearing care professionals to address challenges and advancements in audiology in India.
content:
The All India Institute of Speech and Hearing (AIISH), Mysuru, in association with the Mysuru chapter of the Indian Speech-Language and Hearing Association (MyISHA), organised ‘Hearing Horizons 2025’, a two-day Rehabilitation Council of India-approved national conference, on December 20 and 21 on its premises.
Around 200 professionals and 150 students and audiologists from various parts of the country attended the conference, which featured lectures, manufacturer-led technical sessions, hands-on master class training, a recruitment drive, focus group discussions, and multiple parallel sessions addressing issues in hearing healthcare.
Dr. Kalyani Mandke, one of India’s earliest private practitioners in audiology, who was the chief guest, highlighted the evolution of hearing care practice in India and the need for evidence-based and ethical clinical services.
Dr. B. Mohammed Asheel from the World Health Organization (WHO) emphasised the crucial role of hearing in effective communication and highlighted that hearing aids are essential across the lifespan, supporting speech and language development in children and social participation in adults and older persons.
Dr. M Puspavathi, director, AIISH, emphasised that hearing aid fitting alone does not conclude intervention, particularly in children. She highlighted the importance of post-fitting speech-language therapy for developing effective speech, language, and academic skills while underscoring the need for a comprehensive and multidisciplinary approach to hearing care.
The organisers of the conference, Dr. M. Sandeep and Dr. N. Devi, highlighted that the primary objective of Hearing Horizons 2025 was to bridge the gap between academic institutions and private practitioners.
The conference brought national attention to the increasing burden of hearing loss in India, which affects individuals of all age groups and often remains undetected or untreated. Untreated hearing loss can significantly impact communication abilities, academic achievement, employment opportunities, mental health, and overall quality of life, according to AIISH.
Participants also deliberated on the evolving role of the audiology profession in India, particularly in reaching underserved communities through outreach services and ethical clinical practice. The potential application of AI in hearing care, including hearing aid programming, and follow-up services was discussed.

title: DMK manifesto committee meets Stalin
summary: DMK manifesto committee, led by Kanimozhi, meets with Chief Minister M.K. Stalin at party headquarters in Chennai.
content: The first meeting of the DMK manifesto committee, headed by the party’s Parliamentary party leader Kanimozhi, was held at Anna Arivalayam, the party headquarters, in Chennai on Monday. The committee also met DMK president and Chief Minister M.K. Stalin.

title: Pedestrian crushed to death in Bengaluru; bus driver arrested
summary: A man was killed by a bus in Bengaluru; the driver has been arrested following the incident.
content:
A 42-year-old man died after being run over by a private bus on the Hegganahalli Main Road in Kamakshipalya traffic police limits, police said on Monday.
The deceased has been identified as Chetan Kumar. According to the police, the incident occurred on December 13 at around 7 p.m.
Preliminary investigation revealed that Kumar, who was allegedly under the influence of alcohol, staggered on the road after consuming liquor at a bar.
He reportedly lost balance and fell on the road, and at that time a private bus that was coming from behind ran over him, crushing him to death. The bus driver fled the scene.
The Kamakshipalya traffic police registered a case and later traced the driver. The absconding driver, Narendra, was arrested following the analysis of surveillance footage, the police said.
Further investigation is under way.

title: Congress strangled Constitution by imposing Emergency during Vande Mataram centenary: CM Adityanath
summary: CM Adityanath criticizes Congress for imposing Emergency during Vande Mataram's centenary, emphasizing the song's importance to national duties.
content:
Uttar PradeshChief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Monday (December 22, 2025) said that the Congress — from whose platform Vande Mataram was first sung — “strangled the Constitution" by imposing the Emergency in the country during the centenary celebrations of the national song.”
Initiating a discussion on Vande Mataram in the state Assembly on the second day of the Winter Session, Mr. Adityanath said, “When the occasion of the centenary of Vande Mataram came, the same Congress from whose platform Vande Mataram was first sung, imposed the Emergency in the country in 1975 and throttled the Constitution.”
The Chief Minister said the respect for Vande Mataram is not merely an emotional expression. “It also instils in all of us a sense of our national duties towards constitutional values,” he said.
Calling the song a "symbol of the nation’s soul, struggle and resolve", Mr. Adityanath said, “When Vande Mataram was celebrating its silver jubilee, the country was still under British rule.”
He said the song was composed at a time when the British government, rattled after the First War of Independence, had reached the peak of repression and atrocities, and Indians were being subjected to severe hardships.
At that time, the Congress served as a platform to advance the freedom struggle, the Leader of the House said. “In 1896, Rabindranath Tagore lent his voice to Vande Mataram for the first time at a Congress session, and it became a mantra for the entire nation,” he said.
However, Mr. Adityanath said, “When the centenary of Vande Mataram arrived, the same Congress imposed the Emergency and strangled the Constitution.”
He alleged that the Congress pursued a policy of appeasement and added that as long as Mohammad Ali Jinnah was in the Congress, Vande Mataram was not a decisive point of contention.
"As soon as Jinnah left the Congress, he made it a tool of the Muslim League and deliberately gave the song a communal colour. The song remained the same, but the agenda changed," the Chief Minister said.
"On October 15, 1937, from this very Lucknow, Muhammad Ali Jinnah raised a slogan against Vande Mataram, and at that time, Pandit Nehru was the Congress president. On October 20, 1937, Nehru wrote a letter to Subhas Chandra Bose, saying that its background was making Muslims uncomfortable," he added.
He added that the country is progressing in the direction of fulfilling the dream of Vande Mataram’s immortal composer Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay.
Mr. Adityanath said that as part of a series of programmes launched from New Delhi to mark 150 years of Vande Mataram under the guidance of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, “possibly the Uttar Pradesh Assembly is the first legislature where such a detailed discussion on the national song is taking place”.

title: Leadership issue: CM leaves it to Rahul and high command
summary: Chief Minister Siddaramaiah on Monday addressed speculations on the change of leadership in the State by claiming that Congress leader Rahul Gandhi and the party high command would have to ultimately decide on the matter.
content:
Chief Minister Siddaramaiah on Monday addressed speculations on the change of leadership in the State by claiming that Congress leader Rahul Gandhi and the party high command would have to ultimately decide on the matter.
When his attention was drawn to All India Congress Committee (AICC) president Mallikarjun Kharge’s reported statement that the confusion over leadership change was on account of some local leaders, Mr. Siddaramaiah said he had already spoken to the high command and they had said that they would take a decision.
“Everybody will abide by whatever decision the high command takes,” he said while speaking to reporters in Mysuru on Monday.
Reacting to Mr. Kharge’s statement that no one was bigger than the party, the Chief Minister said it was a fact that everyone must accept.
He criticised the media for repeatedly raising the issue. “What is the need to ask so many questions? After I have already made a statement in the Assembly, there is no need to discuss it again,” he said.
Responding to a question on former Minister K.N. Rajanna meeting Deputy Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar on Sunday, Mr. Siddaramaiah said there was nothing improper about the meeting. “Mr. Shivakumar is the [State] party president; what is wrong in meeting him?” he asked.
On reports that the Deputy Chief Minister had said he himself appointed Mr. Rajanna as Apex Bank president, the Chief Minister said it was immaterial who did it.
“S.M. Krishna was the Chief Minister at the time and the government took the decision. Such a question does not arise,” he said.

title: Schoolchildren’s flash mob brings Mysuru’s heritage alive
summary: Schoolchildren's flash mob and Heritage Treasure Hunt celebrate Mysuru's rich cultural legacy.
content:
Schoolchildren staged a heritage-themed flash mob outside the Mysuru Palace on Sunday morning, showcasing the city’s rich cultural legacy and captivating passers-by.
For nearly half an hour, 170 students of Purna Chetana School, Mysuru, transported the audience into the past through 14 songs rooted in history, folk traditions and patriotism. Their synchronised movements and expressive, enthusiastic performances transformed the quiet morning into a celebration of Mysuru’s timeless heritage.
Following the flash mob, the Mysuru Heritage Treasure Hunt, based on the city’s history and traditions, was flagged off. Inaugurating the event, noted orthopaedic surgeon T.N. Balakrishna Gowda said protecting Mysuru’s heritage is a collective responsibility.
“The uniqueness of Mysuru lies in its history and heritage. This legacy, which has flourished for centuries, must be carefully preserved and passed on to future generations,” he said.
On the occasion, he announced free medical check-ups worth ₹5,000 for the winners at BKG Avanth Hospital here.
Pulmonologist Lakshmi Narasimhan R. also spoke.
At the start of the event, every participating team was provided with a special treasure kit containing 10 clues. Participants were challenged to identify and reach major heritage landmarks of the city, including Cheluvamba Mansion, the Railway Station, ORI, Crawford Hall, the old Deputy Commissioner’s Office and the Town Hall, among others.
Completing the challenge in 1 hour and 18 minutes, Hrudya, a Class 7 student of Purna Chetana School, along with her father, Bhuvaneshwar, won the first prize. Another Class 7 student of the same school, Arohi Singh, along with her father, Santosh Kumar Singh, secured the second prize. Ritvi, a Class 5 student of Vasavi Cultural School, K.R. Nagar, along with Tejesh Gowda, won the third prize. Cash prizes of ₹10,000, ₹7,500 and ₹5,000, along with trophies, were awarded to the winners. School CEO Darshan Raj, CAO Madhurya Ramaswamy, Secretary Dr. Rajini, Trustee Praveen, and others were present.

title: CRDA clears ₹2,015 crore worth projects for Amaravati
summary: CRDA approves ₹2,015 crore for key projects in Amaravati, including layouts, a flood pumping station, and a quantum computing centre.
content:
The 56th meeting of the Capital Region Development Authority was held at the Secretariat on Monday under the chairmanship of Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu, during which projects worth ₹1,358 crore were sanctioned for the development of layouts in the Land Pooling Scheme LPS-8 zone. The authority also approved ₹444 crore for setting up a flood pumping station with a capacity of 8,400 cusecs, ₹109 crore as additional funds for providing facilities in the residential quarters being constructed for All India Services officers, and nearly ₹104 crore for establishing a Quantum Computing Research Centre in Amaravati.
The CRDA further decided to constitute a high-level committee to ascertain the nature of 202 acres of land given by farmers, to determine whether they are jareebu (fertile or irrigated) or metta (dry). It also allotted 23 acres at Sakhamuru village for the construction of a building for the AYUSH Ministry and six acres in Thullur for hotels and a convention centre.
Addressing the meeting, Mr. Naidu directed officials to identify suitable land for establishing a modern cultural centre in the capital region and to complete the Amaravati Quantum Computing Centre within the stipulated time. He instructed that infrastructure in the LPS layouts be created without delay and that issues faced by farmers be resolved expeditiously.
Emphasising planned urban development, the Chief Minister said special focus should be laid on increasing greenery in Amaravati, particularly along the Krishna riverfront, to enhance the city’s aesthetic appeal. Parks should be developed across the capital region, he said, stressing the need for international-standard hotels to cater to visitors.
Municipal Administration and Urban Development Minister P. Narayana, Chief Secretary K. Vijayanand, Special Chief Secretary M.T. Krishna Babu, Principal Secretary S. Suresh Kumar, CRDA Commissioner K. Kanna Babu and Amaravati Development Corporation CMD D. Lakshmiparthasarathy Bhasker were among those present.

title: Eshwarappa urges Governor not to give assent to hate speech Bill
summary: Former Deputy Chief Minister K.S. Eshwarappa has urged the Governor not to give assent to the Bill on hate speech, passed by both the Houses of the State legislature.
content:
Former Deputy Chief Minister K.S. Eshwarappa has urged the Governor not to give assent to the Bill on hate speech, passed by both the Houses of the State legislature.
At a press conference here on Monday, December 22, he said the Bill introduced by the Congress government would take away the rights of the common people.
Its implications would be far more severe than the promulgation of Emergency. “The Congress, earlier, had denied the right to expression by declaring Emergency and put many national leaders behind bars. The Congress is trying to convert the entire State into a prison,” he alleged.
He alleged that the State government brought in the Bill only with the objective of targeting pro-Hindu leaders and organisations. “We will fight against the Bill,” he said.
Further, he cautioned that in future after the Congress was defeated, its workers might face jail term because of the law they brought in.

title: Enhancing knowledge on pest resistance need of the hour in sericulture, says expert
summary: Dr. K. Srinivasulu emphasizes pest resistance and technology transfer for sustainable sericulture at a national workshop in Tirupati.
content:
A.P. Director of Horticulture and Sericulture Dr. K. Srinivasulu on Monday (December 22, 2025) highlighted the importance of enhancing knowledge on pest resistance and climate resilience in the field of sericulture.
He was addressing the students and faculty members as the chief guest during national workshop on 'Transfer of technologies for sustainable Sericulture' at Sri Padmavati Mahila Visvavidyalayam in Tirupati on Monday. Mr. Srinivasulu also said that bridging the gap between research, teaching, and sericulture farming is a necessity.
The two-day workshop was aimed at bringing awareness among farmers, students, and other stakeholders and to facilitate the effective dissemination of proven technologies, eco-friendly practices and digital innovations to enhance productivity, profitability, and environmental sustainability.
On this occasion, organising secretary Prof. N. Vijaya Kumari, Head, Department of Biosciences and Sericulture, presented the objectives of the workshop and spoke about the importance of technology transfer in sericulture.
Vice-Chancellor of SPMVV Prof. V. Uma addressed the gathering and noted the importance of technology transfer in the areas of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning, and introduction of nanotechnology in sericulture research.

title: Sarvesh Singh appointed as Telangana Life Sciences Director & CEO
summary: Sarvesh Singh appointed as Telangana Life Sciences Director and CEO to enhance the state's biotech ecosystem and innovation.
content:
The State government has appointed Sarvesh Singh as the Telangana Life Sciences Director and CEO.
Congratulating Mr. Singh, IT and Industries Minister D. Sridhar Babu urged him to utilise his 22 years of experience in the pharma and Life Sciences sectors to build a strong ecosystem in the State. Mr. Singh called on the Minister at the Secretariat on Monday after assuming charge.
Telangana, which holds a leading position in the country in the Life Sciences and biotechnology sectors, is moving ahead with even greater speed in innovation. One-third of the vaccines supplied to the world are exported from Telangana. Hyderabad has emerged as the global vaccine capital and Telangana ranks number one in the country in pharmaceutical exports, Mr. Sridhar Babu said.
By expanding Genome Valley and strengthening infrastructure, the State government is opening doors for the establishment of new projects in the Life Sciences sector, the Minister’s office said in a release.

title: Tiger caught in Kumbalathamon of Pathanamthitta
summary: Wildlife menace has been severe in the Kumbalathamon-Olikallu region
content:
An adult tiger that had repeatedly strayed into human settlements and attacked domestic animals in the Kumbalathamon area was trapped by the Forest department on Monday.
The tiger, estimated to be around eight years old, was reported to have impaired vision in one eye and was found to be in a weakened condition. It was finally captured in a cage installed along the forest boundary.
According to forest officials, the animal had been active in the region for nearly two months. Following reports of it frequently attacking domestic animals, Forest department had installed camera traps, which confirmed the presence of the straying tiger.
The animal was caught using the carcass of a goat it had killed the other day as bait. ”The animal will be subjected to a medical examinaion, following which it will be released deep inside he Periyar Tiger Reserve,” confirmed an official.
When the tiger returned to feed on it, it was caught. Earlier last month, the animal had been spotted near a house at Kumbalathamon, where it attacked a pet dog, killing it and consuming half of the carcass before retreating into the forest
The tiger’s presence had spread fear among residents living along the forest fringes, with many reluctant to venture out even during daylight hours. In October, the animal had attacked a buffalo grazing in fields close to human habitation. After confirming the tiger’s presence, the Forest department set up the cage on October 28. Although buffalo remains were initially placed as bait, the tiger had managed to evade capture until now.
Wildlife menace has been severe in the Kumbalathamon-Olikallu region, with residents complaining of wild boars frequenting the area day and night, posing a serious threat to agriculture and human safety. Rubber tapping in the early morning hours has also become difficult due to the fear of wildlife attacks. Residents say monkeys and giant squirrels too have been causing extensive damage to crops.

title: Nadda accuses Congress of facilitating Jhiram Valley Maoist attack
summary: Nadda accuses Congress of collusion in the Jhiram Valley Maoist attack, sparking political controversy in Chhattisgarh.
content:
Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)president J.P. Nadda on Monday (December 22, 2025) alleged that someCongressinsiders facilitated the 2013 Jhiram Ghati Maoist attack in Chhattisgarh, which led to the killing of State Congress leaders.
Thirty-two people, including senior Congress leaders Vidya Charan Shukla, Mahendra Karma and Nand Kumar Patel, had been killed while many sustained injuries in the Jhiram Valley attack on May 25, 2013.
“I was the [BJP] in-charge of Chhattisgarh [back then]. I saw the Jheeram Valley incident. Today, I say this with great responsibility, that no one else was providing information and inside details about the Jhiram Valley incident. People who were among them were involved in getting their own people killed, and they were in contact with Naxalites,” Mr. Nadda alleged while addressing the ‘Janadesh Parab’ (people’s mandate festival) at Janjgir Champa.
The event was held to mark the completion of two years of the Vishnu Deo Sai-led BJP government in Chhattisgarh.
The BJP president further said that a decisive action was taken against Maoism under the double-engine government at the Centre and the State, adding Maoism had now been confined to a limited number of villages and districts in the State.
“Nearly 2,500 Naxalites have surrendered in the last two years, 1,853 have been arrested, and top leaders such as Hidma and Basavaraju neutralised,” he said.
Responding to Nadda’s statement, Senior Congress leader and former Chhattisgarh Chief Minister Bhupesh Baghel called the claim a lie and an insult to those who lost their lives in that attack.
“First of all, security agencies, including the NIA, should interrogate J.P. Nadda and demand proof of his claims. J.P. Nadda! We lost our leaders in the Naxalite attack. You are insulting their martyrdom by accusing them of collusion,” a part of his post on X read.
He accused the BJP of attempting to stall the investigations by filing petitions in court when the Congress Government was in power in the State, at a time when the authorities were trying to find out those behind the attack.”

title: Scientists urged to prioritise research in energy storage solutions
summary: Union Minister Pralhad Joshi urges scientists to focus on energy storage research to enhance India's clean energy transition.
content:
Union Minister for Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution and New and Renewable Energy Pralhad Joshi has called upon the scientific community to prioritise research in energy storage solutions and grid stability technologies, particularly for renewable energy sources, to support India’s ambitious clean energy transition.
He was inaugurating a three-day 44th Annual National Conference of the Indian Council of Chemists (ICC) hosted by the School of Advanced Sciences, KLE Technological University (KLETU) on the B.V. Bhoomaraddi campus in Hubballi on Monday.
Addressing a gathering, Mr. Joshi also highlighted India’s vision to emerge as a global manufacturing powerhouse under the Atmanirbhar Bharat initiative, which, he said, is bolstered by unprecedented infrastructure development, including comprehensive railway electrification projects.
Mr. Joshi paid rich tributes to Acharya Prafulla Chandra Ray, revered as the Father of Indian Chemistry, for his pivotal role in nation-building through scientific innovation and institution development.
He commended the Indian scientific fraternity for their extraordinary contributions during the COVID-19 pandemic, emphasizing that science and innovation were instrumental in navigating the global health crisis.
The Minister said that India has attained self-reliance in power generation well ahead of schedule and highlighted its position as one of the world’s fastest-growing economies.
Delivering the keynote address, president of the Indian National Science Academy Ashutosh Sharma outlined the pressing need for chemistry research to align with Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).
He raised an alarm over the escalating environmental crisis posed by microplastics and advocated for innovative bioremediation strategies to mitigate this threat.
Secretary of ICC Rajesh Dhakarey stressed the increasing relevance of multidisciplinary research approaches to tackle complex societal and technological challenges in the modern era.
On the occasion, Director of Research, School of Advanced Sciences, KLETU Tejraj Aminabhavi was honoured with the Lifetime Achievement Award in recognition of his pioneering contributions to polymer science.
An ACS journal cover page dedicated in his honour was unveiled during the ceremony.
In his address, Prof. Aminabhavi traced the evolutionary journey of polymer science and its profound global impact across industries, inspiring young researchers to pursue excellence and make meaningful contributions to science and society.
Presiding over the inaugural ceremony, Pro-Chancellor of KLETU Ashok Shettar emphasised the indispensable role of scientific research in driving societal development. Science and technology must advance in tandem to propel the nation’s holistic progress, he added.
Vice-Chancellor of KLETU Prakash Tewari, treasurer of ICC Manoj Kumar Rawat, conference convenor Nagaraj P. Shetti and others were present.
The national conclave has drawn over 400 eminent scientists, academicians, researchers, industry professionals and students from across India.

title: Mango farmers stage protest demanding payment of dues from pulp industries
summary: Mango farmers in Chittoor protest for overdue payments from pulp industries, demanding fair compensation and government support for their needs.
content:
A protest by mango farmers from Chittoor and Tirupati districts, demanding payment of long-pending dues from pulp processing industries, ended on a positive note on Monday. District Collector Sumit Kumar assured the agitating farmers of fresh negotiations with pulp unit operators to resolve the issue.
More than 300 mango farmers participated in the “Chalo Collectorate” programme, pressing for immediate clearance of pending payments. Protest organisers representing the District Mango Farmers’ Association deplored that several pulp industries had failed to clear dues for mango supplies made over the past seven months, despite directives from the government.
“The delay was unjust and exploitative, especially as farmers we are preparing for the upcoming season. The farmers urgently required capital for pruning, fertilisers and other operations for the ensuing season,” said CPI(M) district secretary Vada Gangaraju.
The protestors asked whether the government would side with the “40 errant industries or 40,000 mango farmers,” and demanded immediate release of all pending amounts, noting that some industries had paid only ₹2-₹5 per kg so far, as against the government’s assurance of ₹8.
Their demands included early commencement of pulp units by May 2026, government-run urban outlets for the sales of table varieties, support for cold storage and cottage industries, and linkage of mango cultivation operations with the MGNREGS scheme.
After the protest, a memorandum was submitted to the Collector, who assured the farmers that discussions with pulp industry representatives would be held at the earliest.

title: Student body hits out at University of Mysore over ‘curbs’ on protests
summary: Students protest against University of Mysore's restrictions on protests, claiming it undermines democratic rights and addresses unmet needs.
content:
All India Democratic Students’ Organisation (AIDSO) has claimed that the University of Mysore (UoM) has reportedly resolved to restrict protests by students on its campuses, including Maharaja’s and Yuvaraja’s colleges, which are constituent colleges of the university.
The student body alleged that the decision was taken in a meeting chaired by the Vice-Chancellor and attended by some police officers and university authorities.
“It has also been apparently conveyed that students should not protest over academic demands and should instead submit written memorandums. This decision by the university administration undermines democratic principles and is an attempt to take away the fundamental right of students to protest against any injustice,” a statement from AIDSO read.
“If the university’s decisions become “anti-student”, it becomes the responsibility of students to question them. Branding such questioning as “interference” and attacking students’ rights reflects the irresponsibility of the university administration. Whether students should submit memorandums or organise protests to voice their concerns is a decision that must rest with the students themselves. Moreover, involving the police in framing university regulations is not only anti-democratic but also contrary to the values upon which Manasagangothri has been established,” said Nithin, district secretary, AIDSO.
In the statement, AIDSO also claimed that there is a shortage of toilets, drinking water facilities, and lecturers at Maharaja’s and Yuvaraja’s colleges. Similarly, in Manasagangothri, students are facing hostel-related issues and a lack of basic amenities. A memorandum highlighting these issues was submitted three months ago, yet none of the problems have been addressed so far. “Instead of ensuring the students’ welfare, the university administration is attempting to suppress students’ movements by imposing restrictions on protests. This is condemnable,” he stated.
The AIDSO Mysuru district committee demanded immediate withdrawal of the restrictions from all UoM campuses.

title: Second phase of magisterial inquiry into Maredumilli encounters on December 27
summary: Second phase of magisterial inquiry into Maredumilli encounters on December 27
content:
Rampachodavaram Sub-Collector Subham Nokwal on Monday issued a fresh notification for separate magisterial inquiries to be conducted on December 27 into two encounters in which 13 Maoists, including commander Madvi Hidma, were killed. The encounters took place in the Maredumilli Agency area of Alluri Sitharama Raju district on November 18 and 19.
The first phase of the magisterial inquiry into the two incidents was held at the Sub-Collector’s office in Rampachodavaram on December 15 and 16.
Speaking toThe Hinduover the phone on Monday, Mr. Subham Nokwal said the second phase of the inquiry was being conducted to provide an opportunity to all stakeholders involved in the encounters, as well as members of the public, to submit statements and information related to the incidents.
On permitting civil society representatives to carry out fact-finding, Mr. Nokwal said a Hyderabad-based advocate had been allowed to visit the sites of the two encounters. He added that the Alluri Sitharama Raju district police had been directed to deploy police personnel to accompany the advocate during the visit.

title: Dhinkaran urges T.N. government to again hold talks with its employees
summary: Dhinkaran calls on T.N. government to resume talks with employees amid impending indefinite strike over unresolved issues.
content:
The Amma Makkal Munnetra Kazhagam (AMMK) general secretary T.T.V. Dhinakaran on Monday urged the State government to hold talks with representatives of the government staff and teachers again for thrashing out legitimate issues concerning them.
In a post, he referred to the announcement of an indefinite strike by the staff from January 6 following, what he called, the failure of negotiations between the two sides.
Meanwhile, in a statement, All India Anna Dravida Munnetra Workers’ Rights Retrieval Kazhagam coordinator O. Panneerselvam urged the Central government to take back its decision to hike the railway fare. He recalled that in July, a hike was carried out and despite his appeal, the Union government had not announced the withdrawal.

title: Alert station master rescues passenger at Pandavapura railway station
summary: Alert station master Abhijit Singh saves a passenger at Pandavapura railway station, showcasing remarkable courage and quick thinking.
content:
An alert station master at Pandavapura railway station in Mysuru division rushed to the rescue of a 55-year-old passenger who slipped while attempting to board the moving train at the station recently.
A press statement issued by Mysuru Division of South Western Railways noted that when Shivaraju Katteri of Pandavapura taluk fell into a “life-threatening” situation while boarding the moving train No. 16219 on December 13, station master Abhijit Singh displayed “exemplary alertness and presence of mind” by saving Mr. Katteri’s life.
Mr. Singh, through “swift and courageous action”, rescued the passenger and prevented a serious mishap, the statement read, adding that the passenger was subsequently provided assistance and is safe.
General manager Mukul Saran Mathur has commended Mr. Singh.

title: Mob lynching: govt. promises justice, protection for victim’s family
summary: Government vows justice and protection for mob lynching victim's family, ensuring a thorough investigation and support measures.
content:
Revenue Minister K. Rajan on Monday assured that the State government would provide all possible protection and support to the family of Ram Narayan Baghel, migrant worker from Chhattisgarh, who was killed in a mob attack in Walayar.
The assurance came after a discussion with the victim’s family and representatives of an action council, held in the presence of District Collector Arjun Pandian and senior revenue officials here.
Addressing the media after the talks, the Minister described the incident as deeply shameful and said the government viewed Ram Narayan’s death with utmost seriousness. “This is an incident that has brought disrepute even beyond Kerala. The government is treating both the crime and the investigation with total seriousness,” he said.
The Minister said a special investigation team (SIT) has been constituted in accordance with the Supreme Court guidelines in the Tehseen Poonawalla case. Five persons had already been arrested, and the SIT would determine whether the crime involved caste-based or racial abuse.
“There will be no compromise in the investigation. Not a single person involved will be spared,” he said, adding that the probe would be thorough and uncompromising.
Mr. Rajan said the case was being handled by invoking Section 103(2) and other relevant provisions, including those relating to attacks on SC/ST communities, in line with Supreme Court directives. He added that the government had taken note of the action council’s demand for a sustained and rigorous investigation.
Referring to the Supreme Court directives issued on crimes against vulnerable communities, the Minister said the Chief Secretary had been entrusted with overseeing the implementation of the guidelines. He reiterated that the government viewed inter-State workers as “guest workers” and was committed to extending them the same protection and welfare measures available to local workers.
The Minister said the Cabinet would seriously consider providing financial assistance from the Chief Minister’s Distress Relief Fund. “The demand for compensation of not less than ₹10 lakh has been noted with due seriousness and will be placed before the Cabinet to ensure appropriate assistance,” he said.
He said the District Collector had been directed to take charge of arrangements, including bearing full expenses for transporting the body to the victim’s native place.

title: Watch: Kerala lynching triggers political outrage over Dalit migrant worker killing
summary: The lynching of Dalit migrant labourer Ram Narayan Bhagal in Kerala’s Palakkad district has triggered strong reactions from political leaders. The Chief Minister, Opposition leaders and Left parties condemned the killing, calling it a blot on Kerala’s humanist legacy. Allegations of hate politics and demands for accountability have intensified following the incident.
content: Report: G Anand

title: Sharnbasva University students secure fourth place in CII national competition
summary: Sharnbasva University students achieve fourth place in a national CII competition, showcasing excellence in higher education analysis.
content:
Students of the Faculty of Business Studies, Sharnbasva University, Kalaburagi, secured the fourth place in a national-level competition organised by the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) for institutions of higher education.
The competition, held on the theme, “Building India’s Higher Education Ecosystem for Global Excellence by 2035”, saw the participation of over 60 universities and centres of higher education from across the country.
The contest was conducted in four rounds.
In the first round, participating teams submitted case studies that were evaluated by a panel of experts.
Based on this assessment, 11 universities and institutions were shortlisted.
These teams then made presentations, following which five universities were selected for the final round at New Delhi on December 17.
The finalists included Symbiosis International University, Pune; Adani University, Ahmedabad; Amity International University, Delhi; Sharnbasva University, Kalaburagi, and Siva Sivani Institute of Management, Hyderabad.
The Sharnbasva University team comprising Aishwarya Biradar, Keerthi Joshi and Humera Fatima, all first-year MBA students, made a presentation before an expert panel and earned appreciation for their analysis. The team secured the fourth place in the competition.

title: 23.16% of the proposals at the global Kerala summit turns into actual investment: Minister
summary: Kerala has already recorded the highest conversion rate in the country in terms of conversion of Expression of Interests into investments with 23.16% of the investment proposals at the Invest Kerala Global Summit in February this year evolving into actual investments, Industries Minister P.Rajeeve said in a statement on Monday.
content:
Kerala has already recorded the highest conversion rate in the country in terms of conversion of Expression of Interests into investments with 23.16% of the investment proposals at the Invest Kerala Global Summit in February this year evolving into actual investments, Industries Minister P.Rajeeve said in a statement on Monday. In the case of projects for which land has been allotted, the conversion rate is 37%.
A total of 449 EOIs woth ₹1.81 lakh crore were signed at IKGS. Around five lakh job opportunities were offered through these projects. Most of the EOIs were signed in sectors such as tourism, food processing, electronic components manufacturing, IT/IT-based industries, wood-based industries, rubber products manufacturing, pharmaceuticals, healthcare, Ayurveda and wellness. Of these, construction of 104 investment projects has begun. Investment of ₹35,463.07 crore and 50,483 jobs are being created in the State through projects that have already started construction, he said.
Mr.Rajeeve said that the government focused its immediate attention on converting the expressions of interest and investment promises into actual investments. For this, the expressions of interest were classified on the basis of investment value. Agencies such as Kerala State Industrial Development Corporation (KSIDC), Directorate of Industries and Commerce and Kerala Industrial Infrastructure Development Corporation (KINFRA) were responsible for implementing these. The Industries Department set up special mechanisms to provide the necessary facilities including various permissions quickly. A monitoring system was also set up to review the project at various levels and at regular intervals. Expressions of interest worth up to ₹100 crore were monitored through the Directorate of Industries and Commerce. KSIDC acts as the nodal agency for expressions of interest worth ₹100 crore and above. Investments in industrial parks and other places are also monitored under the leadership of KINFRA.
Italian animation giant Dynimated and logistics company Avigna have completed their construction and started operations. Adani Logistics Park, Life Science Company under Krishna Ella’s Bharat Biotech, Systrome, S.F.O Technologies, Gasha Steels T.M.T Plant, K.G.A International, Krishna Institute of Medical Sciences, Aqoza Technologies, Vinvish Technologies, W.G.H. Hotels, Jacob & Richard are also included in the companies that started construction work.

title: HDK questions efficiency of CM over non-payment of Gruha Lakshmi amount
summary: H.D. Kumaraswamy criticizes CM Siddaramaiah for delays in Gruha Lakshmi payments.
content:
Union Minister for Heavy Industries and Steel H.D. Kumaraswamy has questioned the efficiency of Chief Minister Siddaramaiah, citing the non-payment of two months’ Gruha Lakshmi scheme benefits to women in the State.
In an interaction with the media at Balehonnur in N.R. Pura taluk of Chikkamagaluru on Monday, Mr. Kumaraswamy questioned where did the ₹5,000 crore, meant for the beneficiaries of Gruha Lakshmi, go if it was not transferred to beneficiaries. “The money should have been transferred in February and March. The issue came to light only now, when we are entering 2026. Did the government hold anybody responsible for the non-payment?” he questioned.
On the issue of change in leadership of the Congress government in the State, Mr. Kumaraswamy said the Congress party had been entertaining people of the State every day on this issue. “The party has got 136 MLAs. We are not interested in who will become the Chief Minister. I am bothered about what development the incumbent government achieved,” he said.
Referring to the State government’s expenditure of ₹47 crore for the Chief Minister’s helicopter trips, Mr. Kumaraswamy said he too could have travelled to Chikkamagaluru by helicopter, given his health. However, he chose to travel by road. “The Chief Minister  is taking a helicopter even for short distances. From Bengaluru to Malavalli, the travel time is hardly one hour. The Chief Minister flew by the helicopter. Again, from Mysuru to Chamarajanagar, the travel by road takes hardly half an hour, but the Chief Minister took the helicopter,” he commented.

title: 30 kW EV fast-charging unit launched at Chamundeshwari Electricity Supply Corporation Limited office
summary: CESC launches upgraded 30 kW EV fast-charging unit in Mysuru, promoting renewable energy and eco-friendly commuting initiatives.
content:
In a significant step towards promoting renewable energy and encouraging eco-friendly commuting, Chamundeshwari Electricity Supply Corporation Limited (CESC) on December 22 inaugurated an upgraded, state-of-the-art 30 kW EV fast-charging facility at its office premises.
The facility was inaugurated on the CESC office premises in Vijayanagar by Ramesh Bandisidde Gowda, CESC chairman and MLA, in the presence of K.M. Munigopal Raju, managing director.
Speaking on the occasion, Mr. Gowda said that the use of electric vehicles was steadily increasing and that CESC is encouraging their adoption. “This initiative will help reduce air pollution, lower dependence on imported fuel and promote the use of green energy,” he said.
The existing EV charging unit at the CESC office has been upgraded to a 30 kW fast-charging facility, enabling two cars to be charged simultaneously. With fast-charging technology, a vehicle can be fully charged in about 40 to 45 minutes.
The new EV charging unit has been set up in collaboration with Zion Electric, and users can access the charging hub through the Zion app. At present, the facility has been made available on a pilot basis for EVs used by the CESC office. Based on an assessment of its performance, maintenance and user experience, the corporation will decide on extending the service for public use in the future.
“CESC is keen to promote the use of renewable energy. With the launch of the EV fast-charging hub, we plan to establish more EV charging centres in Mysuru city and other areas under CESC’s jurisdiction to encourage the use of electric vehicles in the future,” Mr. Raju explained.
D.J. Divakar, CESC technical director, Sharanaamma S. Jangin, chief general manager (technical), G. Renuka, chief financial officer, general managers N.R. Tasneem Tabassum and R. Ramaswamy, and other officials were present.

title: FIR registered against supplier of low-quality tur dal
summary: FIR filed against supplier for providing low-quality, pest-infested tur dal to schools, prompting disciplinary action recommendation for Education Officer.
content:
Chief Executive Officer of the Yadgir Zilla Panchayat Lavish Ordia has recommended to the government taking disciplinary action against the Education Officer, Akshara Dasoha, on the charge of lapse in ensuring supply of good quality tur dal to government-run schools for mid-day meals.
In a release here on Monday, Mr. Ordia said that the during a surprise inspection, tur dal being supplied to schools was found to be of low quality, infested with pests and was also not of the required quantity.
Lab reports of samples have confirmed that the tur dal was of low quality and unsafe for consumption under the FSSAI guidelines.
Following a report, an FIR has been registered against the supplier, Lalit Industries of Kalaburagi, for supplying low-quality tur dal, he said in the release.

title: Pink Line prototype metro train moved to Kothanur depot
summary: Bengaluru's Pink Line prototype metro train successfully transported to Kothanur depot for inspection and testing ahead of operations.
content:
The six-coach prototype train for Bengaluru Metro’s much-awaited Pink Line was moved overnight from the BEML Rail Complex at New Thippasandra to the Kothanur depot on Monday, officials said.
The train set covered a distance of nearly 20 km, with the transportation carried out during night hours as the movement of heavy trailers was permitted only at night in the city limits.
According to officials of the Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Limited (BMRCL), the prototype train, recently rolled out by BEML Ltd., was dismantled and transported in parts on trailers before being reassembled at the depot.
Following its arrival at Kothanur, the BMRCL will begin inspection bay checks and conduct mainline trials to assess the performance and safety of the rolling stock.
“The entire exercise was conducted at night to comply with traffic regulations. After reassembly at the depot, the train will undergo a detailed inspection and testing process,” an official toldThe Hindu.
The BEML unveiled the prototype of the new driverless metro train on December 11, 2025. The train sets have been designed for Namma Metro’s Phase-2 corridors, including Phase 2A and Phase 2B. The Pink Line, one of the most anticipated additions to Bengaluru’s metro network, will connect Kalena Agrahara in south Bengaluru to Nagawara in the north.
After the preliminary checks are completed, the BMRCL will initiate the process of securing mandatory statutory clearances from the Ministry of Railways, the Research Designs and Standards Organisation, and the Commissioner of Metro Railway Safety.
The Officials said that the rolling stock would undergo a series of standard tests before being cleared for passenger operations.
The Pink Line corridor is planned to be commissioned in two phases by the end of 2026, significantly enhancing north-south connectivity of the city.

title: Health, education and jobs remain core priorities of Telangana government: Mallu Bhatti Vikramarka
summary: Telangana's Deputy Chief Minister emphasizes health, education, and jobs as top priorities for improving citizens' well-being and access to services.
content:
Deputy Chief Minister Mallu Bhatti Vikramarka on Monday (December 22) said that health, education and employment remain the central priorities of the government, as it focuses on addressing the everyday concerns of ordinary citizens.
Speaking at the launch of medical services by Vijaya Medical Centre, Mr. Vikramarka said the government was moving forward with a clear objective of ensuring dignity and well-being for all citizens. Welcoming the decision to establish diagnostic centres in second-tier cities and rural areas, the Deputy Chief Minister urged the Centre to organise free medical camps in rural regions and offer comprehensive diagnostic tests. He assured that the State government would extend all necessary support to such initiatives.
Stressing the need to expand quality diagnostic facilities beyond Hyderabad, Mr. Vikramarka said diagnostics play a vital role between health and disease, and between prevention and treatment. With advanced diagnostic services reaching districts such as Warangal, Karimnagar, Khammam and Nizamabad, he said that both the financial and mental burden on people would be significantly reduced. Distance in healthcare, he added, is measured not just in kilometres but in anxiety, delays and costs.

title: Chaitanya Baghel received ₹200-250 crore from liquor scam: ACB chargesheet
summary: Chaitanya Baghel allegedly received ₹200-250 crore from a liquor scam, according to the ACB's latest chargesheet.
content:
Chaitanya Baghel, son of senior Congress leader Bhupesh Baghel, received ₹200-250 crore generated through the alleged liquor scam in Chhattisgarh, the State’s Anti Corruption Bureau-Economic Offences Wing (ACB-EOW) has said in a chargesheet filed on Monday (December 22, 2025).
Earlier, the Directorate of Enforcement (ED), which is probing the money laundering linked to the alleged liquor scam, had said that Mr. Chaitanya Baghel personally handled around ₹1,000 crore generated from the alleged scam.
“In addition to managing the scam money at higher levels, evidence has been found of him (Chaitanya Baghel) receiving a share of approximately ₹200 to ₹250 crore,” the ACB-EOW stated in a press note, attributing this to the eighth and latest chargesheet.
Mr. Chaitanya Baghel was responsible for distributing and managing the scam money collected by co-accused Anwar Dhebar’s team to higher levels through his trusted associates, according to the investigators. The release stated that Mr. Chaitanya Baghel received his share of the money from various firms of Trilok Singh Dhillon, transferred it through banking channels to his family firms, and used it for under-construction real estate projects. He received and invested large sums of the scam money through his family friends and associates, also through banking channels, it is also alleged.
The alleged scam surfaced during Mr. Bhupesh Baghel’s tenure as Chhattisgarh’s Chief Minister and it purportedly caused loss to the exchequer. The ACB-EOW also increased the total face value of the alleged scam, according to Monday’s press statement.
“As of now, the investigation has estimated the total amount of the excise scam to be approximately ₹3,074 crore. However, further investigation suggests that this illegal amount, from all sources, could exceed ₹3,500 crore,” the release said.

title: DIG inaugurates constable training programme in Anantapur
summary: DIG inaugurates a nine-month constable training program in Anantapur, emphasizing discipline, empathy, and law understanding for effective policing.
content:
Deputy Inspector General of Police, Anantapur Range, Dr. Shemushi on Monday (December 22, 2025) inaugurated the nine-month training programme for SCT Police Constables (Civil) at the Police Training College in Anantapur.
A total of 692 trainees belonging to Visakhapatnam, Prakasam, West Godavari, Guntur, Vijayawada City and SPSR Nellore districts are participating in the training.
Addressing the police constables, the DIG said that a constable is the first access point at the ground level and the image of the department largely depends on the police constable. She said constables need to understand the laws like BNS, BNSS, BSA and SLL to discharge their functions.
“The duty of police constable is not only crime prevention, but also maintaining public tranquillity and law and order,” she said, asking the constables to treat all equally above caste, religion, and other lines.
Ms. Shemsuhi Bajpai said that discipline and empathy towards weaker sections should be given utmost important. “To be honest in your job means, saying no to corruption. By doing your duty with utmost sincerely, you will have peace of mind,” she said, adding that the safety and security of people and their property is also the responsibility of a police.
The DIG added that the constables personal behaviour is always under scrutiny. She asked the SCTs to be attentive during training, learn more and also to take care of their health.

title: Parameshwara meets Kharge, says political issues not discussed
summary: Home Minister G. Parameshwara meets AICC president Kharge, denying political discussions amidst speculation over Karnataka leadership changes.
content:
Amidst the tussle for the Chief Minister’s post after the completion of the first half of the five-year term of the Congress government in Karnataka, Home Minister G. Parameshwara on Monday called on AICC president Mallikarjun Kharge at the latter’s residence here.
Though Dr. Parameshwara informed the media that he had not discussed any political issues with Mr. Kharge, the meeting has given rise to various political speculations, including the demand for making the Dalit leader the Chief Minister.
The Home Minister said he had discussed the family issues with the AICC president and endorsed the latter’s view that there was no confusion at the high command level on the issue of leadership change in the government.
Mr. Kharge on Sunday had clarified that the confusion over the leadership issue in the party’s Karnataka unit exists only at the local level and not within the party high command.
Later, Dr. Parameshwara said the Hate Speech and Hate Crimes Prevention Bill, 2025, was not intended to target any specific individual, and he claimed that the Opposition BJP has been unnecessarily politicising it.
Both Houses of the legislature passed the Bill last week. “We have not brought the Bill targeting anyone in particular. This will apply to whoever indulged in hate speech. It has not been introduced with any specific individual in mind. The law must be respected. The Supreme Court has ordered that hate speech should be curbed,” he said.
“We will send the Bill to the Governor. If the Governor seeks clarifications on the Bill, we will provide an explanation,” the Home Minister said.

title: PACS employees urge government to resolve longstanding grievances
summary: PACS employees demand government action on grievances, including pay revisions and service benefits, amidst ongoing hardships.
content:
The Primary Agriculture Cooperative Societies (PACS) Employees Association’s Vizianagaram district honorary president P. Kameswara Rao on Monday urged the government to resolve the longstanding grievances of the staff as they have been facing many hardships for the last two decades due to the absence of promotions, no hikes in salary and other service benefits. The association organised an agitation at the Vizianagaram District Cooperative Central Bank to draw the attention of PACS employees across the State.
Speaking to media, Mr. Kameswara Rao said that more than 6,000 employees were demanding a pay revision commission, enhancement of retirement age up to 62 years on the lines of government staff  and regularisation of services of staff in several districts. He announced that the association would hold a massive protest in Vijayawada on December 29, 2025 and January 5, 2026 to step up pressure on the government to meet their demands. The association’s district president Reddi Satyam and general secretary B. Ramu Naidu, CPI assistant secretary of the district Bugatha Ashok and others were present.
EOM

title: Collector unveils election mascot for the Nilgiris
summary: Nilgiris District Collector unveils election mascot "Neela" to promote voter awareness among youth ahead of the 2026 elections.
content:
The Nilgiris District Collector, Lakshmi Bhavya Tanneeru, on Monday unveiled a mascot - the Nilgiri flycatcher, a species of bird native to the Western Ghats, as part of an awareness initiative aimed at voters in the district.
The district administration said that the mascot, named “Neela” was designed to create awareness among young voters to exercise their franchise during the elections in 2026. The slogan for the mascot was also unveiled “Voice of hills – our vote.” The design was also shown to young, first-time voters at the Government Arts College in Udhagamandalam. An awareness campaign was also held at the college to encourage youngsters to vote in the elections.
The Nilgiris district administration also announced a local holiday on January 7, 2026 on account of Hethai Amman festival, the biggest annual festival of the Badagas. All government offices and educational institutions will remain closed on the day, it said.

title: Ayyappa devotees asked to take ‘Virtual Q Booking’ for entry into Pulmedu forests
summary: Ayyappa devotees must secure 'Virtual Q Booking' for safe entry into Pulmedu forests, following police guidelines for Sabarimala.
content:
Ayyappa devotees proceeding towards Pamba are requested to obtain ‘Virtual Q Booking’ for entry into Pulmedu forests, to avoid congestions and safety risks, said the Kerala police.
In a release issued by the Pathanamthitta district police on Monday, more than 27 lakh devotees visited Sabarimala so far, and the rush is expected to rise for ‘Mandala Puja’ and ‘Makara Jyothi’ darshan. Director General of Police (DGP) Harish Kumar Gupta appealed to the Ayyappa devotees from Andhra Pradesh to follow the instructions of the Pathanamthitta police for a safe journey to Sabarimala.
The Pulmedu forest path covers nearly 16 km. Due to the arduous nature of the paths, elderly devotees, persons with health problems, and children are advised to avoid Nilakkal and Pulmedu routes. Devotees who are in good health condition are requested to take the route through Pulmedu forests. The dense forest and lengthy route lack immediate medical facilities due to huge crowds, the police said.
Entry through Pulmedu forest path via Vandiperiyar Satram is limited to 1,000 devotees, who secured ‘Virtual Q Booking’, per day. These routes are being monitored and entry without valid documentation leads to congestion, and risk for the devotees, as well as the security personnel.
Devotees are also requested not to believe rumours that special passes are being issued for Erumeli traditional forest route. No such passes were provided to the devotees, the police clarified. Pilgrims are requested to obtain ‘Virtual Q or Spot Booking’ at the authorised help desks at Nilakkal, and proceed to Pamba, the police said.
Ayyappa devotees are requested to note and follow the mandatory guidelines of the Kerala police for a safe journey to Sabarimala, Mr. Harish Kumar said.

title: Naidu directs Excise Department to study Haryana’s sub-lease model against belt shops
summary: CM Naidu urges officials to adopt Haryana's model to eliminate belt shops and reform liquor shop procedures in Andhra Pradesh.
content:
Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu on Monday directed the Excise Department to take firm action against belt shops and asked officials to study the sub-lease system followed in Haryana to curb the practice. He also ordered further reforms in the lottery system for allotment of liquor shops, application fee structure, liquor identification system, and other related procedures.
Reviewing the functioning of the department at the Secretariat, Mr. Naidu asked officials to examine the proposal to exempt bars from additional retail excise tax and to accord priority to digital payments wherever feasible.
Officials informed the Chief Minister that the department earned ₹7,041 crore against a target of ₹8,000 crore during the 2024–25 financial year. Liquor sales registered a 4.52% increase between April 1 and December 17, 2025, in FY 2025–26. Digital payments recorded an average growth of 34.9%, with some districts reporting up to 47%.
To curb the sale of spurious liquor, a unique identification number has been assigned to each bottle. Sales of Indian Made Foreign Liquor grew by 19.08%, while beer sales nearly doubled, rising by 95%.
Calling for foolproof implementation of the Hologram Excise Adhesive Labels system, Mr. Naidu said it would help check counterfeiting and tax evasion, thereby safeguarding excise revenue.
Ministers Kollu Ravindra and Kondapalli Srinivas, Principal Secretary (Finance) Peeyush Kumar, and Directors Chamakuri Sridhar (Prohibition & Excise) and Rahul Dev Sarma (Excise Enforcement) were among those present.

title: CPI(M) trails Congress by over 14% votes in Ernakulam
summary: Congress leads CPI(M) by 14% in Ernakulam local elections, securing 6.69 lakh more votes amid diverse party performances.
content:
The Indian National Congress (INC) polled 6.69 lakh votes more than the CPI(M), with a significant vote share difference of 14.02% separating the two parties in the local body elections held in Ernakulam district.
Out of the total 47.77 lakh votes polled across grama panchayats, block panchayats, the district panchayat, municipalities, and Kochi Corporation, the INC secured 17.83 lakh votes (37.34%), compared to 11.14 lakh votes (23.32%) for the CPI(M). The CPI, the second major constituent of the Left Democratic Front (LDF), polled only 2.50 lakh votes (5.25%), while the Indian Union Muslim League (IUML), a key constituent of the United Democratic Front (UDF), secured 1.28 lakh votes (2.69%).
Interestingly, both these parties together polled fewer votes than independents, who managed 4.25 lakh votes (8.91%). The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) secured 5.22 lakh votes (10.94%), while Twenty20, the Kitex Group-backed political outfit, polled 1.91 lakh votes (4.02%). The Bharath Dharma Jana Sena (BDJS), a major ally of the BJP-led National Democratic Alliance (NDA), managed just 17,108 votes (0.36%), while the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) polled even less, at 2,324 votes (0.05%).
The Revolutionary Socialist Party bagged 27,408 votes (0.57%), Janata Dal (Secular) received 694 votes (0.15%), Nationalist Congress Party (Sharadchandra Pawar) secured 11,135 votes (0.23%), Nationalist Congress Party (NCP) polled 248 votes (0.01%), Janadhipathya Kerala Congress 2,598 votes (0.05%), Rashtriya Janata Dal 406 votes (0.01%), Communist Marxist Party 898 votes (0.02%), and Congress (Secular) 16,755 votes (0.35%).
Among the Kerala Congress factions, the Kerala Congress polled 76,919 votes (1.61%), the Kerala Congress (B) 16,862 votes (0.35%), the Kerala Congress (Jacob) 52,252 votes (1.09%), and the Kerala Congress (M) 63,208 votes (1.32%). The Socialist Democratic Party of India polled 37,564 votes (0.79%), Welfare Party of India 6,179 votes (0.13%), Marxist Leninist Party (Red Flag) 674 votes (0.01%), CPI(ML) Red Star 523 votes (0.01%), and Bahujan Samaj Party 260 votes (0.01%).
At least five parties – Indian Christian Front, Indian National League, Lok Janashakthi Party, National People’s Party, and Socialist Party – accounted for votes in just two digits, together making up a vote share of 0.00% each.

title: TDP appoints women, BCs, minorities in key leadership posts
summary: TDP prioritizes women, BCs, and minorities in leadership roles across key districts, enhancing representation in party positions.
content:
The ruling Telugu Desam Party (TDP) has given priority to Backward Classes (BCs), minorities, and women in appointing the party president and general secretary posts in Kurnool, Nandyal, and Anantapur districts.
The TDP had announced new presidents and general secretaries for 25 Parliamentary Constituencies prioritising BCs, SCs and STs on Sunday (December 21, 2025).
In Nandyal district, three-time MLA Gowru Charitha Reddy was appointed as the party president while a minority leader NMD Firoz, son of Minister for Minorities Welfare N.M.D. Farooq, as the general secretary. Ms. Charitha Reddy is a senior politician and was first elected as a MLA from Nandikotkur Assembly constituency in 2004 on Congress ticket defeating two-time MLA Byreddy Rajasekhara Reddy.
With Nandikotkur reserved for Scheduled Castes in the subsequent elections, she shifted to Panyam constituency and contested on YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) ticket in the 2014 elections. She defeated five-time MLA from the constituency, Katasani Rambhupal Reddy, who contested as an independent in the elections.
Denied ticket by the YSRCP to contest the 2019 elections, she shifted to the TDP and unsuccessfully contested the elections against Mr. Rambhupal Reddy who switched over to the YSRCP from TDP. She, however, defeated Mr. Rambhupal Reddy in the 2024 elections by a margin of more than 40,000 votes.
With Rambhupal Reddy as the YSRCP’s district president, the TDP leadership considered a strong leader to lead the party in the district and appointed Ms. Charitha Reddy for the post, party sources said.
A young minority leader, Mr. Firoz, was appointed as the general secretary considering the considerable minority population in the district as well as Nandyal Assembly constituency represented by Firoz’s father Farooq.
Gudise Krishnamma, who was appointed as the TDP Kurnool district president.
                                                            | Photo Credit: 
                                U. SUBRAMANYAM
The party appointed Gudise Krishnamma, woman leader hailing from Valmiki community from Adoni Assembly constituency as the Kurnool district president. Ms. Krishnamma was a senior member of the party who unsuccessfully contested the 2004 Assembly elections on TDP ticket. She remained loyal to the party during turbulent times and was rewarded with the post.
Another senior leader Poola Nagaraju Yadav, who was appointed as the general secretary, also hails from BC community. Party sources said that the party leadership once again reiterated its commitment towards empowerment of BCs by appointing leaders from these communities to the top posts in the district.
In Anantapur district, Pula Nagaraju, who is from Valmiki community from Raidurgam Assembly constituency was appointed as the president. He replaces Kaluva Srinivasulu, who is Rayadurgam MLA and also from the Valmiki community. He is also presently the APSRTC Kadapa Zone regional chairman. G. Sridhar Chowdary, a party loyalist, was appointed as general secretary.

title: Sixth train to be inducted on Yellow Line from December 23
summary: BMRCL to induct sixth train on Yellow Line from December 23, improving peak hour service frequency to 13 minutes.
content:
The Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Limited (BMRCL) has announced that the sixth train on the Yellow Line will be inducted for passenger service from December 23, which is likely to improve service frequency during peak hours.
According to a press release issued on Monday, the addition of the sixth train will enable metro services on the Yellow Line to operate at a 13-minute frequency during peak hours from Monday to Saturday, compared to the existing 15-minute interval. However, on Sundays, the peak-hour frequency will continue to remain at 15 minutes.
The BMRCL officials said, “The enhanced frequency is expected to ease congestion and offer better convenience to commuters travelling on the Yellow Line, which connects R.V. Road and Bommasandra.”
The BMRCL clarified that there would be no change in the scheduled departure of first and last trains from either of the terminal stations, despite the induction of the additional train.
Meanwhile, on Thursday, the seventh train set for Yellow Line arrived at the Hebbagodi depot in Bengaluru. It is expected to be inducted into revenue service in early January after completing mandatory inspections and safety tests, the officials said.

title: 20 farmers injured as van overturns near Bailhongal
summary: Twenty farmers were injured in a van accident near Bailhongal while en route to a convention in Mysuru.
content:
At least 20 farmers were injured in a road accident in Jalikoppa near Bailhongal on Monday.
They were bound for the world farmers convention in Mysuru. They were travelling from Garjur village to the Belagavi Railway Station, to catch a train to Mysuru.
The van overturned and they suffered injuries. However, no one was seriously injured, the police said.
Some of them managed to catch a bus and board the train, while others returned home.

title: Actor rape case: three held on charge of sharing Martin’s video for money
summary: Three arrested for monetarily sharing a video insulting a survivor in the actor rape case, amid ongoing police investigation.
content:
The police have arrested three persons for allegedly sharing, for money, a video released by Martin Antony, the second accused in the actor rape case, which insulted and defamed the survivor. The arrested persons are natives of Ernakulam, Alappuzha and Thrissur.
According to the police, the accused circulated the video after receiving payment and uploaded it on social media platforms on a commercial basis. The video was reportedly shared across more than 200 websites and Facebook pages.
In the video, Martin attempts to deny the rape, publicly naming the survivor and claiming that the crime never took place. This was despite the court convicting him in the rape case. Martin is currently serving sentence in the Viyyur Central Jail.
Thrissur City Police Commissioner Nakul Rajendra Deshmukh said strict legal action would be taken against anyone found sharing or promoting the video. He confirmed that the case against Martin has been registered in Thrissur and that the cyber police had initiated action based on a complaint filed by the survivor.
The police said the wide circulation of the video on social media pointed to a possible organised attempt to malign the survivor and undermine the judicial verdict. Investigation was under way to identify others involved in the coordinated sharing and monetisation of the video.

title: Cold weather forces a change in school schedule in Yadgir district
summary: Yadgir district schools adjust schedules to 10 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. due to severe cold weather until December 31.
content:
Due to acute cold wave conditions during the night and in the early hours of the day, the Education Department in Yadgir district has effected changes in school schedule till December 31.
According to the order passed by the Deputy Director of Public Instructions C.S. Mudhol, as per directions issued by the Yadgir Deputy Commissioner Harshal Bhoyar, the schedule for schools that are following State, CBSC, NCERT and ICSC syllabus will be from 10 a.m. to 4.30 p.m. till December 31 owing to acute cold weather conditions.
“All Block Education Officers have been instructed to ensure that the order passed changing school timings is strictly followed considering the health safety of students,” Mr. Mudhol toldThe Hindu.

title: Buon Natale celebrations to light up Thrissur on December 27
summary: Join the vibrant Buon Natale celebrations in Thrissur on December 27, featuring 15,000 Santas, AI floats, and charity initiatives.
content:
Buon Natale, jointly organised by the Thrissur Archdiocese and the Thrissur Pouravali, will be held in Thrissur city on December 27, promising a grand blend of devotion and carnival spirit.
Union Minister for Culture and Tourism Gajendra Singh Shekhawat, Union Ministers of State Suresh Gopi and George Kurian, State Ministers K. Rajan, R. Bindu and Ramachandran Kadannappally, Leader of the Opposition V.D. Satheesan, along with political leaders and social, cultural and religious heads, will attend the event.
A colourful rally will begin from St Thomas College, circle the Swaraj Round and conclude at the college premises. Around 15,000 Christmas Santas will take part in the procession, moving to a specially choreographed theme song composed this year by noted music director Jerry Amaldev.
One of the highlights of this year’s Buon Natale will be the use of artificial intelligence, with four moving AI-enabled floats, along with 15 large floats depicting the rich cultural heritage of Kerala and India. The moving floats have been designed and built by students under the supervision of teachers from Jyothi Engineering College.
Describing Buon Natale as a celebration of compassion, Thrissur Archbishop Mar Andrews Thazhath said that as part of the event, around 10 houses will be constructed for the poor, irrespective of caste or religion. The keys to these houses will be handed over during the peace meeting. He also announced that three dialysis missions would be handed over to the Jubilee Mission Medical College as part of the initiative.
The celebrations will be organised in all parishes under the Archdiocese, with parish-level committees implementing various welfare schemes for economically disadvantaged families, selected without discrimination.
In addition, the Buon Natale exhibition will be held at Shaktan Nagar, Thrissur, from December 24 to January 5.

title: Calicut varsity authorities deny reports on glitches in K-REAP
summary: Calicut University denies claims of K-REAP software glitches affecting postgraduate students' exam registration and internal marks upload.
content:
The authorities at the University of Calicut have denied reports about technical glitches in the K-REAP software for exam registration.
A section of first-semester postgraduate students attached to various departments on the university campus at Tenhipalam in Malappuram had earlier claimed that they were facing issues while uploading details on to the software. The Kerala Resources for Education Administration and Planning software (K-REAP) was launched by the Kerala State Higher Education Council recently to streamline the academic and administrative functions in State universities.
