These special classes will be held from January to March to all students grouped into above average, average and below average students should be engaged separately.
Termed ‘Mission 40+’, the teachers taking these classes will get ₹1000 per month, while each school will get ₹6000 to bear the travel expenses of students attending these classes from afar. The State government has earmarked ₹3.44 crore for the project, to be borne by Kalyana Karnataka Regional Development Board (KKRDB).
Four students of a private engineering college in Bengaluru, who went to have biryani at Hoskote, wereallegedly kidnapped and robbedby a gang of men in the early hours of December 21, 2025, before being let go. The Avalahalli police have arrested one of the accused and are searching for the others.
According to the police, the students, who had gone to Hoskote, were returning around 5.30 a.m. when they were intercepted near Kada Agrahara village by a gang. The gang allegedly forced the students into a shed near Medahalli, where they were robbed of three mobile phones and ₹40,000 in cash. They were are made to transfer ₹1.10 lakh through a UPI app.

title: Andhra Pradesh to roll out quantum technology courses for school students: Naidu
summary: Andhra Pradesh to launch quantum technology courses for students, enhancing skills for a knowledge-driven economy, announces Chief Minister Naidu.
content:
Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu on Tuesday announced that Andhra Pradesh would soon introduce quantum technology courses to equip students with next-generation skills as part of a broader plan to build a knowledge-driven economy.
During a meeting with representatives of IIT Madras at the State Secretariat, the Chief Minister said students must be prepared early for emerging technologies such as quantum computing and artificial intelligence. He said every student in the State should have basic exposure to these fields and stressed that government and private school students should benefit equally.
Mr. Naidu directed officials to roll out awareness programmes at the school level, with students of Classes 7, 8 and 9 being introduced to quantum concepts in a phased manner. He also asked the Education Department to set up computer laboratories in schools in stages and to coordinate with the Central government for required support.
Representatives of IIT Madras outlined proposals to impart artificial intelligence education through digital platforms in Telugu, English and Hindi. They presented a four-phase action plan to build AI awareness among students over a two-year period beginning next year, which was reviewed during the meeting.
The Chief Minister said a Student Partnership Summit would be organised by the end of January 2026 to provide a platform for students to showcase innovations. Such initiatives, he said, would foster entrepreneurial thinking and encourage students to emerge as future industrial leaders.
Calling for effective use of the Centre’s National Programme on Technology Enhanced Learning, Mr. Naidu directed officials to ensure that over 50,000 technology students receive training in quantum-related skills. He said the quantum curriculum should be finalised by January 2026.
He also reviewed the expansion of true 5G services with BSNL officials. Senior officials from the Education Department and representatives from IIT Tirupati and IBM attended the meeting.

title: CETs for admission to professional courses in A.P. from April 23
summary: APSCHE announces CET schedules for 2026-27, including ECET and ICET exams on April 23 and 28, respectively.
content:
Andhra Pradesh State Council of Higher Education (APSCHE) has released the schedule for Common Entrance Tests (CETs) for admission to professional, technical and non-technical UG and PG programmes for the 2026-27 academic year.
According to the schedule, the Andhra Pradesh Engineering Common Entrance Test (ECET) 2026 will be conducted on April 23, 2026 in two sessions. A.P. Integrated Common Entrance Test (ICET) will be held on April 28, 2026 in two sessions. The Andhra Pradesh Post Graduate Engineering Common Entrance Test (PGECET) will be conducted from April 29 to April 30 and on May 2, 2026 in six sessions.
Similarly, A.P. Law Common Entrance Test (APLAWCET) and A.P. Education Common Entrance Test (AP EdCET) will be conducted on May 4, 2026 in one session each, A.P. Post Graduate Common Entrance Test (AP PGCET) on May 5, 8, 9, 10 and 11 in 10 sessions, A.P. EAPCET (Engineering) on May 12, 13, 14, 15 and 18 in 10 sessions and A.P. EAPCET (Agriculture and Pharmacy) on May 19 and May 20, 2026 in four sessions.

title: Internet services suspended in two violence-hit Karbi Anglong districts in Assam
summary: Internet services suspended in Karbi Anglong, Assam, to maintain peace amid violence and clashes between protest groups.
content:
The Assam government on Tuesday (December 23, 2025) temporarily suspended internet services in Karbi Anglong and West Karbi Anglong districts, following fresh violence during clashes between two groups over the issues of eviction, officials said.
At least eight people were injured,as the two groups of protesters clashed,and the police resorted to lathicharge and fired tear-gas shells to disperse them.
In an official order, the Home and Political Department said in the interest of maintaining greater public peace and tranquility, and to prevent any deterioration of the present situation, internet services have been temporarily suspended.
It will remain in force until further orders.

title: MLA hails A.P. CM Naidu’s honorarium to church pastors
summary: MLA praises A.P. CM Naidu's ₹5,000 honorarium for pastors, highlighting communal harmony and festive celebrations in Vizianagaram.
content:
All major churches in Vizianagaram and Parvatipuram-Manyam districts wore a festive look ahead of the Christmas celebrations on 25th December. SIIMS Baptist Church, Roman Catholic Church, Canadian Baptist Church and others in Vizianagaram witnessed lot of religious activity with special prayers, devotional concerts, and charitable activities.
Several TDP public representatives in both the districts took part in ‘mini Christmas’ celebrations. TDP MLA Bonela Vijaya Chandra organised an event for the Christian community and others in Parvatipuram on Tuesday (23 December, 2025). He hailed Chief Minister Nara Chandrababu Naidu’s ₹5,000 honorarium to 8,427 pastors across the State.
He said that the TDP government had taken several steps for the welfare of Christian families while ensuring communal harmony in the State. He said that special praja darbar would be organised very soon in Parvatipuram constituency.

title: RBI data shows robust industrial growth in A.P. in 2019-24, contradicts TDP–JSP charges, says Jagan
summary: RBI data reveals Andhra Pradesh's industrial growth from 2019-24 contradicts TDP-JSP claims, asserts YSRCP leader Jagan Mohan Reddy.
content:
The YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) president and former Chief Minister Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy has said that the official data released by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) contradicts repeated allegations made by the Telugu Desam Party (TDP) and the Jana Sena Party (JSP) regarding the State’s economic and industrial performance during the previous YSRCP government.
In a post on 'X' on Tuesday, Mr. Jagan Mohan Reddy said that the TDP and the JSP leaders have consistently claimed, both before and after assuming power, that “Brand Andhra Pradesh” was destroyed under the YSRCP regime, investors deserted the State, and that industrial growth came to a standstill between 2019 and 2024. However, according to RBI data released this month, Andhra Pradesh recorded impressive growth in terms of Gross Value Added (GVA) during the 2019–24 period. In the manufacturing sector, Andhra Pradesh ranked first in South India and fifth nationally, indicating a strong performance. Similarly, in overall industry sector growth, the State stood first in South India and eighth in India during the same period.
He said these rankings clearly demonstrate that Andhra Pradesh’s industrial and manufacturing sectors performed robustly during the YSRCP government, contradicting claims that the State suffered from investor flight or economic stagnation.  “If Andhra Pradesh’s brand had truly been destroyed and industries had collapsed, the State’s performance in manufacturing and industry would have been among the worst. Instead, RBI data places Andhra Pradesh among the top-performing States in the country,” he said.
He maintained that the figures reflect the outcome of stable governance and policy-driven growth during his tenure. He questioned whether the narrative of “Brand AP destruction” was politically motivated, pointing to the RBI data as evidence of a “booming economy driven by transformative leadership.”
The YSRCP leader demanded that the ruling coalition explain the contradiction between its political rhetoric and officially published economic statistics, stating that facts, not propaganda, should guide public discourse on Andhra Pradesh’s development.

title: Unorganised workers too will get ESIC medical services, says Shobha
summary: Union Minister Shobha Karandlaje announces free ESIC medical services for unorganised workers, enhancing social security for all labor sectors.
content:
Union Minister of State for MSME and Labour and Employment Shobha Karandlaje has said that free medical services currently available at ESIC hospitals for organised sector workers and their dependents will soon be extended to unorganised workers as well.
These beneficiaries will include agricultural, contract and garment workers and others from the unorganised sector.
Speaking after inaugurating a sports complex, rooftop solar power system and groundwater recharge facilities at the ESIC Medical College in Kalaburagi on Tuesday, Ms. Karandlaje said that the decision to extend ESIC medical services to unorganised workers is in line with Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s vision of providing comprehensive social security to both organised and unorganised labour.
She said that the ESIC hospital in Kalaburagi, with a capacity of 560 beds, is not operating at full occupancy as services are limited mainly to insured persons from the organised sector.
“Despite the extension of the Central Government Health Scheme (CGHS) to this hospital, bed occupancy has not crossed 50%. Expanding services to the unorganised sector will help utilise the infrastructure effectively,” she said.
Highlighting reforms in the labour sector, the Minister said that 29 existing labour laws have been repealed and consolidated into four labour codes aimed at safeguarding the interests of workers.
Emphasising holistic development, Ms. Karandlaje said that sports and yoga are essential for physical and mental well-being of students. Sports play a key role in personality development along with education, she added.
Union Minister of State for Labour and Employment Shobha Karandlaje interacting with medical and nursing college students at the ESIC Hospital complex in Kalaburagi on Tuesday.
                                                            | Photo Credit: 
                                ARUN KULKARNI
Later, Ms. Karandlaje interacted with medical, paramedical and nursing students and staff and heard their grievances. Responding to the demands she said that CT scan and MRI equipment will be provided soon at the hospital. The demand also included a dedicated college bus and stipend for nursing students.
Kalaburagi Rural MLA Basavaraj Mattimod, MLC B.G. Patil, the former MLA Dattatreya Patil Revoor, ESIC Hospital Medical Superintendent Kadlimatti and others were present.

title: GSSS institutions to come under Sri Sringeri Sharada Peetham
summary: GSSS institutions in Mysuru will now operate under the guidance of Sri Sringeri Sharada Peetham, enhancing their educational framework.
content:
The management of Geetha Shishu Shikshana Sangha (R) (GSSS), Mysuru, has announced that all educational institutions run by it will henceforth function under the patronage of the Sri Sringeri Sharada Peetham.
The formal announcement was made by Vidhushekara Bharathi Swami during the Guru Vandana Samarambha held recently at the GSSS Institute of Engineering and Technology for Women (IETW) here.
The decision follows over 18 months of deliberations between the institution and the Peetham. The initiative was led by the then honorary secretary of GSSS, late Vanaja B. Pandit, who approached the Sri Sringeri Sharada Peetham seeking its guidance for the future growth, development and administration of GSSS. The Sangha was founded and nurtured by her late husband, Prof. B.S. Pandit.
Subsequently, the administrator and CEO of the Sri Sringeri Sharada Peetham, Murali P.A., was entrusted with conducting the required interactions and consultations. The Peetham has now formally accepted the proposal to bring GSSS institutions under its fold, according to a press release issued here.
Accordingly, the following institutions will now be guided and directed by the Sri Sringeri Sharada Peetham: Gita Bharathi School of Excellence, Siddharth Nagar, Bantwal Madhava Shenoy High School, Siddharth Nagar, Badri Prasadji Pre-University College, Siddharth Nagar, GSSS Simha Subba Mahalakshmi First Grade College, Metagalli, GSSS Institute of Engineering and Technology for Women, Metagalli, and GSSS School of Architecture for Women, Metagalli, the release read.
The Guru Vandana Samarambha witnessed the participation of over 3,000 people, including students, staff, parents and distinguished invitees. GSSS president M. Jagannath Shenoi, vice-president B.V. Srinivasa Gupta, board member B.K. Nataraj, secretary Anupama B. Pandit, and CEO R.K. Bharath were present on the occasion.

title: Adani Foundation hands over sanitation vans to Muthukuru, Krishnapatnam gram panchayats
summary: MLA Somireddy launches sanitation campaign in Muthukuru and Krishnapatnam, supported by Adani Foundation's sanitation vans for community improvement.
content:
Sarvepalli MLA Somireddy Chandramohan Reddy launched the sanitation management awareness campaign at Muthukuru and Krishnapatnam gram panchayats in SPSR Nellore district, on Tuesday.
The campaign will focus on behavioural changes among the villagers in both panchayats by keeping the surroundings clean. It includes sanitation training to the locals, providing them with sanitation bins, and collecting garbage on a daily basis.
As part of the initiative, the Adani Foundation handed over four sanitation vans to both the panchayats under the Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) funds of Adani Krishnapatnam Port Limited (AKPL).
On the occasion, Mr. Somireddy said, "AKPL and Adani Foundation have shown their commitment by contributing to the sanitation campaign for Muthukuru and Krishnapatnam gram panchayats by providing vehicles and starting sanitation management awareness campaign for the villagers in Public-Private-People Partnership (P-4) model."
"The company through its CSR arm Adani Foundation is committed to promoting the community development and sanitation management among neighbouring villagers of the port. We will continue to make villagers aware of the importance of the sanitation and their responsibility towards keeping their houses and surroundings clean," said AKPL CEO Jagdish Patel.

title: Good response to Mysuru Tree Census initiative
summary: CII Mysuru launches a collaborative Tree Census initiative, engaging over 100 participants to enhance environmental sustainability in the city.
content:
The Confederation of Indian Industry (CII), Mysuru zone, marked the beginning of a collaborative, city-focused Tree Census initiative with a kick-off and orientation programme here on December 22.
The programme brought together over 100 participants from industry, academic institutions and student volunteers, reflecting strong interest in contributing to Mysuru’s environmental sustainability through structured, on-ground action. The initiative is being steered by the CII Mysuru Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) and Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI) Panel, with active support from the Health, Safety, Environment and Wellness Panel, and the Industry–Institute Interaction Panel.
Addressing the participants, Nagaraja Gargeshwari, chairman, CII, Mysuru zone, emphasised that responsible city development requires industries and institutions to look beyond their boundaries and work collectively for long-term public good.
He appreciated the panels for conceptualising the initiative and acknowledged the importance of industry–academia collaboration in ensuring scale, continuity and credibility of such efforts. He also placed on record his appreciation for Smitha Hegde from Centre for Advanced Learning, Mangaluru, for guiding the programme and anchoring the methodology.
During the session, Prof. Hegde highlighted that a scientific yet simple approach to tree documentation is critical for meaningful outcomes. She noted that the use of a standardised, app-based process enables diverse teams to contribute consistently, making city-wide coverage achievable through coordinated participation.
The initiative builds on the initial efforts of Mysuru Green Projects (MGP) and the Centre for Advanced Learning (CFAL), Mangaluru, along with academic institutions in Mysuru, and seeks to take the exercise forward at a larger scale. Going ahead, the Tree Census will be driven through joint teams formed by industry and academia, working together across wards to ensure systematic progress, according to a press release.
CII Mysuru will continue to facilitate coordination and participation as the initiative gathers momentum in the coming months, the organisers said.

title: CM favours mechanism to forge effective coordination between depts to achieve desired results
summary: Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy emphasizes departmental coordination and accountability for effective governance and all-round development in Telangana.
content:
Stressing that there was a need for officials to work with accountability, Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy directed Chief Secretary K. Ramakrishna Rao to review the functioning of the Secretaries every month while he would also personally review the same every three months.
The Chief Minister asked the Secretaries of different departments to submit monthly reports to the Chief Secretary, and underscored the need for effective coordination between different departments as it is of foremost importance to achieve the cherished goal of all-round development of the State.
“Departments working in close coordination with one another is of utmost importance. The desired results cannot be achieved without coordination between officials and different departments,” he said during a meeting with senior officials of different departments here on Tuesday. Two years have passed since the people’s government took over the reins, and the government achieved some results while a planned approach was adopted for other sectors.
The State faced problems in the past due to the absence of comprehensive policies governing the functioning and setting goals in key departments like Energy, Education, Irrigation and Health. The government had therefore announced special policies for the key departments while at the same time, brought out a comprehensive Telangana Rising Vision governing the entire State.
Plans had been prepared dividing the State into CURE, PURE and RARE regions, formulating separate economic growth policies for core urban, peri-urban and rural & agriculture regions. The effort was to ensure that clear policy guidelines were laid down for the all-around development of the State, and these policies would bear fruit only with the cooperation from the administrative machinery.

title: All new APSRTC electric buses, including Palle Velugu, to be air-conditioned, says Naidu
summary: Andhra Pradesh plans to introduce 1,450 air-conditioned electric buses, aiming for a fully electric fleet by 2030.
content:
Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu has directed that all new electric buses to be introduced by the Andhra Pradesh State Road Transport Corporation, including those under the Palle Velugu rural services, should be air-conditioned, underscoring the government’s emphasis on passenger comfort and modern public transport.
Reviewing APSRTC’s electric mobility roadmap at the Secretariat on Tuesday, the Chief Minister said all 1,450 buses proposed for purchase in the next financial year should be electric vehicles. He instructed officials to prioritise the establishment of EV charging stations in the Godavari districts in view of the upcoming Godavari Pushkaralu and to invite tenders at the earliest.
Mr. Naidu approved a long-term plan to replace 8,819 diesel buses with electric buses over the next five years. He also directed that buses with more than eight years of remaining operational life be gradually converted into electric vehicles. Stressing passenger-centric planning, he said transport infrastructure must be strengthened to meet rising commuter demand, particularly after the implementation of the Stree Shakti free bus travel scheme for women.
Highlighting the State’s commitment to sustainable mobility, the Chief Minister said Andhra Pradesh aims to operate only electric and CNG buses by 2030, replacing diesel vehicles in a phased manner. This transition, he said, would significantly reduce pollution and lower APSRTC’s long-term operating costs.
Mr. Naidu suggested outsourcing maintenance of electric buses to private operators to improve efficiency and called for greater focus on cargo transportation, on the lines of Indian Railways, to augment revenue. He also asked officials to explore commercial income opportunities from bus stations.
Officials informed the Chief Minister that under the PM e-Bus Sewa scheme, the Centre is providing 750 electric buses to the State, with in-principle approval for an additional 300 buses for the Tirumala–Tirupati region. A pilot project converting diesel buses to CNG on the Chittoor–Vellore route has also yielded positive results.

title: Workshop held on ‘Uyare’ gender campaign
summary: ‘Uyare – Uyaratte Keralam, Valaratte Pangalitham,’ will be launched on January 1
content: A media workshop to create awareness of ‘Uyare – Uyaratte Keralam, Valaratte Pangalitham,’ a Statewide campaign being launched by the Kudumbashree on January 1, was held here on Monday. State Gender Council gender consultant T.K. Anandi inaugurated the workshop. The campaign aims at enhancing women’s participation in the workforce from 20% to 50% and creating safe workplaces.

title: Centre permits sale of surplus tobacco, says Mysuru MP
summary: Centre allows surplus tobacco sales in Mysuru, addressing growers' issues, confirms MP Yaduveer Wadiyar following government intervention.
content:
The problems faced by tobacco growers in Mysuru Lok Sabha constituency, particularly relating to the sale of excess tobacco, have been addressed, with the Centre issuing a notification permitting tobacco sales.
Confirming this on December 23, Yaduveer Krishnadatta Chamaraja Wadiyar, Mysuru MP, who had highlighted the growers’ issue to the Centre, said that he had met the Union Ministers, senior officials, and Tobacco Board authorities concerned, urging them to take decisions favourable to tobacco growers in his constituency. “The Union government has now responded positively to these representations,” Mr. Wadiyar stated.
The MP said that as per the notification, registered and licensed tobacco growers have been permitted to sell surplus Flue Cured Virginia (FCV) tobacco produced by them at auction platforms authorised by the Tobacco Board. Certain restrictions imposed under the Tobacco Board Act, 1975, have been relaxed to facilitate the disposal of FCV tobacco through official auction platforms, the MP said in a release here on December 23.
The notification also states that for FCV tobacco produced during the 2025–26 season, each registered grower will have to contribute ₹1 per kilogram and 5% of the sale proceeds to the Tobacco Fund, he added.
In a recent letter to Union Minister for Commerce and Industry Piyush Goyal, the MP had sought urgent intervention to facilitate the purchase of tobacco cultivated by growers this season. The data shared by the MP with the Minister stated that nearly 10,000 card-holding farmers had grown about 10 million kg of tobacco. But the crop had been declared unauthorised, pushing them into severe distress, Mr. Wadiyar said.
Citing the acute financial hardship faced by the farming community, the MP had requested the Commerce Ministry to permit the immediate procurement of the produce.
Over the past decade, both registered and unregistered growers in Karnataka have together produced close to 100 million kg of tobacco annually. Owing to climate change and other challenges, the output has now fallen to 80 million kg. The MP has urged the Centre to grant registered-grower status to unregistered farmers and to increase the procurement quota by 10%.

title: Mandya Deputy Commissioner reviews progress of construction of buildings for residential schools
summary: Mandya Deputy Commissioner reviews construction progress of residential schools, emphasizing improved facilities and quality education for students.
content:
Mandya Deputy Commissioner Kumar chaired a meeting to review the progress of construction of buildings for various State-run residential schools in the district.
A total of 43 residential schools, including Morarji Desai, Kittur Rani Chennamma, Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, and Indira Gandhi Residential schools, are functioning in Mandya district.
Reviewing the progress of construction of buildings, Mr. Kumar instructed the officials to inspect the works and take necessary steps for their speedy completion within the stipulated time.
The Deputy Commissioner also discussed the deficiencies in basic facilities in these institutions and directed the officials to place greater emphasis on improving quality education while also strengthening the basic infrastructure in schools.
He said all residential schools must ensure provision of essential facilities like drinking water, food, and toilets to students. He instructed the officials concerned to work proactively to ensure that the intended facilities reach students.
He directed them to take the necessary steps to improve the performance of SSLC students studying at the residential schools through special classes and periodic tests.
Mr. Kumar asked them to prepare a list of problems faced by the residential schools in the district and submit a proposal to the government seeking a solution.
The meeting was attended by Srinivas, deputy director of the Social Welfare Department, Manjula, deputy director of the Backward Classes Welfare Department, Arun Kumar, lead bank manager, and others.

title: Aggrieved TVK functionary blocks Vijay’s car
summary: TVK functionary protests by blocking party president Vijay’s car over dissatisfaction with district secretary appointment in Chennai.
content:
Infighting in a district unit of the fledgling Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam came to the fore on Tuesday when an aggrieved party functionary blocked party president Vijay’s car near the party’s headquarters at Panaiyur on the outskirts of Chennai.
Ajitha Agnel, a TVK functionary from Thoothukudi district who is active on social media, was reportedly upset over not being appointed as the party’s district secretary. She blocked Mr. Vijay’s car and later staged a sit-in protest along with her supporters in front of the party office. TVK functionaries attempted to persuade her to disperse.
TVK deputy general secretary C.T.R. Nirmalkumar said when Vijay Makkal Iyakkam was converted into TVK, several postings were realigned and the number of posts at the district level was reduced. He said it was common for some workers to feel disappointed and such issues occur in all parties. He said Mr. Vijay would sort out the matter.

title: 40th Asian Waterbird Census on January 10, 11 in Godavari estuary
summary: Join the 40th Asian Waterbird Census on January 10-11, 2026, at Godavari estuary to observe endangered migratory species.
content:
The 40th Asian Waterbird Census and 60th International Waterbird Census will enumerate the bird species of Coringa Wildlife Sanctuary and it’s adjoining wetlands on January 10 and 11, 2026.
The Andhra Pradesh Forest Department in collaboration with the Bombay Natural History Society (BNHS), Wildlife Institute of India (WII), and World Wide Fund for Nature (WWF) will enumerate the bird species. This will be the 10th census to be conducted in the Coringa Wildlife Sanctuary and it’s adjoining wetlands.
The census will focus on the presence of four major species endangered Indian Skimmer (Rynchops albicollis), endangered Great Knot (Calidris tenuirostris), Near Threatened Eurasian Curlews (Numenius arquata)andEurasian oystercatcher (Haematopus ostralegus).All the four bird species are migratory which arrive at the Godavari estuary for feeding during the winter.
The Godavari estuary is one of the prominent sites in India, in which Indian Skimmer and Great Knot can be sighted together. Coringa Sanctuary Wildlife Ranger Mr. Vara Prasad said that local birdwatchers would also be welcomed to join in the census.

title: MVD bid to rein in rash driving by delivery boys of e-commerce platforms
summary: MVD addresses rising traffic violations by e-commerce delivery boys, issuing notices to major platforms for improved road safety compliance.
content:
Following a rise in traffic rule violations, the Motor Vehicles department has initiated steps to curb  rash and negligent driving by delivery boys of e-commerce platforms. According to Transport Commissioner C.H. Nagaraju, notices have been issued to delivery representatives of Blinkit, Swiggy, Zepto, Bigbasket etc., following rise in traffic violations by delivery boys of these firms.
The online platforms have been given 15 days to streamline and align policies regarding road safety, failing which  action will be taken by enforcement agencies. Notices have been issued to dark stores and quick delivery platforms after the MVD noted a rise in rash and negligent driving by two-wheeler delivery boys of these companies.
Many online platforms are encouraging delivery of items within seven minutes or 20 minutes, which is one of the main reasons for the increased road safety violations. Speeding, rashness, and non-wearing of safety gear are some of the most commonly noted safety issues among delivery boys, says Mr. Nagaraju.
In normal circumstances, other drivers on the road often avoid them, fearing accidents. The delivery boys rush to deliver their products and catch the next order to maximise their income. Many a time, these delivery boys are given unrealistic deadlines by the online store, and even customers are promised unrealistic timelines to gain market share. However, all these amount to compromises on road safety, say MVD officials.

title: Hate Speech Bill is unconstitutional, alleges BJP
summary: BJP protests Karnataka's Hate Speech Bill, claiming it violates constitutional rights and threatens democratic freedoms.
content:
Terming the Karnataka Hate Speech and Hate Crimes (Prevention) Bill, 2025, as unconstitutional, leaders, workers and supporters of the BJP staged a dharna opposing the proposed legislation and criticised the Congress government for allegedly suppressing the fundamental rights of citizens, in the city on December 23.
The protestors accused the Siddaramaiah-led government of attempting to curb criticism through the Bill and said it was an effort to take away rights given in the Constitution. They alleged that the legislation was aimed at silencing voices speaking against the government. “It is trying to control the Opposition parties and other organisations. The protest was organised to spread awareness on the move,” a statement from the BJP Chamaraja unit read.
Stating that the Bill lacks a clear definition of what constitutes hate speech, the protestors claimed that criticism of government policies and the expression of facts would be branded as hate speech. Through this move, they alleged, the government was trying to ensure that people do not speak out against it.
The BJP leaders and workers further alleged that the proposed law undermines democratic principles and poses a threat to democracy. They claimed that the Bill contains provisions denying bail for certain offences, which they said could lead to the criminalisation of ordinary citizens.

title: Govt. sets the ball rolling for the Bengaluru’s second airport
summary: Govt. initiates plans for Bengaluru's second airport amid rising demand, while KIA continues to expand and innovate.
content:
While the Kempegowda International Airport (KIA) continued to hold on to its position as the third busiest airport in the country, in 2025, the focus was on Bengaluru’s proposed second airport.
With the KIA projected to handle around 80 to 90 million passenger traffic by the end of this decade and expected to run out of capacity by early 2030’s, the State government began initiating plans for a second airport for Bengaluru.
In April a high-level team from the Airports Authority of India (AAI) inspected three sites at Choodahalli and Somanahalli on Kanakapura Road, as well as another location on the Nelamangala-Kunigal Road.
Following its assessment, the AAI team submitted its report to the government which has in turn invited tenders to select an expert consultancy firm to prepare a location suitability and comprehensive technical and financial feasibility report for the proposed airport.
While the State government had identified three sites around Bengaluru for the second airport, some legislators had suggested Sira in Tumakuru district as a location for it. However, the government had said that a greenfield international airport in Sira was not viable.
Meanwhile at the KIA, several new routes and new airlines both international and domestic were added to the existing ones strengthening its position as a top airport in the region.
The work on the Bengaluru Airport City, spread over 463 acres and which will have business parks, a global innovation hub, an education and health district, a retail dining entertainment (RDE) village, a concert arena, a convention and exhibition centre, a knowledge park, an hospitality area, a logistics park, and a central park, was also in full swing during the year.
Towards the end of the year, the Bangalore International Airport Limited (BIAL), which operates the KIA, introduced a new lane segregation system at the pick-up zone in front of the terminals.
While the BIAL defended the enhanced pick-up measures stating it would streamline passenger movement, reduce congestion, and improve safety, discipline, and overall convenience at arrival areas, some passengers and cab drivers had opposed it. Many cab drivers staged protests against the new rules.

title: Bombay HC tells Vijay Mallya to return to India before challenging Fugitive Offenders law
summary: Bombay HC mandates Vijay Mallya's return to India to challenge the Fugitive Offenders law, emphasizing court jurisdiction.
content:
The Bombay High Court on Tuesday (December 23, 2025) declined to hearabsconding businessman Vijay Mallya’s petition questioning the constitutional validity of the Fugitive Economic Offenders Act (FEO Act) unless he first returns to India and submits to its jurisdiction.
Mr. Mallya has moved two petitions before the High Court — one challenging the special court’s 2019 order declaring him a fugitive economic offender, and another questioning the constitutional validity of the FEO Act.
A Division Bench of Chief Justice Shree Chandrashekhar and Justice Gautam Ankhad observed that he cannot pursue both pleas simultaneously while remaining abroad.
“You will have to make a statement as to when you will return to India; only then we will hear the petition challenging theviresof the FEO Act,” the Bench said, directing him to file an affidavit indicating his timeline. “Come back to India, we are here to provide you with a solution,” the judges added.
The Court clarified that while his appeal against the special court’s declaration can proceed even if he stays overseas, the constitutional challenge requires his presence. “How does one wipe out criminal liability without submitting to the jurisdiction of the Court?” the Bench remarked.
Also Read |Vijay Mallya moves Karnataka High Court seeking data from 10 banks on total debt recovery
Senior advocate Amit Desai, appearing for Mr. Mallya, argued that the law does not mandate physical presence for such challenges. “The statute permits a person to question the validity of the Act without being in India. My client has cooperated and his assets worth ₹14,000 crore have been attached against an alleged liability of ₹6,000 crore,” Mr. Desai submitted.
Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, representing the Enforcement Directorate (ED), opposed the plea, citing Section 14 of the Act, which bars fugitives from contesting proceedings while evading Indian courts. He also noted that extradition proceedings in the United Kingdom are at an advanced stage and should not be stalled by these petitions.
Mr. Mallya left India in March 2016 amid investigations into alleged loan defaults by Kingfisher Airlines. He was declared a fugitive economic offender by a Mumbai special court in January 2019 under the FEO Act. Enacted in 2018, the law empowers authorities to confiscate the properties of individuals accused of economic offences involving ₹100 crore or more if they refuse to return and face trial.
The matter has been adjourned to February 12 for Mr. Mallya’s response on whether he will withdraw one petition or indicate a date for his return.

title: Dalit organisations demand special law against honour killing
summary: Dalit organisations in Hubballi demand a special law against honour killing after a tragic incident claiming a pregnant woman's life.
content:
Following the honour killing at Inam Veerapur in Hubballi taluk in which a pregnant woman, Manya Doddamani, lost her life, Vividha Dalita Sangha Samsthegala Mahamandala (a federation of various dalit organizations) has urged the State government to promulgate a special law to address honour killing.
Addressing a press conference along with office-bearers of various Dalit organizations in Hubballi on Tuesday, Gurunath Ullakashi of Samata Sena Karnataka said that Constitutional rights are being violated as existing legal provisions have failed to stop honour killing.
He said that since 2011, several honour killing cases have been reported in the State in which a majority of the victims have been women.
Mr. Ullakashi said that that officials of the Social Welfare Department have failed to respond even after such an incident. None of the Social Welfare officers visited the hospital or contacted the affected family, an example of sheer institutional indifference, he pointed out.
He also criticised women’s welfare and human rights bodies for what he termed a lack of sustained intervention in such cases. Drawing comparisons with other recent incidents, he said that there is selective public sympathy and unequal official attention.
Stating that the organisations will continue their agitation if justice is delayed, Mr. Ullakashi urged the State government to enact a special law exclusively addressing honour killing.
He also sought rehabilitation measures for the victim’s family, including the allotment of 10 acres of land and a government job.
Office-bearers of various organisations Gurappa Chalawadi of Uttar Karnataka Chalawadi Mahasabha, Shakkana Doddamani of Madiga Mahasabha, Shatraiya Pola of Dora Mahasabha, Devanna Itagi of Muchigera Mahasabha, Manjunath Ullakashi, Hanumanth Talwar and Lohit Gavingatti and others condemned the incident in strong terms and demanded stringent punishment to all the accused.

title: V-C selection process at Calicut varsity set to pick up pace
summary: Calicut University accelerates Vice-Chancellor selection process with new committee nominee R. Ramakumar, following court directives.
content:
The process to pick a full-time Vice-Chancellor (V-C) for the University of Calicut (CU) is expected to move faster, with Governor and Chancellor Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar notifying the inclusion of R. Ramakumar, State Planning Board member, as the senate nominee for the search-cum-selection committee on December 22.
Mr. Ramakumar was chosen as the senate nominee at a meeting held on December 18. According to official sources, Registrar Denoj Sebastian subsequently sought his consent as directed by the Kerala High Court. In an interim order issued recently based on a petition filed by the State government, the court had asked the university authorities to ensure the consent of the nominee chosen by the senate for the search panel. Dharmaraj Adat and A. Sabu, who were earlier chosen as the senate nominees, had declined to take up the job.
The sources toldThe Hinduon Tuesday (December 23) that the court, in its interim order, had asked the university authorities to conduct the special senate meeting to elect its nominee in 30 days, ensure the consent of the nominee, and inform the Chancellor about these developments.
After Mr. Ramakumar conveyed his consent to Mr. Sebastian, the Chancellor was informed about it. Thereafter, the notification was issued, the sources said. Now, the standing counsel of the university would inform the court about these developments when the case wtaken up on January 5, 2026, the sources said. The State government filed the case objecting to the Chancellor’s constitution of the search panel after Mr. Sabu informed his unwillingness to be part of it.
Ravindra D. Kulkarni, V-C, University of Mumbai, is the UGC’s nominee and G.U. Kulkarni, Professor, Jawaharlal Nehru Centre for Advanced Scientific Research, Bengaluru, is the Chancellor’s nominee in the panel. The search panel is expected to go through the applications received for the post of V-C after the court’s final order in the case. These developments also follow the truce reached between the State government and the Chancellor over the appointment of V-Cs for the APJ Abul Kalam Technological University and the Digital University Kerala. P. Raveendran was given the full charge of V-C by the then Chancellor Arif Mohammed Khan in July 2024.

title: Children’s special gram sabha to be held at Managalli village in Chamarajanagar
summary: Join the children's special gram sabha on December 24 at Managalli village, featuring live interaction with Minister Priyank Kharge.
content:
A children’s special gram sabha will be held on the premises of the Government High School at Managalli village in Chamarajanagar district on December 24.
A press statement here said the programme will be launched by Minister for Rural Development and Panchayat Raj Priyank Kharge via YouTube Live.
The Minister will also hold a video interaction with the children, read the statement.
Through this interaction, Mr. Kharge will also hold live discussions with the district’s elected representatives, and officials from various departments, said a press statement issued by the Chamarajanagar Zilla Panchayat CEO.

title: Two arrested for ‘defaming’ Minister Gummadi Sandhya Rani’s family
summary: Two individuals arrested for defaming Minister Gummadi Sandhya Rani’s family with false allegations and fake social media screenshots.
content:
Parvatipuram-Manyam Superintendent of Police S.V. Madhava Reddy said that two persons with vested interests had made false allegations of sexual harassment and other charges against Minister for Tribal Welfare Gummadi Sandhya Rani’s son Prudhvi and the Minister’s personal assistant Sathish.
Addressing the media here on Tuesday (23 December, 2025), the SP said that Saluru police personnel arrested Boora Triveni (subordinate in Saluru MPDO office) and her friend Devi Prasad (Junior Assistant in Saluru Municipal Office) on the charges of creating fake screenshots of social media account to defame the Minister’s family as well as the government. He said that they were arrested after receiving the forensic report which confirmed the fake chats and screenshots.
According to the SP, Ms. Triveni, who had secured a job on compassionate grounds, gave ₹5 lakh to Mr. Satish four years ago after he promised her a good post. At the time of the transaction, he was not the PA to Ms. Gummadi Sandhya Rani, who herself was not a minister. However, when Mr. Satish failed to return the amount despite repeated requests, Ms. Triveni developed a grudge against him.
Ms. Triveni filed a case at the Saluru police station in November, alleging that Mr. Satish had sexually harassed her and claimed that the Minister’s son, Prudhvi, had sent her objectionable messages on WhatsApp. Due to pressure from all sections of society, Mr. Satish resigned from his post and, on November 27, 2025, filed a case at the Saluru police station asserting that the allegations were false.
The police sent the chat and screenshots to the Mangalagiri Forensic Department, which, in its report, stated that the chat and phone numbers did not match. Mr. Madhava Reddy said that the department had taken adequate care and conducted a thorough inquiry before arresting Ms. Triveni and her friend Devi Prasad.
“We filed cases on the two persons under various sections for damaging the reputation of the Minister’s family and the government. Further inquiry will continue to identify the motive,” said Mr. Madhava Reddy.
Additional Superintendent of Police V. Maneesha Reddy and Circle Inspector of Saluru town Appala Naidu were also present in the media conference.

title: CREDAI Hyderabad property show from February 6 to 8
summary: CREDAI Hyderabad Property Show 2026 will be held from February 6-8 at HITEX, showcasing approved residential and commercial projects.
content:
The Hyderabad chapter of the Confederation of Real Estate Developers’ Associations of India (CREDAI) on Tuesday announced the CREDAI Hyderabad Property Show 2026, scheduled to be held from February 6 to 8 at the HITEX Exhibition Centre.
According to a release, only projects approved under the Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act will be showcased at the exhibition. A wide range of residential and commercial options will be on display, including apartments, villas, plotted developments and office spaces across Hyderabad.
Addressing the media, CREDAI Hyderabad president N. Jaideep Reddy said, “The recent GHMC and HMDA land auctions have reaffirmed Hyderabad’s position as one of India’s most premium and liquid land markets, particularly across high-growth corridors such as c, Raidurg and Bachupally. These high-value transactions signal long-term demand and are expected to push benchmark prices upward. From a homebuyer’s perspective, this makes the present phase an opportune window to invest before the next price cycle sets in.”

title: Train between Nandyal-Guntakal during morning hours soon, says MP
summary: Nandyal MP announces morning train service between Nandyal and Guntakal, improving commuter convenience.
content:
Nandyal MP Byreddy Shabari said that the Union Railway Ministry gave the nod to run a train between Nandyal and Guntakal during the morning hours.
During the recent Parliament session in the Lok Sabha, Ms. Shabari raised the problems being faced by commuters travelling between Nandyal and Guntakal, with not a single train running between the two destinations during the daytime.
Though four trains ran between the two stations, all of them were during the midnight hours, she said. She sought for a morning train for the convenience of the students, employees and general public. In reply, Union Minister for Railways Ashwini Vaishnaw assured to look into the issue.
In a statement on Tuesday, Ms Shabari said the Railway Minister gave the green signal to run a train between Markapuram Road to Guntakal passing through Nandyal during the morning. Train no. 57408 will start at Markapuram at 4.30 a.m. and reach Nandyal at 7.20 a.m., and from there reach Guntakal at 10.30 a.m. passing through Dhone.
In the return direction, Train no. 57407 will start from Guntakal at 5.30 p.m. and reach Nandyal by 8.30 p.m.. The train will reach Markapur at 10.30 p.m..
Stating that the train service will start soon, Ms. Shabari thanked the Railway Minister for responding positively to her request.

title: ED files PMLA complaint against Sun Pariwar Group over  ₹158 crore fraud
summary: ED files PMLA complaint against Sun Pariwar Group for ₹158 crore fraud involving cheating over 10,000 investors.
content:
The Directorate of Enforcement (ED), Hyderabad filed a prosecution complaint under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA), 2002, against M/s Sun Pariwar Vupadi Management Pvt Ltd. The Special PMLA Court of the Metropolitan Sessions Judge, Rangareddy, took cognisance of the complaint on December 10.
The ED initiated its investigation following multiple FIRs registered by Telangana police against M/s Sun Pariwar, its promoter Methuku Ravinder, and his close associates for allegedly cheating investors under the guise of offering high returns through Sun Pariwar Group companies and Sun Mutually Aided Thrift and Credit Co-operative Society Limited. Investigators found that Ravinder and his associates collected approximately ₹158 crore from more than 10,000 investors, which has been classified as proceeds of crime.
Investigations revealed that the accused floated several schemes promising returns of up to 100% per annum. Various companies under the Sun Pariwar umbrella, including Methuku Chit Fund Pvt. Ltd, Methuku Ventures Ltd, Metsun Nidhi Ltd, Methuku Herbal Limited, and Methuku Medical and Herbal Foundation, were used to collect funds, which were then siphoned off to acquire movable and immovable assets in the names of Ravinder and his associates.
Further, ED found that Ravinder established additional entities, including M/s Pudami Agro Farm Lands, M/s Pudami Infra Projects (India) Ltd, and M/s Divine Infra Developers, under the names of close associates, and launched new ponzi schemes to continue luring investors. The proceeds from these schemes were also allegedly channelled into acquiring assets in the names of these entities.
Earlier, the ED had attached movable and immovable properties worth ₹25.2 crore belonging to Ravinder, his family members and close aides. Further investigation is under way.

title: FSSAI registration camps held at 14 Hyderabad vegetable markets
summary: FSSAI registration camps in Hyderabad's 14 vegetable markets promote food safety and hygiene, receiving 926 vendor applications.
content:
The Telangana Food Safety Department on Tuesday conducted Food Safety and Standards Authority of India c at 14 major vegetable markets across Hyderabad, as part of its efforts to strengthen food safety standards and promote hygiene practices among vendors.
The camps were organised with the objective of facilitating the issuance of registrations and licences under the FSSAI, while also sensitising vegetable vendors on food hygiene, safety norms and the importance of maintaining sanitation within market premises, said a release.
The registration drives were held at Kushaiguda, Uppal Vegetable and Fruit Market, Saroornagar Rythu Bazar, NTR Nagar Vegetable Market, Vanasthalipuram Rythu Bazar, Madannapet Vegetable Market, Mir Alam Mandi, Owaisi Vegetable Market, Monda Market, Mettuguda Vegetable Market, Erragadda Vegetable Market, Gudimalkapur Vegetable Market, Lingampally Market and JNTU Rythu Bazar.
A total of 926 applications were received from vendors seeking FSSAI registration or licences during the one-day exercise. The department has announced another round of registration camps on December 30 at the same locations, providing an opportunity for vendors who were unable to apply earlier to avail the facility.

title: Breach of privacy: actor’s sister petitions police
summary: Actor Dileep's sister petitions police over unauthorized drone surveillance, alleging privacy violations by two television channels.
content:
Actor Dileep’s sister, S. Jayalakshmi, has filed a petition with the Aluva East police against two television channels and their reporters alleging that drones were flown over her brother’s residence in Aluva without permission, thereby violating the privacy of not only the actor but also his family members.
The petition was submitted by Ms. Jayalakshmi on Tuesday.
The channels allegedly flew drones over Mr. Dileep’s house on December 8, when the Ernakulam Principal Sessions Court delivered its verdict in the actor rape case. Mr. Dileep, sixth accused in the case, was acquitted. Before and after the verdict, the channels reportedly captured overhead visuals of Dileep’s residence without his consent.
According to the complaint, visuals of not only Dileep but also other residents of the house, including the complainant herself, were illegally recorded using drones and continuously broadcast by the channels.

title: Central Crime Branch arrest Nigerian national for smuggling cocaine
summary: Central Crime Branch arrests Nigerian national for smuggling cocaine hidden in bread loaves, valued at ₹65 lakh.
content:
The Central Crime Branch (CCB) has arrested a 29-year-old Nigerian national for allegedly smuggling cocaine concealed inside loaves of bread to evade detection.
The accused has been identified as Olajide Esther Iyanuoluwa, a native of Nigeria. According to the police, she allegedly cut open the inner portion of bread loaves, hid 120 gm of cocaine inside, and packed them to make the consignment look like ordinary food items.
Investigators said the accused was transporting the drug from Mumbai to Bengaluru in a private bus, using the unusual concealment method to avoid suspicion during checks. Acting on specific intelligence, the CCB officials intercepted her and conducted a thorough search.
The police seized 120 gm of cocaine, valued at approximately ₹65 lakh in the international market.
Probe revealed that the accused came to Delhi in 2024 on a student visa claiming to pursue studies at a university. However, without enrolling in any college, she stayed in areas such as Ghatkopar (Gala Nagar), Ambawadi, and Nallasopara in Mumbai. She procured cocaine from her friend in Mumbai and, as per his instructions, transported and supplied the same to designated locations.
Further probe revealed that she used to travel from Mumbai to Bengaluru in private buses and transport cocaine by concealing it in bread and similar products to avoid detection.
Based on a specific information, a team of officials tracked Olajide to her friend’s house from the bus stand where she got down and walked to her friend’s house carrying a packet of bread. The police raided the house and initially found nothing. But when they checked the packet of bread she was carrying, they found the drugs concealed inside the loaf, a police officer said.
A case has been registered under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act, 1985, and further investigation is under way to ascertain the source of the drugs, the intended recipients in Bengaluru, and whether an inter-State or international network was involved, the police said.
In a similar case, the Jalahalli police have arrested two drug peddlers hailing from Kerala for allegedly trafficking narcotic substances in the city.
The accused have been identified as Nikhil Raj, 30, and Melvin Monsi, 23. Acting on a tip-off, the police conducted an operation and apprehended the duo, seizing 247 gm of hydro ganja and 19 gm of MDMA worth ₹26.9 lakh from their possession.
According to the police, the accused used to procure the drugs from Kerala and transport them to Bengaluru, where they were allegedly involved in peddling the drugs to customers in the city. The police said Nikhil, a high school dropout, was working as cab driver in the city, while his associate Melvin, a BA graduate and claimed he was a social worker, the police said.

title: Sammakka-Sarakka shrine gets a facelift ahead of Medaram jatara
summary: Sammakka-Sarakka shrine gets a facelift ahead of Medaram jatara
content:
MULUGU
Revenue and Housing Minister Ponguleti Srinivas Reddy on Tuesday said that nearly 80% of the development works at the Medaram Sammakka-Sarakka tribal shrine had been completed.
He stated that the remaining works would be finished by the first week of January 2026 and that the reconstructed shrine would be inaugurated with a grand fete in the presence of Chief Minister  A. Revanth Reddy, his Cabinet colleagues and Opposition leaders ahead of the Maha Jatara (biennial event), which is scheduled to be held from January 28 to 31, 2026.
The Minister, along with local MLA and Panchayat Raj and Rural Development Minister Danasari Anasuya (Seethakka), Mahabubabad MP P. Balaram Naik and Chief Minister’s Adviser Vem Narender Reddy, inspected the ongoing development works at Medaram.
The aerial view of the Medaram Sammakka-Sarakka tribal shrine compound at Medaram in SS Tadwai mandal, Mulugu district.
Addressing a press conference after a review meeting with officials, Mr. Reddy said the works were progressing as planned and were designed to meet requirements for at least the next 200 years. He said devotees could already see visible changes at the sacred site, where the gaddelu (platforms) housing the tribal deities were undergoing a complete makeover, with stone pillars and permanent structures replacing the earlier installations. He emphasised that all Adivasi worship customs were being strictly followed during execution of the works, adding that they had expanded by area of the compound of the shrine by two-and-a-half times for the convenience of the devotees.
A stone structure replaced a Gadde (sacred platform) at Sammakka-Sarakka tribal shrine compound at Medaram in SS Tadwai mandal, Mulugu district.
He also said approach roads were being widened from the existing 50–60 feet to 100–120 feet, along with the development of medians, to facilitate devotees, noting that Medaram had emerged as a major pilgrimage centre in the State and country.
Ms. Seethakka said sculptures carved on stone blocks and pillars depicted Adivasi culture, customs, traditions, rituals, deity worship practices, tools and others passed down through generations. She also addressed the controversy over the Swastika symbol, stating that Adivasi communities had been using the symbol, oriented differently from the Hindu religious symbol, for generations.
A carving depicting the Adivasi lifestyle at Sammakka-Sarakka tribal shrine compound at Medaram in SS Tadwai mandal, Mulugu district.
She added that the installation of Padigiddaraju and Govindraju would be held on Wednesday (December 24) in accordance with Koya Adivasi rituals.
A stone pillar is being set up at Sammakka-Sarakka tribal shrine compound at Medaram in SS Tadwai mandal, Mulugu district.
District Collector T.S. Divakara, Superintendent of Police Sudhir R. Kekan and other officials were present.

title: Walayar mob lynching case: SIT detains two more persons for questioning
summary: The Special Investigation Team (SIT) has detained two more persons for questioning in the Walayar mob lynching case where a migrant worker from Chhattisgarh was lynched to death on the suspicion of theft. Officials said investigators were verifying whether the suspects, both residents of Attapallam, played an aggravating role in the hate crime or were merely mute onlookers.
content:
The Special Investigation Team (SIT) has detained two more persons for questioning in the Walayar mob lynching case where a migrant worker from Chhattisgarh was lynched to death on the suspicion of theft.
Officials said investigators were verifying whether the suspects, both residents of Attapallam, played an aggravating role in the hate crime or were merely mute onlookers.
According to the police, a group of people confronted Ram Narayan Baghel, an odd-job worker from Karhi village in Chhattisgarh, who had arrived in Palakkad to seek work.
The police case was that the group accused Ram Narayan Baghel  of being an opportunistic thief and a criminal alien from Bangladesh, tried him publicly, and then systematically beat the worker to death.
So far, the police have arrested four people in connection with the crime. They are A. Anu, C. Prasad, Murali, and K. Vipin
Investigators were non-committal about their political affiliations, but noted that the suspects had a police record of political violence, including. attacks against CPI(M) workers.
Their arrests sparked a political row, with CPI(M) State Committee member and Labour Minister V. Sivankutty alleging that the accused were committed RSS workers who campaigned for the BJP in the local body polls. He also accused Congress workers of aiding the RSS workers in unleashing wanton violence against Ram Narayan. “The Congress workers attacked Ram Narayan when emergency responders were moving him into the ambulance, he said.
The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) accused the CPI(M) of reading politics into the mob murder and said the suspects were of mixed political affiliations. Congress was yet to respond officially.
State Police Chief Ravada A. Chandrasekhar told reporters that more arrests were likely and police had identified several eyewitnesses to the crime.
Another officer said the police would indict the accused for murder, read with violation of the Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention) of Atrocities Act.
Moreover, the police would seek the accused’s custodial interrogation and judicial permission to transfer the case to a fast-track court, in accordance with the Supreme Court’s guidelines for mob lynching cases.
Investigators said they would also book the accused for hate speech. They said the suspects had created evidence against themselves by video recording Ram Narayan’s public lynching.
Meanwhile, the government dispatched Ram Narayan’s mortal remains by flight to Chhattisgarh. Revenue Minister K. Rajan said Wednesday’s cabinet would weigh the quantum of compensation for Ram Narayan’s family and disburse ex gratia payment from the Chief Minister’s Relief Fund.
Meanwhile, Chhattisgarh Chief Minister Vishnu Deo Sai condemned the incident on social media. On X, Mr Sai announced an ex gratia payment of ₹5 lakh to the bereaved family. He urged Kerala to seek deterrent punishment for the accused in the case.

title: KCCI to plant 5,000 saplings during Green Initiative Year
summary: KCCI announces 2026 as Green Initiative Year, committing to plant 5,000 saplings and promote environmental sustainability.
content:
The Karnatak Chamber of Commerce and Industry (KCCI) has declared 2026 as the Green Initiative Year during which Green Certificates will be issued to guests visiting the chamber.
As part of the initiative, the chamber has committed to planting 5,000 saplings to promote environmental sustainability along with economic growth.
Addressing the media along with other office-bearers, KCCI president G.K. Adappagoudar announced that the chamber will launch new awareness programmes for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) and extend support to facilitate access to various government financial assistance schemes.
He added that upgrading industrial estates will be a top priority for KCCI to ensure a clean and business-friendly environment.
KCCI will further advocate modernisation of godowns at Gadag, Badami, Haveri, Ranebennur and the Amargol APMC Yard in Hubballi to enhance efficiency of freight movement, he said.
Mr. Adappagoudar also said that KCCI will actively contribute to the “Beyond Bengaluru” initiative outlined in the Karnataka IT Policy 2025-2030 which aims to foster balanced regional IT growth by transforming emerging cities into globally competitive IT and ITeS hubs.
The KCCI president said that Incomex-2026, an industrial, commerce and trade exhibition, will be held from April 20 to 24 next. Union Minister for Commerce and Industry Piyush Goyal has agreed to pay a visit to the event.
KCCI office-bearers Praveen Agadi, S.G. Kammar, Veeranna Kallur, Uday Revankar and Prakash Sringeri spoke about various other initiatives and plans of the chamber.
The KCCI 2026 calendar and diary were released on the occasion.

title: TPCC general secretary targets Harish Rao over Kaleshwaram, water disputes
summary: TPCC general secretary targets Harish Rao over Kaleshwaram, water disputes
content:
HYDERABAD
Telangana Pradesh Congress Committee (TPCC) general secretary Chanagani Dayakar targeted BRS MLA and former Irrigation Minister T. Harish Rao, alleging corruption, failure to protect Telangana’s interests, and silence on key issues related to water sharing and governance.
Addressing a press conference at Gandhi Bhavan on Tuesday, Mr. Dayakar questioned why Harish Rao had not responded to the allegations levelled by MLC K. Kavitha regarding corruption and irregularities in the Kaleshwaram project. “If Harish Rao has morals, why is he silent on Kavitha’s accusations?” he asked.
He alleged that BRS leaders, K.T. Rama Rao and Harish Rao, were competing to insult Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy, while the party’s rule had centred on building family assets rather than public welfare. He claimed the BRS had failed to focus on people’s development and the rights of Telangana during their regime.

title: Youth entrepreneurship summit begins in Kasaragod
summary: The Youth Entrepreneurship Summit in Kasaragod fosters innovation and collaboration among young entrepreneurs and industry leaders across Kerala.
content:
The 10th Innovation and Entrepreneurship Development Centre (IEDC) Summit, organised by the Kerala Startup Mission (KSUM) in collaboration with LBS College of Engineering, Kasaragod, began on Monday (December 22), providing a major platform for young innovators and entrepreneurs from across the State.
As part of strengthening collaboration in the start-up ecosystem, the KSUM and the National Association of Software and Service Companies (NASSCOM) signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU). The summit was inaugurated by Uduma MLA C.H. Kunhambu, while N.A. Nellikkunnu, Kasaragod MLA, presided over the function.
Addressing the gathering, Mr. Kunhambu said youth should not only present innovative ideas but also ensure that their ventures contributed meaningfully to society. Entrepreneurs and innovation play a crucial role in transforming Kerala into a knowledge based economy, he said, adding that the State must move beyond a traditional economic model by integrating technology and productivity to enhance output.
Mr. Nellikunnu described the summit as a new and valuable experience for Kasaragod district. Lauding the KSUM, he said its contribution to nurturing young entrepreneurs in the State was significant, and that the summit would open up fresh opportunities. He noted that Kerala was steadily emerging as an industry-friendly State, with procedural hurdles for starting enterprises having been considerably reduced, creating a favourable environment for an industrial resurgence driven by knowledge-based growth.
District Collector K. Inbasekar congratulated young entrepreneurs who arrived in Kasaragod to participate in the summit, noting that the district had witnessed notable development over the past five years. Welcoming participants who travelled by the “Innovation train” from various parts of the State, he invited them to experience Kasaragod’s cultural richness and tourism potential.
Prizes were distributed to winners of the NASA Space Apps Challenge, with team Meteor Resolvers and Celesta emerging as global finalists. It was also announced that the IEDC Startup Summit 2026 will be held on March 7, 2026, at Amal Jyothi College of Engineering, Kanjirappally.
Along with student idea presentations, the summit features expos, panel sessions, masterclasses, and fireside chats. Around 7,000 students, investors, and policymakers are participating in the two-day event.

title: Debate boot camp for students commences in Kurnool
summary: Ridge School in Kurnool launches a debate boot camp to enhance students' critical thinking and public speaking skills.
content:
Ridge School, Kurnool, inaugurated its debate boot camp on Tuesday with the aim of nurturing critical thinking, effective communication, and confident public speaking among students. The boot camp will run till December 29.
The camp is being conducted by Indian Debating League training and development associate Krishaang Kohli, who brings with him rich experience from national and international debating platforms. The sessions are designed to be highly interactive, focusing on logical reasoning, articulation of ideas, rebuttal techniques, and confident expression.
The programme commenced with the lighting of the lamp in the presence of Ridge School CEO Gopinath, CEO Sowmya, and dean Rajendran.

title: Congress Govt. is on defensive following GP poll results: Harish Rao
summary: Congress Govt. is on defensive following GP poll results: Harish Rao
content:
HYDERABAD
The Congress Government in the State appears to be on the defensive following the recent press conference held by Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) president K. Chandrasekhar Rao, and at least half a dozen ministers reacting to the latter’s comments is a clear indication of how they are unsettled with KCR’s reading of the state of affairs in Telangana.
The observation was made by senior leader of the BRS T. Harish Rao, during an informal chat with newspersons here on Tuesday. The victory of over 4,000 BRS-backed candidates getting elected as Sarpanches recently had badly unsettled Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy. Perhaps, it is the Gram Panchayat election results that have made the government consider not holding elections to cooperative societies and instead appoint Congress activists/leaders on a nomination method.
Welcoming the government's plans to give a PowerPoint presentation on the irrigation sector in the Assembly, Mr. Harish Rao asked the government to allow the BRS too for making a presentation. The BRS was being given lesser time in the Assembly compared to Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), and Majlis-e-Ittehadul Muslimeen (MIM), he claimed.
Mr. Harish Rao alleged that the government was planning to divide the GHMC area into three civic bodies and borrow ₹30,000 crore, and that two Cabinet ministers had shared ₹7,000 crore in the name of irrigation projects, and the bills were being sanctioned only to those who were giving 20% commission.
On availing the Krishna waters by Telangana since 2014-15, the BRS leader said it was lowest in 2024-25 at the State had utilised only 28.49% water against 71.51% by Andhra Pradesh from out of 1,004 tmc ft availability. He cautioned the police officers who are “foisting cases against BRS leaders” for getting into the good books of the Chief Minister and they would have the same fate as some officers in AP met after the 2024 elections.

title: Karunakaran led Kerala with vision and political will: Therambil
summary: Therambil Ramakrishnan honors K. Karunakaran's visionary leadership and political will on his 15th death anniversary in Thrissur.
content:
Former Speaker Therambil Ramakrishnan has said that the late Chief Minister K. Karunakaran was a strong leader who shaped modern Kerala and strengthened the Congress with discipline and foresight.
“K. Karunakaran was a ruler who guided the State towards progress with long-term vision,“ Mr. Ramakrishnan said. He was speaking at an event in connection with 15th death anniversary of Karunakaran, after paying floral tributes at his memorial at Murali Mandiram, Punkunnam, on Tuesday.
Mr. Ramakrishnan said Karunakaran implemented countless projects that enabled Kerala to stand tall before the world. He demonstrated that governance need not be surrendered to bureaucracy, but could be driven by strong political will. Fearless in the face of criticism, Karunakaran led the State with clarity of purpose and direction. The vigilance and discipline he maintained in nurturing the Congress party in Kerala, Mr. Ramakrishnan added, remained lessons for today’s leaders and the younger generation.
District Congress Committee president Joseph Tajet presided over the function. In his address, he described Karunakaran as a leader endowed with an extraordinary ability and political acumen to turn even adversaries and challenges to his advantage.

title: HAL is a pan India organisation contributing towards India’s self-reliance: Yaduveer
summary: Yaduveer praises HAL's role in India's self-reliance and growth in the aviation sector during its 86th Foundation Day.
content:
MP for Mysuru Yaduveer Krishnadatta Chamaraja Wadiyar on Tuesday described the Hindustan Aeronautical Limited (HAL) as a pan India organisation contributing towards India’s growth and self-reliance in the aviation sector.
Speaking at the 86th HAL Foundation Day celebrations, Mr. Yaduveer said, “The HAL has grown today to what it has become such a great and grand institution that is pan India working towards so much of what is our new forefront. I think it was a new forefront in the 1940s and it still remains the new forefront today, and I am sure that the advances that the HAL is making will certainly lead India to be self-reliant in the aviation sector going forward.”
Mr. Yaduveer recalled the contributions made by the then Maharaja of Mysore Jayachamarajendra Wadiyar who donated 700 acres of prime land and invested ₹25 lakhs for setting up the Hindustan Aircraft Limited as it was known then.
He said that the HAL was a Mysore Institution which after independence became part of the Government of India and that this aspect needs to be remembered.
“This isn’t a political stage, certainly me being a politician I do not want to get into that but there were certain references made during the past year that this HAL was attributed to a certain family and I think everyone has certainly made their part in nurturing this institution,” he said.
HAL Chairman and Managing Director D.K. Sunil said that the defence PSU should be very clear about what the future demands are and work towards achieving them.
“The aerospace and defence environment will become more competitive and more complex. The need for speed and reliability will increase, the need for reliance and supply chain will go up, and the need for digital tools and modern manufacturing will increase. The HAL must be ready for that future. It must be ready in technology, ready for processes, and ready for partnerships,” he said.
During the event, the cover of a HAL book by Amar Chitra Katha and HAL Mystamp was also unveiled.

title: Rajanna blames DCM for Congress losing LS seats to ‘vote theft’ in Karnataka
summary: Rajanna accuses DCM Shivakumar of Congress's LS seat losses due to 'vote theft' in Karnataka, urging leadership accountability.
content:
Taking a dig at Deputy Chief Minister and KPCC president D.K. Shivakumar on the issue of alleged “vote chori” (vote theft) in Karnataka, senior Congress leader and former Minister K.N. Rajanna has told Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi last month that the Congress could have secured an additional 8-10 Lok Sabha seats in Karnataka if the KPCC chief and Booth Level Agents (BLAs) appointed by the party had paid more attention to prevent vote theft.
In a letter dated November 17, 2025, which has come to the public domain now, Mr. Rajanna said that if other States, too, had avoided similar lapses (vote theft), the Congress party could have won 30-40 more Lok Sabha seats and prevented Prime Minister Narendra Modi from holding the office for a third consecutive time. “Instead, the Congress party would have assumed power, and Mr. Rahul Gandhi would have become the Prime Minister,” he said.
Mr Rajanna, the former Minister and MLA for Madhugiri, who was sacked from the Cabinet for allegedly speaking against the vote theft campaign launched by the party, said, “The purpose of my statement is to emphasise that BLAs appointed by the KPCC have not performed their responsibilities. If our KPCC president, D.K. Shivakumar, and the officials concerned had paid proper attention to these lapses, they could have been prevented. In that case, the Congress party would likely have secured 8 to 10 additional seats in Karnataka”.
Further, Mr. Rajanna, a loyalist of Chief Minister Siddaramaiah, said that he supported the vote theft campaign launched by Mr. Gandhi when he visited Bengaluru.
Defending the present leadership in the government in the State, Mr Rajanna said the Congress came to power in the State in 2013 and 2023 under the leadership of  “Chief Minister Siddaramaiah, who has worked tirelessly to deliver justice to the poor and marginalised sections of all communities – SCs, STs, OBCs, minorities, and other weaker sections”.
Sources in the Congress said that Mr. Rajanna had written letters to Mr. Gandhi earlier, too.  Mr. Rajanna, who has been apparently demanding the replacement of Mr. Shivakumar from the KPCC chief’s post, sought action against those who have misrepresented his words on vote theft.

title: Tiger sightings: Cages, drones deployed
summary: Forest authorities enhance surveillance and deploy drones and trained elephants to monitor and capture tigers near Nanjedevanapura village.
content:
Forest authorities have stepped up surveillance following reports of increased tiger movement in and around Nanjedevanapura village in Chamarajanagar district.
The operation to capture the tigers will be carried out in line with the Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) of the National Tiger Conservation Authority. As part of the operation, two trained elephants from Dubare have been deployed, while forest personnel from various ranges have been mobilised to assist in the exercise. The department has also installed two cages including a walk-through cage and a Tumakuru-type cage to facilitate safe capture, if required, according to a press release issued by the Forest Department.
Four teams of forest staff have been constituted, with each team equipped with a drone for continuous surveillance. During night hours, thermal drones are being used to track tiger movement to ensure round-the-clock monitoring in and around the affected villages.

title: Prostitution, human trafficking key focus for Cyberabad Women Safety Wing
summary: Cyberabad's Women Safety Wing intensifies efforts against street prostitution and human trafficking, rescuing victims and raising awareness in 2025.
content:
Women and children safety remained a key focus for the Cyberabad commissionerate in 2025. The Women and Children Safety Wing (W&CSW) of the Cyberabad police recorded extensive enforcement, rescue and counselling activity in 2025, with a particular focus on street prostitution and anti-human trafficking.
Senior officials revealed the involvement of an increasing number of women students.  As per theannual round-up reportreleased on Tuesday (December 23, 2025), the police booked 121 cases related to street prostitution and arrested 508 persons, including 262 sex workers and 246 transgender persons. As part of the action, 356 individuals were bound over, while 24 sex workers were sent to jail for violations under Section 296 (Obscene acts and songs) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and Section 8 of the Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act.
“We are seeing an increase in number of young women involved in street prostitution. They are bound over and, during counselling, we learn that many are pursuing education in various colleges. The next big category is women working as domestic help,” a senior official informed on condition of anonymity.
