“The mandate of the SIR is to include all eligible voters in the voters’ list and exclude ineligible voters. We request all voters to check whether their names are in the draft roll,” Mr. Kelkar said.
The draft roll has been published amid stiff opposition by the State government which, expressing deep concern over the possible exclusion of “nearly 25 lakh voters,” had sought more time for voters to submit the enumeration forms.
Steps have also been taken to enroll new voters in the roll, he said.
Claims and objections can be filed till January 22, Mr. Kelkar said. The notice phase (hearings and verification) will last till February 14. The final roll will be published on February 21.
If a voter whose name is in the draft roll is excluded after a hearing by the Electoral Registration Officer (ERO), the first appeal can be filed before the District Election Officer (DEO) within 15 days of the order of the ERO.  The second appeal can be filed with the CEO within 30 days of the DEO’s order.
Notices will be served on the elector by the booth-level officers (BLO) and obtain acknowledgement on the second copy, as each notice is issued in duplicate.

title: Improve facilities for devotees visiting Srisailam temple: Endowments Commissioner
summary: Endowments Commissioner urges Srisailam temple officials to enhance facilities for devotees amid increasing visitor numbers.
content:
Endowments Commissioner K. Ramachandra Mohan asked the Srisailam temple officials to give priority to improving basic facilities in the town in view of surge in devotees vising the temple.
Mr. Ramachandra Mohan, who visited the temple on Tuesday, reviewed the development works at Srisailam and instructed officials to take up the works in a planned manner. The Commissioner asked the officials to immediately commence works on the temporary queue complex and complete the same within the next three months.
“Construct a permanent queue complex that would cater to the increasing pilgrim flow in the next 30 years,” he said. He asked the officials to beautify the main road from Gangadhara Mandapam to Nandi Mandapam and also to prepare proposals for construction of an accommodation facility for common devotees near Ganesh Sadan.
Mr. Ramachandra Mohan directed the officials to take up restoration works of the ancient structures in the temple compound including the Nandi Mandapam, Vruddha Mallikarjuna Swamy temple mandapam and also the entrance of Sri Bhramaramba temple. He wanted the officials to take up massive plantation drive as part of environment protection. He suggested that planting of trees like ‘Bilva’, ‘Raavi’ and others should be prioritised for the same.
The Commissioner also reviewed the Annaprasada distribution, Gosamrakshana, administration, audit, accounts, sanitation and other aspects of the temple. He suggested the increase of Siva Sevak services and to provide a facility for interested devotees to register for the seva in the temple website. He wanted the services of the Siva Sevaks to be utilised for distribution of Annaprasadam and water, at queue lines and maintaining queues.
He also wanted officials to promote the use of online booking facilities for darshan and devotees’ accommodation.

title: Short Tunnel: BDA looks into realignment over land acquisition concerns
summary: BDA reviews alignment options for short tunnel project amid land acquisition concerns and compensation objections from property owners.
content:
The Bangalore Development Authority (BDA) has completed a substantial portion of land verification for the initially proposed alignment of the short tunnel-elevated corridor between Hebbal Junction and Mehkri Circle, with preparatory work for land acquisition reaching an advanced stage, officials said.
However, the authority is simultaneously examining a possible realignment of the corridor, and the final land acquisition plan will depend on the alignment that is eventually approved, sources said.
According to the officials, the original alignment would have affected around eight properties, including a small number of privately owned parcels, while the alternative alignment under consideration would impact more than 20 properties.
The officials said the extent of land acquisition and the timeline for initiating the process would be firmed up only after a decision is taken on the alignment, which is currently under review amid concerns raised by owners of private properties over the proposed compensation framework.
The realignment is expected to focus on areas around Baptist Hospital (service road), the northern and eastern edges of the KVAFSU campus, and the approach towards Ballari Road and Mehkri Circle, the officials said.
The officials said that while most of the land identified under the preliminary alignment was government-owned, negotiations were required in cases involving private land. They added that internal discussions on compensation have been re-initiated, as some landowners have expressed reservations about the existing framework.
Under the proposal, traffic between Hebbal Junction and Mehkri Circle will be routed through a combination of a three-lane, twin-bore short tunnel along the Hebbal-Karnataka Veterinary, Animal and Fisheries Sciences University (KVAFSU) stretch, followed by an elevated corridor from the KVAFSU area onwards to Mehkri Circle.
A senior official from the North City Corporation, which is also involved in the discussion, said the reconsideration of the alignment was driven by execution-related concerns. While the original alignment involved fewer properties, some of these parcels were located at critical points such as the tunnel exit, where delays in land acquisition could directly affect construction schedules. An alternative alignment, though affecting a larger number of properties, was being examined for its potential to distribute land acquisition across less sensitive locations, reducing the risk of the project being stalled due to disputes at a single point.
He added that the project requires adequate turning radius and sufficient space for construction activities such as cut-and-cover works and utility shifting.
Compensation concerns have also influenced the review. The officials said that some private landowners affected under the original alignment have raised objections to compensation through the Transferable Development Rights (TDRs), particularly in high-value stretches. They noted that TDRs do not guarantee immediate or predictable returns, making them less acceptable to owners who hold commercially valuable land and within these eight properties, a few also depend on rental income from their properties.
The authority, officials toldThe Hindu,is assessing whether an alternative alignment, involving a different mix of properties and owners, could offer greater certainty in land acquisition. They added that a final decision would be taken after meetings scheduled this week, following which the compensation framework and acquisition process would be formalised.

title: Three drug peddlers, 2 consumers arrested in separate cases; 12 LSD blots and 15 grams of MDMA seized
summary: Three drug peddlers and two consumers arrested in Hyderabad; 12 LSD blots and 15 grams of MDMA seized.
content:
Three drug peddlers and two consumers were arrested by the Elite Action Group for Drug Law Enforcement (EAGLE) Force, Telangana, in coordination with Kushaiguda and Saroornagar police in separate operations across Sainikpuri, Neredmet and Saroornagar, seizing 12 LSD blots weighing 0.2 grams and 15 grams of MDMA along with mobile phones.
In the first case, four persons were arrested. They were identified as Ritish Sudharshanam Arkilla, a student of Osmania University from Hanumanpet in Malkajgiri; Dennis Martin, a private employee from Utham Nagar in Malkajgiri; M. Satish Kumar, a DJ player from Kapra in Sainikpuri, and Panda Stevehans from A.S. Rao Nagar in Neredmet. While Ritish and Dennis were drug consumers,  Satish and Stevehans were involved in peddling, police said.
Following a tip-off, a team of the Hyderabad Narcotics Police wing of the EAGLE Force, along with Kushaiguda police, first apprehended the two consumers. Based on their statements, a follow up operation led to the arrest of the two peddlers at a coffee shop in Sainikpuri. Police recovered 12 LSD blots weighing 0.2 grams and four mobile phones from their possession. During questioning, Stevehans stated that the drugs were procured from Rahul alias Tika of Sainikpuri, Neredmet, who is absconding. Police said efforts were underway to trace him.
The seized drugs and the arrested persons in the first case were handed over to Kushaiguda police for further investigation.
In the second case, EAGLE Force personnel along with the Saroornagar police arrested a drug peddler in Saroornagar and seized 15 grams of MDMA and one mobile phone from him. The accused was identified as Boinapally Krishna Sai Varshith alias Sunny, 25, a resident of Cherukuthota Colony, Saroornagar.
Police said that the MDMA drug was found concealed inside the cotton stuffing of a travel neck pillow carried by the accused. After an initial search of his backpack yielded nothing, officers noticed loose stitching on the pillow and recovered the contraband during a detailed check.
Varshith had moved to Bengaluru in search of employment, where he became addicted to MDMA and began purchasing the drug from local suppliers. He reportedly sourced MDMA from an African supplier identified as Mary, also known as Tamiya, at ₹1,500 per gram and sold it in Hyderabad for ₹5,000 to ₹6,000 per gram. Transactions were conducted through bank transfers and QR codes, with drugs delivered at secluded locations in a “dead drop” method, avoiding direct contact.
Investigation revealed that Varshith’s network included 13 customers, four friends who assisted in collecting money, and eight individuals whose accounts and UPI scanners were used by the supplier to receive payments.
Police said intensified surveillance has been put in place across Telangana ahead of the New Year and warned that anyone involved in drug trafficking, including facilitators, would face strict legal action.

title: Heritage walk in Changanassery
summary: Join the Old Changanassery Heritage Walk to explore historical sites reflecting the rich legacy of the Thekkumkoor kingdom.
content:
‘Old Changanassery Heritage Walk,’ being organised  jointly by the DHARINNI Ecology and Heritage conservation trust and Kerala Pradeshika Charithra Padana Samithi, will be held on Saturday. The walk will begin at 7.30 a.m. from Puzhavathu Vettadikkavu in Changanassery, Kottayam.
The route will cover Kumaramanagalathu Mana, Lakshmipuram Palace, Santhana Gopalamurthy Temple, Ittiyamadom, Menon Veedu, Kavil Bhagavathi Temple, Chitrakkulam, Old Juma Masjid, St. Mary’s Metropolitan Church, Angadi and will conclude at Anchu Vilakku.  These locations have been curated to reflect the history of Changanassery, with emphasis on the era of the erstwhile Thekkumkoor kingdom. For further details, contact: 9605645482.

title: Sabarimala gold theft: Bellary-based jeweller moves Kerala HC seeking bail
summary: Bellary jeweller seeks bail from Kerala HC in Sabarimala gold theft case involving 474 gm misappropriated from temple idols.
content:
The Kerala High Court has sought instructions from the State government on a bail petition moved by Roddam Govardhan, a Bellary-based jeweller, who was arraigned as an accused by the Special Investigation Team in the alleged misappropriation of gold from the Sabarimala temple.
He was charged with misappropriating 474 gm of gold from the gold-plated copper coverings of the Dwarapalaka idols that had been taken to a private firm in Chennai for gold plating in 2019. He was arrested in this connection and charged with offences under the Indian Penal Code and the Prevention of Corruption Act.
In his bail plea, the jeweller submitted that he accepted the gold at the instance of Unnikrishnan Potti, the first accused in the case. He added that he paid ₹14.97 lakh for this in 2019, including through demand drafts in favour of the Sabarimala Executive Officer, and that he further donated 184 gm of gold for gold plating the door frames of the Sreekovil.
The matter has been posted for hearing on December 30.

title: Chairperson’s post to be shared in Maradu municipality
summary: Ajitha Nandakumar and Suneela Sibi will alternate as chairperson of Maradu municipality, focusing on solid waste management initiatives.
content:
Ajitha Nandakumar and Suneela Sibi will take turns in serving as chairperson, each holding the post for two and a half years, of Maradu municipality.
Congress councillors Jinson Peter and P.P. Santhosh will share the post of vice chairperson for a designated period of time. The decision was taken at the Congress Parliamentary Party meeting held on Sunday (December 21, 2025). It is learnt that internal party dynamics between factions in Congress have led to a power-sharing arrangement for the posts of chairperson and vice chairperson.
Considering his seniority, Mr. Peter may get a term of three and a half years as vice chairperson, while Mr. Santhosh will hold the post for the rest of the term.
Ms. Nandakumar will assume office first. A senior leader, she has been active in the political scene. She had served as municipal chairperson for a period of six months in 2015. She was also the chairperson of the works standing committee from 2020 to 2023.
Ms. Sibi, who won from ward  17 (Kundannoor), served as chairperson for around two years during the 2015-2020 term. Ms. Siby is presently the district president of the Mahila Congress and formerly its State general secretary.
The chairperson candidate Ms. Nandakumar said that the priority would be to ensure proper solid waste management in the municipality, noting that waste management was a pertinent issue faced by the residents.
The United Democratic Front is sitting pretty in the council, having won 21 of the 35 seats. The Left Democratic Front won 11 seats, while Independents won three.

title: Centre assures duty hike on titanium dioxide
summary: The Centre plans to hike import duties on titanium dioxide to support Kerala's KMML amid challenges from cheap foreign imports.
content:
In a move that could provide a lifeline to the Kerala Minerals and Metals Ltd (KMML), the Union government has promised to review and potentially hike the import duty on titanium dioxide. Following a high-level meeting led by MPs N.K. Premachandran and K. Radhakrishnan with Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman and Union Minister for Commerce and Industry Piyush Goyal, the Centre agreed to consider reinstating the anti-dumping duty along with increasing the import duty.
The delegation, which included KMML trade union leaders, highlighted how the surge of Chinese imports has destabilised the domestic market, leading to a financial crunch for the public sector undertaking.
Following discussions between a trade union delegation and the Union Finance Minister in previous years, the Union government had successfully imposed an anti-dumping duty on titanium dioxide imported from China to protect domestic manufacturers. However, this protective measure faced a legal setback when the Calcutta High Court stayed the order, citing procedural irregularities in how the duty was implemented. This judicial intervention forced the Union government to subsequently withdraw the anti-dumping duty, leaving companies like the KMML vulnerable to cheap foreign imports once again.
During the recently held meeting, this legal context was presented to the Union Finance Minister, who has now provided an assurance that both the reinstatement of the anti-dumping duty and a general increase in import taxes will be considered to rectify past issues and support the domestic industry.
The KMML is India’s only manufacturing facility that produces high-quality rutile-grade titanium dioxide using advanced Chloride Route technology. To sustain and expand this specialised production, Industries Ministers of Kerala and Tamil Nadu had recently held discussions to explore the possibilities of a collaboration to extract mineral sand from the Tamil Nadu coastline for high-value processing. The project is to combine Tamil Nadu’s vast mineral resource availability with the KMML’s technical expertise. A proposal was also made to source ilmenite, the essential raw material for titanium dioxide, from Tamil Nadu to secure a steady supply chain for the KMML.

title: Survey launched to resolve fishing rights dispute between East Godavari, Konaseema
summary: A new survey will define borders between East Godavari and Konaseema amid ongoing fishing rights disputes in the Godavari river.
content:
A fresh resurvey has been commissioned to identify the administrative borders of the East Godavari and Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Konaseema districts, following a dispute between the fisherfolk of the two districts over fishing rights in the Godavari river.
The dispute remains unsolved as the fisherfolk of Bobbarlanka and Dowleswaram continue to fight over the fishing rights in the Godavari river at Sir Arthur Cotton Barrage in Dowleswaram.
This year, the Dowleswaram Matsakara Sangham won the annual lease signed by the Department of Fisheries, with an entitlement to collect wild prawn seed from the river at Sir Arthur Cotton Barrage. The lease is now in question with the Bobbarlanka Matsakara Sangham raising objections over the lease and restrictions on them from the collection of the wild prawn seed.
In a meeting held here on Tuesday (23 December, 2025), Joint Collectors T. Nishanthi (Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Konaseem District) and Y. Megha Swaroop (East Godavari) have directed the Departments of Fisheries, Irrigation and Survey to conduct a fresh survey to identify the borders of the two districts to find a permanent solution to the fishing rights. The officials met to discuss the dispute based on the directives of the court.
“The Departments of Fisheries, Irrigation and Survey will submit their report on the boundaries of the two districts at Sir Arthur Cotton Barrage on December 30. The next round of talks will be held on the dispute with two parties on January 22, 2026. The collection of wild prawn seed will be banned at Sir Arthur Cotton Barrage until further decision,” said the Joint Collectors in an official release.

title: Unified Family Survey launched to update household records in Andhra Pradesh
summary: Unified Family Survey launched to update household records in Andhra Pradesh
content:
The Government of Andhra Pradesh has launched the Unified Family Survey (UFS), a major initiative to ensure that every household in the State is accurately recorded in government databases. The exercise is aimed at helping the State government reach all eligible families with welfare schemes and public services promptly, while improving the efficiency of service delivery.
Commencing in mid-December, the survey is being carried out through door-to-door visits by staff of Village Secretariats in rural areas and Ward Secretariats in urban localities. Officials will verify and update details of each family to ensure official records reflect their current status.
A core objective of the UFS is to ensure that no eligible family or individual is left out of government welfare programmes. Updated and accurate records will also simplify the process of issuing certificates and approvals, eliminating repeated verification across departments. The survey is being executed using a dedicated mobile application that enables quick and accurate data collection. Wherever possible, existing records are being pre-filled in the app to reduce the time spent per household. Identity verification is done securely via Aadhaar authentication, protecting citizens’ personal information.
By providing reliable household-level data, the UFS will support better planning, policy-making, and implementation of welfare schemes across the State. Officials described the initiative as a major step towards transparent, responsive, and citizen-centric governance.
The government has urged all citizens to cooperate with survey staff and provide accurate information to ensure hassle-free access to welfare services. The UFS, according to a press release, underscores Andhra Pradesh’s commitment to leveraging digital technology and citizen-friendly approaches to strengthen public service delivery and improve the quality of life for every household.

title: Three blackbucks found killed by gunshots in Chikkamagaluru
summary: Three blackbucks killed by gunshots in Chikkamagaluru; investigation underway to identify the culprits.
content:
Three blackbucks were found killed by gunshots at Kallenahalli village in Kadur taluk of Chikkamagaluru on December 23.
The animals were found dead on private agricultural land close to Basur Amrit Mahal Kaval, a conservation reserve known for blackbucks. The animals, two female and one male, are reportedly below the age of two.
Upon finding the animals, locals informed forest officials. The officers visited the spot along with veterinarians. They found the pellets, confirming the gunshots that killed the animals.
Ramesh Babu, Deputy Conservator of Forests of Chikkamagaluru, toldThe Hindu,“We have conducted the postmortem and collected the samples for further examination. Further, we will register a wildlife report and hold the investigation to identify the culprits responsible for the deaths.

title: H5N1: Minister urges people to take precautions
summary: Health Minister urges precautions against H5N1 avian flu, emphasizing safety for those in contact with birds in Kerala.
content:
Health Minister Veena George has cautioned that adequate precautions be taken so that avian flu, which has been reported in some parts of Alappuzha and Kottayam districts, is not transmitted to humans.
The State-level rapid response team which  met here on Tuesday to assess the situation said though H5N1 had never been reported in humans in the State, adequate precautions were needed to protect people from becoming affected.  The department had already issued the Standard Operating Procedures as well as technical guidelines as far as avian influenza is concerned.
The State already has an army of trained One Health community health volunteers and the volunteers in Kottayam and Alappuzha will take the lead in keeping a watch in the field and reporting on any unusual circumstances that may develop as well as creating social awareness on the precautions that people need to maintain.
District-level control rooms have been set up to coordinate field-level activities. Medicines, PPE kits and other protective gear will be stocked in districts.
The department will be conducting careful fever surveillance in the areas where H5N1 has been reported and those with fever, cough , breathlessness and myalgia will be observed closely.
H5N1 can affect hens, ducks, turkey and all fowls and while the infection has not been reported in humans in the State, people who work closely with birds should take all precautions to protect themselves.
Apart from using protective gear and gloves at work, frequent hand-washing should be encouraged. Those developing fever should immediately get in touch with the health workers.
The public will be directed to report any unusual bird deaths or deaths of any mammals to the Animal Husbandry department. Till now, H5N1 has not been reported in mammalian species in Kerala. Dead birds should not be handled. Meat and eggs may be consumed well-cooked.
The department has alerted that farm workers who handle poultry meat or bird droppings manure are at high risk of contracting H5N1 and that such people should don proper masks and gloves while at work.

title: Tirupati police to turn the heat on drunk driving
summary: Tirupati police intensify efforts against drunk driving with new breathalyser kits for highway patrol teams to enhance road safety.
content:
Ministers Vangalapudi Anitha (Home), Anam Ramanarayana Reddy (Endowments) and Anagani Satya Prasad (Revenue) presented 10 breath analyser kits to each of the highway patrol police teams in Tirupati, on Tuesday.
As Tirupati district has 10 national highways and 13 State highways, the kits would be used by the patrol teams to check the motorcyclists and four-wheelers passing on the highways. Collector S. Venkateswar, Superintendent of Police (SP) L. Subbarayudu and Chandragiri MLA Pulivarthi Nani also participated in the event.
Ms. Anitha called road safety as a top priority topic of the State government, along with regulating alcohol consumption. She also called upon the youth to avoid rash driving under peer pressure.
Meanwhile, the SP said that cases would be registered against those caught driving under the influence of alcohol, and their driving licenses would stand suspended for a period of six months. “During the current year, 500 members died in road accidents and around 1,300 were injured in the district alone,” he said, attributing a larger chunk of cases to intoxication on the road.
Simultaneously, the department also identified 40 black spots and arranged barricades and signage boards to prevent accidents.

title: Jayadeva Institute installs advanced blood testing system
summary: Jayadeva Institute enhances patient care by installing the Roche Cobas Pro blood testing system for faster, accurate diagnostics.
content:
Aimed at delivering faster and more accurate diagnostic reports, the State-run Sri Jayadeva Institute of Cardiovascular Sciences and Research has installed a new-generation blood testing analyser.
The NABH-accredited institute has commissioned the Roche Cobas Pro system in its Biochemistry Department, a technology that enables high-throughput and rapid analysis of blood samples. The installation is expected to significantly reduce turnaround time for diagnostic reports at the tertiary cardiac care centre, which handles a heavy patient load every day.
Director of the institute B. Dinesh said around 1,800 to 2,000 patients undergo laboratory investigations daily at Jayadeva. “With the increasing number of patients, there is a need to enhance laboratory capacity so that reports can be delivered within the shortest possible time. This system will help us achieve that,” he said.
The Roche Cobas Pro analyser allows multiple blood tests to be conducted simultaneously and effectively doubles the laboratory’s processing capacity. The system ensures high accuracy while analysing samples in a significantly shorter time compared to conventional analysers.
Dr. Dinesh said faster availability of test results would help doctors examine more patients efficiently and improve clinical decision-making. “In emergency situations, timely access to diagnostic reports is critical. This technology will enable quicker initiation of treatment, which can be life-saving,” he said.
The installation of the advanced analyser is part of ongoing efforts to strengthen diagnostic services and improve patient care at the institute, particularly in view of the growing demand for cardiac and related investigations, Dr. Dinesh added.

title: Kerala govt. suspends Prisons DIG on corruption charges
summary: The VACB’s FIR accuses M.K. Vinod Kumar of seeking sizeable backhanders from relatives of convicts for facilitating their parole
content:
The State government has suspended Deputy Inspector General of Police (Headquarters), Prisons and Correctional Services, M.K. Vinod Kumar, on alleged corruption charges.
The office of Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan stated that the Vigilance and Anti-Corruption Bureau (VACB) had indicted Mr. Kumar last week for abusing his official position to amass illicit wealth.
The VACB’s FIR accuses Mr. Kumar of seeking sizeable backhanders from relatives of convicts for facilitating their parole. The agency alleged that Mr. Kumar also sought money to grant “criminals” special privileges in prison, including the ability to network with their associates outside.
The VACB said Mr. Kumar’s patronage network covered the Thiruvananthapuram, Kannur, and Viyyur Central prisons. Investigators said the agency would investigate whether other prison department officials benefited from the racket.
They told Mr. Kumar also threatened to set harsh conditions for convicts, including denial of parole, if their relatives did not meet the network’s demand for cash.
The VACB had registered the FIR and conducted a preliminary investigation based on several complaints received at the agency’s headquarters here from relatives of convicts and a few lawyers.
The VACB told the court that Mr. Kumar also moved some of the illegal proceeds from the corruption racket to his wife’s bank accounts via Google Pay. It was also probing Mr. Kumar’s financial transactions with other persons, including those in the latter’s department.
The government said Mr. Kumar will remain outside service until the VACB completed the probe.

title: Good response to ‘Porunai Archaeological Museum’ as over 1,600 visitors visit on day one
summary: Over 1,600 visitors flocked to the Porunai Archaeological Museum on its opening day, celebrating Tamil civilization and heritage.
content:
The huge crowd that thronged the ‘Porunai Archaeological Museum’, which was opened to the visitors on Tuesday after it was formally inaugurated by Chief Minister M.K. Stalin last Saturday, were thrilled to see the ancient Tamil civilisation and the attractively showcased artefacts.
Even though the museum was opened at 10 a.m., the crowd started gathering at 9.30 a.m. itself and the 17-minute-long audio – visual show at the museum’s mini theatre set the right tone before getting immersed into the finer details of the museum, like iron smelting interactive board, pearl fishery etc.
While the entry fee for the Indian children is ₹10, the fee for adults is ₹20 and the entry fee for the students is just ₹5. For foreigners it is ₹50 and for children the entry fee is ₹25. Those who carry cameras will have to pay an additional ₹30 and it will be ₹100 for recording the artefacts with video cameras.
Apart from this, ₹25 will be collected for enjoying the 5D ‘Ainthinai’ theatre and ₹25 for virtual reality boat simulator movements (7D).
Commanding Officer of NCC 3 TN Girls Battalion Deepak Singh Samant, a sena medalist, who was here for the past three years and one among the visitors of the archaeological museum on the maiden day, was just thrilled to revisit the ancient Tamils’ civilisation through the artefacts.
“I’ve seen this place from rubbles to this beautiful creation... Similar kind of things should be created everywhere so that the future generation will come to know the ancient civilisation and their ancestors. The technological display of artefacts kept here give more room for interaction through interactive boards which enable the visitors to understand how people made tools from iron, pottery etc. I feel blessed to visit this spot,” Mr. Deepak from Uttarakhand said.
Though the visitors have to pay the additional ₹50 for enjoying the 5D ‘Ainthinai’ and 7D boat simulator, there was roaring response from the visitors on the first day.
“It gave me such a thrilling experience as if I’m sailing in the boat.” said Yasodha of Palayamkottai after she ‘sailed’ in the boat which had been kept in the museum to tell the visitors about the ancient Tamil’s gruelling voyage to sell their priceless pearls to the Romans and the Chinese.
Most of the visitors were awestruck by the artefacts as they saw the ancient Tamil’s iron smelting technique, pearl diving, iron tools etc.
Public visiting at the Porunai Archaeological Museum in Tirunelveli on Tuesday. 
                                                            | Photo Credit: 
                                Special Arrangement
“I feel proud of being the descendent of this great civilisation... The museum will certainly pass on the rich Tamil culture and civilisation to the next generation. It is very good initiative by the Tamil Nadu Government,” said Gomathi of Palayamkottai.
The visitors gratefully recalled the archaeologists who put in their tireless efforts in excavating the artefacts of Adichanallur, Sivakalai, Korkai and Thulukkarpatti.
“We need to know our history and appreciate the archaeologists’ pain in excavating the past glory dating back to 3000 BC. Our children should know this history and this enviably civilized ancient Tamils,” John Samuel of Vallanaadu said.
The Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation, which operated 11 buses on Tuesday from Tirunelveli Junction Bus-Stand and Veinthankulam new bus-stand to the museum via Jeba Garden for every one hour, has planned to increase this frequency during the upcoming holidays.
The museum will remain closed on all Tuesdays, Republic Day, Independence Day and Gandhi Jayanthi.
District Collector R. Sukumar, who visited the museum on Tuesday, appealed to everyone coming to this part of Tamil Nadu for Christmas, New Year and Pongal holidays to visit the museum without fail to learn about the great Tamil civilisation.
“We’re now encountering tonnes of videos on tourist places, food reviews etc. on social media. I appeal to the younger generation to visit Porunai Museum and make videos of our great ancestors and their rich culture and civilization to spread it across the globe. It is our responsibility to make ‘Porunai Museum’ a must visit place,” Dr. Sukumar said.
A total of 1,674 visitors visited ‘Porunai Archaeological Museum’ on day one.

title: Naidu unveils South India Rocketry Challenge–2026 poster
summary: Naidu launches South India Rocketry Challenge 2026, promoting rocket-making skills among students in Andhra Pradesh.
content:
Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu on Tuesday unveiled the poster of the South India Rocketry Challenge–2026, aimed at nurturing rocket-making skills among school and college students. The competition is being organised for the first time under the aegis of the Science City of Andhra Pradesh, Amaravati, with the finals scheduled from January 22 to 24 at Vignan University in Guntur.
The initiative seeks to promote innovation, scientific thinking and hands-on learning, while providing a platform for students to showcase creativity and technical skills in aerospace-related fields. Interested participants can register through the Andhra Pradesh Science City website.
Officials informed the Chief Minister that the challenge will include Chemical Rocketry competitions at the college level and Hydro Rocketry competitions at the school level. Participants aged 16 years and above are eligible for the Chemical Rocketry category, while children aged 6 to 12 years can take part in the Hydro Rocketry segment.
The poster was released at the Secretariat in the presence of BC Welfare Minister B.C. Janardhan Reddy and Special Chief Secretary M.T. Krishna Babu.

title: Centre asks States to hold special gram sabhas for awareness on VB-G RAM G
summary: Centre urges States to conduct special gram sabhas by December 26 for awareness on the new VB-G RAM G Act.
content:
The Union government has written to the Chief Secretaries of all States and Union Territories, asking them to organise special gram sabha meetings to “create widespread awareness regarding key provisions and legal rights” under the newly-enacted Viksit Bharat-Guarantee for Rozgaar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB-G RAM G) Act, 2025.
The new jobs guarantee scheme, hailed by the Union government as a “historic” piece of legislation “aligned with the national vision of Viksit Bharat @ 2047”, was introduced and passed in Parliament during this Winter Session, replacing the 20-year-old MGNREGA amidst protests and objections from across Opposition parties, scholars, and activists.
On December 21, the Secretaries of the Department of Rural Development and the Ministry of Panchayati Raj jointly signed a letter to all Chief Secretaries of States and Union Territories, asking them to hold special gram sabha meetings by December 26, document the proceedings, and upload them in real-time with timestamped and geotagged photos and videos on the Panchayat Nirnay app.
The government went on to say that the Ministry of Rural Development and Panchayati Raj will “closely monitor the progress” of this effort, adding that this would ensure “effective dissemination of information and smooth transition to the new statutory framework”.
The letter from the Centre argued that the VB-G RAM G Act “aims to further strengthen rural employment, livelihood diversification, and socio-economic empowerment through a rights-based framework backed by guaranteed access to wage employment and sustainable livelihood opportunities”. The Centre further urged the States and Union Territories to ensure the “active participation” of villagers, workers, women, Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe households, and vulnerable groups.
The Bill was introduced andpassed in Parliamentthis month, and wasassented to by President Droupadi Murmulast week.
The Union government argued for the VB-G RAM G Bill in Parliament, citing deficiencies with the MGNREGA scheme, including corruption and the alleged misuse of funds by State governments. Under this new law, allocations are set to be capped within a fixed budget, which will be decided by the Union government. The “parameters” on which this will be decided have not been specified so far. Further, it provides for employment to be given only in the rural areas that the Centre notifies.
It increases the number of workdays guaranteed from 100 to 125, but it has also changed the funding pattern, raising the financial burden on States to 40% from 10% under the erstwhile MGNREGA system.
On Tuesday (December 23, 2025), the Left-affiliated All India Agricultural Workers Union (AIAWU) issued a statement, asking all its units and activists to actively participate in the special gram sabhas being called across the country and “openly reject” the new Act, adding that the AIAWU also intends to submit formal resolutions outlining their position on the VB-G RAM G Act, and calling for the restoration of MGNREGA to panchayat presidents and sarpanches across India.
Last week, after the new law was passed, Congress Parliamentary Party chairperson Sonia Gandhi issued a video statement, accusing the Prime Minister Narendra Modi-led government of trying to weaken the MGNREGA scheme throughout the last 11 years, and vowing to fight this new “black law”, which she argued was brought to “bulldoze” the jobs guarantee scheme that had become “a source of livelihood, especially for the underprivileged, exploited, poor and extremely poor people”.

title: CM seeks info on contract and outsourcing staff appointed by BRS govt.
summary: CM A. Revanth Reddy mandates departments to report on contract and outsourcing staff by January 26 amid irregularity allegations.
content:
Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy directed senior officials to furnish information pertaining to the regular, contract and outsourcing employees working in their respective departments.
The Chief Minister set January 26 deadline for the departments to submit information on employees to Chief Secretary K. Ramakrishna Rao. The directions come in the light of the uncertainty over the exact number of employees working on regular as well as temporary basis in different departments, undertakings and allied institutions.
The development assumes significance following the October 25 deadline set by the Finance department to submit information about cadre strength in each department. The direction follows allegations that the BRS government resorted to irregularities in terms of number of contract and outsourcing employees working in different departments and agencies. It was alleged that huge amounts were diverted from the State exchequer in the name of payment of salaries/wages to temporary staff.
Accordingly, a memorandum was circulated to the departments asking them to upload the details of cadre working in the respective departments in the IFIMS (Integrated Financial Management and Information System). The departments concerned will not be permitted to take up the process of claiming salary/remuneration for this month in case of failure to upload the information on the portal, the circular warned.
Though several departments are learnt to have uploaded the details, there were still reports on the leftovers whose names were not included in the IFIMS portal. The matter was brought to the notice of the Chief Minister by senior officials headed by the Chief Secretary resulting in the imposition of deadline for uploading the details.
The Chief Minister wanted the Heads of Departments to verify whether the contract and outsourcing staff were receiving the benefits of PF and ESI and submit details before the Republic Day.
The Chief Minister was firm that there should be no scope for government offices, corporations and other allied agencies to work from private/rented premises as was reported in these columns a couple of days ago.

title: Nothing special about DCM’s Delhi visit, says Karnataka Minister
summary: Karnataka Minister downplays DCM's Delhi visit as routine, hopes for clarity on leadership changes within the party.
content:
There is nothing special about Deputy Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar’s visit to New Delhi. It is a routine administrative issue. He holds two important Ministries and keeps visiting the national capital to meet Ministers and officers. It is not political, Satish Jarkiholi, Minister and Congress leader, said in Bagalkot on Tuesday.
“Karnataka is a big State with a population of seven crore and a Budget of ₹4 lakh crore. He is the Minister of two departments and the party president, so if there is work in any department, he has to go to Delhi,” he told reporters.
He said that K.N. Rajanna was a former Minister and a senior party leader. He has written a letter to Rahul Gandhi to give some information about the party, and there is nothing wrong with it. In fact, we had told him to go to New Delhi and meet the high command to present his point of view. He has met Mr. Shivakumar in Bengaluru. It is natural in a party for leaders to meet. It is also natural for some leaders to have differences of opinion, he said.
The Minister said that he hopes the party high command will end the confusion about the change of leadership in the State. The CM has made it clear several times. He has said he would act as per the high command’s wishes. He has also said there has been no agreement about power sharing, Mr. Jarkiholi said.
The CM and DCM will go to New Delhi for the Congress Working Committee on December 27, he said. The agenda in such meetings is different. It will not be about leadership issues in the State, he said in response to a query.  He said speculation about change of leadership after Sankranti were far from truth.

title: BJP A.P. chief inspects preparations for Vajpayee statue unveiling in Amaravati
summary: BJP A.P. chief inspects preparations for Vajpayee statue unveiling in Amaravati
content:
BJP Andhra Pradesh State president P. V. N. Madhav on Tuesday inspected preparations for the installation of a bronze statue of former Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee in Amaravati. The statue will be unveiled on December 25 at Atal Ji Smruti Van in Venkata Palem as part of the Atal Bihari Vajpayee centennial celebrations.
Atal Ji Smruti Van is being developed as a museum-style memorial showcasing key milestones in Vajpayee’s life and career. Mr. Madhav said the Amaravati installation would be the first Vajpayee statue in the State and would serve as a source of inspiration for future generations, highlighting his integrity, leadership, and public service.
He said Vajpayee’s ideals should guide the youth of Andhra Pradesh in working towards a developed and prosperous State. Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu, Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman, and other national and State leaders will attend the ceremony.
BJP A.P. general secretary Nagotu Ramesh Naidu said the celebrations follow the Atal Modi Supervision Yatra, which began from Dharmavaram on December 10 and has received an enthusiastic public response across the State.

title: PODA piloted by Kerala Police focuses on corporate-led drug prevention
summary: Survey reveals very high drug consumption among financially stable youth in the age group of 25-35 in Kerala
content:
In a major step towards combating drug abuse and subsequent violence among youth in Kerala, the State police department has decided to implement a novel project titled ‘Prevention of Drug Abuse’ (PODA) targeting the employed youths in private and public sectors. As part of the project, youths who enroll in private companies will have to undergo drug tests at regular intervals as suggested by the companies and police administration.
Further, at the time of joining the service (be it private or public), a mandatory pledge to abstain from drug abuse has to be signed by the candidates, along with providing consent to undergo drug testing at regular intervals as the job demands. If drug use is found during tests, disciplinary action, including dismissal, will be taken against the candidates, said State Police Chief (SPC) Ravada A. Chandrasekhar at a media briefing here on Tuesday.
In the first phase, the project will be implemented in the private sector with the cooperation of private enterprises. This scheme can also be implemented in government institutions in the next phase with the permission of the State government. The move was against the backdrop of a survey finding which revealed that the drug consumption is very high among the financially stable youth in the age group of 25-35 in Kerala.
Studies have also shown that the average age of entry into government service through the Public Service Commission (PSC) is 33 years. Since the average age of entry into the private sector is very low, 98% of the youth below the age of 30 work in the private sector. They have access to a lot of money at a young age, giving a spurt to drug abuse among the financially stable youth aged 25-35 working in the private sector, said the police.
To address this crisis, a collaborative initiative is needed, and the PODA project, a policy intervention for the private sector in India, can bring a change by adopting the initiative by the private sector, pioneering corporate-led drug prevention. The Kerala Police has already discussed the implementation of the PODA initiative in the private sector with the leaders of various private sector organisations, such as the Chamber of Commerce and Industry, G-Tech (Group of Technology Companies), FICCI, CII, YI, BNI, KMA, etc., and they have accepted it in principle. The project will be kicked off in the private sector from January 2026.
As part of a recent crackdown on the drug mafia and its supply chains, the State police have registered 30,991 cases in 2025 alone through the special drive called ‘Operation D-Hunt’. Out of which 349 cases were for seizure of commercial quantity, while 957 cases were for seizure of intermediate quantity, followed by 7,718 cases of small quantity.

title: Kishkinda University to host first convocation in Ballari today
summary: Kishkinda University celebrates its inaugural convocation in Ballari, honoring its first MBA and MCA graduates, today.
content:
The first convocation of Kishkinda University, along with the graduation ceremony of its first batch of MBA and MCA students, will be organised on the Mount View Campus in Ballari on Wednesday.
Addressing presspersons in Ballari on Tuesday, Vice-Chancellor of Kishkinda University T.N. Nagabhushan described the occasion as a milestone in the university’s academic journey, reflecting its commitment to quality, value-based and socially-oriented higher education.
Governor Thawar Chand Gehlot will deliver the convocation address. Higher Education Minister M.C. Sudhakar will be a special guest. BJP MP Jagadish Shettar, and MLAs B.M. Nagaraj and Badarli Hampanagouda will be guests of honour.
Chancellor Yashwant Bhupal said that the convocation reflects the university’s academic vision and social commitment. Sri Siddalinga Swami of Suvarnagiri Virakta Mutt will be conferred with honorary doctorate on the occasion.
MBA student Shabana and MCA student Sajja Jagati will receive gold medals for securing first ranks.

title: Samastha doesn’t support theocratic State, but advocates freedom to live as per faith: Jifri Thangal
summary: Samastha advocates religious freedom, opposing a theocratic state, during the Centenary Yatra reception in Thrissur, says Jifri Thangal.
content:
The Samastha does not stand for the idea of a theocratic State, but firmly believes that the country should ensure conditions for people to live according to their religious faith, Samastha president Sayyid Muhammed Jifri Muthu Koya Thangal has said.
He was delivering the message at a reception accorded to the Samastha Centenary Yatra in Chavakkad, Thrissur, on Tuesday as part of the campaign for the organisation’s 100th anniversary conference.
The Thangal said the Samastha would stand with all those who cooperated in protecting religion and would actively intervene in every effort aimed at the welfare of the nation. “Not a single statement against the Constitution of India has ever come from the Samastha, and it never will,” he said.
Referring to the Special Intensive Revision of elector list, he said people should be educated on safeguarding their citizenship rights. He also warned against attempts by any group to exclude or suppress others, cautioning that such moves could have serious consequences.
He said the Samastha Kerala Jam-iyyathul Ulama was not an organisation rooted only in the Muslim community, but one that had found a place in the hearts of Hindus, Christians, believers and non-believers alike. He called for vigilance against pseudo-religious movements that diluted the essence of faith.
The reception meeting was inaugurated by All India Congress Committee secretary T.N. Prathapan. Samastha district president Abdu Khader Musliyar Painkanniyoor presidied. N.K. Akbar, MLA, attended as chief guest.
Mr. Prathapan said the Samastha Centenary Message Yatra had gained added relevance at a time when constitutional values and the country’s freedom were under threat. “We live in times that seek to divide humanity in the name of religion. Attempts are being made to create fear and exploit faith for political gain. Secular Kerala will stand firm with the Samastha to defeat such forces,” he said.

title: Telangana conducts first State-level mock exercise on floods and industrial disasters
summary: Telangana government conducted its first State-level mock exercise on disaster response on Monday in coordination with the National Disaster Management Authority, focusing on preparedness for floods and industrial accidents.
content:
The Telangana government conducted its first State-level mock exercise on disaster response on Monday in coordination with the National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA), focusing on preparedness for floods and industrial accidents.
The large-scale exercise was organised in response to recent climate-related challenges faced by the State, including sudden heavy rainfall and flash floods, as well as a series of industrial accidents reported in recent years.
Based on identified flood-prone zones, the mock exercise was carried out across 12 districts including Khammam, Warangal, Kamareddy, Nizamabad, Medak, Mahabubnagar, Hyderabad, Suryapet, Bhadradri Kothagudem, Nirmal, Jayashankar Bhupalapally and Hanamkonda.
Separate drills addressing industrial disaster response were conducted in five districts including Sangareddy, Medchal-Malkajgiri, Rangareddy, Yadadri Bhuvanagiri and Nalgonda, as well as at the Rajiv Gandhi International Airport in Hyderabad.
State-level mock exercise on disaster response conducted in coordination with the National Disaster Management Authority.
                                                            | Photo Credit: 
                                By Arrangement
Officials said the primary objective of the exercise was to assess and strengthen disaster preparedness at the State and district levels, operationalise incident response systems, evaluate inter-departmental coordination and test the effectiveness of emergency support functions. The exercise also aimed at clearly defining the roles and responsibilities of the State Disaster Management Authority, Telangana Integrated Command and Control Centre, State Disaster Response Force, district collectors and other line departments.
The flood response drills improved understanding of flood risk indicators and emergency procedures, tested early warning and communication systems and helped identify operational gaps. Authorities said the exercises underlined the importance of timely evacuations, identification of safe evacuation routes and shelters, and assessed the readiness of response teams, rescue equipment and logistical support. The drills also highlighted the need for better coordination between agencies, enhanced community awareness, and regular training to maintain preparedness and confidence among responders.
The industrial accident mock exercises provided key insights into the importance of mutual aid among neighbouring industries during emergencies such as fires and chemical leaks. The drills tested standard operating procedures for chemical incidents, fire outbreaks and power failures, while improving awareness of on-site emergency procedures among employees and contract workers. They also assessed alarm and communication systems, evacuation protocols, assembly points and the condition of emergency equipment.
Officials noted that the exercises reinforced the need for stronger coordination with external agencies such as fire services, police and medical teams, and helped management review and strengthen both on-site and off-site emergency plans.

title: RoV study at Mullaperiyar to assess  structural integrity of dam
summary: Underwater RoV inspection at Mullaperiyar dam begins to assess structural integrity and address concerns about potential weaknesses.
content:
An underwater inspection using a remotely operated vehicle (RoV) began at the Mullaperiyar dam in Idukki on Tuesday to assess the  structural integrity of the dam.
According to sources, the inspection is being conducted on the dam’s waterfront portion to determine its strength.
The inspection of the 1,200-ft-long structure is being carried out in 100-metre segments. After each 100-metre section is inspected, the dam’s width will be further divided into 50-metre intervals for a more detailed ROV sweep.
Finally, the middle portion of the dam will be divided into 10-metre sections to collect high-resolution images of the waterfront area.
Sources said earlier studies conducted by the Kerala government had found that the lime-surki mortar and cement mix had eroded, leaving stones visible at a depth of 110 ft.
The ROV study was being conducted following a directive from the Supreme Court. The research was being led by experts from the Central Soil and Materials Research Station, Delhi, using an ROV brought from France.

title: Fact-finding panel on damage of checkdams seeks early completion of probe, action against culprits
summary: Fact-finding panel on damage of checkdams seeks early completion of probe, action against culprits
content:
HYDERABAD
A fact-finding committee comprising retired engineers, professors and others, which visited Tanugula and Adavi Somanpally checkdams following their damage in the alleged blasts, has demanded that the police take stern action against those responsible for the damage after completing their inquiry at the earliest.
The committee said in its report that excessive sand mining would also damage the checkdams. The stay on sand mining in the Manair river imposed by the National Green Tribunal was vacated by the State Government by appealing against the tribunal order in the Supreme Court.
They further requested the police department to complete the investigation into the complaints on blasts at Medigadda barrage of the Kaleshwaram project, Hussainmia checkdam and the recent incidents of Tanugula and Adavi Somanpally checkdams. They also appealed to Minister for Irrigation N. Uttam Kumar Reddy to restore the last two checkdams before the rainy season to bring them back into use.
The fact-finding committee comprising Prof. Seetarama Rao, Prof. Raghava Reddy, V. Prakash, Damodar Reddy, Sridhar Rao Deshpande, Pittala Ravinder and others visited Tanugula checkdam site in Jammikunta mandal of Karimnagar district that was allegedly blasted on the night of November 21. About 90 meters of the 737 meters checkdam was damaged in the blast causing a loss of ₹3.5 crore.
The check dam constructed with ₹23 crore was irrigating 1,000 acres in Tanugula, Gumpula and Shambhunipally village and rejuvenating/recharging the borewells in a 5-km radius to ensure farmers irrigate two crops a year. The checkdam structure withstood 66,000 cusecs of flood released from Lower Manair Dam during the flood season this year, the committee explained.
The team visited the Adavi Somanpally checkdam, which was blasted on December 17, on December 20 and found the debris still lying on the checkdam structure as it was in case of Tanugula and it was possible only in case of a blast and washing away would generally carry the debris downstream.

title: Naidu directs hassle-free paddy procurement, warns of strict action against units harming mango farmers
summary: Naidu emphasises streamlined paddy procurement and warns of strict actions against those harming mango farmers in Andhra Pradesh.
content:
Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu on Tuesday directed the Agriculture and Horticulture Departments to prepare a comprehensive crop calendar covering Kharif–Rabi–Kharif seasons to maximise benefits for farmers. He said harvesting and marketing activities must be aligned with the calendar to ensure better returns to cultivators.
Reviewing paddy procurement and the marketing of various crop produce at a meeting held at the Secretariat, the Chief Minister asked officials to create awareness among farmers about suitable crops for each season, with a focus on quality improvement and proper guidance during harvesting. Ministers K. Atchannaidu and Nadendla Manohar participated in the review virtually.
Mr. Naidu called for strengthening cold chain infrastructure, improving access to domestic and international markets and encouraging processing of agricultural produce. He also suggested optimal use of logistics facilities, including rail cargo, for transporting farm produce across markets in the country.
Directing officials to complete paddy procurement within stipulated timelines in all districts, the Chief Minister addressed bank guarantee-related issues in North Andhra districts by speaking directly to the State Level Bankers’ Committee Convener during the review. He instructed banks to provide uniform bank guarantees across the State so that farmers do not face inconvenience. Emphasising the Speed of Delivering Governance approach, he warned millers against any irregularities in procurement.
Despite financial constraints, the State government has extended ₹184 crore in subsidies to support mango farmers and is paying an additional ₹4 per kg, a benefit not offered by any other State, the Chief Minister said. He urged pulp processing units to act responsibly and support farmers, warning of strict action against anyone deliberately causing losses to mango growers.
Mr. Naidu directed District Collectors to resolve farmers’ grievances within 10 days. He pointed out that farmers in Karnataka and Tamil Nadu are compelled to sell mangoes at prevailing market prices, while Andhra Pradesh is providing incentives to protect its growers. The government, he said, is working to develop a strong ecosystem for Totapuri mango farmers by bringing in more food processing units and has instructed officials to organise a horticulture products exhibition in January.

title: Rahul Gandhi’s leadership now being questioned within Congress and among allies: BJP
summary: BJP questions Rahul Gandhi's leadership amid claims of "anti-national" remarks, losing support from Congress allies and insiders.
content:
TheBharatiya Janata Party (BJP)on Tuesday (December 23, 2025) claimed that questions overRahul Gandhi’s leadership were no longer confined to the electorate but were also being raised from within his own party and among its allies. This is why the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha has gone abroad to make “anti-national” remarks, alleged BJP spokesperson Shehzad Poonawalla
At a press conference, Mr. Poonawalla targeted Mr. Gandhi over his “vote theft” charges made in the run-up to last month’s Bihar Assembly election. “[Congress leader] Shashi Tharoor ji has already gone on record saying that in the past 20 years, the NDA government has done very good work in Bihar. Meaning, he has completely defused Rahul Gandhi’s ‘vote-theft’ narrative,” he said.
ALSO WATCHWatch: Rahul Gandhi’s Berlin remarks trigger political storm, leaders across parties react
Mr. Poonawalla alleged that Communist Party of India (Marxist) MP John Brittas recently remarked that Mr. Gandhi should not have left Parliament and gone abroad. “He made an even bigger disclosure: not only the Left party, but even the DMK was against Rahul Gandhi’s ‘India-bashing’ journey, and he said that Rahul Gandhi does not take his work seriously,” the BJP leader claimed.
He added that Congress MP Imran Masood had backed Mr. Gandhi’s sister and fellow MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra as a potential Prime Minister. “And this was endorsed even by [her husband] Robert Vadra,” Mr. Poonawalla said.
“This means public opinion has already moved away from Rahul Gandhi. From the Left to [Jammu & Kashmir Chief Minister] Omar Abdullah, who rejected Rahul Gandhi’s statements, [NCP (SP) leader] Supriya Sule, Samajwadi Party, Trinamool Congress, all reject everything he says... He now has neither public mandate, nor organisational backing,” Mr. Poonawalla said.
The BJP leader claimed that, a few days ago, Odisha Congress leader Mohammed Moquim had raised questions about the leadership of Mr. Gandhi and Congress chief Mallikarjun Kharge. “Immediately, a ‘fatwa’ was issued by the Rahul Gandhi faction of the Congress party to expel Mohammed Moquim,” said the BJP leader, adding that “even his own allies, family members, and party members are passing one no-confidence motion after another against Rahul Gandhi”.
“And that is why, when Rahul Gandhi lost the public, the organisation, and now perhaps has no support even in the party structure, he once again went abroad to vent his anger against the BJP, and started speaking against the country instead. Once again, he has started anti-India rhetoric, in opposition to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, the people, and their mandate,” said Mr. Poonawalla.
ALSO WATCHWatch: BJP proposing the elimination of the Indian Constitution, claims Rahul Gandhi
Alleging that the ‘Indian National Congress’ had become the ‘Anti-National Congress’, the BJP leader countered Mr. Gandhi’s statement made in Berlin regarding concerns about electronic voting machines, India’s electoral process, the Maharashtra and Haryana polls, and the country’s manufacturing capability. “Why does Rahul Gandhi love China so much? Is it donations, MOUs, or propaganda?” he asked.
In another statement to the media on Mr. Gandhi’s remarks in Germany, BJP spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari accused him of having an “anti-national” mindset, claiming that speaking against the country had become Mr. Gandhi’s policy, intent, and habit.

title: Kuki groups resolve to stop poppy cultivation in Manipur’s Kangpokpi
summary: Kuki groups in Manipur commit to ending poppy cultivation by 2026 to address ethnic conflict and promote community welfare.
content:
Civil society organisations belonging to the Kuki community have resolved to halt poppy cultivation across Manipur’s Kangpokpi district from January 1, 2026.
The resolution by these organisations, including the Kuki Inpi Sadar Hills and the Sadar Hills Chiefs’ Association, is considered significant as poppy cultivation is perceived to be one of the factors contributing to the ethnic animosity in Manipur since May 2023.
More than 260 people have been killed and 62,000 others displaced after the ethnic conflict between the tribal Kuki-Zo and the non-tribal Meitei communities broke out more than two years ago. The State, under President’s Rule since February 13, is yet to recover from the impact of the violence.
In a joint statement issued on Tuesday (December 23, 2025), the civil society organisations said three rounds of meetings were held on December 10, 16, and 19 to resolve against poppy cultivation in Kangpokpi.
“Across all these meetings, every participating organisation and village chief unanimously pledged and committed that poppy cultivation will be completely discontinued in their respective jurisdictions from 2026 onwards,” the statement read.
It said that the decision was taken by the organisations in Kangpokpi district “in the larger public interest, keeping in view the social, environmental, economic, and moral consequences of poppy cultivation, and reflects the collective will of the people”.
The organisations warned that “any village chief or authority found violating or failing to comply with the resolutions adopted during these public consultations would face strict and decisive action”.
Some Meitei organisations welcomed the decision, but noted that it was an acknowledgement that people across the Kuki-dominated landscape have been involved in poppy cultivation. Kuki extremist groups, which signed the Suspension of Operations agreement with the Centre in 2008, allegedly run the poppy plantations.
The poppy plant produces opium and its derivatives, including morphine, codeine, heroin, and oxycodone.
According to a report by Manipur Remote Sensing Applications Centre in December 2024, the Manipur Police and other law enforcement agencies destroyed illegal poppy cultivation on 19,135.6 acres across 12 districts of the State between 2017 and January 2024.
Kangpokpi district topped the list with 4,454.4 acres of poppy plantations destroyed, followed by Ukhrul district with 3,348 acres, and Churachandpur with 2,713.8 acres. In the past few weeks, the security forces destroyed poppy plantations on at least 559 acres in these districts.
Meanwhile, the Kuki Inpi Manipur (KIM), the apex body of Kukis in the the State, called for the solemn observance of Christmas for the third successive year, given the “unprecedented period of suffering and uncertainty” for the people.
“Christmas carries a profound message of hope, peace and divine light, especially during moments of deep pain and uncertainty. Despite immense adversity, the people have remained steadfast in faith and in the belief that justice and peace will ultimately prevail,” KIM president C. Ajang Khongsai said.

title: GBA to audit rejected e-khata applications after employees protest
summary: GBA to audit rejected e-khata applications following protests over suspensions, addressing citizen complaints and potential corruption issues.
content:
The Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA) Chief Commissioner M. Maheshwar Rao on Tuesday announced an audit of e-khata rejections following complaints from citizens that their applications were turned down despite submitting all required documents.
The review, the GBA chief said, would examine whether e-khatas were being denied without valid reasons.
“The government introduced e-khata to simplify the process for citizens. Any hurdles faced by the public in obtaining these documents will be addressed,” Mr. Rao said.
The announcement came amid protests by the GBA Municipal Officers’ and Employees’ Welfare Association, who held a candlelight vigil against the suspension of two officials- Deputy Commissioner of Bommanahalli Zone D.K. Babu and revenue officer Varalakshmi. The officials were suspended by Special Commissioner (Revenue) Munish Moudgil, reportedly for dereliction of duty in issuing e-khatas.
However, sources said that the suspensions came in the wake of several cases where e-khata applications have been rejected without valid reasons, causing inconvenience to the public. Such rejections run into thousands, the sources said.
There has been a tug of war between the revenue officers on the ground and the top GBA leadership over e-khata issues. While citizens and senior GBA officials attribute several rejections to corruption, revenue officers on the ground said they were being targeted by an impractical system. Efforts to remove subjectivity from the system have been opposed.
The association president A. Amrut Raj said, “Revenue employees were being harassed by   Special Commissioner (Revenue) Munish Moudgil, even as they remain overburdened with khata-related work.” He said the association had raised the issue with the GBA Chief Commissioner and demanded that the suspensions be revoked. He added that employees were considering mass leave and work stoppages if their concerns were ignored.
Mr. Moudgil was not available for comment. Mr. Rao, responding to the grievances, assured that he would look into the concerns raised by the employees.

title: KCR responsible for injustice on Krishna waters: BJP
summary: KCR responsible for injustice on Krishna waters: BJP
content:
Hyderabad
Vedire Sriram, former advisor to the Union Ministry of Water Resources and Adviser to the government of Maharashtra, held former Chief Minister K. Chandrasekhar Rao responsible for ‘injustice’ to the farmers of TG regarding Krishna waters.
In a PowerPoint presentation on Krishna water sharing between Telangana and AP, he said that true justice for Telangana regarding river water was possible only through the new Tribunal established by the Central Government.
Later, BJP State president N. Ramchander Rao rebutted the allegations made by KCR against the BJP and the Central government regarding Krishna River water, including the Palamuru-Rangareddy Lift Irrigation Scheme (PRLIS).
He accused KCR of using Telangana sentiments again for political gain after keeping silent for years. KCR’s attempts to insult the central government with deceitful propaganda and derogatory terms will not mask his failures, he said. KCR’s goal is to play “sentiment politics” without placing the actual facts before the people.
Mr. Rao described KCR as an ‘OTP’ politician, which is relevant only for one-time use. By speaking about Telangana sentiments after betraying State’s interests, he has no takers, he said.

title: PG medical: Provisional results of second round announced
summary: Provisional results for the second round of PG medical seat allotment announced; candidates can withdraw documents by Wednesday.
content:
The provisional seat allotment results of the second round for postgraduate medical courses have been announced.
Candidates who have been allotted seats through Medical Counselling Committee (MCC) are permitted to withdraw their original documents till Wednesday at 11 a.m., said H. Prasanna, Executive Director of the Karnataka Examinations Authority (KEA).
A total of 3,164 candidates have been allotted seats in this round, and the list has been published on the official website.
After the release of the provisional results, candidates who have secured seats through MCC but do not prefer those seats may withdraw from their KEA-allotted seats by submitting their original documents. In such cases, ₹25,000 will be deducted from the fees already paid. After 11 a.m. on Wednesday, excluding those who have withdrawn their original documents, fresh seat allotment would be carried out and the final results would be announced, he said.
Regarding admission to postgraduate medical courses, the final results of the second round of seat allotment for in-service candidates have also been announced. Candidates who have paid the fees must submit their original documents at the KEA office by December 24. Thereafter, they should download their admission order and report to the allotted colleges by December 26, he explained.
A total of 59 in-service candidates have been allotted seats in various courses, he added.

title: Fire breaks out at commercial complex in Kumarapuram
summary: A suspected short circuit from a generator is said to be the cause
content: A fire broke out at a private commercial complex in Kumarapuram here on Tuesday due to a suspected short circuit from a generator, triggering panic among the people in the vicinity. The fire broke out on the third floor of Xavier Street Food Café in the evening. The fire tenders rushed to the spot from the Chakkai fire station doused the fire, and brought the situation under control. The officials also confirmed that no major damage occurred to the building other than around 200 sq ft area on the third floor where the fire broke out.

title: Bhatti Vikramarka slams KCR over his ‘we will skin’ remarks against Congress government, vows to make Singareni a global enterprise
summary: SCCL, khammam, bhatti
content:
Deputy Chief Minister Mallu Bhatti Vikramarka on Tuesday slammed BRS president and former Chief Minister K. Chandrasekhar Rao for his reported ‘we will skin’ remarks against the Congress government, saying that the latter was speaking in a ‘derogatory manner’.
He was addressing a public meeting at Pinapaka village in Thallada mandal of Khammam district.
Earlier in the day, he laid foundation stones for three new electricity substations.
Reacting sharply to Mr. Rao’s remarks against the Congress dispensation, he said that people of the State have reposed their faith in the party by electing Congress-backed candidates in 85% of the total seats in the recent Gram Panchayat polls. This is because of the Congress government’s welfare schemes rendering concrete benefits to all sections of people, he added.
Instead of appreciating the welfare programmes, KCR chose to speak about ‘skinning’, which is completely inappropriate on his part, Mr Vikramarka said.
He said, “Congress does not stoop to such language. Through public welfare programmes, the BRS leaders will be taught a lesson.”
Mr Vikramarka questioned why KCR, the leader of the Opposition, did not attend the Assembly even for a single day in the last two years. Why is KCR so afraid of the Assembly? he asked.
“A person who does not come to the Assembly, does he even deserve the post of Leader of the Opposition,” he said.
He said, “Telangana is rising, and leaders from across the country and big industrialists are coming to the State and praising the government. Unable to digest this, KCR came out after two years, made baseless allegations against the State government and then went back to his farmhouse.”
“It is ultimately the people who will teach him a lesson,” he added.
Later, he inaugurated the Singareni Collieries Company Limited (SCCL)’s GM’s office in Sathupalli and also inspected the JVR opencast project-II.
He said that SCCL will participate in a joint venture with the Rajasthan government for the production of 1,500 MW of solar power. The SCCL is expanding on multiple fronts apart from its core coal production to thermal power, solar power, pumped storage, rare earth minerals and critical minerals.
Congratulating the Singarenians on the occasion of Singareni Foundation Day, he said, “The State government, through SCCL, is formulating plans to compete for and secure blocks for lithium, graphite and copper as well. The State government is striving to ensure that SCCL, with its 136-year-old legacy, grows into a global enterprise.”
He said, “Global tenders were floated and expert advice was taken on which countries and states Singareni could enter, and on steps needed to ensure a bright future for Telangana. The SCCL has become a partner by securing tenders for gold and copper mining in Karnataka.”

title: BJP leaders to meet Governor on hate speech Bill
summary: BJP leaders plan to meet Governor to oppose the Karnataka Hate Speech Bill, citing concerns over free speech rights.
content:
The Opposition BJP has decided to take a delegation of its leaders to Governor Thaawarchand Gehlot to appeal to him to desist from giving his consent to the Karnataka Hate Speech and Hate Crimes (Prevention) Bill, 2025, that was adopted in the Winter Session of the State Legislature held recently in Belagavi.
Announcing this while participating in a protest being staged by the party in front of tahsildar’s office in Shikaripura of Shivamogga district against the Bill, BJP State president B. Y. Vijayendra said the party delegation would be taken out to the Raj Bhavan next week.
The BJP staged protests against the Bill in different parts of the State on Tuesday and petitioned the district and taluk magistrates against the Bill. In Bengaluru, such petitions were also submitted to the Governor and the Chief Minister through the Deputy Commissioner.
The protesters termed the Bill as anti-democratic and being opposed to the provisions of freedom of speech.

title: Speaker examining linking the release of MLAs’ development grants to their legislature attendance
summary: Speaker U.T. Khader proposes linking MLAs’ development grants to attendance, aiming to improve legislative participation and accountability.
content:
Taking serious note of the trend of thin attendance of MLAs in the Assembly in the last several legislative sessions, Speaker U.T. Khader is considering a proposal to recommend to the government to cut the MLAs’ local area development grants if they fail to meet a minimum of 70 per cent attendance.
“It is the duty of MLAs to attend the legislature session and represent the people of their constituency as well as that of the State. It is not good on their part to abstain from the legislature,” Mr. Khader toldThe Hinduafter the Winter Session of the State legislature that was held recently in Belagavi.
The speaker confirmed that already a round of consultations with the government had been held on the proposal to link the release of local area development grants of MLAs with their legislature attendance.
It may be noted that even in the just concluded session of the legislature, the Assembly witnessed thin attendance of members. In fact, there were days when hardly 60 to 70 MLAs turned up at the session in the 224-member House.
While there are concerns about declining standards in the legislature debates, the absence of members is viewed more seriously, as the presence of members is crucial to improving the legislature debates and finding solutions to various problems gripping the State.
Sources in the legislature secretariat made it clear that the main intention of examining the proposal to link the release of grant of local area development grants to MLAs’ attendance in legislature was not to punish the legislators, but to discourage them from abstaining from the session and also to remind them that it is their primary duty to attend the session.
The MLAs, irrespective of political affiliations, get an annual local area development fund of ₹2 crore that can be used as per their discretion for the development of their constituency. Perhaps considering the importance of these funds, the Speaker may be thinking of linking their release to attendance.
Meanwhile, former Law and Parliamentary Affairs Minister S. Suresh Kumar underscored the importance of legislators attending the legislature session promptly. “The very nomenclature -- legislator -- indicates that the main role of the legislators is to legislate. To do that, they need to attend the legislature session,” Mr. Suresh Kumar toldThe Hindu.
