He urged all the MPs from Karnataka to raise their voice in favor of Mr. Roshan.
He said he would speak to the police commissioner about the issue of police not acting against a POCSO accused in rural Belagavi. “I believe that the police should not yield to political pressure, especially in POCSO cases. They should take the necessary legal action, including filing a POCSO case. I have read about the case in the media. I will ask the police to act strictly,” he said.
He said that the CM Siddaramaiah would take the final decision on the division of Belagavi district.
“The State Cabinet has already approved the project for the construction of the much-awaited flyover in Belagavi, which will be approximately 2.03 km long from National Highway 48 to Dharmaveer Sambhaji Circle. There is no need to acquire land anywhere for this project. We have decided to extend this project up to the 3rd Gate of Belagavi. This project will reduce traffic congestion in the city and facilitate smooth movement,” he said.

title: MP seeks IIM for Tirupati
summary: MP Maddila Gurumoorthy urges the Centre to establish an IIM in Tirupati to enhance local education and regional development.
content:
Member of Parliament (MP-Tirupati) Maddila Gurumoorthy on Wednesday (December 24) requested the Centre to establish an Indian Institute of Management (IIM) in Tirupati, which has already emerged into an academic hub.
In a letter addressed to Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan, he said an IIM would strengthen public higher education in Tirupati and promote balanced regional development.
“An IIM in Tirupati would significantly enhance access to high-quality management education for local students, particularly those from rural and economically weaker backgrounds, by reducing the need to relocate to distant metropolitan centres,” said Mr. Gurumoorthy in the letter.
He also requested the Minister to undertake a detailed feasibility study for establishing an IIM-level management institute in Tirupati and allocate the required land, financial support and resources for infrastructure development, faculty recruitment and academic programmes.

title: Youth must contribute to building a prosperous nation, says Governor
summary: Governor Thaawarchand Gehlot urges students to leverage education for national progress and uphold cultural values for a prosperous India.
content:
Governor Thaawarchand Gehlot has called upon students to play an active role in building a prosperous and self-reliant nation, describing education as a continuous journey and a nation’s most valuable asset.
He was speaking at the first convocation of Kishkinda University on Mount View campus on Ballari-Siruguppa Road on Wednesday.
Mr. Gehlot said that education should not be confined to the mere acquisition of degree certificates but it should serve as a means to acquiring knowledge and shaping a bright future.
Students must use their learning for the progress of the country, he added.
The Governor emphasised that along with intellectual growth, it is equally important for youth to imbibe human values. Indian tradition imparts cultural and moral values and it is the responsibility of students to carry this legacy forward, he said.
Quoting Swami Vivekananda’s exhortation, “Arise, awake and stop not till the goal is reached”, he urged students to translate knowledge into action and use their skills to help India emerge as a developed nation.
Higher Education Minister M.C. Sudhakar said that establishing educational institutions in regions such as Kalyana Karnataka is challenging and described it as a matter of pride that the university has completed two years successfully.
He said that while the State has 29 private universities, the focus must remain on maintaining academic quality with special emphasis on research and innovation rather than merely increasing enrolment.
During the event, a honorary doctorate was conferred on Siddalinga Swami of the Suvarnagiri Virakta Mutt, Ballari.
Legislators B.M. Nagaraj and Badarli Hampannagouda; Tungabhadra Education Health and Rural Development (TEHRD) Chairman S.J.V. Mahipal, Kishkinda University Chancellor Yashwant Bhoopal, Vice-Chancellor T.N. Nagabhushan, Pro-Chancellor Y.J. Prithviraj were present.

title: Six arrested as excise officials seize over 2.7 kg ganja in Dhoolpet and Secunderabad
summary: Six arrested in Hyderabad as excise officials seize over 2.7 kg of ganja during separate operations in Dhoolpet and Secunderabad.
content:
Six persons were arrested in separate operations carried out by the State Task Force (STF) of the Telangana Excise and Prohibition Department in Hyderabad on Wednesday (December 24), seizing 2.718 kilograms of ganja.
The largest seizure was made in Dhoolpet, where STF-A team booked two cases and recovered 2.466 kilograms of ganja.
Following a tip-off, the team conducted raids at two locations linked to alleged ganja sales. In the first case, the police raided an area near Shiva Mandir in Dhoolpet and seized 1.212 kilograms of ganja. Rajesh was arrested in connection with the case, while another accused, Abhishek Singh, remains at large.
A raid was then carried out at a house, leading to the seizure of 1.254 kilograms of the banned substance. Malabai and Kripal Singh were arrested, while Baldev Singh is absconding. Both cases have been handed over to the Dhoolpet police station for further investigation.
In a separate operation, following a tip-off about ganja consumption in the area, STF-B team conducted a raid near the Blue Sea Hotel in Secunderabad  and seized 252 grams of ganja.
Three persons, identified as Binesh, Pawan and Narsar, were arrested, while another accused, Ghaus Pasha, is absconding.
Four mobile phones were also seized from the accused. They were handed over to the Marredpally excise station for further investigation.

title: Rahul Gandhi meets Unnao rape survivor, says 'we're turning into dead society'
summary: Rahul Gandhi meets Unnao rape survivor, condemning her ill-treatment and highlighting societal failings in justice for victims.
content:
Congress leader Rahul Gandhi met the Unnao rape survivor in New Delhi on Wednesday (December 24, 2025) after she allegedly faced ill-treatment and said India is not just becoming a dead economy but also a dead society.
Rahul Gandhi met the rape survivor at his mother Sonia Gandhi's 10, Janpath residence after the woman staged a protested in Delhi against the bail granted by the high court to the accused in the case, expelled BJP leader Kuldeep Singh Sengar.
The Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha separately said the rape survivor should be treated with respect and that justice should be ensured to her, instead of giving her injustice and fear.
"Is such treatment of a gang rape survivor appropriate? Is it her 'fault' that she has the courage to raise her voice for justice? 	"The fact that her perpetrator (former BJP MLA Sengar) has been granted bail is extremely disappointing and shameful -- especially when the survivor is being repeatedly harassed and is living under the shadow of fear," Mr. Gandhi said in a post in Hindi onX.
क्या एक गैंगरेप पीड़िता के साथ ऐसा व्यवहार उचित है?क्या उसकी "गलती" ये है कि वो न्याय के लिए अपनी आवाज़ उठाने की हिम्मत कर रही है?उसके अपराधी (पूर्व BJP MLA) को ज़मानत मिलना बेहद निराशाजनक और शर्मनाक है - खासकर तब, जब पीड़िता को बार-बार प्रताड़ित किया जा रहा हो, और वो डर के…https://t.co/BZqrVNXMOy
"Bail for rapists and treating survivors like criminals -- what kind of justice is this? We are not just becoming a dead economy — with such inhuman incidents, we are also turning into a dead society," he added.
Mr. Gandhi said in a democracy, raising a voice of dissent is a right and suppressing it is a crime. "The survivor deserves respect, safety and justice -- not helplessness, fear and injustice," he asserted.
The 2017 Unnao rape survivor on Wednesday (December 24) termed the Delhi High Court's decision to suspend the jail term of Sengar "kaal (death)" for her family and said she would move the Supreme Court against the order.
The rape survivor and her mother staged a protest near Mandi House here against the court verdict granting bail to Sengar.
In its order, the high court directed that Sengar shall not come within a five-kilometre radius of the victim's residence and threaten the survivor or her mother. It also said a violation of the conditions would automatically lead to the cancellation of his bail.
Sengar, however, will remain in jail as he is also serving a 10-year term in connection with the custodial death of the rape survivor's father and has not been granted bail in that case.
The survivor was a minor when she was kidnapped and raped by Sengar in 2017.

title: DIET student ‘ends life’ in Vizianagaram
summary: DIET student ‘ends life’ in Vizianagaram
content:
A 22-year-old second-year student at the District Institute of Education and Training (DIET) in Venugopalapuram of Vizianagaram district, died by suicide in the early hours of Wednesday.​
Koneti Mahesh, a resident of Jilleduvalasa in Saluru mandal of Parvatipuram-Manyam district, was found dead in the reading room adjacent to his hostel. A suicide note reportedly cited psychological distress and family problems as reasons for the extreme step, according to Vizianagaram rural police station house officer Ashok Kumar.​
DIET in-charge principal Appala Naidu alerted the police, who arranged a post-mortem at Vizianagaram Government General Hospital.Those in distress can contact helpline 100.

title: National Consumer Day observed in Kurnool college
summary: National Consumer Day in Kurnool highlights consumer rights awareness, featuring insights from District Consumer Protection Forum secretary Vishnu Mohan Reddy.
content: District Consumer Protection Forum secretary Vishnu Mohan Reddy on Wednesday (December 24) stressed the need for every consumer to know their rights and to question when they are denied. He was speaking at a National Consumer Day event jointly organised by the economics and commerce departments of Silver Jubilee College here. Mr. Vishnu Mohan said that December 24 is observed as National Consumer Day to spread awareness among the people about consumer rights. A consumer has right to learn about the product and give feedback.

title: Six-year-old Bharatanatyam prodigy to perform in Hubballi on Sunday
summary: Six-year-old Bharatanatyam prodigy Kumari Poorna Pawar will debut in Hubballi at the Prathama Pallava recital on Sunday.
content:
Kala Sujaya, a centre for Indian classical arts, is organising a Bharatanatyam dance recital titled Prathama Pallava by Kumari Poorna Pawar, a six-year-old dance enthusiast, at Sawai Gandharva Hall at 5.30 p.m. on Sunday.
Addressing presspersons in Hubballi on Wednesday, founder of Kala Sujaya Sujay Shanbhag said that despite her tender age, Kumari Poorna Pawar will present a two-hour debut solo Bharatanatyam performance.
The budding artiste has also been acclaimed as a budding star by Ananya Trust, a prestigious dance institution in Bengaluru, he said.
As part of the recital, Kumari Poorna Pawar will receive the Guru’s blessings in the form of Gejje, symbolising her readiness to perform before an audience, Sujay Shanbhag said.

title: JD(U) seeks special police vigil on Tejashwi Yadav’s alleged aides
summary: JD(U) demands Bihar Police monitor alleged aides of Tejashwi Yadav on foreign trip, citing criminal backgrounds and history-sheets.
content:
The ruling Janata Dal (United) on Wednesday (December 24, 2025) demanded that the Bihar Police take “special vigil” over the activities of history-sheeters and alleged close aides of Leader of the Opposition Tejashwi Yadav of the Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD), who are claimed to be accompanying him on his current foreign trip.
In a one-page letter addressed to the Bihar Director General of Police, JD(U) MLC and party chief spokesperson Neeraj Kumar urged special monitoring of the activities of Ramiz Nemat Khan and Dewa Gupta, who he alleged were close aides of Mr. Yadav and were accompanying him on the foreign visit.
Following his party’s poor performance in the recently concluded Assembly elections, Mr. Yadav reportedly went on a foreign trip. He was also not present during the five-day Winter Session of the State Legislature, which concluded on December 5, 2025. The RJD won 25 seats in the 243-member Assembly, while the Bharatiya Janata Party the JD(U) secured 89 and 85 seats respectively.
“It was during ongoing winter session of State legislature on December 5, 2025, it came to my knowledge through media that hon’ble Leader of Opposition Tejashwi Yadav has gone on a foreign trip along with history-sheeter Ramiz Nemat Khan who hails from Uttar Pradesh’s Balrampur (now Shravasti) district and was, earlier in 2021, arrested in a murder case along with his wife, father-in-law and others,” Mr. Kumar alleged in the letter.
Mr. Kumar also mentioned that Mr. Khan’s wife, Zeba Rizwan, had contested the Tulsipur Assembly election while in jail but lost the election.
In the letter, Mr. Kumar further said that the “possibility of another history-sheeter accompanying Mr. Yadav on his foreign trip cannot be ruled out”. He named Dewa Gupta of Motihari in East Champaran district, whose name, he said, was included among the top 100 criminals of the district.
“It is being said that total 28 serious criminal cases including murder, extortion and land grabbing are lodged against Deva Gupta, son of Hari Kishore Gupta of Chhatauni Chowk of Motihari town and a reward of ₹1,00,000 has also been announced on him,” Mr. Kumar stated in the letter. Mr. Gupta had contested the 2025 Assembly election on an RJD ticket from the Motihari Sadar constituency but lost to BJP candidate Pramod Kumar.
“You’re requested to take cognisance of above mentioned facts and keep strict vigil on people with criminal background who allegedly have gone on foreign trip along with Leader of Opposition Tejashwi Yadav,” Mr. Kumar concluded in his letter to the State police chief.

title: Navi Mumbai court convicts two Bangladeshi nationals for illegal stay in India
summary: Navi Mumbai court convicts two Bangladeshis for illegal stay in India, ordering their deportation after a brief sentence.
content:
A court in Maharashtra’s Navi Mumbai has convicted two Bangladeshi nationals for entering and staying in India without valid passports.
In his order of December 11, a copy of which was made available on Tuesday (December 24, 2025), Additional Sessions Judge (Belapur) C V Marathe, however, did not accept the prosecution’s allegation of forgery of identity documents.
During the trial, Additional Public Prosecutor Sandhya Mhatre told the court that Haidar Ali Ashraf Ali (29) and Fatima Gofar Shaikh (34) were arrested in January this year from Koprigaon, Sector 26, for residing without any valid travel documents or legal permits for their stay in India.
Ali was also alleged to have produced a forged Aadhaar card during the investigation.
The court said the two violated “Rule 5 of The Passport (Entry Into India) Rules, 1950” by residing in India without valid papers.
While the prosecution argued that illegal stays by foreign nationals pose “potential threats to the safety and security of our nation”, the defence said the accused were “poor and illiterate” and had entered India solely for “livelihood without any ill-intention”.
“It is not the prosecution case that the accused persons are involved in any anti-social activities after entering into India without valid passport. They have no criminal antecedents,” the court said.
The court awarded a sentence of 11 months and a fine of Rs 500 to each of the convicted persons. Since the two had been in custody since January 14, 2025 (a period of 10 months and 27 days), the court granted a “set off” for the time already served.
It also directed the Navi Mumbai police chief to take steps for their deportation to Bangladesh through the Bangladesh Embassy.

title: Tribal deities Pagididda Raju, Govinda Raju installed on new platforms at Medaram Sammakka-Sarakka shrine
summary: Medaram jatara
content:
MULUGU
In accordance with tribal traditions, the deities Pagididda Raju and Govinda Raju have been installed on newly constructed Gadde (sacred platforms) at the Medaram Sammakka-Sarakka shrine on Wednesday. Koya priests (known as Vaddes) reinstalled Govinda Raju first, followed by Pagididda Raju, at a ceremony in the morning in the presence of tribals mainly from the clans of Govinda Raju and Pagididda Raju, accompanied by drumbeats and traditional dances.
The ceremony was attended by local MLA and Panchayat Ran and Rural Development Minister Danasari Anasuya (Seethakka), District Collector TS Divakara, SP Sudhir R Kekan, and other officials.  Tight security arrangements were made to prevent devotees from entering the gadde premises during the installation. Priests of Sammakka-Sarakka (Saralamma), Pagiddidda Raju, and Govinda Raju, along with their families, performed traditional pujas.
Speaking on the occasion, Minister Seethakka said, “The tribal way of life and the history of Sammakka-Saralamma are etched in stones used to construct the platforms and the compound of the shrine.  Chief Minister Revanth Reddy is undertaking these development works like a sacred yagna. Some people are criticising and insulting our traditions, which is wrong.”
Minister Seethakka, who also belongs to Koya community, during the ceremony at Medaram shrine on Wednesday.
Minister Seethakka said that during the renovation work, several meetings were held with the tribal priests and the opinions of the elders were taken and the priests were convinced.
She expressed the opinion that since the forest deities are in the same line, it will be easy for the devotees to have darshan. She said that the tribals had a great bond with Bandaru (turmeric powder), adding that the presiding deity Sammakka belonged to Bandari clan.

title: Mayurotsava dance festival in Hubballi today
summary: Join the Mayurotsava dance festival in Hubballi today, featuring performances by Mayura Nritya Academy students and special guests.
content:
Forty students from Mayura Nritya Academy, Hubballi, will present a dance drama, Krishna Charitamruta, as part of a dance festival, Mayurotsava, on Thursday.
Addressing presspersons here on Wednesday, president of Mayura Nritya Academy and danseuse Hema Waghmode said that the event will be organised at Sawai Gandharva Hall in Hubballi.
She said that during the inauguration ceremony at 10.30 a.m., president of Hubballi-Dharwad Urban District unit of the BJP and municipal councillor Tippanna Majjigi, Janata Dal(S) leader Gururaj Hunasimarad and national vice-president of Indian Jain Association Gautama Baphana will participate.
She added that apart from the dance drama, there will be dance performances from students of various branches of the academy.
Chairman of Hubballi-Dharwad Urban Development Authority Shakir Sanadi will be the guest for the concluding ceremony to be held at 4 p.m.
She said that the academy will honour Hindustani vocalist Sujata Gurav with Mayur Sanmana on the occasion.
The festival will conclude with dance performances from another set of students of the academy.

title: MHSRB releases first provisional merit list for 2,322 Nursing Officer posts
summary: MHSRB releases provisional merit list for 2,322 Nursing Officer posts, inviting objections until December 27.
content:
The Telangana Medical Health Services Recruitment Board (MHSRB), on December 23, released the first provisional merit list for the recruitment of 2,322 Nursing Officer posts.
As part of the process, the board has uploaded the details of all 40,423 candidates who appeared for the Computer Based Test, including the marks secured by each candidate, on its official website.
The board has invited objections to the provisional merit list from December 24 until 5 p.m. on December 27. Candidates can log in to the website during this period to submit their representations. After examining the objections received, the board will publish the second provisional merit list.

title: Port workers’ body seeks redress of fishermen grievances in Andhra Pradesh
summary: AIPTWF urges Union Minister to address fishermen's grievances and marine pollution issues in Andhra Pradesh's port areas.
content:
Andhra Pradesh State Chairman of the All India Port Trust Workers’ Federation (AIPTWF) Shaik Khalifathulla Basha met Union Minister of State for Ports, Shipping and Waterways Santanu Thakur at his camp office in New Delhi on Wednesday and submitted a representation highlighting the problems faced by fishermen in Andhra Pradesh.
Mr. Basha told the Union Minister that the fishermen were facing severe livelihood challenges due to marine pollution caused by industrial waste being discharged into the sea, which was leading to a sharp decline in fish availability.
Mr. Basha urged the Union Minister to take immediate and proactive steps to address the problems of fishermen as well as the hardships faced by workers employed in the port yard areas across the State, pointing out that several companies were failing to provide basic minimum facilities to workers.
He also highlighted the issues related to subsidies for mechanised boat owners, including irregular disbursement of diesel subsidies, discrimination in subsidies between longline and trawl net fishing boats, and the discontinuation of subsidies for essential equipment since 2019.
The AIPTWF leader also raised concerns over the alleged improper supply of free diesel to fishermen, stating that despite entitlement to increased quantities and submission of all required documents, diesel was not being supplied in full, or on time.
“This is forcing the fishermen to purchase fuel from private outlets at higher prices and suffer heavy financial losses,” he said, while requesting the Union Minister to intervene immediately on the long-pending issues.
Responding to the representation, Mr. Santanu Thakur assured that steps would be taken to resolve the problems of the fishermen as well as the issues of unorganised workers employed in the port yard areas.s

title: Thackeray cousins want power, not development of Mumbai: Shinde
summary: Eknath Shinde claims Thackeray cousins prioritize power over Mumbai's development ahead of BMC elections.
content:
MaharashtraDeputy Chief MinisterEknath Shindeon Wednesday (December 24, 2025) alleged that the Thackeray cousins have come together only for power, and lack any kind of program for Mumbai’s development.
Shiv Sena (UBT) chief Uddhav Thackeray and Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) president Raj Thackeray earlier in the dayannounced the alliance of their partiesahead of the January 15 Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) elections.
Talking to reporters here, Shinde, who heads the rival Shiv Sena faction, said there was no mention of development at the cousins’ press conference.
“Those who deviated from (late Shiv Sena founder) Balasaheb Thackeray’s ideology have been taught a lesson in the assembly elections last year and the recent municipal council and nagar panchayat polls,” he said.
“They have no development agenda, their goal is only to get power. These people drove Marathi-speakers out of Mumbai. The assembly polls and recent local elections have shown which is the fake and which is the real Shiv Sena,” said Mr. Shinde, who rebelled against Mr. Uddhav Thackeray’s leadership and split the party in June 2022.
He also accused the Thackerays of blocking development projects, and said the Mahayuti government introduced cluster development and expedited redevelopment projects.

title: Govt. to build SHG federation buildings at GP level
summary: Telangana government to build dedicated SHG federation buildings at Gram Panchayat level, empowering women's collectives for self-employment.
content:
The State government has announced revised guidelines for constructing dedicated buildings for village organisations (VO) of the Self-Help Groups (SHGs) and Federations at the Gram Panchayat level across the State. These structures will serve as permanent platforms for women’s collectives, enabling them to function as hubs for self-employment and decision-making, said Panchayat Raj and Rural Development Minister Danasari Anasuya (Seethakka).
In a statement on Wednesday, she said that this initiative marks a historic move to further strengthen women’s organisations at the grassroots level. Each building will be constructed on 200 square yards with a plinth area of 552 sq. ft, at an estimated cost of ₹10 lakh per unit. The decision comes in response to long-standing demands from SHGs for permanent spaces to operate village organizations (VOs) and federations.
“Our aim is to provide respect, security, and confidence to women through these buildings,” she said, adding that the construction will be taken up in phases across all villages.
The process will begin based on Gram Sabha resolutions, with proposals routed through Mandal and District levels and approved by the District Collector. Construction will be supervised by Panchayat Raj engineering staff, and a mandatory social audit will be conducted within six months of completion, as the works will utilise MGNREGS funds.
Minister Seethakka urged district collectors and PR and RD officials to strictly adhere to the guidelines and ensure timely execution of the project to strengthen women’s groups across Telangana.

title: Second KFD testing laboratory to come up in Sirsi soon: Dinesh Gundu Rao
summary: A new KFD testing laboratory in Sirsi will enhance disease detection and control, benefiting local residents significantly.
content:
The Health Department is set to establish another Kyasanur Forest Disease (KFD) testing laboratory at Sirsi of Uttara Kannada district to strengthen early detection and control of the disease, Health Minister Dinesh Gundu Rao said on Wednesday.
Speaking after a review meeting with senior health officials on preventive and preparedness measures against KFD, commonly known as monkey fever, the Minister said that while a laboratory is currently functioning in Shivamogga, the rising testing load has necessitated the setting up of an additional facility. All required equipment has been procured, and the Sirsi laboratory is expected to become operational shortly.
Mr. Rao said the new laboratory would benefit residents of Sirsi, Siddapur and surrounding areas by enabling quicker diagnosis, which, in turn, would help reduce mortality to zero. KFD cases typically rise between October and June each year, particularly in forested regions of Shivamogga, Uttara Kannada, Chikkamagaluru and Udupi districts, he said.
He said the Health department was fully prepared to control the spread of the disease, with regular and systematic screening being conducted in vulnerable areas. So far, preventive testing had been carried out on 1,163 people in Shivamogga, 124 in Chikkamagaluru, 368 in Uttara Kannada and 12 in Udupi. Of these, 13 persons tested positive for KFD and all had recovered following timely treatment.
Mr. Rao said Kasturba Medical College, Manipal, SIMS Shivamogga and KRIMS Karwar have been designated as referral hospitals. In addition, doctors in government hospitals have been trained to handle KFD cases, and treatment facilities have been strengthened at taluk hospitals in Thirthahalli, Sagar, Siddapur, Honnavar, Koppa and N.R. Pura.
Patients who recover after receiving treatment in the early stages of the disease are kept under continuous medical surveillance by the Health Department for a further 21 days. All KFD patients will be provided free ambulance services and complete treatment, the Minister said.
Stressing that there should not be a single death due to KFD this season, the Minister said medicines and medical preparedness were being put in place well in advance. He added that the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) is conducting clinical trials of a new vaccine, which could be made available to the public within a year.

title: 11 arrested as police bust interstate human trafficking gang,  two newborns rescued
summary: Police arrest 11 in an interstate human trafficking bust, rescuing two newborns from illegal sale in Hyderabad.
content:
Eleven members of an interstate human trafficking gang were arrested for their involvement in the illegal procurement and sale of babies. Two infants were rescued in a joint operation carried out by Miyapur police and the Shamshabad Special Operation Team (SOT) on Wednesday December 24.
The accused were identified as Vemula Babu Reddy, 49, a resident of Medchal in Malkajgiri district and native of Kadapa district in Andhra Pradesh; Venkipally Gangadhar Reddy, 39, a resident of Secunderabad and native of East Godavari district in Andhra Pradesh; Daram Laxmi, 28 of Manuguru in Bhadradri Kothagudem district; Ram Hari Roy, 37, a resident of Jeedimetla and native of Shivannagar village in Bihar; Kummari Harsha Roy, 31 of Prashanth Nagar, Moosapet; Sangeeta Debi, 33 of Jagadgirigutta; Gudepu Sujatha, 40 of Narapally and native of Kurnool district in Andhra Pradesh; Suraboina Anuradha, 55 of Secunderabad and native of Siddipet district; Esarapu Jyothi, 35 of Begumpet and native of Nalgonda district; V Madhavi, 28 of Chintal, Hyderabad; and Pothula Sobha, 44 of Musheerabad and native of Nagarkurnool district.
Police said that the accused had formed an organised network and illegally procured newborn babies from poor families who were unable to meet basic needs. The infants were then allegedly sold to affluent, childless couples for large sums through a well-established chain of middlemen.
Investigation revealed that Babu Reddy, an IVF agent, and Gangadhar Reddy are habitual offenders. While Babu Reddy is involved in at least two cases in Alwal and Devarakonda police station limits, Gangadhar Reddy was found to be involved in at least 18 cases across Cyberabad, Rachakonda and Hyderabad police jurisdictions, including offences under the Juvenile Justice Act and the Surrogacy (Regulation) Act.
In the present case, Gangadhar Reddy, along with his associates, procured a newborn from Ahmedabad in Gujarat by paying money to the biological parents through middlemen, with an intention of selling the infant later in Hyderabad. In a similar operation, Babu Reddy allegedly coordinated with Gangadhar Reddy and other associates to procure another infant from Ramanpet in Siddipet district, again by paying intermediaries, to sell the baby to needy couples for a high price.
The arrests were made while the accused were in the process of selling the infants, police said. The two rescued newborns were handed over to Sishu Vihar, Ameerpet, for safe custody.
Further investigation is underway.

title: CPI(M) demands action against police for ‘assault’ on tribals in Eluru district
summary: CPI(M) demands action against police for assaulting tribals and destroying crops in Eluru, highlighting violations of tribal rights.
content:
The CPI(M) demanded stringent action against police personnel allegedly involved in assaulting Adivasi tribals, destroying crops, and harassing women at Buttayigudem mandal in Eluru district.
In a memorandum submitted to Home Minister Vangalapudi Anitha on Wednesday, CPI(M) State secretary V. Srinivasa Rao and Central committee member D. Ramadevi alleged that police, along with revenue officials, attacked tribal families in Inumuru village on December 22. They said the incident took place in the Scheduled Area of the district, raising serious concerns over violations of constitutional safeguards meant for tribal communities.
According to the CPI(M) leaders, 57 tribal (ST-Koya) families have been cultivating 42.77 acres of government wasteland in survey numbers 221, 223, 210, 213 and 217 for generations under podu cultivation. Despite repeated requests for land titles, the issue remains unresolved and is currently pending before the Amaravati High Court. Even though the matter is sub judice, revenue and police officials have repeatedly harassed the tribals, they alleged.
In the memorandum, they claimed that police destroyed standing maize crops using tractors and assaulted protesting tribals, leaving several injured. A tribal man identified as Chandrasekhar reportedly sustained serious injuries, while women were allegedly beaten and forcibly driven away. CPI(M) leaders accused local police of acting under the guise of “protection orders” issued in favour of non-tribal landholders from other districts.
They further alleged that such incidents have become frequent in the region, citing similar actions in nearby villages across Buttayigudem and Jeelugumilli mandals. It accused the authorities of ignoring Government Order Ms. No. 1049 (2007), which bars police intervention in land disputes in Scheduled Areas.
Terming the actions discriminatory and unconstitutional, the CPI(M) leaders demanded immediate disciplinary action against the erring police officers and strict enforcement of laws protecting tribal land rights in Fifth Schedule areas.

title: Belagavi BJP takes out protest march against hate speech Bill
summary: Belagavi BJP protests against the hate speech Bill, demanding its withdrawal for infringing on freedom of expression rights.
content:
BJP members took out a protest march in Belagavi on Wednesday against the hate speech prevention Bill that was passed in the Winter Session of the Assembly in Belagavi recently.
Protestors gathered at the Rani Channamma Circle and marched to the Deputy Commissioner’s office. They raised slogans against the Congress government and demanded that the Bill be withdrawn.
They said that the Bill violates the basic principle of freedom of expression that is guaranteed by the Constitution. They accused the Congress of taking away civil rights of citizens.
They said that the Bill is part of a Congress conspiracy to target its political opponents.
“The Congress government is taking away freedom of expression. This is an act to silence those who speak against the government. The definition of hate speech in the Bill is also unclear,” they said.
They said that it can make any common man an easy target for officers. They submitted a memorandum to the Governor through the Deputy Commissioner’s office and urged him (Governor) to reject consent to the Bill.
Leaders Sanjay Patil, M.B. Zirli, Mahantesh Vakkund, Murughendragouda Patil, Leena Topannanavar, Deepa Kudchi and others were present.

title: 1.6 lakh names struck off electoral rolls
summary: The draft electoral roll for Kollam district, prepared through the Special Intensive Revision process, has been published.  The draft list contains 19,83,885 voters (Male: 9,46,604; Female: 10,37,263; Transgender: 18).
content:
The draft electoral roll for the district, prepared through the Special Intensive Revision process, has been published.
The draft list contains 19,83,885 voters (Male: 9,46,604; Female: 10,37,263; Transgender: 18). As of October 27, 2025, there were 21,44,527 voters in the district; however, 1,60,642 voters were removed due to various reasons such as being under the ASD (Absent, Shifted, Dead) category or being duplicates.
The draft rolls will be distributed to all recognized political parties by the respective Electoral Registration Officers (EROs). Meetings with these parties have been conducted at the district and constituency levels at every stage of SIR 2026 to explain the progress.
The public and political parties can submit claims and objections until January 22, 2026. For voters who could not be mapped during the SIR, EROs will issue notices, conduct hearings, and verify identity documents before making a final decision. All claims and objections received will be resolved by February 14, 2026, and the final electoral roll will be published on February 21, 2026.

title: Govt. invites agri-business companies to partner with farmer groups under KERA project
summary: Kerala government invites agri-business companies to partner with farmers under KERA project, offering grants and technical support.
content:
The State government has invited agri-business companies to partner with Farmer Producer Companies (FPCs) under the World Bank-assisted Kerala Climate Resilient Agri-Value Chain Modernisation (KERA) project. The initiative will offer grant support of up to ₹2 crore per alliance for production investment and business development.
Eligible companies will receive financial assistance along with three years of technical support. The programme aims to create structured market linkages that connect Kerala’s premium agricultural produce to local, national and international markets, ensuring that farmers receive better prices and a secure market linkage.
A total of 150 productive alliances are proposed across the State in three phases. In the first phase, around 50 alliances would be set up in the northern districts of Kasaragod, Kannur, Wayanad, Kozhikode, and Malappuram.
Companies seeking to participate must have a minimum annual turnover of ₹10 crore and prior experience in working with farmer communities in Kerala. Farmer producer companies eligible for the programme should have at least three years’ working experience, a minimum membership of 200 farmers and an annual turnover of ₹10 lakh.
According to officials, the initiative is part of a broader effort to modernise agricultural value chains in the State while promoting climate-resilient practices. By facilitating partnerships with the private sector, the government expects to reduce market risks faced by farmers and create sustainable and scalable models of collaboration.
Interested farmer-producer companies can submit applications through the official KERA portal at https://pa.kera.kerala.gov.in/auth/login on or before December 31. Details are available with the KERA regional project director (phone: 9037824054).

title: Govt. notifies wide-ranging amendments to  Revenue laws revenue reforms, title deed drive signal push for administrative clarity
summary: Karnataka government reforms land administration with new revenue laws, enhancing transparency and accelerating title deed distribution to residents.
content:
The Karnataka government has stepped up efforts to reform land administration by notifying wide-ranging amendments to the Karnataka Land Revenue Act, 1964, and the Karnataka Land Revenue Rules, 1966. The government also accelerated the creation of revenue villages and the distribution of title deeds to long-settled residents living without ownership documents.
The final notification, issued on December 23, brings into force several amendments introduced over the past two to three years, particularly to Section 95 of the Act. In all, amendments have been carried out to 47 Sections of the law, including nine substantive changes aimed at streamlining procedures, improving transparency and making land governance more citizen-centric.
A key feature of the reform is the comprehensive amendment of the Karnataka Land Revenue Rules, 1966, for the first time in 56 years. Changes have been made to 44 rules, marking the most significant overhaul of revenue administration since the sweeping land reforms introduced under the then Chief Minister Devaraj Urs in the 1970s. Officials said the amendments were intended to remove procedural ambiguities and bring consistency in the functioning of revenue authorities.
The changes also seek to introduce greater discipline in revenue courts, which, in the absence of clear guidelines, had in the past, issued orders beyond their jurisdiction, particularly at the sub-divisional level. Clear rules have now been laid down to ensure transparency and quicker access to justice.
The amendments place particular emphasis on simplifying land conversion. District Commissioners have been directed to decide on conversion applications within the stipulated period, with online submission of applications now enabled. If no decision is taken within 30 days, conversion will be deemed to have been granted. Small-scale industries have been exempted from conversion requirements for industrial use up to two acres, while renewable energy projects have also been granted exemptions subject to approval from the Energy Department.
Parallel to these reforms, the government has intensified its drive to regularise unauthorised habitations through the creation of revenue villages and the issuance of title deeds. At a monthly review meeting on December 24, Revenue Minister Krishna Byre Gowda directed all Deputy Commissioners to expedite the process, setting a target of distributing title deeds to 1.10 lakh families by February.
Since amendments to the law were enacted in 2017, title deeds have been issued to 1.08 lakh families up to May 2023, followed by another 1.11 lakh families between May 2023 and 2025. The Revenue Village Creation campaign involves identifying undocumented settlements, conducting surveys, issuing notifications and registering properties, largely benefiting economically weaker sections.

title: Arrangements in place for hassle-free darshan to pilgrims for 10-day ‘Vaikuntha Ekadasi’ in Tirumala
summary: Hassle-free darshan arrangements for 'Vaikuntha Ekadasi' in Tirumala, ensuring smooth access for pilgrims and crowd management.
content:
The Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams (TTD) and  the Tirupati district administration have made elaborate arrangements to ensure a hassle-free darshan of Lord Venkateswara in Tirumala to the scores of devotees visiting the hill shrine on the auspicious occasion of ‘Vaikuntha Ekadasi’.
The authorities have made revised arrangements in the darshan format this year, based on the recommendations of the Cabinet sub-committee comprising Ministers Anam Ramanarayana Reddy (Endowments), V. Anitha (Home) and Anagani Satya Prasad (Revenue), who is also the district in-charge Minister.
As ‘Vaikuntha Ekadasi’ will be celebrated for a period of 10 days from December 30, 2025, to January 8, 2026, the TTD has introduced a new system, wherein the devotees who have been selected through the transparent e-dip process will get darshan for the first three days. At the rate of 60,000 devotees a day, the first three days will see 1.8 lakh devotees having darshan, besides passing through the auspicious threshold ‘Uttara Dwaram’.
For the remaining seven days, it will be a normal ‘sarva darshan’ queue line, where the devotees will get darshan on first-in-first-out basis.
“The city will witness a floating population of one lakh devotees on any given day for the 10 days, and as such we have set up special help desks at vital points to guide the pilgrims, traffic regulations, real-time monitoring of the situation on the trekking routes, the ghat roads, and the temple vicinity,” Collector S. Venkateswar told the media here on Wednesday.
He said the real-time feed from the command control system in Tirumala would be used to plan crowd management strategies. Similarly, a separate route plan was in place for the protocol VIPs visiting the hill shrine.
Superintendent of Police (Tirupati district) L. Subbarayudu said Tirupati and Tirumala would remain fortified for the period, with the deployment of 3,000 policemen on special duty. The Police Department would work in tandem with the TTD’s in-house Vigilance & Security wing to control the crowd.
He also announced to use drone cameras over Alipiri, Srivarimettu trekking routes, the Tirupati railway station and the central bus station to monitor the crowd influx.
Both the officers appealed to the public to depend on the TTD’s official broadcasting arms, or recognised media houses, and not believe in the rumours spread on the social media platforms. In the same vein, they warned the social media users not to mislead the public with fake news or half-truths.

title: Murder accused arrested with MDMA
summary: In a targeted operation at Panmana Edappallikotta, the Kollam Excise Enforcement and Anti-Narcotic Special Squad, led by Inspector Dileep C.P., arrested two men for the possession and smuggling of 11.649 g of MDMA
content:
In a targeted operation at Panmana Edappallikotta, the Kollam Excise Enforcement and Anti-Narcotic Special Squad, led by Inspector Dileep C.P., arrested two men for the possession and smuggling of 11.649 g of MDMA.
The accused have been identified as Ratheesh (39), son of Janardhanan Pillai from Meenad, Kollam, and Amitabh Chandran (39), son of Pushpachandran from Kappil Mekku, Alappuzha.
Following the seizure, a case was registered under the NDPS Act, and both individuals were taken into custody as part of an ongoing investigation into regional drug trafficking networks. The accused were apprehended during an inspection conducted as part of the Christmas-New Year Special Drive. Officials had intercepted the suspects acting on a tip-off from the Excise Intelligence Bureau.
Investigations revealed that the accused, Ratheesh and Amitabh Chandran, are seasoned criminals and history sheeters.
Amitabh Chandran is an accused in a 2023 murder case in Kayamkulam involving the fatal stabbing of a young man. During the current arrest, officials recovered a 29 cm long dagger from his possession. Similarly, the first accused, Ratheesh, is involved in multiple attempted murder cases.
The duo reportedly procured the synthetic drugs from a Nigerian national in Bengaluru to distribute in Kerala during the festive season.
The operation was carried out by a team including AEI Prem Nazir, PO Prasad Kumar, and CEOs Ajith, Aneesh, Sooraj, Jojo Julian Cruz, Abhiram, WCEO Varsha, and CEO Subhash.

title: For govt., 2025 ends with a positive note with reforms to check impact of high interest loans
summary: The Telangana government aims to reduce high loan interest burdens through reforms, fostering economic growth and financial stability by 2025.
content:
Payment of high interest for loans obtained by the BRS government continues to haunt the State finances in the year 2025, even as the Congress government is trying hard to improve the general economy of the State, which registered slow pace of growth over the past couple of years.
The interest burden of the State has been mounting with the State government paying ₹18,486 crore till November end against ₹19,369 crore budgeted for the entire financial year. The interest payment is indicative that the government could end up paying interest in excess of ₹25,000 crore, almost 10% of the overall revenue receipts estimated at ₹2.29 lakh crore, at the end of the fiscal.
The situation was not different during the previous fiscal year when the government remitted interest of ₹26,688 crore against ₹17,729 crore estimated for the financial year. A majority of these loans were obtained for the much-publicised Kaleshwaram project, which saw structural failures. “We have to borrow more to repay the interest,” was how a senior Finance department official summed up the situation.
Financial constraints notwithstanding, the government is ensuring payment of salaries to staff on the first of every month and clearing dues pending payment to employees over a period of time, releasing ₹700 crore every month. A major initiative has been taken in the last couple of months to overcome the frequent financial problems. The Finance department, after sustained efforts, secured approval of the Union Finance Ministry to swap high-interest loans with low-interest ones.
As a result, high-interest loans worth ₹26,103 crore with relatively short repayment tenures were swapped with low-interest ones with longer tenures, officials said. The government had targeted clearance of other higher-interest loans in the coming days easing strain on the finances.
The impact of the decision will be seen in the coming years with a reduction of the interest burden, allowing the government to spend on programmes aimed at boosting the general economic growth. One of the key areas that the department is trying to address is arresting the leakages, while initiatives like the recent Telangana Rising Global Summit, which saw memorandums of understanding (MoUs) signed for more than ₹5.75 lakh crore investments, are sure to boost the economy.
“Some of these MoUs will definitely materialise as we have focused on the follow-up action,” Finance Secretary Sandeep Kumar Sultania toldThe Hindu. He explained about the steps that were taken to ensure the revenue-earning departments increase their contribution to the exchequer with a focus on completion of the projects, attracting investments and giving boost to industry by improving infrastructure.
According to him, restructuring of high-interest loans would lead to a reduction in the interest burden, while the focus on projects and industry will create new jobs, thereby allowing money circulation. “We have the support of Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy and Deputy Chief Minister Mallu Bhatti Vikramarka, who are in favour of initiatives like loan restructuring. We are moving ahead in a planned manner to balance growth/development by gradual restructuring to reduce negative impact on finances,” he said.
The department had therefore ushered in an Aadhar-based e-sign system for clearance of various bills, and the paperless system is being extended to all treasury offices across the State. The department took steps to clear pending bills worth around ₹3,000 crore pertaining to the Centrally sponsored Schemes. This was in addition to the payment of ₹926 crore, ₹50 a quintal, as a bonus for fine rice procured from the farmers. Steps were taken to ensure updation of Aadhar numbers of more than 10.7 lakh government employees, including contract, outsourcing, daily wage and honorarium to arrest leakages.

title: Army deployed in Assam's violence-hit West Karbi Anglong
summary: Army deployed in Assam's West Karbi Anglong to restore order after violence resulted in two deaths and numerous injuries.
content:
Army has been deployed to maintain law and order in violence-hit West Karbi Anglong district of Assam, Director General of Police Harmeet Singh said on Wednesday (December 24, 2025).
Speaking to reporters at the worst-hit Kheroni area, Mr. Singh appealed to the people not to indulge in violence and asked community elders to make "misguided" youths understand that problems can be solved only through dialogue.
"Army columns have reached here, and they have marched through these areas. The situation is totally under control now," he said.
The police are investigating the violence that happened over the last two days, he said.
"We will arrest the culprits. Let the situation stabilise first," he added.
Two persons were killed, and 45 others, including 38 police personnel, injured as violence rocked West Karbi Anglong district.
Agitators from the Karbi community had been on a hunger strike for the last 15 days, demanding the eviction of alleged illegal settlers, who mostly hail from Bihar, from Village Grazing Reserve (VGR) and Professional Grazing Reserve (PGR) lands in tribal belts.
They went on a rampage on Monday (December 23, 2025) after police took away three agitators from the protest site in the early hours, a move which the administration later claimed was for their hospitalisation.

title: BJP to celebrate Vajpayee’s birth anniversary in Hubballi today
summary: BJP celebrates Atal Bihari Vajpayee’s birth anniversary in Hubballi with a memorial event featuring speeches and a film screening.
content:
The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) will organise a programme, “Good Governance Day – Atal Ji Memorial”, in Hubballi on Thursday to mark the birth anniversary of the former Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee.
Addressing media persons in Hubballi on Wednesday, Hubballi Dharwad East Yuva Morcha unit president Praveen Kubasad said that the programme will be held at 5 p.m. at Durgadbail Circle in Hubballi.
The former Minister and MLC C.T. Ravi will be the chief speaker at the event.
Union Minister Pralhad Joshi will inaugurate the programme.
The chief guests will include MLAs Mahesh Tenginakai and Arvind Bellad, MLC Pradeep Shettar and the former MLA Ashok Katave.
Mr. Kubasad said the event will include a screening of the film “Main Atal Hoon” highlighting the key moments of Vajpayee’s life and career.
He also said that arrangements have been made to ensure smooth traffic movement, while there will be enough parking space. He ensured that the public will not face any inconvenience.

title: Woman dies after being assaulted by husband in Miyapur
summary: A woman dies after her husband allegedly assaults her during an argument in Miyapur; investigation ongoing.
content:
A woman died after she was allegedly assaulted by her husband during a quarrel while travelling in a car in Miyapur on Tuesday (December 23, 2025).
The deceased, identified as Vijayalakshmi, was married to the accused, Konchepu Raraju, for about 14 years and they had two sons.
The case came to light following a complaint by Vijayalakshmi’s relative stating that Raraju had developed an addiction to alcohol and other vices, leading to frequent disputes between the couple.
Police said that on Tuesday, at around 2 p.m., the couple were travelling in a car to visit a relative when an argument broke out between them again. During the quarrel, Raraju allegedly assaulted Vijayalakshmi, causing her to lose consciousness. Though she was immediately shifted to a private hospital in KPHB, the duty doctor declared her brought dead.
A case was booked by the Miyapur police and the body was shifted to Gandhi Hospital mortuary for postmortem examination. Further investigation is underway.

title: Kerala to introduce nativity card to address citizenship concerns
summary: Kerala introduces a permanent nativity card to enhance citizenship verification and simplify residency proof for residents.
content:
The Kerala Cabinet on Wednesday decided to introduce a nativity card as a new identification document to prove residency as part of measures to address contemporary concerns related to citizenship checks. Announcing the decision at a press conference in Thiruvananthapuram on Wednesday, Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan said that the Cabinet had approved in-principle the issuance of a permanent nativity card with a photo in place of the nativity certificate currently being  issued in the State.
“The plight of people who find it difficult to prove their existence is worrying. For this, the person should have an authentic and legally backed document. The government intends to introduce such a document in Kerala. The card can be used for services related to the State government and for other needs. The tahsildars will be responsible for distributing the card,” he said.
The nativity certificate, in its current form, is a document that proves the birth and long-term residence of a person in a State. However, it is not a legally binding document. At present, a nativity certificate has to be obtained several times in connection with each need. The government had received complaints in this regard. With the introduction of the card, these problems will be resolved. The Revenue department has been tasked with submitting the draft law to give legal validity to the nativity card for the consideration of the Cabinet in consultation with the Law department, he said.

title: Two Bengaluru police officers arrested in bribery case
summary: Two Bengaluru police officers arrested for bribery, involving amounts of ₹30,000 and ₹2 lakh in separate cases.
content:
The Lokayukta officials on Wednesday held the Assistant Commissioner of Police, Malleswaram sub-division, red-handed while allegedly accepting a bribe of ₹30,000 from a hotelier to allow him to run his business beyond permissible time limits.
The accused, identified as Krishna Murthy, was arrested and booked under the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988. The trap followed a complaint by Sanjay Kumar, manager of a hotel in Rajajinagar. The ACP had allegedly demanded ₹50,000 to allow the hotel to operate beyond the government-mandated permissible hours.
A day earlier, a sub-inspector posted at the Chikkajala police station was held red-handed accepting a bribe of ₹2 lakh for filing a ‘B report’ in a cheating case. The Lokayukta police registered a case based on a complaint lodged by Ravikumar. PSI Shivanna was arrested while he was allegedly accepting the bribe money, officials said. Officials said a cheating case was registered at the Chikkajala police against Ravikumar. To file a ‘B report’ in the case, Shivanna allegedly demanded a bribe of ₹3 lakh.

title: CM to inaugurate new surgical block at Kottayam medical college
summary: The new surgical block at Kottayam Medical College and several other newly completed facilities will be inaugurated by Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan in January, Health Minister Veena George has said.
content:
The new surgical block at Kottayam Medical College and several other newly completed facilities will be inaugurated by Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan in January, Health Minister Veena George has said.
The facilities that have been completed include the surgical block, paramedical hostel, cath lab, biogas plant, renovated outpatient department and a lactation unit. In addition to the existing seven operation theatres, seven more have been made operational. The Minister said efforts are under way to complete the remaining works and make all facilities fully functional at the earliest.
A high level review meeting chaired by Health Minister Veena George was held to assess the progress of development works at Kottayam Medical College. Cooperation Minister V.N. Vasavan also attended the meeting.
The Health Minister directed officials to ensure that all ongoing development works at the medical college are completed in a time bound manner. Construction of the cardiology block, built at a cost of ₹36 crore, has been completed, while work on the infectious diseases block, estimated at ₹10 crore, is progressing. Directions have also been issued to initiate steps for constructing a new men’s hostel. Approval has been granted to start a postgraduate course in emergency medicine.
The Minister further instructed officials to expedite procedures for demolishing the unused EFG block. It was also decided to convene a special meeting involving the Electricity Minister and KIIFB representatives to discuss the construction of a 110 kV substation to ensure uninterrupted power supply to the hospital.

title: ‘Mission 40 for 90 Days’ launched to shore up SSLC ranking in Mandya
summary: Mandya launches 'Mission 40 for 90 Days' to boost SSLC exam scores, ensuring all students achieve a minimum of 40 marks.
content:
In a bid to improve the overall SSLC performance in Mandya district, local authorities launched a unique initiative to ensure that every student secures a minimum of 40 marks.
The campaign, titled ‘Mission 40 for 90 Days’, was launched earlier this month. Mandya Zilla Panchayat CEO K.R. Nandini reviewed its progress and held discussions with the Education Department staff on December 24 to fine-tune the campaign and ensure better outcomes.
Ms. Nandini said all high schools in the district had been instructed to conduct practice tests aimed at making SSLC students achieve 40 marks, on December 18, 19, and 20. ‘’Based on these tests, special attention and remedial classes have been advised for 5,221 students who scored less than 50%,’’ she said.
Feedback on the initiative revealed that many students could not practice as much as they would have liked to owing to the shortage of notebooks.
Hence, it was decided to procure and distribute notebooks to schools under Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) funds. ‘’Some organisations have already been approached to support notebook distribution through their CSR allocations,’’ the Zilla Panchayat CEO noted.
Meanwhile, a monitoring committee comprising officials from various departments will be formed to oversee the progress of the campaign.
Gram panchayats have also been directed to provide necessary support to schools within their jurisdiction to shore up the results.
Ms. Nandini said special awards will be given to nodal officers, block education officers (BEOs), and headmasters of schools that achieve good results in the SSLC examinations.
In the review meeting, the performances of schools in K.R. Pet, Pandavpura, and Srirangapatana taluks came under scrutiny as the number of students in these taluks who had scored below 50% was high. The officials and BEOs concerned were instructed to pay special attention to these taluks. However, students in Mandya North and South zones had fared well and the officials were therefore directed to ensure that their scores breached the 90% mark.
The CEO also instructed officials to credit the pending gratuity amount to 217 retired cooking staff who served under the Midday Meal Scheme in government and aided schools in the district. The payment has to be made on January 1, 2026.
G. Lokesh, deputy director of the Education Department, Yogesh, principal, DIET, various BEOs, and nodal officers were present.

title: Flute programme in Belagavi
summary: Join us for a captivating flute and tabla performance in Belagavi on January 26, 2026, at Nivedarpana Academy.
content:
Nivedarpana Academy will organise a flute performance by Madhu Kulkarni and a tabla performance by Shrihari Diggavi in Belagavi on January 26, 2026.
The event will be held on the academy premises in Rani Channamma Nagar at 10 30 a.m.

title: T.N. govt. sanctions ₹289.63-crore relief for crop damage
summary: Tamil Nadu government approves ₹289.63 crore relief for farmers affected by crop damage from unseasonal rains.
content:
The Tamil Nadu government on Wednesday issued an order sanctioning ₹289.63 crore from the State Disaster Response Fund as relief for the crops damaged on 5.66 lakh acres due to rain during the northeast monsoon in November and December 2024, and unseasonal rain in January 2025.
In a press release, Minister for Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare M.R.K. Panneerselvam said revenue and agriculture officials had conducted field assessments in the affected districts. After confirming crop damage of over 33%, proposals seeking relief were obtained from the Collectors concerned and examined.
Based on the assessment, the extent of crop damage was estimated at 4.90 lakh acres for agricultural crops, and 76,132 acres for horticultural crops. Based on the estimates, ₹289.63 crore had been sanctioned as relief for 3.60 lakh farmers. The amount will be credited to the bank accounts of the farmers, the Minister added.

title: Centuries-old duck-rearing practice at risk as avian flu hits Kuttanad again
summary: Avian flu outbreaks threaten Kuttanad's traditional duck farming, risking livelihoods and leading to significant declines in duck populations.
content:
Recurring avian flu outbreaks have pushed Kuttanad’s centuries-old traditional duck farming to the brink of collapse.
The latest outbreak of avian influenza (H5N1)—the seventh in the region in the past 11 years—was confirmed earlier this week in one ward each of eight panchayats in Alappuzha district and in four villages in Kottayam. It has already resulted in the death of around 55,000 birds, including large numbers of ducks, chickens and quails in the two districts. Another 25,000 birds will be culled later this week as part of containment measures.
Duck farming has long been a consistent source of income for several families in Kuttanad. However, repeated bird flu outbreaks have severely affected livelihoods. Most farmers rear ducks twice a year, particularly targeting the Christmas and Easter festive seasons.
Ramachandran G., a seasoned duck farmer from Cheruthana in Alappuzha, lost 12,000 of his 15,000 ducks, which were 30 days old, to the latest outbreak. The remaining birds are scheduled to be culled in the coming days. “I was raising the ducks with an eye on the 2026 Easter season and have suffered losses to the tune of around ₹20 lakh. This is the second time I have incurred losses due to avian flu. In 2014, though my 4,500 ducks were not directly affected, they were culled as part of containment measures. I do not want to return to duck farming any time soon,” says the 67-year-old.
Though the outbreaks have directly affected only a small number of farmers, the impact has been widespread. Restrictions imposed by the authorities, as part of the efforts to contain the highly pathogenic virus, on the trade of duck meat and eggs—along with those of chicken and quail—have hit almost all stakeholders in the sector.
According to farmers’ associations, the number of large duck farmers in the backwater region—those with flocks of 2,000 birds or more—has declined sharply from about 1,500 to fewer than 250 over the years. “The latest outbreak, confirmed on the eve of Christmas, has all but ended hopes of a revival after last year’s outbreak and the subsequent restrictions on hatcheries and poultry operations. A decade ago, between 10 lakh and 15 lakh ducks were reared in the region annually. That number has now fallen to around three lakh and is certain to decline further. More big and small farmers are considering exiting the sector entirely. The government should provide compensation to the affected farmers soon,” says B. Rajasekharan, president, Aikya Tharavu Karshaka Sangham.
Unlike poultry farming elsewhere, where birds are reared indoors, duck farming in Kuttanad—known for its vast backwaters and paddy fields—is largely conducted in the open. Farmers move ducks from one location to another for feeding. Experts say this practice increases vulnerability to diseases such as avian influenza as the region is frequented by migratory birds, believed to be a primary source of the virus. They warn that local duck breeds such as Chara and Chembally face the risk of extinction.
“Avian flu usually spreads through migratory birds, and continuous monitoring could help prevent outbreaks to some extent. Unfortunately, India lacks a system for monitoring migratory birds. Kuttanad attracts these birds due to its waterlogged terrain, and their arrival cannot be prevented. The government’s priority is to contain the spread, especially since there is a risk of the virus mutating,” says an Animal Husbandry department official, while urging the people to be more cautious.

title: Social media acquaintance assaults woman in Bengaluru, held
summary: The Jnanabharathi police have arrested a 29-year-old man for allegedly stalking, harassing, and sexually assaulting a young woman after befriending her through social media.
content:
The Jnanabharathi police have arrested a 29-year-old man for allegedly stalking, harassing, and sexually assaulting a young woman after befriending her through social media.
According to the police, the accused established contact with the victim via social media and began pressuring her to accept his love. Despite her repeated refusals, he allegedly continued to stalk her, follow her movements, abuse her using obscene language, physically assault her and threaten her.
The police said that on Tuesday, around 3.20 p.m., the accused went to the PG accommodation where the victim was staying and again forced her to accept his proposal. When she refused, he allegedly assaulted her by hitting her on the head, back, and legs, forcibly grabbed her shirt, attempted to tear her clothes and sexually harassed her before fleeing the spot.
Within hours of registering the case, the police traced and arrested the accused, identified as Naveen Kumar N., 29, a resident of Billamaranahalli village, Yelahanka. He has been taken into custody.
Following the incident, the woman vacated the PG accommodation due to fear and trauma. The police said the victim had shifted four to five PGs in the last six months to escape the accused’s harassment and had been staying at Sai Baba PG for the last two months. Investigators revealed that the accused had earlier created disturbances near the PG premises and had repeatedly followed and harassed the woman wherever she moved. Due to the continuous harassment, the victim had reportedly quit her job as a telecaller.

title: ED restitutes assets worth ₹63 crore to SBI and UCO Bank in GS Oils case
summary: ED returns ₹63 crore in assets to SBI and UCO Bank, linked to GS Oils money laundering case.
content:
The Directorate of Enforcement, Hyderabad, has completed the restitution of attached properties valued at about ₹63.05 crore to public sector banks in connection with a money laundering case involving M/s GS Oils Limited.
According to the ED, properties worth ₹62.30 crore were restored to the State Bank of India, while assets valued at ₹75 lakh were restituted to UCO Bank under the provisions of the Prevention of Money Laundering (PMLA) Act. The properties had been attached during the course of the ED’s investigation into the case.
The ED initiated its probe against M/s G S Oils Limited and others in 2016, based on FIRs registered by the CBI’s Banking Securities and Fraud Cell in Bengaluru and the CBI’s Anti-Corruption Branch in Nagpur. The cases stemmed from complaints filed by SBI and UCO Bank, which alleged that loans sanctioned to the company had turned non-performing assets due to non-repayment, causing a wrongful loss of ₹274 crore to SBI and ₹32.33 crore to UCO Bank.
Investigations revealed that the company had availed multiple credit facilities from the two banks, all of which subsequently became NPAs due to fraudulent practices by the accused. The ED found that loan amounts were round-tripped and parked in associate companies before being withdrawn in cash or used to purchase land in the names of those entities. These properties were then mortgaged again to secure further loans. The probe also uncovered diversion of large sums of bank funds through fraudulently issued letters of credit to related shell firms for bogus supply of material, with the proceeds ultimately being channelled back to the promoters.
Following the investigation, SBI and UCO Bank were advised to file restitution applications under Section 8(8) of the PMLA before the Special PMLA Court at Nampally in Hyderabad. The ED conveyed its concurrence for the restitution of the attached immovable properties to enable their restoration to the victim banks.
The Special PMLA Court, through orders dated March 24, 2025, and December 17, 2025, allowed the restitution petitions filed by SBI and UCO Bank, paving the way for the return of the assets. The properties include agricultural and industrial lands located in Adilabad, Asifabad and Mancherial districts of Telangana, as well as land in Wani in Maharashtra.
The ED said that the restitution marked a step in its efforts to ensure that proceeds of crime are returned to rightful claimants and that victims of financial fraud are compensated.

title: Nirmala Sitharaman to visit her adopted village in West Godavari on December 28
summary: Nirmala Sitharaman will visit her adopted village on December 28 to inspect projects and inaugurate training for fisherfolk.
content:
Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman will inspect the ongoing projects, including the sea protection wall being built at a cost of ₹13.50 crore, at her adopted village, Pedda Mynavani Lanka, on the Narsapuram coast in West Godavari district on December 28.
In an official release, District Collector Chadalavada Nagarani said that Ms. Sitharaman would also inaugurate a drone and Artificial Intelligence training programme for the fisherfolk, at the digital bhavan in the village.
Her visit also includes inauguration of a temple at Kavitam village and interaction with the fisherfolk on their needs and infrastructure facilities.s

title: Music programme in memory of Shivamogga Subbanna to be held on December 28
summary: Join us on December 28 for a heartfelt music tribute to Shivamogga Subbanna at Kuvempu Ranga Mandira.
content:
Abhiruchi, a cultural organisation, in association with the Kannada and Culture Department, Kuvempu Trust at Kuppali, and Shamanna Trust of Shivamogga, has organised a music programme in memory of noted singer Shivamogga Subbanna. The programme will be held at Kuvempu Ranga Mandira here on December 28 at 5.30 p.m.
Vinay Shivamogga, one of the organisers, in a press meet here on December 24, said that the programme had been organised to pay tributes to Jnanapeetha awardee Kuvempu and Subbanna, proud natives of Shivamogga. Subbanna was the first playback singer from Karnataka to win a national award. He had been known for rendering poems written by Kuvempu.
A team of well-known singers, including Pancham Halibandi, Surekha Hegade, Shruthi Raghavendra, Vinay Nadig, Parth Chirantan, and Pruthvi Gowda will present Subbanna’s songs.
Kadidal Prakash, secretary of the trust, Umesh Haladi, assistant director of the Kannada and Culture Department, Subbanna’s wife Shantha Subbanna, and others will take part in the programme, he said.

title: Soldier convicted under POCSO Act
summary: A soldier in Belagavi convicted of sexually assaulting a minor, sentenced to 10 years and ordered to pay compensation.
content:
A Belagavi court has convicted a solider under POCSO Act of sexual assault on a minor after making a false promise of marriage.
The VIII Additional District and Sessions Court here on Tuesday sentenced Nagaraj Dhanapal Camanna to 10 years in prison and imposed a fine of ₹10,000 on him.
The judge also sentenced him to three years in prison with a fine of ₹5,000 for the offence under Section 420 of the IPC and six months in prison and a fine of ₹5,000 for an offence under Section 506 of the IPC.
The man had known the girl for several years. He promised to marry her and sexually assaulted her repeatedly in a village in Belagavi district since April 2022.
The girl opposed it, saying that they were not married yet. But the soldier forcibly raped her. He also threatened to kill her and her relatives, if she were to reveal their affair to anyone.
The District Police filed a charge sheet based on the testimony of the victim and investigation.
Judge Shivaputra Dindalakoppa of the VIII Additional District and Sessions Court, who heard the case, said that since the charge has been proved, he was sentencing accused Nagaraj.
The judge ordered compensation to be paid to the victim.
Government pleader Kiran S. Patil argued on behalf of the State.
Police officers K.G. Deepu and Shivashankar R. Ganachari conducted the investigation, said a release.

title: Actor Vinayakan discharged from hospital
summary: Actor Vinayakan, injured while filming Aadu 3, has been discharged from the hospital and advised six weeks of rest.
content:
Actor Vinayakan, who was injured during the shooting of a movie at Thodupuzha, was discharged from a private hospital in the city with instructions to rest for at least six weeks.
The actor sustained injuries, particularly to his shoulder and neck, during the shooting of an action sequence forAadu 3directed by Midhun Manual Thomas.

title: Station Mahotsav: Railway legacy revisited in Malnad
summary: Discover the rich railway heritage of Malnad at Station Mahotsav, celebrating Sagar Jambagaru's historical significance and community connections.
content:
Long before the State was criss-crossed by highways that bridged the distance between various regions, it was the rail network that knitted the hinterland and provided the link to the larger world beyond.
And for the quaint village of Jambagaru, it was the metre guage rail that helped open up the vistas to the Malnad region and connected it with the plains.
This slice of history, which is fast eroding from public memory, came to light again when the Mysuru Division of the South Western Railway recently celebrated Station Mahotsav at Sagar Jambagaru station.
Constructed in 1938-39, the station was known by the code S.R.F in the metre gauge era, while Talaguppa was TLGP.
According to the railway authorities, the line was laid to move Malnad’s resources and later became indispensable during the Linganamakki Dam works, making the railway not just a mode of travel but part of the region’s development story.
It was established by the then Mysore State Railways and is a proud symbol of how rail connectivity shaped the social, economic, and cultural life of the Malnad region.
A lesser-known fact is that the station’s historical significance is intertwined with royal and national milestones to a certain extent. The extension of the railway line from Anandapur to Sagar in 1938 coincided with the visit of Sir Mirza Ismail. In 1949, Maharaja Chamaraja Wadiyar arrived at Sagar by train to inaugurate the Mahatma Gandhi Power Plant and later visited Jog Falls.
As the lifeline of the region, Sagar Jambagaru Railway Station received newspapers, postal mail, and daily essentials that arrived by train, connecting the town to the outside world.
The station also hosted several eminent personalities, including Dr. Rajkumar, and many others who used the Station’s guest lounge during their visits.
Though meter gauge operations ceased in 1994 owing to gauge conversion, the railway’s bond with the region endured. A two-coach rail bus followed, and sustained efforts by a Broad Gauge Committee led by N. D’Souza resulted in the introduction of the Mysuru–Sagar Intercity Broad Gauge train in 2011. Today, 10 trains operate on the route, serving not just Sagar but passengers from Sirsi, Siddapura, Hosanagara, Soraba, Kumta, Honnavar, and Bhatkal.
Station Mahotsav, an Indian Railways initiative to highlight station heritage and public service, is an attempt to educate younger generations about the railways’ role in nation-building, said the authorities.
Folk and film artist Lakshmi Ramappa Gademane and retired railway employee Ramadas P.D. were felicitated, while students of Nirmala Girls High School presented cultural programmes.
Railway officials, retired employees, artists, and members of the public attended the event, which concluded with a renewed resolve to preserve the rich legacy of Sagar Jambagaru Railway Station for future generations.

title: IIM-Kozhikode declares CAT results
summary: IIM-Kozhikode announces CAT 2025 results, with over 2.5 lakh candidates and 12 achieving a perfect score.
content:
The Indian Institute of Management-Kozhikode (IIM-K) released the Common Admission Test (CAT) 2025 results on Wednesday (December 24, 2025).
Candidates can download their official CAT 2025 scorecards by logging into the CAT 2025 website (https://iimcat.ac.in), using the CAT application login ID and password.
IIMK Director Prof. Debashis Chatterjee announced the results here. Over 2.5 lakh candidates appeared in the MBA entrance exam conducted on November 30. This year, 12 candidates secured a perfect 100 percentile.

title: ‘Vote theft’: DKS takes jibe at Rajanna
summary: DKS responds to Rajanna's vote theft claims.
content:
After Congress MLA and former minister K.N. Rajanna blamed Deputy Chief Minister and KPCC president D.K. Shivakumar for not checking alleged vote theft in Karnataka during the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, the latter took a jibe at Mr. Rajanna on Wednesday, saying, “I don’t have enough experience; I will come back with adequate training.”
In a letter to Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi, Mr. Rajanna had blamed Mr. Shivakumar for not preventing “vote theft” in the State and said had Mr. Shivakumar, as the party’s State president, addressed the “lapses” in the appointment of booth-level agents (BLA), the party could have won an additional 8 to 10 Lok Sabha seats.
In a reply to a question on Mr Rajanna’s letter on the alleged vote theft issue at a press conference in Delhi, Mr. Shivakumar said, “I don’t have enough experience; I will come back with adequate training.”
To a question about the Cabinet expansion, he said, “Ask the Chief Minister; he is the suitable person to answer this question.”
