title: Will ensure job for every Bihari in Bihar: Samrat Choudhary
summary: Deputy CM Samrat Choudhary vows to create one crore jobs for Biharis, emphasizing education and local employment opportunities.
content:
Bihar Deputy Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary on Wednesday (December 24, 2025) said he had pledged to ensure employment for every single Bihari in the State. It was his resolve that the youth of Bihar should study in Bihar and get employment in their own State.
“Our government is continuously working towards the goal of one crore jobs and employment opportunities. We will fulfill this promise made to the public in the next five years at any cost. A separate department has also been created for this purpose,” Mr. Choudhary said.
Mr. Choudhary was addressing the youth at “Goonj,” the annual programme organised by the ABC College of Education in Neura, Patna. In his address, he mentioned Bihar’s historical, cultural, and intellectual heritage, stating that Lord Buddha attained enlightenment, and Lord Mahavira and Guru Gobind Singh Ji were born on this very land.
The seniorBharatiya Janata Party (BJP)leader said the land of Bihar had been a land of knowledge and sacrifice, and now was the time to bring back that glorious history. He said providing employment to the people of Bihar within Bihar was the government’s priority.
Taking a strict stance on law and order, he said a cleaning operation had been started and every single criminal would be sent to jail and no criminals would be spared.
Mr. Choudhary also said the people of Bihar were good and believe in good governance.
“A few people tarnish the image of Bihar with their actions. Biharis have the capacity to build every part of the country — be it Chandigarh or Delhi; Bihar has made a significant contribution to their development. Now, work is being done to transform Bihar so that people do not have to go outside for work,“ he added.
Calling education and skill development the foundation of change, Mr. Choudhary said there were only six medical colleges and a handful of engineering colleges in Bihar.
He said engineering education was being provided for a fee of just ₹10 and the number of polytechnic colleges had increased from 13 to 53. He appealed to the youth to study diligently in college and make a name for themselves in their respective fields, calling them the brand ambassadors of Bihar in true sense.
Listing out the schemes for youth, Mr. Choudhary said the government had implemented schemes such as the bicycle scheme, uniform scheme, scholarships, and financial assistance for preparing for competitive examinations so that no child was deprived of education due to financial constraints.
“Employment and financial assistance are being provided to empower women. Through the industrial policy, efforts are being made to transform Bihar into an industrial hub. Bihar is rapidly progressing on the path of development,“ he said.
Mr. Choudhary added that the State budget, which was once ₹6,000 crore, had now increased to ₹3.17 lakh crore and this was a transformed Bihar and this transformation had been made possible by the hard work and dedication of the youth.

title: Students trained by Adani Skill Development Center land jobs
summary: Adani Skill Development Center celebrates five students securing jobs with Tata Electronics and Amara Raja after completing training.
content:
Adani Skill Development Center (ASDC) on Wednesday (December 24) announced that five students, trained under the Domestic Data Entry Operator (DDEO) course, have secured job offers from Tata Electronics Group in Bengaluru and Amara Raja Group’s Mangal Industries Limited in Tirupati.
The placed students are P. Tharun, T. Chandrasena and I. Sandhya from Lingavaram village; and K. Sreekala and Jeevan Pradeep from Muthukur village. Jagdish Patel, chief executive officer, Adani Krishnapatnam Port Limited (AKPL), felicitated them.
On the occasion, he said: “AKPL is committed to making 5,000 local men and women employable through its skilling arm ASDC and Adani Foundation over the next five years, focusing on project-affected and peripheral villages through skill development in various trades.”
The initiative is part of AKPL’s Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) efforts, aiming to enhance employability and livelihood opportunities for rural women and youth. Fisherfolk community leaders and gram panchayat representatives were present during the felicitation programme.

title: Ten devotees injured after bus rams median on Chennai - Bengaluru Highway in Ranipet
summary: Ten devotees injured when a bus crashed on Chennai-Bengaluru Highway; police restore traffic and investigate the incident.
content:
Ten devotees, mostly women, were injured after the tourist bus they were travelling in hit a concrete median on the Chennai - Bengaluru Highway (NH 48) at Puttuthakku village near Arcot town in Ranipet in the early hours of Wednesday.
Police said that devotees, mostly women, in surrounding villages near Tirupattur town hired two tourist buses to visit Melmaruvathur Amman temple in Chengalpattu. Each bus, on an average, had more than 50 devotees. Buses were proceeding towards the temple on the stretch when the bus that was going in front hit the median after bus driver S. Pushpalingam, 30, a native of Tirupattur, lost control of the vehicle.
Ten devotees and the bus crew were injured in the accident, which happened around 5 a.m. Immediately, other motorists and passersby rescued injured persons, who were then admitted at the Government Taluk Hospital in Walajah town.
Based on an alert, Ratnagiri police inspected the spot. Police towed the damaged vehicle from the carriageway and restored traffic flow on the route. A case was registered. Police said drowsiness of the bus driver could be the reason for the accident A probe is under way.

title: Telangana DCA seeks 100 more drug inspectors as enforcement load outpaces manpower
summary: Telangana DCA seeks to recruit 100 more drug inspectors to manage the growing enforcement demands across 50,000 regulated units.
content:
The Telangana Drugs Control Administration (DCA) is operating under a manpower constraint that senior officials say is no longer proportionate with the scale and complexity of the pharmaceutical ecosystem it is expected to regulate. This comes at a time when the enforcement responsibilities continue to expand across retail, wholesale, manufacturing and laboratory surveillance.
At present, the DCA oversees nearly 50,000 regulated units across the State, including around 48,000 retail medical shops, about 760 manufacturing units and a large number of wholesale establishments. Against this, the number of drug inspectors stands at just about 65 to 70, supported by a small  team at its headquarters and a laboratory staff strength of roughly 10 to 15 personnel.
Speaking toThe Hindu, Director General of Telangana DCA, Shahnawaz Qasim, said: “A proposal seeking recruitment of at least 100 additional drug inspectors was recently submitted to the government. The plan envisages a five-year budgetary roadmap, with the initial phase focused on strengthening laboratory capacity, followed by expansion of field-level enforcement.
The manpower crunch has direct implications for enforcement timelines. While the department has mandated that action on not-of-standard-quality (NSQ) medicines must be initiated within 21 days, inspectors are often stretched between inspections, court appearances, joint operations with central agencies and administrative duties. In several cases, a single inspector is required to handle as many as 25 inspections while simultaneously coordinating with the police, attending court hearings and participating in joint inspections with the Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO).
Despite these constraints, Mr. Qasim said that the DCA has maintained strict enforcement standards. Following inspections, show-cause notices are issued and depending on the severity of violations, licences are suspended or cancelled, or warnings are issued with mandatory follow-up inspections. “All enforcement actions are reflected in the monthly reports submitted to the CDSCO,” he added.
To bolster testing and surveillance capacity, renovation of the Central Drugs Testing Laboratory (CDTL)  is currently underway using central grants, with second phase of upgradation also in progress. “Proposals have additionally been sent for setting up three regional laboratories at Mahbubnagar, Nizamabad and Warangal, which would supplement the central facility and reduce delays in sample testing,” said Mr. Qasim.

title: ‘Coimbatore has huge potential for GCC investments’
summary: Coimbatore has the potential to attract investments for GCCs with its vast talent pool, says an ANSR study
content:
Several companies abroad are looking at Coimbatore to set up their global capability centres (GCC), according to ANSR Global, a consulting firm that facilitates setting up of GCCs.
According to ANSR’s latest city-specific data, 2025 marked a transition for Coimbatore from the engineering and textile industries to GCCs. Coimbatore has more than 60 GCCs and has the potential to be a leader among emerging cities in attracting GCCs. It has almost 2.3 lakh experienced technology professionals and almost 60,000 candidates graduate from its colleges annually.
“What’s drawing GCC interest to Coimbatore in 2025 is not just cost — it’s predictability and scalability. Enterprises are increasingly leveraging the city for analytics and data engineering roles; AI-adjacent and support functions; and engineering services linked to tier-1 innovation hubs,” it said.
“Coimbatore is no longer just a feeder city — it’s becoming a GCC execution hub in its own right, especially for talent-led scale and AI-adjacent work,” the ANSR report said.
Smitha Hemmigae, Managing Director at ANSR, said that in the last five years, Coimbatore saw an annual growth rate of 20 % to 22 % in the GCC segment. A lot of these are in E R& D and manufacturing. Coimbatore offers talent pool, relatively low cost infrastructure, and the IT eco system. It has close to a dozen incubators that nurture startups. The city has potential for all GCCs that want to expand to emerging cities. With the Tamil Nadu government providing incentives for GCCs, Coimbatore has huge potential, she toldThe Hinduon Wednesday.

title: Pinarayi announces ₹30 lakh compensation for kin of mob lynching victim
summary: Pinarayi Vijayan announces ₹30 lakh compensation for family of lynching victim Ram Narayan Bhagale, highlighting xenophobic crime.
content:
Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan on Wednesday announced an ex gratia of ₹30 lakh to the bereaved family of Ram Narayan Bhagale, a Dalit migrant worker from Chhattisgarh who was mob lynched after being tried publicly as an “illegal immigrant and thief” from Bangladesh at Wayalar in Palakkad last week.
Mr. Vijayan said a gang of “xenophobic criminals inspired by schismatic hate ideology” murdered the hapless odd-jobs-man who had arrived in Kerala seeking work to support his two children, wife and mother.
He said the government would deposit ₹10 lakh each in the children’s names as a secure financial investment, with the interest supporting the family until the minors reached adulthood.

title: Remand prisoner allegedly assaults two officers in Mattancherry jail
summary: A remand prisoner allegedly assaulted two officers in Mattancherry jail, resulting in injuries and threats of further violence.
content:
A remand prisoner allegedly assaulted two prison officers inside the sub jail at Mattancherry after he reportedly got enraged by the officers’ instructions to return to his cell after breakfast.
Thanzeer, an accused in a few cases, reportedly attacked assistant prison officers Rijumon Silvester and Binu Narayanan near the jail’s guard office around 7:30 a.m. on Tuesday (December 23, 2025). A case was registered by the Mattancherry police based on a complaint filed by the injured officers later in the day.
According to the first information report, Thanzeer struck Mr. Silvester on the right hand with an iron lid of a vessel storing potable water. He went on to twist the right arm of Mr. Narayanan. Both the officers suffered fractures in the alleged assault.
The accused also threatened to eliminate the officers upon release from jail. He has been remanded in judicial custody after being arrested in a case registered by the Thoppumpady police for obstructing police officers from discharging their duties, police sources said.
He was booked on charges including voluntarily causing grievous hurt, assault or criminal force to deter a public servant from discharge of duty, and criminal intimidation under relevant sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.

title: Collector inaugurates shop selling products made by persons with intellectual disabilities
summary: Collector V.R. Subbulaxmi inaugurates a shop in Vellore supporting products made by individuals with intellectual disabilities.
content:
Collector V.R. Subbulaxmi inaugurated an exclusive shop that sells products that are made by persons with intellectual and developmental disabilities at Sathuvachari near Collectorate office in Vellore on Wednesday.
Officials of Autism Residential Community (ARC), which organised the event, said the shop is part of ‘Made By Special Hands’ initiative that displays and sell handicrafts made by persons with Intellectual and Developmental Disabilities (IDD), which includes persons with autism spectrum disorder (ASD), attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), Down’s Syndrome, and Learning Disability (LD).
The handmade products include paintings, jewellery, puzzles, mugs, mats, candles, and paper bags. The shop is located at 143, South Avenue, Phase 1, Sathuvachari, Vellore. The shop will be open between 11 a.m and 7 p.m on all days except on Sundays.
At present, ARC, which has been serving the community since 2022, provides educational and developmental training for persons on the autism spectrum across all age groups at its Day Activity Centre (DAC) at Sathuvachari.
Currently, 18 students attend the DAC which is supported by a multidisciplinary team of special educators, occupational therapist, vocation therapist, speech therapist, and teaching assistants.
The enclave offers participating individuals a dignified opportunity to earn, a safe place to work, get recognition for their talent, opportunities for vocational skill development, and a pathway to independence and dignity.
On the occasion, Babu, Differently Abled Welfare Officer, Vellore, G.V. Sampath, Chairman, Naruvi Hospitals, Pradeep Jeyathilak, CEO, Autism Residential Community, parents and supporters of the special needs community were present.

title: Polavaram Project Authority satisfied with progress of works
summary: Polavaram Project Authority expresses satisfaction with construction progress, emphasizing timely completion and adherence to approved schedules.
content:
The Polavaram Project Authority (PPA) has expressed satisfaction over the progress of construction works at the Polavaram irrigation project.
A high-level PPA delegation, led by Chief Executive Officer Yogesh Paithankar, visited the project site on Wednesday to review the status of the ongoing works.
The PPA team conducted an extensive inspection of various components, including the Polavaram Hydroelectric Power Project being executed by the Megha Engineering and Infrastructures Limited (MEIL). It also reviewed the components such as the spillway, diaphragm wall, Gap-1 and Gap-2, and upstream and downstream cofferdams.
OIfficials informed the PPA team that works were being executed as per the timelines fixed by the Water Resources Ministry, the Polavaram Project Authority, and the State Government. They said that meticulous planning was underway to ensure completion of the project by 2027, in line with the government’s objective of completing the project ahead of the Godavari Pushkarams.
Emphasising the strategic importance of the project, Mr. Yogesh Paithankar said the Central Government was according high priority to the project and directed the officials and the executing agencies to ensure timely completion, without delays, strictly adhering to the approved schedules and action plans.
The construction progress of the hydropower station was explained by MEIL COO Satish Babu.
The delegation included PPA Member-Secretary M. Raghuram, Chief Engineers C.V. Subbaiah (Power) and M. Ramesh Kumar (P&D), and Director K. Shankar, among others. The team was briefed on the project progress by Water Resources Department Engineer-in-Chief K. Narasimha Murthy.

title: Ex-serviceman ends life in Hassan
summary: Ex-serviceman Kalleshappa, 58, tragically dies by suicide in Hassan amid ongoing harassment over his coffee farm.
content:
An ex-serviceman died by suicide at Ghattadahalli in Belur taluk on December 23. The police have identified him as Kalleshappa, 58.
After retiring from the Central Industrial Security Force, he was granted three acres of land, on which he built a farm and cultivated coffee. About 10 days ago, he visited his brother Ninge Gowda’s house at Ghattadahalli. Noticing that Kalleshappa remained worried all the time, Mr. Gowda enquired and learned that a few people had been constantly harassing him at his farm.
On December 23 morning, Kalleshappa was found dead. He had reportedly shot himself with the revolver that he got while in the service.
Mr. Gowda, in his complaint to the Halebidu police, stated that the people who had been harassing Kalleshappa also allegedly took away his coffee beans, forcing Kalleshappa to end his life.
(Caution: Those in distress and facing suicidal thoughts can call the State’s helpline 104 or call the toll-free number 14416 for counselling.)

title: State seeks allocation of 40-45 tmc of water in river linking projects
summary: Karnataka seeks 40 to 45 tmcft of water allocation in river linking projects to enhance water supply for Kalyana Karnataka region.
content:
Deputy Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar, who participated in the 24th meeting of the National Water Development Authority (NWDA) in New Delhi, has sought allocation of 40 to 45 tmcft of water to Karnataka in the river-linking project of the Godavari and Cauvery and the Varada and Bedti rivers.
Briefing about the outcome of the meeting on Wednesday, he demanded that the Centre provide an additional five tmcft of water to the Kalyana Karnataka (KK) region of the State by linking the inter-State Godavari and Cauvery rivers for drinking water purposes.
The State has been allocated 15.90 tmcft of water by linking the Godavari and Cauvery rivers and 18.50 tmcft of water by linking the Varada and Bedti rivers within the State. A total of 34.40 tmcft of water has been allocated under both projects, said Mr. Shivaumar, who also holds the Water Resources portfolio.
In the first phase of the Godavari-Cauvery river linking project, 148 tmcft of water will be diverted, of which only 15.90 tmcft has been allocated to Karnataka. “We have sought details as to where the water will be given and how it should be used,” he said.
Noting that he had instructed officials of the Water Resources department to prepare a detailed project report for linking the Varada and Bedti rivers, he said the estimated cost of the project was ₹10,000 crore, with 90% of the expenditure borne by the Centre.
The NWDA has been formed under the leadership of the Union Minister of Jal Shakti for river linking, and all States are its members.
“In the wake of the Supreme Court ruling, I have told the Union Minister that we will submit all the documents related to the proposed Mekedatu reservoir across river Cauvery,” he said.
Mr. Shivakumar also demanded funds announced in the Union Budget for 2023-24 for the Upper Bhadra Project. He urged the Centre to issue a notification with regard to the Upper Krishna Project.

title: Indian farmers should learn to compete at global level, says Minister
summary: Indian farmers must embrace new technologies to compete globally, says Minister at Horticulture Mela in Bagalkot.
content:
Indian farmers have to learn to be globally competitive by adopting new technologies in cultivation, processing and marketing their produce, Minister Satish Jarkiholi said in Bagalkot on Tuesday.
He was speaking at the valedictory function of the Horticulture Mela organised by the University of Horticultural Sciences.
“Days are gone when farmers worried only about growing their food. Now-a-days, they need to be shrewd businessmen. They need to adopt modern cultivation and harvesting technological tools, embrace new technology for post-harvest processing and even for marketing their produce. This comprehensive view of agriculture will save farmers and lead to their all round development,” he said.
He presented awards to the best farmers.
“In today’s competitive era, we have to compete in every field — be it exploring the market, growing new varieties, growing more in less land and food processing. We have to accept the challenges before us. We also have to prepare for that. This will enable us to compete at the global level,” he said.
He said that the Horticulture Sciences University has helped farmers in North Karnataka by introducing many new varieties and technologies.
“Many of us have already adopted them. The major crop in this region is sugarcane. But then, a large number of farmers grow horticulture crops like vegetables, flowers, fruits, spices and high value products like areca and coconut,” he said.
“There is also a great need for alternative crops. The horticulture fair is also inspiring farmers to learn from each other,” he said.
Awards were given to Ramesh H. of Bengaluru Rural District, Muniraju B.N. of Bengaluru Urban District, Devaraju G. of Ramanagara district, Channakeshava Swamy of Tumakuru, Sudeshkumar Pattanashetty of Koppal district, Padmavati Bagodi of Raichur district, K. Basappa Channabasappa of Ballari district and Sri Maheshwara Swamy of Vijayanagara district.
MP P.C. Gaddigoudar urged farmers to stay in contact with their counterparts and remain updated with new technologies.
He requested young farmers to explore crops other than sugarcane. “Growing only sugarcane reduces soil fertility. Along with harvesting good crops, attention should be paid to maintaining soil fertility,” he said.
Vice-Chancellor of University of Agricultural Sciences Dharwad P.L. Patil, Horticultural Sciences University Vice-Chancellor Vishnuvardhan and others were present.

title: Pawan Kalyan extends financial aid to elderly woman, family in Ippatam
summary: Pawan Kalyan provides financial support and personal assistance to an elderly woman and her family in Ippatam.
content:
Deputy Chief Minister K. Pawan Kalyan on Wednesday visited Ippatam village in Mangalagiri constituency and extended personal and financial support to an elderly woman and her family.
Pawan Kalyan went to the residence of Indla Nageswaramma, who had openly resisted house demolitions in Ippatam during the previous YSRCP regime, after villagers offered land for the Jana Sena Party (JSP) Formation Day meeting in 2022. Recalling his assurance to stand by her, the Deputy Chief Minister enquired about her health, spoke to her family members, and reassured them of continued support.
As part of the visit, he presented a sari as a Sankranti gift and handed over ₹50,000 for household expenses. He announced that ₹5,000 would be given every month from his salary towards Nageswaramma’s upkeep. He also provided ₹1 lakh to support the education of her differently-abled grandson Manoj Sai and facilitated ₹3 lakh from the Chief Minister’s Relief Fund for the cancer treatment of her son Kondaiah.
Meanwhile, residents of Kolanukonda and Ippatam villages gave him a warm welcome. During his return, Pawan Kalyan interacted with daily wage workers, addressed local grievances, and directed officials to resolve issues related to pensions and basic infrastructure.
Legislative Council Government Whip Pidugu Hariprasad said the visit reflected Pawan Kalyan’s commitment to honouring promises and standing with people in distress.

title: Third-time councillor Saiji Jolly to be Aluva municipal chairperson
summary: Saiji Jolly, a third-time councillor, is appointed Aluva municipal chairperson after Congress secures a majority in local elections.
content:
Third-time councillor Saiji Jolly is set to be the chairperson of Aluva municipality, where the Congress has won a clear majority of 16 out of 26 seats in the local body election. Ms. Jolly was selected unanimously by the Congress Parliamentary Party as its nominee for the top post on Tuesday (December 23, 2025).
Ms. Jolly was deputy chairperson in the previous council, headed by M.O. John, a Congress veteran. This time, she won from the Nazreth ward, defeating the BJP’s Sivapriya G. Kammath.
Born and brought up in Delhi, Ms. Jolly moved to Aluva after her marriage with footballer-turned actor Jolly Moothedan in 1998. A postgraduate in fashion technology, she has worked as a fashion coordinator before entering politics.
Ms. Jolly debuted into electoral politics in 2010 winning from the Market ward. Though she contested the election in 2015 from the General Hospital ward, she could not repeat the win. She fought again from the Market ward in 2020 and won.
Ms. Jolly said her priority would be to ensure the development of Aluva in tune with the vision of her party leadership.
The Congress has also nominated Fassil Hussain, another third-time councillor, for the post of deputy chairperson. He was the chairperson of education, arts and sports standing committee in the previous council.
The Left Democratic Front has six councillors, including four Independents backed by the front, while the National Democratic Alliance has four in the municipality.

title: Kavitha says she is the people’s voice and not a puppet of any party
summary: K. Kavitha claims to be Telangana's true voice, rejecting puppet allegations and addressing irrigation failures and corruption issues.
content:
Telangana Jagruthi president K. Kavitha asserted that she was the true voice of the people of Telangana and categorically rejected allegations that she is being operated from behind by someone.
While acknowledging that mistakes were committed during the BRS regime, she accepted moral responsibility for the period she was part of the party and apologised to the people wherever injustice had occurred.
Strongly criticizing the RRR project, Ms. Kavitha alleged that road alignments are being changed repeatedly to protect the lands of influential individuals, while poor farmers are being pushed into distress. She pointed out that despite High Court orders, alignments continue to be altered due to corruption. Jagruthi will launch an online movement on this issue and organise a round table meeting with affected farmers in Hyderabad on January 5.
Highlighting irrigation failures, she said that not even a single drop of water has reached farmers through the Baswapur reservoir under the Pranahita–Chevella project, despite massive land acquisition. She demanded immediate completion of canals, fair compensation to displaced farmers and strict accountability of officials.

title: CPO dismissed from service citing indiscipline
summary: Senior police officer Umesh U.S. dismissed for indiscipline, including social media misconduct and insulting senior officials.
content:
Umesh U.S., a senior Civil Police Officer attached to the Aranmula police station, has been dismissed from service for repeatedly insulting the State police force and senior officers on social media and for committing acts of indiscipline.
The dismissal was ordered by Pathanamthitta District Police Chief R. Anand. The dismissal order noted that allowing him to continue in service would obstruct the functioning of the police force and tarnish the image of the government.
The action, initiated under the Kerala Police Act, cited persistent behavioural misconduct as the reason for dismissal. It also stated that the senior CPO had earlier faced multiple disciplinary actions for violations related to social media conduct. Mr. Umesh has the option to file an appeal against the dismissal.
As per the order, Mr. Umesh had previously been served memos for violating social media conduct guidelines issued by successive State Police Chiefs. However, instead of submitting appropriate explanations, he posted the memos along with his defiant replies on Facebook.
An inquiry conducted by the Pathanamthitta District Police Chief found that as many as 11 departmental inquiries had been initiated against him, eight of them related to defamatory social media posts targeting senior officers.
Disciplinary action, including  withholding of salary increments, had also been taken against him for criticising the then City Police Commissioner in connection with Sabarimala duty, mocking the government’s UAPA actions using film scenes, and posting content perceived as supportive of accused persons. Action had also been initiated against him on charges of personal misconduct.
The dismissal order noted that Mr. Umesh had publicly mocked decisions related to salary disbursement. It also found his claim that he failed to attend the inquiry due to non-payment of salary to be false. Mr. Umesh had earlier been transferred from the Feroke police station in Kozhikode to Aranmula as part of disciplinary action.
When contacted, Mr. Umesh said he would be moving an appeal against the decision. Mr Anand, meanwhile, was not available for comment despite multiple attempts.

title: Endowments Commissioner inspects Srisailam temple staff quarters
summary: Endowments Commissioner inspects new staff quarters at Srisailam temple, emphasising development and infrastructure improvements for employees.
content: Endowments Commissioner K. Ramachandra Mohan on Wednesday (December 24) inspected the new quarters for the employees of Sri Bhramaramba Mallikarjuna Swamy temple at Srisailam Project Colony in Sundipenta. Nearly 300 permanent staff currently reside in the temple town, and they will be shifted to the quarters in phases, officials said. The shifting is part of the temple management’s decision to develop Srisailam on a par with Tirumala. Mr. Ramachandra Mohan, who inspected the progress of the work along with engineers, ordered the construction of internal roads and installation of street lights. He also wanted them to have tree saplings planted, particularly those of neem, `kadambam’, and almond. He also asked the officials to prepare the proposals for the construction of a temple in the quarters. A total of 297 houses are being constructed for the staff.

title: Hyderabad cyber crime police warn public against fake e-challan payment links
summary: Hyderabad police warn against fake e-challan payment links to prevent cyber fraud; stay safe and verify official sources.
content:
The cyber crime wing of the Hyderabad police issued a warning against cyber fraud cases involving fake e-challan payment links being circulated through SMS and WhatsApp messages.
Cyber fraudsters are sending deceptive messages claiming that pending traffic challans are due for payment and urging recipients to clear them immediately using a link provided in the message. These links closely resemble official government websites, making it difficult for users to distinguish them from genuine portals.
Officials said that once users click on the fake link, they are asked to enter their vehicle registration number, following which a challan amount is displayed. When victims proceed to make the payment, malicious software may be installed on their mobile phones or their banking credentials may be compromised, leading to unauthorised transactions and mobile hacking.
The cyber crime police have advised citizens to make traffic challan payments only through official government portals and cautioned against clicking on suspicious or unknown links received through SMS, WhatsApp or social media. They reiterated that government departments do not send payment links through WhatsApp or personal messages.
The public has also been urged not to share OTPs, UPI PINs, debit or credit card details, or personal information on unverified websites, and to install applications only from official app stores. Keeping mobile phones updated with the latest security patches and antivirus software was also emphasised.
In cases of cyber fraud, victims have been advised to immediately disconnect mobile data or Wi-Fi, contact their bank to block transactions or cards, dial the cyber fraud helpline number 1930, lodge a complaint on the cybercrime reporting portal, and approach the nearest cyber crime police station.

title: Kollam district administration steps up food safety enforcement
summary: Kollam  Collector N. Devidas has given instructions to conduct extensive and stringent inspections across the district to ensure food safety during the Christmas and New Year season.
content:
District Collector N. Devidas has given instructions to conduct extensive and stringent inspections across the district to ensure food safety during the Christmas and New Year season.
Presiding over a meeting to review the district’s general situation, the Collector on Wednesday directed the Food Safety Department to expand its ongoing enforcement activities.
So far, inspections have been conducted in 236 establishments, resulting in the closure of seven unlicensed shops. Notices were issued to 23 establishments while 15 others were fined. Additionally, 23 samples of items, including cakes and wine, have been sent for laboratory testing.
“Health cards will be made mandatory for cooks and helpers in government schools and anganwadis. Furthermore, food safety awareness classes are being conducted in schools. It was noted that Kollam and Karunagappally railway stations have received FSSAI’s ‘Eat Right Station’ certification after a successful audit. Special training is also being provided to Anganwadi cooks, ration dealers, hotel/restaurant entrepreneurs, and traders,” said the Collector.
During the meeting, the Collector released the promotional board for ‘Arogya Thallika,’ an awareness programme launched by Food Safety department to promote balanced dietary habits to combat lifestyle diseases. The meeting was attended by Assistant Food Safety Commissioner A. Sakeer Hussain, District Supply Officer G.S. Gopakumar, and officials from Kudumbashree, Supplyco, and the Fisheries department

title: Sanctity of TTD compromised during YSRCP rule, alleges R&B Minister Janardhan Reddy
summary: R&B Minister Janardhan Reddy claims YSRCP compromised TTD's sanctity, pledging corrective measures and development initiatives under the current government.
content:
Alleging that grave irregularities had taken place in Tirumala during the YSRCP term, Andhra Pradesh Minister for Roads and Buildings B.C. Janardhan Reddy on Wednesday said the sanctity of the Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams (TTD) was compromised under the leadership of former Chief Minister Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy.
Addressing the media at the TDP central office in Mangalagiri, Mr. Janardhan Reddy said the irregularities committed during the YSRCP term were gradually coming to light.
He said the alleged use of adulterated ghee in the preparation of the sacred laddu prasadam had triggered nationwide outrage. Devotee facilities were grossly neglected, forcing pilgrims to face severe inconvenience, the Minister alleged. Mr. Janardhan Reddy said people were gaining clarity on the irregularities and the role played by then TTD Board Chairman.
Refraining from elaborating further “as the matters is sub judice,” he said the coalition government had begun correcting the system by ensuring strict quality testing of all the ingredients used in the prasadam and other services, including donated materials.
He said the government had decided to allow 90% of the common devotees to have darshan on the auspicious Vaikuntha Ekadasi. He said the public response to the coalition government’s governance was positive.
Highlighting the development initiatives, the Minister said industrial investments, recruitment drives and infrastructure projects were accelerating under Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu’s leadership. He also announced major road works worth ₹3,000 crore and assured completion of key projects within stipulated timelines. He also extending Christmas greetings to the public.

title: NHAI backed InvIT gets SEBI nod
summary: The National Highway Authority of India (NHAI) sponsored Raajmarg Infra Investment Trust on Wednesday received approval from the SEBI as an Infrastructure Investment Trust (InvIT) to enable monetisation of road assets through retail and domestic investors.
content:
The National Highway Authority of India (NHAI) sponsored Raajmarg Infra Investment Trust on Wednesday received approval from the SEBI as an Infrastructure Investment Trust (InvIT) to enable monetisation of road assets through retail and domestic investors.
The initiative marks an important step in broadening public participation in the National Highway infrastructure growth story, said a press statement issued by the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways.
Last month, NHAI had incorporated Raajmarg Infra Investment Managers Pvt. Ltd. (RIIMPL) as the Investment Manager for the Raajmarg Infra Investment Trust (RIIT).
RIIMPL has been established as a collaborative venture with equity participation from leading banks and financial institutions, including State Bank of India, Punjab National Bank, NaBFID, Axis Bank, Bajaj Finserv Ventures Ltd, HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, IDBI Bank, IndusInd Bank, and Yes Bank.
Member (Finance), NHAI, NRVVMK Rajendra Kumar will be the Managing Director and CEO (Additional Charge) of the Investment Manager company.
The NHAI relies on several sources of funding for development of national highways other than the budgetary allocation, which include includ Toll Operate Transfer, InvIT and securitisation. In ToT model private investment is invited in completed road assets by granting toll collection rights in return for an upfront payment to NHAI; InvIT where infrastructure asset owners transfer multiple revenue-generating asset Special Purpose Vehicles (SPVs) to a trust which issues units to investors to raise funds that are subsequently invested in the development of infrastructure assets; NHAI also s authorized to raise long term finance from banks by securitizing user fee receipts from toll plazas as an alternate mode of asset monetisation.
NHAI has raised ₹49,000 crore till financial year 24-25 in ToT; ₹43,000 crore through InvIT; ₹40,000 crore through secrutisation.

title: Karnataka Dalit Sangharsh Samiti condemns ‘honour killing’, questions pro-Hindutva leaders
summary: Karnataka Dalit Sangharsh Samiti condemns honour killing, questioning pro-Hindutva leaders' silence on caste-based violence in society.
content:
Condemning the honour killing of a pregnant young woman in Hubballi, Karnataka Dalit Sangharsh Samiti (DSS), founded by Prof. B. Krishnappa, has questioned the silence of various mutt heads and leaders of pro-Hindutva groups.
M. Gurumurthy, State convener of DSS, at a press conference here on December 24 said that the brutal murder of the young woman by her father exhibited the deep-rooted caste-based hatred in society. The father killed his daughter because she married a boy from another community. The boy and his family members also suffered injuries in the incident.
“Recently, RSS leader Mohan Bhagawat stated that there was no caste-based discrimination in society, but caste-related confusion has been created by politicians for their benefits. Then, how does RSS view the honour killing? Does the killing not show how caste-based atrocities have been continuing in society?” he asked.
Mr. Gurumurthy alleged that Hindutva forces had been attempting to bring in Manusmriti in place of the Constitution. Recent statements by pro-Hindutva leaders exhibit their agenda, he added. Another RSS leader, Dattatreya Hosabale, advocated the removal of “secular” and “socialist” from the Indian Constitution. A group of saints who participated in the Maha Kumbh at Prayagraj announced that a draft Constitution for a Hindu nation had been prepared. “These statements show that these forces have no respect for the Indian Constitution, which promotes equality, irrespective of the caste. Such statements indirectly encourage the people who practise caste and perpetrate caste-based atrocities,” he remarked. He also demanded fair compensation for the boy’s family.
Advocate K.P. Sripal opined that the honour killing had left the entire population with a sense of guilt. “We claim to be a civilised society. But the murder has shown how badly we behave. We all should bow our heads in shame. I don’t know why the religious heads of various mutts and so-called Hindutva leaders are silent over the death,” he commented.

title: Prakasam police recover 342 stolen mobile phones worth ₹50 lakh in three months
summary: Prakasam police recover 342 stolen mobile phones worth ₹50 lakh in three months, totaling over 6,447 phones since November 2021.
content:
The Prakasam police on Wednesday (December 24) said that they recovered 342 stolen mobile phones worth ₹50 lakh over the past three months. Superintendent of Police V. Harshavardhan Raju handed over the phones to their owners at District Police Office in Ongole.
Addressing the media, he said the police recovered over 6,447 stolen mobile phones worth nearly ₹9.50 crore across the district since November 2021 and handed over them to their owners. “The police have formed a special team to trace stolen mobile phones,” the SP said.
“Complain to the police if someone tries to sell a high-value mobile phone at a low price. In case of buying a second-hand mobile phone, it is advisable to check the bill before purchase,” he added.

title: Congress divided over selection of  Thodupuzha municipal chairman nominee
summary: Sharp dissent has surfaced within the Congress over the selection of the municipal chairperson for the Thodupuzha municipality, where the party won with a good margin of seats in the local body election.
content:
Sharp dissent has surfaced within the Congress over the selection of the municipal chairperson for the Thodupuzha municipality, where the party won with a good margin of seats in the local body election.
During the election campaign, the party had projected Nisha Soman for the chairperson’s post. However, in a sudden shift, nine out of the 10 Congress councillors submitted a letter to the District Congress Committee (DCC) and Kerala Pradesh Congress Committee (KPCC) presidents demanding the appointment of Litty Joseph as the chairperson of the municipality.
The rift became public as posters appeared across Thodupuzha town. Attributed to “Congress workers”, the posters alleged that the municipality does not need a “rubber stamp” chairperson and criticised the proposed leadership change.
A senior Congress leader stated that a UDF meeting on Wednesday evening would finalise a solution. “The party is considering whether Ms Soman will serve as chairperson for this term or a subsequent one,” the leader said.
In the local body election, UDF gained  power in Kattappana municipality with 20 seats, and LDF got 12 seats. In Thodupuzha municipality, LDF won only three seats, and UDF won 19 seats. The National Democratic Alliance (NDA) won nine seats. The political numbers in the 34-member Thodupuzha municipality remains delicate. Following the 2020 local body elections, the Left Democratic Front (LDF) won 13 seats, the UDF won 12, and the BJP secured eight, while a Congress rebel running as an independent won one seat. The LDF originally seized power in 2020 by awarding the chairmanship to the Independent Congress rebel, Saneesh George.
Meanwhile, the UDF has finalised leadership for the Kattappana municipality in the district. UDF district chairman Joy Vettikkuzhi has been selected as the chairperson, with Leelamma Baby as vice-chairperson. According to party sources, Mr. Vettikkuzhi will serve for the next three years, after which another candidate will be selected to complete the term.

title: Possibility of resuming boating at Madiwala Lake to be examined
summary: Officials are exploring the revival of boating at Madiwala Lake as part of its development into a tourist attraction.
content:
M. Maheshwar Rao, Chief Commissioner, Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA), has directed the officials to explore the possibility of developing Madiwala Lake into a tourist attraction.
Mr. Rao told the South City Corporation officials to examine the possibility of restarting boating at the lake, which was operational earlier.
Madiwala Lake is undergoing development at a cost of ₹15 crore, with works such as walking tracks, culverts, children’s play areas, streetlights, toilets, and bridge construction in progress. A bridge is proposed on the Madiwala Lake bund road to ease vehicular movement near the bus stand. Mr. Rao directed officials to expedite all works.

title: EAGLE Force cracks down on MDMA network, four arrested
summary: EAGLE Force arrests four in Telangana, dismantling an MDMA supply network linked to peddler Sai Varshith.
content:
Four individuals, including three drug consumers, were arrested by the Elite Action Group for Drug Law Enforcement (EAGLE) Force, Telangana, in connection with anMDMA supply network linked to an earlier case involving peddler Sai Varshith.
The arrested were identified as Guda Surendhar Varma, B Vishnu, Deeti Vaibhav and Medipally Praneeth Reddy. The action was taken as a follow-up to the earlier case registered against Sai Varshith, with EAGLE Force teams picking up the suspects from their respective residences.
According to officials, Surendhar Varma, Vishnu and Vaibhav were regular consumers who had been purchasing MDMA from Varshith for the past one year at a price of ₹5,000 per gram. All three tested positive for drug consumption during medical examination. The fourth accused, Praneeth Reddy, though tested negative, played a key role in facilitating financial transactions for the drug trade.
Investigation revealed that Varshith had closed his Canara Bank account in August 2025 after a case was registered against him at the Domalguda police station in an attempt to evade police surveillance. Despite this, he allegedly continued his illegal activities by collecting cash from trusted customers and routing the money through Praneeth Reddy.
Police said Praneeth Reddy, a childhood friend of Varshith, transferred the collected money from his bank account to accounts and QR code scanners provided by a Nigerian drug supplier identified as Mary, also known as Tamiya. This financial arrangement allegedly enabled the continued procurement of MDMA and helped sustain the illegal operation.

title: Resham Kisan Divas celebrated at Central Sericultural Research and Training Institute in Mysuru
summary: Resham Kisan Divas in Mysuru celebrated sericulture advancements, recognizing farmers and promoting new technologies for enhanced silk production.
content:
Central Silk Board (CSB)–Central Sericultural Research and Training Institute (CSRTI) in Mysuru celebrated Resham Kisan Divas on December 23 by felicitating progressive sericulture farmers from different parts of the State and appealing to farmers to adopt new technologies to make India the world’s largest producer of raw silk.
Prathibha H.R., joint director of the Sericulture Department, Mysuru, who inaugurated the programme, stressed the need for bivoltine silkworm rearing, wider mulberry spacing for improved weed management and mechanisation, and effective utilisation of subsidies to enhance cocoon quality and productivity, said a press statement here.
Dayananda, in-charge director of CSRTI, highlighted the importance of properly designing a silkworm rearing house, ensuring adequate ventilation, and adopting climate-resilient silkworm hybrids such as TT21xTT56 and MV1XS8 to meet international silk quality standards. Presently, India occupies the second position after China in raw silk production in the world.
CSB member B.S. Nanjundaswamy said the board was involved in continuous research and development efforts towards the welfare of farmers. He, however, underscored the need to address occupational health hazards in sericulture practices.
Technical sessions during the event featured expert presentations by CSB-CSRTI scientists on the improved mulberry variety AGB-8, integrated pest and nutrient management, judicious use of pesticides, organic fertilisers, drip fertigation, and disease management.
Farmers and scientists discussed issues such as whitefly infestation, root rot, powdery mildew, nano-fertilisers, mulberry spacing, cocoon prices, and adaptability of newly released varieties.
Meanwhile, the deputy director of the Sericulture Deparment, Mysuru, informed participants about the free distribution of inputs and newly developed disease management technologies by the department.
The programme also included an exhibition of recent sericulture technologies, the screening of a technology film, exposure visits to laboratories and experimental fields, and the distribution of technical handbills.
Six progressive sericulture farmers from different parts of south Karnataka were conferred certificates of appreciation for their adoption of bivoltine sericulture technologies, best management practices, and production of high quality cocoons.
The awardees are K. Madayya, Mysuru, Krishne Gowda, Mysuru, L. Paramasivamurthy, Mysuru, Nagesh, Mandya, Basavarajappa, Chikkamagaluru, and Sharath Kumar, Mandya.
The event, attended by more than 70 farmers, officials from the Sericulture Department, and CSRTI staff, was coordinated by scientists Joycy Rani and Manjappa, besides senior technical assistant Justin Kumar.

title: Protests continue in Dharwad, Haveri, Kalaburagi against honour killing
summary: Protests erupt in Karnataka against honour killing of a pregnant woman, demanding justice and awareness on caste discrimination and women's rights.
content:
Protests continued to be staged against the honour killing at Inam Veerapur village in Hubballi taluk of Dharwad district for the second day on Wednesday with members of various organisations coming out to strongly condemn the incident in which a pregnant woman was murdered by her father for marrying outside caste.
The protests were held in Dharwad, Haveri and Kalaburagi.
In Dharwad, under the aegis of Mahila Dourjanya Virodhi Okkuta, members of various organisations and eminent personalities came together to stage the protest against the honour killing and condemn it strongly.
Addressing the protestors, speakers expressed anguish and shock over the brutal assault and murder of the pregnant woman who chose to marry outside her caste.
Even after so much advancement and talk of women empowerment, women are not being allowed to take independent decision on marriage which is highly condemnable, they said.
Submitting a memorandum on behalf of the okkuta, they said that stringent punitive action should be taken against the father of the pregnant woman and those who instigated it and connived with him in carrying out the brutal assault on the couple and her in-laws who are now recuperating in a hospital.
They also said that awareness programmes on secularism and gender equality should be organised in schools and colleges to prevent recurrence of such incidents.
Members of DYFI, Students Federation of India (SFI), Dalit Rights Committee (DHS), Dalit Sangharsh Samiti (DSS), Nomadic Community Organisation and organisations of farmers, writers and artistes staged a protest in front of the Tahsildar’s office in Haveri to condemn the honour killing.
Addressing the protestors, State secretary of the Democratic Youth Federation of India (DYFI) Basavaraj Pujari urged the State government to ensure strict punishment for those responsible, irrespective of their relationship with the victim.
He said that the killing of Manya Doddamani, who married a Scheduled Caste youth, reflected deep-rooted caste prejudice and intolerance. He said that the brutal killing of the pregnant woman by her own family for marrying outside her caste has exposed the persistence of caste hatred and social discrimination.
Recalling the reformist ideals of Basavanna, he said that inter-caste marriages were promoted centuries ago to eradicate caste divisions, yet such incidents continue to occur.
Mr. Pujari urged the State government to provide legal protection to these inter-caste couples, enhance incentive schemes to support them economically and socially and extend special facilities like reservation benefits.
He further demanded public awareness programmes in districts prone to honour killings and sought effective implementation of the recommendations of the G.S. Verma Committee and the Ugrappa Committee to prevent atrocities against women.
A memorandum was submitted to the State government through the Tahsildar by Mr. Pujari and office-bearers of other organisations, including Udachappa Malgi, Veeran N. Gaddi, Narayan Mandal, Kalandar Alligowda and Harish Korpade and others who led the protest.
Members of the Maryade Hayta Virodhi Horata Samiti staging protest a outside the Deputy Commissioner’s office in Kalaburagi on Wednesday.
                                                            | Photo Credit: 
                                ARUN KULKARNI
Terming the honour killing of Hubballi as extremely sensitive and deeply disturbing, members of the Maryade Hatya Virodhi Horata Samiti staged a protest in front of the Deputy Commissioner’s office on Wednesday, condemning the brutal murder of the pregnant woman by her father.
Addressing the protesters, samiti members and activists K. Neela, Arjun Bhadre and A.B. Hosamani said that the case reflected the sensitive and alarming nature of honour-related crimes which were increasing across the State due to intolerance towards the choice made by young people, particularly women.
Such incidents undermine Constitutional values and pose a serious challenge to social harmony, they added.
The agitators demanded that the State government treat the matter with utmost sensitivity and enact a specific and stringent law to prevent honour killing.

title: KLU convocation to be held on December 27
summary: KLU's 15th convocation on December 27 will award degrees to 5,000 students, featuring notable speakers and special honors.
content:
National Academy of Sciences, India (NASI), president Vinod K. Singh will attend the 15th convocation of KL Deemed to be University, scheduled to be held on the university campus at Vaddeswaram in Guntur district on December 27.
At a press conference on Wednesday, KLU Vice-Chancellor G. Pardhasaradhy Varma said Mr. Singh would deliver the convocation address, while Managing Director of Tata Memorial Centre, Mumbai, and Chairperson of the IAP Pediatric Hemato-Oncology division Sripad Banavali will be the guest of honour.
Mr. Pardhasaradhy said degrees will be awarded to 5,000 students — 184 Ph.D. scholars, over 700 postgraduate students and more than 4,500 undergraduate students — who completed studies during the 2025 academic year. He said the graduates comprised 340 MBA, 105 M. Tech, 40 Law, 3,200 B. Tech, 12 Architecture, 48 B. Pharmacy, 330 BCA, 325 BBA, 37 B. Com, 18 B. Sc (Visual Communication), 25 BA, 180 B. Sc Agriculture, 14 M. Pharmacy, 32 M. Sc (Chemistry), and 220 MCA Degree holders.
The degrees will be conferred in person to the students, he informed, adding that additionally, 44 students, who demonstrated exceptional academic excellence in the previous academic year, will be awarded gold medals, while 40 students will receive silver medals, along with cash prizes.
University registrar K. Subba Rao, who is also the convocation coordinator, said elaborate arrangements were being made for the smooth conduct of the event. He said K. Subramanyam and K. Ramakrishna would be the chief conveners for the event.
The press meet was attended by the university pro-chancellor K.S. Jagannadha Rao, MHS dean M. Kishore Babu and other officials.

title: Congress protests in Bengal over renaming of MGNREGA; State Congress chief courts arrest
summary: Congress protests in Bengal against MGNREGA renaming, condemning the removal of Gandhi's name and calling for urgent action.
content:
West Bengal Congress leaders and workers in Kolkata held a protest against the renaming of MGNREGA on Wednesday (December 24, 2025) and marched to Raj Bhavan where many courted arrests, including State Congress president Shubhankar Sarkar.
Over 38 Congress leaders and workers were arrested during the protests as many scuffled with the Kolkata Police. They were not allowed to reach the Governor’s residence and were not able to meet with the governor to voice their concerns.
“The scheme has been stopped in West Bengal for over three years. We want to know why the common people in rural Bengal will not get work due to the failures of the State and Central government.” Mr. Sarkar said during the protests. They also demanded that State government call for an all-party meeting in the State and take up the matter in Delhi to release funds for West Bengal which has been suspended since 2022.
“We strongly condemn the Modi government’s decision to remove Mahatma Gandhi’s name from the 100 Days’ Work (MGNREGA) programme and rename it as “VB-G Ram G”. By misusing Lord Ram’s name, Narendra Modi is tarnishing the revered image of Ram,” an official statement from the Congress State Committee said.
Congress leaders said that removing Gandhiji’s name from the 100-day work scheme is an insult to the Father of the Nation and also an insult to his vision for the upliftment of rural India and its people.
They also alleged that the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) has been systematically trying to dismantle this scheme since they came to power in 2014. Notably, the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA) was enacted in 2005 by the Congress-led Manmohan Singh government.
The Trinamool Congress government and Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee on multiple occasions have already condemned the removal of Gandhiji’s name from the scheme. In retaliation, Ms. Banerjee’s government decided to rename their State’s job guarantee scheme as ‘Mahatma Shree’ to honour Mahatma Gandhi.

title: Minor gives birth to baby; case booked against school van driver in Hassan
summary: A minor girl was allegedly raped by a school van driver in Hassan district several months ago. The incident came to light after the survivor delivered a baby on December 22.
content:
A minor girl was allegedly raped by a school van driver in Hassan district several months ago. The incident came to light after the survivor delivered a baby on December 22.
The girl, studying in a private school, was taken by her parents to a doctor after she complained of stomach pain. The doctor then stated that she was pregnant.
After enquiry, the parents learned that the driver had committed the crime. The Hassan police have registered the case under the POCSO Act, 2012, besides other sections of the BNS. The accused is on the run.

title: Folklore awards announced
summary: Kerala Folklore Academy Awards 2023 announced, honoring talent across categories with cash prizes and citations.
content: Minister for Cultural Affairs Saji Cherian on Wednesday announced the Kerala Folklore Academy Awards for the year 2023. A total of 162 awards were announced across various categories, including fellowships, Guru Puja Award, literary award, youth talent awards and for documentary making. The fellowship carries a cash prize of ₹15,000, while the general awards, Guru Puja award, literary award and documentary-making award carry a cash prize of ₹7,500. The awards also include a citation and a medal.

title: UDF breaks deadlock on power sharing in local bodies of Pathanamthitta
summary: The prolonged indecision within the United Democratic Front over seat sharing in the district panchayat and civic bodies in Pathanamthitta is finally nearing resolution.
content:
The prolonged indecision within the United Democratic Front over seat sharing in the district panchayat and civic bodies in Pathanamthitta is finally nearing resolution.
According to sources, the party has broken the deadlock arising from competing claims by various groups by finalising power sharing arrangements spanning up to three terms. As per the agreement, Deenamma Roy, a member from the Pramadam division, will serve as president of the Pathanamthitta District panchayat for the first two years. The remaining three years will be shared equally between M.V. Ambili and Neethu Mamman Kondoor.
Similarly, Anish Varikkannamala will serve as vice president for the first three years, while Kerala Congress leader Sam Eeppan will hold the post for the remaining two years.
In Adoor municipality, Congress leader Reena Samuel will take over as chairperson for the first two years, after which the remaining term will be shared between Jyothi Surendran and Preethu Jagathy. Sasikumar will serve as vice chairperson during the first term.
In Thiruvalla municipality, Kerala Congress leader S. Lekha will be the chairperson, while the Congress has proposed K.V. Varghese for the vice chairperson’s post. In the second term, Saramma Francis will take over as vice chairperson.
In Pathanamthitta municipality, Sindhu Anil will serve as chairperson for the first two years, followed by Geetha Suresh for one year. Ambika Venu will hold the post during the final two years. Muslim League leader A. Sagheer will serve as vice chairperson for the first two-and-a-half years, after which the remaining term will be shared between Congress leaders Saji K. Simon and Abel Mathew.
Similar power sharing arrangements have been finalised in block panchayats as well.

title: AHINDA convention in Mysuru to push for Siddaramaiah’s continuation as Chief Minister till term-end
summary: AHINDA convention in Mysuru on January 25 aims to support Siddaramaiah's continued leadership as Chief Minister.
content:
AHINDA organisations have decided to hold a mega convention on January 25 in Mysuru to vigorously push for Siddaramaiah’s continuation as Chief Minister for the remainder of the term.
Representatives of AHINDA organisations met  in the city on December 24 under the leadership of K.S. Shivaram, president of Karnataka State Backward Classes Awareness Forum, and chalked out a plan to mobilise a large number of people for the event.
The plans to hold an AHINDA convention in support of Mr. Siddaramaiah comes amid the ongoing speculation over a possible change of guard in the State, with reports of Deputy Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar angling for the coveted post.
Mr. Shivaram, however, sought to make it clear that the convention was not aimed against anyone. “It is also not a show of strength. It has been organised to clearly explain why Mr. Siddaramaiah is necessary for the AHINDA sections and to discuss these issues in depth,” he said.
Reacting to questions from certain sections of the media over the possibility of Mr. Siddaramaiah’s absence from the event, Mr. Shivaram dismissed the reports as purely speculative. “It is too early to comment on the matter,” he toldThe Hindu,while refusing to rule out the possibility of Mr. Siddaramaiah’s participation in the AHINDA convention.
Earlier, addressing the preparatory meeting attended by representatives of various AHINDA organisations, Mr. Shivaram said the implementation of the recently held social and educational survey was possible only under the leadership of Mr. Siddaramaiah, who has emerged as the voice of the AHINDA sections in the State after former Chief Minister D. Devaraj Urs.
The forum’s president further added that the Chief Minister has stood as a strong barrier against communal forces. “Hence, communal elements and sections of the upper castes are conspiring against him. Mr. Siddaramaiah represents the identity of AHINDA communities and we will not give him up under any circumstance,” Mr. Shivaram said.
He also stated that Mr. Siddaramaiah was not merely “fortunate” to become the Chief Minister. “He is a leader with commitment and ideology who has become the Chief Minister through sheer dint of hard work,” Mr. Shivaram pointed out, expressing confidence that the Congress high command will take an appropriate decision in the regard.

title: Vidyashala alumnus felicitated for national achievement
summary: Dr. Ravish Suresh Bannihatti, a Vidyashala alumnus, honored for topping the national INI-SS exam in DM Cardiology.
content:
Dr. Ravish Suresh Bannihatti, who secured the first rank in the country in the Institute of National Importance Super Specialisation (INI-SS) exam for DM Cardiology, was felicitated by Sri Ramakrishna Vidyashala here on December 24.
A native of Hosahalli in Bhadravati taluk, Dr. Bannihatti completed his high school and PU education at Sri Ramakrishna Vidyashala and was the State topper in the science stream in the second PUC examination held in 2016.
Addressing the students, he shared his guidance on achieving success in competitive examinations and also boosted the students’ confidence through a pep talk. He took questions from students of his alma mater and cleared their doubts.
The programme was attended by Swami Muktidananda, president of Sri Ramakrishna Ashram and trustee of Belur Ramakrishna Mutt and Mission, Swami Yukteshananda, correspondent of Sri Ramakrishna Vidyashala, and T.K. Chandrashekar, principal of Sri Ramakrishna Vidyashala, among others.

title: Inam Veerapur residents air grievances as MLA, Deputy Commissioner visit them
summary: Residents of Inam Veerapur express concerns during a visit by officials amid ongoing tensions following an honour killing.
content:
With the situation continuing to be tense in Inam Veerapur village of Hubballi taluk of Dharwad district where the honour killing was reported on Sunday, Deputy Commissioner Divya Prabhu G.R.J., along with Kundgol MLA M.R. Patil and police officials, visited the village on Wednesday.
Meanwhile, the number of arrested people in the case has increased to eight. A search is on for the remaining accused.
The Deputy Commissioner and the MLA, accompanied by Superintendent of Police Gunjan Arya, Police Inspector Murugesh Channannavar and members of Dalit organisations, visited the houses of Vivekanand Doddamani and his relatives which have been locked and barricaded now as the family members are being treated at a private hospital in Hubballi after they suffered injuries in the attack.
Security has been tightened as a precautionary measure.
The Deputy Commissioner and the MLA interacted with the village residents some of whom aired their grievances.
Member of Legislative Council F.H. Jakkappanavar and others speaking to an injured person during his visit to Vivekanand Hospital in Hubballi on Wednesday.
                                                            | Photo Credit: 
                                SPECIAL ARRANGEMENT
Meanwhile, MLAs Mahesh Tenginakai and Prasad Abbayya and MLC F.H. Jakkappanavar visited Vivekanand Hospital in Hubballi on Wednesday to meet and enquire about the health of Vivekanand Doddamani (husband of the deceased Manya) and his family members who are getting treated for injuries they sustained in the assault.
Mr. Jakkappanavar was accompanied by Dalit leaders Venkatesh Sagabal, Ashok Doddamani, Basavaraj Benakal and others during the visit.
He consoled the family members and extended financial assistance personally.
Mr. Tenginakai and Mr. Abbayya consoled the victims and sought details from the doctors about their health and the treatment being given.
On Tuesday night, Ms. Divya Prabhu visited the private hospital where the injured are getting treatment and handed over a cheque of ₹5 lakh to the family members of Vivekand Doddamani.
Along with Vivekanand Doddaani, Mareppa Doddamani, Sunil Harijan, Sangeeta Harijan, Renavva, Ananya Doddamani, Yallappa Doddamani, Huvamma Doddamani sustained injuries in the assault and are being treated at Vivekanand Hospital in Hubballi.
The Deputy Commissioner enquired about their health and sought further details from the doctors treating the injured.
Earlier, there was high drama for some time at the hospital as members of Dalit organisations staged a protest taking exception to the Deputy Commissioner’s visit to hospital on the third day of the incident.
They tried to block her car and staged a sit-in to register their protest against what they termed official apathy. The police intervened to bring normality.

title: Kerala seeks restoration of slashed crores from borrowing limit, submits memorandum to Centre
summary: Kerala requests restoration of ₹22,350 crore from its borrowing limit, citing fiscal challenges and urgent economic needs.
content:
The State government has once again urged the Centre to restore several thousands of crores of rupees allegedly slashed from its borrowing limit, including ₹5,944 crore deducted from the limit for the last quarter of 2025-26, pointing out that the State is facing “serious fiscal challenges” arising from multiple shocks to State revenues and constraints on borrowing capacity.
Kerala has sought, among other things, the restoration of ₹5,944 crore deducted from the borrowing limit reportedly citing off-Budget borrowings by special purpose vehicles (SPV), ₹965.16 crore cut in April 2025 to make up for a shortfall in the Integrated Goods and Services Tax (IGST) balance, and ₹3,323 crore cut in connection with the Guarantee Redemption Fund (GRF).
The total amount that the State seeks to be restored comes to a little over ₹22,350 crore under various components.
Finance Minister K.N. Balagopal placed the request before the Centre during a meeting with Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman in New Delhi on Wednesday.
Although Kerala is entitled to ₹12,516 crore as its borrowing limit in the last quarter of 2025-26, the Centre had given consent only for ₹5,636 crore. The “magnitude and timing” of the deduction of ₹5,944 crore have caused severe fiscal stress to the State, Kerala has informed the Centre. This amount was reportedly deducted on account of the off-Budget borrowings by the SPVs Kerala Infrastructure Investment Fund Board and the Kerala Social Security Pension Ltd.
“Acute cash flow constraints” presently faced by the State includes timely payments of salaries and pensions, welfare and social security measures and the funding of infrastructure works, according to the memorandum. “Such a sharp reduction in borrowing headroom at this critical stage would inevitably disrupt public service delivery and adversely impact the State’s economy,” Kerala has informed the Centre.
Further, the State has also reiterated certain demands that it had raised earlier too. This includes a request that it be allowed an additional borrowing of ₹6,000 crore over the net borrowing ceiling for bearing 25% of the land acquisition cost of the development of National Highways.
Kerala has observed that ₹14,358 crore has already been deducted from the State’s Gross Borrowing Limit in 2025-26 on account of off-Budget borrowings, non-investment in the GRF and Public Accounts Accrual.

title: Govt. releases ₹50.50 crore Christmas gift for pastors in Andhra Pradesh
summary: Andhra Pradesh government allocates ₹50.50 crore for pastors, providing a monthly honorarium of ₹5,000 from December 2024.
content: The Andhra Pradesh Government has announced a special Christmas gift for pastors. Following Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu’s assurance that the monthly honorarium for them would be credited in time for the festival, the government on Wednesday released a sum of ₹50.50 crore for 8,418 pastors, covering the period from December 2024 to November 2025. Each pastor would receive a monthly honorarium of ₹5,000, totalling ₹60,000 for the 12 months, a press release said.

title: Centre imposes ban on new mining leases in Aravallis; protected zone to be expanded
summary: Centre bans new mining leases in Aravallis, expanding protected zones to safeguard the ecosystem and prevent environmental degradation.
content:
The Centre on Wednesday (December 24, 2025) issued directions to States for a complete ban on granting new mining leases in the Aravallis, officials said.
The Ministry of Environment and Forests has also directed the Indian Council of Forestry Research and Education (ICFRE) to identify additional areas and zones in the entire Aravallis where mining should be prohibited over and above the areas already prohibited for mining by the Centre.
"This prohibition applies uniformly across the entire Aravalli landscape and is intended to preserve the integrity of the range. The directions are aimed at safeguarding the Aravallis as a continuous geological ridge extending from Gujarat to NCR and at stopping all unregulated mining activities," a senior official said.
"The ministry has also directed the ICFRE to identify additional areas and zones in the entire Aravallis, where mining should be prohibited, over and above the areas already prohibited for mining by the Centre, based on ecological, geological and landscape-level considerations," the official added.
The ICFRE has been directed to undertake this exercise while preparing a comprehensive, science-based Management Plan for Sustainable Mining (MPSM) for the entire Aravalli region. The plan, which will be placed in the public domain for wide stakeholder consultation, will assess the cumulative environmental impact and ecological carrying capacity, identify ecologically sensitive and conservation-critical areas, and lay down measures for restoration and rehabilitation.
Ongoing mining activities are to be regulated stringently, with additional restrictions, to ensure environmental protection and adherence to sustainable mining practices.
"The government stands fully committed towards long-term protection of the Aravalli ecosystem, recognising its critical role in preventing desertification, conserving biodiversity, recharging aquifers and providing environmental services for the region," the official said.
In November 2025, the Supreme Court accepted a uniform legal definition of what constitutes the Aravalli Hills and Aravalli Range on the recommendation of a committee led by the Environment Ministry.
Under this definition, an "Aravalli Hill" is a landform with an elevation of at least 100 meters above its local surrounding terrain and an "Aravalli Range" is a cluster of two or more such hills within 500 meters of each other.
The Congress has alleged that the move would effectively lead to the opening of tens of thousands of mines and cause irreversible environmental damage.
In a post onX, Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh said the recent "clarifications" on the ancient mountain range given by the Environment and Forest Minister raise more questions.
"Aravallis are part of our natural heritage and have great ecological value. They need substantial restoration and meaningful protection. Why is the Modi government hellbent on redefining them? To what end? For whose benefit? 	 "And why are the recommendations of a professional organisation like the Forest Survey of India being deliberately ignored and set aside?" he asked.
Mr. Ramesh also said, "The very recent 'clarifications' given by the Union Minister of Environment, Forests, and Climate Change on the Aravallis issue raise even more questions and doubts."

title: BJP stages protest over Hate Speech Bill
summary: BJP protests against Karnataka's Hate Speech Bill, labeling it unconstitutional and an attack on freedom of speech.
content:
BJP supporters and activists staged a protest criticising the State government over the Karnataka Hate Speech and Hate Crimes (Prevention) Bill, 2025, in the city on December 24.
The activists were led by T.S. Srivatsa, Krishnaraja MLA, who dubbed the proposed legislation as a draconian act to curb freedom of speech and suppress the opposition.
The activists raised slogans against the government and said that the Bill was not only unconstitutional but an attempt to muzzle the voices of those criticising the government.
BJP leaders tore copies of the Bill and carried placards with slogans on black backgrounds to signal that it was a black law that would take away the freedom of speech from people. The BJP activists said the agitation would be intensified in the days ahead and be held across the State. They further expressed concerns that if it becomes a law, it could be used as a tool for political vendetta by the Congress.

title: UDF announces Sabarinadhan as Mayor candidate in Thiruvananthapuram Corporation, BJP remains undecided
summary: The UDF will also field Mary Pushpam, who has served as a councillor in the past few terms, for the Deputy Mayor post
content:
Even as the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), the single largest party in the Thiruvananthapuram Corporation, continued to maintain suspense regarding its Mayor candidate, the United Democratic Front (UDF) on Wednesday declared K.S. Sabarinadhan as its candidate. The former Congress MLA had won by a narrow margin from the Kowdiar ward in the recently conducted local body elections. ‘
The UDF will also field Mary Pushpam, who has served as a councillor in the past few terms, for the Deputy Mayor post. The front had put up an improved showing this time around, winning 19 seats, as it reversed the downward trend witnessed in the previous two elections. However, the Mayoral fight will be largely symbolic considering the numbers in the 101-member council.
Two days ago, the Left Democratic Front (LDF) had decided to field R.P. Sivaji, long-time councillor and Vilappil area secretary of the Communist Party of India (Marxist), for the Mayor post. The LDF’s tally of seats had fallen from 51 seats in 2020 to 29 seats this year. However, the BJP’s inability to get a majority appears to have led the front to contest the Mayor election.
The BJP, which held a meeting in Thiruvananthapuram on Wednesday, appeared to be unsure about announcing its candidate even two days ahead of the Mayor election on Friday. Former district president V.V. Rajesh, three-time councillor Karamana Ajith and R. Sreelekha, former Director General of Police, are in contention.
Despite scoring a historic victory at the Thiruvananthapuram Corporation in the local body elections, the BJP has still fallen one seat short of the required majority number of 51 in the 101-member council. The two Independent candidates who won in the Kannammoola and Poundkadavu wards have kept their options open.

title: Passport redressal centre inaugurated
summary: A new Passports Redressal and Migrants Facilitation Centre was inaugurated in Rayachoti to assist local residents with passport issues.
content: A ‘Passports Redressal and Migrants Facilitation Centre’ was inaugurated in Rayachoti by Kurnool Range Deputy Inspector General (DIG) Koya Praveen on Wednesday (December 24). Speaking on the occasion, Mr. Praveen said that the centre was opened to bring services of the police nearer to the people. He said a good number of people from Annamayya district go abroad for jobs and higher studies. The centre was set up for the convenience of such people and to redress their problems in passport verification and others. Superintendent of Police Dheeraj Kunubilli was also present.

title: Bird flu recurrence exposes government failure: Kodikunnil Suresh
summary: Kodikunnil Suresh, MP, has expressed concern over the outbreak of highly pathogenic avian influenza in several places in Alappuzha and Kottayam districts.
