title: Sand lorry owners’ federation raises concern over poor quality of M-sand in T.N.
summary: Tamil Nadu sand lorry owners raise concerns over poor-quality M-sand from unauthorized units amid high demand and inadequate regulation.
content:
Members of the Tamil Nadu State Sand Lorry Owners Federation have flagged concerns over poor quality of M-sand owing to the mushrooming of unauthorised M-sand manufacturing units across the State.
The Federation noted there are about 4,000 M-sand manufacturing units in the State. Of this, only 478 M-sand manufacturing units were approved for quality by the Public Works Department (PWD).
S. Yuvaraj, president of the Federation, said several constructions relied on M-sand, particularly in the absence of river sand quarries over the past few years. The State has a daily demand of nearly 25,000 loads of M-sand. In Chennai alone, the demand is about 8,000 loads of M-sand daily, and the shortage of 2,000 loads is met through adulterated sand. M-sand is priced at ₹55 to ₹60 per cubic foot.
While licences for operation of quarries and crushers units are provided by the Mining Department and Tamil Nadu Pollution Control Board (TNPCB), most of them are functioning without quality checks. This has led to the use of substandard materials in residential constructions and government projects, he said.
In a complaint lodged at the Fort St. George police station, the Federation sought action against the authorities concerned in the PWD and Natural Resources department for failing to enforce M-sand rules and curb illegal M-sand manufacturing units. The Federation demanded that all units functioning without proper approval must be allowed operate only after a review by a committee formed by the State government.
Officials of the PWD said the product quality certification was voluntary. The department’s high-level committee has, so far, provided quality approval certificates to 500 units and it is valid for three years for those who own quarries, and for one year for crusher units. Quality checks are conducted for product approval and the renewal of certification. The Natural Resources department is in the process of framing the rules.

title: Forest Department and outsourced personnel get insurance coverage in Karnataka
summary: Karnataka's Forest Department secures insurance for staff and outsourced personnel, enhancing financial protection for wildlife conservation workers.
content:
The Forest, Ecology and Environment Department of Karnataka has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Bank of Baroda to provide ₹1 crore accident (death) insurance to officers and staff of the Forest Department and ₹20 lakh insurance coverage to outsourced personnel.
Environment Minister Eshwar Khandre said the frontline Forest Department staff work day and night, facing dangers while protecting forests and wildlife, and the department has lost several brave green warriors. “This MoU has been signed to provide social and financial security to all of them.”
Mr. Khandre further said that outsourced frontline staff also play a significant role in forest and wildlife conservation. Hence, a ₹20 lakh insurance facility has been extended to outsourced personnel.
“Bank of Baroda will provide ₹1 crore accidental death insurance to all permanent employees of the Forest Department, irrespective of their salary and cadre. In case of death while on duty, the bank will additionally pay ₹25 lakh,” he said.
If department employees continue their pension accounts with Bank of Baroda, the personal accident insurance coverage will remain valid up to the age of 70 years. In addition, the bank will provide life insurance coverage of ₹10 lakh to permanent employees.
The Minister said that awareness should be created about this initiative, and that staff have been instructed to open salary accounts with Bank of Baroda.

title: Here are the big stories from Karnataka today
summary: Karnataka Today newsletter: Six charred to death after bus-truck collision in Chitradurga, and more
content:
As many as five persons heading to their native places for the weekend died and another 28 persons were injuredwhen a container truck hit a sleeper bus, triggering a fire, on the National Highway near Javanagondanahalli in Hiriyur taluk of Chitradurga district in Karnataka early morning on December 25. The driver of the truck, said to be a native of Uttar Pradesh, also died, taking the toll in the accident to six.
Around 2 a.m., the truck carrying beverages from Maharashtra to Nelamangala near Bengaluru jumped over the road divider and hit the oncoming private sleeper bus heading to Gokarna from Bengaluru. The impact set off a fire. Many, including the bus driver and his assistant, succeeded in jumping off the vehicle. However, six persons died. The deceased are Bindu V, her five-year-old daughter Grema, Manasa, Navya and Rashmi Mahale. They were all heading to Gokarna from Bengaluru.
The Hiriyur Rural police haveregistered an FIRagainst the driver of the container truck on the charge of causing death by rash and negligent driving. Meanwhile, CM Siddaramaiah and PM Narendra Modiannounced ex-gratia compensationto the accident victims. While the CM announced ₹5 lakh to the families of the deceased and ₹50,000 to each injured, Mr. Modi announced an ex-gratia of ₹2 lakh from the PM National Relief Fund (PMNRF) for the next of kin of the deceased and ₹50,000 to each injured.
Read our full coveragehere.
The driver of a private bus, whose timely judgementsaved the lives of schoolchildrenen route to Dandeli in Karnataka for a study tour, has received appreciation from local people. Sachin, a native of Holenarasipur in Hassan district, was driving the bus carrying 43 children from a private school in T. Dasarahalli in Bengaluru.
“The sleeper bus overtook me. My bus was a few feet behind when a truck from the opposite direction crossed over the divider and hit the sleeper bus. Due to the impact, the sleeper bus swerved left, and and hit my bus. I moved off the road, crossed the fencing and parked my bus on the service road. All the children in my bus are safe,” Sachin toldThe Hindu.
Karnataka’s Transport Minister Ramalinga Reddy said the primary reason for the collision on NH 48 was that theimpact was likely near the diesel tank of the bus. “The bus caught fire immediately because the impact was near the fuel tank. The truck driver might have been driving rashly or may have dozed off, as the accident occurred late at night,” the Minister said.
Responding to concerns over a spate of similar accidents reported in different parts of India in recent months, Mr. Reddy said that both the Transport Department and the police have been regularly conducting awareness programmes for bus and truck drivers, with a special focus on the risks associated with rash driving and fatigue during night-time travel.

title: Newly-wed woman found dead; family alleges foul play
summary: Newly-wed Aishwarya found dead in Bengaluru; family suspects murder by husband amid allegations of harassment.
content:
A 26-year-old newly-wed woman was found dead under suspicious circumstances at her residence in Bagalagunte, barely a month after her wedding.
The deceased has been identified as Aishwarya. Her family has alleged that she was murdered by her husband, and the incident was made to appear as a case of suicide.
Aishwarya is the elder daughter of Mamata and Krishnamurthy, residents of Nagamangala. She was an MBA graduate and married Likhith Singh, a resident of Bagalagunte, following mutual consent between both families. The wedding took place 27 days ago.
The family members of the deceased alleged that within a few days of the marriage, Aishwarya had complained of harassment by her husband. On Monday morning, both families reportedly held a reconciliation meeting to resolve the dispute. However, later in the evening, Aishwarya was allegedly assaulted, following which she was found dead.
The police said Aishwarya was found dead when the family members arrived. The husband reportedly informed her parents that she had ended her life. However, the victim’s family has expressed strong suspicion and alleged foul play, claiming that the husband strangled her to death and staged it as a suicide.
Based on the complaint, the Bagalagunte police have registered a case and launched an investigation.
(If you’re in distress or having suicidal tendencies, please reach out to these 24/7 helplines: KIRAN at 1800-599-0019 or Arogya Sahayavani at 104 for help.)

title: No fly zone declared in Tiruvannamalai on December 26-27 for Chief Minister’s visit
summary: No fly zone in Tiruvannamalai on December 26-27 during Chief Minister M.K. Stalin's visit for an agriculture exhibition.
content:
Tiruvannamalai Collector K. Tharpagaraj on Thursday declared the district will be a no fly zone on December 26-27 during the visit of the Chief Minister M.K. Stalin, who will inaugurate a two-day agriculture exhibition in Tiruvannamalai town and distribute government financial assistance to beneficiaries.
According to a press release, all individuals and civil agencies are prohibited from flying any non-conventional aerial objects in the district without any prior permission on the said day. The district police will destroy or confiscate any UAVs that violate this restriction.
Further, the operator found violating these orders will be charged under the provisions of law. Approval for utilisation of drones by any operator or civil/government agency is governed by guidelines issued by the Ministry of Home Affairs, the release said.

title: Chief Minister Stalin to inaugurate 280 free houses for Sri Lankan Tamils in Tiruvannamalai on December 27
summary: Chief Minister Stalin to inaugurate 280 free houses for Sri Lankan Tamils in Tiruvannamalai on December 27, enhancing living conditions.
content:
Chief Minister M.K. Stalin will inaugurate 280 free houses built for Sri Lankan Tamils, who have been living in rehabilitation camps at Kasthambadi village near Polur town in Tiruvannamalai, at a cost of ₹22.62 crore on December 27 during his visit to the district.
Officials of the District Rural Development Agency (DRDA), which executes the project, said the Sri Lankan Tamils have been living in dilapidated single room houses with bare minimum facilities since camps were set up in early 1990s. “The new housing quarters also has other facilities like Over Head Tanks (OHTs), community centre and public library. A workshop also forms part of the housing quarters where free vocational training will be provided to beneficiaries,” H.S. Ravi, Tasildar for Sri Lankan Tamils (Tiruvannamalai), toldThe Hindu.
Along with DRDA officials, K. Tharpagaraj inspected the new houses in the village ahead of its opening by the Chief Minister. “All these years, we have been living in a make-shift house with no basic amenities. The new free houses will end our ordeal, providing a decent living for our children,” said K. Sokki, a resident.
Divided into three phases, DRDA officials said the multi-crore work has provided free houses for 111 benefarcies in 2023 under phase-1 of the project. Of total 830 houses in the on-going phase-II work, 252 houses were given to beneficiaries in October this year (2025) and another 280 houses will be given by Mr. Stalin on December 27 (Saturday). “Remaining 190 houses will be given in the third phase of the project. In other words, all Sri Lankan Tamil families (1,131) in the district will be covered under the initiative,” Mr. Ravi added.
As per norms, each house, on an average, will cost ₹8.10 lakh for the State exchequer. Each house, which will be 291 sq.ft, will have a living room, bedroom, attached washroom and a kitchen. The new house comprises a free water connection and power supply.
The camp with new houses will also get a community centre, a common centre for children and a fair price shop. Approach roads to the camp area from the main road will also be re-laid. The initiative was launched by the Chief Minister, M.K. Stalin at a function in Vellore in November 2021.
Tiruvannamalai has the highest number of 11 camps with 3,196 persons. Vellore, Tirupattur and Ranipet have two camps each. A total of 2,239 families have resided in these districts since 1990.
During his visit, Mr. Stalin will also inaugurate 314 completed projects worth ₹2,095 crore. Some of them includes ₹30.15 crore new bus terminus, ₹12.17 crore separate building for public grievances at Collectorate, ₹32.16 crore wholesale vegetable, fruits and flower market complex and ₹Rs 2.83 crore police station for Arunachaleshwara temple.
The Chief Minister will also lay foundation stone for 46 new works including ₹161.90 crore widening of Tiruvannamalai - Harur Main Road, Arcot - Tindivanam Road and Kancheepuram - Thiruvathipuram Road into four-lanes.

title: State keen to allot 100 acres in Mandya to U.S.-based firm, says M B Patil in a letter to HDK
summary: Karnataka aims to allot 100 acres in Mandya to U.S. firm Sanson Group for semiconductor manufacturing, says Minister M.B. Patil.
content:
Karnataka’s Large and Medium Industries Minister M.B. Patil has written to Union Minister for Heavy Industries and Steel H.D. Kumaraswamy, making it clear that the State government is keen on allotting 100 acres of land in Mandya district to the U.S.-based semiconductor fabrication company Sanson Group for establishing a manufacturing unit. However, despite repeated efforts, senior officials of the company could not be reached regarding the proposal.
In a release, Mr. Patil said Mr. Kumaraswamy had written to the State government on October 31 regarding the matter, to which a positive response was sent on November 24. “Meanwhile several attempts have been made to contact Sanson Group’s Chief Technology Officer and Head of Indian Operations, Abhay K. Rai, to seek further details of the proposed project. However, there has been no response from his side so far,” Mr. Patil said.
He said there was no hurdle to allotting 100 acres of land to the company in Mandya district at a location with adequate water supply, power, and connectivity. He added that if a formal request was received from the company, the feasibility of land allotment, along with the required approvals and infrastructure support, would be examined and the proposal would be taken forward expeditiously. The responsibility for coordinating the process had been entrusted to Commissioner of the Karnataka Industries Department Gunjan Krishna, he said.
Stating that the State government was committed to promoting high tech industries, Mr. Patil said it was eager to ensure that the proposed investment project does not slip out of Karnataka. He added that the project would contribute to employment generation and industrial growth in regions outside Bengaluru.

title: Use of chemical fertilisers root cause of many diseases, says Amit Shah
summary: Amit Shah advocates for natural farming, linking chemical fertilizers to diseases and emphasizing benefits for farmers and public health.
content:
Union Home Minister Amit Shah on Thursday (December 25, 2025) termed chemical fertilisers as the root cause of many diseases and made a strong pitch for natural farming, saying it not only increases farmers' income but also saves water and promotes public health.
Addressing a Farmers' Conference held in Rewa,  Mr.Shah said the government was developing a "complete system" — from soil and laboratory testing, certification to packaging — to ensure that the agricultural produce of the country's farmers reaches global level in a better way as there is a huge market for natural farming in the world.
"Chemical fertilisers are the root cause of many diseases today. Natural farming is an approach that doesn't reduce farmers' income, but instead makes their produce pure," he said.
Natural farming is a traditional practice that people have forgotten over the time. A dung and urine of a single indigenous cow can help cultivate 21 acres of land, he said.
"It (natural farming) increases income, saves water, and relieves people from many diseases," he added.
Mr. Shah, who is also Minister of Cooperation, said approximately 40 lakh farmers in the country have adopted natural farming and he has personally practised it on his farms.
This has increased production, not decreased it, he said.
"There is a huge market for natural farming in the world and to ensure that the produce of the country's farmers reaches the global market in a better way, a complete system is being developed - from soil testing to certification, laboratory testing of the produce and packaging," Mr. Shah added.
According to him, Prime Minister Narendra Modi has established two big cooperative institutions through the Ministry of Cooperation, which are doing the work of certification of natural farming produce, its testing in world-class and modern labs, packaging, marketing and export.
Mr. Shah said, "In the coming time, more than 400 laboratories across the country will provide certificates to the farmers, due to which their income will increase by almost one-and-a-half times." It can guide many farmers and cowherds towards progress, he said.
"There is also a cowshed here, and a complete range of natural farming methods based on cow dung has been developed. This approach, which generates incomes of up to Rs 1.25 lakh per acre of land, will certainly prove to be a great blessing for small farmers," he said.
Earlier, Mr. Shah visited the Basaman Mama Cow Project and described it as a "very good approach".
Basaman Mama is worshipped as a folk deity in the Vindhya region. It is believed that he sacrificed his life to protect the environment in this region in the 8th century.
Chief Minister Mohan Yadav, Deputy Chief Minister Rajendra Shukla, Minister Prahlad Patel and several other leaders were present at the event.

title: Youth held for smuggling ganja in Vaniyambadi
summary: A 28-year-old man was arrested in Vaniyambadi for smuggling 14 kg of ganja from Andhra Pradesh in tourist bags.
content:
A 28-year-old youth from Kerala, Mohammed Afsal, was arrested by Vaniyambadi Town police at the bus terminus in the town in Tirupattur district on Thursday on charges of smuggling 14 kgs of ganja in tourist bags.
Police said during a routine patrol at public places, a special police team found Afsal loitering with two large tourist bags at the bus terminus. The police questioned him about the purpose of the visit to the town. As Afsal gave contradictory answers, police checked his two bags and found ganja in them. During interrogation, Afsal told police  he brought the contraband from sellers in Andhra Pradesh. To evade surveillance by police, he boarded local buses to go to Kerala to deliver the consignment to retail sellers in the area.
Police seized the contraband. A case was registered. The arrested person was lodged at sub-jail in Tirupattur town.

title: Three car passengers killed in accident in Tiruvannamalai
summary: Three passengers killed in a car accident with a bus near Tiruvannamalai; investigation ongoing.
content:
Three people, including two women, were killed after the car they were travelling in collided with a Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation (TNSTC) bus near Vettavalam village on the Chittoor-Cuddalore Highway, close to Tiruvannamalai town.
Police identified the deceased as S. Kalaivanan (60), B. Pounnu Ammal (70), Kanagavalli (36), and V. Govindaraj (42), all relatives from Vengaikaal village under Tiruvannamalai Corporation limits.
Initial inquiries revealed that the group was taking Pounnu Ammal, who had been unwell, to a hospital in Villupuram for treatment. The driver, Kalaivanan, reportedly lost control of the car and hit the oncoming government bus, which was travelling from Villupuram to Bengaluru with approximately 35 passengers.
Kanagavalli died at the scene. The three other car occupants were injured but were rescued by motorists and passersby and admitted to the Government Medical College Hospital in Tiruvannamalai. Pounnu Ammal and Kalaivanan later succumbed to their injuries. All bus passengers and crew escaped unhurt. The bus driver fled the scene and remains at large.
The Vettavalam police have registered a case. The bodies have been sent for postmortem, and the mangled car was towed away to restore traffic. An investigation is underway.

title: We do not need anyone’s certificate to hold AHINDA convention, says Satish Jarkiholi .
summary: Satish Jarkiholi says the upcoming AHINDA convention in Mysuru will proceed.
content:
“The AHINDA convention planned in Mysuru on January 25 will go on as per schedule. We do not need anyone’s certificate to hold such an event,” Satish Jarkiholi, Minister and Congress leader said on Thursday.
Speaking to repoerters at his Bengaluru home,. Mr. Jarkiholi  said AHINDA is a social movement and not a political show of strength. However, it can bring political benefits to the party. The successful organisation of the AHINDA convention in Davanagere was one of the reasons for the party coming to power last time,” he said.
“Organising conventions of deprived and backward communities certainly strengthens the party. Such innovative political experiments should keep happening now and then.  The AHINDA movement is our strength. However, there is no rule that we should be organising AHINDA conventions or Dalit conventions. Anyone can do it. We welcome it,” he said.
The AHINDA convention being organised in Chief Minister Siddaramaiah’s home town of Mysuru is being seen as a show of strength by his loyalists such as Satish Jarkiholi to send a message to the party high command to let him complete the five-year term.
Deputy Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar, the apparent contender for the post, has played down the news, by saying he would wish the organisers the best of luck.

title: Congress holding discussions to form alliance with VBA for Maharashtra civic polls: Harshwardhan Sapkal
summary: Congress is exploring an alliance with Vanchit Bahujan Aghadi for Maharashtra's civic polls, enhancing election strategies and candidate selection.
content:
Maharashtra Congress chief Harshwardhan Sapkal on Thursday (December 25, 2025) said his party is holding discussions to form an alliance with Prakash Ambedkar's Vanchit Bahujan Aghadi (VBA) for the upcoming municipal corporation elections.
Both parties have authorised their local leadership to take decisions on an alliance, Mr. Sapkal said after a meeting of the Congress state election committee at Tilak Bhavan in Dadar.
"There is a strong desire among leaders on both sides for a Congress-Vanchit alliance. There is good communication between the leaders, and sincere efforts are being made to make the alliance possible for the corporation polls," Mr. Sapkal said.
At the meeting held in Tilak Bhavan, candidate selection for 28 municipal corporations excluding Mumbai, based on recommendations from district Congress committees and keeping social representation in mind, were discussed along with strategies for election management.
Leader of Opposition Vijay Wadettiwar, Legislative Council group leader Satej Patil, former chief ministers Prithviraj Chavan and Sushilkumar Shinde, former ministers and AICC office-bearers, attended the meeting.
Mr. Sapkal said the civic poll schedule was announced on December 15, following which the party immediately began its election planning.
He added that discussions are also underway with the Shiv Sena (UBT) led by Uddhav Thackeray, a constituent of the Maha Vikas Aghadi and INDI bloc.
Mr. Sapkal added he is not directly involved in alliance talks for the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation.
AICC secretary U.B. Venkatesh has been entrusted with holding discussions with the Vanchit Bahujan Aghadi, he said.
Polls to 29 municipal corporations, including Mumbai, will be held on January 15, while votes will be counted the next day.

title: A.P. will be garbage-free soon, says MA&UD Minister
summary: Andhra Pradesh aims to be garbage-free with eight new waste-to-energy plants, transforming waste into electricity and improving sanitation.
content:
Andhra Pradesh will soon become a garbage-free state with the establishment of eight Waste-to-Energy Recycling Plants. Apart from the existing two plants in Visakhapatnam and Guntur, the government has announced four plants at Nellore, Kakinada, Kadapa and Kurnool. Two more plants are coming up at Vijayawada and Tirupati, MA&UD Minister Ponguru Narayana said.
On the sidelines of a review meeting at Nellore Municipal Corporation (NMC) on Wednesday, he said, “Though the YSRCP government had left over 85 lakh tonnes of garbage, the coalition government had cleared it two weeks ahead of the deadline of October 2. The state will be garbage-free once the remaining 30 lakh tonnes are removed from the dump yard grounds.”
“The State produces nearly 7,500 tonnes of garbage a day. With the help of the waste-to-energy plants, it will be converted into electricity. Companies like Jindal Urban Infrastructure Limited and Antony Lara Renewable Energy Private Limited will be investing ₹350 to ₹400 crore to set up each plant,” he said.
Speaking about the measures to avoid the threat of floods in Nellore, he said, “The government has sanctioned ₹50 crore for the repair of canals. As per the new plan of the NMC, only 20% of the people who are living by encroaching on the canals will lose their houses.”
Referring to the anti-encroachment drive, the Minister said, “Steps will be taken to ensure that the poor people are given alternate options like TIDCO houses. Some people are spreading falsehood over the issue for political gains.”
The Minister presented Chief Minister Relief Fund (CMRF) cheques of ₹22.42 lakh to 29 beneficiaries.

title: Interstate zip theft gang arrested at Secunderabad station; gold jewellery worth ₹25 lakh recovered
summary: Interstate gang arrested at Secunderabad station; ₹25 lakh in gold jewellery recovered from thefts on long-distance trains.
content:
Two persons of an interstategang involved in thefts on long-distance trainswere arrested by the Government Railway Police and Railway Protection Force (RPF) at Secunderabad Railway Station on Thursday (December 25, 2025), leading to the recovery of gold ornaments weighing about 210 grams, valued at ₹25 lakh.
The arrested accused were identified as 39-year-old Kokila Maniraju alias Raju Selvam, a resident of Bengaluru, and 27-year-old S. Dina, from Vellore district in Tamil Nadu. The police said both were apprehended at around 8 a.m. near gate number 2 of the Station while loitering allegedly with the intention of committing thefts.
Investigations revealed that Kokila was a habitual offender who was previously been jailed in four property offence cases registered at various police stations in Hyderabad. Dina, who was struggling financially, is said to have approached Kokila about a month ago, after which they allegedly decided to commit thefts together.
On the night of December 2, the accused booked tickets in the AC coach of the Nanded Express, posing as passengers travelling from Visakhapatnam to Charlapalli. The Police said that while other passengers were asleep, the duo tactically opened the zips of bags belonging to two women passengers and stole purses containing gold jewellery. After the thefts, they moved to another coach and later got down at Charlapalli Station and managed to escape.
Cases have been registered under Section 305(c) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita in connection with the two thefts. Further investigation is underway.

title: Hyderabad police rolls out intensify drunk driving checks ahead of New Year; 304 motorists caught on first day
summary: Hyderabad police intensify drunk driving checks until December 31 to ensure public safety ahead of New Year celebrations.
content:
The Hyderabad City Traffic Police haveintensified enforcement drives across the Hyderabad Police Commissionerateto ensure public safety ahead of the New Year Eve.
Special drunk driving inspections began on Wednesday (December 24, 2025) and will continue till December 31, the police said. On the first day of the drive, 304 motorists were caught driving under the influence of alcohol, including one minor. Police seized 304 vehicles from the violators as part of the enforcement action.
Hyderabad Police Commissioner, V.C. Sajjanar, personally supervised field-level drunk driving inspections at the TG Study Circle in Banjara Hills around the midnight. He reviewed inspection procedures, assessed the performance of personnel on duty and issued instructions to streamline enforcement.
During the drive, the Commissioner interacted with motorists caught driving under the influence and cautioned them about the risks associated with drunk driving, stating that such behaviour endangered both drivers and other road users.
Speaking to the media, Mr. Sajjanar said a special enforcement drive had been launched across the city to prevent any untoward incidents during the festive period. Seven additional platoons have been deployed to strengthen the existing force, while intensive checking is being carried out at 120 locations within the Hyderabad Police Commissionerate limits.
The Commissioner warned that there would be zero tolerance towards drunk driving. Vehicles of violators would be seized immediately, a fine of ₹10,000 imposed and offenders could face up to six months in prison. Depending on the seriousness of the violation, police would also recommend to the Transport Department permanent cancellation of driving licences, he said.
The traffic police have appealed to citizens to act responsibly and avoid driving after consuming alcohol, stating that strict legal action would continue through the New Year period.

title: BJP names V.V. Rajesh as Thiruvananthapuram mayoral candidate after historic win
summary: BJP names V.V. Rajesh as mayoral candidate after historic victory in Thiruvananthapuram, ending 45 years of Left rule.
content:
The BJP on Thursday (December 25, 2025) decided to field former district president V.V. Rajesh as its candidate for the post of Mayor of the Thiruvananthapuram Corporation, which the party won for the first time, ending 45 years of Left rule.
Woman councillor Asha Nath will be the party's candidate for Deputy Mayor.
The names were announced by the party's State general secretary, S. Suresh, at a meeting of the newly elected BJP councillors of the corporation and the party's district leaders.
The decision followed prolonged discussions within the party's State and district leadership.
Earlier, discussions had focused on retired DGP R. Sreelekha as a possible mayoral candidate, but a section of the party is learnt to have opposed her elevation.
Just ahead of the announcement, in a post onX, BJP State chief Rajeev Chandrasekhar said he had met BJP national president J.P. Nadda and national working president Nitin Nabin to seek their guidance on organisational issues related to the party's Kerala unit.
"On behalf of every karyakarta, I thank them for their support," he said.
The BJP secured control of the Thiruvananthapuram Corporation with 50 seats, breaking a Left stronghold that had lasted for four decades. The Congress-led UDF also made significant gains by doubling its seat tally.
In the three-cornered contest, Thiruvananthapuram ultimately swung in favour of the BJP.

title: SC/ST Commission chairman condemns killing of pregnant woman over inter-caste marriage in Dharwad
summary: Karnataka SC/ST Commission chairman visits Inam Veerapur, condemning a tragic honor killing and addressing community concerns.
content:
L. Murthy, chairman, Karnataka Scheduled Caste, Scheduled Tribes Commission, on Thursday visited Inam Veerapur village in Hubballi taluk of Dharwad district, where a pregnant woman was allegedly killed by her father for marrying outside their caste.
Dr. Murthy visited Vivekanand Doddamani, husband of the deceased, and his family members at Vivekanand Hospital in Hubballi, where they are undergoing treatment. Dr. Murthy later held a meeting with the officials before heading to the village.
Speaking to presspersons after meeting the injured persons, Dr. Murthy said that it was highly condemnable that the heinous act had been committed in a district known for its culture.
L. Murthy, chairman, Karnataka Scheduled Caste, Scheduled Tribes Commission,  visiting the injured persons at a private hospital in Hubballi on Thursday.
                                                            | Photo Credit: 
                                KIRAN BAKALE
He said that a young woman had been killed for marrying outside her caste, and what was even shocking was the fact that deep-rooted hatred towards the lower caste had resulted in a father killing his own daughter. Although the police arrested the accused, there was an atmosphere of fear in the village. Steps would be taken to provide permanent rehabilitation to the family after addressing the issue with the government, he said.
To a query, he said that he had received a few complaints against officials in connection with the incident and steps would be taken to punish the guilty after thorough inquiry.
During his visit to the village, Dr. Murthy visited the house of Vivekanand Doddamani, who had lost his wife in the incident of honour killing, the place of assault, and where the murder took place, and collected information from the residents, police officials and members of various dalit organisations about the incident. He gave instructions to the officials.
Dr. Murthy was accompanied by Sunil Ukkali, member of the commission; H.S. Shivaramu, secretary; Gunjan Arya, Superintendent of Police; Geeta C.D., Additional DC, and office bearers of the Dalit organisations M. Aravind, Gurunath Ullikashi, Premanath Chikkatumbal, and Paramesh Kale.
Pramod Mutalik, head of Sri Rama Sene, visited the hospital and enquired about the health of the injured persons in the assault. Expressing shock over a father killing his daughter over inter-caste marriage, he said the incident showed deep-rooted casteism in the society and that the dream of B.R. Ambedkar has not been fulfilled yet. He demanded that the accused in such cases should be shot dead.

title: Chandrababu Naidu breaching bail conditions, alleges YSRCP leader
summary: YSRCP accuses CM Chandrababu Naidu of breaching bail conditions and misusing power to close cases against him.
content:
The YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) has accused Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu of “closing all cases against him within a month by misusing institutional powers.”
“The party will pursue the issue, including taking it to the notice of the Supreme Court,” said party general secretary and former Additional Advocate General Ponnavolu Sudhakar Reddy while addressing the media in Hyderabad on Thursday.
“Mr. Naidu has been breaching his bail conditions by influencing institutions to close cases against him. We will approach the highest judicial authority to expose his misdeeds,” he said.
“The police who filed cases against Mr. Naidu are now clearing him, citing ‘mistake of fact’, and this clearly indicates his influence over institutions,” the YSRCP leader alleged.
“Mr. Naidu had been jailed for 53 days in the skill development case. The police filed a chargesheet after questioning 150 witnesses and recording statements of 18 officials in the alleged ₹371-crore scam. The Central agencies were also involved, and some of the accused served jail term. Despite a quash petition pending before the Supreme Court, the case has been closed,” the YSRCP leader alleged.
Mr. Sudhakar Reddy also alleged that Mr. Naidu was involved in cases such as Inner Ring Road, assigned lands, and liquor scam, all running into crores of rupees. “We will knock on the doors of the apex court and take the matter to its logical conclusion,” he said.

title: Christmas celebrated with traditional gaiety in Mysuru
summary: Mysuru celebrated Christmas with traditional gaiety, featuring festive gatherings, prayers, and cultural programs at various churches.
content:
Christmas was celebrated with traditional gaiety and religious fervour at churches across the city on December 25.
St. Philomena’s Church, St. Bartholomew’s Church, Hardwicke Church, and Wesley Cathedral witnessed many devotees gather to offer prayers and catch a glimpse of infant Jesus in his crib. Most churches in the city and those on the outskirts were illuminated on Christmas Day.
At St. Philomena’s Church, many attended midnight mass, apart from tourists and persons from different faiths pouring in to experience the festive vibes at the heritage structure, which was constructed in 1936.
In the run up to the festival last week, the Bishop of Mysuru, Francis Serrao S.J., had conducted special prayers to herald Christmas at the Mysuru Central Prison. He had addressed the inmates and spread a message of love, empathy and compassion. This was followed by cultural programmes.

title: NITK develops jute-based geocell as alternative to plastic in road works
summary: NITK develops jute geocells as a sustainable, cost-effective alternative to plastic for road construction and slope stabilization.
content:
Researchers at the National Institute of Technology Karnataka (NITK), Surathkal, have developed an industrially manufactured ‘jute geocell’ that can replace plastic geocells used in road construction and slope stabilisation.
The project is funded by the National Jute Board under the Union Ministry of Textiles and was executed at NITK Surathkal in collaboration with Birla Jute Mills. It is designed to be cheaper, environmentally sustainable, and suitable for large-scale use, particularly in rural and ecologically sensitive regions.
Geocells are three-dimensional, honeycomb-like structures placed beneath roads or on slopes to strengthen weak soil, improve load-bearing capacity, and control erosion. At present, most geocells used in India are made from petroleum-based polymers such as high-density polyethylene or polypropylene. While effective, these materials are expensive, non-biodegradable, and raise long-term environmental concerns, including microplastic pollution.
Laboratory studies conducted as part of the NITK research show that jute geocells perform on par with conventional polymeric geocells. Tensile strength tests recorded values of about 15.7 kilonewtons per metre, comparable to or higher than many plastic geocells currently in use. Plate load tests showed that soil reinforced with jute geocells achieved up to a 120% increase in bearing capacity, along with a significant reduction in settlement.
One of the key reasons for this performance is the natural surface texture of jute. Researchers found that the surface roughness of jute geocells is more than 10 times higher than that of polymeric geocells, which allows stronger interaction between soil and reinforcement. This improves load transfer without the need for perforations or chemical treatments commonly used in plastic systems.
A major innovation of the study lies in its manufacturing method. Instead of hand-stitched natural fibre geocells, which are labour-intensive and inconsistent, the team developed a mechanised stitching process using existing jute mill machinery. Jute fabric is cut into uniform strips and assembled into a honeycomb structure through machine stitching to enable consistent quality and industrial-scale production. This approach reduced production costs by nearly 80%, making the technology economically viable for public infrastructure projects, officials from the NITK said.
Because of their cost advantage and environmental benefits, the jute geocells are considered suitable for rural and low-volume roads, pavement subgrade and base reinforcement, slope stabilisation and landslide mitigation, erosion control on embankments and riverbanks, landfill cover systems and retaining structures.
From an environmental perspective, jute is a biodegradable and carbon-negative natural fibre, with cultivation capable of sequestering approximately 4.88 tonne of carbon dioxide per tonne of fibre. The technology also supports India’s domestic jute industry and rural employment.
The researchers noted that as a natural material jute is biodegradable and its long-term durability under extreme environmental exposure requires further study. However, for many temporary and semi-permanent infrastructure applications, this characteristic is seen as an advantage rather than a limitation.
Future work will focus on large-scale field trials, development of Indian standards for natural fibre geocells, enhancement of durability through eco-friendly treatments, and integration of the technology into national rural road and slope protection programmes. The system also has potential for adoption in other developing countries facing similar cost and environmental constraints.

title: BRS leaders hit back at CM for using ‘abusive’ language against KCR
summary: BRS leaders criticize CM Revanth Reddy for using abusive language against KCR, calling it unbecoming for a Chief Minister.
content:
HYDERABAD
The Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) questioned the ‘uncalled for’ comments made by Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy against BRS and its founder K. Chandrasekhar Rao, and said such language against the one who fought for and achieved statehood to Telangana is unbecoming of a Chief Minister.
Speaking at Siddipet, former minister T. Harish Rao said Mr. Revanth Reddy was using ‘street language’ against Mr.Chandrasekhar Rao who achieved Telangana. But for Mr. Chandrasekhar Rao, Mr. Revanth Reddy would not even have become a Minister, let alone becoming the Chief Minister.
“One can’t expect better language given the political journey of Mr. Reddy so far and he’s know for horse-trading the legislators as he was caught red-handed with money while trying to bribe an MLC in the past for enlisting his support in the Legislative Council election to a candidate fielded by the party with which Mr. Reddy was associated with then,” Mr. Harish Rao said.
He alleged that Mr. Reddy was doing real estate business with the lands acquired for the Pharma City project and his government was clearing bills only to those who were giving 20% commission.
At Suryapet, another former Minister, G. Jagadish Reddy, said with his cheap comments Mr. Revanth Reddy had proved again that he was only a ‘low-level’ leader. He sought to know whether Mr. Chandrasekhar Rao had ever taken Mr. Revanth Reddy’s name during the last two years. Instead of speaking on the issues raised by Mr. Chandrasekhar Rao, the Chief Minister was getting personal as he had nothing to claim or tell about.
Whip of BRS Legislature Party K.P. Vivekanand said it was unfortunate that the State was being headed by a person whose language was worsening against opponents and that his two-year rule had proved he had learnt nothing even after getting elected as ZPTC member, MLC, MLA, MP and becoming Chief Minister. Party leaders Rasamayi Balakishan, Chirumarthi Lingaiah and others also reacted.

title: North Zone police warn liquor shop owners against violations
summary: North Zone police warn liquor shop owners of strict action for excise violations and emphasize public safety compliance measures.
content:
The Hyderabad City Police conducted a coordination and sensitisation meeting with liquor shop owners operating within the North Zone, warning them of stringent action for any violation of excise rules or lapses affecting public safety.
The meeting, chaired by North Zone DCP S Rashmi Perumal, focused on the responsibilities of licence holders in maintaining law and order and ensuring strict compliance with excise regulations. Wine shop owners were instructed to adhere to permitted liquor sale timings and were categorically warned against selling alcohol to minors or allowing consumption by underage persons.
Police officials stressed the need to prevent overcrowding and ensure orderly conduct at all premises, while cautioning licence holders against overcharging, illegal sales or unauthorised extension of operating hours. Owners were also directed to install CCTV cameras covering entry and exit points, billing counters and common areas, and to ensure that the systems remain functional with adequate data backup for review when required.
The police made it clear that in the event of assaults, quarrels or medical emergencies, immediate intimation to the police is mandatory and that FIRs would be registered without delay against those responsible. Owners were also directed to deploy trained, physically fit and alert security personnel capable of handling crowd control, especially during peak hours, and to ensure that security staff remain sober at all times.
Police cautioned that any breach of excise rules or the instructions issued during the meeting would invite stringent legal action. The public was also urged to cooperate with enforcement agencies and adhere to the law to ensure public safety and orderly conduct.

title: Leverage potential of PPP model to strengthen healthcare infrastructure, says Union Health Minister J.P. Nadda
summary: Union Health Minister J.P. Nadda urges states to adopt PPP model for healthcare expansion, offering significant financial support through Viability Gap Funding.
content:
The Union Government has called upon State governments to extensively utilise the Public–Private Partnership (PPP) model to accelerate the expansion of healthcare infrastructure and improve the quality of medical services.
Emphasising the vast potential of the PPP in the health sector, the Central government has advised the State governments to prepare project plans to be implemented over the next three years.
Union Minister for Health and Family Welfare J.P. Nadda has addressed a letter to Andhra Pradesh’s Minister for Health, Medical Education and Family Welfare Satya Kumar Yadav in this regard.
In the letter, Mr. Nadda has outlined the successes achieved through the PPP model in various sectors since 2000, while underlining the growing necessity of adopting the model in the healthcare sector.
Along with the letter, Mr.  Nadda has also shared the comprehensive policy document detailing the framework for implementing the PPP projects in the healthcare sector.
To encourage PPP projects in healthcare, the Centre has offered substantial financial support under the Viability Gap Funding (VGF) scheme.
Up to 60% of the total project cost will be provided as VGF assistance for setting up medical colleges and other healthcare infrastructure, says Mr. Nadda. For pilot projects, the funding can go up to 80%, he says. This is in addition to the 50% assistance towards operational expenses for the first five years, he adds. The VGF support will be shared equally by the Central and State governments, the Union Minister says.
Rapid expansion of healthcare infrastructure, improved quality and accessibility of services, enhanced efficiency through innovation, sustainable project development through shared risks, increased transparency and accountability, and faster and better healthcare delivery are some of the key benefit of the PPP model, Mr. Nadda says in the letter.
Noting that projects worth over ₹2,000 crore have been approved under the VGF scheme so far, the Union Minister says that 919 dialysis centres are operating under the PPP model across 20 States.
To effectively tap the emerging opportunities, the Union Minister has advised the Andhra Pradesh Government to set up a dedicated PPP Cell to facilitate project planning and coordination with the Centre.
Responding to the letter, Mr. Satya Kumar, while expressing gratitude for the guidance and support being extended by the Centre, has outlined the government’s efforts to develop 10 medical colleges in the State under the PPP model.

title: Private firm employee held with a live bullet at Cubbon Park Metro Station
summary: A 21-year-old employee was detained at Cubbon Park Metro Station for carrying a live bullet during a security check.
content:
Security personnel at the Cubbon Park Metro Station caught a 21-year-old private firm employee who allegedly carried a live bullet, during a routine security check on Tuesday.
The suspect, identified as Mohammed Suhail, a resident of Chikkamagaluru, was attempting to enter the station when the security staff checked his baggage at the entry gate and found a live bullet. He was immediately detained and later handed over to the Commercial Street Police for further investigation.
Based on a complaint filed by G.N. Lokesh, assistant sub-inspector, Suhail has been booked under relevant sections of the Arms Act, 1959 and taken into custody.
During questioning, Suhail reportedly told the police that he had got the bullet from his friend, a hairdresser from Chikkamagaluru, and kept it as a keepsake, the police said.
The police have sent the seized bullet to the Forensic Science Laboratory (FSL) for analysis and have launched a probe to verify his claims.

title: ‘Neuro Justice Trilogy’ proposes function-based approach to disability assessment in accident cases
summary: The Neuro Justice Trilogy advocates for a function-based approach to disability assessment in motor accident compensation cases.
content:
In a step towards rethinking how courts assess disability and compensation in motor accident cases, the Neuro Justice Trilogy and the Neuro Justice Framework Handbook were released at the NIMHANS Convention Centre here on Thursday.
Authored by functional neurosurgeon Sharan Srinivasan and neurorehabilitation expert Prathiba Sharan, the books argue for a shift from a symptom-based assessment of injury to a function-based understanding of disability- focusing on how neurological injury affects a person’s ability to live, work, and participate in society.
Supreme Court judge Aravind Kumar, who released the books, said the work reflected a meaningful intersection of law, neuroscience, and ethics, and underlined the growing importance of interdisciplinary approaches in shaping future justice systems.
Former Supreme Court judge R.V. Raveendran, who has delivered several landmark judgments in motor vehicle accident cases, said the trilogy provided judges with a clearer roadmap to deal with complex neurological disabilities that are often inadequately captured by conventional medical certificates.
Minister for Health Dinesh Gundu Rao said the framework had relevance beyond courts, particularly for public health and rehabilitation. He noted that integrating medical science with governance was essential to ensure fair outcomes for accident victims and their families.
Deputy Speaker of the Karnataka Legislative Assembly Rudrappa Lamani, who recently recovered from brain and spinal injuries he suffered in a serious road accident, spoke of the lack of awareness around neurorehabilitation services. He stressed the need for affordable, multidisciplinary rehabilitation centres in every district, noting that many patients and families remain unaware of facilities that could aid recovery.
Speaking at the event, Dr. Srinivasan said the idea of ‘Neuro Justice’ emerged from years of treating trauma patients who survived injuries but struggled to secure fair compensation because the functional impact of brain injuries was poorly understood in legal settings.
The neurorehabilitation expert, Dr. Sharan, highlighted the challenge of ‘invisible disabilities’ such as memory loss, behavioural changes, and impaired decision-making, which often go uncompensated despite severely affecting quality of life.
A key feature of the launch was the introduction of the Neuro Justice Framework (NJF) version 1.0, a structured model to assess functional disability. The framework incorporates global disability classifications and Indian legal provisions to help courts better evaluate loss of function, rehabilitation potential, and fair compensation.
Police Commissioner Seemanth Kumar Singh and several senior neurologists and rehabilitation experts attended the event. Experts from neuroscience and disability advocacy also shared perspectives, including Paralympian K.Y. Venkatesh, who spoke about the importance of restoring dignity and participation after injury.
Published in public interest by the Swasthya Aarogya Foundation Trust, the trilogy seeks to address delays and inconsistencies in motor accident compensation cases. The authors noted that with nearly nine lakh such claims pending nationwide, a function-based approach could help courts deliver more timely and equitable justice.

title: Kerala Lok Bhavan's December 25 event draws flak from Labour Minister Sivankutty
summary: Kerala Minister Sivankutty criticizes Lok Bhavan's Good Governance Day event on Christmas, calling it undemocratic and against labor rights.
content:
Kerala General Education Minister V. Sivankutty on Thursday (December 25, 2025) strongly criticised the decision to hold special programmes at Lok Bhavan on Christmas Day, alleging that employees were effectively denied a holiday on a major festival.
The Minister made the remarks after Lok Bhavan observed Good Governance Day on December 25 to mark the birth anniversary of former Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee. Sivankutty, who also holds the labour portfolio, alleged that staff were asked to report for duty on Christmas.
He described the move as "highly objectionable" and contrary to the principles of labour justice.
Mr. Sivankutty said the action appeared to be part of a broader pattern, referring to earlier orders issued in Uttar Pradesh, including those denying holidays to schools.
He said the subsequent clarification by Lok Bhavan authorities — that participation in the programme was "optional" — was an attempt to mislead the public after the issue triggered controversy.
"As long as instructions come from senior officials, [optional] remains only in name," the Minister said, adding that asking employees to attend office on a major religious festival was undemocratic.
He further said that using an internationally celebrated festival day for official programmes challenged India's secular values and stressed that such practices must be corrected.
Earlier on Wednesday (December 24), Lok Bhavan said in a press release that an "unnecessary controversy" was being created over the observance of Good Governance Day on December 25.
It had maintained that participation by Lok Bhavan staff in the function was optional.

title: Will hold general council meeting as planned: G.K. Mani
summary: G.K. Mani reaffirms the planned general council meeting amid opposition from Anbumani Ramadoss's faction ahead of Assembly elections.
content:
PMK leader G.K. Mani on Thursday strongly condemned the move of the rival faction led by Anbumani Ramadoss urging the Salem police to deny permission for the general council and executive council planned by the party’s founder S. Ramadoss’s faction in Salem on Monday (December 29, 2025).
Speaking to reporters at Thailapuram near Tindivanam, Mr. Mani said the faction led by Dr. Anbumani was resorting to drama and termed it as a move to divert public attention in order to hold alliance talks for the upcoming Assembly election.
It was Dr. Ramadoss who founded the PMK and “all party cadre are with him”. He has been running the party for 46 years, and the proposed general council and executive council meetings will go ahead as planned, he said.
Mr. Mani added that Dr. Ramadoss was expected to make important announcements regarding the alliance for the upcoming Assembly election.

title: CM must maintain dignity, says Bandi Sanjay
summary: CM must maintain dignity, says Bandi Sanjay
content:
Hyderabad
Union Minister of State for Home Bandi Sanjay Kumar found fault with Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy’s recent remarks against former Chief Minister K. Chandrasekhar Rao, saying the language used was inappropriate and unbecoming of the office he holds.
Interacting with the media at the BJP state office on Thursday, Mr. Sanjay stressed that the Chief Minister must maintain dignity and restraint in public speech and urged him to refrain from using such expressions in the future.
Holding KCR responsible for injustice to Telangana in Krishna river water allocation, he claimed that it was KCR who agreed to accept 299 TMC out of 575 TMC. He said this was stated by then Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy in an Apex Committee meeting and asserted that the BJP was ready to make the agreements public if necessary.
Referring to the Kaleshwaram project, Sanjay questioned why investigations were limited to ₹9,000 crore when the alleged scam ran into ₹1 lakh crore. He also criticised the handling of the phone tapping case, alleging that over 6,000 phones were tapped during the BRS regime and claimed the involvement of KCR’s family.
On civic politics, he dismissed claims by Congress over recent by-election victories and asserted that the absence of party symbols in Panchayat polls made attribution of results misleading. He claimed BJP’s vote share and number of seats had increased significantly, particularly in Karimnagar Parliamentary constituency.
On GHMC elections, Bandi Sanjay said BJP would contest independently and was confident of winning the Mayor’s post. He accused Congress of planning an alliance with MIM and asserted that BJP’s objective was to make Hyderabad “MIM-free.”

title: Delhi air quality improves as AQI drops to 234; deterioration likely in coming days
summary: Delhi's air quality improves to AQI 234 but is expected to worsen in the coming days, impacting health.
content:
he capital breathed slightly easier for the second consecutive day, with the air quality improving to the 'poor' category and an AQI of 234 recorded on Thursday (December 24, 2025).
Transport emissions and pollution from neighbouring cities continued to contribute significantly to the capital's air pollution load, according to official data.
Delhi's 24-hour average air quality index (AQI) stood at 234 at 4 p.m., remaining in the 'poor' category, compared to 271 recorded at the same time a day earlier, according to the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB).
This marked a significant improvement from the 'severe' AQI of 412 recorded at 4 p.m on Tuesday (December 23, 2025).
Out of the 40 functional air quality monitoring stations in the city, 10 recorded moderate AQI levels below 200, including Lodhi Road, IIT Delhi, Indira Gandhi International Airport and Aya Nagar, while 27 stations remained in the poor category.
Two stations — Jahangirpuri and Bawana — recorded very poor air quality with AQI readings above 300.
As per the CPCB classification, an AQI between 0 and 50 is considered 'good', 51 and 100 'satisfactory', 101 and 200 'moderate', 201 and 300 'poor', 301 and 400 'very poor' and 401 and 500 'severe'.
Data from the Decision Support System (DSS) for Air Quality Management showed vehicular emissions were the largest contributor to Delhi's pollution load on Wednesday, accounting for 18.5 per cent.
This was followed by industries in Delhi and adjoining areas (9.5 per cent), construction activities (2.5%) and waste burning (1.6%).
Among the NCR districts, Jhajjar in Haryana contributed the highest share to Delhi's pollution at 17.6%, followed by Rohtak (5.9%) and Sonipat (3.1 %), the data showed.
The predominant surface wind was from the northwest, with wind speeds reaching up to 10 kmph during afternoon hours on Thursday, according to the Air Quality Early Warning System.
The air quality is likely to deteriorate to the very poor category in the coming days, according to the forecast.
On the weather front, Delhi recorded a maximum temperature of 22.6 degrees Celsius on Wednesday, 1.9 degrees above normal, while the minimum temperature settled at 6.5 degrees Celsius, slightly below normal, the India Meteorological Department said.
Relative humidity stood at 63% at 8.30 a.m. and 84% at 5.30 p.m.
The IMD forecast a minimum temperature of 8 degrees Celsius on Friday (December 26, 2025), with moderate fog expected.

title: Vocalist Ashok Huggannavar passes away
summary: Hindustani classical vocalist Ashok Huggannavar, 64, passes away, leaving behind a legacy of music and teaching.
content:
Noted Hindustani classical vocalist and music teacher Ashok Huggannavar, 64, passed away in Hubballi during the early hours of Thursday.
He is survived by wife Veena, who is a teacher and son Vinayak who is a scientist and vocalist.
A native of Yaraguppi in Kundgol taluk of Dharwad district was a gold medalist in MA music and held a postgraduate degree in Botany. After having served as a music teacher at MPE Society’s SDM College in Honnavar for several years, Ashok Huggannavar had retired in the year 2021 and post-retirement had settled down in Hubballi.
Ashok Huggannavar had trained under Pandit Lingaraj Buva Yaraguppi of the Gwalior gharana of Hindustani music for nearly 12 years and had won appreciation for his distinct style.
He had served as a member of Karnataka Sangeet Nrutya Academy and was a recipient of several awards, including ‘Karnataka Kalashri’, ‘Mansur Award’, Ragashree and other awards. He had performed at various national music festivals.

title: Seven arrested for ganja peddling

title: A year of policing in Telangana, with a personal touch
summary: A year of policing in Telangana, with a personal touch
content:
“By the end of this year, I realised people were looking at me beyond the transgender tag. Today, I am not a ‘transgender assistant’. I am just a cop, and that acceptance healed years of hurt.” That reflection from Shiva Ram captures what 2025 came to mean for dozens of lives across Hyderabad, a year in which policing extended beyond enforcement and reshaped everyday realities through dignity, inclusion and trust.
Shiva Ram regulating traffic at the bustling JBS junction as part of the Telangana Police’s maiden initiative to induct transgender persons into its traffic force.
                                                            | Photo Credit: 
                                The Hindu
Once confined to his home and nearly forced by his family into marrying an older man, Shiva Ram now spends his days regulating traffic at the JBS junction part of theTelangana Police’s maiden initiative to induct transgender persons into its traffic force. Looking back, he says the most profound change was how the uniform became a new identity, one that slowly replaced doubt with acceptance.
That change is most evident on his journey home from Secunderabad to Uppal after duty. “People salute me. Neighbours and shopkeepers say, ‘The traffic cop is here,’” he says. “They’ve seen me in uniform for a year now and accepted me that way. It’s a moment of pride every single day.”
K Srivalli, who joined the force alongside Shiva Ram, describes the year as a return to self-worth. Before her induction, survival meant begging and sex work at traffic signals where people deliberately looked away. Today, she stands at those same junctions in uniform, directing traffic with authority. “This year has been a wonderful comeback for me,” she says. “I used to feel invisible. Now people wait for my signal.”
K Srivalli guiding a motorist to wear helmet while driving at a busy junction in Mahankali
                                                            | Photo Credit: 
                                The Hindu
For Srivalli, the most significant change was internal. The job encouraged her to resume her education through Dr. Ambedkar Open University, and she now thinks about a future without hesitation.
The impact of the initiative has extended beyond individual journeys. With other civic departments preparing to induct transgender employees andCyberabad deploying transgender traffic assistants, the experiment has begun to normalise inclusion within public systems long resistant to change.
In a similar bid to encourage reintegration and reduce stigma, theRachakonda Police deployed reformed history-sheeters as traffic volunteersat busy junctions, offering them a structured second chance through visible public service and daily interaction with commuters.
A total of 60 reformed rowdy sheeters have been deployed as traffic volunteers for managing traffic at major junctions like Uppal, LB Nagar, and ECIL alongside the Rachakonda traffic police officials.
                                                            | Photo Credit: 
                                By Arrangement
Another initiative where Telangana emerged as a first mover was the allotment of 2BHK homes to atrocity victims under the Indiramma Indlu housing scheme. For survivors, the house represented far more than shelter.
Sonal, who dropped out of engineering after surviving sexual assault, says the year helped her close chapters she once believed would define her forever. In 2025, she cleared the Telangana Law Common Entrance Test, enrolled in an LLB through distance education, found work as a teacher, married, and moved into her own home. “I didn’t know healing could look like this. Having a safe place made everything else fall into place,” she says.
View of the 2BHK Dignity Housing township in Kollur village in R.C.Puram Mandal in Sangareddy District
                                                            | Photo Credit: 
                                NAGARA GOPAL
For Kumari Hema, a 32-year-old mother, the year ended a long cycle of uncertainty. After being repeatedly asked to vacate rented homes once her past became known, she finally received a house of her own under the scheme. “I lived in fear of the next eviction. Now my child and I know where we belong,” she says.
At the community level, initiatives such asVruddhulu Samrakshanain Hyderabad’s North Zonequietly reshaped daily life for over 750 elderly citizens living alone. Regular police visits reduced isolation, fear and vulnerability to fraud, leaving them with a sense of reassurance.
An officer from the North Zone talking to one of the senior citizens living by himself during the visit.
                                                            | Photo Credit: 
                                By Arrangement
Meanwhile, programmes such as Sanghamitra, Margadarshak and Project Safe Stay strengthened safety frameworks for women and working professionals across Cyberabad, particularly in the IT corridor.

title: 21  injured as stray dogs go on biting spree in Vemulawada
summary: Stray dogs injure 21 in Vemulawada, prompting urgent calls for action to address the growing stray dog issue.
content:
A pack of stray dogs went on a biting spree injuring as many as 21 persons, including several devotees, in the temple town of Vemulawada in Rajanna Sircilla district in a span of 24 hours since Wednesday afternoon.
The first incident was reported at Jatara grounds where a rabid dog went berserk and bit eight devotees late on Wednesday afternoon. At least 13 others including several devotees and local residents were bitten by stray dogs in separate dog bite incidents that were reported in the temple town till Thursday morning, sources said.
The injured persons were administered first-aid and anti-rabies vaccines at the Government Area Hospital in Vemulawada. Four of them were referred to the District Headquarters Hospital in Sircilla for better treatment.
The incident triggered renewed demands for immediate steps to check stray dog menace in Vemulawada.
The temple town, popularly known as ‘Dakshin Kashi’, witnesses a huge turnout of devotees ahead of Medaram Sammakka-Sarakka jatara scheduled to be held in Mulugu district from January 28 to 31, 2026.

title: Tributes paid to Vajpayee in Mysuru on his birth anniversary
summary: Mysuru honors Atal Bihari Vajpayee on his 101st birthday, celebrating his lasting contributions to national development and unity.
content:
Tributes were paid to former Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee on his 101st birthday here on December 25, with speakers recalling his role in shaping key national programmes, some of which continue to be implemented even in present times.
Yaduveer Krishnadatta Chamaraja Wadiyar, Mysuru MP, and others made floral offerings to Vajpayee’s portrait and highlighted his contributions to the country.
Mr. Wadiyar said many initiatives launched by Vajpayee, including the National Highways Development project and Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana, are still being implemented across the country and have helped shore up development. These initiatives were aimed at improving infrastructure and governance as well, he added.
The MP recalled that Vajpayee took the bold decision of conducting nuclear tests despite tremendous pressure from various countries, and said the tests helped pave way for India to emerge as a nuclear power.
Vajpayee’s term in office was marked by an atmosphere of cooperation, with many Acts and Bills receiving support even from his political opponents, said Mr. Wadiyar.
“That was the kind of political culture that prevailed then, and it is something we should draw inspiration from,’’ he added.
Referring to the national vision of Viksit Bharat, the MP said Vajpayee had laid the foundation for long-term development thinking and institutional reforms. He added that the country remains indebted to the former Prime Minister and should seek to emulate his approach to governance and public life.
Other party speakers described Vajpayee as an “Ajatashatru”, a leader without enemies, highlighting his inclusive politics and statesmanship.
As part of the week-long tribute programme in Mysuru, a series of public activities including sports meets, cleanliness drives and health camps are being organised to mark Vajpayee’s contribution to the nation.
L. Nagendra, former MLA and city unit president, and Pratap Simha, former MP, were among those present.

title: Maharashtra MP’s claim of privilege violation unjustified, says senior SC lawyer
summary: Senior SC lawyer Mohan Kataraki deems Maharashtra MP's privilege claim unjustified, affirming the legality of Belagavi's restraining order.
content:
Mohan Kataraki, senior advocate in the Supreme Court, said that the claim by Dhariyasheel Mane, MP for Maharashtra, that the Belagavi district administration violated his privilege by issuing him a restraining order is unjustified.
Mr. Kataraki toldThe Hinduthat Mohammad Roshan, Deputy Commissioner, Belagavi, had acted within the law to prohibit the Maharashtra MP’s entry into Belagavi for the Black Day observation by MES.
“The privilege complaint Mr. Mane has against the DC is devoid of legal foundation. The prohibitory order under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), the successor to Section 144 CrPC, was a valid administrative action to prevent apprehended breach of peace during the sensitive “Black Day” observance tied to the Maharashtra-Karnataka border dispute. Such orders bind every individual universally, and nobody, including a Member of Parliament, a Member of Legislative Assembly, or even the Chief Minister and Prime Minister, is exempt from their operation. Parliamentary privileges under Article 105 shield only proceedings within Parliament, not extraneous political activities that could inflame tensions in a volatile region,’’ he said.
“Belagavi district administration authorities have consistently applied similar preventive restrictions on leaders from both states during border-related events. The DC’s measure was prudent, impartial, and essential for public order. Equating routine law-and-order enforcement with contempt of Parliament distorts constitutional equilibrium and disregards the Supreme Court’s settled position on the dispute. In view of the above and in my view, the Speaker of Lok Sabha is likely to dismiss the motion moved by Mr. Mane,” he said.

title: Telangana continues to record single digit temperatures
summary: Telangana experiences single-digit temperatures, with minimums dropping though cold wave alerts were lifted
content:
Various parts of Telangana continue to record single digit temperatures, thoughcold wave alert has not been in effect for the past few days. India Meteorological Department (IMD) in its bulletin on Thursday (December 25) said that the minimum temperatures are likely to be below normal by 3°C to 4°C, at isolated pockets during the next two days.
The lowest of 6.9°C was recorded in Tiryani of Kumaram Bheem Asifabad between Wednesday and Thursday morning, according to Telangana Development Planning Society (TGDPS). This was followed by 7.4°C in Kohir of Sangareddy and 8.5°C in Moinabad of Ranga Reddy. The lowest temperature recorded this winter so far was 4.5°C from December 20 to 22.The TGDPS Meteorologists earlier said that the cold conditions are likely to ease in the State by December 27.

title: Children’s Special Gram Sabha held in Chamarajanagar district
summary: Children's Special Gram Sabha in Chamarajanagar empowered kids to voice concerns, promoting transparency and rural development.
content:
The Children’s Special Gram Sabha was held at Managalli Gram Panchayat in Chamarajanagar district’s Hanur taluk on December 24, providing children with a platform to present their demands and suggestions before authorities.
Described as a model initiative, the gram sabha was virtually inaugurated by Priyank Kharge, Minister for Rural Development and Panchayat Raj, who also held a video interaction with the children.
The gram sabha was organised by the Chamarajanagar Zilla Panchayat and Department of Rural Development and Panchayat Raj.
The children highlighted several issues, including the need for an ‘Akshara Dasoha’ (midday meals) room, a dining hall, a playground, sports equipment kits, toilets, drinking water, and prevention of drainage water flowing in front of the school. They also pushed for the improvement of village roads and the addressal of problems caused by wildlife intrusion.
Mr. Kharge said the issues and demands raised by the children in the gram sabha should be taken seriously and immediate action must be taken in this regard.
He said immediate proposals for road works should be submitted, apart from allocating a dining hall and separate room for Akshara Dasoha. He also promised to provide the sports equipment and other facilities through Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) support.
The Minister also asked the children about their aspirations and what additional facilities they require for better learning. The students shared their ambitions about becoming doctors, deputy commissioners, and IAS officers. Mr. Kharge advised them to study diligently and pointed out that the district Deputy Commissioner, Zilla Panchayat CEO, and Superintendent of Police were all women, who serve as sources of inspiration.
Mr. Kharge also issued directions that a list of books useful for competitive exams be stocked in school libraries.
M.R. Manjunath, Hanur MLA, who inaugurated the Children’s Gram Sabha, said programmes like this act as spaces for children to air their demands. Such efforts will promote transparency, accountability, and rural development, he added.
Chamarajanagar Zilla Panchayat CEO Mona Roat delivered the introductory talk while Deputy Commissioner Shilpa Nag, Superintendent of Police B.T. Kavitha and senior State-level officers participated in the programme virtually.
Managalli Gram Panchayat president Somashekar presided over the programme while the gram sabha proceedings were live-streamed on YouTube.

title: V. Muraleedharan questions legality of Kerala Cabinet's nativity card decision
summary: V. Muraleedharan questions the legality of Kerala's nativity card decision, calling it unnecessary and politically motivated.
content:
Senior BJP leader V. Muraleedharan on Thursday (December 25, 2025) questioned the legal validity of the Kerala Cabinet's decision to introduce apermanent, photo-embedded nativity card, alleging that the move was unnecessary and "politically motivated".
Reacting to the in-principle approval given by the Cabinet on Wednesday (December 24), the former Union Minister said the authority to determine citizenship rests with the central government and asked why the State needed to introduce another identity document when Aadhaar already contains comprehensive personal details.
"There is a mystery behind this nativity card," the BJP leader said, adding that the move raised serious legal and constitutional questions.
He alleged that the decision was aimed at wasting public money and accused Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan and his colleagues of eyeing election-related funding through the project.
Mr. Muraleedharan said the Left government had a history of making announcements that placed a burden on the public exchequer without offering any real benefit to ordinary people.
He urged the government to withdraw decisions that led to the misuse of taxpayers' money.
Referring to the now-stalled SilverLine rail project, he said the government was currently engaged in removing the yellow boundary markers that had earlier been installed, again at public expense.
"This clearly shows how poorly thought-out decisions are being taken," he said.
The criticism came a day after Chief Minister Vijayan announced that the Cabinet had given in-principle approval for replacing the existing nativity certificate with a permanent, photo-embedded nativity card.
Mr. Vijayan had said the current system forced people to repeatedly obtain certificates for different purposes and lacked statutory legal backing.
The Chief Minister said the new card would help people easily prove their birth, residence or permanent status in Kerala and prevent exclusion.
He added that the Revenue Department had been asked to prepare a draft law, in consultation with the Law Department, to give the card legal validity.
The BJP, however, has mounted a strong attack on the proposal.
Party State president Rajeev Chandrasekhar has said the move would be legally challenged, calling it an example of "dangerous separatist politics" and alleging that it was meant to divert attention from the ruling front's recent electoral setbacks.

title: BRS can’t chant the Vedas after abusing political opponents: Congress MP Chamala
summary: Congress MP Chamala criticizes BRS leaders for abusive politics, urging them to reflect on their own moral standards.
content:
Bhongir Member of Parliament Chamala Kiran Kumar Reddy accused the Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) leaders, including former Minister T. Harish Rao, BRS president K. Chandrashekar Rao, and party working president K.T. Rama Rao of promoting an abusive political culture, yet blaming the Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy.
Responding to recent remarks by Mr. Harish Rao against Mr. Revanth Reddy, he said the former Minister’s behaviour resembled ‘demons chanting the Vedas’, alleging that Mr. Rao spoke about morality as if ethical standards applied only to political opponents. He advised Mr. Harish Rao to first reflect on Mr. Chandrashekar Rao’s own history of foul language.
“Mr. Chandrashekar Rao introduced abusive language into politics. He even holds the patent rights for it,” the MP remarked, adding that during the agitation period and later as Chief Minister, Mr. Chandrashekar Rao spoke without restraint or responsibility.
The Congress MP asserted that Chief Minister responds politically when Mr. Chandrashekar Rao speaks politically, but warned that if the BRS leaders resort to personal abuse, the CM is equally capable of responding in the same tone.
He also criticised Mr. Harish Rao for allegedly making violent and provocative remarks, including references to tying people to trees and unleashing thugs, while accusing him of pretending to be a scholar and moral preacher. Mr. Rama Rao also came under criticism, with the MP alleging that the former speaks without decorum and believes that no one other than himself understands IT or irrigation.
