title: Man arrested for burning wife to death in Hyderabad’s Nallakunta; mother manages to save daughter
summary: Husband arrested in Hyderabad for allegedly murdering wife by fire, while mother saves their young daughter during the attack.
content:
A 26-year-old woman was burnt to death by her husband in Nallakunta on Wednesday (December 24, 2025), allegedly after a domestic dispute. The incident taking place in front of their children, police said. The accused was identified as 31-year-old Venkatesh, while the deceased was 26-year-old Triveni.
The Nallakunta Police Inspector, K. Maruthi Prasad, said the accused was arrested within 24 hours from Ameenpur while he was attempting to leave the city.
According to the officer, the couple were natives of Huzurnagar and had married about eight years ago after being in a relationship for sometime. They later moved to Hyderabad, where both were working as daily wage labourers.
“The couple had frequent quarrels, with Venkatesh allegedly suspecting his wife’s fidelity and even questioning the paternity of the daughter,” said the officer.
Earlier this year, the couple had separated after Venkatesh allegedly asked Triveni to quit her job. However, they reconciled in October and resumed living together in Nallakunta. On December 24 morning, Venkatesh consumed alcohol, purchased petrol from a nearby outlet and brought it home.
“Venkatesh woke up their son, gave him food and asked him to go outside, in a bid to save him from the attack. He allegedly intended to kill the daughter as well. He then poured petrol on Triveni and set her on fire,” explained the officer, adding that Triveni managed to save the girl.
Neighbours rushed in after hearing screams and attempted to rescue the victims. Triveni suffered severe burn injuries and succumbed, while the daughter sustained minor burns and was shifted to hospital for treatment.
A case has been registered by the Nallakunta police and further investigation is under way. Police said the accused was produced before a court after his arrest and remanded to judicial custody.

title: In a historic first, BJP takes charge of Tripunithura municipality
summary: BJP makes history by electing P.L. Babu as chairperson of Tripunithura municipality, marking its first municipal victory in Ernakulam.
content:
The Bharatiya Janata Party’s (BJP) P.L. Babu has been elected chairperson of theTripunithura municipality, thus marking the first time the party has come into power in a municipality in Ernakulam district.
Mr. Babu was elected chairperson after two rounds of voting, as the 53-member municipality returned a hung verdict. The BJP-led NDA emerged as the single largest bloc with 21 seats, followed by the Left Democratic Front (LDF) with 20, and the United Democratic Front (UDF) with 12.
In the first round, K.T. Akhiladas of the LDF and C.A. Shaji of the UDF were also in the fray, with all three candidates securing votes corresponding to their respective seat shares. Since no candidate achieved the simple majority of 27 votes, a second round of voting became inevitable, from which the UDF abstained. Mr. Babu again polled 21 votes, while Mr. Akhiladas received only 18, as two votes—that of CPI(M)’s vice-chairperson candidate Bindu Shailendran and O.K. Hariharan—were declared invalid.
Radhika Varma was elected vice-chairperson in the election held later in the afternoon.
For Mr. Babu, who represents the Valiyathara ward, this marks his second stint as councillor, while Ms. Varma, elected from the Ambalam ward, is a three-time councillor. Mr. Babu currently serves as general secretary of the BJP central zone, and Ms. Varma is a member of the BJP State Council.
Had the LDF and UDF joined hands, they could have prevented the BJP from taking charge. However, both chose to field candidates in the elections for the posts of chairperson and vice-chairperson. The LDF has traditionally been the dominant force in Tripunithura since its formation in 1978 and had secured a simple majority in the last election as well.
The BJP’s growth in the temple town has been rapid. After opening its account in the municipality with a single seat in 2010, the tally rose to 13 five years later, when it dislodged the UDF as the principal Opposition. In 2020, the party further improved its tally to 15 before adding two more seats in mid-term by-elections.

title: Mining mafia destroying Aravali hills, looting public resources: Surjewala
summary: Surjewala accuses mining mafia of looting resources and destroying Aravali hills, causing environmental harm and public distress.
content:
Congress leader Randeep Singh Surjewala on Friday (December 26, 2025) alleged large-scale illegal mining in Haryana's Aravalli region, claiming it has caused massive environmental damage and huge losses to the state exchequer.
The Rajya Sabha MP charged that the "mining mafia" was openly looting public resources and destroying the Aravalli hills, with little concern for the environment.
The Congress general secretary said the Directorate of Enforcement has revealed that illegal mining in the Dadum hills of the Aravalli region has not only harmed the environment but also defrauded the government treasury of ₹1,200 crore.
Five people had lost their lives in a mining-related accident in the Tosham area in the past, but alleged no effective action was taken even after the tragedy, he said on X.
He further alleged that around 383 hectares of Aravalli hills in Charkhi Dadri district was facing destruction due to illegal mining and that it was continuing under political protection.
Mr. Surjewala said locals were living in fear due to night-long mining activity, heavy machinery noise and constant movement of vehicles. Houses were developing cracks and people were experiencing tremors, but complaints were being ignored, he charged while slamming the BJP government for failing to stop illegal mining and endangering both the environment and the lives of people.

title: India’s economic growth continues to create career opportunities for youngsters, says Director of Indian Institute of Petroleum and Energy
summary: India's economic growth offers abundant career opportunities for youth, emphasizes the Director of the Indian Institute of Petroleum and Energy.
content:
Director of Indian Institute of Petroleum and Energy Shalivahan on Friday (December 26) said that India’s continuous growth in all sectors would provide ample career opportunities for youngsters in spite of temporary challenges due to various factors.
Along with former minister and chairman of the Avathi Group Muttamsetti Srinivasa Rao, he inaugurated GYAN-2k25, a two-day national-level technical fest in Avanthi Institute of Engineering and Technology of Cherukupalli of Vizianagaram district.
Speaking on the occasion, he said the students who focus on developing skills and knowledge continuously in their respective courses would shine very well with the creation of lakhs of job opportunities in all sectors, including software, finance, energy, petroleum and other sectors.
Associate director of Cognizant AI Lab-Bengaluru Rituparna Datta said that the youngsters with additional skills are able to get ₹1 crore per annum packages in various companies. Infosys Group manager of Visakhapatnam Konchada Kishore Kumar, assistant professor of National Institute of Technology-Warangal Rimjhim, Brahma Kumaris organization representative Mani and others were present. Earlier, the guests observed various projects of students in the college premises. Smart Prosthetic Leg, Voice Controlled AI Robot, Robotic Arm, Ultrasonic sensor based moving dustbin and others exhibited in GYAN-2k25.

title: Stampedes, fires and plane crash: A list of major tragedies India witnessed in 2025
summary: Explore India's tragic events of 2025, including stampedes, fires, and a devastating plane crash, claiming numerous lives.
content:
India was witness to aseries of major tragedies with over a dozen incidentsclaiming several lives in 2025. The accidents spanned multiple categories including transportation disasters, crowd crushes at religious and political events, industrial fires, infrastructure collapses, and one of the deadliest aviation disasters in the country’s history.
Almost halfway through the year, the country also faced a terror attack in Jammu and Kashmir’s Pahalgam which led to a military confrontation with Pakistan via ‘Operation Sindoor’ in May 2025.
While investigations are under way in most of the cases, here’s a chronological list of the major incidents that occurred in the country this year:
Devotees' belongings like clothes, blankets and backpacks seen strewn around the spot where a stampede broke out on Mauni Amavasya at Maha Kumbh in Prayagraj on January 29, 2025. 
                                                            | Photo Credit: 
                                PTI
At least 30 people were killed and over 60 other were injured in astampede at the Maha Kumbh in Uttar Pradesh’s Prayagrajin the wee hours of January 29. Barricades collapsed under the pressure of lakhs of pilgrims gathered on the Akhara Marg, leading to the trampling of devotees waiting to take a holy dip at Sangam on the auspicious occasion of Mauni Amavasya. Nearly 7 crore people performed the snan (holy dip) till 6 p.m that day, as per official figures.
While the State government’s official claim was of 37 deaths, aBBC News Hindireportsaid that at least 82 people were killed in four incidents of stampede at Maha Kumbh on January 29.
Probe:Uttar Pradesh government constituted a three-member judicial commission under the chairmanship of Justice Harsh Kumar, a former judge of the Allahabad High Court. Besides the task of ascertaining what led to the stampede, the commission was also asked to give suggestions to prevent recurrence of such incidents in future.
People gather at the site following the death of several passengers after they stepped down due to a rumour of fire and were run over by another train passing on the adjacent tracks, in North Maharashtra's Jalgaon district, on January 22, 2025. 
                                                            | Photo Credit: 
                                PTI
At least 12 people were killed on the evening of January 22 when they jumped down from the Lucknow-Mumbai Pushpak Express following rumours of a fire and were then hit by another train speeding down the adjacent track, in Maharashtra’s Jalgaon district.
The Maharashtra government announced an ex-gratia of ₹5 lakh for the families of the deceased.Seven victims were identified as Nepali migrant workers, for whom the Pushpak Express to Mumbai Metropolitan Region (MMR) is an important connection, for employment.
Probe:Jalgaon District Collector Ayush Prasad dismissed reports of any spark or smoke as the fire brigade’s foam team was never used during the rescue operation. In the preliminary inquiry, it was found that after the Pushpak Express stopped, the driver activated the flasher light and applied the brakes as per rules. The curvature of the train was nearly two degrees, which obstructed visibility and reduced the distance for applying the brakes. Even people could not see the train coming. Pilots tried their best to avoid the incident, the Chief Public Relations Officer said.
The spot where the New Delhi Railway Station stampede broke out on February 15, 2025.
                                                            | Photo Credit: 
                                Sushil Kumar Verma
At least18 people were killed and over 15 others injuredin a stampede that broke out on February 15 night at the New Delhi Railway Station. The incident was preceded by a swell in crowd of passengers waiting to board trains for Prayagraj where the Maha Kumbh was under way.
An ex-gratia of ₹10 lakh to the next of kin of each deceased, an amount of ₹2.5 lakh each to the grievously injured and ₹1 lakh each to other injured has been paid.
Probe:In August, Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw told the Rajya Sabha that a big headload falling from one of the passengers triggered the stampede. In a written reply,  he shared the findings of the high-level committee constituted to examine the circumstances.
Gujarat Police and Deesa nagarpalika workers remove debris at the Deepak firecracker unit, where a blast occurred on April 2, 2025 killing 21 people, including eight children.
                                                            | Photo Credit: 
                                 Vijay Soneji
Twenty one persons lost their lives while six others were injured on April 1, after an explosion and blaze ripped through a godown where firecrackers were allegedly stored and manufactured illegally, leading to thestructure collapse in Gujarat’s Banaskantha district.
Probe:While the State and Central governments responded quickly with an announcement of aid and the arrest of the owners, the factory was operating without a licence to manufacture.
All the deceased persons were migrant workers from Harda and Dewas districts of Madhya Pradesh.
Security forces busy in search operations on April 23, 2025, in the Baisaran area of Pahalgam where 26 tourists were killed and several others injured.
                                                            | Photo Credit: 
                                Imran Nissar
Twenty six people, mostly tourists, were killed by a group of terrorists in one of the most deadly attacks on civilians in the Baisaran meadows in the upper reaches ofPahalgam in Jammu and Kashmir on April 22. It was the first major terror attack on civilians in Kashmir since the Centre ended J&K’s special status in 2019.
Operation Sindoor:In response to the Pahalgam attack, the Indian armed forces on May 7 carried out precision strikes on nine terrorist hideouts in Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK).
Probe:A National Investigation Agency probe found direct involvement of three Lashkar-e-Taiba terrorists in the attack. They were killed in the July 28 encounter code-named ‘Operation Mahadev’ on the outskirts of Srinagar.
Rescue operations after a fire broke out in a building near Gulzar Houz in the Old City area of Hyderabad in Telangana on 2025.
                                                            | Photo Credit: 
                                Ramakrishna G.
Seventeen persons, including eight children aged between one and seven, were killed after amassive fire engulfed the Modi residence in Gulzar Houz, a stone’s throw away from Charminar, at around 6 a.m. on May 18.
The family was a household name, known for their strong foothold in the pearls and jewellery business in Hyderabad. The residence, built in the early 1900s, was a traditional Nizam-Hyderabadi structure with no external balconies or fire escapes.
Probe:A short circuit in the electric panel board of the property triggered the blaze, a probe by the Telangana State Disaster Response and Fire Services found.
A crowd of fans gather in large numbers during Royal Challengers Bengaluru’s felicitation ceremony after their winning the Indian Premier League (IPL) 2025, in front of Vidhana Soudha, in Bengaluru on June 4, 2025.
                                                            | Photo Credit: 
                                PTI
A day after Royal Challangers Bengaluru’s IPL triumph, lakhs of fans thronged the M. Chinnaswamy Stadium and also the Vidhana Soudha where the Karnataka government had organised a separate felicitation event on June 4.In the resulting chaos, 11 persons— all under the age of 40 — lost their lives, and at least 50 others sustained injuries in the stampede.
Probe:CM Siddaramaiah also announced a judicial inquiry by a one-man commission led by former Karnataka High Court judge Michael D’Cunha. A Special Investigation Team (SIT), led by Additional Director-General of Police B. K. Singh, was formed and a top RCB official, and three others from the event management company were later arrested.
On June 12, Air India flight AI 171, a Boeing 787-8 aircraft en route London Gatwick, crashed into a medical hostel complex shortly after take off from Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel International Airport.
                                                            | Photo Credit: 
                                Vijay Soneji
On June 12,Air India flight AI 171, a Boeing 787-8 aircraften route London Gatwick, crashed into a medical hostel complex shortly after take off from Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel International Airport. The aircraft burst into flames, killing 241 out of 242 people onboard and 19 individuals on the ground. There was one survivor passenger.
The Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB)released its preliminary report on July 12.
Probe:The 15-page preliminary report focused on the “engine 1 and engine 2 fuel cutoff switches having transitioned from Run to Cutoff position”, resulting in the fuel supply cutting off. There is also one sentence that in the “cockpit voice recording, one of the pilots is heard asking the other why did he cutoff. The other pilot said he did not do so.” The report also said that it has no recommended actions concerning the aircraft type, the engine (GE’s GEnx-1B70/P2), and the manufacturers.
The AAIB has maintained that the preliminary report is to provide information about “what” happened, and that the final report would come out with root causes and recommendations.
Multi-agency teams carried out a rescue operation on Mahisagar River bridge in Vadodara district on July 11, 2025, after a portion of the four-decade-old bridge collapsed on July 09, 2025.
                                                            | Photo Credit: 
                                 Vijay Soneji
At least 20 people died after a section of the four-decade-old Gambhira bridge in Gujarat’s Vadodara district collapsed early on July 9, 2025,sending several vehicles crashing into the Mahisagar river below.
The bridge served as a vital link between central Gujarat and the Saurashtra regions, connecting Anand and Vadodara districts. It was built in 1985 by a Lucknow-based company.
Probe:As per a high-level probe committee’s initial findings, the collapse occurred due to pedestal and articulation crushing.
Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam chief Vijay during a rally in Karur, Tamil Nadu, on September 27, 2025.
                                                            | Photo Credit: 
                                M. Moorthy
On September 27, thousands of people gathered in Karur, Tamil Nadu, to attend a rally by actor-turned-politician Vijay. As the chief of the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam party arrived hours late, the crowd swelled and surged towards his vehicle,triggering a stampede that killed 41 peopleand injured over 100 others. Most of the adult victims were between 18 and 30 years of age.
Probe:The Supreme Court on October 13 ordered a Central Bureau of Investigation probe. This came after the top courtsuspended the Chief Minister-appointed Commission of Inquiryheaded by former Madras High Court judge Justice Aruna Jagadeesan, on the ground that the CBI had taken over the case.
The 25-page order of the top court in October had questioned the Single Judge’s decision to direct a SIT probe when the petition before it had only sought the framing of guidelines for the conduct of political rallies in public places.
At least 19 passengers were charred to death when a bus caught fire on the outskirts of Kurnool district on October 24, 2025. 
                                                            | Photo Credit: 
                                Nagara Gopal
At least 19 passengers were charred to death and several others were injured when a luxury private bus travelling from Hyderabad to Bengaluru caught fire onKurnool-Hyderabad National Highway No. 44 in Andhra Pradeshon October 24. In all, 43 persons were in the bus.
Probe:According to the preliminary report, the accident occurred due to over speed, poor visibility and fuel leakage after the bus collided with a bike that had been knocked to the ground earlier in a hit-and-run incident.
Security personnel at the blast site near the Red Fort on November 10, 2025.
                                                            | Photo Credit: 
                                Sushil Kumar Verma
A high-intensity explosion in a slow-moving car outside the Red Fort in New Delhiclaimed the lives of 13 people and injured more than 20 otherson November 10, sparking a nationwide alert and a probe involving multiple agencies across States.
Probe:A doctor from J&K’s Pulwama, identified as Umar Nabi, teaching at the Al-Falah University in Faridabad, emerged as the likely sole occupant of the car which exploded. The NIA, which took over the probe, made its ninth and latest arrest in the case on December 18.
A view of the charred Birch by Romeo Lane nightclub at Arpora in North Goa, on December 8, 2025.
                                                            | Photo Credit: 
                                K. Murali Kumar
At least25 persons were killed and six others suffered injuriesin a massive fire that erupted at ‘Birch by Romeo Lane’ nightclub in North Goa after midnight on December 7, 2025.
Probe:Police have so far arrested eight people, including the nightclub owners Saurabh Luthra, Gaurav Luthra, and Ajay Gupta, and five others. They have started the process to secure a Blue Corner Notice against British national Surinder Kumar Khosla, to whom the land had been leased out to.
Cranes clear the charred remains of buses after a fog-hit pile-up involving several buses and cars triggered fires on the Yamuna Expressway, in Mathura, on December 16, 2025. 
                                                            | Photo Credit: 
                                PTI
At least 19 people lost their lives in amulti-vehicle pile-up on the Yamuna Expressway in Mathuraon December 18, 2025. Around 90 people were injured in the accident which occurred on December 16 after eight buses and two smaller vehicles collided on the expressway, triggering a massive fire.
Probe:An investigation into the incident has been ordered under the supervision of Additional District Magistrate (Administration) Amresh Maurya. To prevent such accidents in future, the State government has issued a set of directions, including movement of vehicles in convoys, suspension of traffic when visibility is extremely low and installation of CCTV cameras along the expressway.

title: BJP leader V.V. Rajesh sworn in as Mayor of Thiruvananthapuram
summary: Three-time councillor G.S. Asha Nath is contesting as the deputy mayor candidate of the BJP
content:
Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) leader V.V. Rajesh was on Friday sworn in as the Mayor of Thiruvananthapuram, making it the first time that the party is coming to power in any Corporation in Kerala. Mr. Rajesh got 51 out of the total 100 votes, including one vote from Independent councillor M. Radhakrishnan. The Left Democratic Front (LDF)’s Mayoral candidate R.P. Sivaji got 29 votes, while the Congress-led United Democratic Front (UDF)’s K.S. Sabarinadhan got only 17 votes with two of the UDF votes becoming invalid.
Sudheesh Kumar, the independent councillor from Powdikonam and a Congress rebel, did not cast his vote. The election to the Vizhinjam ward was postponed earlier due to the death of a candidate. District Collector and Returning Officer Anu Kumari administered the oath to Mr. Rajesh. A large number of BJP workers who had begun gathering at the Corporation premises in the morning, erupted into spirited sloganeering as he completed his oath.
“I hope to use my experience and abilities to take along everyone to ensure development in the 101 wards of the Corporation. As a representative of the party ruling this country, my aim is to ensure that Thiruvananthapuram will be one of the three Indian cities with the biggest developmental activities happening in the next five years,” he said in his first address as the Mayor.
Although R. Sreelekha, former Director General of Police who won from the Sasthamangalam ward, was earlier tipped to be the Mayor, a section of the BJP leadership stood firm for Mr. Rajesh, considering his long years of experience in building the party at the grass-root level in the district. The party leadership is learnt to have promised bigger roles for her in the future.
It is noteworthy that Ms. Sreelekha left the council hall soon after Mr. Rajesh took oath and before he began his first address, and even before the Opposition councillors would leave the hall. Three-time councillor G.S. Asha Nath is contesting as the deputy mayor candidate of the BJP.
Ending over four decades of the Left Democratic Front (LDF)’s hold over the Thiruvananthapuram Corporation, the BJP-led National Democratic Alliance (NDA) secured power in Thiruvananthapuram Corporation by winning 50 out of the 101-seats, one short of the majority figure.

title: Three arrested in Anantapur for trade in illegal weapons
summary: Three individuals were arrested in Anantapur for illegally trading weapons, including country-made guns and ammunition.
content:
A gang was busted following an investigation ordered by Superintendent of Police P. Jagadeesh after it came to the notice of the police that a gym operator in the city was in possession of a firearm and it was also test fired. A case was registered on December 12 for an in-depth probe.
Speaking to reporters on Friday (December 26), Mr. Jagadeesh said the arrested are gym operator Nalli Rajashekar Reddy of Anantapur city and police arrested Rohit Parmar and Shivam Singh Parihar, both hailing from Morena district of M.P.
The SP said Rohit Parmar and Shivam Singh played a key role in the illegal purchase, storage and transportation of weapons and in the supply and transport of illegal weapons, while Rajasekhar Reddy assisted them.
Mr. Jagadeesh said the three accused were operating as an illegal arms supply gang with mutual contacts. “Rohit Parmar and Shivam Singh Parihar had been purchasing country-made guns and bullets at low prices from unidentified persons in the Gwalior–Morena regions for the past few years and illegally supplying them to other States. Rajashekar Reddy came into contact with Rohit Parmar and Shivam Singh Parihar about three years ago while visiting Jalandhar, Punjab, to purchase gym equipment,” the SP said.
Believing that a gun would be useful to intimidate troublesome individuals at his gym, Reddy purchased a gun with their help and kept it. Using local contacts and business links, Reddy assisted the other accused in selling weapons, the SP said.
During interrogation, the accused disclosed that a country-made gun could be purchased in Madhya Pradesh for about ₹40,000 to ₹50,000 and sold in States like Andhra Pradesh for a profit of ₹20,000 to ₹30,000 per gun. Motivated by this illegal profit, they planned to procure and sell multiple guns, which ultimately led to their arrest.
The SP warned that possessing or using illegal weapons in public places is a serious crime and will not be tolerated. Strict legal action will be taken against offenders. Mr. Jagadeesh said investigation is ongoing to identify other persons involved in the illegal arms supply network.

title: Incidents of violence against minorities in Bangladesh cannot be dismissed as political violence, says MEA
summary: MEA condemns violence against minorities in Bangladesh, urging justice, while addressing H-1B visa concerns with the U.S. government.
content:
Ministry of External Affairs on Friday (December 26, 2025) said that itcondemns the gruesome killing of Hindu youth in Bangladeshand expects the perpetrators to be brought to justice.
Ministry of External Affairs said that “India closely following developments in Bangladesh.”
In a press briefing on the Bangladesh developments, the MEA also talked about thereturn of BNP’s Tarique Rahman. It said “India supports free, fair polls in Bangladesh; this development should be seen in that context.”
The MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said “Continuing hostilities against minorities in Bangladesh including Hindus, Christians and Buddhists matter of grave concern.”
He said “Over 2,900 incidents of violence against minorities documented in Bangladesh by independent sources during tenure of interim government.”
The MEA spokesperson reiterated that “Incidents of violence against minorities in Bangladesh cannot be brushed aside as media exaggeration or dismissed as political violence.”
On the problems faced by Indians following rescheduling of H-1B visas, the MEA said “We have flagged these issues and our concerns to U.S. side.”

title: Kacheguda-Yesvantpur Vande Bharat Express to halt at Hindupur on trial basis from December 27
summary: Trial halt for Kacheguda-Yesvantpur Vande Bharat Express at Hindupur begins on December 27, in effort to enhance regional rail connectivity.
content:
South Western Railway has announced a two-minute experimental stoppage for the Kacheguda–Yesvantpur Vande Bharat Express at Hindupur station starting December 27.
Train No. 20703 (Kacheguda–Yesvantpur) will arrive at Hindupur at 12.08 p.m. and depart at 12.10 p.m. On the return journey, Train No. 20704 (Yesvantpur–Kacheguda) will halt from 3.48 p.m. to 3.50 p.m.
According to South Western Railway, the trial stoppage is aimed at improving rail connectivity and offering faster, more convenient travel options for passengers in the Hindupur region.

title: Salem West MLA R. Arul lodges complaint against PMK leader Anbumani
summary: Salem MLA R. Arul files complaint against PMK leader Anbumani over factional disputes and upcoming party meeting.
content:
Salem West MLA R. Arul, who owes allegiance to Pattali Makkal Katchi (PMK) founder S. Ramadoss, on Friday (December 26, 2025) lodged a complaint with the Salem Police Commissionerate against Anbumani Ramadoss, who heads another faction of the party. This followed a complaint lodged by the Anbumani faction against the proposed general council and executive committee meeting of the party to be convened by Dr. Ramadoss in Salem on Monday (December 29, 2025).
The Anbumani faction’s complaint claimed that he was the president of the PMK and that others should not use the party’s flag and name. It urged the police to refuse permission for Dr. Ramadoss’ meeting.
However, Mr Arul, in the counter complaint, contended that the Delhi High Court on December 6 said thatDr. Anbumani was not the president of the PMK. “Dr. Anbumani wasexpelled from the party on September 11, 2025. So, he has no connection with the party and could not claim the party. According to the PMK bylaws, Dr. Ramadoss alone can conduct the general council and executive meeting,” he said, seeking action against Dr. Anbumani and his supporters.

title: Nurse murdered at home in Bengaluru, colleague arrested
summary: Bengaluru nurse murdered; colleague arrested, Police suspect that argument over marriage led to fatal confrontation.
content:
Bengaluru police have arrested a 25-year-old nurse for allegedly murdering his 39-year-old colleague following an argument over marriage. The accused has been identified as Sudhakar, a native of Hassan.
The deceased, Mamatha H.L., was a resident of Pragathipura at Kumaraswamy Layout in south Bengaluru. She was found murdered in her house on December 25 morning.
According to the FIR, Mamatha had been working as a staff nurse at Jayadeva hospital for the past four years. She shared a rented house with a female colleague.
A senior police officer said Mamatha got acquainted with Sudhakar, a colleague, about a year ago. Investigations revealed that the two were friends and Mamatha had been suggesting that they get married. However, recently Sudhakar’s family fixed his marriage with another woman, leading to frequent arguments between the two, according to the police.
On December 24, Mamatha’s roommate was at work when Mamatha returned home with Sudhakar. The next morning, Mamatha’s roommate asked the landlady to check whether Mamatha was at home. When there was no response after knocking on the door, the landlady peeped through a window and saw Mamatha lying on the floor in a pool of blood. She immediately alerted the neighbours and informed the police.
Initially, the police relied on technical inputs and crime scene evidence. They got a breakthrough when they established that a man, later identified as Sudhakar, had dropped Mamatha home the previous night.
An investigator toldThe Hinduthat Sudhakar and Mamatha discussed the wedding after reaching her house. The discussion escalated into a heated argument, during which Sudhakar allegedly got hold of a kitchen knife and attacked Mamatha in her neck and throat. He fled the scene after she collapsed, fearing arrest. The alleged incident occurred during the intervening night (December 24 and 25) between 11.50 p.m. and 12.30 a.m.
The Kumaraswamy Layout police have booked Sudhakar under BNS Section 103(1), which pertains to murder, following a complaint from Mamatha’s brother. He was arrested on December 25 evening. A Bengaluru court has remanded Sudhakar to police custody.
“We have recorded his statement, but the weapon is yet to be recovered. Further investigation is under way to verify the claims made by the accused,” the officer said.

title: Drone patrolling across Sathya Sai district from January 1, says Superintendent of Police
summary: Drone surveillance begins January 1, 2026, in Sathya Sai district to enhance crime control and provide evidence against offenders.
content:
Drone surveillance and patrolling will be intensified across the district from January 1, 2026, District Superintendent of Police S. Satish Kumar said.
The SP on Friday (December 26) handed over five drones worth ₹24 lakh, including two night vision drones, to Puttaparthi Urban, Puttaparthi Rural, Hindupur, Madakasira, and Nallamada circle police officers. Speaking on the occasion he said, drone surveillance will be useful to effectively control crime and the offenders will also be punished as the recorded footage will act as an evidence.
He said night vision drones were already provided to Hindupur, Madakasira, Kadiri, Dharmavaram and Penugonda and these will be used for patrolling during night times starting January 1, 2026. The SP said drones would come handy in preventing crime also to keep a tab on gambling, consumption of ganja and alcohol in remote and secluded areas.
Mr. Satish Kumar urged general public as well as business persons to instal CCTVs at their premises for surveillance.

title: CMO refutes media reports of CM calling up Thiruvananthapuram Mayor V.V. Rajesh to congratulate him
summary: CMO issues press release clarifying its position
content:
Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan’s office has refuted media reports that he had called up Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) leader and Thiruvananthapuram Mayor elect V.V. Rajesh to congratulate him. According to a press release issued from the CMO on Friday afternoon, Mr. Rajesh had called the CM’s personal assistant to speak to the Chief Minister.
Since the Chief Minister was not with him at that time, the PA said that he could connect later. After that, the PA called and connected to the Chief Minister. Mr. Rajesh told the Chief Minister that he was going to be elected as the Mayor and that he would meet him in person after that. The CM responded by saying ‘Congratulations’.
“However, the news that was spread later claimed that the Chief Minister called Mr. Rajesh and congratulated him. This is contrary to the facts and creates misunderstanding,” said the release.

title: Ex-MNS leader Prakash Mahajan joins Shiv Sena
summary: Ex-MNS leader Prakash Mahajan joins Shiv Sena ahead of municipal polls, aims to strengthen the party as spokesperson.
content:
Former Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) leader Prakash Mahajan on Friday (December 26, 2025) joined Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde-led Shiv Sena, barely two weeks before the municipal corporation polls in the State.
Mr. Mahajan, the brother of late BJP leader Pramod Mahajan, had been associated with Raj Thackeray-led MNS since its formation in 2006, but quit the party earlier this year due to differences with its leadership.
Also Read |BMC polls: Deadlock persists over couple of seats between Sena (UBT), MNS
Speaking to reporters, Mr. Shinde said Mr. Mahajan will be a Shiv Sena spokesperson and contribute to building the organisation.
Elections to 29 municipal corporations in Maharashtra will be held on January 15, and votes will be counted the next day.

title: Call to address frequent snarl up on Thamarassery pass
summary: Volunteers’ groups submit memorandum to District Collector seeking his immediate intervention
content:
Members of various voluntary organisations working for the conservation of Thamarassery ghat road have called upon the district administration to adopt immediate measures for resolving the recurring snarl-up on the inter-district mountain pass.
In a memorandum recently submitted to the District Collector, the complainants pointed out that the uncontrolled entry of heavy goods carriers was found worsening the situation in the wake of the New year season. They said the movement of emergency vehicles was at stake with the uncontrolled situation.
“There is not even a single dedicated crane to remove the vehicles involved in road accidents. The delayed action often leads to long hours of traffic blocks on the mountain pass,” said S. Renjith, a member of the volunteers’ group. He said the entry of multi-axle vehicles should be restricted during the festival time as a temporary solution.
In the memorandum, the volunteers’ groups also called for the widening of the sixth, seventh and eighth hairpin curves. Till the completion of the widening works, heavy vehicles should be diverted via Kuttiyadi pass, they demanded.
Meanwhile, police sources said traffic diversions via Kuttiyadi pass were under consideration in the wake of noticing a heavy vehicle flow to the ghat road area. A final decision would be taken after holding a meeting with the District Collector, they said.

title: Unnao rape case: Protest outside Delhi HC against suspension of Sengar's jail term
summary: Protesters, including women's activists and the Unnao rape survivor's mother, rally against the suspension of Kuldeep Sengar's jail term.
content:
Scores of protesters, including women activists along with the Unnao rape survivor's mother, demonstrated outside the Delhi High Court on Friday (December 26, 2025),days after the sentence of Kuldeep Sengar, a former BJP MLA who was convicted in the case, was suspended.
The protesters, holding placards, raised slogans such as “Balatkariyo ko sanrakshan dena band kro” (stop protecting rapists) in support of the Unnao rape survivor.
Women activists from the All India Democratic Women's Association participated in the protest along with activist Yogita Bhayana and the survivor's mother.
Speaking toPTI, the survivor’s mother said she had come to the high court to protest as her daughter had endured immense suffering.
“I am not blaming the entire high court, but only the two judges whose decision has shattered our trust,” she said.
The mother added that earlier judges had delivered justice to the family, but the accused had now been granted bail.
“This is an injustice towards our family. We willapproach the Supreme Court, as I have faith in it,” she said.
The Delhi High Court on Tuesdayordered the release of Sengar, who is serving a life term in the case, on bail pending the disposal of his appeal against his conviction by a trial court in December 2019.
In its order, the court directed that the former Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) MLA shall not come within a five-kilometre radius of the victim’s residence or threaten the rape survivor or her mother, and said any violation of the conditions would automatically lead to the cancellation of his bail.
However, Sengar will remain in jail as he is also serving a 10-year sentence in connection with the custodial death of the survivor's father and has not been granted bail in that case.

title: Air pollution: Delhi HC asks Centre to reply on plea to reduce GST on air purifiers
summary: Delhi HC directs Centre to respond to plea for reduced GST on air purifiers amid worsening air pollution in the capital.
content:
The Delhi High Court on Friday (December 26, 2025) directed the Centre to submit a detailed affidavit to apetition seeking lowering of goods and services tax on air purifiersin view of worsening air quality in the national capital.
A vacation Bench of Justice Vikas Mahajan and Justice Vinod Kumar granted the Centre 10 days’ time to file its reply to the petition, while posting the case for further hearing on January 9.
During the hearing, Additional Solicitor General N. Venkataraman, representing the Centre, stated that meetings of the GST Council have to be held physically and that it was not possible to convene such meetings through video conferencing.
The ASG further highlighted that the GST Council is a constitutional body and that voting has to be done only in person. He sought time to submit a detailed affidavit from the government in response to the petition.
The public interest litigation filed by advocate Kapil Madan sought directions to the central government to classify air purifiers as “medical devices” and reduce the goods and services tax to the five per cent slab. Air purifiers are currently taxed at 18 per cent.
The petition stated that purifiers cannot be treated as luxury items in view of the “extreme emergency crisis” caused by severe air pollution in Delhi.
On December 24, the court had directed the GST Council to meet at the earliest and consider lowering or abolishing GST on air purifiers.
The matter was listed on Friday to inform the court when the Council could meet and whether it was possible for it to convene virtually, if not physically.

title: After backlash, BIAL increases free parking duration at T1 arrivals at Bengaluru airport
summary: BIAL extends free parking at Bengaluru airport's Terminal 1 arrivals from 10 to 15 minutes following criticism by cab operators.
content:
Following criticism of the newly-introduced pick-up regulations, Bangalore International Airport Limited (BIAL) has extended the free parking duration at the Terminal 1 arrival area at Kempegowda International Airport in Bengaluru, effective from December 26 from 10 minutes to 15 minutes.
BIAL stated: “We have extended the free parking duration at Terminal 1 arrival pick-up areas P3 and P4 from 10 minutes to 15 minutes. This enhancement is designed to provide greater ease and flexibility for passengers and their families, while supporting smoother traffic flow and a more seamless arrival experience.
“To further ease passenger movement and enhance the arrival experience, passengers can choose between a fleet of shuttles (every 7 minutes), 6 cars, and 10 buggies operating to and from the P3/P4 pick-up areas. This ensures convenient, frequent, and assisted movement for passengers.”
Under the earlier pick-up regulations implemented at Terminal 1 on December 13, commercial vehicles were required to wait in the designated P3 and P4 parking areas, where a complimentary parking period of 10 minutes was provided. This free waiting duration has now been increased to 15 minutes. Beyond this period, cab operators will be charged ₹100 for the first 30 minutes, followed by ₹50 for each additional hour.

title: Nooranad Leprosy Sanatorium hosts Christmas love feast
summary: The programme was held under the leadership of social activist Johnson V. Idikkula, with the support of Shot Pulikkathra Koinonia Group
content:
A Christmas love feast was organised at Nooranad Leprosy Sanatorium by ‘Nanmayude Snehakkoodu’ collective on Wednesday.
The programme was held under the leadership of social activist Johnson V. Idikkula, with the support of Shot Pulikkathra Koinonia Group. Volunteers set aside their daily routines to spend the day with the inmates and share a festive meal with them.
Mr. Idikkula, a resident of Thalavadi, has been visiting the sanatorium for over 30 years and coordinating charitable activities there in association with various organisations.
The Christmas–New Year gathering was inaugurated by Ajoy K. Varghese, member, Niranam grama panchayat.

title: CAT-2025 Karnataka topper wants to join IIMB
summary: Karnataka topper Govind Balasubramanian aims for IIMB after scoring 100 percentile in CAT-2025, aspiring for MBA and mentorship.
content:
Govind Balasubramanian, who appeared for the Common Admission Test (CAT), the all-India entrance exam for admission into the Indian Institute of Managements (IIMs) and other top B-schools, three times in a row to secure a seat in the Indian Institute of Management Bangalore (IIMB), has also become the Karnataka topper by scoring 100 percentile marks in CAT-2025.
Originally from Kerala and working as a data scientist at a private firm in Bengaluru, Mr. Balasubramanian had written CAT-2025 at the Bengaluru centre this time.
“My dream is to do Master of Business Administration (MBA) in IIMB. I had scored 100 percentile in the CAT-2022 earlier. But I did not get a seat in IIMB in the viva. So, last year I attempted the CAT-2024 and scored 99.97 percentile of marks. But last time also, I did not get a seat in IIMB either. So again, this year I have written the exam and scored 100 percentile, and I am looking forward to the viva. This time I will get admission even if I get a seat in IIMB or IIM Ahmedabad,” he said.
“I studied Electronics and Telecommunication Engineering from BITS Pilani K.K. Birla Goa campus and graduated in 2023. Since childhood I have an interest in Maths and Logical questions. These sections in the CAT question paper helped me score 100 percentile,” he said.
Sharing his future dreams withThe Hindu, Mr. Balasubramanian said, “After completion of my MBA, I would like to explore opportunities in product management and consulting. I also want to mentor students for CAT and GMAT exams. I have already started a community of students, where I will be trying to mentor them and my aim is to convert that into institution or online coaching,” he added.

title: Academy of Comparative Philosophy and Religion plans competitions
summary: The Academy of Comparative Philosophy and Religion announces national competitions for students during a February 2026 conference in Belagavi.
content:
The Academy of Comparative Philosophy and Religion (ACPR) situated in the Gurudev Ranade Mandir will organise a series of national level competitions for students.
This is part of a three-day national conference scheduled in February 2026.
All four competitions are for undergraduate, post-graduate and doctoral and other research students.
ACPR Secretary M.B. Zirali told reporters in Belagavi on Friday that apart from cash prizes, winners will get opportunities to showcase works of art, present songs and deliver speech at the conference and publish essays in the ACPR journal.
Solo singing competition will be held February 10, 2026. The last date for submitting application is December 31.
An essay competition will be organised on the Life and Works of Dr. R.D. Ranade and Comparative Philosophies and Religions. Entries have to be in English and the essay should be 2,500 to 3,000 words long.
There will be a drawing competition for school students up to standard 10 and another for general category without age limit on the theme of saints of India. It will be held on February 8.
There will be a national elocution competition on Dr. R. D. Ranade and Comparative Philosophies and Religions. The speech can be in English, Kannada and Marathi languages. It will be held on February 9. The last date for submitting application is January 31.
For more details, ACPR can be contacted on Ph: 7624889972 or email academic@acprbgm.org.

title: Goa nightclub fire: Court extends police custody of Luthra brothers till December 29
summary: Goa court extends police custody of nightclub owners Luthra brothers until December 29 following deadly fire that killed 25.
content:
A Goa court on Friday (December 26, 2025) extended till December 29 the police custody of brothers Saurabh and Gaurav Luthra, owners of the Birch by Romeo Lane nightclub where 25 people were killed in a devastating fire earlier this month.
The siblings had fled to Thailand just hours after the tragedy that occurred in Arpora village on December 6 and were deported from that nation on December 17.
The judicial magistrate first class of Mapusa court extended the police custody of Saurabh and Gaurav Luthra till December 29, their advocate Parag Rao told reporters.
Their initial 10-day remand expired on Friday (December 26).
Mr. Rao said that his clients did not oppose the extension of custody, as they want to cooperate with the investigating officer.
The Luthras, who are currently in the custody of Anjuna police, were not at their nightclub when the blaze broke out, he said.
The Anjuna police have registered a case against the brothers for culpable homicide not amounting to murder and other offences.
Eight persons have been arrested so far, while police have initiated the process for the issuance of a Blue Corner Notice against British national Surinder Kumar Khosla, an accused who has fled to the United Kingdom.

title: Drunk driver drags motorcycle for half a kilometre in serial accident on ORR
summary: Drunk driver drags motorcycle for half a kilometre in Bengaluru, injuring rider and causing multiple accidents on Christmas Eve.
content:
In a serial accident on Christmas Eve, a 38-year-old man allegedly rammed into two cars and multiple motorcycles and dragged a Royal Enfield, lodged under his car, for about half a kilometre on the Outer Ring Road in the western part of Bengaluru.
The motorcyclist, Rohith S., 32, suffered injuries to his chest, hands, and legs, while others escaped unhurt. The accused, Srinivasa K.V., 38, was allegedly driving under the influence of alcohol, police said. He was chased down by other commuters and assaulted before being handed over to the police, an investigator toldThe Hindu.
According to the FIR, the incident occurred around 7.15 p.m. on Wednesday (December 24) near the Sumanahalli flyover, when Rohith was returning home.
Rohith told the police that Srinivasa, driving a SUV rammed into his Royal Enfield while he was riding towards Nagarabhavi Circle. The impact flung Rohith onto the road, while his motorcycle got lodged under the front of the car.
A senior police officer confirmed that Srinivasa did not stop and dragged the motorcycle for about half a kilometre. “Midway, he crashed into two more vehicles, prompting other commuters to chase and intercept him,” the officer said.
When intercepted, Srinivasa allegedly refused to step out of the car and locked himself inside. An agitated crowd broke a window, pulled him out, assaulted him, before handing him over to the police. A purported video of the accident has captured the entire sequence of events.
Kamakshipalya police have booked Srinivasa under Sections 281 (rash driving on a public way) and 125(a) (act endangering life or personal safety of others) of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023.
Police have also booked him for drunk driving, seized his car, and said they will recommend cancellation of his driving licence. As the offences are bailable, he is currently out on bail.

title: Congress alleges corruption, administrative failure in BMC; releases 'chargesheet'
summary: Mumbai Congress releases a chargesheet against BMC, alleging corruption and administrative failures amid a lack of elected representatives.
content:
The Mumbai Congress on Friday (December 26, 2025) published a "chargesheet" against the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC), alleging large-scale corruption, administrative failure and financial irregularities in the civic body's functioning.
Speaking to reporters, Mumbai Congress president Varsha Gaikwad claimed that the BMC, Asia's largest civic body, which has been without elected representatives for more than three years, has failed to ensure transparency and accountability in governance.
The "chargesheet" highlights alleged irregularities in civic works, tender processes and expenditure of public funds, she said.
The former Minister alleged that key civic departments were functioning without proper supervision, leading to delays in public works, poor quality infrastructure and hardship to citizens, and accused the civic administration of favouring select contractors and mismanaging funds allocated for essential services.
Also Read |Polls for BMC, 28 other municipal corporations on Jan. 15, vote count on Jan. 16
Despite the BMC being the country's richest municipal corporation, basic amenities such as roads, water supply and drainage systems were in poor condition in several parts of the city, she claimed, demanding an independent probe into the allegations.
The Congress, in the chargesheet, alleged that for three years and nine months, the Mahayuti government had denied citizens their voting rights.
Listing 13 points, the party termed the BMC as "Brasht Mahayuti Corporation", highlighting poor water supply, public transport and traffic woes.
Ms. Gaikwad said that the Mumbai Congress will contest the January 15 civic polls on the issue of development without creating unnecessary disputes.
"Under the administrator's rule, Mumbaikars were looted, as there were no elected representatives for three years. We have raised our voice against bad roads, traffic problems, air pollution and potholes. The administration has damaged the country's financial capital and done injustice to the people," she said.
The Congress wants to become the voice of Mumbaikars seeking justice and progress, she said, adding that the party will fight for development without creating disputes over caste, religion, region or language.
The long-awaited polls to 29 municipal corporations in Maharashtra, including Mumbai, where elections have been due since early 2022, will be held on January 15, and votes will be counted on January 16.

title: BNP’s Tarique Rahman visits his father’s grave 17 years after return from self-exile
summary: Tarique Rahman visits his father's grave 17 years after returning from exile, honoring former president Ziaur Rahman in Dhaka.
content:
BNP acting chairman Tarique Rahman on Friday (December 26, 2025) visited the grave of his father and Bangladesh's former president Ziaur Rahman in Dhaka, 17 years after he returned home from self-exile in the U.K.
The 60-year-oldBangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) acting chairman returned to the country on Thursday(December 25, 2025) after living in London since 2008.
Rahman reached Zia Udyan in a red-and-green bulletproof bus and paid floral tributes at the grave, offering 'dua' and 'munajat' for the eternal peace of his father’s soul, news portal bangla.daily-sun.com reported.
BNP founder Ziaur Rahman was a Bangladeshi military officer who served as the sixth president of Bangladesh from 1977 until his assassination in 1981. He retired from the army in 1978 with the rank of lieutenant general.
The BNP leader was accompanied by senior party leaders during the visit.
According to the Daily Star newspaper, members of the Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB), Rapid Action Battalion (Rab), police and the army barred media personnel and party activists from entering the grave area and its surroundings.
While Rahman was paying respects, party leaders and activists gathered in front of the entrance and chanted slogans.

title: Delhi court grants bail to six accused in India Gate protest case over ‘Maoist slogans’
summary: Delhi court grants bail to six protesters accused of raising Maoist slogans during the India Gate agitation on November 23.
content:
A Delhi court on Friday (December 26, 2025) granted bail to six protesters arrested in connection with an agitation on Kartavya Path, where slogans were allegedly raised in support of slain Maoist commander Madvi Hidma.
Additional Sessions Judge Amit Bansal granted bail to Ilakkiya, Ayisha Wafiya, Ravjot Kaur, Gurkirat Kaur, Abhinash Satyapathi and Kranti. A detailed order is awaited.
The protest took place at the India Gate on November 23, during which some agitators were accused of raising pro-Hidma slogans and using pepper spray on the police trying to contain them.
According to the police, 23 protesters were arrested in two separate cases lodged at the Parliament Street and Kartavya Path police stations.

title: India imposes anti-dumping duty on two Chinese products
summary: India imposes anti-dumping duties on Chinese steel and refrigerant gas to protect domestic industries from unfair pricing.
content:
India has imposed anti-dumping duty on two Chinese goods, a refrigerant gas and certain kinds of steel products, during the month so far to guard domestic players from cheap imports from the neighbouring country.
These duties were imposed as these products — cold-rolled non-oriented electrical steel, and 1,1,1,2-Tetrafluoroethane or R-134a — were exported to India from China at below normal prices.
On steel goods, India has imposed $223.82 per tonne on certain Chinese firms, while on few others $415 per tonne was imposed for five years, according to a finance ministry notification.
On the gas, up to $5,251 per tonne was slapped for five years.
As per a separate notification, India said it has imposed anti-dumping duty on imports of 'Calcium Carbonate Filler Masterbatch' exported from Vietnam. It is widely used in plastic industry.
These duties are imposed after the commerce ministry's investigation arm Directorate General of Trade Remedies (DGTR) has conducted probes separately for each of these items and recommended the duty.
Anti-dumping probes are conducted by countries to determine whether domestic industries have been hurt because of a surge in cheap imports.
As a countermeasure, they impose these duties under the multilateral regime of the Geneva-based World Trade Organisation (WTO). The duty is aimed at ensuring fair trading practices and creating a level-playing field for domestic producers vis-a-vis foreign producers and exporters.
India, China, and Vietnam are members of the WTO.
India has already imposed anti-dumping duties on several products to tackle cheap imports from various countries, including China.
Imposition of high tariffs by the U.S. on several countries have led to dumping of goods in countries like India.

title: India conveys concern to U.S. over cancellation of H1B visa interviews
summary: India expresses concern to the U.S. over postponed H-1B visa interviews for thousands of applicants, causing significant hardships.
content:
India on Friday (December 26, 2025) said itflagged its concerns to the U.S. over cancellation of pre-scheduled H1B visa interviewsof large numbers of Indian applicants  and that both sides are engaged on the issue.
Theinterviews of thousands of H-1B visa applicants slated from the middle of this monthin India have been abruptly postponed by several months to scrutinise their social media posts and online profiles.
Some of the applicants, whose visa appointments were scheduled last week, received e-mails from US immigration authorities informing that their interviews are being pushed back as late as May next year.
The government of India has received several representations from Indian nationals who are facing problems with their rescheduling of their visa appointments, External Affairs Ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said at his weekly media briefing.
Visa-related issues pertain to the sovereign domain of any country, he said, adding: "we have flagged these issues and our concerns to the US side, both here in New Delhi and in Washington DC."
Mr. Jaiswal said several Indians have been stranded for extended periods of time in India causing a lot of "hardships" to them and their families.
"The government of India remains actively engaged with the U.S. side to minimise the disruptions caused to our nationals," he said.
The mass cancellation of scheduled interviews of the H-1B visa applicants in view of the enhanced vetting measures has resulted in significant delays in their return to the U.S.
The rescheduling of the interviews is for all applicants who were previously given appointments from December 15 onwards.
Most of them were already in India and are now unable to return to the US pending their new interview dates since they don't have a valid H1B visa to travel back to the U.S. for their jobs.

title: ISKCON plans to hold grand Vaikunta Ekadasi celebrations on Tuesday
summary: Join ISKCON Hubballi for grand Vaikunta Ekadasi celebrations on Tuesday, featuring rituals, cultural programs, and public darshan.
content:
The ISKCON Hubballi-Dharwad temple will hold grand celebrations of Vaikunta Ekadasi on Tuesday.
Addressuing presspersons in Hubballi on Friday, Vice-President of ISKCON Hubballi-Dharwad Raghottam Dasa said that the first phase of a new temple will also be inaugurated on the occasion.
“On this day special entrance on the northern side of Vishnu temples will be ceremonially opened. As part of the celebrations, a gold-painted Vaikuntha Dwara will be erected at the temple entrance. The Vaikuntha Dwara Puja will commence at 8.30 a.m., following which the gate will be open to the public from 9 a.m. to 9 p.m.,” he said.
He said that various rituals will be held during the day and in the evening, there will be cultural programmes, including classical dance performances by Vidushi Hema Waghmode and Vidushi Sahana Bhat, along with their troupes.
Darshan will be available for the public from 9 a.m. to 9 p.m. and elaborate arrangements have been made for vehicle parking.

title: New Assembly Secretary assumes charge

content:
Rendla Tirupati assumed charge as the new Secretary of the Telangana State Legislative Assembly on Friday taking over responsibilities from V. Narasimha Charyulu.
Later Mr. Tirupati, along with Mr. Narasimha Charyulu, paid a courtesy visit to the Speaker of the Legislative Assembly Gaddam Prasad Kumar at his residence. title: Zero drugs policy during NY fete: Hyderabad Police Commissioner
summary: Zero drugs policy during NY fete: Hyderabad Police Commissioner
content:
With New Year’s Eve approaching, the Hyderabad City Police will enforce a zero drugs policy across the city to ensure drug-free celebrations, Police Commissioner V.C. Sajjanar said on Friday.
Mr. Sajjanar chaired a high-level coordination meeting at the Integrated Command and Control Centre in Banjara Hills, where he directed senior and field officers to maintain strict surveillance across the city during the festivities. He instructed officers to remain vigilant and ensure coordinated action to prevent the use and circulation of narcotics.
A multi-layered security plan involving the Hyderabad Narcotics Enforcement Wing, Task Force, Special Branch and local police units would be implemented. Special surveillance teams have been deployed at pubs, hotels, restaurants and event venues, with instructions to monitor those who were involved in drug-related cases in the past two years. Police have also been asked to prepare a list of known drug-peddlers and consumers and track people entering the city for New Year celebrations.
Private gatherings at service apartments and hostels would also be monitored to prevent illegal activities. All New Year celebrations at pubs, hotels and restaurants will be permitted only until 1.00 a.m., and strict action will be taken against violators, including cancellation of licences if illegal activities are detected.
To manage crowds, police will strengthen check-posts and barricades at key locations such as Maitrivanam, Necklace Road, Tank Bund and KBR Park. Mr. Sajjanar instructed officers to ensure that security arrangements do not inconvenience the general public and that celebrations remain peaceful.
“Our objective is that not a single drug case should be reported in Hyderabad during the New Year celebrations,” the Commissioner said.

title: As a son, I’ll take pride in my father’s achievements: KTR
summary: KTR defends his father's legacy while addressing political tensions and language use in Telangana's leadership dynamics.
content:
HYDERABAD
Working president of Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) K.T. Rama Rao asked Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy whether a son would not get angry if somebody abuses his (KTR’s) father, who had fought for the statehood of Telangana, achieved it and elected twice as the Chief Minister by people.
“If a son can’t take pride in the achievements of his father, who else would. In case Mr. Revanth Reddy does any good work, his children will take pride or else they would hesitate to take his name”, Mr. Rama Rao said after admitting a few Congress leaders of the Serilingamaplly constituency into BRS here on Friday.
Several Congress leaders, including Mr. Revanth Reddy, were asking BRS chief and Leader of the Opposition K. Chandrasekhar Rao to attend the Assembly. Mr. Reddy was sweating just with one press conference by Mr. Chandrasekhar Rao and if he attended the Assembly, the CM would get unsettled, Mr. Rama Rao claimed.
Referring to Mr. Revanth Reddy’s comments that he (KTR) had pursued his Intermediate in Guntur, Mr. Rama Rao sought to know what was wrong in it. He studied at Pune and in the US too. The Chief Minister, who is finding fault with his (KTR’s) education in Guntur, had married off his daughter to a Andhra (Bhimavaram) person, Mr. Rama Rao said.
On Mr. Reddy’s ‘abusive’ language against Mr. Chandrasekhar Rao, Mr. Rama Rao said he too would know such language but was holding back, respecting the Chief Minister’s chair. “I could use such abusive language in Urdu, Hindi, Telangana and English, if need be,” Mr. Rama Rao said. While condemning the abusive language, Mr. Rama Rao said he too could say that he felt like hitting the CM with footwear but refrain from making such comments.

title: Will not allow BJP to create communal disharmony in T.N., says Stalin
summary: Stalin vows to prevent BJP's communal disharmony in Tamil Nadu, highlighting state achievements during the 'Dravidian Model' government.
content:
Chief Minister M. K. Stalin on Friday said he would not allow the BJP to succeed in its attempt “to create communal disharmony” in Tamil Nadu.
“As long as Stalin and the ‘Dravidian Model’ government are there, the BJP will never succeed in its attempts to create communal disharmony in the State. People will chase them with votes,” he said after inaugurating the Integrated Collectorate complex at Veeracholapuram near Kallakurichi. added.
Adverting to various achievements made by Tamil Nadu, he said these denoted a developed India. On the other hand, he claimed, “the scenario is different in States ruled by the BJP where poverty, communal clashes, lynching, unemployment and attack on education remain.”
He alleged the BJP has created a situation where even children and differently-abled persons were attacked during Christmas. The Chief Minister charged, it is this model the BJP is trying to introduce in the State but the people of Tamil Nadu are very cautious.
Against the backdrop of the recent row over lighting of the Karthigai Deepam, Mr Stalin said devotees of Lord Muruga offer worship at the [Sultan Sikkandar Avulia] dargah atop the Thirupparankundram hillock while “Muslim brothers” offer rose milk to Hindus during the Chithirai festival in Madurai and Christians offer Pongal during the first day of the Tamil monthThai. “The unity and harmony of Tamil Nadu’s people—who affirm that every religion is equally acceptable—is what keeps pricking the eyes of the BJP, which wants to split the people by engaging in communal politics!” he said
Mr Stalin, who also laid the foundation stone for new projects worth ₹386.48 crore, said Tamil Nadu was numero uno State in the country in all sectors thanks to the work accomplished during the last four-and-a-half years of the ‘Dravidian Model’ government .
According to him, the previous AIADMK regime was not able to achieve even 5 % of the growth achieved by the current dispensation.
Mr. Stalin said that during the previous 10 years of AIADMK rule the State was in ruins. But the State has sprung back and it’s growth trajectory is on the upward trend during the Dravidian model government. “This is my open challenge. Can the AIADMK prove that they have achieved at least 5 % of what was accomplished by this government during their tenure?
Stating Tamil Nadu’s growth was unparalleled in the country, Mr. Stalin said it was the only State in India to achieve double-digit economic growth rate in real terms during 2024-25 at 11.19 %. The State has achieved all this without any support from the Centre.
Mr. Stain said that Tamil Nadu is the leader in the country whether it is in terms of Gross State Domestic Product (GSDP), automobile exports, electronics exports, non-leather footwear production, Startup rankings. Tamil Nadu also had the highest women workforce in India, he said.
“We have reached this place despite the Centre indulging in deceit and putting speed breakers to stop the State,” he said.
Mr. Stalin said his government focuses on the development of all sectors, districts, and sections of society, implementing schemes that aim not only to provide monetary benefits but also to achieve social benefits that enhance the quality of life. He said that the people’s verdict in the upcoming 2026 elections would be the crown for the achievements made during the four-and-a-half year rule of the ‘Dravidian Model’ government.

title: Roll back fare hike, SUCI(C) urges Railways
summary: SUCI(C) protests fare hike at Dharwad Railway Station, demanding rollback and improved passenger safety and amenities.
content:
Demanding that the railway fare hike be rolled back, members of Socialist Unity Centre of India (Communist) staged a demonstration in front of the Dharwad Railway Station on Friday.
Addressing the protestors, district secretary of SUCI(C) Laxman Jadagannavar said that the huge railway network built with public funds is meant to serve the people.
However, on the pretext of staff expenses, the Centre has unilaterally and indiscriminately increased railway fares.
Terming the fare hike as anti-people, Mr. Jadagannavar said that last year also the Railway authorities increased railway fares on the same pretext.
He said that a railway journey has remained a nightmare as the number of railway accidents has increased because of neglect towards maintenance of railway services and an increase in corruption.
The authorities have failed to take the requisite steps to improve services and the condition of railway coaches on a majority of the railway routes, he said.
While the Union government will get an additional revenue of ₹600 crore from the fare hike, the problems of railway passengers will continue unabated, he said and urged the government to withdraw the fare hike immediately.
He also demanded that requisite steps be taken to ensure passenger safety, time management and adequate passenger amenities.
SUCI(C) district committee member Gangadhar Badiger emphasised the need for increasing the number of general and sleeper coaches for the benefit of general public.
SUCI(C) office-bearers Thayidas M.B., Deepa Dharwad, Sharanu Gonawar, Madhulatha Goudar, Bhavanishankar Goudar, Ganga Kokare and others led the protest.
Subsequently, a memorandum addressed to Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw was submitted to the Station Master.

title: Punjab and Haryana HC reduces man's death penalty in minor's rape, murder
summary: Punjab and Haryana HC commutes death sentence to life imprisonment for man convicted of raping and murdering a minor girl.
content:
The Punjab and Haryana High Court has commuted a man's death sentence for the rape and murder of a five-and-a-half-year-old girl to rigorous imprisonment for life, and acquitted his mother, observing there is no IPC section to punish her for "trying to protect her Raja beta".
Sentencing the convict to rigorous imprisonment for life with 30 years of jail without remission, the court opined that the murder was, apparently, because of panic to destroy the evidence of rape and not a premeditated act. It also increased the fine amount to ₹30 lakh.
Pronouncing the verdict, the bench of Justices Anoop Chitkara and Sukhvinder Kaur also observed that family members, especially mothers, often have such blind love for their "precious" sons that, no matter how imperfect or villainous they might be, they are still regarded as 'RajaBetas'.
While acquitting the mother of all charges against her, the judges pointed out that she prioritised shielding her son instead of informing the police or seeking justice for the victim. "This social attitude, however appalling, is not new; it is deeply embedded in the region's patriarchal mindset and culture," they said.
A trial court in 2020 condemned Virender alias Bholu to death and sentenced his mother Kamla Devi to rigorous imprisonment for conspiracy and destruction of evidence in the 2018 rape and murder case.
The high court, in its December 23 verdict, observed that while deterrence through threat of death may still be a promising strategy in some frightful areas of murderous crime, to espouse a monolithic theory of its deterrent efficacy is unscientific.
"So we think it right to shift the emphasis, to accept composite factors of penal strategy and not to put all the punitive eggs in the 'hanging' basket but hopefully to try the humane mix," it said.
"It appears that the subsequent murder was because of panic to destroy evidence of rape and not a premeditated act. Therefore, the convict's life should not be taken away by the judicial process, and instead, to save the children and females, he can be incapacitated by imposing a suitable sentence that is also proportionate to the heinous and gruesome crime of raping and killing a girl aged five-and-a-half years, whom the accused was well familiar with," the high court stated.
It also observed that there was no allegation to substantiate that there was no possibility of the reformation of the convict on the death row, which creates an alternative view that would not validate the capital punishment.
This gives rise to two views — one favouring capital punishment when in a situation keeping a criminal alive is so dangerous that taking away life remains the only option, and the other view is to keep such a convict in custody for the longest possible time permissible under the law to do substantial justice to all concerned, the court further said.
"Therefore, when two views are possible before this court, to impose or not to impose a death sentence, then the view for not awarding the capital punishment must be preferred over the other extreme irreversible sentence," it said.
The court said any sentence to be proportionate must be stable and balanced like a table, and for any table to be stable, all its legs must be comparable. "Thus, the courts, while awarding a sentence, are under an obligation to consider the (a) crime, (b) victim, (c) criminal and his family, and (d) society and the State".
It said the convict has no criminal antecedents, and his conduct in prison is not violative, which makes reformation possible. "To save the other kids and females, the convict must stay inside the four walls of the prison until he is closer to the sunset of his virility," it observed.
"In the light of the referred judicial precedents, the death sentence is commuted to the rigorous imprisonment for life; however, considering the victim's age to be five years and seven months, we are convinced to impose a sentence of 30 years, without remission, which, in the peculiar facts and circumstances, would be justified and would also safeguard the other girls on the street from the pervertedness of the convict," the verdict stated.
The High Court also acquitted the convict's mother, Kamla Devi, of all charges against her.
It, however, said, "Unfortunately, in this part of India, family members, especially mothers, often have such blind love for their precious sons that, no matter how imperfect or villainous they might be, they are still regarded as 'Raja Betas.'  	"Kamla Devi, after discovering that herRaja-beta,Bholu, was not as gullible as his name suggested, and he had assaulted and brutally killed a girl-child aged five, prioritised shielding her son instead of informing the police or seeking justice for Laado. This social attitude, however appalling, is not new; it is deeply embedded in the region's patriarchal mindset and culture."
"Kamla Devi's only fault is that she was trying to protect her Raja-beta, for which she cannot be punished under the Indian Penal Code, however condemnable her conduct may be. Thus, there is no legally admissible evidence to make out a case for criminal conspiracy or for destruction of evidence against Kamla Devi," the high court Bench said.
The girl was raped and murdered in May 2018 by Virender alias Bholu, an employee of her father who worked as a small-time tent installer. Virender had been working with him for about five to six years.
On May 31, that year, the girl's father and Virender went to install a tent a short distance away. Virender went to the victim's home to get the lunch of the victim's father.
While returning, the girl accompanied Virender. As the girl's father napped after lunch, Virender took the girl to his home, where he raped her and then killed her with a kitchen knife. He then hid the body in a container where his mother used to store flour. Kamla Devi was not at home that time.

title: Adequate fertilizers available in all districts, says A.P. Markfed director
summary: A.P. Markfed ensures adequate fertilizer supply across districts, countering claims of shortages and supporting farmers' needs.
content:
Adequate fertilizers are available in all the districts, as AP Markfed has taken special care to ensure sufficient quantity of supplies to farmers in the State, said Andhra Pradesh State Co-operative Marketing Federation Limited (A.P. Markfed) Director Anepu Ramakrishna Naidu on Friday (26 December, 2025).
He said that there is no shortage of fertilizers in the State, contrary to what the YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) has projected, and urged the opposition party to visit Rythu Seva Kendras and Primary Agriculture Cooperative Societies to see the stocks maintained to meet farmers’ requirements during the Kharif and Rabi seasons.
Mr. Ramakrishna, who attended the 13th general body meeting of the Markfed held recently in Vijayawada, spoke toThe Hinduhere about the government’s initiatives to meet the expectations of the farmers. “Chief Minister Nara Chandrababu Naidu increased the budget from ₹40 crore to ₹85 crore this year to ensure that Markfed stocks fertilizers adequately and to prevent private dealers from fleecing farmers with higher rates,” he said.
He said that the Markfed has been handling around 3,000 tonnes of DAP, 500 tonnes of MOP and one lakh tonnes of Urea in 2025-26 with an aim to meet the requirements of the farmers in both the seasons. The government has given the responsibility to Markfed to take up market intervention activities to enable farmers to get remunerative prices for their produce during Rabi season also. The Markfed fixed Minimum Support Price (MSP) for all products including green gram, black gram, sorghum , pearl millet, finger millet and others.
“Markfed has been getting timely support from National Agriculture Cooperative Marketing Federation of India Limited and National Cooperative Consumers’ Federation of India Limited. Their support is also crucial for Markfed to meet its financial requirements.” Mr. Ramakrishna added.

title: Year Ender/Telangana health sector in 2025: Reforms advance, but delays and disruptions persist
