summary: Telangana's health sector in 2025 faces reforms alongside persistent disruptions, staffing gains, and urgent infrastructure challenges.
content:
The year 2025 unfolded as a challenging yet transitional phase for the Health department, marked by a blend of incremental reforms, budgetary support and recruitment gains, alongside recurring disruptions, regulatory lapses and delayed infrastructure projects. While the government initiated several long-pending measures, the year also brought out the continuing gap between policy intent and execution.
The year began with unrest among MBBS students at the Government Medical College Asifabad, who protested against faculty shortages. Their agitation brought attention to concerns over academic standards, training quality and patient care in newly established government medical colleges, many of which continue to struggle with staffing and infrastructure constraints.
Soon after, the State’s flagship Aarogyasri health insurance scheme faced a major disruption when the Telangana Aarogyasri Network Hospitals Association (TANHA) announced a temporary halt to admissions, citing unpaid dues of over ₹1,100 crore. The 10-day standoff affected access to care for thousands of beneficiaries before services resumed following assurances from Health Minister C. Damodar Raja Narasimha on phased payments.
Regulatory oversight came under scrutiny with the exposure of an illegal kidney transplant racket at Alakananda Hospital in Saroornagar. Investigations revealed that the private hospital had carried out transplants without mandatory authorisation, raising concerns over monitoring mechanisms and enforcement of transplant laws in the State.
Amid these developments, the government made a key administrative move by appointing Dr A. Narendra Kumar as the first full-time Director of Medical Education (DME) since Telangana’s formation in 2014. The post had remained under additional charge for more than a decade.
Infrastructure projects, however, continued to face delays. In January, the foundation stone was laid for the new Osmania General Hospital (OGH) building at Goshamahal, a long-pending demand of doctors working in the dilapidated heritage structure. The hospital was announced to be built at a cost of ₹2,700 crore with an initial completion timeline of two years. Construction, however, began only in October, and the executing agency later stated that the project would take 30 months, pushing timelines further.
Photographs of the proposed Osmania General Hospital building. The foundation stone for the new building was laid by Telangana Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy at Goshamahal, Hyderabad on Friday, January 31, 2025.
                                                            | Photo Credit: 
                                NAGARA GOPAL
Similarly, the 1,000-bed Telangana Institute of Medical Sciences (TIMS) at Sanathnagar, which was expected to be inaugurated this year, remained unopened despite multiple proposed dates.
On the policy front, the State budget for 2025-26 allocated ₹12,393 crore to the health department, an increase of ₹925 crore or 8% over the previous year. In March, the Legislative Assembly unanimously passed the Telangana Transplantation of Human Organs Bill, 2025, aimed at aligning State regulations with the Central Act and strengthening safeguards against illegal organ trade.
Public health indicators offered a mixed picture. Data from the Special Bulletin on Maternal Mortality in India 2019-21 showed Telangana’s maternal mortality ratio (MMR) at 45 deaths per 100,000 live births, a marginal rise from 43 in the previous period. While the increase contrasted with the national decline, Telangana continued to rank among the better-performing States in maternal health outcomes.
June saw renewed scrutiny of hospital management following a food poisoning incident at the Institute of Mental Health (IMH) in Erragadda, which resulted in one death and illness among around 70 patients. The Health Department relieved the in-charge Resident Medical Officer (RMO) and suspended the food supplier’s contract.
The same month, the National Medical Commission (NMC) issued show-cause notices to 26 government medical colleges over deficiencies in infrastructure, clinical material and faculty. Following a report inThe Hindu, Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy directed officials to prepare a comprehensive action plan for all 34 medical colleges in the State.
Unrest among MBBS interns in private medical colleges over non-payment of stipends also prompted the government to order a statewide vigilance inquiry. By September, the year came full circle with TANHA hospitals once again announcing suspension of Aarogyasri services, citing arrears nearing ₹1,400 crore.
Despite these challenges, recruitment remained a bright spot. Over the past two years, more than 11,000 posts have been filled in the Health Department, and recruitment is underway for over 5,000 more positions.
As 2025 ends, Telangana’s health sector stands at a crossroads, with momentum in staffing and policy reforms tempered by the need for timely execution.

title: Doddata, Bayalata in six Dharwad villages today
summary: Cultural programmes featuring Doddata and Bayalata will showcase traditional folkart in six Dharwad villages this Saturday.
content:
Sri Maruteshwara Doddata Sanga in collaboration with the Department of Kannada and Culture, Dharwad, will organise cultural programmes featuring traditional folkart forms such as Doddata and Bayalata in six villages, including Alagavadi, on Saturday.
Addressing media persons in Hubballi on Friday, noted Bayalata storyteller Teevanti Bheema Reddy Meti said that the programme will be held on the Government Model Primary School Grounds in Alagavadi.
He said that 15 folk troupes will perform not only in Alagavadi but also in five neighbouring villages. Each team is expected to perform for about 30 minutes.
Mr. Meti said that Sri Maruteshwara Doddata Sangha has been organising such traditional cultural performances since 1976 with the aim of preserving and promoting folkart forms.

title: Publicity campaign launched for cloud kitchen initiative by SHG in Mandya
summary: Mandya launches “Akkana Butti” cloud kitchen initiative to provide nutritious meals to offices, promoting self-help group empowerment.
content:
Mandya Zilla Panchayat Chief Executive Officer Nandini K.R. launched the publicity campaign for a self-help group’s cloud kitchen initiative called “Akkana Butti”, which seeks to supply nutritious packed meals to offices and other institutions in Mandya.
She released the pamphlets of the “Akkana Butti” food preparation centre in the presence of all branch heads and executive officers of Zilla Panchayat in the office recently. The initiative by the self-help group - Sanjeevani Federation – of Bevinahalli seeks to “supply clean, tasty, chemical-free and nutritious packed meals to government offices, private offices, banks and other institutions”.
She pointed out that this was the first such programme in the state to deliver packed meals to offices through self-help gropus and wished the federation success in its efforts.
Ms. Sudhamani, a woman member of the self-help group, said lunch would be available six days a week and a different menu would be served every day.
She said “Akkana Butti” food preparation centre had been set up with the slogan “Just dial the number, and your meal will reach your office”. She assured a supply of quality food to the offices.
The CEO said she will take steps to explore the possibility of procuring lunch, snacks, coffee and tea from the self-help groups for meetings held at Zilla Panchayat and other offices. She instructed all the taluk panchayat executive officers to draw up plans in the regard.
Mandya Zilla Panchayat’s planning director Roopashree K.N., Deputy Secretary (Development) Lakshmi P., Deputy Secretary (Administration), Shivalingaiah, Chief Planning Officer Dhanush, and taluk panchayat executive officers of the district were present.

title: Kalyana Karnataka issues sidelined during Winter Session, says MLC
summary: MLC Shashil Namoshi criticizes the Winter Session for neglecting key Kalyana Karnataka issues despite its agenda to address them.
content:
Member of the Legislative Council Shashil Namoshi has alleged that key issues concerning the Kalyana Karnataka region were largely ignored during the recent Winter Session in Belagavi despite the stated agenda that it was meant to address the concerns of North Karnataka.
Addressing a press conference in Kalaburagi on Friday, Mr. Namoshi said that the region continues to lag behind in terms of poverty alleviation, basic infrastructure, education and irrigation but these issues did not receive adequate attention during the session.
He said that while the session was projected as one focusing on North Karnataka, budgetary allocations and discussions remained largely centred on Belagavi and Hubballi.
He also criticised the State government for failing to properly implement the 8% reservation mandated under Article 371(J) in State-level recruitments for candidates belonging to Kalyana Karnataka region.
Posts earmarked for the Kalyana Karnataka region are being shown as backlog vacancies and later diverted to the general category. This is serious injustice and deliberate conspiracy against the youth from the region, he added.
Mr. Namoshi also pointed out that government employees from Kalyana Karnataka are facing discrimination in promotions, with the roster system not being followed as per the rules.

title: Vizag-based commerce platform offers instant cashback on purchases from local stores
summary: Discover local stores and earn instant cashback on purchases with Payzo, empowering neighborhood businesses in Visakhapatnam.
content:
A Visakhapatnam-based commerce platform, ‘Payzo’, claims to offer instant cashback on local purchases.
“The mobile application enables users to discover nearby stores, make payments, and earn cashback on everyday purchases — making local shopping more rewarding,” say founders Shankar D, an entrepreneur from Visakhapatnam, and Vyshnavi Chenna from Hyderabad.
“Our team brings together strong local market understanding and execution expertise,” Ms. Vyshnavi toldThe Hindu.
“We have launched the App in July 2025. We aim to make local shopping more rewarding and support neighbourhood businesses,” said Mr. Shankar.
“ For any other app, the reward points are  a promotion strategy. For us, cashback is our USP,” Ms. Vyshnavi added.
“Using location-based technology, Payzo allows users to browse local businesses based on category, distance, and discount percentage. Once a payment is completed, cashback is credited to the user’s Payzo balance and can be redeemed on future purchases at partner stores,” they said.
For merchants, Payzo offers free onboarding through a dedicated vendor mobile application.  “All discounts offered on the platform are fully merchant-funded,”  the founders assert.
Looking ahead, Payzo plans to expand its offerings with features such as bill payments and product-based bookings.

title: Mysuru temple to distribute more than 2 lakh laddus on New Year's day
summary: Mysuru temple to distribute over 2 lakh laddus as prasad on New Year's Day, continuing a beloved tradition since 1994.
content:
In continuation of a tradition initiated in 1994, the Yoga Narasimhaswamy temple in the city will distribute more than 2 lakh laddus as ‘’prasad’’ to the visitors on January 1, 2026, to mark New Year.
The laddus have been prepared with various ingredients to replicate the taste of the ones distributed in Tirupati, according to the temple authorities.
The distribution of the laddus, which will replicate the flavour of Tirupati laddus, will commence at 4 a.m. when the temple portal will be open to the devotees, and will go on till 11 p.m.
Speaking to media persons, Bhashyam Swami, a Sanskrit scholar and the founder of the temple at Vijayanagar, said here on Friday that there will be special religious rites, and the temple premises and the presiding deity will be decorated with flowers procured from Srirangam in Tamil Nadu.
After the performance of various rites, the distribution of laddus will commence. This year, about 10,000 large laddus weighing 2 kg each and nearly two lakh laddus weighing 150 gm each, will be distributed free of cost, according to Bhashyam Swamiji.
The temple administrative officer, Srinivasan, stated that laddu preparation commenced on December 20 and will continue until December 31, 2025. Nearly 100 individuals have been recruited for the purpose. The exercise entails usage of large quantity of ingredients including 100 quintals of groundnut floor, 200 quintals of sugar, 10,000 litres of edible oil, 500 kg of cashew nuts, 500 kg of raisins, 250 kg of almonds, 1,000 kg of diamond sugar, 2,000 kg of boora sugar, 50 kg of pistachios, 50 kg of cardamom, 50 kg of jackfruit and japatra, 50 kg of emerald camphor, and 200 kg of cloves, according to the temple authorities.
Bhashyam Swami said the laddu distribution began in 1994 with about 1,000 laddus, following a suggestion by Kannada matinee idol Dr. Rajkumar. During a visit to the temple in 1993, Dr. Rajkumar had highlighted the difficulty faced by ordinary devotees in obtaining Tirupati laddu prasads and suggested that similar laddus be distributed free at the Mysuru temple. He made a financial contribution and expressed the wish that the practice be continued annually in keeping with the wish of his family.
Over the years, the number of devotees has increased steadily, with annual laddu distribution rising from a few thousand to nearly two lakh. The laddu prasad is sent to Dr. Rajkumar’s family every year since its inception, the authorities added.

title: Walk Within padayatra starting in Dharwad today
summary: Join the Walk Within padayatra in Dharwad, promoting environmental awareness and community engagement from today until December 31.
content:
A padayatra titled Walk Within has been organised by Swami Vivekananda Youth Movement (SVYM) in Dharwad and surrounding villages starting Saturday. It will conclude on December 31.
Addressing presspersons in Dharwad on Friday, North Karnataka Regional Head of SVYM Jayant K.S. said that the foot march will be led by founder of SVYM R. Balasubrahmanyam.
The objectives of the padayatra are raising environmental concern, self-reflection and community engagement.
The inaugural ceremony of the padayatra will held at DIMANS (Dharwad Institute of Mental Health and Neurosciences) auditorium on Saturday at 10 a.m. with cancer surgery specialist Vijayalakshmi Deshmane participating as guest.
Mr. Jayant said that experts from various fields, students and general public will take part in the padayatra covering 10 km on foot every day.
Around 50 participants will visit villages and engage in discussions and reflections on people’s lives, achievements and challenges, he said.
On the first day, the participants will halt at Daddikamalapur. They will halt at Kalakeri on the second day, Devarahubballi on the third day and Managundi on the fourth.
The padayatra will conclude with a formal valedictory ceremony at Vidya P. Hanchinmani Science PU College, Nugikeri in Dharwad, on December 31 at 1 p.m.
For further details, call Ph: 7760222262 or 8217878059.

title: Two men killed as unauthorised well caves in at Kil Kotagiri in Tamil Nadu
summary: Two men die after an unauthorized well collapses in Kil Kotagiri, prompting calls for a police investigation.
content:
Two men died after they were buried alive when a portion of a well, which was being illegally constructed in Honatty near Kil Kotagiri, caved in on them on Friday afternoon.
The  deceased were identified as S. Selvan, 50, from Gundada in Kotagiri, and Sathish, 45, from Honatty.
According to the police, five men were working at the site of a resort, where they were involved in the unauthorised construction of a well.
The men were reported to be involved in the construction of a 30-foot-deep well, when at around 11.30 a.m, a portion of it caved in on Selvan and Sathish, who were working inside it. The other workers, who noticed the incident, tried to rescue the two men. While they managed to retrieve one of their colleagues, he died on the way to hospital, officials said.
The Police as well as the Fire and Rescue Services personnel managed to retrieve the body of the second person, and both the bodies were sent for postmortem.
Activists have called on the police to conduct a detailed inquiry as to how the construction of a well escaped the attention of the local panchayat, and as to why construction was not stopped as the well was unauthorised. They also called for strict action against the owners of the property.

title: CM to participate in CWC meeting today, likely to seek high command’s nod for Cabinet reshuffle
summary: Karnataka CM Siddaramaiah attends CWC meeting today, seeking approval for a Cabinet reshuffle and potential new KPCC president.
content:
As uncertainties over a possible change of Chief Minister in Karnataka continued to dominate political discourse, Chief Minister Siddaramaiah reached New Delhi to participate in the Congress Working Committee (CWC) meeting on December 27.
“Yes, I am going to the CWC meeting,” the Chief Minister said in reply to a question by mediapersons in Davanagere on Friday.
Deputy Chief Minister and KPCC chief D K Shivakumar has not been invited to the CWC meeting. However, Mr. Shivakumar met AICC chief Mallikarjun Kharge at the latter’s residence in Bengaluru on Thursday and reportedly discussed the political issues.
Sources in the Congress said that the CWC meeting is unlikely to take up the leadership change issue. However, the issue could be discussed with central leaders of the party either before or after the CWC meeting.
As speculation over power-sharing for the Chief Minister’s post continued, sources maintained that the two leaders were engaged in “mind games” and seeking publicity.
While Mr. Kharge maintained that the matter should be resolved at the local level, Mr. Siddaramaiah has strongly advocated that he would continue in the post till the party high command’s blessings are with him.
Mr. Shivakumar downplayed the leadership change issue and said he would continue to be the loyal party worker.
Meanwhile, it is being speculated that the Chief Minister might place a request on appointment of a new KPCC president if he gets an “appropriate time and opportunity” to discuss the issue with Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi. Loyalists of the Chief Minister have been seeking replacement of Mr. Shivakumar from the post of the KPCC president for the past few months.
The Chief Minister is also likely to seek the party high command’s nod for the State Cabinet reshuffle, which is long overdue. Mr. Siddaramaiah has been mentioning that he will undertake a Cabinet reshuffle if the party’s central leaders clear the proposal.
Meanwhile, Congress MP for Koppal K Rajashekar Basavaraj Hitnal on Friday said Mr. Siddaramaiah would continue in the post for the full five-year term. The electorate voted for the party for the five-year term, and the Chief Minister had implemented guarantee schemes as promised in the poll manifesto, he said.
In another development in Bengaluru, supporters of Housing Minister B.Z. Zameer Ahmed have installed posters and banners in different localities mentioning his name as “upcoming DCM”.
Besides extending Christmas and New Year’s greetings, banners mentioned “upcoming DCM” Zameer Ahmed, in a move to send a message to the party high command in the wake of the pending State Cabinet reshuffle.

title: Pulse Polio drive: State exceeds target with 103% coverage
summary: Bengaluru's Pulse Polio drive achieves 103% coverage, vaccinating over 64 lakh children in a successful four-day campaign.
content:
The State has exceeded its target in the four-day Pulse Polio campaign that concluded on December 25, achieving 103% coverage of children in the age group of 0 to 5.
A total of 64,25,399 children were administered polio drops against a target of 62,40,114, according to official data. The campaign, which began on December 21, was conducted in a single round using the bivalent oral polio vaccine (bOPV).
The vaccination was carried out at booths on December 21, followed by door-to-door visits over the next three days to ensure that no child was missed. While 96% of the target group was covered during the booth-level drive, the remaining children were reached during house-to-house visits.
Under the routine immunisation programme, every child is entitled to five doses of oral polio vaccine and three doses of inactivated polio vaccine (IPV).
Kodagu district recorded the highest coverage at 121%, followed by Bengaluru Rural (112%) and Chikkamagaluru (111%). Uttara Kannada and Mandya districts reported 109% coverage each, while Udupi and Chitradurga recorded 106% each. Shivamogga reported the lowest coverage at 98%.
Minister for Health Dinesh Gundu Rao said the Health Department had systematically organised the campaign, reaching families in remote, hilly, and hard-to-access regions of the State.
He said special focus was placed on high-risk and hard-to-reach areas, including villages in forest and hilly regions, brick kilns, migrant settlements, urban slums, farmhouses, and transit points such as railway stations, metro stations, airports, and seaports.
India is a polio-free country, and sustaining that status is a collective responsibility, the Minister said.
The national campaign is being conducted as a precautionary measure to guard against the risk of importation, as polio cases continue to be reported from neighbouring countries. In 2025, Pakistan reported 51 cases and Afghanistan 10 cases of wild poliovirus.
For the campaign, the Health Department set up 33,258 booths, supported by 1,030 mobile teams and 2,096 transit teams. A total of 1,13,115 vaccinators and 7,322 supervisors were deployed.

title: Andhra Pradesh CID busts international cybercrime racket, arrests 14 persons
summary: Andhra Pradesh CID dismantles an international cybercrime racket, arresting 14 individuals and seizing multiple electronic devices.
content:
The cybercrime wing of the A.P. Crime Investigation Department (CID), in association with the Department of Telecommunications (DoT), has busted a racket involving criminals from various countries.
Acting on the directions of CID Director-General of Police Ravi Shankar Ayyanar, several teams have conducted raids in Goa, West Bengal, Telangana, Odisha, Visakhapatnam and Bihar, and arrested 14 persons, including a Vietnam national, on charges of their involvement in the racket.
The investigation officers confiscated 14 SIM boxes, 1,496 SIM cards, eight routers, seven cameras, 22 cellphones, and other electronic gadgets, Adhiraj Singh Rana, CID (Cybercrime) Superintendent of Police, told newsmen at the CID headquarters in Mangalagiri on Friday.
The accused were collecting SIM cards using fake fingerprints, e-KYC, ID cards, and other documents, and  using them for committing various crimes, he said.
DoT Deputy Director General Hemanth Rathwae, while explaining the modus operandi of the accused, appealed to the people to be cautious while submitting details to the telecom operators. He also appealed to the public to cooperate with the Telecom Department and the police in preventing frauds.
CID Deputy SP B. Ravi Kiran said cyber offenders from Cambodia, Vietnam, Mayanmar, Malaysia, Thailand and other countries were involved in the racket. The accused caused a loss of about ₹20 crore in the State, he said.
“The accused were routing international calls as local calls by using SIM boxes imported from China and resorting to digital and other frauds,” Mr. Ravi Kiran said.
“The CID will conduct more raids in the neighbouring States soon,” the investigation officers said.
Mr. Ravi Shankar appreciated the officers for unearthing the international racket.

title: Bengali actor Parno Mittra joins Trinamool ahead of 2026 Assembly elections
summary: Bengali actor Parno Mittra joins Trinamool Congress, citing a need for course correction before the 2026 Assembly polls.
content:
Bengali film actor and former Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) leader Parno Mittra joined the Trinamool Congress on Friday (December 26, 2025), ahead of the West Bengal Legislative Assembly elections scheduled for 2026.
Ms. Mittra, who had joined the BJP in 2019, had contested the 2021 Assembly elections from the Baranagar constituency. She lost the seat to then Trinamool candidate Tapas Roy, who later switched to the BJP in 2024.
“I joined the BJP six years ago. People often make mistakes, but I feel the time has come to rectify mistakes. That is why I am joining Trinamool today,” she said.
Ms. Mittra added that her political journey with the BJP did not progress in the manner she had envisaged.

title: Hiriyur bus fire once again raises concern about safety of sleeper coaches
summary: Recent bus fire tragedy in Hiriyur highlights urgent safety concerns for sleeper coaches, prompting calls for stricter regulations and checks.
content:
The deadly fire triggered by an accident on NH 48 near Hiriyur in the early hours of December 25 has once again brought the spotlight firmly on the safety of sleeper buses.
Seven people were killed after a container truck rammed into the Gokarna-bound bus from Bengaluru, triggering a fire that rapidly engulfed the vehicle and left passengers with little time to escape.
The tragedy has once again caused concerns that have surfaced repeatedly after similar accidents in recent years, particularly those involving fire. In October, a Bengaluru-bound private sleeper bus caught fire following an accident in Kurnool district of Andhra Pradesh, claiming 19 lives. The scale of fatalities in such incidents has underlined the unique risks posed by sleeper coaches, where passengers are often lying down in confined spaces and evacuation can be slow and chaotic.
Industry representatives acknowledge that sleeper buses, while popular, come with inherent safety challenges. Speaking toThe Hindu, Nataraj Sharma, president of the Karnataka Private Bus Owners’ Association, said, “Sleeper buses are relatively uncommon globally and are used extensively only in India.”
“They are in demand because they combine overnight travel with the comfort of sleeping berths, especially on long routes. But from a design perspective, these buses are unscientific. The aisles are narrow and movement is restricted, which makes them unsafe during emergencies,” he said.
Mr. Sharma noted that existing body-building norms mandate a minimum of four emergency exits, two at the front, one at the rear and one in the middle, but added that mere compliance on paper was not enough. “Sricter enforcement of safety norms and awareness among passengers are critical. Safety has to be treated as non-negotiable,” he said.
Tracing the evolution of sleeper coaches in India, he said the concept gained momentum around the mid-1990s as highway infrastructure improved, with formal recognition coming only around 2007. Despite their popularity, he pointed out, regulatory oversight has not kept pace with their growth. Sleeper buses typically have fewer berths than seated buses but charge fares that are 30% to 50% higher, making them commercially attractive to operators and comfortable for passengers, a combination that has fuelled their rapid spread.
Speaking toThe Hindu, Transport expert M.N. Srihari said that authorities often fail to adequately scrutinise the quality of body construction and modifications carried out at private body-building workshops. “While these buses carry the branding of well-known manufacturers, the truth is that original equipment manufacturers supply only the engine and chassis. The rest of the bus is built elsewhere, and that is where serious compromises often occur,” he said.
Mr. Srihari suggested that safety could be substantially improved if emergency exit procedures were mandatorily explained to passengers before departure, similar to safety briefings on flights. “There is a need for compulsory crash testing of the entire bus assembly, not just the chassis, to ensure that sleeper coaches offer meaningful protection during accidents,” he added.
In the aftermath of the recent Kurnool accident, the Karnataka State government issued a circular mandating enhanced safety measures in passenger buses. The directions require both private and State-run operators to provide additional emergency exit doors, install more fire extinguishers and comply with other prescribed fire-safety norms.
Speaking toThe Hindu, Minister for Transport Ramalinga Reddy said that the Transport Department and the police have been conducting regular awareness programmes for bus and truck drivers, with a particular focus on the dangers of rash driving and fatigue during night-time travel. “We are also carrying out periodic checks to ensure that all categories of buses comply with mandatory safety requirements, including functional emergency exits, fire extinguishers, fire-retardant materials and properly maintained electrical systems,” he said.

title: Speed boat service launched in Kozhikode
summary: Kozhikode launches a speed boat service between the beach and Beypore to enhance adventure tourism with safety measures.
content:
Minister for Public Works and Tourism P.A. Mohamed Riyas on Friday (December 26, 2025) launched a speed boat service between Kozhikode beach and Beypore as part of the Tourism department’s coastal tourism promotion initiatives. The service will be conducted with stringent safety measures.
Speaking on the occasion, Mr. Riyas said the new boat service along the coastline would offer a novel experience for tourists. He added that boats with improved facilities would be launched soon.
Officials coordinating the project said as many as 13 persons would be able to board the speedboat at a time. Maintaining a safe speed, the boat would reach Beypore in 15 minutes, they added, noting that special packages for tourists would also be available.
District Police Chief (Kozhikode City) T. Narayanan, Kerala Tourism Infrastructure Limited chairman S.K. Sajeesh, port officer Hari Achutha Warrier, and District Tourism Promotion Council secretary T. Nikhil Das were present.

title: CM pays tribute to Dr. Manmohan Singh
summary: CM A. Revanth Reddy and leaders honor Dr. Manmohan Singh's legacy on his first death anniversary in Hyderabad.
content:
Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy along with Deputy Chief Minister Bhatti Vikramarka and other senior leaders paid floral tributes to former Prime Minister Dr. Manmohan Singh on his first death anniversary on Friday.
The tributes were offered at CM’s Jubilee Hills residence, where the leaders remembered the contributions of the former Prime Minister to the nation. The leaders recalled Dr. Manmohan Singh’s distinguished service to the country and his role in shaping India’s economic reforms, describing him as a statesman who worked tirelessly for national development.
CM’s Advisor Vem Narender Reddy, Legislative Council Chief Whip Patnam Mahender Reddy and Nalgonda Member of Parliament Raghuveer Reddy were among those present.

title: Muslims, Christians give traditional cremation to Hindu woman in Belagavi
summary: Muslims and Christians unite to honor a Hindu woman's final rites in Belagavi, showcasing interfaith compassion and community support.
content:
Members of a Muslim family, along with a Christian social worker, cremated a 70-year-old Hindu woman who was living alone, in Belagavi on Thursday.
Shantabai Krishna Jagade was living in a rented house owned by Mohammad Gade of Gandhi Nagar in Belagavi. She lived there for over 20 years and the Gade family treated her like a member of their family.
She fell ill a week ago and the landlord’s family admitted her to hospital and attended to her. But she passed away on Thursday. Her far relatives who lived in another town were informed. They could not travel to Belagavi for the final rites.
The Gade family contacted social worker Iqbal Jakati. He, in turn, informed Mayor Vijay More, a methodist Christian. The duo completed the formalities in the hospital and received the body.
Members of the Gade family, Mr. Jakati, Vijay More and his son Allan More sought the help of their friends and organised the cremation in the Sadashiv Nagar mortuary as per Hindu traditions.

title: Karkala’s Yaksha Rangayana to perform three plays in Bengaluru
summary: Yaksha Rangayana from Karkala will stage three plays in Bengaluru from December 27 to 29, showcasing regional cultural richness.
content:
The artistes of Yaksha Rangayana, based in Karkala, will bring three productions to Bengaluru, to be staged from December 27 to December 29.
The repertory theatre will perform Dr. Shivarama Karanth’s Somiya Soubhagya, a musical directed by Ganesh Mandarti, at Suchitra Cinema and Cultural Academy, on December 27 at 7 p.m.
The other two plays are Mahatmara Baravigaagi, a Kannada adaptation of R.K. Narayan’s ‘Waiting for Mahatma’, directed by Srikanth N.V., and Egyptian playwright Tawfiq al-Hakim’s Gulaamana Swatantrya Yatre, directed by B.R. Venkataramana Aithal.
Both plays will be staged on December 28 and December 29, respectively, at Kasturi Ba Aptha Rangamandira at 7 p.m.
The Yaksha Rangayana, established in Karkala in March 2022, is among the six branches of Rangayana in Karnataka, set up with the aim of nurturing the State’s diverse regional languages, dialects and nuances.
The repertory envisions building a modern theatre using the myths, stories and poems of Yakshagana, while also spreading the cultural richness of coastal Karnataka.

title: CPI plans massive centenary public meeting at Khammam on January 18
summary: CPI announces a major centenary public meeting in Khammam on January 18, aiming for five lakh attendees to showcase its relevance.
content:
The Communist Party of India (CPI) will organise a massive public meeting at Khammam on January 18 as part of its centenary celebrations, aiming to demonstrate that communism cannot be eliminated, CPI State Secretary and MLA Kunamneni Sambasiva Rao said on Friday.
Addressing the media at the CPI State office, he said the public meeting would be organised with five lakh people on an unprecedented scale to counter claims that communists no longer exist.
He announced that Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy would be invited to the meeting to convey a message of communal harmony. Leaders of national Left parties and representatives from 40 countries would also be invited to participate in the centenary celebrations. A conference of national Left party leaders would be held in Khammam on January 19.
The centenary celebrations of the Communist Party of India (CPI) were held with grandeur in Hyderabad, highlighting the party’s hundred-year-long ideological and political journey.
The event, jointly organised by the Telangana Martyrs Memorial Trust and Telangana Arasam, brought together families of freedom fighters, progressive writers, artists and intellectuals.
Former High Court judge Justice B. Chandrakumar criticised the ruling establishment, alleging that exploiters were being projected as patriots, while those protecting national resources through sacrifice were being branded as enemies. He was addressing the gathering at Ravi Narayana Reddy Auditorium.
CPI National Secretary Palla Venkat Reddy recalled the CPI’s historic role in the freedom movement and the Telangana armed peasant struggle against the Nizam’s autocratic rule, stating that the party had liberated nearly 3,500 villages through mass resistance.
Former MLA and Telangana Martyrs Memorial Trust president Chada Venkat Reddy. Two books, ‘ShathaAruna Geethanjali’, a compilation of 100 songs edited by S.V. Satyanarayana and Kandimalla Bharathi, and ‘Hundred Years of CPI – Milestones in History’ were formally released. Kandimalla Pratap Reddy presided.

title: Two pilgrims collapse, die on the way to Sabarimala
summary: Two pilgrims collapse and die on the trek to Sabarimala, highlighting the challenges faced along the popular forest path.
content:
Two Sabarimala pilgrims collapsed and died on the Sathram-Pullumedu forest path while on the way to the Sannidhanam on Friday. The deceased have been identified as  Balaji, 43, from Karur in Tamil Nadu and  Kumbakonam resident Rajkumar, 52.
According to Azhutha Range officer D. Benny, the two devotees arrived with two separate group of devotees from Tamil Nadu. While trekking through the forest path, they collapsed and died. One person collapsed near Seethkkulam, and another pilgrim collapsed near Pullumedu. The bodies were shifted for post-mortem examination.
On November 20, a pilgrim from Hyderabad had collapsed and died near the Sathram-Sannidhanam path.
Meanwhile, this year the traditional forest path witnessed a heavy rush of pilgrims. Till December 26, a total of 1,27,311 pilgrims trekked through the Sathram forest path to the Sannidhanam.

title: KGMOA  protests against change CHC timings
summary: KGMOA protests government order extending CHC timings, citing insufficient resources and potential impact on patient care quality.
content:
Government doctors have taken exception to an order issued by the government “unilaterally”  extending the outpatient clinic timings in Community Health Centres (CHCs) in the State from 9 a.m till 6 p.m. The current timings of the OP clinics in the CHCs are from 9 a.m. till 2 p.m.
Expressing its strong protest, the Kerala Government Medical Officers’ Association (KGMOA) said that the government’s move to extend the timings without ensuring adequate human resources in healthcare institutions would impose a huge burden on clinicians and seriously affect the quality of care rendered to patients.
The order issued by the government on December 20 says that those CHCs which have a minimum of three doctors should ensure that the OP clinics function from 9 a.m. till 6 p.m.
It further said that CHCs which are currently rendering in-patient care  and those CHCs which are currently functioning till 6 p.m, should continue to maintain the current timings.
The KGMOA pointed out that the work conditions as well as responsibilities of CHCs are quite different from that of Family Health Centres. The government has neither been following its  own orders regarding the basic human resources requirements in these institutions nor has it created a single additional post for CHCs, it said.
Of the three doctors in a CHC, the civil surgeon, who is the charge officer, usually has his hands full with administrative work as well as the implementation of various national and State health initiatives. This leaves the other two doctors to handle the OP clinics till 6 p.m., taking turns. This would burden the doctors who have to manage  250-300 patients.
“There are GOs issued earlier, which says that a CHC should have one civil surgeon and four assistant surgeons and that a CHC running in-patient clinics round the clock  should have seven doctors, apart from the charge officer. But most CHCs are barely managing with temporary hands. Doctors are forced to work without availing offs or casual leaves or holidays because people get agitated if at all the doctor is not available,” a government doctor said.
“In one of the FHCs in Chirayinkeezhu, there are just two doctors. The lone lab technician and one of the doctors have been put on Sabarimala duty, which means that the other doctor has to manage the OP clinic alone on all days, unable to take even a casual leave if required. This is a human rights violation,” he added.
“Without at least four doctors, OP clinics in CHCs cannot be run till 6 p.m. It is not physically possible to give the best of care to patients unless adequate human resources are in place. It will lead to unnecessary tension and patient dissatisfaction in CHCs,” said Jobin Joseph, KGMOA general secretary.
The government should withdraw its impractical decisions or provide adequate personnel in healthcare institutions. Any attempt to overburden doctors who are already under severe stress would be resisted, the KGMOA said.

title: Suspended SVU professor found dead in car near Alipiri
summary: Suspended SVU professor V. Sardar Guguloth found dead in car near Alipiri, prompting police investigation into his death.
content:
The Tirupati (West) police on Friday found the body of V. Sardar Guguloth, a suspended professor of Sri Venkateswara University, inside his car parked near Alipiri here.
As the body was in a highly decomposed state, the police suspect that he had died at least three days earlier. Mr. Guguloth was suspended about three months ago on disciplinary grounds for allegedly remaining irregular to classes after becoming addicted to alcohol.
Local residents noticed a foul smell emanating from the parked vehicle and alerted the police, who force-opened the car and recovered the body.
He is survived by his wife Meenabai, a school assistant in Chittoor, and two daughters.

title: Sindhu Anil elected chairperson of Pathanamthitta
summary: A. Sageer of the IUML was elected vice-chairperson
content:
Congress councillor Sindhu Anil of the United Democratic Front (UDF) was elected chairperson of the Pathanamthitta municipality on Friday. A. Sageer of the Indian Union Muslim League (IUML) was elected vice-chairperson.
The 33-member municipal council comprises 17 UDF councillors, 13 from the Left Democratic Front (LDF), and one member each from the Bharatiya Janata Party and Social Democratic Party of India, besides an Independent councillor. Ms. Anil, who represents ward 27, will serve a two-year term as chairperson in line with a decision of the UDF district committee.
In the Adoor municipality, Congress councillor Reena Samuel was elected chairperson and D. Sashikumar of the Congress as vice-chairperson. Ms. Samuel represents ward 3 and Mr. Sashikumar, councillor from ward 12, is serving his fourth term.
In Thiruvalla, S. Lekha of the Kerala Congress was elected chairperson of the municipality and Congress leader K. V. Varghese as vice-chairperson. Ms. Lekha represents ward 21, while Mr. Varghese, a former municipal chairperson, represents ward 10.
Meanwhile, in Pandalam municipality, LDF candidate M.R. Krishnakumari of the CPI(M) was elected chairperson and K. Manikuttan of the CPI was chosen as vice-chairperson.

title: Congress alleges ₹112 crore kickback benefited former Prasar Bharati chief Navneet Kumar Sehgal
summary: Congress accuses former Prasar Bharati chief Navneet Kumar Sehgal of a ₹112-crore kickback scheme, questioning PM Modi's silence.
content:
Citing a recent media report and confidential 254-page document of the Directorate of Income Tax (Investigation), the Congress alleged that former Prasar Bharati chief Navneet Kumar Sehgalwas the biggest beneficiary of a kickback network that siphoned off nearly ₹112 crore from Uttar Pradesh government schemes between 2019–20 and 2021–22. The party also questioned Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s silence on the matter.
Mr. Sehgal resigned as Chairman of Prasar Bharati on December 2, with a year still remaining in his tenure. According to a report published by news portalNewslaundry, based on the confidential Income Tax document, Mr. Sehgal was identified as the largest alleged beneficiary of the kickback network.
Senior Congress leader Pawan Khera, who heads the party’s Media and Publicity Department, said in a statement that despite these “serious allegations, there is no publicly known criminal prosecution or departmental action following the sharing of the findings”. He pointed out that the Income Tax Department closed the case after accepting Mr. Sehgal’s explanation. Subsequently, he was appointed Chairman of Prasar Bharati in March 2024. Mr. Khera also addressed a press conference on the issue at Congress headquarters in Delhi.
While the official reason for Mr. Sehgal’s resignation was not known, Mr. Khera said, “Speculation is rife that his resignation is linked to his past association with Hiren Joshi and the betting app controversy.” Mr. Joshi currently serves as Officer on Special Duty (OSD) for Communications and Information Technology at the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO). Mr. Khera further claimed that “reports now suggest Hiren Joshi is being replaced” by Mr. Sehgal, a 1988-batch IAS officer from Uttar Pradesh.
He questioned Mr. Modi’s silence on the issue. “What other rackets are operating in the PMO, and who is accountable? If officials linked to betting app scams can function at the heart of the PMO, what does this say about PM Modi?” he asked, but did not elaborate on his charge regarding “betting app scams”.
Mr. Khera also raised questions about the “current status” of Mr. Joshi, asking whether he had “been formally removed, suspended, or placed under investigation? Is PM Modi personally shielding him from scrutiny?”
He accused Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath of shielding Mr. Sehgal, claiming the State government failed to act even after the Income Tax Department shared its findings.
“Is this not an outright whitewashing of corruption, even as PM Modi continues to chant ‘na khaunga, na khane dunga’? [I will not take bribes, nor will I let others take bribes] Is it not the truth that the double-engine government has deliberately avoided action because it too had dipped its hands into the loot siphoned off from schemes meant for artisans and small workers?” Mr. Khera said.

title: A.K. Hafeez assumes office as first UDF Mayor of Kollam
summary: A.K. Hafeez becomes Kollam's first UDF Mayor, marking a significant political shift after 25 years of LDF governance.
content:
Marking a watershed moment in the city’s political history, the Kollam Corporation entered a new era on Friday as Congress councillor A.K. Hafeez assumed office as the first-ever Mayor from the United Democratic Front (UDF). The transition signifies the end of a quarter-century of uninterrupted governance by the Left Democratic Front (LDF) and a major realignment in the region’s political landscape.
The mayoral election commenced on Friday morning at the Corporation council hall, presided over by District Collector and returning officer N. Devidas.
Mr. Hafeez, representing the Thamarakkulam division, emerged victorious with 27 votes, comfortably defeating LDF candidate P.J. Rajendran, who secured 16 votes. Immediately following the formal declaration of the results, Mr. Devidas administered the oath of office to Mr. Hafeez, officially marking the start of his term as Mayor.
During the afternoon session, the council elected Udaya Sukumaran of the Tangassery division as the Deputy Mayor. Mirroring the mayoral results, she secured 27 of the 56 votes polled. In a ceremony symbolising the commencement of the new administration, Mr. Hafeez administered the oath of office to his deputy.
Her appointment followed a series of intense deliberations within the UDF coalition. Although alliance partners had initially championed candidates such as Shaima (RSP) and Majida Wahab (IUML), the deadlock was resolved through a phased power-sharing agreement. Under this arrangement, Ms. Sukumaran, a veteran Congress councillor, will hold the office for the first three years, after which the position will be transferred to coalition partners for the remaining two years of the five-year term.
In the 2025 local body elections, the UDF had secured a historic landslide victory in a territory long regarded as an impregnable LDF fortress. By capturing 27 of the 56 divisions, the coalition achieved a remarkable reversal of fortune, a stark contrast to its underwhelming performance in the 2020 polls.
The new Mayor steps into his role with a proven track record in local governance. A seasoned political figure, he had previously served as the Leader of the Opposition in the council from 2015 to 2020 and at present leads the Indian National Trade Union Congress as its district president.

title: Government is giving health sector top priority, says Minister
summary: Minister B.C. Janardhan Reddy prioritizes health, inaugurating a ₹5.33 crore Community Health Centre to benefit local villagers.
content:
Minister for Roads and Buildings B.C. Janardhan Reddy on Friday (26 December, 2025) said that the State government is giving top priority to health sector and is ensuring medical services under expert doctors in government hospitals on par with private hospitals.
Mr. Janardhan Reddy, along with Minister for Minorities Welfare N. Md. Farooq and District Collector Rajakumari Ganiya, inaugurated the Community Health Centre, constructed at a cost of ₹5.33 crore from NABARD funds, at Yaluru village in Gospadu mandal on Friday. Speaking on the occasion, he said that the State has called tenders for ₹150 crore- ₹160 crore to construct health clinics in Nandyal district alone.
Mr. Janardhan Reddy said that the previous government had only laid foundation stones for hospitals but is claiming that it had constructed them. It had also failed to provide better infrastrucute facilities at the hospitals, he added.
He said that the 30-bedded hospital at Yaluru will benefit the people of nearby villages as they were forced to visit the government hospital at Nandyal for their medical needs.
Earlier, Mr. Janardhan Reddy conducted a brief tour of Banganapalle, where he visited the old MRO office which is under renovation. He also made a surprise visit to the godown used to store PDS stocks and inspected the quality. He also participated in the unveiling of NTR statue at Yaluru village along with Mr. Farooq.

title: CM Stalin inaugurates new projects worth ₹1,773.67 crore
summary: CM Stalin inaugurates ₹1,773.67 crore in projects, including 2,525 completed initiatives and new developments in Kallakurichi district.
content:
Chief Minister M.K. Stalin on Friday inaugurated infrastructure projects and laid foundation stone for new schemes amounting to ₹1,773.67 crore in Kallakurichi district.
He inaugurated a total of 2,525 completed projects and laid the foundation stone for 62 new ones worth ₹386.48 crore.
The notable projects among those completed include the Integrated Collectorate complex in Kallakurichi. He also distributed welfare assistance to the tune of ₹1,045 crore to 2.16 lakh beneficiaries.
The Chief Minister also announced the creation of a new block with Vanapuram as its Headquarters and construction of new buildings for the Government Arts and Science College at Ulundurpet at ₹18 crore.
He also announced the creation of a new SIPCOT industrial estate at an estimated cost of ₹10 crore in Ulundurpet and construction of Combined Court Buildings and quarters in Kallakurichi costing ₹120 crore.
Ministers E.V. Velu, Anbil Mahesh Poyyamozhi, C.V. Ganesan and Collector M.S. Prasanth were present.

title: Kolusu holds Praja Darbar, directs officials to resolve grievances
summary: Minister Parthasarathy conducts Praja Darbar, urging officials to promptly address public grievances and ensure timely resolutions.
content:
State Minister for Housing and Information and Public Relations Kolusu Parthasarathy held a Praja Darbar at his office in Nuzvid on Friday, drawing an encouraging response from the public. The Minister received 16 petitions from people belonging to different mandals of the constituency.
Some grievances were resolved on the spot after the Minister issued immediate instructions to the officials concerned, while directions were given to address the remaining petitions within a stipulated time.
Addressing the gathering, Mr. Parthasarathy said every petition received at the Praja Darbar should be examined thoroughly and resolved without delay. He noted that people from four mandals of the constituency attend the weekly programme with the hope of redressal of their problems.
The Minister instructed officials to treat the petitions seriously and, wherever necessary, conduct field-level inquiries to resolve the issues. He warned that any delay or negligence in addressing public grievances would invite strict action against the officials concerned. He said timely resolution of petitions would improve public satisfaction and gradually reduce the number of grievances.
Officials from various departments, public representatives, coalition leaders and villagers from different places participated in the Praja Darbar.

title: Rajasthan CM hits back at Gehlot over Aravalli remarks, says no tampering will be allowed
summary: Rajasthan CM Bhajanlal Sharma defends Aravalli integrity against Gehlot's remarks, asserting commitment to protecting the ecologically sensitive region.
content:
Rajasthan Chief Minister Bhajanlal Sharma on Friday (December 26, 2025) hit back at Congress leader Ashok Gehlot over his statements on theAravalli mountain range, asserting that his government will not allow any tampering with the ecologically sensitive region.
Mr. Sharma alleged that it was during Congress regimes that extensive mining activity took place in the Aravalli area and questioned who had altered the definition of the mountain range in 2002-03 and 2009-10.
"Who changed the definition of Aravallis and how many mining leases were issued in the region during those years?" the Chief Minister asked, accusing the Congress of spreading misinformation.
How is the Aravalli range to be protected? | Explained
Mr. Sharma said, "Our government is committed to protecting the Aravalli range and no kind of tampering will be allowed in the region." He claimed that during the Congress rule, even stone and sand mining was allowed in the Aravalli region, and said Mr. Gehlot was "only creating noise and spreading rumours".
Mr. Sharma also accused Congress leaders of misleading the public on several issues, including the Citizenship Amendment Act (CAA).
"When we brought the CAA, they created panic by spreading rumours, but our government implemented it and also gave land titles to displaced people," he said.
Referring to Congress' criticism over issues such as electoral processes and citizenship verification, Mr. Sharma said his government would not allow illegal immigrants to stay in the State.
Taking a swipe at Ashok Gehlot, Mr. Sharma said the former Chief Minister was trying to remain relevant through social media posts, adding that accountability would be ensured.
Citing Prime Minister Narendra Modi's statement of "Na Khauga-Na Khane Dunga", Mr. Sharma said anyone found guilty of corruption will have to return what he has taken.

title: Congress’s Molly Jacob elected Alappuzha municipal chairperson
summary: Independent councillor Jose Chellappan elected vice-chairperson of the civic body
content:
Molly Jacob of the Congress was sworn in as the chairperson of the Alappuzha municipality on Friday. Independent councillor Jose Chellappan, representing the Mangalam ward, was elected vice-chairperson of the civic body.
The Congress-led United Democratic Front (UDF), which emerged as the single largest bloc with 23 seats in elections to the municipality held earlier this month, got the support of Mr. Chellappan in the election to the chairperson post.
In the first round of voting to the chairperson post, Ms. Jacob, elected from the Beach ward, secured 24 votes in the 53-member council. Her rivals, Left Democratic Front (LDF) candidate K.K. Jayamma of the Communist Party of India (Marxist) [CPI(M)] and National Democratic Alliance (NDA) candidate Prema Udayakumar of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), bagged 23 and five votes respectively.
The top two candidates fought it out in the second round, in which the NDA councillors stayed out. Ms. Jacob defeated Jayamma by a slender margin of one vote (24-23). In both rounds, councillor S. Faizal of the People’s Democratic Party voted for the LDF candidate, while the lone councillor of the Social Democratic Party of India (SDPI) abstained from voting.
Mr. Chellappan was elected vice-chairperson of the Alappuzha municipality with the support of the UDF councillors. He polled 24 votes.
Besides Alappuzha municipality, elections to the posts of chairperson and vice-chairperson were held in other civic bodies in the district on the day. Lalitha Raveendranath of the Congress was sworn in as the chairperson of the Mavelikara municipality, while K. Gopan of the Congress was elected vice-chairperson there.
Manish Keezhamadathil of the Congress was elected chairperson of the Chengannur municipality. Sally James of the Congress is the new vice-chairperson.
In the Cherthala municipality, S. Sobin of the CPI(M) was sworn in as chairperson and N.L. Valsala Kumari of the Communist Party of India (CPI) was elected vice-chairperson.
Vrinda S. Kumar of the Congress was elected chairperson of the Haripad municipality. M.B. Anil Mithra of the Congress is the new vice-chairperson of the civic body.
In Kayamkulam municipality, Sarath Lal Bellari of the Indian Union Muslim League (IUML) was sworn in as the chairperson and Ambika of the Congress was elected vice-chairperson.

title: Venkatagiri residents push to rejoin Nellore district amid reorganisation concerns
summary: Venkatagiri residents advocate for rejoining Nellore district, citing administrative convenience and public sentiment during reorganisation concerns.
content:
Minister for Endowments Anam Ramanarayana Reddy, who previously represented Venkatagiri constituency, urged the State government on Friday (26 December, 2025) to retain Rapur, Kaluvoy and Saidapuram mandals in Nellore district, citing administrative convenience and the need to respect public sentiment.
On the final day of submitting objections to the proposed reorganisation exercise, Mr. Reddy received representations from the residents of the three mandals, who cited proximity to Nellore as the reason. Mr. Ramanarayana Reddy not only wanted the mandals to be merged in Nellore district, but also wanted their inclusion in Atmakur revenue division for easy administration.
It may be noted that after the Venkatagiri, Sullurpet, and Gudur constituencies of Sri Potti Sri Ramulu (SPSR) Nellore district were appended to the adjoining Tirupati district during the District Reorganisation Exercise in 2021, parts of Gudur and Venkatagiri openly expressed their willingness to remain with Nellore district.
Even as Gudur is witnessing the slogans “Tirupati Vaddhu, Nellore Muddu,” parts of the Venkatagiri constituency have also expressed their opinions recently.
Meanwhile, the Minister felicitated MLC Beeda Ravichandra on his election as the TDP’s Nellore district president and also congratulated district general secretary Chejerla Venkateswara Reddy and Nellore Mayor Roop Kumar Yadav.

title: Rural development suffered a setback during YSRCP’s tenure, alleges TDP MLC
summary: TDP MLC Alapati Rajendra Prasad criticizes YSRCP for rural development setbacks and fund mismanagement during their tenure in Andhra Pradesh.
content:
Telugu Desam Party (TDP) MLC Alapati Rajendra Prasad on Friday alleged that rural development in Andhra Pradesh suffered a severe setback during the tenure of the YSR Congress Party (YSRCP).
“It is an irony that the YSRCP leaders are talking about village welfare after destroying the Panchayat Raj system in the State during their five-year tenure,” Mr. Rajendra Prasad told the media at the TDP central office.
He accused former Chief Minister Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy of diverting funds meant for village development, weakening constitutionally elected sarpanches, and running a parallel system through volunteers.
He alleged large-scale irregularities in schemes such as MGNREGS and Jal Jeevan Mission, claiming that thousands of crores of rupees were misused, while villages were left without basic infrastructure.
The MLC alleged that farmers suffered immensely during the previous regime, citing rising farmer suicides, procurement issues, and the controversial land titling system. He said public anger over these policies resulted in the YSRCP winning just 11 Assembly seats in the 2024 elections.
Highlighting the coalition government’s initiatives, Mr. Rajendra Prasad said pending dues of ₹1,674 crore of panchayats were cleared within a month of assuming office.
“The government is reviving villages through ‘Palle Panduga’ programme, constructing roads, water tanks, and farm ponds, and releasing Finance Commission funds to restore true village self-governance,” he added.

title: Thar Desert could expand up to Delhi, warns Sachin Pilot over threat to Aravalli hills
summary: Sachin Pilot warns that redefining Aravalli hills could threaten ecology, expanding the Thar Desert towards Delhi.
content:
Senior Congress leader Sachin Pilot on Friday (December 26, 2025) warned that the Centre’s redefinition of theAravalli hillscould strip away protection from nearly 90% of the range, posing grave ecological risks, including expansion of the Thar Desert up to Delhi.
Mr. Pilot joined the National Students’ Union of India’s (NSUI) ‘Save Aravalli – Save the Future’ march in Jaipur, accompanied by his son who made his first appearance on a political stage. The Aravallis, Mr. Pilot stressed, act as a natural shield against air pollution, preserve groundwater, and sustain biodiversity. “If the Aravallis are destroyed, the desert could reach Delhi,” he cautioned.
Police stopped the march at the Government Hostel intersection in Jaipur citing permission limits, after which the protest concluded peacefully.
Citing Forest Survey of India (FSI) data, Mr. Pilot said the Centre’s definition would exclude most of the range. “There are 1.18 lakh hills below 100 metres and only 1,048 above 100 metres. This means nearly 90% of the Aravalli area would go outside the definition and become unprotected,” he explained.
​Green washing: On the Supreme Court, mining in the Aravallis
The Congress leader dismissed government assurances that no activity would occur without permission as “misleading” noting that similar restrictions have existed for two decades without curbing illegal mining. “Despite these bans, mining continues under the government’s nose. What steps are being taken to stop it?” he asked.
Mr. Pilot underscored the Aravallis’ role in preventing desertification and protecting ecology. “Whether it is air pollution, groundwater, or biodiversity, the Aravalli acts as a security shield,” he said, questioning the government’s intent. “Is the government helpless, under pressure, or simply lacking intent?” He criticised repeated clarifications without legal action, pointing out that the Centre has not approached the Supreme Court to resolve the definition issue.
Alleging a broader political design, Mr. Pilot accused BJP governments at the Centre and in Gujarat, Rajasthan, Haryana and Delhi of acting to “destroy the Aravalli range”. “All these governments seem to be racing to see how fast the Aravallis can be wiped out,” he said.

title: UDF secures power in all six municipalities in Kottayam
summary: UDF triumphs in Kottayam, electing Diya Binu Pulikkakandam as one of India's youngest municipal chairpersons.
content:
The Congress-led United Democratic Front (UDF) has staged a significant comeback in Kottayam district, securing power in all six municipalities.
In Pala, the Kerala Congress (M) was thrown out of power for the first time in the history of the municipality. The UDF came to power with the support of an Independent collective, which includes three members, and a Congress rebel.
Diya Binu Pulikkakandam was elected chairperson, becoming one of the youngest municipal chairpersons in India. In the 26-member council, she received 14 votes, defeating Betty Shaju of the CPI(M)-led Left Democratic Front, who garnered 12 votes. In the vice-chairperson election, Congress rebel Maya Rahul defeated Biju Paloopadavan of the LDF by the same margin.
In the Kottayam municipality, senior Congress member M.P. Santhosh Kumar was elected chairman, while Sheeba Punnan of the Congress was elected vice-chairperson. Both received 32 votes in the 53-member council. Mr. Santhosh Kumar defeated C.N. Sathyanesan of the CPI(M), who received 15 votes, and T.N. Harikumar of the BJP, who received six votes. In the vice-chairperson election, Ms. Punnan defeated Sheeja Anil of the CPI(M) and Divya Sujith of the BJP.
In Ettumanur, Tomy Kuruvila Pulimanthundam of the Congress was elected chairman with 21 votes in the 36-member council. In the vice-chairperson election held in the afternoon, Congress member Pushpakumari won by securing the same number of votes.
In Erattupetta, V.P. Nazar of the Indian Union Muslim League (IUML) and Fathima Anzar of the Congress were elected as chairman and vice-chairperson respectively. Both of them won 16 votes in the 29-member council. Mr. Nazar defeated E.A. Savad (10 votes) of the LDF and Subair Vellappally (three votes) of the SDPI, while Ms. Fathima defeated Shajitha Veliyath of the LDF and Sajmi Sihas of the SDPI.
K.G. Abdul Salam Rawthar of the Congress was elected the chairman in the Vaikom municipality. In the 27-member council, Mr. Rawthar secured 13 votes, while D. Ranjith Kumar of the LDF received nine votes. Two of the three BJP members were present but abstained from voting. One did not turn up. Two Independents also abstained from voting.
In Changanassery, Congress member Jomy Joseph was elected chairman with the support of four Independent members. In the 37-member council, Mr. Joseph, who secured 16 votes, defeated A. Nazeer of the LDF, who got nine votes and N.P. Krishnakumar of the BJP, who received eight votes. Meanwhile, K.M. Nejiya of the Congress was elected as vice-chairperson in the election held in the afternoon with the same margin.

title: Indian Railways plan to double originating train capacity in 48 major cities by 2030: Ministry
summary: Indian Railways aims to double train capacity in 48 cities by 2030 to meet growing travel demands, enhancing infrastructure.
content:
The Railway Ministry on Friday (December 26, 2025) said that to keep up with the rapid and sustained growth in travel, the capacity of major cities to originate new trains needs to be doubled in the next five years.
It added that the current infrastructure needs to be augmented so as to meet the requirements of the upcoming years.
Highlighting actions needed for doubling the originating capacity by the year 2030, it plans to augment the current terminals with additional platforms, identify and create new terminals in and around the urban area, construct maintenance facilities, including mega coaching complexes and increase the sectional capacity with traffic facility works, among others.
"While planning for increasing the capacity of terminals, stations around terminals will also be considered so that capacity is evenly balanced. For example, for Pune city, Hadapsar, Khadki and Alandi have been considered for increasing capacity along with increasing platforms and stabling lines at Pune station," the Ministry said.
It added, "The above exercise will be done for both suburban as well as non-suburban traffic, keeping in view the distinct requirements of both segments." The Ministry will submit a comprehensive plan of stations in the 48 major cities to the Planning Directorate. Some of these cities are Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, Hyderabad, Bengaluru, Patna, Pune, Mathura, Agra and Ludhiana, among others.
"The plan will include the works planned, proposed, or already sanctioned to achieve the goal of doubling the capacity of handling trains in a time-bound manner,' the Ministry said.
It added, "While the plan to double the capacity is by 2030, it is expected that capacity will be increased progressively in the next 5 years so that the benefits of capacity addition can be reaped immediately. This will help in meeting the traffic requirement progressively over the years. The plan will classify actions under three categories, i.e., immediate, short-term, and long-term." 	 Officials said that the proposed plan should be specific with clear timelines and defined outcomes.
"While the exercise is for specific stations, however, each Zonal Railway (ZR) should plan for increasing the capacity of trains running over their divisions so that not only terminal capacity is increased but also the sectional capacity and operational constraints at stations or yards are also addressed," the Ministry said.

title: Officials instructed to be alert against drug use during New Year celebrations
summary: Mysuru officials urged to prevent drug use during New Year celebrations and promote awareness about its harmful effects.
content:
Additional Superintendent of Mysuru district police Malik has instructed the officials of various departments to ensure that drugs are not used during the New Year celebrations.
Presiding over the district-level committee meeting of Narco Co-ordination Centre (NCORD) held at the Deputy Commissioner’s office in Mysuru on Friday, Mr. Malik referred to the expanding network of narcotic drugs and emphasized the need to create awareness among the public and students about the harmful effects of drug abuse.
With the New Year approaching, he instructed the officials to take necessary steps to ensure that the narcotic drugs are not used during the celebrations.
He said awareness programmes on the ill-effects of drugs should be conducted in schools and colleges. “Since, there is a higher possibility of drug use in the shops located near colleges, special attention should be paid to such areas”, he said while also stressing the need to install CCTV cameras in schools and colleges and said teachers should closely monitor ‘grey areas’ within the educational educations.
Banners carrying information on the harmful effects of drugs should be installed near schools, colleges and in public places. Officials should conduct awareness programmes for students and take steps to prevent drug use, he said.
If information about the drug trafficking or the existence of drug networks comes to light, it should be reported to the police immediately and co-ordinated investigations should be carried out in the collaboration with them.
Deputy Commissioner of Police (Traffic and Crime) N.S. Sundar Raj and district-level officials from various departments were present.

title: 473 full-service Aadhaar centres from September 2026: UIDAI CEO
summary: UIDAI plans to expand Aadhaar centres from 88 to 473 by September 2026, easing access for adult applicants across India.
content:
The Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI) will increase the number of full-fledged Aadhaar enrollment and update centres for adults to 473 from the current 88 by September 2026, UIDAI CEO Bhuvnesh Kumar toldThe Hindu.
While children can be enrolled for Aadhaar at post offices, adult enrollees have fewer places to go. Since adult applicants may have to travel past multiple districts to reach a centre, the expansion will help them, Mr. Kumar said. Such centres offer all modification and enrollment services. Some Aadhaar details can be updated online, but changes in biometrics and updating one’s name after a certain limit require visit to a centre.
Mr. Kumar said UIDAI wants to ensure that there is at least one centre in two districts.
The number of adult enrollees is likely a small percentage of Indians (the precise share cannot be calculated due to the lack of a nationwide Census since 2011), but even a small percentage could translate to lakhs of people due to India’s population. “We are working with Google and we will soon have Google locations for Aadhaar centres,” Mr. Kumar said.
Field verification
Mr. Kumar said that due to concerns of illegal immigration, Aadhaar has been issued in recent months “only after field verification” by district administrations. Most adult applicants include non-resident Indians or overseas citizens of India, the latter being foreign nationals with ties to India either by marriage or parentage. Foreign nationals who live in India are permitted to have an Aadhaar as it is not proof of citizenship.
UIDAI is working on the integrity of data by restricting changes in date of birth of Aadhaar holders. “If someone has two different dates of birth in two different documents, one is false,” Mr. Kumar said. People who had to change the date of birth once will be allowed to do so after filing an affidavit admitting a clerical mistake but doing so twice will not be allowed, he said.
Parents who falsified their children’s date of birth during Aadhaar enrollment risk criminal action, Mr. Kumar said, referring to a case in which the Allahabad High Court ordered the filing of an FIR against a parent over irregularity surrounding a child’s date of birth.

title: Kolkata Metro’s Blue Line services disrupted for about 43 minutes after girl jumps on tracks, dies
summary: Kolkata Metro's Blue Line services were briefly disrupted after a person jumped on the tracks, causing delays during peak hours.
content:
Metro services on the Blue Line (Dakshineswar to Kavi Subhash) were disrupted on Friday (December 26, 2025) evening after a 17-year-old girl jumped onto the tracks at Netaji Bhavan station, officials said.
The girl was rescued from the tracks and rushed to a nearby hospital where doctors declared her ‘brought dead’, they said.
The incident occurred around 5.17 p.m. as a southbound train was entering the station, prompting a suspension of services for around 43 minutes, Metro Railway officials said.
Earlier, police said that a man tried to jump onto the tracks.
The disruption caused significant inconvenience to commuters during the evening peak hours.
“Normal services over the entire stretch of Blue Line resumed from 6 p.m.,” the official said.

title: Kochi Mayor was chosen strictly in accordance with KPCC guidelines, says Satheesan
summary: Satheesan clarifies Kochi Mayor's selection followed KPCC guidelines, emphasizing UDF's political stance against alliances with opposition parties.
content:
Leader of the Opposition V.D. Satheesan said his involvement in the Kochi Corporation election ended with victory for the United Democratic Front, and that the Mayor was selected strictly in accordance with Kerala Pradesh Congress Committee (KPCC) guidelines.
Addressing the media here on Friday (December 26, 2025), Mr. Satheesan pointed out that even before the KPCC guidelines were made public, some media outlets had already speculated on who the Mayor would be. “How many people can you decide as mayors? Only one person can be made Mayor,” he said.
He explained that the UDF had announced mayoral candidates in advance only in Thiruvananthapuram and Kollam. In all other local bodies, the selection was based on the KPCC circular. In Thrissur too, the Mayor was chosen after seeking the opinion of councillors, and no one was imposed from above.
Mr. Satheesan further emphasised that clear instructions had been issued against any association with the BJP, CPI(M), or the SDPI. If anyone were to win with the support of these parties, they were directed to resign immediately. “This is a political decision of the UDF,” he said.

title: Seven killed, seven injured in road accidents in Andhra Pradesh
summary: Seven people died and seven others were injured in separate road accidents in Andhra Pradesh's Nandyal and Guntur districts.
content:
Seven persons were killed and seven others injured in two road accidents reported in Nandyal and Guntur districts in the early hours of Friday.
Four persons were killed in a head-on collision between a private travels bus and a SUV in Allagadda mandal of Nandyal district. Two persons suffered severe injuries in the accident.
The police said that the driver of the SUV, which was on its way to Hyderabad from Tirupati, lost control of the vehicle, veered onto the divider, and rammed into the travels bus coming in the opposite direction at Nallagatla. The bus was proceeding to Puducherry from Hyderabad.
The deceased, all occupants of the SUV, were identified as Shravan (21), Gunderao Kulkarni (46), Itikadi Narasimhulu (30), and Siddappa (50). The severely injured persons, Siddharth Kulkarni and Shiva Sai Kulkarni, who were also travelling in the SUV, were rushed to the Nandyal Government General Hospital for treatment.
The police said that the victims were residents of Nizampet in Hyderabad, and had been accompanying ‘Shiva Svamis’ for the last couple of days and cooking for them during their pilgrimage.
Allagadda DSP K. Pramod and Circle Inspector B.V. Ramana rushed to the spot and supervised the rescue operations. The bus passengers were shifted to another vehicle for their onward journey.
R&B Minister B.C. Janardhan Reddy, Agriculture Minister K. Atchannaidu and Home Minister V. Anitha expressed shock over the loss of lives, and directed the officials to provide best treatment to the injured.
Guntur district Superintendent of Police Vakul Jindal inspecting the accident spot on Friday.
In another accident, three persons were killed on the spot when a private travels bus rammed a stationary car on National Highway-16 under the limits of Nallapadu police station in Guntur district.
The police said the car was proceeding to Suryapet in Telangana from Tirupati.
“At around 5.30 a.m., when the car reached Kommineni Cold Storage, the driver stopped the vehicle on the road margin as he felt drowsy. As he stepped out of the vehicle to wash his face, a private travels bus rammed the car from behind, killing three of the eight occupants on the spot,” said Nallapadu Circle Inspector Kandepu Vamsidhar.
The deceased were identified as Kunchala Venkataiah (65), his wife Kunchala Suseela (56), and Navila Mahesh (28), all native of Suryapet district. The five other occupants of the car escaped with injuries. They were shifted to a nearby hospital.

title: UDF hands over chairperson position to IUML in Thodupuzha municipality
summary: UDF transfers chairperson role to IUML's Sabira Jaleel in Thodupuzha, amid internal Congress disputes over candidate selection.
content:
Following an internal dispute within the Congress over the selection of the municipal chairperson, the United Democratic Front (UDF) has handed over the position to the Indian Union Muslim League (IUML) in Thodupuzha.
According to sources, the decision followed a deepening tussle among the 10 Congress councillors. The Congress has 10 councillors and eight for the IUML in the municipality. On Friday, the UDF announced Sabira Jaleel of the IUML as its chairperson nominee. During the municipal election, Ms. Jaleel secured the seat with 22 votes. Her opponents Sreeja Rajesh of the Bhartiya Janata Party (BJP) and Kavitha Aji of the Left Democratic Front (LDF) received nine and six votes respectively. Two Independent councillors supported the UDF, while one Independent abstained from voting.
Under the new UDF power-sharing agreement, Ms. Jaleel will serve as the chairperson for the next two years. The Kerala Congress (Joseph) faction will then hold the post for one year, followed by a Congress councillor for the final two years.
On the election day on Friday, the rift deepened within the Congress. During its parliamentary party meeting on the same day, UDF block president Shibli Sahib announced that Litty Joseph wouldbe the future Congress chairperson in the upcoming term, andeven collected councillors’ signatures to formalise the decision. However, District Congress Committee (DCC) president C.P. Mathew objected anddirected that the minutes be corrected.
Kerala Pradesh Congress Committee (KPCC) general secretary and Congress councillor Nisha Soman, who was the party’s initial candidate for the post, stated that she would file a formal complaint with the State committee. Ms. Soman alleged that the block president was pursuing a personal agenda.
