They took three days to register the FIR and did not invoke relevant provisions of law, including Section 109 (attempt to murder) and Section 117(4) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita relating to grievous hurt by a mob on grounds such as race or caste, as well as provisions of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act,” CDFI founder Suhas Chakma said on Saturday (December 27, 2025). He added that this delay enabled the prime accused to flee.
The organisation said the killing of Anjel Chakma mirrored earlier incidents of racial violence, including the death of Nido Tania, following which the M.P. Bezbaruah Committee had recommended either a standalone law or suitable amendments to existing criminal laws to address such crimes.
“The amendments in the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, including Section 196 on promoting enmity on grounds of religion, race, place of birth or language, are inadequate to address racial discrimination and violence faced by people from the northeast,” the CDFI said.
The organisation urged the Union Home Ministry to direct the Uttarakhand government to invoke murder charges under Section 103(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, ensure the immediate arrest of the prime accused, and provide ₹1 crore as compensation to the victim’s family. It also sought the setting up of a dedicated helpline for people from the Northeast in Dehradun, similar to the Special Police Unit for North-Eastern Region in Delhi.
Earlier, Tipra Motha founder and royal scion Pradyot Kishore Manikya Debbarma had also demanded justice for Anjel Chakma and his family.

title: MVD issue notices to online firms over safety risks posed by  ‘10-minute delivery’ service
summary: MVD issues notices to online firms for unsafe ‘10-minute delivery’ services, citing risks from reckless driving and safety violations.
content:
The Motor Vehicles Department (MVD) has issued show-cause notices to online food aggregate companies in Ernakulam over concerns that their “10-minute delivery” service is violating road safety norms.
Action has been taken against firms found to have breached safety standards. It was found that due to the intense pressure from companies to deliver goods within a fixed time, delivery agents were driving at excessive speeds and recklessly. Signal violations, improper lane changes, and riding without safety gear have become common among riders, posing serious accident risks.
The intervention comes in the backdrop of reports of two-wheelers involved in such services meeting with accidents and even fatalities in different parts of the State. The notice has asked companies to explain how they can ensure that ultra-fast delivery systems do not compromise road safety, and what measures have been adopted to safeguard riders.
Interactive |Explore dark patterns in e-commerce apps
Officials observed that such business models send out the wrong message that time is more important than life. Transport Commissioner Nagaraju Chakilam warned that fast-delivery systems must be reviewed with road safety in mind, and strict action will follow if violations continue. The Ernakulam Enforcement Regional Transport Officer said that inspections related to this issue will be intensified in the coming days.

title: Defamatory post: Congress leader released from police custody
summary: Congress leader N. Subrahmanian released from police custody after interrogation over a controversial AI-generated post involving Chief Minister Vijayan.
content:
The Chevayur police on Saturday released senior Congress leader and Kerala Pradesh Congress Committee (KPCC) Political Affairs committee member N. Subrahmanian, who was taken into custody in connection with a case registered against him for sharing an AI-generated photograph depicting Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan along with Sabarimala gold theft suspect Unnikrishnan Potti.
Mr. Subrahmanian, who was kept in police custody a few hours after medical check-upfor interrogation, was allowed to go after recording his statement on the incident. He was also served notice to turn up for interrogation again on December 29.
The Congress leader alleged that the police came up with the “surprising action” based on the instruction from an unknown senior police officer. He claimed that the Left Democratic Front (LDF) was showing its intolerance in different forms following the huge setback it faced in the recent local body elections across the State.
Expressing protest against the police action, a group of Congress workers came in support of Mr. Sbubrahmanian and camped in front of the Chevayur police station. They also sang a ‘controversial’  song alleging that the police were acting in favour of the LDF government.
In a statement issued here on Saturday, KPCC president Sunny Joseph said the police action against the senior Congress leader was challenging the democratic rights of citizens and meant to hamper their fundamental right to expression. He also claimed that the Sabarimala gold theft and related developments were very much haunting the Pinarayi Vijayan government.
Speaking to reporters at his office in North Paravur on Saturday, Leader of the Opposition V. D. Satheesan accused Mr. Vijayan of increasingly behaving like an autocrat and becoming a disgrace to the State.
Mr. Satheesan said the Chief Minister cannot intimidate Congress and UDF leaders into submission through what he described as autocratic acts. “We will ask all our leaders to post the picture showing the Chief Minister with Potti. Let him arrest all of us,” he declared.
The First Information Report related to the defamatory Facebook post was registered on Friday  based on a complaint that the content was intended to provoke conflict and promote enmity between different groups. Accordingly, Mr. Subramanian had been booked under Sections 192 (wantonly giving provocation with intent to cause riot) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and Section 120 of the Kerala Police Act.

title: Lights, flowers add zing to year-end festivity in Thiruvananthapuram
summary: Experience the enchanting blend of lights and flowers at Thiruvananthapuram's Vasantholsavam, running until January 4.
content:
The light festival at the ongoing Vasantholsavam on the Kanakakkunnu Palace grounds in the city has been drawing visitors in hordes, offering an immersive experience by its scale and grandeur. The festival of flower and lights, organised by the State Tourism department in association with the district Tourism Promotion Council (DTPC), was opened on December 24, elevating the Christmas and New Year vibe.
Besides seamlessly blending with the stunning range of flowers on display at the show, the lighting spectacle has many surprises for the visitors. Greeting the guests at the entrance is a giant snow sleigh and arch, striking an instant resonance with holidayers. The installation features an archway comprising six reindeer, each standing to a height of 12 to 15 feet, leading up to a sleigh positioned on a top deck, together rising to 50 to 60 feet from the ground level.
Visitors are then taken through a tunnel of lights, an illuminated pathway providing a unique walkthrough experience. Another widely appreciated experience is an electric forest, a high-tech lighting zone featuring a lit-up forest. Taking the guests through a futuristic experience is the space tunnel, a cosmic-themed light corridor. Then comes ‘The Tunnel of Shades’, an installation intermingled with light and shadow, creating a range of visual patterns.
Located at the main lawns of the verdant palace grounds is the crystal forest, an installation featuring trees wrapped in contrasting pink and blue lights. An interactive installation called ‘Light Amaze’ where visitors can navigate through a glowing labyrinth, a windmill called ‘The World of Reflections’, a spectacle called ‘Mirror Garden’ using reflective surfaces to multiply the impact of the lighting designs and the ‘Garden of Infinity’ giving the illusion of an endless field of light are other the attractions on the sprawling compound.
More surprises are in store, including Kaleido-House, a structure inspired by kaleidoscopes, offering shifting patterns and colours to those inside. The show also has a set of thematic zones such as the ‘Scandinavian Christmas’. It features an igloo, allowing visitors to experience a realistic “snow world” in the heart of the capital city.
The ‘China Town’ is designed as a culturally themed zone featuring “The Giant Red Dragon” and the ‘Pathway of the Lanterns’. The ‘Flaming Grounds’, meanwhile, is a high-intensity lighting installation mimicking the movement and glow of fire. There are also walkways and interactive areas, two distinct pathways featuring unique lighting styles to guide visitors through the different event zones. Vasantholsavam and the light festival will conclude on January 4.

title: UAS Raichur to host 3-day international conference from December 29
summary: Join UAS Raichur for a three-day international conference on sustainable innovations in agriculture from December 29 to 31.
content:
The University of Agriculture Science (UAS), Raichur, and National Agricultural Development Cooperative Ltd. (NADCL), Baramulla, Jammu and Kashmir, are jointly organising a three-day international conference on “Sustainable Innovations in Agriculture, Veterinary, and Allied Sciences” (both online and offline) at  the University of Agricultural Sciences, Raichur, from December 29 to 31.
Jagruti B. Deshmanya, conference organising chairman and administrative officer, UAS, Raichur, said on Saturday that the contribution of agriculture and allied sectors was essential in achieving this vision, and to complement this goal, the current International Conference aims to analyse the quality, scale of adoption, and overall impact of sustainable innovations in agriculture and allied technologies at the State, national, and international levels.
More than 500 participants, including technologists, research scholars, academic and agro-industry representatives, policymakers, and students from different States of the country, are expected to participate in the conference. In addition, the participants from Kuwait and other countries are expected.
The conference will witness oral and poster presentations under the thematic areas of agriculture, veterinary, and allied sciences and will be inaugurated by C. H. Srinivasa Rao, director, Indian Agricultural Research Institute, New Delhi, and M. Hanumanthappa, Vice-Chancellor, University of Agricultural Sciences, Raichur, will preside over the inaugural session.

title: Karnataka saw a steady flow of  investments in calendar year 2025
summary: Karnataka attracted ₹10.27 lakh crore in investments in 2025, fostering growth and job creation across diverse sectors.
content:
In 2025, Karnataka has attracted investment of ₹10.27 lakh crore through its biannual investment exposition, Global Investors’ Meet (GIM), held in February.
M.B. Patil, Minister for Large and Medium Industries, said that over 60% of these investments have been realised in the 2025 calendar year, while 2026 and 2027 would witness a flurry of activities as these projects would begin to take physical shape on the ground across the State.
According to him, over 70% of these investments would go to “Beyond Bangalore” with north Karnataka capturing some 45%. The incentive structure, under the new Karnataka Industrial Policy, promoted investments Beyond Bengaluru by offering capital subsidies of up to 30% and enhanced PLI (production linked incentive) support in these regions, Mr. Patil said.
Mr. Patil said, over and above GIM commitments, an additional investment of ₹30,000 crore came from electronics, aerospace, and manufacturing spaces.
These investments were led by Vayu Assets (for HDI PCB manufacturing), ASM Technologies (ESDM manufacturing and precision engineering), Silfex India Manufacturing, a Lam Research subsidiary (Capital equipment for semiconductor manufacturing for Auto/EV), River (2W EV manufacturing facility), and Volvo (expansion of truck and bus production facility). In the aerospace and defence sector, IndiGo announced investment to set up its second MRO (maintenance, repair and operations) equipped to handle both narrow-body and wide-body aircraft, and other industries including Balaji Wafers to open food processing and snacks plants.
However, he said, MoU conversion progress was still under way, adding, with 46% of GIM commitments converted and single-window applications filed. The manufacturing sector has been showing strong traction, with conversion levels at around 60%, the Minister said.
“Each investor has already been assigned a nodal officer to handhold them throughout the application process,” he said. A recent meeting chaired by the Chief Minister reviewed approval processes and directed departments to shorten timelines, the Minister said.
In addition to GIM investments, the foreign direct investment (FDI) flow to Karnataka stood at $6.63 billion, which is ₹50,000 crore. “Over the years, Karnataka has consistently featured as one of the top States in India for FDI,” said the Minister.
Mr. Patil and his team visited Japan and Korea twice and received investments of ₹6,500 crore and another ₹5,000 crore, during the calendar year 2025. Mr. Patil led business exploratory delegations to at least 10 countries, including the U.S., U.K., Japan, Korea, Germany, Netherlands and conducted at least 30 meetings with potential investors from diverse industry domains.
On investment outlook for 2026, the Minister said the State has a strong lead pipeline of over ₹1 lakh crore and key sectors that would pump in these investments include, Electronics & Semiconductors (₹50,000 crore), Auto & EV Manufacturing (₹20,000 crore), Aerospace & Defence (₹10,000 crore), core Manufacturing (₹10,000 crore) and others (₹25,000 crore).
The State has an ambitious goal to attract ₹7.5 lakh crore in investments and create 20 lakh jobs by 2030 under the Karnataka Industrial Policy 2025–30.
In the calendar year 2026, a ministerial delegation will be visiting Germany (aerospace) and the U.K. (for other industries) again. In addition, the State would also have a strong presence at the World Economic Forum (WEF) scheduled to take place between January 19 and 23, 2026, at Davos, Switzerland.
Industry observers said that the key thing is to ensure that the intent is converted into action. Harish Bijoor, founder of Harish Bijoor Consults Inc., said, “The ultimate goal is to translate intent into action. We need to track this process with care. Plan, implement and evaluate.”
Murthy B.S., CEO, Leadership Capital, a CXO hiring firm and a people expert said, “Today, investments go where talent goes. Across the entire sunrise sectors of tech, clean energy and EV ecosystem, Karnataka is the clear leader.” The investments in 2025 would create thousands of new jobs in the State in next two years and more jobs in the years after that, Mr. Murhty estimated.

title: A. Mahendran sworn in as Alappuzha district panchayat president
summary: A. Mahendran of CPI(M) is sworn in as Alappuzha district panchayat president, with Sheena Sanalkumar as vice-president.
content:
A. Mahendran of the Communist Party of India (Marxist) [CPI(M)] was sworn in as the president of the Alappuzha district panchayat on Saturday (December 27, 2025). CPI(M) member Sheena Sanalkumar was elected vice-president of the local body.
In the election to the president post, Mr. Mahendran, representing the Nooranad ward in the district panchayat, polled 16 votes, while his rival, John Thomas of the Congress, secured eight votes. At the election held at the district panchayat conference hall, the returning officer and District Collector Alex Varghese administered the oath of office to the president.
Alappuzha district panchayat president A. Mahendran.
                                                            | Photo Credit: 
                                SURESH ALLEPPEY
Ms. Sanalkumar, representing the Aryad division, defeated her rival, Babitha Jayan of the Congress, by a margin of 16-8 votes in the election to the vice-president post. Mr. Mahendran administered the oath of office to the vice-president.
In the elections held earlier this month, the CPI (M)-led Left Democratic Front (LDF) secured a majority in the Alappuzha district panchayat by winning 16 out of the total 24 seats. The Opposition Congress-led United Democratic Front (UDF) won eight seats, increasing its tally from two seats five years ago.
Alappuzha district panchayat vice-president Sheena Sanalkumar.
                                                            | Photo Credit: 
                                SURESH ALLEPPEY
Officials said the election to the district panchayat standing committee chairpersons would be held on January 6 at 10.30 a.m. MLAs P.P. Chitharanjan and H. Salam, Additional District Magistrate Asha C. Abraham and others attended.

title: Minister Lad visits family of girl killed over inter-caste marriage in Dharwad
summary: Minister Santosh Lad visits family of honour killing victim Manya Doddamani, offering support and condemning caste-based violence.
content:
Labour Minister and the district in charge of Dharwad district, Santosh Lad, on Saturday, visited the family members of Manya Doddamani, who was killed by her father for marrying outside of their caste at Inam Veerapur in Dharwad district.
The Minister visited the family at a private hospital in Hubballli on Saturday, where they are undergoing treatment. He assured them of requisite assistance from the State government.
Speaking to presspersons later, Mr. Lad said that it was shocking that even after 79 years of independence, the country was still witnessing such incidents, displaying the dominance of the caste system that had resulted in the death of a woman who dared to marry outside her caste.
Expressing shock over the incident, he said that nowhere should such ghastly acts, where a father inhumanely killed his daughter, should take place, and humanity should prevail over other emotions.
Mr. Lad appreciated the Police Department for taking the requisite measures to prevent escalation of the matter. He said the government and the district administration would stand with Vivekanand Doddamani and his family.
Mr. Lad said that the Deputy Commissioner has initiated an inquiry into the issue. Two police personnel and a panchayat development officer have been suspended for dereliction of their duties, he said. Based on the inquiry report, further action would be taken on erring officials, he said.
Subsequently, the Minister, accompanied by officials, visited Inem Veerapur and the place where the assault took place. Speaking to presspersons after the visit, he said that the family was a follower of twelfth-century reformer Basavanna, who strived for creation of an egalitarian society.
The Minister emphasised the need for living with the feeling that humanity was the greatest caste and imbibing compassion as part of their life was necessary, and then only would it be a true tribute to Basavanna. He assured that steps would be taken to hold grama sabhas with the cooperation of leaders from all political parties and officials to restore bonhomie among members of different communities in the village.
The Minister was accompanied by N.H. Konaraddi, MLA for Navalgund; ZP CEO Bhuvanesh Patil; SP Gunjan Arya, Additional DC Geeta C.D., and other officials and members of dalit organisations.
In addition to the compensation by the State government, the district-in-charge Minister extended a financial assistance of ₹2.50 lakh. The family has been provided a compensation of ₹5 lakh by the State government.

title: Pitroda inadvertently revealed Congress part of anti-India global alliance: BJP on Rahul’s Germany visit
summary: BJP claims Sam Pitroda revealed Congress' ties to an anti-India alliance during Rahul Gandhi's recent Germany visit.
content:
TheBJPon Saturday (December 27, 2025) alleged that Sam Pitroda “inadvertently” exposed the Congress by “revealing” that it is part of an “anti-India” global alliance and that Rahul Gandhi often visits abroad to attend their events, hoping his party would return to power at the Centre with their support.
Referring to Mr. Pitroda’s remarks in his latest interview with a news channel, BJP national spokesperson Sudhanshu Trivedi alleged that the Congress overseas department chairperson revealed that the party holds an “official position” in the Global Progressive Alliance (GPA) with Gandhi being a part of its presidium.
“Rahul Gandhi’s traditional family advisor and architect of his mindset and psychology, Sam Pitroda, in an interview yesterday (Friday), inadvertently exposed the real face of the Congress. He said the Congress is a part of the Global Progressive Alliance and Rahul Gandhi had recently visited Germany to take part in its meeting,” the BJP Rajya Sabha MP told a press conference at the party headquarters here.
Mr. Trivedi alleged that the GPA is associated with a network of organisations engaged in setting “anti-India narratives”, and demanded that the Congress must explain its “role” in such a grouping.
“Rahul Gandhi has started daydreaming of gaining power with the support of anti-India forces since he is witnessing all such possibilities ending with the Congress,” he said, referring to the Congress leader’s meeting with Berlin-based Hertie School president and professor Cornellia Woll during his recent visit to Germany.
The professor is one of the trustees of the Central European University, funded by U.S.-based billionaire investor George Soros’s Open Society Foundation, he alleged.
“At the World Economic Forum meeting in Davos in January 2020, George Soros, while signalling out the name of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, had said that he had kept one billion dollars to re-establish civil society in the world and eliminate nationalist forces,” Mr. Trivedi added.
Noting that Mr. Pitroda in his interview also stated that the GPA is an alliance of 110 democratic countries, the BJP leader said other than the “western world”, only India, New Zealand, Australia and Japan in the east are “consistent vibrant democracies”.
“I want a clear answer from the Congress. Which are these 110 countries which, in the disguise of being democratic nations, try to damage India, the cradle of democracy in the world?” he posed.

title: Anti-poaching camp staff killed in tiger attack in Bandipur
summary: Anti-poaching camp staff member killed in a tiger attack at Bandipur Tiger Reserve, highlighting risks faced by wildlife protectors.
content:
A staff member of an anti-poaching camp was killed in a tiger attack at the Bandipur Tiger Reserve on December 27.
The deceased has been identified as Sanna Haida, who was attached to the Maralahalla anti-poaching camp in the Bandipur division and was engaged in regular patrolling duty in the tiger reserve.
S. Prabhakaran, director, Bandipur Tiger Reserve, said Haida was accompanied by three others while gathering grass seeds when the tiger pounced from the thickets and injured him. This happened at around 12.30 p.m.
Though all the anti-poaching camp staff were armed, there was hardly any response time as the attack was sudden and swift.
Haida suffered severe injuries and died on the spot. Originally from Hunsur, he had moved with his family to Bandipur after being deployed for patrolling duty to protect the wildlife and forest.
Forest officials rushed to the location soon after receiving information about the incident and shifted the body for postmortem examination, which was conducted as per procedure.
Though the incident cannot be described as a “human-wildlife conflict” as the tiger attack took place deep within the jungle, senior officials said it was a tragic and an unfortunate encounter that underscored the inherent risks and dangers faced by frontline forest staff who work in remote, wildlife-rich areas, often under challenging conditions, to protect the forests and wildlife.
Authorities said compensation will be paid to the deceased’s family members as per government norms. Conservationists called for reviewing the existing precautionary measures provided to the patrolling staff in sensitive zones, particularly in tiger reserves.
Bandipur Tiger Reserve is one of India’s premier wildlife habitats, with a tiger population of 154 as per the 2024 Phase IV population estimation exercise, which was carried out between November 2023 and February 2024. But Forest Minister Eshwar B. Khandre, in reply to a question in the Assembly, rounded off the figure to nearly 200.
Despite the high density of wildlife in the Bandipur-Nagarahole belt, it is rare for staff on duty to be attacked or killed during patrolling, though such incidents have taken place in the past.

title: V.R. Sudarshan urges CM to appoint deserving party leaders to boards of PSUs
summary: V.R. Sudarshan calls on the Chief Minister to appoint qualified party leaders to public sector boards.
content:
Former Chairman of the Legislative Council and KPCC vice-president V.R. Sudarshan has urged the State government to appoint deserving party leaders to various public sector boards as non-official directors without further delay.
In a letter to the Chief Minister, the Congress leader suggested to Siddaramaiah to consider the names recommended by the committee headed by Home Minister G. Parameshwara for various government-owned boards and corporations.
He has also drawn the attention of the Chief Minister to the nomination of party cadres, proposed by legislators, MPs, DCC chiefs and senior leaders of the party, to various public sector undertakings as non-official directors on the boards.
Mr. Sudarshan said, “We are also happy to note that you will become the longest-serving Chief Minister of the State from January 7, 2026.”
In a letter to Deputy Chief Minister and KPCC chief D.K. Shivakumar, Mr. Sudarshan urged him to convene a meeting of KPCC office-bearers and the executive committee to discuss the political scenario in the State and the implementation of various policies and programmes of the government.

title: SHANTI Act: Who is liable for nuclear incidents under the new law?
summary: Capped at ₹3000 crore, SHANTI undercuts the operator’s cost of nuclear incidents while allowing foreign suppliers to walk away with no liability
content:
“Not a single clause or word which says anything about supplier liability,” saidCongressMP Manish Tewari in Lok Sabha. His peer Shashi Tharoor added, “A supplier, who has provided faulty equipment, walks away without any liability and Indian tax-payers are made to bear the brunt”.
The newly passed Sustainable Harnessing and Advancement of Nuclear Energy for Transforming India (SHANTI) Act, 2025 has made drastic changes to liability laws in case of nuclear accident — exempting suppliers (foreign or domestic) from any statutoryliability, while capping the liability of nuclear plant operators to ₹3,000 crores.
‘SHANTI’, which replaces the two existing laws governing India’s nuclear sector —  the Atomic Energy Act, 1962 and the Civil Liability for Nuclear Damage Act, 2010, has now become an Act afterPresident Droupadi Murmugave her assent on December 21. TheBill was passedthrough both Houses on December 17, 18, after the Centre refused to refer the Bill to a Parliamentary Standing Committee for further scrutiny.
Opposition MPs, lawyers, nuclear scientists have pointed out the pitfalls of the Act such as – single composite licence for several processes, statutory vacuum, absence of long-term radioactive waste management plan, restricted information and dilution of civil liability in case of nuclear incidents/malfunction.
The Act holds the nuclear plant operator responsible for any incident that occurs during either installation, transport of material prior to installation and after. The operator is held responsible for any loss of life, work, injury, damages. However, the limit of liability on these operators is capped at ₹3,000 crore in case the installed capacity of the nuclear plant is above 3600 MW (mega-watts). For a nuclear plant with a capacity less than 150 MW, the liability is set at ₹100 crore. If the liability exceeds the upper limit, the Centrewill bear the liable.
It also exempts the operator from any liability if the incident occurs due to a natural disaster, armed conflict, hostility, civil war, insurrection or terrorism. The operator is also not held liable if any damage is suffered by a person on account of his own negligence. In all such exemptions, the Centre will take upon the liability. Any plant can also be exempted from liability if the risk involved is deemed ‘insignificant’ by the Centre. There is no mention of supplier in the entire Act, exempting them from any liability or punitive action under this law.
“The liability of the Fukushima disaster in Japan is about $200 billion and it is likely to go up,” said Dr. E.A.S Sharma, former Principal Adviser (Energy), while speaking toThe Hindu.He adds, “Imagine if your actual liability is about three lakh crores, and then what is the use of having a cap of three thousand?”.
Defending the graded liability in Parliament, Union MoS Jitendra Singh said that it gives a level-playing field so that ‘participation is possible at every scale’. He claimed that by putting higher liability on large reactors and lower on small reactors, SHANTI ensures fair risk-sharing, responsible participation and a safety-first approach.
“Irrespective of this (lower installed capacity), when an accident takes place, it can be like an atom bomb. Almost up to 30, 40 miles, you know, it can affect people’s health and there will be radioactive contamination,” counters Dr. Sharma. He says use of substandard material in nuclear reactors and design defects are very common in the global nuclear industry.
Bumper cars in abandoned Pripyat, Ukraine in the largest city in the exclusion zone surrounding the Chernobyl reactor, April 9, 2016. Thirty years later, there are signs of commercial clear-cutting in supposedly off-limits forests around the site of the nuclear disaster in Ukraine. Photo: The New York Times
Senior advocate Prashant Bhushan warns that such a low liability cap can create an incentive to suppliers and operators to cut corners. “The Supreme Court has laid down a principle that if you are operating a hazardous industry, then you are absolutely liable to the full extent of the damage. When your liability is capped at such a ridiculously low amount, it contravenes Article 21 – the Right to Life. You are endangering the life of the people, and you are virtually exempting the supplier and the operator,” says Mr. Bhushan.
Highlighting the strain the additional liability will place on Centre’s budget, Dr. Sharma adds, “Previously, NPCIL was the only operator and now private players will be there. One nuclear accident like Fukushima, can take away 1/3rd of the budget expenditure for a year. You will not have any money for your social justice schemes, education, health, infrastructure, crippling India’s finances”.
ALSO WATCHWatch: US law flags India’s nuclear liability rules days after Parliament passes SHANTI Bill
“When Fukushima took place in 2011, under public pressure, the Department of Atomic Energy introduced a bill to constitute an independent nuclear regulatory authority. This Bill went to the Parliament Committee which made some very far-reaching suggestions to strengthen the autonomy of the regulator. Surprisingly, after that, Department of Atomic Energy just remained silent. Now after 13 years, SHANTI has constituted the Atomic Energy Regulatory Board (AERB), but does not make it independent,” explains Dr. Sharma.
Under SHANTI, the AERB is a seven-member board with all appointees made by the Centre, sapping any semblance of independence from the body. This Board sets limits of radiation exposure to the workers and the public, limits for radioactive releases and discharges to environment, sets safety standards in all aspects of operation, working conditions, transport, waste disposal etc.
It also grants safety authorisation, regulates nuclear facilities, advises the Centre on safety, radiological surveillance and preparedness in response to nuclear emergencies. In case of a nuclear incident, the AERB will provide its recommendations within fifteen days from the date of occurrence of such nuclear incidents for notifications. The Board can exempt any radioactive material or any radiation generating plant from the requirement of safety authorisation.
“It (AERB) is subordinate to Department of Atomic Energy and they are supposed to regulate the department’s nuclear facilities?” questions Dr. Sharma. While the Act does not allow any civil court to entertain any suit which falls under the AERB, Centre and Appellate tribunals’ jurisdiction, the High Court and Supreme Court can intervene, clarifies Mr. Bhushan.
“The Act compromises Make in India and gives access to foreign players to all this nuclear and fissionable material. Suppose there is some negligence and it (nuclear material) gets into terrorists’ hands or it happens deliberately, a nuclear disaster can happen. This Act is a complete sell-out to foreign companies and to Adani, compromising the country’s safety, security and sovereignty,” concludes Mr. Bhushan.

title: Sapna Book House launches 70 Kannada titles
summary: Sapna Book House celebrates Karnataka Rajyotsava by launching 70 Kannada titles, enhancing accessibility to diverse literature across the state.
content:
Sapna Book House, a leading brand in publishing and sale of books, marked a major milestone by launching 70 Kannada works at its Mysuru branch and across several cities in Karnataka, on December 27.
Speaking at the event, writer and critic Pradhan Gurudutt said the publishing house has rendered yeoman service to the cause of Kannada literature over several decades.
“Very few institutions can match its sustained output. What it does more is propagate literature rather than the business of publishing and selling. It has been known for the quality of its books,’’ he added.
Publishing and launching 70 books at the same time is no small achievement as it involves complex logistics, including coordinating with authors, editors, printers, and distributors. “Such an exercise itself reflects the institutional strength and commitment of the publishers,” said Mr. Gurudutt.
A release issued by Sapna Book House said 70 Kannada titles, spanning all major genres, have been published to commemorate the 70th Karnataka Rajyotsava. The books include works by senior as well as younger writers, both established and new, drawn from different parts of the State.
Sapna Book House has made a significant contribution to the growth of the Kannada book industry by publishing a large number of representative works every Rajyotsava season in November, honouring writers and offering special discounts on Kannada books, stated the release.
It cited senior litterateurs to point out that few institutions in India have dared to publish so many books in any single language at one time.
The objective behind the initiative is to make books from all fields of knowledge easily accessible to Kannadigas and thereby help strengthen Kannada as a language of everyday life, the release said.
As part of Rajyotsava celebrations, Kannada books were sold at discounted prices at all 24 Sapna Book House outlets across Karnataka during November, and the present programme was organised to formally honour the authors by launching their works, according to the publishing house.
It said the event was special as the 70 books were being launched simultaneously at all branches of Sapna Book House, including in Bengaluru, Mysuru, Mangaluru, Hubballi, Kalaburagi, Belagavi, Hassan and Davangere, which, it said, underscored the State-wide scale of the initiative.
T.V. Venkatachala Sastry, scholar, Maddikere Gopal, president, Mysuru District Kannada Sahitya Parishat, and others were present.

title: Bengaluru police issue strict guidelines for New Year event places
summary: Bengaluru police enforce strict New Year guidelines for event venues to ensure public safety and compliance with regulations.
content:
Police Commissioner Seemant Kumar Singh on Friday held a coordination meeting with owners of event venues across the city. The attendees of the meeting include owners of pubs, bars, clubs, hotels, and restaurants.
The meeting, held at the Commissioner’s office, focused on ensuring public safety, law and order, and strict compliance with rules during celebrations on December 31.
The Commissioner emphasised that all organisers must obtain mandatory permissions from concerned authorities and adhere to the conditions laid down. Prescribed timings for New Year events must be strictly followed, and separate permission is required for the use of sound systems, with noise levels not exceeding permissible limits.
Venue owners were instructed to issue entry tickets strictly as per approved capacity and ensure that alcohol is not served to minors under any circumstances. For security, thorough screening of all entrants was made compulsory, with directions to immediately report any suspicious individuals or objects to the police.
Fire safety equipment must be installed without fail, along with measures to prevent stampedes. Organisers were also told to ensure adequate backup power arrangements to handle any power outages during events.
No entry to parks after 6 pm
In view of New Year celebrations, the Bengaluru West City Corporation and Central City Corporation have ordered restrictions on public entry to parks and lakes after 6 pm on December 31.
In a release, the corporations said large public gatherings are expected across the city on New Year’s Eve, which falls on Wednesday. Such gatherings could lead to untoward incidents and disturbance of public peace during the night.
“As a precautionary measure in the interest of public safety, entry to all parks and lakes under the jurisdiction of the Central and West City Corporations will be temporarily restricted after 6 pm,” the statement said. Other city corporations are also likely to issue similar directions in their respective jurisdictions.
The corporations have instructed officials to install clear signboards at all parks and lakes informing the public about the restrictions. They have also been directed to coordinate closely with the Police Department to ensure effective implementation of the order.

title: Kochi metro and water metro to operate additional services on New Year’s Eve
summary: Kochi Metro and Water Metro will offer extended services on New Year’s Eve, ensuring convenient travel for celebrations.
content:
Metro services from Edappally station to Aluva and Tripunithura will operate till 11 p.m. from December 26 to January 3. On New Year’s Eve (December 31), services will run at 20-minute intervals until 1:30 a.m. The last service from Aluva and Tripunithura terminals will depart at 1:30 a.m., while the final train from Edappally station will be available until 2:00 a.m.
On the night of December 31, Kochi water metro services will resume after a short break on the High Court–Mattancherry and High Court–Vypin routes, operating from midnight to 4:00 a.m. on January 1. On the Fort Kochi route, water metro services will be operated on New Year’s Eve only till  7:00 p.m, according to a release.
Water Metro services on the High Court–Mattancherry, High Court–Vypin, and High Court–Fort Kochi routes will conclude at 7:00 p.m. on December 31.  Services on the High Court–Mattancherry and High Court–Vypin routes will then resume from midnight to 4:00 a.m. on January 1. Services on other routes will continue as usual.

title: GBA revenue officers alleged harassment by Munish Moudgil, he denies
summary: GBA revenue officers allege harassment by Munish Moudgil, who denies the claims amid ongoing disputes over e-khata applications.
content:
The GBA-Municipal Officers’ and Employees’ Welfare Association have written to Deputy Chief Minister and Bengaluru Development Minister D.K. Shivakumar, alleging abuse and mental harassment by Munish Moudgil, Special Commissioner (Revenue), Greater Bengaluru Authority.
Following the suspension of two revenue officials by Mr. Moudgil over alleged dereliction of duty in issuance of e-khatas, the association recently held a candlelight vigil, prompting the GBA Chief Commissioner, M. Maheshwar Rao, to announce an audit of rejected e-khata applications. However, the association had demanded the officials be reinstated and that Mr. Moudgil should apologise to revenue officers.
In their letter to Mr. Shivakumar, the association president A. Amruthraj alleged that Mr. Moudgil mentally harasses, abuses revenue officers with abusive language in the morning video conference. “As officers take this call at home in the morning, even the family members of the officers are disturbed, upset over the language used,” the letter stated. It further alleged that revenue officers were working under immense pressure and Mr. Moudgil had not taken them along, but instead abuses them.
The letter claims that six revenue officers have died of stress in August - September, 2025. The association has sought time with Mr. Shivakumar to air their grievances.
Responding to these allegations, Mr. Moudgil called them ‘completely unfounded’ and said they ‘appear to be aimed at shielding erring officers from accountability and undermining measures taken to protect citizens’ rights’.
“Over the past three months, approximately 1 lakh final e-khatas have been issued. During the same period, around 25,000 applications were rejected, many of which were found to have been rejected on wrongful or untenable grounds. In response, a Special Rejection Audit is currently underway, and corrective as well as disciplinary action is being initiated against officers found responsible for such irregularities. In this context, I have recommended suspension and disciplinary proceedings against certain Revenue Officers who were found to have blatantly harassed citizens by unjustifiably rejecting their e-Khata applications.Following this action, false and baseless claims have been made..”, he said in a statement issued on Friday evening.

title: Minimum temperatures in Telangana to be below  2°C to 3°C for the next three days
summary: TG temperature
content:
Minimum temperatures across Telangana are likely to be below normal by 2°C to 3°C at isolated pockets over the next two to three days, according to India Meteorological Department (IMD). In its latest bulletin, the IMD did not issue any cold wave alert saying that dry weather is very likely to prevail over the State.
Hyderabad and its surrounding areas for the next 24 hours will see mainly clear sky. “Mist or hazy conditions are very likely to prevail during morning or night hours. The maximum and minimum temperatures are likely to be around 28°C and 13°C respectively,” the bulletin said.
Meanwhile, according to Telangana Development Planning Society (TGDPS), between December 26 and 27, a total of seven districts in the State recorded temperatures of 10°C or below. Sirpur in Kumaram Bheem Asifabad recorded the lowest minimum temperature of 7.4°C.
This was followed by 7.6°C in Kohir (Sangareddy), 8.8°C in Bheempoor (Adilabad), 9.2°C in Moinabad (Rangareddy), 9.4°C in Akbarpet (Siddipet), 9.5°C in Gandhari (Kamareddy) and 10°C in Pembi (Nirmal).
The remaining 27 districts recorded temperatures ranging between 10°C and 14°C. In urban locations, Uppal in Medchal Malkajgiri recorded 10.7°C and Tirumalagiri in Hyderabad recorded 11.7°C.

title: Danam Nagender ready to resign and seek fresh mandate
summary: Danam Nagender ready to resign and seek fresh mandate
content:
Hyderabad
Khairatabad MLA Danam Nagender expressed confidence in his political support from people and declared that he was prepared to resign from his post and seek a fresh mandate through a byelection, if required.
Addressing a meeting of party workers at Himayat Nagar on Saturday, the senior leader said that his confidence stemmed from the unwavering support of the party cadre. He credited his six consecutive victories as MLA to the hard work, dedication and loyalty of party workers.
Mr. Nagender, who was elected on the BRS ticket, shifted his loyalties to Congress after the elections. He also contested on the Congress ticket in Parliament elections from Secunderabad and lost.
The Khairatabad MLA also launched a sharp attack on leaders of the Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS), accusing them of lacking political decorum. He took exception to what he described as the use of informal and inappropriate language while referring to the Chief Minister’s office.
Issuing a stern warning, he said that those indulging in criticism must also be prepared to face counter-criticism, stressing on responsibility in political discourse.

title: New railway time table to come into force from January 1
summary: New railway timetable effective January 1; check train timings on IRCTC or NTES before travel.
content: SCR has advised passengers travelling from January 1 onwards to check the actual train timings before the commencement of their respective journeys. The information pertaining to the trains and changes in the timings at the related stations can be obtained either by visiting the IRCTC website (www.irctc.co.in) or National Train Enquiry System (NTES). Indications are that eight of the 25 trains starting or ending in Secunderabad or Kacheguda have slightly altered timings at the originating stations within SCR, said a press release on Saturday.

title: BJP seeks increased security at Mysuru palace, monitoring of migrant vendors
summary: BJP demands enhanced security at Mysuru Palace and regulation of migrant vendors amid rising crime concerns and recent incidents.
content:
The BJP has sought the deployment of Central Industrial Security Force (CISF) or any national security agency at the Mysuru palace, expressing serious concern over what it called a deteriorating law and order situation in the city owing to a spate of crimes in the recent past.
Addressing a press conference on December 27, BJP Other Backward Class Morcha leader Raghu and city BJP president L. Nagendra flayed the district in-charge Minister H.C. Mahadevappa and the State government for “playing down’’ serious incidents, including the cylinder blast near the palace in which three persons died.
Stating that such incidents ‘’cast a shadow over Mysuru’s image’’, the BJP leaders said that the government was content with labelling these as ‘’unfortunate” or “accidental”, thus diluting the gravity of the situation. The cylinder explosion is not a mere ‘’unfortunate incident’’ but a warning bell for authorities to ramp up security, they added.
Besides, there is no regulation to the entry of Mysuru palace. It is time to reduce the footfall to ensure that only licenced vendors operate in the vicinity. Security should be beefed up by deploying CISF, said Mr. Nagendra and Mr. Raghu. Security arrangements are grossly inadequate not only at Mysuru palace but other tourist hotspots as well, they said.
Incidentally, Yaduveer Krishnadatta Chamaraja Wadiyar, Mysuru MP, expressed a contrarian view on the issue and termed the explosion as accidental, thus implying that it is not a reflection on the law and order situation in Mysuru.
Mr. Raghu and Mr. Nagendra criticised the district authorities, including the police, for not maintaining any information or data on the number of migrant vendors, their origin, and so on, saying that it amounted to an intelligence gap.
Calling for compensation to the families of those who died in the cylinder explosion, the BJP leaders criticised Mr. Mahadevappa for giving what they termed a “clean chit” even before a full probe could be launched.
Former mayor Shivakumar and others were present at the press conference.

title: Patel Ramesh Reddy warns KCR, KTR for their language against CM Revanth
summary: Patel Ramesh Reddy warns KCR, KTR for their language against CM Revanth
content:
HYDERABAD
Telangana State Tourism Development Corporation (TGTDC) Chairman Patel Ramesh Reddy strongly condemned the language used by BRS president and former Chief Minister K. Chandrasekhar Rao and  MLA K.T. Rama Rao against Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy. He said that the people of Telangana are ashamed of the words being spoken by the father-son duo and warned them to hold their tongues.
Addressing the media at Gandhi Bhavan on Sarurday, Mr. Ramesh Reddy accused KCR and KTR of introducing ‘vulgar language’ into Telangana’s politics. “Our society observes that their language has gone beyond that of street rowdies,” he said, adding that the public will not remain silent if such remarks continue.
He alleged that KCR has been hiding in his Erravelli farmhouse for eight months and started speaking out only to divert public attention. “We strongly condemn the language used against the CM. KCR should play the role of a responsible Opposition leader,” he said. Taking a sharp dig at KTR, Mr. Ramesh Reddy said, “Is this the language you use after studying in America?
Highlighting Mr. Revanth Reddy’s rise, he challenged KCR to come to the Assembly and debate issues of exploitation during the previous regimes. The Chairman also criticised BRS MLA G Jagadish Reddy for "using objectionable language to please KCR".

title: Two Karnataka men arrested, stolen property worth ₹70 lakh recovered
summary: Two Karnataka men arrested in Anantapur for theft; stolen property worth ₹70 lakh, including gold and silver, recovered.
content:
Anantapur police arrested two men from Karnataka allegedly involved in property offences and recovered stolen property worth ₹70 lakh, including gold and silver ornaments from them.
Speaking to the media on Saturday, Superintendent of Police (SP) P. Jagadeesh said the accused Yadavalli Manju and P. Ramadasu, both hailing from Bellary in Karnataka, were friends and addicted to liquor, cricket betting, gambling and other vices. They planned to earn easy money and decided to commit property offences including chain snatchings, thefts and burglaries at locked houses.
According to the police, the accused travelled to Anantapur, Tadipatri, Gooty, and nearby places on two-wheelers, selected isolated areas and targeted solo travellers and snatched gold ornaments from them. Similarly, they used to travel in buses and steal luggage and other valuables of passengers. They also used to break into locked houses.
The accused would then sell the stolen valuables to meet their expenses, the SP said. Mr Jagadeesh said the duo were involved in similar cases in Bellary and Guntur earlier.

title: 10.56 lakh names deleted as EC releases Assam's draft electoral rolls after Special Revision
summary: The Election Commission of India deleted 10.56 lakh voter names in Assam's draft electoral rolls after a special revision.
content:
The names of 10.56 lakh voters have been deleted after thespecial revision of electoral rolls in Assam, where assembly polls would be in less than six months.
According to the integrated draft rolls released by the Election Commission of India (ECI) on Saturday (December 27, 2025), the State has a total of 2,51,09,754 voters, excluding 93,021 D-Voters or doubtful voters. Additionally, the names of 10,56,291 voters have been deleted due to death, shifting, or multiple entries.
D-Voters are a category of voters in Assam who have been disenfranchised by the government on account of their alleged lack of proper citizenship credentials. D-Voters are determined by special tribunals under the Foreigners Act, 1946, and the person declared as a D-Voter is not given a voter card.
Gates and windows: On the SIR and single-appeal window
All related particulars, such as name, age and photograph, of D-Voters have been carried forward to the draft electoral roll without any change.
The draft rolls were published after house-to-house verification of the special revision was held from November 22 to December 20.
Now, voters will be able to file claims and objections till January 22, 2026 and the final electoral rolls will be published on February 10, a statement said.
Of the 10.56 lakh, 4,78,992 names were deleted because of deaths, 5,23,680 voters were found to have moved from their registered addresses, and 53,619 demographically similar entries were identified for correction, it said.
The verification was conducted in 61,03,103 households across the State, it added.
The exercise involved 35 District Election Officers (DEOs), 126 Electoral Registration Officers (EROs), 1,260 Assistant Electoral Registration Officers (AEROs), 29,656 Booth Level Officers (BLOs) and 2,578 BLO Supervisors, the statement said.
Political parties deployed 61,533 Booth Level Agents (BLAs) to assist and monitor the process, it said.
While theSpecial Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rollsis underway in 12 States and Union Territories, including Kerala, Tamil Nadu and West Bengal, where elections would be due along with Assam, a special revision was ordered by the ECI in the northeastern State.
Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar had said, "Under the Citizenship Act, there are separate provisions for citizenship in Assam. Under the supervision of the Supreme Court of India, the exercise of checking citizenship is about to be completed". According to officials, the special revision stands somewhere between the annual special summary revision and the SIR.
The statement said the special revision is aimed at preparing an error-free electoral roll by facilitating enrolment of eligible un-enrolled electors, correction of clerical errors in name, age and address, removing names of deceased persons, shifting electors, and identifying and deleting multiple entries.
The State has a total of 31,486 polling stations following rationalisation, it said.

title: 2025 was an eventful year for Kerala
summary: In 2025, Kerala achieved digital literacy, poverty eradication, and faced significant political and environmental events, shaping its remarkable narrative.
content:
The year 2025 witnessed major developments in Kerala, from the UDF sweep in the local body polls after a decade-long wait to the acquittal of Malayalam actor Dileep by a trial court in the 2017 actor abduction and assault case, and controversies relating to the Sabarimala Sree Dharma Sastha temple.
The State made national headlines during this period by becoming a fully digitally literate State and the first State in the country to be free from extreme poverty.
While not all these developments were game-changers, some warrant a closer look:
January 9:Iconic singer P. Jayachandran dies, marking the end of anera of soulful melodies in various languages
February 21:Kerala government organises two-day InvestKerala Global Summitas a means to attract investments. Later in the year, Industries Minister P. Rajeeve said the State recorded the highest conversion rate in the country in terms of conversion of Expressions of Interest into investments, with 23.16% of the investment proposals at the Invest Kerala Global Summit evolving into actual investments
March 27:Foundation stone laid fortownship project for survivors of the 2024 landslides in Wayanadas part of a comprehensive rehabilitation project. It is coming up on some 65 hectares of land. The disaster claimed 254 lives and left 128 missing
May 19:A section ofNational Highway 66 caves in near Kooriyad, Malappuram district. The collapsed portion, along with its retaining wall, falls onto the service road built over a reclaimed paddy field, causing the nearby paddy field to split and form a small hill. The collapse of the newly built NH stretch and the deep cracks developed on the highway stretches in Thrissur, Kozhikode and Kannur districts catch the Union and State governments off guard, after questions are raised about public safety and the technical feasibility of ambitious road projects in the State
May 25:Liberian-flagged ship MSC ELSA 3 sinks off the coast of Kerala, causing serious environmental and livelihood damage. The vessel goes down with 640 containers, including 13 with hazardous cargo and 12 containing calcium carbide, apart from 84.44 MT of diesel and 367.1 MT of furnace oil. All 24 foreign crew members on board are rescued by the Navy and the Coast Guard. The shipwreck impacts water quality, plankton, benthos, fish eggs and larvae, and higher marine life, apart from causing serious environmental and livelihood damage
June 5:The Raj Bhavan, now renamed as Lok Bhavan,insists on displaying a saffron-flag-bearing image of ‘Bharat Mata’sitting astride a lion, arguably emblematic of the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh’s (RSS) notion of a Hindu nation, at an official event, sparking protests from the ruling Left Democratic Front (LDF) government. Agriculture Minister P. Prasad skips the event, stating that political symbols have no place in Constitutional offices or State events. In no time, it becomes a full-blown row between the State government and Raj Bhavan
June 9:MV Wan Hai 503, the Singapore-flagged cargo ship, catches fire some 44 nautical miles off the Azhikkal coastin Kerala, raising concerns about marine biodiversity and maritime safety. A joint rescue operation launched by the Coast Guard and the Navy saves the lives of 18 people from the cargo ship. However, two crew members sustain serious injuries in the incident, while four others, reportedly citizens of Taiwan, Indonesia, and Myanmar, who are involved in firefighting efforts, go missing
June 14:AnF-35B fighter jet of the Royal Navymakes an emergency landing at Thiruvananthapuram International Airport. The combat jet remains grounded there for over a month, creates much sensation and curiosity in India
June 23:The much-debated Nilambur assembly byelection witnessesUnited Democratic Front (UDF) candidate Aryadan Shoukathoutpacing Left Democratic Front (LDF)’s M. Swaraj by a significant margin of 11,077 votes. The election sees Left legislator-turned-independent candidate P.V. Anvar secure 19,760 votes, unsettling the conventional political dynamics in Malappuram district
June 28:Dr Haris Chirakkal, head of the Urology department at Trivandrum Medical College Hospital, kicks up a row by taking to Facebook tohighlight the shortage of critical surgical equipmentat the hospital. It sparks a debate about facilities in public health sector
July 2:Kerala University is at the centre of a major controversyafter Registrar K.S. Anil Kumar allegedly attempts to prevent Governor Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar from attending a programme organised by a Sangh Parivar-affiliated group at Senate Hall. The event, marking the 50th anniversary of the Emergency, becomes contentious over the display of a disputed image of Bharat Mata. The issue culminates in the Registrar’s suspension and brings out the differences between the university syndicate and the VC Mohanan Kunnummal. In December, Anil Kumar is transferred back to his college as Principal
July 7:Kerala government moves an Admiralty suit in the High Court against the vessel MSC Akiteta-2, which is owned by MSC Shipping Company, as security for a ₹9,531-crore compensation claim for marine and coastal pollution, the subsequent loss of livelihood caused to fishers, and the ‘remediation’ measures following the sinking of the company’s container vessel MSC Elsa-3 off the coast of Kerala on May 25
July 21:Veteran CPI(M) leader and former Chief Minister of Kerala V.S. Achuthanandanpasses away aged 101. The death of the tall leader, a revolutionary who acted as the conscience of the people, sees the masses across the political spectrum unite in grief
August 2:Death of veteran critic and social commentator M.K. Sanoo, who taught several generations of students and also functioned as a Left Front legislator in the Kerala assembly
August 15:In a keenly contested election to the office of theAssociation of Malayalam Movie Artistes (AMMA), actors Shwetha Menon and Kukku Parameswaran are elected president and general secretary, defeating actors Devan and Raveendran, respectively
August 21:Kerala is declared the first fully digitally literate State in India, marking the completion of the first phase of the Digi Kerala project, a State government programme implemented across all local bodies to bridge the digital divide. In the surveys carried out among 1.5 crore people from 83.46 lakh families across the State, 21.88 lakh people are identified as digitally illiterate. Out of this, 21.87 lakh people, comprising 99.98% of the participants, complete the training to use basic digital tools and successfully complete the evaluation. The project was initially launched as a pilot in the Pullampara panchayat in Thiruvananthapuram in 2021 and later expanded across the State
September 23:Versatile actor Mohanlal is conferred with the country’s highest cinema honour, the prestigious Dadasaheb Phalke Award 2023, for his contributions to Indian cinema
October 6:An alleged theft of gold from the sculpture casings at Sabarimala shrinerocks the Kerala assembly, with the Opposition raising it on the floor. The controversy erupted after a former temple assistant, Unnikrishnan Potti, raised the issue. A report by the Travancore Devaswom Board (TDB) Vigilance wing finds serious lapses. Kerala High Court sets up a special investigation team (SIT) to probe. The SIT arrests Unnikrishnan Potti along with key officials of TDB, including two former presidents, both CPI(M) leaders
October 8:Kerala Assembly passes theWild Life Protection (Kerala Amendment) Bill, 2025, and the Kerala Forest (Amendment) Bill, 2025, in the wake of widespread unrest over incidents of human-animal conflicts across the State. It also seeks changes to the Wildlife (Protection) Act of 1972
October 15:Industries department unveils theKerala Export Promotion Policy, Kerala Logistics Policy and Kerala environmental, social, and governance (ESG) Policy, as well as the Kerala Hi-Tech Framework, aimed at transforming the industries sector in the State by positioning it as an attractive destination for sustainable initiatives
October 19:Kerala government’s decision to ink an agreement for implementing PM SHRI(PM’s Schools for Rising India) in State schools despite its differing stance on the same courts a huge controversy, with the CPI, the second largest constituent of the ruling front, fiercely opposing the move. The CPI says the govt is against the National Education Policy 2020 and PM SHRI, and that the signing has been done without any discussion in the Cabinet. The government is eventually forced to withdraw from the MoU
October 25:Kerala experiences a significant surge inamoebic meningoencephalitis casesand deaths in 2024-2025, with reports of numerous infections and scores of fatalities, largely attributed to the brain-eating amoeba Naegleria fowleri entering through the nasal passages from contaminated freshwater. Until October 25, the total number of cases reported in Kerala was 144, along with 30 deaths
November 1:Kerala is declared free from extreme poverty.  The LDF government, which announced its intent to make Kerala free from extreme poverty in its first Cabinet meeting in 2021, went about the mission through a grassroots-level process involving every local body in the State. After several levels of vetting, 64,006 extremely poor families — comprising 1,03,099 individuals, many lacking basic documents — were identified based on the four-point criteria of access to food, health, means of livelihood, and housing. Microplans were prepared for each family and land, houses, jobs, medical treatment, medicines, and palliative care facilities provided as per individual needs
November 3:State film award forbest lyricist to Vedan originally named Hirandas Muraliturns controversial as he faces charges of sexual assault, drug abuse and illegal possession of wildlife trophy
December 4:Congress ousts its Palakkad MLA Rahul Mamkootathilfrom the party in the wake of a court denying him bail in a case of sexual assault. The MLA has had multiple allegations of sexual crimes against him
December 8:A session court in Kerala acquits Malayalam actor Dileep in the sensational case of abductionand rape of a leading actress in 2017. The trial court convicts six others in the case. Dileep is accused of criminal conspiracy in the case. The government says it will appeal against the verdict
December 13:Congress-led UDF registers a resounding victory across all the three-tier local bodiesin the State, including Corporations and Municipalities, dealing a serious blow to the aspirations of the LDF. The UDF takes the lead in 505 of the 941 grama panchayats, compared to LDF’s 340. In block panchayats, UDF wins 79, compared to the 63 of the LDF. The UDF also wins four of the six municipal corporations. In the district panchayats, both fronts win seven each, while of the 85 municipalities, UDF emerges victorious in 54, and LDF can win only 28. The BJP-led NDA topples the 45-year rule of the Left in Thiruvananthapuram corporation by emerging as the single largest alliance
December 17:Ending a prolonged and acrimonious stand-off between Lok Bhavan and the State government,Governor Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar appoints Ciza Thomas as Vice-Chancellor (V-C)of APJ Abdul Kalam Technological University (KTU) and Saji Gopinath as V-C of the Kerala University of Digital Sciences, Innovation and Technology (Digital University Kerala – DUK). The compromise comes against the backdrop of the intervention of the Supreme Court in the VC appointment
December 20:Actor-screenwriter-director Sreenivasan passes awayfollowing a prolonged illness. A common man’s scenarist, Sreenivasan contributed scores of witty one-liners to Keralites’ daily life
December 23:More than 24 lakh voters in Kerala are excluded from the draft electoral rollpublished by the Election Commission of India (EC) after a Special Intensive Revision (SIR). However, voters whose names are missing from the draft roll can submit claims until February 21. The draft electoral roll has 2.54 crore voters
(Compiled by Dhinesh Kallungal)

title: Merger of civillian enclaves in Secunderabad Cantonment with expanded GHMC remains unfinished
summary: Secunderabad Cantonment's merger with GHMC remains incomplete, highlighting ongoing civic challenges and demands for elected representation.
content:
When the Greater Hyderabad Municipal Corporation (GHMC) on December 25 announced a major expansion following the merger of 27 neighbouring municipalities, it outlined a restructured civic body comprising 12 zones, 60 circles and 300 wards. Along with the announcement, the civic body released a revised jurisdictional map. The map, however, showed a small area out of its jurisdiction — the Secunderabad Cantonment area.
The Secunderabad Cantonment spans around 10,000 acres and is divided into land seven categories. Of this, A1 and A2 lands, covering about 5,670 acres, are owned by the Indian Army. B1 lands, totalling around 414 acres, belong to the Central government. B2 lands, spread over 2,676 acres, are privately owned by residents, while B3 lands, measuring about 501 acres, are old grant lands that will continue to be retained by the Government of India. B4 lands account for 98 acres of vacant land. The C category, classified as cantonment land, extends over about 260 acres, of which the government will retain key spaces such as the Bison Polo Ground and Gymkhana Ground, leaving roughly 160 acres of civilian area. In addition, there are about 235 acres of civil areas.
In all, around 3,071 acres are proposed to be merged into the GHMC, which will include 2,676 acres of privately owned B2 lands, 235 acres of civil areas and 160 acres from the cantonment category, while the remaining areas will continue under the control of the Indian Army and the Central government. The omission of the Cantonment has once again brought into focus the long-pending demand for merger of its civillian areas with the GHMC.
Secunderabad Cantonment traces its origins to 1798, when an alliance between Hyderabad’s Nizam Sikander Jah and the British East India Company led to the establishment of a military cantonment north of Hussainsagar. Named Secunderabad after Sikander Jah, the area continues to retain its distinct administrative identity more than two centuries later.
At present, the cantonment falls under the jurisdiction of the Secunderabad Cantonment Board (SCB), which functions under the  Ministry of Defence (MoD).
Residents and civic groups within the cantonment have for years sought integration with the GHMC, arguing that a merger would help address persistent infrastructure and governance issues by bringing the area under a larger urban framework. Following a decision of the Defence Ministry to merge civillian enclaves in the periphery of cantonments across the country with the urban local bodies formal discussions on the merger began in 2022. As part of it a six-member committee involving the Municipal Administration and Urban Development department of the Telangana government was constituted.
The State government later issued a single-line no-objection certificate (NoC) permitting the proposed SCB-GHMC merger to move forward. Based on this, the Union government constituted a high-level committee and asked the Cantonment Board to submit a final report within a month. However, there has been no public update on the process since then.
An aerial view of Rasoolpura, which covers Ward 2 of Secunderabad Cantonment area. Despite being located in a bustling area of Hyderabad, parts of Secunderabad Cantonment Board struggle with inadequate infrastructure and erratic water supply.
                                                            | Photo Credit: 
                                NAGARA GOPAL
“There has been complete silence after the committee was asked to submit its report. While Hyderabad has been developing rapidly, the Cantonment continues to function under outdated regulations. Building bylaws dating back to 1924 are still in force, infrastructure is poor, and there is a growing civic deficit,” general secretary of an NGO Cantonment Vikas Manch Sanki Ravinder Babu said.
Not all residents, however, see the merger as the solution. Some argue that the immediate issue is the absence of an elected civilian body in the cantonment. Telukunta Satish Gupta, a social activist said that with the GHMC becoming even larger, it could become more difficult for residents to get civic works addressed. “We feel the merger may not bring much change. What we need first are elections to be held here,” he said.
Cantonment board elections have not been conducted since 2020, with the last polls held on January 11, 2015. “Nearly 12 years have passed without an elected civilian body, a situation that critics say has deprived thousands of residents of their constitutional right to democratic representation. The lack of infrastructure development is often attributed to the delayed merger with the GHMC, but the more immediate cause is the prolonged absence of elected representatives,” he added.

title: Primacy to public feedback on district reorganisation, says Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister Chandrababu Naidu
summary: Andhra Pradesh CM Naidu prioritizes public feedback in district reorganization, announcing final changes by December 31.
content:
Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu on Saturday directed the officials to go ahead with the proposed reorganisation of districts, divisions, and mandals with minor modifications, according primacy to public opinion.
The Chief Minister reviewed the objections and suggestions received on the preliminary notification and instructed the officials to issue the final notification after incorporating necessary changes.
The State government had issued the preliminary notification on November 27, proposing the reorganisation of districts, including creation of three new districts and five new revenue divisions. It had sought objections and suggestions from the public for one month. A total of 927 objections and representations were received from across the State.
Chairing a review meeting at his camp office, in which several Ministers and senior officials participated, the Chief Minister  discussed at length the objections and suggestions received, and emphasised that public sentiment should be respected while taking final decisions on administrative restructuring.
Following public demand, Mr. Naidu directed that five mandals of the Gudur Assembly constituency be merged with Nellore district again. Discussions were also held on proposals to retain Railway Koduru in Tirupati district, Rayachoti in Madanapalle district, and Rajampet, Siddhavatam and Ontimitta in Kadapa district. A final decision on these was yet to be taken.
In view of its large geographical size, it was agreed to bifurcate Adoni into two mandals. In Anakapalli district, it was decided to establish Addaroad Junction division in place of Nakkapalle division. Munagapaka mandal would be included in Anakapalli division, while Achyutapuram mandal would come under the proposed Addaroad Junction division.
The Chief Minister made it clear that there would be no changes in the proposed Polavaram district with Rampachodavaram as its headquarters, and it would remain as mentioned in the preliminary notification.
The government decided to retain several changes already proposed in the preliminary notification. These included shifting Nandigam mandal in Srikakulam district from Palasa division to Tekkali division; moving Cheedikada mandal in Anakapalli district from Narsipatnam division to Anakapalli division; and transferring Samarlakota mandal in Kakinada district from Kakinada division to Peddapuram division.
In Prakasam district, Addanki, Ballikurava, Santamaguluru, J. Panguluru and Korisapadu mandals of Addanki Revenue Division would be included in Prakasam district. Marripudi and Ponnaluru mandals of Kanigiri Revenue Division would be shifted to Kandukur Revenue Division and merged into Prakasam district. The remaining two mandals of Kandukur division— Varikuntapadu and Kondapuram — would be shifted to the Kavali division.
In Chittoor district, Bangarupalem mandal of Palamaner division would be shifted to Chittoor division. Chowdepalle and Punganur mandals would be moved from Palamaner division to Madanapalle Revenue Division, while Sadum and Somala mandals would be shifted to the Piler Revenue Division in Madanapalle district.
In Sri Sathya Sai district, a new Madakasira Revenue Division would be created. Amadagur mandal would be merged into Puttaparthi Revenue Division, while Gorantla mandal would be included in Penukonda Revenue Division.
After incorporating these changes, the State government would issue the final notification on December 31, 2025.
Ministers Anagani Satya Prasad, P. Narayana and V. Anitha, and Special Chief Secretary (Revenue) Sai Prasad were among those who attended the review meeting.

title: Adivasis from remote hamlets to visit Hyderabad first time to witness urban development
summary: Adivasis from remote hamlets to visit Hyderabad first time to witness urban development
content:
ADILABAD
In an attempt to expose indigenous communities to urban life, Minister for Tourism, Culture, and Archaeology Jupally Krishna Rao has announced an “Education and Exposure Tour” for Adivasis of the remote Kummarikunta hamlet.
During a visit to Utnoor mandal in the district on Saturday, the Minister interacted with Gond families and sought to understand the challenges faced by those living deep in the forest, far from the reach of urban areas.
Noting that Adilabad is often referred to as “Mini Kashmir” by tourists, he observed that local residents remain largely unaware of the progress in the outside world.
“To address this, the Tourism and Culture Department will facilitate an all-expenses-paid visit for the residents of Kummarikunta to Hyderabad. The tour is designed to introduce the Adivasis to the city’s historical heritage, modern skyscrapers, and the Metro Rail system,” he said, adding that youngsters from this village would also be shown professional sporting facilities for cricket, volleyball, and badminton.
Reflecting on the 78 years since India’s Independence, Mr. Jupally expressed deep concern over the persistent lack of basic amenities in tribal pockets and directed officials to ensure that living standards in these hamlets are improved through immediate government intervention. He laid special emphasis on education, calling it the most powerful tool for change, and urged adults to at least learn to sign their names to protect themselves against exploitation.
The Minister further assured that the government is committed to providing the four essentials food, shelter, education, and healthcare specifically promising that every eligible family in the gudem (settlement) would be provided with a pucca house. He also distributed blankets to the elderly.

title: A.P. Brahmin Corporation Chairman accuses YSRCP of propaganda against Tirumala
summary: AP Brahmin Corporation Chairman accuses YSRCP of false propaganda, defending Tirumala's festive arrangements and demanding accountability for misleading reports.
content:
Andhra Pradesh Brahmin Corporation Chairman Bucchi Ramprasad on Saturday slammed the YSR Congress Party for allegedly spreading false propaganda and hurting the sentiments of devotees of Tirumala.
Addressing the media at the Telugu Desam Party central office in Mangalagiri, Mr. Ramprasad said the government had made elaborate arrangements for the 10-day Vaikuntha Ekadasi festivities to ensure a smooth darshan experience for pilgrims.
He said a special committee was monitoring the arrangements and that Ministers Anagani Satyaprasad and Vangalapudi Anitha had already reviewed the preparations. Mr. Ramprasad dismissed reports carried by YSRCP-affiliated media outlets alleging a stampede as baseless and said the hill shrine remained peaceful.
Alleging large-scale corruption during the previous YSRCP regime, he said Tirumala was treated as a revenue source. Mr. Ramprasad demanded an apology from Mr. Y. S. Jagan Mohan Reddy for remarks that, he said, hurt the sentiments of devotees and urged the government to take strict action against fake social media campaigns targeting the temple.

title: Unnao rape case: Police detain Congress leader, activists protesting near Parliament
summary: Police detain Congress leader and activists protesting near Parliament against bail granted to Unnao rape convict Kuldeep Singh Sengar.
content:
Delhi Police on Saturday (December 27, 2025) detained activist Yogita Bhayana, Congress leader Mumtaz Patel and several other protesters who were staging a sit-in near the Parliament complex to oppose the suspension of the life sentence of Unnao rape convict Kuldeep Singh Sengar, an official said.
The protesters reached the area around 4 p.m. and sat on the road, raising slogans and demanding the cancellation of the bail granted to Sengar by the Delhi High Court last week, he said.
The police personnel announced through loudspeakers that the area near Parliament was not a designated place for protests and asked the demonstrators to disperse. When the protesters refused to vacate the spot, they were removed from the site and detained, the officials added.
VIDEO | Delhi: Police detained activist Yogita Bhayana and several others during a sit-in protest near Parliament.The demonstration was held in response to the Delhi High Court's order suspending the life sentence of Kuldeep Singh Sengar and granting him bail pending the…pic.twitter.com/AMhpTarYKh
