The detention came a day after the Unnao rape survivor's mother, along with activists from the All India Democratic Women's Association and Yogita Bhayana, staged a protest outside the Delhi High Court. The survivor's mother had said she would approach the Supreme Court against the high court's order and expressed faith in the apex court.
The Delhi High Court on Tuesday (December 23) ordered the release of Sengar, an expelled BJP MLA, on bail pending disposal of his appeal against his conviction in the 2017 rape case. The court, however, imposed strict conditions, including barring him from entering within a five-kilometre radius of the victim's residence.
Sengar will continue to remain in jail as he is also serving a 10-year sentence in connection with the custodial death of the survivor's father and has not been granted bail in that case.

title: Laly James’  suspension exposes rift in Thrissur Congress
summary: Laly James' suspension reveals deep divisions in Thrissur Congress amid cash-for-posts allegations during the party's first day in power.
content:
The Congress party’s return to power in the Thrissur Corporation after a decade was marred on the first day by bitter infighting, explosive allegations, and the suspension of senior councillor Laly James, exposing deep cracks within the district party unit.
What should have been a moment of pride and celebration for party workers quickly descended into a public slugfest of allegations and counter-allegations. The controversy erupted when Ms. James, a four-time Congress councillor, alleged that she was sidelined from mayoral consideration because she was unable to provide money allegedly demanded by party leaders.
She alleged that newly elected Mayor Niji Justin, along with her husband, had met multiple leaders carrying a “box”, though she said she did not know what the box contained. According to Ms. James, the District Congress Committee (DCC) president himself called her and said money was needed for the system to move forward, claiming it was for the party.
She launched a sharp attack on   All India Congress Committee general secretaries K.C. Venugopal and Deepa Das Munshi, questioning their understanding of Thrissur politics and accusing them of insulting grassroots level workers by deciding the mayoral candidate from above. Ms.  James also warned that if disciplinary action was taken against her, she had her own ways to “teach discipline” to those imposing it.
Responding to the allegations, DCC president Joseph Tajet dismissed the claims and challenged Ms. James to clarify whether she had ever “given a box” during her four terms as councillor. “I have never asked anyone for money. You can check the CCTV footage from my office and home to know the truth,” Mr. Tajet said.
He added that the three councillors shortlisted for Mayor post, including Ms. James, were informed that each would get a chance as Mayor on a rotational basis, and that only Dr. Justin’s name was announced initially because the core committee had not yet decided the tenure.
Meanwhile, senior Congress leaders privately admitted that the crisis escalated due to failures at the district leadership level. They said confusion arose because only Dr. Justin’s name as first-term Mayor was announced, allegedly based on the DCC president’s unilateral decision, creating confusion within the party.
Despite her suspension, Ms. James reiterated that she stands firmly by her allegations and insists she will remain a Congress worker till her last breath. She said she learned about the disciplinary action through media reports and accused the DCC president of acting without maturity. Ms. James claimed the leadership hastily branded her statements as emotional and imposed suspension without issuing a show-cause notice or giving her a chance to be heard.
She ruled out joining either the  Communist Party of India (Marxist) or the  Bharatiya Janata Party and said she would not approach the AICC or the Kerala Pradesh Congress Committee, alleging both were aligned with those she accused of acting against her. She again alleged that Dr. Justin may have paid party funds, which could have influenced the mayoral decision, while maintaining that she had done nothing to harm the party.
The Congress leadership, however, said Ms. James’ suspension followed an urgent inquiry by the DCC into allegations that had pushed the party into a crisis. The KPCC announced the suspension through a press release without specifying its duration.

title: BJP sets history by capturing power in two panchayats in Palakkad
summary: BJP makes history in Palakkad by winning two panchayats and retaining municipal control for a third consecutive term.
content:
The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) has made history by capturing power in two grama panchayats in the district and retaining control of the Palakkad municipality for a third consecutive term. The party has come to power in the Akathethara and Pudur grama panchayats, ending decades-long CPI(M) rule in both local bodies.
In the Akathethara grama panchayat in the Malampuzha Assembly constituency, represented in the past by former Chief Ministers and CPI(M) stalwarts like E.K. Nayanar and V.S. Achuthanandan, the BJP wrested power by bringing an end to 38 years of CPI(M) rule. The BJP secured 10 seats in the 19-member panchayat, while the Left Democratic Front (LDF) won eight seats and the United Democratic Front (UDF) one.
The BJP had opened its account in Akathethara in 2005 with two seats. It increased its tally to five in 2015 and seven in 2020, before capturing power this time with a clear majority of 10 seats.
P. A. Bindu, who won from Ward 5 (Thekkethara), was elected panchayat president on Saturday. The post, reserved for a Scheduled Caste woman, saw her secure 10 votes. G. Sujith, BJP president of the Malampuzha constituency committee, was elected vice-president.
In the Pudur panchayat in Attappady, the BJP ended LDF rule by winning eight of the 14 wards. C. Thankavel was elected president, while M. Pushpa was chosen as vice-president.a

title: Woman convict released from Mysuru jail on good conduct shifted to rehabilitation home as kin remains untraceable
summary: Woman convict released for good conduct from Mysuru jail is sent to rehabilitation home due to untraceable relatives.
content:
A life convict who was released from Mysuru Central Prison earlier this month on the basis of good conduct has been sent to a rehabilitation home for women in her native place, Hassan, as her friends and relatives remain untraceable.
A statement issued by V. Sheshumurthy, Chief Superintendent of Mysuru Central Prison, said Shanthamma, wife of Manjappa, was sentenced to life imprisonment and slapped with a fine of ₹20,000 in November 2016 under Section 302 of the Indian Penal Code for a case registered in the Banavara police station in Hassan.
Ms. Shanthamma was released from Mysuru Central Prison on December 9, 2025, as per the orders of the Government of Karnataka.
However, as no blood relatives or friends came forward at the time of her release, the station house officer, Banavara Police station, and panchayat development officer, Banavara, Hassan district, were contacted.
Upon confirmation that no family members or blood relatives could be traced, she was admitted to Shakti Sadan, the women’s rehabilitation home in Hassan, and escorted there by the prison’s women staff, Mr. Sheshumurthy said.
Officers and staff of Hassan Prison have been visiting Shakti Sadan from time to time to inquire about Ms. Shanthamma’s health.
Meanwhile, the Director General of Police, Prisons and Correctional Services, Bengaluru, has announced a cash reward of ₹10,000 to the prison staff, said Mr. Sheshumurthy.

title: Prakash Raj criticises move to privatise Vizag Steel, medical colleges
summary: Prakash Raj criticises government privatisation efforts of Vizag Steel and medical colleges, urging public resistance against anti-people policies.
content:
Film actor Prakash Raj on Saturday criticised the Central and State governments for what he described as attempts to hand over vital sectors such as healthcare and major public sector establishments, including the Visakhapatnam Steel Plant, to the private sector. He said only sustained mass agitations could stop governments from pursuing what he termed anti-people, anti-worker and anti-farmer policies.
Speaking to the media at a private hotel on the sidelines of the Centre of Indian Trade Unions(CITU) 18th All India Conference, Mr. Prakash Raj said he felt honoured to be invited and considered it his responsibility to attend the meet. Referring to the proposed privatisation of the Visakhapatnam Steel Plant, he said it was evident that efforts were being made to sell the plant to a private entity, alleging that those in power were favouring corporates.
He alleged that people questioning the government were being harassed by the police, and claimed that preventive detention laws were being invoked against dissenters, while those accused in high-profile cases such as the murder of activist Gouri Lankesh and the Unnao rape case were out on bail.
On the State government’s proposal to run medical colleges under the Public Private Partnership model, Mr. Prakash Raj said the move would place an additional burden on the people. He said it was for citizens to decide whom they should support and strengthen, and added that it was due to sustained agitations that the Karnataka government had withdrawn its decision to hand over 1,007 acres of land to corporates.
Commenting on films such asThe Kerala StoryandDhurandharreceiving public attention, he alleged that political parties were investing in movies aimed at influencing public opinion, and claimed that those in power were even campaigning for such films.
Mr. Prakash Raj also condemned remarks made by Tollywood actor Sivaji against women, describing the language used as highly objectionable. He said people should boycott films if ticket prices were increased beyond reasonable limits.
On recent encounters involving Maoists, he said the government should not resort to encounters, asserting that they were not terrorists. He called for dialogue and efforts to bring them into the mainstream.
Former MLA M. A. Gafoor and CITU State general secretary Ch. Narasing Rao were among those present.

title: Headless body found in river in Bidar district
summary: Headless body discovered in Bidar river; police investigate identity and circumstances surrounding the gruesome find.
content:
A decomposed, headless body of an unidentified man was found in a river near the bridge at Islampur village in Bidar district on Saturday.
According to the police, the body, believed to be that of a man aged between 35 and 40 years, was found near a bridge on the outskirts of Islampur village. The head was severed from the body, and both legs and the torso were reportedly tied with electric wires.
The incident came to light after a complaint was lodged by Yallaling, a resident of Islampur village.
A case has been registered at the Janwada police station, and a probe to ascertain the identity of the deceased and the circumstances surrounding the crime is under way. Efforts are on to trace the missing head.

title: 173 security personnel injured in Karbi Anglong violence: Assam Police
summary: 173 security personnel injured in Karbi Anglong violence; situation improving as authorities maintain strict vigilance and internet suspension.
content:
Altogether 173 security personnel, belonging to both Assam Police and CRPF, were injured in violence earlier this week in which two persons were killed in West Karbi Anglong district, police said on Saturday (December 27, 2025).
The situation in the trouble-torn districts of Karbi Anglong and West Karbi Anglong was limping back to normalcy with no report of any untoward incident.
''173 personnel of the Assam Police and @crpfindia were injured in the incidents on 22–23 December 2025 under Kheroni PS under West Karbi Anglong. 139 received first aid at the spot, while 33 were sent for treatment to various hospitals'', the Assam Police said in a post on X.
A strict vigil is being maintained in the districts by security forces, with prohibitory orders in place and internet services suspended.
Agitators from the Karbi community had been on a hunger strike for 15 days, demanding the eviction of alleged illegal settlers, who mostly hail from Bihar, from the Village Grazing Reserve (VGR) and Professional Grazing Reserve (PGR) lands in the tribal belts.
They went on a rampage on Monday (December 22) after police took away three agitators from the protest site during the early hours, reportedly to a Guwahati hospital as their health had deteriorated, which the administration later claimed was for their hospitalisation.
The Kheroni area in West Karbi Anglong district witnessed widespread violence on Tuesday, as one person was killed in police firing and another was burnt alive inside his house.
There was an attempt to evict the settlers last year, but a petition was filed in the Gauhati High Court, which passed an interim order staying the eviction process.
Meanwhile, a tripartite meeting was held on Friday (December 26, 2025) between the state government, Karbi Anglong Autonomous Council (KAAC) and the protestors, with Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma assuring that the government will move the Gauhati High Court for an early order on its previous stay on eviction in grazing lands in both the districts.

title: Police warn public against New Year greeting scam circulating on WhatsApp
summary: Hyderabad police warn against WhatsApp New Year greeting scams that could compromise personal and financial data. Stay cautious!
content:
The cyber crime police of Hyderabad have issued an alert warning the public against fraudulent New Year greeting links being widely circulated on WhatsApp ahead of the celebrations, cautioning that clicking on such links could compromise personal and financial data.
Police said users may receive messages claiming to offer personalised New Year greeting cards or digital gifts, often urging recipients to click a link to view the content. These links, officials said, typically trigger the download of malicious APK files that install spyware or malware on mobile phones.
Once installed, the malicious software can provide hackers access to bank accounts, one-time passwords, photo galleries and contact lists, leading to financial loss and misuse of personal information, police said.
Cyber crime officials have advised the public to avoid clicking on unknown or suspicious links, particularly those asking users to install or update an application to view greetings. Citizens were told to restrict themselves to opening plain text messages, images or videos received from trusted contacts.
Officials said increased scam activity is common during festive periods and appealed to the public to remain cautious and alert as the New Year approaches.

title: UDF assumes power in 71 of 82 panchayats in Ernakulam
summary: UDF secures 71 of 82 panchayats in Ernakulam, with Twenty20 backing Congress in a significant political shift.
content:
In a major shift in political equations, the Kitex-backed Twenty20 supported the Congress-led United Democratic Front (UDF) in Vadavucode-Puthencruz grama panchayat in Ernakulam district.
Congress’ Reji Thomas was elected panchayat president on Saturday (December 27, 2025) as two ward members of Twenty20 voted for him. The Congress’ Deepa Biju was elected vice-president. It helped the UDF wrest the panchayat from the Left Democratic Front (LDF) after 10 years, though it has only seven members, while the LDF has eight.
The UDF has come to power in 71 of the 82 grama panchayats in the district, while the LDF has been restricted to seven. District Congress Committee president Mohammed Shiyas termed it a ‘record win’ for the Congress and its allies in Ernakulam. Twenty20 has won the president’s post in four grama panchayats.
The election of heads of grama panchayats and block panchayats had its share of twists and turns, besides the surprise ‘coalition’ in Vadavucode-Puthencruz grama panchayat.
In Vadavucode block panchayat, the LDF’s Amrutha Sanoop became president through draw of lots as both the LDF and the UDF had five members each. Twenty20 has four members there. Vypeen is the only other block panchayat where the LDF has come to power, while the UDF has won the remaining 12.
The LDF’s K.P. James became president in Pothanikkad grama panchayat through draw of lots.
In Chendamangalam grama panchayat, CPI(M) rebel Fazal Rahman voted for the Congress’ P.A. Haridas who was elected president. Mr. Rahman’s stand proved crucial as it helped the UDF, which has nine members, gain the required majority of 10 votes.
The elections in Vengola grama panchayat was postponed after members of the LDF and Twenty20 did not turn up for voting.
The four grama panchayats where the Twenty20 won power are Kizhakkambalam, Aikkaranadu, Thiruvaniyoor, and Poothrikka. In Poothrikka, where both the UDF and Twenty20 had won seven seats each and the LDF two, Twenty20 won the president’s post through draw of lots. The Congress bagged the vice-president’s position.

title: Kudumbashree’s Technoworld to become Kerala’s first women-led IT incubation centre
summary: Kudumbashree’s Technoworld in Kozhikode will be Kerala’s first women-led IT incubation center, empowering women in digital careers.
content:
At heart, C.P. Jisha remains a homemaker, balancing the demands of domesticity with a thriving professional life. Every morning, after attending to her household chores, the 50-year-old walks towards a workday she once only dared to dream of.
Today, she is one of five women at the helm of Technoworld, an IT unit established by the Kudumbashree Mission in Kozhikode more than two decades ago. By January, it will become Kudumbashree’s first incubation centre for women in IT, online services, and digital field training in Kerala.
​“I came here looking for a job, and now I am helping other women find their own careers. That makes everything worth it,” Ms. Jisha says.
Inaugurated on March 18, 2004, Technoworld is an IT unit that began with a loan of ₹3.5 lakh and has grown into a workspace with assets worth nearly ₹80 lakh. Operating from a building at the Civil Station in Kozhikode, the unit started with data entry work for the Regional Transport Office when government offices were slowly transitioning to computers.
From just 10 computers and a printer, the unit has grown to house over 50 computers and other improved facilities. The initiative is run by K. Vijaya (team leader), N.P. Sabira (secretary), K. Divya, Jisha, and A. Beena. What started with 10 members eventually narrowed down to this core group of five, who chose to stay on through financial uncertainty and changing working conditions.
​The centre trains women who want to enter the digital services sector, guiding them on how to start similar units, manage workflows, and master basic software tools and data entry.
​According to P.C. Kavitha, district mission coordinator for Kudumbashree Kozhikode, the success of Technoworld lies in how the women utilised the support they received. “Kudumbashree provides the same support to everyone. How carefully and fully they used the opportunity given to them makes the difference,” she says.
The team’s journey has been shaped by unity and consistent support. “We stood together through everything. That is the reason we are here today,” Ms. Vijaya says, recalling the early days. “In 2004, a ₹3.5-lakh loan felt like a huge amount. We were worried about whether we could repay it. But we chose to work while still taking care of our families, and we survived the hustle.”
Sabira, a resident of Kallayi, says the infrastructure for the incubation centre is ready in every sense. “Now we are waiting for those women with dreams to come in,” she says.
The centre will welcome women aged 18 and above, expecting a stream of young students, homemakers, and those who want to return to work later in life. “There were days we stayed late in the office whenever we had a tight deadline, mostly for data entry work. The five of us have become a safe haven for each other,” she says.
​Over the years, Technoworld has handled a wide range of digital work for government offices, including services at motor vehicle offices, hospital kiosks handling birth and death registrations, and the Kozhikode Corporation office. One of the largest assignments the unit undertook was the 2011 Socio-Economic and Caste Census, which required extensive data work. The unit also prepared voters’ lists for the Kozhikode Corporation and 38 panchayat elections in 2005. Besides this, the unit has trained around 250 people under various Central and State government schemes and has employed over 2,500 individuals to date, with 72 people currently working across different assignments.

title: Wheelchairs donated to SCR for use in railway stations
summary: DP World donates 50 wheelchairs to SCR for railway stations, enhancing accessibility and opening upgraded TTEs Rest Room in Hyderabad.
content: SCR Hyderabad Divisional Railway Manager Santosh Kumar Verma was handed over 50 wheel chairs donated by the DP World company as a part of its corporate social responsibility (CSR) for use in railway stations. An ₹10 lakh upgraded and refurbished Travelling Ticket Examiners (TTEs) Rest Room was opened at Kacheguda Railway Station on Saturday. Principal Chief Commercial Manager Ity Pandey, Senior DCM Anirudh Pamar Z and other officials were present, said a press release.

title: Two killed after lorry overturns near Gudiyatham
summary: A lorry accident near Gudiyatham claimed two lives, including a woman, after it overturned on a steep hill road.
content:
A 45-year-old woman was among two persons who were killed in a road accident after a poultry feed-laden lorry overturned on a hilly road at Sainagunda village near Gudiyatham town in Vellore on the Tamil Nadu - Andhra Pradesh border on Saturday.
Police said the deceased were identified as K. Devi, a dairy farmer in Sainagunda village near Gudiyatham, and Mohammed Inayatullah, 56, a lorry driver from Andhra Pradesh.
Initial inquiry revealed that Inayatullah loaded around 15 tonnes of poultry feed from a farm in Palamaner village near Chittoor in A.P onto the lorry to go to the poultry farm in Thirukovilur town. He was driving on a steep hill road in the remote Sainagunda village when he saw cowherd Devi, who was taking her cows for grazing.
Police said that as he tried to steer the wheels away from the cows, he lost control of the vehicle that then overturned on the carriageway.  Lorry driver Inayatullah and Devi was killed on the spot.
Immediately, other motorists and passersby alerted Gudiyatham Taluk police, who rushed to the spot. They sent the bodies to Government Taluk Hospital in Gudiyatham for postmortem. The mangled lorry was removed from the carriageway to restore traffic movement on the route. A case was registered. A probe is under way.

title: Actress Rakul Preet Singh’s brother absconding in drugs case
summary: Actress Rakul Preet Singh's brother, Aman, is wanted in a drug case involving cocaine and MDMA in Hyderabad.
content:
The Masab Tank police have launched a manhunt to nab Aman Preet Singh, brother of actress Rakul Preet Singh, in connection with a drugs case. On December 19,  the police booked two men for possession, transportation and sale of cocaine and MDMA.
The accused arrested in the case are Nitin Singhania, 35, a real estate broker from Malakpet, and Shranik Singhvi, 36, a businessman from Troop Bazaar. The case was registered based on a complaint filed by a sub inspector of Masab Tank police station following a drug seizure near Chacha Nehru Park on December 19.
According to the FIR, police intercepted a grey car near the park parking area after receiving specific information about a planned drug delivery. During the search operation, officers recovered 43.7 grams of cocaine and 11.5 grams of MDMA concealed in the dashboard of the vehicle. The drugs were verified on the spot by the clues team.
During interrogation, the accused allegedly disclosed that they were procuring cocaine and MDMA from a Nigerian supplier using a mobile contact saved under a pseudonym, with deliveries being made in Hyderabad through African couriers. They stated that the drugs were meant for sale to a limited group of consumers in the city.
The FIR names several alleged consumers, including Aman Preet Singh, who is currently absconding. Police said teams have been formed to trace and apprehend him. Investigators are also trying to identify and locate the main supplier and intermediaries involved in the supply chain.
Police seized the car used for transporting drugs, along with two mobile phones belonging to the accused, which allegedly contain details of contacts and financial transactions linked to the case.
The case has been registered under Sections 8(c), 22(b)(c), 27(a), 27(A) and 29 of the NDPS Act, read with relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.

title: Alliance talks between NCP(SP) and NCP for Pune civic polls hit dead end
summary: Alliance talks between NCP (SP) and NCP for Pune civic polls have stalled, jeopardizing collaboration ahead of January elections.
content:
Talks between the NCP (SP) and the Ajit Pawar-led ruling NCP over a possible alliance for the next month's Pune civic polls appear to have hit a dead end, with the latter not agreeing to the Sharad Pawar-led party's proposal for contesting the elections on their respective poll symbols.
Elections to 29 municipal corporations in Maharashtra, including Mumbai and Pune, will be held on January 15. The last date to file the nominations is December 30.
Senior NCP (SP) leader Ankush Kakade said his party leadership in Pune met Deputy Chief Minister Ajit Pawar on Friday (December 26, 2025) but talks over the possible alliance for Pune civic polls could not progress.
"No talks could take place over the alliance between us. We went to meet the NCP leaders to convey that NCP (SP) will contest the election on its symbol and they can fight on their symbol (if the alliance takes place ). It seems they are not ready for this proposal," Mr. Kakade said.
He said the NCP (SP) working president Supriya Sule is also of the opinion that since NCP (SP) has been with Maha Vikas Aghadi (MVA), the party will prefer to stay with its alliance partners - Congress and Shiv Sena (UBT).
NCP's election symbol is an analogue alarm clock, while NCP (SP) has been allotted the symbol of a man blowing a 'turha' (traditional trumpet).
Two days back, NCP (SP) city unit president, Prashant Jagtap resigned from the party amid the talks about alliance between two NCP factions. Jagtap joined Congress on Friday (December 26).
According to Congress leaders, Jagtap refused to align with "communal forces" and chose their party without compromising on ideology.

title: 13 booked as Jagan’s birthday celebrations trigger ‘public outrage’ in A.P.
summary: Public outrage erupts in Andhra Pradesh as Jagan’s birthday celebrations involve animal sacrifices and violent acts by YSRCP cadres.
content:
The Andhra Pradesh government has swung into action following ‘public outrage’ over  the birthday celebrations of YSRCP president and former Chief Minister Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy.
The government took a serious view of the complaints received by the Police Department over the alleged violent and disturbing activities by the YSRCP leaders and cadres, which triggered a ‘public outrage’.
Cases have been registered against 13 persons, including a sarpanch with allegiance to the YSRCP, while several people have been detained. The birthday celebrations triggering controversy were reported from Puttaparthi, Dharmavaram, and Gopalapuram, with the authorities concerned removing ‘offensive’ flex boards and initiating legal action, according to the CMO officials.
According to information, the government received reports indicating that some YSRCP activists resorted to activities intended to intimidate citizens. At several places, pregnant women were allegedly assaulted, while animal sacrifices were carried out in public view, and the blood was reportedly smeared on banners and portraits of Mr. Jagan Mohan Reddy.
Flex boards depicting Mr. Jagan Mohan Reddy, armed with knives, with slogans encouraging destruction, were reportedly put up.
The police received multiple complaints from citizens, leading to the registration of cases. YSRCP cadres reportedly performed animal sacrifices in Kalyanadurgam, Uravakonda, and Singanamala constituencies.
In Raptadu constituency, the birthday celebrations reportedly involved sacrificing a sheep and pouring blood on a former MLA’s banner. A YSRCP worker allegedly kicked a pregnant woman named Sandhya Rani, reportedly distressed by the noise from bow-and-arrow demonstrations. He was taken into police custody.
The Police Department has warned that strict action will be taken against such activities, the officials said.

title: Safety measures to be in place for smooth conduct of Cochin Carnival
summary: Cochin Carnival ensures safety with extensive police presence, strict guidelines, and coordinated emergency services for a secure celebration.
content:
The district administration has instructed officials of various departments to ensure all safety measures are in place ahead of the Cochin Carnival where thousands are expected to turn up for New Year celebrations at Parade Ground and Veli Ground in Fort Kochi.
The instructions were issued after a meeting chaired by Collector G. Priyanka and Kochi Mayor V.K. Minimol on Saturday (December 27, 2025) to review the steps taken by different departments for the smooth conduct of the mega event.
The meet decided to put in place all required safety measures in a time-bound manner. Maximum number of police personnel will be deployed for keeping law and order. The police will arrange parking facilities, imposing traffic restrictions and ensuring CCTV surveillance in the area, an official release issued after the meeting said.
Inspections will be conducted by the Corporation and Food safety department at makeshift food stalls in the carnival area. Strict action will be taken against stalls that fail to adhere to safety guidelines. The Kerala Water Authority will take steps to ensure supply of potable water for revellers, according to the release.
Steps will be taken to control rush in jankars, Water Metro ferries, and others. The Kerala State Road Transport Corporation will conduct seven bus services on the route, while private buses that obtain special permits will be allowed to operate additional services. Bio-toilets will be installed on the carnival premises.
The Fire and Rescue Services department will install lights at the required spots. It will also make use of scuba team and civil defence volunteers in emergency situations. The District Medical Officer will be ensuring the services of ambulance and medical teams.
The Public Works department (PWD) will inspect the construction of Pappanji (the giant effigy of an old man), which will be set on fire on New Year, to ensure that all safety aspects are followed. The Kerala State Electricity Board has been instructed to ensure uninterrupted power supply in the area.
Round-the-clock co-ordination centres will be set up at Parade Ground and Veli Ground to coordinate the services of different departments.
Deputy Mayor Deepak Joy, Sub Collector Grandhe Sai Krishna, Deputy Commissioner Aswathy Jiji and Deputy Collector (disaster management) K. Manoj were among the officials who attended the review meet.

title: Officers’ association warns of boycott over Bihar Minister’s conduct
summary: Bihar Revenue Service Association warns of boycott over Deputy CM Sinha's remarks damaging officers' dignity and public trust.
content:
In a letter addressed to Chief Minister Nitish Kumar, the Bihar Revenue Service Association (BiRSA) has complained against the conduct of Deputy Chief Minister, and Revenue and Land Reforms Department Minister Vijay Kumar Sinha. The letter, dated December 24, 2025, raises serious objections over the language used by the the Minister against officers of the department during a public hearing.
“Remarks made by Mr. Sinha on public platforms for some time have not only deeply damaged the dignity of the State’s revenue administration but have also deliberately made an entire service cadre the subject of public ridicule and outrage,” BiRSA stated.
“The scenes that are constantly being broadcast in the media and on social media clearly show that, in the pursuit of popularity and immediate applause, administrative norms, principles of natural justice, the spirit of Articles 14 and 21 of the Constitution and service rules are being disregarded,” BiRSA said in the letter.
“Statements like, [I will suspend them right away, answer here, in front of the public, get an explanation and take immediate action, and the decision will be made on the spot], are not in line with a Constitutional democracy. This language is neither indicative of administrative discretion nor the rule of law,” the association further stated.
The letter, signed by BiRSA president Anand Kumar and general secretary Saurabh Kumar, pointed out that the ongoing public hearing in which “an immediate court martial or mob justice” was not representative of democratic administration, but rather a theatrical style of governance.
Mr. Sinha often forget that the National Democratic Alliance (NDA) government had been in power for past two decades, and in his statements, he negated the contributions of previous Ministers and departmental heads, giving an impression that all previous leadership had been completely inactive, and that no improvements had been made in the department, “as if the entire administrative burden of the past 100 years has suddenly fallen on his shoulders”, the association said.
Ministers and elected representatives should be subjected to similar public questioning on budget, planning and policy failures, BiRSA said.
“If not, then why are only revenue officers being subjected to public humiliation? The culture of on-the-spot justice has been the hallmark of dictatorial tendencies, not democracy,” BiRSA said.
Praising its own officers, BiRSA’s letter stated that the current regional officers had made unprecedented improvements despite limited resources, including in “digitisation, online mutation, dispute-free mutation campaign and successful revenue collection campaign”.
It also added that “continuous public humiliation” would not only demoralise officers but also cripple the effectiveness of the administration.
BiRSA demanded that indecent and punitive statements against revenue officers on public platforms should be stopped immediately, and departmental monitoring should be conducted only through established legal and administrative procedures.
It also called for a regular and accessible system for communication at the level of Principal Secretary and Departmental Minister.
“If the ‘public dialogue’ model is to be implemented, it should be applied equally to all departments and elected representatives. A serious policy-level discussion should be held on the historical and structural problems of the Revenue Department,” BiRSA stated.
The association warned that if the situation was not improved soon, it would be compelled to consider a “collective boycott of such events and activities”.
Reacting to the letter, Mr. Sinha on Saturday (December 27) said that the ‘Land Reforms Public Welfare Dialogue’ had been launched with the objective of making the systems more transparent, accessible and accountable.
“This initiative is neither for grabbing headlines nor for giving speeches or discouraging any officer or employee. Its sole purpose is to listen and understand the real problems of the people and ensure their resolution,” he said.
The initiative was being conducted with complete respect for the Constitution, Constitutional institutions, and judicial boundaries, the Minister said.
Earlier this week, the Bihar Judicial Services Association sought Mr. Sinha’s apology for allegedly making objectionable remarks against a judge.

title: Why did ECI appoint micro observers in Bengal when State has the lowest voter deletions in SIR, asks Abhishek Banerjee
summary: Abhishek Banerjee questions ECI's appointment of micro observers in Bengal amid low voter deletions and demands transparency on infiltrators.
content:
Trinamool Congressnational general secretary Abhishek Banerjee on Saturday (December 27, 2025) questioned why theElection Commission of India (ECI)appointed micro observers inWest Bengalwhen it had the least number of voter deletions in the special intensive revision (SIR) process.
Based on previous claims by theBharatiya Janta Party (BJP), where they alleged that there are over one crore “infiltrators” in West Bengal, Mr. Banerjee, the second-in-command in the Trinamool, asked the list of infiltrators to be published by the ECI.
“According to the draft electoral rolls data published by the EC, Tamil Nadu had 12.57% voter deletions, Gujarat had 9.95% deletions, Chhattisgarh had 8.76% deletions, Kerala had 6.65% deletions, in West Bengal the number was the lowest at 5.79%...still they appointed micro observers here not in the other States where there were massive deletions,” Mr. Banerjee added.
The SIR was carried out in West Bengal just to “harass” the people, Mr. Banerjee said. Of the 58 lakh deleted voters in the draft voter list, he also asked the ECI to clarify who among these people are “infiltrators”. He also raised questions about why the ECI is not sending show cause notices to these alleged “infiltrators” to identify them.
“If cleaning the voter list is your goal, then publish the names of the 1.36 crore people who have been flagged in the logical discrepancies category... Why are you not transparent about it? Why is the EC scared to publish the list?” Mr. Banerjee asked.
The Trinamool Lok Sabha MP from Diamond Harbour constituency also said that he will head to New Delhi on December 31, where he will pose these questions to the ECI officials and meet Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. “If they do not answer our questions, we will gherao the ECI office and protest,” Mr. Banerjee said. He said the ECI officials should apologise to the people of West Bengal if they do not publish the list of “infiltrators” and “logical discrepancies” for instilling unnecessary fear in the people.
The MP said the party will take to the streets in West Bengal from January 2 and take these pressing issues to the people of the State.
Mr. Banerjee also raised questions about why the other States that share borders with Bangladesh have not been made part of the SIR process, like Assam, Tripura, Meghalaya, and Mizoram to identify and take out alleged “Bangladeshi infiltrators” and why West Bengal was singled out.

title: Three arrested for harassing woman scooterist
summary: Three youths arrested in Bengaluru for harassing a woman scooterist, following viral footage of the incident.
content:
In a swift action, the Sudduguntepalya police on Saturday arrested three youth for harassing a motorcycle-borne woman and followed her on a two-wheeler in BTM Layout on Thursday night.
The incident occurred at midnight on December 25 when the woman was riding her scooter alone. A passer-by noticed the act and recorded it on his mobile phone which went viral on social media. As per the report which was tagged to the city police online account, the accused riding on a motorcycle, without helmets, followed the woman for nearly two km, riding recklessly and attempting to intimidate her.
The accused were seen swerving the motorcycle close to the woman’s scooter and blocking her path at several points, creating panic and fear. The woman, who was wearing a helmet, managed to continue riding despite the harassment.
A motorist driving behind recorded the incident on video and shared it on social media, tagging the Bengaluru Traffic Police. The footage shows the bikers violating traffic rules and engaging in dangerous riding.
The video triggered widespread outrage online, with netizens demanding strict action against those involved. The police based on the registration number of the bike, tracked down the accused identified as Roshan, 19, Ayan, 19, and Rihan khan, 18.
Roshan and Ayan were employees at a chicken shop, while Rihan was working in a garage in the BTM layout first stage.

title: Government criticised for turning a blind eye to rampant footpath encroachment, ‘neglect’ of Mysuru’s heritage
summary: BJP leaders criticize the Congress government for neglecting Mysuru's heritage and allowing rampant footpath encroachments, compromising pedestrian safety.
content:
The Congress government in the State and the district administration has come under flak for their “inept” handling of civic and heritage issues pertaining to Mysuru.
Addressing a press conference here on December 27, L. Nagendra, BJP city unit president and former MLA, Raghu, BJP OBC Morcha leader, and former mayor Shivakumar, criticised the local authorities for allowing rampant and unchecked encroachment of footpaths in the city, thus diluting the heritage brand of Mysuru.
There is not only rampant encroachment, but unregulated street vending, which has compromised pedestrian safety, said the BJP leaders, pointing to a slew of such examples.
The footpaths in key areas — including Sayyaji Rao Road which cuts through the core tourism zone, and in residential areas like Saraswathipuram — had become virtually unusable for pedestrians. ‘’While hawking has traditionally been part of Mysuru’s urban fabric, the lack of a clear vending policy has resulted in chaos,’’ the BJP leaders lamented.
“There is a need for a structured hawking policy. Vendors must be given designated zones and protected, but the rights of pedestrians should be respected too. Today, shopkeepers themselves are dumping merchandise on footpaths, pushing people onto busy roads,” said Mr. Nagendra. The BJP leaders said footpaths had effectively turned into slums in several parts of the city, including around K.R. Hospital, along Sayyaji Rao Road, and Saraswathipuram, owing to the mushrooming of eateries on both sides of the roads.
While acknowledging the need for livelihoods, they demanded removal of hotels and eateries operating illegally on footpaths, especially where pedestrian movement has been completely blocked.
The police, they alleged, were “helpless spectators” focused on collecting traffic fines while failing to clear encroachments in the heart of the city.
With no elected councillors in place for nearly two years, they said the onus lays squarely on the Mysuru City Corporation Commissioner to take initiative. Questioning the delay, they demanded immediate conduct of civic elections. The BJP leaders also raised concern over encroachments and new layouts coming up around Chamundi Hills in the name of development, and called for conservation measures.
On heritage conservation, they accused the Siddaramaiah-led government of apathy. “Mysuru’s heritage is being diluted. The government sees the palace only as a source of revenue, not as a heritage monument,” Raghu alleged, adding that the Chief Minister, despite being from Mysuru, had failed to protect the city’s legacy.
They cited the dilapidated state of the old Deputy Commissioner’s office, the stalled restoration of Devaraja and Vani Vilas Markets, neglect of the Lansdowne Building, and the endangered condition of several other structures, including the Yuvaraja College, to drive home their point. No funds had been allocated for heritage conservation, they alleged, pointing to the unrepaired Saraswathipuram fire brigade building years after its collapse.

title: T.M. Sasi is Palakkad district panchayat president
summary: N. Saritha was elected vice-president
content:
CPI(M)’s T.M. Sasi was elected president of the Palakkad district panchayat on Saturday. N. Saritha, also from CPI(M), was elected vice-president.
Mr. Sasi defeated United Democratic Front (UDF) candidate K.G. Eldo, while Ms. Saritha emerged victorious over UDF’s Rafeeqa Parakkot.
Left Democratic Front (LDF) has 19 members and UDF 12 in 31-member district panchayat.
T.M. Sasi,  president, Palakkad district panchayat.
                                                            | Photo Credit: 
                                K.K. Mustafah
Mr. Sasi, a native of Mudappallur, was elected to the district panchayat for the first time. He currently serves as a member of the CPI(M) district secretariat.
Ms. Saritha is the district treasurer of the All India Democratic Women’s Association.
N. Saritha, vice-president, Palakkad district panchayat.
                                                            | Photo Credit: 
                                K.K. Mustafah
District Collector M.S. Madhavikutty administered the oath of office to Mr. Sasi. Speaking after taking charge, he acknowledged the huge responsibility entrusted to him and sought the support of his colleagues, the opposition, and CPI(M) leaders to carry out development initiatives effectively.

title: R. Lathadevi takes charge as Kollam district panchayat president
summary: R. Lathadevi from CPI elected president of Kollam district panchayat, securing 17 votes in a competitive election.
content:
Left Democratic Front (LDF)’s R. Lathadevi (CPI), elected from the Chadayamangalam division, assumed office as the new president of the Kollam district panchayat on Saturday (December 27, 2025). She received 17 votes out of the 27 votes cast, while United Democratic Front (UDF)’s Meera (Congress) , representing the Thalavoor division, secured 10 votes.
District Collector N. Devidas, serving as the returning officer, administered the oath of office. The ceremony, held at the district panchayat hall, was attended by the president’s husband and Minister G.R. Anil, Minister for Animal Husbandry and Dairy Development J. Chinchurani, and CPI(M) district acting secretary S. Jayamohan. Also present were former presidents P.K. Gopan and Sam K. Daniel, former Minister Mullakkara Ratnakaran, former Mayor Honey Benjamin, Additional District Magistrate G. Nirmal Kumar, district panchayat secretary Suresh Kumar and various political party leaders.
Kollam district panchayat president R. Latha Devi.
                                                            | Photo Credit: 
                                 C. SURESHKUMAR
During the afternoon session, S.R. Arun Babu [CPI(M)], representing the Neduvathur division, was sworn in as the vice-president and the oath of office was administered by the newly elected president. Mr. Arun Babu secured 17 votes, while his opponent, Varun Alappad (Congress) from the Kulasekharapuram division, received 10 votes.

title: Srisailam temple nets record online revenue of ₹73 lakh
summary: Srisailam temple sets record with ₹73 lakh online revenue from 12,000 transactions, enhancing devotee convenience and services.
content:
For the first time in its history, the Sri Bhramaramba Mallikarjuna Swamy temple at Srisailam achieved a record revenue of ₹73,19,314 through online sale of sevas and darshan tickets, on Friday (December 26).
In a joint statement here on Saturday, temple trust board chairman Pothugunta Ramesh Naidu and executive officer (EO) M. Srinivas Rao said the temple management had made available sparsha darshan, ₹300 athi sheegra darshan and ₹150 sheegra darshan tickets online, apart from 14 arjitha sevas. These can also be availed through Mana Mithra WhatsApp governance number 95523 00009, they said.
They said the record revenue came through 12,000 transactions done on a single day and through the sale of darshan tickets, laddu prasadams, arjitha abhishekams, arjitha sevas, donations, kesha kandanam (head tonsuring) and other tickets.
Similarly, ₹73,75,511 revenue was generated offline and the total revenue of the day stood at ₹1,46,94,825. “It is for the first time that such a large revenue was generated on a normal day,” they said, and added that the management made all arrangements to cater to the needs of the large number of devotees that visited the temple. The services of temple officials and voluntary service of Siva Sevaks was widely used to ensure hassle-free darshan to the pilgrims, they said.
The temple management appealed to the devotees to use the online services of the temple for their convenience. They had also opened several online registration help centres at key locations within the town.

title: CPDCL snaps power supply to Kanaka Durga temple in Vijayawada citing non-payment of ₹3.08 crore dues
summary: CPDCL temporarily cut power to Vijayawada's Kanaka Durga temple over ₹3.08 crore dues, later restoring supply after discussions.
content:
The Andhra Pradesh Central Power Distribution Company Limited (APCPDCL) has stopped power supply to the Sri Durga Malleswara Swamyvarla Devasthanam here citing non-payment of bills amounting to ₹3.08 crore.
It, however, restored power supply following discussions held by the temple officials on Saturday.
“Supply has been restored in and around the temple premises,” according to temple Executive Officer Seena Nayak.
The temple’s solar plant at Apparao Peta, near Pamula Kaluva, has been supplying 24 MW of power daily to the Andhra Pradesh electricity grid at no cost for the past two years. In return, the Electricity Department has been providing power free of cost to 10 designated services of the temple.
Recently, the department sought payment of bills for these services, prompting discussions to resolve the issue.
As per information, the temple management, despite multiple reminders, has allegedly not cleared the bills since February 2023, forcing officials to disconnect supply from the HT line.
Following discussions between the temple authorities and department officials, supply in and around the temple premises has been fully restored.
Considering the sentiments of devotees, the temple authorities have ensured power supply to essential services using backup generators.

title: Five IAS officers promoted to cadre of Secretary to Government in Andhra Pradesh
summary: Five IAS officers in Andhra Pradesh promoted to Secretary to Government cadre, effective January 1, 2026.
content:
The Andhra Pradesh government has promoted five IAS officers of the 2010 batch to the Super Time Scale (Level-14 in the Pay Matrix), equivalent to the Secretary to Government cadre, with effect from January 1, 2026. The officers promoted are Narayana Bharath Gupta, Amrapali Kata, J. Nivas, Gandam Chandrudu and Chadalawada Naga Rani.
Following the promotions, Dr. Narayana Bharath Gupta has been retained in his current post and re-designated as Commissioner of Collegiate Education and State Project Director (RUSA); Amrapali Kata will continue as Vice-Chairperson and Managing Director of the Andhra Pradesh Tourism Development Corporation; Gandam Chandrudu has been posted as Commissioner of Labour, relieving M.V. Seshagiri Babu of the full additional charge; Chadalawada Naga Rani will continue as Collector and District Magistrate of West Godavari district.

title: Visakha Steel General Hospital celebrates its 34th Formation Day
summary: Visakha Steel General Hospital marks its 34th Formation Day with awards, speeches, and recognition of healthcare excellence in Visakhapatnam.
content:
Visakha Steel General Hospital (VSGH) celebrated its 34th Formation Day at VSGH, Rashtriya Ispat Nigam Limited, in Visakhapatnam on Saturday (27 December, 2025). VSGH is a 160-bedded hospital serving employees of Visakhapatnam Steel Plant and their families.
RINL, Director (Commercial), G.V.N. Prasad graced the occasion as the chief guest while Dr. C.V. Rao, Interventional Cardiologist, CARE Hospital, Visakhapatnam attended as the Guest of Honour.
Dr. J.N. Sarangi, GM (M&HS), welcomed the gathering and highlighted recent initiatives to strengthen medical services and upgrade hospital infrastructure. He thanked doctors, paramedical staff, medical administration, and outsourcing staff for their dedicated service.
Addressing the gathering, Mr. Prasad appreciated the comprehensive healthcare services provided by the VSGH. He commended the hospital for conducting regular health awareness sessions and medical camps. He emphasised the importance of preventive healthcare and conveyed his best wishes to the entire VSGH team.
The Dr. Kuppachi Krishna Murthy Gold Medal for Best Doctor was awarded to Dr. Ravishankar A. Rao, DGM Medical, VSGH and Y. Lakshmi Prabhakar Gold Medal for Best Nurse was awarded to P. Rajeswari, Assistant Manager Nursing, VSGH.
On the occasion, Dr. C.V. Rao delivered a talk titled “Predict, Prevent, and Protect from ASCVD (Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease)”. Prizes were distributed to winners of various competitions conducted in connection with the Formation Day celebrations. Doctors, specialists, paramedical staff, medical administration, and outsourcing staff were present during the function.

title: Preacher Dhirendra Shastri using government aircraft kicks up a storm
summary: Dhirendra Shastri's arrival on a government plane sparks controversy as Congress questions public money misuse and police conduct.
content:
A video showing Bageshwar Dham head and spiritual preacher Dhirendra Shastri arriving in Chhattisgarh on a government aircraft, and an on-duty police officer touching his feet, has drawn sharp criticism from the Opposition Congress, which is questioning the alleged misuse of public money.
Mr. Shastri, accompanied by State Minister Guru Khushwant Saheb, arrived in Raipur on Thursday (December 25, 2025) for a religious discourse in Bhilai town of Durg district. The purported clip shows the two alighting from the aircraft and a police officer in uniform first saluting the minister and then removing his cap and shoes before proceeding to touch the religious preacher’s feet.
Congress spokesperson Sushil Anand Shukla questioned the government’s move to provide a plane for Mr. Shastri. “The government should issue a clarification on this matter. This is tantamount to looting the State treasury,” he said.
Mr. Shukla claimed that Dhirendra Shastri was not a religious leader of the Hindu community or of Sanatan Dharma. “He may be a storyteller or a self-proclaimed godman who performs rituals and spells, but he is neither a religious scholar nor the head of any recognised religious institution. His conduct and ideology are against the country’s composite culture. Hinduism and Sanatan Dharma work to unite people, while Dhirendra Shastri creates mutual animosity,” Mr. Shukla added.
Meanwhile, several social media users also criticised the government for sending the aircraft, alleging that the Minister’s trip to Satna, from where Mr. Shastri purportedly travelled to Raipur, was a way to sidestep protocol-related questions. Opinions were more divided regarding the police officer touching Shastri’s feet.
The Minister called the allegations baseless. He toldThe Hinduthat he had gone to Satna to attend a meeting. “The Congress does not have any issue, so they are levelling such allegations. They should not talk about misuse of public money after all the scams that surfaced during their rule,” he said.

title: No understanding with CPI(M), BJP and SDPI in local bodies, says Satheesan
summary: He says that anyone within Congress overlooked for chairperson posts in local bodies may say whatever they wish
content:
Leader of the Opposition V.D. Satheesan has said that while the United Democratic Front (UDF) may accept support from parties such as the Communist Party of India (CPI) and Twenty20, it does not want the backing of the Communist Party of India (Marxist) [CPI()M], Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), or Social Democratic Party of India (SDPI) in the election to the key posts in the local bodies.
“We have also instructed district units that anyone elected as local body chiefs with the support of these parties should resign immediately,” he told media persons here on Saturday. “Has any party in Kerala ever done that?” he asked.
He reiterated that the Congress selected chairperson candidates for local bodies strictly in accordance with party procedure. He said that anyone overlooked for the post may say whatever they wish.
Potential mayoral candidate and Kerala Pradesh Congress Committee general secretary Deepthy Mary Varghese had repeatedly alleged that the KPCC circular was violated in the selection of the mayoral candidate for Kochi Corporation.
Mr. Satheesan emphasised that while the Congress follows a democratic process in candidate selection, in the CPI(M) it is the party that makes the decision.

title: Family members scattered across draft SIR voter roll will be brought together, says Chief Electoral Officer
summary: Chief Electoral Officer assures families will be regrouped in polling stations after draft SIR voter roll dispersals.
content:
After the draft electoral roll under the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) was published in  the State on December 23, many families have found it hard to track down their own kin. This is because, on the roll, they are either scattered within the same polling station or across multiple stations. But if things pan out, these voters will be regrouped under the same polling stations.
According to election officials, such dispersals occurred primarily on account of the adjustments made to limit the number of voters to 1,200 per polling station in line with an Election Commission of India (EC) decision. The EC decision was meant to avoid long queues on polling days.
The situation where members of the same family being dispersed across polling stations or being listed  apart from each other in the same stationhas also made it difficult for political parties to examine the draft roll and track down voters, political parties informed Chief Electoral Officer (Kerala) Rathan U. Kelkar at the weekly political party meeting on SIR here on Saturday.
Mr. Kelkar said steps will be taken to regroup scattered members of such families under one polling station. “We will identify such people who are scattered and re-serialise and regroup them as a family under one polling station,” he said.
The EC has 25,468 polling stations in Kerala at present. With the voter population being limited to 1,200 per station, steps have been taken to add a little over 5,000 more polling stations.
Mr. Kelkar’s office is also preparing to publish the details of which voters have been transferred from one polling station to another as part of the rearrangement of polling stations.

title: CM Stalin inaugurates farm expo, projects worth ₹ 700 crore in Tiruvannamalai
summary: CM Stalin inaugurates a ₹700 crore agricultural expo in Tiruvannamalai, enhancing farmer knowledge and promoting advanced farming techniques.
content:
Chief Minister M.K. Stalin on Saturday inaugurated a two-day mega agricultural exhibition and projects worth over ₹ 700 crore in Tiruvannamalai town.
Addressing farmers and agricultural experts at the farm exhibition here, Mr. Stalin said that the farm exhibition will help farmers to know more about advance technologies available in the farm sector. Apart from farm equipment, the exhibition will also help them to learn about a new variety of seeds, farming methods, marketing techniques, food processing methods, and crop insurance.
The expo also features interactive sessions between farmers and farm experts under 13 different topics., enriching farmers. “In the past five years, the Tamil Nadu government has released water from Mettur dam on time for irrigation, benefiting around 20 lakh farmers in the State,” he said.
The Chief Minister said that a separate annual budget for agriculture was introduced by the Dravidian model of governance in 2021, highlighting the importance given to the farm sector by the DMK regime. Since then, five agriculture budgets have allocated ₹ 1.94 lakh crore. In fact, the farm budget for 2024-25 has a budget allocation of ₹ 45,661 crore, which is 33% higher than the 2021-22 farm budget.
The Chief Minister said that Uzhavar Santhais (farmers’ markets) were given a facelift. In the past five years, 125 refurbished farmers’ markets and 14 new farmers’ markets were also opened in the State to help small farmers sell their produce directly to consumers.
In terms of crop damage, Mr. Stalin said that ₹ 631.76 crore has been compensated for 20.84 lakh farmers for crop damage of 32.81 lakh acre since 2021. During 2024-25, 5.66 lakh acres of farmland were damaged due to the northeast monsoon for which the Tamil Nadu government has released ₹ 289.63 crore as compensation for 3.60 lakh affected farmers in the State. He also added that assessment is being made for crop loss for the 2025 season.
The Chief Minister announced that the existing dilapidated rented building of the paddy procurement centre in Peranamallur village near Vandavasi will get a permanent building at a cost of ₹3 crore. The new building will have a capacity to store 500 metric tonnes of grain with common rooms for farmers to rest.
Deputy Speaker of Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly, K. Pitchandi, Minister for Public Works E.V. Velu, Minister for Agriculture and Farmer’s Welfare M.R.K. Panneerselvam, Minister for School Education Anbil Mahesh Poyyamozhi, and Tiruvannamalai Collector K. Tharpagaraj were present on the occasion.

title: Improving organ donor risk mapping and traceability
summary: Human rabies has been an escalating public health challenge in Kerala, sparking risks of donor-derived infections
content:
Three weeks ago, the US Centres for Disease Control (CDC) reported that a kidney transplant recipient had contracted rabies and died 51 days post transplant and that the infection had been traced back to the organ donor.
This is a rare incident and CDC says that since 1978, there have been four organ donors through whom 13 recipients developed rabies.
In Kerala, where deceased donor organ donation programme is still in a nascent stage, this has sparked conversations about the risk of donor-derived infections that evade routine screening and the adequacy of current organ donor screening protocols
The concerns are all the more relevant because in Kerala, where over three lakh animal bites are reported annually, human rabies has been an escalating public health challenge in recent years.
The Transplantation of Human Organs and Tissues Act, 1994, mandates that every organ donor — living or deceased — must be medically evaluated before organs are retrieved, and that there should be a thorough review of the donor’s medical and social history, including travel history, any potential exposure to animals (recent bites/scratches, contact with wildlife) and any symptoms of encephalitis of unknown origin, says Noble Gracious, executive director, K-SOTTO.
No nation specifically mandates rabies testing for all donors because human-to-human transmission of rabies is rare. India has not reported any such cases so far, though literature shows that there have been two instances of rabies in recipients following corneal grafts.
“There are clear screening protocols and donors are tested for systemic viral infections, alongside mandatory tests for HIV, Hepatitis A, B and C, syphilis and Cytomegalovirus. Donor evaluation also requires epidemiological history, clinical assessment to identify risks like animal exposure or unexplained fever or encephalitis. Among exclusion criteria for organ donation are active malignant disease or a history of malignancy that poses a high risk of infection. We also manage to do ultrasound scan, chest Xray and CT scan of donors,” Dr. Gracious says.
Donor risk mapping or screening and donor traceability are keys to safe, ethical and effective organ transplantation and it is directly linked to patient safety, transplant outcomes and the public trust in the organ transplantation programme.
Kerala, as it moves for an expanded organ transplant programme and a dedicated organ transplantation institute, will need to pay more attention to these aspects.
“Apart from the regulatory aspects, donor traceability is critical to the clinical outcomes of a transplant and just as CDC did, we need to be able to trace back if any post-transplant infection, malignancy or any disease that the organ recipient might develop in the long run is possibly linked to the donor.
As for donor risk mapping, I think we need to go much beyond the basic donor screening tests that we are doing at  present to ensure the absolute safety of recipients. However, there are huge operational challenges involved, especially with regard to the high donor evaluation and maintenance costs, which we are still trying to surmount, so that we can expand the panel of screening tests,” Dr. Gracious says.
The law says that donor families should not be burdened by the costs of donor screening and maintenance and that the expenses must be borne by the recipients, institutions or the government.
“We have to begin the screening tests when we identify a potential organ donor in the ICU. There are instances when after brain death certification, the donor becomes ineligible for donation due to some medical reasons or the donation does not materialise because of lack of consent. The vexing question is, who will bear the huge expenses involved in donor screening and haemo-dynamic maintenance if the donation does not go through?,” asks a critical care expert in one of the private hospitals.
As the central agency in charge of coordinating the deceased donation, K-SOTTO feels that a corpus fund should be set up to cover the donor evaluation and maintenance costs, which the organ recipient or transplant hospitals should later reimburse K-SOTTO, after the donation goes through. This system is also one way to ensure that the operational costs do not stand in the way of hospitals in certifying brain death.

title: Assam Assembly elections fight for protecting 'swadesh', 'swajati': Himanta
summary: Assam's CM Himanta Biswa Sarma emphasizes upcoming elections as a fight to protect identity, culture, and community against external threats.
content:
Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma on Saturday (December 27, 2025) said that the upcoming Assembly elections will be a fight to protect 'swadesh' (nation) and 'swajati' (own community), along with the identity, land and culture of the people of the State.
Unrest unlimited: On the crisis in Bangladesh
BJP represents the last light of hope that will ensure that the State is not pushed into an abyss of darkness by infiltrators from Bangladesh, the Chief Minister said at the party's executive meeting in Guwahati.
"The forthcoming elections are not about hopes and aspirations. It is about dedicating oneself to the cause of protecting 'swadesh' and 'swajati'. I am sure people know that the BJP is their last hope. They will vote for us, and we will win this election," Mr. Sarma said.
He alleged that the "weakness of the Congress and its politics of polarisation" led to the gradual creation of "another civilisation which now has a 1.5 crore-strong population".
"In the 2011 Census, when we see the breakup of Hindus and Muslims, we find the latter comprise 34%, and if we exclude the 3% Muslims of Assamese origin, we find that infiltrators comprise 31%," he said.
There was no census in 2021 and when it happens in 2027, the population of Muslims of Bangladeshi origin is estimated to be around 40%.
"Some may say that all can coexist as our religion welcomes and includes all, but the recent developments in Bangladesh have shown us that they believe in exclusiveness," Mr. Sarma said.
The Chief Minister said that when Dipu Das can be burnt alive in Bangladesh, "the Assamese people can well imagine what the situation in the State will be after 20 years".
"During the last Eid in Dhubri, I had to go there when beef was thrown outside people's homes and the meat was openly consumed. In lower and central Assam, there have been instances of Hindu girls becoming victims of 'Love Jihad'. Assamese people are selling off their lands and shifting to towns and cities. These are issues that have endangered the Assamese identity," he added.
Referring to Siliguri's Chicken's Neck Corridor that connects the Northeast with the rest of India, Mr. Sarma said, "Who is there on either side? There are no Hindus but only those who have come from Bangladesh. When they have come is irrelevant. If there is a war between India and Bangladesh, who will these settlers support? Where does their loyalty lie?" he asked.
Mr. Sarma claimed that there is no other place where the population of the indigenous people has dipped to 60% of the total population.
"During my lifetime, I have seen the population of the infiltrators rise from 21% to nearly 40% and my children will find during their lifetime that the population of the Assamese community has come down to 30%," he added.
He accused the Left parties of spreading the narrative that Assam is the land of 'Sankar-Azan' (Vaishnav saint Sankardeva and Sufi saint Azan Fakir) but this is "wrong as it is the land of 'Sankar-Madhav' (referring to Sankardeva's illustrious disciple Madhavdeva)".
The CM asserted that the BJP will be the shining light for the people of Assam who see darkness ahead.
"We will have to fight relentlessly to protect our 'jati, mati and bheti' (community, land and roots)," he added.
"We will fight and definitely win. The legendary Ahom general Lachit Barphukan could defeat the Mughals when he was sick and we will defeat the forces that are threatening our identity, land and culture," Mr. Sarma added.
The Assamese are not weak or alone today as they have Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union Home Minister Amit Shah with them, he added.

title: SHANTI Act: What is still under centre’s control in India’s ‘open’ nuclear sector?
summary: With an aim to reach 100 GW nuclear capacity by 2047, SHANTI has allowed private players full entry into the sector
content:
“The opening of other sectors such as electricity to private parties have been very rewarding. We also have a goal to achieve Net Zero by 2030. Hence, we must move from traditional sources of energy to clean sources. Nuclear Power is Aatmanirbhar, clean and can provide 24x7 energy,” argued UnionMoS Dr. Jitendra Singhin Parliament.
Defending the drastic changes brought in the nuclear sector by the Sustainable Harnessing and Advancement of Nuclear Energy for Transforming India (SHANTI) Act, 2025, Dr. Singh stated that privatisation will ensure ‘cheaper power over time’ and ensure energy security. The Act, which replaces two laws - the Atomic Energy Act, 1962 and the Civil Liability for Nuclear Damage Act, 2010, has received the President’s assent on December 19 – a day afterParliament passed it.
My speech in Parliament today on the nuclear-related SHANTI Bill:https://t.co/12aEveoI0n
“One person can control mining, fuel fabrication, reactor operation and waste handling. This concentration of power with one entity is dangerous,” warned Congress MP Shashi Tharoor when the Bill was debated in the Lok Sabha, urging the Centre to send it to a select committee for further scrutiny. To no avail, each House debated and passed the Bill in a day on December 17-18
Here’s a look at how much of India’s nuclear sector is open to private players
Apart from any government company, any company (whether domestic or foreign), any joint venture or any person permitted by Centre, can apply for a single licence to - build, own, operate or decommission a nuclear power plant or reactor, fabricate, refine, enrich nuclear fuel. This licence can be used to import, export, store, transport nuclear fuel, any technology or software to be used for the above processes.
Only after safety authorisation, will they be permitted to undertake these activities. Upon application, Centre can extend, renew a company’s licence or safety authorisation for any period of time it deems necessary. It may also modify, suspend, cancel or curtail the duration of the licence. Centre also has the power to exempt any radioactive material or any radiation generating plant from safety authorisation.
“In May 2025, US President Donald Trump passed an executive order in which he stated that they (US) should enhance diplomatic pressure on countries for getting more business for their (US) nuclear reactor companies. Very surprisingly, the SHANTI Bill was bulldozed through Parliament last week,” says Dr. E.A.S Sharma, former Principal Adviser (Energy) The Hindu.
“And then, on December 19 (a day after Parliament passed SHANTI), Mr. Trump signed the National Defense Authorization Act, in which they (US) said India and other countries should be brought in alignment with US liability requirements. They don’t want to take any liability for a possible accident, which is attributable to their lapses, reactor design defects, use of substandard material.
U.S. President Donald Trump signs the National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) for fiscal year 2018 in the Roosevelt Room of the White House in Washington, D.C., U.S. on Tuesday, Dec. 12, 2017. Photo: Getty Images via AFP
With the entry of foreign reactors in Indian nuclear plants, he says that usage of different technologies will result in no standardisation in operation. Lamenting that India is moving further away from Dr. Homi Bhabha’s nuclear vision for India – indigenous core, reactors and fuel, he adds, “Imported fuel is very expensive. Uranium suppliers around the world have formed a monopoly, and they declare terms on the price”.
However, only Centre or wholly-owned government institution can deal in enrichment or isotopic separation of radioactive substance, management of spent fuel, production of heavy water. Mining of any land, seabed for uranium or thorium will also be carried out only by these government institutions and any mined substance will be under government control. They will not be sold, transferred, or otherwise disposed of unless the Centre permits it.
The fissile material, spent fuel, heavy water used in any nuclear process will remain under the surveillance and control of Central government. A national registry of radioactive substances will be maintained by Centre which can also inspect any consignments or plant for such substances to ensure its security.
Dr. Sharma counters this stating that Centre has allowed mining of nuclear materials through the years by weaking its mining laws. He explains, “Monazite – which is an ore for thorium, was banned from private mining, restricting it only to public sector like Indian Railroad Ltd. However, Dr. Manmohan Singh, in UPA-I, came under pressure and allowed sand mining by private players but not monazite. The problem is when you mine beach sands minerals, monazite will be present. So, they (Centre) set the the permissible limit at 0.5%. All of it (monazite) must be kept under surveillance of Department of Atomic Energy”.
Beach sand minerals, also called rare earth, comprise a suite of seven minerals — garnet, sillimanite, rutile, ilmenite, leucoxene, zircon and monazite. File
                                                            | Photo Credit: 
                                The Hindu
Inspite of being under ‘surveillance’ of the Centre, Dr. Sharma cites several instances when monazite wassmuggled by private playersin Odisha, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu. In February this year, Madras High Court ordered a CBI probe after finding massive illegal mining of monazite with the “collusion, corruption and connivance” among politicians, the executive and the private miners.
“The Department of Atomic Energy staff is limited and all that there is no surveillance, so some of these private miners have been quietly smuggling out monazite. In 2019, all private mining of beach sands were banned. But in 2021, the NDA government amended the Mines and Minerals Development Regulations Act (MMDRA) to permit private mining in beach sands and soon Adani applied to mine sands in Odisha and Andhra Pradesh. With SHANTI, they claim that no mining for nuclear materials will be allowed, but using MMDRA such minerals can be mined and problems of smuggling will persist,” says Dr. Sharma.
Even the spent fuel which will remain under Centre’s surveillance is not feasible due to its limited manpower, opines Dr. Sharma.
The most troublesome aspect of SHANTI is section 39 which gives Centre the authority to declare ‘any information’ as restricted, giving it a blanket exemption from Right to Information (RTI). The information which it can restrict includes – location, design, construction, operation of nuclear reactors, processing and extraction of nuclear materials, research on such materials and any proposed plants to be operated. No one is allowed to publish any of the information deemed restricted by the Centre.
While Dr. Sharma agrees that some information should be restricted from the public, he points out that private players will now have access to it, which was not the case when only NPCIL was India’s sole nuclear operator.
“Private players will now know how much fuel is processed, how much fissionable material, heavy water is used, but civilians will not know. Once you allow private players, anybody (even a foreign agency) can become a partner with that private firm, and access this information. We won’t even know which foreign agency is a partner of this private company.”
Highlighting the need for civilians to know about spent fuel stored in their vicinity, he warns, “Nuclear waste is highly radioactive and it does not lose its radioactivity for decades. So wherever you store it, it will be a threat to people’s health and endangers their lives. Even a low radiation from (nuclear waste or stored spent fuel) can cause cosmogenic diseases among people”.
With an aim to reach 100 GW nuclear capacity by 2047, Dr. Singh claimed that India’s nuclear sector needed rapid expansion which was possible only via private players. Touting nuclear energy as a clean source, he said it would “provide better cancer treatment & diagnostics, safer food preservation, clean drinking water, improved agriculture and reliable supply for India’s growing AI, data centres, hospitals and industries”.
Decrying rapid nuclear sector expansion, Dr. Sharma says, “Groundwater around nuclear power plants too face radioactive contamination. Even in case a nuclear plant needs to be decommissioned after an accident, it cannot be done immediately due to radioactivity. The government has not taken people, parliament into confidence. Everything is one-sided, and driven by business interests”.

title: Yaduveer takes objection to using building constructed to house passport office for private purposes
summary: Mysuru MP Yaduveer objects to the misuse of a passport office building for private purposes, demanding immediate investigation and action.
content:
Yaduveer Krishnadatta Chamaraja Wadiyar, Mysuru MP, has taken serious exception to using the government building constructed to house the passport office in Ittigegudu for private purposes.
In a press statement here on December 27, Mr. Yaduveer said it had come to his notice that the building, constructed by Mysuru Development Authority, has not been used for the intended purpose for several years.
Instead, it has been handed over to private individuals or institutions, he said, while pointing out that it was an “extremely serious and illegal matter”.
Making it clear that there will be no compromise whatsoever on the matter, the Mysuru MP said he will bring the issue to the notice of the Ministry concerned and seek appropriate action.
