The problem, according to senior officials in the Fisheries Engineering Department, is unique to this specific stretch of the deltaic coast. Experts point to the Vennar Basin to be the reason. As the river discharges sediment into the sea, the shallow gradient of the shelf — where one must travel nearly 1 km into the sea to reach a depth of even 3 metres — prevents the silt from being washed away.
Between June and September, the littoral drift moves this soil from south to north, depositing a thick layer of fine clay that lacks the structural integrity to support weight. “It is a peculiar phenomenon not seen any where on the delta coast,” a senior official said. “We tried to build a breakwater at Vellapallam, but the earth simply swallowed it,” he recalled.
For the women who manage the logistics on the shore, the delay is devastating. T. Jeyaeswari of Vanavan Mahadevi and Vijayakumari S. of Pushpavanam point out that lack of a functional landing centre forces them to carry heavy loads across the sinking clay, often resulting in physical injuries.
The scale of the crisis is best reflected in the ₹132-crore project at Vellapallam. Despite nearly ₹100 crore being spent and 80% of the work completed, the project is in jeopardy. Roughly 70% of the massive breakwater stones — some weighing several tonnes — have simply sunk to the seabed.
A revised estimate for an additional ₹100 crore has been submitted to the government, but as the bureaucracy deliberates, the sea continues to swallow the huge stones. In Pushpavanam, a ₹25-crore small fishing harbour remains a proposal on paper. In Vanavan Mahadevi, where 450 families await a fish landing centre, a foundation stone was laid with much fanfare, but not a single brick has been laid.
“The government thinks building a harbour is the only solution,” says Jones T. Spartegus, a prominent researcher and coastal activist. “But they are ignoring the ecological reality. Since 2014, our policies have shifted heavily towards “culture fishing” (aquaculture) over “capture fishing” (traditional sea fishing). We have stopped the basic maintenance that kept these villages alive.”
Mr. Spartegus said in previous decades, bar-mouth dredging was done periodically. The silky soil would be dredged and deposited on the opposite side of the shore to maintain a natural balance.
A senior Fisheries Department official said that if the revised estimate is sanctioned, sand movement can be arrested by constructing a more effective breakwater.

title: State govt. committed to developing cooperative sector, says Minister
summary: Minister Satish Jarkiholi emphasizes the state government's commitment to strengthening the cooperative sector for rural economic development.
content:
The State government is committed to developing the cooperative sector, which is the backbone of the rural economy, Minister Satish Jarkiholi said in Belagavi on Sunday.
He was speaking at the silver jubilee celebrations of the Karnataka Rajya Souharda Samyukta Sahakari Federation at the KLE Society BS Jirge Hall.
Addressing the meeting from the S.S. Patil podium, he said that the State government will formulate policies and rules in consultation with members of cooperatives.
“I will try to resolve various issued raised by cooperatives by arranging a meeting of cooperative leaders with Chief Minister Siddaramaiah,” he said.
“The contribution of the cooperative sector to the country’s economy is invaluable. Cooperatives have spread to all sectors and cooperative societies have become multi-service centers in support of rural development. Currently, these cooperative societies are moving towards a lot of profit and more such cooperatives should be added to our district,” he said.
“Now-a-days, cooperative societies are not just limited to offering cash and credit-based services. Several societies are offering product-based services, like joint purchase of farm inputs like seeds and fertilisers, distribution of equipment and procurement of farm produce from producers, food processing, value addition, building common customer base and sale assistance. Such activities have increased the confidence of the people. It is an encouraging development,” he said.
“Today, the cooperative sector has received recognition and special attention is being paid to strengthening the agricultural sector and the development of farmers. It is becoming very difficult for people to get loans, especially from nationalised banks. However, cooperative societies are working to deliver money at their doorsteps. May such cooperative societies grow even more,” he said.
Satish Jarkiholi inaugurated an exhibition organised by the federation.
Minister Lakshmi Hebballar said that she believed that serving in the cooperative sector is equal to serving God.
“We have seen that the cooperative sector is improving the economy of the last person in society. The Souharda institutions are working hard for the economic prosperity of the poor. Many poor people and soldiers have deposited their salary money in the bank and it is our responsibility to ensure that such poor families are not treated unfairly,” he said.
KLE Society chairman Prabhakar Kore spoke against the trends of governments trying to take over cooperative institutions and exert increasing control over the sector.
“The cooperative sector that started 120 years ago has witnessed tremendous growth till now. Even now, the cooperative movement is alive due to the dedicated efforts of several cooperators,” he said.
MLA Laxman Savadi said that nine out of 10 Souharda cooperative institutions are functioning properly.
“We should all focus on the task of developing the lives of the poor. Let us all work hard within the scope of the cooperative sector for the development of the rural poor and farmers. We need to look back on the achievements of the cooperative sector in the last 25 years and move forward,” he said. He appreciated the efforts of the former Minister for Cooperation S.S. Patil.
G. Nanjanagowda presided over the programme.
The former MLC Mahantesh Kavatagimat, BJP MP Jagadish Shettar, MLA Asif (Raju) Seth, the former Minister S.S. Patil, federation director Jagadish Kavatagimat, regional manager Basavaraj Hongala, the former President Manohar Maski, leaders S.R. Satishchandra, H.V. Rajiv, U.H. Ramappa, C.N. Parasivamurthy, Anoop Deshpande, Vishwanath Hiremath, Gurunath Janthikar, B.H. Krishna Reddy, Sachin Patil, A.R. Prasannakumar, Sharanagouda G. Patil and Deputy Registrar of Cooperative Societies Ravindra Patil and others were present.

title: Seven of inter-State gang arrested for ATM theft using shutter tampering trick in Warangal
summary: Seven-member inter-State gang arrested in Warangal for ATM theft using shutter tampering technique, recovering ₹5.10 lakh in cash.
content:
The Warangal Police have unearthed a new modus operandi involving attention diversion and tampering of ATM cash dispenser shutters to steal money, with the arrest of a seven-member inter-State gang at Kazipet on Sunday.
According to Central Zone DCP Kavitha, the accused targeted specific ATMs  by inserting steel plates behind the cash dispenser shutters, blocking the cash from being dispensed.
“While customers received debit alerts indicating successful withdrawals, no cash came out of the machines. After the customers left the ATM premises assuming a technical fault, the accused re-entered using duplicate keys and retrieved the cash trapped inside the dispenser,” she added.
The gang was arrested in connection with a case registered at Kazipet police station and cash amounting to ₹5.10 lakh was recovered, along with two cars, iron blades, duplicate keys and seven mobile phones.
The arrested accused were identified as Areef Khan (23), Sarfaraj Khan (24), Aas Mahmood (29), Shakun Khan (33), Aslam Khan (33), Sharukh Khan (27) and Sameer Khan (23), all hailing from Alwar district of Rajasthan and engaged in various occupations including driving, farming and mechanical work.
Police said accused no. 1 to 4 were habitual offenders who had formed a gang after being trained in Rajasthan by a person who previously worked with an ATM maintenance company. They selectively targeted ATMs maintained by a particular private company, using iron plates to block the cash dispenser shutters. After security measures were enhanced in Rajasthan, the gang shifted operations to several States.
During November and December, the gang moved to Warangal district and resumed operations within the limits of Kazipet, Subedari, Hanmakonda and Mills Colony police stations, the DCP said.  Early on Sunday, when the gang had attempted to repeat the offence at an SBI ATM in Kazipet, they were nabbed.

title: Entry of multi-axle vehicles restricted on Thamarassery pass during daytime
summary: Daytime restrictions on multi-axle vehicles at Thamarassery pass aim to prevent traffic jams and ensure emergency vehicle access.
content:
The entry of multi-axle vehicles and heavy goods carriers on the Thamarassery pass will be restricted for at least a week as part of measures initiated by the Thamarassery police to prevent traffic bottlenecks on the mountain road. The restrictions will be in force during daytime hours until further notice.
According to the police, multi-axle vehicles will be diverted through the Kuttiyadi pass as part of the traffic regulations. They said the upcoming New Year celebrations were also a factor behind the decision to regulate the movement of heavy vehicles on the ghat road.
The police said a rise in the number of multi-axle vehicles had led to recurring traffic snarls on the route, hampering the movement of emergency vehicles. There were also instances in which the free passage of escort vehicles was affected.
Officers from Thamarassery police station said immediate legal action would be taken against violations of lane discipline and illegal parking. They also cited complaints of rash driving and speeding by tourist vehicles.
Members of the Thamarassery ghat road protection committee said a dedicated recovery van was needed to respond quickly to rescue calls. They pointed out that the absence of crane services often forced other road users to wait for hours.
Members of various voluntary organisations also called for the launch of an exclusive emergency rescue service for the mountain pass, citing incidents that had stalled traffic on the inter-district route for hours. They said the entry of multi-axle vehicles should be banned at least until 10 p.m.
Meanwhile, local administrators demanded the widening of the sixth, seventh and eighth hairpin curves on the route. They said the diversion of heavy vehicles via the Kuttiyadi pass should continue until the widening works are completed.

title: BLO’s body found in Bengal, work-related pressure alleged; SIR anxiety claimed over 50 lives: TMC
summary: BLO found dead in Bengal amid work pressure; TMC alleges over 50 lives lost due to electoral roll anxiety.
content:
A Booth Level Officer (BLO) was found dead inWest Bengal's Bankura district on Sunday (December 28, 2025), triggering allegations that work-related pressure linked to the ongoingSpecial Intensive Revision (SIR)of electoral rolls may have played a role, police said.
The incident occurred in Ranibandh block, where the body of the deceased, Haradhan Mandal, was recovered from a school premises on Sunday (December 28, 2025) morning. The police said they found a a note left back by the deceased.
Accusing the BJP of “bulldozing” the SIR process, TMC national general secretary Abhishek Banerjee alleged that over 50 lives have been lost "to panic, anxiety, exhaustion and fear engineered by a voter-cleansing operation designed for BJP's electoral gain".
"Mandal was a schoolteacher by profession and served as the BLO of Booth No. 206 under the Rajakata area of Ranibandh block," a police officer said.
According to the officer, a note bearing the deceased's signature was recovered from the spot, in which he reportedly referred to being unable to cope with work pressure as a BLO.
"We have seized the note and sent the body for post-mortem examination," he said.
The police initiated an investigation to ascertain the circumstances leading to Mandal's death. Officials said all angles are being examined.
Abhishek Banerjee, in an X post, accused the BJP of “bulldozing” the SIR process.
"The death toll keeps mounting as another BLO appointed and engaged by the @ECISVEEP has taken his own life under the inhuman pressure of a hurried, chaotic and politically motivated SIR process,” he claimed.
Alleging that the BLO killed himself, Mr. Banerjee claimed that Mandal, in the note, held the “inhuman nature of the task” responsible for his decision.
“What should have been a methodical process has instead been bulldozed through by a pliant, complicit Election Commission, bending its spine to serve the political arithmetic of one party and the ego of one man,” he said.
“And as for the BJP, if people drop dead from fatigue, despair or terror, it is an acceptable collateral cost, a convenient footnote in their power play," Mr. Banerjee, the de facto number two in the TMC hierarchy, said in the X post.
West Bengal will neither forgive nor forget, he said, adding: “History is watching.”
The SIR exercise began in the state on November 4.
(Assistance for overcoming suicidal thoughts is available on the State’s health helpline 104, Tele-MANAS 14416, and Sneha’s suicide prevention helpline 044-24640050)

title: Kiran Uppar seeks BJP ticket from West Graduates segment in Council polls
summary: Kiran Uppar, BJP youth leader, seeks party ticket for Karnataka West Graduates Constituency in upcoming Legislative Council polls.
content:
BJP youth leader Kiran Uppar, who is an architect by profession, has said that he is an aspirant for BJP ticket in the elections to the Legislative Council from the Karnataka West Graduates Constituency.
Addressing presspersons along with his well-wishers in Hubballi, Mr. Uppar said that he has been committed to rendering public service from his college days working closely with students and youth leaders.
He has contributed to the twin cities in his own way through Colour My City Foundation which focuses on city beautification, government school improvement, cleanliness drives and inclusive civic initiatives, he said.
His friend and co-founder and CEO of AkashX, Kartik Kulkarni, emphasised the need for giving opportunities to youngsters in politics as they brought with them new ideas towards development.

title: IUML chooses SC woman as Malappuram district panchayat vice-president
summary: IUML elects SC woman A.P. Smiji as Malappuram district panchayat vice-president, marking a significant political shift.
content:
MALAPPURAM
The Indian Union Muslim League (IUML) created a political surprise by electing a Scheduled Caste (SC) Hindu woman to the general seat position of vice-president in the Malappuram district panchayat.
A.P. Smiji is the daughter of former district panchayat president A.P. Unnikrishnan.
P.A. Jabbar Haji was elected president of the district panchayat. The United Democratic Front (UDF) faces no opposition in the council, having won all 35 divisions.
The name of Ms. Smiji, a lawyer by profession, was announced by IUML State president Syed Sadikali Shihab Thangal.
Ms. Smiji was elected from the Tanalur division of the Malappuram district panchayat by a margin of 6,852 votes.

title: Organisations seek withdrawal of PD Act against farmers’ leader
summary: Roundtable meeting demands withdrawal of PD Act against farmers’ leader Appala Raju and protection for Imanuru villagers.
content:
Various organisations have demanded the immediate withdrawal of the Preventive Detention (PD) Act invoked against farmers’ leader M. Appala Raju and sought his unconditional release from prison. They also urged the authorities to withdraw what they described as “false cases” filed against tribal residents of Imanuru village in Eluru district and to ensure their protection.
These demands were made at a roundtable convened by farmers’, workers’, agricultural labourers’, and mass organisations here on Sunday. Speakers at the meeting accused the State government of siding with anti-social elements while suppressing those questioning land acquisitions and corporate interests. Criticising both the Centre and the State, they alleged that the TDP-led government headed by Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu was violating laws by targeting farmers and fishermen protesting against policies that threatened their livelihoods.
Andhra Pradesh Rythu Sangham State secretary K. Prabhakar Reddy chaired the meeting. Former Minister Vadde Shobhanadreeswara Rao, Supreme Court advocate Potturu Suresh Kumar, senior High Court advocate Sunkara Rajendra Prasad, and former MP P. Madhu condemned what they called the misuse of the PD Act against Mr. Appala Raju, general secretary of the Anakapalli District Rythu Sangham. They said the law, intended to deal with criminals and smugglers, was being wielded against a leader defending the rights of farmers and fishermen.
Leaders of the All India Lawyers’ Union announced their plans to challenge Mr. Appala Raju’s detention in higher courts and pledged to extend continued legal and organisational support. Agricultural Workers’ Union State general secretary V. Venkateswarlu demanded the withdrawal of cases against the Imanuru tribals and called for adequate protection for them.
Representatives from CITU, SKM, AIKMS, KVPS, Jagruti Rythu Sangham, and AIDWA strongly condemned what they termed authoritarian measures and vowed to continue their struggle until justice is delivered and Mr. Appala Raju is released.

title: BRS ready to debate its 10-year rule in Assembly: MLA KP Vivekanand
summary: BRS is set to debate its 10-year rule and address Congress government's failures in the upcoming Assembly session.
content:
Quthbullapur MLA and BRS Whip K.P. Vivekanand on Sunday said the Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) was prepared to debate both the two-year rule of the Congress government and the 10-year tenure of former Chief Minister K. Chandrashekhar Rao in the Assembly. He said the party would question the government’s handling of the Palamuru–Ranga Reddy Lift Irrigation Scheme  (PRLIS) and its alleged tendency to bypass the promised six guarantees.
Addressing a press conference at the Assembly, Mr. Vivekanand said that the main Opposition would strongly raise issues concerning what he termed the failures of the Congress government during the forthcoming Assembly session beginning on December 29.
The MLA said the BRS would also highlight issues related to the management of residential educational institutions, particularly the deaths of students in Gurukuls. He said the party strongly opposed the merger of 22 municipalities into the Greater Hyderabad Municipal Corporation (GHMC), alleging that the move was unscientific and carried out without public consultation.
He said the BRS would raise concerns over what he termed bogus bonuses announced for farmers and the government’s failure to address farmer suicides, which he attributed to a shortage of urea.
The BRS leader said the party would also hold the government accountable for the alleged misuse of Singareni Collieries Company Ltd (SCCL) funds for organising a football match involving international player Lionel Messi at Uppal stadium.

title: Civil Aviation Ministry’s 24x7 control room seeks to address passengers’ issues promptly
summary: The Civil Aviation Ministry's 24x7 control room swiftly addresses passenger grievances, ensuring timely resolutions and improved travel experiences.
content:
To address air travellers' grievances more promptly, the Civil Aviation Ministry has set up the Passenger Assistance Control Room (PACR) that functions round-the-clock to resolve the issues.
Officials from the Ministry, Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA), airlines and Airports Authority of India (AAI), are among those working at the centre, which monitors operations, attends to passenger calls and coordinates real-time assistance.
The PACR or the control room was operationalised on December 10 in the wake of the operational disruptions at IndiGo. Besides, there have been flight disruptions and delays due to fog and other issues.
Elaborating on the control room, Civil Aviation Secretary Samir Kumar Sinha said there has been a marked improvement in grievance redressal and there has been a positive response from air passengers and other stakeholders.
According to the Ministry, air travellers grievances raised through various channels are being addressed through the PACR in the national capital, allowing timely resolution through close coordination with airline representatives.
In a statement, Mr. Sinha said the collaborative approach ensures timely information dissemination, effective facilitation and prompt grievance redressal.
"Over 13,000 passenger grievances, received through AirSewa, social media and call channels, have been resolved, with cases expedited and prioritised through close monitoring at the Passenger Assistance Control Room (PACR)," he said.
During a visit to the PARC on Sunday afternoon, some of the people who are part of the control room shared their experience.
The complaints vary from flight cancellations to lost baggage to even meal not being served onboard.
IndiGo's Director Customer Experience Pratik Arjun Sen said there is a mixed bag of queries from passengers and the grievances are sought to be resolved at the earliest.
Since the disruptions earlier this month, the customer experience team has been working hard to address the issues, including ticket refunds, and there has been a significant improvement, he noted.
Ajeet Tiwari, Assistant Manager of Operations at SpiceJet, said flight delays are among the grievances flagged by passengers and at the centre, the work flow is smooth with issues getting addressed.
Lisa Agarwal, who is part of the Customer Happiness Team at Air India Express, said the grievances include those related to lost or damaged baggage, meal not being served onboard a flight.
The grievances are sought to be resolved within 72 hours of receiving them, she added.
Akasa Air's Senior Customer Service Agent Shahbaj Alam mentioned the queries are mainly related to service issues as well as flight cancellations and ticket refunds, and at the centre, the airline gets at least 15-16 queries daily.
Ravneet Kaur, an official with the ministry, said the enquiries are mainly about ticket refunds and lost baggage, and the grievances are looked into promptly.
All of them are working at the centre, which is operational 24x7.
In the statement, Sinha said issues such as frequent flight delays, inadequate or delayed refunds, long queues, poor passenger facilities at airports, and incidents of lost baggage have continued to affect passenger experience across the aviation ecosystem.
"These concerns highlighted the need for a structured, systematic, and coordinated response rather than ad-hoc interventions," he added.

title: Messi Kolkata event chaos: Court extends police custody of chief organiser till January 9
summary: Court extends police custody of Messi event organiser Satadru Dutta amid allegations of mismanagement and financial misconduct until January 9.
content:
A court in West Bengal on Sunday (December 28, 2025) extended till January 9 the police custody of Satadru Dutta, the chief organiser of Argentine footballer Lionel Messi's event that dissolved into disorder earlier this month.
After the completion of his initial police custody, Mr. Dutta was produced before the Bidhannagar Sub-Divisional Court, where public prosecutors levelled multiple charges against him.
Mr. Dutta, who was arrested on December 13 over alleged mismanagement in the Salt Lake stadium event on that day, was also accused of entering into contracts with food and beverage suppliers without prior government approval and being involved in alleged corruption amounting to Rs 23 crore.
The prosecution emphasised that Mr. Dutta wields significant influence, and for this reason, he should not be granted bail.
"The investigation requires further probe into the financial transactions and pre-planned arrangements for the event. His bail plea was rejected, and he (Dutta) was sent to police custody till January 9," a senior police officer told reporters outside the court.
Mr. Dutta was seen entering the courtroom holding a copy of the Gita.
His bail plea, moved by his counsel, was opposed by the prosecution, which described the incident as pre-planned and alleged that Mr. Dutta was the main person behind the alleged mismanagement.
The police informed the court that a contract for supplying food and beverages at the stadium had been finalised even before discussions were held with the administration for arrangements during Messi's programme.
According to the police, the official food and beverage contract value stood at ₹40 lakh while Mr. Dutta allegedly received ₹60 lakh in cash.
It was also stated that tickets worth around ₹19 crore were sold for the event, with over 34,000 tickets purchased.
The police told the court that Messi left the field within 20 minutes of the programme, alleging that this too was part of a pre-planned sequence.
The police also pointed out that while professional sports event management companies were engaged for Messi events in three other cities, no such company was appointed for the Kolkata programme, a decision that has now come under scrutiny.
What was supposed to be a marquee football spectacle turned into widespread violence and disorder at the stadium on December 13 after Messi’s brief and tightly ring-fenced appearance, his first at the venue since 2011, left large sections of the crowd frustrated.
Angry fans, many of whom had paid ₹4,000 to ₹12,000 — and in some cases up to ₹20,000 in the black market — ran riot at the venue after failing to get even a glimpse of their favourite superstar from Argentina.

title: Campaign to settle unclaimed bank assets
summary: ‘Ningalude Panam Ningalude Avakasham’ (Your Money, Your Right) will be held on December 29 from 10.30 a.m. at Hotel Nani in Kollam
content:
In order to identify the rightful owners of unclaimed bank deposits in the district, a special campaign titled ‘Ningalude Panam Ningalude Avakasham’ (Your Money, Your Right) will be held on December 29 from 10.30 a.m. at Hotel Nani in Kollam.
Organised by the Department of Financial Services (DFS) under the Ministry of Finance, the event will be inaugurated by District Collector N. Devidas and aims to return funds from accounts that have remained inactive for over 10 years.
Currently, the district holds approximately ₹147.03 crore in unclaimed deposits across 6.63 lakh accounts. District lead bank authorities have said that attendees can check for any deposits owed to them at the camp, where they will receive guidance on the necessary documentation to prove ownership. If the required documents are provided, facilities will be available to help claimants secure their money. Following the camp, assistance centres will also be set up at major banks for further support. For more information, the public may contact 9447905980.

title: Eight test positive for drugs at concert in Cyberabad
summary: Eight drug consumers were detected at a Cyberabad concert during a joint anti-drug operation by the Telangana EAGLE Force.
content:
Eight persons were found to have consumed drugs during a joint anti-drug operation conducted by the Telangana EAGLE Force along with the Cyberabad Police at a concert held at Quake Arena on December 27.
The individuals were identified as Trisha (22), Mohan (23), Shravan (26) Riyaz (26), Sabrina (27), Vishal (27), Yashwanth (28), and Bharath (35). The concert featured Ukrainian artiste Artbat and was held amid heightened vigilance ahead of the New Year festivities.
According to an official statement from the EAGLE Force, the operation was launched based on specific intelligence that drug consumers were likely to attend the event. Surveillance was mounted well in advance and preventive checks were carried out at the venue using drug testing kits sourced from international medical technology firms.
Fourteen persons were screened during the operation, of whom eight tested positive for drug consumption. Five of them admitted to consuming drugs, while three initially denied it. The police said re-testing using different equipment confirmed the results. All those who tested positive were already under the radar of the EAGLE Force.
Officials said that the operation was deliberately limited in scale to avoid disruption to public order, despite inputs suggesting a larger presence of drug users at the event. The action, they said, was part of a broader preventive strategy as the State steps up monitoring during the festive season.

title: Golden hour surgery at Palvancha CHC saves man who tried to end life
summary: Doctors at the Community Health Centre in Palvancha of Bhadradri Kothagudem district saved the life of a man who suffered a severe neck injury after attempting suicide.
content:
Doctors at the 50-bed Community Health Centre (CHC) in Palvancha of Bhadradri Kothagudem district saved the life of a man who had tried to end his life, highlighting the role of timely intervention at peripheral healthcare facilities.
The patient, a native of West Bengal who runs a noodle cart near the bus stand in Kothagudem, sustained a severe neck injury after attempting suicide due to personal issues around two weeks ago. Given the seriousness of the injury, he was supposed to be shifted to MGM Hospital-Warangal for advanced treatment.
While the patient was being transported, Ravi Babu, District Coordinator of Health Services (DCHS) of Bhadradri Kothagudem and an ENT surgeon, received information from the patient’s family. Acting swiftly, he intervened en route and decided to perform an emergency surgical procedure at the Palvancha CHC on December 9.
With the patient’s chances of survival appearing bleak, Dr. Ravi Babu, along with the Palvancha CHC staff, worked continuously for nearly two hours to stabilise him. “The surgery, which would ordinarily be carried out at a super-specialty hospital, was performed at the CHC during the critical golden hour. Following the procedure, the patient was shifted to the ICU at the Area Hospital, Bhadrachalam, for further observation and treatment,” said Dr. Ravi Babu.
After receiving round-the-clock care for two weeks, the patient was discharged on December 22.
Bhadradri Kothagudem District Collector Jitesh V. Patil described the incident as a reflection of strengthening public healthcare system in the district.
“The successful surgery demonstrated what government doctors are capable of when they receive encouragement and administrative support. Even in Agency areas, remarkable medical intervention is possible when doctors are motivated,” said Bhadrachalam MLA Tellam Venkata Rao.
(Roshni suicide prevention helpline: 8142020033/44 and 040-66202000/ 2001)

title: African cheetah at Mysuru zoo passes away
summary: Bruke, a six-year-old African cheetah at Mysuru zoo, dies from meningitis after battling health issues.
content:
Bruke, the African hunting cheetah at the Mysuru zoo, passed away on December 27. He was six years and eight months old when he succumbed at around 1.30 a.m., with the cause of death attributed to meningitis.
Anusha, executive director of Sri Chamarajendra Zoological Gardens, said that Bruke had been refusing food for three days before his demise and through veterinarians administered treatment, he did not respond.
Bruke was acquired from Anne Van Dyke Cheetah Centre, South Africa, on August 17, 2020.

title: 87.5% conviction rate achieved in red sanders smuggling cases in 2025: Tirupati SP
summary: Tirupati SP reports an 87.5% conviction rate in red sanders smuggling cases, highlighting successful inter-State operations and arrests.
content:
Red sanders smuggling, which is rampant in Seshachalam and Nallamala forests comprising Tirupati, Chittoor, Annamayya, Kadapa, Nellore, Prakasam and Nandyal districts, witnessed a sharp decline in the year 2025, while the conviction rate has improved significantly.
Interestingly, the Red Sanders Anti Smuggling Task Force (RSASTF) has also initiated attachment of properties of potential smugglers, and is currently devising a system to ensure its fool-proof implementation.
The year saw 32 cases being disposed of by courts, 25 convictions, four acquittals and three abated cases. “We achieved a conviction rate of 87.5%, the highest since the inception of RSASTF, which is attributed to quality investigation, timely filing of chargesheets and close coordination with prosecution,” said Superintendent of Police (SP) L. Subbarayudu
Addressing a media conference here on Saturday, along with Superintendent of Police (RSASTF) P. Srinivas, and Chief Conservator of Forest C. Selvam, he said the 10 most-wanted smugglers were arrested from Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and most vulnerable places like Katigenahalli, Sarjapura and Malur in Bengaluru and rural taluks.
The department also invoked Preventive Detention (PD) Act in two cases this year against notorious smugglers.
Several major inter-State operations were carried out in Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Gujarat and New Delhi, where precious logs worth ₹16.5 crore were seized. “We managed to disrupt long-distance smuggling routes and supply chains,” Mr. Subbarayudu said.
The department also issued 212 Non-Bailable Warrants (NBWs) and arrested 52 absconding criminals by continuously raiding their residences through geo-mapping.
Divisional Forest officers V. Sai Baba (Tirupati), K. Ramakonda Reddy (flying squad), Additional SP J. Kulasekhar, Deputy Superintendents V. Srinivasa Reddy and Md. Shareef (both RSASTF) and Assistant Conservator J. Srinivas took part.

title: Block panchayat member’s house allegedly attacked
summary: Block panchayat member Rajani Thekke Thayyil's house was allegedly attacked, with an unexploded bomb found on-site.
content:
An unidentified gang, allegedly comprising Communist Party of India (Marxist) workers, reportedly attacked the house of Rajani Thekke Thayyil, a member of Vadakara block panchayat, on Sunday (December 28). An unexploded steel bomb was reportedly recovered from the premises of the house following the incident.
According to police sources, Rajani’s accidental casting of a vote in favour of a United Democratic Front (UDF) candidate had helped UDF assume power in Vadakara block panchayat. The election ended in a tie, with the LDF and the UDF securing seven seats each.
Rajani, a Rashtriya Janata Dal activist who contested the election under the banner of the LDF, had been placed under suspension for six months following the accidental casting of a vote in favour of UDF candidate Kottayil Radhakrishnan. On Sunday, the police registered a case as part of the continuing investigation into the incident.

title: Congress will ensure 50% representation for women and youth in 2026 elections: Satheesan
summary: Congress in Kerala pledges 50% representation for women and youth in the 2026 elections, says Leader V.D. Satheesan.
content:
The Congress party in Kerala will ensure 50% representation for youth and women in the organisation as well as in candidate selection for the upcoming elections, Leader of the Opposition V.D. Satheesan has said. He said that senior Congress leader Rahul Gandhi had instructed the State unit to take measures to this effect.
“The implementation of steps for representation of youth and women does not mean that those from older generations will be asked to step back. The new generation should also have an opportunity. All of us came up that way. We cannot decide that no one should come after us. Women and the youth will definitely have more representation. That is the desire of the Congress national leadership. We will accept the advice and opinions of the senior leaders and also field those who can contest among them. No one will be left out,” said Mr. Satheesan.

title: A.H. Vishwanath decries “neglect” of Mysuru’s heritage, flags security lapses at palace
summary: A.H. Vishwanath criticizes the government's neglect of Mysuru's heritage and highlights security concerns at the palace after a tragic incident.
content:
Accusing the State government of neglecting Mysuru and its heritage, A.H. Vishwanath, MLC, expressed concern over security lapses around the palace following the helium gas cylinder explosion in which three persons died last week.
Speaking to media persons on December 28, the MLC said it is regrettable that though Chief Minister Siddaramaiah hails from Mysuru, he has not spoken a word on the issue nor convened a meeting to review the security arrangements around the palace. Mr. Vishwanath said such an attitude is an outcome of his general apathy towards all things related to Mysuru palace or the heritage of the city.
“This is not a small issue. The death of three persons near the palace should be treated as a warning bell or  wake-up call. There are glaring security issues as vendors without any identity or authorisation operate around the palace at will. One cannot rule out the possibility of any anti-social elements exploiting the security loophole and causing damage to the palace in the future,” said the MLC.
He said Mysuru is known for its heritage but the State government is apathetic towards conservation, and this is reflected in the absence of any policy in this regard. Many heritage structures known for their architectural fineness, including the old Deputy Commissioner’s office, are languishing in neglect, said Mr. Vishwanath.
Continued and unchecked commercial activity around the palace premises pose danger and a review meeting should be convened immediately to plug the security loopholes, he added. “The CCTV surveillance camera near the palace is not functional and is a pointer to the general apathy towards security measures,” the MLC noted.
Turning his criticism to the maintenance of Mysuru’s heritage structures, including the palace, the MLC said there is no accountability from the government, though the chief secretary of the State heads the Mysuru Palace Board. Similarly, the district in-charge Minister H.C. Mahadevappa is also indifferent to all things related to heritage and has not taken any interest in the subject, he added.
The Mysuru palace is like no other and is an irreplaceable monument with a collection of rare antiques that are integral to the State’s and country’s cultural history and heritage, said Mr. Vishwanath, who accused Mr. Siddaramaiah of “utter neglect” of heritage.
Calling for vetting the identity of vendors who operate around the palace, the MLC suggested issuing identity cards to them and providing them with a dedicated place from where they can sell their wares. Tourism, he said, was the backbone of Mysuru’s economy and should be regulated.
But owing to the Chief Minister’s lack of interest, and absence of any policy for conservation of heritage structures, Mysuru has become an eyesore and a slum city, said the MLC.

title: Coalition government neglecting temples, hurting Hindu sentiments, says YSRCP leader Malladi Vishnu
summary: YSRCP leader Malladi Vishnu criticizes coalition government for neglecting temples and hurting Hindu sentiments in Andhra Pradesh.
content:
YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) leader and former MLA Malladi Vishnu on Sunday (28 December, 2025) criticised the coalition government, alleging large-scale neglect in the management of temples across Andhra Pradesh and accusing it of hurting Hindu sentiments for political gains.
Speaking to the media at the YSR Congress Party central office in Tadepalli here on Sunday, Mr. Vishnu said that since the coalition government came to power, repeated incidents of mismanagement and sacrilege have taken place at major temples including Tirumala, Annavaram, and Kasibugga. He alleged that devotees feared for their safety when visiting temples because of administrative failures and inadequate basic arrangements.
The former MLA accused the Chandrababu Naidu-led government of politicising Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams (TTD) and turning a blind eye to repeated lapses, such as poor vigilance, improper management of goshalas and frequent incidents of cow deaths. He claimed that when YSRCP leaders questioned these issues, cases are being filed against them.
Mr. Vishnu also alleged that incidents of illegal cow slaughter and large-scale storage of beef, particularly around Visakhapatnam, were going unchecked under the coalition regime. He also cited incidents of stampedes, power outages at major temples and lack of coordination among departments as evidence of governance failure.
Contrasting this with the previous YSRCP government, he said several reforms were introduced to protect temple properties and improve administration. He asserted that people were openly expressing anger over the coalition government’s handling of temples and demanded immediate corrective measures to restore devotees’ trust.

title: Then a Harita Karma Sena volunteer, Rajani now helms a local body in Idukki
summary: Representing UDF, Ms. Rajani defeated CPI candidate Nisha Anish by a margin of 264 votes
content:
In an achievement that will be etched in the history of State’s local governance, Rajani K.A., a volunteer with the Haritha Karma Sena, has now entered the halls of power with her presidentship of Erattayar grama panchayat in Idukki.
Representing the United Democratic Front (UDF), Ms. Rajani contested from the Nalumukk ward, defeating Communist Party of India (CPI) candidate Nisha Anish by a margin of 264 votes. Following the UDF’s victory in nine out of 15 wards, the party leadership chose Ms. Rajani to lead the panchayat.
A touching gesture marked the transition from being a sanitation volunteer to leading the council. On Saturday (December 27), as she prepared to assume office, her former Haritha Karma Sena colleagues gifted her a saree. They insisted she wear it for her swearing-in ceremony, even helping her drape it before she took the chair. Images of this heartfelt moment have since gone viral on social media.
“The Haritha Karma Sena volunteers worked as a family for the past five years. It was a deeply memorable event for me. I never expected such a gift from my co-workers. My co-workers’ gift shows their happiness in this shared pride. It proves that anyone, regardless of their background, can reach such positions,” said Ms. Rajani.
A volunteer since 2021, Ms. Rajani has spent years visiting homes across the panchayat for waste collection. “Erattayar is already a model for waste management, and I intend to make our initiatives even more effective. Additionally, I plan to focus on tourism development within the panchayat,” she added.
Her family — husband Karunan, a timber worker, and children Aparna and Akash — stood by her during this proud moment. According to Congress leaders, Ms. Rajani will serve as president for the next one and a half years as part of a term-sharing agreement. “I will step down when my turn ends to allow other eligible members to lead,” she said.
Notably, the Erattayar panchayat was recently praised in the Economic Survey presented by Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman for its excellence in waste management driven by grassroots worker empowerment.

title: 784 PG doctors to join teaching and secondary hospitals soon
summary: 784 new PG doctors are set to enhance medical services in teaching and secondary hospitals across the State starting January 1.
content:
Minister for Health, Medical Education and Family Welfare Satya Kumar Yadav has said that 784 new Post Graduate doctors (senior residents) will be joining teaching and secondary hospitals in the State from January 1.
Those who had joined the PG courses in 2022-23 under the convener quota would be given postings in the secondary hospitals, including Community Health Centres, area and district hospitals, and teaching hospitals, the Minister said in a release on Saturday.
“A list is being prepared to categorise PG doctors as per their specialities so that their services can be utilised properly,” the Minister said, adding that the option for registration was open till December 29, and those who had received their postings should report for duty by January 5.
These doctors, spread across 23 specialities, have to work compulsorily in teaching hospitals for six months and in hospitals falling under the Directorate of Secondary Health for another six months. They will be paid ₹80,500, as per G.O. No 723 issued in December 2024.
“There are 110 PG doctors in General Medicine, 91 in General Surgery, 87 in Gynecology, 81 in Anesthesiology, 53 in Orthopedics, and 58 in Pediatrics. The others are from Radiology, Ophthalmology, ENT, Dermatology, and other specialties and PG non-clinical courses,” the release said.
Out of 784 PG doctors, 393 will work in Community Health Centres, area and district hospitals, while the remaining in 17 teaching hospitals in the State.
Director of Secondary Health Chakradhar Babu said medical services for patients would improve further in these hospitals with the arrival of the new batch of senior residents.

title: 377 booked for drunk driving during weekend special drive in Cyberabad
summary: Drunk driving
content:
The Cyberabad traffic police booked 377 drunk driving cases during a weekend special enforcement drive conducted between December 26 and 27, as part of intensified checks across the commissionerate to curb driving under the influence of alcohol.
Miyapur topped the list with 48 cases followed by Shadnagar with 42 cases and Shamshabad and Chevella with 35 cases each. Jeedimetla with 13 cases was among the areas with lowest cases followed by KPHB and RC Puram with 15 cases each. Kukatpally recorded zero cases.
According to the police, the majority of the offenders were riding two-wheelers, accounting for 300 cases, followed by 58 cases involving four-wheelers. Seventeen cases were registered against three-wheelers, while two heavy vehicle drivers were also found driving under the influence.
Based on blood alcohol concentration levels, police said 317 offenders recorded BAC readings between 35 mg/100 ml and 200 mg/100 ml. Another 39 offenders were found with BAC levels ranging from 201 mg/100 ml to 300 mg/100 ml, while 21 motorists registered dangerously high levels between 301 mg/100 ml and 550 mg/100 ml. All the accused will be produced before the court.
Officials said that anyone found driving in an inebriated condition and causing a fatal accident would be booked under Section 105 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, which deals with culpable homicide not amounting to murder and carries a maximum punishment of 10 years’ imprisonment along with a fine.
Meanwhile, during the previous week from December 22 to 27, courts disposed of 55 drunk driving cases. Of these, one person was sentenced to both fine and imprisonment, five were ordered to pay a fine and perform social service, while 49 were penalised with fines alone, as per the Cyberabad traffic police.

title: Revanth Reddy has pushed Palamuru back to distress migration, alleges KTR
summary: KTR accuses Congress of reversing Palamuru's development, pushing it into distress migration and jeopardizing farmers' water rights.
content:
HYDERABAD
Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) working president K.T. Rama Rao on Tuesday accused the Congress government and Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy of reversing the development achieved in Palamuru (combined/erstwhile Mahabubnagar) district and pushing it back into distress and migration for livelihoods.
Addressing a meeting of the newly elected Sarpanches and Upa-Sarpanches with the support of BRS in Nagarkurnool district, he said the Congress government had failed to carry forward key irrigation and development projects and was undoing the progress made during the BRS regime. Despite being in power for two years, the present government had not completed even 10% of the works initiated earlier, he alleged.
“Palamuru was made green and prosperous under Mr. Chandrashekar Rao’s leadership. Today, without even lifting a basketful of soil, the Chief Minister is indulging in irresponsible and abusive rhetoric. Congress has once again turned Palamuru into a migration district by stalling projects and drying up irrigation sources,” Mr. Rama Rao said.
Stating that nearly 90% of the Palamuru-Rangareddy Lift Irrigation Scheme’s head works were completed when Mr. Chandrashekar Rao was in power, he said that the Congress government cancelled approved tenders and crippled the project after coming to power. “Mr. Revanth Reddy had compromised on Telangana’s rightful water share and severely impacted farmers,” he added.
He stated that former Chief Minister K. Chandrashekar Rao was preparing for another phase of struggle to protect Palamuru–Rangareddy project, safeguard Telangana’s water interests and stand with farmers and he would soon visit Palamuru to mobilise support for protecting Telangana’s water rights. He highlighted how the investment support given to farmers in the form of Rythu Bandhu had been made irregular and how the government forced farmers to plead for urea, standing in long queues even during cold conditions.
Mr. Rama Rao accused the Congress of coming to power with unrealistic promises and cheating the public after assuming office. He said the Chief Minister resorted to abusive language whenever questioned about the implementation of poll promises even after completing two years in power. “Mr. Revanth Reddy is only obsessed with criticising Mr. Chandrashekar Rao,” he added.
Further, he stated that the Revanth Reddy government was eyeing nearly 9,300 acres of land in Hyderabad allotted to industries at concessional rates in the larger interest of development and employment, by bringing in HILT policy.
Party leaders M. Janardhan Reddy, C. Laxma Reddy, V. Srinivas Goud, R.S. Praveen Kumar, G. Jaipal Yadav, A. Venkateshwar Reddy, B. Harshavardhan Reddy, P. Narender Reddy and others participated.

title: Nine Telangana districts record temperatures below 10°C; Sirpur lowest at 7.1°C
summary: Nine Telangana districts experience sub-10°C temperatures, with Sirpur recording the lowest at 7.1°C, according to recent data.
content:
A total of nine Telangana districts recorded temperatures of 10 or below between December 27 and 28, said data from Telangana Development Planning Society (TGDPS). Sirpur in Kumaram Bheem Asifabad district recorded the lowest minimum temperature of 7.1°C
This was followed by 7.5°C in Kohir (Sangareddy), 8.3°C in Bheempoor (Adilabad), 8.8°C in Moinabad (Rangareddy), 9.4°C in Gandhari (Kamareddy), 9.6°C in Yeldurthy (Medak) and Pembi (Nirmal), 9.8°C in Mominpet (Vikarabad) and 10°C in Saloora (Nizamabad).
The remaining 24 districts recorded temperatures ranging between 10°C and 14°C. In urban locations, Uppal in Medchal Malkajgiri recorded a minimum temperature of 10.8°C and Tirumalagiri in Hyderabad recorded 11.5°C.
Meanwhile, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) in its latest bulletin said that the minimum temperatures in Telangana are likely to be below normal by 2°C to 3°C, at isolated locations during the next two days.
Hyderabad and its surrounding areas for the next 24 hours will see partly cloudy sky. “Mist or hazy conditions are very likely to prevail during morning or night hours. The maximum and minimum temperatures are likely to be around 27°C and 14°C respectively,” the bulletin said.

title: Amaravati farmer Rama Rao laid to rest; CPI(M) demands immediate government action
summary: Amaravati farmer Rama Rao's funeral sparks CPI(M) demands for government action on farmer issues and ex gratia support.
content:
The last rites of Amaravati farmer Rama Rao, who collapsed and died during a CRDA meeting in Mandadam, were performed on Sunday (December 28) at the local crematorium on Sunday. A large number of farmers, relatives and local residents participated in the funeral procession.
CPI(M) State secretariat member Ch. Babu Rao, capital region secretary M. Ravi and other party leaders attended the funeral and criticised the State government and the Capital Region Development Authority (CRDA) for what they termed as callous negligence of farmers’ issues.
Speaking on the occasion, Mr. Babu Rao said that although Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu had reportedly assured the bereaved family of support over the phone, no concrete measure has been announced so far. He condemned the CRDA for issuing statements claiming it was not at fault, instead of acknowledging the grievances raised by Rama Rao regarding improper plot allotment in low-lying areas and issues related to road expansion and house removals.
He alleged that blaming the deceased farmer by claiming he had not lodged complaints or had consented to road widening was highly objectionable. Mr. Babu Rao demanded that the CRDA withdraw its statements, apologise to farmers, and that the Chief Minister immediately announce at least ₹50 lakh as ex gratia to Ramarao’s family along with allotment of suitable plots.
Warning of protests, if the government failed to respond, CPI(M) leaders said responsibility for any agitation would rest solely with the government.

title: Main accused in police recruitment scam booked for misconduct in jail
summary: Rudragowda Patil, main accused in a police recruitment scam, faces new charges for misconduct in Kalaburagi Central Prison.
content:
Main accused in the Police Sub-Inspector recruitment scam Rudragowda Patil (RD Patil) was booked again on Saturday for creating disturbance inside the Kalaburagi Central Prison.
According to prison officials, Patil objected to a routine barrack inspection and engaged in a verbal altercation with jail staff. He questioned their authority to conduct inspection and refused to allow them to proceed without prior permission.
Following the incident, a complaint was lodged at the Farhatabad Police Station by Superintendent of Kalaburagi Central Prison Anita.
Sources said that the inspection is being carried out as per instructions from senior officials.
The staff also recalled how Patil had created trouble when he was released from prison for two weeks following a Supreme Court order last month. At that time too, jail authorities filed a complaint of misbehaviour and assault.
Prison officials said that Patil has been repeatedly involved in indiscipline in the jail.

title: Kerala Muslim Jamat demands bifurcation of Malappuram district
summary: Kerala Muslim Jamat calls for Malappuram district bifurcation to enhance access to facilities for its 4.7 million residents.
content:
The Kerala Muslim Jamat has demanded that Malappuram district be bifurcated to improve access to facilities for the district’s 4.7 million people.
Kerala Muslim Jamat district president Koottampara Abdurahman Darimi urged the State government to consider creating a new district to ensure fairness for the 4.7 million residents of Malappuram.
“It is high time that Malappuram district was bifurcated. This is the only way to provide equal facilities to all people irrespective of caste or religion,” said Mr. Darimi.
He raised the demand while addressing gatherings at Vengara and Kottakkal on Sunday (December 28), marking the conclusion of district-level build-up rallies organised ahead of a Kerala Yatra by the Kerala Muslim Jamat, as part of the centenary celebrations of the Samastha Kerala Jamiyyathul Ulama.
Muslim Jamat leaders Kanthapuram A.P. Aboobacker Musliar and Syed Ibrahim Khaleel Bukhari Thangal will lead the Kerala Yatra from Kasaragod to Thiruvananthapuram, raising the slogan ‘with humanity’. The yatra is scheduled from January 1 to 16. It will be given receptions at Areekode and Tirur in the district on January 7 and 8, respectively.
Addressing build-up rallies at Kondotty, Manjeri, and Malappuram on Sunday, district jatha captain Vadassery Hasan Musliar condemned the Karnataka government’s ‘bulldozer raj.’
He described the demolition of houses belonging to poor residents as an attack on the rights of the underprivileged, adding that poor minorities and marginalised communities were the main victims of the ruthless drive in Yelahanka.
The Kerala Muslim Jamat demanded that the Karnataka government rehabilitate the helpless people displaced in Bengaluru and Yelahanka.

title: Local body polls: elections of standing committee members from January 5 to January 7
summary: Local body elections for standing committee members in Kerala will take place from January 5 to January 7, 2025.
content:
The elections of the members of the standing committees of local bodies in the State will be held from January 5 to January 7, State Election Commissioner (SEC) A. Shajahan said on Sunday (December 28, 2025). Once the members are elected, the chaipersons of the committees will be elected.
Grama panchayats and block panchayats have four standing committees: finance, development, welfare, and health and education. District panchayats have five committees: finance, development, works, welfare, and health and education.
In the municipalities, members will be elected to six panels, viz., finance, development, welfare, health, works, and education and arts/sports. The six Corporations have eight committees: finance, development, welfare, health,  works, town planning, tax appeal, and education and sports.
In the grama panchayats and blocks, the returning officers of the local bodies concerned will conduct the elections of the members and the chaipersons of the committees. In the Corporations and district panchayats, the Additional District Magistrate is the returning officer. The SEC has also appointed returning officers for the municipalities.
One seat each in all committees including finance has been reserved for women. The SEC has also issued a notification on the reserved seats for women in the chairpersons’ posts. Elections will be first held to the reserved posts.
If the number of candidates exceeds the number of posts, a preferential voting mechanism will be employed, the SEC said.

title: Kerala State Human Rights Commission seeks report about attack on Attappady tribal youth
summary: Kerala's Human Rights Commission investigates alleged attack on tribal youth Manikandan in Attappady, following theft accusations.
content:
The Kerala State Human Rights Commission (SHRC) has registered a case and directed a police officer of deputy superintendent of police (Dy.SP) rank to investigate the incident in which a tribesman was allegedly attacked in Attappady after being accused of theft.
Commission chairperson Alexander Thomas registered a case suo motu and asked the police officer to look into if the crime was registered, what actions were taken against the accused, what treatment was given to the victim and what sections were included in the First Information Report.
The Dy.SP will have to submit a report in three weeks. The Dy.SP has been asked to attend a sitting that Mr. Thomas will hold at the PWD Guest House here on January 27.
Manikandan, 26, from Palur in Pudur panchayat of Attappady was allegedly attacked after being accused of theft by a man named Ramaraj a couple of weeks ago. Manikandan suffered injuries on his head and body. His family alleged that the police had initially refused to register a case and take action against Ramaraj.
However, the police arrested Ramaraj after the incident was reported in the media.
The SHRC chairperson will hold a sitting here on Monday morning.

title: Doctor advises early screening for thalassemia and sickle cell in pregnant women
summary: Doctor recommends early thalassemia and sickle cell screening for pregnant women to assess child risk during pregnancy.
content:
Pregnant women should undergo screening tests for thalassemia and sickle cell anaemia within 14 to 16 weeks of pregnancy to determine in advance whether the child is at risk, said paediatrician V. Sridevi at an awareness programme on Sunday (28 December, 2025). The programme was organised by Praja Arogya Vedika (PAV) and the Indian Academy of Paediatrics at A. Konduru mandal in NTR district on Sunday.
Dr. Sridevi said that thalassemia and sickle cell anaemia are inherited blood disorders, and while thalassemia is a condition where there is an insufficient amount of haemoglobin that leads to anaemia, sickle cell anaemia occurs when red blood cells, usually round, take a sickle shape, causing obstruction to blood flow, which can result in pain, fatigue, and even stroke.
“If both parents are carriers or have the disease-causing gene, children can be affected. If the mother is a carrier, then there is a 25% chance that the child may be affected, 25% chance of the child remaining unaffected and 50% chance of the child becoming a carrier,” Dr. Sridevi said, adding that it is therefore important for pregnant women to go for timely checks and early treatment. Timely treatment and measures can reduce risks and help prevent thalassemia in the future, she said.
Later, Praja Arogya Vedika State honorary president K.V.S. Sai Prasad cautioned the public against taking iron supplements without doctor’s advice. He said excess iron can accumulate in the body. Around 200 people participated in the seminar and underwent free blood tests on the occasion.
PAV’s NTR district general secretary G. Vijay Prakash, Kinnera Memorial Foundation founder K. Rajagopal, A. Konduru Kidney Patients Welfare Association members and others were present.

title: For over a decade, 82-year-old man spending his retirement days taking free tuition for slum children in Bengaluru
summary: An 82-year-old man in Bengaluru dedicates his retirement to teaching slum children, transforming their futures through free education.
content:
Every day between 4 p.m. and 6.30 p.m., since 2013, a home in J.P. Nagar turns into a classroom where small batches of students learning English, mathematics, and science lessons. These classes have helped many of them join college and make careers across various fields.
For more than 12 years now, an 82-year-old man in Bengaluru has been spending his evenings teaching children who cannot afford private schooling, let alone tuitions.
This began after C.S. Narayanan moved to Bengaluru from Chennai. During one of his regular evening walks around Puttanahalli lake with his wife Kamala, Mr. Narayanan met Usha Rajagopalan of the Puttanahalli Lake Trust. She spoke to him about children from the slums around the lake who were dropping out of school and asked if he could help teach them. This marked the beginning of what he describes as the most rewarding journey of his life.
Mr. Narayanan had retired and returned to India after a long career in the U.S., where he worked in oncology departments. He was looking to volunteer at a cancer hospital when he agreed to help the children. Despite not knowing Kannada, he returned to the lake the next day with Kannada–English dictionaries and began teaching basic spellings, reading, and mathematics.
Initially, only a handful of children came. “Lessons were worked out word by word through the dictionary... The numbers slowly grew from six to eight, and then to more than 20, making it difficult to give each child individual attention,” he said.
That was when he decided to move the classes to his home. “I limited each batch to around 15 students and made it clear that I would only teach children whose families could not afford paid tuition elsewhere. Over time, the number settled into smaller groups of about eight, making it possible to track each child’s progress,” he said.
Three months into the classes, he made a simple rule- English only during class hours. The idea, he said, was to remove hesitation and force familiarity. Many of the children had to begin from the very basics, such as spelling simple words, reading short sentences, and revisiting elementary math.
The children came from different schools and grades, with many following the State syllabus. As expenses mounted textbooks, uniforms and examination fees, Mr. Narayanan began reaching out to NGOs and individuals for support. In some cases, organisations stepped in to sponsor students fully. In others, parents contributed small amounts so they were not entirely dependent on him.
Among his earliest students were the children of his domestic worker. Both are now employed in software companies. Over the years, several others have gone on to study engineering, join the armed forces or got employed in the IT sector. Since he began teaching in 2013, Mr. Narayanan, who has raised over ₹30 lakh now, said there has not been a single instance of a student dropping out due to lack of funds.
Even visits to his own children, who live in the U.S., are planned around the school calendar here. Laughing, he said his children tease him that he spends time with them according to the convenience of his students. He said he prefers to travel only during breaks, worried that long gaps might disrupt the children’s routine. “If they lose interest, it’s hard to bring them back,” he said. Once a year, he also takes the children out, which he believes is, for many of them, their only outing outside their neighbourhood.
Pooja, one of his first students and the daughter of his domestic help, recalled struggling in school, especially with English, and she was on the verge of dropping out. She joined Mr. Narayanan’s classes scoring single-digit marks. With steady help, she said, things slowly changed. Her ‘tuition uncle’ later helped her move to a different school and encouraged her to continue studying.
She went on to complete her BCA and MCA and now works with a software company in Bengaluru.

title: 2025 a year of crises, probes and reform for TTD
summary: In 2025, TTD faced crises and controversies while implementing reforms and enhancing services amid ongoing investigations and public scrutiny.
content:
The year 2025 has proved to be one of the most testing periods in the recent history of the Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams (TTD), the statutory body that manages the world-famous shrine of Lord Venkateswara. A succession of crises, investigations and political sparring placed the revered temple trust under sustained public scrutiny, raising questions over administration, accountability and institutional oversight.
The year began on a tragic note. A stampede during the issuance of Vaikuntha Ekadasi darshan tokens in January claimed six lives and left several others injured, exposing serious lapses in crowd management at a time of heavy pilgrim influx. The incident set an uneasy tone for the months that followed, as the TTD struggled to cope with the fallout from past controversies while confronting new allegations.
Already weighed down by unresolved issues from the previous year — including the Parakamani cash-counting scandal, accusations of adulterated ghee used in laddu prasadam, irregularities in engineering works and disputes over promotions — the trust sought to restore confidence through corrective measures. However, those efforts were soon overshadowed by fresh controversies, notably the alleged irregularities in the supply ofAnga Vastrams, the disputed land exchange proposal with the State Tourism Department and other procurement-related issues.
Throughout the year, the TTD remained in the news as findings from multiple investigative agencies surfaced one after another. A Special Investigation Team (SIT) led by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), alongside parallel probes by the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) and the Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB), kept the institution under constant scrutiny. Political parties further intensified the debate, trading charges and drawing the shrine’s governance into the larger arena of State politics.
The CBI-led SIT submitted a status report to the Supreme Court in the adulterated ghee case, alleging large-scale fraud and the use of palm oil derivatives in prasadam preparation. Acting on the court’s directions, the team — comprising officials from the CBI, State police and the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) — identified serious weaknesses in procurement procedures and suggested the involvement of kickbacks and external influence in contract allocation. Several arrests followed, including those of prime dairy suppliers, a Delhi-based chemical trader and a former Executive Engineer (Procurements). Past chairpersons and executive officers were also questioned regarding oversight lapses. Meanwhile, the High Court continued to monitor the ongoing Parakamani investigation.
Further controversy erupted when a vigilance inquiry exposed an alleged ₹54.95-crore scam involving the supply of inferior polyester ‘Anga Vastrams’ (shawls) billed as pure mulberry silk over nearly a decade. Laboratory tests ordered by the TTD under its present Chairman B.R. Naidu and conducted by the Central Silk Board in Bengaluru and Dharmavaram confirmed that the material was not silk, as claimed.
Amid the turbulence, the TTD introduced a set of reform measures aimed at improving services and rebuilding trust. Devotees welcomed the improved quality of laddus and meals at the free food complex. Following Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu’s instructions, feedback registers were placed across major service points, recording high satisfaction levels from visiting devotees.
In a first for the temple’s history, the TTD announced that only online Sarva Darshan tokens would be issued for common pilgrims during the first three days of the Vaikuntha Ekadasi festival beginning December 30. The board also unveiled a master plan for a complete transition to electric mobility, replacing diesel and petrol vehicles with eco-friendly alternatives. Expansion ofanna prasadamservices and digital payment facilities across all 60 temples managed by the TTD in various States further signalled a push towards operational modernisation and enhanced transparency.

title: Unnao rape victim, family protest at Jantar Mantar
summary: Unnao rape victim and family protest at Jantar Mantar, demanding justice and security following the suspension of Kuldeep Singh Senger's sentence.
content:
The victim of the 2017 Unnao rape case, along with her family, and activists held a protest at Delhi's Jantar Mantar on Sunday (December 28, 2025) against the suspension offormer BJP MLA Kuldeep Singh Senger's life sentenceby the Delhi High Court in the case.
Demanding stricter accountability from authorities, the victim, who was present during the protest, said that their family should be provided more security.
"I'm requesting the Chief Minister to provide us security; these people are powerful. Please save your daughter," she said. " My husband was expelled from his job, we are unemployed, where will we go?" she said.
The demonstrators raised slogans against what they described as undue leniency towards the convict, arguing that the action taken so far fell short of public expectations.
The mother of the victim said that they trust the Supreme Court and hope that justice will be delivered in this case.
"We were beaten up, our relatives were beaten up, fake cases were registered against our relatives; I request the government not to release him," she said.
On December 23, the Delhi High Court suspended the jail term of Mr. Sengartill the pendency of his appeal, saying he has already served seven years and five months in prison, and had granted him conditional bail.  He will, however, remain in jail since he is also serving 10 years' imprisonment in the custodial death case of the victim's father and has not been granted bail in that case.
TheSupreme Court is slated to hear on Monday (December 29, 2025) a plea by the CBIchallenging the Delhi High Court order. According to the cause list, a three-judge vacation bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices JK Maheshwari and Augustine George Masih is likely to hear the matter.
Protesters from All India Progressive Women's Association (AIPWA) and All India Students' Association (AISA) also joined the protests on Sunday and claimed that the case had brought to light the influence of political power in criminal matters. They warned that any dilution of responsibility would undermine faith in the justice system.
"The Supreme Court must pay heed to the echoes of Jantar Mantar, that Kuldeep Singh Senger belongs in jail and ensure safety and justice to the survivor and her family," AISA said in a statement.
The protesters called for transparent proceedings and firm action, insisting that accountability must extend to all those involved, regardless of status or connections.
A police source said a woman was removed from the protest site as she was trying to enter the area with a placard in support of Mr. Sengar.
She was removed from the protest site peacefully, the source said, adding that no scuffle-like situation was reported during the protest.
"The victim and her mother were sitting at the protest site. But they had some health issues. Medical attention was immediately provided to them. Teams are checking their health condition," added the source.
Mr. Sengar, 59,  is a former four-time MLA from the Unnao region. He contested on BSP and SP tickets before joining the BJP in 2017 and winning from Bangermau.
Meanwhile, Mr. Sengar's daughter has asked the people of Unnao to refrain from resorting to any kind of protest and said her family has complete faith in the judicial process..
In a post on X in Hindi late on Saturday (December 27) night, Aishwarya Sengar said, "I humbly request all the people of Unnao to please refrain from resorting to any kind of protest. You are our family, and in this difficult time, we must not lose patience. We have complete faith in the judicial process. Your restraint and blessings give us strength."

title: YSRCP prioritises formation of committees to strengthen party structure
summary: YSRCP focuses on timely committee formation to strengthen its structure, guided by a newly established task force.
content:
YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) State coordinator Sajjala Ramakrishna Reddy on Sunday emphasised the need to prioritise the constitution of party committees, calling on leaders to execute the process in a time-bound manner.
Addressing an online conference with regional coordinators and district party presidents, Mr. Ramakrishna Reddy described the committee formation exercise as a special drive to be completed by the first week of February.
He said that party president Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy had instructed that the appointments be systematic and meaningful.
Mr. Ramakrishna Reddy highlighted the critical role of the committees in building a robust organisational structure, and urged leaders to expedite the formation of village and ward-level committees, ensuring that all related data was accurate.
Revealing plans to connect with nearly 15 lakh cadres directly, he said the initiative aims to create a disciplined and well-organised workforce.
Digital managers had already been appointed in every constituency, and orientation programmes were underway to guide leaders on committee formation, he said.
Pilot projects in the Kadapa Parliament constituency, Vemuru, Punganur, and Madakasira had been completed, he said. To monitor the process closely, a task force had been set up, he added.

title: UDD approves OTS for pending water bills, likely to start from January first week
summary: UDD approves a One Time Settlement for Bengaluru water bills, starting January, waiving interest and penalties for prompt payments.
content:
The Urban Development Department (UDD) has, on December 23, approved a One Time Settlement (OTS) scheme for pending water bills in Bengaluru.
The State Cabinet had approved a proposal for the same on November 27. The scheme will likely open in the first week of January and the window will be open for three months, V. Ram Prasath Manohar, Chairman, Bangalore Water Supply and Sewerage Board (BWSSB), said.
BWSSB has an arrears of ₹701 crore, of which ₹439 crore is the principal and the rest ₹262 crore has accumulated as interest and penalty. Under the OTS scheme, those who clear the outstanding principal amount in a single instalment will have their interest and penalty waived.
“There will be no room for any middlemen. Customers can directly register themselves on the official BWSSB website. Additionally, a dedicated mobile app is being developed for this purpose. Once registered, customers will be intimated about the payment window and the deadline,” Mr. Manohar said.
“The waiver process is automated. As soon as the customer pays the principal amount, the software at the back-end will automatically waive the accumulated interest and penalty charges. Once the software is ready, we will launch the scheme, most likely in the first week of January,” he added.
A similar OTS for pending water bills was implemented in Hyderabad successfully twice, and the BWSSB has adopted a similar scheme, sources said.
The BWSSB has drawn up a proactive approach to reach defaulters. “Special teams from BWSSB will personally visit government buildings and commercial complexes to facilitate the settlement. For residential buildings, local officials will reach out to consumers,” Mr. Manohar said.

title: KPHB Police register missing case after man fails to return home, family finds distress note
summary: KPHB Police investigate a missing person case after a man leaves a distressing note about financial struggles and family responsibilities.
content:
The Kukatpally Housing Board (KPHB) Police have registered a missing person case after a 47-year-old man reportedly left his residence on Sunday (December 28, 2025) and failed to return, with his family later finding a handwritten note expressing distress over financial and personal issues.
According to a complaint lodged by his wife, Thota Divya, 40, a private teacher, her husband Thota Naveen Kumar, 47, who worked at CBJ Gold and Diamonds, left their home in Addagutta, KPHB Colony, at around 11 a.m. on his motorcycle.
Before leaving, he told her that he had kept money in the cupboard and asked her to buy medicine for their younger son.
Police said that after some time, the complainant opened the cupboard and found a letter written in Telugu, in which Naveen Kumar expressed anguish over his inability to meet family responsibilities, including his children’s education and medical needs. In the note, he alleged that the staff at his workplace had taken ₹50,000 in cash and gold ornaments from him and stated that his concerns about his son’s medical treatment were not addressed.
Based on the petition, KPHB police registered a missing person case and launched an investigation. Officials said efforts were on to trace his whereabouts and verify the contents of the note as part of the inquiry.
(Roshini suicide prevention helpline number are: 8142020033/44 and 040 66202000/2001.)

title: SDPI blames LDF, UDF for BJP’s third term in Palakkad
summary: SDPI blames LDF and UDF for enabling BJP's third term in Palakkad through political opportunism and duplicity.
content:
The Social Democratic Party of India (SDPI) said the Bharatiya Janata Party’s (BJP) third consecutive term in the Palakkad municipality was made possible, despite the party lacking a majority, by the “hypocritical stances of both the Left Democratic Front (LDF) and the United Democratic Front (UDF).”
SDPI leader Mohammed Ilyas said here on Saturday that the BJP assumed power in the Palakkad municipality despite holding only 25 of the 53 seats in the council because of the blatant political duplicity of both the LDF and the UDF.
