He said the LDF and the UDF could have kept the BJP out of power by backing an Independent candidate for the municipal chairperson’s post. “But sadly, both fronts took a stance that indirectly helped the BJP,” he said.
Mr. Ilyas accused the LDF and the UDF of effectively allowing fascist forces to stay in power, despite their vocal criticism of fascism. “The BJP’s continued rule in Palakkad is no accident; it reflects the political opportunism of both the UDF and the LDF,” he said.

title: Kovalam fishers write to Union government against the proposed reservoir project
summary: Kovalam fishers urge the Union government to halt a reservoir project threatening the Buckingham Canal's natural flow and livelihoods.
content:
Residents of Kovalam Kuppam, along with those of the surrounding villages in Chengalpattu district, have requested the Union Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways to intervene immediately and prevent obstruction of the Buckingham Canal by a reservoir project proposed at Kovalam.
In a letter, they have highlighted the potential threat posed by Chennai’s sixth reservoir project, saying it will block the natural flow of the canal, a key part of National Waterway-4 (NW-4). The petition was submitted to the Secretary of the Union Ministry and the Chairman and Regional Director of the Inland Waterways Authority of India (IWAI).
The residents have argued that the project, spearheaded by the Tamil Nadu Water Resources Department, could severely impact the livelihood of local fishing communities and marginalised groups, including the Adi Dravidar and tribal populations.
Under the National Waterways Act, 2016, the Buckingham Canal has been declared a national waterway. Its management and maintenance have been placed under the jurisdiction of the Union government. The petitioners have said any effort to alter the course of the canal without permission from the Centre will amount to a violation of this legal framework.
“The obstruction of these waterbodies will have a devastating impact on our community’s access to fishing resources and, by extension, our right to livelihood,” according to the letter.
The residents have called for a restraining order to halt the project, requesting that the Tamil Nadu government be prevented from interfering with the natural flow of the Buckingham Canal. They have also demanded protection of the traditional fishing rights of these communities and have urged the IWAI to conduct an on-site inspection and organise a public hearing to address the concerns of the local population.

title: Marking foundation day, AIDSO steps up protest against school closure
summary: AIDSO marks its foundation day with protests against school closures and calls to oppose anti-student education policies in Karnataka.
content:
The All India Democratic Students Organisation (AIDSO) on Sunday observed its 72nd foundation day across several districts in Karnataka with programmes, flag hoisting and renewed calls to oppose what it termed anti-student education policies of the State government.
In Kalaburagi, the foundation day was marked by flag hoisting and a meeting at the AIDSO district office.
Addressing a gathering, district council secretary Venkatesh Devadurg said that the organisation has, for more than seven decades, built student movements across the country against educational injustice.
“AIDSO is committed to the idea of scientific, secular, democratic and universal education. In Karnataka too, we are actively fighting policies that harm public education,” he said.
AIDSO activists taking part in the 72nd foundation day event in Hosapete, Vijayangara district, on Sunday.
                                                            | Photo Credit: 
                                SPECIAL ARRANGEMENT
He strongly criticised the State government’s Karnataka Public Schools magnet scheme saying that it will lead to the closure of nearly 40,000 government schools and push the poor and working-class children out of the education system.
“Under the guise of reforms, education is being handed over to private interests. Closing government schools will permanently shut the doors of knowledge for lakhs of poor children,” he said and called for a united struggle to protect public education.
AIDSO district vice-president Preeti Doddamani, joint secretaries Rahul Jadhav and Yuvraj Rathod and several students were present.
Activists observing the 72nd foundation day of AIDSO in Ballari on Sunday.
                                                            | Photo Credit: 
                                SPECIAL ARRANGEMENT
At another foundation day event in Ballari, AIDSO leaders recalled that the organisation was founded on December 28, 1954, inspired by the ideas of Shivdas Ghosh, with the objective of ensuring free and equal education for all students without discrimination.
State secretariat member Ravikiran J.P. said that commercialisation has made higher education inaccessible to poor students.
“The system has created a situation where only those with money can study medicine, engineering or higher courses,” he said and added that governments are acting contrary to the ideals of social reformers and freedom fighters.
District president K. Eeranna warned that the proposed closure and merger of schools will hit rural students the hardest. “Government schools in villages are the only option for poor children. If they are shut down in the name of merger, many students will be forced to drop out,” he said and called upon students and the public to oppose the move.
In another event in Hosapete of Vijayanagara district, AIDSO district secretary U. Umadevi expressed concern over the increasing commercialisation of education saying that poor students are being denied access to medical, engineering and higher education.
“The present system has created a situation where only those with money can pursue higher studies. Governments, which are supposed to provide free education, are instead promoting its commercialisation,” she said and urged students to carry forward the ideals of social reformers and freedom fighters who fought for universal education.
AIDSO district joint secretaries Chandra, Akash, Gnanesh, Neema and Mary, along with several students, took part in the foundation day programmes.

title: Sandur National Farmers Day event showcases integrated farming model
summary: JSW Foundation's National Farmers Day event in Sandur promotes integrated farming, showcasing successful practices and supporting local farmers.
content:
JSW Foundation organised a National Farmers Day programme and model farm demonstration at Taluru village in Sandur taluk of Ballari district on Sunday highlighting the benefits of integrated farming practices and sustainable agriculture.
The event showcased the success of progressive farmer T. Veeresh, who has adopted an integrated farming model by cultivating 23 crops, including betel leaf, banana and onion.
His farm, which generates substantial income, was presented as a model for other farmers in the region.
Addressing a gathering, South Zonal Head of JSW Foundation Peddanna Beedala said that the foundation is promoting integrated farming among 300 farmers in 10 selected villages.
“Farmers have already received initial training. In the coming week, we will distribute soil health report cards, organic fertilisers, vegetable seeds, vermicompost kits, 20 Giriraj native chicks and essential plants for one or two acres per farmer, along with hands-on training,” he said and urged farmers to actively participate and benefit from the initiative.
Experts from the Krishi Vigyan Kendra, Hagari, guided farmers on integrated farming practices, soil and water management, pest control, modern techniques and crop selection suited to the Sandur region.
Senior scientists P. Palaih and S. Ravi also addressed farmers queries and offered practical advice based on local conditions.
Manager of Indian Farmers Fertiliser Cooperative, Ballari, Hanamantappa led the visit to the model plots and explained crop layout, farm management practices and real-time applications of integrated farming.
JSW Foundation programme executive Nagana Gowda, representatives of implementing partner SCODWES, including Raja and Gangadhar, progressive farmers, including Veeresh and Basappa, and more than 100 farmers from surrounding villages attended the programme.

title: WINGS Thiruvananthapuram bird count records 188 species
summary: WINGS Thiruvananthapuram 2025 recorded 188 bird species, highlighting biodiversity across various habitats in the district.
content:
WINGS - Birds of India Nature Awareness Programme, Thiruvananthapuram 2025, a district-level bird count that covered wetlands, forests, hill stations, campuses and urban landscapes across the district, recorded 188 species, WWF-India, which coordinated the event with the Trivandrum Birding Team, said on Sunday.
The Kottoor forests yielded 85 species, the highest among the 10 regions surveyed during the one-day event on December 14. The list included Changeable hawk-eagle, Common buzzard, Small Minivet, and Black-naped monarch. The Arippa forest, along the Thiruvananthapuram-Shengottai route, also  emerged as a species-rich site, yielding 83 species, the WWF-India said in a statement.
With the help of forest guides of the Kerala Forest Development Corporation (KFDC), the participants  recorded the Sri Lanka frogmouth, a hard-to-find bird in the forests of the Western Ghats. “The Jawaharlal Nehru Topical Botanic Garden and Research Institute (JNTBGRI), situated on the foothills of the Western Ghats, yielded 50 species, reaffirming that campuses outside protected areas can serve as significant biodiversity hotspots,” the WWF-India said.
Hill and forest ecosystems also showed high diversity. Ponmudi recorded 67 species, including the Lesser coucal, Brown-backed needletail, White-rumped spinetail, and Common rosefinch. Bonacaud recorded 73 species, including Indian pitta, Square-tailed bulbul, Rufous babbler, and large numbers of Brown-backed needletail, reflecting effective coexistence between people and wildlife in well-maintained forest areas, the statement said.
Black-naped blue monarch
                                                            | Photo Credit: 
                                Special arrangement
The Vellayani-Punchakkari wetland, often dubbed the birding hub of the capital city, yielded 76 species, including the Amur falcon, Peregrine falcon, and Baillon’s crake. Kadinamkulam Lake recorded 36 species, including Eurasian whimbrel, Common redshank, and Stork-billed kingfisher.
Fifty-one species were reported from the Akkulam-Veli region, indicating that such rapidly changing urban spaces continue to harbour significant biodiversity, according to the participants. Around 500 Lesser whistling ducks were sighted on the National Centre for Earth Science Studies (NCESS) campus, highlighting the role of institutional campuses as refuge or biodiversity hotspots in fast-changing urban landscapes, the WWF-India said.
The team that surveyed the Thiruvananthapuram zoo and the Kesavadasapuram paddy fields recorded 46 species, underlining the importance of urban wetlands. The presence of migratory birds such as Indian pitta, Orange-headed thrush, Brown-breasted flycatcher, Blue-throated flycatcher, and Grey wagtail at the zoo reflected the good ecological health of the city’s green spaces, the organisers said.
Nearly 50 volunteers from different sections of society participated in the exercise. The participants included scientists, experienced birdwatchers, nature enthusiasts, forest guides from the KFDC Arippa, and college students.
Malabar grey hornbill
                                                            | Photo Credit: 
                                Special arrangement
This year marked the 19th edition of the survey. The  initiative was started by Sunjoy Monga, renowned as Mumbai’s Birdman, who passed away on May 28, 2025. Saju S. Nair, Assistant Conservator of Forests (Social Forestry); Dileep M.R., Director of the Kerala Institute of Travel and Tourism Studies (KITTS); Renjan Mathew Varghese, State Director, WWF-India; Anushreedha S.S., Project Officer, WWF-India; and A.K. Sivakumar and Govind Girija, coordinators of WINGS Thiruvananthapuram 2025, addressed the participants.

title: Elderly woman injured at Secunderabad railway station dies during treatment at Gandhi Hospital
summary: Elderly woman injured at Secunderabad railway station dies in Gandhi Hospital after a month of treatment.
content:
A 74-year-old woman who was found injured at Secunderabad Railway Station last month died while undergoing treatment at Gandhi Hospital on Saturday (December 27, 2025). The deceased was identified as Poonuru Vijayalakshmi, a homemaker, and resident of Fatehnagar in Sanathnagar.
According to the police, Vijayalakshmi was found injured near gate number 2 of Secunderabad Railway Station on November 11. The incident was brought to the notice of the Public Deputy Station Superintendent, who alerted the Government Railway Police at Secunderabad. She was immediately shifted to Gandhi Hospital for treatment. She succumbed at around 3 pm on December 27.
Hospital authorities informed the police about her death, following which officials preserved the body in the hospital mortuary for postmortem examination and the relatives have been informed. If no relative comes forward, the body will be handed over to the Greater Hyderabad Municipal Corporation after completing the required formalities.

title: Telangana DCA raids unqualified practitioner in Karimnagar, seizing 39 types of unlicensed medicines
summary: Telangana DCA raids unqualified practitioner in Karimnagar, seizing 39 types of unlicensed medicines worth ₹15,011.
content:
Officials of the Telangana Drugs Control Administration (DCA) conducted a raid at the premises of an unqualified medical practitioner in Karimnagar on Saturday (December 27). The raid was carried out at Laxmi First Aid Centre where K. Laxminarayana was conducting clinical practice without possessing required medical qualifications.
During the inspection, DCA officials found 39 varieties of medicines stocked at the clinic without a valid drug licence. Of these, 35 varieties were physician’s samples, including antibiotics, analgesics and anti-ulcer drugs. The total value of the seized stock was estimated at ₹15,011.
The officials also detected several antibiotics such as Cefixime, Ofloxacin, Cloxacillin, Amoxycillin and Azithromycin at the premises. The DCA cautioned that the indiscriminate sale and use of antibiotics by unqualified persons could have serious public health consequences, including the emergence and spread of antimicrobial resistance.

title: Kerala politics spills over to Karnataka after eviction drive in Bengaluru
summary: Kerala politics heats up in Karnataka as eviction drive sparks tensions ahead of the 2026 Assembly elections.
content:
The close political battle between the Communist Party of India-Marxist (CPI-M)-led Left Democratic Front (LDF) and the Congress-led United Democratic Front (UDF) in Kerala seems to have spilled over to Karnataka ahead of the assembly polls in Kerala, expected to be held in April/ May 2026. The statements of Kerala Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan and All India Congress Committee (AICC) general secretary (Organisation) K.C. Venugopal over the demolition of over 150 “illegal” structures in Kogilu Layout in Bengaluru are being attributed to their political agenda ahead of the elections.
Mr. Venugopal’s statement on Saturday criticising the demolition, which seems to have made Congress leaders in Karnataka embarrassed, came close after Mr. Vijayan termed the demolition in Faqir Colony and Waseem Layout as “brutal normalisation of bulldozer raj”. He said, “Sadly, the Sangha Parivar’s anti minority politics is now being executed under a Congress government in Karnataka”.
While Karnataka’s Deputy Chief Minister and KPCC president D.K. Shivakumar hit back at Mr. Vijayan for “unnecessary interference without an understanding of the facts,” the central Congress leader, in contrast, expressed “AICC’s serious concern”. This has put the Karnataka Congress leaders on the backfoot.
At the centre of their statements, a political observer based out of Thiruvananthapuram pointed out, is the upcoming Assembly elections expected to be closely fought. “The Congress has done well in the recently-concluded local bodies elections in Kerala, even as CPI (M) has ceded ground to the BJP. By using the demolition that has affected families from minority communities, the CPI (M) wants to portray Congress in a poor light, that they are not safe under the Congress regime”. Kerala has a high Muslim electorate, especially in the Northern districts.
In the 2021 Kerala assembly polls, the CPI (M) polled 25.38 % of the total votes, winning 62 seats, while the Congress polled 25.12% of the total votes winning 21 seats. The total vote share of LDF was 41.5 % while it was 38.4 % for UDF.
Mr. Vijayan’s statement has been followed up by the visit of CPI (M) leaders to the demolition site. CPI (M) Rajya Sabha member from Kerala A.A. Rahim, and Independent legislator and former Minister in Left Democratic Front (LDF) K.T. Jaleel were among those who visited Kogilu. At the national level, CPI (M) is part of the Indian National Developmental Inclusive Alliance (INDIA) bloc led by the Congress.
Within the Karnataka Congress, though there is a feeling that demolition could have been better handled, “outside interference” has irked the leaders. “It is well known that Mr. Venugopal is an aspirant for the Chief Minister’s post if Congress comes to power in Kerala. As a CM aspirant, he must have found it fit to jump into an issue already raised by Mr. Vijayan. Why would AICC interfere in internal issues of a State otherwise? ” a senior Minister said, insisting that the demolition had no communal angle. “Is it wrong to vacate illegal structures?”
Meanwhile, it is also learnt that the CPI (M) Karnataka leaders have conveyed to their counterparts in Kerala that the party machinery in the State is strong enough to fight the case on its own. “We feel that outside interference will not help the cause since it becomes political”.
The Congress government has been under the lens over its outreach to Kerala over the past two years. A compensation of ₹15 lakh provided to a resident of Wayanad in Kerala in an elephant attack and a subsequent announcement of ₹10 crore to compensate 100 families affected by floods in Wayanad came under attack by the BJP. While Wayanad was initially represented by the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi, his sister Priyanka Gandhi represents the constituency now.

title: CPI demands withdrawal of PPP policy for medical colleges
summary: CPI demands withdrawal of the PPP policy for medical colleges, citing concerns over privatisation and access for underprivileged students.
content:
CPI national secretary K. Ramakrishna demanded that the government immediately withdraw its proposal to run medical colleges under the Public-Private Partnership (PPP) model and ensure that all newly established government medical colleges remain under full government control.
In a statement on Sunday (December 28), Mr. Ramakrishna alleged that Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu was acting with undue haste and rigidity in attempting to privatise medical colleges under the guise of PPP. The move was being unanimously opposed by political parties, student and youth organisations,and intellectuals across Andhra Pradesh, he said.
Citing a recent article by former Union Health Secretary Sujatha Rao, Mr. Ramakrishna said the PPP model in medical education would not only inconvenience patients but also adversely affect students from poor and middle-class families. Land, buildings, infrastructure and other resources for the new medical colleges were created entirely with government funds, making it unjustifiable to hand them over to private players, he said, and termed it “immoral” that the government was even willing to pay staff salaries for two years while allowing private entities to collect fees from students.
The CPI leader accused the coalition government of effectively transferring public assets into private hands and questioned claims by the Health Minister regarding bidder interest in tenders. He warned that privatisation of education and healthcare would make them inaccessible to the common man and reiterated CPI’s strong opposition to the PPP policy in medical colleges.

title: Scouts and Guides helping shape children’s personality, says Speaker
summary: The 29th India Scouts and Guides Jamborette emphasizes character building and responsible citizenship in children, says Speaker U.T. Khader.
content:
The 29th India Scouts and Guides Jamborette 2025 was inaugurated at Phoenix Public School in Honaga village of the district on Saturday.
Speaker U.T. Khader, who inaugurated the event, said that Scouts and Guides institutions around the world are helping in shaping children’s personality.
“Children are the wealth of the country.  It is everyone’s dream to make India the first in the world. It is only possible for India to become strong if students become responsible citizens,” he said.
“Students should know the value of time and use it properly to shape their personality. He said that your personality will take you to a higher position in the coming days. Children should become good citizens and take up high positions and participate in social service and reform activities,” he said.
“While it is the job of teachers to educate children, it is the job of Scouts and Guides to teach discipline to children,” Legislative Council Chairman Basavaraj Horatti said.
He said that outdoor activities of Scouts and Guides have the potential to teach life lessons for students. He said that “children who participate in the jamborette learn lessons like everyone is equal, regardless of caste and religion.”
He said that focus on voluntary service is akin to the principle of work is worship taught by Basavanna and others reformers.
BJP MP Jagadish Shettar said that such events can help students lead a disciplined life.
Bharat Scouts and Guides is doing the work of providing physical and mental stimulation to students along with school activities, he said.
He recalled his long association with State Scouts and Guides Commissioner P.G.R. Sindhia, saying that they have worked as volunteers and student leaders in the ABVP.
Education Minister Madhu Bangarappa said that it is the responsibility of the Education Department to ensure that Scouts and Guides continue to grow to be in the forefront.
Scouts and Guides are very important for grooming good citizens for the future. He said that the department will increase its support to the institution. Such activities will be promoted in every school. That will help children pick up values and discipline, he said.
District in-charge Minister Satish Jarkiholi said that it is a matter of pride that the programme is being organized in Belagavi district.
“Children should make the best use of such nation building activities. This is like a factory that teaches skills and human values. The students who participate in this training are given an opportunity to become good citizens and move forward to build a great India,” he said.
Mr. Sindhia said that the work of Scouts and Guides is spiritual and not limited to any religion. He said that the erstwhile king of Mysore Nalvadi Krishnaraja Wodeyar started Scouts and Guides within a few years of its launch in England.
“It has a glorious history of personality development that grooms empathetic citizens. Scouts and Guides are working in more than 200 countries. Social development and education are our goals,” he said.
Sri Shivasiddha Shivacharya of Muktimath, Police Commissioner Borase Bhushan Gulbarao, Zilla Panchayat Chief Executive Officer Rahula Shinde, DDPI Leelavati Hiremath and Scouts and Guides District Chief Commissioner Gajanana Mannikeri, district officer Rajshekar Chalageri and others were present.
State organizing officer Manjula and others were present.

title: At Indian History Congress, Kerala CM Pinarayi Vijayan  calls for resisting political distortion of history
summary: Kerala CM Pinarayi Vijayan urges historians to resist political distortion of history and uphold evidence-based scholarship at Indian History Congress.
content:
Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan on Sunday (December 28, 2025) warned that history as a discipline is facing a sustained political assault, with communal and obscurantist forces distorting curricula and undermining academic institutions.  He called on historians to defend evidence-based scholarship to safeguard democracy.
Inaugurating the 84th session of the Indian History Congress, Mr. Vijayan said the rewriting of history over the last decade had moved beyond academic debate into organised political project. He alleged that institutions such as National Council of Educational Research and Training (NCERT), University Grants Commission (UGC) and Indian Council of Historical Research (ICHR) were being reshaped ideologically, while Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) textbooks were being systematically hallowed out to suit a narrow vision of the past.
The Chief Minister pointed out that the dilution or removal of key themes from school syllabi, including the Mughal period, popular resistance movements against caste oppression, communalism and the trauma of Partition. He said the ideological depth of figures such as Bhagat Singh had been stripped away, while the freedom struggle was increasingly portrayed as uncontested and led by a few icons.
Describing the omission of the Malabar Rebellion of 1921 as particularly telling, Mr. Vijayan said the erasure of leaders such Variyamkunnath Kunhahamed Haji and Ali Musaliar amounted to removing an entire chapter of anti-imperialist struggle led by rural poor.
He criticised attempts to elevate figures with marginal roles in the freedom movement while belittling Mahatma Gandhi, calling it a sheer distortion of history.
The marginalisation of Marxist historiography and scholars such as D.D. Kosambi, R.S. Sharma, Romila Thapar and Irfan Habib, he said, reflected discomfort with history as a critical discipline grounded in evidence and debate.                                                        Mr. Vijayan also warned against the capture of research bodies through ideologically driven appointments and the promotion of pseudo-scientific claims, arguing that attacks on scientific temper and dissent would inevitable strengthen authoritarianism.
Highlighting Kerala’s alternative historical trajectory shaped by anti-caste struggles, social reform and class politics, he said figures such as Ayyankali, Sree Narayana Guru and movements like the Vaikom Satyagraha are being marginalised in national narratives, as was the 1957 elected communist government and its reforms.
Defending history, the Chief Minister said, was a democratic duty. “History will not be surrendered. Truth will not be replaced by mythology. Scholarship will not bow to power,” he said, assuring the State government’s full support to the Indian History Congress and its efforts to uphold a secular, inclusive and scientific approach to the past.

title: JSP will prove its strength in local body elections, says party general secretary
summary: JSP's general secretary asserts the party will showcase its grassroots strength in upcoming local body elections following new leader joinings.
content:
Jana Sena Party (JSP) State General Secretary T. Siva Sankar said on Sunday (December 28, 2025) that the party would prove its strength at the grassroots level in the upcoming local body elections. YSRCP leaders Nadipena Srinivasa Rao, popularly known as Jammu Srinu, Nadipena Sasi Bhargavi and others joined JSP in the presence of Mr. Sankar’s at a programme organised by A.P. Turpu Kapu Corporation chairperson Palavalasa Yeshaswi and senior leader Adada Mohana Rao in Vizianagaram on Sunday.
Speaking on the occasion, Mr. Sankar said that JSP allows leaders of other parties into the fold after thorough verification of their background. He congratulated Mr. Jammu Srinu for selecting JSP and hoped that the joining of new leaders would further strengthen the party in rural areas of Vizianagaram and other parts of the State.

title: Chess tournament from Monday
summary: It will be inaugurated by District Collector Alex Varghese
content: The Canara Bank N.V. Prabhu Memorial International Fide Rated Open Chess Tournament- 2025 will be held at YMCA Alappuzha from December 29 to January 2. It will be inaugurated by District Collector Alex Varghese on Monday at 9.30 a.m.

title: Congress seeks disqualification of Agali panchayat president
summary: Congress seeks disqualification of Agali panchayat president N.K. Manju for alleged anti-defection law violations after party switch.
content:
The Congress has approached the State Election Commission (SEC) seeking the disqualification of its member N.K. Manju, who switched sides and became president of the Agali grama panchayat with the Left Democratic Front (LDF) support on Saturday.
The Congress has demanded that Ms. Manju, who was elected from Chinnaparamba (ward 20) of the Agali panchayat, be disqualified under the anti-defection law. The party has also decided to move legally against Ms. Manju.
Meanwhile, Ms. Manju said that she had not been given any whip by the party. She said she got votes in the panchayat president’s election irrespective of parties. While the LDF got 10 votes, the United Democratic Front (UDF) got only nine votes in the president election. Three members of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) stayed away from voting.
The Congress has also decided to seek explanation from its councillor Prasobh in the Palakkad municipality for his failure to vote in the vice-chairperson election. Mr. Prasobh was denied permission to vote as he reached the council five minutes late.
Mr. Prasobh said that he went home to take medicine due to illness, but the Congress leaders were unconvinced.

title: CPI(M) to hold protest assemblies against new MGNREGS regulations
summary: The scheme, which was originally fully funded by Centre, has undergone a significant shift to a 60:40 cost-sharing ratio between the Centre and the State
content:
CPI(M) Kollam district committee will organise protest and defence assemblies across the district on January 5 to protect the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (MGNREGS). The committee condemned the Central government’s recent actions as “anti-people,” alleging that the State-sponsored dismantling of the scheme threatens the very survival of the poor.
“The scheme, which was originally fully funded by the Central government, has undergone a significant shift to a 60:40 cost-sharing ratio between the Centre and the State. Under the new regulations, the Centre will also set expenditure limits; any spending by the State exceeding these caps must be covered entirely by the State’s own treasury. The upcoming protest specifically demands the immediate clearance of ₹527.69 crore in MGNREGS arrears currently owed to Kerala by the Central government,” said the State leadership.
They added that Left-wing representatives in Local Self-Government institutions will introduce resolutions in their upcoming meetings against the Centre’s moves to undermine MGNREGS.

title: ‘Ram Rajya’ is the benchmark for good governance, says Chandrababu Naidu
summary: Chandrababu Naidu calls 'Ram Rajya' the ideal for governance, emphasizing ethical leadership and the significance of the Ram Mandir.
content:
Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu visited Ayodhya on Sunday and offered special prayers at the Ram Mandir.
Addressing the media later, Mr. Naidu said, “Ram Rajya is the ultimate benchmark for exemplary governance.” The Chief Minister emphasised that the principles followed during Lord Rama’s rule had set an enduring standard for good governance. “We measure the quality of administration by the ideals of Ram Rajya,” he said, highlighting the importance of ethical and people-centric leadership.
Lauding the newly constructed Ram Mandir in Ayodhya, Mr. Naidu said the temple stood as a symbol of India’s rich culture and tradition. The completion of the temple, after years of debates and controversies, fulfilled the aspirations of the people and established Ayodhya as a major spiritual centre in India, he said.
The Chief Minister also praised the Government of Uttar Pradesh led by Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath for exemplifying good governance, alongside the temple’s construction. He expressed hope that the Ayodhya Ram Mandir would serve as a guiding model for other temples across the country.
Mr. Naidu further asserted that India’s technological and developmental progress could not be hindered by anyone, and stressed the pivotal role of States such as Uttar Pradesh and Bihar in achieving the vision of a Viksit Bharat by 2047.
In a post on X, Mr. Naidu said, “Today, I was blessed to have darshan and offer prayers at the divine and magnificent Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Mandir in Ayodhya. It was a peaceful and spiritually uplifting experience to be here once again. Lord Shri Ram’s values and ideals are timeless lessons for us all. May they continue to guide and inspire us always.”

title: 140th National Congress Foundation Day celebrated in Mysuru
summary: Mysuru Congress celebrates 140th Foundation Day, emphasizing constitutional values and opposing BJP's politics, with key leaders addressing the gathering.
content:
The district unit of the Congress celebrated the 140th Foundation Day of the party in the city on December 28, with a resolve to uphold constitutional values and oppose the BJP’s brand of politics.
The event, held at Congress Bhavan under the aegis of the Mysuru District Congress, underlined the importance of adhering to the party’s ideology and conviction. The chief guest was former Minister Kimmane Ratnakar.
Building the Congress party cannot be achieved merely by offering floral tributes, he said, and told party workers, “The true respect to the Foundation Day lies in taking the Congress’ ideas and ideology to the people.”
Mr. Ratnakar lashed out at the BJP for insulting national leaders and said it is even prevalent among a section of the educated, terming it as a reflection of distorted thinking.
The former Minister said the Congress is the only party which had consistently opposed the ideology of the RSS. Given the fundamental difference between the two, party workers should continue to fight the BJP’s ideological stance. Unless one studies the BJP’s ideology, it will be difficult to understand why it must be opposed, said Mr. Ratnakar.
Coming down heavily on the BJP, he said more than 450 million people in the country live in poverty and the government led by Prime Minister Narendra Modi had failed to address unemployment and hunger issues.
He also warned that the BJP is attempting to alter the Constitution, so the Congress should take a firm ideological stand against it.
Dr. B.J. Vijay Kumar, Congress district unit president, said nearly 5,000 freedom fighters had invested as shareholders in the National Herald newspaper and alleged that the Hindu Mahasabha and RSS had opposed the paper even on national issues pertaining to the freedom struggle at that time. In the present times, there are attempts to control it by misusing the Enforcement Directorate, he added.
The party workers were informed that as per the decision of the national Congress Working Committee, movements related to the National Herald and vote theft should not be halted under any circumstance.
Five senior Congress leaders were felicitated to mark the occasion.
R. Murthy, City Congress Committee president, K. Harish Gowda, Chamaraja Assembly constituency MLA, D. Thimmayya, MLC, H.A. Venkatesh, Karnataka Pradesh Congress Committee spokesperson, and others were present.

title: Maharashtra police bust three illegal drug manufacturing units in Bengaluru
summary: Maharashtra police raid three illegal drug manufacturing units in Bengaluru, arresting four and seizing synthetic drugs worth crores.
content:
In a major crackdown on synthetic drug manufacturing ahead of the New Year, the Maharashtra Anti-Narcotics Task Force (ANTF) busted three illegal drug manufacturing units in Bengaluru. Sources said synthetic drugs worth crores were seized and four accused have been arrested.
The operation was carried out by the Konkan division of the Maharashtra ANTF following the trail of a recent drug seizure in Mumbai.
On December 21, the Maharashtra police seized drugs worth ₹1.5 crore in Mumbai and arrested Abdul Khader Shaikh. His interrogation led to the arrest of Prashant Yallappa Patil, a native of Belagavi, Karnataka.
Based on Patil’s disclosure, ANTF teams conducted raids at three locations in Bengaluru, uncovering alleged full-fledged synthetic drug factories operating under the guise of an event management firm named “RJ Event”.
The drug units were located in Horamavu, Yerapannahalli and Kannur. One of the factories was found operating from a shed built inside a farm, strategically located in a remote and isolated area to evade police attention, sources said.
During the raids, the police allegedly seized 4.1 kg of solid MD, 17 kg of liquid MD, totalling 21.4 kg of synthetic drugs. In addition, drug-manufacturing machinery, chemicals, and equipment were also confiscated.
The accused have been identified as Prashant Yallappa Patil (Belagavi), Suraj Ramesh Yadav (Rajasthan), Malkhan Ram Lal Bishnoi (Rajasthan) and one more associate.
Investigators suspect the drugs were being supplied to multiple States across the country, with large-scale production under way specifically for New Year celebrations.
The case has triggered serious questions about Bengaluru Police’s intelligence failure, as such large-scale drug manufacturing units were operating within city limits without detection.
This is the second such incident of drug factory busted. A mephedrone (MD) drug manufacturing factory operating out of a garage was busted in Mysuru in July 2025 through a joint operation by the Mumbai and Mysuru police, leading to four arrests and the seizure of drugs and raw materials valued at approximately ₹390 crore.
Taking strong exception to the lapse on the part of the jurisdictional police, Home Minister G. Parameshwara ordered the City Police Commissioner to conduct a probe and submit a report.
However, Dr. Parameshwara said claims of a ₹58 crore seizure was far from the truth. He clarified that based on inputs from Maharashtra Police, a joint operation involving Mumbai Police, Bengaluru City Police, the NCB and SOCO teams led to the arrest of an accused in Bengaluru, who was found in possession of 4 kg of mephedrone chemical, valued at ₹1.2 crore.
He dismissed allegations that Bengaluru Police had failed to act, stating that joint inter-State operations are routinely conducted based on shared intelligence. Claims about three drug factories being unearthed were also termed false.
The Home Minister warned that strict action would be taken against any officer — whether DCP, ACP or local officials — found responsible for lapses. “Action will not be limited to suspension alone,” he said.
According to sources, the Home Minister made it clear that merely claiming seizures worth “hundreds of crores” would not absolve officers of responsibility.
Meanwhile, former Chief Minister and senior BJP leader Basavaraj Bommai alleged that the situation clearly indicates police complicity. “When Maharashtra police have to come and bust a drug manufacturing unit in Mysuru and drug-selling dens in Bengaluru, it shows that police here are colluding with drug traffickers,” he alleged.
He claimed that drugs are freely available across the State, including within school and college limits in Ranebennur and Haveri.
Warning of serious consequences, he said, “Just as there was ‘Udta Punjab’, Karnataka is now heading towards becoming ‘Udta Karnataka’ if the government does not act immediately.”

title: 85th edition of Numaish to open in Hyderabad on January 1 with expanded safety, transport and civic arrangements
summary: The 85th Numaish in Hyderabad opens January 1, featuring enhanced safety, transport, and visitor amenities until February 15.
content:
The exhibition will continue till February 15 and will be open daily from 4 p.m. to 10.30 p.m. on working days, and till 11 p.m. on Saturdays, Sundays and public holidays
The 85th All India Industrial Exhibition, popularly known as Numaish, is scheduled to be inaugurated on January 1 at the Exhibition Grounds in Hyderabad, with elaborate arrangements in place for security, fire safety, transport connectivity, medical services and visitor convenience. The exhibition will continue till February 15.
The exhibition will remain open daily from 4 p.m. to 10.30 p.m. on working days, while on Saturdays, Sundays and public holidays it will operate until 11 p.m. The entry ticket has been priced at ₹50 per person, while children below the age of five years will be allowed free entry.
Connectivity to the exhibition grounds will be supported by enhanced public transport arrangements. Metro Rail services from Gandhi Bhavan and Nampally Metro stations will run with increased frequency and extended operating hours to match exhibition timings. The Telangana State Road Transport Corporation (TGSRTC) will also operate special bus services to the venue, said Minister for Industries and Commerce D. Sridhar Babu during a press conference on Sunday.
Stalls nearing completion for the upcoming 85th All India Industrial Exhibition, also known as Numaish at the Exhibition Grounds, Nampally in Hyderabad on Sunday.
                                                            | Photo Credit: 
                                SIDDHANT THAKUR
Free parking facilities for two-wheelers and four-wheelers will be available around the exhibition grounds at Gruha Kalpa, Chandra Vihar, Gagan Vihar and Bhimrao Vada, the open compound adjacent to the Telangana Public Service Commission (TGPSC) office building. An automated multi-level paid parking facility will also be available near Handloom House, located less than 100 metres from Gate No. 1 of the exhibition grounds at the Gandhi Bhavan entrance.
“A total of 106 security personnel will be deployed at the gates and within the premises to ensure visitor safety and prevent prohibited items from being brought into the grounds. In addition, 138 day volunteers will assist visitors, with particular attention to women and elderly persons, while 76 night volunteers will be deployed to safeguard the belongings of stallholders. The entire exhibition grounds and surrounding areas will be under CCTV surveillance, with 120 cameras installed,” the Minister added.
Stalls nearing completion for the upcoming 85th All India Industrial Exhibition, also known as Numaish at the Exhibition Grounds, Nampally in Hyderabad on Sunday.
                                                            | Photo Credit: 
                                SIDDHANT THAKUR
Extensive fire safety measures have also been put in place. Two underground water storage tanks with a capacity of 1.5 lakh litres each have been installed and connected to 82 fire hydrants, maintaining constant water pressure of 7 kg per sq cm. As many as 45 trained volunteers will monitor the hydrant system. Additionally, two fire engines with a capacity of 10,000 litres each will be stationed within the Exhibition Grounds by the Fire Department throughout the event.
A total of 1,050 manufacturers and artisans from different parts of the country, along with local participants, will be showcasing their products. Around 20 food stalls will serve a variety of cuisines.

title: BJP hits back at YSRCP over allegations on medical college under PPP model
summary: BJP defends PPP model for medical colleges, criticising YSRCP's allegations as baseless and aimed at creating public confusion.
content:
The BJP criticised the YSRCP for spreading misinformation regarding medical colleges under Public-Private Partnership (PPP) model.
In a statement on Sunday, BJP A.P. spokesperson Sadineni Yamini Sarma described the YSRCP’s allegations as a baseless attack aimed at creating confusion and fear among the public.
Referring to the letter written by Union Health Minister J.P. Nadda to A.P. Minister for Health Satya Kumar Yadav, defending the PPP model, Ms. Yamini Sarma  said the letter highlighted that the model has already been successfully implemented in 20 States, with 919 diagnostic centers currently operational. The Union government provides up to 80% viability gap funding, and each project receives financial support of ₹5 crore. The letter also emphasised the urgent need to complete the construction of medical colleges promptly to ensure citizens receive high-quality healthcare services, she said.
Ms. Yamini Sarma accused the YSRCP of resorting to false narratives and venomous statements over allegations of crores of rupees in medical college projects, suggesting that the party fears exposure of widespread corruption under the Jagan government. She also called on YSRCP leaders, including its president Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy, to act responsibly and prioritise public welfare instead of misleading people with baseless claims.

title: Education only path to development, says  Nirmala Sitharaman
summary: Nirmala Sitharaman emphasizes education as the key to development during the inauguration of new school facilities and an AI hub.
content:
Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman on Sunday said education alone was the true pathway to development, and urged youth to focus on education and sports, which bring global recognition and prestige to India.
Ms. Sitharaman was speaking after inaugurating the computer and science laboratories, and other basic infrastructure worth ₹18 lakh in the Zilla Parishad High School at Pedamainavanilanka village of Narasapuram mandal in West Godavari district. The facilities were provided with the support of the Union Bank of India.
Addressing the students, she said both the Central and State governments were committed to ensuring that every student pursued higher education and achieved greater heights in life.
Interacting with the students, she stressed the importance of digital classrooms in helping them understand global developments and meet modern education standards.
She particularly urged the youth from the coastal regions to pursue higher studies and contribute meaningfully to the development of the State and the nation.
“Focus on education; development and welfare are our responsibility,” Ms. Sitharaman said, adding that a combination of education and sports could elevate India’s standing on the global stage. “Shaping the country’s future rests with today’s youth.,” she added.
Union Minister of State for Steel and Heavy Industries Bhupathiraju Srinivasa Varma, Andhra Pradesh Finance Minister Payyavula Keshav, Water Resources Minister Nimmala Ramanaidu, BJP State president P.V.N. Madhav, District Collector Chadalavada Nagarani, Superintendent of Police Adnan Nayeem Asmi, and several MLAs were among those present.
Mr. Madhav said the transformation of the remote coastal village of Pedamainavanilanka reflected Ms. Sitharaman’s sustained commitment to development. He noted that despite her demanding responsibilities as Finance Minister, she had shown consistent concern for protecting the village from sea erosion and supporting development initiatives over the past decade.
Later, Ms. Sitharaman inaugurated the Cyient AI & Future Skills Hub at the Digital Bhavan in the village. Established under the Cyient Foundation, the centre aims at promoting rural employment and empower youth and women with AI-based, future-ready skills, aligning with national initiatives such as Digital India, Skill India and Viksit Bharat-2047.
Cyient Limited’s founder-Chairman B.V.R. Mohan Reddy said the initiative reflected the company’s commitment to inclusive digital growth, noting that the foundation had already digitised over 120 government schools and provided digital literacy to more than 35,000 students.

title: CPI(M) alleges Congress-BJP nexus behind power shifts in Mattathur
summary: CPI(M) accuses Congress of collaborating with BJP in Mattathur, exposing tactical voting and defections undermining local democracy.
content:
The mass defection of the Congress members in Mattathur in Thrissur to the Bharatiya Janata Party-led (BJP) front is a premeditated and well-planned move carried out with the full knowledge of the Congress leadership, alleged K. V. Abdul Khader, secretary, Communist Party of India (Marxist) [CPI(M)] Thrissur District Committee.
“Eight Congress representatives did not hesitate to betray even the voters who elected them, choosing instead to align with the BJP’s communal politics. What has unfolded in the district is merely a new version of the unholy alliances earlier witnessed in Vadakara and Beypore. The so-called suspension action taken against those involved is nothing more than an attempt to throw dust in the eyes of the public,” he said.
In the Paralam panchayat, where the Congress and the BJP had equal strength, the Congress handed over power to the BJP by deliberately invalidating its own vote. No matter how much justification is offered, this episode once again exposes how real and deep the Congress–BJP undercurrent truly is, he alleged.
In Chovannur too, the Congress showed no hesitation in securing the president’s post with the support of the Social Democratic Party of India (SDPI) votes. This has triggered strong criticism, even from within the party’s own ranks.
The Congress party’s collaboration with communal and fascist forces will ultimately erode its own political base. A strong and united mass movement will be raised against this communal nexus of the Congress, Mr. Khader added.

title: Mattathur political drama deepens as suspended Congress members hit back
summary: Political tensions escalate in Mattathur as suspended Congress members reject defection claims and accuse CPI(M) of corruption cover-up.
content:
The political turmoil in the Mattathur grama panchayat showed no signs of abating, with rebel Congress members stepping forward to counter the party leadership’s claims, even as the District Congress Committee (DCC) announced suspensions.
Addressing a press conference here on Sunday, panchayat president Tessy Thomas and expelled former DCC general secretary T.M. Chandran categorically denied allegations that Congress members had defected to the BJP. They described as ‘blatantly false’ the DCC president’s claim that a party whip had been issued for the president election or that Congress members had formally joined the BJP. Mandalam president Shafi Kalluparambil and other ward members were also present at the press meet.
Mr. Chandran said the members had taken a clear and conscious political stand on the change in leadership. He alleged that the developments in the president election were the fallout of a ‘conspiracy’ by the CPI(M) to cover up corruption in previous ruling committees by allegedly ‘buying off’ Congress member K.P. Ouseph.
According to Mr. Chandran, 24 candidates contested under the UDF banner, and with the Congress and LDF having equal strength of 10 members each, the presidency would have been decided by draw, giving either Mr. Ouseph or a CPI(M) nominee a 50% chance. “To eliminate that uncertainty, the CPI(M) bought off Mr. Ouseph,” he alleged.
Mr. Chandran further said that when the president election began, Mr. Ouseph’s name was proposed by CPI(M) members, prompting Congress members to put forward Tessy Thomas, an Independent candidate. He claimed BJP members may have voted for the Congress candidate due to their hostility towards the CPI(M). “Ms. Thomas secured 12 votes while Mr. Ouseph got 11,” he said.
The members also said no one had sought explanations from them and that they had not received any formal communication regarding expulsion from primary party membership. They insisted they would never join the BJP and said the leadership of the party and the KPCC should intervene to resolve the crisis in Mattathur. They maintained that supporting an Independent president was based on local political realities and public sentiment, and that they had not adopted any anti-party stance.
Meanwhile, a DCC press release announced the suspension of Mr. Chandran, Mr. Kalluparambil and 10 ward members for violating party guidelines and engineering ‘alleged’ mass defection in Mattathur to align with the BJP. The party also suspended Nidheesh A.M. and Sabetta Varghese for violating party directions by contesting the president and vice-president posts in Chovannur grama panchayat.

title: Congress to contest 100 seats in 126-member Assam Assembly polls next year: Gaurav Gogoi
summary: Congress plans to contest 100 seats in Assam's 2026 Assembly elections, rejecting alliances with AIUDF, asserts Gaurav Gogoi.
content:
Assam Congress president Gaurav Gogoi said on Sunday (December 28, 2025) that the party will contest 100 seats in the 126-member State Assembly elections next year, leaving the remaining constituencies to its alliance partners.
He also asserted that the Congress will not forge any understanding with AIUDF, terming it a "communal" party.
Addressing a meeting on the 141st foundation day of the party, Mr. Gogoi said that in order to defeat the “anti-people BJP”, the Congress will contest the 2026 Assam Assembly elections by forming alliances with like-minded parties.
He said that “under no circumstances, a communal party like the AIUDF will be included in this alliance”.
"The Congress will "contest 100 constituencies, out of the 126 seats in the state, while the remaining assembly segments will be left for alliance partners through mutual discussions," he said.
“Under the leadership of the Congress, the dignity that has been taken away from the people of Assam will be restored. The Congress believes in peace and unity, while the BJP thrives on unrest and division. The Congress has faith in the Constitution, whereas the BJP seeks to destroy democracy and establish a form of authoritarian rule,” Mr. Gogoi claimed.
The Congress’ deputy leader of opposition in Lok Sabha alleged that the BJP is systematically snatching away the rights of the people.
Mr. Gogoi claimed that the poor benefited during the tenure of former Chief Minister Tarun Gogoi, and assured that if the Congress returns to power, the people would witness “real and meaningful change”.
He asserted that a separate law will be enacted to take strict action against those spreading religious hatred if the Congress comes to power.
“Whether it is a church, ‘namghar’ (Vaishnavite place of worship), temple or mosque, anyone who attempts to desecrate a place of worship will face strict punitive action. In Assam of Sankardeva-Madhavdeva and Ajan Pir, divisive forces will never be tolerated," the Congress MP said.
As part of the Congress' foundation day celebrations, Mr. Gogoi hoisted the party flag and paid floral tributes to the portraits of Mahatma Gandhi and Assam’s cultural icon Zubeen Garg.
A procession was also taken out in Tezpur on the occasion, with top state party leaders, including former presidents Bhupen Borah and Ripun Bora, participating in it.

title: Implement internal committees under POSH Act in party offices across A.P., says CPI(M)
summary: CPI(M) urges Andhra Pradesh Women's Commission to implement internal committees under POSH Act in political party offices for workplace safety.
content:
CPI(M) State secretary V. Srinivasa Rao on Sunday wrote a letter to the Andhra Pradesh Women’s Commission Chairperson Rayapati Sailaja, urging her to ensure the effective implementation of internal committees under the Prevention of Sexual Harassment (POSH) Act in political party offices across the State.
In his letter, Mr. Srinivas Rao welcomed the Commission’s efforts to amend and strengthen the POSH Act for wider application in Andhra Pradesh. He highlighted that although political parties were currently exempt, CPI(M) has voluntarily adopted the law’s spirit and implemented it across its offices in the State.
He said that since the law came into effect, the party had taken necessary measures for compliance. During the 2018 CPI(M) All India Conference, the party had passed a resolution to implement the law in all party offices nationwide. Consequently, internal committees were established at the central, State, and district levels, including Andhra Pradesh, with boards publicly displayed at the State office.
Mr. Srinivas Rao stressed the growing need to prevent sexual harassment at workplaces, especially in political environments, and requested the Commission’s guidance to ensure all parties comply. He called for monitoring measures to protect women employees and activists, particularly those entering politics, from any harassment or misconduct by senior or influential individuals.
The CPI(M) leader expressed hope that the Women’s Commission would pay special attention to the establishment of internal committees in all political party offices and ensure that women were provided with a safe and supportive working environment.
A copy of the board displayed at the CPI(M) State office was attached to the letter for reference.

title: BJP-led NDA wins control of eight grama panchayats in Alappuzha
summary: The front wins four of the seats through a draw of lots
content:
The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)-led National Democratic Alliance (NDA) assumed power in eight grama panchayats, including four through draw of lots, in Alappuzha district on Saturday.
Following the Kerala local body elections earlier this month, the NDA emerged as the single largest bloc in four grama panchayats – Budhanoor (seven seats), Karthikappally (six seats), Neelamperoor (seven seats) and Thiruvanvandoor (five seats).
BJP’s Pramod Kumar and Sreeja Sreekumar were elected president and vice-president of Budhanoor grama panchayat, respectively. In Karthikappally, the saffron party’s Ullasan P. was sworn in as president, while Vineetha was elected vice-president. Vinayachandran R. and Neethu Joseph, both BJP members, assumed office as president and vice-president of Neelamperoor panchayat, respectively.
In Thiruvanvandoor, the Congress-led United Democratic Front (UDF), which won four seats in the local body polls, was able to match the NDA’s strength with the support of independent member K.K.S. Kurup. However, BJP member Smitha Rajesh assumed office as president of the local body after she and Kerala Congress (UDF) candidate Shiny Thomas were tied in the election to the president’s post even after the second round of voting (five votes each). This led to a draw of lots, which went in Ms. Rajesh’s favour. Meanwhile, Mr. Kurup was elected vice-president with the support of UDF members and another independent.
Besides these four local bodies, the NDA also came to power in Ala, Chennithala Thripperuthura and Chennam Pallippuram, all through draw of lots. In Ala, where the NDA and the UDF secured five seats each, Aneesha Biju and T.G. Rajesh, both BJP members, were elected president and vice-president, respectively. V. Binuraj of the BJP assumed office as president of Chennithala Thripperuthura, where the NDA and the Left Democratic Front (LDF) won seven seats each, while Ajitha Devarajan of the Communist Party of India (Marxist) was elected vice-president. In Chennam Pallippuram, BJP’s V. Vineetha and Dinesh Kumar were sworn in as president and vice-president, respectively.  In the elections, both the NDA and the UDF secured seven seats each in the local body.
In Pandanad, the post of panchayat president was reserved for a Scheduled Caste (SC) woman. Though the UDF, with six members, was the single largest bloc in the local body, its SC woman candidate lost the local body polls. The LDF also does not have an SC woman member. Jiji Kunjukunju of the BJP became president of the panchayat unopposed. Meanwhile, Geevarghese P.G. of the Congress was elected vice-president.
Elsewhere in the district, the LDF assumed power in 35 grama panchayats and the UDF in 27. Polls to the posts of president in Veeyapuram and Nedumudi will be held on Monday. In block panchayats, the LDF came to power in eight and the UDF in four.

title: Newborn taken to Hubballi from Koppal with zero-traffic arrangement
summary: A critical newborn was urgently transferred from Koppal to Hubballi using a zero-traffic corridor for life-saving treatment.
content:
A newborn boy suffering from a critical congenital condition was shifted from the Koppal Institute of Medical Sciences (KIMS) to Karnataka Medical College and Research Institute (KMCRI) Hospital, Hubballi, under a specially arranged zero-traffic corridor on Sunday to ensure timely life-saving treatment.
The baby was born late on Saturday night at the government hospital in Kuknoor taluk in Koppal district.
The newborn belongs to Mallappa and Vijayalakshmi, residents of Guttur village in Kuknoor taluk.
Doctors noticed that the newborn had severe complications, with the intestines protruding outside the abdominal cavity, necessitating immediate advanced medical intervention.
Following initial stabilisation at the Mother and Child Hospital in Koppal, doctors decided to refer the infant to KMCRI Hubballi for higher treatment. To avoid any delay, the district authorities arranged a zero-traffic corridor with the support of the Police Department.
Five ambulances were deployed to ensure uninterrupted movement, while medical personnel continuously monitored the infant’s condition during transit. Police regulated traffic along key routes to facilitate a smooth and swift passage for the convoy.
However, the newborn’s condition remains critical, while every effort is being made to save his life, sources said.

title: Five arrested with drugs, ganja and 70 non-duty paid liquor bottles in multiple raids across Hyderabad
summary: Five arrested in Hyderabad raids for drug and liquor trafficking, with significant seizures of MDMA, ganja, and non-duty paid liquor.
content:
Five persons were arrested and drugs, ganja and non-duty paid liquor bottles were seized in a series of enforcement operations conducted by excise officials across parts of Hyderabad and Rangareddy districts.
In the first case, following a tip off that drugs were being transported from Bengaluru to Hyderabad, the State Task Force (STF)-B team carried out vehicle checks near Shamshabad. A cab arriving from Shamshabad airport was stopped and searched, leading to seizure of 5.39 grams of MDMA, six non-duty paid liquor bottles and three mobile phones.
The accused, identified as Sai Charan, was taken into custody and handed over to the Shamshabad Excise Station along with the seized material.
In another major seizure, STF teams seized 6.3 kilograms of ganja being smuggled from Odisha during a raid near Raghavendra Bhavan in HUDA Colony, within the limits of Saroornagar Excise Station.
Three persons from Odisha, identified as Behan Dure, Jagannath Dal and Saroj Jalari, were arrested. They were produced before the Saroornagar Excise Station along with the contraband for further legal action.
State Task Force officials presenting the accused and the seized contraband before the media on Sunday
                                                            | Photo Credit: 
                                By Arrangement
In a separate operation, Shamshabad District Task Force (DTF) personnel conducted a raid in Ramguda and seized 1.3 kg of ganja from a man identified as Dilip Koche, a resident of Assam.  The accused and the seized ganja were handed over to the Serilingampally Excise Station for further investigation.
Meanwhile, during vehicle checks, the officials seized 64 non-duty paid liquor bottles that were being transported to Hyderabad from various locations. The seized liquor was handed over to the Rangareddy  enforcement team with the assistance of the Maheshwaram and Meerpet police. Investigations are underway in all the cases.

title: Stress laid on fostering artistic and cultural awareness among students
summary: Sargotsavam 2025 promotes artistic awareness among students, aiming to prevent substance abuse and foster cultural engagement in youth.
content:
Minister for Registration and Museums Kadannappally Ramachandran on Sunday (December 28) said fostering artistic and cultural awareness among students was essential to prevent them from drifting towards dangers such as substance abuse.
He was inaugurating ‘Sargotsavam 2025’, the State-level arts festival of students from model residential schools under the Scheduled Tribes Development department, at the Collectorate ground here. He said that cultural festivals like Sargotsavam, which blend creativity and imagination, could play a key role in involving youth in nation-building.
The Minister said the State government followed a policy of inclusion, ensuring equality for communities that had once faced neglect and oppression. Kerala, he said, had created conditions for people to live with dignity and equality across sectors.
Presiding over the function, K.V. Sumesh, MLA, said Sargotsavam was an important platform that enabled students to showcase their creative talents alongside academic pursuits. M. Vijin, MLA, was the chief guest. Kannur Corporation councillor Leesha Deepak and Scheduled Tribes Development department Director Mithun Premraja were present.
Earlier, a colourful procession announcing the festival was taken out in the town. The event will conclude on December 30.

title: Indian knowledge systems needs protection, preservation, says NSU Vice Chancellor
summary: NSU Vice Chancellor emphasizes the need to protect and preserve ancient Indian knowledge systems for future generations' benefit.
content:
National Sanskrit University (NSU) Vice Chancellor G.S.R. Krishna Murthy said that the ancient Indian knowledge system needs protection and preservation for the benefit of future generations of the country.
He released the book ‘Foundation of Indian Knowledge System: Political, Economic Strategic Agriculture and Veterinary Sciences’ written by Hanumanthu Lajapathirai, former Vice Chancellor of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar University and Director of Valmiki Research Centre of Ramanarayanam temple in Vizianagaram.
In a note released on Sunday (December 28, 2025), Dr. Krishna Murthy said that modern science would benefit from ancient wisdom, as reflected in books written by individuals with a national perspective. Dr. Lajapathirai thanked Dr. Krishna Murthy for promoting Indian culture, tradition, and heritage.

title: BRS wants Assembly session for at least 15 days to debate all issues
summary: BRS demands a 15-day Assembly session to debate crucial state issues, criticizing Congress for inadequate legislative days.
content:
HYDERABAD
Senior leader of Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) and former Minister T. Harish Rao alleged that the Congress had spoiled every established system in the State, including the legislature, and as against its demand for holding sittings for at least 45 days a year when in Opposition, the sessions were held only for 40 days in two years.
In an informal chat with newspersons on the eve of the winter session of the Assembly on Sunday, he reminded that the BRS government in the past had conducted the sessions on an average of 32 days a year compared to Congress’s 20. The Congress government had run the Assembly for 24 days in 2024 and for just 16 days in 2025.
Of the 40 days of sitting during the last two years, two days went for condolence motions, three days for tabling white papers, one day for discussion of the Kaleshwaram Commission report and one day for backward classes reservation enhancement. He demanded that the government run this session at least for 15 working days and the BRS was ready to participate in the debate on any issue brought up by the government. He also appealed to the government to take up discussion on the issues raised by BRS too.
Mr. Harish Rao demanded a discussion on the government writing a letter to the Ministry of Jal Shakti to clear Palamuru-Rangareddy Lift Irrigation Scheme with 45 tmc ft water utilisation against the originally intended 90 tmc ft, urea shortage, HILT policy, incomplete crop loan waiver, crop bonus, irregular Rythu Bandhu, food poisoning in residential schools, employees’ issues and others.

title: Vijayawada’s real estate sees moderate progress in 2025
summary: Vijayawada's real estate shows moderate growth in 2025, hindered by global uncertainty despite government efforts to boost the sector.
content:
The real estate sector in and around Vijayawada reported a gradual progress in the year 2025, however, industry experts consider it to be slightly off the mark as they had expected a boom following the shift in focus to Amaravati capital region.
Confederation of Real Estate Developers’ Associations of India (CREDAI), Andhra Pradesh, secretary D. Rambabu said the sector fell short of meeting their expectations this year. Despite the government’s efforts to streamline the approval process, such as amendments to the Building Rules 2017, introducing the Self-Certification Scheme (SCS) 2025, and abolishing the NALA Act, the business has been slow, he said.
Explaining the reasons, Mr. Rambabu said: “The sector has been witnessing a temporary slowdown due to global economic uncertainty. Due to shifting foreign policies, foreign institutional investors and NRI investors have adopted a wait-and-watch policy.”
However, the scenario is not all gloom. Land prices in areas surrounding Amaravati jumped by 15-20% since early 2024, with some areas seeing up to 40% year-on-year increase in residential demand, he said, adding that the rental market in the city had seen average demand.
CREDAI Vijayawada chapter chairman C. Sathish Babu agreed with Mr. Rambabu and said that while there is a clarity on the capital now, infrastructure has not come to Amaravati yet. “Investors need to feel confident. While the government has been taking positive steps, we feel it may take one to two years for the results to show. At present, it is a buyers’ market, and not the sellers’,” Mr. Sathish Babu said.
There are also other issues, including the lingering effects of policies taken during the previous regime, 5% GST, 7.5% registration fee, that have brought the business down. Also, the Vijayawada-Guntur region has many people who settled in foreign countries. “NRI investments contribute heavily to the market here. The global trends have affected their role,” Mr. Sathish Babu said.
While real estate brokers in the city feel the capital has brought all the activity to Tadepalli and Vijayawada outskirts and the city itself seeing a lull in the rental business, Builders’ Association of India, Amaravati, Chairman Maturi Ranganath predicted growth for Vijayawada in the next 10 years.
Meanwhile, National Real Estate Development Council (NAREDCO) Central Zone president Sandeep Mandava is hopeful that the business will improve next year. “While the first half of 2025 opened to a slow start, the business picked up in the second half. At present, momentum is picking up in Tadepalli, on the airport side, in areas close to the airport, including Poranki in the city. We expect this to continue,” Mr. Sandeep Mandava said.

title: Sumesh Achuthan is IFFCO director
summary: Sumesh Achuthan elected as IFFCO director, representing Kerala, Tamil Nadu, and Puducherry in the cooperative's board.
content:
Chittur-Thattamangalam municipal chairperson Sumesh Achuthan was elected director of the Indian Farmers Fertilizer Cooperative Ltd (IFFCO), one of the largest cooperative movements in the world.
Mr. Achuthan will represent Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Puducherry regions in the 21-member IFFCO director board.
With 36,000 cooperative societies under it, the IFFCO is the largest cooperative fertilizer producer in the country. It reaches out to 5.5 crore farmers in the country with fertilizers through cooperative bodies.
Prior to Mr. Achuthan, P.P. Thankachan and Jose Kuttyani were the only representatives from Kerala to serve on the IFFCO board of directors.
Mr. Achuthan contested the IFFCO election as the Thattamangalam Service Cooperative Bank’s representative from Palakkad district.

title: Some seers oppose Babaleshwar Basavadi Sharanara Bruhat Hindu Samavesha
summary: Lingayat seers oppose the Babaleshwar Hindu Samavesha, citing political motives and concerns over abusive remarks by a prominent seer.
content:
Some Lingayat seers have opposed the Basavadi Sharanara Hindu Bruhat Samavesha in Babaleshwar of Vijayapura district planned on Monday.
Abhinava Murughendra Swami of Mamadapura Virakta Math, Masabinal, Sri Siddarama Shivayogi and Gunadal Vivekananda Devaru told reporters in Vijayapura on Sunday that the event has been planned in support of Sri Adrushya Kadasiddheshwara Swamij of Kaneri Math who is facing allegations of using abusive language against some Lingayat seers.
“No religion preaches hate. All faiths speak of love, affection and coexistence. However, the Kaneri Math seer has been displaying hatred towards people of some faiths. He has also insulted Lingayat seers repeatedly. This cannot be accepted. True Veerashaiva Lingayat seers will not support it,” Murughendra Swami said.
“The Kaneri Math seer has been reprimanded by the Supreme Court for his use of abusive words. This samavesha is being held to glorify a swami who has insulted swamis with abusive words and for political purposes. None of the real swamis will participate in this,” Murughendra Swami added.
Siddarama Shivayogi of Masabinal said that the Babaleshwar event is a political rally and not a spiritual event. “It should be cancelled, if the community is to get a positive message. Otherwise, the society will get a message that seers are creating problems among the community,” he said.
Sri Vivekananda Devaru of Gunadal said that the speeches of Kaneri Math seer are not fit to be a role model for younger seers. He demanded that senior seers speak and act in a way that inspire younger ones.
Meanwhile, Vijayapura MLA Basanagouda Patil Yatnal has also opposed the event saying it is being used by some BJP leaders for their political benefits.
BJP leader Vijugouda Patil, who has lost from Babaleshwar several times, is using the event to increase his chances the next time. “He is not a great leader. He is organising it for his selfish interest. I will not attend any such event,” Mr. Yatnal told reporters in Vijayapura on Saturday.
Earlier, Hindu activist Raghava Annigeri told reporters that over 300 Hindu saints and Lingayat seers will attend the Hindu Samavesha.
“We are strongly opposed to the travel ban of Sri Adrushya Kadasiddheshwara Swamij of Kaneri Math. Instead of punishing those who routinely insult Hindu Gods, the State government has banned the entry of Kaneri Math seer to some districts. However, his ban to Vijayapura is ending now and he is eligible to speak at Babaleshwar. The Kaneri Math seer has replied to those who spoke insulting Hindu deities in their own language,” Mr. Annigeri said.
He denied suggestions that it is a political meeting. “This is a Hindu Shakti Sangam. Hindus should work together as this is not a time for us to fight among ourselves. There is no need to give importance to the statement made by some people’s representatives who are against our interests,” he said.

title: Panel to recommend reviving student body election
summary: Karnataka's Congress government forms panel to recommend revival of student body elections after decades-long ban.
content:
Student union elections that have been banned for over three decades in Karnataka are being sought to be revived by the Congress government.
A nine-member committee has been formed to recommend ways to hold student body elections in the State through which new leaders could be identified. The panel that will have Ministers M.C. Sudhakar and Sharan Prakash Patil, MLCs Saleem Ahmed and Puttanna, besides former Youth Congress presidents and NSUI presidents, will submit a report to the government, Deputy Chief Minister and KPCC President D.K. Shivakumar said on Sunday.
Speaking at the Congress Foundation Day, Mr. Shivakkumar said that the current crop of leaders, including himself, came to politics through student body elections. “Later when violence during the student body elections surged, it was stopped”.

title: NITK uses machine learning to predict landslides in Western Ghats
summary: NITK develops SVALSA, a machine learning-based landslide warning system for the Western Ghats, enhancing disaster preparedness and safety.
content:
Researchers at the National Institute of Technology Karnataka (NITK), Surathkal, have developed an integrated landslide early warning framework designed specifically for the Western Ghats, one of India’s most landslide-prone regions.
The system, called Slope Vulnerability and LandSlide Assessment (SVALSA), combines rainfall analysis, real-time monitoring of soil behaviour and surface movement, and machine learning to provide reliable landslide warnings while reducing false alarms.
The Western Ghats account for nearly 60% of reported landslides in India, with most triggered by intense and prolonged rainfall. Recent disasters, including the July 2024 Wayanad landslide, have highlighted the limitations of existing warning systems and the need for more accurate, site-specific alerts.
At present, landslide warnings in India are largely based on rainfall thresholds, where alerts are issued when rainfall crosses certain intensity or duration limits. These systems, while useful, often fail to account for what is happening inside the slope itself. As a result, they can generate frequent false alarms or miss impending failures when soil conditions deteriorate even under moderate rainfall.
The SVALSA framework addresses this gap by moving beyond rainfall-only alerts. It integrates hydrological data, soil strength behaviour and visible surface deformation into a single decision system that reflects how slopes actually fail in the Western Ghats. More than 90% of landslides in the region occur in residual soils formed from weathered rock, where changes in moisture content and soil suction play a critical role in slope stability.
The SVALSA device is currently under patent application. The research was developed by Varun Menon under the supervision of Sreevalsa Kolathayar, with funding support from the Department of Science and Technology (DST), IMPRINT (Impacting Research Innovation and Technology), and the National Technical Textiles Mission (NTTM) under the Ministry of Textiles.

The system operates through a three-stage warning mechanism implemented as a Python-based algorithm on a compact processing unit.
In the first stage, rainfall data from government records and past landslides are analysed using a machine-learning method called K-Nearest Neighbour (KNN). The model compares current rainfall with earlier landslide-triggering events and filters out low-risk situations, reducing unnecessary alerts. Tests showed the method to be highly accurate.
If rainfall conditions appear risky, the second stage assesses soil stability using a modified version of the simplified Bishop method, which factors in soil moisture and suction based on unsaturated soil mechanics. Laboratory tests confirmed that slope stability decreases as soil absorbs more water.
