The study, led by P.O. Nameer, Dean, College of Climate Change and Environmental Science, KAU, analysed the presence of two common migratory duck species — Garganey and Northern Pintail —and compared their distribution with 10 bird flu epicentres reported in April/May 2024.
“Garganey and Northern Pintail numbers peaked in the districts between February and March. Crucially, both species were largely absent in April in the three districts when bird flu cases were reported and their sightings were far from the epicentres,” said Dr. Nameer, adding that migratory birds could not be confirmed as the source of avian influenza without virological testing.
The report further raised concerns about biosecurity lapses, particularly the practice of bringing ducks from Tamil Nadu and rearing them in wetlands.
Earlier, an expert panel constituted by the Animal Husbandry Department (AHD) following the 2024 avian flu outbreak suggested that migratory birds could be the source of the virus.
Boby Rajan, chief disease investigation officer, State Institute for Animal Diseases, Palode, said the assumption that migratory birds could be the source of the infection was based on “circumstantial evidence”.
Most avian flu outbreaks coincided with migratory seasons and initially occurred in wetland regions of Alappuzha and Kottayam, which attract large numbers of migratory birds. Dr. Rajan pointed out that the virus strain detected in domesticated birds in Kerala was the same as that found globally.
He said there was no mechanism for screening migratory birds. “Migratory birds act as reservoir hosts without showing symptoms and that collecting samples is difficult as they roost in marshy or inaccessible areas. Though samples collected earlier by the Avian Disease Diagnostic Laboratory (ADDL), Thiruvalla, tested negative, the possibility of infection from migratory birds cannot not be ruled out solely on that basis,” Dr. Rajan added.
Besides the ADDL, Kerala Veterinary and Animal Sciences University (KVASU) and the AHD, among others, collected samples from migratory and wild birds over the years, but none tested positive for avian influenza.
T.P. Sethumadhavan, former director, KVASU, and professor, University of Trans-Disciplinary Health Sciences and Technology, Bengaluru, said repeated outbreaks in Kuttanad called for detailed research and strong diagnostic studies.
“Though the government in 2015 assured that a National Centre for Bird Flu would be established in Alappuzha, nothing has materialised so far. Instead of assumptions, stakeholder-driven research, including comprehensive epidemiological studies, is required, along with a clear assessment of economic losses. Universities such as KVASU and the AHD should take the lead with greater emphasis on multidisciplinary studies,” Dr. Sethumadhavan noted.
Dr. Nameer, meanwhile, suggested continuous monitoring of wild birds, stricter biosecurity checks on poultry transport from neighbouring States, regular farm inspections and coordinated field investigations involving ornithologists, veterinarians and public health experts for early detection of avian influenza.

title: Two policemen in the dock for harassing and extorting ₹500 from four men in Bengaluru
summary: Two Bengaluru policemen face charges for allegedly extorting ₹500 from four men during a late-night harassment incident.
content:
Two policemen are in the dock for allegedly harassing a group of four men returning home late at night in Byappanahalli and forcing them to pay ₹500 for ‘venturing out’ in what they claimed was a ‘sensitive area’.
The incident occurred on Sunday night when the four men booked a cab from Indiranagar to Byappanahalli. After getting down and while walking towards their residence, they were allegedly intercepted by two beat policemen in Sadanandanagar.
The policemen reportedly questioned them for being out late at night and claimed the area was under “high alert” following a robbery reported last month. Despite the men explaining their identity and reason for being there, the policemen allegedly refused to let them go.
According to the victims, the policemen threatened to book them under the Karnataka Police Act and warned that a Hoysala patrol vehicle would be called to take them to the police station. When the men objected, the policemen allegedly claimed they had the authority to do so and produced an old form dated 2022 to make the threat appear official.
The policemen initially demanded ₹1,000 to let them go, which was later negotiated down to ₹500. The amount was paid on the spot.
The entire conversation was recorded on a mobile phone, and the victims later raised a complaint on social media, tagging the Bengaluru City Police. Following the post, the police officials said they have begun probing the incident and have sought further details from the victims.

title: Killing of Tripura student in Dehradun a horrific ‘hate crime’: Rahul Gandhi
summary: Rahul Gandhi condemns the killing of Tripura student Angel Chakma in Dehradun as a horrific hate crime fuelled by toxic narratives.
content:
Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi on Monday (December 29, 2025) called the killing of a Tripura student in Uttarakhand's Dehradun a "horrific hate crime", as he accused the ruling BJP of "normalising" hate.
Twenty-four-year-old Angel Chakma from Nandannagar in the West Tripura district was attacked by a group of six people when he objected to an alleged racial slur on December 9 in Dehradun. He succumbed to his injuries while undergoing treatment on December 26.
In a post on X, Mr. Gandhi said hate does not appear overnight.
"What happened to Anjel Chakma and his brother Michael in Dehradun is a horrific hate crime," he said.
"Hate doesn't appear overnight. For years now, it is being fed daily — especially to our youth — through toxic content and irresponsible narratives. And it's being normalised by the hate-spewing leadership of the ruling BJP," he said.
Mr. Gandhi said India is built on respect and unity, not fear and abuse.
"We are a country of love and diversity. We must not become a dead society that looks away while fellow Indians are targeted. We must reflect and confront what we are allowing our country to become," he said.
"My thoughts are with the Chakma family and the people of Tripura and Northeast. We are proud to call you our fellow Indian brothers and sisters," Mr. Gandhi added.
Tripura Chief Minister Manik Saha on Sunday (December 28, 2025) said his Uttarakhand counterpart Pushkar Singh Dhami has assured him that all persons responsible for the murder will be arrested.
Thousands of students under the banner of Tipra Indigenous Students' Federation on Sunday (December 28, 2025) organised a candle march here seeking justice for Angel Chakma. The students covered a distance of around one kilometre from the North Gate of Ujjayanta Palace.

title: Narcotics wing arrested two men on charge of peddling drugs; ₹2.5 crore worth narcotic substances seized
summary: Bengaluru police arrest two drug peddlers, seizing narcotics worth ₹2.5 crore ahead of New Year celebrations.
content:
Ahead of New Year celebrations, the Central Crime Branch (CCB) Narcotics Control Wing has arrested a Nigerian National and a delivery executive and seized narcotic substances worth ₹2.5 crore in two separate operations in the city.
The officials arrested 45-year-old Christopher in the Soladevanahalli Police Station limits, and  seized 1 kg and 70 gm of MDMA crystals, 60 ecstasy pills, ₹2 lakh in cash, one mobile phone, and a laptop. The total value of the seized items is estimated at ₹2.25 crore.
The police said the accused arrived in India last year on a business visa and was sourcing MDMA at low prices allegedly from foreign nationals based in Delhi and Mumbai. He was preparing to supply the drugs to known customers during New Year celebrations.
Investigations revealed that the accused had been involved in drug peddling earlier as well, and a case under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act had previously been registered against him at the Soladevanahalli Police Station. He was then remanded in judicial custody. After his release, he allegedly resumed drug-trafficking activities.
Delivery executive arrested in Bandepalya
In another operation conducted in the Bandepalya Police Station limits, the CCB arrested  Naveen Raj, 26, an inter-State drug peddler and seized 100 LSD strips, 5 gm of cocaine, and a mobile phone used for the crime. The seized contraband is valued at ₹25 lakh.
The accused, a native of Tamil Nadu, was working as a delivery executive for an online commercial company and also peddling drugs. The police said he used to procure LSD strips and cocaine from unidentified persons at lower prices and sell them at higher rates to known customers.

title: Rachakonda police book over 300 motorists for drunk driving
summary: Rachakonda police apprehend over 300 motorists for drunk driving during a weekend enforcement drive, emphasizing strict legal consequences.
content:
Rachakonda police booked more than 300 motorists for drunk driving during a special weekend enforcement drive conducted across the commissionerate limits between December 22 and December 28.
Police said that the traffic wing carried out extensive checks as part of the special drive, leading to the seizure of two-wheelers, cars and auto rickshaws from offenders found driving under the influence of alcohol. All those caught were booked and will be produced before the court as per law.
Officials said a majority of the motorists were found with blood alcohol concentration levels ranging from 35 mg per 100 ml to 200 mg per 100 ml, while a smaller number recorded significantly higher levels. Police reiterated that driving under the influence of alcohol poses a serious risk to public safety and will attract strict legal action.
Traffic police also said courts disposed of several drunk driving cases in the previous week, imposing fines totalling ₹2,07,500.
The Rachakonda police warned that if an accident results in death due to drunk driving, a case will be registered under Section 105 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, which deals with culpable homicide not amounting to murder and carries punishment extending up to ten years of imprisonment along with a fine.

title: Congress has split into two; it’s Priyanka versus Rahul camps now, says BJP
summary: BJP claims Congress is divided into Priyanka and Rahul camps, highlighting internal strife and calls for leadership change.
content:
The BJP on Monday (December 29, 2025) alleged that the Congress has split into two with one being the Priyanka Gandhi Vadra's camp and the other that of her brother Rahul Gandhi, and the clamour within the main opposition party to replace Gandhi with "anyone" is gaining "strength".
There was no immediate reaction from the Congress to the BJP's claim.
The BJP had recently alleged that Mr. Gandhi, the Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha, speaks against India and defames the country on foreign soil because he is "rattled" by the fact that his party colleagues and even family members are showing "no confidence" in him.
"The Congress has split into two parts. Earlier, we used to see this in Karnataka, Rajasthan and Telangana. But now, there is a split at the national level," BJP national spokesperson Shehzad Poonawalla told PTI Videos.
"It's now Rahul's Congress versus Priyanka's Congress," he said, launching a fresh attack on the grand old party.
Mr. Poonawalla alleged that the split in the Congress has come out in the open after senior party leader Digvijaya Singh praised the BJP and the RSS.
"Earlier, people from Priyanka Congress like Imran Masood, Robert Vadra and others were attacking Rahul Gandhi. After Digvijaya Singh's statement, which is a direct attack on Rahul, the Congress has now gone into more 'tukde-tukde' mode," he said.
"Congress leaders like Manickam Tagore and Revanth Reddy, who are part of the Rahul Gandhi camp, are attacking Digvijaya Singh. They are also attacking and abusing the RSS, and praising Sonia Gandhi and Rahul Gandhi," the BJP spokesperson added.
On the other hand, Mr. Poonawalla alleged, senior Congress leader Salman Khurshid came in Singh's support,  saying that "Digvijaya Singh is hundred per cent right".
"So it is clear as daylight that there is no mission and vision in the Congress. It is only confusion and division in the party," he said, adding, "The Congress has split into two today. Revanth Reddy and others are in the Rahul camp while Digvijaya Singh, Salman Khurshid and others are in the Priyanka camp."
Mr. Poonawalla alleged that there is a "huge lobby" in the Congress which does not take Rahul Gandhi "seriously".
"They are saying 'Rahul hatao, Priyanka lao; kisi ko bhi lao aur Congress bachao (remove Rahul Gandhi, bring Priyanka Gandhi in his place; bring anyone but save the Congress)'," the BJP spokesperson said.
"This movement is gaining strength," he added.
In a post on X last Saturday (December 27, 2025),Digvijaya Singh lauded the organisational power of RSS-BJPas he shared Narendra Modi's old picture and said how a grassroots worker went on to become the chief minister and prime minister by sitting at the feet of their leaders.
The senior Congress leader, however, backtracked later, saying he only talked about the organisation and its strength, and not the BJP or the RSS, as he was staunchly against the two.
Asked about Mr. Singh's remarks, Mrx. Khurshid told reporters on Sunday (December 28, 2025), "We have a lot in the Congress, and others should learn from the Congress instead. We certainly don't need to learn from the RSS as we oppose that ideology."

title: Churches in focus as Christmas violence threatens BJP’s political calculus ahead of Assembly elections
summary: Church violence raises concerns for BJP's political strategy in Kerala ahead of elections, as church leaders voice strong criticism.
content:
Notwithstanding a high-profile outreach initiative by Prime Minister Narendra Modi to strengthen the Bharatiya Janata Party's (BJP) foothold among the Christian community, unease among Catholics in Kerala over a perceived surge in anti-Christian attacks by alleged Sangh Parivar groups appears steadily escalating into a heated political discourse.
Expressing deep displeasure over the spate of violence in northern and central India,Deepika, the mouthpiece of the Syro-Malabar Church, did not hold back its criticism of the Prime Minister in an editorial published on Monday (December 29, 2025). “When Hindutva extremists vandalised Christmas decorations and unleashed violence, the Prime Minister, who came to church to offer prayers, was not doing it to reassure the citizens of the country, but to show off to leaders of foreign countries. Perhaps, he could have addressed the authorities of the Union  government. Otherwise, he could have condemned the attacks or taken a firm stance against them,” read the editorial.
The episode, which follows closely on the heels of the attack and arrest of two nuns in Chhattisgarh over alleged religious conversion, has struck a particularly sensitive chord in Kerala. It has sparked widespread debate in parishes across Central Travancore, a region historically known for sending a large number of missionaries to northern India. Political parties across the United Democratic Front (UDF) and the Left Democratic Front (LDF) too have condemned the attacks and highlighted the gaps in the BJP’s outreach to Christians in Kerala.
“Things have reached a point where even Christmas goods cannot be sold openly in the streets in north India,” says Jose K. Mani, chairman of the Kerala Congress (M). Kottayam MP K. Francis George, Deputy Chairman of the Kerala Congress that is part of the UDF, meanwhile, has termed the attacks "an infringement on the freedom of worship."
For the BJP, the timing could hardly be worse. With Assembly elections just months away, the episode threatens to undermine the party’s political traction among Catholics, especially in the Central Travancore and north Malabar settlement areas. In response, the party has launched outreach missions with Church leadership under Union Minister of State George Kurian.
“This concerted attempt by a section of the media and politicians to tarnish the image of the BJP among the Christians has been going on for a while now. To counter this, the party has been in constant touch with Church leaders to allay any concerns,” said Sumit George, president of the Minority Morcha in Kerala.
The BJP-Church relationship in Kerala has seen dramatic swings in recent years. Ties warmed with Mr. Modi’s meeting with top bishops in Kochi in 2023, while subsequent attacks on churches in Manipur strained this fragile bond. The party attempted to regain ground by supporting the Church’s criticism of  pro-Palestinian stances and encouraging greater political participation among Christians. The recent attacks on nuns in Chhattisgarh, followed by reports of Christmas-related violence, appear to have once again put the BJP’s position among Kerala Christians in a spot.

title: ‘Spread humanity, show kindness to build a health society,
summary: Join the fifth State-Level Scientific Conference in Yadgir, promoting kindness and scientific thinking for a healthier society.
content:
President of the fifth State-Level Scientific Conference Vishwaradhya Satyampet on Monday laid stress on the importance of spreading humanity, brotherhood and kindness and defeating communal hatred, religion and caste-based clashes to build a healthy society based on the Constitution and protect democracy.
He was delivering his presidential speech on the second day of the conference being organized here by the Karnataka State Scientific Research Council, Bengaluru, the Department of Science and Technology, Manava Bandhutva Vedike and other organizations.
The ISRO, the Jawaharlal Nehru Planetarium, the Indian Air Force, Visvesvaraya Industrial and Technological Museum, Mobile Planetarium, K. Steps, National Aeronautical Laboratory, DRDO and CFTRI Mysore have extended coordination for the conference.
He said that people should join hands together to eradicate superstition and blind belief in society. "If we developed scientific thoughts and followed the principles of the Buddha, Basava, Ambedkar, Savitribai Pule, Periyar and others, who fought caste discrimination, it will become much easier to building a healthy society based on the Constitution and uphold its values," he said.
He sharply targeted the "ruling politicians" for dividing people based on caste and religion and forcing them to live under a serious threat.
"Under the present circumstances, Brahmarakshasas are encouraging divisive forces to dominate the common people in the name of caste and religion. I don't know how many will be sacrificed to such Brahmarakshasas. Therefore, we must defeat them by progressive thoughts to ensure that the message of Rashtrakavi Kuvempu, Sarvajanangada Shantiya Tota, is widely followed,” he said.
Mr. Satyampet said that the State government might have introduced the Karnataka Hate Speech and Hate Crimes (Prevention) Bill 2025 in a hurry.
He said that "other political parties may send the progressive thinkers behind bars by misusing the law if they openly criticise the government and its caste-based politics. Therefore, the State should re-examine its decision to introduce such a law.”
Minister for Public Works Satish Jarkiholi has said that despite technical development, people still believe in superstition and have blind beliefs.
"The Karnataka State Scientific Research Council has been organising such conferences in the State to create awareness among the public about superstition and other such activities. I and Minister Sharanbasappa Darshanapur will put in sincere efforts to reserve grants for the council to extend support with financial aid,” he said.
Mr. Jarkiholi said that the country essentially required more people who will take the principles of social reformers like the Buddha, Basava, Ambedkar and Savitribai Pule to each house to fight superstition.
He requested the organisers to conduct the next State-level conference in Belagavi.
Earlier, Minister for Small Scale Industries Sharanabasappa Darshanapur, who inaugurated the second day events of the conference and science exhibition, extended his support to the event and appealed to the public to join hands to develop humanity.
The former Superintendent of Police S.K. Umesh cautioned against extortion and blind beliefs in the name of God and appealed to people to follow scientific thinking.
In his address, Shantaveera Gurumurugharajendra Swamiji of Khasa Mutt said that this conference has been organized with an aim to creating awareness about scientific thinking.
Mr. Satyampet and other achievers in different fields of life were felicitated, while six books written by Hulikal Natraj were released during the event.
MLA Channareddy Patil Tunnur, Sharanagouda Kandkur, Raja Venugopal Naik and others were present.

title: Houselisting and Housing Census likely in Kerala over a one-month-period during April-September 2026
summary: The first phase will be followed by Phase II - Population Enumeration - in February 2027
content:
Houselisting and Housing Census, which constitutes the first phase of the nationwide Census 2027, is expected to be held in Kerala over the course of one month any time between April and September in 2026.
The Joint Director, Census Operations (Kerala), has forwarded a detailed proposal to the State government with respect to the preliminary arrangements for the mammoth exercise. The first phase will be followed by Phase II - Population Enumeration - in February 2027.
“The first phase will be conducted during the course of one month recommended by the State government during the prescribed April-September period,” a senior official at the Census Directorate said. Normally, teachers are deployed for the Census, and this time also, this is the plan. But the numbers have not been finalised yet, the official said.
Houselisting and Housing Census is meant to collect useful data on the “quantity and quality of housing, availability of amenities and assets in households besides providing an unambiguous frame for enumeration,” according to Census officials.
The State government has given its nod to proposals concering the appointment of Census functionaries. The notifications regarding the appointment of Census officers and their functions and responsibilities will be issued in due course.
For the conduct of the mammoth exercise, the Directorate of Census Operations (Kerala) has proposed a “graduated break-up of the entire State into a pyramid of territorial justidictions.” The primary break-up will be on the basis of the revenue districts. “Each district will be divided into urban and rural areas. The Municipal Corporations, Municipal Towns, Cantonment Boards and those areas as approved as Census Towns and Outgrowths will constitute urban area; the rest will form the rural area,” a December 23 order issued by the State government’s General Administration Department, based on the proposals of the directorate, said.
The Director of Census Operations is designated as the Chief Principal Census Officer for the exercise. In the districts, the District Collector concerned will be the Principal Census Officer.
The ‘pre-test’ for Census 2027 in Kerala was heldin sample areas in Ernakulam, Idukki and Palakkad districts in November.
The Union government had in June this year announced plans for conducting the Population Census - 2027 in two phases along with the enumeration of castes. The previous Census, held in 2011, also came in two phases. Phase 1 lasted from April 1, 2010, to September 30, 2010 , and Population Enumeration, which constituted Phase II, was held from February 9 to February 28, 2011.
The decennial exercise, which should have been held in 2021 after 2011, has been delayed. Census 2011 had placed Kerala’s population at a little over 3.34 crore.

title: Fake demands under MGNREGA will not be entertained: Centre
summary: Centre ensures no fake demands under MGNREGA during transition to new employment law, addressing concerns in parliamentary meeting.
content:
The Rural Development Ministry informed the parliamentary standing committee on Monday (December 29, 2025) that it was coordinating with the State governments to ensure that no “fake demand” was raised under theMahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA)during the interim period before the implementation of The Viksit Bharat –Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) VB – G RAM G Bill, 2025, the new legislation that would replace the rural employment guarantee scheme.
The Parliamentary Standing Committee on Rural Development, headed by Congress leader Saptagiri Ulaka, held its first meeting on Monday (December 29, 2025) after therepeal of the MGNREGAby Parliament on December 18.
During the meeting, sources said, Samajwadi Party MP Ramashankar Rajbhar asked the Ministry to explain how it planned to tackle demand during the transition period when the new law was implemented and the MGNREGA was phased out. Since the MGNREGA was a demand-driven scheme, he pointed out, the government could not artificially suppress this demand. In response, Ministry officials reportedly said they were coordinating with the States to ensure that no “fake demand” was raised. Panel chairperson Mr. Ulaka and other members questioned the government on how it planned to distinguish between genuine and fake demand.
The meeting, which lasted nearly two hours, saw several BJP members criticising the MGNREGA. According to sources, several BJP members detailed various welfare schemes run by both the Centre and the States that provide “free health and free food,” arguing that in such a scenario, a rural employment scheme became redundant. Other BJP MPs, the sources said, flagged corruption cases affecting the rural employment scheme.
The government also informed the panel that it was intouch with the West Bengal governmentand would clear the dues it owed to the State. However, neither the amount owed nor the timeline for release was shared. Trinamool Congress members had staged an overnight dharna in Parliament after the Viksit Bharat G Ram G Bill was passed past midnight in the Rajya Sabha.
The release of funds to West Bengal under the scheme was stopped in March 2022 by the Centre, invoking provisions of Section 27 of the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act, 2005, owing to continued non-compliance with the Central government directives by the State. The Centre owes ₹3,082.52 crore to States, of which ₹1,457.22 crore was wages for completed work by registered workers.

title: Kanthapuram to launch 16-day ‘Kerala Yatra’ for Samastha centenary
summary: Kanthapuram to lead a 16-day 'Kerala Yatra' for Samastha centenary, promoting unity across Kerala's districts.
content:
Close on the heels of a rally led by Samastha Kerala Jem-iyyathul Ulama president Sayyid Jifri Muthukkoya Thangal, rival Sunni leader Kanthapuram A.P. Aboobacker Musliyar has announced plans to launch a 16-day ‘Kerala Yatra’ under the banner of the Kerala Muslim Jamaat to commemorate the Samastha centenary.
Mr. Musliyar will lead the ‘Kerala Yatra’, which carries the theme ‘With Humans’. The yatra will begin from Kasaragod on January 1 and conclude in Thiruvananthapuram on January 16. The Kerala Muslim Jamaat is a feeder organisation of Samastha and is engaged in propagating the ideas of its parent body.
“As part of the centenary celebrations, a full-fledged Samastha convention will be held in 2026, the details of which will be announced later. The organisation has drawn up a detailed action plan for the future,” Musliyar told the media here on Monday (December 29).
The yatra will commence at Syed Maudany Makham at Ullal in Kasaragod. Samastha president of this faction E. Sulaiman Musliyar and chairman of the Kerala Yatra, K.S. Attakkoya Thangal, will hand over the flag to yatra captain Kanthapuram Musliyar at 3 p.m. The yatra will spend a day in each district of Kerala and will also pass through Gudalur in the Nilgiris district of Tamil Nadu.
Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan and Leader of the Opposition V.D. Satheesan are expected to attend the valedictory function at Putharikandam ground in Thiruvananthapuram on January 16. Several other political leaders and people’s representatives are also expected to attend receptions organised in various districts.
Responding to queries, Mr. Musliyar said Samastha had no role in the LDF’s defeat in the recent local body polls and had no plans to enter politics in the near future.
He said Samastha did not consider a person’s religion or political affiliation while extending help, citing the case of Nimisha Priya, the Kerala nurse convicted of murder and facing a death sentence in Yemen. He said the organisation had done everything possible to secure her release, but the matter now rested with the Yemen government.

title: NSS aims at taking students from campus to community, says scholar
summary: Scholar Narendra Badasheshi emphasizes NSS's role in bridging education and community development during its inauguration at Sidhartha Law College.
content:
Renowned social science scholar and social activist Narendra Badasheshi has said that the National Service Scheme (NSS) has been designed to take students from campus to the community enabling them to use their education for the development of society they come from.
He was speaking after inaugurating the regular activities of NSS at Sidhartha Law College in Kalaburagi on Monday.
“NSS aims to take students from campus to the community. You have come from the community to campus for education. After acquiring knowledge on campus, you must return to your community and work for its development and welfare,” Mr. Badasheshi said and urged students to actively involve themselves in community-oriented programmes.
Referring to Mahatma Gandhi’s vision for India, he said that the NSS was launched as a tribute to the Father of the Nation to realise his dream of rural development.
“It is now being implemented by the Union government in coordination with the State governments to encourage young people to participate actively in social development,” he said.
Mr. Badasheshi also highlighted other youth initiatives such as the National Cadet Corps and the Nehru Yuva Kendra Sangathan and appealed to students to associate themselves with at least one such organisation.
“Anybody can live for himself or herself. But human beings are social animals. We must live not only for ourselves but also for others,” he said.
Quoting from a saying that winners do not do different things but do things differently, he called upon students to grasp its deeper meaning and apply it in their lives. On social service, he advised students to help those genuinely in need rather than those who are already in a position to help others.
Sharing his experience with NSS field activities, Mr. Badasheshi recalled an initiative at a hamlet near Kalaburagi where open defecation was widely practised.
“Through sustained awareness during an NSS field camp, individual toilets were constructed for almost all households within a short span with people’s participation and government support. This shows that NSS is not about working for people but working with people for community development,” he said and stressed that public participation is crucial for the success of any welfare programme.
Speaking on the occasion, faculty member Tippeswamy explained the objectives of NSS and said that participation in such programmes will greatly benefit law students.
“Leadership qualities, communication skills, honesty and the ability to understand social problems and resolving them are crucial for a successful legal career,” he said.
College principal S. Chandrashekhar presided over the programme.
NSS coordinator K.G. Jawali and faculty members Mahantesh Bidnoor, Aparna Shindhe, R.D. Mahalalaxmi, Kavitha and others were present.

title: Tirumala all set for Vaikunta Ekadasi with focus on common devotees
summary: Tirumala prepares for Vaikunta Ekadasi, prioritising common devotees and ensuring smooth darshan for 1.76 lakh pilgrims.
content:
The famed hill shrine of Lord Venkateswara at Tirumala has been meticulously spruced up for Vaikunta Ekadasi, the most sacred festival observed on December 30 across Sri Vaishnavite shrines.
In a significant initiative aimed at prioritising the common pilgrim, the Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams has suspended all categories of darshan tickets during the initial phase of the festival and decided to permit only Sarva Darshan or Dharma Darshan for the first three days of the 10-day Vaikunta Dwara Darshanam, beginning on Ekadasi day.
Elaborate arrangements have been put in place to facilitate darshan for about 1.76 lakh devotees who have already obtained online Sarva Darshan tokens for the first three days. To ensure smooth and uninterrupted movement of pilgrims, nearly 20 hours of darshan have been scheduled on the first day of the Ekadasi festival.
Devotees holding Srivani tickets and Special Entry Darshan tokens will be permitted to have darshan from January 2 onwards.
To streamline crowd management and ease access to the Vaikuntam Queue Complex, the temple administration has earmarked three separate entry routes based on darshan slots. Pilgrims scheduled for morning darshan will be allowed entry through the Krishna Teja Guest House route, those with afternoon slots through the ATGH area, and night-slot devotees through the Silathoranam circle.
Adding to the festive grandeur, the inner precincts of the main temple complex and its surroundings have been exquisitely decorated with several tonnes of flowers in varied hues, presenting a resplendent sight in keeping with the spiritual significance of the festival.

title: Students told to develop soft skills to succeed in careers
summary: Students urged to master essential soft skills for career success at a seminar in Vijayawada.
content:
Every student should master five skills — communication, problem solving, analytical thinking, marketing and negotiation — to get ahead in their careers, T. Dharma Theja, professor at Paari School Of Business.
Speaking at a seminar titled 'Careers in Management, Technology and Sciences’, organised by The Hindu FIC and SRM-A.P. in collaboration with KKR & KSR Institute of Technology and Science (KITS-Guntur) on Monday (December 29) to educate students on various options at PG level, Mr. Dharma Theja said that while these skills will be taught at undergraduate level, one learns to apply them in business schools. He encouraged students to study till postgraduation to master their subjects.
Adding to that, V.V.S. Pradeep, assistant director for PG Admissions, SRM-A.P., said students should also work on improving their critical thinking abilities. KITS principal P. Babu and secretary Koya Shekar advised students to think out of the box to explore career opportunities. He added that there are many career options in addition to the IT sector. Later, students participated in a quiz and five winners were given prizes.

title: Safety workshop held for chemical factories in Hyderabad
summary: Safety workshop in Hyderabad enhances awareness for chemical factories, emphasizing worker safety and industry efficiency for Telangana's development.
content:
The National Safety Council, Telangana Chapter, in collaboration with the Department of Factories, Government of Telangana, organised a one-day workshop on safety awareness for chemical factories on Monday (December 29) at Surana Auditorium of the Federation of Telangana Chambers of Commerce and Industry. Around 120 delegates from chemical factories across Telangana participated in the programme.
Addressing the gathering, Principal Secretary to Government, Labour, Employment, Training and Factories Department, M. Dana Kishore emphasised that human safety and plant safety were critical to achieving the goals of Rising Telangana 2047, as envisioned by Chief Minister Revanth Reddy. He said even small investments in safety systems could result in significant gains for the industry by improving production efficiency and worker well being. He stressed that the safety of workers was essential for the development of industry, society, the State and the nation.
The Principal Secretary also underlined the need to enhance the skill level of workers in factories and other sectors to move towards a developed Telangana. He advised the Department of Factories and other stakeholders to organise a week-long safety awareness campaign in the first week of March 2026. He added that worker safety would not be compromised and urged factory managements to adopt self regulation in safety practices.
Director of Factories, Telangana, Y. Mohan Babu, said that in line with the instructions of the Principal Secretary, the department has been conducting training programmes on a continuous basis. He said that during December 2025 alone, five training programmes were organised at different locations across the State to increase safety awareness among workers and management. He stressed the importance of safe handling of materials and proper maintenance of equipment, and requested participants to further train workers under their supervision.
Senior officers from the Department of Factories, V.V. Sasi Kumar, honorary secretary of the National Safety Council, Telangana Chapter, and expert faculty members from UNICEF, Hetero Drugs Limited, Aragen Life Sciences and 4S Techno Systems took part in the programme.

title: Arogyam Anandam: reception for awareness procession
summary: Join the Arogyam Anandam awareness procession in Chengannur, promoting wellness and healthy living ahead of the statewide campaign launch.
content:
Ahead of the launch of the Arogyam Anandam Vibe 4 Wellness, a Statewide campaign by the Health department, a reception will be accorded to an awareness procession at Chengannur on Tuesday (December 30, 2025).
It will be inaugurated by Fisheries Minister Saji Cherian at Christian College at 9 a.m. The Arogyam Anandam Vibe 4 Wellness campaign, which focuses on promoting healthy food habits, age-appropriate exercise, adequate sleep and overall health care, will be rolled out on January 1.
District Collector Alex Varghese will preside over.

title: 38th edition of Hyderabad Book Fair concludes, draws 16 lakh visitors
summary: The 38th Hyderabad Book Fair attracted 16 lakh visitors, highlighting a resurgence in reading interest among young audiences.
content:
The 38th edition of the Hyderabad Book Fair concluded on Monday, December 29, marking a rise in public participation, with organisers estimating a footfall of around 16 lakh visitors over the 11-day event.
The fair, which began on December 19, recorded a sharp increase compared to the 12 lakh visitors in 2024. Organisers described the response as one of the strongest in recent years, noting a particularly encouraging turnout of young readers.
“The large presence of youngsters challenged the widespread perception that reading habits are declining due to increased screen time. At least half of the visitors were young people and stalls selling Telugu books received a strong response. Telugu publications accounted for nearly half of the stalls at the fair, reflecting sustained interest in regional language literature,” said R. Vasu, secretary of the Hyderabad Book Fair.
Mr. Vasu also said that a book donation initiative set up at the venue received an overwhelming response. A total of 124 donors contributed books, filling three DCM trucks. The collected books will be distributed in villages across Telangana where access to reading material remains limited, he said.
Speaking at the closing ceremony on Monday, former Supreme Court Judge Justice B. Sudershan Reddy said the large turnout was noteworthy in this age of growing digital addiction. “It is heartening to see lakhs of people attend the fair and there were very few books that could not be found at the event,” he added. Justice Reddy also appealed to the organisers to ensure that a pocket size Telugu version of the Constitution of India is made available at the book fair next year.

title: Iranna Kadadi meets Om Birla on behalf of Belagavi administration
summary: Iranna Kadadi supports Belagavi administration to Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla amid Maharashtra MP's complaint over entry restrictions.
content:
Rajya Sabha member Iranna Kadadi has told Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla that no rule has been violated by the Belagavi district administration in prohibiting Maharashtra MP Dhairyasheel Mane from entering Belagavi district.
Mr. Kadadi met Mr. Birla in New Delhi on Monday in support of the Belagavi district administration with regard to a complaint submitted by Mr. Mane against Belagavi Deputy Commissioner Mohammed Roshan to the Speaker’s office.
Mr. Kadadi spent some time with Mr. Birla to give a comprehensive explanation on the matter. He said that there was no violation of the rights of the MP by the Deputy Commissioner.
In a release, Mr. Kadadi said that Belagavi district borders Maharashtra and Goa and citizens of all languages, including Kannada, live there in harmony with a sense of brotherhood. However, some organizations organize Black Day events and protests on the occasion of the Rajyotsava on November 1 and during the Winter Session in Belagavi.
“Many leaders from neighboring States come to such protest meetings and make provocative speech which causes unnecessary confusion. In such a situation, the district administration's first and foremost duty is to protect the interests of all linguistic people living there," he said.
“In that context, the decision taken by the Belagavi Deputy Commissioner, who is the District Magistrate, to restrict the entry of MP Dhairyasheel Mane, who intended to attend a Black Day meeting, is not a violation of rights, but a legal measure to maintain peace and order in the district,” he said.
“In this situation, it is extremely unreasonable and illogical to demand action against the Belagavi Deputy Commissioner by filing a complaint with him [Speaker] saying that the MP's rights have been violated. The Deputy Commissioner justified the order as being completely Constitutional and within the scope of the law and brought the actual situation to the notice of the  Speaker and gave the related details,” he said.
The Speaker gave a patient hearing and responded positively. He assured that he will not take any unilateral decision but will investigate the background of this incident. He has assured the people of Karnataka that there is no need to worry, the release from Mr. Kadadi said.

title: CM Siddaramaiah orders stringent security measures for New Year celebrations in Bengaluru
summary: CM Siddaramaiah mandates strict security and traffic measures for safe New Year celebrations in Bengaluru, prioritizing women's safety and crowd management.
content:
Chief Minister Siddaramaiah has directed police and other departments to enforce stringent security measures to ensure that no untoward incidents occur during New Year celebrations in Bengaluru.
Chairing a high-level meeting with senior police and departmental officials on Sunday, the Chief Minister reviewed the precautionary arrangements being put in place across the city.
Emphasising women’s safety, Mr. Siddaramaiah instructed officials to take preventive steps and ensure that celebrations take place without any incidents involving harassment or violence against women.
To facilitate safe travel after celebrations, he directed the Bengaluru Metropolitan Transport Corporation (BMTC) to operate a large number of buses after midnight so that people can return home conveniently.
The Chief Minister also ordered special measures for crowd management at key locations including M.G. Road, Brigade Road, Church Street, Koramangala, and Indiranagar, and stressed the effective use of modern technology to prevent stampedes or other mishaps.
As part of the security plan, 20,000 police personnel will be deployed across Bengaluru, including 1,200 policemen roped in from other districts. He instructed that women police personnel be deployed in larger numbers and that ‘Chennamma Teams’ be actively utilised.
The officials said that the city has been equipped with four control rooms, 78 watch towers, 164 women help desks, and 55 ambulances to manage emergencies. Over the last three days alone, the police have registered 3,500 drink-and-drive cases.
In a bid to prevent accidents, two-wheeler movement will be prohibited on 50 flyovers in the city on New Year’s Eve.
The meeting was attended by Home Minister G. Parameshwara, Political Secretary to the Chief Minister Naseer Ahmed, Chief Secretary Shalini Rajneesh, Police Commissioner Seemant Kumar Singh, Director-General and Inspector-General of Police M.A. Saleem, Greater Bengaluru Authority Chief Commissioner Maheshwar Rao, and other senior police officials.
Traffic restrictions
The movement of vehicles on M.G. Road, Brigade Road, St. Marks Road, Resthouse Road, and Residency road has been restricted on Wednesday night till Thursday morning.
All types of vehicles are prohibited on all over bridges in the city (except the flyover leading to the International Airport).
The movement of two-wheelers is also prohibited on the flyover road of the International Airport from 10 p.m. on December 31 to 6 a.m. on January 1.
To prevent the movement of heavy goods vehicles in the Central Business District area, diversions will be made at Old Udaya TV Junction, Khode, Townhall Junction, Chalukya Junction, Domlur, and Mehkri Circles.

title: Free sparsha darshan for Chenchus on Vaikunta Ekadasi in Srisailam
summary: Free sparsha darshan for Chenchus at Srisailam temple begins on Vaikunta Ekadasi, December 30, from 11 a.m.
content:
The management of Sri Bhramaramba Mallikarjuna Swamy temple in Srisailam, which had earlier decided to provide ‘sparsha darshan’ to local Chenchu tribals on one day of every month, will start the same from ‘Vaikunta Ekadasi’ falling on Tuesday (December 30).
In a joint statement on Monday, the temple trust board chairman P. Ramesh Naidu and executive officer (EO) M. Srinivasa Rao said that the Chenchus will be allowed to enter through the queue line at the Old Donation Counter from 11 a.m..
Mr. Ramesh Naidu said Chenchus have a special place in the history and traditions of Srisailam temple. The local Chenchu tribals consider Bhramaramba Devi as their daughter and Mallikarjuna Swamy as son-in-law, he added.
Mr. Srinivasa Rao said that the Chenchus were being invited for the ‘Brahmotsava Kalyanotsav’, which would be held during the ‘Sankranti Brahmotsavams’. The Chenchus will offer new clothes, ‘yagyapaveetam’, and waist belt to the presiding deities.
Chenchus have also been given special invitation to participate in the ‘Varalakshmi Vratam’ performed during ‘Sravana Masam’, and were also invited for the recently-concluded ‘Koti Deepotsavam’ held during ‘Karthika Masam’.
The temple administration is taking the help of local ITDA in identifying the Chenchus for the free special sparsha darshan.

title: Dating apps under scanner after spike in digital crimes
summary: Police investigate dating apps amid rising digital crimes, including online grooming, data theft, and financial fraud targeting minors.
content:
The police have put the operation of several newly launched dating apps under scrutiny following a spike in crimes involving digital predation, online grooming of minors and theft of personal data. The move follows confidential complaints received by the State’s high-tech crime inquiry cell.
Sources said the presence of minors on such unverified apps could pose serious risks, leading to financial fraud and sexual exploitation. “Sensitive banking details and personal information of several users are in the possession of operators of these unregistered platforms, raising concerns over data breaches and leaks into the public domain,” they said.
A senior police officer associated with the investigation cited a recent high-profile case from Kasaragod in which a minor boy was allegedly sexually exploited by 16 adults he had met through a dating app created exclusively for the LGBTQ community. Government officials were also among the accused, the officer said, adding that the operators of such online “matchmaking” platforms often remain untraceable due to the illegal nature of their operations.
The police sources said social media advertisements promoting these dating platforms have attracted a large number of young users. The involvement of celebrities as promoters has further encouraged people to sign up on such insecure platforms, often by paying registration fees and furnishing incorrect personal details, including age.
An IT expert currently working with the Kerala Police Cyberdome said that text chats and video calls on such insecure platforms could be leaked at any time due to weak encryption. The risk of blackmail using sensitive content exchanged during live chats is also high, he said.
Officers of the cybercrime investigation wing said downloading unverified dating apps could facilitate the theft of digital data stored on personal devices. Illegal access to contacts, photographs, messages and banking details, as well as third-party data sharing, is possible through such apps, they said.
A Sub Inspector who was part of the investigation into the Kasaragod cybercrime case said that while some confidential complaints related to fraudulent apps had reached the police, many victims were reluctant to come forward to protect their identity. Several users had reportedly lost money after signing up on untrustworthy platforms, he added. He said the police were conducting awareness programmes, including initiatives such as D-AD (Digital De-Addiction), to promote healthy online behaviour.

title: DGP calls for greater awareness among public to prevent cybercrimes like digital arrest
summary: DGP emphasizes public awareness to combat rising cybercrimes, revealing significant financial losses and ongoing police challenges in Andhra Pradesh.
content:
The Andhra Pradesh police is facing challenges in controlling cybercrime, ganja transportation and on crime against women, said Director General of Police (DGP) Harish Kumar Gupta.
While the public lost about ₹815 crore, police froze ₹98 crore in banks and refunded ₹3 crore to the victims in cyber offences, the DGP explained.
Giving the crime data for the year 2025 at a press conference here on Monday, Mr. Harish Kumar Gupta said the overall crime decreased by 6.17% in the year.
Asked about the challenges for the police in the State, the State police chief said that checking cybercrimes, ganja transportation and crime against women and children were the major challenges.
“Police handled over 62,000 complaints related to cybercrimes and registered 2,332 cases in 2025. Regarding digital arrest cases, accused were operating from China and other countries and were exchanging money into cryptocurrency, which has become tough for the police to recover,” the DGP said.
He stressed the need for creating awareness among the public to prevent offences like digital arrest.
Narcotics cases declined to 1,727 this year, as against 1,875 in 2024. Police arrested 9,478 accused, seized 1,525 vehicles used for smuggling ganja and other drugs and attached properties worth about ₹9.11 crore.
The Elite Anti-Narcotics Group for Law Enforcement (EAGLE) head and Inspector General of Police Ake Ravi Krishna said that surveillance has been stepped up on inter-state ganja peddling gangs operating in A.P.
“We are coordinating with the Anti-Narcotics Force (ANTF) of other States and Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB) to check smuggling of ganja and drugs. Our teams are moving in other States to check ganja transportation,” he added..
Regarding bodily offences, the DGP said that murder cases declined to 856 as against 772 in 2024, and kidnap cases came down to 645 from 768. Detection in property offences was 56% and the recovery was about 55% in 2025, Mr. Harish Kumar Gupta said.
Crimes against women decreased to 16,347, as against 16,994 in the previous year. There was a significant reduction in rape, gang rape and murder, assault on women and other crimes, the DGP said adding that POCSO Act cases reduced by about 11%.
However, there was a rise in economic offences. In all, 8,034 cases were registered in 2025, while the last year's figure stood at 7,667.
The AP Police Department is planning to organise a two-day workshop for IPS officers in January 2026, which will focus on strengthening structural engineering, technology, skill development and other techniques, the DGP said.
IGP (Operations) Ch. Srikanth, AP Forensics Director G. Pala Raju, DIG (Law and Order) K. Fakeerappa, IGP (Sports) K.V. Mohan Rao, DIG (Administration) R.N. Ammireddy and other officers were present.

title: Operation Bar Code: VACB carries out checks at bar hotels, excise offices across Kerala
summary: VACB conducts surprise checks at bar hotels and excise offices in Kerala to investigate illegal liquor sales and corruption.
content:
The Vigilance and Anti-Corruption Bureau (VACB) on Monday conducted surprise checks at bar hotels and excise circle offices across the State following information about the alleged sale of illegal and spurious liquor, officials said.
The VACB, in a statement, said the checks were conducted under an operation code-named “Bar Code” at 66 bar hotels and the excise offices concerned from 10 a.m.
According to the VACB, information was received that some bars were selling illegal or spurious liquor, commonly referred to as “seconds,” and that certain excise officials were allegedly accepting monthly bribes and liquor from bar owners to avoid inspections and action.
The VACB said that during the New Year season, when liquor consumption increases, some bar hotels violate the Abkari Act, the Foreign Liquor Rules, and licence conditions to make excess profits, allegedly with the connivance of excise officials.
The agency also received information that liquor procured at lower prices from neighbouring States and Union Territories was being smuggled into Kerala and sold through bars, the VACB said.
It was also alleged that such liquor was mixed with liquor purchased through the Kerala State Beverages Corporation and spirit to produce blended liquor for illegal sale.
The VACB said the findings of the checks would be examined and further action will be taken based on the outcome of the inspections.

title: 43 students fall sick after consuming midday meal in Shorapur
summary: Forty-three students in Shorapur fell sick after a midday meal; all have been treated and discharged from the hospital.
content:
As many as 43 students of a lower primary school located in Timmapur in Shorapur city have fallen sick after consuming midday meal on Monday.
According to Taluk Health Officer Raja Venkatappa Naik, the 43 students have been brought to the Taluk Hospital for treatment.
Out of them, 42 students got treatment in the outpatient department (OPD), while one student was admitted. She was then discharged after necessary treatment.
All 43 students have been sent back, he added.
Students complained of becoming unwell, while one of them showed signs of mild giddiness after consuming rice and sambar served to them, sources said.
But anxious parents said that the staff served lizard-contaminated food without checking it and demanded action against those responsible.
When contacted, Block Education Officer Yallappa Kadlur toldThe Hinduthat he rushed to the hospital after receiving information.
All students are out of danger and discharged now, he added.
He said that he will ask midday meal officers to send food samples to laboratory for testing to ascertain the reason that led to the incident.

title: Water Metro service to be disrupted
summary: Water Metro services in Kochi will be suspended on December 30, 2025, from 1:30 p.m. to 5:00 p.m.
content: Water Metro services from the High Court terminal to Fort Kochi, Vypeen, South Chittoor, and Mattancherry will be suspended on Tuesday (December 30, 2025) from 1:30 p.m. to 5:00 p.m. due to the Champions Boat League being held at Marine Drive. Services will resume after 5:00 p.m. However, the Mattancherry–Willingdon Island service will operate as usual, according to a communication.

title: UDF wins Vengola panchayat in postponed election
summary: UDF wins Vengola panchayat election, securing nine votes against LDF’s eight, with Shamitha Shereef elected president.
content:
The Congress-led United Democratic Front (UDF) has retained power in Vengola grama panchayat with Shamitha Shereef of Pathippalam ward getting elected as its president on Monday (December 29, 2025). V.H. Muhammed of Kandanthara ward, also from the Congress, was elected the vice-president.
Ms. Shereef and Mr. Muhammed defeated Elsy Eldhose and Jaseela Noushad of the Left Democratic Front (LDF), respectively. The UDF candidates secured nine votes against the LDF’s eight. Twenty20 which has six members and Social Democratic Party of India which has one member abstained from voting.
The elections were conducted on Monday after it was postponed due to lack of a quorum on Saturday (December 27, 2025) when the heads of three-tier panchayats were held across the State. Both LDF and Twenty20 had stayed away from voting on Saturday leaving the council without the required number of 14 members to conduct the elections.
Of the 82 grama panchayats in the district, the UDF has assumed power in 71, including Kalloorkad, where it supported an Independent to the post of the president. The LDF has been restricted to seven while the Twenty20 gained power in four, including Poothrukka, where it won the president’s position through a draw of lots.

title: Ex-TDB member Vijayakumar arrested in Sabarimala gold theft case
summary: Ex-TDB member Vijayakumar arrested in the Sabarimala gold theft case, becoming the 10th accused in the investigation.
content:
Former Travancore Devaswom Board (TDB) member N. Vijayakumar was arrested on Monday in connection with the Sabarimala gold theft case, the police said.
Mr. Vijayakumar was a member of the Travancore Devaswom Board (TDB) during the tenure of the former President A. Padmakumar, who has already been arrested in the case related to the missing of gold from the door frames of the Sreekovil (sanctum sanctorum).
During the tenure of the board, approval was given to hand over gold plates to the prime accused, Unnikrishnan Potti, for electroplating in 2019.
Mr. Vijayakumar was summoned to the Special Investigation Team (SIT) office in Thiruvananthapuram for questioning. After the interrogation, his arrest was recorded, sources said. He will be produced before the Kollam Vigilance court.
Mr. Vijayakumar became the 10th accused to be arrested by the SIT as part of the probe into the case.
Earlier, the Kerala High Court, while considering a petition related to the Sabarimala gold theft case, had criticised the SIT for not probing the role of former TDB members K.P. Shankardas and Mr. Vijayakumar.
The SIT was constituted on the directions of the High Court, which earlier this month granted the team an additional six months to complete the investigation.

title: A.P. Cabinet ratifies ₹7,387 cr. loan for Amaravati, okays 10% road cess on vehicles, DA hike for govt. staff
summary: Andhra Pradesh Cabinet approves ₹7,387 crore loan for Amaravati, new road cess, and DA hike for government employees.
content:
The Andhra Pradesh State Cabinet meeting, chaired by Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu, approved a series of major policy decisions on Monday, covering infrastructure development, social welfare, administrative restructuring, and public service improvements across the State.
Among the key approvals were a ₹7,387.70 crore loan from the National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD) under the NIDA scheme for infrastructure projects in Amaravati, and the introduction of a 10% “Road Safety Cess” on motor vehicles subject to life tax.
Disclosing the details to the media, Revenue, Registration & Stamps Minister Anagani Satya Prasad, along with Ministers Nadendla Manohar and Satyakumar, said the Cabinet ratified government orders issued on December 11, 2025, under G.O. Ms. No. 269 by the Municipal Administration & Urban Development Department (MA&UD). These orders authorise the AP Capital Region Development Authority (APCRDA) Commissioner in Vijayawada to secure the NABARD loan. Subject to a 5% guarantee fee, the funds will be used for critical infrastructure development in Amaravati. Officials have been empowered to obtain State guarantees, execute the loan agreement, and complete all necessary documentation, a move expected to accelerate the city’s urban development plans.
The 10% Road Safety Cess, approved through an ordinance amending the AP Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1963, will generate approximately ₹22.5 crore per month, or ₹270 crore annually. The revenue will be allocated to the Andhra Pradesh Road Development Corporation for road improvement, safety measures, and accident prevention. With around 73,000 new vehicles registered monthly and the recent reduction of GST on motor vehicles from 28% to 18%, the cess is not expected to place a heavy financial burden on vehicle owners.
On the welfare front, the Cabinet approved a 3.64% increase in Dearness Allowance (DA) and Dearness Relief (DR) for State government employees and pensioners, effective from January 1, 2024. The hike raises DA/DR from 33.67 % to 37.31 %, with benefits beginning in October 2025 salaries, providing financial relief amid rising living costs.
The government also outlined plans to develop Greater Vijayawada and Greater Tirupati as major urban centres. Chief Minister Naidu highlighted that 21.8 lakh ration cards are being distributed by January 9, 2026, with errors corrected and outdated photos removed. He assured substantial development for Polavaram and personal oversight for Rayachoti’s growth.
Medical and Health Minister Satyakumar stated that despite financial challenges, the government is correcting past mismanagement and empowering women economically, with nearly ₹3 lakh crore invested in basic infrastructure and new road connectivity planned from Machilipatnam to Hyderabad’s Future City.
Civil Supplies Minister Nadendla Manohar added that unprecedented allocations, including up to ₹5,000 crore under the NTR Bharosa scheme, have been made for pensions and welfare programmes, reflecting strong government commitment to social security and inclusive development.
These decisions collectively highlight the State government’s focus on balanced regional growth, infrastructure modernisation, and citizen-centric governance across Andhra Pradesh, they said.
EOM

title: BJP MLA Sharanu Salagar booked for ‘failure’ to repay loan
summary: BJP MLA Sharanu Salagar faces legal action for failing to repay a ₹99 lakh loan taken during the 2023 elections.
content:
A case has been registered against Basavakalyan BJP MLA Sharanu Salagar on the charge of failing to repay a loan of ₹99 lakh taken from his distant relatives during the 2023 Assembly elections.
A complaint has been filed by Sanjukumar Sugure, a resident of Jai Shankar Colony in Basavakalyan in this connection.
Acting on the directions of an Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate (ACJM) in Bengaluru, the Basavakalyan police registered the case on Saturday.
According to the complaint, Mr. Salagar borrowed ₹99 lakh as loan between January 2023 and February 2023 when he was contesting the Assembly elections.
The MLA reportedly assured the complainant that the loan amount will be repaid within six months. However, the complainant has said that the money has not been returned even after two-and-a-half years.
Mr. Sugure has stated that he has lent [before the disputed loan] money to Mr. Salagar on several occasions in the past which has been repaid.
“Based on that trust, I extended financial help and also, because he is a distant relative of mine,” the complainant said.
The complainant further said that after repeated demands for repayment, a meeting was held on September 14, 2025 in the presence of family members, during which Mr. Salagar agreed to return the amount and issued a cheque.
However, when the cheque was deposited, it was dishonoured as the bank account of the legislator was closed, he said.
Mr. Sugure also accused Mr. Salagar of abusing and threatening his wife and son when they visited his house seeking repayment of the money. The complainant has said that the MLA has acted with an intention to cheat him.
A case has been registered at the Basavakalyan Police Station. Investigation is under way, the police said.

title: Dagadarthi airport project receives Cabinet nod
summary: Nellore's Dagadarthi airport project receives Cabinet approval, advancing efforts to resolve land disputes and stimulate local industrial growth.
content:
The State Cabinet on Monday gave its nod to the latest proposal submitted by SPSR Nellore district administration to take the stalled Dagadarthi airport project forward.
The airport project has been in the news for over two decades. Of the 1,300 acres required for the project, the district machinery identified 882 acres of government land, but the remaining 418 acres in Damavaram, an Inam village, got entangled in legal hassles.
The farmers, who have been the perpetual lease holders of the alleged land, moved the court and even got a stay in 2017. Ever since, the authorities have been trying for rapprochement.
District Collector Himanshu Shukla, who held multiple meetings with the stakeholders, arrived at a consensus solution of paying ₹13 lakh per acre for the 418 acres in question.
Mr. Shukla formally thanked the Nellore MP Vemireddy Prabhakar Reddy, Ministers Ponguru Narayana and Anam Ramanarayana Reddy and MLC Beeda Ravichandra for playing a key role in taking the proposal forward.

title: A.P. Cabinet Sub-Committee reviews litigation policy
summary: Andhra Pradesh Cabinet Sub-Committee reviews the State Litigation Policy 2025 to improve governance and streamline legal processes.
content:
The Andhra Pradesh Cabinet Sub-Committee on Monday held its first meeting to review Andhra Pradesh State Litigation Policy 2025, aimed at strengthening governance and streamlining the State’s legal framework.
The meeting, chaired by Law and Minority Welfare Minister N. Md. Farooq, was held at the Velagapudi Secretariat. Revenue Minister Anagani Satya Prasad, Civil Supplies Minister Nadendla Manohar, and Health Minister Satyakumar Yadav attended, while Home Minister Vangalapudi Anita could not participate due to unavoidable reasons.
The committee discussed measures to reduce avoidable litigation, speed up dispute redressal mechanisms, and enhance transparency and accountability across government departments. Mr. Farooq said the panel would examine administrative processes to prevent delays, ease the burden on courts, and ensure the timely and lawful filing of appeals.
Key initiatives include strengthening Lok Adalats, promoting alternative dispute resolution, and adopting proactive case management strategies. The Ministers will submit recommendations on policy interventions to improve governance efficiency.
Mr. Manohar directed Law Department Secretary Pratibha Devi to compile details of pending cases across departments before the next meeting. The committee will also study litigation policies followed by States such as Gujarat and Karnataka to strengthen A.P.’s policy framework.
Mr. Farooq said the steps form part of the coalition government’s broader effort to strengthen the legal system, minimise avoidable court cases, and enhance administrative efficiency across the State.

title: Central Prison at Cherlapalli rolled out major reforms and upgrades in 2025
summary: Central Prison, Cherlapalli, rolled out wide-ranging reforms this year to boost inmate rehabilitation, modernise facilities, ease overcrowding and strengthen prison industries and staff welfare, reinforcing its status as a model prison.
content:
The Central Prison, Cherlapalli, implemented a series of infrastructural, healthcare and rehabilitative reforms this year, reinforcing its status as a model prison under the Telangana Prisons Department’s reform-oriented approach. The initiatives focused on inmate rehabilitation, modernisation of facilities, reduction of overcrowding, prison industries and staff welfare.
After a gap of five years, the Annual Sports Meet for prisoners was held in 2025. A total of 220 inmates from across the State stayed at Cherlapalli for two months, underwent training and participated in the event, which officials said was aimed at promoting discipline, teamwork and positive behavioural change.
Healthcare facilities at the prison were upgraded, with the hospital modernised to a capacity of 100 beds and the medical dispensary equipped with new laboratory, diagnostic and dental facilities. Individual medical files and digitised health records are now maintained for each inmate to ensure better monitoring and continuity of care.
Administrative buildings, officers’ chambers, barracks and prison walls were renovated and repainted while cleanliness standards were improved across the premises. Prisoners were involved in maintaining a prison garden as part of skill-building initiatives.
A barrack building project with a capacity of 300 prisoners, which had remained stalled for four years, was revived and brought to the final stages of completion. The facility is expected to become operational shortly and ease overcrowding at the prison.
Prison industries were modernised with advanced equipment, and prison-made products were standardised and branded with a uniform logo. A store room-cum-godown was established within the prison, and a proposal is under consideration to set up a dedicated retail outlet for prison-made articles.
A separate barrack has been earmarked for a de-addiction centre, which will provide counselling and rehabilitative support for inmates affected by substance abuse. The meditation hall and meeting hall inside the prison were also renovated to support inmate well-being and organised activities.
Staff welfare measures included the conversion of unused staff quarters into a recreation and function hall and the construction of new restrooms for outside escort police personnel.
Central Prison, Cherlapalli, received several high-level visits during the year, including during the 7th All India Prison Duty Meet. Union Minister of State for Home Affairs Bandi Sanjay and Telangana Minister D. Sridhar Babu visited the prison and reviewed its industrial units, while senior police officers, women IPS officers, IAS Officers’ Wives Associations and 203 trainees from All India and Central Civil Services also toured the facility.
At the 7th All India Prison Duty Meet held in 2025, the Central Prison, Cherlapalli, was awarded the Gold Medal for Best Prison Hygiene following a nationwide assessment by the Bureau of Police Research and Development.

title: ED issues notice to interrogate Ex-MLA P.V. Anvar in KFC loan misappropriation case
summary: ED summons former MLA P.V. Anvar for interrogation in KFC loan misappropriation case involving ₹22.3 crore non-performing assets.
content:
The Directorate of Enforcement (ED), probing the alleged misappropriation of loans by former MLA P.V. Anvar from the Kerala Financial Corporation (KFC), has issued a notice asking him to appear for interrogation, officials said on Monday.
Sources said that Mr. Anvar has been asked to appear before the Enforcement Directorate (ED) office in Kochi on December 31. Officials said the notice was sent to Mr. Anvar by post and email.
Mr. Anvar is currently associated with the All India Trinamool Congress, which was recently included as an associate party of the Congress-led United Democratic Front.
The ED had carried out raids on the residences and business premises linked to Mr. Anvar in Malappuram in November this year. The agency is probing a ₹7.5-crore loan granted by the KFC to Malamkulam Constructions, a firm associated with Mr. Anvar, in 2015.
Subsequently, loans amounting to ₹3.05 crore and ₹1.56 crore were sanctioned to Pee Vee Aar Developers using the same collateral properties within a short interval, resulting in a total non-performing asset (NPA) of around ₹22.3 crore, the ED said in a statement.
The statement said the ED identified as many as 15 bank accounts held in the names of different persons, allegedly benamis, through which suspected transactions had taken place.

title: Waste management to get top priority, says Eloor chairperson Laiji Sajeevan
summary: Eloor chairperson Laiji Sajeevan prioritizes scientific waste management and plans an annual calendar for effective waste processing initiatives.
content:
Ensuring proper waste management measures will be a priority area for the newly-formed council in Eloor municipality under the Left Democratic Front (LDF), according to its chairperson Laiji Sajeevan.
The intent was to continue with various projects initiated by the previous Left front-led council, she said on Monday (December 29, 2025). Ms. Sajeevan pointed out that a proposal to formulate an annual calendar of waste management–related activities would be placed before the council for approval. It would outline plans to step up existing waste management projects under the annual Plan Programme, she said.
The Eloor municipality achieved ‘waste-free’ status under the government’s ‘Malinyamuktha Keralam’ initiative in March 2025. It earned the status for its initiatives to ensure proper segregation, collection, and processing of non-biodegradable waste, as well as source-level management of food waste. The civic body achieved a 100% target in the collection of user fees from waste generators by deploying members of the Haritha Karma Sena (HKS) in all wards. They are involved in the doorstep collection of non-biodegradable waste.
Ms. Sajeevan said the focus would be on ensuring the scientific processing of waste generated in various wards. The civic body had earlier approved a bylaw to ensure the scientific collection and disposal of plastic waste, following a directive from the Department of Local Self-Governments to initiate steps to curb the plastic menace. The ‘Plastic Waste Management Bylaw’ specified the responsibilities of waste generators and the civic body in accordance with various environmental laws.

title: Punjab Cabinet approves elevation of Banur to tehsil, land revenue law amendments
summary: Punjab Cabinet elevates Banur to tehsil, amends land revenue laws, and launches e-services portal for improved public service delivery.
content:
The Punjab Cabinet, led by Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann, on Monday (December 29, 2025) approved a series of administrative and governance reforms aimed at improving public service delivery and citizen convenience.
The Cabinet cleared the upgradation of Banur sub-tehsil to a full-fledged tehsil in Sahibzada Ajit Singh (SAS) Nagar district and the creation of Hariana as a new sub-tehsil in Hoshiarpur district.
The move is expected to ease access to administrative services and reduce travel for routine official work.
The Cabinet also cleared amendments to the Punjab Land Revenue Act, 1887, particularly in the appeals process.
The changes aim to reduce unnecessary litigation, save time for litigants and prevent harassment of non-litigants, officials said.
The amendments will provide legal recognition to digital land records and digital signatures, strengthening paperless record-keeping and improving transparency in land administration.
The government has already launched an e-services portal to simplify land-related procedures.
Through the platform, citizens can apply online for ‘Khangi Taqseem’ (family partition) and avail services such as land demarcation, dispute resolution, land transactions, compensation for crop damage and issuance of Jamabandi copies.
In another decision, the State Cabinet approved a one-time relaxation in the upper age limit for contractual Special Teacher Educators working under the Samagra Shiksha scheme to enable their regularisation in the School Education Department.
The decision aims to ensure continuity of inclusive education for children with special needs and will not entail any additional financial burden on the State exchequer, the officials said.

title: Man sentenced to death in 2011 murder case of woman
summary: A court in Medchal-Malkajgiri district has awarded death sentence to a 35-year-old man for the murder of a woman in 2011.
content:
A court in Medchal-Malkajgiri district has sentenced a man to death for the murder of a woman whose body was found in the bushes near the Bharatnagar flyover in Sanathnagar in 2011. The court also imposed a fine of ₹10,000 on the convict.
The accused, Karan Singh, 35, alias Kamma Singh, was convicted under Section 302 (murder) of the Indian Penal Code by the III Additional District and Sessions Judge cum Principal Family Court at Kukatpally. The judgment was delivered after the conclusion of the trial in the case registered by Sanathnagar police.
Around 9 p.m. on July 18, 2011, Sanathnagar police received information from Kappari Ramu about the body in an open area with bushes at a godown beside the Bharathnagar flyover. Police found the naked body of the unidentified woman bearing multiple stab wounds. A case of murder was registered and investigation was taken up.
During the course of investigation, police collected material evidence and, on August 11, 2011, arrested Karan Singh, a blacksmith by profession and a resident of Gurudwara Street in Bidar, Karnataka. He was remanded to judicial custody. The charge sheet was later filed before the court by the investigating officer.
During the trial, the court, after evaluating the evidence on record, held the accused guilty and awarded the death sentence.

title: Focus on overcoming hurdles posed by regulations under ‘green zone’ in Kalamassery, says chairperson Jamal Manakkadan
summary: Kalamassery's chairperson, Jamal Manakkadan, prioritizes overcoming green zone regulations to advance vital infrastructure projects.
content:
Jamal Manakkadan, the newly elected chairperson of Kalamassery municipality, has accorded top priority to resolving issues related to the ‘green zone’ demarcation under the existing structural plan of the civic body.
The first meeting of the new council, to be held on January 1, 2026, will discuss measures to overcome hurdles in the construction of new infrastructure projects in the civic body in view of the restrictions imposed under green zone regulations, as per norms prescribed by the Department of Town Planning.
Mr. Manakkadan said that the restrictions on construction under the green zone regulation would impact the setting up of buildings on the land proposed for the judicial city, as it falls within the green zone. The first council meeting would decide on forwarding an appeal to the State government seeking relaxations in the existing regulations. If the government did not grant approval, the council would take legal recourse after holding the required consultations, he added.
The chairperson pointed out that the civic body had not been able to implement various infrastructure projects due to the curbs imposed under the zoning regulations. “We have sought the help of retired chief town planners as part of formulating an action plan to find a permanent solution to the issue,” he said.
