summary: Address VCs concerns on funds and recruitment, BJP tells govt.
content:
The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) has called upon the State government to urgently respond to the concerns raised by Vice-Chancellors over severe faculty shortages and inadequate funding in  universities. The party warned that continued neglect would push the higher education system into an irreversible crisis.
“Two years have passed since the Congress government came to power but is yet to fulfil the assurances made to the education sector in terms of funds, recruitment or infrastructure and the recent meeting of Vice Chancellors (VCs) has exposed the failures,” charged State party vice president Kasam Venkateshwarlu at the State office.
Addressing a press conference, he claimed that the VCs meeting has been 'historic' as they had unanimously expressed their dissent on issues related to the education system. The education sector has ‘collapsed’ with the just 7.6% budget allocation and most varsities not even having executive councils.
“Revanth Reddy government had announced ₹1,000 crore for Osmania University. Where are the actual allocations? A committee led by former MP K. Keshav Rao and a Cabinet sub-committee headed by Industries & IT Minister D. Sridhar Babu are yet to submit their reports. What is the Education Commission doing?,” he questioned.
The BJP leader pointed out that Telangana was formed on the issues of education, jobs and water but the current government, after making many promises, has been evading accountability and playing with the future of students and teachers.
If the KCR government ‘destroyed’ the education sector, the Revanth Reddy government is completely ‘ruining’ the higher education. When VCs are pleading funds for basic infrastructure and has made it clear that varsities cannot run with contract and part-time lecturers, it laid bare the pathetic the condition of universities in the State, he said.
The government is not paying fee reimbursement for degree colleges even while the Congress leaders speak of fee regulation, turning schools into talent hubs, upgrading polytechnic colleges, internships, and industry training. But none of these have been implemented, he maintained.
Mr. Venkateshwarlu urged the government to act upon the anguish expressed by the VCs and take steps to adopt the National Education Policy (NEC). The issues raised by VCs should be put up for discussion in the winter Assembly session and the government must fulfil its responsibility to save the education system, he added.

title: Bank of Baroda opens new branch on Vishwa Manava Double Road
summary: Bank of Baroda inaugurates a new e-lobby branch on Vishwa Manava Double Road in Mysuru.
content:
Bank of Baroda has opened a new branch with an e-lobby at Vishwa Manava Double Road in Mysuru.
The branch was inaugurated by Manoj Chayani, the bank’s zonal head and chief general manager, Bengaluru zone. The inauguration ceremony was attended by T.V.S. Sharma, regional head and assistant general manager,  and Marala Vidyasagar, deputy regional head, Mysuru region.

title: Mysuru Deputy Commissioner issues instructions for arrangements atop Chamundi Hills ahead of devotees’ visit on January 1
summary: Deputy Commissioner directs arrangements for New Year devotees at Chamundi Hills, ensuring safety and convenience during their visit.
content:
Anticipating the arrival of a large number of devotees at Chamundi Hills on January 1, which marks the start of the New Year 2026, Deputy Commissioner G. Lakshmikanth Reddy has instructed officials to make all necessary arrangements for the occasion.
Chairing a meeting of officials in the city on December 30, Mr. Reddy pointed out that the Lalitha Sahasranama programme is scheduled for January 2 at Chamundi Hills. This will be followed by the weekend, falling on January 3 and 4.
Pointing out that there is a likelihood of many devotees visiting the Chamundeshwari temple fordarshanduring the period, he instructed officials to increase the number of queue lines and take all necessary measures to prevent overcrowding.
He also told them to ensure smooth vehicular movement and adequate parking arrangements without any inconvenience. In case of heavy crowding, he suggested that even vehicles of dignitaries be parked near the Mahishasura statue and that battery-operated vehicles be arranged thereafter for transportation.
Mr. Reddy ordered officials to make arrangements for drinking water at more locations. He further said that additional sanitation staff should be deployed to maintain cleanliness.
Directions were also issued to Karnataka State Road Transport Corporation officials in Mysuru to operate additional bus trips to Chamundi Hills during the period.
The Health Department has been asked to deploy two ambulances. Further, he said that the food items and prasada provided by donors have to be checked for quality even if these have been preparedat the Dasoha Bhavan.
The officials have been asked to remain vigilant so that no untoward incident occurs.
The meeting was attended by Mysuru Zilla Panchayat Chief Executive Officer Yukesh Kumar, Chamundi Hills Authority secretary Roopa, Chamundeshwari Temple priest Shashishekhar Dikshit, and other officials.

title: Mumbai civic polls: Congress ally VBA fails to get candidates in 20 seats
summary: Mumbai civic polls: Congress's alliance with VBA falters as 20 seats remain uncontested, prompting a potential strategy rework.
content:
The much-hypedalliance between the Congress and Vanchit Bahujan Aghadi(VBA) for the Mumbai civic polls suffered a ground reality jolt when it was revealed that the Prakash Ambedkar-led VBA lacked candidates to contest in 20 of 62 seats allocated to it.
With the deadline for filing nominations for the January 15 elections ending on Tuesday (December 30, 2025), the VBA 'disclosure' may require Congress to rework the poll strategy.
The 143-62 seat-sharing formula was announced on Sunday (December 28, 2025) between the Congress and VBA for the 227-member Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) elections. It was decided to allot some seats to the Rashtriya Samaj Paksha and RPI (Gavai) faction.
“The VBA informed the Congress that it didn't have candidates in 20 seats and has "returned" them,” a Congress leader said. Reacting to the development, Shiv Sena spokesperson Sanjay Nirupam stated he sympathises with the voters of Congress in 20 wards.
The VBA has some pockets of influence among Dalit voters in Mumbai and parts of Maharashtra. The party, led byDr. B R Ambedkar's grandsonPrakash Ambedkar, mainly derives its strength fromNavboudh (neo-Buddhist)electorate.

title: Chandrababu Naidu, family on New Year vacation in Southeast Asia
summary: Chandrababu Naidu, family on New Year vacation in Southeast Asia
content:
Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu and his wife Nara Bhuvaneswari left on Tuesday for a popular tourist destination in South East Asia on a five-day personal visit abroad. Human Resource Development Minister and his son Nara Lokesh, along with his wife Nara Brahmani and son Devansh, had earlier left for another destination in the region.
The overseas visit has reportedly been planned as a private vacation coinciding with the New Year 2026 celebrations, according to senior government sources. Mr. Lokesh and his family are expected to join Mr. Naidu and Ms. Bhuvaneswari during the trip. They are likely to spend the New Year abroad and return to Andhra Pradesh in the first week of January.
The visit follows an intense and demanding work schedule in recent months. Sources said the Chief Minister and Mr. Lokesh decided to take a brief break to rest and rejuvenate before resuming their administrative responsibilities with renewed focus.

title: Political theatre unfolds after Surendran’s questioning by SIT in the Sabarimala gold theft case
summary: Former Devaswom Board Minister and CPI(M) State committee member, Kadakampally Surendran, was questioned in the golf theft case on Tuesday
content:
Some political theatre unfolded on Tuesday after news broke that the Special Investigation Team (SIT) probing the Sabarimala gold theft had questioned former Devaswom Board Minister and Communist Party of India (Marxist) [CPI(M)] State committee member, Kadakampally Surendran.
Television camera crews mobbed Mr. Surendran in Thiruvananthapuram, prompting him to request calm. “I answered SIT’s questions,” he said.
Mr. Surendran dodged pointed questions about whether he had blamed former Travancore Devaswom Board (TDB) president A. Padmakumar, another CPI(M) leader, who is currently on judicial remand on charges of causing an undue pecuniary advantage to the main suspect, Unnikrishnan Potti, and, reciprocally, causing a loss to the public exchequer. Mr. Surendran also refused to answer whether he had any prior acquaintance with Mr. Potti.
Hours later, journalists mobbed Mr. Padmakumar when the SIT produced him at the Enquiry Commissioner and Special Judge, Vigilance, overseeing the case.
Earlier, Mr. Padmakumar had stirred controversy by dropping hints about the alleged role of some “saintly higher-up” in the crime. When asked whether he meant Mr. Surendran, Mr. Padmakumar remarked somewhat cryptically, “Neither eaters of dead flesh nor hunting dogs. Ayyappa knows the truth.”
The Congress-led United Democratic Front (UDF) had turned its guns on Mr. Surendran and, by extension, the CPI(M), for the crime, making the scandal the central platform of its local body campaign.
Leader of the Opposition V.D. Satheesan accused Mr. Surendran of repeatedly hosting Mr. Potti, thereby allegedly giving the prime suspect in the case a prominent role in Sabarimala under the previous Left Democratic Front (LDF) government. UDF social media accounts also shared photos of Mr. Potti alongside Mr. Surendran, mostly at charity events. Mr. Surendran subsequently sued Mr. Satheesan for liaison.
Mr. Satheesan accused the government of delaying the SIT’s questioning of Mr. Surendran for months, fearing a setback in the local body elections.
Senior Congress leader Ramesh Chennithala said the names of more “big sharks” would emerge in the public domain.
Law Minister P. Rajeeve said the SIT would cover all aspects of the case and that the recording of statements did not necessarily imply culpability for the crime.
On Monday, CPI(M) State secretary M.V. Govindan underscored that the party would take action against its political appointees on board the TDB based on the final report. He said the CPI(M) would protect no one, and media witch hunts and opposition attacks would not force its hand.

title: NAVA to host book release, present awards in Dharwad today
summary: NAVA hosts a book release and awards ceremony in Dharwad today, celebrating Rajyotsava with notable artists and contributors.
content:
The National Academy of Visual Arts (NAVA) will, in association with JSS Halabhavi School of Art, organise a book release function and present awards as part of Rajyotsava celebrations in Dharwad on Wednesday.
Academy president S.C. Patil told reporters in Dharwad on Monday that over the past 20 years, the National Academy of Visual Arts has published 31 books. It has been working to recognise painters, sculptors and writers.
“NAVA publishes three books every year and organises several art-related activities annually, without any government grants or donations. We also present awards as part of our Rajyotsava celebrations,” he said.
NAVA will confer the 2025 Rajyotsava Awards on N.M. Datanal (Dharwad), B.M. Patil, V.D. Sali (Raibag), K.V. Shankar (Hubballi) and Bharati Maru (Udupi).
Chairman of D.V. Halabhavi Memorial Trust B. Maruti, who is a 2025 Rajyotsava Award recipient, will also be felicitated at the JSS Halabhavi School of Art at 3 p.m.
JSS administrator S.G. Biradar will inaugurate the event.
The former Vice-Chancellor D.B. Nayak, the former Principal of Halabhavi School of Art Suresh Halabhavi, the former Principal of Vijay Kala Mandir Ashok Akki and artist G.S. Bhoosagond will participate in the programme, he said.

title: Kogilu demolition: Move to rehabilitate Kerala immigrants nothing but minority appeasement, says B.Y. Vijayendra
summary: B.Y. Vijayendra criticizes Kerala immigrant rehabilitation as minority appeasement, pledging BJP protests against Karnataka's state policies.
content:
B.Y. Vijayendra, BJP State president, took a dig at the State government over its decision to rehabilitate those who lost their houses to the administration’s demolition drive in Kogilu Layout in Bengaluru. “The State government’s decision to allot houses in Bengaluru to illegal immigrants from Kerala is based on the policy of minority appeasement. BJP will organise intensive protests against it across the State,” Mr. Vijayendra said in Belagavi on Tuesday
“The state government had taken the right decision to evict illegal settlers from Kerala in Kogilu in Bengaluru. Officials demolished their illegal houses. But the government made a ‘U-turn’ after facing criticism from Kerala Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan and the Congress high command. Now the illegal immigrants have been promised houses in Bengaluru. This is nothing but an act of minority appeasement,” Mr. Vijayendra told reporters. The State BJP chief was in the district to participate in some functions of the Lingayat Math.
Mr. Vijayendra condemned the act and said, “We condemn this act. The houses built by the government with taxpayers’ money are meant for poor Kannadigas, not Malayalees. The government should prioritise distributing houses to the people of Karnataka. If any houses are left, then, the settlers can be considered,” he said.
He criticised the State government for the alleged delay in paying the compensation to farmers who suffered crop loss. “We wonder if the Karnataka CM has any functional autonomy. He seems to be listening to the party high command only to save his shaky chair. Deputy Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar, who is competing for the post of CM, is trying to impress the high command. They have no regard for the interests of the people of the State. They are just following orders of their leaders, like Rahul Gandhi and K.C. Venugopal. The State government is delaying paying compensation to farmers who suffered crop loss. But it is acting swiftly to distribute houses to minorities from Kerala. This is not acceptable. If Housing Minister B.Z. Zameer Ahmed wants to allot houses to the Kerala immigrants, let him build houses on his private property,” he said.
He said the Congress government’s policy of appeasement had continued unabated despite embarrassing situations like some people shouting ‘Pakistan Zindabad’ slogans in the Vidhana Soudha, and setting fire to a Dalit MLA’s residence in Bengaluru.
Mr. Vijayendra claimed that the State Cabinet was trying to introduce changes to the law to grant station bails to those accused of illegal cow transport, but dropped the idea after some Ministers opposed it. He said the BJP’s protests against the government had succeeded in most cases. “If not for our protests, a Minister would not be jailed for the ST development corporation scam, and the CM would not have returned sites he obtained illegally from MUDA,” Mr. Vijayendra said.
He said that the BJP would protest the delay in payment of monthly incentives to women under the Gruha Laxmi scheme. “The amount due to women in February and March this year was around ₹5,000 crore. Minister Laxmi Hebbalkar gave wrong information to the House during the Winter Session. This shows that she has no idea what is going on in her department. It is also possible that she is involved in financial irregularities, like the diversion of those funds. She should clarify. CM Siddaramaiah, who holds the Finance portfolio should also clarify,” he said.
“The third issue that the Opposition would raise is the drug menace. It is unfortunate that the Maharashtra police conducted a raid in the CM’s constituency and unearthed a drug-manufacturing network. Drugs are sold, trafficked, and consumed in all villages and towns of the State. The State government has failed to contain the menace. It is trying to turn the State into Udta Karnataka, on the lines of Udta Punjab. We will not sit quietly. We will organise protests. A final decision on the format of the protest will be taken in the core committee meeting in Bengaluru on January 5,” Mr. Vijayendra said.
BJP would decide on its candidates for the Zilla panchayat and taluk panchayat polls after district-wise meetings in Bengaluru from January 5, he said.
MLAs Abhay Patil and Nikhil Katti, party district-level leaders and others were present.

title: PIL in Supreme Court seeking action against racial violence targeting northeastern citizens
summary: PIL filed in Supreme Court demands action against racial violence targeting northeastern citizens following the brutal murder of Anjel Chakma.
content:
A PIL was filed in the Supreme Court seeking judicial intervention to address the "continuing constitutional failure" to prevent and respond to racial discrimination and violence against citizens from northeastern states and other frontier regions.
The PIL was filed on December 28 in the backdrop of the brutal killing of Anjel Chakma, a 24-year-old MBA student from Tripura, who succumbed on December 26 to grievous injuries sustained in a racially motivated attack in Selaqui area of Dehradun.
Chakma from Unakoti district's Machmara went to Dehradun after completing his graduation in Holy Cross School, Agartala, to pursue MBA, where he was stabbed to death in the presence of his younger brother Michael.
The family members of Chakma want capital punishment or at least life imprisonment for all the accused involved in the incident. Anoop Prakash Awasthi, a Delhi-based lawyer, has made the Centre and all the states and Union territories as parties to the PIL.
"That the present writ petition is being filed seeking issuance of writ under Article 32 of the Constitution seeking issuance of writ in the nature of mandamus, order, direction or any other appropriate writ for the violation of fundamental rights as under article 14, 19 (1) a & (g) and 21, and thus seeking judicial intervention to address the issue of racial discrimination and violence against Indian citizens from the north-eastern states and other frontier regions of India," the plea said.
"We are Indians. What certificate should we show to prove that?" words that tragically became the last recorded assertion of Chakma about his constitutional belonging before the confrontation escalated into brutal violence, it said while recounting the offence leading to his death.
The plea referred to media reports about Chakma's death.
The attackers allegedly assaulted and stabbed both brothers and Chakma sustained severe injuries to his neck and spine, remained unconscious throughout his treatment, and died after more than fourteen days in intensive medical care, it said, adding his death triggered widespread anguish, protests, and demands for justice across the country.
"Issue an appropriate writ (ad interim till a legislation is made) in the nature of formulating comprehensive guidelines, recognising 'racial slur' as a separate category of hate crimes and determining punishment for the same," the plea said.
It sought a direction to the Centre and the states to create a "nodal agency or a permanent body or commission or directorate" at the central level as well as at the level of each state where such racial crimes can be reported and redressed.
"Direct the respondents at central level as well as at the level of each state to make and create a dedicated special police unit in each district/metropolitan area to address the racial crimes," it said.
The plea sought a direction to the Centre and the states to organise "workshops and debates at educational institutes on the issue of prevailing racial discrimination and ways to redress the same".
The petition said that despite the unmistakable hate-based and racial motivation behind the crime, India's criminal justice system lacks any mechanism to recognise or record racial bias at the initial stage of investigation.
As a result, such offences are treated as ordinary crimes, "erasing motive, diluting constitutional gravity, and perpetuating a pattern of impunity", it said.
The plea said that the killing of Chakma is not an isolated incident but part of a long-standing pattern of racial abuse and violence against citizens from the northeastern states.
The petition recalls earlier cases, including the death of Nido Taniam in 2014 and numerous assaults on students and workers in metropolitan cities, incidents that have been formally acknowledged by the Centre in parliamentary replies but, according to the petitioner, remain unaddressed through any dedicated legislative or institutional framework.

title: Forum for Good Governance urges Telangana government to halt GHMC corporators’ study tour
summary: Forum for Good Governance requests Telangana to cancel GHMC corporators' study tour, citing waste of taxpayer money.
content:
The Forum for Good Governance (FGG) has urged the Telangana government not to approve a proposed study tour of 145 Greater Hyderabad Municipal Corporation (GHMC) corporators, arguing that the visit would serve no public purpose and amount to a waste of taxpayers’ money as the corporators are nearing the end of their term.
In a representation dated December 30 (Tuesday), addressed to the Principal Secretary of the Municipal Administration and Urban Development Department, the forum said that the Standing Committee of the GHMC had cleared the proposal in its meeting on December 29. The study tour is intended to expose corporators to urban governance practices in other cities.
The forum, however, pointed out that the term of the current set of corporators ends in February 2026. By the time the proposed tour is completed, it said, there would be “hardly any time left” for the elected representatives to apply the knowledge gained from such a visit. As a result, the exercise would not benefit the people of Telangana in general or Hyderabad in particular.
Describing the proposal as an avoidable expense, the forum said the tour would amount to squandering public funds without any tangible return. “The idea behind a study tour is meaningful learning and implementation, neither of which is possible when the term is about to end,” the representation said.
The letter, signed by Forum for Good Governance president M. Padmanabha Reddy, requested the Principal Secretary to intervene and stop the proposed tour. A copy of the representation has also been marked to the GHMC Commissioner, seeking similar action.
The government and the GHMC are yet to respond publicly to the forum’s objections.

title: Sabarimala gold theft case: SIT questions Dindigal-based businessperson with alleged links to illegal antique trade
summary: SIT interrogates Dindigal businessman linked to illegal antique trade in Sabarimala Gold Theft, probing potential interstate rackets.
content:
The High Court-appointed Special Investigation Team (SIT) on Tuesday (December 30, 2025) questioned a Dindigal-based businessperson, who allegedly goes by several aliases, including D. Mani, in connection with the criminal misappropriation of gold-plated artefacts from the Sabarimala Ayyappa Temple.
Officials said the SIT had interviewed Mr. Mani in his office last week, based on a statement from a Non-Resident Keralite businessperson that sought to link the Tamil Nadu resident to the illegal trade in religious artefacts, including those of supposed antique value.
Officials said Mr. Mani and an acquaintance, who identified himself as Balamurugan, reported to the Crime Branch office in Eanchakkal, Thiruvananthapuram, for questioning.
The SIT is yet to name Mr. Mani as an accused in the case. Mr. Mani has protested his innocence to journalists from Kerala who visited him in Dindigul last week.
However, officials said the expat businessperson’s deposition, given at the behest of former Kerala Home Minister and senior Congress leader Ramesh Chennithala, has opened a new line of enquiry, requiring more time and possibly additional investigators.
They said the Crime Branch will likely approach the Kerala High Court to seek permission to expand the SIT and extend the deadline for filing the final report in the case.
Mr. Mani had emerged as the latest focus of the investigation after the expat alleged that the former had contacted wealthy collectors claiming to have idols and other high-value religious artefacts for sale.
Officials said the SIT was verifying Mr. Mani’s antecedents, including any links to Unnikrishnan Potti, the prime accused in the case. Moreover, the SIT has reportedly interviewed several acquaintances of Mr. Mani in Tamil Nadu, possibly to profile him based on their character statements.
Officials said the SIT suspects its investigation might meander into interstate rackets that palm off ordinary everyday objects, including metal pots and idols, as rare treasures with magical properties to unsophisticated, overeager, wealthy collectors for significant sums of money.
They noted that the Tamil Nadu and the Kerala Police had registered several cases involving the use of pseudoscience to mislead buyers into believing that the vessels they hoped to sell were made of rare alloys with supernatural properties.
An official said the “rice-puller” scam, which targeted impressionable wealthy collectors in Kerala, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu, involved the clever use of hidden magnets and rice grains mixed with minute iron shavings to stage fake “magical” demonstrations to persuade prospective buyers.
An investigator said the SIT was reluctant to pursue such lines of investigation without hard evidence linking such rackets to the Sabarimala gold theft.

title: Nainar Nagenthran alleges dilution of Horticulture Department’s functioning
summary: BJP's Nainar Nagenthran accuses DMK of undermining the Horticulture Department and misappropriating ₹141 crore in scams.
content:
BJP Tamil Nadu president Nainar Nagenthran on Tuesday (December 30, 2025) alleged that the DMK government was diluting the functioning of the Horticulture Department, and failed to provide small and marginal horticulture farmers with adequate expertise.
In a post on X, he said the ruling DMK had “swindled” ₹141 crore through alleged scams in the department, and was trying to dilute its uniqueness by making it a wing of the Agriculture Department.
Mr. Nagenthran said the government had forced Horticulture Department employees, secondary grade teachers, and nurses to protest, thereby halting the functioning of the government.
“The DMK government, which neglects the demands of government employees, will fall because of its arrogance,” he added.

title: SCR warns against flying kites near railway tracks, stations
summary: SCR warns against flying kites near railway tracks due to risks of electric shocks and serious accidents.
content:
The South Central Railway (SCR) has appealed to the general public to strictly avoid flying kites near railway tracks, stations, yards and other installations. The overhead traction lines carry high-voltage electricity, and even indirect contact through kite threads can result in fatal accidents.
Multiple cases were reported across various zones of Indian Railways, where individuals suffered severe electric shocks or fatal injuries after coming into contact with kite threads entangled with 25 kV Overhead Electric Traction (OHE) lines.
Use of Chinese-imported kite threads, often metallic or chemically treated, act as conductors of electricity. When such threads come in contact with live overhead traction equipment, they pose a grave threat not only to human life but also to critical railway electrical infrastructure, potentially leading to service disruptions and safety hazards for passengers and railway staff, said a press release on Tuesday.

title: Dalits protest against Hubballi honour killing
summary: Dalits protest in Hubballi against honour killing of a pregnant woman, demanding justice and protection from rising violence.
content:
Members of Karnataka Rajya Chalavadi Mahasabha and other organisations took to the streets in Hubballi on Monday against the recent honour killing in Inam Veerapur village in Dharwad district in which a pregnant woman passed away.
Protestors condemned the murder of the pregnant woman by her family members who were upset that she married a Dalit. They demanded death penalty for the accused.
They walked from Ambedkar Circle to the Tahsildar’s office to express their protest.
They said that attacks against Dalits and cases of families killing their women who marry Dalits are increasing and demanded steps to stop such acts.
They also demanded compensation to the families of victims. It is unfortunate that in the land of Basavanna, Dalits are not able to live peacefully.
Mahasabha president Parameshwar Kale and others were present.

title: Congress leader criticises BJP leaders for comments on hate speech Bill
summary: Congress leader H.C. Yogeesh criticizes BJP for opposing the hate speech Bill, linking it to their history of hate speech.
content:
Congress leader H.C. Yogeesh has criticised BJP leaders for their stance on the hate speech Bill passed by both houses of the Karnataka Assembly.
In a press conference at Shivamogga on December 30, Mr. Yogeesh opined that BJP leaders are worried about the implications of the Bill because they are known for making hate speeches. S.N. Channabasappa, Shivamogga BJP MLA, attracted a criminal case in 2015 for making a comment targeting Chief Minister Siddaramaiah. Similarly, former Minister K.S. Eshwarappa had been facing cases for making provocative statements.
“Many BJP leaders have urged the Governor not to give assent to the Bill passed by the legislature. Their stance clearly shows that they do not want harmony in the State. However, the State government has brought this Bill with the objective of stopping hate crimes and hate speeches, which could lead to disturbing law and order,” said Mr. Yogeesh, who contested the Shivamogga Assembly polls on a Congress ticket in 2023.
He further demanded that BJP leaders speak on issues concerning the development of the State and the welfare of deprived sections.

title: Maganti Sunitha moves HC seeking direction to nullify Jubilee Hills MLA Naveen Yadav’s election
summary: Maganti Sunitha petitions Telangana High Court to nullify Naveen Yadav's election, citing undisclosed criminal cases in affidavit.
content:
BRS nominee in Jubilee Hills assembly constituency by-election, Maganti Sunitha, filed an election petition in the Telangana High Court on Monday seeking a direction to declare null and void the election of Congress candidate Naveen Yadav as MLA.
She stated in the petition, which is likely to be heard in a day or two, that Naveen Yadav failed to furnish in his election affidavit the details of seven criminal cases registered against him. She said in the plea that seven First Information Reports (FIRs) issued against Yadav in different police stations were pending for adjudication. The petitioner maintained that the Telangana Chief Electoral Officer through a memo issued on October 14 had directed all the contestants of the by-election to declare their antecedents. Not adhering to this amounted to violation of the orders of the Supreme Court issued earlier, she contended.
The contestant also stated that Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy, during the election campaign at Rahmathnagar, provoked the voters by holding a sword in his hand and appealed to the people to vote for Congress candidate Naveen Yadav. The CM also tried to lure votes by stating that ‘Muslims exist and get respect because of Congress ‘.
The Telangana High Court had allowed a criminal revision case filed by a person named Dastagir Shareef seeking a direction to set aside the order of 17th Additional Metropolitan Magistrate of Maheshwaram in Rangareddy in a matter related to Bhoodan lands. The petitioner wanted the Maheshwaram police station Inspector to investigate into the alleged fraudulent transfer of Bhoodan lands in survey no. 181 of Maheshwaram on the names of some private persons.

title: Tourists banned from hill stations, other hotspots on New Year's Eve: Chikkamagaluru Deputy Commissioner
summary: Chikkamagaluru bans New Year's Eve tourist visits to hill stations to prevent incidents, allowing only pre-booked accommodations.
content:
The Chikkamagaluru district administration has banned tourists from visiting tourist attractions in the district, including hill stations, between 6 p.m on December 31 and 6 a.m. on January 1. This is a precautionary measure to avoid untoward incidents during New Year celebrations.
Deputy Commissioner Meena Nagaraj C.N. on December 29 issued the order banning tourists from visiting Mullayyanagiri, Seethalayyanagiri, Manikyadhara, Zhari Falls, Honnammanahalla, Galikere, Hirekolale Kere, Diamond Falls in Chikkamagaluru taluk, Ethina Bhuja, Devaramane, Rani Zhari, Ballalarayana Durga, Bandaje Falls, Kudige Falls in Mudigere taluk, Kyatanamaki, Dudrapada, Hanging Bridge,Abbugudige Fallsin Kalasa taluk, Ayyanakere, Madagada Kere in Kadur taluk, Kemmannugundi, Kallathagiri and Hebbe Falls in Tarikere taluk.
However, tourists who have booked rooms at homestays and resorts on the way to these tourist places are allowed to travel to their destinations The Deputy Commissioner issued the order as per the recommendation of the district police.

title: Silent march to be taken out on January 5 against honour killing in Hubballi
summary: Join the silent march on January 5 in Hubballi to condemn honour killings and advocate for justice and protection for Dalits.
content:
Dalit organisations will take out a silent march on January 5 condemning the honour killing in Inam Veerapur village of Hubballi taluk in which of Manya Doddamani passed away.
Addressing presspersons along with other Dalit leaders in Hubballi on Monday, Internal Reservation Agitation Committee member B.R. Bhaskar Prasad said that thousands of activists will participate in the silent procession, wearing black armbands.
The march will begin from the Siddharoodha Math and culminate in a public meeting at Nehru Maidan where an appeal will be made to society to prevent such incidents in the future.
Mr. Bhaskar Prasad said that the incident reflects the failure of the State government, the district administration and the Social Welfare Department to protect Dalits.
He said that the rally is not intended to project the issue as party versus party, caste versus caste, or organisation versus organisation and appealed to people across political affiliations, castes and communities to participate in it. He also appealed to traders to voluntarily close their establishments and join the protest, clarifying that there will be no compulsion to do so.
Among the demands placed before the State government are, referral of the case to a fast-track special court or a judicial inquiry, implementation of an anti-honour killing law, strict punishment for the accused and adequate protection and compensation for the victim’s family.
The organisers also sought a government job for Vivekanand Doddamani and the allotment of 10 acres of land to the family.
The former Minister Hanumanthappa Alkod, Dalit leaders Marasandra Muniyappa, Vijay M. Guntral, Venkatesh Sagabala and Basappa Madara were among those present at the press conference.

title: Woman arrested with MDMA and LSD blots in Banjara Hills
summary: A woman was arrested in Banjara Hills with MDMA and LSD as police intensify anti-drug efforts ahead of New Year celebrations.
content:
The Telangana Elite Action Group for Drug Law Enforcement (EAGLE) Force, in a joint operation with the Banjara Hills police, arrested a 47-year-old woman and seized MDMA and LSD blots from her near Road No. 3 in Banjara Hills as part of intensified anti-drug enforcement ahead of the New Year celebrations on Tuesday.
The accused, identified as Hassa, a resident of Banjara Hills, was apprehended near a mobile phone shop in the area. Police said she tested positive for methamphetamine and amphetamine during medical examination. The seized contraband and the accused were handed over to the Banjara Hills police for further legal action.
Investigation revealed that Hassa confessed to having developed links with a Goa-based drug supplier identified as Romi Bharath Kalyani during a visit to the coastal State in December 2024. She allegedly began procuring MDMA from him and continued to source narcotics during multiple visits to Goa in March, July, October and December 2025.
Police said that during her most recent visit on December 26, 2025, the supplier allegedly handed over MDMA and LSD blots to her at Siolim and later in Mapusa. The accused also admitted that on some occasions, acquaintances from Hyderabad consumed MDMA along with her.
The investigation has brought renewed focus on Romi Bharath Kalyani, a repeat offender under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act, who was arrested earlier in multiple cases across Hyderabad, Mumbai and Goa. Earlier this year, he was arrested by the Golconda police in a case involving cocaine, MDMA and ecstasy pills and was released on bail in November. Police said efforts were underway to nab him.
Officials said surveillance had revealed that the supplier procured drugs from Nigerian nationals and distributed them to Indian consumers through a wide network, including contacts in Hyderabad. His activities allegedly continued even during periods of incarceration, with associates managing operations.
Appealing to the public, the police cautioned youth against falling prey to drugs in the name of party culture and celebrations, warning that substance abuse causes long-term harm to individuals, families and society.

title: Court issues non-bailable warrant against activist Mahesh Shetty Thimarody
summary: Court issues non-bailable warrant against activist Mahesh Shetty Thimarody for failing to appear in an inflammatory speech case.
content:
A court in Belthangady in Dakshina Kannada district has issued a non-bailable warrant (NBW) against activist Mahesh Shetty Thimarody for his failure to appear before the court in a case registered against him for his alleged inflammatory speech.
The Principal Civil Judge and JMFC, Belthangady, on December 24, rejected the application filed by Thimarody’s counsel seeking exemption from appearance. Observing that no grounds were made for his absence, the court issued a non-bailable warrant against Thimarody.
The Belthangady police had registered asuo motucase against Thimarody, accusing him of making an inflammatory speech at the Hindu Samaja Rakshana programme on the Mahamayi Marigudi premises in Bedrabettu of Belthangady taluk on February 8 this year. It was alleged that his speech created doubts about Dharmasthala and other Hindu temples. He was accused of hurting religious sentiments and disturbing peace by creating discord among communities.
The Belthangady police filed the chargesheet on December 17.
It may be noted that the Special Investigation Team, which is probing the alleged mass burial of bodies in Dharmasthala village, hasfiled a complaint report before the Belthangady court,accusing Chinnaiah, Thimarody, Girish Mattennnavar, T. Jayanth, Vittala Gowda and Sujatha Bhat of perjury and other criminal offences.
The Assistant Commissioner, Puttur, recently issued orders forexterning Thimarody, who is accused in 22 criminal cases, from Dakshina Kannada to Manvi in Raichur district.

title: Labourer hammered to death by co-worker at construction site in Bengaluru
summary: A labourer was fatally attacked with a hammer by a co-worker during a drunken altercation at a Bengaluru construction site.
content:
A 31-year-old labourer was hammered to death allegedly over a drunken brawl at a construction site in J.P. Nagar 8th stage during the early hours of Monday.
The victim has been identified as Bhagirath Bapri, a native of West Bengal.
According to the police, Bapri and another labourer, Biplab Mandal, 27, who were both working and residing at the construction site, consumed alcohol together late at night. An argument broke out between the two over a trivial issue after Bapri allegedly used abusive words against the mother of the accused, which soon escalated into an altercation.
In a fit of rage, the accused allegedly attacked Bapri with a hammer, resulting in fatal injuries.  The incident came to light the next morning when other workers arrived at the site and found Bapri dead. Based on information, the Konanakunte police conducted an inspection and registered a case.
The police later tracked down Mandal and took him into custody for  further investigation.

title: Chittoor district records 26 per cent drop in crime rate in 2025
summary: Chittoor district sees a 26% crime rate drop in 2025, attributed to community policing, technology, and focused enforcement.
content:
The Chittoor district police recorded a significant 26 per cent reduction in overall crime in 2025, with a total of 5,216 registered cases, compared to 7,034 in 2024.
Addressing a press conference on the annual crime report here on Tuesday, Superintendent of Police (SP) Tushar Dudi attributed the improvement to strengthened community policing, focused enforcement, and extensive use of technology.
The SP said that crimes against women decreased by 12.63 per cent, while economic offences dropped by 21.65 per cent.
Cybercrime showed a significant decline of over 40 per cent, reflecting sustained awareness campaigns and swift response mechanisms. Property offences also registered a marginal decrease, with a notable improvement in recovery.
Mr. Dudi said that the police recovered stolen property worth ₹8.39 crore in 2025, increasing the recovery rate to 73 per cent, compared to 48 per cent the previous year. Additionally, 1,021 stolen mobile phones valued at ₹2.04 crore were traced and returned to victims, and ₹68.44 lakh was recovered and refunded to cyber fraud victims.
Women’s safety remained a top priority, with six Shakti teams deployed across the district and large-scale legal and cyber awareness programmes conducted for women and girl students. The Shakti App crossed 6.14 lakh downloads, aiding quicker emergency response. In road safety enforcement, police booked 2,772 drunk-and-drive cases, imposing fines totalling ₹27.7 crore, and seized 100 vehicles driven by minors in Chittoor town alone, he said.
The SP observed that several high-impact cases, including murders for gain, dacoity attempts, inter-district burglary gangs, and sexual offences, were detected, leading to major recoveries and arrests. Under the POCSO Act, multiple convictions were secured, including life imprisonment and long-term sentences in cases involving sexual offences against minors.
Mr. Dudi maintained that technology-led policing expanded significantly, with over 2,400 CCTV cameras installed across the district, aiding detection in 152 cases. New Police Command and Control Centres, drone surveillance, ANPR systems, and innovative Falcon and Mini Falcon vehicles enhanced monitoring, traffic enforcement and crime prevention.
The district police reaffirmed their commitment to protecting life, property and public order through proactive, people-centric and technology-enabled policing, he said.

title: Another straying tiger trapped in Pathanamthitta
summary: Forest officials rescue a three-year-old tiger trapped in a well in Pathanamthitta, raising concerns about wildlife straying into human areas.
content:
Amid growing concerns over the straying of wildlife into human settlements, forest officials on Tuesday rescued yet another tiger from a village on the forest fringes of Pathanamthitta district. Earlier this month, authorities had trapped an eight-year-old tiger that repeatedly ventured into human habitations and attacked domestic animals in the Kumbalathamon area
The tiger was rescued on Tuesday after it  fell into a well near the house of Kollamparambil Sadasivan, a resident of Villoonnipara, near Chittar. The incident came to light when Sadasivan’s family noticed the animal got stuck in the well around 5 a.m. Police personnel from the Chittar station reached the spot, followed by a team from the Forest department.
A preliminary examination indicated that the female tiger was around three years old. A specially trained team from the Periyar Tiger Reserve was rushed to the site and after efforts lasing over seven hours, the team managed to secure the tiger using a net. The animal was then lifted out of the well and administered two doses of tranquilliser before being shifted in a cage to the forest station.
“The initial plan was to rescue the animal by pumping out  water from the well. However, that could have enabled the tiger to escape, and the option was therefore ruled out,” a forest official said. Veterinary experts were brought in to assess the animal’s health condition and the animal was confirmed healthy.
“Permission has been sought from the Chief Wildlife Warden for releasing the animal back into the deep forests,” the official added.
While residents in the region have often raised complaints about wild elephants, forest officials said this was the first time a tiger had been sighted in the area.
The incident has triggered fresh concerns among residents living along forest fringes.

title: Revised railway timetable to come into effect on January 1
summary: Southern Railway's revised timetable, effective January 1, 2026, enhances train speeds and operational efficiency for improved passenger experience.
content:
The revised time table of the Southern Railway will come into force on January 1, 2026, marking a significant milestone in the ongoing modernisation and capacity enhancement of rail operations across the zone. This revision also reflects Southern Railway’s efforts to improve operational efficiency, punctuality and overall passenger experience. As part of this initiative, around 65 mail, express and superfast trains will operate at enhanced speeds next year, leading to appreciable reduction in travel time and improved punctuality. These speed enhancements have been made possible through extensive infrastructure development works, including track strengthening, improved maintenance practices, signalling upgrades and the introduction of enhanced safety systems.
Select mail, express and passenger train services operating over upgraded sections will benefit from improved schedule reliability and reduced journey duration. Prior to the implementation of higher speeds, comprehensive inspections and safety trials have been conducted to ensure full compliance with all prescribed safety standards. Train crew have also been suitably trained, and operational protocols have been updated to support the revised timetable seamlessly, said Railways in a statement here on Tuesday.

title: DGP’s remarks show collapse of policing in Andhra Pradesh: YSRCP
summary: DGP’s remarks show collapse of policing in Andhra Pradesh: YSRCP
content:
YSR Congress Party Legal Cell working president Jalla Sudarshan Reddy on Tuesday criticised what he described as a sharp deterioration in the law-and-order situation in Andhra Pradesh, stating that recent remarks by the Director General of Police themselves reveal the extent of the collapse in policing in the State.
Addressing a press conference, Mr. Sudarshan Reddy referred to the DGP’s justification that accused persons in an animal sacrifice case were made to walk on the road owing to the non-availability of a patrol vehicle. He said such explanations effectively legitimise violations of the law by the police. When those entrusted with upholding the Constitution themselves disregard legal procedures, public confidence in the justice system is bound to erode, he observed.
Mr. Sudarshan Reddy alleged that police interference in civil disputes, intimidation and abuse of authority have become routine, while the government has failed to exercise effective supervision. He said the Andhra Pradesh police, which had secured the top national ranking during the previous YSR Congress Party government, has now slipped to the 36th position under the present coalition regime, reflecting serious administrative and disciplinary failure.
He further alleged that police officers are increasingly functioning under political pressure and, in some instances, even defying court orders. Referring to the Kadiri incident, he accused the police, along with sections of what he termed the ‘yellow media’, of politicising a private family dispute to falsely target the YSRCP.
Mr. Sudarshan Reddy also alleged selective enforcement of the law, claiming that while crimes are allowed to flourish unchecked, false cases are being foisted on those who question government failures. He warned that such misuse of power would not go unaccounted for in the future.

title: BJP and Shiv Sena finalise 143-8 formula for Nagpur civic polls, NCP to go solo
summary: BJP and Shiv Sena set 143-8 seat sharing formula for Nagpur polls
content:
TheBJPandEknath Shinde-led Shiv Sena on Tuesday (December 30, 2025) announced candidates for all 151 seats in the Nagpur Municipal Corporation elections, while another Mahayuti ally, the NCP, has decided to contest separately.
The BJP will contest a maximum of 143 seats, leaving just eight seats for Shiv Sena. The list was shared by Nagpur city BJP president Dayashankar Tiwari.
In a related development, Maha Vikas Aghadi (MVA) constituents, the Congress and NCP (SP), have decided to contest the Nagpur civic polls separately, with the Sharad Pawar-led party accusing the ally of not allocating 15 seats.
Nagpur NCP (SP) president Duneshwar Pethe claimed on Tuesday (December 30) that discussions with Congress leaders continued until Monday (December 29) night. “However, later the leaders stopped responding to our phone calls, which indicated that they do not want to forge an alliance,” he said.
“It seems the Congress wants to help the BJP and decided against allying with us,” the NCP (SP) leader alleged.
Elections to 29 municipal corporations in Maharashtra will be held on January 15, and the votes will be counted the next day. The deadline for filing nominations is Tuesday (December 30), while January 2 is the last date for withdrawal. The final list of candidates will be published on January 3.
In the last election held for the 151-member Nagpur civic body in 2017, the BJP won 108 seats, the Congress 28, BSP 10, Shiv Sena (undivided) 2, and NCP (undivided) one seat.

title: Three killed in separate road accidents
summary: Three fatalities reported in separate road accidents across Bengaluru's Bellandur, Whitefield, and K.R. Puram on Monday.
content:
Three people were killed in separate road accidents in Bellandur, Whitefield, and K.R. Puram on Monday.
A 27-year-old motorcyclist was killed after his two-wheeler skid and fell near the Iblur Junction. Police identified the deceased as Sachin Vahane, 27. He was allegedly riding at high speed when he lost control of the vehicle and fell on the road, the police said.
He was employed at a private company.  The Bellandur traffic police have registered a case.
In another incident, an autorickshaw driver was killed and three passengers were injured after the vehicle overturned near a petrol bunk on the Whitefield-Sarjapur Road.
The deceased has been identified as Swamy, 58. The injured passengers were shifted to a nearby hospital. The Whitefield traffic police have registered a case. In a third incident, a 65-year-old pedestrian was killed after being hit by an unidentified vehicle near Devasandra in K.R. Puram.
The victim has been identified as Venkataswamy, 65. The K.R. Puram traffic police have registered a case and launched a probe to trace the vehicle that was involved in the accident.

title: AIDSO leaders pledge to fight to protect public education
summary: AIDSO leaders vow to protect public education and uphold student rights at their 72nd Foundation Day in Dharwad.
content:
AIDSO leaders took a pledge to fight to protect public education and uphold the rights of students in Dharwad on Monday. They were speaking at the 72nd Foundation Day of the student organisation.
District secretary Shashikala Meti said that AIDSO, founded in 1954, has been leading struggles across the country against issues affecting students.
“The organisation was founded with the great objective that no child should suffer from hunger, that every student should receive free education without discrimination based on caste or religion and that democratic, scientific and secular education should be available to all. It was founded on December 28, 1954, in the erstwhile Calcutta, inspired by the ideas of Shivdas Ghosh. We should all stick to our founding ideals,” she said.
“Today, poor students are unable to pursue medical, engineering and higher education due to the commercialisation of education. The system has created a situation where only students with money can access education. In the past, great leaders such as Savitribai Phule, Jyotirao Phule, Vidyasagar, Bhagat Singh and Netaji fought to ensure education for every student. But today’s governments, contrary to their ideals, are depriving poor students of education. The governments, which should provide free education, have itself turned education into a business. Therefore, it is the responsibility of students to adopt the ideals of these great leaders and work towards realising their dreams,” she said.
“It is sad and unfortunate that even after 80 years of Independence, honour killing has not stopped. In the recent times, such an incident has been reported wherein a father killed his own pregnant daughter simply because she married a Dalit. This reflects the deeply entrenched caste mentality in society which deserves strong condemnation,” she said.
AIDSO district president Sindhu Kaudi opposed the State government’s move to close government schools in rural areas in the name of merger with the Karnataka Public Schools.
“This means closing down of more than 40,000 government schools across the State. Such schools help the rural poor gain literacy and education. If they are shut down in the name of merger, poor students will be pushed away from education. Students and the general public should join the struggle to save the more than 40,000 government schools,” she said.

title: Rajam lecturer Vaka Srinivasa Rao awarded Ph.D. in Mathematics
summary: Vaka Srinivasa Rao, a lecturer at Sri GCSR Degree College, earns Ph.D. in Mathematics for his research on dark energy.
content: Lecturer of Sri GCSR Degree College, Rajam, Vizianagaram district, Vaka Srinivasa Rao has been awarded a Ph.D. by the Gandhi Institute of Engineering and Technology, Gunupur (Odisha), after successfully completing his research in the subject of Mathematics. His thesis, titled “Investigation on Dark Energy Cosmological Models in Certain Theories of Gravitation”, was carried out under the guidance of Assistant Professors V. Ganesh and K. Dasu Naidu. Several lecturers and students congratulated Mr. Vaka Srinivasa Rao on receiving his Ph.D.

title: ‘Helmet bouquets’ launched to promote road safety in Tirupati district
summary: Tirupati launches 'helmet bouquets' to promote safety, encouraging helmet use as thoughtful gifts for loved ones this New Year.
content:
Following the police department’s strict enforcement of helmet rule in the State, new ways to popularise its use have emerged in Tirupati district. The latest trend — ‘helmet bouquets’— decorated helmets meant to be gifted to the near and dear with a message of road safety for the New Year.
Inspired by the new helmet rule, Blue Petals Florist in Tirupati launched these unique bouquets. Regional Transport Officer K. Muralimohan, who unveiled the concept on Tuesday, expressed concern over motorcyclists still viewing helmet use as optional, despite its mandatory status. While acknowledging the government’s leniency with violators, he emphasised the importance of social responsibility in promoting safety.
“These helmet bouquets are meant to be gifted by loved ones — a sister to a brother, a wife to her husband, or a girlfriend to her boyfriend. The idea is to encourage youth to wear helmets gifted by those who care about them,” said C.B.V. Saikumar Reddy of Blue Petals Florist.
The bouquets can be customised with helmets in various colours, styles (half/full), and genders, along with flowers, fruits, and chocolates. Prices range from ₹1,000 to ₹10,000. For more details call 93999 39390.

title: Vice-President to visit Golden Temple in Vellore on January 3
summary: Vice-President C.P. Radhakrishnan will visit Vellore's Golden Temple on January 3, following President Murmu's recent visit.
content:
Vice-President of India C.P. Radhakrishnan will visit Sri Narayani Peedam, also known as the Golden Temple in Thirumalaikodi village on the outskirts of Vellore Corporation limits on January 3 (Saturday).
Police said that security arrangements will be made around the temple premises. Around 150 police personnel  will be deployed during the visit. Operation of drones and other non-conventional aerial objects will be prohibited.
As per plan, the police said Mr. Radhakrishnan will reach the temple by helicopter from Chennai. He will visit the temple premises, including a meditation centre, during his hour-long stay there before returning to Chennai.
Mr. Radhakrishan’s visit comes after President Droupadi Murmu, who visited the temple on December 17.

title: Logo of ASAP’s Superskill Hero Awards campaign unveiled
summary: ASAP Kerala launches 'Superskill Hero Awards' to honor youth transforming lives through skill development, unveiled by actor Tovino Thomas.
content: ASAP Kerala, under the Department of Higher Education, has launched the ‘Superskill Hero Awards’ campaign aimed at identifying and celebrating real-life heroes who transform their lives through skilling. Actor Tovino Thomas released the campaign logo at a ceremony presided over by Minister for Higher Education R. Bindu in Thiruvananthapuram on Tuesday. The initiative seeks to highlight the critical role of skill development alongside academic education in enhancing the employability of young people. Through the Superskill Hero Awards, ASAP Kerala will honour youth who successfully complete ASAP courses in an exemplary manner or secure meaningful employment through skilling, thereby inspiring more young people to pursue skill-based learning. The campaign also underscores the message that anyone can become a real-life superhero by cultivating the skills demanded by a rapidly changing world.

title: Kanakadasa’s works embody universal human consciousness, says scholar
summary: Scholar Mallepuram G. Venkatesh highlights Saint Kanakadasa’s works as embodying universal human consciousness in a recent lecture.
content:
Saint Kanakadasa’s works embody a universal human consciousness, scholar and former Vice-Chancellor of Sanskrit University Mallepuram G. Venkatesh said in Kaginele on Monday.
“Kanakadasa’s poetry and hymns reveal a vision of universal human awareness. His Ramadhanya Charite is not only a unique Kannada poem but also a famous satirical work, while Kanakadasa’s transition from a life of indulgence to one of spiritual pursuit is evident in his works,” he said.
He was delivering a lecture on “Saint Kanakadasa and Universal Human Consciousness” organised by the Kaginele Development Authority.
“Kanakadasa’s life is one of personal growth and collective contribution, as reflected in his poetry and hymns. His poetic heart gave Kannada literature numerous wonderful poems, while his sage-like heart imparted a universal human consciousness to Kannada culture as can be seen in the universal human message in Kuvempu’s Aniketana poem,” he said.
President of the Haveri Zilla Sahitya Parishat Lingayya B. Hiremath expressed satisfaction with Kaginele Development Authority’s recent cultural and literary initiatives.
“Kaginele Development Authority Commissioner Mukkanna Karigar is trying to transform the authority into a cultural centre. The Sahitya Parishat will support all its activities,” he said.
Resource persons Basavaraj Sinnur, Jagannath Genannavar and others spoke.

title: Temples are remembered when polls approach, Chouhan takes dig at Mamata on Mahakal temple plan
summary: Shivraj Singh Chouhan criticizes Mamata Banerjee for exploiting religion for electoral gains ahead of West Bengal elections.
content:
Union Minister and BJP leader Shivraj Singh Chouhan on Tuesday (December 30, 2025) took a swipe at West Bengal Chief Minister and Trinamool Congress supremo Mamata Banerjee over aproposed Mahakal temple in her State, saying some people make such plans and recite religious texts only when elections approach, but maintain stoic silence when religious institutions are attacked.
Talking to reporters at his residence in Bhopal, Mr. Chouhan noted temples and religious rituals are matters of faith, but some Opposition parties use religion solely for electoral gains.
On Monday (December 29), Ms. Banerjee declared at a programme in Kolkata that the foundation stone of a Mahakal temple would be laid in Siliguri in north Bengal in the second week of January, and that land has been identified, and funds have been arranged for the project.
Asked about the West Bengal CM’s announcement, Mr. Chouhan stated, “When elections are around the corner, only then temples are remembered by some people. I believe temples or other religious activities are matters of faith. When these religious institutions are attacked, such people remain silent. But as elections approach, many start wearingtripund(sacred mark), begin reciting the Hanuman Chalisa and remember the Durga Saptashati. I think people know this truth,” the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) leader asserted.
Mr. Chouhan stressed that faith should be respected and not used as a political tool.
Assembly elections in West Bengal are due in March-April 2026. The Banerjee-led Trinamool Congress is currently in power in the State, while the BJP is the main Opposition.

title: Tribals in Nagarahole pass resolutions against relocation, seek implementation of Forest Rights Act provisions
summary: Tribal communities in Nagarahole oppose relocation and seek enforcement of the Forest Rights Act through an awareness march.
content:
Tribal communities in several villages in Nagarahole have passed resolutions opposing relocation of forest-dwelling communities under the pretext of rehabilitation.
They have also opposed research or commercial activity without their consent and reiterated that any initiative on their ‘’traditional lands’’ should be undertaken only with the prior approval of the gram sabhas as mandated by law.
These and other resolutions were passed  during the ongoing awareness march on the implementation of provisions of the Forest Rights Act (FRA) 2006. It is being held across tribal hamlets in Nagarahole.
The march, which began on December 21 and has covered about 70 km, entered its 10th day on December 30. It is an initiative of the members of Nagarahole Adivasi Jamma Paale Hakku Sthapana Samiti (NAJHSS).
Flagged off from Thitimathi Aiyrasuli village in Kodagu district, the march traversed through the villages of Nalleri forest region and reached Bavali in H.D. Kote taluk of Mysuru district. NAJHSS members said they covered revenue villages inhabited by members of the Jenu Kuruba, Beta Kuruba, Yerava and Paniya communities.
As part of the campaign, gram sabhas are being convened along the route to discuss provisions of the Forest Rights Act and issues related to its non-implementation in areas falling within the Nagarahole Tiger Reserve.
Meetings have been held with villagers, who discussed delays and rejections in the recognition of individual and community forest rights under the FRA. NAJHSS representatives also stated that gram sabhas in at least 18 villages have expressed support for the march so far.
Each day, participants walk seven to 10 km and visit two to three villages, where discussions are held with elders, youth and local leaders on the role of gram sabhas under the Forest Rights Act.
Issues raised during the meetings include the process followed in declaring protected areas, the status of community forest resource rights in notified national park and tiger reserve areas, and the pending recognition of habitat rights of the jenu kuruba community, which is classified as a Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Group (PVTG).
The awareness march is scheduled to conclude on January 1, 2026, by when it will have covered about 29 villages in the Nagarahole region.
On January 2, 2026, which marks the 20th anniversary of the enactment of the FRA 2006, NAJHSS plans to organise a protest at Kerehadi village near the Nagarahole Udburu Gate in H.D. Kote taluk.
‘We expect support from over 50 villages, including those from Periyapatna taluk,’’ said J.K. Thimma and P.C. Ramu, members of NAJHSS.

title: Global spice routes conclave to unveil heritage network
summary: Join the global Spice Routes Conclave in Kochi, starting January 6, to explore heritage tourism and cultural connections.
content:
Declaration of the Spice Routes Heritage Network and charter presentation will set the stage for engaging conversations at a three-day international Spice Routes Conference scheduled in Kochi from January 6, spotlighting the shared maritime and cultural heritage and its continued relevance in the global narrative. The event, to be organised by the Muziris Heritage Project in collaboration with Kerala Tourism, will be held at Bolgatty Palace.
The first of its kind event in the country, the conference is conceived as an intellectual and cultural platform that reconnects the ancient Spice Route with contemporary global discourse. Besides thematic presentations, the conference will feature technical sessions on topics such as Governing and Sustaining Transnational Heritage Corridors, Heritage Tourism: Question of Sustainability, Re-imagining Spice Routes for Tourism, Digital Spice Routes, Muziris Re-imagined, and Knowledge Tradition in the Region.
The event will explore new ways to strengthen cultural and heritage tourism among a host of countries which are part the famed global trade corridor. According to Tourism Minister P.A. Mohamed Riyas, “the conference aims at positioning Kerala as an attractive destination that offers in-depth experiences rooted in history, heritage and culture.”
The conference seeks to position Kerala not merely as a destination but as a living crossroad of global heritage and maritime civilisation. Paper presentations, conversations, poster displays, art shows, film screening, performances, site visits and so on will be part of the conference.
The event will offer delegates a deeply immersive cultural journey into Kerala’s living heritage. The Muziris Heritage Project partners with the Kochi-based art collective Aazhi Archives, led by multimedia artist Riyas Komu, for holding photographic exhibitions and art shows at various sites in Kochi. M.H. Ilias of Mahatma Gandhi University is the academic consultant who has designed the academic sessions.
Three photographic exhibitions, Chavittunatakam (K.R. Sunil), Seeing is Believing (Biju Ibrahim) and Migrant Dreams (Aazhi Archives), will be held at the main venue. Two performances, Kaarkuzhali (songs of Jews of Kochi) by playback singer Reshmi Sateesh and Chavittunatakam by Thampi Asan and team of Gothuruth, will also be staged. The event will see 38 international delegates from 22 countries, besides participants from across the country.

title: State govt. to re-open Dharwad Aadhaar centre soon
summary: Dharwad's Aadhaar service centre will soon reopen, expanding citizen access to essential services, confirms Deputy Commissioner Divya Prabhu.
content:
The State government will re-open the Aadhaar service centre in Dharwad soon, Deputy Commissioner Divya Prabhu G.R.J. said in Hubballi on Monday.
She said that the Dharwad centre was closed as its tender period got over but it will be restarted soon.
“Steps have been taken to start Aadhaar service centers to serve the citizens of the twin cities and one such centre started working in Hubballi today. The Aadhaar center that was previously operating in Dharwad has temporarily stopped its service as the tender period has expired and steps have already been taken to start an Aadhaar service center in Dharwad soon through a new tender process. The district administration has submitted a proposal already,” she said.
She was speaking after inaugurating the new Aadhaar Seva-UIDAI center at the Jola Complex behind SBI Bank in Bhavaninagar in Hubballi.
“An Aadhaar Kendra was functioning successfully in Hubballi from 2019 to 2025. After its tender period ended, the new tender process was completed and now this center has been re-opened in Keshwapur. Earlier, there were a total of eight centers in the State. After the re-opening, the services have been expanded to 22 major centers,” she said.
“People will now be able to register for a new Aadhaar card, correct name, address, mobile number and date of birth, update biometrics, photo, fingerprint and eye scan and other Aadhaar related services,” she said.
Members of Dharwad Dhwani staging a protest against the closure of an Aadhaar centre in Dharwad on Monday. 
                                                            | Photo Credit: 
                                SPECIAL ARRANGEMENT
Earlier, members of Dharwad Dhwani staged a protest against the closure of Aadhaar centres in Dharwad.
They gathered in front of the office of the Deputy Commissioner, demanding reopening of an Aadhaar Seva Kendra.
Congress leader Deepak Chinchore said that Union Minister Pralhad Joshi is behind the move to shift the Aadhaar centre in Dharwad to Hubballi.
“Hundreds of people used to visit this centre daily for services such as Aadhaar card enrolment, name correction, updates and corrections, change of address, mobile number linking and other related services. The centre used to provide services in a simple manner and within a short time, even for a large number of applicants. As a result, people not only from Dharwad city and rural areas but also from neighbouring taluks used to come here. However, after the centre was shifted to Hubballi, residents of the city and surrounding areas are facing severe difficulties,’’ he said.
“Although Aadhaar-related services are available at the post office and at a few private online centres in the city, timely service is not available for a large number of applicants. Moreover, as higher fees are being charged for these services, it has opened the door for exploitation of the general public,” he said.
Protestors took out a padayatra from Mandi Plaza near Kittur Chennamma Park to the Deputy Commissioner’s office. The Aadhaar Seva Kendra has been operating in the Mandi Plaza building. However, the centre was abruptly shut down on Sunday and has now been shifted to Keshwapur in Hubballi. They demanded the continuation of this centre.
In a memorandum submitted to the Deputy Commissioner office, they warned of an agitation if the centre is not reopened.
Leaders like Ishwar Shivalli, Basavaraj Jadhav, Gouramma Balogi, Shivanand Kavali, Manju Nadatti, Santosh Pattanashetti, Bheemappa Kasai and others were present.

title: Secunderabad Cantonment residents seek board elections and to fast-track merger with GHMC
summary: Secunderabad Cantonment residents urge the Ministry of Defence for immediate board elections and merger with Greater Hyderabad Municipal Corporation.
content:
Resident Welfare Associations from the Secunderabad Cantonment area have submitted a representation to Joint Secretary, Ministry of Defence Rajesh Mittal, seeking immediate conduct of elections to the Secunderabad Cantonment Board (SCB) and to expedite the merger of civilian areas with the Greater Hyderabad Municipal Corporation (GHMC). The representations were handed over during his visit to Hyderabad on Tuesday.
The Confederation of Cantonment Residents Welfare Association, Secunderabad, said SCB elections have not been held since 2020, with the last elected board completing its term after the January 2015 polls. Citing democratic norms that mandate local body elections every five years, the association said civilians in cantonment areas continue to be denied this right. It added that the absence of an elected board has stalled development, left civic issues unresolved and weakened accountability and grievance redressal mechanisms.
In a separate representation, the Cantonment Vikas Manch urged the Ministry to expedite the excision of civil areas of Secunderabad Cantonment and their merger with the GHMC through a clearly defined timeline.
“Residents of the cantonment have for decades lived under restrictive and outdated regulations that have hindered planned urban development, despite the area being located in the heart of Hyderabad. While GHMC has expanded and modernised by absorbing surrounding gram panchayats and corporations, the cantonment has remained an island of stagnation, cut off from municipal infrastructure funding and democratic administrative benefits,” the representation said.

title: Year Ender 2025: Industries, a mixed bag teaming with hopes
summary: Year Ender 2025: Industries, a mixed bag teaming with hopes
content:
Calendar year 2025 for Telangana from an industries perspective was eventful, marked by several significant, some controversial and arguably a few avoidable developments.
At a broad level, the intent to consolidate and attract investments, be it in manufacturing or the services sectors, was evident with the Telangana Rising Global Summit towards the year-end hitting the crescendo. It was a year when Chief Minister Revanth Reddy’s government found its feet, sought to sharpen focus on industrial growth as a key pathway to achieve accelerated economic development, especially the $1 trillion GDP by 2034 goal, even as some of its own decisions, new tariffs and visa regulations of the U.S., as well as a major industrial accident in Hyderabad’s neighbourhood cast a shadow.
As has become an annual feature, this year too took off with major investment announcements from the World Economic Forum. For the second year on a trot, the CM-led the delegation to the prestigious event in Davos. The team returned with ₹1.78 lakh crore investment commitment on projects with a potential to generate nearly 50,000 jobs. Amazon Web Services, Sun Petrochemicals, Tillman Global Holdings, Jindal, HCL, Infosys and Wipro figured in the list.
This even as several other big names from Eli Lilly to Vanguard choose Hyderabad for establishing global capability centres. GCCs are the latest in the process of offshoring work and unlike the back offices of the past not just help cut cost but also add value with core innovation work, including harnessing Artificial Intelligence. Shaping GCCs into Global Value Centres has become a stated objective of the government as much as its efforts in making firms see value in going to tier II and III locations.
Beyond firming up its reputation as a preferred destination for IT firms, Hyderabad also built on its image as a Life Sciences and Defence and Aerospace hub. Government of India’s emphasis on Make in India as well as indigenisation and self reliance in defence manufacturing besides the peek into future of wars that Operation Sindoor provided only bolstered the case of Hyderabad to take up more work. Vaccine makers and pharma companies continued to chart new territories.
However, for a State whose industrial foundations rest on MSMEs, one of its decisions that stoked controversy and political backlash was Hyderabad Industrial Lands Transformation Policy to relocate industrial units within city limits beyond Outer Ring Road and convert the vacated lands for other uses such as residential, commercial, institutional and recreational purposes in addition to creating space for IT firms. MSME leaders said such move should be preceded by creation of ecosystem from basic roads, transportation to social infrastructure since not just lakhs of people dependent on the units but their families will be also impacted.
The six-month sunset clause in (HILTP) could mean only a few plot holders vacating. But that should be enough to create conditions forcing remaining units to move out in near future.
A sudden, steep increase in electricity bills following change in the billing norm, withdrawal of time-of-day (ToD) power tariff concession, time taken for issue of supporting government orders to implement MSME Policy 2024 guidelines are some other matters of concern for trade and industry. The government is also quiet on the new Life Sciences Policy as well as the proposed Green Pharma villages.
2025 was witness to a devastating industrial accident that many believe could have been avoided with enhanced monitoring, enforcement and compliance. More than 50 people dead and many were injured in the explosion and fire at Sigachi Industries unit, near Hyderabad.
Speedier action is something industry favours, from disbursement of pending incentives to measures to reduce cost of doing business.
While officials spoke of proposed tweaks to TS-iPASS system of approvals and setting up a dry port, it was the Telangana Rising Summit the government choose to unveil medium to long term plans for inclusive, sustainable development.  Many were centred around proposed Bharat Future City. It announced a ₹1,000 crore Fund of Funds for startups and how Telangana is poised to become a skill capital on the back of the Young India Skills University. One of the highpoints was companies committing ₹5.75 lakh crore investment.

title: Stadium, ring road, and hospital upgrade among priorities, says Koothattukulam municipal chief
summary: Koothattukulam's new chairperson, Regi John Plathottathil, prioritizes stadium, ring road, and hospital upgrades in his development agenda.
content:
Regi John Plathottathil has outlined a five-point development agenda, which will serve as the focal point during his initial days as chairperson of Koothattukulam municipality, located on the eastern outskirts of Ernakulam district.
Among his top priorities is the establishment of a municipal stadium to meet the sporting needs of the youth and to nurture hidden talent. The lack of proper sporting infrastructure has long been a demand of the people in the municipality.
The construction of a ring road is another priority identified by Mr. Plathottathil. Although a small allocation was made for the project a decade ago, little progress has been achieved since then. “The proposed ring road will ease traffic congestion in Koothattukulam town and benefit commuters passing through,” he said.
Upgrading the infrastructure at the government taluk hospital has also been given prominence. “It remains a taluk hospital only in name. The goal is to ensure round-the-clock service with improved facilities and additional doctors,” Mr. Plathottathil stated. He is equally confident about setting up a modern municipal office along with a shopping complex, which would generate revenue for the municipality.
Mr. Plathottathil, a first-time councillor chosen for the chairperson’s post by the Congress parliamentary party, is determined to break the dubious trend in which no chairperson has ever completed a full term. Although the United Democratic Front holds a comfortable majority in the 26-member council, his selection-aligned with the K.C. Venugopal faction of the Congress ‘I’ group, was far from smooth.
