He prevailed over seasoned councillor and former chairperson Prince Paul John of the ‘A’ faction in the parliamentary party meeting.
Reportedly, the Ernakulam District Congress Committee suggested a split term of two-and-a-half years each for Mr. Plathottathil and Mr. John. However, the faction supporting Mr. Plathottathil was unwilling to grant Mr. John more than a year, citing its majority in the parliamentary party. Mr. John considered this an affront to his stature and rejected the offer. Further drama surrounding the post cannot be ruled out.

title: Police conduct final inspection ahead of New Year Eve celebrations
summary: Police finalize security measures for New Year celebrations in Bengaluru, ensuring public safety and effective crowd management.
content:
With New Year celebrations set to begin from Wednesday night, senior police officials  conducted a final inspection of security and crowd management in the city’s Central Business District, including M.G. Road and Church Street.
Deputy Commissioners of Police (DCPs) carried out inspections to review bandobast, CCTV coverage, traffic diversions, parking facilities, lighting, and barricading, as part of the New Year countdown preparations.
The inspection was led by Central Division DCP, Akshay M. Hakay and West Division Traffic DCP Anoop Shetty, who reviewed the arrangements and verified whether security measures were in place as per the approved deployment map.
Speaking to reporters, West Zone Joint Commissioner of Police Vamsi Krishna said, “The department is fully prepared for New Year celebrations and all necessary arrangements have been made to ensure public safety. Security has been strengthened on Brigade Road, M.G. Road, and Church Street.”
He said barricades and lighting systems have been installed, and the police have also taken note of suggestions from the public, which can be submitted through a QR code-based feedback system.
As per the traffic and crowd movement plan, Kaveri Junction will serve as the entry point and Opera Junction will function as the exit point. Standing or loitering on public roads will not be permitted, he said.
The police have installed over 360 CCTV cameras in the immediate area, with around 6,000 additional cameras deployed across the city. A command and control centre has also been set up to monitor celebrations in real time.
The police have directed pubs and bars to close by 1 a.m. In addition, 50 flyovers across Bengaluru will be closed as part of traffic regulation measures.
Visitors heading to pubs and bars have been advised to use K.C. Das Road for entry and exit via Opera Junction. Separate pathways have been arranged for women and families to ensure safer movement.
The Chickballapur administration has announced the closure of Skandagiri and Kaiwara, popular tourist destinations close to Bengaluru, on January 1, while the district police have announced the closure of Nandi Hills from 2 p.m. on December 31 to 10 a.m. on January 1.

title: Devotees throng temples on ‘Vaikunta Ekadasi’
summary: Devotees flock to temples for special prayers on Vaikunta Ekadasi, braving the cold to honor Lord Venkateshwara.
content:
Hundreds of devotees thronged several temples of Lord Venkateswara Swamy to offer special prayers on the occasion of Vaikunta Ekadasi in spite of the cold weather in the early hours of Tuesday (December 30, 2025). At the historic Ramateertham temple, devotees offered prayers after completing the Giri Pradakshana, which was organised on this auspicious day.
A.P. Sadhu Parishad president Swami Srinivasananda, Ramateetham Seva Parishad founder Jyoti Prasad and others coordinated arrangements for the devotees.
Astalakshmi Sametha Iswharya Venkateswara Swamy temple located in Ayyannapeta, outskirts of Vizianagaram witnessed huge rush of devotees from 5 a.m. onwards. The temple trustees Durga Balaji, D. Umadevi and others made elaborate arrangements for the darshan of Lord Venkateswara Swamy through “uttara dwaram” (entrance through North side of the temple). The devotees offered special prayers in Kalyana Venkateswara Swamy temple located at Ring Road, TTD’s Venkateswara Swamy temple located near Balaji junction and Venkateswara Swamy temple at Thotaplalem and other places.
Shiva Balaji temple located in bankers’ colony of Srikakulam wore a festive look with special decoration with flowers. Priest of the temple Gopinambala Sitaramacharyulu performed Abhisekham to the presiding deity on the occasion.

title: BC leader hails Modi for conducting caste-based census
summary: BC leader R. Krishnaiah praises Modi for approving India's first caste-based census, advocating for 50% reservations and community welfare.
content:
Rajya Sabha MP and president of National Backward Classes Welfare Association R. Krishnaiah hailed Prime Minister Narendra Modi for giving his assent to conduct the country’s first-ever caste-based census.
Addressing a media conference here on Tuesday, he said the association demanded 50 per cent reservations for the BC community in education, employment and the political domain, which would be possible only by taking up a caste census.
“I hail Prime Minister Modi for agreeing to take up caste-based census for the first time in the 77 years of independent India,” Mr. Krishnaiah said. He referred to the proposed caste census as the only way to ascertain the exact population of the backward classes across the country, in order to extend them benefits in proportion to their numbers.
Mr. Krishnaiah wanted 50 per cent reservation of seats for the BC community in the parliament and assembly elections, a special development scheme with ₹2 lakh crore and an exclusive cabinet ministry to oversee the welfare activities of the community.
BJP State official spokesperson Jalli Madhusudhan and media panellist K. Sridhar took part.

title: Defence Ministry inks ₹4,666 cr. contracts for battle carbines, torpedoes
summary: The Defence Ministry signs ₹4,666 crore contracts for battle carbines and torpedoes, enhancing military capabilities and promoting indigenisation.
content:
The Ministry of Defence on Tuesday (December 30, 2025) signed defence procurement contracts worth ₹4,666 crore for the acquisition of Close Quarter Battle (CQB) Carbines for the Indian Army and Navy and Heavyweight Torpedoes for the Indian Navy, in a major push towards modernisation and operational preparedness of the Armed Forces.
The contracts were inked in the presence of Defence Secretary Rajesh Kumar Singh at South Block, New Delhi, officials said.
According to Ministry of defence, under the first contract, over 4.25 lakh CQB Carbines along with accessories, valued at ₹2,770 crore, will be procured for the Indian Army and the Indian Navy from Bharat Forge Ltd and PLR Systems Pvt Ltd. The induction of these indigenously manufactured carbines marks the culmination of a long-standing effort to replace legacy small arms with modern, high-lethality weapons in line with the ‘Aatmanirbhar Bharat’ vision.
Designed as a key component of the modern infantry arsenal, the CQB Carbine offers a compact design, high rate of fire and enhanced lethality, providing a decisive advantage in close-combat and confined-space operations. The project also underscores growing government–private sector synergy, strengthening the Make in India initiative while boosting employment, supporting MSMEs, and deepening India’s indigenous defence manufacturing ecosystem, the Ministry added.
The second contract, valued at approximately ₹1,896 crore, was signed with WASS Submarine Systems S.R.L., Italy for the procurement and integration of 48 Heavyweight Torpedoes along with associated equipment for the Indian Navy’s Kalvari Class (Project-75) submarines. The acquisition will significantly enhance the combat capability of the Navy’s six submarines under the class.
Officials said delivery of the heavyweight torpedoes is scheduled to commence from April 2028 and will be completed by early 2030. Equipped with advanced technological features and robust operational capabilities, the torpedoes will strengthen the Navy’s underwater warfare prowess.
The latest acquisitions underline the Government’s commitment to meeting the evolving operational requirements of the Armed Forces through the induction of advanced and niche technologies.
In the Financial Year 2025–26, the Ministry of Defence has so far signed capital acquisition contracts worth ₹1,82,492 crore, reflecting a sustained focus on the modernisation and indigenisation of India’s defence forces.

title: Congress top brass should decide on leadership change before Budget preparation: HM
summary: Home Minister G. Parameshwara urges Congress leadership decision before February's Budget preparation to ensure effective governance.
content:
As the tussle over leadership change is unlikely to end soon, Home Minister G. Parameshwara on Tuesday said that the Congress high command has to decide on the leadership issue before the Budget preparation in February.
Speaking to reporters, he said whether there should be a leadership change or not will be decided by the Congress high command.
“The Budget preparation will begin in February; if the high command has to decide anything on this issue, they should decide before that,” Dr. Parameshwara said.
“Someone will have to prepare the Budget, right? The Budget has to be presented based on the assurance we have given to the people of the State. It will be done,” he added.
Asked about his supporters’ demand to appoint him as the Chief Minister in case the party decided to replace Mr. Siddaramaiah, the Home Minister said, “Those who say that Prameshwara should become CM, they would have said it out of affection towards me. How can I tell them not to say such things?”
Chief Minister Siddaramaiah, who also holds the Finance portfolio, asserted that he would present his 17th budget next year.

title: Madurai to enter Twin Cities Partnership with Camberley for cultural exchange and educational collaboration
summary: Madurai and Camberley partner for cultural exchange and education, enhancing ties through a formal agreement during Pongal celebrations.
content:
The Pongal celebrations in the ancient city of Madurai will mark the signing of a Twin Cities Partnership with Camberley, a town in the United Kingdom. Mayor of Surrey Heath Louise Ashbery and her delegation will visit Madurai and Theni during the festival and sign the agreement with the Madurai Corporation Commissioner. Camberley is the home town of Colonel John Pennycuick, the British engineer who built the Mullaperiyar Dam.
“The agreement marks a new chapter in cultural exchange, educational collaboration, and global development between the two cities. The visit of Mayor Councillor Louise Ashbery and her delegation symbolises a renewed bond between the two regions, rooted in history and focused on future progress,” said Santhana Beeroli, a documentary film-maker, who had earlier traced the memorial of Colonel John Pennycuick and his family members.
Chitra Vijayan, Commissioner of the Madurai Corporation, has already written to Louise Ashbery regarding the Twin Cities Partnership, as Chief Minister M.K. Stalin is keen on fostering such agreements. “The Government of Tamil Nadu and the Madurai Corporation welcome your proposal to explore a formal twinning arrangement. We share your belief that such a partnership holds significant potential for fostering cultural, educational, and economic exchanges,” Ms. Vijayan said in her letter.
Tamil Nadu’s Minister for Minorities and Non-Resident Tamils Welfare  S.M. Nazar has already visited St. Peter’s Church in Camberley.
In her response, Louise Ashbery said she was interested in visiting Tamil Nadu “to learn more about the historic city of Madurai, explore the links between our communities, and gain a deeper understanding of Tamil culture”. “I am particularly keen to learn more about Colonel John  Pennycuick and the lasting impact of the Mullaperiyar Dam on the region,” she added.
Mr. Beeroli said Ms. Ashbery and her delegation would meet the Chief Minister on January 11 in Chennai before travelling to Madurai, where they would participate in the Pongal celebrations on January 14 and sign the agreement on January 16. The partnership is a long-term collaboration between cities in different countries, aimed at promoting cooperation in education and research, culture and heritage, tourism, economic development, and urban governance and sustainability.
Mr. Beeroli noted that one of the most impactful outcomes of the partnership would be the creation of new academic and scholarship pathways for Indian students. “Through this initiative, students from Tamil Nadu will gain access to U.K. universities, exchange programmes, and joint research opportunities. It will especially benefit students from Madurai and surrounding regions, offering them global exposure and access to high-quality education,” he said.

title: CPI(M) turns to Kumarakom to bolster narrative of Cong.-BJP collusion
summary: CPI(M) targets Kumarakom to highlight alleged Congress-BJP collusion following a significant power shift in local governance.
content:
Amid the raging political slug-fest over the Mattathur panchayat in Thrissur, the   Communist Party of India (Marxist) has now set its sights on the Kumarakom panchayat in Kottayam, where it lost power for the first time in 55 years, seeking to underline its claims of a Congress-Bharatiya Janata Party nexus in the State.
As part of the offensive, the party on Tuesday openly challenged the Congress, asking whether it had the courage to expel those who engineered the alleged collusion to manipulate the mandate in the Kumarakom panchayat. “From Mattathur to Kumarakom, it is the Congress that has manipulated the system, allowing the front with the largest number of seats to assume power where no party has a majority,” alleged K. Anil Kumar, a member of the CPI(M) State committee.
The dramatic power shift in the local body last week saw an Independent, A. P. Gopi, assume charge as president with the backing of the United Democratic Front and three BJP members, decided by a draw of lots. In the aftermath, the BJP  initiated action against three of its elected members, expelling them from primary membership of the party for violating the party whip.
Highlighting the pre-election manoeuvring, Mr. Anil Kumar said the collusion was evident long before polling. “The collusion was most evident at the district panchayat level. While the BJP secured 2,617 votes in the grama panchayat, its district panchayat candidate received only 610 votes. Conversely, the UDF, which got 4,441 votes in the grama panchayat, saw its district panchayat candidate secure 6,419 votes. A similar pattern of collusion is visible in the Thiruvaarp grama panchayat as well,” he pointed out.
The Congress, however, defended the outcome by maintaining that it has only supported an Independent. “Mr. Gopi is a former local committee secretary of the CPI(M) and contested as an Independent. We  have no obligation to facilitate his return to the party from which he had earlier parted ways,” said Thiruvanchur Radhakrishnan, MLA.

title: Police step up vigil on New Year eve
summary: Special force formed to maintain law and order on New Year’s eve on Wednesday
content:
The police in the district have stepped up their preparations to curb incidents linked to New Year celebrations. They have formed a special force to maintain law and order on New Year’s eve on Wednesday.
Under the leadership of District Police Superintendent Ajit Kumar, a 1,500-member police force will be on high alert on Wednesday night. The deployment includes six DySPs, 28 inspectors, 145 sub-inspectors, 1,225 civil police officers and 92 women police personnel.
According to police sources, special squads will keep a close watch on individuals involved in anti-social activities and take action to prevent drug use and alcohol consumption in public places. Routine vehicle checks will also be carried out, and security along the district borders will be strengthened.
The police will keep a close watch on New Year DJ parties held at tourist spots, clubs, hotels and restaurants. The police said that crackdowns on drugs would be intensified and if any drug use is detected, the party organisers would also face legal action.
The police said that action would be taken against people bursting firecrackers on roads and other public spaces as well as those writing graffiti on streets. Violators of microphone regulations and firecracker rules will also face legal action.
Mr. Ajit Kumar said that all bars in the district must close by 11 p.m. and that New Year celebrations should conclude by the same time.

title: Special drive against drunk-driving: 3,716 cases booked
summary: Bengaluru traffic police booked 3,716 drunk drivers in a week-long enforcement drive to enhance road safety and prevent accidents.
content:
The city traffic police have booked as many as 3,716 motorists for drunk-driving during a special enforcement drive conducted between December 22 to December 29.
According to a release, during the week-long drive, the police checked over 2.66 lakh vehicles and booked 3,716 motorists.
The police said that the intensive checks were carried out at key junctions and accident-prone stretches, especially during night hours. The drive aims to deter reckless driving and reduce fatal accidents on city roads.
Authorities have stated that the special drive would continue on a regular basis as part of sustained efforts to improve road safety and prevent loss of lives due to drunk-driving.

title: Hanumanthu Sairam re-elected as APNGOs president for sixth term
summary: Hanumanthu Sairam re-elected as APNGOs president for sixth term, leading Srikakulam's association alongside new officials.
content: APNGOs Association members on Tuesday (December 30, 2025) unanimously elected Hanumanthu Sairam as the president of the association of Srikakulam district. He was elected to the post for the sixth consecutive time. The members also elected Challa Srinivasa Rao as the general secretary of the association and K. Jayarao as the associate president of the district body. Six others namely Rayi Venugopal, T. Someswara Rao, P. Janakiram, D. Sriram Kumar, P. Sravani and L. Jaganmohana Rao were elected as vice presidents. APNGOs association’s former State general secretary Chowdary Purushottam Naidu congratulated the new team, asking them to work sincerely to resolve grievances of the employees.

title: Sanskrit university Syndicate members flag concerns over revenue from KCA cricket stadium project
summary: Sanskrit university members express concerns over revenue sharing from KCA's cricket stadium project on university land.
content:
The Syndicate members of Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit who had raised concerns over the proposed cricket stadium project mooted by the Kerala Cricket Association (KCA) on the main campus in Kalady, near here, have cited the lack of any revenue earnings for the university in return for providing free user rights on the land to the cricketing body for a period of 33 years, it is learnt.
These members had flagged their concerns at the Syndicate meeting that discussed the revised master plan of the proposal submitted by the KCA on December 19. They have urged the university authorities not to finalise the project proposal without addressing their concerns.
As per the initial estimates, around six acres would be required for the project. The KCA will have to meet the cost and expenses incurred towards developing cricket facilities, according to the draft agreement.
K. Unnikrishnan, Syndicate member and former Principal of Government Sanskrit College, Thiruvananthapuram, said that the university land holds premium real estate value in view of its proximity to the Kochi airport and other key destinations.
He said that the draft agreement lacked clarity on whether the university will receive a share of the revenue earned by the KCA through the utilisation of the stadium and its allied facilities, he said. Prof. Unnikrishnan said that the university could explore funding options available under central schemes like ‘Khelo India’ to enhance its sporting facilities as an alternative plan.
The university authorities stated that there was no transfer or sale of land to the KCA. The cricketing body will only have land use rights, according to an official release issued on December 27.
The KCA will develop/construct multi-sports facilities, including a football ground with an athletic track. It will also construct and hand over a sports hostel to the university, it said.

title: YSS Dhyana Mandir to be inaugurated in Tirupati on January 3
summary: YSS Dhyana Mandir in Tirupati will be inaugurated on January 3, promoting meditation and spiritual growth.
content:
The Yogoda Satsanga Society of India (YSS) has built a new ‘Dhyana Mandir’ (meditation temple) at Nalanda Nagar in Tirupati West. The new temple will be formally inaugurated by YSS, Ranchi, vice-president Swami Smaranananda Giri on January 3.
The YSS chose Tirupati in view of its spiritual significance and the idea had taken shape 35 years.
YSS Tirupati unit founder D. Sreenivasulu and secretary P. Rajasekhara Reddy, both retired professors, formally released a poster announcing the event here on Tuesday. “The Tirupati unit was first conceived in 1989 and is set to attain fruition now,” said Mr. Sreenivasulu.
The three-storey facility has been constructed at a cost of ₹2.27 crore and is designed as a ‘sermon in stone’, a spiritual concept where the architecture serves as a silent teacher, guiding visitors towards inner peace, explained Mr. Reddy.
The chief guest, Swami Smaranananda Giri, who featured in the list of ‘Top 100 Great IITians dedicated to the service of the nation’, will deliver a spiritual discourse on the occasion.

title: HAL enters civil helicopter market as Dhruv NG completes inaugural flight
summary: HAL's Dhruv NG helicopter successfully completes its inaugural flight, marking India's entry into the civil helicopter market.
content:
Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL) on Tuesday (December 30, 2025) marked a breakthrough in India’s civil aviation ecosystem as the Dhruv New Generation (NG) helicopter successfully undertook its maiden flight at HAL’s Helicopter Division in Bengaluru, signalling the PSU’s formal entry into the civil helicopter market and a significant step towards self-reliance in civil aviation.
The inaugural flight was flagged off by Union Minister for Civil Aviation Kinjarapu Ram Mohan Naidu in the presence of D.K. Sunil, Chairman and Managing Director, HAL; Maneesh Kumar, Joint Director General, DGCA; Sanjeev Razdan, CMD, Pawan Hans Ltd; and senior HAL officials.
During the event, HAL also received the DGCA certification for ‘Indigenous Manufacturing of the Shakti Civil Engine’, a first-of-its-kind achievement in Indian aviation. This marks the first aero engine certified by the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) for indigenous production, representing a significant leap in India’s self-reliance in critical aviation technologies. The milestone was achieved with the participation of Safran Engines and close coordination with the DGCA.
HAL informed that the Dhruv NG is progressing steadily towards full civil certification within the next three to four months, positioning it as a key platform for India’s growing civil helicopter market.
Describing the occasion as a “flight ofAatmanirbhar Bharat,” Mr. Naidu said the maiden sortie reflected India’s growing confidence and capability in aviation manufacturing.
“This flight marks an important milestone in Indian aviation. I can see thesankalpof a Viksit Bharat taking wings. HAL has successfully conducted the inaugural flight within a year of showcasing the demo. Dhruv NG has emerged as a platform for several operators, and Make in India is now a seal of global quality,” he said.
Dr. Sunil termed the Dhruv NG the cornerstone of the company’s civil aviation expansion.
“The Dhruv ‘New Gen’ helicopter builds on the proven Dhruv Mk 1 civil platform, which has already clocked over 24,000 flying hours. It has been specifically upgraded to meet the rigorous demands of the global civil aviation market,” he said, adding that the helicopter offered enhanced safety, high performance and cost-effectiveness, making it a strong indigenous alternative to imported platforms.
Designed and manufactured in India, the Dhruv NG is a 5.5-tonne, light twin-engine, multi-role helicopter, engineered to operate across diverse and challenging Indian terrains. With its improved systems and civil certification road map, the platform is expected to play a significant role in strengthening India’s indigenous civil aviation ecosystem and reducing dependence on foreign helicopters.

title: As 2025 bows out, Kolkatans say there is nothing to cheer about
summary: As 2025 ends, Kolkata faces uncertainty and concerns about communal divides ahead of the critical 2026 Assembly elections.
content:
As the year draws to a close, the general opinion in what is often called the ‘City of Joy’ appears to be that 2025 is not something to be looked back upon fondly for West Bengal, and that 2026 too should be treated with caution because Assembly elections will be held then and there will be attempts to create a communal divide.
“I think people are very much disturbed by the election process. I am personally worried about our long tradition of communal harmony. It is not new for us to aim for votes of the minority community in order to achieve victory. And for the last few years, given the changed political scenario, the Opposition has been trying to get votes of the majority Hindu people by trying to destroy communal harmony,” celebrated Bengali writer Amar Mitra toldThe Hindu.
“This is a secular country,” the writer, a winner of the O. Henry Award and the Sahitya Akademi Award, said. “Political parties should not talk against the minority people. I must also mention the attack on poor Bengali-speaking people in a few States. This is a threat to our democracy; it’s my right to go and work anywhere in the country,” Mr. Mitra said.
According to a State government officer who did not want to be named, the outgoing year, for West Bengal, was neither transformative nor tranquil and was marked by a recurring pattern where “serious governance challenges coexisted with spectacle-driven narratives”.
“Cases of rape in law and medical colleges shook the public conscience. The SSC (School Service Commission) recruitment scam continued to erode trust among thousands of aspirants. The SIR (Special Intensive Revision) issue further deepened anxieties over transparency and administrative fairness. The visit of Lionel Messi dominated headlines and social media — a major administrative failure, a shame for the entire State. Cultural and religious assertions — seen in renewed debates around the Babri Masjid, and the public chanting of Gitashlokas(verses) — added to political polarisation,” the officer said.
Exactly the same thought is voiced by Shreya Datta, a doctoral research scholar at the University of Calcutta, and much younger than the officer. “In 2025, Bengal appeared to be outwardly stable, but there was a quiet erosion of trust. People were politically aware, yet emotionally detached. Otherwise, we would not have watched and quietly accepted the aftermath of one of the biggest recruitment scams that saw 26,000 people losing their jobs. Looking towards 2026, the election doesn’t feel like a promise of renewal, it feels more like a moment of reckoning. Bengal must answer a difficult question: Are we choosing between futures, or merely negotiating how to live with disappointment? What worries me is not only polarisation but also exhaustion. Intellectual fatigue. Moral fatigue,” Ms. Datta said.
Fellow scholar Ayan Ghosh is also of the opinion that those living in Bengal had nothing in 2025 to look back at. “From losing jobs to being beaten in other States for speaking one’s mother tongue to the establishment of the Jagannath Temple using taxpayers’ money; from the deportation of a pregnant woman to Bangladesh to the recent Messi fiasco — all of these have humiliated us as a Bengali-speaking community. The entire political system failed us. What we need for 2026 is a reset button. We need to delete jingoistic flavours from political discourse rather than engage in discussions on the deletion of voter lists,” Mr. Ghosh said.
Rajiv Kumar Pandey, the Kolkata secretary of the West Bengal Hindi Speakers’ Society, feels the rise of unemployment is the root of the present political scenario in the State. “There was a time when people from other States came to Bengal to look for employment opportunities. But factories here shut down and young people from Bengal began going to other States to look for jobs. It was unemployment that changed the political equations here and allowed communal forces to create a space for themselves. But I feel people are finally seeing through their motives and I expect 2026 to be constructive for us,” Mr. Pandey said.

title: Police inspector of Sadashivanagar station in Bengaluru booked for dowry harassment and assault on wife and children
summary: Bengaluru police inspector booked for dowry harassment and assault on his wife and children, following a detailed complaint.
content:
A police inspector of the Sadashivanagar police station has been booked allegedly for harassing his wife over dowry, physically assaulting and intimidating her and children.
Based on the complaint filed by the victim, Kavya, the north division women’s police station has registered an FIR against the accused and his relatives.
Kavya alleged that her husband Girish B.P. subjected her and their children to repeated physical abuse and dowry-related harassment.
According to the complaint, Kavya has alleged that Girish assaulted their daughter with a cricket bat and also attacked family members with a glass bottle under the influence of alcohol. She said that he had been physically abusive towards her and the children and had been harassing her for dowry since 2017.
In her complaint, Kavya stated that at the time of their marriage, around 15 years ago, her family spent approximately ₹30 lakh, including 250 gm of gold jewellery and ₹5 lakh in cash. She alleged that an additional ₹10 lakh was later given to her husband. Despite this, he continued to demand more money and subjected her to mental and physical harassment.
The complainant has alleged that her husband threatened to have her killed if further dowry was not paid. She has accused him of having an extramarital relationship.

title: Examine if temples can grow sandalwood for their religious customs: Karnataka HC
summary: Karnataka High Court directs Forest Department to explore allowing temples to grow sandalwood for religious practices amid supply issues.
content:
The High Court of Karnataka has directed the Principal Secretary, Forest Department, to examine whether religious institutions, temples and mutts could be allowed to grow their own sandalwood trees for the express purpose of using only for their religious customs and practices.
If the temples could be permitted to grow their own sandalwood trees, then the government can formulate necessary policy for that purpose, the court said.
Justice Suraj Govindaraj passed the order while partly allowing a petition filed, way back in 2011, by Sri Krishna Mutt, Udupi. The petitioner-mutt had sought a direction to the Forest Department to release the remaining quantity of the 1,087 kg of sandalwood, which the government had agreed to supply to the temple every year since 1921.
The mutt had filed the petition as the government had supplied only 30 kg of sandalwood as against the agreed quantity. The sandalwood paste, prepared by rubbing sandalwood billet against a grinding slab, in a semi-liquid form is used for the puja of Lord Krishna as well as distribution of it as prasada to the devotees, the mutt had told the court.
However, the government told the court that it is not possible to supply sandalwood in such a large quantity in the present circumstances due to shortage of availability of sandalwood, but 10 kg of sandalwood billets could be supplied to the mutt, if necessary application is made, every year as is being done in case of Muzrai Department notified temples.
The Forest Department has pointed out to the court that up to 20 kg of sandalwood billets for A-Class temples and 10 kg for B-Class notified temples are being supplied every year based on the availability on receipt of applications for this purpose. Since the petitioner-mutt is not coming under Muzrai Department, a maximum of 10 kg of sandalwood billets could be supplied every year, based on availability, if necessary application is made by the mutt, the court was informed.
However, the mutt had contended that use of sandalwood for cremation dead bodies of two VVIPs recently show that there is availability of sandalwood.
Taking note of the provisions of the Karnataka Forests Act, 1963, shortage in availability of sandalwood trees, and present policy of the government on supply of sandalwood for temples, etc., the court asked the petitioner to submit an application for supplying 10 kg sandalwood billets every year subject to availability and the Deputy Commissioner, Udupi, should act on the application within 30 days.

title: Mavelikara court acquits accused in Vishal murder case
summary: 20 people, including one minor, were charge-sheeted in the case. Of these, 19 faced trial and were acquitted by the court
content:
The Additional District and Sessions Court III, Mavelikara, on Tuesday acquitted all the accused in a case relating to the murder of Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP) activist Vishal in 2012. The verdict was delivered by judge P.P. Pooja.
Vishal, a 19-year-old degree student at NSS College, Konni, sustained stab injuries in an attack allegedly carried out by members of the Campus Front, the student wing of the Popular Front of India, near Christian College, Chengannur, on July 16, 2012, where he had gone to welcome first-year degree students. Two other ABVP activists were also injured in the attack.
A total of 20 people, including one minor, were charge-sheeted in the case. Of these, 19 faced trial and were acquitted by the court, which observed that the prosecution had failed to prove the charges against them beyond reasonable doubt. The case, initially investigated by local police, was later handed over to the Crime Branch.
The prosecution said it would file an appeal against the verdict in a higher court.

title: PM urged to suspend execution of VB-G Ram G
summary: Chief Minister Siddaramaiah urges PM Modi to suspend VB-G Ram G, citing concerns over its impact on MGNREGA's intent.
content:
Chief Minister Siddaramaiah has urged the Centre to suspend the implementation of the Viksit Bharat-Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB-G Ram G) since it would defeat the very intent of the original MGNREGA, a demand-driven, right-based guarantee scheme.
In a letter to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, the Chief Minister said, “The repeal of MGNREGA weakens the right to work, centralises decisions, and shifts an unfair burden onto States”.
The new Act guarantees 125 days of work per year against 100 days in the MGNREGA. Under the new Act, the Central and the State governments would share the expenditure in the ratio of 60:40 against the 90:10 in the previous law.
“The new Act involves serious constitutional, financial and governance concerns,” Mr. Siddaramaiah said.

title: Remand prisoner escapes from Kuthiravattom mental health centre
summary: A remand prisoner accused of murder escapes from Kuthiravattom mental health centre, prompting police alerts and investigations.
content:
A 25-year-old youth who was accused of stabbing a woman to death and injuring her sister at Elamkulam, near Perinthalmanna in Malappuram district, in June 2021, in an apparent reprisal for rejecting his romantic advances, reportedly ran away from the Government Mental Health Centre, Kuthiravattom, on Monday night (December 29).
According to reports, Vineesh Vinod, a native of Narukara near Manjeri in Malappuram, was a remand prisoner in the Central Jail, Kannur. He had been undergoing treatment at the mental health centre for the past two weeks. The jail staff noticed his absence in the cell during their routine checking around 11 p.m. Vineesh is believed to have drilled a hole in the washroom to get out of the building.
This is the second time Vineesh has escaped from the mental health centre. He was admitted here in 2022 with mental health issues. Though Vineesh had run away from the facility then as well, the police were able to nab him. He was again admitted here earlier this month.
The police have issued an alert in railway stations and bus stations. Closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage outside the hospital is also being examined.

title: Kaneri Math seer defends his use of language against Lingayat seers
summary: Kaneri Math seer defends his language use against Lingayat seers, emphasizing colloquial expressions and urging unity within Hinduism.
content:
Sri Adrushya Kadasiddeshwar Swami of Kaneri Math defended his use of abusive words against some Lingayat seers saying that he uttered commonly used words in colloquial language and that there is no need to take them seriously.
He was speaking at the Basavadi Sharanara Bruhat Hindu Samavesha in Babaleshwar of Vijayapura district on Monday.
“The words I uttered are very commonly used in rural North Karnataka. No one needs to take them seriously. However, I used such a language to reprimand some seers who are trying to damage the basic pillars of Hinduism. There is an urgent need to do so,” he said.
“No other seer was ready to reprimand those trying to cause damage. I’m ready for all consequences. I have the courage to do so. That is why I reprimanded them. I also warn them that such behaviour is not acceptable. My warnings seem to have worked. I threw a bomb three months ago and it is still having its effect. There are fireworks every day. My words have had such an effect that they are coming to me with folded hands and requesting me to stop speaking. To such people, I say, you started it and therefore, you should stop it,” he said.
He said that due to his warning, attacks on Hindutva by Lingayat seers and leaders have come down drastically. “Common people are holding them accountable for insulting Hinduism. My warning has caused heart attacks in some leaders. One person even told me that my words shocked him so much that he was forced to get a stent in his heart. Another told me that he has vowed never to speak of anything other than Basavanna and nationalism. To such people, who have regretted their remarks and have had a change of heart, I say, join me and let us work towards strengthening our religion. We are not enemies and let us retain our friendship,” he said.
He said that the seer of Bhalki Math has gone to Union Minister V. Somanna to resolve the differences between Kaneri Math seer and other seers. “Mr. Somanna called me on my mobile phone and asked me to speak to the seer. I said I carry no animosity towards anyone and asked him to work with me. I may have ideological differences with you, but I have great affection for you. I will stop talking about you people, the day you stop trying to divide the Lingayat Samaj. I want you to declare that Veerashaiva and Lingayat are one. You should not try to portray that Basavanna was an atheist and that he was anti-Vedas. That day, I will keep quiet,” he said.
The former Deputy Chief Minister K.S. Eshwarappa, several Lingayat seers and other community leaders were present.

title: Kurnool district witnesses slight increase in crimes in 2025
summary: Kurnool district sees a slight crime increase in 2025, with notable decreases in murders and crimes against women.
content:
Kurnool district reported a 0.7 per cent increase in overall crime rate in 2025, however, there has been a decrease in number of murders and attempt to murder cases when compared to 2024.
Addressing the media on the annual crime statistics for the year, Superintendent of Police (SP) Vikrant Patil said that while a total of 4,022 cases were registered during 2024, the numbers slightly increased to 4,051 in 2025. Mr. Vikrant Patil said the number of murders in 2025 was 29 compared to 34 in 2024, recording a 15 per cent decrease. Similarly the number of attempt to murder cases were 29 in 2025 compared to 41 in 2024 (29 per cent decrease). The cases of kidnappings in 2025 were 17 compared to 16 last year.
Meanwhile, the recovery of stolen property stood at 68.24 per cent, Mr. Vikrant Patil said. While ₹8,90,33,984 was stolen, the recovery stood at 6,07,59,891. Dacoities, robberies, daytime thefts and night thefts increased in 2025.
The number of accidents witnessed a steep jump in 2025. While a total of 547 (270 fatal and 277 non-fatal) accidents were reported in 2024, the same spiked to 658 (278 fatal and 380 non-fatal).
Mr. Vikrant Patil said crimes against women came down in 2025. While 10 rape cases were reported in 2024, five cases were registered this year. Similarly, the POCSO cases registered in 2025 were 37 as against 61 in 2024. Crime against SCs and STs have also come down by 13.71 per cent in 2025.
On the other hand, 64 cybercrime cases were reported in 2025 as against 107 in 2024, registering a 40 per cent decrease. Police refunded ₹82.90 lakh into the bank accounts of complainants, while over ₹5.86 crore in bank accounts were frozen. The police recovered 1,873 mobile phones worth ₹3.7 crore this year.
The enforcement drives have increased when compared to previous year, the SP said, adding that while 1,613 drunk and drive cases were registered in the last year, the same shot up to 9,196 cases. Similarly, 17,392 cases of open drinking cases were registered in 2025 against 4,338 last year.

title: New Year 2026: Kodagu police issues instructions against consumption of drugs and noise pollution
summary: Kodagu police prohibit drug use and noise pollution for New Year 2026 celebrations, ensuring a safe environment for all.
content:
The Kodagu district police has issued a set of instructions for New Year festivities prohibiting the public from selling, supplying or consuming narcotic drugs, and using sound systems that exceed the permissible decibel levels.
Kodagu attracts a large number of visitors including foreign tourists for New Year celebrations, organised in different parts of the hilly district.
A statement issued by Kodagu District Police Superintendent K. Ramarajan said owners or representatives of homestays, resorts and lodges should inform the local police if they come across the sale, supply or consumption of prohibited narcotic substances on their premises.
“If it is found that owners or their representatives have failed to provide information and have instead facilitated the sale or consumption of narcotic substances, cases will be registered against them under Section 25 of the Narcotic Drugs and Pyschotropic Substances (NDPS) Act. Legal action and steps will be taken to cancel their licenses,” the statement warned.
He also called upon the general public to inform the police if they come across visitors from within the district or tourists staying in homestays, resorts and lodges involved in the sale, supply or consumption of narcotic substances under the guise of rave parties. The public, he said, should call the Kodagu district police office by dialling 08272-228300 or 9480804900.
He also said that owners of homestays, resorts and lodges should adhere to the Noise Pollution (Regulation and Control) Rules, 2000, by ensuring that sound systems and loudspeakers do not exceed the permissible decibel levels prescribed by the Pollution Control Board for different zones.
All clubs, lodges, resorts and homestays in the district have also been instructed to mandatorily maintain registers and ensure that CCTV cameras installed on their premises are in proper working condition.
They have also been directed to record complete details of tourists visiting clubs, lodges, resorts and homestays in their registers and compulsorily obtain one valid photo identity proof of each guest staying on the premises.
While adequate police personnel will be deployed for New Year celebrations, strict instructions have also been issued to owners, managers and vendors of liquor shops to open and close their premises within the prescribed timings.
The police will deploy officials and staff in sensitive locations to prevent bursting of crackers and explosives in public places while taking precautionary measuers to ensure that the New Year festivities do not cause inconvenience to neighbouring residents.
The Police Superintendent also warned that organising New Year celebrations with DJs or hosting parties is prohibited in forest areas, river banks and public places.
Additional staff will be deployed at existing checkposts in the district while new checkposts will be set up at strategic locations to conduct inspections and prevent the transportation of any illegal materials, the statement said.

title: Chilly weather triggers a surge in tourism, Munnar witnesses hours-long traffic blocks
summary: The traffic crisis turned fatal on Sunday when a 35-year-old man died after the vehicle transporting him got stuck in a snarl
content:
Snowfall in the upper reaches of the mountains as well as the chilly weather that has desccended on the Munnar hills, severe traffic congestion, with vehicles stranded for four to five hours on major routes has become a recurrign sight. Stakeholders said that for the past week, the destination has been paralysed by hours-long traffic blocks. Recently, Idukki District Police Chief K.M. Sabu Mathew’s vehicle was also trapped in the congestion.
The traffic crisis turned fatal on Sunday when a 35-year-old man died after the vehicle transporting him got stuck in a snarl. Mariswami Palraj, a resident of Vattavada-Koviloor, was found vomiting blood at his home on Sunday morning. Relatives and neighbours attempted to rush him to Munnar, located around 43 km from Koviloor. However, the vehicle was trapped for hours enroute; by the time they reached Top Station, Mariswami had lost his life.
According to sources, Munnar is currently experiencing overcrowding that far exceeds its carrying capacity, especially on holidays. “The arrival of tourists is many times higher than what the destination can handle. Large tourist buses often get stuck on narrow roads, creating a block that lasts for hours,” said a source. “On Christmas Day, many tourists were trapped in their vehicles for hours without access to drinking water or basic toilet facilities. An e-pass system, similar to those in Ooty and Kodaikanal, could help regulate vehicle flow,” said the source.
Vinod Vattekkatt, a managing committee member of the Kerala Travel Mart (KTM), noted that while blockages are normal during weekends, the current situation is extreme. “Increasing the number of traffic police at major spots would help. Furthermore, Munnar lacks proper parking facilities. Most roads are narrow, and when tourists park on the roadside, it results in hours of gridlock,” said Mr. Vattekkatt.
G. Sojan, coordinator of the ‘My Munnar Movement,’ suggested implementing a dedicated bus service system from Rajamala, Mattupetty, and Top Station to the town. These three routes see the most rush at weekends and holidays. A shuttle service would allow tourists to see the sights while keeping private vehicles off the narrowest roads,” he explained.
Anil P.B., Vice President of the Greens Munnar initiative, suggested that a multi-level parking system on Devikulam Road is essential to decongest Munnar town.
The temperature drop in the second week of December continues to attract lakhs of tourists eager to experience the chilly weather and frost-covered grasslands, but many are trapped in the block, and the dream vacation is turning into a nightmare for many.

title: Former Dharmadam MLA K.K. Narayanan dead
summary: Former Dharmadam MLA K.K. Narayanan, a senior CPI(M) leader, has passed away at age 77.
content:
Senior Communist Party of India (Marxist) leader and former Dharmadam MLA  K.K. Narayanan passed away on Tuesday. He was 77.
According to sources, he collapsed while attending a National Service Scheme camp at Peralassery, his native place. Though Mr. Narayanan was rushed to a hospital, he could not be saved.
A former president of the Kannur district panchayat and the Kannur district secretariat of the CPI(M), Mr. Narayanan was elected MLA from Dharmadam in the 2011 Assembly polls. He was also the chairperson of AKG Memorial Cooperative Hospital and the Kannur District Cooperative Bank.

title: Revanth assisting Andhra’s Polavaram-Nallamalasagar project, alleges BRS
summary: Revanth assisting Andhra’s Polavaram-Nallamalasagar project, alleges BRS
content:
BRS senior MLA and former minister T. Harish Rao has accused the Congress government of enabling the neighbouring Andhra Pradesh government to plunder Telangana’s water resources in the name of the Polavaram–Nallamalasagar Link Project (PNLP) through its imprudent actions.  He demanded that the State government exert pressure on the Centre by staging a protest in front of the Central Water Commission (CWC), which, he alleged, had granted permission to A.P. to use 200 TMC ft of water from the Godavari.
Addressing a press conference at the party State office on Tuesday, Mr. Rao alleged that Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy is assisting the Andhra Pradesh government because N. Chandrababu Naidu is his political mentor. He also accused Mr. Reddy of making blatant false statements regarding the meeting convened by the Union Ministry of Jal Shakti, which was attended by the Chief Ministers and Irrigation Ministers of both Telangana and Andhra Pradesh on July 16, 2025 in New Delhi.
“Mr. Revanth Reddy initially said he would not attend the meeting, but he did. He later claimed that the Godavari–Banakacharla link was not on the agenda, yet it was included. Although he asserted that the topic was not discussed, it was indeed deliberated at the meeting, and Revanth Reddy even signed the related documents,” Mr. Rao said. He added that the Andhra Pradesh government had indeed withdrawn the  Polavaram–Banakacharla Link Project after Karnataka and Maharashtra stated they would claim their share of water under the Bachawat Tribunal award if water was diverted from the Godavari to the Krishna.
“In light of this, the Andhra Pradesh government is now proposing the Polavaram–Nallamalasagar Link Project (PNLP). However, this new project would severely harm Telangana’s water interests,” he said, demanding the Congress government to take immediate steps to prevent Andhra Pradesh from executing the project.
Mr. Rao also criticised the State government for appointing retired IAS officer and former Andhra Pradesh Chief Secretary Adityanath Das as the head of a committee to resolve water disputes between Telangana and Andhra Pradesh. He demanded Das’s removal from the committee, alleging that he had previously acted against Telangana’s water interests.

title: Mysuru to ring in New Year with fireworks against illuminated palace backdrop
summary: Mysuru welcomes the New Year with a stunning fireworks display against the illuminated palace, enhancing festive celebrations and safety measures.
content:
The illuminated Mysuru palace will form the backdrop for the fireworks that will light up the midnight sky to usher in the New Year.
This is in continuation of the tradition since 2017 and draws thousands of residents and tourists to the heritage precinct to savour the transition from the old to the new.
The fireworks will last 15 minutes and be the visual focus of the city’s New Year celebrations — a spectacle that matches the grandeur of similar displays in the backdrop of iconic structures elsewhere in the world.
The celebrations coincide with the ongoing Maghi Mela, also known as the winter festival, which began on December 21. As part of the festival, the palace has been illuminated in the evenings daily since then. Visitors have also been treated to a flower show and elaborate floral arrangements on the palace premises, adding to the festive ambience.
Subramanya, deputy director of the Mysuru Palace Board, said a series of cultural programmes have been held for the last nine days and have been a great hit with both tourists and locals. On December 31, the highlight of the evening will be a musical performance by the Mysuru Police Band, which will render English and Carnatic numbers. It is scheduled to commence from 11 p.m. to midnight.
The cultural programme will provide the ceremonial build-up and countdown to the fireworks that will begin at midnight to ring in the New Year.
The one-minute display will entail the use of ‘’green crackers’’, said Mr. Subramanya, and there will be a visual spectacle of light but devoid of any sound.
In the wake of the recent helium cylinder blast near the palace that claimed three lives, authorities have put in place enhanced security and safety measures.
Police deployment has been intensified in and around the palace area, local vendors have been cleared from sensitive zones, and access points are being closely monitored. A fire engine and ambulances will be stationed on site as a precautionary measure.
Police Commissioner Seema Latkar has issued guidelines and protocols for the public, which has been urged to adhere to these and ensure that the celebrations are peaceful and incident-free.

title: Kadapa district ranks first twice in State in disposal of cases
summary: Kadapa district leads in case disposal, resolving over 57,000 cases, while addressing crime and improving citizen outreach in 2025.
content:
The Kadapa district police focused on clearing pending cases and improving its citizen outreach programme in 2025.
As a result, the district ranked first twice (in two quarters) in the State in disposal of cases at the National Mega Lok Adalat. Also, 57,632 cases registered across various police station limits were settled through Lok Adalats. Similarly, 9,300 out of the 9,704 complaints received under the Public Grievance Redressal System (PGRS) were resolved within stipulated timelines.
Addressing a year-end media conference to highlight the district’s performance in 2025, Superintendent of Police (SP) Nachiket Vishwanath Shelke said murder cases decreased by 9 per cent, factional violence almost disappeared, riots decreased by 33 per cent and white collar crime dipped by 16 per cent.
Meanwhile, attempt to murder cases reduced by 9 per cent, cases under SC/ST atrocities declined by 9 per cent, while kidnapping of women fell by 33 per cent. Dowry deaths showed a 67 per cent fall, Mr. Nachiket explained.
The major challenge in 2025 came in the form of 57 cybercrime cases, of which 33 were solved and 62 offenders arrested. Of the total ₹16.47 crore lost by the victims, only ₹21.52 lakh could be recovered and returned to the complainants. “Of the 4,693 transactions traced across 135 bank accounts, we got a freeze of ₹3.05 crore”, he added.
Mr. Nachiket also inspected the valuables recovered after the Yerraguntla police arrested the alleged bag lifting gang. The police recovered stolen property worth ₹75 lakh, including 507 grams of gold, 1.5 kg of silver, ₹61,000 in cash, a car worth ₹4 lakh, and arrested nine accused, eight of them belonging to the Godavari district, who were involved in 23 cases across the State.

title: Koli Kabbaligas stage protest seeking Scheduled Tribes status
summary: Koli Kabbaliga communities protest in Kalaburagi, demanding Scheduled Tribes status from the State government with 3,000 participants.
content:
Thousands of members belonging to the Koli, Kabbaliga, Ambiga, Besta and Barik communities took out a protest march in Kalaburagi on Monday, demanding that their communities be included in the Scheduled Tribes (STs) list.
The protest began at Jagat Circle after the religious head of the community Sri Shanta Bheeshma Chowdaiah Swamy of Sri Nijasharana Ambigara Chowdaiah Peeta, Narsipura, Haveri, offered floral tributes to B.R. Ambedkar and social reformer Basaveshwara.
After the religious leader flagged off the protest march, the protestors waving flags bearing the image of Nijasharana Ambigara Chowdaiah reached the Deputy Commissioner’s office, where the community leaders addressed the rally.
Around 3,000 people from various parts of the district participated in the protest march. Throughout the protest march they raised slogans against the State government and praised the community leader late Vittal Heroor.
Vehicular traffic was disrupted for about an hour at Jagat Circle, while the main road outside the Deputy Commissioner’s office was blocked till early evening.
Addressing the gathering, MLC Talawar Sabbanna said that the communities have been demanding Scheduled Tribes status since 1996. Although proposals seeking inclusion under Scheduled Tribes were forwarded to the Central government several times, they have been repeatedly rejected and returned.
Mr. Sabanna urged the State government to submit a fresh recommendation to the Central government along with proper documentation.
Community leader Shivakumar Natekar said that the agitation is not directed against any political party or government but is aimed at securing Constitutional rights.
Mr. Natekar said that despite the community being deprived of benefits available to Scheduled Tribes for nearly three decades, the successive governments have failed to address the issue effectively.
He criticised the Siddaramaiah-led Congress government, which claims to represent marginalised sections, for failing to forward the proposal to the Centre even two years after coming to power.
He urged Rural Development and Panchayat Raj Minister and district in-charge Priyank Kharge to intervene and ensure that the long-pending demand of Koli-Kabbaliga community is fulfilled.
Some protestors also said that a section of community leaders have tried to foil the protest by misguiding people and preventing their participation by stopping them on the outskirts of the city.
MLC N. Ravi Kumar, community leaders Sharanappa Talawar and Shobha Bani and others also spoke at the protest rally.

title: Shivamogga police conduct special drive on ganja consumption and sale
summary: Shivamogga police launched a special drive, booking 177 cases and recovering significant amounts of ganja and MDMA.
content:
The Shivamogga police conducted a special drive against the consumption and sale of ganja in the last two months and booked a total of 177 cases.
Shivamogga Superintendent of Police G.K. Mithun Kumar on December 30 informed the media that in November, the police booked 82 cases. Among them, 74 cases were related to the consumption of ganja and there were 76 accused persons. Besides that, eight more cases were registered against 12 persons on charges of ganja sale and cultivation. The police recovered 4.5 kg of ganja and 26 gm of MDMA worth over ₹4.91 lakh that month.
Similarly, in December, the police registered 95 cases. Of them, 86 cases were related to consumption of ganja and nine cases were related to the supply and sale of the drug. The police recovered nearly 9 kg of ganja, worth over ₹4.5 lakh.
The police have intensified the drive to stop the consumption and sale of ganja, following reports of an increase in ganja consumption in the district.

title: Youth murdered in Shivamogga
summary: A 26-year-old man was murdered in Shivamogga, allegedly by relatives, amid suspected family disputes.
content:
A man was found murdered, allegedly by his relatives, at Vinoba Nagar in Shivamogga on December 29. The police identified the deceased as Arun, 26, a resident of Kashipura in the city.
Two accused hit him with lethal weapons near the vegetable market in Vinoba Nagar. The police rushed to the spot after learning about the incident and shifted him to the hospital, where he was declared dead. He is survived by his wife and child.
The police suspected it to be a murder over differences among relatives.  Shivamogga Superintendent of Police G.K. Mithun Kumar told the media that two people had been taken into custody for questioning.

title: ED flags ₹2,883-crore liquor scam in Chhattisgarh involving bureaucrats and politicians
summary: ED uncovers ₹2,883 crore liquor scam in Chhattisgarh, implicating bureaucrats and politicians in extensive corruption and illegal activities.
content:
The Enforcement Directorate (ED), in its supplementary prosecution complaint, has detailed what it described as a “massive corruption” in the Excise Department of Chhattisgarh between 2019 and 2023, allegedly resulting in the generation of Proceeds of Crime worth about ₹2,883 crore.
The agency has named 59 new accused persons, taking the total number of accused in the case to 81.
According to the ED, its investigation has uncovered a well-organised criminal syndicate that subverted the State’s liquor policy for personal gain through a multi-layered mechanism involving illegal commissions and the sale of unaccounted liquor.
The syndicate allegedly generated illegal earnings through four distinct channels. “Bribes were charged from liquor suppliers on official sales, facilitated by artificially increasing the ‘landing price’ paid by the State, effectively financing the bribes through the State exchequer,” the agency said.
Another method involved a parallel system to sell “off-the-books” country liquor through government shops using duplicate holograms and bottles procured in cash, bypassing excise duties and taxes. Annual bribes were also allegedly paid by distillers to maintain market share and secure operational licences in the State.
“A new licence category was introduced to extort commissions from foreign liquor manufacturers, with 60% of profits diverted to the syndicate,” the agency said.
Alleging a deep-rooted conspiracy across the then State’s administrative and political hierarchy, the ED said those arraigned in the latest complaint include senior bureaucrats such as retired Indian Administrative Service (IAS) officer Anil Tuteja, then Joint Secretary, and IAS officer Niranjan Das, then Excise Commissioner. They were allegedly instrumental in manipulating the policy and ensuring the syndicate’s unhindered operation.
Arun Pati Tripathi, Indian Trade Service officer and Managing Director of the Chhattisgarh State Marketing Corporation Limited, was allegedly tasked with maximising illegal collections and coordinating “off-the-books” country liquor sales.
“Additionally, 30 field-level excise officers, including Janardan Kaurav and Iqbal Ahmed Khan, were arraigned as accused for facilitating the sale of unaccounted liquor in exchange for fixed per-case commissions,” the ED said.
The political executives named in the case include “high-ranking political figures, including then Excise Minister Kawasi Lakhma and Chaitanya Baghel (son of the then Chief Minister)”, for their alleged role in granting policy approvals and acquiring or using proceeds of crime in business and real estate ventures. Saumya Chaurasia, then Deputy Secretary in the Chief Minister’s Office, was allegedly identified as a key coordinator for handling illicit cash and managing the placement of compliant officers.
The syndicate was allegedly spearheaded by Anwar Dhebar and his associate Arvind Singh. Private manufacturers, including Chhattisgarh Distilleries Limited, Bhatia Wine Merchants and Welcome Distilleries, were alleged to have knowingly participated in the illegal manufacture of liquor and payment of commissions.
“Facilitators such as Siddharth Singhania (cash collection) and Vidhu Gupta (duplicate hologram supply) were also found to be key private actors in the said fraud,” the agency said.
The ED has so far arrested nine individuals, including Anil Tuteja, Arvind Singh, Trilok Singh Dhillon, Anwar Dhebar, Arun Pati Tripathi, Kawasi Lakhma, Chaitanya Baghel, Soumya Chaurasia and Niranjan Das.
The total attachment in the case currently stands at ₹382.32 crore. “These attachments include 1,041 properties linked to bureaucrats, politicians and private entities, such as Hotel Vennington Court in Raipur and hundreds of assets belonging to the Dhebar and Baghel families,” the agency said.
The ED has also attached properties worth ₹68.16 crore belonging to Chhattisgarh Distilleries, Bhatia Wine Merchants and Welcome Distilleries, taking the cumulative attachment against the three distillers to ₹96.55 crore.
The agency alleged that the syndicate increased the “landing rates” or procurement prices paid by the government to these distilleries. In return, the distillers allegedly paid illegal commissions ranging from ₹75 to ₹125 per case.
Between April 2019 and June 2022, around 60,50,950 cases of “off-the-book” liquor were allegedly supplied to the syndicate.
The ED has also attached assets worth about ₹38.21 crore belonging to Niranjan Das and 30 other excise officials.
The investigation under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act is based on a First Information Report registered by the Raipur Anti-Corruption Branch.

title: Shivamogga Youth Congress activists urge CM for a law against ‘honour killings’
summary: Shivamogga Youth Congress urges CM to enact strict laws against honour killings, highlighting recent tragic incidents and caste-based violence.
content:
The Shivamogga city unit of the Youth Congress demanded that the State government bring in a strict law to stop honour killings in the State. Representatives of the forum submitted a memorandum addressed to the Chief Minister, to the Deputy Commissioner’s office in the city on December 30.
The workers said that a recent case reported in Hubballi — a farmer, opposed to his daughter’s choice of a life partner, killed her — was an inhuman act and had made people of civilised society bow their heads in shame. The incident showed how caste-based atrocities are deep-rooted in society. Only by bringing in a stringent law can such crimes be stopped, they argued.
Referring to certain statements online, the workers opined that a section of people, practising the caste system, had been defending the crime. This attitude stresses the need for timely intervention of the ruling government by bringing in laws. The government should encourage inter-caste marriages and ensure protection of couples who marry against the wishes of their families, they said.
The courts also ruled that “honour killings” deserved to be dealt with seriously. So, the Chief Minister should take the recent case seriously and initiate the process to formulate a strict law, the workers stated in the memorandum.
Shivamogga district Congress Committee general secretary K. Ranganath, Youth Congress activists H.P. Girish, Sharath Mariyappa and others were present.

title: Thrissur Mayor unveils vision for a people-centric, future-ready city
summary: Thrissur Mayor Niji Justin outlines a vision for transparent, inclusive governance focused on urban development, women’s safety, and community engagement.
content:
Promising accountable governance rooted in public trust and expectations, Thrissur Mayor Niji Justin has laid out an ambitious road map for the city’s future, unveiling ‘Thrissur@2075 Vision.’
Stressing transparency as the cornerstone of her administration, the Mayor announced at a meet-the-press organised by the Thrissur Press Club on Tuesday that a White Paper detailing the Corporation’s current financial position would be released soon. The focus, she said, would be on comprehensive urban development that balanced infrastructure growth with social responsibility.
As part of long-term planning, Dr. Justin announced a Thrissur development conclave, envisaged as a platform to chart the city’s growth over the next 50 years. The conclave would bring together stakeholders from health care, education, business, finance, youth groups and the media. Urban beautification and sustainable development would be key themes of discussion.
To address the city’s deteriorating road condition, the Mayor said special squads would be formed, involving local councillors and residents’ associations, to ensure time-bound repair of damaged roads through regular field inspections.
To address one of the city’s most pressing issues, she announced plans to establish shelters for stray dogs and to strengthen the Animal Birth Control (ABC) programme. Dogs captured under the scheme would not be released back to the streets, and gaps in the existing system would be addressed.
Public grievance redressal would be strengthened through regular adalats, aimed at resolving citizens’ complaints through continuous and structured interaction.
In the interest of food safety, the Corporation would introduce a grading system for hotels, with emphasis on hygiene, sanitation and clean restroom facilities.
Addressing women-centric infrastructure, the Mayor acknowledged the lack of clean public toilets for women and announced plans to set up well-maintained “pink washrooms” at major public locations across the city.
The Mayor, a health-care professional, said women’s and children’s health care would be a priority area, with awareness programmes, fitness initiatives, open gyms and mental health support systems at the local-body level.
Plans to ease traffic congestion would include developing MG Road as a model road under a fast-track project. Tile works on the road in front of the KSRTC stand would be completed by January 6. Renovation of the Aranattukara Tagore Centenary Hall would also be completed in early January.
Preparations for the Thrissur Pooram would begin in January itself, in coordination with the Devaswoms and the State government, with special emphasis on making the festival more women-friendly.
The Mayor said a 100-day action plan would be finalised after discussions in the newly elected council and implemented with its approval. Public opinion and suggestions, she added, would guide the city’s dream projects, with priority for basic needs such as water supply, lighting, roads, cleanliness, beautification and senior citizens’ welfare. “All projects will be implemented only after collective deliberation with the 56 councillors,” Dr. Justin said, underlining her commitment to participatory governance.
She said steps would be taken, in accordance with the law, to refund the excess tax collected by the previous Corporation council, as promised in the United Democratic Front’s election manifesto. She said the proposal to return the excess tax to the public would first be placed before the council for approval and subsequently submitted to the State government for necessary sanction. The refund process would begin only after government clearance was obtained.
In a symbolic gesture of social commitment, the Mayor announced that she would not accept bouquets or mementos at public functions, urging organisers to instead contribute to the Mayor’s Relief Fund for dialysis and chemotherapy patients.

title: No scarcity of urea in Telangana for Rabi season
summary: Telangana assures farmers of ample urea supply for the Rabi season, with 2.25 lakh MT readily available across the state.
content:
Farmers in Telangana need not worry about the availability of urea during the ongoing Rabi season, as sufficient stocks are in place across the State, according to official sources.
Authorities have confirmed that nearly 2.25 lakh metric tonnes (MT) of urea are currently available with private dealers and government agencies, including cooperative societies and Markfed. The fertilizer is adequately stocked in all 32 districts, ensuring smooth supply for agricultural needs.
The Centre has allocated 10.40 lakh MT of urea to Telangana for the Rabi season. Of this, the State has already received 5.7 lakh MT, slightly exceeding the pro-rata requirement of 5.6 lakh MT scheduled from October. Farmers have so far purchased 3.71 lakh MT during the ongoing season.

title: Medical camp opens for Sabarimala pilgrims in Kumily
summary: A medical camp for Sabarimala pilgrims has opened in Kumily, providing 24-hour healthcare during the Makaravilakku season.
content:
The Kumily grama panchayat has opened a medical camp to provide healthcare facilities for Sabarimala pilgrims during the Makaravilakku season.
The camp, located in the Forest Office building in Kumily town, was inaugurated by Kumily grama panchayat president M.M. Varghese on Tuesday. It will provide allopathy, ayurveda, homoeopathy, and siddha treatments, said Kumily panchayat secretary R. Ashok Kumar.
“The camp will function until the Makaravilakku festival. it will operate 24 hours a day. Thousands of pilgrims use the Kumily route, and this camp will provide significant relief to them,” said Mr. Kumar.
The opening follows a recent directive from Idukki District Collector Dinesan Cheruvat. While the Forest department initially objected to the facility, permission was granted following a meeting on Sunday between Mr. Varghese and Periyar Tiger Reserve (PTR) East Deputy Director P.U. Saju.
Relations between the local body and the Forest department have been strained recently, with the department blocking the installation of temporary toilets for pilgrims at the Sree Dharma Shasta Temple, near Kumily, and seizing equipment intended for the work.
According to sources, after repeated obstructions, the District Collector warned Forest officials that the administration would invoke the Disaster Management Act to ensure the installation of essential medical and sanitation facilities.
Meanwhile, Mr. Varghese sent a letter to the Chief Minister and the Forest Minister stating that the local body is struggling to arrange parking and other essential facilities for Sabarimala pilgrims due to repeated objections from the Forest department.
Recently, the District Collector directed the department to open the Anavachal ground for temporary parking. However, the department blocked the move, claiming that a Supreme Court order prohibits such actions.
Speaking to mediapersons, Mr. Cheruvat. stated that he found no such court orders, and that the department has not provided a copy of any such ruling. “I have sent a letter to the government requesting that parking be allowed on the Anavachal ground during the Makaravilakku season. I hope the government will issue a clear directive to the Forest department regarding this,” said Mr Cheruvat.

title: Sabarimala temple opens for Makaravilakku
summary: Sabarimala temple reopens for Makaravilakku with heightened security and management for the influx of pilgrims.
content:
The Ayyappa temple at Sabarimala opened on Tuesday evening for the Makaravilakku festival season.
Melsanti E.D. Prasad reopened the sanctum sanctorum at 5 p.m., accompanied by Tantri Kandararu Mahesh Mohanaru. This was followed by the opening of the Malikappuram Devi temple. Even before the ceremonial opening, a steady stream of pilgrims, especially from neighbouring States, began their ascent to the temple via Pampa and Pullumedu .’
The temple, which closed after the Mandalam pilgrimage season on December 27, will remain open until January 19. The Makaravilakku festival is scheduled for January 14 and the temple will close for the season on the morning of January 20.
Ahead of the opening, the Fire and Rescue Services carried out a final round of cleaning at the Sannidhanam, Pathinettam Padi, Malikappuram, and the Aravana counters. This followed a large-scale cleanup drive from the Sannidhanam to Appachimedu undertaken earlier by multiple departments.
Security arrangements have been significantly stepped up, with a 1,593 member police force deployed under the leadership of Crime Branch Superintendent of Police M. Krishnan. Key duty points include the sanctum sanctorum, Pathinettam Padi, Valiya Nadapanthal U-turn, Sharamkuthi, Marakoottam, Malikappuram and Pandithavalam.
The Travancore Devaswom Board has also put in place extensive arrangements to manage the expected surge in pilgrim inflow during the festival period.
Meanwhile, tension flared along the traditional forest route from Erumely on Monday evening after devotees were prevented from entering the forest, with officials stating that the path would open only at 7 a.m. on Tuesday. After being kept under restrictions for several hours, pilgrims eventually crossed over, ignoring official instructions.
At Koikkakkavu and Azhuthakkadavu, devotees, frustrated by prolonged waiting, broke through restrictions and continued their journey. Similar scenes unfolded at Perurthodu, another stretch of the traditional route, where protests erupted following disruption to the pilgrimage.
Devotees had earlier blocked the the Perurthodu-Irumbunnikkara road and staged a road blockade, sitting on the road and chanting bhajans. A heated exchange broke out with the police before the situation was brought under control.

title: Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan to inagurate Vibe 4 Wellness campaign on January 1
summary: Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan will inaugurate the Vibe 4 Wellness campaign on January 1 to promote healthy living in Kerala.
content:
Kerala might be the diabetes capital of the country but more alarming is the increase in the new cases of hypertension identified in the State in the health survey screenings using Shylee app, says Health Minister Veena George.
The Health department’s survey puts the prevalence of hypertension in Kerala at 34% and that of diabetes at 24%  among adults above 30 years of age, she added, while addressing mediapersons here on Tuesday.
Data from the India Hypertension Control Initiative, which is being implemented in the State suggests that roughly one-third of the adult  population has hypertension.
However, it is possible that this screening data might have underestimated the total prevalence of hypertension in Kerala, for the ICMR-INDIAB study, which was a population-based epidemiological survey done between 2008-2020, had put the hypertension prevalence rate in Kerala at over 44%.
Ms. George said that the annual health survey done through  the Shylee  app was in its third year and that the consistently high prevalence of risk factors were an indication that the State needed to launch a new campaign that would address all four aspects of healthy living, including  good dietary habits, sleep hygiene, physical activity and self care.
The Vibe 4 Wellness campaign will focus on creating awareness amongst people on what constitutes a healthy, balanced diet, the role of physical activity and how good sleep hygiene is important for one’s physical and mental well being. Awareness programmes are being organised targeting school and college students, youth, elderly, food vloggers, fitness clubs, hotels and clubs too.
It will be formally inaugurated by Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan on January 1. The campaign is expected to draw in 10 lakh people into a new routine of healthy diet and physical activity.
She pointed out that the poor quality of diet was evident from the fact that anaemia prevalence was  high amongst women in Kerala, regardless of their socio-economic status.
Ms. George said that the Janakeeya Arogya Kendras (JAK) or former subcentres were now emerging as popular community-level healthcare delivery points.
In 2025 alone, 34.8 lakh women had attended the women wellness clinics held there, while 30.5 lakh people had attended the NCD clinics.
