The JAK health clubs were helping people get into a routine of physical activity also, with 95.76 lakh people participating in various health-related sessions in 2025.
Ms. George said that the year-long community-level cancer-screening programme initiated on February 4 this year had so far screened over 20 lakh people.
Through the programme, 278 new cases of breast cancer and 90 pre-cancerous stage of breast cancer; 84 new cases of cervical cancer and 218 cases of pre-cancerous cervix; 58 new cases of oral cancer and 28 pre-cancerous stage of oral cancers and 12 new colon cancers had been detected. Early detection through screening has given these people a chance of curing their cancer completely through appropriate treatment, she said.

title: Minister says honour killing accused will face punishment as per law
summary: Minister R.B. Thimmapur assures justice and support for honour killing victims' family, emphasizing social issues beyond legal solutions.
content:
Minister R.B. Thimmapur visited Inam Veerapur village in Dharwad district on Tuesday and met the victims of a recent honour killing.
He met members of the family of Vivekanand Doddamani whose pregnant wife was killed by her family for marrying outside caste and consoled them.
He asked them to live without fear and assured them of protection. He also told them that the accused will face punishment as per law. “It is an unfortunate incident. It should not have happened. But now, we have to forget about it and move forward,” he said.
He said that the victims will be compensated.
He told reporters later that it is a social issue and not just a law and order one.
“All problems cannot be solved by law. We need to address some long-standing social evils like caste discrimination and promote social harmony. The State government will not only strive to provide justice to the victim’s family in this case but also work towards the larger goal of avoiding such incidents in future,” he said.
He visited some of the family members who are undergoing treatment at Vivekananda General Hospital in Hubballi. He told them that the State government will bear the cost of their treatment.
Sri Basava Murthy Madara Channayya Swami, Deputy Commissioner Divya Prabhu G.R.J., Superintendent of Police Gunjan Arya, Zilla Panchayat Chief Executive Officer Bhuvanesh Patil and others were present.

title: Gujarat approves Indian AI Research Organisation at GIFT City
summary: Gujarat approves the Indian AI Research Organisation at GIFT City to enhance AI research through a public-private partnership.
content:
Gujarat Chief Minister Bhupendra Patel on Tuesday (December 30, 2025) granted in-principle approval for the establishment of the Indian AI Research Organisation (IAIRO) to strengthen research and development in artificial intelligence.
The proposed facility will be set up under a public-private partnership (PPP) model through a tripartite collaboration involving the State government, the Central government and the Indian Pharmaceutical Alliance (IPA), according to officials.
The initiative was aimed to accelerate India’s AI ecosystem in line with the vision of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and under the guidance of the Chief Minister, they said.
The IAIRO would be operationalised as a special purpose vehicle (SPV) at GIFT City near Gandhinagar from January 1 and would be registered as a non-profit entity under Section 8 of the Companies Act, 2013.
An estimated budget of about ₹300 crore had been earmarked for the first five years of the project, with the State government, the Centre and the private partner each contributing 33.33%, they said.
The IPA has joined the initiative as the anchor private partner and will contribute ₹25 crore in 2025–26. The alliance comprises around 23 leading pharmaceutical companies, including Cipla, Torrent Pharmaceuticals and Sun Pharma.
The project aligns with the objectives of the India AI Mission of the Union Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, as well as the AI Action Plan of the State government’s Science and Technology Department.
The officials said the State government had also constituted an AI task force to promote sustainable development and improve quality of life through the application of AI in sectors such as healthcare, education and agriculture.
IAIRO is envisioned as a multidisciplinary hub for artificial intelligence, with core activities including advanced research and development, creation of AI-based products and solutions, and fostering collaboration among academic institutions, industry, start-ups and the government.
The organisation will also focus on intellectual property creation, capacity building and policy-oriented research, and will operate under a hybrid compute model integrating on-premise infrastructure.

title: Two-way cultural exchange to anchor Telangana’s tourism vision for 2026
summary: Telangana's tourism vision for 2026 emphasizes a two-way cultural exchange between rural and urban areas to enhance visitor experiences.
content:
Placing a two-way cultural exchange between rural and urban Telangana at the heart of the State’s tourism roadmap, Minister for Tourism and Culture Jupally Krishna Rao on Tuesday (December 30) outlined a strategy aimed at reimagining tourism as a shared cultural experience rather than a one-directional showcase.
Addressing a workshop titledTourism and Its Vision – 2026, organised by the Telangana Tourism Development Corporation (TGTDC) in Hyderabad, the Minister said that Telangana must move decisively towards global benchmarks in hospitality, innovation and visitor experience if it is to emerge as an international tourism destination by 2026.
Explaining the proposed model, the Minister said tourists from within the country and abroad should be introduced to the lifestyles, cuisines and traditions of rural and tribal communities, allowing them to engage with local cultures in a meaningful way. In parallel, rural and tribal populations would be encouraged to experience the State’s urban transformation through guided visits to heritage landmarks and historic sites, along with exposure to metropolitan life, including public transport systems such as the Metro Rail.
“This exchange-driven approach would help bridge social and cultural divides while ensuring that tourism benefits were shared more equitably across regions,” the Minister added.
He also called for the development of a new pool of well-trained, multilingual tourist guides to overcome language barriers and improve visitor interaction.

title: Master plan for town, market renovation top agenda of Angamaly’s new chairperson
summary: Angamaly's new chairperson, Reetha Paul, prioritizes a master plan, market renovation, and town beautification initiatives.
content:
A master plan for the development of the town is among the priorities of Reetha Paul, the newly elected chairperson of Angamaly municipality, though her immediate focus will be to complete the ongoing development works. The Congress leader, who was elevated to the chairperson’s chamber after winning sixth term as a councillor, also said that steps for the beautification of the town will be initiated without delay.
Renovation of the Angamaly market and rectification and maintenance of canals in the local body are also among Ms. Paul’s priorities.
“A master plan on town planning has to be finalised. The lack of a modernised slaughterhouse in the town is a major concern. It will require at least ₹10 crore to build one with all necessary facilities, as per rough estimates. The project requires funding from the government,” she said. She exuded hope that the works on the market could be completed with the local body’s own funds.
The chairperson said efforts to get established ownership rights over 52 cents belonging to the municipality in the town would continue. Once the local body gets the land parcel, steps to construct a municipal town hall there would be initiated, she added.
She said waste management in the municipality has been going on well with biodegradable waste being processed at the source and the Haritha Karma Sena collecting non-biodegradable waste, including plastic. “We have the provision to distribute bio compost bins for around 1,000 families too. If there are households still requiring the bins, we can distribute them. Steps will also be taken to expand the non-biodegradable waste collection facility,” she added. Ms. Paul said more CCTV cameras would be installed in required spots to improve public safety measures. She said other plans would be formulated and finalised as per the requirements of each ward.
Ms. Paul, who represents the Mullassery ward, will be the chairperson for the first two years. She has to vacate the chamber for Independent councillor Luxy Joy for the next two years, as per a power-sharing agreement. The Congress will decide the chairperson for the remaining year. While Wilson Mundadan will be the deputy chairperson for the first three years, another Independent councillor Varghese Vempliath has been promised the post for the remaining two years.

title: Prakasam district sees slight fall in crime rate in 2025
summary: Prakasam district's crime rate fell 6.61% in 2025, attributed to drones, CCTV, and enhanced policing efforts.
content:
Prakasam district witnessed a marginal fall of 6.61 per cent in overall crime rate in 2025. Against the 8,371 cases registered in 2024, the current year witnessed only 7,818 cases. The district also solved several sensational cases during the year.
Addressing a year-end media conference in Ongole on Tuesday, Superintendent of Police (SP) V. Harshavardhan Raju said the year witnessed 1,122 cases on bodily offences, 632 cases on property-related offences, 709 women-related crime, 757 road accidents, 44 cybercrime cases, which were actually much lesser than the number witnessed in 2024.
Mr. Raju said property worth ₹4.44 crore had been recovered of the total ₹8.70 crore-worth stolen property, pegging the recovery rate at an impressive 51.02 per cent. He attributed the fall in crime to the deployment of drones, CCTV cameras and enhanced night beats in sensitive areas.
“129 of the 136 missing girls and 264 out of the 292 missing women were traced, registering an impressive success rate at 94.85 per cent and 90.41 per cent respectively,” Mr. Raju said. The district also recorded details of 3,891 migrant labourers as part of curtailing crime.
Deputy Superintendent (Ongole) R. Srinivasa Rao, Inspector Srinivasa Rao (Special Branch), Deva Prabhakar (DCRB), V. Venkateswarlu (IT core), Vijay Krishna (Taluk PS) were present.

title: Naidu delivering results-driven governance, says TDP Andhra Pradesh president
summary: TDP president Palla Srinivasa Rao praises Naidu for results-driven governance and announces grassroots outreach on welfare schemes.
content:
Reaffirming that governance must be judged by outcomes rather than slogans, Telugu Desam Party (TDP) State president Palla Srinivasa Rao said Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu was delivering results-driven administration anchored in accountability and performance. Since assuming office, he noted, the NDA coalition government had been translating its promises into action, restoring public trust and stability in governance.
Addressing party leaders and cadres, Mr. Srinivasa Rao urged them to actively communicate the government’s achievements at the grassroots level. As per the Chief Minister’s directions, the ‘Prajala Sevalo Prabhutvam’ (Government at the Service of the People) outreach programme will be held on December 31 and January 1, with party functionaries visiting households to explain welfare initiatives, policy outcomes and benefits in a festive spirit.
Contrasting the present administration with the previous regime, he said Andhra Pradesh had suffered five years of fiscal stress, institutional decline and stalled development. Under Mr. Naidu’s leadership, the State had, he said, decisively moved from disruption to development, reviving investor confidence and mobilising ₹25 lakh crore in investments, laying the foundation for 26 lakh jobs.
Mr. Srinivasa Rao highlighted the ‘Super Six’ welfare initiatives, with nearly ₹70,000 crore committed, including ₹51,000 crore towards pensions. Welfare and development, he stressed, were being pursued together, ensuring inclusive growth while strengthening the State’s economic future.

title: Himachal apple growers oppose reduced import duty on New Zealand apples
summary: Himachal apple growers seek intervention against reduced import duties on New Zealand apples, fearing severe impacts on their livelihoods.
content:
Apple growers inHimachal Pradeshfear that the Centre’s proposal to slash the import duty on New Zealand apples from 50% to 25% following a trade deal will severely impact their livelihoods and have sought Governor Shiv Pratap Shukla’s “intervention to safeguard livelihoods”.
In a memorandum submitted to the Governor on Tuesday (December 30, 2025), a group of apple growers led by Kuldeep Singh Rathore, the Congress MLA from Theog constituency in Shimla district, has raised concerns about the proposed reduction in import duty from 2026-27.
Mr. Rathore said the reduced duty will cause a significant loss of market share for Indian apples and bring down prices, pushing apple growers – struggling with climate change-induced uncertainties, rising input costs, labour shortages, and shrinking margins – into deep economic distress.
The leader said that the apple industry forms the “backbone of Himachal Pradesh’s rural economy” and contributes approximately ₹5,500 crore annually and supports over 1.5 lakh families, most of whom are small and marginal farmers. “The State produces around 6.5 lakh metric tonnes of apples every year, accounting for nearly 25% of India’s total apple production. With average landholdings of only one to two acres and limited scope for diversification due to the hilly terrain, apple cultivation remains the primary source of livelihood for these farmers,” he said.
Mr. Rathore said implementation of the FTA in its “present form” will set a “dangerous precedent”. “Other major apple-exporting nations such as the U.S., Chile, and Italy which together account for over 40% of global apple exports are likely to demand similar concessions, which will be disastrous to farmer community of Himachal Pradesh,” he said.
“We also urge the Government of India to restore the import duty on apples to 100% as a necessary protective measure for domestic growers and reconsider the complete elimination of import duty on kiwi fruit under the proposed FTA with New Zealand,” he added.

title: P. Vishwanathan scripts history for the Paniya tribe
summary: P. Vishwanathan, first Paniya tribal Chairman of Kalpetta Municipality, vows to improve conditions for his community and promote development.
content:
P. Vishwanathan, a watchman by profession and a folk singer by passion, now has an entirely new address and role. The 40-year-old from the Kurunthan Unnathi (tribal colony) at Edaguni has been elected Chairman of the Kalpetta Municipality in Wayanad. Incidentally, he is the first person from the Paniya tribal community in the country to reach such a position.
Mr. Vishwanathan contested the recent local body elections from the Edaguni ward of the Kalpetta municipality. Though it was a general ward, he won by a margin of 196 votes — the highest in the municipality — and was later chosen as Chairman by the ruling Left Democratic Front (LDF), as the post was reserved for Scheduled Tribes.
Until the day he assumed charge as Chairman, Mr. Vishwanathan had been working as a watchman at the Civil Station branch of the Kalpetta Service Cooperative Bank. A known folk singer, he is part of the Karinthandan folk music group and also serves as the district president of the Adivasi Kshema Samithi (AKS). He entered politics through the Democratic Youth Federation of India in 2013 and became a councillor in the municipality in 2015.
The new Chairman is the son of Radha and Kili and hails from the Kurunthan Unnathi, which consists of just four huts with tin sheets and tarpaulin roofs, housing seven families. In his new position, Mr. Vishwanathan has vowed to bring about a change in this situation. “There are more than 56 unnathis in Kalpetta. I wish at least one of them could be modernised with the support of the State government,” he said.
Paniyas are the largest tribal community in the State. Other tribal communities in Wayanad include the Kattunaikkar, Adiya, Kuruma, Kurichya and Oorali. Mr. Vishwanathan said he aims to understand the distinct features of each tribe and unnathi before designing development projects for them. He also pointed out that funds earmarked for tribal welfare often fail to make a significant impact due to the lack of foresight on the part of implementing agencies.
The Chairman also hopes to facilitate the comprehensive development of Kalpetta, including the construction of a town hall and welfare initiatives, particularly for senior citizens. His family includes his wife Sunitha and children Vaishnav Das and Vaishnavi.

title: At peace meeting, Inam Veerapur elders say honour killing unfortunate
summary: Elders in Inam Veerapur condemn honour killing, promoting harmony and support for victims amidst community tensions.
content:
District administration officials convened a peace committee meeting in Inam Veerapur village near Hubballi on Monday, where in a case of honour killing a pregnant woman was killed by her family for marrying outside caste recently.
A team led by Deputy Commissioner Divya Prabhu G.R.J, Superintendent of Police Gunjan Arya and Social Welfare officers met the village elders.
The leaders agreed to forget the past and live in harmony in future. Members of the Doddamani family who suffered caste discrimination and attacks recently will be welcomed into the village and allowed to live in peace.
“People of various communities, including Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, Lingayat, Veerashaiva, Muslim, Kuruba, and others have been living in harmony for centuries. This was one unfortunate incident. We will not treat this as a problem facing the village. Let the law take its own course,” they said.
They also urged the Deputy Commissioner to take up some pending development works in the village.
The Deputy Commissioner said that the State government will provide due compensation, livelihood support and legal aid to the victims. She said that the State government will protect families from the deprived communities. Police will ensure victim and witness protection, she added.
She urged leaders to work together to ensure that such incidents do not recur.
Mr. Arya said that there is a need to live in harmony and follow the rule of law. He said that all stakeholders have to work to ensure that the victims gain enough confidence to live in peace.
The police will provide complete protection to the village, he said. “The victim’s family needs support at this crucial juncture. All of us need to stand with them,” he added.
At one point, there was an argument between two groups. But the police and senior officers pacified them.
Leaders of various associations Suresh Khanapur, Premnath Chikkatumbal, Paramesh Kale, Chandrashekar Yadger, Sridhar Kandagal, Kenchappa Mallammanavar, Shankargouda Patil, Gurusiddaiah Hiremath, Lalita Madli, Basavaraj Walikar, Renuka Huilgol, Shivanand Manakwad, Hanumant Walikar, Shivanand Mekar, Ramesh Madar and others spoke.
Officials of various departments were present.

title: FemiRides transforms women’s mobility and safety
summary: FemiRides empowers women through a safe mobility platform, offering driving training and job opportunities since 2020.
content:
At a time when concerns about women’s safety in public transport continue to dominate the urban discourse, FemiRides—a women-for-women mobility platform founded by Behara Vijaya Radhika—is quietly reshaping how women travel while also creating opportunities for them to earn.
The idea behind FemiRides took shape in 2020, Ms. Radhika said, adding, “Women must not only feel safe, but also should be in control of their journeys. Driving is more than a skill, it is freedom, dignity, and livelihood.”
The initiative began on a small scale with just one female driver. “Initially, not many women showed interest due to lack of female instructors. Eventually, a 50-year-old woman came forward and received training. That single step became a turning point, and today over 500 women have learned to drive, supported by a growing team of 50 trained women instructors,” Ms. Radhika said.
However, Ms. Radhika soon realised that long-term plan required training more women, not merely employing them. She registered a women’s driving programme under an ITDA project that was initially approved, only to be withdrawn following a change in the government. Despite the financial setback, she persisted, registering a driving school, starting with one vehicle and gradually expanding to five.
The early years from 2021 to 2024 were marked by resistance, resource constraints, and repeated setbacks. Nevertheless, the platform attracted women from diverse backgrounds, including ASHA workers and Anganwadi teachers, who first joined as learners and later became earners. “Feedback prompted me to replace the male instructor with a female instructor. The first such instructor was hired at ₹25,000 per month. Soon, women began training others, creating a cycle of empowerment,” she said.
In 2023, FemiRides was formally incorporated and launched operations by October. The two-wheeler training and ride service quickly gained traction, enabling women to commute and work independently. Today, the platform offers multiple services, including ride booking, driving school, women driver hire, trips, and tours, and has trained over 500 women. FemiRides operates a fleet of more than 15 cars (including electric vehicles), 60 bikes, and 10 autorickshaws.
She said the safety protocols include GPS monitoring, Aadhaar verification, basic vehicle mechanics training, and continuous ride tracking. Services extend beyond Visakhapatnam and they can also be engaged for longer travel to places such as Hyderabad, Vijayawada, Araku, and Srikakulam. The initiative has partnered with Coromandel, Infosys for CSR-driven training programmes.
Ms. Radhika, with the slogan“Restart. Rebuild. Reset”, said that franchises are planned across Andhra Pradesh, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, and Chhattisgarh, and that two dedicated apps are under development.
(The author Gouthami Paltati is an intern with The Hindu)

title: A.P. Backward Classes Commission seeks objections on proposal to group Goud, Gammalla, Kalali and Goundla communities
summary: A.P. Backward Classes Commission invites objections from Gammalla, Kalali, and Goundla communities on proposed grouping with Goud.
content:
Members of the Goud (Gammalla), Kalali and Goundla communities have submitted a representation to the Andhra Pradesh Backward Classes Commission seeking that these communities be brought under a single nomenclature, “Goud/Gowda”, and that caste verification certificates be issued accordingly.
Following the request, the Commission convened a meeting on December 3, 2025, with representatives of the Goud or Gowda communities to hear their submissions. However, the Commission observed that no representatives from the Gammalla, Kalali or Goundla communities, either individually or through recognised caste associations, attended the meeting to present their views.
In view of the absence of these communities and to ensure a transparent and inclusive process, the Commission has invited objections or comments from members of the Gammalla, Kalali and Goundla communities on the proposed grouping. Objections, if any, should be submitted in writing to the Andhra Pradesh Backward Classes Commission, Flat No. 48, 6th Cross Road, Municipal Employees Colony, Vijayawada, on or before January 6, 2026.
The announcement was issued by the Commission’s Member Secretary, S. Tanuja Rani, who said the exercise was aimed at eliciting the views of all concerned sections before any decision is taken on the proposal.

title: Minister writes to Centre requesting temporary toll exemption during Sankranti
summary: Minister writes to Centre requesting temporary toll exemption during Sankranti
content:
With lakhs of people expected to travel during the upcoming Sankranti festival, the Telangana government has put in place an extensive action plan to ensure smooth traffic movement on national highways, particularly the busy Hyderabad–Vijayawada corridor.
Roads and Buildings Minister Komatireddy Venkat Reddy chaired a high-level review meeting at Dr B.R. Ambedkar State Secretariat to finalise preventive measures, keeping in view past experiences of severe traffic congestion.
Addressing officials, the  Minister directed that all departments must be on duty for three days before and three days after the festival, and heavy vehicles should be restricted from using highways during peak festive travel days.
A special incident management and control room will be set up, with 108 ambulances, medical teams, revenue officials, police, R&B and NHAI staff placed on continuous alert.
Mr Venkat Reddy announced that he would personally monitor the situation by touring the highways on a motorcycle and conduct field inspections at critical congestion points such as Toopranpet and Abdullapurmet.
He instructed officials to ensure that there are no hour-long traffic snarls on the Hyderabad–Vijayawada highway, which witnesses nearly one lakh vehicle movements per day during the festival season.
The Minister also revealed that he has written to Union Road Transport and Highways Minister Nitin Gadkari, requesting temporary toll exemption during Sankranti, as lakhs of people would be travelling during the festival and also for the Medaram Jatara. He said he was prepared to meet the Union Minister personally, if required.
“If necessary, the R&B Department is ready to make nominal payments at toll plazas to ensure free flow of traffic,” he said.
Officials were instructed to halt lane closures, road works involving heavy machinery and construction activity during peak festive days, and to carry out unavoidable works only at night when traffic is minimal.
Special attention will be paid to congestion-prone stretches such as LB Nagar–Vanasthalipuram, Panama Godown, Hayathnagar, Ramoji Film City, and areas like Choutuppal, Narketpally, Kattangur, Peddakaparthy, Gundrampally and Tekumatla.
The review meeting was attended by R&B Special Chief Secretary Vikas Raj, Yadadri-Bhuvanagiri Collector Hanumanth Rao, Nalgonda Collector Ila Tripathi among others.

title: CM gives directions for development of TCUR
summary: CM A. Revanth Reddy directs GHMC zonal commissioners to enhance sanitation and develop Telangana Core Urban Region with a five-year plan.
content:
Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy put the onus of maintaining the city’s sanitation on the newly designated 12 zonal commissioners of the Greater Hyderabad Municipal Corporation and asked them to be on the field every day to monitor their designated areas.
In a review meeting with higher officials of the GHMC on Tuesday, the Chief Minister sought to lay out a road map for the zonal commissioners towards planned development of the Telangana Core Urban Region. He asked the corporation to formulate a five-year action plan towards development of the newly-expanded GHMC area.
He said the most difficult task before them was the waste management in the city, and directed them to conduct sanitation special drives regularly, once every 10 days.
CCTV cameras should be installed at lakes, drains and locations where garbage is dumped illegally. The roads should be clear of waste, he said, and informed them about the government’s decision to completely eradicate plastic [single use] from the TCUR region. He asked the GHMC, HYDRAA and water board to begin de-silting of storm water drains and sewage network from January.
Speaking about comprehensive measures for pollution control within the city, Mr. Revanth Reddy said a decision has been made to enforce Electrical Vehicles in the TCUR area instead of diesel buses and autos. He directed the officials to use technology to induce transparency into services such as issue of birth and death certificates, trade licences and others. He asked the officials to ensure that the city has adequate number of streetlights and be in contact with the colony and residential welfare associations.
Special chief secretary of the Metropolitan Area & Urban Development will act as the coordinating authority among various civic wings, he informed.
He issued directions with regard to vector control and disease prevention, and speedy grievance redressal in the city.

title: Left parties condemn police curbs ahead of SEZ hearing
summary: Left parties condemn police restrictions ahead of SEZ hearing, alleging suppression of opposition voices on proposed ethanol factories in Nellore.
content:
Left parties on Tuesday strongly condemned police detentions and restrictions in Nellore district, alleging that the government was attempting to suppress public opinion ahead of a public hearing on the proposed ethanol factories at the IFFCO Kisan SEZ in Racharlapadu village of Kodavalur mandal.
In a joint statement, the leaders said that police action was aimed at preventing opposition voices from participating in the public hearing on projects that could have serious implications for agriculture, the environment and local livelihoods.
The statement was issued by V. Srinivas Rao of the CPI(M), G. Eswaraiah of the CPI, P. Prasad of CPI(ML) New Democracy, Jasti Kishore Babu of CPI(ML), Katam Nagabhushanam of MCPI(U), B. Bangara Rao of CPI(ML) Liberation, M. Ramakrishna of CPI(ML) New Democracy, B. S. Amarnath of SUCI(C), P. V. Sundararamaraju of the Forward Bloc and Janaki Ramulu of the Revolutionary Socialist Party.
They alleged that leaders of various Left parties were either arrested or placed under house arrest while proceeding to attend the public hearing. Those detained included CPI(M) district secretary Moolam Ramesh, Y. Mohan Rao, Mooli Vengayya and T. Gopal; CPI(ML) New Democracy leaders Sagar, Lakshmireddy and Y. Ramakrishna; SUCI(C) leader Basavaraju; BSP leader M. Bati Srinivasulu; Forward Bloc leader P. V. Sundararamaraju; Revolutionary Socialist Party leader Janaki Ramulu; and CPI(ML) Liberation leader B. Bangara Rao. Others attempting to reach the venue were detained at the Kovur police station.
The Left parties said land had been acquired from farmers nearly 25 years ago for the Kisan SEZ, but no meaningful development had taken place so far. They alleged that the government was now seeking to permit chemical and ethanol-based industries in the area, which would adversely affect agriculture, the environment and the livelihoods of local residents.
Terming the police action authoritarian and undemocratic, the parties demanded the immediate release of all detained leaders, withdrawal of house arrests, and the conduct of the public hearing in a free, lawful and democratic manner. They also urged the government to withdraw its proposal to allow polluting industries in the region.

title: Tenant arrested for murdering elderly woman and dumping her body in Godavari
summary: Tenant arrested for murdering his landlady and dumping her body in the Godavari river for theft in Hyderabad.
content:
A 33-year-old man was arrested by the Nacharam police for murdering his landlady and disposing her body in the Godavari river, turning a missing case into a murder-for-gain case within days of its registration.
The accused, Maddhu Anji Babu alias Anji, was apprehended at Poduladda Junction in Razole mandal of Konaseema district in Andhra Pradesh. He is accused of murdering 65-year-old Suredde Sujatha at her house in Baba Nagar, Mallapur, on December 19, 2025. The case was registered at Nacharam police station on December 28.
According to the police, Anji Babu, who had taken a portion of the victim’s house on rent about two months ago, strangled her to death with the intention of stealing valuables. He stole gold ornaments and, with the help of his associates Durga Rao and Yuva Raj, disposed of her body in Godavari river in the Konaseema region.
Following the arrest, the police recovered stolen gold jewellery, including four bangles, a gold chain and two gold ear-studs, along with mobile phones  and other incriminating material.
Investigations revealed that the victim was living alone and that the accused came to know that she possessed gold ornaments and cash, which prompted him to hatch a plan to kill her. Police said there was no prior relationship between the two apart from the recent tenancy arrangement.

title: Railways to develop stations in Ernakulam to boost train handling capacity
summary: Southern Railway plans to enhance Ernakulam terminals, expanding capacity and facilities to improve passenger and freight services.
content:
The Southern Railway will undertake the phase-two redevelopment of the three major railway stations in Ernakulam shortly. The Railways have decided to develop terminals in three cities, including Ernakulam, Coimbatore, and Chennai, as part of the Railways’ vision to boost the train handling capacity of terminals in major cities across the country. As part of this, the terminal redevelopment works are under way at the  Ernakulam Junction, Ernakulam Town and Thripunithura stations, which together handle a substantial share of passenger and freight traffic in Kerala.
The major works under the initiative include expanding the existing terminals with additional platforms, stabling lines, pit lines, and adequate shunting facilities, identifying and creating new terminals in and around urban areas, and setting up maintenance facilities, including mega coaching complexes. The project also covers increasing sectional capacity through traffic facility works, upgrading signalling systems, and adding multitracking at various points to handle the increased number of trains.
Redevelopment of Ernakulam Town Railway Station is planned in two phases at a total cost of ₹150.28 crore, with phasing designed to ensure uninterrupted passenger operations during construction. Phase I is under way in the southern part of the station area. Existing facilities such as staff quarters, parcel office, duty station master room, and substation and OFC rooms, were relocated to facilitate execution.
Structural works have already been completed, including those for the west terminal building, while finishing works are in progress. Major components of Phase I include multilevel car parking for 200 cars, fire protection, painting and finishing works, a 12-metre-wide foot overbridge, and platform development. The first phase is expected to be commissioned by May 2026. This will be followed by the second phase of work. The retendering for the Ernakulam Junction redevelopment project has been completed, and work will commence shortly. Thripunithura Amrit Bharat Station redevelopment works are in the final phase, according to a statement from the Railways.

title: A.P. raises ₹4,000 crore through open market borrowings
summary: Andhra Pradesh raises ₹4,000 crore in open market borrowings, totaling ₹86,000 crore for the year to meet fiscal commitments.
content:
The Andhra Pradesh government has raised an additional ₹4,000 crore through open market borrowings (OMB) at the close of the calendar year,  to meet expenditure and cash flow requirements. The borrowing was conducted through the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) through the auction of the State securities.
With this latest tranche, the total open market borrowings mobilised by the State during the current calendar year have crossed ₹86,000 crore. The year-end borrowing was necessitated by routine fiscal commitments, including welfare disbursements, infrastructure spending, and settlement of pending bills. Officials say that the borrowing exercise was undertaken strictly in accordance with RBI norms and within the limits approved for the State.
Data on the State’s borrowing pattern reveal a steady and sustained reliance on monthly securities auctions. The government has been raising funds through RBI-conducted auctions almost every month, with borrowings not falling below ₹1,000 crore in any given month. In May, the State raised ₹7,000 crore, the highest monthly borrowing during the year. This was followed by significant borrowings in June, including a ₹6,000 crore tranche and another ₹5,550 crore raised in the same month. Borrowings remained elevated in the latter half of the year as well, touching ₹5,000 crore each in August and September.
Officials noted that recourse to market borrowings typically intensifies towards the end of the financial and calendar year, when expenditure peaks. They said the funds raised would help ensure uninterrupted implementation of government programmes and timely payments to contractors, beneficiaries and departments.
Officials attributed the higher borrowings during these months to increased expenditure commitments arising from welfare schemes, development works and the clearance of accumulated liabilities. Monthly securities auctions, they said, have become a routine feature of State finances amid rising obligations.
The government has emphasised that it is following a calibrated approach to debt management, balancing developmental priorities with fiscal prudence. Officials also pointed out that the borrowings are being structured across different tenures to manage repayment pressures.
According to official sources, the maturity period of these market borrowings ranges from six to 16 years, with some securities carrying repayment obligations extending up to 2046.
While longer-tenure instruments help spread repayments over time and ease immediate fiscal stress, they also commit future governments to servicing debt for decades. With a significant portion of the ₹86,000 crore raised this year falling into the medium- and long-term category, Andhra Pradesh’s long-term debt profile has come under close scrutiny.
The scale and frequency of borrowings have drawn attention from fiscal analysts and financial institutions monitoring the State’s debt sustainability. Officials, however, maintain that all borrowings are within approved limits and remain essential to maintaining administrative continuity and funding key development and welfare initiatives.

title: MGU presents its annual Budget
summary: MGU's 2026-27 budget emphasizes skill-based education, AI research, and innovative programs to enhance entrepreneurship and collaboration.
content:
The annual Budget for Mahatma Gandhi University (MGU) for 2026-27 places a heightened focus on skill-based education and entrepreneurship.
The Budget, presented recently by P. Harikrishnan, convener of the finance subcommittee of the Syndicate, envisages a revenue of ₹658.7 crore, an expenditure of ₹685.7 crore, and a deficit of ₹27 crore.
According to MGU Vice-Chancellor C. T. Aravindakumar, the Budget aims to identify research ideas aligned with industrial needs and to facilitate the development of innovative technologies. Dedicated research centres will be established to explore the potential of artificial intelligence (AI), with scope for collaboration with other universities, government agencies and industry partners. A special fund will also be earmarked for enterprises that leverage AI.
The university has also initiated steps to establish the State’s first Constituent College, subject to government approval. Plans are in place to integrate high-quality teaching and research and to introduce emerging areas of knowledge. The Budget offers a proposal to establish a community radio station under the University.
An international 3D printing and bioprinting centre will be set up at the university to support research advancements in tissue engineering, regenerative medicine and life sciences.
The Budget also envisages conducting a feasibility study in collaboration with the Indian Institute of Space Science and Technology (IIST) to explore the possibility of a satellite launch programme. Joint degree programmes will be launched in collaboration with national and international universities. In anticipation of the phasing out of the affiliation system, international schools will be established to offer globally relevant and contemporary programmes and curricula.
To enable students enrolled in the four-year undergraduate programmes to demonstrate competencies through hands-on training and to promote skill oriented learning, the Budget proposes the development of micro-industrial production units within the university campus.
In addition, MGU plans to collaborate with start-ups on a company model to commercialise the expertise of its IT department by converting it into software products, thereby generating revenue.

title: West Godavari district saw 19% drop in crime due to enhanced measures, says SP
summary: West Godavari district experiences a 19% crime reduction thanks to increased surveillance and advanced policing measures, reports SP.
content:
The police have installed 3,742 CCTVs in West Godavari district to prevent crimes, and drones were pressed into service to keep a tab on anti-social elements and maintain surveillance at open and abandoned places, said Superintendent of Police Adnan Nayeem Asmi at the annual press conference here on Tuesday (December 30, 2025).
Due to efficient policing and the use of technology, overall crime in the district dropped by 19.03 percent. About 32 critical cases were solved using footage from 3,742 CCTVs and drones, the SP said.
Mr. Nayeem Asmi said that the police have registered 5,076 cases in 2025, as against 6,269 cases in the previous years. Crime rate was declined due to preventive measures to check crimes and regular enforcement, the SP added.
There were no murder for gain cases and the property offences, including thefts and house burglaries, have come down 516 in 2025 from 698 last year (26 per cent drop), and rioting cases fell to two this year from 13 in 2024.
In cybercrime cases, police froze ₹96.92 lakh and refunded about ₹42 lakh to the victims. A 13-member cyber fraudsters gang, who threatened a retired professor in Bhimavaram and looted ₹78 lakh, was busted. Police recovered ₹42 lakh and froze ₹19.90 lakh in the case, the SP said.
Regarding Narcotic and Drugs Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act, 1985, police arrested 60 ganja peddlers and consumers in West Godavari district, and destroyed 1,236 kg of ganja.
Cases related to crime against women dropped to 697 in 2025, as against 763 cases last year (9 per cent decline) and the police registered 33 SC and ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act cases, which were 72 last year (54 per cent drop), Md. Nayeem Asmi said.
Construction of SP Camp Office, Tanuku Rural, and Town police station was taken up at a cost of ₹9.49 crore. Regarding welfare of police personnel, medical tests, worth ₹8.90 lakh were conducted on 1,272 force in the district.
In 2026, plans are afoot to impart training to the police officers on AI-based investigation techniques to prevent and detect crimes, the SP said.
Additional SP V. Bheema Rao, Dy. SPs M.V.V. Satyanarayana, Raghuveer Vishnu, G. Sriveda, D. Viswanadh and other officers were present.

title: Uttam refutes Harish’s allegations
summary: Uttam refutes Harish’s allegations
content:
Irrigation Minister N. Uttam Kumar Reddy refuted the allegations made by BRS MLA and former Irrigation Minister T. Harish Rao regarding Polavaram-Nallamala Sagar project, asserting that the State government is seriously pursuing the matter and exploring all possible options, including legal remedies, to stall the project.
In a statement, the minister said the Telangana government had already filed a writ petition in the Supreme Court against Andhra Pradesh in this regard. “The writ petition filed by the Telangana government is WP No. 1258 and is listed on Monday, January 5, before the Chief Justice of India in Court No. 1 as Item No. 11. This clearly shows that the Telangana government is aggressively fighting the Polavaram–Banakacherla/Nallamala Sagar project. What Harish Rao stated to the press is completely false,” said the Minister.
It may be recalled that Telangana approached the Supreme Court on December 16, seeking to restrain Andhra Pradesh from proceeding with the Polavaram–Nallamala Sagar Link Project (PNLP), through which the neighbouring State proposes to divert 200 tmc ft of water from the Godavari to the Krishna basin. In its writ petition, Telangana sought directions to restrain Andhra Pradesh and its agencies from preparing a detailed project report (DPR) and executing the project.

title: Sexual assault of minor: accused awarded 65 years of RI and fine
summary: A Kodungalloor court sentenced a man to 65 years in prison for sexually assaulting a minor girl, plus a fine.
content:
In a case of sexual assault of a minor girl, a special fast-track POCSO court in Kodungalloor has sentenced the accused to a total of 65 years of rigorous imprisonment under various sections, along with a fine of ₹1,35,000.
The accused, Jishnu, 28, of Kodungalloor, was convicted and sentenced by special POCSO court Judge V. Vinitha. The court ordered that the fine amount, once recovered, be paid to the survivor as compensation. In case of default in payment of fine, the accused will have to undergo more than 10 additional years of rigorous imprisonment.
According to the prosecution, the accused, with the intent to sexually assault the girl who was below 15 years of age, lured her by feigning romantic interest and subjected her to repeated sexual abuse. The incident came to light after the survivor disclosed the abuse to her family, following which a complaint was lodged with the Mathilakam police.
The investigation was jointly conducted by the then Station House Officer T. K. Shaiju and Sub-Inspector Lalson, who subsequently filed the chargesheet before the court. The prosecution was represented by Special Public Prosecutor Sulal K.S.

title: Traffic snarls on Ghat Road: Cong. MLAs from Wayanad launch ‘satyagraha’
summary: Congress MLAs from Wayanad protest traffic issues on Ghat Road, demanding urgent solutions for ongoing congestion and road repairs.
content:
Two Congress MLAs from Wayanad launched a day-and-night ‘satyagraha’ outside the district collectorate here on Tuesday evening (December 30) seeking a solution to the recurring traffic snarls on the Thamarassery Ghat Road connecting Kozhikode and Wayanad districts.
Meanwhile, the district administration has placed restrictions on the movement of multi-axle vehicles and heavy vehicles on the road from January 5 in view of the ongoing road repair works and for clearing wooden logs on the sixth, seventh, and eighth hairpin bends. A release from the Executive Engineer, National Highway Division, Public Works department, said that such vehicles would be diverted via the Kuttiyadi mountain pass or the Nadugani mountain pass.
Traffic block has become a regular affair on the Ghat Road in recent days, and the situation is worsened by the rush of vehicles due to the Christmas-New Year holidays. The road comes under the Kozhikode district administration. Social critic M.N. Karassery opened the day-and-night ‘satyagraha’ by T. Siddique, Kalpetta MLA, and I.C. Balakrishnan, Sulthan Bathery MLA.
Addressing the media earlier, Mr. Siddique claimed that he had got stuck on the road at least 34 times in the past few years. The Congress leader claimed that there had been occasions when he had to go to Thrissur to catch a train to Thiruvananthapuram to attend the Assembly session, as he missed the train from Kozhikode.
“The traffic block is affecting the social life of the people of Wayanad as well as its development. We all know that Wayanad has no air, rail, or sea connectivity. Road connectivity is the district’s only link to the outside world,” Mr. Siddique said. He alleged that though decisions had been taken even at the level of the Additional Chief Secretary to address the traffic block on the road and the Kerala State Human Rights Commission had issued orders for the purpose, nothing was happening on the ground. The demand to have a mobile mechanical unit and a crane service unit was yet to be addressed. Blaming the State government and the Wayanad and Kozhikode district administrations for the impasse, he claimed that senior citizens, women and children had to suffer without drinking water and other basic facilities once they were stuck on the road.
The Congress MLA demanded that a permanent system, involving government departments such as the Local Self-Governments and Home, and voluntary organisations, should be set up to address the issue. Mr. Siddique said that steps should be taken to start the construction on the Poozhithode-Padinjarethara alternative road to Wayanad, along with the bypass road from Chippilithode to Thalippuzha.

title: After backlash, ECI directs home verification for elderly, ailing, disabled voters during SIR hearing in West Bengal
summary: ECI mandates home verification for elderly and disabled voters in West Bengal, addressing backlash over in-person hearing requirements.
content:
Amid outrage among a section of the electorate over elderly and ailing voters being summoned for hearings under the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) in West Bengal, the Election Commission of India (ECI) has directed officials not to call such electors — particularly those aged 85 years and above — for physical hearings.
In a notification issued on Monday, the Additional Chief Electoral Officer asked all District Magistrates to ensure that electors aged 85 years and above, as well as those ailing and persons with disabilities, are not required to appear in person. If notices have already been issued, officials have been instructed to contact the electors over the phone and carry out the verification at their residences.
Hearings for SIR began in West Bengal on December 27. Notices sent to a large number of elderly persons as well as persons with disabilities, had created anguish among the people.
Earlier this week, the ECI issued fresh instructions to district election officials (DEOs) in the State not to summon for hearings those who have been identified as ‘unmapped’ but whose names or ancestral connections are present in the 2002 voter list.
Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee on Tuesday (December 30, 2025) questioned why booth-level agents (BLAs) were not allowed during the SIR hearing process. Protests erupted in different parts of the State over the demand to allow BLAs at the hearing centres. On Monday, the hearing was halted in Hooghly district’s Chinsurah after Trinamool Congress MLA Asit Majumdar objected to the exclusion of BLAs during the process.
Addressing a public gathering in Bankura, Ms. Banerjee said that the SIR was a huge “scam” being conducted with the help of artificial intelligence (AI). “They have allegedly used AI to delete 54 lakh names, falsely attributing these actions to Electoral Registration Officers (EROs). The ERO association has sent letters saying they did not carry out this work,” she said. Ms. Banerjee threatened to gherao the Election Commission office in Delhi if the names of legitimate voters are deleted during SIR in the State.

title: Excise officials seize 229 liquor bottles at Pahadishareef ahead of New Year celebrations
summary: Excise teams seized 229 liquor bottles in Hyderabad, enhancing enforcement ahead of New Year celebrations to combat illegal trade.
content:
Excise enforcement teams seized 229 liquor bottles during special checks conducted at Pahadishareef as part of intensified measures ahead of the New Year celebrations, officials said on December 30.
Officials said the checks were carried out after receiving information that liquor sourced from the airport as well as from Goa, Delhi and Haryana was being transported into Telangana through the Pahadishareef road.
The raids were conducted by the Rangareddy State Task Force (STF)-B team with the support of personnel from the Saroonagar and Maheshwaram Excise Stations. All seized liquor bottles were handed over to the Saroonagar Excise Station for further action under the Excise Act.
In a separate operation, enforcement teams carrying out checks on the Sangareddy main road seized 7.165 litres of liquor that was being illegally imported from Goa. Officials said such drives would continue in the coming days to prevent unlawful liquor trade and ensure compliance with excise regulations during the holiday season.

title: 1,200 police to be deployed for crowd management at New Year revelry in Fort Kochi
summary: 1,200 police will manage crowds at Fort Kochi's New Year celebrations, ensuring safety and traffic regulations for attendees.
content:
A comprehensive crowd control plan will be in place for the New Year Celebrations in Fort Kochi on the intervening night of Wednesday (December 31, 2025) and Thursday (January 1, 2026), top district officials said here on Tuesday (December 30, 2025).
Around 1,200 police personnel, including 13 Deputy Superintendents of Police, 28 Inspectors, and 163 sub-inspectors from within and outside the district, will be deployed for crowd management and maintaining law and order, said District Police Chief (Kochi City) Putta Vimaladitya. New Year celebrations, mainly the burning of Pappanji effigies, will be held this year at Parade Ground and Veli Ground.
Flying drones in the Carnival area without prior permission has been banned, Mr. Vimaladitya said.
Vehicle entry via the Ro-Ro ferry from Vypeen to Fort Kochi will be allowed only until 4 p.m. on December 31. Between 4 p.m. and 7 p.m., only pedestrians and the public can use the Ro-Ro service. After 7 p.m., Ro-Ro services from Fort Kochi will be suspended.
All vehicles arriving at the Vypeen Jankar Jetty after 4 p.m. must be parked in a parallel manner along LNG Road from Kalamukku Junction. Only service buses will be allowed to the jetty after 4 p.m.
Both Ro-Ro ferries will be anchored at Fort Kochi Jetty after 7 p.m. and will continuously carry passengers from Fort Kochi to Vypeen.
Vehicles coming from Alappuzha to Ernakulam must take the Aroor–Kundannoor–Vyttila route from noon onwards, as entry via Edakochi will be restricted. After 4 p.m., no vehicles will be allowed into Fort Kochi by road. If crowds increase, entry restrictions may be enforced earlier, and vehicles will be stopped at outer points such as BOT, Swift Junction, Kannangatt, Edakochi, the south side of Perumpadappu Bridge, and Puthenthodu. The old Mattancherry Bridge will be made one-way, allowing only outgoing traffic from Fort Kochi via Thoppumpady.
Private and KSRTC buses transporting the public from Ernakulam, Edakochi, and Thoppumpady must terminate at the Fort Kochi bus stand by 5 p.m. After 5 p.m., all buses will stop at the temporary bus stand at Cochin College Ground in Mattancherry. People returning from Fort Kochi can walk to the ground and board connecting buses from there. After midnight, KSRTC and private buses will be available for the return journey from Cochin College and Vypeen.
Vehicles will be blocked at the following locations: BOT East Junction, CIFT Junction, BOT West Junction (near the court), Edakochi Bridge, Pashnithode Bridge, south side of Perumpadappu Bridge, Puthenthodu Junction, Pappangamukku, Jubilee Junction, Manthra Bridge, Pallathu Raman Junction, Veli West Dronacharya Road, and Veli West K.B. Jacob Road.
Designated parking areas include Aspinwall Ground, Cabral Yard Ground, St. Paul’s School Ground, Delta School Ground, Oceanus East Side Ground, Bishop House Front, Dronacharya Main Gate (north side, inside fencing), Dronacharya Main Gate (south side up to Odatha, inside fencing), Veli School Ground, east and west sides of the road from Kemperi Junction (Convent Road and Ajantha Road), Pandikkudi Junction to Old Shap Junction, west side of the road from Koovappadam to Parippu Junction, Cochin College Ground, TD School Ground, Aasia Bai School Ground, MMOVHS Ground, South Moolamkuzhi CC Group Ground, vacant land at Thoppumpady Junction, and Thoppumpady Corporation Stadium Ground. Vehicles coming via Vypeen must park on both sides of LNG Terminal Road at Puthuvype near Kalamukku.
Vehicles of Fort Kochi residents parked along the roads will be moved to designated grounds such as St. Paul’s School Ground and Delta School Ground (South Gate). Vehicles of visitors staying in hotels and homestays should not be parked on the roads.
District Collector G. Priyanka, Kochi Mayor V.K. Minimol, and Sub-Collector Grandhe Sai Krishna also addressed the media, urging the public to strictly follow safety guidelines during the celebrations.

title: Curriculum and textbook revision for Classes I to XII in Kerala nearing completion
summary: Kerala's curriculum and textbook revision for Classes I-XII is near completion, adhering strictly to the state's independent framework.
content:
The process of curriculum and textbook revision for Classes I to XII is nearing completion in the State, General Education Minister V. Sivankutty said here on Tuesday.
Since 2022, the Union government has been attempting to push its own policies through the National Education Policy (NEP) during curriculum revisions. However, all academic changes introduced by the State will strictly follow the Kerala Curriculum Framework formulated independently by the State, he said.
All 597 textbook titles being prepared for Classes I to X and the 39 revised textbooks for Class XI being brought out this year will follow the Kerala Curriculum  framework.
Kerala will academically resist all attempts by the Centre to  force the NEP and unilaterally  impose curriculum changes. The textbooks being prepared by the State will reflect the its long-standing priorities in education, its secular and democratic values and scientific temper, Mr. Sivankutty said.
At the Higher Secondary level, Kerala has for a long time been using some NCERT textbooks during the first and second year. However, in recent times it has been found that  significant portions in History, Political Science and Sociology books are being deliberately omitted from the textbooks.
Hence, Kerala is now preparing to bring out its own textbooks in these three subjects to ensure academic continuity and contextual relevance, Mr. Sivankutty said.
The revised Higher Secondary first year textbooks will be formally released by the end of January. In 39 titles, approximately four lakh textbooks are being printed for distribution.
The State government is disregarding the additional financial burden it might incur in this regard, he added.
In addition to reforms, the Curriculum Committee meeting scheduled for January 8 will discuss the reports on the impact of heavy school bags on the health of and the proposal to revise the schedule of mid-summer vacation in schools.
The structural report on measures to be taken to further democratise classroom spaces in the State schools by redesigning seating arrangements and eliminating the traditional “back bench” concept will also be discussed at the meeting, Mr. Sivankutty said.

title: Applications invited for Chief Minister’s Research Fellowship for Minorities
summary: Apply now for the Chief Minister’s Research Fellowship for Minorities in Kerala, offering ₹2.4 lakh for eligible students.
content: Applications have been invited for the Chief Minister’s Research Fellowship for Minorities. Students belonging to religious minorities from Kerala who are doing regular/full-time research in UGC-recognised universities and institutions can apply for the fellowship. A one-time fellowship of ₹2.4 lakh, with ₹20,000 allocated for each month, will be provided for eligible candidates. The applicant should not be a recipient of fellowships or other financial assistance from the Union or State governments or universities. A total of 30% of the fellowships are reserved for female applicants and 5% for differently abled persons. Applicants should have an account in any scheduled commercial bank. The completed application should be submitted in person or by post to the Director, Minority Welfare department, 4th Floor, Vikas Bhavan, Thiruvananthapuram - 33, before January 15. For queries, please contact: 0471-2300523, 2300524, 2302000.

title: Hyderabad Traffic Police announce restrictions and diversions for New Year celebrations
summary: Hyderabad Traffic Police announce restrictions and diversions for New Year celebrations to ensure safety and smooth traffic flow.
content:
The Hyderabad Traffic Police have announced a series of traffic restrictions, diversions and enforcement measures across the city on the night of December 31 in view of plans of large-scale New Year celebrations, particularly around major public gathering points and entertainment hubs.
Police said adequate traffic personnel would be deployed at 217 key junctions and intersections across the city to ensure smooth movement and road safety. Special focus areas include markets, malls and high-footfall locations such as Tank Bund, NTR Marg and PVNR Marg along Necklace Road, as well as commercial and nightlife zones in Jubilee Hills, Banjara Hills, Punjagutta, Khairatabad, Saifabad and surrounding areas.
Need-based traffic restrictions will come into force from 11 p.m. onwards on Tank Bund and adjoining roads and will remain in place until the celebrations conclude. Vehicular traffic, including private and public transport, will not be allowed on NTR Marg, PVNR Marg and Tank Bund between 11 p.m. and 2 a.m. on the intervening night of December 31 and January 1. Several diversions will also be implemented around Hussain Sagar to regulate traffic flow and prevent congestion.
As an additional measure, all flyovers in the city, except those at Begumpet and Tolichowki, may be closed on a need basis during the same period. The PVNR Expressway flyover will remain open exclusively for passengers travelling to the Rajiv Gandhi International Airport with valid air tickets.
Entry of private travel buses, lorries, heavy goods vehicles and heavy passenger vehicles into Hyderabad city limits will be restricted between 10 p.m. on December 31 and 2 a.m. on January 1. Such vehicles, including contract carriages bound for Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka and other States, have been advised to use the Outer Ring Road.
Visitors planning to access Tank Bund on foot have been advised to park their vehicles at designated locations, including the Secretariat visitors’ parking, HMDA parking near Prasads Multiplex, GHMC Head Office lane, Race Course road (beside NTR Ghat), Adarsh Nagar lane, NTR Stadium and nearby approved areas. Hotels, clubs, bars and event organisers have been directed to make special parking and security arrangements and to regulate traffic around their premises. They have also been instructed to ensure liquor service is restricted to permitted hours and to provide safe transport options for intoxicated patrons.
The traffic police said intensive enforcement drives would be carried out to curb drunk driving, overspeeding, rash and dangerous driving, wrong-side driving and other violations. Stringent action will be taken against offenders, particularly those involved in stunt biking, racing and reckless driving. Motorists were reminded that drunken driving is a punishable offence under the Motor Vehicles Act, attracting a fine of ₹10,000 and/or imprisonment, with stricter penalties for repeat offenders.
Appealing to the public to cooperate, the Hyderabad Traffic Police urged motorists to avoid driving under the influence of alcohol and to use public transport or cabs where possible. Commuters have been advised to follow official traffic updates on the Hyderabad Traffic Police social media platforms or contact the traffic helpline in case of emergencies. The police said the measures were being implemented in the interest of public safety and wished citizens a safe and happy New Year.

title: Sabarimala gold theft: HC allows inclusion of two more cops in SIT
summary: Kerala High Court approves adding two more officers to SIT investigating the Sabarimala temple gold theft case.
content:
The Kerala High Court on Tuesday allowed the inclusion of two more police officers in the special investigation team (SIT) that had been constituted to probe the alleged misappropriation of gold from the Sabarimala temple.
A Bench of Justice Ziyad Rahman A.A. and Justice M.B. Snehalatha allowed the inclusion of two officers in the rank of Circle Inspector in the team, on a request by the head of the probe team for more personnel.
The court had earlier this month granted six more weeks to the SIT to conclude its probe into the alleged misappropriation of gold from the Dwarapalaka idols and also from the door frames of the temple. The matter was posted for hearing on January 14.

title: BLAs can submit up to 10 claims and objections forms to BLOs daily: EC
summary: BLAs can submit up to 10 claims and objections daily, requiring verification of details, says the Election Commission.
content:
The Election Commission of India on Tuesday said Booth Level Agents (BLAs) of recognised political parties could submit up to a maximum of 10 application forms for claims and objections per day to the concerned Booth Level Officers (BLOs).
In a statement, Chief Electoral Officer Archana Patnaik said BLAs had to submit the forms along with an undertaking stating that the applications had been personally verified and that the particulars furnished were correct.
The BLOs will verify such forms, digitise the contents and forward them to the concerned Assistant Electoral Registration Officer or Electoral Registration Officer, who will scrutinise the forms and take appropriate action on a case-by-case basis.
The announcement was made as part of the claims and objections period, which began on December 19 and will continue until January 18, 2026, under the Special Intensive Revision of the electoral rolls in Tamil Nadu.
The draft electoral roll for the State was published on December 19, in which nearly 97.37 lakh electors out of 6.41 crore were deleted, bringing the total electorate down to 5.43 crore.
As of December 29, a total of 7,32,367 people had submitted Form 6 and Form 6A applications seeking inclusion as electors, while 9,450 people had submitted Form 7 for exclusion.
The Election Commission has also organised special camps during weekends. On December 27 and 28, a total of 5.58 lakh people submitted Form 6 and 8,260 people submitted Form 7 in the special camps.

title: ACB nabs mandal surveyor in Nirmal district
summary: ACB nabs mandal surveyor in Nirmal district
content:
The Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) on Tuesday arrested a mandal surveyor attached to the Tahsildar’s office in Nirmal mandal for demanding and accepting a bribe of ₹7,500 for an official favour related to land demarcation.
The accused officer, identified as N. Bala Krishna Varma, was trapped by the Adilabad Range ACB after he demanded the bribe for carrying out demarcation of land and handing over thepanchanamapertaining to the complainant’s father-in-law. The bribe was accepted through a private person, identified as Pola Nagaraju, who was acting as an assistant to the public servant.
The ACB said the surveyor had initially demanded ₹15,000 and accepted ₹5,000 as part payment, later insisting on the remaining ₹10,000. Following a request from the complainant, the amount was reduced to ₹7,500. The tainted cash was recovered from the possession of the private individual at the instance of the surveyor.
Both the surveyor and the private person were arrested and will be produced before the special court for SPE and ACB cases in Karimnagar. Further investigation is under way.
The ACB reiterated its appeal to the public to report any demand for bribe by public servants by calling the toll-free number 1064, assuring that the identity of complainants would be kept confidential.

title: NDA government ignored both education, health sectors, alleges Vizianagaram Zilla Parishad chairperson
summary: Vizianagaram chairperson criticizes NDA government for neglecting education and health, impacting students and farmers in 2025.
content: Vizianagaram Zilla Parishad chairperson Majji Srinivasa Rao on Tuesday (December 30, 2025) alleged that 2025 was a bitter year for the people as NDA government had ignored both education and health sectors. Addressing a media conference here, he said that thousands of students were being forced to pay college fees as the government had not cleared fee reimbursement dues to many engineering and degree colleges in Vizianagaram and other districts.  He said that the move to privatise Vizianagaram government medical college had shocked everyone in the district.  Mr. Srinivasa Rao said that the farmers were unable to get remunerative prices for paddy and other produces as the government failed to take up market intervention to stop the drop of the prices in the open market.

title: GHMC’s footprint grows but civic outcomes lag in 2025
summary: In 2025, GHMC expands significantly but faces ongoing challenges in infrastructure and sanitation management amid improving finances.
content:
The Greater Hyderabad Municipal Corporation has remained largely a work in progress during the year 2025, with no major achievements to speak of, nor any calamitous events to bring it down.
The expansion of the corporation towards the year-end leading to creation of the largest municipal corporation in the country area wise, has been the sole noteworthy event this year. Government has added to the GHMC’s purview, 20 municipalities and seven municipal corporations which fall fully or partially within the Telangana Core Urban Region.
The area governed by the corporation has grown more than threefold with the move, from 650 square kilometres to 2,053 square kilometres. A ward delimitation exercise followed, at the end of which GHMC emerged in its new format with 300 wards/divisions parcelled into 12 zones and 30 circles.
Over the past 12 months, no major infrastructural project has been grounded, and very few were completed. Beginning with the inauguration of a four-kilometre flyover between Aramghar and Nehru Zoological Park, the year has also seen opening of the P. Janardhan Reddy flyover at Gachibowli, and the parallel Road over Bridge (ROB) at Falaknuma, both initiated as part of the Strategic Road Development Plan (SRDP).
The Hyderabad City Innovative and Transformative Infrastructure (H-CITI) project with 38 components, launched with much fanfare towards the end of 2024, has not progressed much this year, with hardly any project hitting the ground running. While tendering process has been completed for several components, property acquisition stands as a major hurdle.
On the sanitation front, the corporation has had the most depressing year, with garbage mounds flourishing uncontrollably across the city. Sweeping of the roads, the most basic function of a civic body, has remained wanting, as the workforce was not managed effectively. A 100% door-to-door collection is still a distant dream, and garbage clearance from public areas too has slid this year, flagging serious supervision lapses.
The corporation, amply aided by the Hyderabad Disaster Response & Asset Protection Agency (HYDRAA), fared better in flood management despite intense localised rains extending up to November this year. Hectic last minute desilting operations by HYDRAA saved the day for the civic body, though it had not helped four persons being washed away by storm water in three different instances.
GHMC’s financial condition has started to look up from its insolvent status back in 2023-24, thanks to the rising property tax collection and fund infusion by the government from time to time. For the financial year ending March 31, 2025, the corporation set a new record, with ₹2,038 crore in property tax collection. Another record followed, with GHMC’s Early Bird scheme fetching an unprecedented tax collection of ₹901 crore within the first month of the financial year. Government grants for the corporation through the year amounted to a substantial ₹1,704 crore, mostly for the H-CITI project.

title: Bank employees stage protest seeking five-day banking system
summary: Bank employees in Vizianagaram protest for a five-day banking system, citing increased workload and need for better work-life balance.
content: Vizianagaram District Bank Employees Coordination Committee president B.V. Prasad and secretary Murali Srinivas on Tuesday (December 30, 2025) urged all banks to implement a five‑day banking system, stating that working six days a week has become a heavy burden on employees. Bank employees staged a protest, following a call given by the United Forum of Bank Unions, at the State Bank of India’s main branch on GT Road in Vizianagaram on Tuesday. Speaking on the occasion, Mr. Prasad said that five-day week system would ensure more productivity as the employees would be able to have proper rest over the weekend. The leaders of the Committee Ina Ramesh, Rajasekhar Gupta and others were present.

title: Rare Imperial Eagle spotted in Mudumalai Tiger Reserve
summary: Rare Eastern Imperial Eagles have been spotted in Mudumalai Tiger Reserve, highlighting its importance as a winter habitat for migratory birds.
content:
Wildlife enthusiasts have confirmed the presence of an Eastern Imperial Eagle visiting the Mudumalai Tiger Reserve (MTR) during the winter migratory season.
A pair of the rare Eastern Imperial Eagles (Aquila heliaca), was spotted by Murali Moorthy. One particular picture captures one of the raptors with another rare bird – an endangered Egyptian vulture.
Speaking toThe Hindu, Mr. Murali said that the bird breeds primarily throughout Western and Central Asia, while they also migrate during winter to parts of Africa, the Middle East as well as South and East Asia.
Arockianathan Samson, from the Bombay Natural History Society, who was part of a team of researchers who documented 58 species of raptors in MTR between 2011 and 2022, said that the tiger reserve provided an ideal habitat, food availability and a conducive climate for raptors to flourish.
“Most raptors also prefer areas with little anthropogenic pressures and good food availability,” said Mr. Samson.
During the breeding season, the Imperial Eagle prefers open landscapes with scattered forests, commonly known as forest-steppe habitats. These areas provide tall trees for nesting and open grounds for hunting. The breeding range stretches across a vast region—from Western Europe through Eastern Europe and Central Asia, and further into Siberia and northwestern China.
As a top predator, the Imperial Eagle plays a vital role in maintaining ecological balance by controlling populations of rodents and other small animals. Its presence is often a sign of a healthy ecosystem.
However, habitat loss, disturbance, and reduced food availability threaten this magnificent bird across its range. Protecting both its breeding grounds and wintering areas is essential for ensuring its survival, added Mr. Samson.
This year has witnessed a large influx of winter migrants, especially birds of prey, added Murali Moorthy, who said that while Greater spotted eagles - another winter migratory species, were also recorded in 2024, that the numbers this year were far higher.
Despite the encouraging sightings, conservationists have also appealed to the Forest Department and the Nilgiris district administration to consider imposing limitations to the number of visitors allowed into the tiger reserve, especially during the peak tourist season months in the summer and winter.
“As the tiger reserve is a biodiversity hotspot, it is now also subject to pressures from tourism, with it probably being the most heavily visited region of the Nilgiris only apart from Ooty town. In the coming years, these pressures will only increase, so the government must begin considering a tourism policy that can be implemented to reduce such pressures. This will protect not just native wildlife, but also winter migrants from across the world which visit MTR each year,” said a conservationist from The Nilgiris.
“Continuous sightings of the Imperial Eagle have been documented through the global bird-watching platform eBird from 2020 to 2025, confirming that the Imperial Eagle regularly visits Mudumalai, highlighting the importance of the landscape,” said Mr. Samson, who had also recorded the species in 2017.
“Most of these records were made between November and February, which coincides with the species’ winter migration period. These repeated observations strongly suggest that Mudumalai Tiger Reserve serves as an important wintering habitat for the Imperial Eagle. The presence of open grasslands, forest edges, and abundant prey in the reserve likely supports the species during its long stay away from its breeding grounds in Europe and Central Asia. Such records underline the global conservation value of Indian protected areas and the need to safeguard wintering habitats for migratory birds that travel thousands of kilometres across continents,” he added.

title: Pawan Kalyan virtually lays foundation for Sankaraguptam drain modernisation in Konaseema
summary: Pawan Kalyan initiates ₹20.77 crore drain modernisation project in Konaseema to resolve drainage issues and protect coconut plantations.
content:
Deputy Chief Minister Pawan Kalyan on Tuesday virtually laid the foundation stone for the modernisation of the Sankaraguptam Major Drain in Konaseema district, addressing long-standing drainage problems affecting coconut farmers in the region.
Participating from the Mangalagiri camp office, he was joined virtually by Minister for Water Resources Nimmala Rama Naidu. The programme at Shankaraguptam was attended by Razole MLA Deva Varaprasad, Konaseema District Collector Mahesh Kumar and senior officials of the Water Resources Department.
The modernisation project, estimated to cost ₹20.77 crore, is aimed at improving drainage and protecting thousands of coconut trees that have been under threat due to persistent waterlogging.
Recalling his visit to the Razole constituency, Mr. Pawan Kalyan said he had personally witnessed the damage caused to coconut plantations due to blocked drains. He said nearly one lakh coconut trees had been damaged, highlighting the urgency of the issue. He added that the matter was immediately brought to the attention of Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu and an action plan was prepared.
Expressing satisfaction over the pace of execution, Mr. Pawan Kalyan said the works commenced within 35 days, ahead of the planned 45-day schedule, and credited the swift support of the Chief Minister. The project will cover a stretch of 8.5 km to 16.5 km of the drain and include strengthening of embankments up to 14.5 km on both sides.
He reiterated the coalition government’s commitment to farmers’ welfare and said similar drainage modernisation works across East Godavari district would require an investment of nearly ₹4,000 crore.
The project is expected to provide immediate relief to hundreds of coconut farmers and prevent future losses caused by drainage issues, reinforcing the government’s focus on safeguarding agricultural livelihoods in the Konaseema region.

title: Congress accuses the ECI of making arbitrary changes to the process of conducting SIR
summary: Congress criticizes the ECI for arbitrary changes in the SIR process, demanding transparency amid concerns over voter deletions.
content:
