title: Kochi Muziris Biennale artwork controversy: artist Tom Vattakuzhy says he didn’t intend to hurt anyone’s sentiments
summary: Artist Tom Vattakuzhy defends his controversial Kochi Muziris Biennale artwork, clarifying intentions and historical context behind the piece.
content:
Artist Tom Vattakuzhy, whose artwork displayed at the ongoing Kochi Muziris Biennale had invited the wrath of the Catholic Church on Wednesday (December 31, 2025), termed the development as ‘unfortunate’ while stating that he had never intended to hurt anyone’s faith or sentiments.
“Born into a Christian family, most of my works had been inspired by the humanism seen in Christian values. This artwork is an extension of that thought process and not a distortion of The Last Supper as alleged by those opposing it,” he said.
The work in question is part of the ‘Edam’ exhibition at the Garden Convention Centre in Bazar Road, which brings together the works of 36 artists, reflecting a wide range of artistic practices and voices.
Mr. Vattakuzhy, whose work has long been part of Kerala’s cultural and literary landscape, said that his work was inspired by the playMridhavangiyude Durmruthyuby writer C. Gopan and not based on the theme of Last Supper. “The story itself is inspired by a poem written by Vyloppilli, which, in turn, draws from historical events. I have always been inspired by the works of masters based on the early Renaissance. I believe in humanistic art,” he said.
A statement by the curators of the exhibition, including K.M. Madhusudhanan and Aishwarya Suresh, pointed out that the artwork depicted Mata Hari, a historically documented figure and a convicted spy, in the moments preceding her execution by the French Army. Mata Hari was also an exotic dancer, and the use of nudity in the work was directly linked to this historical and narrative context. The painting by Mr. Vattakuzhy was therefore part of a long-established chain of artistic and literary interpretation that moved from history to poetry, from poetry to prose, and from prose to visual representation. Within this continuum, the painting was neither isolated nor gratuitous, but firmly grounded in a recognised tradition of cultural and artistic engagement, it said.

title: Two accused of witchcraft burnt alive in Assam
summary: A couple in Assam was burned alive by villagers after being accused of witchcraft, highlighting ongoing superstitious violence.
content:
GUWAHATI
A couple accused of practising witchcraft was burnt alive by a group of villagers in central Assam’s Karbi Anglong district on Tuesday (December 30, 2025) night, police said.
The deceased were identified as 43-year-old Gardi Birowa and Mira Birowa, 33, of No. 1 Beloguri Munda village in the district’s Howraghat area.
A district police officer said the assailants set the couple’s house on fire after injuring them with sharp weapons inside.
“We have launched an investigation to identify and arrest those involved in the crime, likely an outcome of deep-rooted superstitions,” a senior police official said after visiting the site on Wednesday (December 31, 2025) morning.
Locals said the victims were accused of bringing misfortune upon the village by practising witchcraft.
Assam has been grappling with the witch-hunting issue for decades. Police said witchcraft-related violence is punishable under the Assam Witch Hunting (Prohibition, Prevention, and Protection) Act of 2015, apart from relevant Sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.
Official records show at least 160 people were killed in witch-hunting incidents across Assam between 2001 and 2019. Most of these incidents were recorded in Chirang, Goalpara, Kokrajhar, Udalguri and Sonitpur districts.

title: Bengaluru police haven't arrested a single ‘producer’ of narcotics in two years
summary: Bengaluru police have not arrested any narcotics producers in two years, focusing instead on peddlers and consumers.
content:
Data presented by Home Minister G. Parameshwara in the recently concluded Karnataka Legislature session shows that the Bengaluru City Police haven't arrested a single “producer” of narcotics in 2024 and 2025, targeting only peddlers and consumers.
This gains significance in the light of how Mumbai police followed up on a peddler’s arrest there and unearthed three synthetic drug manufacturing units in Bengaluru last week. The Maharashtra Police had similarly dismantled a drug manufacturing unit in Mysuru in July earlier this year.
Mysuru police have also not arrested a single “producer” in 2024 and 2025, which is true across the State. While 5,901 cases were booked during this period, it led to the arrest of 3,961 peddlers, 4,741 consumers, and only 90 producers. Sources said that most of these producers arrested are those growing ganja in their fields and not those manufacturing synthetic drugs.
This indicates that investigations into narcotics cases have rarely tried to establish the full chain of narcotics from the source to their consumers. Data also shows that following the arrest of a peddler, the focus seems to be on his/her clientele rather than the source.
It is through establishing the full chain of narcotics from the source to the consumers, a Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) in any narcotics investigation, that the Mumbai Police busted three synthetic drugs manufacturing units in Bengaluru. Mumbai Police arrested a peddler and built up the chain of the source of the narcotics from him to a man in Belagavi and then to the three units in Bengaluru.
*All 2025 figures until November 30, 2025
Hitendra R., Additional Director General of Police (Law and Order) and the chief of the newly formed Anti-Narcotics Task Force (ANTF), Karnataka, acknowledges the problem. “We have observed that almost all narcotics cases aresuo motucases and chargesheets are filed against a single accused. This means that the investigation has not unravelled the whole chain of the narcotics network from the source to the consumer. Investigators seem content with filing chargesheets against a single peddler. This needs to change. Investigators have to work even harder and uncover the full chain. ANTF is working towards bringing this change in the investigation and trial of narcotics cases in the State. Change is gradual, but we are definitely on that path,” he said.
A senior official in Bengaluru City Police said that in most cases of synthetic drugs,  it leads them to other peddlers in Goa, Mumbai, and Delhi, and rarely have they come across manufacturers themselves. “A lot of resources are required to follow and trace the entire chain in all the cases, which we do not have,” another officer said.
Meanwhile, there have been  allegations of corruption, extortion, and collusion with peddlers in narcotics probes as well. For instance, a Departmental Enquiry (DEs) has been under way against 11 policemen of Chamrajpet and J.J. Nagar Police Stations for allegedly being constantly in touch with a notorious drug peddler, Salman, and helping him in his crimes. Four policemen from Ramamurthy Nagar Police Station allegedly let go of a peddler they caught red-handed. Three police inspectors, in whose jurisdictions Mumbai Police unearthed synthetic drug manufacturing units, have now been suspended. Totally, 30 police personnel are under the cloud of suspicion and DEs pending against them in connection with narcotics cases across the State, data presented by the Home Minister shows.
For now, the oversight of ANTF, formed as per the mandate of the Union Ministry of Home Affairs on August 1, 2025, has  led to a jump in the number of cases booked.   “ANTF is reviewing narcotics cases every month and issuing necessary directions and advice to the police commissioners and SPs. Its impact is already seen in the increase in the number of cases registered after the formation of the ANTF,” said Mr. Hitendra.
Data presented by the Home Minister shows the State recorded 3531 cases from January 1 to July 31, 2025, and from August 1 to November 30, the State booked 2,387 cases, recording a significant jump. Mr. Hitendra hopes there will be a qualitative change in the investigation and trials of narcotics cases over the next few months.

title: Cabinet approves construction of six-lane Nashik-Solapur-Akkalkot corridor at ₹19,142 crore
summary: Cabinet approves ₹19,142 crore six-lane Nashik-Solapur-Akkalkot corridor to enhance regional connectivity and boost economic growth.
content:
The Union Cabinet on Wednesday (December 31, 2025) approved the construction of six-lane greenfield access-controlled Nashik-Solapur-Akkalkot corridor inMaharashtrawith a total capital cost of ₹19,142 crore.
The 374-km project will be constructed on BOT (Toll) mode, according to an official statement.
This project will provide connectivity to important regional cities such as Nashik, Ahilyanagar, Solapur connecting to Kurnool, it said.
This infrastructure is a significant step to facilitate integrated transport infrastructure development under the PM Gatishakti National Master Plan principle, it added.
Also Read |Fadnavis asks officials to make ready plan to build ‘India’s biggest shipyard’
The greenfield corridor from Nashik to Akkalkot is proposed to be connected to the Delhi-Mumbai Expressway near Vadhawan port interchange, Agra-Mumbai corridor at Nashik at junction with NH-60 (Adegaon) and Samruddhi Mahamarg at Pangri (near Nashik).
The statement said the proposed corridor will provide through connectivity from west coast to east coast.
From the Chennai port end, four-lane corridors are already in progress from Chennai to Hasapur (MH Border) via Thiruvallur, Renigunta, Kadappa, and Kurnool (700 km long).
The primary purpose of the proposed access-controlled six-lane greenfield project corridor is to improve travel efficiency and is expected to reduce travel time by 17 hours and reduce the travel distance by 201 km.
Nashik-Akkalkot (Solapur) connectivity will improve logistics efficiency for freight originating and terminating at major National Industrial Corridor Development Corporation (NICDC) nodes of Kopparthy and Orvakal.
The six-lane access-controlled greenfield corridor with close tolling, supporting average vehicular speeds of 60 km/hour with design speed of 100 km/hour.
This will reduce the overall travel time to about 17 hours from 31 hours, while offering safer, faster, and uninterrupted connectivity for both passengers and freight vehicles, the statement said.
According to the statement, the project will generate about 251.06 lakh man-days of direct employment and 313.83 lakh man-days of indirect employment.
The project will also induce additional employment opportunities due to increase in economic activity in the vicinity of the proposed corridor, it said.

title: Students from Northeast protest at Jantar Mantar against Anjel Chakma’s killing in Dehradun
summary: Angel Chakma death: Northeast students protest at Jantar Mantar for justice following Tripura student's murder, demanding a thorough investigation and accountability.
content:
Students from the Northeast on Wednesday (December 31, 2025) staged a protest at the Jantar Mantar in New Delhi demanding justice for Tripura student Anjel Chakma,who died of a stab injury in Dehradun recently.
Hundreds of students from the Northeast studying in Delhi University participated in the protest organised under the banner of Northeast Students' Society of Delhi University (NESSDU), demanding a thorough investigation into Chakma’s killing.
Chakma (24) from Unakoti district in Tripura was attacked by a group of six people when he objected to racial slurs hurled at him and his younger brother in Dehradun on December 9. He succumbed to his injuries at a hospital on December 26.
Dehradun police has arrested five of the six accused. One of them, Yagyaraj Awasthi, a resident of Kanchanpur district in Nepal, is absconding.
Speaking toPTI, NESSDU president Pointing Thokchom said, “We demand the case be transferred to the CBI and the family be compensated properly. There should be a law to protect students from the Northeast from racial abuse and attacks.”
Bipul Chakma, vice-president of the All India Chakma Students' Union, alleged that the Uttarakhand administration delayed the investigation, prompting the students to gather at the Jantar Mantar demanding justice.
Also read |Treat racial slur as separate category of hate crime: petition
“I went to Dehradun on December 11 after Anjel Chakma’s father called me since nobody was helping. I have been a victim of racial abuse myself at DU. We want this vicious cycle of racial abuse and attacks against Northeast students to stop,” he said.

title: Address technical, procedural and administrative issues related to SIR: Haris Beeran
summary: Haris Beeran urges the Election Commission to resolve issues hindering overseas Indians' electoral participation and access to voter information.
content:
Rajya Sabha MP Haris Beeran has urged the Election Commission of India (EC) to address issues including those related to ‘non-mapping’ cases and place of birth issue faced by overseas electors under the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in Kerala.
In a letter to Chief Electoral Officer (Kerala) Rathan U. Kelkar, the Indian Union Muslim League (IUML) MP cited a number of “technical, procedural and administrative” issues. According to him, the EC website was restricted to India IP addresses, which created a “significant barrier” for overseas Indians. The website should be made globally accessible so that electors could download voter information and submit their applications, he said.
In his letter, Mr. Beeran also drew attention to an issue that the IUML had been consistently raising at the political party meetings on SIR conducted by the CEO. The ‘Place of Birth’ field in Form 6A, used by overseas electors to enroll, was restricted to a dropdown menu of Indian States. This configuration excluded Indian citizens who were born abroad, making it impossible for them to accurately complete the application, he said.
A ‘Born outside India’ option should be added, he said. In the case of expatriates, there should be a provision for conducting SIR-related hearings either online or through an authorised representative since they could not appear before the Electoral Registration Officer (ERO) in person, he said. He also urged the EC to extend the  deadline for submission of documents under the ‘No Mapping’ cases.
Mr. Beeran also asked the EC to ensure that voters would not have to furnish fresh documents in cases where clerical errors had occurred on the part of booth-level officers (BLO) or for the correction of minor data errors and ‘logical discrepancies’ due to the translation of the 2002 voter list from Malayalam to English.

title: Young India Skill University trains over 1,000 students in 2025
summary: Young India Skills University achieves milestone by training over 1,000 students in skill-based programmes
content:
The Telangana government’s prestigious initiative, the Young India Skill University, has reached another significant milestone by training over 1,000 students by December 2025, within a short span of its inception.
Established to equip Intermediate and Degree students with job-ready skills, the university has emerged as a notable institution in the skill education sector by achieving this target in record time.
The university is currently offering skill-based training programmes in sectors such as Logistics, Healthcare, Life Sciences, Pharmaceuticals, Banking and Financial Services, and Information Sciences. Through short-term and certification courses, students are being trained with industry-relevant skills to enable immediate employment upon course completion.
Several leading organisations, including Microsoft, Dr. Reddy’s Laboratories, AIG Hospitals, Apollo Hospitals, and GMR Cargo, have partnered with the university. With proactive support from the State government, these companies are providing internships, practical training, and employment opportunities to students, officials said.
S. Swapna Sirasanagandala, who joined Dr. Reddy’s Pharma Associate Apprentice Course, said the six-month programme offered strong hands-on practical exposure along with valuable on-the-job training. “Apprenticeship stipend and placement was provided after successful course completion,” she said.
Seelam Nikhil, a Supply Chain Certification Course student, joined 09 Solutions as a Functional Consultant intern with a monthly stipend of ₹30,000. Y. Tanya Prakash, Endoscopy Technician student — who got her training from the AIG Hospitals and was placed there — says it has been a game-changer for her career. Similar is the experience of P. Sujeeth Alex, who got selected by GMR Air Cargo Hyderabad after the Key Consignor Executive Course.
The university is also preparing to launch Degree and Postgraduate programmes from the 2026–27 academic year with a job-guarantee-oriented approach.
The university was set up at the initiative of Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy, and its foundation stone was laid on August 1, 2024. It is run under the Public–Private Partnership (PPP) model.
The Chief Minister serves as the Chancellor of the University, while Anand Mahindra is the Chairman of the Board. The university is headed by Vice-Chancellor V.L.V.S.S. Subbarao.
Construction of the permanent campus at Future City is underway, spanning 57.8 acres. The campus will feature 43 classrooms, a 600-bed hostel, and a state-of-the-art laboratory block covering 84,000 sft. The government has set a target to complete Phase-1 of the campus by March 2026. Courses are now offered from a temporary campus at IIIT Hyderabad.

title: II PUC practical exams in Karnataka to be web-streamed to curb malpractice
summary: Karnataka's II PUC practical exams will be web-streamed and monitored with CCTV to prevent malpractice and ensure integrity.
content:
To prevent malpractice in II PUC practical examinations and to preserve the sanctity of evaluation, Karnataka School Examination and Assessment Board (KSEAB) has taken steps to conduct the practical exams of 2025-26 under web streaming.
In addition, it has also taken steps to install CCTV cameras in all examination centres and upload the practical exam marks online to the KSEAB server from the examination centres.
“To prevent any shortcomings in the II PUC practical examinations, a circular has already been issued to implement web streaming and a system of entering marks online at the examination centres from this year, and the examinations will be conducted accordingly,” said Gopalakrishna H.N., Director of KSEAB.
KSEAB will conduct II PUC practical examinations at the district level, headed by the Deputy Directors of Pre-University (DDPUs) of the respective district, from January 27 to February 14.
In subjects with practicals, the theory paper will be for 70 marks while the practical exam will be for a total of 30 marks. There is no minimum marks limit for students to pass the practical examination, with a maximum of 30 marks. However, students need to score at least 21 marks to pass the theory exam out of a maximum of 70 marks.
The minimum marks required for each subject, including both the theory and practical exams, is 30. However, students need to score a total of 33% marks this year to pass.
Students can appear for the theory exam even if they are absent from the practical exam. But, the minimum marks required to pass must be obtained in the theory exam.
However, it has come to the notice of the board that students are scoring maximum marks in the practical exams and scoring less marks in the theory section. There have also been incidents where students who performed poorly in practical exams were given good marks.
“Such unethical practices raise doubts about the sanctity of the evaluation of practical exams,” the KSEAB opined.
The KSEAB is already conducting SSLC and II PUC exams through web streaming. In a similar vein, it has been decided to conduct the practical exams also through web streaming.
Artificial Intelligence (AI) enabled cameras will be installed in every examination centre where II PUC practical exams are held and the examination activities will be monitored from the KSEAB headquarters directly. If any irregularities are found, the authorities concerned will be alerted immediately.
The Board has implemented a system of online entry of marks at the time of evaluation of SSLC and II PUC answer sheets from the evaluation centres. It has also been decided to implement a system of entering practicals marks directly to the Board’s server online from the examination centre this year.
CCTV installation has been made mandatory in all examination centres to monitor the examination processes, including the entry of unauthorised persons.
“A District Practical Examination Committee should be formed to conduct the practical examination, with one Principal of the respective science subject as the coordinator and two senior science lecturers as members. This committee should prepare the schedule of all the practical examination centers in the district and appoint internal and external examiners. No change in the schedule should be allowed. If any shortcomings are found in practical examinations or if there are complaints, the DDPU will be directly responsible and disciplinary action will be taken against them,” the KSEAB warned.

title: Cabinet approves widening, strengthening of highways project in Odisha

content:

title: Charlie Chaplin to return to Kolkata this New Year in exhibition by top Bengal artist
summary: Join celebrated artist Shuvaprasanna in Kolkata for a unique exhibition honoring Charlie Chaplin from January 2 to 22.
content:
Shuvaprasanna, one of Bengal’s most popular artists in the present day, is to begin the New Year with celebrating Charlie Chaplin by holding a 20-day exhibition of 30 of his artworks that depict the iconic actor.
“The 20th century saw the rise of two geniuses whom the world would remember for their remarkable contribution to the cultural arena. One is Pablo Picasso, the​ revolutionary Spanish artist, and the other is Charlie Chaplin, not only an actor, filmmaker, and humourist but also a great critic of fascism. Chaplin had a deep understanding of the society and he expressed that understanding through his performances — from silent cinema to the talkies,” the Kolkata-based artist said about his subject.
The exhibition, which he has titled ‘A Genius and the Common Man’, will begin at the Kolkata Centre for Creativity on January 2 and go on till January 22. What’s special about these artworks is that Mr. Shuvaprasanna has used acrylic ink — instead of conventional paint — to create them.
“My works are a way to delineate my admiration for the unparalleled influence that Chaplin wielded. I have meticulously studied and tried to replicate the virtuoso’s facial expressions, postures and gestures. Instead of using pastel colour or oil colour or acrylic, I chose a type of acrylic ink that can be sprayed and I got the desired result,” the artist explained.
When asked why he handpicked Chaplin as his subject and whether he was still relevant today, Mr. Shuvaprasanna said that some individuals transcended time and became eternal, one of them being the legendary actor. “Through multiple dimensions, he brought joy, influenced people, and even portrayed sorrow — often using irony, satire, and humour to respond to the injustices and conditions of the world. They were, in the truest sense, humanists,” he said.
“Chaplin expressed his resistance to fascism through his gestures and facial expressions. Similarly, when modernity emerged — initially perceived as mechanical and devoid of life — he explored these ideas through various creative works. Later, throughTheGold Rush, he portrayed life in a remarkably unusual way. The terrifying upheavals of that era were depicted through his expressions and creations in a manner that continues to illuminate us even today. Such individuals are eternal; they never grow old. Their work surpasses time,” Mr. Shuvaprasanna said.

title: Watch: Remembering personalities who passed away in 2025
summary: As 2025 draws to a close, we bid goodbye to celebrities and personalities from various fields, from across the world, who passed away this year.
content:
Compilation: Kanishkaa Balachandran
Editing: Shibu Narayan

title: Peace, normalcy can be restored in Manipur only if assembly is dissolved: Congress
summary: Congress claims dissolving Manipur's Assembly is essential for restoring peace and addressing the people's grievances in ongoing crisis.
content:
ManipurCongress president Keisham Meghachandra on Wednesday (December 31, 2025) said the only means to restore peace and normalcy in theethnic strife-torn Statein 2026 is to dissolve the Assembly and hold fresh elections.
Mr. Meghachandra told reporters, "While everyone else is celebrating the New Year everywhere, in Manipur, we are not seeing these celebrations. The only solution for the welfare of the people of the State is to dissolve the present Assembly. Our demand is the dissolution of the Assembly and a fresh mandate. It's the only means to bring peace and normalcy in the State."
Mr. Meghachandra also said, "The ongoing crisis has exposed the failure of the present dispensation to address the aspirations and grievances of the people." The Congress leader also expressed hope that the New Year would bring clarity, justice, and a people-driven political change for lasting peace in Manipur.
Meanwhile, BJP MLA Tongbram Robindro told reporters, "We have had several festivals and celebrations, including the Sangai festival, Orange festival, Christmas and Meitei's own Emoinu festival in November and December."
“At such festive time, I appeal to all the people across the communities to forgive and forget all differences and misunderstandings and return to earlier peace, normalcy, and cordial relations with the coming of the new year," Mr. Robindro said.
Manipur has been under President's rule since February 13, after then Chief Minister N. Biren Singh, who was heading a BJP-led government, resigned on February 9 following ethnic violence that claimed over 260 lives since May 2023.
The 60-member State Assembly, which has a tenure till 2027, has been put under suspended animation. After the imposition of the President's rule, Governor Ajay Kumar Bhalla had taken a number of steps to restore peace and bring back normalcy, including asking those who looted arms from security forces to surrender them.
Theviolence between the Meitei and Kuki communitiesstarted after a 'Tribal Solidarity March' was organised in the hill districts to protest against the Meitei community's demand for Scheduled Tribe (ST) status.

title: Farmers oppose Salem Yarn Colouring Park citing water contamination
summary: Farmers protest Salem Yarn Colouring Park, citing potential water contamination and demanding project relocation for community protection.
content:
Alleging that the State government and the district administration were destroying water resources in the name of establishing a textile park, members of the All India Kisan Sabha (AIKS), affiliated to the Communist Party of India (Marxist), staged a demonstration on Wednesday (December 31, 2025) opposing the project. They are demanding that the project be relocated, citing its adverse impact on farmers and the public.
The farmers said that though the project had been named the Salem Yarn Colouring Park (SYCP) and proposed on 187 acres at Jagir Ammapalayam, it was effectively a dyeing park that would lead to contamination of water sources in more than 40 villages in the region. They said they had only recently become aware of the project’s implications, leading to strong opposition.
If implemented, the project would contaminate groundwater, affecting drinking water sources as well as water used for agriculture and domestic purposes, they alleged. They blamed the district administration for failing to seek the consent of local residents before proposing the project.
Terming the handling of the issue by both the State government and the district administration unacceptable, the farmers pointed to groundwater contamination in Tiruppur, Perundurai, and Pallipalayam due to dyeing units and reiterated their demand that the project be relocated.

title: Anantapur registers significant drop in crimes in 2025
summary: Anantapur sees a 22.5% drop in crime in 2025, thanks to effective policing and enhanced public safety measures.
content:
Anantapur district registered a significant 22.5 per cent decrease in crimes in 2025 compared to the previous year. While 8,841 crimes were registered in 2024, the numbers came down to 6,851 this year.
Addressing the media here on Wednesday, Superintendent of Police (SP) P. Jagadeesh attributed the decrease in crime to effective policing and priority to public safety. The SP said 530 cases were registered, and 50 per cent  (₹3,63,55,170) of lost property was recovered in 2024, while in 2025, of total 527 cases, 55% (₹5,15,34,098) of lost property was recovered. “This was possible only due to the increased use of technology,” he said.
Similarly, there was a decrease in chain snatchings and murder for gain cases. Mr. Jagadeesh said the number of murder cases decreased from 57 in 2024 to 42 in 2025. “The main reasons for these murders were petty quarrels,  jealousy, and family and property-related conflicts,” he said. Similarly, attempt to murder cases decreased from 66 in last year to 59 in 2025. “Kidnapping cases increased slightly from 28 to 31, while overall, bodily offences decreased by 7 per cent,” he said.
The SP said special focus was laid on curbing crimes against women and it registered a decrease in 2025. “While 733 cases were reported last year, this year the number was 644. Murder of women decreased by 56 per cent, from 18 last year to eight this year,” he said.
Mr. Jagadeesh said there was also a decrease in POCSO cases from 83 in 2024 to 71 in 2025. “Awareness programmes were conducted in educational institutions and villages in collaboration with local police on the uses of the Shakti App, women’s protection laws, child marriages, and other issues,” he said.
Meanwhile, 836 missing persons’ cases were registered in 2025, and police solved 613 cases, while 223 cases are yet to be traced, the SP said.
The district also reported a dip in fatal and non-fatal road accidents by 9 per cent — from 544 in 2024 to 496 in 2025. “While 343 people died in accidents last year, 291 fatalities were recorded this year. The number of injured also decreased by 15 per cent, from 652 to 555. The reduction in road accidents has been a result of measures such as creating public awareness on road accidents and their consequences, imposing fines for violations, focusing on curbing drunk driving, and others,” he said.

title: Jana Sena Party eyes 100% strike rate in local body polls
summary: Jana Sena Party aims for a 100% strike rate in local body polls, bolstered by successful initiatives under K. Pawan Kalyan.
content:
Jana Sena Party leader Avanapu Vikram on Wednesday expressed confidence that the party would achieve a 100% strike rate in the forthcoming local body elections, similar to its performance in the 2024 general elections. He said the party’s public image had strengthened significantly following the effective implementation of the ‘Palle Panduga’ and other programmes by the Rural Development and Panchayat Raj Departments, which are handled by Deputy Chief Minister and Jana Sena Party president K. Pawan Kalyan.
Along with Jana Sena Party leader and former chairperson of the Vizianagaram District Cooperative Marketing Society, Avanapu Bhavana, Mr. Vikram released the party’s 2026 calendar and addressed a media conference. He explained the party’s initiatives aimed at winning public support in the local body elections.
Mr. Vikram said that the Union government had selected the A.P. Panchayat Raj Department for the Rashtriya Gramswaraj Abhiyan award, as the State secured first place in the implementation of schemes formulated by both the Union and State governments. He added that the party would soon launch a new membership drive, noting that people from all sections were keen to join Jana Sena Party due to its clean image and the effective administration of Mr. Pawan Kalyan.

title: Autorickshaw drivers to organise Chalo Assembly on January 3 over unkept promises
summary: Autorickshaw drivers in Hyderabad plan a Chalo Assembly on January 3 to demand unfulfilled government promises and fare increases.
content:
Autorickshaw drivers unions on Wednesday resolved to organise a Chalo Assembly programme on January 3, demanding that the Telangana government make good on their assurances made to the drivers.
At a round-table meeting, the Telangana State Auto Drivers’ Associations Joint Action Committee demanded that the government take steps to ensure that the problems faced by auto workers were raised in the Legislative Assembly and Council. They also sought an immediate increase in auto meter minimum fare.
They also pointed to the importance of constituting a welfare board for transport workers and a financial assistance of ₹12,000.
JAC convener B Venkatesham appealed to all auto workers across the State to ensure the success of the proposed programme.

title: YSRCP leader alleges erosion of law and order in Andhra Pradesh
summary: YSRCP leader Varudu Kalyani criticizes the NDA government for rising crime and eroding law and order in Andhra Pradesh.
content:
YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) State Women’s Wing president and MLC Varudu Kalyani on Wednesday criticised the government for surge in crimes, especially against women, and erosion of law and order across Andhra Pradesh.
Addressing the media at the party headquarters, Ms. Kalyani alleged that the NDA government betrayed the trust of people in the last 18 months, leaving women vulnerable and public safety in disarray.
Ms. Kalyani said despite promises of six welfare schemes for women, the government neglected their implementation, leaving victims without support.
In contrast, the previous YSRCP administration had introduced the Disha App and 18 dedicated police stations to ensure swift response to emergencies, she said.
Under the coalition government, the State ranked 36th nationally in law and order, with response times for emergencies averaging 26 minutes, well above the national average of 18 minutes.
Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu had openly acknowledged the rise in crimes against women, she claimed.
The MLC reaffirmed that the YSRCP would continue to support women and safeguard their rights. She called on the coalition to urgently address women’s safety and implement promised welfare schemes without delay.

title: Two-day Mannam Jayanti celebrations to begin on Thursday
summary: Join the 149th Mannam Jayanti celebrations on January 1-2, featuring tributes, discussions, and cultural programs at NSS headquarters.
content:
The 149th birth anniversary celebrations of Mannathu Padmanabhan, founder of the Nair Service Society (NSS), will be held at Mannam Nagar, a specially prepared venue at the NSS headquarters in Perunna on January 1 and 2.
According to the NSS, an all Kerala Nair delegates’ meet will be held on January 1 and the jayanti celebrations the following day. The celebrations will commence with the offering of floral tributes at the Mannam Samadhi on January 1. NSS general secretary G. Sukumaran Nair will deliver a briefing on NSS’ activities, achievements, and its stand on various socio-political issues, especially those affecting the community at the delegates’ meet which will commence at 10.30 a.m. NSS president M. Sasikumar will preside. Cultural programmes will follow.
Cyriac Thomas, former member of the National Minority Commission, will inaugurate the Mannam Jayanti celebrations at 11 a.m. on Friday. Mr. Sukumaran Nair will welcome the gathering. Poet and lyricist Rajeev Alumkal will deliver the remembrance speech on Mannathu Padmanabhan.

title: Students, youth urged to take the lead in spreading awareness on crime prevention
summary: Police Commissioner urges students and youth to lead crime prevention awareness efforts during an inaugural event in Kalaburagi.
content:
Laying emphasis on the role of youth in curbing crime in society, Police Commissioner S.D. Sharanappa on Tuesday called upon students and young people to take the lead in spreading awareness on crime prevention among communities.
“Youth are the future of this country. First, you must be aware of themodus operandiadopted by criminals and the ways to prevent crimes. Once you are informed, you can spread awareness in your neighbourhoods and communities to help minimise crime. You should become ambassadors of positive change in society,” he said.
He was speaking after inaugurating an awareness drive as part of Crime Prevention Month at SVP Circle in Kalaburagi. The event was jointly organised by the city police and United Hospital.
Stressing the importance of various helplines established by the Police Department for general and specific emergencies, he urged people to make use of them without hesitation.
“There are dedicated helplines to help people reach the police and other government agencies during emergencies. Dialling 112 is sufficient for any policing requirement. You need not go to the police station during emergencies; the police will reach you within 10 minutes,” he said.
Referring to cybercrimes, he said that early reporting can significantly improve the chances of recovering defrauded money.
“The Cybercrime Helpline 1930 must be used immediately in case of online fraud. Youth must not only be aware of these helplines but also sensitise people around them to their importance for effective crime prevention,” he added.
The Police Commissioner also expressed concern over the growing number of lives lost in road accidents across the country due to traffic violations and urged citizens to strictly adhere to traffic rules.
“More than 1.70 lakh people lose their lives in road accidents every year in the country. Nearly 40% of them are two-wheeler riders, mostly due to riding without helmets. In Kalaburagi alone, over 70 lives have been lost in road accidents this year,” he said and added that strict compliance with road safety norms can drastically reduce fatalities.
Highlighting the importance of people’s participation in crime prevention, he said, “The crime rate in Kalaburagi has come down by nearly 50% compared to previous years. This has been possible due to sustained police efforts and active public cooperation. Road accidents have, however, not seen a drastic decline. People’s participation is vital to building a crime-free society.”
Echoing similar views, senior general surgeon at United Hospital Mohammed Abdul Baseer said that a fearless and crime-free society can be achieved only through close coordination between the police and civil society.
“The police are meant for the people and citizens should never hesitate to approach them. We feel safe because police personnel work round the clock to protect us,” he said.
As part of the programme, students from various colleges performed dances to patriotic songs, drawing applause from the audience.
Assistant Commissioner of Police Sharanabasappa Subedar, United Hospital consultant neurosurgeon Vinaysagar Sharma and others were present.

title: Coalition govt. harassing village secretariat staff: YSRCP
summary: YSRCP accuses coalition government of harassing village secretariat staff while failing to provide necessary support and resources.
content:
The YSRCP on Wednesday (December 31) accused the coalition government of failing to provide basic facilities and institutional support to village secretariat staff and then holding them responsible for not completing tasks assigned to them.
Addressing media persons here, YSRCP Party Employees and Pensioners Wing president Nalaru Chandra Sekhar Reddy alleged that the government is planning to issue memos to over 28,000 village secretariat staff for allegedly failing to spread public awareness on Mana Mitra App.
He said the government’s assumption that every citizen owns and uses a smartphone is flawed. “There is still hesitation and fear among a large section of people in using smartphones. Hardly 20% of the population uses smartphones effectively. Expecting everyone to download and use an app is unrealistic,” he said.
Mr. Chandra Sekhar Reddy accused the coalition government of weakening the village secretariat system after scrapping the volunteer mechanism. “Despite staff making sincere efforts to spread awareness among the people, though such duties are not part of their job card, the government is now contemplating punitive action against them,” he alleged.
He termed the move to issue memos without providing proper infrastructure and resources as condemnable and demanded that the government immediately stop what he called harassment of employees.
Further, Mr. Chandra Sekhar Reddy alleged that the coalition government continues to pursue an anti-employee policy by withholding four Dearness Allowances (DAs) and Interim Relief (IR), not announcing the Pay Revision Commission (PRC) and stalling other financial benefits. “Employees’ savings are being diverted for other purposes, adding to their distress,” he claimed.
The YSRCP leader demanded that the government take responsibility for policy failures and refrain from targeting grassroots staff who are already working under difficult conditions.

title: Siddaramaiah meets Kerala CM at Sivagiri Mutt, holds cordial talks
summary: Karnataka CM Siddaramaiah meets Kerala CM Pinarayi Vijayan for cordial talks at Sivagiri Mutt after recent political tensions.
content:
After the recent verbal duel with Kerala Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan over the demolition of illegally constructed houses in Kogilu Layout in Bengaluru, Karnataka Chief Minister Siddaramaiah on Wednesday met Mr. Vijayan at Sivagiri Mutt near Thiruvananthapuram and held cordial talks.
The demolition of houses in Bengaluru has become a political flashpoint between Karnataka and Kerala after Mr. Vijayan termed the demolition drive an act of “bulldozer raj” and apparently compared it to the alleged “anti-minority” drive implemented by the BJP government in Uttar Pradesh.
Mr. Siddaramaiah, who was on a visit to Kerala, met his counterpart Vijayan at a programme at the Sivagiri Mutt and exchanged pleasantries. Both chief ministers were on the stage and enquired about the well-being of each other.
During the visit, Mr. Siddaramaiah paid his respects at the tomb of Sree Narayana Guru. On X, Mr Siddaramaiah said that he was delighted with the warm welcome he received from Gyanateertha Swami and the followers of the guru when he landed at the Thiruvananthapuram airport to participate in the programme to be held at the Sivagiri Mutt.
Speaking at the 93rd Sivagiri annual festival, Mr. Siddaramaiah said Sree Narayana Guru (1856-1928) was a philosopher, spiritual leader, and social reformer who led a reform movement against the injustices of the caste system in Kerala to promote social and economic equality.
The Chief Minister said Sree Narayana Guru was not just a saint. He was a movement for equality and morality. The holy place should take steps to eradicate caste oppression and lead the society towards social justice. “The Sivagiri Mutt is not just a pilgrimage centre but a moral university of India’s conscience. This is an intellectual and global movement of humanity,” the Chief Minister said.
The Mutt campus is spread across 200 acres. Sree Narayana Guru breathed his last in this mutt in 1928.
The programme was attended by Sachchidananda Swami, head of the mutt; AICC general secretary K.C. Venugopal, Karnataka Higher Education Minister M.C. Sudhakar and MLC B.K. Hariprasad.

title: Himachal may roll out regulated cannabis cultivation within months, says CM Sukhu
summary: Himachal Pradesh plans to legalize regulated cannabis cultivation, aiming for ₹1,000-2,000 crore in annual revenue, says CM Sukhu.
content:
The Himachal Pradesh government is moving towards legalising and regulating cannabis cultivation, with projections indicating that a fully developed framework could generate annual revenues of ₹1,000 crore to ₹2,000 crore for the State.
“We are working on finalising the modalities of the policy, including rules and regulations surrounding the hemp cultivation, keeping in view the provisions of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985, and the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Rules, 1989. I am hopeful that in a month or two it should be ready, which would then be approved by the State Cabinet,” Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu toldThe Hinduon Wednesday (December 31, 2025).
Mr. Sukhu said that for decades, cannabis has grown wild across the valleys of Kullu, Mandi and Chamba, often associated with illegal drug trade. The proposed policy, however, aims to reposition the crop for its medicinal value, including pain management and anti-inflammatory applications, as well as for use in the textile, paper and packaging industries.
Hemp is a variety ofCannabis sativacultivated for industrial and medicinal purposes. While cannabis cultivation remains illegal under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985, a legislative committee has recommended permitting non-narcotic cannabis for medicinal, industrial and scientific use.
The Chief Minister said the policy would mandate that industrial hemp cultivation maintain a tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) content of less than 0.3%, ensuring that the crop remains non-intoxicating while retaining its industrial utility.
“We have identified this natural resource as a versatile industrial asset for producing high-value goods ranging from eco-friendly textiles to bio-plastics. This ‘green to gold’ initiative aims to move the State away from illicit trade towards becoming a hub in the global bio-economy through regulated hemp cultivation,” he said.
With farmers increasingly abandoning traditional crops due to damage caused by wild animals, Mr. Sukhu said the initiative could provide an alternative and sustainable livelihood. “This strategic shift is designed to replace hemp’s narcotic image with a productive identity. Regulated cultivation can generate ₹1,000-2,000 crore annually once fully operational. It will also help capture markets currently dominated by illegal trade and imports, particularly in the pharmaceutical and wellness sectors,” he added.
The Chief Minister noted that Chaudhary Sarwan Kumar Himachal Pradesh Krishi Vishvavidyalaya, Palampur, and Dr. Y.S. Parmar University of Horticulture and Forestry, Nauni, are already conducting pilot studies to develop high-yield, low-THC hemp varieties suitable for the Himalayan region.

title: Lokayukta catches Public Prosecutor accepting bribe in Kalaburagi
summary: Lokayukta arrests Kalaburagi Public Prosecutor for accepting a ₹25,000 bribe linked to an atrocities case.
content:
A Public Prosecutor attached to the High Court of Karnataka in Kalaburagi was caught by the Lokayukta Police on the charge of accepting a bribe on Tuesday.
The accused, identified as Rajamahendra, was caught red-handed while accepting ₹25,000 as part of a ₹50,000 bribe demand.
According to Lokayukta officials, the bribe was sought for extending a favour to an accused in a case registered under the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act.
The complainant, identified as Naveen, reportedly approached the Lokayukta after the Public Prosecutor demanded money to extend cooperation in the case.
The trap was laid near the High Court premises where Rajamahendra was caught while receiving the advance amount. He was subsequently taken into custody and subjected to interrogation.
The operation was conducted under the supervision of Lokayukta Superintendent of Police Siddaraju and Deputy Superintendent of Police Sheelavanth.

title: COVID-19 ‘scam’: D’Cunha commission submits final report to Karnataka CM
summary: The D’Cunha commission reports COVID-19 procurement irregularities to Karnataka CM, revealing significant expenditure and calling for transparency reforms.
content:
The John Michael D’Cunha commission, which investigated alleged irregularities in COVID-19 procurements and management in Karnataka during the erstwhile BJP government, submitted its final report to Chief Minister Siddaramaiah on Wednesday.
The final report was related to COVID-19 procurements in the Bengaluru Urban and Belagavi districts. A sum of ₹63.79 crore was spent in the Bengaluru Urban district for the purchase of equipment. A sum of ₹42.19 crore was spent on the procurement of equipment in Belagavi district, said a release from the chief minister’s office.
Chief Secretary to the Chief Minister Shalini Rajneesh was present when the commission submitted its report. Earlier, Mr. D’Cunha, a retired High Court judge, had submitted a second interim report to the Chief Minister in April 2025.
The Congress government ordered a probe into the alleged scam involving the purchase of PPE kits and medicines and the administration of drugs, among other things, during the pandemic.
“The commission has not released the reports in the public domain; however, considering the public interest involved in the subject, and the immediate need for reforms and transparency in public procurement, the government may consider releasing the reports at the earliest,” the report said.

title: Take care of health, Vizianagaram SP tells police personnel
summary: Vizianagaram SP A.R. Damodar emphasizes the importance of health for police personnel amid profession-related hazards during a retirement ceremony.
content:
Vizianagaram Superintendent of Police A.R. Damodar advised police personnel to take care of their health, noting that the profession often involves hazards such as night shifts, long journeys and irregular food timings.
Mr. Damodar felicitated Assistant Sub-Inspector Tirumala Raju Suryanarayana Raju and head constable M. V. R. Simhachalam (Rama), who retired from service on Wednesday.
Speaking on the occasion, he urged them to take necessary precautions to maintain good health and wished the retirees a peaceful post-retirement life.
Former MLC Pakalapati Raghuvarma, Gandhi Smaraka Nidhi Vizianagaram city president Karrotu Satyam, Andhra Pradesh Teachers’ Federation honorary president Bankuru Joginaidu and others also felicitated Mr. Simhachalam and recalled his services as president of the Vizianagaram District Police Welfare Association.

title: Crimes in Andhra Pradesh decline by 6.17% in 2025, says Home Minister Anitha
summary: Andhra Pradesh sees a 6.17% decline in crime in 2025, highlighting significant progress in public safety and policing reforms.
content:
Andhra Pradesh Home Minister V. Anitha on Wednesday said the State recorded significant progress in crime control, policing reforms, and public safety during 2025, with the overall IPC/BNS crimes declining by 6.17%.
Releasing the Home Department’s annual performance note, Ms. Anitha said notable reductions were recorded in riots (53.88%), crimes against SCs and STs (24.32%), crimes against women (3.82%), POCSO cases (11.4%), and NDPS cases (7.9%).
Property crime detection and recovery rates stood at 56% and 55% respectively, which were well above the national average of 33.8%. Courts delivered 510 convictions, including 126 life sentences, in cases relating to crimes against women and children.
Highlighting women and child safety, Ms. Anitha said Operation TRACE enabled the police to trace 1,262 missing girls and 2,648 women within four months. Self-defence training was imparted to 12.95 lakh girls and women across 14,625 institutions. The deployment of 1.4 lakh CCTV cameras helped solve 2,514 cases, while 347 drones supported aerial surveillance leading to detection of 6,993 cases. ERSS-112 response time was reduced by 50% to 15.53 minutes, exceeding national standards.
The Home Minister said cyber FIRs declined by 18.94%, ₹98 crore was frozen, and ₹3 crore refunded to the victims. As part of the anti-narcotics drive, the police destroyed 99,836 kg ganja, arrested 9,478 accused, and completely eradicated ganja cultivation in Alluri Sitharama Raju district.
Ms. Anita said over ₹815 crore was spent on police welfare, 6,015 constables were recruited and stipend enhanced. She added that reforms in prisons, fire services, prosecution, sainik welfare, and disaster management strengthened governance, ensuring improved safety and resilience across Andhra Pradesh.

title: Traffic block: Idukki Collector bans road-widening work
summary: Works on Kochi-Dhanushkodi National Highway continues to cause hours-long traffic blocks on the route to Munnar
content:
As the road-widening work on the Kochi-Dhanushkodi National Highway continues to cause hours-long traffic blocks on the route to Munnar, Idukki District Collector Dineshan Cheruvatt has issued a temporary ban on the road-widening works.
The order, issued under the Disaster Management Act, states that the administration received multiple reports of severe traffic blockages. “Road-widening activities involving heavy machinery, occurring alongside the movement of tourist vehicles, pose a major threat to travellers. Consequently, all widening work must be suspended until further notice,” said the order.
The Collector also directed the Idukki District Police Chief, the Devikulam Sub-Collector, and the Devikulam Tehsildar to monitor the situation and report on actions taken by the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI).
According to officials, the Pallivasal-Munnar stretch witnessed massive congestion during the Christmas holidays, leaving tourists trapped in their vehicles for three to four hours. Following these repeated traffic snarls, tourism stakeholders urged the district administration to take immediate action to resolve the gridlock.
The sudden surge in visitors follows an early onset of winter in Munnar. On December 20, the hill station recorded sub-zero temperatures, drawing tourists from across the globe to experience the chilly weather. This inflow ultimately led to the current traffic crisis.

title: Congress plans protests seeking restoration of MGNREGA
summary: Congress plans state-wide protests demanding the restoration of MGNREGA, claiming recent changes by the NDA government harm rural employment.
content:
In response to a call given by the All India Congress Committee (AICC), State-wide protests would be staged with alliance parties and people’s organisations in support of the demand for immediate restoration of the  MGNREGA, said APCC president Y.S. Sharmila on Wednesday.
In a post on X, Ms. Sharmila asserted that Andhra Pradesh was the birthplace of MGNREGA, with the scheme taking shape and achieving outstanding success under former Chief Minister Y.S. Rajasekhara Reddy (YSR).
“Launched in the State in 2006, the employment guarantee programme became a national model for drought relief, rural development, livelihood security, prevention of migration and enhancement of rural purchasing power,” she said, adding that “over the past 20 years, Andhra Pradesh is said to have received nearly ₹1 lakh crore, providing employment to about 1 crore people annually, which is credited to the Congress-enacted NREGA law.”
Ms. Sharmila criticised the BJP-led NDA government for “diluting and undermining” MGNREGA through policy changes and a new framework referred to as the VBG RAMJI Act.
“The original law guaranteed 100 days of employment as a legal right, with gram sabhas deciding works and the Centre fully funding wages, whereas the new system centralises decisions, limits work to selected areas, reduces employment to 60 days, shifts 40% of the financial burden to States, and encourages contractor-driven projects,” she said.
Describing the new framework as “anti-poor and destructive to Gram Swaraj,” she demanded immediate withdrawal of the new framework and restoration of the original MGNREGA.

title: ‘Akka Pade’ launched in Mandya for protection of women and children in distress
summary: Akka Pade launched in Mandya to provide immediate protection and support for women and children in distress.
content:
‘Akka Pade’, comprising personnel from the State Women Home Guards, has been launched in Mandya with the aim of providing immediate protection to women and children who are at risk or in distress.
The Akka Pade vehicle was launched by N. Cheluvarayaswamy, in-charge Minister of Mandya district, in front of the Mandya Zilla Panchayat office on December 30. Deputy Commissioner Kumar, Zilla Panchayat Chief Executive Officer K.R. Nandini and Mandya district Police Superintendent Mallikarjun Baladandi were present.
Akka Pade has been constituted by the Department of Women and Child Development in co-ordination with the Police Department.
According to a statement here, the primary objective of Akka Padeis to offer swift protection to women and children facing danger or distress. “Driven by compassion and community service, the Akka Padefunctions as a responsive safety unit and an educational force that raises awareness and ensures timely intervention in society,” said the press statement.
The Akka Pade team will conduct patrols in sensitive areas and respond promptly to distress calls involving women and children. “It will also carry out legal awareness campaigns in schools, markets, and neighbourboods on issues such as gender equality, child protection, legal rights, helplines and reporting mechanisms,” the statement added.
The initiative seeks to encourage victims to seek legal assistance without fear by establishing a friendly and trustworthy presence in the community.

title: Vehicle allotted to Akka Squad flagged off in Bidar
summary: Minister Eshwar Khandre launches vehicle for Bidar's Akka Squad, a model initiative for women's and children's safety in Karnataka.
content:
Forest, Ecology and Environment Minister and Bidar district in-charge Eshwar Khandre has said that the Bidar Akka Squad, launched by the State government to prevent crimes against women and children, has already emerged as a model for the entire State.
He was speaking after flagging off a vehicle allotted to the Akka Squad at the Police Parade Grounds in Bidar on Tuesday.
The Minister said that the Akka Squad, functioning under the leadership of the Department of Women and Child Development, in coordination with police personnel, is playing a key role in ensuring the safety of women and children by conducting patrols in public places.
“The Akka Squad is acting as a vital bridge between safety and awareness in society. It is an important step towards women’s empowerment and creating a sense of security among women and children,” he said.
State advisor to the Akka Squad Shiny Pradeep Gunti said that the initiative was launched with the idea that a district can be safe only if women feel secure.
She said that the Superintendent of Police has ensured systematic implementation of the squad.
“So far, the Akka Squad has helped prevent two child marriages, shifted accident victims to hospitals and protected girls from harassment in public places. The squad will continue to work for the safety of women and children,” she said.
Addressing a gathering, Superintendent of Police Pradeep Gunti said that the Akka Squad has been formed as a women-led force to protect women.
“The initiative aims to provide immediate assistance, courage and confidence to women and children. The Akka Squad has now been strengthened using digital technology and has been expanded from the district level to the State level,” he said.
Additional Superintendent of Police Chandrakant Pujari, Deputy Superintendent of Police N.D. Sannidi, Circle Inspectors Vijaykumar Bhavge, Palakshayya Hiremath and K.M. Biradar, along with officials from the Women and Child Development Department, educational institutions and various schools and colleges, attended the programme.

title: Sports meet for State government staff to be held on January 8 and 9
summary: Mysuru to host district-level sports meet for state government staff on January 8-9, featuring various competitions at multiple venues.
content:
The Mysuru district-level sports meet for State government employees will be organised on January 8 and 9 at the Chamundi Vihar Sports Complex here.
Deputy Commissioner G. Lakshmikanth Reddy announced this while presiding over a preparatory meeting on organising the 2025–26 district-level sports meet, at the Zilla Panchayat office on December 31.
He said competitions in hockey, wrestling, kabaddi, volleyball, basketball, kho kho, ball badminton, athletics, weightlifting, bodybuilding, powerlifting, chess, throwball, swimming, carrom, yoga and tennis will be held at the Chamundi Vihar Sports Complex.
Football and shuttle badminton events will take place at the University of Mysore Sports Pavilion, while table tennis events will take place at Maharshi Valmiki School. Cricket matches will be held at the K.G. Koppalu Kennegowda Stadium.
Cultural competitions featuring Hindustani classical and light classical music, Carnatic classical and light classical music, folk songs, dance forms including Kathak, Manipuri, Kuchipudi, Odissi, Bharatanatyam and folk dance, instrumental music involving string instruments and percussion instruments, besides a handicrafts exhibition and short drama competitions, will also be held at the indoor stadium at Chamundi Vihar.
The Deputy Commissioner instructed officials to ensure adequate police bandobast at all venues. The District Health and Family Welfare Officer has been directed to arrange an ambulance with necessary medicines.
The Mysuru City Corporation was directed to arrange drinking water and other basic facilities.
Zilla Panchayat Chief Executive Officer S. Yukesh Kumar, Mysuru City Corporation Commissioner Shaikh Tanveer Asif and officials from various departments were present.

title: Supreme Court vacation benches including of CJI Surya Kant sits during winter break for first time
summary: Supreme Court holds vacation benches for the first time during winter break, ensuring timely justice for urgent cases.
content:
The Supreme Court has held vacation courts for the first time, with Chief Justice of India Surya Kant himself sitting twice during the winter break to hear urgent matters involving life and liberty, as well as those requiring immediate judicial intervention.
The top court holds vacation benches during longer summer break, which has now been rechristened as partial court working days, but this year was the first instance when the apex court held vacation benches even in a shorter winter break.
The Supreme Court was closed for the Christmas and New Year holidays from December 22 to January 2, 2026. It will reopen on January 5.
Justice Surya Kant, who was sworn in as Chief Justice of India on November 24, had made it clear on December 19 that vacation benches, including him, would sit during the winter break to hear urgent matters.
On December 22, the first day of the winter break, a vacation bench comprising the CJI and Justice Joymalya Bagchi sat to hear 17 urgent matters including several criminal and civil cases.
A statement issued by the top court said that special sittings had been arranged to ensure the timely consideration of pressing cases that required immediate judicial intervention during the vacation period.
Similarly, on December 29, a three-judge vacation bench headed by CJI Kant sat to hear a suo motu case on a new definition of Aravallis amid public outcry and kept in abeyance its November 20 directions that accepted a uniform definition of these hills and ranges.
It said there is a need to resolve “critical ambiguities”, including whether the 100-metre elevation and the 500-metre gap between hills criteria will strip a significant portion of the range of environmental protection.
The vacation bench comprising Justices J.K. Maheshwari and Augustine George Masih stayed the Delhi High Court order suspending the life sentence of expelled BJP leader Kuldeep Singh Sengar in the 2017 Unnao rape case and said he shall not be released from custody.
While hearing the CBI’s plea challenging the high court order, the vacation bench sought Sengar’s response, saying that substantial questions of law have arisen in the matter that require consideration.
On the last day of the year, a vacation bench of Justices M.M. Sundresh and Prashant Kumar Mishra conducted online hearings of two cases, including one on a habeas corpus petition alleging illegal arrest by the Uttar Pradesh Police and the other related to a civil case regarding a property dispute.
On December 29, the top court also came out with a standard operating procedure (SOP) prescribing timelines for advancing arguments in all cases and written notes by lawyers appearing before it.
The step aims to improve court management and expedite the delivery of justice.
The SOP, which comes into force with immediate effect, says, “Senior advocates, arguing counsel and/or advocate-on-record, shall submit the timelines for making oral arguments in all post-notice and regular hearing matters, at least a day prior to the commencement of the hearing of the case. The same shall be submitted to the Hon’ble Court through the online portal for submitting appearance slips already provided to the advocate-on-record (AoR).”
It said that the arguing counsel, including senior advocates, through their AoR or nodal counsel, nominated by the bench, if any, shall file a brief note or written submission not exceeding five pages after serving a copy on the other side at least three days before the date of hearing.
“All counsel shall strictly adhere to the timelines fixed and conclude their oral arguments,” the circular, signed by four apex court registrars, said.
CJI Kant had earlier indicated that the top court would be coming out with some parameters in the new year to rationalise judicial time.

title: ED seizes ₹5 crore in cash, jewellery worth ₹8 crore in money laundering case
summary: ED seizes ₹5 crore in cash and ₹8 crore in jewellery linked to a money laundering case involving Inderjit Singh Yadav.
content:
The Enforcement Directorate (ED) has seized about ₹5 crore in cash, jewellery worth over ₹8 crore, and documents of properties valued at about ₹35 crore in a coercive high-value private loan settlements case.
The searches were carried out in the case allegedly involving “strongman” Inderjit Singh Yadav and his accomplices, Apollo Green Energy Ltd, and other associated entities/persons. “The recoveries have been made from the premises of Aman Kumar, one of the associates,” said an agency official.
Mr. Inderjit is absconding and currently operates from the United Arab Emirates. According to the ED, the investigation on money laundering has been initiated, based on more than 15 First Information Reports (FIRs) and chargesheets filed by the police in Haryana and Uttar Pradesh, in connection with his “illegal extortion, coercive loan settlement of private financiers, arms intimidation and earning commission from such illegal activities”.
The search operation continued on Wednesday (December 31, 2025) for the second day on the premises allegedly linked to Aman Kumar at Sarvpriya Vihar in Delhi.
“₹5.12 crore in cash as well as a suitcase full of gold and diamond jewellery worth ₹8.80 crore were found. A bag filled with cheque books, documents pertaining to properties worth about ₹35 crore was also seized,” the official said.
“Bank officials have been roped in count the currency notes,” the official added.
The agency has alleged that “certain corporate houses like Apollo Green Energy Ltd and others allegedly borrow huge sums of money in cash from private financiers based in Jhajjar (Dighal) and issue post-dated cheques as security”.
“Investigation also revealed that Mr. Inderjit acted as a strongman and enforcer, facilitating coercive settlement of these high-value private loan transactions and financial disputes running into hundreds of crores of rupees. These settlements were allegedly executed through threats, intimidation, and the use of armed associates/local armed gangs with the involvement of organised crime syndicates operating from abroad,” the ED said.

title: Four passengers injured after two sleeper buses crash near Chandapura flyover
summary: Two sleeper buses collided near Chandapura flyover, injuring four seriously and causing traffic disruption on the Bengaluru–Chennai highway.
content:
At least four passengers were seriously injured and several others sustained minor injuries after two sleeper buses collided near the Chandapura flyover on the Bengaluru–Chennai National Highway in Anekal taluk on Tuesday.
According to police, the accident occurred when a sleeper bus heading towards Chennai from Bengaluru crashed into the rear of another bus, resulting in a major collision.
Preliminary investigation suggested that overspeeding and loss of control by the driver may have led to the accident.
Several passengers onboard sustained injuries, with four reported to be in critical condition. The injured were immediately shifted to a nearby private hospital. Following the accident, traffic movement on the Bengaluru–Chennai National Highway was disrupted for some time, leading to congestion in the area.
The Suryanagar police conducted an inspection and have registered a case.

title: Double-engine government in Andhra Pradesh lays strong foundation for a brighter 2026, says Lanka Dinakar
summary: Andhra Pradesh's double-engine government aims for a prosperous 2026 with ₹8.55 lakh crore investments and 8.23 lakh jobs generated.
content:
Chairman of Implementation of the 20-Point Programme Lanka Dinakar on Wednesday said 2025 marked a transformative year for Andhra Pradesh, with the double-engine government laying a strong foundation for a prosperous 2026.
Addressing the media at the Secretariat, Mr. Dinakar extended the New Year greetings to the people and reaffirmed commitment to Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu’s vision of Swarna Andhra Pradesh, aligned with Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s Viksit Bharat mission.
He highlighted that investments worth ₹8.55 lakh crore were approved in 2025, generating 8.23 lakh jobs, while MoUs worth ₹13.25 lakh crore signed at the CII Summit in Visakhapatnam were expected to create over 16 lakh jobs.
Welfare schemes under the Super Six benefited farmers, women, students, and the poor through direct transfers, free LPG cylinders, and free bus travel.
Major progress was recorded in Amaravati development, construction of Polavaram project, education, healthcare, pensions, and Anna Canteens, he said.
Administrative reforms, district reorganisation, and strong central support further strengthened governance, he said. Expressing confidence, Mr. Dinakar said the government would continue with the same dedication in 2026 to achieve inclusive growth and people-centric development.
Mr. Dinakar highlighted record investments of ₹8.55 lakh crore and employment generation for over eight lakh people, with additional opportunities expected from MoUs signed at the CII Summit. Welfare schemes such as Annadata Sukhibhava, Talliki Vandanam, Deepam-2 and Stree Shakti directly benefited crores of citizens, he said.
With continued central support and administrative reforms, he expressed confidence that 2026 would further accelerate sustainable and equitable development.

title: Vigilance and Enforcement detects tax evasion worth ₹228 crore in 2025, recovers over ₹213 crore
summary: Vigilance and Enforcement detects ₹228 crore tax evasion in 2025, recovering over ₹213 crore through enhanced inspections in Telangana.
content:
The Vigilance and Enforcement (V&E) Department recorded significant enforcement gains in 2025, detecting tax evasion worth ₹228.31 crore and realising ₹213.58 crore for the State exchequer through intensified inspections and enforcement drives across Telangana, according to its annual report released on Wednesday (December 31).
Between January and December 2025, the department entrusted 292 enquiries to field units, of which 480 were completed and submitted, indicating improved efficiency in enquiry disposal. As part of routine enforcement, 203 route checks were conducted during the year, covering 18,137 vehicles. These operations resulted in the booking of 3,994 cases and the collection of ₹12.51 crore towards penalties and taxes.
In the Civil Supplies sector, the department carried out 451 inspections covering fair price shops, Minimum Livelihood Security points and private premises. These inspections led to the booking of 53 cases under Section 6A of the Essential Commodities (EC) Act and 38 BNS cases, along with 24 other cases. Officials also seized 24 vehicles and confiscated essential commodities valued at ₹114.95 crore.
The department said special focus was placed on sensitive and priority areas such as cotton and paddy procurement, seed distribution, fertiliser supply, and the overloading of passenger and transport vehicles. These checks were aimed at protecting farmers’ interests and ensuring transparent implementation of government policies.
The V&E department urged citizens to report irregularities or misuse of government funds or resources through its toll-free number 14432.

title: HDMC delegation plans to meet CM over land swap issue
summary: HDMC delegation, led by Union Minister Pralhad Joshi, seeks a meeting with CM Siddaramaiah over land swap concerns.
content:
A delegation of Hubballi-Dharwad Municipal Corporation (HDMC) members will meet Chief Minister Siddaramaiah to seek allotment of land on which the old court building is standing in exchange for land given by the urban local body to the Karnataka State Law University.
Union Minister Pralhad Joshi will lead the delegation, Mayor Jyoti Patil announced in Hubballi on Tuesday.
“The all-party delegation will request the Chief Minister to allot us land in exchange for the land that we have given away,” she said.
Member Rajanna Koravi said that the delegation can have the meeting with the Chief Minister in Belagavi.
Ms. Patil said that the delegation was planning to meet the Chief Minister in Belagavi during the Winter Session, but members of the Opposition in the Hubballi-Dharwad Municipal Corporation failed to get an appointment from the CM’s office.
She said that she then brought the matter to the notice of Mr. Joshi who has promised to lead the all-party delegation. She asked Opposition leader Imran Yaligar to get an appointment from the Chief Minister’s office.
Earlier, the former Mayor Veeranna Savadi raised the issue saying that the transfer process is still pending.
He reminded that Law Minister H.K. Patil has promised the municipal corporation of handing over the old court premises as per the resolution made while granting the municipal corporation land to Karnataka State Law University.
Corporation Commissioner Rudresh Ghali said that the Indore tour of members from all parties and officials was funded from the grants sanctioned under Swachh Bharat Mission-2.
“This was meant for capacity building and other activities. As much as ₹85 lakh was sanctioned to the municipal corporation that was used for the tour,” he said.
“The tour was very useful for the officials as well as the members. In the coming days, various plans will be implemented,” he added.
This was in response to a query from member Tippanna Majjagi.
The former Mayor Ramanna Badiger said that the tour was very helpful. And, various things can be implemented individually in the respective wards.

title: Kalinga community looks to regain political influence in Srikakulam district
summary: The Kalinga community aims to regain political influence in Srikakulam through unity and increased representation in upcoming elections.
content:
The Kalinga community, one of the most influential social groups in Srikakulam district, has stepped up efforts to secure adequate representation for its leaders in the coming local body polls and the 2029 general elections. As part of this strategy, the community organised a massive gathering — theKalinga Atmiya Sammelanam— at Etcherla on December 28, drawing an estimated crowd of nearly 55,000 people.
Prominent leaders across political parties attended the meeting, including former Union Minister Killi Kruparani (Congress), Duvvada Jeeviteswara Rao (Congress), TDP MLA of Srikakulam Kuna Ravikumar, former Speaker and YSRCP leader Thammineni Seetharam, MLC Duvvada Srinivas, BJP leader Pudi Tirupati Rao, JSP leaders Daneti Sridhar and Pedada Rammohana Rao, and SSR Charitable Trust founder and industrialist Sura Srinivasa Rao.
“The unity of the Kalinga community is the need of the hour. It will help us assess the socio-economic status of our people and take steps for their development. Similar meetings will be organised soon to strengthen this unity,” said Mr. Sura Srinivasa Rao in a press release.
According to sources, community leaders Duppala Venkata Rao, Pappala Ramesh, Chintada Rammohan, and Potnuru Suryam held a preparatory meeting at Ms. Kruparani’s residence a few weeks earlier. They resolved to bury internal differences and work collectively to restore the community’s political relevance. The leaders expressed concern that, despite being numerically strong in the district, Kalinga candidates for the Srikakulam Lok Sabha seat have suffered successive defeats.
The Kalinga community has produced several MPs in the past, including Boddepalli Rajagopala Rao, Hanumanthu Appayyadora, Kaniti Viswanatham, and Killi Kruparani. In recent years, however, Kinjarapu Rammohan Naidu of the Velama community has won the Srikakulam parliamentary seat three times since 2014, while Kalinga candidates from the YSRCP and Congress failed to make an impact.
Community leaders are also worried about declining representation in the Assembly. Once dominant in constituencies such as Narasannapeta and Palasa, the Kalingas have lately found those seats being allotted to candidates from other communities, including Velama, Turpu Kapu, and fishermen groups. At present, the Kalingas represent only two of the seven Assembly segments in the Srikakulam Lok Sabha constituency — Amadalavalasa (Kuna Ravikumar of TDP) and Ichchapuram (Bendalam Ashok).

title: Yaduveer seeks probe into claims in video on alleged illegal immigrants working in Bengaluru
summary: Mysuru MP Yaduveer urges investigation into claims of illegal Bangladeshi immigrants working in Bengaluru to ensure public safety.
content:
Yaduveer Krishnadatta Chamaraja Wadiyar, Mysuru MP, has urged Home Minister G. Parameshwara to conduct an investigation into the claims made in a video by alleged illegal immigrants from Bangladesh working in Bengaluru.
In a letter to the Home Minister, Mr. Wadiyar referred to a video posted on a social media platform showing three men claiming to be illegal immigrants from Bangladesh. Pointing out that the men were claiming to be living and working in Bengaluru as security guards and auto drivers, the MP’s letter said they were also seen inviting others to come to the city for work.
Mr. Wadiyar also referred to another video in which a woman suggested that people should move to Bengaluru to avoid the strict action being taken against illegal immigrants in Assam.
“Such statements create a public impression that Karnataka is becoming a safe place for illegal immigrants,” he said, urging Mr. Parameshwara to conduct a detailed and time-bound investigation into the claims made in the viral video and verify the immigration status of the three men.
